reviews.comment: Lots of chances for extra credit, but professor was neurotic.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Prof. Griffin is a dull lecturer, making the mandatory lectures a pain to go to. He and his TAs never get things graded on time and discussion is a waste of time since they just make you work on assignments during it. Do yourself a favor and take another math course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class is not worth it, the problem is the professor. All he does is read off the lecture slides and doesn't actually teach anything. He loves to give tons of busy work, then follows by not grading the work for months. He expects a student to make every single class without exception. Spare yourself the frustration and choose a different math.

If you haven't taken stat before, good luck because you will be learning almost solely off of his slides. The slides are great, but the way he lectures is quite unengaging. Lectures are mandatory and 3 times a week. You also have to code which isn't difficult but it doesn't add to your understanding. But overall not a horrible class

He made stats dull and uninteresting which is disappoting bc I'm a Philosophy, Politics and Economics major and having a strong foundation in statistics is important in those fields. His course uses R Studio and Acrobatiq as it's core component but beyond that he puts in zero effort to engage or make lecture interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Griffin is EXTREMELY thorough with pretty much everything he says or writes. This is nice, but it does get annoying. He does a good job of giving students every possible way to learn stats, but this course is a lot of work. He teaches R, but seems like it's just busy work thrown in last minute. But, in the end, I really learned a lot.

The thing making this class difficult is the professor behind it, treating the introductory stat class as though it were a 300 or 400 level class. All the work feels like busywork, his lectures are just reading off the slides, which in-turn are just whatever the textbook says. He also takes forever to grade and give feedback, which is often needed.

Took him asynchronous during COVID this semester. He reads off mediocre slides and barely teaches. He relies on students to use an extension website called Acrobatiq, which is not helpful in teaching at all. He is also quite rude when it comes to helping students individually, in other words, I would never take him again.

I took STAT100 as an asynchronous class and it was mediocre at best. Matthew Griffin was an extremely lazy professor that just read slides off to the class instead of actually teaching. I wish I could say I learned something but I would be lying. He averages quiz grades incorrectly and gives everyone such low quiz grades.
Avoid him. Class is already hard for a 100 level course.

Won't be able to respond to emails immediately but TAs were there instead. Lectures were very clear as well as grading criteria. Crystal clear on what he's expecting from students and there's numerous sources. Very open and understanding. Lots of time to get work done. Notes/ lecture slides + practice exams were very useful and clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: COVID made this class asynchronous (except for discussions). Never seen the man once, unless you go to office hours. He posts all of his slides and expects you to do homework to make up for class time. NEW: all students will be using R/R Studio for some homework. His Practice exams are just like the real exams so take advantage. Online textbook bad

I had Prof Griffin during the Pandemic and he holds asynchronous classes. He's a very nice guy, but he was very bad at grading assignments and getting them back to us on time. 1 Midterm and 1 Final was each worth 30% of the grade. The take-home portion of exams was pretty tough, but the online portion of exams was very easy.

Took during COVID so everything was online, he didn't teach any synchronous classes so I never met or saw him. his class was organized though and he was available for questions. tests always had lots of zoom reviews and other ways to prep. I wish he had done more to interact with students, but the class was run well

The workload for this class is not that hard so long as you keep up with all of his lectures. His problem sets can be annoying at times, but as long as you do it with help from others, then you're good. His exams are almost similar to the practice exams he gives out, so just take the practice exam repeatedly until you know everything on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is definitely a great professor! His lectures contained lots of practice problems and he gives you a bunch of extra credit opportunities. There are a lot of assignments but some are dropped at the end of the semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I had the class online so Ive never talked to the guy but its STAT. You learn everything on acrobatiq, his lectures are incredibly redundant and not worth looking at. But the class is easy.
I am not a math person and att and I went into STAT at first giving little to no effort, this is a class that you can and will have success in if you just give effort.

People say Griffin is the easiest. But I'm pretty sure he is just the clearest instructor, which makes it feel easier. Yes, the exams are clearly aligned with the study guides and homeworks and the lectures, but I am not sure that this qualifies as "easy." Rather, it just means the course is actually well-designed and makes sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I'm bad at math but it was easy! Attendance wasn't required but sometimes there were worksheets(closer to the tests, they count as extra credit). Tests are EXACTLY like the study guides- just the numbers are changed. He's super accessible to ask questions & h. Hardest part was the labs, but work w/ others & it's fine. He's super understanding.
Griffin isnt the best at explaining things but this course is super easy. And if youre ever confused you can always go to GSS meetings and exam review sections hosted by TAs and peer mentors.
He gives lots of extra credit oppurtunities but his teaching isnt the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Griffin was a good professor. Although his lectures can sometimes be boring, you learn most of the material from Acrobatiq. He gives lots of resources to succeed in his class: extra credit, peer mentors, etc. Overall easy class, but I still learned a lot about statistics.
Best Teacher at UMD

The class was set up sort of weird but Prof. Griffin is nice and super understanding, especially if you go to lecture. Everything is done online and the system is sort of annoying but the tests are very similar to the review packets and are not too hard at all. He gives lots of extra credit in lecture and will sometimes count attendance points

If you do not take STAT100 with Professor Griffin then you are making a huge mistake. He is super kind and really cares about his student. Make sure you show up to class and never leave class early. He tends to hand out extra credit towards his exams at the beginning of class and then will give out more extra credit at the end of class too.

Don't take Mazzulo, take Griffin. He is so much easier. I'm terrible at math and I ended this class with my final grade over 100%. I won't lie, there is a lot of online work which is pretty time consuming, but most of the work is just graded for completion. His test averages are always super high and he gives many extra credit opportunities.

Prof. Griffin gives lots of extra credit and there are a lot of class activities that are easy points. I didn't go to discussion and that hurt my grade a little but other than that it wasn't too bad. His exams are exactly how he describes them and if you do the study guide you're set. The class was structured very nicely.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Was super strict about trivial things in my opinion. Didn't explicitly take attendance, but tried very hard to punish people for not coming to class and often complained about it heavily, seemed very against accepting late work, and was very grumpy about in class assignments. That said, he was a great lecturer with fair exams.

Definitely a great STAT100 professor. He is very helpful for assignments and always is happy to help out students. He like to get to know the students better and develop good relationships with them. Expect extra credit opportunities for his exams! It's super helpful!
One of my favorite professors. Was easy to understand and always there for help. Would highly recommend!

Prof Griffin teaches math the way it should be taught. He really tries to get us to understand the concepts behind whatever problem it is we are looking at. The class challenged me. But thanks to Prof Griffin, I was not only able t o master the concepts but also get a decent grade! For those if you failing, you gotta show up and do the work!

Very good teacher. The class is obviously easy (at least to most people) but his resources and teaching methods are very clear and helpful to the course. Tests are easy and all assignments are online.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He REALLY cares about his students and is an amazing professor. If you need to take STAT100 at UMD, take it with Professor Griffin! He knows all of his student's names and will make sure everyone understands the material.

Professor Griffin above all else, is a great guy. Although the class was easy, I still learned a lot. Griffin learned hundreds of students names in just a couple weeks, and made me feel like he really cared. Cool teacher, fun guy, and still managed to learn. Would definitely recommend him to any prospective student.

Pretty easy and straightforward. He kind of treated the class as if we were high school students. Lots of online assignments and the tests were really easy -- they're basically the same format as the review. He posts lectures online too, which is nice. He also responded to emails fairly fast. Definitely not a bad guy!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I'm not a math person at all but with a little work and very clear instruction from Professor Griffin, this class was made very accessible. Clear classwork, easy exams, and very straightforward assignments out of class. Highly recommend!

Prof. Griffin is just an all around nice guy. Although he taught the material a bit too fast for me to fully comprehend, he was always able to explain it very well one-on-one. His tests follow the same format as the practice problems and assignments that he gives, no surprises there. I'm not such a "math person," but I thrived with Prof. Griffin.

Professor Griffin is a really sweet guy who really wants to make sure you know what youre doing. Much of the class relies on online assignments but he does a good job of making that information more clear. He is extremely understanding about any assignments you might miss.

My favorite professor of the semester! He made it a mission to learn all of our names and really cared about all of us. We had a group classwork everyday that explained each concept. I felt very prepared for each exam due to the notes, lecture slides, and study guides. Totally recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is pretty much based on the online interactive textbook assigned for the class (Acrobatiq). If you are doing the readings you should have no problem doing well on this class, and the lectures will mostly feel like a review. There's 20 unannounced class activities during lectures, but are 4% of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Professor Suarez is an incredible individual and professor. He truly cares about his students and wants the best for them. Attendance was not mandatory but recommended, as there are engaging activities. There are two quizzes and one exam, all fair. I would recommend Professor Suarez to anyone, and so would my peers!

Self entitled teacher. Joke of a class and waste of time. Wastes class with weird group work, doesn't teach anything or help your grade. 4 assignments, extremely ambiguous rubrics. He didn't allow me to do a final project because I missed a class on Thanksgiving week. He is better off teaching children not college students, his career is a joke.

He didn't teach us much. He spent most of lectures telling us inspirational stories about his life and went over 5 slides at the end. You have to study for exams outside of class, cause most of lecture is spent doing time-wasters like building paper towers and "staring into each other's eyes" (an actual activity we did to practice eye contact).

He is a good teacher and very passionate about teaching.  There only thing that will mess up your grade is the quizzes.  The quizzes are small so only one wrong question makes a difference. But as long as you attend classes and put in a little effort you'll get a good grade.

Gerald Suarez is nice but not a great professor. He spent a lot of class time doing activities that did not make sense for the business and entrepreneurship world. We spend the entire semester doing pointless activities until the last few weeks where we do a final presentation. Overall, the class teaches you nothing about business.

Professor is great, but the class is awful. The projects and presentations are very unclear. This gened seems super easy, but the lack of clear information on what you need to do to get a good grade is huge. Also, 3 hour lecture aint it.

Nothing is learned. Show up to class, take quizzes on things he didnt teach, get grades. Often assignments are graded by his TA, who for some reason grades hard for no reason. Final project is very important, and he takes off unnecessary points not outlined in assignment info. would not recommend for anyone looking for a responsive and caring prof

Great guy all around, even if class is difficult he is very accommodating and genuinely cares about students. Goes above and beyond to make class not boring and generic, highly recommend glad I could have him as a teacher.

Professor Suarez is definitely one of the best professors at UMD. He truly cares about his students' development. The class was not the usual lecture and exams, instead interactive and engaging course. There is a midterm and final group project that makes up most of your grade. As long as you attend classes and pay attention you will be fine.
Professor Suarez is simply brilliant.

Professor Suarez has a few major strengths. He has unparalleled professional experiences that have enabled him to provide top-level insight and education. His second biggest strength is his ability to make that information palatable. You enjoy learning from him as much as you enjoy what you are learning. Expect a healthy challenge.

Professor Suarez is an outstanding Professor. If you're looking to grow as an individual and as a student there is no better class. Be Warned; You will likely be challenged. P. Suarez has unquestionable experience (15 years serving in the President in the White House) that manifests itself through every lecture and insight. I highly recommend him.
She just randomly will not put assignment due dates in Canvas. Difficult to deal with, making the class more difficult then it should. Doesn't grade

391. don't take with goodson. the assignments have no structure at all, theres no rubrics or specific details on what to write about, and the topics aren't interesting. she hasn't graded anything yet and we're half way through the semester. the class itself shouldn't be that hard, she's just overcomplicating it. don't take it with her.

Took her 391 class. The worst english professor you can take please do not take under any circumstances. She never grades anything on time and delays grading for weeks or even months so you don't know what your grade will be till the end. Her grading criteria and rubrics are basically nonexistent so you do not know what to expect. Very disorganized
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Please, do not take her class. Look for another professor. This class will exhaust you. It absorbs all of your time and willingness.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is a friendly professor, but she is not flexible. If you are busy or taking other classes, I do not recommend taking this class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Goodson is the worst professor I've ever had, her extremely rigid approach and lack of empathy make me wish I could rate lower. Her grading is extremely harsh and irrational, penalizing students for issues beyond their control. Communication is frustrating, and feedback is inconsistent. Avoid taking a class with this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Seemed nice in the beginning but the class was unorganized, gave readings instead of teaching how to write the papers, never explained how to write the papers, no rubrics and papers seemed like grad school papers and she never answered emails. Everyone was lost the entire semester, take another prof

Professor Goodson is a mess. She is very unclear in everything she gives out, whether it be readings, assignments or papers. The directions to everything are confusing, she never answers emails, and she does not even have a full syllabus schedule. It took her 5 weeks to grade our first paper and she did not even give feedback. Don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Assignment guidelines are always incredibly unclear. She overcomplicates simple assignments and grades unfairly. No one ever knows what is going on or what the point of the class is. She "doesn't believe in rubrics" and instead provides cluttered, often fairly useless, assignment sheets. Easily my least favorite class/prof in my 4 years at UMD.

Most of the time the things he's discussing are completely unrelated but I'm always so engaged and feel like I'm learning important things regardless. This is one of the only classes I get genuinely sad about missing because he's hilarious. Grades SUPER easily and gives barely any assignments.Definitely recommend, one of my favorite professors.

First of all, let me say I was in the ARTT260 class, but it wasn't an option.

I loved Greg, he goes on a lot of rants that are sometimes unrelated, but they are also super entertaining. The actual graded workload is super light, but I still learned so much from this class. I highly recommend! He also provides all extra content for free :)

Greg is absolutely amazing- so funny, and such great insights. He knows a ton about film. He isn't a fast grader and can be a little uncommunicative, but he isn't harsh with his grading and is accommodating. You have to go to class to understand what's going on, but it's so fun, you'll want to go!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A great class, I got a lot from it. The professor had great insights into the films and I enjoyed the lectures, they were all interesting. If you enjoy the films, you will enjoy the lectures. As long as you write a decent essay, you will do well.

He rambles a lot, but it gives him character - it's not really as bad as it sounds in the reviews. I took two of his classes, this was for my last full semester on campus. Fair grader who clearly loves his work, although he had a tough semester, so it took a while for him to get papers back to us.

If you like film and art this class is really enjoyable. Yeah his lectures are super tangential but he's really interesting and funny and knows SO much about film and philosophy so the tangents are informative and helpful for the papers. Class is graded on 2 papers but if you support your ideas and are thorough you will do well.

Interesting class with good film material. Lectures are terrible. 60+ minutes of mostly useless tangents by cynical, egotistical prof. Still, very easy class if you can put up with the lectures. Also, required weekly blog entries are annoying.

Good teacher and interesting class but like everyone else says he definitely does go on rants for half the class that are totally unrelated to class. I still learned a lot and enjoyed the class- good for HA Core. Movies are good.

He's a really interesting, funny guy. He does go off on tangents that can sometimes make his lectures hard to follow, but we generally went over everything from lecture in discussion. The films are interesting and the tests are easy; you just have to make a good argument in your essays. Attendence is necessary though - you can't miss the movies.

Whoever said this class was hard thats rediculous. As long as you saw the movies and listened to him it was easy. Essays were cake as long as you said something that made sense and you could support. Class was full of tangents and jokes. Easy HA core!!

awesome class. goes on these ridiculous rants that don't seem to ever end, however, the movies are for the most part ones that are worth watching. class is interesting. easy class. 2 essays, one midterm, and one final. if you go to class, you get an A. simple as that

Greg was hilarious. He drank a 2 Liter bottle of soda everyday in front of class and told the most random stories/jokes. His  film class was surprisinly hard though. I'd take another class of his, but not this one again... it was a lot of work/memorizing terms.

Good professor with an open class.  Prone to tangents, but usually good ones.  TA runs the class outisde of lecture moreso than with other professors.  The TA from this year was exceptional, but rumor has it he's gone now.  The class could very likely be different next year as a result.  In any event quite possibly my favorite class of the year.

great class. very interesting movies, good tas, good discussions, exams weren't too bad, just support what you say. he likes gilmore girls and talks a little too much (its the pepsi) but...otherwise, great. take it.
This was a really wonderful class. One of my fav and he gives you a new appreciation for film. He is an interesting and hilarious lecturer. You'll want to come to class.
ITS BORING AND HE THINKS HE IS WITTY...BUT HE IS AN IDIOT. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

Prof. Metcalf is great - his tangents are great, and he's always cracking lame (but still funny) jokes.  The movies in the screenings are fairly good (with a few exceptions - by no means are they all exciting, but they all open your mind past the normal conventions of Hollywood films).  Read the textbook and study to pass.  Great professor!

Prof. Metcalfe is awesome! I think he is my favorite professor right now. Yes he goes on tangents, but those tangents are fun, at times tied in with whatever we are discussing in class that day. He's always smiling, and is funny and quirky. But also very knowledgable. If you wanna sign up for CMLT280, get Metcalfe!

Yes, he tend to ramble, but give the man a break -- he was in a car accident recently and was on some pretty heavy painkillers when I had him.  Extremely knowledgeable.  Do your reading -- unannounced quizzes -- and don't skimp on the essays.  Light workload.  Enjoyable experience (minus Last Year at Marienbad).

I think he's one of the best professors at Maryland. He's brilliant, he's knowledgeable, he's got a great sense of hummer, and he's a really interesting guy. But he's not for everyone, some people just don't get him.

he's a good guy, he'll help when you ask him for help.  he knows his stuff, beyond what you can expect, imagine the most knowledgeable person in film, he's more than that.  workload not much, but make sure your work is good or you're screwed.

He rambles. This man starts tangents on tangents on tangents. His class is really interesting, though. I loved it. It's not an intense workload, either. But do not ever think you can get away with being disrespectful in his class.

Very knowledgable professor, pretty chill, and very interesting subject matter. Be prepared for a short writing assignment, two group projects (although you only have to do one), a final group project, and nightly readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors - the class material was interesting and relevant, but he took it to the next level. I loved taking this class purely because of Dr. Greene.

He is actually the best professor at UMD. I have no idea if he has received any distinctions or awards but I would 10000% take him again. He is very understanding and wants his students to excel. The class is really easy if you pay attention and apply every feedback you get properly. There are reading but nothing too heavy or intensive. Take him.

Greene is cool, caring. He has high expectations but just follow the rubric and write well and you'll do fine. Go to class for the clicker questions. Lots of reading. We only had one exam, and it was mostly on the readings. Multiple projects, but they were fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I took INST201 with Professor Greene and I thought he was amazing. I was interested in every lecture. Every class he had a system of taking attendance and making sure you read so YOU MUST SHOW UP. If I could take this class again with him I absolutely would. If you go to his office hours he listens and tries to give advice, highly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: A great professor, does tons of hands on demonstrations, very engaging lectures, really approachable and kind, and made a lot of jokes. I learned the material well.

Professor Goodman is enthusiastic about this subject. I am not strong in physics, so I struggled a lot in this class. He records lectures and posts them, but sometimes that is not helpful as not all of the information you need to know is on there. Overall, I liked having class with him, but am definitely not taking physics any time soon.

Goodman isn't a bad person but he should retire. Got a substitute prof once instead of cancelling, went on trips for other projects twice during the semester. When he finally cancelled a class for the first time, left a sign on the room door instead of sending out any email/canvas message. Info is taught in a confusing way. Would not recommend.

Dr. Goodman is such an amazing professor! The class is interesting by itself, but he makes the content even more interesting through his fun lectures and demonstrations. 100% would take him again if possible!
Probably one of the best Professors at UMD and the bets in the PHYS dept.

Goodman is one of the best professors I had on UMD campus. He is very caring and extremely knowledgeable about the materials he teaches. His office hour is always helpful and always easy to find him. Take him if you can you won't regret it. But go to the lecture and pay attention to class otherwise you won't pass
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Goodman is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He's very helpful and actually cares about his students.  He's very lenient with his grading because he clearly wants us to actually learn something from him as opposed to simply trying to maintain a good GPA. Take this class seriously though, it is somewhat challenging but very interesting.

Take this class. He is amazing, charismatic, smart, and loves to teach. His class is amazing, but you have to be there every class to get a good grade because that's the only way getting a good grade. The lecture slides are only some notes for him to teach, not really NOTES that you want for study. So be there. Great teacher.

This guy is amazing! He is a very down to earth guy but has a ridiculous resume. His knowledge on the subjects is unrivaled and has actually had hands-on experience on most of the stuff he talks about. His classes are fun and his tests are very fair. Go to class for the entertainment, not because you have to! A++

Absolutely wonderful class. Goodman is hilarious and keeps the class lively. You can tell he's very passionate about what he teaches. Tests are pretty fair, homework is easy, lectures are fun (you'll actually want to go), and the demos are cool. Oh, and he's a fantastic photographer as well.
Professor goodman is the man... Take this class he is willing to help with anything you need and extremely leniant

By far the most interesting class I have ever taken at Maryland. Although attendance is not mandatory, you get points, and sometimes extra credit, for answering clicker questions. As someone who usually skips all of her classes, he actually made me want to show up and learn. Plus he is cute!

By far the most interesting class I have ever taken at Maryland. Although attendance is not mandatory, you get points, and sometimes extra credit, for answering clicker questions. As someone who usually skips all of her classes, he actually made me want to show up and learn. Plus he is cute!
Extremely helpful. He made the course interesting. Great sense of humor. One of the best professors at UMD.
Extremely helpful. He made a course I had little interest in a fascinating subject. Great sense of humor. Best professor I had at UMD.
He really knows what he's talking about and that makes class material easier to understand. He's a fair grader and just seems like an all around nice guy.

Professor Goodman is great! He is extremely helpful if you have any problems, tests are usually 8-10 questions and each cover about 10 lectures, but as long as you look over them and study, you will do fine. There is one paper that you can pretty much choose anything to write about within the class' interest. Curves big time. Very interesting class

he's incredibly entertaining; more interested in showing the experiments to the class than just explaining. sometimes the things he explains are completely over your head, but he puts his notes on blackboard afterwards. most info is from the book but going to class is a really big plus if you're not so physics-minded (like me). definitely recommend
Dr. Goodman is the best professor I've ever had.  He's very entertaining, and he makes the subject matter applicable and interesting.  He obviously really loves teaching.  ABSOLUTELY take his class.
Goodman rocks. He is very much like Hank Scorpio, the supervillian from the Simpsons. Highly entertaining.
too easy class was actually kind of fun
He is an uninspiring prof, I would not take his class again. Didn't learn a thing.

pretty easy class; as long as you read the textbook and watch the videos for each week. everything leads up to a huge group project at the end of the semester (4k words for the first part, 800 for the second) which was the most "challenging" part, but as long as you get good teammates who pull their weight, the class isn't hard at all.

James Green is an NPC, but he's a true entrepreneur for charging $30 for a textbook and you getting a free A in return. Unfortunately, it was my own fault that I didn't after taking it during high school and forgetting a week while my school went on spring break. You WILL get an A just by doing the work as long as you're not forgetful.

I mean, eh. Take this class if your schedule is filled and you cannot have another  class in your schedule.  It's  not an easy A, more like an easy B. Even if you read the textbook,  the answer isn't clear. If you get a 4/5 on the quiz itll take ur grade by like four points because these quizzes are, for some reason, worth 45% of your grade!

This class is easy... as long as you are never sick or have outer life events because he would refuse to understand!! Take it if nothing ever happens and your family doesn't have emergency as well as never getting sick!!
Unsympathetic and unhelpful. Honestly no words. No sympathy for other people.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took ENES460 online over the winter session.  This course is mainly common sense and by the end, I was no longer watching any of the videos.  I was just completing the assignments.  You do not need his book to succeed.  Plan ahead because you have to conduct a lot of interviews in a short time.  The feedback he provided didn't feel personalized.

grade comes from: Buying his book and clicking through the pages, weekly online quizzes, and one major 3000 word-final based on completion that you work on throughout the semester. Online quizzes are worded weirdly sometimes but you can ctrl+f most of the answers directly from the textbook, however each question wrong deducts 1% of grade. Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took ENES140 and ENES210 at the same time. Most of your grade comes from weekly quizzes that can do some damage at the end if you miss one or two. They were easy though, as long as you at least skimmed through the textbook (which is mandatory btw). I know a lot of people take this as an easy Gen-Ed but I found the material to be pretty relevant.

I wouldn't say that he's an easy A, rather the means to get an A aren't hard. Quizzes, readings, and a final paper are all you have to do. The quizzes are cake if you stay on top of it. Try not to miss any, the points will add up in the end. The final paper isn't hard as long as you follow instructions and try you'll get an A.

reviews.comment: James Green is the worst teacher I have ever had in my entire life. All he cares about are his degrees and his fat paycheck. He doesn't care about his students. All he does is gives a ridiculous amount of busy work that, in the end, doesn't help you learn about what it takes to be an entrepreneur. WASTE OF TIME AND MONEY!!

If you are looking for an easy A class, take this class. The workload is one weekly activity and one quiz per week. The professor provides lecture recordings that help you with the weekly activity. reviews.comment: Took him for ENES140 online, which is a super easy class.  He did a good job organizing the material and providing timely feedback for work.
This class was very easy. Would definitely recommend taking this course.
Awesome content and Professor

Dr. Green is very reasonable with the work he gives. The modules are very helpful and easy to navigate through. Dr. Green is one of the few  professors who care and understands if you need certain accommodations. The class was very helpful and motivated me to look into business ventures! Thank you Dr. Green
Class is very manageable is you do everything on time

This was an easy class to take and helped me learn about the realm of entrepreneurship. I would say the class doesn't have much connection to engineering, but it was still nice to take. The textbook was decent, and his syllabus is pretty concise on class requirements. While I didn't talk with him much, he had a good overall structure for the class.

He is a reasonable professor and ENES210 was very simple with him. 30-60 minute weekly lectures, about an hour of work outside class, if you work at a decent pace. Only thing is that you have a 4k word paper at the end of the class. Not super difficult, and he's helpful if you send him emails, but keep this in mind so it doesn't sneak up on you!

Other than 30 min synchronous online lectures, this class gives like 1-2 hours of work per week. Every week there was one assignment and a quiz. Both easy. Final project at the end is 4K words, a little much but not hard either.

final project is overwhelming if you don't do well on the activities throughout the semester. He made the project individual when in the past I heard it was a group project. Regardless it was still an easy A. Quizzes are a huge part of your grade but read the book and you're good.
Very strict, does not give chances to make up assignments or provide extensions even if it's for a situation beyond your control. Is not understanding at all. Very rude and does not respect students.

Professor Green is one of the best professor I've had the privilege of learning from. He makes his lectures super interesting by incorporating real world examples to all the concepts he teaches. Really enjoyed his class.

Overall, the class was easy to follow and not a large time commitment. The paper was confusing at first but he was quick to reply to all my questions and always provided positive feedback. Although the class was to fulfill a Gen Tech, I wouldn't mind taking a similar class

This class is really valuable and pushes you outside of your comfort zone. There is a textbook that helps with quizzes and the final project. The lectures are great and provide useful information for the project! The professor is helpful and will reply promptly (usually within 24-48 hours.) You have to be willing to do the work. Great class!

reviews.comment: I really appreciated this class and found it to be valuable! At first, I was nervous to be in his class. However, I have come to realize that this class is not bad! reviews.comment: Easy A. This is a class you take to get a gen Ed and move on and he knows that. You have to buy his textbook. Overall, this course is mot worth the extraordinary amount money one class costs. But if you want an easy A and barely do any work this is for you.

ENES210 was an easy A but it never felt like he really cared too much. the class seems more like he's trying to sell you on himself rather than teach you. grades are all very easy, make sure you have a good group for the project, but he wasn't personable or super friendly

This class is fairly easy with only 5 simulations, weekly quizzes/assignments, and a group project at the end. You have to buy the textbook that he created for $25 and you must buy it since it has the simulations. The class is a really easy class if you get a good group. Everyone splits up the work and you'll be fine. No midterm/final exam!

He has ENES210 basically automated. The lectures are pre-recorded but synchronous, all of the weekly modules appear ahead of time automatically, you get the point. The class is centered around a group project, so if you get a poor team, you're doomed to do everything on your own. Otherwise, the professor is fine. No complaints. Relatively easy A.

He requires you to use a book that is redundant. It is not worth the money and you don't really use the book. As well his lectures (at least right now during covid times) are only 15-20min and he glosses over the important parts but is repetitive on nonessential information. If it wasn't for credit I would not take this class.

He grades easy but you need to come to class for the in class activities or else your grade will drop significantly. When you ask for help he is condescending and acts like you are bothering him. The whole class is based around a group project. He does not put in simulation grades until the very last minute even though theyre graded on the website

Good professor, great lecturer, but most of the class was either working on a group project or doing online quizzes at home. Fairly easy to get an A as long as you stay on top of due dates and go to class.

ehhhh. should be an easy A, but you have to read a lot of course material just to answer 5 question quizzes and home works. He does not accept late work for any reason. Final project is really easy if you put in effort.

I do the readings and use them while I take each quiz, but he words the questions so specifically that it's impossible to do well. NOT as easy as it looks

This class was a huge pain. So much work in the form of simulations, quizzes on elms, interviews, papers, and a huge 4,000+ final paper. I would totally avoid this class altogether as an elective. He really makes you work to get an A. The textbook is an interactive ebook that is very easy to read but still costs money. Avoid this class if possible.

For the first part most of the material is common sense, but make sure to pay attention to the simulations. I slacked off and when he started putting them in at the end of the semester my grade went down LOW. The final project was fine too.

The quizzes had nothing to do with the lecture material, if you didnt read everything and take extensive notes you had no shot. He changed the final exam instructions and did not alert the class and that caused a lot of people to lose points. It was extremely stressful and did not need to be that way. Do not take this class.

Not an easy class. It is a SCAM for you to buy his book that teaches you nothing, I learn more from reading a bathroom stall. There was in class activity every week so if you don't go to class, you won't know what do

So this semester WHEN I TAKE ENES210 he wants to make the average in the class a B MINUS. It's just crazy how unnecessarily rude he is and how mediocre his grading criteria is. Dr. Green is a condescending person and quite rude. He requires you to buy his own online textbook which is like $30 and without it, you can't do the assignments. reviews.comment: Not an easy A class anymore!! As a business major, I took this class as a GPA booster but I am totally wrong. The professor put too much weight on final exams and final project. Final exam is extremely difficult even though you read all the readings and go to every class.

Easy class, especially if you've taken business classes. The important thing was keeping up with material. Since it was online, it is easy to forget about. But the textbook readings were super short and easy to understand and reading them made the assignments extremely easy.
This class is extremely easy even though the writing parts are unnecessarily tedious.

The entire class is based off of one group project that requires so much work for a 200-level course. Prof. Green rarely lectures, so classes are spent completing in-class activities instead. He forces you to buy his textbook, which was very poorly edited. One of the worst professors I've ever had.

reviews.comment: Easiest class at UMD but Green wasn't very lenient when it came to grading.

Easy class, but they changed it from past years. Lots of online writing assignments, and some online quizzes. Online textbook purchase is mandatory. No final, but a group project at the end. Still one of the best ways to get an A on UMD campus.

Although they made enes140 harder by adding in 5 analyses (each 10-12 questions and 200 words per question), the class is still an easy A class and frees up your schedule immensely. Just make sure you actually do everything and submit them on time.

All of his videos are literally just him saying exactly what's in his textbook. He adds in maybe 5 new factoids but it's so boring. I think as long as I don't forget that I'm taking this class (b/c it's all online), the A will be easy. Some TedTalks he's linked are interesting but it's a lot of excess material if you're taking this as a GenEd.
The only good thing about this class was that it was an easy A. If you put any sort of effort into the class it's impossible to get less than that. Good GPA boost, but don't expect to learn anything.
Easy class. You don't need spend lots of time on it

Gave a 3/5 simply b/c it is an online class and the only thing I know about him is through the weekly email he sends. Pretty easy class - take if you need its GenEd - an A is very manageable as long as you turn in your work and do the proper word count on the Analysis projects. Still waiting on final to be graded, but have a high A so far.
Hes just out here for the money, he makes 200k a year just from kids buying the book, class is a joke, just do all the assignments and you will get an A+. No in person lectures
Easiest class you'll take at UMD, if you need a GPA booster take this

He rarely responds to emails and when he does, they aren't helpful. The class itself was fine, but not as easy as everyone says it is. I didn't feel like I learned anything. The readings and lectures were very example heavy but didn't actually explain what anything actually is.

Really good online course. So long as you read and watch the online lectures, you are sorted. The load is not so much. Perhaps at max an hour a day depending on what you are doing. Doesn't really respond to email, but then again he has about a thousand students for that one class.

good teacher and will explain something if you ask during class, but will not address emails. also tries to act like a  hard ass but he is actually a good guy. good teacher and easy course.
Great class. Great prof. Learned a lot and enjoyed discussions in class.

This class was really easy. You only get about 3 short essays for the semester, and one group project which is your final. He may scare you in the beginning saying that the course is hard, but its really not. Its pretty much a breeze as long as you come to class. His teaching is also very good, he explains everything fully. Need a break? take this.

One of the worst CS professors I have ever had. He has restrictive office hours times and his refusal to accept any communication outside of office hours makes him impossible to reach out to when there's a problem submitting assignments. Was very disrespectful when I tried to ask a question about a project before class that TAs couldn't answer.

A really boring guy. One of the most difficult parts of this class is staying awake during lecture.  For exams just review the practice tests he gives. Projects feel like walking across campus with a person on your back. It's not that difficult of a task, he just makes it so. There is extra credit on most projects, but its not a lot (6/100 points)
Larry's class has a clear structure - attend lectures, do worksheets, and you'll do well. The projects are challenging but doable with preparation. Unstuck ai was a lifesaver for exam prep.
Awful Prof!

Don't go on your phone in lecture - he will call you out.
Pay attention in lecture and do the worksheets and you'll do well. There is also extra credit opportunities for every project.

Most mid Prof you'll see or have in ur entire life. His exams are fair but you do need to study weeks ahead. It's hard to talk to him unless it's office hours and there could be assignments during lectures and no recording. Passing him won't be an issue as long you actually put in the time and read a textbook he says to read.

Larry is the WORST CS professor I have ever had. His lectures are 75 minutes, incredibly boring, graded worksheets in almost every one of them, and you can't have laptops in his CS lecture. He stopped grading in the middle of the semester and at that point I had a B-. Grades dropped today 15 days after the final, and I just found I failed.

Gives clear criteria for his projects, every edge case is given. Doesn't test you on what you shouldn't know. TA's are accessible most hours. Lectures are structured.

reviews.comment: Don't take him if you're anything other than a verbal learner because all he does is talk. He's also condescending, which is upsetting being new to coding.

people who be giving Larry 1-2 have skill issues, he is strict with his rules but also easy to understand. His lectures are recorded for people who need to review some materials which is good. Ensure you go to all his Lectures and Discussions because sometimes they graded worksheets. Projects are very descriptive, Test are the fairest they can be

I feel like people give Larry a hard time, but truly had so much fun in his class. I had him for 132 and 216 and he is an amazing teacher, he made everything easy to understand. He is so quirky, so if you like that, Larry is your guy. Sheena Sheep 4ever.

Live Laugh Love Larry. Manz is very clear about his policies, but as long as you follow them all you'll have a fine time in his class. He always makes jokes (albeit dad ones) and does what he can to keep students enganged during lecture. A generous man (not professor!!!) who gives out chocolate, but does take a long LONG while to grade. Luv him tho

Some might find him to be a good instructor while others might not. His lectures are at times a bit boring but he does his best to make them interesting through his sense of humor. His project descriptions and extremely detailed and his exams are fair.
He is the larry. He's amazing

What a guy! I will say, he tends to be passive-aggressive to people who don't show up to class, but he always cracks me up in lectures. The perfect way to describe him is funny without trying to be. A caring guy who will love you if you follow his rules :). His project descriptions also have jokes scattered about and are entertaining to read thru.

Herman is really underrated. He has a unique style that does take getting used to. His best aspect is the fact that he's almost an ok lecturer at best. Other than that this man is a complete and udder jerk. reviews.comment: Never picking him again. Nearly impossible to get office hour help throughout the semester. Everything in this class was oddly structured and did not make sense.

He is so disrespectful. He made it so difficult for me to use my accommodations. He is a very slow grader.
