I guess he teaches okay. But from Fawzi, hes a big drop in quality. If you want someone who focuses on the students dont choose him.

Projects are very tough and lengthy. Exams are pretty average for a CS class, but still pretty tough. Herman has good lecturers, but is often boring and tough to pay attention to. 132 with him went very well, but 216 with him was not too good. Way too much time required for this class.

Larry explains everything clearly and the exams are fair. He also tries to make the content easier given the difficulty of the course. That being said, he can be boring and monotonous when he lectures, making him a little hard to pay attention to. Also, the projects of CMSC216 can be a pain to deal with, so be prepared for long hours of coding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Larry is much better than the rating he's given here. He's eccentric but he's a really good teacher and gives out a lot of study materials

If you're truly interested in learning about CS rather than just trying to get a good grade, then Larry is a great professor. His lectures are very informative and he tries to keep them interesting with his humor. The projects and exams can be challenging but they are fair. If he says to read a chapter that's not covered in class, READ IT.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Fantastic lecturer (not a professor!), could be touch on policy from time to time. But his lectures are genuinely well-written and straightforward. The projects are challenging yet manageable. He deserves better tbh.

Pay attention to the project descriptions and do the practice tests and you'll do fine. He has an interesting personality that not everyone likes, but he knows a ton and expects a lot from his students. He doesn't answer emails, but if you can get a hold of him outside of class, he's very eager to help.

Obsolete to say to the least  outdated materials copied from past years for more than a few decades. Computer Programming has changed a lot in 20 years, while he is still talking about bubble sort and simulating Unix command-line systems. Pathetic. Poor students have to deal with these old and obsolete learning methods.
Larry truly cares about this students and will help them out during office hours if they ask for it. His exams are hard but fair. Attending class is a must if you want to do good in class.

Larry is a fun and hilarious teacher. His projects have very clear expectations and his tests are straightforward (with lots of review material provided). He is also extremely careful about what he says and takes the class very seriously. (He will correct himself in the next class if you let him know about a mistake he made in lecture.)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He spends probably about 7-10 total minutes per 50 minute lecture telling people to either: 1. Telling students to not sit in the back rows (He's obsessed with this) 2. Telling people to get off their phones or laptops. I stopped going to his lectures because he would spend almost 20% of the already short lecture time on nonsense like this.

Larry is not a bad professor. His lectures can get boring because he has a really monotone voice which makes it hard to stay engaged, but he will joke around to keep things light-hearted. He does know the material but is strict when it comes to electronics in the lecture hall. DO NOT sit in the back row. Good 'Ol Larry

Overall, not a good teacher. His lectures are very wordy and he restricts any electronics, so it may be hard for those who usually take notes on laptops. His tests and projects are absurdly long which take longer to understand and his grading criteria are strict in every way possible. Choose another teacher if you have other options!
Actually decent lecturer. Tried his best to make the class funny. Quite annoying sometimes but explained everything well in class.

Herman is a straightforward, clear instructor who makes lectures boring, yet comprehensible. He is very picky about coding style and his exams are very short, so it is easy to lose a lot of points. You can still earn a good grade if you do the exam practice and review the worksheets. Overall, he's not as bad as people say he is, but he is annoying.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Herman is an okay instructor. He will spend the first ten minutes of every lecture saying the same things everyday. He will also waste serious amounts of class time to call people out for being on their cell phone. Overall, tests were pretty difficult, but the discussion worksheets aren't graded for accuracy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Although he is very strict on students sitting in the back of the lecture hall and against cell phone use, his lectures were great and he is a very funny guy. I think many people don't give him the credit he deserves. His lectures are very understandable but his exams are tough and have a tough grading system.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall, not a good teacher. His lectures are very wordy and he restricts any electronics, so it may be hard for those who usually take notes on laptops. His tests and projects are absurdly long which take longer to understand and his grading criteria are strict in every way possible. Choose another teacher if you have other options!
Provides detailed descriptions for projects. Fair exams with realistic practice exams/homeworks to help prepare. Boring lectures, funny sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall a low quality "teacher". He is not a professor. During his lectures he gets off topic frequently and classes are always behind. He says to ask question and be involved, but when students raise their hand to ask, he says "ask me after class". He has does not allow laptops or electronic of any type in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I just came here to defend my man Herman. You need to pay attention in class to get much out of him - You will learn a lot if you do so, more than other professors. It looks to me that only the people who dont attend class and not put in effort hate the guy. He is also nice outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Larry is a solid lecturer. It takes a couple lectures to get used to his style though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I had him for CMSC132, and had to take him again due to lack of seats, and If you thought that CMSC132 was bad, this was worse as it his him again. Now with longer lectures, and moves through syllabus at a faster pace. And, also leaves chapters for "self-reading" on which we are tested thoroughly without any explicit in-class explanation to topics.

He is the most bogus professor there can be. His in-class policies do make sense, but most students end up falling asleep listening to his monotone voice and revised jokes which he has written on paper. Unlike other CS Professors, he isn't understanding at all when you have genuine concerns and problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a good instructor but the problem is that you don't really learn in his class. His material is we prepared and tests can be sometimes insane. He is a harsh grader though. Look for other professors if you get an option.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Herman is a good professor that gives clear instructions on what he wants his students to do. His project descriptions are usually really long but very specific making the projects a lot easier. He is a funny guy that opens up to most students but doesn't really show it unless you pay attention in class. A bit of a hard grader but overall good guy.

His projects are slightly difficult & make you think but they are manageable if you put in the work. You will finish the course actually having knowledge in CS if you actually do the projects, HW,& WS. He says SOOO about every 5 mins but if you can get over that & his love for walruses he's not that bad- as long as you're putting in work as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Herman is by far the funniest professor I have had up to this point. He is a really nice guy and his projects and exams are pretty fair. He will give you practice exams and practice worksheets that are optional and will be very helpful for preparing for exams. Id definitely take him again; he puts a lot of effort into the materials he makes.
Larry is very funny and entertaining. He explains things well. His tests are fair. He can be a little arrogant.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Herman is really funny, but he's strict on a lot of small things like he won't let you use phones or sit in the back row, or he WILL call you out. His slides and lectures are very useful, but they weren't necessarily interesting. HIs exams sometimes have trick questions tho. I'd recommend taking him again because he seems to know what he's doing.

Herman is a pretty good teacher. You may get some not-great grades on tests, but he curves at the end of the year. He can be pretty scary, especially when he's mad, but he's generally very nice. Start projects early, and go to TA office hours ASAP if you have problems! He changes what animals he uses for examples annually so he doesn't go insane

So in spite of what the last few reviews say, Herman's not that bad. He teaches the material well, and his tests are fair, if challenging. There are certainly better lecturers in this department, but he's a fine choice. He has some rather irritating expectations of students during lecture, but you get used to it. Pay attention and you'll do well.
Terrible, PERIOD!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: He's horrible, don't take him NO MATTER WHAT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class isn't too hard, but this guy is so annoying with everything he does. Freaks out if you don't sit in one of the front rows, won't answer questions unless it's the perfect time for him, doesn't respect students. Also takes longer to grade projects/exams than anyone I've had.
Larry Herman is super paranoid, he has no respect for you, he thinks he is the best and that he is untouchable. I know this is a  very competitive program but at least act descent.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Larry Herman, repeats senseless things 50 million times, he rambles on about his weird animal obsession, not only his teaching style but how he treats human beings  in my option should be looked into, IT'S A HUGE RED FLAG. he basically treats like trash. He is super paranoid when he post his slides, notes etc. he put passwords and coding on them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Nice guy, funny, posts PowerPoint online, and gives constant advice to help pass the class. Projects can even be turned in a couple days late. Tests are pretty hard, but the exam reviews are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Larry Herman is a 4/10. Only liked his project descriptions and how he wants students to learn. His exams were hard generally speaking(some easy questions then wtf hard ones), practice exams are not really helpful. Teaches 95% of class with lecture slides. Tries to be funny with giraffes. Scary stare. Learned from him though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Herman is an acquired taste. At first, you might think he's a little weird with his mannerisms, but then he starts to grow on you. His lectures are fairly straightforward and the exams aren't crazy hard if you put some effort into studying. Just make sure you don't sit in the back row and whatever you do, DON'T call him by "Professor".

Herman is a hilarious dude. His passion for giraffes has become a quality he really tries to share with the rest of his students. His tests may be tough at some points but in the end, he teaches the material well. I would retake him again gladly and listen to him praise the giraffe kingdom all over again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE HIM!!!!!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Herman is a p good teacher. Funny to see other reviews see him talking about llamas -- he's moved on to giraffes. He has a little tolerance for people who don't follow his rules (eg texting, yelled at this girl for writing after the time on the test finished), but nothing wholly unfair. I plan on taking another class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love Larry Herman! I had him for cmsc132 and cmsc216. Generally speaking I think his exams are hard and his projects are easy. I love his lectures a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is the very definition of nuisance. No one likes him, not even the staff. His homework description is indecipherable. In exams and quizzes, he gives a big portion of points to corner-case questions. Do not expect any jokes in lecture, because he has absolutely no humor and he just cannot stop talking and pause a little bit for us to understand!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: One of the worst if not the worst. Talks about llamas nearly every lecture and also makes inappropriate comments to girls to illustrate  certain concepts. Projects aren't too bad, but beware of his strict grading criteria.  Exams are terrible. Very condescending and will not answer email (well he does, just to tell you he doesn't). Worthless slides
Cool guy

Larry's lectures are awesome! I loved his class and I recommend that you try to get Larry. His projects are easy! If you want to do well on the exams, be sure to study "homework" assignments. The exams will always be the same content and format as the study materials he posts on ELMS. Good luck and have fun!
Larry has some bizarre mannerisms (whats with all the llamma's, man?) but he's generally a funny and clear teacher and his office hours are very helpful.

Had him for 132 and 216. He's very precise in what he wants in terms of coding style, but that just makes you a better coder in the long run. Exams are kinda tough, but they're usually pretty similar to the practice exams. He can be "mean" and intimidating, but he's not there to be your friend. Very smart, gives help when you ask for it

A very good professor. He can be a bit intimidating and kicked people out of class for being on their laptops but he explains the material very well and tries to make jokes throughout the lectures sometimes. He is what you'd expect out of a normal college professor.

The best professor I've ever had. Herman is an outstanding teacher. You will learn a lot.  Remember, a teachers primary job is to teach. Everything else is secondary. Truth is, if you love learning, then you'll love Herman's class because you learn a lot.  You can definitely get an 'A', but you need to put a considerable amount of time into it.

People believe Herman is mean or boring with his no cell phone or computer policy during class but it has helped a lot. He makes sure everyone is paying attention in lecture and he really knows computer science! He makes it easy enough for even the lowest level comp sci majors to understand. If you pay attention you will hear him attempt at jokes.

Larry is a solid teacher. He isn't earth-shatteringly good, but guess what? He was the best CS instructor I ever had. Unlike some other CS teachers at UMCP, he isn't deranged and his grading criteria is clear.
I actually think he is pretty funny.

I had him twice for 132. First time I got a D, so I had to retake. I didn't pass the first time because I thought that I could sleep through class and get by. PAY ATTENTION. TAKE DOWN CAREFUL NOTES. His tests are tough, but if you know your stuff fairly well, you should be able to pass. Oh yeah, he's got an attitude, so be mindful of that.

Tough but fair.  Everything I lost credit for was my own fault, usually from  skipping a crucial lecturediscussion.  TAs, office hours very helpful.  Attendance taken but not for a grade.  Projects and homework are VERY time-consuming but not overly difficult. Full disclosure: took this course at another school prior but had to retake it at UMD

Projects are tough and if you are not a good coder then this is not for you. Big chunk of score in midterms and finals are for coding. He provides you the final review and tells you that questions on finals will be lot like midterms but heck no. His intentions are good but he is just not a professor material.
Lacks some social skills but is a well-intentioned man. Has great lecture slides and really knows the material.
Though his program descriptions may be a bit long, overall the class is not too challenging with Herman.

Herman's class is designed so it's near impossible for the normal student get an A(or B). To receive good grades, you must overwork yourself. He takes attendance and his midterms cover unexpected material that are usually not in practice exams or projects. His slides are mediocre and leaves out answers to questions in them. (which end up on exams)

I'm pretty sure the guy's reasonable for what he teaches. That being said, I went to about 1% of his lectures. I still got a C because the TA's were awesome in discussion, but probably would have gotten a good grade, had I gone to lecture regularly.
The worst Compsci instructor in the department, he returns grades extremely late, you will not know you are failing until you check your final grade, trust the other reviews and don't take him

Despite what most people say about him, I thought he was a great professor. Everything that people hate about him he only does for the benefit of the student(not using phone in class/telling people to move to the front of the class). I also thought he was a pretty hilarious guy. He also goes out of his way to answer questions in class. Great guy

I do not like him at first. But around the midterm 1, I gradually turn to like him. He explain each concepts clearly. His exams are fair. Also, he is lenient enough to give a 4 day postpone on a project this semester. Probably the best teacher you can have for 132, according to my feedback from friends about other 132 teachers.

I will start by saying that I am in no way opposed to hard work. However, this class meets 5 days a week and there are so many assignments that it begins to take over your life. I find that there is not much time to work on other classes when he throws a programming exercise at you randomly and gives you 24 hours to complete it.
Smart guy , all I care about his having a smart person lecture me ,so for that hes the best cs professor i've had so far.

Not a terrible teacher, but the core of this professor is evil. Hes heartless and rude to his students. Hes smart and can teach well but I've never meet anyone who treats his students with as much disrespect as he does.

One of the worst professors and most pointless classes I have ever taken in my life.Herman takes very outdated material and complicates it so com sci majors cannot even help.Spent hours on projects and papers and they accounted for a very tiny portion of my grade.Impossibly hard test where the class average was in the 60s. Avoid Herman at all costs

Have discussion after lecture, a lot of the discussion exercises would have been helpful if I had learned the info from lecture first. He tells you all the info  you need to know in class (but I have experience in java so this may be a little bias). He  gives a lot of examples. Exams are time consuming, so work fast.

His lectures are completely clear and organized, and concepts are explained precisely. If you follow his policies, no trouble interacting with him. He sometimes shuts down kids trying to sound smart asking questions alluding to future material. Some may find this mean, but it stops time-wasting during lecture. His humor is very dry, in a good way.

The class wasn't very hard, but as a professor, Herman doesn't accept even simple questions through email (must go to office hours), didn't assign our first project until half way through the semester (we only had 4 projects), and is terrible about getting grades back in a timely fashion.

You get your money's worth with the diabolical Larry Herman, but that is all you get.  He does not care about you.  He cares about C programming.  This class was sink or swim, but I went in knowing nothing about C and came out with an A in the class.  Go to class every day, read the book and pay attention and you will do fine.

Textbook is 10 years old; project specs are too long and obtuse.  This guy is teaching coding procedures that are 10 years old.  C++ would have been a better choice.  Worse, the projects themselves do not reflect what is being taught in the class.  LH is not helpful, doesn't get grades back in a timely fashion, and his lecture slides are useless.

He has a very sarcastic teaching style, which I didn't find helpful. Won't deal with email questions at all, insists all questions (including non technical) be asked in person after class or during office hours. Project specifications were vague, exams were tricky.

Horrible, not as bad of a teacher as he is a person.  Would not accept simple questions via e-mail, you must come to his office hours.  Also not lenient on scheduling conflicts for tests.  Very anal when it comes to academic dishonesty and test regulations.

Has the worst grading policies, he will take 4ever to get a grade back, so if you get something wrong on proj #1, you will do it wrong on proj #2 because he won't get your grade back soon enough. Puts all work on TA's, does not want to deal with anything on his own. He is a little boy who won't accept responsibility and won't admit to being wrong.

worst teacher ever. simply asked him one question before class, refused to answer it. i sent him an email asking him the question agian and insisted on not answering it. oh yeah and this was days before na exam as well and the question was regarding a project. horrible guy, honestly could disappear from maryland and never never never be missed

I didn't find this professor as bad as others say he is. Everyone said that the tests are gonna be brutally hard but I found them to be reasonable and I am just an average student. He is strict about attendance but attending his lectures did help me and he do help if you go to his office hours. One thing that suck is that 15% of proj is style so wa

Horrible professor...if you have the option to take the class next semester with a different professor, do that. Writes project specifications that are always wrong the first time and won't fix them until you see him in office hours. Start your projects early, prepare for him to shirk responsibility on his mistakes, and expect delayed deadlines.

I found his projects fair, but his tests were difficult because he tests you on non-important, very subtle things about the C language.  Public tests for projects were sometimes incorrect.  Was not very approachable before class.  Takes him forever to get graded assignments returned.  His lectures are boring and monotone.  I wouldn't recommend him.

This was my hardest class. His exams are very hard, and his lecture notes are totally useless. The notes just have the questions on them, and no answers. the answers are given on the board in class. Nice person.

hermans projects are VERY easy. i aced every single one except 1 that i didnt even make time for. other than that, even though the project descriptions are long, they cover everything. if youre stupid like many of the kids, youll be in TA office hours all the time askin stupid ?'s but otherwise u can pull it off on ur own like me... tests are hard
Very unhelpful, very bad at telling jokes.
He is the worst teacher ever. I have taken a class with him but he seems like a person who does not change even he repeats same jokes every sem. I will say not to take his class.

Larry Herman is organized as a professor, but his policy states basically that you should NOT form a study group.  You would expect people with no programming experience to form a study group, but if you do that, you will be accused of academic dishonesty.  Do not like him and hope his cat dies.

On of the worst teachers I have ever had. I was forced to miss the final exam because of an emergency root canal. My cheek was swollen the size of a grapefruit. I brought a not from the orthopedic surgeon and all..his comment was I should have informed him the day before the exam. Stay away from him

Larry Herman is a very organized teacher, yet he is very anal retentive and unaccesable as a teacher. He is unwilling to help, and my personal advice is not to attend his office hours, after seeking his help on a project, he then decided I was cheating, and accused me of academic dishonesty.

Any programming course in 3-400 level will not be easy. 330 is both lab and lecture/theory. Herman is very clear and there will be no suprises on the test. Hes a bit of a pain but tolerable. The lecture is clear but you need to study hard to do well.
He does not care about his course at all
Worst professor ever
Took Bing for ENES100. You won't get too much out of his lectures, but he is a really nice guy. Show up to class and put in effort for your OSV and you will get an A.

Was his first year ever teaching this course. While some people might say that he was not a good professor, I found that given that this course is not meant to be content heavy he was great. Basically if you showed good effort for the OSV you get an A. This class is more of a learning experience between and among students. Cool dude nonetheless.
One of the best professors I have ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: One of the best Arabic professors I have ever had, one of the best professors I've had period. Super helpful and understanding, and he always puts in the work to make sure everyone understands the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I highly recommend taking a class with Ahmed! He is really good at simplifying grammar concepts. Thanks to him, I recently majored in Arabic.

Professor Ahmed was by far the BEST language teacher I've ever had. He was kind, caring, understanding, and he always made class super interesting. He does not teach directly out of the book, he comes up with fun, interactive activities. You can just tell he is extremely experienced at teaching and educating. Take him if you want to really learn!!!

It was my favorite class; the professor was very engaging and aware of progress in students and paid attention to their language. He was an excellent teacher and taught material very well. He had his office hours available through the entire week and that was very accommodating.

I could not be more satisfied with a class. It was my favorite class last semester, fun activities, very helpful feedback, and interesting lectures. You will move out of your comfort zone, and you will really enjoy it. We used a text book with plenty of extra activities. I would take it again!

Prof Hanafy is the best of the best! I am taking more Arabic classes just because of his teaching style and how much he is really helpful. I can speak in Arabic now :) !! I would definitely take his class again.

Best professor I've ever had, encourages everyone in the class and makes learning a difficult language much easier. Originally planned to minor in Arabic but now I'm an Arabic major and doing study abroad because Prof Hanafy has been so helpful. He works really hard to make sure his students are learning well

Prof. Hanafy is the best language professor I have ever had. He will encourage you to speak in Arabic, and it really works very well. I learned much more than I expected and I have more confidence now. That is why I registered for the following class with him. the class is already full!

Ustaz Ahmed is one of the best professors at umd. His teaching style is amazing and so simple. He wants his student to be successful in the class and he works really hard for it. He generally expects students to participate in class and I believe that is important since it's a language course. I want all my Arabic classes to be taught by him. GEMM!

An absolutely amazing professor who has a clear love and passion for his classes. He is flexible in his availability to help outside of class and encourages you to perform your best. The textbook is really useful for supplementing so be sure to use and read it.
This is my first elective course in Arabic and I wish I had taken Ahmed's class earlier. He is awesome and very helpful teacher. Would take it again!
He is the best!

He is really a great teacher! If you want to learn Arabic, definitely take his class. He is very patient and encourages questions. You will feel comfortable with the language. He does not make you feel discouraged if you do not know something. I liked this class.

He is a really great teacher, every lecture was a joy to attend,! If you want to learn Arabic, definitely take his class. He is very patient, encourage questions. You will feel comfortable with the language. He does not make you feel discouraged if you do not know something.

He is awesome! If you want to learn Arabic, definitely take his class. He is very patient, encourages questions, makes you comfortable with the language and doesn't make you feel discouraged if you don't know something. I learned much more than I expected.

I took some Arabic classes in community college before and was not planning to take more. I gave it a try for the credits at UMD and now I have a major in Arabic. Thanks to ustaaz Ahmad, I started believing Arabic is easy but you need to have the enthusiastic teacher to help you and give you the right feedback. He is an excellent teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I have learned much more I expected in an introductory class. Ahmed is the best language teacher I have had so far. Try to take hiss class. Definitely recommend!
never again
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: If you really want to learn Arabic, this is nor for you. In class group assignments last 1rh, no structure and lack of support materials.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Ahmed is the best professor, quickest grader, gives most accurate feedback, and he is always available to answer questions. I learned much more than I expected from a class. For sure, this is my most favorite class.

This was the best Arabic class that I have taken so far at UMD. Ahmed is an amazing teacher and he always made us comfortable with the new material. He is always available for questions and office hours and provides the best feedback. So far, he is my favorite professor on campus!

One of the most wholesome professors on this campus. Extremely patient with beginners and enjoys answering students questions. So glad to have had the pleasure to be taught by him, he truly makes learning arabic engaging and enjoyable.

Ahmed is an amazing Arabic teacher, but he makes you work for the grade. He is probably the quickest grader I have ever has and really enjoys students coming to office hours. If you turn in your homework and generally put in the effort required of acquiring a new language then your grade will be fine. He is an excellent teacher

Ahmed is the best professor I've ever had! His grammar explanations are amazing, and he is happy to help students get a better grasp of concepts from class during office hours. He really makes you motivated to learn and has effective, creative teaching methods. Definitely try to take a class with him!

Ahmed is awesome! I think he's one of the nicest professors in the Arab department. For an intro class, I learned way more than I ever expected thanks to him. He does make everyone participate but don't sweat it if you don't know something, he'll happily help you. This was actually one of my favorite classes!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: very nice guy. most of the course is mainly reading on your own but he clarifies everything well in class. the majority of the class is also speaking in small groups so you eventually become comfortable with everyone too. i would take him again if i could!

I've only had him for intro to Arabic but Ahmed seems like one of the best. Very pleasant egyptian guy and doesn't make you feel discouraged by not knowing/understanding a word. I will admit that this class gets me out of my comfort zone a lot but it is a foreign language class and he happily answers any questions. Def recommend!

Overall I really enjoyed this class and I highly recommend Professor Isaacs. He tells you exactly what you need to know and practice in order to do well in the class. Go to office hours and GSS and discussion and you will do great. The best part is that he rarely takes more than 24 hours to put grades in.

reviews.comment: This was the worst class I've taken at UMD. No due dates for hw or project on syllabus, no reading day, lecture format didn't match hw/exam questions at all, and the month long project is useless busy work. During finals week we had a hw due (w/3 days notice), project due, and the final one day after another. I couldn't study for the final at all.

This was the most poorly run class I have ever taken at UMD. During finals week we had a hw due with 3 days notice, month-long project and the final, all back to back. No reading day. No hw due dates given on syllabus. Lecture format didnt match exam or hw questions at all. I learned nothing from this class except to scrape for partial credit.

Horrible transition into Online learning. Never listened to student feedback and was not good at all at communicating deadlines. Most of the class ended up watching a different professors lectures all semester because Yoon was terrible.

It was tough going into the class as is in a normal setting, but the current pandemic made things much worse. His exams barely if not reflected what was focused on in classes. His grading prompts were terrible and the format of the exams were worse. You are basically banking on a few questions which counted towards the majority of your grade.

Yoon seems nice and his lectures are fine. However, he made up weird exams that did not reflect the information or the format of the practice exams. He handled moving classes online during the pandemic HORRIBLY. Information about exams was posted only a couple days before the exam would be taken placed and they made decisions very last minute.

The absolute WORST class I have taken here, even worse than 351. Things were bad before COVID, and everything just went further south once online: abysmal online lecturing, extremely difficult tests, and vague projects that were super confusing. Avoid if possible, take someone else. Thank god for P/F. What a disaster of a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class will be your first class where you have to figure out how to do projects your own. Lectures kind of help, but you will need to go to office hours and diligently work on the projects. Thank god P/F semester. Just go to his lectures and study your own. Trust me it will help in few weeks.

He is one of the worse prof you will find in UMD He doesn't know how to explain stuff. Project are hard and he doesn't help at all He doesn't inform about exam change due date change from inbox or announce. You will regret taking his class. Trust me avoid him . If not you will spend one sem plus umd tution money
