reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had. He gives good and time-consuming projects. Moreover, the exams are hard. Even worse, his lectures and lecture skills are dry and uninformative. He is nice but taking his class is not.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Yoon is a terrible professor. I attended every single lecture and was very confused during most of them. He managed to turn a simple curriculum into a very difficult class. I basically taught myself everything and got help from my friends. If I relied only on lectures I would have failed for sure. The exams are also nothing like the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures went too fast and when he gave homework or tests, it barely reflected what he taught us. The average of the class is so low (60%). He's a nice guy and will take time to explain, but if the material is hard for you to understand he won't be much use. The TAs were the most useful, but even sometimes they didn't understand him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Yoon is amazing. He is an very nice person at heart. His exams and projects speak something else though. They tend to be hard but as long as you focus in lecture and discussions you should be good. His exams are ok also. They arent the worst but not the best. if you use the study guide the TA provide then you should be good.

I came into this class with ZERO programming experience with computers and I really regret it. It's extremely difficult to concentrate during Yoon's lectures for they're extremely boring and I can't understand what he's saying. His projects are extremely hard and time consuming and his exams are ridiculously difficult with a terrible timing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Yoon is the worse. He gives difficult projects and long test that you can't finish in 50 minutes. Yoon is a very boring lecturer and he spends too much time in class explaining how to do a project because he makes them too difficult for an intro to computer science class. He is a nice person but nice doesn't cut it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Yoon really didn't teach me anything in this course. I taught myself literally everything outside of class. Luckily, our grades were largely made up of projects, as I failed every single one of the tests/quizzes, despite studying for them. Prof. Yoon was nearly unavailable after class. He flaked on many students, leaving unanswered questions.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Professor Yoon expects too much of his students for an Intro to Programming class which many students take for merely a Gen ED. If you do not have prior experience in programming it can be very overwhelming and difficult. The class is lecture heavy and many times "lecture code" strongly correlates to the projects, quizzes, and exams.

The content learned in this class was not hard, but the prof had high expectations for an intro class. He made the quizzes and projects really complex for students who have little to no coding experience. Definitely take advantage of TA office hours for projects, they will really help. Midterm and final were a little easier than the quizzes.

Ilchul Yoon is always looking out for the students. Granted he isn't the most popular guy around-- due to the fact that he doesn't baby you. Most of the students expected this Gen ed to be a breeze because it is a Gen Ed, but they were wrong(and so was I). His homework isn't mandatory and I feel like that was a major problem. lectures were v good.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: CMSC122 is supposed to be for students who have little to no background in coding. The class is fast paced for an intro class so you end up teaching yourself. He assigns multiple projects and you have multiple quizzes. The exams are rather hard. He's a nice guy but not the best lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Not infosci major? Good luck in this class. Projects fairly easy. Tests/quizzes (handwritten) are crazy tough.

This class is meant to be an intro class that goes at a slower, more understandable pace for those who have no background of coding. However, there are multiple projects you have to do which are not explained at all and are graded at extremely tough standards. We are treated as if we have experience when we don't. Do not take this class.

The class would not have been so difficult if he would explain. It is a beginners class but he does not seem to understand that. The lectures are extremely dry and not a good style of teaching. He also is not the easiest to understand and follow along.

Professor Yoon is a nice and careful lecturer. He provides enough time and hints for us to work on our projects and labs. However, he is not good at lecturing. So, if you do not have prior coding experience like me, you need to teach yourself to keep the pace with his lectures.

Very nice man but this class structure is not good. Uses processing for way too long. Slides and projects are not written well. Lectures were boring a lot of the time. Honestly I can not recommend this instructor even though he genuinely is a nice guy and wants you to succeed but this class was not a fun experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: If you have prior knowledge in comp sci, he's great. Goes through slides quickly and listens and extends deadlines if need be. If you don't know every concept is teaching is very fast and is taught through examples. The TAs are great though!

Professor Yoon is a very kind hearted man and I enjoyed this class. This was my first CS class, and I really enjoyed the emphasis on projects and learning by doing versus pure memorization. His lectures can be a bit dry at times, but otherwise a good professor. Lots of extra credit opportunities too. Definitely recommend.

There are tons of amazing cs professors at UMD and Yoon ranks up there with the best. I came here to write this because some were complaining, but to tell the truth, the material for 411 is just really dry and I think he did as good a job as humanly possible to make it interesting. He's extremely passionate and engaging for such a boring subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a very nice guy, but his lectures are boring. It's very hard to understand him during lecture. In person, he is very nice and helps out a lot. He responds to email in a timely manner. He doesn't use a step by step learning process. Usually, he'd make you go for a slam dunk without sufficient amount of practice.

Professor yoon is a kind-hearted man, but its his first year and he is terrible at teaching CMSC131. He has endless mistakes on his presentations, Doesnt explain things well and gives you hard exams where you barely have time to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I have learned a lot about investing and derivatives through hands-on experience. Joseph Rinaldi is a passionate teacher who takes the time to help interns understand the industry. I have been able to sit in on calls with CIOs and other professionals providing real-world exposure. It has been a great learning experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: As an intern at Quantum Financial Advisors, I gained more real-world insight than I ever did in class. Joseph Rinaldi took the time to teach me how to analyze markets and even helped refine my resume. He is both inspiring and genuinely invested in his interns' success, caring deeply about our growth just as much as his clients'.

As an Intern at Quantum Financial Advisors, Joseph Rinaldi's wealth management firm, I have learned so much. Whether it's learning how to efficiently analyze financial markets or getting help with my resume, Joseph Rinaldi shows that he cares about his interns just as much as his clients.

As an intern at Quantum Financial Advisors, I can say I've learned quite a bit from Mr. Rinaldi! He is very knowledgeable, and I know I can count on him if I have any financial questions. I highly recommend his internship opportunities if you're looking to springboard into a career in finance/investments!

Mr. Rinaldi is extremely knowledgeable and does a great job connecting course material to real-world finance. Assignments and projects are practical and help build research and analytical skills. Expectations are clear, and he provides useful feedback that improves your work. Very supportive and professional, and always willing to help.

The Quantum Financial Advisor Internship was excellent. They provided real-world experience, helped me open a Roth IRA, and helped edit my resume to stand out more. This internship is a great, structured learning experience.

I am grateful for the experience of working at Quantum Financial Advisors. As someone pursuing a career in finance, I've learned a great deal about investment strategy, portfolio management, and the importance of personalized financial planning. Joe and the supervising team were incredibly supportive and always willing to share their knowledge.

After working with Mr. Rinaldi at Quantum Financial Advisors, I have nothing but the best to say about his services. He provided me with all of the guidance and support that I needed in order to better improve my financial investing acumen.

Joe Rinaldi is one of the best professors I've ever had. He genuinely cares about his students' success and is always willing to help with any questions. His saying, 'I'll open the doors for you, all you have to do is walk through it,' is something I've never heard from any other professor.
loved being taught by mr.rinaldi! he was such a fun vibe in the class and taught us a lot

\

I've been working as an Investment Intern under Joseph Rinaldi for just under a month at Quantum Financial Advisors. Joseph has played a pivotal role in broadening my internship opportunities, notably securing an interview with PIMCO. He has helped my decision-making regarding various internships and helping improving my financial literacy.

Joe is a wonderful and insightful mentor always looking to make the best moves for you. He provides you with hands on experience about how to run a financial firm and sharing his expertise and market insights. You can always learn something from him.

Joe Rinaldi is an outstanding professor. His teaching style is engaging and practical, focusing on real-world applications of finance that go beyond textbooks. Joe takes the time to break down complex concepts and makes them relatable, ensuring that every student or intern truly understands the material.
Fun and brought real world experience to the classroom. Helped his students get jobs

Mr. Rinaldi is a great teacher. In addition, he allows his students to intern at his financial advisory firm, Quantum Financial Advisors. I interned there for a summer and it was an awesome experience where I learned about prospecting, research, and using Bloomberg Terminal. Rinaldi also helped with my resume and job search. Great guy!

Brings real world experience into the classroom. Sponsors "Lunch and Learn with Leon Cooperman", brings students to Barrons roundtable.  Lastly, offers students internships and helps them with FT employment.
Good professor. Would recommend.

Professor Rinaldi's Futures and Options course was my strongest learning experience. The way Rinaldi teaches is clear and engaging.   Another factor that distinguishes Professor Rinaldi from others is his genuine nature. He cares about his students and goes out of his way to help get his students jobs. This is a must take Professor and course.

Professor Rinaldi is a great teacher. He is very easy to talk to and likes to get to know his students. He offers internships and his financial advisory firm, Quantum Financial Advisors, for the fall and spring semester. Overall, he is a great professor to have and his class is a joy to take.

Mr. Rinaldi did an exceptional job at delivering a message to the students of MSU and has motivated students to start investing now in order to grow their wealth and establish financial independence. Mr. Rinaldi's initiative to come speak to the students of MSU shows his dedication to giving back to the  community despite his busy schedule!

As a result of Professor Rick's class, I now write more intentionally and more impactfully. He helped me not only to grow as a professional but also to get an internship I didn't thought had shot at. (I just ended a sentence with a preposition—thank you, Professor, for teaching me that this is ok.)

Professor Rick teaches you not only how to write. He teaches you how to be a professional. His focus on career advice and life lessons, such as how to write an email, how to humanize a number, and how to brand yourself, were easy to understand and powerful. I would take this class again if I could.

I never thought I'd learn so much about writing in such a short period. I have become a better writer in every way, from the length of my paragraphs to my use of contractions. Best class of the semester, no question.

You can tell from day one that Professor Rick loves what he teaches. His energy is contagious—it made even late-night lectures feel exciting. It's rare to find a professor who makes learning feel this alive. Easily one of the best professors at UMD.

It's invigorating to have a professor who teaches you things you never even thought about, who cares about your progress, who gives you so many opportunities to improve (by revising assignments, bonus points, and extra credit). Professor Rick's class is a breath of fresh air!

I used to dread writing. But Prof. Rick completely changed my outlook. His lectures are so engaging and energetic that I found myself actually excited to go to writing class! He's passionate, inspiring, and an amazing teacher all around.

This class was the equivalent of boot camp. Professor Rick's patient guidance made me smarter, stronger, and more resilient. I walked out of his course knowing more than I ever expected. Five stars because I respect the results.

This class was the equivalent of boot camp. Professor Rick doesn't sugarcoat things, and his questions can be sharp—but his guidance made me stronger. You either rise to his standards or you don't pass. No fluff, just pure knowledge. I walked out of his writing course knowing more than I ever expected. Five stars because I respect the results.

Writes fake reviews, often picks on students, it is very confusing to me why he does this. But I don't recommend taking his class at all he is very lecture heavy and does pop quizzes at random times. On top of making weird comments to all students.

Professor Rick is an absolute gem of a professor! I always felt awake and energized in his class––even though it met from 6:30-9PM. He pushes his students to think on their feet and participate in class. His lessons on PowerPoint, speaking and email are ones that I will take with me for the rest of my life.

Taking this class was truly of the best decisions I have made. For example, the class on emails was great; the GPS trick will be something I use for the rest of my life.  Also, the professor's teaching style (making students participate) made me think on my feet, which I previously gave me anxiety.

Jonathan Rick is easily one of the best teachers I've had at UMD, at community college, and in high school. For instance, he gives you extra credit if you catch a mistake of his. No other professor rewards that kind of participation. And he has you submit an anonymous Exit Ticket at the end of each class, where you write a comment - good or bad.

Professor Rick cares deeply about his students' success. He challenges you to think outside the box and spends a serious amount of time editing your papers (even though outside his class, if you ask). His presentations, lectures, and assignments are practical and engaging, and he makes class time sail by. I wish I could take this class again!

Professional Writing with Professor Rick was one of the most valuable courses I took at UMD. It taught practical skills—emails, LinkedIn, personal branding—while debunking writing myths and reshaping my approach: purposeful, audience‑aware writing, no more writing "simplistically". He's a great communicator both inside and outside the classroom.

Prof. Rick changed the way I write. He gave me confidence in myself & taught me how to write clearly and succinctly. He worked with me many times to revise and tailor my résumé, which I credit as the reason I now work at my first-choice company. I would give him 5 stars if I could! His class, his personality & his teaching style are exceptional

Professor Rick is one of those rare professors who make a lasting impact on his students. If you're looking to become a better writer, look no further—this is the class for you. Professor Jonathan is so detail-oriented that even the smallest aspects of your work are thoughtfully reviewed. He doesn't just grade you; he helps you grow!!!

If you think business writing is just another requirement, you haven't taken Professor Jonathan Rick's class. He makes it a skill worth mastering, teaching you how to write emails that get replies, résumés that stand out, and arguments that persuade. His feedback, as precise as it is practical, ensures every word earns its place. Take his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took this class because my roommate recommended it. Thanks to Prof. Rick, I am a better writer and a clearer thinker. His classes are thought-provoking and move quickly, and he makes sure everyone participates. The markup he leaves on your papers shows that he reads everything you write, and he is quick in replying to emails.

Do not take this class if you want an easy English credit. Office hours are after class, but assignments are due before, leaving no chance for help. The professor enforces strict grading, even failing papers for minor format errors. Redoing work requires an extra essay for a small grade boost. He is not afraid to fail you, so choose wisely.

I took this class 7 years ago and still think about the lessons I learned. This class really prepares you for the workforce and I wish more people I work with had taken similar classes. Prof Rick was a great teacher and very supportive.

Very passionate lectures that are easy to pay attention to. Very up front with his high expectations, but it is worth it because you actually learn useful things. This class will make you a better writer and Professor Rick's attention to detail proves he actually cares about helping students become better writers. Can't ask for much more.

Professor Rick is a brilliant teacher. He transformed my writing (and the way I think about writing), and my new resume and cover letter helped me land the top job I applied for. I always looked forward to his class, and I enjoy emailing him from time to time.

If you come to class, pay attention, and put effort into your work (which should be a given) this will be one of the most beneficial classes you'll take. 
The assignment, slide decks, and material is all deliberate and well thought-out, and Professor Rick commonly asks for feedback on assignments and how to improve them.

ENGL394 with Professor Rick has proven to be one of the most useful courses I've taken at UMD. He truly cares about helping students grow professional and personally.. He makes lectures both educational and humorous. TAKE ENGL394 WITH PROFESSOR RICK.

Professor Rick is one of the best professors I've had at UMD. He's funny and knows how to keep his students engaged. As long as you attend class, follow instructions, and genuinely put in your best effort, you'll do well. He teachers real world skills that are actually useful in our future careers, which is not common from my experience.
His assignments aren't hard as long as you follow instructions. His classes are a lot of fun, and he makes it a point to constantly interact with students.

Professor Rick is easily one of the best professors here. He's a stickler w/ grading (he admits it) but if you pay attention it's not hard to get an A on every assignment. There's no busy work, only 1 assignment once or every other week, the readings take 10 mins max to do. I got so much out of his class, he really wants you to do well and learn.

Professor Rick provides everything you need and more as a business writing professor. His interactive lectures teach you in depth tactics to create a resume, produce a proper email/memo, and enhance your overall writing ten fold in just a semester. He uses gives his students the same advice that he would give to his professional peers.

Professor Ricks class was by far the most helpful in preparing me for post college, professional life. His guidance on résumé writing, cover letters, and email etiquette stand out as things I will carry with me for years to come. Students must put in the work to succeed, but those who do will find a great professional connection moving forward.
The professor is tough but fair. He'll call you out if you are not trying enough. He pushed me to do better and I did. He knows his stuff well so you'll learn a lot.

Professor Rick was an excellent lecturer and really made a 3 hour long professional writing class entertaining and interesting. He is very accomplished in his field and it shows. He is picky when it comes to writing, BUT his feedback is great and detailed and if you apply that feedback to future papers you're golden. Overall, great prof and class!

He's a tough grader from the first day of class. There is no rubric he follows by, if he doesn't think you are right it's wrong. He is very self-centered and boasts about himself and can be very rude to his students at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Rick seems to take points away at random over the smallest things. One extra space between words and a 6 sentence paragraph being "too long" were the only feedback for a paper that was given a failing grade. Speaks very patronizingly to students. Overall, worst professor I have ever had in my entire educational career.

He's a tough grader, but should that stop you from taking a class that will empower you to properly communicate with others in their future careers? He taught me SO MUCH about creating effective résumés and cover letters, etc.. If you are worried about your grade, regrades and in-class extra credit is awarded for participation will boost your grade

This course makes you think and gives you a chance to learn real life job skills. This course from any other prof is useless and *boring.* His bad reviews are from people who don't read his hw instructions. Sorry, in the real world, you need to read instructions, or you don't get paid. Want to goof off and get an easy A? Don't take this class.
Professor Rick will teach you skills that will help you thrive in the real world. He is a thorough instructor, who is passionate about the subject-matter he teaches!

Honestly he should stick to doing his own workshops. He is a ridiculously hard grader and takes off/adds points for the most random things. He's got too much energy so that will be helpful for paying attention. Don't take his class unless you have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Teaches some good things, but other lessons are not as serious as he makes it out to be. Grades way tougher than necessary.
Every single class he would just walk up to the board and write proofs. I have never had a less engaging class in my life. He had to curve the class so hard that an 81 was an A and a 63 was a B-.

Fair Grader, Challenging Weekly Quiz, Tricky but not difficult exams, Require reading the textbook (even not covered in the lecture). Pay attention to MATLAB. Super efficient e-mail replier (love that most).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Rosenburg is an alright teacher. Lectures are posted online, but most of the content is copied straight from his notes that he provides, so they aren't very useful. Online exams/quizzes were annoying since you had to type in equations, but they were manageable. Attendance is mandatory for discussions but not lectures. Not the best, not the worst.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: He is very intelligent, but he can not teach properly nor is he able to clearly display the material. He jumps from materials and is theory heavy so he does not really use examples to help the students understand. Moreover, his tests are complicated and I had to literally teach myself all the materia before the final. Do not choose him for diff eq.

He is a fair grader and very helpful when you have a question about the material. He uses just enough proof and intuition to help learn without getting tedious, and his sense of humor is great. There were 4 midterms, 3 online quizzes, and 8 MATLAB group projects. His exams are easy if you know the content, and the questions often hint at solutions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: As a lecturer, he is lacks the ability to introduce and explain complicated topics well, and he is boring at times. However, he does write good, legible notes on the board so be sure to pay attention to those. The MATLAB home works are especially difficult if you have no coding experience, be prepared to teach yourself sometimes. Nice guy tho

Homework was done on MATLAB in groups, exams were taken on paper individually. This was my biggest gripe with the class. The lectures were dry and boring, but informative if you could stay focused. Do not overlook the MATLAB assignments, they could be the saving grace for your grade.

I had him for 406, and he was brutal. 2 midterms, each 5 questions that are 20 pts each. He doesn't give much extra credit, and in each midterm he will ask a proof theoretical question. Most of his questions are very intuitive thinking questions, not so straightforward. He's brutal, because he curves using a median and smaller standard deviation.
Interesting course by a nice guy: fair marker, reasonable homework and exam questions, and good text book. Doesn't teach with much enthusiasm though

Up front he gives you 2.5% wiggle room. This is a very challenging course. You have to work very hard. The biggest challenge of your life. Reading the textbook, doing problems, attending lecture, going to discussion, weekly quizzes & matlab homework assignments, & going to TA office hours are all essential. Rosenberg did me a favor, I am grateful.
He is a great teacher, really helpful. I learned from him, and look forward to taking future classes taught by him. He is by far my favorite professor!

I read the other comments and I couldn't believe they were talking about the same person.  His lectures were fine, he just expects you to read the book and work to understand the material.  Very helpful.  Easily understood, if you work.  Yes, he expects you to think during the exams, not memorize equations.  Avoid him if you expect an "easy" grade.

He's a smart guy, but he isnt a good teacher. I relied on my TA to pass the class, and at the lectures i would just plan my homework for the week. The tests are hard, but if you have a good ta, and go to discussion, you should do ok. you do have to teach yourself alot of the material tho, unless you go to office hours.

Knows what he's doing, but he doesn't do a good job communicating the material. Easier grading then Francis Gulick, but it wasn't of much use to me with a lack of understanding. I saw a lot of familiar faces when I retook this course. Wasn't always respectful. Take with Denny Gulick if you can survive 8 AM class, or Francis Gulick otherwise.

Really difficult, hard to understand, he's helpful if you seek him out. You don't need to go to class. You do need to go to discussion once a week because they'll be a quiz. He posts all quiz and exam dates, and what material is covered in class. The book is useful. Do the online HW, it helps and counts for a test grade.

Worst MATH teacher ever.... i took this class a semester before and averaged an B on all the tests... i retook it with him and averaged an E o n the exams even though i knew all the material. he kills on careless mistakes and he is a horrible teacher. He likes to screw u on problems even if u know the material in and out
What can I say, boring...mumbles, talks very fast.   Too much MATLAB. Switchto someoneelse if you can.
knows his stuff but not a good teacher.  Lots of Matlab

this teacher definately knows math. the only problem is getting it from his head to yours. try to at least read the book (which can be just as cryptic), if you dont want to do the problems. i hear hes actually really helpful if you go in for office hours though. btw his laugh is hilarious/scary (hes laughing about math...) math lovers will be fine.

By far the worst professor I've ever had.  Smart as hell, but this guy should not be teaching.  Talks to board--and good luck trying to take notes in his class, its like he's on crack...avoid this guy!!!

Probably one of the worst classses I ever took.  MATLABS are everything, if you don't know them, you're basically screwed.  Exams are mega hard, and lectures are mega boring, and discussion will save you if you have a good TA, unfortunatley I didn't, I got an A on one of the exams and still didn't pass.

You write more words than numbers in this class. Very unclear, and barely gives any examples to help you understand. Tests are a killer (3 or 4 probs worth 25 pts each)!! Too much Matlab hw also on exams. And TAs aren't any better! I dont think he curved anything cuz I still didnt pass the class, and I'm pretty sure not many ppl did.

This guy is a horrible proffesor.  Doesn't take time to explain himself fully.  Very full of himself.  Exams are incredibly hard, average for all exams was around a 50%.  Take another professor for this class, they are a lot better that this nerd.

If you do not like matlab do not take this prof he gives matlab hw and matlab is a large part of his exams.  Not very approachable and boring.  I eventually stopped going to class and taught myself from the textbook because i could not learn anything from him.  Exams are very difficult although he does curve.  I would recommend a different prof.

Seems a bit full of himself after I talked to him one on one.  Needs to be more personable when teaching classes; he writes and talks into the chalkboard for the whole class.  Boring math class.  Lots of MATLAB.

Well, the best the math dept. can offer. I found this class to be fairly easy however he's a tough grader. Don't be suprised to lose all the points for a problem b/c of careless mistakes on exams. Matlab programming also included in this course. Doing the HW is the best way to understand the course.
Mike is an amazing professor because he teaches not only mechanics but also how to approach challenges and truly wants you to succeed in life!
He's real nice and really makes his class an environment where you can succeed, one of the most dedicated to perfecting the skill of teachers among the teachers on this campus

From my own experience, I can say that Mike is a good professor. He wants to see you put in work for the class but not overdo it as he knows you are a student juggling other courses. If you want a decent grade (> C+) go to lecture, watch his online videos when needed, do groupwork, and study for exams one week before (completing ~2 problems/day).

Professor Mike is an awesome teacher. His lectures, guidelines, and rubrics are super clear, and he is a super funny teacher. Most people go to lecture because they are so enjoyable. Highly recommend you take his class, his students grades compared to other teachers are significantly better and he makes the class fun.

Explains concepts in interactive way that students can understand. His youtube was especially helpful. Lectures are well-rounded but he often dismisses questions/hand during class so you have to do office hours or try your luck after class. Exams are straightforward following practice exam structures. Hardest to easiest exam: exam 2, 3, 4 (final),1
Mike is great. Great lectures, extra credit opportunities, and a very friendly guy. There is no better teacher for ENES102.
The GOAT. Rest of the reviews are accurate this guy rocks.

Had to retake this class, and was astonished on how easy this class can be with the right teacher. Mike is the best, explains everything super clear and helpful. He actually teaches you to pass the exams rather than adding unnecessary information into the course. 10 outta 10 professor

Mike was very intentional about wanting his students to do well in enes102. He does a great job in showing how much he cares and often connects the lessons to things you already have background knowledge about.

Awesome professor with lectures that are both information dense and very entertaining. The exams questions cover all the material in the section, but with how good he is at explaining things the exams are pretty easy.

Super fun teacher. There is a good amount of homework but he actually teaches you everything you need to know so the tests are easier. Attendance isn't technically mandatory, but he won't give everyone extra credit if attendance falls below a certain number. Overall, great teacher and just make sure to no procrastinate on the homework.
He's a great teacher and if he's available I would take him.

Mike is the best professor I've had at UMD by far. You can tell he really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. Every lecture was super engaging and I found it a lot easier to learn that way. I definitely recommend taking him for 102. Also, Mike has a youtube channel which has numerous review videos which I found to be very helpful!

Mike is an incredible professor who cares about each and every one of his students. His lectures are engaging and he finds creative ways to explain otherwise boring concepts. Getting Mike for Enes102 is honestly like winning the lottery.

Michael is an outstanding professor who actively keeps students engaged in ENES100 during the 2.5 hour classes. One of his greatest gifts is bringing students together even when we are in different groups, majors, or even other classes. If you want a good laugh, great stories, and inspirational videos, I highly recommend Michael.

Mike is one of the funniest and most engaging professors I've ever seen. He makes boring topics interesting and he has tricks to make hard topics easier to learn. He does everything right. I 100% recommend taking his classes. It'll be a great experience.
Mike is great but the class is hard get ready to work. Definitely take Mike if you can he's the goat.
The Lebron James of ENES100

Mike is the GOAT. Had him for my first semester at umd and couldn't ask for a better first professor. Very laid back, but not in a sense that discourages students from completing their work. He encouraged students to learn on their own during our vehicle capstones, but was always more than happy to help out when students asked for assistance.
Mike is a great teacher who does everything in his power to help you succeed. If you have the option always go for his class. Keep the 8 peat!
Mike is one of the best professors I have ever had. He's funny in a sarcastic way and encourages you to ask questions and give him feedback. I 100% recommend his classes!
Had him for my class in Iceland. Awesome cool guy that's fun to be around.
Awesome guy!! Really cool and the best professor to take for this class and any other he offers. Wish I could take him again.
Mike is an amazing professor and made me more confident that I am in the right major. Would 100% recommend for ENES100!

While Mike's lectures are very good and his feedback is very solid, his grading leaves a LOT to be desired. He waits until the feedback is submitted, then grades like he's trying to fail people. Did me and my team super dirty, taking points for no good reason. Avoid.

Professor Mike brings an engaging and fun approach to this class. His lectures are captivating, and he genuinely cares about student success. Utilize resources like unstuckstudy ai alongside the free textbook to excel in this manageable course.

Mike was genuinely one of the best professors I've had during my time at UMD. He makes class fun and engaging and always tries to relate problems to real life situations. Fluids is typically a very challenging course, but the way Mike supports and helps his students makes it very manageable. I highly recommend taking this professor.

Mike is genuinely one of the most engaging and caring professors I've had the pleasure of working with. He is able to take complex topics and make them accessible through his excellent lectures. He truly cares for his students and goes out of his way to get to know them and guide them to success. Take anything you possibly can with Mike!!

Mike cares a lot about his students and helping them learn. He also puts a lot of effort into making his classes approachable, enjoyable, and applying them to the real world. If he didn't know the answer, he would come to class the next time prepared to answer it. A passionate professor who cares about his students and their education.
Mike makes the topics you learn really engaging and fun, best prof I've had

This is a review for the Iceland study abroad program. Mike was very knowledgeable and fun, and even was the trip photographer. Overall, it is a once in a lifetime experience made even better by the great professors.
funny and super nice. Understanding and provides a ton of ways to catch up on missed lectures

He is an amazing Professor who truly cares about the success of his students. Always made the lectures engaging and interesting, and also provided ample opportunity to succeed in the class. In addition, Mike provided great constructive criticism and advice that helped us think creatively and ultimately complete our tasks with greater success.

Mike was definitely the best professor I've had! He made every single one of his lectures engaging and hilarious. He offers so many different opportunities for extra credit and makes it clear how much he cares for each and every one of his students; he really wants everyone to succeed. He's the best and made the class super fun!

The study abroad program in Iceland was amazingly cultivated to show us what the country has to offer. The class balanced fun with education into the renewable energy systems of Iceland. Traveling on interesting field trips and bonding as a group makes this trip a one of a kind opportunity.

Mike is one of a kind. He made us realize that learning is easy if we include all the fun! He always cares about all his students and gives them the best classroom experience possible. He tells a lot of stories and jokes here and there during his lectures to make us feel engaged and excited. He has a bursting personality and able to inspire others!

Mike is by far my favorite professor that I've had at UMD. He truly cares about his students and wants you to succeed. The class environment was friendly and welcoming. We were frequently encouraged to have conversations with our neighbor at the beginning of class, and I would always laugh during lecture. Mike is a fair grader and a great teacher.

Mike is part of a rare breed of professors who care about students more than whether the final calculations were correct or the product was successful. He emphasized the process of becoming an engineer, working with others, and learning valuable skills. Your grade should be fine as long as your team reflects on what went wrong/what can be improved.

If you can take Mike, do it. He creates dynamic lectures through humor and demonstrations, which makes an otherwise mundane topic fairly bearable. He also isn't so far removed from his days in mechanics, so he understands some students' feelings towards it. He goes out of his way help students succeed in the class. Great professor.

Professor Mike was, without a doubt, the absolute best professor/teacher I have ever had in my entire life.
 - Answers questions thoroughly, do not be afraid to ask for clarification!
 - Friendliest and funniest professor I've had, I genuinely looked forward to coming to class each week!
 - You get what you give, be enthusiastic and you'll succeed!

Mike is a legend. His lectures are very clear and concise, and he also has lecture videos on Youtube. He teaches like a peer or TA, he's like "this is what you're going to encounter" and "this is how to solve it." If you have any questions, go to his office hours, he breaks down the questions and helps you solve them. Bonus, he's a great baker.
Mike is awesome, he will help you out a ton in this class and he is by far the best teacher for ENES100 and ENES102 from what I have seen. Take him for sure, literally a no brainer.

Amazing professor & course. Definitely an experience of a lifetime. We visited breathtaking places and made great memories. We also learned a tremendous amount about geothermal power generation, along with the interactions between power generation and the environment, through fun and interesting field trips and activities.

Mike Galcynzski is the best professor for taking this course and probably many others. He teaches theory, but goes more in depth on how to actually solve problems which is more important for higher exam grades. I would take him again or recommend him to any other student taking the same course. For ENES102 specifically I recommend Mike.

Professor Mike cares about his student and tries to make the class fun and keep students engaged while teaching the class. Lecture is very important and you should attend every class to make sure you understand the material covered in class. He also ensures that we collaborate with our coursemates to prepare for the exams. Seats go quickly, sign up

This guy is AMAZING!!! He is always available if I ever needed help. He made learning REALLY fun, too. He always made lectures interesting with all his funny stories and jokes. He is always willing to answer your questions during class and outside. He is a very practical grader and offers so many resources in order for you to do well in his class.
Pretty good! This class is the most enjoyable I had, and a lot was due to Mike!

Mike is a wonderful professor! He is incredibly supportive and helpful, and cares a lot about his students. He has also created videos online for the course that go in-depth and really help you understand the course content more. He also provided extra credit and wanted to see all his students succeed. Mike's lectures are also always entertaining!

Mike is a very entertaining professor who makes the subject fun and easy to understand. He is encouraging and is helpful if you have trouble with the material. If you like jokes and relatable topic connections while you learn he is your guy.

I took ENME407 during the Winter 2023 term in Costa Rica and Mike was the best professor I could have asked for. He was very knowledgeable about the country and all the course content, and was well-organized and cared about the education and fun of all his students. In just two weeks, I learned so much and experienced so much. Would recommend!

Taking this study abroad course with Mike was one of the best experiences in my undergraduate studies. The trip was very well planned - including pre- and post-trip events. Mike's lectures were very engaging. Assignments were very reasonable to do while travelling. He also made a great effort to help people on the trip when problems came up.

Mike is a great professor and a great fit for any study abroad program. He truly cares about his students and pushes them to succeed. Sometimes slow to grade however he stays very communicative about anything and everything. One of the best on campus.
The best professor you could get for ENES100. I had a very fun time throughout this class, and Mike has the ability to energize all his students.
Not else much to say. Make sure you sign up for his class early because they get taken fast! Favorite professor on campus.
Mike is the GOAT

Sadly I have zero prior background with all of the course content on the trip, but there is no other classes like this that even a person like me could learn so many new things that I could never imagine learning previously from the memorable sceneries, site visits, and lectures in such a short period of time. Worth every single dollar spent there.
He is very nice and professional! Fluids is a hard course but professor Galcynski makes the lectures fun and gives real world examples to help understand the material better! Enjoyable class overall!

Very fun class and THE prof to take for ENES100. You will get the most out of this class with Mike as your prof and have fun doing it. He could be a comedian so it is a very entertaining class. Most entertaining and caring prof I will probably ever have. Also, super easy class. You learn a lot. Extra credit. He brings in homemade baked goods too!

Mike was an excellent professor. He really took the time to design the class to be as immersive as possible. I never felt like I was doing busy work or wasting my time, I always felt like I was learning. I had a lot of fun in this class, even though the task at hand was very difficult.

BEST professor. Inspired me to become an engineering major. I came into ENES100 with no prior experience with any engineering concepts; Mike made such a wonderful environment where we all learned from each other and friends with all of your classmates. He is a fair professor and a true mentor. He makes great baked goods so you'll be fed too!!

Mike has an amazing personality and is second to none when it comes to teaching. He is passionate about what he does and cares deeply for his students. The only downside is that he's a Philadelphia sports fan, but he more than makes up for said shortcoming :)

A very passionate professor, with an aim to make sure that you truly understand the application of what you are learning. Desires for every student to do well, not just in class but at Maryland in general. He greatly encourages participation, questions, group study, interaction etc. Very caring and helps this very difficult class be a bit easier.

Mike was such a great professor and he made ENES100 the most fun class I've taken so far. I would absolutely recommend anyone take him as your professor as no matter what he is teaching, he is caring, knowledgable, and always there to help.

Mike is a great professor! He's compassionate, caring and patient with every student. He truly wants to see everyone succeed. I took ENES100 with zero knowledge of coding and Arduino circuits, and Mike explained them in a way that made sense! As long as you put forth effort, he will see that, and you will get the grade that reflects that.

Mike was such an amazing professor. He was funny, encouraging, and entertaining in class. The class itself can be difficult if you are like me and put a lot of time and energy into the project, but I learned so much it was worth it. Mike encouraged us to think like engineers and try things outside of our comfort zone and baked us goodies.

ENES100 was the best class I have ever taken and it could not have been without Mike as my professor. From the lecture portion to the building phase, Mike genuinely cares about the success of his students. Mike provides the opportunity, and its up to you to take it.
Mike is the best, plain and simple. Funny as well. Very fun class.

Professor Mike is without a doubt one of the best professors I've ever had. his lectures are organized and enjoyable, he communicates well with his students and he just makes a great learning atmosphere in general. You can obviously see how much he cares about his students and how much he loves teaching; I hope I could take more classes with him.

there are homework assignments every week and you are given plenty of practice problems that range from easy to a bit more complex. Lectures are interactive and very productive, you will learn a lot attending them. Mike encourages students to study together for exams. Exams also reflect material covered in lectures and homework.

Mike genuinely cares about each and every one of his students. You really do get out what you put into his class, so work hard and always ask for help. His lectures are always full of great stories and are very informative--make the two hours fly by! He has lots of group activities to have you get to know your team better and make great friends!

Mike is easily one of the best professors you could ever hope to learn from, not just at UMD but life as a whole. His lectures were full of humor which helps a 2 hour lecture fly by and gets you wishing you could stay longer. Mike clearly cares about each and every one of his students, and will always find ways to help you succeed. WE LIKE MIKE!!!
Mike's class is very funny and you learn a lot in it.

I LOVED THIS CLASS WITH MIKE!! He is the absolutes best and makes learning so so fun and easy in this class. The class structure was incredibly clear and while you would mostly be working with your group, Mike and a UTF were always accessible and helpful when needed. I highly recommend taking any class with Mike if possible!!

Mike is an incredible professor, and is probably one of the best educators I have had in my entire career as a student. Mike is the master of using fun metaphors to explain rather complicated concepts and topics, and he makes you feel smart just by listening to him. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE take any class you can with him.

Mike Galczynski is an absolute legend. I've literally had nobody teach me so well and enjoy the content I was learning in class. His skills and abilities allowed me to gain such great friends in this course and maybe even lifelong buddies. Not only that, but he has given me a great opportunity to help expand my passion in video editing.

Mike is great. He provides really clear deadlines and explanations as well as out of class content to reinforce learning. ENES100 is essentially a large group project where you build a small vehicle to complete tasks. At the end of the semester there is a competition. Mike's sections consistently preform better than others because of him as a prof.

Professor Mike is simply amazing. Every day he comes well prepared to class with an amazing personality and ready to make a lot of jokes. His lectures are great and he always puts his students first. He is enthusiastic about the ENES100 competition and is always inspiring us students to think creatively about how to make our project be the best.

Mike is the best professor I have taken or will ever take again! He gives excellent and helpful information. Other professors are boring and hand out too much work, but Mike is the opposite. The class is difficult, but he makes it better. In addition, he does like to see you make an effort though, so do so! He also brings snacks like cookies :)

Professor Mike is probably the best professor I've ever taken or will ever take again! Compared to other ENES100 professors he's in another universe. Super funny, super helpful and understanding. Really pushes students to interact with each other and strive for excellence. 10/10 !

Gives great and helpful information from the past to explain what past students have done and builds off from and implements announcements at a timely pace. Course was done so that real world advice such as internship methods became novel extra pieces of information.

Mike encourages success, connections, and creativity. At first glance, he seems to be a funny guy who can bring energy to the classroom but throughout the semester, you realize how intelligent he is. On top of that, he is always willing to guide any student achieve their goals in the classroom but also in their future. A true gem of a person.

Mike is a truly special professor. Most of the reviews you read about him are spot on. He loves to teach and it's apparent by listening to just his first lecture. Mike has a ton of knowledge and is always willing to lend a helping hand. Even better, Mike loves to bake and brings treats into class. His laugh is infectious and he's an awesome person.

Mike is one of my favorite teachers!! Such a genuinely nice person who wants the best for all his students, in and out of the classroom. While he's a tough grader, he provides the necessary material to do well in the class and is eager to answer your questions. He does like to see you make an effort though, so do so! He also brings snacks :)

Top professor I've ever had. He took a class that is well known to be difficult and taught harshly from other professors, and turned it into a very fun, intersting, engaging, and simplier to understand course. Mike is truly an educator ahead of his time. Plus, his wisdom he shared after our final exam truly changed my life. Take him!!

Mike is very personable and energetic. ENES100 is basically a giant group project and he gives his students a lot of support and advice for how to succeed. Our group was struggling a lot near the end and he took the time to help us redesign parts of our OTV. Make sure you ask him and the TFs questions because they are happy to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Mike is a very personable teacher, has a good sense of humor that makes his lectures more interesting and he also teaches in a creative way using real world examples. He is also very reasonable in what he asks you to do on his exams, unlike some other professors who have taught the class before. If you have the opportunity to take his class, do it.

Mike is a great professor and puts a lot effort into his presentations. He has an enthusiastic attitude, great stories of when he was a student/engineer, and a great sense of humor that made the class interesting and valuable. In sum, if you pay attention in class and do your part on your team for the OTV project, you will do well in his class.
Really wants his students to succeed, great professor
He's a really good professor and is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He's always there to lend a helping hand and always encourages us to persist despite failure.

Mike was a great professor throughout the entire semester. The lectures were usually pretty fun and not at all a bore. He'd be engaged the entire time and would engage the class as well. His teaching style was digestible and you're really able to pick up on everything as long as you pay attention. Not many HWs, prepared you greatly for Exams.

This was Mike's first semester teaching fluids but you would never know that if he didn't tell you. He's so passionate about teaching and makes lectures really clear it makes learning the material so much easier. The class is hard and you can't get around that, but he did a great job helping us understand. I wish Mike taught all of my classes!

Mike is probably one of the best teachers Ill ever have. He made learning about engineering both fun and informative, all the while working tirelessly to make sure students could understand and enjoy learning the content both in person and online.

This was the first semester Mike has ever taught Fluids and overall he did an awesome job. He makes lectures interesting and relates topics to real-world events. He did not give an excessive amount of homework and the exams were based right on the lectures and homework. He was very direct and I would highly recommend him to anyone!

Mike is exactly what you are looking for when coming into engineering at UMD. His class is not easy, it is fair. If you do the work, you will get a good grade. You do feel the pressure of the course, though this is engineering, what did you expect. He does well-transitioning students into the curriculum and if you are stuck he will be there.

I love his teaching style and sense of humor. He got great video editing skills and ofc baking skills! This class is quite a lot of work so don't underestimate it cuz it's 100 lvl. But Mike was there for students at all times. He is very understanding and was not too strict on deadlines as the class was pretty fast-paced. Regards, Green Goblin ;)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Mike has a unique persona and was always able to impress me with the lectures. Personally found him to be really funny and the lectures more bearable and engaging. He also bakes desserts and offers great opportunities!!
Mike is a great professor and I could not recommend him more heavily. Took the class over the summer and he was very understanding about obligations his students had outside of the course.

Mike is one of the best instructors I've had. His pre-recorded lectures are funny and informative, and he kept his class super engaging despite it being all virtual. He is very clear with his expectations but is also very accommodating. I highly recommend participating in his class and putting in the extra effort, as it will go a long way.

A great teacher for ENES100 and gave a friendly introduction into engineering studies. He is a very kind guy and wants only the best for his students, and does this by giving thorough feedback and creating very cool concepts for projects. Although he graded a little more harshly than I initially thought he would, Mike is one my favorite teachers!

Mike is probably one of the best teachers out there. He brings so much enthusiasm and laughter to class and spreads it to the students that welcome his energy and vibe with open arms. Mike also provides excellent feedback on assignments and projects that he assigns while also introducing further insight on the subject. 10/10!

Mike creates great videos to help keep you engaged in the content. He also gives grate feed back, is accessible outside of class, and is eager to communicated with his students. Great teaching style. %100 recommend you take what ever classes you can with Galczynski.

Although I took this class during the summer (only 6 weeks) and was online, Prof Mike created a wonderful learning environment that really promoted the understanding of course content. The lectures were always a joy to watch, his office hours (alongside his UTFs) were always helpful, and he always provided useful material to study for exams.

Professor Galczynski is easily the greatest instructor I have ever had. I was hesitant to take such a short class, but his commitment to helping his students understand the material and effective communication skills made it beyond worth it. Do yourself a favor and enroll in the sections being taught by him.

Professor Galzynsky truly cares about his students. He really knows how to explain complex concepts without making them dull. Galzynsky is a professor who loves a good corny joke! He fully uses office hours to help students study, but he is also totally down to just chat and tell stories. He is also an incredible baker and brings in goodies!

Mike is the best professor I have had at the university of maryland and i wish that he could teach all of my classes. Really easy to understand and he always relates the material back to real world examples so it gives meaning to the work that you are doing. If you have a chance to take one of his classes you will learn so much.
If you ever want to meet someone who figured out what they were born to do it is Prof. Michael G. He's got it all, showmanship, expertise, and compassion. Keep it up Mike!

Mike was a great professor. His online lectures were the first ones that I actually enjoyed watching every time. While the class has a lot of material, Mike's teaching style made it hard to get bored. Would definitely recommend.

Mike is the best professor I had so far. The videos he made for class are really informative and funny. Mike is always available to help and he tries to make students learn and get the best out of them. The class projects especially the final project is really one if the best times in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Best teacher I have had at UMD so far. His asynchronous lectures were extremely engaging and at times even funny. He really cares about his students

Mike is a rare gem among professors. He goes above and beyond to engage every student and makes learning fun with his sense of humor and video editing skills. Even though the lectures are self paced, Mike is always quick to respond and is there for his students. I highly recommend him!

Mike is an amazing professor. I read his reviews on this site before I took him and didn't understand why they were so high. After taking him, I get why. For example, I struggled through the first exam but Mike helped me and I was able to turn my grade around. He's very lenient, kind, and a great teacher in-person or online (my section had both).
you cab tell he puts a lot of effort into the class it can be difficult at times but there are a lot of study materials you can use

Mike is one of the best professors I've ever had. While ENES102 has a relatively hefty workload, Mike made the material incredibly easy to digest with his well-organized and timestamped series of prerecorded lectures. He responds to questions swiftly and thoroughly, and his humor is one of a kind.
One of the best professors I've ever had. He really cares about the class and his students. His lectures are actually interesting to watch and has great teaching skills. Plus he can bake really well.

Mike and Neel really saved online learning for me during the lockdown. Honestly had various other personal issues going on at the same time and Neel and Mike were especially accommodating. Besides that the coursework was difficult for me but if you do exactly what Mike says you'll be fine. Mike's acting chops deserve an oscar.

In a time of often unengaging and isolating online learning, Mike provided something I could look forward to. His videos were hilarious and engaging, and the classwork and projects provided lots of hands on learning. Mike cares so much about his students and wants us all to do our best. Could not recommend more.
If you have the opportunity to take any class with him, it would be a disservice to yourself to not take it. His passion for teaching really shows even over a completely online semester.

Mike is one of the only professors I have had so far who actually really cares about his students. He puts forth a lot of effort into all his lectures, and making sure students actually understand the material being taught in class. He also gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit, as well as practice for exams.

Mike was an amazing professor! ENES102 is a hard course but his lectures and spirit make the class so much more fun. He really wants all his students to succeed and reached out to me after the first exam to go over problems I had trouble with. He really does go the extra mile to make this class not only informative but fun as well.

reviews.comment: He's a great guy
Best Professor Ever Hands Down
Mike is the most passionate professor that Ive had. Because of this, he can expect a lot from his students. If you are taking enes102, definitely try to get Mike.
Mike is an amazing professor and made ENES100 very enjoyable. He puts a lot of effort into everything he does and he cares a lot about his students. Take him if you can!

Take Mike's class, you won't regret it! Grading? Fair. By no means should you slack off, but if you put reasonable effort into your work you WILL succeed. Lectures? Amazing. They are video edited to be entertaining and engaging while teaching you what you need to know. Personality? A gem. Mike cares and is genuinely invested in his students.

Mike is one of the best professors I have ever had. He clearly care a lot about his students. He is super funny and makes awesome videos to make class more engaging. He loves engineering and wants to inspire his students.

Professor Mike is incredibly personable and really cares about his students. I had him for both ENES100 and ENES102 and he teaches the material very well, making sure no student is left behind. You can reach out to him anytime for whatever you need and it was a great comfort to have him as my professor.

Mike is a teacher who clearly cares and puts a lot of effort into his videos and classes. This made online learning easy and enjoyable. The group projects in ENES100 were lots of fun while also being a good challenge.

The professor made class engaging and interactive. I got to know my fellow students throughout the semester which helped with the group projects. Class was always interesting and I could tell that the professor really cared about our education. He was always excited to teach and got the rest of the class excited as well.

Mike is an awesome professor who genuinely cares about his students. He definitely shows passion in what he teaches and that is reflective of how he chooses to communicate the course material to his students.

One of the best professors at UMD. His lectures are very entertaining, he cares a lot about his students. He is very lenient when grading exams, he also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. You get what you put into this class, so do the extra credit, do the practice problems and most likely you'll get an A.

Mike brings his love of engineering and baking to the classroom with utmost enthusiasm. He doesn't spare the details when teaching, and enabled me to learn curriculum and enjoy it. Fair warning, you get out of the class what you put in, so if you're looking for low effort this may not be for you. I would definitely take Mike as my professor again.

I had a blast with his class and would trade my left kidney for him to teach all of my science courses for the rest of college. Great editing skills and I wish I had spent more time enjoying his class rather than stressing about my other classes. He really teaches you how to enjoy the experience of working with others and learning.

Professor Galczynski is perhaps the best professor I have ever had for a class. His lecture videos were engaging and entertaining, and after watching each one I felt I had an excellent grasp of the subject. My father is an engineer as well and he watched Mike's lectures purely because he loved the way he taught. Hands-down, best professor at UMD.

Mike is the best professor I had in my first semester at UMD. He put a lot of time and effort into his online lectures that made them very enjoyable to watch, and gave plenty of optional opportunities for students to receive help, allowing for students of all skill levels to excel as efficiently as possible.

Best prof I've had. Cares so much about the students, always available to help. Lectures are super engaging. And at the end of the year as long as you've been putting in the work he'll curve your grade. Actually cares that his students are well supported, engaged, and actually learning something. I can not recommend taking a class with him enough.
He is very inspirational, kind, and cares about his students. There are few professors like him! Take him if you can.

The lecture videos were very funny and engaging and the groupwork and homework assignments really helped me to learn the material. He is very accessible and provides lots of materials to help prepare for tests and provided lots of extra credit to help us out in the time we're in right now. You can tell how much he cares about his students!
Awesome lectures. Adapted very well to online teaching.

Mike is a great professor. He is very approachable and shows he truly cares about his students succeeding. His lectures are very entertaining and he provides many opportunities to practice the material. If you practice, you will succeed in this class.

His lecture videos are very engaging, unlike a lot of other professors. He does good examples on the subjects and the group work is helpful for preparing for the exams. He was well prepared for online learning.

This professor is the best out there. You can tell that he cares so much about his students, and his lectures are god tier. To be completely honest, this guy should hold a workshop for other professors on how to teach the class because the world would be so much better if every professor exemplified his teaching style.

Mike is such an amazing professor, and if you have the opportunity to take a class with him, definitely don't pass it up. He is super engaging and makes difficult content easy to understand. It's evident that he really cares about his students, and goes above and beyond to help them. He also makes incredible lemon bars. 100% would take again.

Mike is the best teacher you can take for this course. He works hard to get to know his students on a more personal level. Be prepared for a lot of working with other classmates and some class participation. He will push you to do your best on the group projects, but is very caring and supportive. If you ask for an extension youll probably get it.

Out of all my professors, Mike is the only one that made meaningful connections to his students, and it's clearly evident that he cares about the success of each and every one of them. His lectures were funny yet educational and prepared you completely for exams. I had a great time and learned a lot, so I hope to have him again next semester.

So my review will be a little unique, but I'd say more so than engineering mechanics, professor Galczynski taught me how to be a successful college student and in some broader respects how to live. More so than grades, what you'll learn will make you both a better college student and a better person. Oh and he taught mechanics pretty well.
Just gotta say, he's an amazing professor all around, especially with the effort he puts into his videos.0

Mike doesn't doesn't only just care about whether his students understand the content, but he also drops amazing advice both in terms of career and life in general. Even online, he was incredibly interactive with his class. I only wish that my class was longer so I could spend more time learning from him.
I would sell my soul to have Mike Galczynski teach every one of my classes for the rest of college. Also, if you ever see him at Eppley, dont be afraid to say hello.

Mike is genuinely the best professor I've had at UMD. His lectures are always super clear and also include "bloopers" at the end to give you a little break. His exams are always super straightforward and if you don't understand something he is sure to help you out. If you have the chance to take Mike, TAKE THAT CHANCE!

Professor Galczynski is not only a fantastic professor and teacher but truly a friend to the students. Of all the professors I had, Mike made the greatest effort by far to keep his students engaged and entertained in an online environment. If you get your choice for ENES100, Mike is the professor you want to have!
Super super generous and fantastic teacher! Definitely knows how to have fun and teach well. Very supportive of my shenanigans, and replaced most mandatory class time with extra credit. 10/10!

makes great lectures that are easy to understand and really cares about his students. he has a good sense of humor and makes a mean lemon bar! if you stay on top of your work and study youll do just fine in the class. 10/10 would recommend mike to anyone
Great professor, enthusiastic energy which makes class enjoyable. 10/10

Professor Mike is one of the best ENES100 professors at UMD. Despite being online and not completing the traditional OSV project, Mike made the class fun, educational, and enjoyable! On group projects, he encouraged all members to work beyond expectations and to do their best. He gave valuable feedback and truly cares about all his students.

This teacher was hands down my favorite I have had. He puts so much effort into crafting lectures that actually make you learn along with hilarious bloopers to make sure you stay engaged. His class was my favorite even though it was a tough one. I one thousand percent recommend taking his class if you get the chance as you will not be disappointed.

Honestly, Mike is the GOAT god, as referenced by Will and I in his class. He makes his videos interesting and his bloopers are a full-on saga like the Marvel Cinematic Universe. He was one of the professors that would teach you very well for one second, and then be talking about fantasy football the next. Overall, he is the greatest professor ever!

Michael Galczynski is undoubtedly one of the BEST professor at UMD Engineering. He makes very funny and engaging video lectures (incredible bloopers). Best thing about him is that he gives away loads of extra credit! Mike is very caring and helpful and yes, if you're in his offline class in future... You'll get to enjoy his delicious lemon bars!

Professor Mike is a phenomenal professor, he teaches very well and makes difficult content easier to understand. Mikes class consistently have the highest test scores compared to other professors because of this. I highly recommend taking this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mike has got to be the best professor at all of UMD, hes hilarious and makes class time fly by. He is always willing and excited to help students with projects and ideas. There is never a dull moment with Mike in the room. 11/10 If you have the chance to take a class with Mike and dont, you made the wrong choice.

Mike managed to make the impossible possible with virtual ENES100. His lectures are entertaining and will keep you engaged through 2 hours of Zoom. He is accessible outside of class, and helps when possible. Mike also puts tons of effort into his instructional videos in an effort to please his students. Do yourself a favor and take Mikes class!
Absolute blast. He brought us lemon squares and baby pumpkins. Handled Zoom well, although 2 hour long classes can get a little mundane.

Absolutely wonderful professor. Super great and enthusiastic about teaching and does a great job with a smile. Likes to give our rewards to students and I am sure that anyone who has taken him will know that his baked goods are the best. Do be prepared to study and work hard as its not an easy A.
He is honestly going to probably be the best professor I'll ever have.

He's an amazing professor if you can take him!! TBH the only reason that I did not get an A is that I didn't put in any work. If you do a couple of hours of practice problems and watch the lectures every week you'll definitely get a B, probably an A

Professor Galczynski was one of the best professors I have had, clearly caring about his students and giving them the material and the practice that they need to succeed in an engineering science class. Lectures were asynchronous, and there were bonus homework and group work sessions every week, as well as a mandatory Friday group class.

He is a great professor and he really relates to his students. He also wants them to do very well and makes the presentation very easy to understand while making the class very fun. Take his class if you can.

Mike is one of the BEST professors you can ever get. He makes Mechanics 1, a very difficult and boring class, likeable. He goes the extra mile to make his lectures hilarious with bloopers and jokes. He takes complex ideas and makes them understandable for even a 3rd grader. On exams and assignments, he grades very clearly and leniently. THE BEST!!!

Seriously, if you are going to take ENES 102, PLEASE CONSIDER TAKING IT WITH MIKE! You can obviously see how much effort he put into explaining the concepts and approaches to do exam-like problems, which helps me to not only know what I should study and get high scores on exams, but to also learn how to apply these concepts in real world settings.

Mike's enthusiasm for engineering and teaching is infectious. He provides copious examples of him personally working through problems that are very similar in complexity to anything he puts on the tests. I went in to every test confident that I knew exactly what he expected us to be able to do and how he expected us to do it.

Mike is AMAZING!!! He puts a lot of time and effort into making and editing his lecture videos. He explains everything in a very simple, clear, and exciting way. Best, most charismatic professor I have ever had! Handling these online classes in the best way, ENES102 and ENES100 have been great experiences with Mike. Fun class! I learned a lot!

Mike was an amazing professor! Understanding the material was often difficult but, he put forth great effort to ensure the success of his students. The tests were relatively hard so make sure that studying is a priority.

During both semesters, ENES 100 & 102, I felt privileged to have experienced the teaching of an enthusiastic, knowledgeable and receptive educator. His capacity to embrace the inquisitive and challenging spirits of undergrads, and intuitive approach showcasing science, is refreshing. His primary directive clearly is the success of his students.
Mike's a great guy and an entertaining teacher. He goes the extra mile for his students and makes sure the workload is manageable.
Mike, One of the best teachers I had this past semester. He is really nice, genuinely cares for his students and is very understanding. His lectures are full of fun and jokes.

Mike is one of the most passionate teachers I have had. He cares about helping students do well and challenges them in the process. He also likes to relate the material from class to real-world applications.

Mike is a really great teacher. He clearly cares a lot about his students and the course, and wants them to love taking the class as much as he loves teaching it. His lectures were consistently entertaining, and he is very approachable if you need help with anything. He does grade on the tougher side, but it pushes you to improve in class.

One of the best professors Ive ever had. I did not put online but half the class was online after COVID. On campus his lectures were fun & informative, and online so were his videos; he is really good at explaining and will help you understand all the concepts if you dont get something. Make sure to do HW and practice problems prior each exam.

Hands down the best professor I've had during my three years at UMD. All of his lectures are interesting and very unique. If the class does well on exams, he'll bake the whole class treats and give out additional prizes. He also explains concepts so that they've very easy to understand. I wish he taught more classes so I could be in his class again

Mike was the best! Even though I had a two hour class period, he always made the lectures really fun and engaging. He was hilarious and had really great stories.
