Professor Madoo is an awesome lecturer. Her lectures are funny and entertaining, and she knows her stuff. Your whole grade is based on three exams and participation in lecture, but it's super easy because the exams are online.

This is my third time having Dr. Madoo, and I can definitely say she's hands down the best professor I've ever had at UMD. She's really funny and she has a passion for what she does. Not to mention she is also very helpful and she truly cares about her students. If you even have the opportunity to take one of her courses you'll love it.
easy class, exams are not hard at all just read the textbook, exams are open note so there is no reason not to do well on them. Caring person accessible outside of class, great stories

This class is super easy and interesting. She makes the class enjoyable. There are 3 tests and they are non-cumulative and online. The tests are super easy if you go to lecture. It is impossible not to A if you go lecture and all of your discussion classes.

Dr. Madoo is definitely one of the funniest professors I have ever had at UMD. She talks about her personal life during lectures which makes them so interesting! However, she doesn't post notes so you NEED to attend lectures because the exams are based off the lectures. If you show up to class you'll do great. I highly recommend taking her class.

She is nice & a decent teacher overall: 

1. There's 6 Tests (It's more like short 20 question MC quizzes), 1 paper in the middle, 1 final paper in place of final, and participation 
2. She is strict with attendance, be careful about skipping classes
3. She talks freely about her personal life rather than focusing on lecture so do your readings!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Madoo's class was easy. However, she is by far the WORST professor I have ever had at UMD. She has zero flexibility for students. She has no tolerance for late assignments even though she has a 10% deduction written in her syllabus. She lacks understanding and empathy and does not care about your success if you are struggling.
3 main tests and participation grades for coming to discussion. Good professor and easy class.

I loved this class. Professor Madoo is very kind and always willing to help. Attendance is not mandatory, but make sure you know someone in class to copy the notes from because she will not provide them for you. Her exams are open-note and online, and most of the questions are from the lecture. Have your resume on you when guest speakers come.

dr madoo was a great professor. the class was an easy a, but the material was interesting and she did a great job of explaining everything. tests were easy as long as you listened to lectures and discussions and the class was very straight forward

This prof. was inflexible, lacked understanding for students, & seemed to care little about students' success & made things extremely difficult during COVID, which was disappointing to see considering the circumstances of this semester have had a big impact on students' mental health and well-being. Course was easy but take it with a better prof.

I previously had Dr. Madoo for CCJS100, and I liked her then. I remembered her mentioning this class specifically, and I finally had the chance to take it. Didn't regret it at all. She's really passionate about what she teaches, and she doesn't make things too difficult, either. Just make sure you're not solely relying on lecture notes for exams.

This was my favorite class yet at UMD. Lectures were so interesting. Discussion attendance is required but my TA was also really good. Participate and read the textbook and you will easily do well on exams. She's such a great prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: One of the easiest classes. Prof Madoo is super sweet. Her lectures get right to the point and they were short (online). If you watched and took notes, you would ace the tests. One discussion a week and you have to participate but it's easy participation. 3 tests, Discussions each week. That's it. Take her for the intro CCJS class, very worth it.

This course was a joke, but this was the least understanding professor that I think I have ever had. On top of that, the only interaction is with the TA (Prof. posts all the lectures on day 1). Not one shred of empathy for students extenuating circumstances, even during the COVID pandemic.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably one of the easiest classes on campus if you need a GPA boost, but a waste of your time. No interaction with the professor at all. All lectures (extremely boring) are posted on day one and discussions are with the TA. Also, zero consideration given for students during COVID pandemic.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Madoo was great, and made the class super easy. Our grade was comprised of three non-comprehensive open-note tests and discussion participation. There was only one lecture to watch per week, and the work load was very manageable.

All you had to do was read the textbook, listen to the lecture (which basically regurgitated the textbook, but listen anyway because there is material that will be on the test), and attend the discussion. EASY A! Also, Professor Madoo holds office hours before every exam (only 3) where she goes over the content covered.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a sweet lady and super interesting lectures. Not too much work to earn an A if you just pay attention

This class had recorded lectures from Dr. Madoo and discussions with a TA. You don't speak with the prof unless you attend office hours, which I'm not a fan of, but her lectures are clear. The only grades are a few exams that are very easy and straightforward, and then attendance. Only work is reading the textbook which is long but helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Madoo is honestly one of the best I have experienced so far at UMD. She is a great lecturer and is really able to hold your attention. A majority of your final grade will be based off exams, but if you read the textbook and takes good notes an A is very acheivable. I love her!
Only 3 tests throughout the semester and they're non-cumulative. Only other grades are discussion grades weekly. Easy A definitely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Madoo gives great lectures. Be sure to take notes on them because there are some things not in the text book that are fair game for the exam. As long as you stay on top of the readings and attend discussion, it should be an easy 3 credits. The concepts are pretty straightforward and the exams are non-cumulative, so that's nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was very disappointed taking this Professor during the pandemic and they lacked care and concern for what students were going thru and dealing with. One bad assignment can ruin your entire grade for this class. The participation was performative only. Would not advise taking this Professor during COVID as they had no shred of empathy.

Excellent lecturer. Makes even some not-super exciting material more readable. She offers lots of other projects besides just reading too - movies, articles, books so it's not just mundane texts and lectures. She will go out of her way to make sure you understand and earn your very best grade possible. Highly recommend Madoo!!!

Although the course was easy, Professor Madoo is probably the least understanding professor that I've ever had. She tries so hard to be likable and relatable, however, she truly has no regard for the wellbeing of her students. She does not give out extensions regardless of any extenuating circumstances.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Madoo is a great lecturer. Her classes are always interesting. She brings guest speakers and she brings in personal stories to help us understand concepts. She explains things really well, and her transition to online due to the pandemic was straightforward and easy.

Fun, informative lectures. She doesn't give out the slides so you need to go, but she makes it worth it. Exams are super easy, and discussion work is basically all participation based. Definitely recommend.
She is almost always available for questions and gives amazing lectures. Sometimes, Madoo brings in a guest speaker and they're really cool (ex, US Marshal, FBI Agent, Parole Officer, etc).

Madoo is the BEST. Her lectures are always interesting and engaging and she brings really cool speakers into class. You NEED to go to lecture because she doesn't post slides and she says important stuff. But, she will literally tell you what's on the exam so it's worth it. Take Madoo if you get the chance, she is actually the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Madoo is really funny and will base her test off of lecture material with few being from the textbook. So just go to lectures (with a skim of the chapter) and pay attention and you should be fine.
She is smart and nice but her lectures are pointless, she covers 2 slides over 50 minutes so if you can have someone send you notes from class then you don't need to go.

Dr. Madoo is an amazing lecturer. She often uses personal experiences to convey concepts. Her lectures are funny and entertaining. The course material is not difficult, and if you do the readings and attend lectures, you will definitely get an A. The course material is interesting, and I would love to take another class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Madoo! She is very funny and straightforward. Her tests aren't hard at all if you dedicate yourself and study. She usually goes over what you'll need to study for the exams. The paper we had to do was outlined VERY clearly. If you miss lecture you'll probably miss some exam questions. Write down things she says that AREN'T on the slides!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Madoo overall is a good professor, she obviously cares about the subject and wants you to succeed. Lecture is easy and she makes it interesting. However she can come off as pretty condescending at times, especially during her office hours, which I don't appreciate.... never talk down to a student because they don't understand something
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Madoo was great. Her lectures are funny, not too dense, and she tells you specific points that will be tested. If you actually read (you need to for the quizzes) read and listen in lecture, it's a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor!!! My best lecture thus far, I actually looked forward to it. She's very funny and entertaining and her exams are easy. What may trip you up are the quizzes you get in your discussion, because the TAs make them up, besides that the midterms are easy! Take her! She loves what she does you can tell!

Dr. Madoo went on maternity leave halfway through the semester, and she was honestly missed. Her lectures are fun, and her tests are fair. There's one paper, biweekly quizzes, 3 exams and weekly readings. If you show up to the lecture and moderately try, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Madoo is an AMAZING professor. She's super smart, hilarious, and her exams and quizzes are super straightforward. I've taken her for this class and for 100 my freshman year and I can't wait to take her classes again when she's back from maternity leave! She's a great professor and wants to see us all do well.

Madoo is an amazing professor who is really funny and caring! Her lectures are super enjoyable and interesting. The class involves a lot of reading but if you really wanted to you could just memorize the terms on Quizlet. Overall easy A.

Dr. Madoo is a real gem! She's absolutely hilarious. She also went to UMD so she's really relatable. Her exams are pretty straightforward and multiple choice. She also goes over what you need to know for the exams beforehand. 11/10 would recommend

Really awesome professor! If you get the chance, you should take a class with her. She is very knowledgeable about her subject and invites interesting guest speakers. Exams were easy as long as you came to classes and skimmed the textbook. One of the best professors I have had!

Professor Madoo is extremely passionate about the subject and makes lectures really interesting and easy to understand. You don't have to go to lectures, but tests do have questions specific to things discussed in lecture, so you should go. As long as you attend class and read the textbook, the class it really easy to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved her.

They say hindsight is 20/20. I say I made a great decision taking CCJS100 with Dr. Madoo. Her lectures include info not in textbook that are on the exam. There are only 3 exams and then, discussion. I recommend reading the book for her class. Class is not intensive. She brings in interesting guest speakers. Some lectures bore me, other not.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Favorite prof at UMD, you have to show up but there's not much extra work besides showing up and doing the reading. You should study for her tests but it's nothing arduous. Her tests are straightforward and she does not try to trick you. Highly respectable person and teacher.

Madoo knows the material well and is passionate about it. 3 tests in the semester and you have to STUDY for them. They are not tricky and as long as you study for a couple hour before the exam you will be fine. Take her if you are interested in CCJS, but don't expect an easy A with no hard work
Really good Professor.

Just a phenomenal teacher! She loves incorporating stories and experiences in her lectures which makes them very interesting. GO TO LECTURE though because you have assignments when the guest speakers come but she doesn't tell you when they are going to come. Relatively simple class if you show up and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Madoo for CCJS100, in person, and CCJS342, which was online. She has been the best professor I ever had at UMD and makes everything easy and fun to learn.

This class is extremely easy. As long as you show up to most lectures, take notes and go to your discussion classes to take the quizzes you should get an A. She's not a boring teacher at all so attending her lectures are actually worth it. Plus, the guest speakers she brings in are also entertaining. Overall, easy class and good professor.

Wow. She is great. Honestly one of the best professors I have ever had. She is hilarious and her lectures are amazing. She has the best stories and makes lecture so interesting. You will not want to miss a lecture just because of the stories you might miss. Wish I could take her for every class.
Professor Madoo is a gem! Her lectures are interesting and easy to follow. I highly recommend her! If you prepare for quizzes and exams you will do fine.

Without a doubt, take this class. Fulfills an HS gen ed and even though you have to come to class for lecture slides, it's entertaining and not a waste of time. Only real assignment is a discussion paper- but is easy to pull an A. 3 non cumulative exams which are all easy to pass. Guest lecturers and stories made this class one of my favorites.

She's so funny and such a great teacher. She doesn't let you use laptops in lecture but it honestly had no effect on my grade. You can tell she really wants her students to do well, she doesn't try to trip you up on tests.
She has great stories and guest speakers. Plus shes hilarious

She is the very few teachers that I love her speaking style and explanations. The class consists of 3--50-80 multiple choice exams, a paper, and other discussion materials. Gives 2% E.C. from her Kahoot quizzes at some lectures. Very disciplined about her rules. Readings, 20-30 pages long for 1-2 each chapter a week is not asking for much.
Madoo is one of the best professors I have had at UMD, she is hilarious and truly cares about her students.

Easily one of the best professors I have ever had. She really wants her students to get an A. I took this class as a gen ed and do not regret it. Her lectures are great, she makes them fun, and I really enjoyed her. 3 easy exams including the final, which was not cumulative, and 1 easy paper.

Dr. Madoo is amazing! She is probably the funniest professor in the ccjs department. She makes class very interesting and explains things very well. We had a lot of great class discussions and the book we read was so eye opening. Her papers are super easy and she gives great feedback. There are random in class graded assignments though!

Dr. Madoo is a by no chance a good professor or person. I took this class after looking at the reviews at Rate my Professors and also because my friends told me take her class. But, unfortunately the class was extremely hard for just one Gen-ed. On top of that, she doesnt even allow electronics in class. Horrible person, horrible class.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Madoo is the BEST professor I have ever had! She is engaging, intelligent, and works with you to get the grade you want. She is always available to talk about classes or life in general. She explains everything clearly in class and captives her students. If you have the opportunity to take a class with her, do it!

I took this class as my first CCJS course at UMD and Professor Madoo was simply wonderful. She was funny, had great guest speakers and did not require attendance or participation. Highly recommend and plan on taking CCJS498G in the future!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Madoo is very passionate and caring about the subject and her students. She makes the material interesting and easy to learn. The only downside about the class is that she moves quickly through material and there are only two exams and a few quizzes, plus a few other assignments that make up the grade.

I loved coming to her class because she always made the class interesting. However, her TAs should have been english majors since they destroy everybody's grades at the end of the semester with the paper assignment. Went from a A to B bc they wanted to be picky with the grading. But Madoo gave us extra credit bc of her TAs. Great Class, horrible TA

Take her class it is an easy A. Dr. Madoo is a great professor and she makes the class very interesting. We watch videos, have real attorneys, cops, and alumnis come in and talk to the class. You can use the book but it is not necessary, EVERYTHING on the exam is straight from the lecture slides.

Dr. Madoo is an amazing professor! It isn't necessary to read the textbook because she goes over most things in class but it's always helpful because you can miss important things. She is so funny and makes lecture interesting with guest speakers and videos. Go to class, take notes and it's an easy A.
She is just an ok teacher!! Honestly, she doesn't teach nicely in class. You will just have to refer the book and study from it properly if you wanna get an A in the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Dr. Madoo seems like a pretty cool person, but the class was just dull. For a 400 level course, it was relatively shallow and repetitive. The class is in no way hard, its just difficult to stay interested in the material. The chapters in the book and the readings are long but basically just reiterate the same themes over and over again.

Dr. Madoo is a really awesome professor here at UMD! Her lectures are very informative, yet laced with humor to keep us students awake and entertained. The only work that you have to do in this class outside of exams are in the discussion sections (two 2 paged papers) and participation stuff. Not an easy A, but not extremely difficult either.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Madoo is an amazing professor and an awesome person too. You have to attend all her lectures to do well because she doesn't post notes and has test questions pulled directly from things she goes over in her powerpoints. She's hilarious and makes her lectures and the entire class easy and enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Favorite professor this semester! She was hilarious and made all of the textbook material very clear. If you go to lecture there is no way you won't get an A. She's a great teacher!
Best professor! I highly recommend Professor Madoo. Lectures are interesting and she is funny.

Best professor ever! Attendance is not taken in lecture, but if you want to understand the material and get good grades, you better go to lecture. Dr. Madoo makes every lecture interesting and is very interactive with the students.

SHES SUCH A GREAT PROF. Her lectures are great, and she's really funny. She tells personal stories, shows vids and movies, and even has guest speakers come in. Its a really well rounded class and her lectures are super helpful. One of the few classes I actually look forward to.
Very funny Teaches well  Lectures are always interesting Straight to the point

Dr. Madoo is an INCREDIBLE professor. She expects her students to pay attention in class, and asks for no technology in the classroom (which could be a deterrent for some), but ultimately, her lectures are really informative and helpful, not to mention amusing, as she tries to include anecdotes within her lectures so they aren't too material heavy.

Class time was always fun and interactive, very fair homework/exams, very approachable and caring. The course really challenges you to learn concepts in an intuitive manner (e.g. understanding the difference between probability and statistics). Highly recommended. Dr. Krivtsov is an exemplary professor and an inspiration to live up to.

Professor Krivtsov is an excellent instructor who explains complex reliability concepts clearly and connects them to real-world applications. He is approachable, supportive, and provides constructive feedback. His passion and clarity make ENRE640 both challenging and rewarding. I highly recommend taking his class!

Very passionate professor, very engaging lectures, uses many practical real-world examples from his full-time work at Ford. The course is challenging but very well taught. Highly recommend Dr Krivtsov and his course at UMD.

Prof. Basil it was amazing. Extremely knowledgeable and willing to share. After my years of working experience in the field of reliability, I can say I learnt a lot from Prof.
Alex, our TA, was extremely knowledgeable, also available at all time, too.
Both of these people are assets to the university of Maryland and the students

Professor does an excellent job of applying the coursework to real world applications and situations. Very fun lectures and good/challenging homework problems. I felt like I really learned the content and have the ability to apply it in my career.

Inspiring, contagious enthusiasm. Cares very much about students, tries hard to ensure that everyone really understands the material. Very accessible and positive in answering questions during lectures and asynchronously. Amazing breadth and depth of knowledge. Content is challenging in the best possible way. Highlight of my experience at UMD!

On Teachers appreciation day, I am reminiscing the insane learning I had in 
ENRE640. Dr Krivitsov's practicality and love towards math is the inspirational best I got @ UMD. I thank him for electing to share his knowledge despite his busy professional career. It has shaped my career and I'm sure will shape the careers of many budding rel engineers

Best professor Ive ever had. You can tell he loves teaching. 1. Content is extremely well structured and clear. 2. He responds to all questions 3. He is at the forefront of the field and shares it with u 4. Cares that you understand the key concepts 5. Constantly challenges you in hw, tests and class 6. Funny Amazing professor.
His lectures are entertaining and interactive. Each topic includes an example of its application in the field. His exams are tough but his grading is generous.

Hands down best class I have taken in my master degree beside maybe one other class. Dr. Krivtsov is really knowledgeable and always uses real life examples so that makes it really easy to understand the course material. clear explanation, accessibility outside classroom and great course content are not only but best features about Dr. Krivtsov.
Excellent professor. Extensive industry experience incorporated into lectures. Engaging dialogue with students. This has been my most challenging and favorite grad course.

Professor Krivtsov is an amazing teacher and leader in the reliability industry. Anyone who takes his course is truly lucky to be able to learn from his experience. This course requires hard work and dedication, but you will be rewarded with a practical skill-set for the working world.
Excellent Course! Energetic, entertaining and highly competent. Favorite grad course I've had.
Competent and engaging.
5-star!

I loved her class and felt like she genuinely cared about us as students. She cares about actual learning rather than just grades which I appreciated so much. I'd definitely take another class with her!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Definitely take her classes, she's a great teacher, and has a lot of sympathy for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Korobkin was such a great professor. Her lectures were very engaging and she went out of her way to include many guest speakers throughout the semester. Workload was not bad at all, just 5 discussion posts and exams. I recommend her class to everyone and she takes student feedback very seriously.

Professor Korobkin listens and cares about teaching and actually takes student feedback into account when designing the course. The class itself was also great, a general overview of monuments and memorials. Lectures are worth going to. Also it satisfies a gen-ed req which is great.

Dr. K is a great professor in the English department. He is very responsive to emails and gives very clear feedback in assignments. He is a fair grader, and if there is something you do not understand, he is excellent at clearing it up. He has a very laid-back demeanor, and he shows that he cares about his students. Please take a class with him.

Really nice professor and manageable class. All homework is graded on completion. He is very understanding to any extenuating circumstances as well. I definitely think I became a better writer because of this class, so take him if you get the chance.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had Dr. K during Spring 2023. We were not in the classroom a lot of the time, which was a bit strange, but whenever he and I met on Zoom during our normal class time, he was super helpful with answering questions I had. I found him to be a very fair grader and he offers great feedback. Take this class with him
He was such a good professor. Very helpful and responsive to emails. Would def recommend him to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: prof kolakoski was the best. so chill and always responds to your messages. he is very understanding and is always willing to help his students. lots of writing and activities but you can do those without going to class. definitely best english teacher here!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was "in person" but I swear he cancelled class at least once and week or made it "asynchronous". The writing assignments were manageable and he did a good job breaking down the assignments.

This class was very laid back, but also helped me improve my writing. I wouldn't consider the homework load light, but it was manageable. He was super understanding and if I needed any extra help he was always available. VERY easy grader. As long as you do the work on time you will get a good grade.
He's a great guy and is very down-to-earth. He knows you have other classes and adjusts for that. Awesome professor overall and I am so happy I had him.

Dr. Kolakoski is the best and I am so happy I had him. As someone who dislikes English, I genuinely enjoyed the class! Assignments were graded off effort (except for papers but there were only 3 and they were straightforward and still seemed to be graded leniently). I had him online because of COVID but 10/10 recommend! So nice and understanding!!

Despite the amount of work he gives, Dr. K is a great professor and cares a lot about his students. He will give you an extension on anything as long as you ask. Most of his lectures were asynchronous. He also allows his students to submit anything past the due time (11:59 pm) as long as it's submitted before he wakes up.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Kolakoski is a super easy and considering prof given online classes and the pandemic. Most of the class is asynchronous and is pre-structured. That said, he is very lenient with extensions. The only down side is he takes a really long time to grade your work but will make accommodations for you if you have an upcoming assignment.

All round a solid English Professor, note that he is a tough grader. Albeit, your technical writing skills will improve by choosing his class. If you want to be an even better writer, definitely go to his office hours.

I really enjoyed taking Kolakoski this semester! He is extremely considerate of his students and is very easy to talk to. His lectures were so interesting, and I enjoyed the readings/books we read as well. You have a lot of dissuasion boards and some pop quizzes, but overall they were very fair. Take him! I feel like Im a much better writer now :)

Kolakoski is such a great guy! Even with a new baby and everything, he still manages to answer our questions. So there are a lot of discussion boards and some (pop) quizzes, but theyre straightforward and manageable. You always have readings to do, but again its pretty fair. Hes an easy guy to talk to and he gives great feedback on essays!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. K is great! My American Dream in Ethnic American Lit class has been my fav at UMD so far. Super eye opening and inspiring material, and Dr. K encourages you to share your opinion and feel comfortable doing it. There is a lot of reading and you have to do it and come to class to pass, but it's an easy A if you just participate and try your best.

Overall a good teacher. Really nice, understanding, and approachable. Its extremely difficult to get an A on any paper and he is pretty stingy about giving As in general. Rarely gives As on papers, but its always nice when you do get one because you know its good. Learned a lot in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Really tough grader, makes you work hard for good grades. Don't expect a 100 on a major assignment because he'll flat out tell you he doesn't give them. He's also very unclear about what specifically should be in your papers. He's helpful if you go to office hours though, and you probably will learn to be a better writer by the end of the course.

Took Professor K for ENGL101H as a Engineering Major and his class was my favorite above all of my engineering classes. He is a personable teacher who is more than willing to go meet with you outside class. He is a tough grader but makes crystal clear what should be in the assigned papers so as long as you have what he asks for you should get an A.

This class was definitely hard but his lectures were easy to understand and he overall taught well. As a warning though the class gets much harder in the second half of the semester. The curve helped a lot, I ended with a 77% and that became a B+ with the curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The midterms are easy if you study enough. The lectures are a bit boring, but he posts all of the slides to canvas which is really awesome. You are allowed to have a double sided notecard for all exams, which is extremely helpful and is NOT a standard among CHEM135 professors. The final exam was pretty diffucult though.

Dr. Lascio is a genuinely great person with interesting and helpful lectures. The grading is ~10 long online HW (guaranteed 100%), 3 manageable midterms, and a hard final. Study heavily, do the homework, go to lectures, do the discussion worksheets, and you will do well. He also HEAVILY curved our final grade. Overall, TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!

This professor is very understanding. One of the best chemistry Professor I have had, he goes over everything and tells you what to study and what not to study in the exam. Allowed us to use a study card during the test.

Great guy. He is usually available to be contacted through email and will make sure that he answers your question. The lectures and discussion were really unhelpful. The exam were a bit difficult, and he couldn't realize why people were doing terrible (rush through and skipped chapters). Expecting students to do it on their own.  Do not recommend.

Very understood, and pro student. Hes always on our side. Not to mention that he doesnt think any question is dumb or waste of time. I took his class online and he managed to be outstanding, I could only imagine how better he would be in person. I needed extra help and he stayed with me on multiple occasions HOURS after lecture.

lascio is a really caring professor. When I needed help in the beginning of the semester he helped me a lot and was genuinely interested In helping. After going to office hours and working hard I got great grades later on in the course and ended up with a B which is a miracle considering how I started off. His grade cutoffs were amazing.

Professor Lascio is one of the best! He's very approachable and responds to emails super fast! His tests are nearly the exact same as his practice ones with only maybe a few surprise questions! He's very caring and it's obvious he wants his students to all succeed! There was also a nice grade cut-off at the end of the course! Highly recommend him!
Worst professor at UMD. Incredibly rude and plays favorites with his students. Ignores his emails. I sincerely abhor this professor.

I dont like this prof because at the end of the course he did these unfair grade cut-offs. I had a 90 and that wouldve been an A- either way, but instead of doing a fair/equal curve, he made ppl with the lower grades get higher ones they didn't deserve. It helped ppl who failed but not ppl like me who earned their grade. I emailed and he ignored me
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lascio is super duper nice and cares about his students. Although occasionally hell explain a simple thing for a very long time. I didnt expect to get a good grade in this class BC chem was never my strong suit. Class is exam-based. He said hes going back to being a TA for gen chem 2, but if he's a professor again then I def recommend him!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lascio is a super good guy. He cares a lot about the well-being of his students. Chem is hard in general so you definitely have to work for it and online lectures are kinda boring, but he tries to make it better. Emailing him is always sure to be helpful and he keeps students updated. Extra credit is offered as in class questions too!

You can tell Lascio really cares about his students and enjoys teaching!! The grade is very dependent on the exams so if you are a bad test taker, get ready to study! Hes very accommodating and understanding as well, all the exams are open note but no internet!! would 1000% recommend
Lascio is the GOAT. Chemistry is hard in general, but hes very relatable and understanding so he makes the class as easy as possible.

Professor Lascio was absolutely amazing, he cares so much about his students and the field he studies, and clearly loves teaching. I would recommend him to anybody who is taking chemistry, just make sure you attend his lectures. He is always willing to help and loves doing so.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lascio is a good guy but he is definitely a hold your hand type of Professor. He spends 30 minutes explaining one simple little example problem and as a result, his class is always WAY behind everyone elses. The class is so easy but its very boring. I got an easy A by not paying attention to any of the lectures and not going to discussion/Gss.

Professor Lascio is the best!! He makes Chemistry so fun and it always prepared to help any student struggling. He is willing to stay after class to help and replies to emails immediately. He also gives very clear and helpful feedback so you can always know exactly where to improve.

Lascio is a goat. He is so nice. His exams are "open note" meaning you should not use google but use all your notes. He is really understanding but of course chemistry is really hard. His exams are super similar to in class homework so you can get by for sure. And he says if the class average is low at the end of the semester, he will curve it!

Lascio is a good professor and he is very caring and nice but your grade is entirely based on exams which many do bad on. If you can do great on the exams then this class will be great but if you're a bad test taker you will be struggling a lot. Sometimes he doesn't go over important topics in the lecture so going to office hours are very importan

Professor Saunders is very reasonable with homework load and due dates, and brings some cheer to the class. The quiz questions are easy if you did any of the reading, and they won't kill you if you miss a handful of classes. I would definitely take his class again

The class was so, so easy. I barely went to lecture and never once went to discussion. The only downside is that he does give six pop quizzes (drops your two worst) in lecture, so I missed a couple. Exams were so easy, though, that it didn't really matter. TA was pretty sexy.

Oh MY GOD!!?!?!?!?!?!?!  HE is SOOO SMEXY.  not to mention the perfect teacher.  The class is interesting, engaging, funny, higher learning, just perfect overall.  He has that like older man smexyness i love as well.  I WANT TO HAVE HIS BABIES
He was a good professor, I'm assuming his PHIL140 class is much more interesting because the PHIL100 class felt dry and boring. Good professor, bad class to take.
Great guy. Loves his job. He will really help you out if you need him to. His lectures are not that boring, he makes them interesting. He is very clear and not dull. This is a good class take it.

Saunders is a nice guy and he keeps the class interesting.  Attendance is kind of mandatory because there are 6 pop quizzes.  He drops the 2 lowest quiz grades.  Midterm questions were given to you beforehand as were the questions for the (noncumulative) final.  Readings were kind of long and dull but not too bad.  The 2 papers weren't hard either.

I think he is a great professor. You could tell he loves his job and keeps his class fun and interesting. The class isnt too hard, if you study and do the assigned papers (only 2), you'll get a good grade.
No Comments

I had CCJS 360 and 498O, very caring about his students and make sure everyone is fine. He definitely changed my mind about my career goals and now focus on children and youth. he teaches from his own personal experience which makes it interesting.

I had CCJS 360 and 480O, one of the best professors in UMD and changed my mind about my career goals. He knows his material and explains the material with his own experiences in the field and inspires other students. He is very caring about his students and makes sure no one feels uncomfortable in class or the material.

I had prof Morlier in 3 of my semesters. I love the way he teaches, he loves his students and care about them. He never gives a lot of work. He believes that all of his students are very smart. He loves to help students who are struggling in the class or in any other class. Take him, you will enjoy his lectures.

Super friendly, he loves his students. He really care about his students. He does not give a lot of work, he will give you only 3 quizzes in the semester and give you A. Prof Morlier helped me a lot in my classes. His lecture are funny, you won't feel the time when you are in his class. I recommend him 100%
Best Prof ever. He loves his students, he would give you extra point if you need it. He really cares about his students. I would take him over and over again.

Enjoyed Professor Morlier. He does require 3 papers for the CCJS 321 class, 2 of which have to be 10 pages long and the last project 15 pgs - I think that's just a UMUC requirement. Overall, I would take another one of his classes in the future.

The teacher was great, I enjoyed her lectures, and it was easy to know what I needed to note down for the weekly open-note quizzes or exams. Just make sure to have written down your notes and pay close attention to the lecture. Very easy to learn, and you can tell she is passionate. She sometimes checks in with the class to understand our workload.

I thought she was the worst person ever. In lecture, she takes attendance. She also will run through the roster and randomly call on people. The projects were graded fairly, but it's kind of a lot of work for a gen ed. I wouldn't say it's the easiest class ever, but it's not super hard. She's very snarky and rude.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Professor May does a great job of trying to make the lectures more engaging and set in a current perspective. One thing, however, is that she runs through slides very fast. When I've met with her after class, I noticed that she doesn't handle questions very well so expect a snarky answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Class is very interesting and fair game. If you show up and do your work you'll do fine. Grade is based off discussion attendance, projects every week, clicker questions, and online quiz every week. Professor is very nice and available frequently. Overall an enjoyable class!

It was a BL class, so there was her lecture, a reading component, and a workshop with a TA. The class was about introducing the concept of architecture, so professor May did well to help students ease into an architecture mindset. There is some creativity involved with projects, but professor May and the TA's help a lot, and are available for help.
Really great professor. Grading is easy but the classes are still rigorous.
Great professor, I would highly recommend for tax!
do not take

Milton seems like a nice guy, but he just isn't a good professor. He gives out assignments without really teaching you how to do it, and he expects you to know things that aren't even covered in the class.

The class was very dry and the professor uses publisher powerpoints to teach his lectures. Reading the textbook was more helpful than going to class, but I still went to class because he was a stickler for attendance. Exams are open book, limited notes, so it's helpful to read the book.

Taxation of individuals. Great professor, show up in class for trivia extra credit opportunities. The questions from the extra credit opportunities are almost always on the exams. Allows one sheet of paper front and back PER chapter and open book tests! Hes AWESOME! he does take attendance for participation.  the final is not cumulative.
Many things to love about her class. What I liked more is how clear she is. Recommend. You'll learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She's very knowledgeable about the topic and so enthusiastic about student success. Highly recommended.
She's an amazing professor, probably the best I've had at UMD. She's kind and brilliant. She also knows a lot of people in the field and is willing to help you.
easy going, very smart
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved her class. her dry sense of humor really had me cracking up
She's fabulous! Really nice and super caring.
Class was worth it based on the resume writing exercise alone.
My class with her was great. She's super knowledgeable.
My class with her was great. She's super knowledgeable.
I actually liked her class. Prof Lalwani is very approachable and quickly gets back to you.
Prof. Lalwani is such an inspirational teacher. I took her because it's required, but it became my favorite. She creates community where she goes.
Hers was one of the few classes I actually attended. She's really nice and has a really good deadpan sense of humor. Seeing her students succeed matters to her, and she really tries to help them.
I took the health professional writing class with her over the summer several years and really learned a lot. She's super nice and accessible outside of class.

I can't thank Prof. Lalwani enough. She changed my life. She's a formidable presence in the classroom, no doubt, but that's because she's serious about ENGL 394. We worked hard, but she supports you, and we were super sad when the class ended. Amazing prof.

I took ENGL 393 with the professor years ago and am still in contact with the professor. When I reached out for a letter of recommendation for medical school, she agreed. I am now heading to medical school and have Professor Lalwani to thank.

I took ENGL 393 with the professor years ago and am still in contact with the professor. Don't buy the other reviews. She's amazing and knowledgeable, and it showed in her class. When I reached out for a letter of recommendation for medical school, she agreed. I am now heading to medical school and have Professor Lalwani to thank.

Professor Lalwani is caring and responsive when answering student questions. I would recommend her for a low stress environment in ENG394.
I appreciated the professional feedback on things I would inevitably have to complete like the Resume assignment. 
Deadlines are communicated before the start of every class; a nice reminder of what is expected.

She is a tough but fair teacher. She truly cares about teaching her students and as such if you are invested, you learn so much. Your effort in the course will be directly proportional to what you get out of the course and grades. She cares about students, meeting with them to help them plan their future and advocating for them if they ask.

Mandatory conferences for an asynchronous course, depend on peer reviews for feedbacks on major assignments, lots of unnecessary work, etc. Rough drafts are graded as if they are final drafts. Harsh grader. Overall course load was way too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Teachers pretends to care but actually is quite strict in grading for things shes failed to cover.

DO NOT RECOMMEND. Passive aggressive, rude, unprofessional. She grades harshly and forces you to do tons of long, tedious assignments. Constant peer reviews that aren't particularly helpful, and then SHE leaves comments like "did you even read the assignment?" Grades on attendance even though it's an asynchronous course. Thumbs down.
Her class can be very taxing mentally, the workload is quite heavy as well.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. I signed up for an asynchronous class but had mandatory synchronous zoom sessions where the only thing covered was material we had already read in our asynchronous work. Feedback was one of two paragraphs copied and pasted for all students with no justification for deductions. She ruined what should have been a useful class.

Scary lady with an idc attitude. Her feedback is extremely vague and its like a guessing game trying to figure out what shes referring to. Grading is based off of a generic, vague rubric. Grammar heavy. Did not help improve my writing abilities.

Took it online during the summer. Surprised about all the other ratings because she provided a lot of good (& timely) feedback. She seemed to care about everyone's success and had clear instructions. As long as you complete all parts of the assignments IN DETAIL, you're good. There were 3-4 writing assignments and some small discussion posts

Prof Lalwani is okay. You don't get a lot of useful, timely feedback from her and have to rely on peer feedback for your final drafts. Tough grading on the peer reviews and first drafts, which drags down your grade. I wouldn't recommend her if you have a better choice, but I don't think she's too terrible.

Absolutely awful professor. Posts assignments about 12 hours before they're due and is an extremely tough grader while giving absolutely no constructive feedback for students to improve. She returns feedback on first drafts maybe 6 hours before the final draft is due, so you have virtually no time to edit your final paper. Horrible communicator too
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unprofessional ways to handle conflicts with students. Make sure to rate her accordingly. Halfway through the semester, she will trick to give a good review. At the end of the semester, she will lie about an extra 5 points if 75% complete the survey! Used the 30 min of the last class to force you to fill out the survey with a fake smile. STAY WOKE
Avoid her at all cost!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is an incredibly helpful professor and I owe a lot of my writing abilities to her and her class. Might be a tougher professor but she was always very supportive both inside and outside of the class, and leaves constructive feedback on assignments. She was always open to review assignments and discuss projects outside of class as well.

Disaster. She was teaching communication to a class of analytics grad students with zero clue why that is different from 'finance'. Not once posted lecture notes, graded arbitrarily, provided little constructive feedback, picked specific students to make examples of, spent half the course rambling off topic. Keep the receipt.

While there are short deadlines, the papers are not hard to write and she doesn't expect a lot to receive an A. Read the material and write based off that. One group project that took a lot of effort, make sure you choose a technical topic that your interested in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I dont know what to tell you. She puts assignments up 12 hours before theyre due. Not clear at all. If you take this class and are trying to get an A - you WILL regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: No communication, short deadlines aka less than a day to write 800+ words. Haven't heard back about grades in weeks. Book is required and lectures are based around book material, expects you to cite book in papers due the same day.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This professor seems nice enough outside of class, but she assigns surprise assignments with no warning with maybe 14 hours to complete it. She burns the class out and is unfair with assignments (often worth 0 points). It is not a class for learning, but is about trying to get whatever you can in by a deadline. If you have a choice, don't. (2017)
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very challenging professor. Extremely knowledgeable, but also requires much more than most other ENGL393 professors. Expect to write a ton on short deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: pt2. The exams are difficult, but they are open note, and 100% based on the slides. You can succeed in this class easily if you show up every week to lecture + lab, take notes, start the hw 4 days in early (he usually gives1-2 weeks for each hw), and study 1-3 days before each exam. Can be easy to fall behind in, but just got to lecture n lab :).

He is an old fashioned, straightforward professor and it works GREAT in his favor. The homework (there are 7, and they are the only assignment besides the 2 exams and 1 practical) is based on the slides which are very clear / no fluff. Going to lab nor lecture is mandatory, he instead gives bonus points if you show up! Wants you to succeed :) pt1.

Dr. Zhou is very knowledgable about GIS and clearly enjoys his job. He wants everyone to succeed, but the class does get increasingly difficult as it moves on to more theoretical topics later in the semester. Some of the HW questions were excessively difficult when we hadn't discussed that specific type of question before.

Class is only based on lectures/PowerPoint, 5 hw assignments/1 exam, and questions are sometimes worded weirdly/notclear, ppts can be confusing. Professor Naijum does explain things well through lectures but the labs involving rstudio with a teaching assistant were not watchable. They just copied and pasted things in rstudio without an explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zhou is great, there are some difficulties with taking his class especially with understanding his lectures so make sure you keep up with everything. First exam, make sure to use resources like youtube to understand the content better and second exam is basically everything from the in class questions he does. Easy grader as well.

The hws are weighted more than the exams and they're more difficult. The questions are worded weirdly on both things. The math part of the material can get confusing, but most of it is conceptual. The lectures can be really boring and most people do not attend since the slides are posted. He will go over some of the hw answers in class sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zhou's classes can go by pretty slow, but he spends an extensive amount of time for each topic, so you can really understand each concept. There's not that much course material that you would have to know, and he explains concepts very well. If there are questions on homeworks and labs, he would answer them in class.

I really love taking classes with Dr. Zhou. His classes are hard, but he truly cares about his students and their learning. His homeworks are difficult and require a lot of problem solving along with what you learn in lecture, but it really is the best method to learn. He is really knowledgeable and enthusiastic about his content-DONT SKIP LECTURES

Naijun is very kind and knowledgeable, and gives very manageable homework. The only downside is that lectures can be very boring, and basically everything you need to know comes from lectures. Regardless, the course itself was not at all difficult with him. He does include a generous curve for his course.

He's a really nice professor and is very responsive to his emails. You need to show up to class to understand what is going on. The only grades are the exams but there are a few extra credit pop quizzes throughout the semester to encourage attendance.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Also had Naijun for GEOG306 and GEOG373. He's a very entertaining and interactive lecturer. He obviously cares a lot about his students. All the assignments are fair, although sometimes question wording is slightly unclear. Labs are straightforward for all 3 courses. Homework can be tedious, but never too difficult to figure out.
Tough professor, but I think it's just because of online classes. It's a tough time for both students and professors

Professor Zhou has been great for all three classes Iv'e taken with him. He is incredibly knowledgeable of everything in the geospatial field. He is occasionally hard to understand and if you ask questions you may get a long winded answer that ins't exactly what you asked but he is very flexible and accommodating to students who put in the effort.

Professor Zhou has a lot of experience within the field that is GIS, yet, struggles in effectively communicating course material. Without a textbook for reference, the course material is strictly communicated via slides and his personal annotations. Yet, his annotations are often confusing and cluttered.

zhou is a great professor. even though attendance isnt part of the grade, I would go because he walks through useful examples which are helpful for the exams (all of which are open note, open computer, and noncumulative). I would recommend this professor, he is a funny and cool dude.

No partial credit on tests/quizzes. A lot of questions are vague, especially on the practical. It seems if you don't state the answers from the lecture slides verbatimly, he will just mark it wrong. Back to the practical, just a poor structure of the labs; he needs to have the TAs show the answers to the homework questions/guide on the practical.

I didn't hate his class and I wasn't super in love with it either. After moving to the front to hear better, it was easy to understand his lectures. Does include tidbits written on the board and not done in powerpoint, so it's important to attend class. Labs are spoonfed directions until the practical, which was horrendous. Midterm was super easy.

This man is a God!!!! Professor Zhou knows literally everything there is to know about GIS after being trained from the halls of University Wisconsin-Madison. While other children were playing in sand, Professor Zhou was playing with his atlas. Zhou is like an abstract painting, even though you can't understand him, his teaching is still beautiful.

Overall a decidedly average professor. Lectures are difficult to pay attention to but, he posts his slides on line.  Exams are taken directly from lecture slide so, if you can't pay attention in class, thoroughly reading the slides is a must. He's also very clear about what is expected from you on the exam. Study what he tells you too.

Had him for two classes so far.  Yes the lectures are pretty boring. Fell asleep a lot of times.  But he grades REALLY easy!!! Do not even bother to buy the textbook.  The exams are straight from his lecture slides.  Gives ALOT of partial points.  Even if you answer is wrong, using the correct method will give you FULL points!

Great Prof.  and a nice human being. Has a pretty good grasp of GIS. i owe all my GIS skills to him. Exams straight out of slides. Labs are little difficult but quite doable with a good TA to help you around.

Had him for two classes, and found it extremely hard not to either fall asleep, or catch myself daydreaming. His clarity is the poorest I have every seen at UMD, he expects alot out of his students, and there is ALOT of self teaching. Get a study buddy/group for any of his classes- you will need to spend spmetime outside of class teaching yourself

Professor Zhou is an excellent teacher (and also a cutting-edge GIS scientist).  There were some technical glitches with the labs, but I understand these have now been resolved.  This is not an "easy" class, but the struggle is well worth the knowledge and technical expertise gained.
he is an all right teacher but his test are really off his slides and he grades fairly well if you study. he is not the livelist person but if you do the work and study the slides you should be ok.

The class is seperated into lab and lecture. There is a complete disconnect between them. Ideas could be expressed and comprehension would be better if lecture and lab met. He also fixates on a point to tedium. Chalkboards are this man's Achilles heel.
Go to labs. review power points. ask questions, as much as you want. do well in your lab and u should do well in class overall.

From an academic standpoint point, I liked her neuroscience based courses and she's knowledgeable. However, not the most understanding. I got sick during my fall semester and needed to get a procedure done and provided doctors note for when I missed an exam and I was accused of making up my doctors note. I had to repeat a lot about my situation.
She is very funny and kind. I like her as a professor but I didn't like how the whole course was graded based on only a few things and the tests were harder than average.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The topics covered were interesting and the tests were multiple choice, which were relatively easy if you study. She takes the time to help you if you're struggling and truly cares about your success. She does go on tangents, but that's what I like most about her lectures.

Dr. Navarro is a very knowledgeable professor with passion for neuroscience. Lectures are clear and can sometimes be a lot but studying definitely helps. It is very clear that she cares a lot about student learning and connect material to real world examples and shows helpful videos. Exam material comes straight from the slides! Study the slides!!

Dr. Navarro Cebrian is an excellent professor and truly cares about her students. Lectures are very interesting, and she is great at answering questions in and out of class. Her tests are extremely fair and mostly based on lecture material. Neur200 can be challenging, but Dr. Navarro makes the content as straightforward as it can be.

I was intimidated going into Neur200, but Dr. Navarro made the course understandable. She would often times ask the class if they understood and didn't mind explaining things again. I would be mindful that there is a lot of information that you need to know, mostly all of it in the lectures. Also, your grade mostly comes from four exams.

Dr. Navarro is an incredible professor! She is so kind and caring. The class content is so interesting and she shows very cool videos that relate to what we are learning. Exams, a paper, and discussion posts make up your grade. She is so helpful in office hours! I loved the class so much that I am now a neuroscience major!

I skipped every class and still finished with a B. As long as you study the slides the exams are a breeze. Other than those she has a project that includes a paper and presentation. It really isn't bad considering she gives like 2 months to do each part. Communicate with your group mates, use your time wisely, and you'll be fine.

Professor Navarro is a good professor. Her class is purely lecture-based, with her going over the slides; she will occasionally play a video or two, which could be helpful. There are four exams and one group presentation, and none of the exams are cumulative. The exams are pretty straightforward if you study. Overall 8/10!

Dr. Cebrian is very accomplished and respected, however, I did not like the way she structured the class. It's basically instruction straight from the powerpoints and there's little engagement between her and students outside of class. The TA mainly handled issues regarding grading and clarifying expectations which were not clear from the start.

Passed with a +B. 4 tests(non-cumulative), 1 group paper, 1 PowerPoint presentation. Thats all. Study, it will be needed. Take notes, engage and pay attention. Professor is great. She is very nice and caring. Tries to give students less stress be having less assignments. Very adaptive. Would definitely take again. Do not be intimidated but ready.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Ahmadian was a very good teacher and her grading & assignments were always clear and straightforward. She has a well-organized class structure and Canvas page, however, there are a lot of assignments (around one per class) and attendance is mandatory. She gives textbook readings but they are not necessary for the class (in my opinion).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Ahmadian was incredibly kind and the material was very engaging. The class is heavily discussion based so be prepared to share and talk in a group setting. There is very few tests/projects, but there is a good bit of reading required.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Ahmadian comes off with very high expectations at first but she is ultimately a pretty easy grader as long as you dont stray from the guidelines. She is also kind and accommodating. I wouldn't recommend buying the textbook, each time we use it in class it is on the board, and we do not use the material for homework.

Although she may appear intimidating at first, she isn't that harsh of a grader. As long as you come to every class and finish all of the homework assignments on time, you can get an A. However, be prepared for a lot of writing and papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: Although she seems intimidating at first, she isn't that harsh of a grader. As long as you come to every class and you finish your assignments on time, you can get an A. Just beware of a lot of papers and writing homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Most of class dropped the course by the second class. I should've too. He whispers more quietly than a librarian and mumbles nonstop so good luck understanding what he's saying. Lecture slides are terrible so you're going to waste time by being in class. He speaks about his friends half the time and is extremely test heavy. Run and don't look back.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do anything you can to get out of taking this class. He's one of the worst professors I've had. I simply could not track his lectures, and it was hard to understand the words he spoke. His grading curriculum is set up so that it's impossible to end the class with an A (coming from a Marketing major who predominantly earns A's).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Beware! This class was an absolute joke. Professor Sarna is extremely knowledgeable in the field but entirely incompetent as an undergraduate professor. In one semester we had 6 assignments with no opportunities for extra credit. There were 3 exams weighted 20%+ and the exams covered so much material in very little time. Spare yourself the trouble
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Sarna does not seem super interesting... until you see all of his experience. Look up his LinkedIn. He really knows his stuff, but lectures can be dull. Focus on the three exams and the homework and your grade will be fine. I used the textbook to teach myself the later chapters and found it was just as effective. Overall grade/midterms curved
The lectures WILL drain the life force out of you. They are so boring and barely make sense. Hated this class fr!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most of the grade is exams, with a few projects sprinkled in. Projects look nothing like exams, and there is no homework. This may sound nice, but it means that there is barely any review material for exams. Most people failed the exams simply due to the lack of good review material. Also not a good lecturer, takes way to long on simple stuff

He is very quiet and reserved. He talks in a monotone voice for an hour and 15 minutes every lecture. It is so dry. He comes up with these outlandish analogies that make zero sense. I learned nothing from his class and taught myself everything from the textbook. I stopped going to class around mid-way through the semester. Don't take him if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is just way more difficult than it needs to be. The exams are very dense with content and the final is cumulative. He also doesn't curve grades. Sarna's lectures are dry and the work you have to do outside of class is crazy. I highly recommend choosing another macro professor if you can because achieving success in his class is tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Avoid taking him at all costs. Sarna genuinely doesn't look like he cares about his students. His lectures are entirely unhelpful and the "mock exams" are useless compared to actual exams and only half the questions. He isn't transparent about class grade averages either and doesn't allow us to take exams back to review. And, he DOES NOT CURVE.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
Professor Sarna teaches very little in our lectures, choosing instead to fill time with needlessly complicated analogies and stories. He largely expects us to self learn the class material from the textbook ahead of time. 

Sarna also does not curve, whereas the other econ201 professor curves generously
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's just not a good lecturer: Mumbling like talking to himself, and he explain easy concepts in-depth with unnecessary analogies but glides through the more difficult ones. Makes interesting material EXTREMELY dry. I knew he was boring but still registered bc I liked the topic, now I regret my decision

Sarna really tries to make econ interesting with his lectures. He's hilarious and knowledgeable, and definitely well respected. Exams aren't hard either if you do the practice tests and have solid notes. I hated the asynchronous fashion of the class but he was a good professor overall.
He knows so much about economics and explains main ideas so clearly. Highly recommend!! Also flexible and resourceful as remote

Prof. Sarna is a great professor! Very few homework assignments and no large projects. Manageable amount of reading from the textbook. Seems to want students to succeed considering he regularly offers review sessions before exams. My only complaint is that exams are a little difficult, and lectures are a little repetitive of the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: His lectures are very dry and he makes minimal effort to engage with his students. The material itself is not too difficult, but I had to self-study because he would just read through his slides during class.
He's very nice but the lectures are boring and half of what he says is irrelevant. The tests do not resemble the hw in the slightest and he words test questions really weirdly.

Very VERY boring, I went to class for 4 weeks and started self-studying. Reading the textbook by yourself honestly works a lot better than going to his lecturers. It's hard to understand what he's trying to teach and it WILL confuse you. does not give any extra credit or curve opportunities, doesn't really give a crab about students.

He is an INCREDIBLY nice man. The material isn't that complicated, its all application of what you learn in Principles. The tests are unnecessarily challenging because of the way he words questions. There is a group project in the beginning which he grades very leniently. Go to class bc the slides arent that useful without the lecture content.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Sarna is a very nice guy but not the best teacher. He just goes off of slides that he posts online so lectures arent mandatory. He is always open to answer questions but he is also terrible with technology. Tests make up a huge part of your grade so study hard for them.

Awesome class! But you need to participate in class discussions. A must take if you are looking for a job or have an interview and economics is important to you. You learn hands down the impact of the economic policies using a policy simulation exercise. Overall, an A Plus class!!

Uch, DO NOT TAKE, ESPECIALLY IF YOU ARE AN EXPERIENCED ECON MAJOR. He words questions horribly and confusingly on tests so if you have no background then you can just memorize what he tells you but if you know about economics then he is just confusing. He asks general questions and then there is a lot of awkward silence. TERRIBLE
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Multiple times I was falling asleep in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Awesome class lectures. You need to attend all class to get a good grade. I learnt a lot in this class. I would highly recommend the class. Prof. Sarna is hilarious and makes the class very interesting and motivates students to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's a caring and good guy, but for me, was extremely boring. This is the only class where I debate going or not just cause I get so bored and hardly learn anything. If you take him, I'm sorry to say you're better off learning with the textbook.
worst professor I have ever had. would not take him, his class is unorganized and hard to follow. do not take. his TA's do more work then he does.

Good professor. Exams come straight from the test bank of the two required textbooks. The other assignments are a joke because there was little to no variance in the grades, so even if you crush the presentation/paper, you'll only get a few points higher than someone who spends an hour or two on it.

Dr. Sarna is a good professor. His lectures are powerpoint heavy and he often just reads them. Doing practice exams is essential. Also aiming for a 100% on ur hw grade will help boost your grade. Start the HW early. TAs are either helpful or wildly unhelpful. Exams are all multiple choice so test taking skills apply. I liked the course overall.

Sarna is a very nice person, but when it comes down to his lectures, he's definitely not the best. He doesn't answer emails. This was my lowest grade because the final screwed everyone over. He is definitely the better choice to take if you have to take econ though.
Prof makes it so easy to understand the complex concepts. He is also a very kind and lighthearted person who manages to make class engaging with his fun examples. Pay attention and study!
I don't think I've learned anything in this class; he's a really nice guy but a terrible teacher. He spends most of the class talking in nonsense metaphors and I'll be lucky if I pass this class.
Koofers is key, naveen is sly but has a good heart and wants students to get good grades

You don't even need to go to this class to get an A or a B. He repeats questions from old exams so if you can find those that is helpful. Theres 7 homework assignments throughout the semester that don't take too long but he drops 2 so there's very little homework.

Good guy and respectful. Only complaint is how he's not clear at narrowing down what you need to know, you have to poke around the textbook a lot on your own. A HUGE help would be if he'd post multiple practice exams with answers instead of only one per exam that's only half the length. Micro was a cakewalk for me and I found myself struggling here
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I am so grateful that I had professor Sarna for macro. He makes it so easy to understand the complex concepts. He is also a very kind and lighthearted person who manages to make class engaging with his fun examples. Homework problems were significantly different from test problems, but tests were very straightforward. Pay attention and study!

Professor Sarna was very helpful for students. He made sure to explain everything clearly and in simple terms. He was always available for any questions or just to talk after class and during office hours. Tests were very straightforward and easy, only multiple choice.

Professor Sarna is a very nice man, which a decent sense of humor and a huge passion for Economics. This isn't a history class, this is basically an expansion of what you learned in your beginner Econs. I thought tests were hard. His graphs he draws aren't very well explained. Don't buy the textbook. No one used it in the whole class.

Naveen is such a sweety. For me, ECON201 was very difficult but he makes sure to do all that he can to make things clear and help you out. He even incentivized a test. If you got a 100 he bought you starbucks. He's a nice man who has funny stories and really makes sure to be there for his students.

Sarna was great. He explains concepts very well and loves having a constructive dialogue with students. He has a lot of real world knowledge from his time at the World Bank, and a pretty good sense of humor. I would definitely recommend taking him

This guy is great. He is friendly Indian man who genuinely cares about the subject. He posts all of his powerpoints online so missing class is not ever an issue. Occasional problem sets due, but lowest 2 grades are dropped. Great teacher.

Great class and the best prof. I have had on campus. You will learn a lot of real life economics.  Take it  - if you can.  The class has more students on waitlist than enrolled in the class.  I loved the class and the teacher.

At first, I was really his teaching style. But then I noticed that he raises his voice at the students. I find this unacceptable. I was probably not the only one afraid to answer a question in class and be wrong. He comes off too strong and that creates tension in class. BUT I think the content of the class will help us in our future careers.
