Very good professor. The class can get a little boring, but try to go if you struggle with the concepts. A lot of the stuff came easy to me, so the quizzes and tests were just basic economics to me. The final presentation is a grade booster. My group started two days before it was due and we got an A. Just work hard on it and you'll be fine.

Dr. Sarna is a great prof! He explains the material very clearly and will not move on until majority of the class understands the topic. Requirements for this class are 7 online hw's (drops two), 2 exams, and a final. Prof Sarna does not curve but it is very easy to get an A in his class!
He's the man.  Knows his stuff and has interest in YOUR learning it.  Friendly, and yes, he's Mexican--but there is no real language barrier if you listen to him!
Excellent lecturer. really knows his stuff. Always helpful.

Good: friendly professor, knowledgeable but like most physicists/mathematicians, cannot convey his knowledge very well. Had helpful homework sessions 3+ times a week. Bad: quirky, language barrier, spends a lot of time going over proofs and not figuing out how to solve general physics problems. Textbook is NOT helpful at all-- it is expensive.

Something must have happened in the last few years because every review on this site seems extremely out of date. She is ornery, and extremely uptight about everything. Her lectures are mandatory but completely devoid of any useful information. Complete waste of time, where she spends every class reading off of slides, never leaving her chair.

Professor O'Neill was one of the best professors I have ever had. Here grading criteria are clear. She gives great feedback on your work that can help you improve your writing. She is also a very fair grader and will give you as much credit as possible for the work that you have done. I highly recommend taking any English class with her.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Gave lots of feedback on assignments but grading criteria was not always clear. Very generous with extensions and grades. Had some technical issues with being online. Assignment directions were sometimes very in depth and sometimes almost non-existent. Sometimes responded to emails quickly and sometimes not at all. Lots of writing, so stay ahead!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is very understanding that her students are STEM majors with heavy class loads and will give extensions. Her directions for assignments are clear and complete making it easy to know exactly how to approach each one. Her feedback is also very helpful, make the corrections she gives and you get an A. She can be slow to post assignments to ELMS
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. ONeill provides so much knowledge and insight into the world of science writing. It is clear that she has a lot of experience in this field and the things that I learned over this semester will be extremely useful going forward. While Dr. ONeill might seem mean at first she is actually very helpful, understanding, and caring! Would take again
Legitimately told me "I don't like the way you write I will never give you higher than a C". That should say it all. Take romantic lit with another professor if you can to save the headache.

Don't listen to the 2 bad reviews. Very engaging and interesting lectures. If you pay attention in class and take notes you will pretty easily pass but, definitely have to actually put in work for an A. A lot of reading but, final really wasn't bad. Took 319C.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Lots of reading. Very good discussions. Fun if interested in character dissection, philosophy, and incorporating the insights you learned to your real life. The class was more like a discussion room. I learned a lot about myself through other characters from the texts.

This comments post isn't long enough to tell how bad he is.  Suffice it to say I will never take one of his classes again if I can help it.  Absolutely awful!  PS- this is coming from someone with a 4.0 gpa (prior to this semester), not some slacker who doesn't want to work.

This class could be interesting, but in order to get a good grade, you have to reiterate everything he says in class on the exam. It is all about how he interprets it, and there is no room to argue or even suggest your opinion on a certain text or poem. You can pass the class if he like the way you write and if you memorize what he says in class.
He was totally rude and sarcastic. He was uncaring when I was sick and showed no sympathy for missed work. I would not suggest him.

I was in a car accident and was in the hospital for two weeks. Prof. Wang was completely uncaring, and insisted I make up all the work, even though I asked for an incomplete. He's also fond of picking pets in the class, who can get away with anything, while the other students have to mimic everything he says in order to get passing grades.

This class entirely depends on how hard you work. Make friends in the lab so you can work together on them because they're very tricky sometimes. However the quizzes aren't even that bad, the professor almost always tells you what will be on the quiz about a week before. Just make sure you do really good on the first 2 or 3
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Lab assignments/modules are easy to complete so long as you have understanding and practice for the programming. Quizzes, on the other hand, is another matter. The quizzes are based on topics we barely cover during lecture, and then we're expected to complete in less than an hour. It really stressed me out and killed my A for the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class was interesting at first, seeing as though the labs and practice modules were easy to complete. However, when the professor brought programming quizzes to this class, my grade had suffered due to how difficult the quizzes were in terms of coding and time limit. You do bad on one quiz, and it ruins your overall grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: At the start of the semester, this class was pretty easy. The only things I had to focus on were lab assignments and modules. Then, during the middle of the semester, the professor decides to do quizzes that are not multiple choice but instead programming. There are only 5 quizzes, yet they killed my grade since they focus on the harder topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm writing this review as an MS-1 because this was the only class out of all my undergrad courses with exams that actually resembled the ones I take now. Take her class - it will help you get into the habit of thinking like a clinician. And remember you can do it!! just keep going :)

She has a thick accent and goes fast but you learn to understand it after a while. Slides are a mess often but include everything you need to know for exam. I highly recommend GSS but this class requires a lot of self studying because of so much content. Put in the work and you'll do good in her class. Also final isn't cumulative.

talked at the speed of light. wants you to write exactly how she words it from her lectures and will not give you credit if you paraphrase but are still correct. wants it her words only. TAs are strict as hell. Avoid if you can is not worth it. she is fashionable tho
Her tests were very difficult and her PowerPoints were very messy and unorganized. I would recommend taking any other prof.

Do your research before going into this class with her. It is not worth the trouble. There are lot of other professors who teach the class better than Opoku where you can learn better as well. Opoku is hectic and would make an Ok masters/ phd advisor but a terrible undergrad professor. 

You have been warned. Rest is on you.

She is impossible. DO NOT take her. Her lectures are unorganized, fast, and a mess. Her TA took the class with other professors and often contradict what she says in her lectures. Half the time spend is trying to figure out what she said is correct. She is not approachable outside of class. Please do not take her. You have been warned.

Dr. Opoku has a PhD in Physiology and is the most apt to teach anything anatomy, physiology and endocrinology related out of all the BSCI professors. Her extreme mastery of the subject matter is impressive and made even the most difficult concepts look simple as long as one was ready to memorize and put in the hard work.

Absolutely avoid taking a class with this professor. She is out of touch with those students experiencing the topic for the first time, using a litany of acronyms every chance she got. Add this to her extremely difficult exams (only grades you receive) which are primarily differential diagnosis questions more akin to step1 than undergrad. Avoid her

Pay attention to her examples of test questions because they will be on the test, but try to take a diff prof

She is also really rude when emailing .

reviews.comment: Opoku is really knowledgeable and a great professor for BSCI201. Some tips for this class: write everything she writes on her notes sheet, do the study guides before each test, go to GSS, and study a bit every single day.

reviews.comment: She's taught this class for 20+ years and it shows! You have to put in the work, but you'll reap what you sow. Take good notes and go to lecture, because most of her tests are straight from the notes. Don't be afraid to go to office hours. She's very funny and a fantastic anatomy professor. Will miss her.

reviews.comment: had her in the summer.  she needs to spend less time playing dress up and more time showing up to class.  she showed up late to EVERY class and just randomly canceled other classes. then she wanted everyone to stay 10 minutes later for every class, because she canceled class.

Greatest anatomy teacher at UMD. I would highly recommend taking her. The class is hard but it will be anywhere you take it. She really knows her stuff, I would take another class with her in a heartbeat.

Professor Ratnapala is the worst art teacher at UMD. He is exhasutingly slow and incompetent. Dont take this class unless you have to and even then try and see if you can get out of it.

This guy looks like he hates his life. Plays favorites. Gives the worst critiques I've ever seen. reviews.comment: Nare is Nare, he's nice if you approach him with an open mind and attitude. Attendance is not mandatory for an A but if you want to learn and perfect your skills then you must link with people both in and out. Overall good professor.

Very intelligent, clear, and fair professor, sincerely the art department doesn't have good/ quality professors but he's one of the few exceptions. I took his class during the winter session, it was a bit quick, but the assignments were clear and very useful in and outside class. I got to make a movie and print a catalog of my artwork!
Very helpful.  Learned a lot.  Good class to take.

This class does require a lot of work outside of class. A lot of students were intimidated after the first day of class and my class shrunk by 1/3.  However, if you stick with it and turn in all your assignments on time, you'll be fine. He's a great professor with a witty sense of humor. It was a fun class and I learned a lot.
he's cool
Students are lucky to get this guy.  If they're willing to work hard as responsible adults, they will benefit greatly from his tutorship.
If you fall asleep during class or don't pay attention he will not make you feel bad at all!  He will simply teach you what you missed without any guilt trip!

as long as you get your stuff turned in on time, nare lets you re-sumbit your work so you can get a better grade if needed. just do all the assignements and you'll get an A or B. hes got great sense of humor.

it's a hard class with lots of work outside of class. but you also learn alot through that process. he works you hard but it's still a good class that i'd recommend

one of the most helpful graphic design classes I have ever taken.  if you care about the class you will get so much out of it.  He is not a creative designer, but helps you learn the programs and build on your creativity.  A must take class

Nare is a good person, but should not be allowed to teach.  He assigns too much work that needs to be done outside of class, costs money, and involves driving/other logistics.  His perennial TA, Irem is useless.

Really great professor who actually understands how to format content for students to digest. Her lectures are incredibly helpful for studying, so you know what tests will actually be on. She has field trips and is just all-around a really nice person who is sociable with the class. Wish she taught more variety so other students got to have her.

Love love love Dr. Burk, I can never say enough good things about her!! This class is more difficult in technicalities because it's an advanced elective, but her tests are not as daunting as they seem!! Just be prepared to spend some time outside of class to study and memorize some things. Lots of extra credit opportunities!

By far one of my favorite professors at UMD. Dr. Burk is a great lecturer and is very lenient when it comes to grading and assignments. However, this class is not an easy A. You will need to put in the effort, but once you study and attend lectures, everything is relatively smooth sailing. Offers extra credit assignments. Would 100% take again.
Dr. Burk is great! This class is easy enough if you study, but it certainly is not an easy A! You need to know your stuff for the exams and lab practical. Do not assume it will be easy.

Dr. Burk is the best professor in the Animal Science department at UMD. I had to reflect on how amazing of a teacher Dr. Burk was- she is incredibly smart about everything related to horses and has a thoughtful answer for any question. She is so humble and will go above and beyond to help students succeed. Take any/all of her classes!!
Absolutely one of the best professors I have ever had.

As an abroad exchange i was worried that i'd struggle but it was super fun, she was amazing at teaching and labs were very fun. tests were full of material and too short on time. this is not an easy A but a very interesting class with a great lab. gained a lot and have endless respect for her- always with a smile and an expert at what she does.
She has realistic expectations and makes the material easy to understand. The lab is super fun but you still learn a ton.

Great class, very interesting and enjoyable. It could be challenging for people who expect it to be easy but if you put in the expected effort, it's easy to do well. Dr. Burk is a great professor and very engaged with her students.

Great teacher! Really knows her stuff and is passionate about what she teaches.  Be careful with tests as she is extremely picky and wants you to literally write down every detail for the essays and short answers.  do that work and you can't fail.

Dr. Burk's exams are fair.  There was only a slight curve because exam averages were in the low 80s or high 70s.  She can be forgetful and easily distracted from the main point of her lectures.  Attendence in lecture is not mandatory and she posts the lecture notes.

One of the worst professors there is on zoom. She waits until the last week of the semester to grade anything. Gives out 0/10 if you don't make her editor of your google doc. Makes you do group projects on zoom even though it is 10x harder because it is an online class. Always has an attitude when you bring up something she did wrong.

I don't understand how this person is still employed at this university. She is unprepared, unorganized, lazy, rude, and condescending. She has students lead discussions. She doesn't teach. She sits there and belittles her students and adds nothing productive to the conversation. Assignments are vague and changing. She is not approachable at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Get ready to read 70+ pages a day apart and write reflections. You have to have your camera on and participate; she's horrible at giving feedback it's like she doesn't read or listen to your work before she criticizes every piece. The moral of the story is don't take this class, not with her, at least :)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Poorly communicates and is often condescending when asked a question. Few opportunities to improve your grade since little feedback is provided and no clear guidelines are set. Syllabus and schedule constantly change and class structure is disorganized. She sometimes makes an effort to engage students, but for the most part is unapproachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Osuji is nice and definitely means well, but the weekly coursework was a little much. Two readings a week that are over 20-30+ pages and two paragraph reflections due after every reading that are only worth one point was a lot. The turnaround time for each reading/reflection is also very quick for the amount of reading required.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: try and avoid her. we learn the same thing in different fonts every lecture. very disorganized and never grades anything on time. she's literally confused herself and the course is just all over the place. she also assigned 25+ papers 2 times a week all for a paper that is worth one point ??? didn't enjoy the course.

I loved her! There's a different reading for each class - some harder than others - but very interesting. There's a response for each reading so twice a week, but just 500 words and very casual, only worth 1 point each. Two group projects but they're not bad. She cares about what she's teaching and what you have to say. 10/10 would take again.

Professor Olmert was my advisor for my Honor's project. When I sent him drafts of my play, he wouldn't give me advice. He would not meet with me, and when we did schedule meetings, he was often times late (once by four hours). On the day of the defense, he told me I "f*cked up" my project, which was entirely disrespectful and inappropriate.

Olmert knows so much about the film industry. Brought the director of a film MFA program to class. Hears student input on class material. Overall, you take him to learn more about the world. No matter the material, Olmert teaches you how to be a better human. He made me love learning again. Great guy. Great professor. Amazing person.

The class itself was pretty straightforward with a few essays and quizzes on the material. The professor didn't use ELMS but used Facebook instead, which made it hard to see what grades I had in the class. I just found him disorganized and annoying because he would curse loudly in class and go on a ramble. Would not take this class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment:
I took four classes with Olmert. If you're passionate about learning and show up outside class to let him know that you care, then he's really easy. He gives tons of extensions and grades really leniently. (Final grades are usually better than the sum of your test scores.)
He's very dis-organized and chaotic which is fun for spontaneous students.

I took Dr.Olmert's Engl 379T class in the spring of 2020. I can't believe he doesn't have a 5/5 rating. He has so much wisdom and stories about pretty much everything. I love his style of having a community on Facebook where his past and present students can interact. Take any of his classes. You will gain a lifelong valuable connection.

I took 454 during COVID and I LOVED him, 1 of my favorite profs. Cares about students, what they're going through and how they want to learn, and while he is disorganized, you will not be penalized for it. His teaching style is so unique (a little all over the place) but he's so passionate, making it fun to listen to (could say more, out of space)
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Olmert is wonderful! I learned a lot about plays in this class, like how they use characters and themes and oppositions to make their points, as well as how they tie into cultural and historical movements. But Olmert also taught us a lot about the human aspects of plays. All of this really impacted me academically and personally as well.

Olmert is one of the best English professors ive had the pleasure of taking a class with at UMD. I went into the class expecting to dislike it as I had never considered myself a huge fan of drama and plays, but found a new appreciation that I will carry on. 10/10 Would recommend his class.

Absolutely amazing professor. Super interesting and insightful. really pushes you to do more with your life and take more risks. if you show initiative he'll set you up with opportunities to succeed. has lots of great connections! grading is kind of unclear, but not unfair. Doesn't give anyone a bad grade unless they genuinely don't care.

Olmert is undoubtedly amazing if you know how to finesse a class. He is unorganized, but is so knowledgable if you can follow his lectures. He is VERY passionate about the books he'll have you read in class and as long as you love the books and show interest in them, easy peasy!

Dr. Olmert is the best professor I've ever had. He's not very organized, so that might be hard for some people, but if you can get passed that, he's a brilliant and very kind man. I want to take every class I can with him. I learned more from him than I did from all my other professors combined, and he genuniely cares about all of his students.

I took a study abroad course with this professor in London a few years back. It was a horrible experience. He has quite a temper and lost it quite a bit over the course of the three-week course. He seriously got into it with one of the students and they actually left to go home early because of it. Arrogant and inappropriate. Don't recommend.

Professor Olmert is amazing.  I was in two of his classes twenty years ago, and I still remember things he's pointed out.  It's true his classes are not for sleeping through, but totally worth it.  Changed my life for the better.
Do the work and show up to class. Take good notes, as exams will have questions on things he mentioned once in passing. Definitely an interesting experience, class was never boring!

Honestly the smartest teacher I've ever had the pleasure to know. His lectures can be hard to follow but if you're into this type of stuff (aka English) any class he teaches is more than worth the work you need to put into it.

One of the most brilliant professors you will see at this University. His classes can be rigorous if you're expecting a typical linear lecture style. I would say attending class is mandatory. The man is an encyclopedia and you will learn so much just listening to his tangents. Do the work and this professor will make you a lifelong learner
The BEST

Loved his class! And so does he, drama is his passion. You really have to do the reading but if you do the work and really engage in class he'll cut you slack on deadlines and assignments. I took this class 5 years ago and I still remember what I learned.
He's honestly a genius. He's not easy, but if you just sit there and absorb everything he says you'll be thankful.

He is one of the worst English professors I have ever had, and I love English. He makes you buy $200 worth of books and barely touches on them.  His lectures are unorganized and involve him randomly cursing and throwing random facts at you.  He is very intelligent, but his teaching style and the class is just horrendous.

If you live and breathe theatre, then you will be likely to love Prof. Olmert's classes. But if you just have a healthy yet casual interest in theatre and thought ENGL244 would be a nice CORE class, please do yourself a favor and think again. Olmert's lectures are unorganized and arrogant, and he expects you to memorize EVERY random thing he says.

Hard to describe his class, it's not typical. He's a very interesting, brilliant guy. A shameless anglophile-he'll teach you a lot about British language and culture, whatever class you take from him. You either like him or you don't. If you do, you wind up taking him over and over again and get easy A's (you just have to get through the 1st time).
This professor quite literally changed my life.  I never really looked at anything the same again after spending time in his class.  He even made Shakespeare fun...

Dr. Olmert is an AMAZING professor.  He is extremely knowledgeable and makes lecture fun and interesting.  His quizzes require some studying and the books he picks are far from boring.  The only problem is his lack of structure - no schedule of syllabus and sometimes random rants.  But definitely worth it!
No Comments

Olmert is funny and a down to Earth kind of guy. He knows a lot and wants to share everything he knows with his students. Unfortunately, this makes his classes a bit confusing because he lectures on topics that are all over the place. But if you show up to class, take decent notes, and have a good TA then it's actually a rewarding experience
Lectures are all over the place, and you have to go to lecture becuase his exams are drawn right from the notes.  The novels are pretty good, if you do the work, this class is pretty fun.

Personally, I enjoyed this class.  Olmert is smart and clever.  He jumps around when lecturing but is full of information.  Makes class fun and interesting.  Take good notes though, exams are all from lecture notes.
He never stayed on one topic for longer than a minute and my notes were all over the place. Exams based purely on the ridiculous things he found important during his ramblings. Chaos

I hate English classes, but Olmert made class interesting and hilarious. He can make a topic interesting for anyone. He's very knowlegeable about both English and facts in general. He is great but the class is not very easy. He is a little intimadating, but is willing to talk to you. I would say he is worth it!
Olmert is the most interesting, fun professor ever. Everyone should take his Shakespear classes. I loved this professor.

He talks, you listen. No structure. A complete waste of your time.
Great guy, very easygoing
If Jesus Christ taught a class, it wouldnt have a damn thing on Olmert's lectures. Olmert is my favorite professor to the max.

no class discussion, only he talks, and only HIS opinions matter.  If you like a very unstructured learning envriroment, then GREAT... but if you like syallibi, then forget it!  VERY pertentious, emails resume to class... if you are a theater major, you will like this class, otherwise you wont.

Dr. Olmert is an amazing professor.  He knows more about every subject than any other professor I have ever had.  I took three of his Shakespeare courses because I just could not get enough of his teaching.  I definitely would recommend him!
He's a walking encyclopedia on british history and things related.. A definite must take.
Olmert is by far the best professor you will ever have- and probably the smartest man you'll ever meet.

WORST CALC TEACHER EVER! How is he still employed? He's rude, he doesn't know how to teach, and isn't understanding of people's situations at all. IF YOU WANNA GET AN A, IT'S ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE WITH HIS CLASS. good luck.

A bad person and worse professor. Tim rarely went into great detail in lectures, expecting text to be the main resource to consult. In exams Tim was without hyperbole, abusive. Yelling at students, just being needlessly rude. For a mandatory course, Tim made it unbearable. I withdrew as I don't intend to receive a poor grade from a poor professor.

I'm horrified, my 1st exam:
1. Never put up a timer, which he promised
2. Raised his voice, "You're not in kindergarten anymore."
3. W/h 3 min left, he raised his voice again to clean up 
4. Said "he doesn't understand why we don't listen." The room was quiet & everyone was listening 

The average was 50.3% for an ELEMENTARY Calc Exam.

If I could rate him a 0, I would. He doesn't teach the material and often goes on unrelated rants. He's rude and yells frequently, even during tests, making it hard to focus. He gets mad when students ask questions, which makes it harder to learn. This is a required course, and he's the one making it far more difficult than it needs to be.

In my entire life of education at any given institution I have never had a MATH teacher or professor use a powerpoint to “teach”. Whether you go to the lectures or just use the online lectures, all he does is talk through a powerpoint. In the discussion sections the TA's are also told to not help us. This class feels like a trap, avoid at all costs

reviews.comment: Didn't go to lectures and still passed. Just because I had to teach myself everything since I failed the first two exams when I tried GOING to all of his lectures. he's horrible at lecturing and just goes based on his own slides. I only passed because I had to teach myself EVERYTHING. And who tells his students to spend 5 hours on homework??

He wasn't that bad. I failed because of my own problems. He def wasn't the best lecturer but the TA I had was really good. Pilachowski was ok, he talked a lot about road laws for some reason. A lot of people don't like him tho.

It was quite difficult to sit through his lectures, which is why I appreciated the fact that in person attendance was not mandatory so long as you watch his online videos. Reads off the slides and is quite passive-agressive. If you have a background in Calc already, you'll be fine, otherwise, steer clear.

If you want to keep your sanity STAY AWAY FROM PILACHOWSKI! I took calc in highschool thinking this class would be an easy A, I was wrong. His exams were extremely difficult and had nothing to do with the homeworks or lectures. Be ready for lots of word problems. If you were like me and had/has to endure this pain I wish you great luck.

if you don't know calc coming into this course STAY AWAY. lectures are not helpful, exams are difficult, and are often on content not covered in class. The majority of my learning was teaching this material to myself and using the textbook and homework. his TA is also awful and can't explain anything. he also gets mean and yells at students 0/5

He was one of the worst math teacher I have had. Do not take his class. all he does is read off the slide. also he thinks everyone has taken the same math class and remembers everything from high school. He dosnt explain what his is doing well. Also he give 3 HW a week that take each a hour.

Pilachowski's lectures can be dry, but his online videos are super helpful. The exams are tricky, so do the practice worksheets and try Unstuck study for study prep. Overall, a solid professor if you're willing to put in the work.

Professor Pilachowski is just fine. Not my first choice to take again, but not worth upending my schedule to avoid. His lectures are easy enough to follow, but don't skip them. Absolutely go to discussion. Decent professor overall.

DO NOT TAKE HIM. I studied nearly 6 hours daily for his class and still ended up failing. He does NOT teach any content, he significantly lacks understanding when it comes to personal matters. He assigns WAY too much online homework. Like 3-4 assignments per week that took me 1-2 hours each to complete, not including studying. Do. Not. take. Him.

DO NOT CHOOSE TIM AS A PROFESSOR. YOU WILL FAIL THIS CLASS!! All he does is read from the slides and expects you to understand. Also if you've never taken a Calc class before this you will struggle a lot.

PLEASE do not take Tim. He does not lecture, he just reads off of slides, and if you are anything like me, you learn math better when math is actually performed during the lecture instead of an audiobook of the textbook. He is also not logical at all when it comes to grading matters and excused absences.

Tim wastes a lot of time during lectures talking about himself and how much he hates VEO scooters. He expects everyone to know everything and makes the homework 10 times harder than what he "teaches" in class. For his review sessions, he tells us to work with someone next to us and doesn't actually show us how to do the problems. Avoid him.

He basically wants you to know everything before hand and expects you to understand the material after only a few steps. He wastes a lot of time in lectures talking about his personal life and refuses to make up for it. He gives the most basic examples during lecture and then the homework looks nothing like what was taught. Avoid him if you can.

Known for being a horrible teacher. Whenever an older student hears that I have him, they just laugh and tell me good luck. If you are reading this before signing up for his class, don't ever. If you can change it still, do. I already took calculus once (not at UMD), and his teaching style still made this hard for me.

reviews.comment: he gives out a lot of homework and makes you do the homework for future lessons before he teaches them in the lectures.. ??

Do. Not. Take. This. Class. The class is badly organized with unclear examples in lecture, and the lectures contain way too much information for an hour 15. TA isn't helpful at all, although he tries really hard to be. Paglione might be great for upper level PHYS classes.
We have to read a ton of a book for the class, but its not insane as long as you pace yourself. A good class, a pretty good teacher so far I'll update later if things change.

Tough homework, tough exams (despite their nice font). The class examples don't help with the homework, and the prof cannot handle tough questions during class. Professor is funny and relates to students. Basically, I didn't get the grade I wanted because the atmosphere was relaxed to the point that I thought I was doing fine. Indifferent, bad TA.
Great designer and teacher
just a boring professor

This is probably my favorite class. Professor Quiros is a really cool guy, and it seems like he's a really good architect (google him). He wants everyone in the class to act like professional adults, which is a very good thing. GO TO LECTURES. The class is really interesting if it's your thing, and you can get a 100% if you love it. I did.

Qu is very disorganized making the TAs very disorganized. Avoid at all costs. If you didnt take enee140 get ready for hell first few weeks because nobody is going to explain the unix system to you. My TA absolutely sucked his grading was mych harder than the other TAs. His midterms 2 are bs

Do not take Qu! I had issues with my TA especially with his grading compared to the other TAs and Qu was no help. He rarely if ever responds to emails. His accent is hard to understand and his instructions are not very clear. Most of the time he will give the ruberic to the TAs after the assignmnet so grading is wack

Dr. Gang Qu is a reasonably nice man, however, his class structure for ENEE150 is horrible. It focuses on 3 large projects throughout the semester, and very little on deep understanding of how to code, and how to code well. He is very disorganized, takes ages to send TAs rubrics, and contradicts himself in assignments constantly.

Dr. Qu does not pace the class well, so you're left with a lot of very hard content crammed at the end. It is almost impossible to keep up with the class, and as a result of his time management, he is unable to take questions on the most difficult material. The only redeeming qualities are that he recorded the lectures and dropped the lowest exam.

Prof. Gang Qus English proficiency is poor. Due to his weakness in English, he just reads from slides during lectures. But his slides are filled with grammar and spelling mistakes. On top of that, his accent is hard to understand. The biggest problem is, the question papers he prepares are hard to understand due to his poor usage of English.
Probably one of the worst professors at UMD. Posts final grades over one month after the semester ends. Writes the most ridiculous midterms and finals that are unrelated to what were doing in class.

Professor Qu defines a new level of atrocious. His midterm and final are ridiculously hard because they are irrelevant to what he covers in lecture. He posts projects late, so we only got 5 days to do projects the syllabus says we were supposed to get 3-4 weeks for. The concepts are easy, but Professor Qu's disorganization makes the course harder.

Nice guy, terrible teacher. The guy shows no care or concern if his students understand the content that he teaches. He teaches his material at his own fast pace and forces self study at home. The exams are extremely hard and the averages are always really low. Unlike other teachers, he does not offer any online resources.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The sole reason why I might not make the engineering school. One problem is that class after class I sit and have to see him go through topics at his own pace without explaining them very well. The biggest problem would have to be the exams, however. Exam averages are around 60% and often contain questions we were never taught how to do.

Professor is usually nice, but doesn't teach very well. Lectures are often hard to follow. The tests are curved and grading is 'lenient' (however exam average still high 60s post curve). Tests are more difficult than what was taught. He once changed exam questions midway through since he made them the day before. Take another professor.

Avoid this professor if you value your GPA. He is very rigid and unwilling to meet students halfway, even with exam averages as low as 60%. You are essentially expected to be an expert on the material the moment you walk in. To pass you need to spend every min to studying bc the lectures don't prepare you for the difficulty of the exams.

Didn't prepare us well for exams, every exam had a class average of 60-65%. Problems in class were 1-2 steps, exams were 3-5 steps and rarely did previous semester exams prepare you well for exams. Heard O'Brien was just as difficult, so prepare yourself.
horrible teacher. exam average is 60%

Prof Padhi made finance tolerable. He came in every day with a smile on his face and gives multiple opportunities to get extra credit. You can even have a notes sheet on all exams. Every time I went to a lecture, I felt I learned something from it.

I cannot recommend Dr. Padhi enough. One of my favorite professors I've ever had at UMD. If you're going to take 340 I would definitely take it with Pahdi. His passion for finance is evident in his lectures and he is always willing to try to explain a topic in a different way if it wasn't clear the first time. Love him!

Padhi is a pretty good professor. The in-class worksheets/problems are helpful. Participation is graded on accuracy but if you come to class to do the problems he/TAs will explain them. Video lectures and unnecessarily long and confusing but you have to watch them to do the quizzes. Exams are very difficult so you need to study a lot to do well.

BMGT340 is a pretty difficult class but he clearly tries to make it as accessible as possible. He's also super friendly and clearly loves what he teaches. I usually hate flipped classrooms but he does it really well and I feel like I get a lot out of each class given that you have to complete and submit practice problems throughout each class.

Dr. Padhi was an amazing professor for BMGT340. I took him over the summer and even though the work load was about 25-30 hours per week, you can get a B+ to an A if you grind and put in the time to do all of the work. The tests were open notes but were still challenging. He very accessible outside of class and is one of the best professors @ Smith!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Padhi is a good professor. He knows the content well, and the course is pretty straightforward as long as you apply yourself. He has a dry sense of humor that I found pretty funny. Padhi gives you a ton of materials to study, so as long as you prepare for the exams it is pretty easy to get a high grade in the course.

Taking BMGT340 with Padhi was great. He gives his students the resources needed to succeed in an already hard class to take at the B-School. He gives out note outlines to fill out in class (which are a great help for exams) and is great at explaining tough concepts. Take Padhi!

Great Professor for a fairly difficult topic to learn. He is very good at teaching difficult concepts step by step and made online classes fun. He really cares and does a great job. You have to put in the work but if you do, youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: 100% take Padhi over Hallows. He gives you the materials to be successful in a very challenging class. Always respectful to students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The professor is a nice person. Very helpful in office hours. His teaching style is decent, practice questions in class are easier than on exams. The concepts are challenging but provides a lot of resources to study and TA are always willing to help out! Nice person, hard class .
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Took him for BMGT 340 as well. A really smart and caring prof. Knows his stuff well and will spend time with you if you have any questions (even questions about current events). Class is hard in the sense that it is math heavy but he goes over all the important formulas before any exam and provides enough practice exams to ace the exams. best @ UMD

This class is extremely hard but padhi encourages you to asks questions and genuinely seems like he wants everyone to do well. The tests are very hard and more difficult than class examples so prepare for them as much as you can. Before all the extra credit was graded I had a grade of a B- and I ended with an A- so DO ALL THE EXTRA CREDIT!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Padhi is a nice professor. He gives a lot of homework, so be ready to spend a long time studying for this class! His tests are challenging but if you work hard, you will definitely pass. The quizzes have 2 attempts so its very nice. There are also a few extra credits throughout the semester that allows you to improve your grade too!

Cannot stress enough that I hate this guy. Teaches the equivalent of 1+1 in class then on the tests you need to know high level calculus and use formulas they don't give you. Artificially makes the tests harder by adding useless information. This class isn't even about finance, it's about trying to understand what the test questions are asking for

Cannot stress enough how terrible this class is. The fact that the business school still lets them teach this class is absurd considering how many complaints they must get every semester. You have to learn on your own because class time is dedicated to easy problems and the HW is all hard. If Hallows or Padhi sees this just know you are the worst.
Absolute nightmare of a class. You might as well teach yourself because he won't be able to. Will need to do a lot of extra learning by yourself to just make it by.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He is not a good teacher, he acts as if he cares. Does not make time to help you succeed. And my grade is a reflection of his teaching. FiND another university to take this course. You are NOT required to take it AT UMD. TRUST ME.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a good lecturer, and way better than Hallows. The problem with the class is that you learn how to do problems in class, in HWs and Quizzes, but then on the test they put problems 10x harder than any you've learned. I don't understand why they wouldn't teach you the type of problems on the test. Definitely take him over Hallows though.

Professor Padhi genuinely does not care about his students. He is very egotistical when answering questions in class, but acts as though he is open to all questions. He is barely available when you need help. DO NOT USE OLD EXAMS AS AN INDICATOR OF WHAT TO EXPECT ON YOUR OWN EXAMS! Avoid taking him if you can.

Do not take this class at this school . You can take it at Towson or Baltimore county. Not a good teacher, was not able to teach the material so you can understand it. Was not accessible outside of class. Only 1 TA for 100 students. (no help there) You are on your own. He doesnt care to see you succeed in his class bc if he did he would make time.

This class is challenging, but Padhi provides a lot of extra credit opportunities. He drops the lowest exam, gives random assignments, and makes every exam out of 105%. His lectures are enjoyable, but he does go on tangents and runs out of time. Study with friends and watch videos to supplement the class time.

This professor is knowledgeable but he has no business being an educator. First off, his exams this semester have had an avg of 60% and he hardly curves. He has very little ability to explain concepts when asked questions. Unfortunately, he is the only prof that teach this class. Will be taking this course at another school. Sorry but hes just ��

Every BMGT student takes 340 and it's a pretty demanding course. It's tough but Padhi is a good teacher and a good person. He's very knowledgeable. The homeworks are arduous and difficult but you can pass if you try.

This professor was very nice and understanding. The class itself is very challenging and will require a lot of studying, but he is there to answer questions you may have and tries to make sure the whole class is following along. In class participation helps, and he does go over every topic that is going to be on exams.

The amount of homework you have and studying, you would THINK would help you on his exams. Good luck with that thought because the moment he gives you the exam you have absolutely no idea how to figure out most of the problems he gives as they aren't anything like the ones you do in class and aren't like the ones on MFL either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof Padhi was a great professor. I liked him very much personally. The class is very challenging and is meant to be, but the course gives students every opportunity to do well with a whole lot of homework, practice, and extra assignments to boost poor exam grades. I think this course was very fair although difficult

Overall, Padhi is an okay lecturer. He can be all over the place, but he know's what he's talking about. In terms of exams, they are VERY HARD. You must put a lot of studying to the exams, or you will easily fail. Also, there is a TON of homework, and sometimes it isn't easy, so be prepared for that. Study a TON and attend class, and you'll be good
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Padhi is very smart, but he gets off topic a lot and sometimes can talk excessively. However, he is a very generous grader. He drops and curves grades. Also, he lets you use a one-sided cheat sheet for exams and the final is optional. Just make sure you use his study guides so you can pass his exams, or the cheat sheets won't be useful.

Padhi is a nice guy. Finance is a difficult class to begin with and while he tries to help you as much as he can the tests were harder than any math tests I've ever taken. The questions were purposely worded differently than what we did in class. I never got higher than a C on tests and I was never absent from class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He goes through the problems very quickly just so he can move on without taking into consideration that not everyone understood what he did to solve the problem. If he realized that it is his teaching style that leads to horrible grades on tests than he would be a better teacher.

Padhi is a nice person but his teaching style is awful. The problems you go over in class are different than his exam problems. Studying using the worksheets done in class aren't a big help. His practice exams help a little but the problems on the real exam are written as though they are for Finance majors rather than MKT, IB, or Accounting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Some of the questions on the test were nothing like we did in class or even on the homework. He is nice though.

Prof. Padhi is a good guy, who taught a difficult class with sincerity and clarity.  There may have been a lot of content, but he allowed a full 8.5x11 (one side) sheet of notes for every test, and 3 for the final. There was lots of room to get a good grade, with homework, quizzes, tests, projects, and curved tests. So glad I took his class.

Quint is an great lecturer. The classroom atmosphere is very relaxed, and the goal is to be able to talk about art. Lots of class field-trips to the National Gallery of Art. Graded on Final Paper and on Final Exam. The Final Paper is broken down into smaller parts. The Final Exam is detailed- focus on artwork details and general history.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: I wasn't really interested in the class material itself but i think he knew most people were only taking the class for core and made it as appealing as possible. There isn't a lot of work but go to class and take notes or the final is rough (though it is take-home).

Great professor, really interesting. Gets you excited in what he's talking about. And the last project is making up your own museum exhibit, which is fun. As long as you think and participate, you'll be fine!
Very comprehensive coverage of content and clear expectations. Very fun and laid back approach that rewards participation

Amazing professor with lots of industry experience. He is extremely respectful and aware of how busy students are so he makes sure that his class covers what you need, but does not waste your time with things like extra busywork assignments. He genuinely wants everyone to succeed in his class and excel in their future careers.
Amazing teacher and everything about his class was great. Learned a lot of interesting topics about being a manager and leader. TAKE HIM!

Professor Thomason is amazing. He clearly loves teaching and he has a lot of great industry experience that he shares during class. He wants every student to succeed. His class is one of the most interactive classes I've taken. Part of it is that we have participation points but the other part is his consistently enthusiastic and positive energy.

I took this class over the winter. Professor Thomason is good at teaching! I personally learned a lot from this class, its very engaging. Make sure you manage your time in that way you will get the assignments done before their deadlines. Quizzes are decent! The final was quite difficult, but if you understand the material honestly you will pass.

Had him for BMGT364 over the winter semester. None of the work was really that hard just tedious and took hours to complete or write up. The quizzes were hard but we had multiple attempts on them. The only thing that was somewhat difficult was the final. He is interesting and good at communicating. Looking forward to taking him for BMGT495.

Dr. Mower is nice, but his classes were frustrating. Content leans heavily toward one perspective and often feels more opinion-based than fact-driven (very liberal). He overuses jargon for simple ideas. KNES287 quizzes are manageable, but KNES225 was difficult . Time management is inconsistent.
super manageable class, your writing skills will be improved tremendously by the end of the course. emphasis is placed on using academic AND non Academic sources

Uses big words to explain simple terms. Weekly essays and quizzes are graded fairly harshly. I wish he organized his class in a way that didn't feel so repetitive, you do the same exact assignments every week. I would love to have different assignments to engage with course material. Overall a nice professor, passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: easy and chill class I never went to lectures. might be annoying if u arent a knes major because there are weekly quizzes and mini essays but they are online and you can just control f his slides but he uses rly big words for no reason and its confusing

The name "Sport in American Society" is very misleading.  One would get the idea that this class would focus mostly on sport and something along the lines of how sport influences our society.  If you get that impression you'd be wrong.  This class is mostly on race and gender inequality with many arguments that are not purely factual.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the worst classes ever. I took this class for a gen ed, big mistake. Every week, we could never finish the lecture so he would make you watch the rest of it on a 2 hour long podcast. Then we would have to write a 350 word essay, read articles, watch videos, then take a quiz and repeat next week. Never have I worked so hard for a B in gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Mower's course is really interesting. The course material and lectures were definitely very dense and it was irritating that he could never finish the material during lecture. Honestly, the material isn't hard but his vocabulary is really pretentious and if simplified, it would be much easier to understand. The weekly essays are not too hard.

Uses the most complex words to explain the simplest of things. I leave this class everyday feeling stupid because I really just don't understand what he is saying. Interesting concepts and a nice guy, but there is just too much going on. He never finishes class and tells us to watch his recorded lectures for the rest of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You should want to participate in this class. A true rare gem and the best class I have ever taken period. This course provoked a lot of profound thought and opened my mind to new forms of racial injustice that I never even knew existed. Dr. Mower is also super accommodating and passionate about the effects of sports on black men and it shows!

Professor Mower is a really cool guy and his lectures were really interesting. It was my favorite class to go to. The workload is very low - there are two projects and a midterm essay and a final essay. However, the grading was unnecessarily harsh.

I had Dr. Koulish in Fall 2022. He has a very disorganized teaching style and most lectures were him going on random tangents and allowing debates between students. Most classes, we did not get through all of the slides, and this led to the online quizzes being super difficult. Shoutout to the TA, Monica, for grading leniently, she is a life saver.

Dr. Koulish is a really nice guy, but lecture is just him rambling and going off on tangents. I was confused as to whether or not I should take notes for the class. Also, his quizzes are poorly worded, which is what made them difficult, but shoutout to the TA Monica for grading them leniently.

Very disorganized and ramble-y, be prepared to gain nothing from lectures. Lots of readings are assigned per week, but you could def get away with light skimming. Our TA Monica was incredibly helpful and understanding and kept us in the loop. Quizzes were at-home (...), and fairly difficult but were graded leniently (again, shoutout Monica).
Koulish talks a lot during his lectures to the point where it's confusing if youre supposed to be taking notes or not and the quizzes are based off stuff from multiple weeks prior.

Koulish's class isn't that difficult, but his disorganization is overwhelming. Many of his assignments are unclear and he constantly assigns work outside of the syllabus. If you're passionate about immigration law and social issues and thinking critically about these things, then maybe go for it. Otherwise, you'd be better off taking something else
He really rambles in his lectures and the stuff that he says is not even on the VERY DIFFICULT test that he assigns.

This guy kinda just has a good ol time during lectures and doesn't teach for the work he assigns. He sort of just seems to wing it on everything. He's smart but he drove me insane. If you're interested in JLT scholars I would personally stay away, but maybe it's right for you.

Not a bad person and is passionate about the subject, but did not know how to teach. His grading seemed arbitrary at times, like he never wanted to give full credit. His tests and quizzes also were extremely difficult because his expectations for what you need to know were unclear. Almost all of my class failed a quiz and he blamed the students.

Gives an insane amount of reading each week and takes months to return grades. Had to drop because this class took up way to much time and he gives very difficult tests and I had no idea how well I was doing on the writing assignments since he takes several months to grade. He goes on tangents in lectures and tests you on the tangents. Also boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was awful. I had to take it as part of the MLAW minor program, but it was definitely the worst class Ive taken. Professor Koulish does not grade assignments but continues assigning things. He constantly changes the syllabus and lectures mostly include him just rambling on all class. Definitely would not recommend this class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Knows what hes talking about but doesnt make the material engaging or interesting. He doesnt proofread his slides and takes forever to grade assignments.
He does a great job and is extremely helpful, he makes classes interesting and is very knowledgeable about the subject matter.

An interesting professor to listen to. He loves discussion and gives a participation bonus to people who raise their hands in class. The exams can be somewhat tricky and it will require a bit of studying to get the A grade. Workload is moderate.

Be ready to read. It'll be a lot. The class is great and engaging. He is not an easy grader but he's very respectful, understanding and accommodating  with his students' needs. Just be ready to think and use everything you learn for a good analysis.

this was a really great class! the readings are heavy, but he's a really great guy.  while attending lecture is not mandatory, it is essential to understanding the material.  there are online readings too.. so its a heavy amount.  attendance of discussion sections is mandatory only if you care about that 20% of your grade.  best professor ever!!!

Koulish is amazing. Totally knows the topic, explains it well, and uses relevant examples.  He has an extremely interesting background adn is super approachable.  He answeres questions in lecture too. I had him in Fall 2010, and my TA was also really great.

I was very disappointed in the way that he taught the class. He came in after the first professor was unable to teach and the first professor set the bar high, and he was unable to reach such a high standard. He can be humorous but a good personality doesn't equal a good teacher.

He is phenomenal and clearly knows his field. I wish he could do the discussion sections too. One of his TA's truly sucks due to the inability to engage the class, it's sad. The material is great but the TA can't teach it. No wonder people are not attending sections

Good Teacher overall. Puts powerpoints online so it's easy to catch up if you miss class. Midterm was easy, but the TA's all seemed to grade really hard. One complaint: He LOVES Madison, Wisconsin and mentions it all the time. Hes very Liberal and teaches in that way. He also isn't that good at answering questions, some what confusing.
Good professor. He is very passionate in the topics discussed. You will indeed learn a lot from this class!

teaches like he is teaching to masters students maybe i'm just slow but i can usually grasp things pretty quickly and this i could not. I had to get a tutor to explain things in simple terms to me and even after that I'm still lost He has an accent No problem with that but it just made it a little bit tougher occasionally

Ricardo is a poor professor. Doesn't communicate expectations to students and then gets angry when those unspoken expectations are not met. Additionally, ambiguous with grading and not keen on explaining himself. AVOID

This is the worst professor I have had at UMD. I never write reviews but this class really struck a nerve with me. Exams are difficult, averages are low, his lectures are not helpful because he doesn't explain things. AVOID HIM!!!!!!!

Dr. Araneda definitely shows our the learning environment is supposed to be for a typical 400-level bio class.  Often times, the material is self-learned and any concepts not clear from reading is meant for lecture.  Exams may be moderately difficult, but he compensates with a large curve.
Very helpful, accessible, and responsive to student concerns.

Very difficult, but rewarding if you put in the work. Only reason I am writing is I saw him several times outside class and he was very helpful. Ended up working hard for a A- and was a great review for the MCAT

Araneda is not a good professor. He is a tough love type of prof, and doesnt seem to really care about teaching so students can learn. Tests are very difficult and nit picky. I thought this class was going to be very helpful and a culmination of my time so far at UMD. It wasnt. Avoid him. Good luck.

I took BSCI440 with Araneda in Spring '10. He is a horrible Professor. Lectures were boring, often over students heads and the professor was rude. He was unresponsive to student's questions or concerns. Avoid him.

This professor is not as easy as the other two comments make it seem. Araneda is a tough professor! His exams are very difficult and has high expectations for his students. He doesn't curve either!I would definitely recommend taking another professor with a higher percentage in A's!
cool teacher, may seem a little quite but will help you with just about anything,  tests are a bit different too
Great Overall teacher, willing to help with anything . Exams were straight forward and easy if your study

If you are stuck taking this class with Todd like I was, I advise that you commit to self studying early. As everyone else said, his lectures are very hard to follow and honestly not super helpful. If you have a solid math background or are good at teaching yourself, you will do fine. He makes getting an A possible even if exams dont go great!

Prof Rowland is a cool guy, but his lectures are not helpful in the slightest. For the most part, you can teach yourself all of the material. His practice exams are nearly identical to the exams, some of the exams he let the students write a few questions for, and sent out and answer to one of the questions on the exam for a free point.

The lectures aren't super helpful. Although Dr. Rowland is very nice, he isn't the best lecturer. If you have specific concerns about your grade, he will definitely help though. His exams are very similar to the practice exams, so be sure to utilize those. If your TA is bad, you are better off studying on your own.

Lectures are not necessary and you can probably learn it better/ less confusing on your own. But he is a caring guy and fun to chat with. He would give answers to the homework's and quizzes if you asked him. Doesn't do +/- scale and made it clear but after emailing him, he was nice enough to give me an A-. Exams are similar to practices ones.

Overall the content of his class isn't hard, but his lecturing style is just not great. He tends not to stay on topic and I usually end up working on other things during his lecture. He is actually a very nice person and is super willing to help or fix grades. I ended up teaching myself the majority of the content.

Do not read the old reviews saying exams were like practice ones. The exams got so hard and were not like any practice. Averages on them were in the Cs or Ds, which is absurd for a 100-level class. Take MATH 135 with Zhao, not Rowland. It is not worth it to get a B or C for a 4-credit class, thereby wrecking your GPA. Harder than Calc AB/BC for me.

Professor Rowland is a nice guy, but he is not skilled in teaching. His lectures are so scattered its hard to watch and the TAs don't really know what they are doing either. Its an easy course you just have to teach yourself everything. The exams are not too difficult because they are almost identical to the practice exams.

Trust me, I'm usually an A- student.

Lectures were hard to follow, but with the way the course is set up between Lectures, GSS, and Discussion, learning the content and getting help should be no problem... except, I had no time for GSS, and my TA was unhelpful. 141 is a sink-or-swim class, and you need to set extra time aside for practicing.
He has really bad lectures but the TAs kinda make up for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Hes a little all over the place and I basically taught myself most of the content but hes understanding and the assignments are meant to help you learn.

Rowland is a very nice person and truly cares about his students. His notes and lectures are pretty difficult to follow b/c theres no real structure so be prepared to do a lot of self-learning. However, he gives plenty of practice and the practice exams are very similar to the real exams in terms of format and questions. The course is not too hard.

Professor Rowland is a very caring person and answers emails fast. However, his lectures are all over the place and the info taught by the TA and professor are different so it is extra confusing. The exams are okay, make sure you understand the practice exams because they're very similar. Make sure to pay extra attention in lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof. Rowland is seriously one of the sweetest people ever and really tries to get to know every student but he's just not that good at explaining the concepts and would often get lost along the way while doing a problem. That being said it is still possible to get an A in this class and he's not the worst choice. He's very understanding and nice.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why Professor Rowland has such poor reviews. He is a great professor and cares deeply about his students and wants them to succeed. Go to class, pay attention to assignments and put in time for practice before the exams and you will do well. I would 100% recommend taking him.

When you have pop quizzes he tends to give you the information you need on the day of the quiz so you kind of have to teach yourself with the textbook sometimes. He is a nice person though, and will give you points back on your exams if it was graded unfairly. The homeworks are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Rowland is super nice. His lectures can be a little hard to follow but I think as he gets more experienced that will get better. Make sure to ask any questions you have because he will answer them in great detail which for me personally was very helpful. Also make sure to absolutely go to discussions because they are super helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Rowland could be one of the nicest guys Ive ever met and he made a typically extremely difficult class at UMD very manageable!!
Really nice guy. Talks a little to get used to his lecture style but he does everything he can to be helpful

Dr. Rowland is a nice guy but he's not a great professor. It's obvious that he knows the material but he is unable to teach it. He also has a lot of lectures but they aren't helpful. You will mostly be learning from the textbook and the discussions with the teaching aids. Exams are similar to practice exams so make sure you study with them!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Rowland is a great guy, really funny, nice, and down to earth. The lectures werent very helpful (he tend to go on tangents and doesnt explain things very well) but discussion sections make up for it. The class isnt hard, just go to discussion, do the worksheets, and make sure you understand the practice exams!

Dr. Rowland's lectures are not the greatest, but I saw some improvements as the semester progressed. He truly cares about his students, which is evident in his accessibility and tests that aren't too difficult. I recommend to read the sections, complete practice problems he assigns before lecture, and attend discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I took MATH141 online with Rowland. TBH he's not the best teacher, but overall such a nice guy. He was always available during office hours and was able to explain stuff better. Make sure to do the practice problems and read the textbook. In the begging the lectures were rough, but he's gotten better throughout the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He's a very nice person but this is his first year teaching and he's not doing too well. I feel sorry that his first year being a lecturer is virtual but he does not explain the material very well. His lectures are very disorganized and abstract, does not teach you anything about solving problems. I practically taught myself through khan academy.
He really wants you to learn and goes out of his way during office hours to make sure you understand. Hes a new teacher and the lectures have gotten better since the start of the semester.

The other reviews are gassing it. Literally the easiest class I've taken this sem. Every hw is in partners and if you just establish a good relationship with your partner in the beginning, you won't be left doing them alone. The TAs are really helpful; they teach pretty much all the actual math that you need. Easy A if you've taken AP Stat.

Rowland is all around a great guy who is trying his best. His lectures are somewhat a waste of time other than an entertainment source. The TAs saved this class and discussions are awesome. Tests are easy because he gives practice tests that go over exactly what you need to know. Lots of grades help keep grades high. Just do the work.
Dr. Rowland is a really nice guy, but his lectures are very disorganized. He always goes off tangent, making the class harder than it needs to be.

Overall Hes a very nice person not a rude teacher. But when it comes to teaching he is horrible. So get ready to teach yourself. At times he didnt even know the answer to practice midterms which was a little disappointing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not a very good teacher. Overall a super nice guy, and you can tell he is very smart... but his ability to explain the material is less than adequate.
Incredibly hard to get in contact with, did not show for scheduled virtual office hours and just generally unresponsive. Her emails are impossible to understand due to the grammatical errors.

I really enjoyed this class! I found the material interesting, exams were not hard if you studied the lecture material. The lab can be a little time consuming but not bad- all group projects in lab. Overall great class!

I've had her for three classes each class has been very laborious. She is so lovely and nice and you can tell she really cares about her students, but she is always busy and it shows. She mostly reads off the slides in class, and you def need the textbook, and her exam study guides aren't very accurate to the actual exams. good luck :)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. U is easily one of the best, if not the best professor in the UMD Dietetics department. She cares about her students and wants them to do well not only in class but in life! 350 was really hands-on as a course, and she expects you to take those aspects of foodservice in stride. Show up, put in hard work & study for exams - you will do just fine

Lectures were kinda boring but Dr. U talked a lot about future goals and had lots of guest lecturers (John Hopkins, NIH, sports dietitian). So that aspect was interesting. Exams were decent, mostly multiple choice. Lab was long and time consuming but also super easy. Overall, a mostly easy class. Just memorize the powerpoints and show up to class.

She is a nice person. She just shouldn't teach. She makes the material more confusing than it needs to be. I don't think this rating is useful because if you're in the dietetics program your forced to take her for 380, 350 and what ever Medical Nutrition Therapy is. I think it's sad that UMD is considered to have a good program with her as a direc

Extremely unorganized. I was better off skipping class and reading the book because going to lecture just confuses you. Exams do not cover material from her lectures she just pulls questions from old RD exams but doesn't warn you. Seems extremely overworked & has no idea why students are frustrated w her class. Incredibly nice person 1-on-1 though.
so unorganized.

The most difficult intro level course you're ever going to take. He will do everything in his power to not explain anything, and when he does it will be in the most confusing way that is humanly possible. The only slightly easy part about the class is the essay grading is fair lenient, balanced out by the midterm and final being a guaranteed F.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was able to explain everything clearly and thoroughly. I was able to keep up with the class with ease. I felt comfortable asking questions and when I did he always gave very insightful answers. It's definitely a harder workload course but it challenges you and he has your best interest at heart.
He can't give a straight answer to anything
Very condescending and expects you to already understand economics even tho this is an INTRO course
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am posting just to WARN students to avoid this professor. Having been in a course for an ELECTIVE 100 level class, this felt like 300 level work. The professor interrupts while some students aren't finished answering or asking questions. Even if the class is recorded, he likes to give pop up quizzes, unfinished notes with zippy quick explanation

He is very accessible and really wants his students to succeed. This course was extremely challenging and needed a lot of time dedicated to it. COVID updates to his normal syllabus: No final, dropped lowest midterm, and several quizzes. He curved to a B (I think he did this in normal semesters). Very knowledgeable and passionate about economics.
