reviews.comment: This class is so interesting and applicable in todays world. Beyond that, Professor Gorhams lectures are engaging and never boring. The assignments are very easy and manageable. If you need extra credit, this is a good online 3 credit class that you'll definitely get an A in.

Professor Gorham-Oscilowski's lectures are very engaging and informative; it's impossible to get bored in her lectures. In addition, she has a clear criteria for all of her assignments that she will happily give feedback on. She has a very impressive way of making difficult content very understandable and clear. Definitely recommend  her as a prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Super easy class, but didn't learn much. Class was really just common sense. Really didn't even need to come to lectures or do any of the assigned readings. Pretty easy grader, but the TA was nit-picky. There is one fairly easy paper and one final research-based project. No tests or final exam. A few quizzes during the first half of semester.

She does not like to give out 100s, she will give you a 99.5 and take off for something pedantic. She won't give anyone a perfect score, so if that part of your GPA is important to you, don't take her class.

I took this class for an easy gen ed and it was not bad at all. You'll have exit tickets after class that are pretty short. There were group assignments. There were 'papers' but they honestly had a maximum of like 500 words which is not hard. She was very nice and the content was actually interesting. I definitely recommend!

Super kind professor, very accessible through email and the course is very applicable outside of class. I took this class because I needed a gen ed, and ended up learning valuable concepts all while earning an A. Homework is manageable and there were group projects but they were by no means a big stressor. Would recommend this course.

Super easy gen ed. Honestly one of the best classes I've taken because of how applicable it is. There is a group project where some of the assignments can seem stressful, but they really aren't the worst if you all work together.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Prof. Gorham was a great lecturer and teacher for 152. For a gen ed I thought it was too much work, but her lectures and readings were helpful in understanding the material. She grades fairly and as long as you do the minimum you'll get an A. She's very clear in what she expects and you can email or meet with her for more specifics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Probably the best online class I have ever taken, plus she is one of the writers of the textbook, at first it seems like a lot of text without any pictures but the content is really good and I have even looked to it in other classes. I suggest you take this class online
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Gorham was absolutely amazing and I would take one of her classes again! You'll have about 4-5 assignments due every week but they're mostly little quizzes and summaries. Very helpful and easily accessible outside of class. Lots of articles to read that you need for quizzes but just crtl+f them. Easy A class, great needed gen ed.

Ursula is a nice lady who loves to talk about her family life. She is caring, understanding, and responsive to emails. The class is pretty easy, and there are alot of opportunities for extra credit. However, she can be a very harsh grader on papers, discussions, and exams for no reason. It is hard to get an A on her any of her assignments.

Best class ever. Weekly quizzes and discussion post, midterm and final (which are both open-note AND YOU HAVE THE WHOLE DAY TO FINISH), and 2 written assignments. She offers so much extra credit(which can be earned from just showing up to class--which you should already be doing) that I ended up with a 99% in the class. Easy A, just do the work!
She is a great professor who really engages her students and is there for you if you need help. She is very passionate about her job and her students. She is the best professor you can take at UMD!

Really great professor. The lectures are powerpoint heavy, which can be boring sometimes. She allows the use of electronics in class. There is an online midterm and no final exam in this class. The textbook is not required but it is recommended, and there are a lot of readings.

She isn't a bad professor, but she could be boring sometimes. She makes you read a lot and goes over heavy PowerPoints. Other than that, she is a pretty chill teacher. You're allowed to use electronics in class and she's willing to work with everyone's schedule. Her midterm was online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Online course. A ton of reading but she touched on the important parts in her lectures. Only class this semester that I felt good about. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I got a 99% in the class. He is just an awful person. The entire course is group work and I was randomly paired with the laziest people. I complained to him about them not doing the work and he did nothing about it. He was very disrespectful over emails.

Underhill is one of the coolest professors I have had so far. He really knows how to interact with his students and is incredibly nice and fun to be around. He's almost like that awesome high school teacher you once had. He is that chill. The class was incredibly easy and interesting even though I'm not majoring in COMM. Take a class with this guy!

Underhill is legit. knowledgeable, fair, and his class is priceless. The assignments are pretty fun. I will never forget the debates we had in his class. So many classics. Its a class you need in life.

great professor, tries t keep class funny and interesting. atmosphere is laid back and work isnt hard. midterm wasnt hard either and only hard part would be the day of the speeches if you get nervous. grading is by peers and also by the prof but grading is also fair.
the only hard thing about this class is giving the debates..

Steve is a young, hilarious hippie. The class I took with him was only 50 min long, and the 1st 20 min always consisted of us jamming out to eachothers music because steve wanted us to get to know eachother better through music. the only assignments you get are speeaches (3 for the semester lol) and the midterm and final were ridiculously easy.
This class was a breeze. Barely any homework. We just talked about random stuff during class. Significantly easier that other comm classes.

Dr. Upshaw is kind and obviously loves art history. Her lectures are clear, and she was very clear about how her tests would look, and even gave specific examples in class of how we should answer. Memorization is key!

This is Professor Upshaw's first year at UNCW. For being a first year professor you'd think she would be a light grader, really understanding, helpful, etc. Well, you'd be wrong one of the worst professors I have had. You have to use her material that she deems as proper evidence, structure of paragraphs must be above perfect, and many more. Bad

Dr. Upshaw is a very engaging lecturer and tries her best to engage the class in the material. The homework is pretty light (only one page of reading a week) but she expects thoroughness and is a bit tough for grading. She's very strict on attendance, so you have to be there.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I thought she was a great teacher, this was my first class of college and she set the bar high but in a good way. She explained the material very thoroughly and would always stick around if you needed clarification. She made me obsessed with art history from taking one class. Youll be glad you took this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took this class for the gen ed credits and I am so glad I did. She has really good lectures, but there are almost no notes on her PowerPoints, just the artworks so pay attention to everything she says. The midterm and final aren't too bad, just memorization. She also only assigns a few things during the semester, but she is a fairly easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Upshaw was incredible! She cares a lot about the artwork she is presenting and it reflects that! However (for my ARTH201), there were only 2 assignments outside of the mid-term and final. She's a pretty easy grader and is very considerate, but it will show if you didn't go to a lecture. Her slides are just the art and don't contain the notes.

I loved Abby she was an awesome professor. She made the lectures really interesting and engaging and seemed to genuinely care about her students. She was a little slow on grading and her tests her kind of hard, but you will get a good grade if you study.

Really easy class to understand overall.   One homework per week other than exam/break weeks, which take around an hour or so to complete.  She references a textbook if you need additional help, but just going to lectures and doing the homework to reinforce each week's concepts with a little extra studying before exams was more than enough for me.
Need a GPA inflator? Take her course, and you will more than fine.

I really like Uler. Very caring and fair- will meet you halfway if you need help. The homeworks are useful for preparing for exams. The lectures are good, and the textbook is a good supplement. Exam heavy, but lots of partial credit. The only reason she isn't a 5 is that she is a bit bland and lectures get boring sometimes. Would recommend Uler

Tests are a BIG chunk of your grade so if your not a good test taker you will struggle. She does curve the exams though,but don't depend on the curve because the exams are hard. She always makes sure to have office hours even when she is very busy. Do the homework! It really helps cement concepts. Her lectures are hard to understand sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall I was not a huge fan. She has a bad habit of making you feel very stupid when you ask questions. If you are not good at physics be warned because she doesn't seem to understand not everyone is great at physics. Thank goodness for our incredible TA or I would have failed the class.

She is very convoluted in the way she explains things. If you do not have existing knowledge of physics the class is confusing. The class itself is mainly partnered labs with quick daily homework which she provides somewhat helpful feedback on.

The materials Arpita(ExpertTA) uses has a really bad textbook for PHYS275. My TA was kind of bad as well. She explains things nicely one-on-one, which is nice but I feel like the class is poorly designed. We do a lot of experiments where the theoretical basis has not yet been established (ex: we do a waves exp).She wastes time in the start of class
Easy lab and lab reports everyday and test were straight forward and open note.

Straight-forward lab. Mostly easy lab work. Follow the instructions and ask questions when something's unclear. Fairly minimal homework (every 1 out of 3 classes or so had 20-30 minutes worth of homework). 2 midterms, no final (repeats classwork). Prof Upadhyaya was helpful and clear. Recommended and would take another lab with her in the future.

She's super nitpicky! Claimed that you cant go back and do "peer responses" but you can as I was able to in another class I was taking. Super critical with work when in reality its a beginning writing class. 10/10 Would Not recommend She should be an advance writing professor not an intro class. It was very discouraging.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Nitpicky feedback. EXCESSIVE complicated directions w/instructions for your instructions. New reading material, updates, tips, suggestions, announcements are posted almost daily, with several posts/reminders in a day. This is overwhelming and deterring even to an A+ student. Reading materials are far left, lacking variety. Best Advice: Stay Away!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The differences between Professor Uhrick's class and my other classes were night and day! While other professors give vague, minimal feedback, Professor Uhrick engages with each student and gives phenomenal guidance on grammar and writing! She gives in depth help, going above and beyond to ensure her students grasp each concept! Highly recommend!

Great professor. Umisha is a very kind professor that wants the class to do well. If you fear/hate public speaking take this class. She does an excellent job promoting a healthy environment to cultivate speaking skills. Plus she grades hella easy.

Umisha was an absolutely amazing professor! She made class very interesting. There are online quizzes which you have 3 attempts for, they're not hard if you've read the chapter. There are also 3 main presentations (4 but the last is a recorded one) which ae graded very easily (I bombed the first and got a 92.) Overall, really good pick for gen ed.

Umisha KC is a great professor! I was nervous for a public speaking class and she made it so enjoyable and interesting. There are about 4 summative speeches, daily assignments to get students engaged, and a few quizzes. She really cares about her students and I feel a lot more confident with public speaking after taking her class!

Umisha KC was amazing for an online comm class. Only 1 synchronous class a week and asynchronous activities were clear and easy. Gives good feedback had interesting classes. Will work with you, likes to have fun, and is a great prof. You wont go wrong with her.

I am currently about to fail her class highkey depending on the final to bring my grade up. SHE DOESNT LET U VIEW OLD EXAMS. So i genuinely do not know how or what to improve since i do very well on homeworks. Overall the class shouldnt be hard but if you mess up two exams ur kinda screwed and theres no projects or extra credit so

If you don't do the online textbook reading (Smartbook) you're kinda screwed. I recommend locking in on the three exams so you don't have to take the final. Lots of charts and graphs, but that's to be expected in an Econ course.

Easy peezy. You'll be in class a hour max, even though its almost a 2 hour course. Just show up or let her know you can't make it to receive an alternate assignment. There's no hard content, exams, or quizzes, just a final group project that doesn't require much work outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of students so lecture moves fast, not mandatory but kinda is because you need the lesson to learn. 4 exams in one semester with optional final. You definitely have to spend some time on homework to understand the chapter. If not, you won't do good on the exams, (30 multiple choice with 2-4 short answer). Need to be somewhat good at math

Professor Scandizzo was okay at best. Econ is not really an interesting subject to me personally by any means, but she at least made them applicable to simpler scenarios. Not sure what's got her so hung up on blueberries, to each their own I guess. She gave me a bit of a harder time at the beginning of the semester because of my service dog, though
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Scandizzo is a terrible professor! There are 2 midterms and the final which are very different from the study guide and very difficult. She's decent! Her lectures are more detailed than the textbook, in my opinion. reviews.comment: Pretty boring lecturer but they were kind of informative. She loves blueberries though, and she won't stop talking about them. Weird if you ask me, but to each their own I guess.

reviews.comment: Took AP Econ in highschool so this class was an easy A, other ppl tend to struggle tho.  Definitely take Scandizzo, her lectures are well explained and other professors added in more material.  Smartbooks and homework every week but you get a second attempt.  Probably be helpful to take notes on the textbook if you're gonna skip class

What did Nicki Minaj say? "Ayo they could never make me hate you!" I dont know why these reviews are so bad, Professor Scandizzo was great. She grades super fairly, and if you make an honest effort in this class there is no way you can fail. She makes trade policy as interesting as she can honestly. Theory based classes > Math based classes.

People are exaggerating. I show up to class like once every 2 weeks and I still ended up doing fine on all the exams. The homework and smart books are kind of tedious but if you do it your grade should be fine. Even if you don't understand anything like a week before an upcoming exam, just go to those GSS exam sessions and do the practice exam.
This class requires a lot of time and effort.  Homework assignments take a long time to complete and you'll be studying for exams a lot.

She read right off of slides and did not explain concepts very well. In order to do well on exams, attending class is necessary. She doesn't assign many assignments, so preparing for tests and doing well on them in important for obtaining a good grade.

reviews.comment: If you go to class and study, you will do fine. Her lectures are clear and helpful.

reviews.comment: Scandizzo is really great. Her examples in class are simple to follow and she is clear in her explanations. Go to class, attend GSS, and review as much as you can. I did extremely well on the first test, but not as well on the second. It is a tough class. I recommend taking her if you can because she cares a lot about the success of her students.

I was nervous about taking econ, but Professor Scandizzo made the information super accessible. If you attend lectures, take notes, and study for midterms and the final, you'll be totally fine. Attend GSS too, it's super helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Scandizzo was really out to ruin my mental health. I would think I understood material, then bombed exams. I do not know what she did to make her exams so hard, but beware. It was weird because you either did really well in her class or did awful. You were asleep by the end of the lecture, but the workload was manageable.

I do NOT like her teaching style. She just reads off of the powerpoint, yet doesn't explain to us what the stuff actually means. I had to reteach myself everything before the exams. The TA's are the reason I got through the course, they were very helpful with review sessions. She is also not a nice person and does not care about her students. 2/10

She's a very good professor, gave a lot of homework and required that you read the book, lectures were essentially just retellings of what you read in the book. She gives practice exams that are almost exactly the same as the actual exam (she re-uses questions on some exams)

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER YALL, there is a reason she has this bad of a review. I dreaded this class, take microecon at a community college, save yourself the pain. the curve was also horrible

Prof. Scandizzo is just not great and the class is tough. She is a boring lecturer and pretty disorganized with uploading materials. You will essentially teach yourself everything. I found Dr. Scandizzo to be a great professor. She has a wealth of knowledge but manages to simplify the material into a way that is clear and digestible for students. reviews.comment: She is one evil professor that has no empathy.

I do not recommend this professor, very unorganized with answer keys and does not care about students. Exams are not reasonable and her excuse is because it's open note. She also doesn't allow enough time for the practice exam to be up and I don't understand the reason behind it. Take this class with someone who actually knows how to teach

Prof Scandizzo is decent at lecturing, but you have to read the textbook to stay ahead in this class. Smartbook and homeworks are due every Wednesday and Monday, respectively. reviews.comment: Ngl stopped going to lecture after the 3rd week of school. So boring and dry and she's just not good at teaching. reviews.comment: Dr. Scandizzos lectures are taught based off the textbook chapters, so reading the textbook is a necessity if you plan on not attending class. the smart books are graded on completion and the homework on accuracy, but you do get 2 attempts for the homework and many quizlets have been made. There are 4 exams which are very specific, but open note.

reviews.comment: Homework assignments are unnecessarily long and don't relate to the exams. Professor's lectures are also just based off the textbook.

Scandizzo is really good at explaining the difficult concepts inside the class, but she talks like you already have some knowledge on the topic. I would highly recommend doing the smartbooks before you go over it in class. Also if you go to every class, its impossible to get below a 90. The tests are weirdly specific but they aren't that difficult.

reviews.comment: The class is fairly straightforward and the homework load is not that bad. The exams will make or break your grade obviously. Make sure you read!!! The exams cover 3-4 chapters at a time so there is a lot of content to cover.

Professor Scandizzo is well-versed in her subject and simplifies it very well. She also builds up the material in a logical way, instead of following the exact format of the online book used. The material can be tough to get through since there's so much of it, but if you take good notes and keep up with the readings and homework you're do great.

reviews.comment: Do not take, assigns so many homework problems not even similar to what she teaches. Her exams have so many questions in such a short period of time and her excuse is that it's open note. Has no compassion for her students, honestly such a horrible professor. Do not take !!
Do not take this professor, so many assignments and basically just reads off the slides.

I basically never joined lecture because the textbook and reviews match the tests exactly. She's better than some reviews say. If you designate some time to just read the textbook before the tests, you'll have no problem.

Scandizzo hadn't taught econ for a while and it was evident in her lectures. If you want to do well in this course, I recommend going to the GSS sessions and other TA sessions for help. reviews.comment: A lot of people thought this class had way too much work for it being an intro to microeconomics course. At the end of the day, it is easy if you put in the time and read the textbook and take notes. I definitely would have struggled a lot if I hadn't had some prior knowledge of micro before taking it. Scandizzo is very organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This course was helpful in prepping for econ career. There wasn't to much work, only meet online between 12-1 on Fridays.
Super nice and always attentive to students

I don't recommend taking her for an intro class. She seems like a nice person with a lot of knowledge of ECON. However, between online learning and it being her first time teaching such a large intro lecture, she was super overwhelmed which explains all the bad ratings this semester. She just doesn't know how to effectively teach a large class.

Wad unresponsive to questions and inflexible when it came to deadlines/grades. Third exam average was a 68% (it's an intro class) and she refused to curve it. reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Scandizzo is really nice but as an online class ECON200 was more teach-yourself. If you want to ask questions about the material you're better off going to OH cause she mostly ignores questions during Zoom lectures. Tests are hard but going to the GSS sessions is really helpful for learning the material (more helpful than class lectures imo).

I like the structure of the class and the workload isn't all that bad. The exam questions are pretty straightforward and the quizzes are taken in groups with 2 attempts. I will warn you that are few lectures, so if you are unwilling to take the time to teach yourself, you shouldn't take this class.

The teacher seems really nice from the ratings that students posted a few years ago. Now that we are doing online lectures I believe she makes it difficult for all of us to understand. You ask questions in zoom chats and she might not even answer them. The tests are nothing like the practice tests she gives out. Very difficult to learn on your own.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She does not teach anything. Her test are nothing like the GSS reviews or even what the TAs claim to help you with. She is rude and does not answer questions. Her test are insane and she will not curve test grades no matter how awful the entire class does because of her lack of instruction & teaching.

She gives a lot of homework and her tests are ridiculous. She just goes over a powerpoint and does not answer questions. Her last test was on chapters 6-12, and 70 percent of the test was chapter 6. It was nothing like the review tests and worksheets.
Does not teach you anything, and does not answer questions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance is not mandatory, but she gives you the notes and it's easier than reading the dense textbook. Exams were pretty fair if you study hard. Sometimes she asks specific questions. If you happen to not study that, then there goes 10 pts. The only thing I dislike is the group component of the class. Overall, solid professor and great class.

Very fair professor. Ive taken a few classes with her and shes awesome. Shes one of those teachers that you an tell she loves what she does. Respectful towards students and attendance isn't mandatory with is a huge plus.

One of the best professors around, good lectures, fair homework, exams are hard because all of them are short answers. Knows her stuff. I'm taking another one of her classes this semester. Coming to classes is recommended even though attendance is not mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Teaches the way all professors should: explained the material, wrote all relevant information on the board instead of forcing you to figure out what's important, tons of assignments that are simple but keep you on track, and clear cut exams. Very interesting material too!

I had Professor Vaziri for both years of the program, and he played a huge role in my growth as a designer. He's tough but genuinely cares, and his direct feedback helped me improve quickly. The projects from his classes became strong portfolio pieces that helped me stand out in interviews and job applications.

Professor Vaziri has a really interesting background and has so much experience to share. He expects a lot but he does this because he wants to see you produce good work. You have to be serious about your future as a designer if you want to do well, anyone who doesnt take the subject seriously is wasting all that Professor Vaziri has to offer.

Professor Vaziri is a great professor. He is definitely tough in ARTT356, just because there are a lot of assignments back-to-back, but later on in ARTT457, the workload is much more reasonable. He gives very blunt feedback, but it is very helpful, and he truly wants you to become a better designer.

Professor Vaziri has made my experience in the graphic design program incredibly valuable. His lessons focus on the why, more than how, and I feel like I have grown so much under his guidance. I highly recommend taking any class with him. He is a bit tough at first, but is because he cares deeply about his students and pushes you to succeed.

A lot of the class was self-taught in terms of UX and Figma so be prepared for some YouTube tutorials and Google searches. Prof. is straightforward about his critiques and it is best to implement them to have a better design. There is not any feedback for any points taken off for final project grades so try to get feedback every other class.
I dropped the class on first day because there were a lot of readings and assignnments and a recorded presentation for a async class is a no no

Professor Beshel was amazing. I really enjoyed her class. She was very caring and is willing to work with her students to make sure everyone is on track. She did not mind pushing back dues if necessary. She gives good feedback. Overall, she is a great professor I would recommend her to anyone planning to take ENGL 101.

She is sooo sweet and caring. She really has the best interest for her students. She takes attendance EVERY class so don't plan on skipping. No exams but 3 papers around 4-5 pages (including in class written final). One group project that is 25-30 minutes. We had to read like 6 books but they're all good. Overall easy and would recommend.

reviews.comment: i LOVE this woman. professor beshel is kind, caring and truly wants her students to do well. each class is riveting and truly engaging. the class discussions have led to the class becoming a true community, with professor beshel at the helm. i love her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She's honestly the best, I love her sm.

She is amazing! She really cares about how her students are doing and wants them to do well. She is a very easy graders and gives you an opportunity to revise one assignment. If you approach her with questions, she goes above and beyond when answering. On one of my papers that I was stuck on she helped me fine 5 good sources! :)

Mrs. Beschel is a pretty good professor. As someone who hates English, this class was still pretty easy. Overall easy grader if you do your work properly. She is understanding and will push back due dates if she feels necessary.

Professor Beshel is well versed and super sweet. She sincerely cares about the well being of her students, both in the classroom and outside. We rarely used the books even though she says we will use them. Would definitely take her again.

Mrs. Beshel was honestly one of the best English instructors I've ever had in my life. She's very understanding and grades pretty easily. There are a lot of assignments in her class, but sometimes she'll give extensions if she feels like the class really needs it. She really wants you to buy the books, but you dont need them at all

She is a nice person overall, but an awful professor. When she explains topics, you can tell she understands them, but has no idea how to teach them to others. Assignments had no direction whatsoever and when asked for clarificaiton she gave vague answers.

I have now taken VK for for three classes, not by choice. She grades things harshly but on whims so if she likes you, you get higher grades, but never perfect. Her rubrics say "exceeding expectations" is necessary for 100s. Will give people different grades for having the same answers. Not helpful when you talk to her about it too.

This class was miserable. There was so much busy work given weekly. She would take off random points with no explanation on the models and content outlines, it felt almost impossible to get a perfect score on them. The exams were way too long, she expects very specific answers. Most students did not finish the exams on time.

Simply an OK professor. She relies heavily on a textbook that is overwhelming and unhelpful. Physiology is a tough class with lots of content and she doesn't really make it clear what is important and what's not. Very tough grader with unhelpful feedback. If you have to take this class, focus on the processes and how they work rather than vocab.

If you don't want to own your own farm one day, do not take this class. It wasn't what I expected it to be. She prides herself on not giving points out and isn't always clear about what she wants. I honestly cant stand her teaching since ANSC212. Weekly quizzes, weekly parts of the semester project due, and get ready for group presentations.

She wasn't as bad as the reviews make her out to be. The exams aren't easy but they're manageable to pass if you put in the effort to study. You can pass the class if you fail 1 or 2 exams because there are other opportunities to boost your grades although the busy work is annoying. She doesn't always seem to enjoy answering questions during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's honestly not that awful. Decent amount of homework (content outlines + lectures + 1 page reports + a quiz weekly). She loves to ask questions she asked before on exams, so pay attention in activities and during the quizzes. She uses the textbook, but I was able to just skim it. Decent lecturer, activities/drawings in class were helpful

Dr. VK's lectures are really hard to follow. Her drawings and handwriting are really sloppy. She does not like to answer your questions in lecture and you basically teach yourself physiology in this class. reviews.comment: 2 lab reports and they were graded extremely hard. reviews.comment: Great lecturer. He is clearly knowledgable on European History, and he also prompts us to not only think of history as events, but instead poke deeper into analyzing the broad strokes of history. If you can get past his Italian accent, you will surely enjoy yourself.

Professor Villani is the worst teacher I've ever had. The lectures were chaotic and confusing with zero structure clarity. reviews.comment: His accent is really annoying

Dr. Villani is an amazing professor, regardless of his accent. It's clear just how much he cares and is passionate about history just from his lectures alone. He is passionate and you can tell he cares about what he teaches, but lectures are hard to get through. I am a stem major and this class is my worst grade.

reviews.comment: Professor Villani is clearly an expert in his field, and is truly passionate about his teachings! He gives you all the material needed to succeed, and while he will point out the flaws or mistakes in your work, he will give you a fair grade nonetheless. As long as you show up and remain engaged with the material, you will pass easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really great professor! He knows a lot about his subject and is clearly passionate about it! He is easy to reach for office hours and gives good detailed notes on your papers. In terms of assignments, there are only around 4 for the entire term, worth 25% each, so you really want to do well on those if you want to get a good grade in the class.
If you can get over a pretty heavy Italian accent, he's a wonderful professor. Very kind, fair grader, and offers a lot of insight into history from a European perspective.

He's a nice guy and all and the class was not difficult but the way he talks is so irritating I want to pull my hair out. He has a heavy italian accent and he mumbles and freezes A LOT. It drives me crazy!!! Especially the constant mumbling.

Previously was in his 339O class and now this one. A great guy who has interesting lectures. This time I read parts of the textbooks and I should get an A so I recommend you do too. As long as you demonstrate that you've read some of the text you should get at least an A-. Really passionate about what he teaches, only 4 grades for the class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy, who has an Italian accent so he can be a little hard to understand. The most important thing to note is that the two classes I've had with him only have 4 essay exams (some taken home) worth 25% of the grade. Going to lectures/relying on slides can give you a B+. Reading the textbook even a little can get you an A- or better. Also funny!

reviews.comment: Great prof, has trouble time managing in lecture. REALLY interesting class though. You have to read the books, but he's a fairly easy grader.

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at UMD!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a very lenient grader. He brings chocolate for the class pretty much every class and offers extra credit opportunities for attending lectures by guest speakers and writing short reports on them. HIST333 will have a lot of RELS students so be prepared to ask history questions if you don't want the class to be too religious studies heavy.

Native Italian, so his English is broken at times. His knowledge of Medieval and Renaissance Europe/Italy is not broken though. He was super patient w me as i worked 50 hrs a week, i turned everything in late he didn't penalize me even one time. Really nice guy, he personally knows the experts in his field. Cool cat.

I am taking Renaissance Europe with Professor Villani While he seems nice enough his lectures are hard to follow. He is actually from Italy so he seems to know a lot about the subject he is teaching but he just has not grasped the language enough to have a smooth lecture. He is constantly searching for the right words. Not easy to concentrate.
Easy professor, super nice and helpful. Class did have lots of hw and work but It's easy to get by if you complete. 100% recommend her.

Prof. Victoria is the BEST professor EVER! She is very approachable and flexible. There are some group projects, but they are very easy. This is the first class I really enjoyed to take. I was never bored. She prepares you for the exams, so you should be fine as long as you participated. She is wonderful and I totally recommend Prof. Victoria.

If you take Spanish with any professor, I highly recommend Professor Arvay. She is so caring and accommodating to students. She knows her stuff and wants all students to do well. I do not have a single bad thing to say about Professor Arvay.

Prof Arvay is super nice and helpful. She wants her students to succeed, and is really approachable if you have any questions. There's a few homework assignments a week but they're all pretty simple, and all of the tests are straightforward and she prepares you for them well. I definitely recommend- I'm taking SPAN301 with her next semester.
Amazing Professor and an industry expert.   He is highly popular and his classes have a huge waitlist - so opt in as early as can be hard to enroll. Very caring towards student needs and kind

Nice professor. He gave us the option of having the class online or in-person. He expects a lot out of the team presentations. Willing to answer questions. Was flexible on when we could take the exams.

He's all right, very kind and compassionate, genuinely wants students to learn and apply themselves. The mandatory attendance gets annoying but all 495 courses are like that. You don't necessarily need to talk as much as in other courses, just show up. I would say be thorough with some of the assignments since he can be a bit of a tough grader.
An amazing professor who is a real life corporate expert . Emphasizes learning over grades and will always go the extra mile for the students

I really liked Gambhir up until the last few days of the semester. You have no idea of your final grades until they are posted. He graded the final presentations extremely hard, 75 being the average, and those grades are a huge portion of your final grade. Honestly would not recommend him because of how unfair and unclear his grading is.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Gambhir is an amazing and caring professor. I enjoyed every moment of his class and we only met once a week instead of two so that was an added bonus. He is an easy grader and provides feedback on your group presentation. The homework was straightforward. You don't want to miss out taking this class with him!

The best professor I have ever had. So inspirational and caring, he genuinely loves his students and cares for them. Just show up to class and he will make sure that you succeed. Nothing but respect for him.

This is one of the easiest and most useful classes I have taken. Prof Gambhir is very laid back and his focus is on learning, not being a harsh grader. Almost everyone in the class gets an A, just show up to class and you're fine. Take this class with him, you will not regret it.

He is a very genuine professor and makes learning fun. Very chill about class and straightforward. Simply show up do a little bit of work and will get an A. Actually learn in his class instead of only passing.

He is the kindest professor I have ever had at UMD. He truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed. His tests come straight from the lectures and if you try at all in his course you will get an A. You also get extra credit if you go to every class!

He does not want to see you fail at all, he is such a supportive teacher. Took this class for the business minor and was scared at first but he made this class fun and easy. He is so the boy and gives extensions. There are multiple group projects but they are not hard.

RVC was an amazing professor. She is very flexible with deadlines and will always push you to do your best work. She will push you to turn in your best work possible and will always provide you with feedback to help with future papers. 100% recommend her , especially if you're a freshman looking for ENGL101 and a great professor.
Took english 101 with her and man she was a hard grader. Not everyone is going to be born an author nor has the desire to be one. DO NOT RECOMMEND
Rachel is one of the nicest professors I've ever had. That being said, she is an extremely tough grader for a 100 level writing course.

Rachel (she tells you to call her that) is an incredibly hard grader for a baseline requirement class. Her lectures are long and confusing and she grades the class like a 300 level course. She's nice, but certainly not the best professor.
Very strict grader, nothing makes her happy
I took this class online and suffered. Its a lot of work! I recommend this class but not if you already have a heavy load. There are 5  required books plus other small readings.
The material for this class was interesting, many of the reading were good, but it was a lot of work and Rachel expect were very high. I do recommend this class but get ready to work!

Rachel is a good instructor, but the course-load is ridiculous for a 200 level course, and her expectations are very high. Overall I can say the class is fun, but when it comes down to grading you will get blindsided.

Hmm interesting..my higher  level course does not require the amount I've done in this class. Discussions are fun but if you are in need of literature credit, take someone else because this class is definitely not 200 level.

Rachel is fantastic. She's excellent at regulating discussion and encouraging ideas out of people. The people I talk to in the class agree that it's something to look forward to. Rachel's really understanding, and she clearly knows what she's talking about, especially if you ask her for help. Wish she taught other classes so I could take those!
She's tough but wants her students to work hard. Her class truly prepares you for classes 300 and up. If anyone has an issue with her, it's because of their work ethic.

Rachel is clearly excited about her subject. She expects a lot of class participation. She loves to hear everybody's opinions and gives a ton of feedback on essays. However, her instructions on the essay assignment sheet can sometimes be confusing as she expects the student to know how to do things that I don't think are taught until the 300 level

She is fun and enthusiastic about the material. She loves class involvement and encourages us to think outside the box. She is challenging, which is important at this level. She tells you what you need to work on and I will recommend her to anyone willing enough to progress in their education. I am a better writer and I have her to thank for that.
Such a harsh grader. A waste of time and money.

Rachel is one of those TAs that really knows that she wants to hear everyones side of the novel that was discussed and read during lecture. She is the one that you should try out in order to get started on discussion sections.

Most of your grade are exams which only cover about 25% of whats taught in lecture so its hard to study just from that. Only good part is the practice tests which are very similar to actual exams- it's definitely your best bet for studying. Homeworks also take lots of time and again only like 25% if the homework content is actually tested.

reviews.comment: long and boring lectures that don't help with exam content whatsoever, it's more beneficial to teach yourself the entire course instead with the textbook. along with that, has clicker questions during lectures to make sure people show up. only benefit is a built in 10% curve into the syllabus (aka 60% is a C- to pass)

He has an accent that makes lectures almost impossible to understand. His lectures have ABSOLUTELY NOTHING TO DO WITH HOMEWORKS. Lectures are a waste of time. Worst class ever. Unless you have taken chemistry before, do not expect to pass this class with this professor. This class basically just shows how good you are at teaching yourself chemistry

This class is insanely difficult if you haven't taken chem before, his lectures are long and unclear, and he doesn't seem very hopeful for anyone's success; half the class risks failing and he tells them to "do better." There's no way around buying the textbook, so get that $90 ready, and get ready to spend hours teaching yourself.

reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Vedernikov is very likable and his exams are fair. The online learning experience was rough but he made it doable. Be sure to study the old exams he sent out and prepare for the exams because they weigh much.

Vedernikov genuinely knows what he is talking about, so don't be afraid to ask him questions. However, getting by with only his lectures will be extremely difficult. The textbook will definitely be helpful for passing his exams. He also has clicker questions for easy points at the start of almost every class so attendance is basically mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing professor. Lectures were engaging and clear, and very open to questions. He grades very fast and the practice exams are extremely helpful. Overall super nice person who wants his students to do well and I would recommend taking his class.

He has a pretty thick Russian accent that I honestly couldn't understand. He was amazing though, when I told him I was struggling, he basically started tutoring me one on one in his office like twice a week for free. Great, caring guy, just difficult to understand. He's also extremely intelligent but doesn't show off.

I took AP chem in high school, and I still didn't do well in this class.  Vedernikov has a monotone lecture and he barely actually speaks into the mic, so trying to hear his lectures is difficult.  The lectures are only mandatory in the sense that he has clicker questions at the beginning and sometimes end of class but he posts his lectures online.

Vedernikov is a great professor. Clear lectures, very approachable for office hours. He really knows and loves chemistry, yet isn't a showoff. You learn a bit about every element on the periodic table. Periodic trends are covered in depth. Some of the "random" tidbits you learn here actually showed up on the Chemistry GRE!

Think of the worst possible teacher ever . . . now Vedernikov is 20x-50x worse.  No effort to help students, horrible office hours, lectures cover NOTHING relevant to the exams, no exam curves, and just plain aggrivating.                                 AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Class is useless except for clicker questions. You either have to know the material, or work really hard to teach yourself. If not for AP Chem in high school, I would have been screwed.

He is the best! He is really helpful and he posts all of his old exams. His tests cover all the material of his past exams, so there are no curveballs on his tests. Attendance is mandatory, since he gives clicker questions. I got an A in this class, but you cannot be lazy and must work hard. If you fail, it is not his fault, it is your own.

First of he really does care about his students. I have never seen a teacher grade exams and post students grades so fast so that is great. His 3rd exam was really, really hard. I dont know where some of those questions even came from. If you want to do well you have to go to class and work hard on the homework. It helps. Overall it was an ok class

He's a really nice guy. Some concepts he explains well, some not so much. Attendance is necessary because of clicker questions (this sucked at 8am). However, his exams are pretty easy because he gives you a practice one for each that is essentially the same. Not too hard to get a good grade.

regardless of other peoples comments,i think tht he's the best professor i could have for chem he could hve a accent but thts rly e z to get over with if u rly want 2.His lectures can be confusing sometimes if u dont attend lectures regularly!! Extra credit is also available on the exams & he gives a previous yr exm 2 study which r r'ly gr8.TAKEHIM

He is AWESOME!!!!!!The absolute best chem professor at UMD. He makes sure that everyone understands before moving on with the lecture and always welcomes questions. Come to class, sit in the front, read the textbook and do the practice problems and you'll have no trouble getting a good grade.

I was shocked to read some of the comments people had written. It is rare at UMD that you will find a professor that is as dedicated to helping his students understand the material as Dr. Vedernikov. He is extremely nice and very approachable and despite his accent makes the most difficult concepts easy to understand.Pay attention and youll do well
Hard to understand.. I didn't get anything out of going to lecture.

This guy is the BOMB. hes so chill, laid back, and a frieken genious. i remember him never saying 'i dont know' to something anyone asked. and hes always willing to help. yea he is kinda quiet - you need to sit in the front or good luck. and he has a thick accent, but u get over it. he has his own quirky sense of humor :)

His class rocks. You have to do well on the first 3 exams, and especially on the first exam. Don't blow off the first exam or any of the regular homework. The final is harder than you expect. He sometimes gives extra credit on the 2nd or 3rd exam. Read the material beforehand, especially for the first 2 exams.

this man is so hard to understand. not just because of his accent but because what he teaches in class has nothing whatsoever to do with homework given or what is on the tests.  i had to withdrawl from the lecture to ensure that i wouldnt get an F.  the book is where the real learning comes from.  horrible professor, switch for your own sanity!

In 4 years of college, and I have never had a prof. who was this bad. Dr. V.'s lectures are confusing, and do not relate at all to homework. He is very quiet and if you sit more than 5 rows back, you can't hear him. The exams had little to do with lectures. You have to teach yourself. Take Dr. Eichorn instead.

Attendance is mandatory, might as well do something productive. He focuses on specific things in the book, so just bring the book with you to class, and take general notes. do the problems in the book, and read it, it's the only way to learn well. he is hard to follow, but the class overall is easy. remember to sit in the front!

This man is a genius. He is really smart, and he is really passionate about Chemistry. He has a strong accent, but this is really easy to get over if you actually attend lecture. He's a great person, and he really cares about your grade if you talk to him. Just stay focused, he curves if everyone does bad, and he is genuinely a great person.
HORRIBLE!!! Switch professors if you want to pass general chemistry.

Horrible. Make sure to study from the book. What he goes over in class has nothing to do with what is on the homework and tests. Make sure to study the book and do not rely on the practice exams...they are useless.
attend lecture, sit in the front, take notes, do the book problems, and you'll be fine. he is helpful if you ask questions, and he cares about students understanding the material.
... strong accent .. not loud enough... does not know how to teach. office hours were useless.
Ugh, horrible.

Dr. Wu is a very supportive profession! This course can be quite challenging, but Dr. Wu and her TAs offer many different avenues of support that are very helpful. This class covers a lot of complex content, but staying on top of your notes and using the resources available in this course makes learning the content much easier

Dr. Wu is one of the best and most caring professors I have had the honor of having a class with. Dr. Wu genuinely cares about her students more than any professor I've had in the past. Ample opportunity for extra credit and to show your work ethic. This course is lecture heavy with difficult material make sure to be prepared and dedicated

Dr. Wu was a breath of fresh air in comparison to other upper-level science courses. Her lectures are given from a point of passion and love for the field of molecular biology and she has those same traits for her students. If you put the effort in, she will see that and do everything she can to ensure you do as well as possible in her course.

The content in this course was at times, a little difficult. But because I had Dr. Wu, I felt that I was supported through out taking the class. She was very accessible outside of class through emails, zoom, and also held office hours every week where she would sit and answer many student questions regarding homework assignments or lecture material

I really liked BSCI410 with Dr. Wu! She cares a lot about her students and is passionate about the material! The assignments were mostly applications than about memorization- exams were open note (and only the best 2/3 count, including the final), but you want understand the material well for them. Extra credit for the group project was generous!

Dr. Wu is the most caring and considerate professor I have had at UMD. She genuinely wants to get to know her students outside of class and has a very evident passion for genetics. Her exams are hard, but she gives opportunities for extra credit. This is not an easy A, but Dr. Wu makes it possible for you to succeed if you put in hard work.

I loved BSCI410 with Dr. Wu! Dr. Wu is very kind and truly wants her students to succeed. I always went to her office hours, and she is very willing to help and gives great advice to students. My main technique during studying which helped me succeed is to rewatch the recordings and write notes/summaries on top of the slides! Amazing class!

Dr. Wu is hands down one of the nicest and most caring people at UMD. Her exams can be a little tough but this is a 400-level course. Records all her lectures. Very lenient in terms of turning in late assignments and gives a lot of opportunities for extra credit (HW, exams). HUGE CURVE at the end of the semester.

This is a very interesting course! Dr. Wu incorporates a lot of real-world connections/applications. Although there is a lot of material covered, the exams are open-note and have built-in extra points. She is also a very understanding teacher and will work with you to help you do well. There are also a lot of extra credit opportunities!

I loved Dr. Wu for BSCI410. She did a great job explaining the different concepts of molecular genetics. Molecular genetics can be very complicated , but she was very accessible outside of class. Dr. Wu always came into class wearing a smile. Her cheery disposition was very infectious and made going to class early in the morning fun!

I loved have Dr. Wu as a professor! She was also very attentive to her student's needs! During office hours, she always made sure to speak to every student that attended do if you had several questions she would always try to answer each and every one of them.

At first, I was very intimidated by her class due to the complex subject matter. However, I expressed this concern to Dr. Wu, and she was extremely helpful and receptive. I always get nervous talking to professors, but she helped me to calm my nerves and create a plan. I would sincerely advise students to meet with her- she does want you to succeed

I highly recommend taking this course with Professor Wu. She is a very sweet professor who genuinely cares about her students' success. The course content includes quizzes, homework assignments, clickers, and exams. The exams were tough, but they are open-note, and the lowest score gets dropped. There are also plenty of extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Wu is an extremely fair grader and lecturer. The content can be difficult, but she drops your lowest of the 3 exams, a couple homeworks, a couple quizzes, etc. Chances are, you are taking her class because you have to fulfill major credits (like I did) but as long as you attend lectures and study a fair amount, you should do fine in this class.

Dr. Wu was one of the most approachable and kind teachers I had at UMD. The subject is hard but Dr. Wu gives you a lot of resources to do well on her exams and has office hours before exams where you can get a lot of your questions answered. You have to study hard but overall I learned a lot and feel like this class has prepared me for grad school.

Honestly dont understand all the 5 star ratings, she is so incredibly out of touch with deciding which she should give as assignments and quizzes. Not to mention her actual lecturing is pretty useless but you still have to go class to take the graded for correctness clicker questions that she puts up for 30 seconds max

If you plan to take BSCI410, you should definitely take it with Dr. Wu. She grades generously, and offers extra credit/drops assignments! You will have to put in your share of the work, but if you need help she is super accessible. If you are a bio major trying to choose your genetics credit, take 410 with Dr. Wu!

Dr. Wu is a very caring and understanding professor. She wants her students to succeed and is always available to help and listen to student feedback. She covers a lot of material in lecture at a fairly fast pace, but she provides opportunities to ask questions in office hours, on Piazza, or via email.

This class is doable as long as you listen to lectures, ask questions, and are organized. Her class is lecture-heavy, however, there are recorded zooms that you can watch before/after to make sure you understand the information. Dr. Wu also is accessible outside of class to help with homework assignments, test preparation, and lecture questions.

Dr. Wu is helpful when students are interested in learning the content. She is open to scheduling office hours. The exams were open note, but students still should review the material before they go into the exam. I personally thought the first exam was harder than the second, but other students in previous semesters disagree. The exams are fair.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: BSCI410 with Dr. Wu was one of the most fair courses I have ever taken as a bio major! She truly cares about her students and takes time to explain things and ask for student feedback. Her grading structure allows you to absorb the information without being overly stressed about memorizing the tiny details (exams and assignments are open note).

The content of BSCI410 can be difficult to understand but Dr. Wu is great at answering any questions you may have. Dr. Wu wants her students to succeed, she even reached out to the students who didn't do well on her first exam to see if there was anything she could do to help.

Pretty content heavy course, but professor was incredibly helpful both in class and during office hours. Dr. Wu quickly and is really nice :)

Lectures are fast paced so highly recommended to clear them up via email/office hours as well as reviewing recordings when possible.

Dr. Wu is a super caring professor who will take the time to help you if you are confused. The lowest exam is dropped and there is an extra credit assignments available. On the other hand, her lectures and assignments can be a bit confusing in the wording, so make sure to ask questions. Use your resources and you’ll get the grade you want.

BSCI 410 covers a lot of material which often doesn't seem to fit together. However, Dr. Wu’s lectures cover all of the relevant information for exams and she wants her students to excel which is evident by the amount of extra credit offered and her willingness to assist with homework questions.

BSCI 410 has a ton of content, a lot of which is new technology/concepts that weren't covered in BSCI 222. However, Dr. Wu records lectures and posts slides which makes reviewing material easy. Also, she is really good at answering questions about lecture material/homework in class and in office hours. There is also extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Wu is a great professor and person! I took BSCI410 and the content itself is difficult. However, Dr. Wu makes herself available if you ever have any questions or need help. I have never had a professor at UMD that *actually* cared and is as considerate as Dr. Wu. If you put in the time and effort you will get the grade you desire in this class.

Dr. Wu's wording can be a little confusing at times, but she overcomes this by being SUPER available for students to clarify material and questions regarding the HWs. She's a super nice professor and offers a ton of extra credit to boost your grade. Definitely not easy material, but Dr. Wu tries to make it easy to get a good grade.
Definitely a caring professor! Take advantage of the extra credit assignments and use outside sources like the textbook since the lectures aren't always super clear.

Dr. Wu is genuinely so kind and cares about her students. Her lectures can be a bit confusing at times but if you ask for clarification after class or during OH you should understand the material fine. The textbook is helpful, use it! Dr. Wu offers plenty of office hours and is available on Piazza constantly! Many extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Wu can be a little confusing in lectures, but going to office hours really helps because she can give better explanations then. I didn't really like the textbook, but other people heavily relied on it. She gave a lot of extra credit opportunities and tried to make the class as fair as possible. In general, she's a very nice person.

I absolutely love Dr. Wu! She is the sweetest professor I've ever had at UMD, and she really knows her stuff! The material is pretty hard to grasp at first, so I HIGHLY recommend going to office hours and asking questions on piazza. Exams are challenging, but fair and based more on applications - lots of extra credit. Make sure to study a lot tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Interesting class and really kind professor. Truly wants her students to succeed and gives chances for points through clickers, homework, extra credit, and dropping your lowest scores. Dr. Wu is very knowledgeable about the content and super helpful at office hours - many times even a simple 5 minute conversation greatly improved my understanding.

Dr. Wu is such a kind person but her dictation, confidence, and complete explanations in her lectures lack so much. The fact that she never speaks in complete sentences but with so many "commas" did make gaining the information very confusing. Puts too much additional information in her slides.

Dr. Wu is a really nice lady and great professor! The material may seem overwhelming at first but she gives tests that are open note and a lot of extra points! She is very friendly so if you need any extra help don't be afraid to ask her! Participating in class will get you on her good side.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is a really good professor- she cares about how her students feel, she is very accessible, and she has clear expectations for the class. If you meet those expectations of watching lectures, doing assignments (there are a lot but mostly participation), going to office hours every now and then, you're in good shape to do well in her class!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is a good professor and actually wants her students to succeed and understand the material. Her lectures are sometimes difficult to understand ( it is a tough topic overall), but she is very helpful during in-office hours. She is really nice, but to get a good grade, you really need to know how to apply the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is very accessible outside of class! She's incredibly caring and wants her students to learn as much as they can. Open note exams, but you should definitely still study for them. Her homework allows for unique application of the material and it helped me understand topics a lot better!
Dr. Wu is great! Her lectures are really insightful and informative. Later in the class, she has some really interesting lecture topics.

Dr. Wu is my absolute favorite professor at UMD. I've never met a professor so kind! She really cares for her students and wants them to do well. She was always accessible outside class and she creates an environment where it's so easy to ask questions! Three exams offered, but one is dropped. Difficulty is on par with other upper-level bios.

Dr. Wu's lectures can be hard to follow sometimes, but she records lectures and is always approachable during class and office hours for questions. Like what many others have said, she is a caring professor who is willing to work one-on-one with you during office hours on topics or homework questions you found confusing.

Dr. Wu is a really nice professor and very friendly to approach. Lectures can be dense but you can always ask questions if you're confused. She does offer some ec opportunities which really help. Studying and making sure you know the material before the exam is very important even though exams are open book. Really nice professor!

I had Dr. Wu for both HLSC322 and BSCI410. Her lecture style has improved extremely since HLSC322 and she is an excellent professor. Her lectures are now very coherent and easy to follow. She is very nice and super approachable outside of class. Her tests are a bit tough but fair, and test real application of content.

She was an amazing professor for BSCI410. She was able to easily communicate the topics of the class and go into detail during her lessons. At times she does tend to talk very quickly but if you ask she will always slow down and re explain anything you don't understand. She is very approachable after class and during office hours.

Very sweet lady whose grade distribution is very significant of how the class will take course. If you put in work yourself you will do great. Amazing professor who cares about her students and will go out of her way for her students

Dr. Wu may have rambled a bit in lecture sometimes, but I went to office hours with Dr. Wu, and she was very caring and wanted her students to succeed. She is very knowledgable, and things made much better sense when she explained them one on one. I encourage you to take the very poor reviews lightly, as I know many of them are extremely biased.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Despite all of the bad reviews, i found that she is actually a very nice person. it's true you might not get or understand what she teach in the class right away ( I mean, BSCI410, what do u expect), but try to go to her office hour. I found this very helpful bcs she can go over each slides that you don't understand and teach you in more details
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu was never prepared for lectures, and it doesn't really seem like she knows what she's doing. She tests on obscure material that doesn't reflect what is covered in class.

reviews.comment: Lectures are mostly useless. She is not a good science communicator and does not have well prepared PowerPoints or delivery. The textbook is your only hope to learn the material but that doesnt mean thats what will show up on the tests.

Unorganized powerpoints and lectures. Actually has no idea what she's talking about sometimes and has stated mid-lecture "I don't really know this that well so you should probably google it" and then moves on. Tests are bad assessments of knowledge and real application of information often goes untested.

Disorganized lectures. Doesn't seem like she knows what she's talking about. Tests are disorganized and test on minute details instead of actual concepts. Discussion is a waste of time but the only easy points in the class

reviews.comment: Dr. Wu is remarkably disorganized and a poor lecturer. Her tests are clearly unfair, with seriously vague questions. This class is emotionally draining.
