reviews.comment: Quite possibly the worst professor at UMD. Does not know how to teach any of the information and seems like she doesnt know the content herself. Grading is completely arbitrary, tests do not reflect material learned in class, and other assignments are useless and not helpful.
made course seem impossible and intimidating. does not post ANYTHING on canvas, insists on meeting individually, which is unnecessary. would not recommend to anyone.
Prof. Williams is very experienced in the journalism world, but I would not recommend this class, or him, to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor makes the course harder than it needs to be. He doesn't put assignments on canvas so the criteria is super vague. Most of the lectures are about him and his experiences and writing. Some of the assignments were also about him too, which was a little weird.
The best on the whole campus

Wayne is awesome. One of the best courses at UMD.  Take his class. Real teacher. Real topic (book banning). Not politically biased. He takes on book banning from all sides, gives the legal history of obscenity laws, psychological/sociological aspect, etc. Also read (sometimes) some kickass books.

Passed with A. 2 different weekly assignments based on books to read, some papers and one small exam/quiz. Do all assignments and try your best to get best grade. Very understanding of students, light grader. Very funny, tries to engage class. Would take again for sure. Do not be afraid, he is good. Class is an eye opener. Engage in discussions.

Wayne is a passionate educator that truly cares about his students and the course material. He praises your work and offers clear feedback on what can improve. Lectures can be a bit boring but I thought it was worth it just to listen to him chuckle at his own jokes.

Dr. Slater is an amazing educator. He is so passionate about his craft that you can't help but go along with him. He doesn't care much for strict grades, but that's not to say that you won't learn; he is an incredibly educated and gifted teacher. I highly recommend his Forbidden Books course.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Slater is an incredible educator. He is passionate about his class and his students and he does everything he can to help you learn. His lectures can be long-winded at times, but much of the class is spent in group discussions. The most challenging part of the class was the amount of reading. We had 9 young adult novels plus the course text.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Truly a passionate and thoughtful teacher. Assignments are abundant but manageable. Would take his class again in a heartbeat.

Slater is awesome. He kind of drones on sometimes, but if you actually listen to what he is saying, he makes a lot of sense and will make you think. I took his censorship class (edci288w) and he was very fair, and his co-instructor or GA or whatever was also awesome (James Groff- they make a good team).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Slater is one of the most understanding, kindest, and helpful professors at UMD. I took his EDCI288W. There were things that frustrated me about the course, but overall, I found it a very enjoyable and engaging experience.

Dr. Slater is such a nice professor and so helpful. He really cares about what you learn in the class and he wants you to be interested. If you go to class and pay attention you will do well. Dr. Slater is very passionate about the subject that he teaches and about teaching in itself. I encourage you to take this course.
What a gift from the academic gods!!  A pure treasure.
Awesome Professor, loved this class. A lot of useful strategies for future teachers on helping kids learn how to read. Keep up with the readings, and attend class, easy A!

Dr. Slater is the best professor I have had at UMD. He is extremely knowledgeable, helpful, and caring. I will continue to email him with any questions I have throughout my career because he is an amazing resource for advice and expertise.
One of only 2 professors I actively sought for more courses in undergrad or grad school.  A great teacher.
Dr. Slater's a great professor.  He's very knowledgable and gives practical classroom applications.  Assignments are pretty easy.  Highly recommend!

Lecture is set up as a "business meeting" which really is consumed of turning and talking to your neighbors, then discussing points as a class. All of the cases we studied were 10+ years old, leaving them essentially irrelevant. Grading was never clear or had any real rubric

Wesley and his class are both awful. I'd rate him ZERO if this platform allowed it. He has absolutely structure for his class. He is very hostile and rude. His only resort is encouraging a student to withdraw and not flexible in exploring other options. "Turn and talk to a neighbor" were mentioned a minimum of at least 11 times in a SINGLE session.

Wouldn't round up my grade after I was 0.1% away from an A- then proceeded to send a nasty email to all students stating that he would not round up grades no matter what and to not email him or else he will lower your grade unless its for a miscalculation.

Compared to most other 495 teachers, Wesley is the best. Clear instructions and explanations, fair grading, and the group projects are very manageable. Overall no complaints, lectures are a little boring but that's mostly because of the material not his style. Very knowledgeable and helpful with feedback.

Professor Wesley is very knowledgable when it comes to company strategy concepts, but the lectures were presented as if we were part of a business meeting rather than a classroom. He's a pretty lenient grader and the projects are pretty engaging. Overall, he's a solid choice just make sure you do the work and ask questions during lectures.

I love this professor! He cares deeply about his students and goes out of the way to help them learns. Do your best in each assignment and you will get good grades. Definitely participate in class and you will be fine!

He is not the most exciting lecturer, but you can tell he is very intelligent. He looks stern but he is happy to answer questions. It can be hard to know exactly what he wants from you on individual assignments but don't worry the group assignments save you if you don't do as well on individual ones.

I did not like this class or the professor. I think he put the least minimum effort into teaching the course. I was at B + even before he curved it and he claims he curved the class. He is not considerate of people who just feel shy in class to speak up. Very subjective grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I usually don't write reviews, but I wanted to leave one for him. Dr. Losert was one of the best professors I had in undergrad. Physics isn't really my thing, but he made the class fun and easy to follow. His exams were fair, and he gave partial credit as long as you showed your work.
Worst teacher i've had at UMD

Okay, may be the worst teacher in the world. but if you have any prior physics knowledge, TAKE THIS PROFESSOR, HIS CURVE IS RIDICULOUSLY RIDICULOUSLY HUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUUGE. I CAN'T EMPHASIZE THAT ENOUGH. I got like a C average on every exam, and bombed the final, and got an A in the class!!

This guy, seriously?  He's the nicest guy in the world, but sadly he can't teach at all.  He is very nice and cares about his students, but the lectures are useless.  I had never taken physics prior to this class, and I had no idea what was going on!  Don't take this class if you are looking to get an A.  Take Hailu Bantu or another professor.

Losert is an ok guy. Physics 161  overall is a hard class both to teach and learn. Do the mastering physics homework it saved my grade. The tests are HARD. The final is quite possibly the hardest thing i ever saw. The class is curved greatly though so that will help. go to class for clicker points and he is quite funny

As others have said, his curve is ridiculous. You can get a 68 on a test, and that's an A. Unfortunately, he doesn't teach at all, so don't even expect to do that well on his exams. Do not take him unless you already know physics or are willing to learn on your own.

I loved Losert. As boring as his lectures were, and even though he didn't really know what he was doing half the time, he was still ok. His curve is amazing... sets the average to a B. I got a 65 on a test which turned out to be an A. LOVE his curve, and he really wants his students to do well.

if u read the book and compare to his lectures, it will quickly come to your attention that he barely teaches any of the stuff u need to know for his tests.  only for those with enough motivation to read the book.

Relatively easy exams in comparison to his assigned homeworks. He can't teach though, so there's really no point in going to his lectures unless you want to earn "clicker" points. Not recommended for someone that has never taken any highschool physics.

Nice guy but he makes cool stuff boring. I really wanted to understand the subject... I didn't even need the credit, I just wanted to learn. I sat in the front row of the huuuuuge lecture hall but I ended up falling asleep. Sorry, dude... I felt bad but you can't keep me awake? He does let you make up late work and redo papers... like I said, nice.

this prof. is horrible-I do not recommend him at all..he is nice but he does not know how to teach. The exams are difficult and have nothing to do with lecture. Dont take physics with him unless you want to go home and do all the work by yourself. he gives alot of HW too ..

THis professor is a nice guy but his teaching skills are poor. He doesn't do examples in class and he seems to get confused about what he is talking about sometimes. Try not to take this class with this professor unless you are good enough to learn physics on your own.

I love this professor she is an angel and so smart and passionate about her work. The reading assigned is very intense in volume, but if you have a genuine interest in mythology it's worthwhile. I found the content very enjoyable. Lecture is not mandatory but I would recommend going there is a lot of important information covered that's on quizzes.

Ton of assigned reading! While lectures are not mandatory, you really should go if you don't fully take the time to read all the material. Professor Wasdin herself was nice and includes modern examples to engage the students and make the class a little more interesting. I found lectures are just boring if you do all the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Wasdin is smart, considerate, and passionate about classics. Her class certainly isn't easy, but Wasdin is always more than happy to answer questions, give advice, or even read and review your work outside of class. The readings can be dense and dry, but Wasdin helps this by interacting with the material and breaking down topics in lecture.

I enjoyed this class and learned so much. It was easy to get points because there are weekly responses and quizzes and they helped keep me accountable. There is a lot of tough reading but its easy to research them to understand better. Some papers that were a bit tough but nothing bad. Very fun elective and super informative

Prof Wasdin is super sweet and down to earth and you can tell she cares about the topic. other than that the class is basically on you. she has awesome and clear lectures that reflect exactly what her quizzes and assignments are. just a lot of reading but if you're into mythology itll be easy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she structured such an interesting course! our assignments were rly engaging and thoughtfully designed: create own translation, comment on other translations, etc. really unique latin class! she was kinda condescending towards our comments in class if they werent right, which is the point off. but she's a generous grader, smart, funny, & thoughtful

Professor Liu is my lab professor. He often tells students “just don't make mistakes”, when I attended his office hours and asked a question he simply told me “you made a mistake” then walked away. I also witnessed Professor Liu laugh in a students face asking “are you slow or stupid? Do you go to class?” when the student asked a question in lab.

Professor Liu is a very good professor to take. He is super caring and wants to make sure students succeed. If you genuinely put in effort, and do all of your work, it's almost 100% sure you'll pass. He makes tests fair and will even occasionally curve depending on how the class does as a whole. Absolutely recommend!
Just enjoy his courses!

Fluid mechanics is one of the hardest ENME3XX's in the major. Liu did his best to make it manageable. He spends a lot of time on derivations, but he boxes the relevant equation at the end. You can ignore everything up to that point. His derivations are usually wrong anyway, you'll catch plenty of mistakes. His example problems are good though.

FYI: I took this class in the summer. Professor understands it's a hard class and tried his best to have everyone pass. However, he's not a great teacher. Most of lecture was him deriving equations and then a few practice problems (what you need). We had one big group project, a couple labs, 2 exams, and a quiz every class (again, summer class).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures are so long and boring. You cannot take good notes because of how fast she goes through them. The final exam is completely based on the textbook where she makes us read 20-30 pages before every class. The exam was strictly memory based off of the study guide. Her grading is also off. Not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is the absolute worst. I signed up for this class because I thought it would be interesting and fun but it was the total opposite. Lecture was so boring and she went through slides way too fast. For the exam she said if we studied the study guide we would pass but majority of the questions I studied weren't even on the exam. Terrible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: literally the worst. lectures were so boring even though the content could have been extremely interesting. assigned 50-75 pages of reading a night and gave us quizzes on the reading that were extremely specific- down to words on a single page.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Quiz every day and the questions will be from a quote that you breezed over on the 7th of 60 pages you had to read that night. The "textbook" is not actually a textbook. Also she is extremely boring! The material isn't hard she just makes you not want to learn it. 3 papers that you turn into one long paper at the end. And a pointless group project.

She is known for assigning 50 pages of reading before every class, and then giving a quiz to complete one sentence from on page of the assigned 50. She has also managed to make extremely interesting course material dull and lifeless. It's almost impossible to be able to sit through an entire lecture without zoning out.
She was such a difficult professor to have. The exams were very test heavy and such a BIG portion of the grading. She would drop 1 exam and a few quizzes but it still wasn't enough to pass the class
I loved the topic of the class but it was difficult!!! The exams are heavy hard! If you want to pass this class go to office hours but this class will take a lot of your time to study

She grades harshly + exams are hard.

wouldn't recommend. tests are difficult. lecture slides are somewhat confusing and don't explain things well.

reviews.comment: This professor is new and is still trying to figure things out, but if you're struggling and reach out to him he'll help! He does care about his students and wants you to do well, you just have to put in effort. Calc is hard, and it can be hard to teach it, but I think you'll get out what you put in.
The questions on the quizzes and exams are very hard.
Doesn't explain things in an understandable way AT ALL. Every homework question had complicated answers that are hard to enter into webassign accurately.

Dr. Williams is a great guy. If you show that you care about the class (by going to office hours, going to lecture), it will pay off and it makes the class less difficult and less daunting. This was the hardest class I took my freshman year first semester, but it's manageable with effort. Exams are frequent so stay on top of work by ASKING FOR HELP

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM. I attended every lecture, had a strong friend network, and was a straight-A student with AP Calc BC credit—still brutal. He's an AMAZING person, but exams are unpredictable and overcomplicated, pacing is extreme, resources are lacking, and other Calc 3 professors had much better outcomes.

Very nice and kind guy. He is a good lecturer, but his tests are very difficult. Knowing the material is NOT enough; you will also need how to know how to decipher every word problem known to man. The class average for our first test was 42% (and he doesn't curve). My roommate's class with a different professor had an average of 80%
Class is super hard, but he gave us cookies a week before finals to soften the blow, 4 stars
Terrible just terrible
Such a good professor, just go to class and do the assignments and you'll be good for the exam. Lots of homework, but you'll get used to it. Also recommend going to his office hours.

reviews.comment: Do NOT take him, I never had anything below an A for math in hs and this was my first math course, skipped taking math115 cs of scheduling and had to take math140 bcs required for major, hated it more than anything. He is such a wonderful professor but so strict. Had a few extenuating circumstances stances but he made my situation harder :(

His exams are ridiculously hard. No amount of practice problems they provide will prepare you for it. I received a D on my first exam, so I decided to drop, as I felt I understood it much better than my grade suggested. I took this course with another professor and got a B+ overall with a much better understanding of the material. Just a bad prof.

Really good guy, but really bas professor. I had to miss a test due to school excused reasons and let him know 3 weeks ahead of time with a signed note asking if it was ok to make up the test the following day. He made me take the test in the middle of a lecture in the front row facing the lecture so he could watch me for cheating. Do not take!

Dr Williams was excellent! He's very charismatic, and puts in the effort in lectures to help you understand the material with examples. Sometimes he skips topics, which can hurt your understanding for the Webassigns, so make sure you have a good TA. The test questions are copied from worksheets and the textbook, so do the practice problems too.

Worst prof ever. Went from never having anything less than an A to almost failing this class. His lectures he spends doing 1 or 2 problems, only writes on chalkboard, horrible notes, messes up the due dates for almost every WebAssign, & at the end he made us do group hw where we had to find people... idk. Do not take him if you can prevent it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Lot's of homework, but it will help you in the end. Attendance not mandatory but if you don't show up, good luck. Lectures are really good, he writes on the chalkboard very big and clear, his voice is easy to hear. He doesn't do a lot of examples but he goes through each one that he does do very thoroughly. He isn't hard, the class is hard.

I honestly don't know why Dr. Williams has so many bad reviews. He's a great lecturer and explains everything really well. If you pay attention in class, and redo the problems done in the lecture, the ones he suggests in the lecture, and the ones suggested in the syllabus you should honestly be fine. Take him!

He's fine most of the semester, but the last two exams were awful because he didn't know how to teach the content. Furthermore, he gives like 10x the amount of work in the last week (!!when we should be studying for finals!!).

The only reason I took him is because the way he weighs his class is more fair than other professors.

I learned that attending his classes is essential. Math is a subject where regular attendance is crucial, and he stresses this point. It's plain and simple: understanding math requires effort and practice. I personally found that the more effort I invested, the better my grades became.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: WebAssign is the worst. I'm not sure if it's the professor's fault but its graded, takes a ton of time and is not a useful for tests and just makes learning more difficult and take longer. The professor is good but most of your time spent learning is own your own no matter what professor you have. They all use WebAssign and give the same exams.

The professor says to read the book and do practice problems because they are the most important but they are not graded. He picks a couple problems from the web assign and book to go over in class which are not helpful for the graded homework or test. The book is very difficult to follow. The classes are very fast and confusing. Tons of webassign!

Good lectures, easy to reach outside of class. He did have a lot of tests and quizzes but they were all practically identical to the problems he does in class and the practice exam. Some of them are literally EXACTLY the same as practice exams, I'm talking same numbers, wording, and EVERYTHING. You'll probably pass if you just go to class #bars.

his lectures themselves aren't that bad. But it's him. He suggests that you should go in for office hours but he isn't helpful when you're there. I went in and he told me to just check over my notes and asked how I even got the answer for my homework. The class itself I will say his practice exams are useful but I think I'm just bad at calculus.

He is a great lecturer he speaks clearly, has good hand writing, and explains content very well. His tests are extremely hard. The questions on the test were often nothing like the suggested problems from the textbook so no matter how hard you studied the textbook problems you would still do poorly. To get an A you have to put in a lot of time.

Dr. Williams was an exceptional lecturer and 100% knew the content he was covering. I really liked the way he handled the class and felt like he gave me a great understanding of the content. The tests are really difficult and word problem heavy, but if you study they are definitely doable. Highly recommend Dr. Williams.

One of the hardest professors to rate.  Among the best lecturers in the math department, and allows some class time for problem solving in groups (huge in a class centered around proofs).  Exam problems are selected directly from a given list of practice problems.  *Very* tough grader though, and does not give much of a curve, if any.

His exams are poorly written as they are nothing like what is given to you as practice problems. You know the exam is poorly written when the average of the exams is so low, yet the attendance to his classes remains consistently high. It is disheartening to spend days practicing problems and studying only to get a grade in the C- to F range.

Honestly not a bad professor. I see why a lot of people may not like him, but he certainly isn't your worst option. The fact that he's young helps out a lot. The Matlab isn't bad if you know what you're doing or have friends that do, the homework is tedious but not too intense, but just beware of the final.

The first week you have a quiz on precalc, but gets added as extra credit. His exams are very hard, but he does take them straight from the textbook and webassigns, theres just too many to do all of them again before the exam. Lectures are thorough.

As long as you go to lectures, complete the homeworks, and do the practice problems, you will be fine. His tests are very fair and there were never any surprises. 4 midterms and one final, so it helps you keep up with the information. I loved his outfits too.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not the worst MATH140 professor, but certainly not the best. My TA did a better job teaching the material than the professor for the most part. There are 4 midterm exams throughout the semester, some of which are hard. Two worksheets and homework assignments per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall a pretty cool professor, and was ok at teaching the material. He copies textbook problems and puts them on the test so as long as you're doing all the required work and study diligently you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Williams was a solid lecturer and very accessible outside of class in-office hours. Super nice and chill guy as well, I enjoyed his lectures and would take the course again.

Literally one of the worst professors I have ever had. Claims that if you need help to come to office hours, when all he does is bash you when youre there. Ive never met a professor be so inconsiderate when seeing a student put in so much work. If you cant make it to class have fun getting notes from someone else and it not making much sense.
as long as you read the textbook and do the hw, you'll do fine on the exams. super chill guy and easily reachable. good handwriting too.

He's a really nice professor, and explanations are good. Also most people who give hate, probably don't listen during lecture, cause most of his exam questions are literally copy-pasted questions from the book. He even gives a list of suggested problems, and if you do that + WebAssign properly, the class and exams should be easy enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Decent lecturer. He writes definitions on the board and then does problems related to the definition, but doesn't really try to make you understand the definition before jumping into the problems. TAs do a good job of explaining content which he doesn't have time to explain (classes move fast). Regardless of lecturer, course content is tough.

Worst math professor in department. If you have to take him then wait a semester. Hes extremely disrespectful to students and clearly doesnt know how to teach. You can get the answers form him for exams and it wont matter because hell still give you no points. Avoid this man at all cost, he doesnt know how to run/teach a class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy, so I wont give him a 1, but this was definitely the hardest class Ive ever taken. He was also very hard to communicate with regarding how he grades and didnt tell us anything useful about a possible curve. Barely a C- class avg I think.

reviews.comment: The exam problems don't look like anything you'll see in lectures or practice problems. All the exams had to be regraded to bring the class average to a 50% because the questions are all overly complicated and you don't get enough time. On one assignment the class average was a 2.2/35. The prof has no compassion or understanding, very unresponsive.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Williams is a decent lecturer, but his exams do not reflect material done in class or the EXCESSIVE homework assigned each week. If you do not have significant time to dedicate to Calculus, I wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Tests are completely ridiculous. The averages on the tests are always terrible and they drag down your grade. Quizzes were okay. MATLAB assignments and HW were easy points.
Absolutely ridiculous grading criteria. Average exam grades in my class were around 60, and that definitely wasn't because we didn't understand the material. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There are quizzes almost every week which are pretty easy. Oftentimes, the exam questions would be completely different from homework problems or problem sets but if you do all of the problems you should be fine. Write down every example he provides in lectures! The Matlab assignments are kind of a pain but they help your grade.

Honestly, Dr. Williams was an okay professor. He talks really slow so you can speed up your lectures to 2X the speed and knock them out. His exams were always difficult and he is really against curving. If you can do all of the problems on his problem sets, you will be fine. You aren't screwed if you get stuck with him, just prepare to work for it.

Dr. Williams clearly knows the topic well, but the tests and quizzes would alternate between being stuff we had learned about, and abstract ideas that we were somehow expected to be able to apply what we know to solve, all in a shorter time period than if we were actually in class. If you are exceptional at math, then you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Williams is a solid lecturer. His tests and assignments were fair and not too hard, but could be challenging at times. There was almost no graded homework, but you have to do the suggested problems to do well. His style of teaching is mostly writing down definitions and doing examples, but when he does explain things more, he does well.

Dr. Williams is clearly a good professor, I just found that despite studying more than 20 hours a week, most of the tests were still incredibly difficult, to the point where we had often never seen questions similar prior to the test. The class was online, which may have affected the overall difficulty.
One of the best professor's I've had at UMD. He made the class a lot easier than it should've been, and also writes down everything he says, which is greatly appreciated. Also, he's attractive

reviews.comment: The class would have been much harder if I hadn't already taken calc before. He is a pretty good professor though.

For a calc class, the materials was difficult coming from someone who had taken calc before but would not say the class is impossible. The teacher, in my opinion, was approachable and good, but I you have to put a good amount of effort in this class

I went from pre-calc to his MATH120 class. He writes out the definitions but then jumps straight into practice problems without taking time to explain them. I had friends in the class who had taken calc before and assured me that I wasn't just slow and that he made it more confusing then it had to be. The way he words his tests can trip you up too

Im the worst at math, I failed math 115 and was really worried about calc but I was really surprised by how well he teaches. reviews.comment: Dr. Williams is a great lecturer and makes everything much easier to understand. He's easy to get along with and a good guy. Personable and will help you as much as possible as long as you put in the work. Highly recommend.

Not many homework assignments given, but they were fairly difficult and time consuming. Quizzes every week were easy, but the exam were incredibly hard and weren't curved in most circumstances. He spends alot of time writing definitions in lecture instead of explaining the concepts and mathematical theory.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Pros: He records all his lectures and puts them online, so you can always review the material he goes over. Unfortunately, I think he spends too much time simply copying out the definitions for certain topics. Tests are also difficult in that the integration required is oftentimes long and tedious when the integration shouldn't be the focus

Williams is a really great professor. His lectures are very good. Minimal graded HW or quizzes in discussion. As a commuter student he's the best thing ever. Since he's my only class 2 days a week, I don't go and watch the recording later. Saves me 6+ hours in the car every single week, which lets me pick up more shifts at work. The best.

Dr. Williams is a great lecturer. He actually interacts with students and is always willing to help anybody with anything. However he will make you work for a good grade. His tests can be hard but if you do the hw and stay with the readings you will be fine. MATLABs and hw were meant to be a grade boost and they were so take advantage of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Inspirational

reviews.comment: JUST TAKE THE CLASS AND YOU WILL SEE. GREAT PROFESSOR... He is always available to help students. Makes material easy to understand and he fully prepares you for tests. He is the BEST professor ever!! Very fair, knowledgeable, intuitive, smart, receptive, relates well to all students with class material and socially as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: An OK lecturer. Lectures like a summary of a textbook, which was an unhelpful style for me. Hard tests: low highs for an H-section. I got an A for 90.5% (i.e., no minus), which I think was in place of curving. Justin has online 246 notes which were more helpful than the online textbook. Not great, but I'd not postpone taking a class to avoid him.

His lectures are very clear and detailed with numerous examples. He has 4 tests, 8 quizzes, 3 hw and 3 matlab assignments. He drops the lowest test grade and two quiz grades. Other than the tests, the assignments are meant to be easy and help your grade. His tests are difficult and he rarely curves but he teaches exactly what you need to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Lectures are heavily concept oriented. Lots of homework. Exams were not too hard. Quiz every week. Definitely not an easy A. If you are willing to do the work and actually learn the material well take him. concepts I learned here helped me a lot with my electrical engineering courses. Likable personality, and kinda attractive.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very swaggy dude (rocks a different pair of shoes almost every day). But on a serious note, his lectures and his ability to simplify complex mathematical concepts are second to none. The one catch is that his exams are extremely difficult and require a complete understanding of concepts. But overall it's worth it.
He's an amazing teacher and a great lecturer. Really knows his stuff. That being said, the midterms (we had 4 - the lowest grade was dropped) were extremely hard. This is not an easy A at all.
Had him for 310 and loved him, can't wait to take Math410 for him next fall. He is a great lecturer and lenient grader.
Easiest A in Math241. He does not give "-" grades so you need a 90 for an A. Removes lowest test grade. Quizzes+Homework simple and easy. Final curved.

Dr. Williams is a great lecturer, really good at describing the physical interpretation of concepts so that they can be easily visualized. Tests require studying but are fair, took Calc 3 in high school but didn't feel I really understood it until taking Dr. Williams's class. Pay attention in class and do the suggested problems and you'll do well.
Awesome guy. Really helpful. Logic mind. Great personality

Dr. WIlliams is a great lecturer, really cares about his students and truly understands the material and is great at breaking it down into concepts that are easy to understand. Quizzes are easy if you do suggested problems, Tests are pretty tough, but its a hard class so what do you expect. Office hours are very chill and worth while. TAKE HIM

Nice guy. He takes too long doing problem examples in lecture and writing definitions straight out of the book. Quizzes are easy if you do suggested problems (100% accurately) so get a solution manual (copy). Tests are not that great, however, because they do not reflect material learned in class/problems that well. Take another professor for the A

He's a really likable guy. He moves very fast in lectures, but he tries his best to make sure everyone understands. He only has a few graded homework assignments, but you'll have to keep up with the ungraded suggested problems to do well. He does drop your lowest test grade and 4 lowest quiz/homework grades.

He's very good at giving lectures and teaching material but moves incredibly fast.  Tests and quizzes are MUCH more difficult than anything seen in class.  Very harsh grader.  Took FOREVER to put grades in online.  Only take him if you are extremely good at math already

Great lectures. Great at describing what you should be visualizing. Seems to really care that students understand the material. Because of this the tests are hard & aren't congruent with study materials/example problems. Put a question on a test he told us WOULDNT be on it. Got an A in Calc1/Calc2/Diff-Eq; dropped this class. Take a different prof.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Du has honestly been the best math professor for me by far in college. Her lectures are so clear and her tests are pretty straightforward as well. Would definitely have taken her for Calc II if she hadn't stopped teaching it this semester. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. 10/10 recommend!
More than 90% of Prof. Du's Calc I students still chose her Calc II class. Calc II was a hard course, but Prof. Du made it manageable. Her notes were very clear and organized.

She is amazing, super sweet and caring, I took her for calc one and two and wish she was teaching three. She is an excellent professor, and extremely respected in the field. Her exams are easier than the norm, but the final was still managable, because she taught us so well and prepared us for everything.
Professor Du cares the students, knowing our names after day one. Her explanations are very clear. She also provides solutions to all tests, which are extremely useful. Highly recommended!
He is awesome, helpful and a bit tough too. Great experience.

This professor gives tons of homework like 27 questions with 15 questions which are similar but require a rediculous amount of calculation. I stay up late to 5:00 a.m. to finish it but his TA only pick five questions to grade. A minor mistake would be -0.1 for 27 questions but it can be -0.5 for 5 graded questions. You easily lose your point.

This is not your average math class. Just to start it off, you have two papers for the class - one 12-page, and one 18-page, as the midterm and final (also, written in LaTeX). We started with a class size of 20 and by week 3 it was down to 6 of us. Lectures were him writing down notes from another source on a paper for us to copy. Warning: No take.

Under no circumstances should you take a class with this Professor. Yanir is condescending, teaches by reading the textbook, makes you ask questions at beginning of lecture for participation credit, reads your questions and doesnt actually answer it (he often just says I dont know) and harshly grades you on 5 quizzes and one final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: the concepts in class are easy to understand and generally interesting, but assignments takes a lot of time (usually a few hours per week) and her system of grading is confusing. even if you follow the rubric for each assignment to a T, she'll find a way to be nit-picky and take points off for small reasons.

She is so incredibly helpful and gives great feedback. She allows you to get creative with assignments and is incredibly unbiased and respectful if you share controversial opinions. She is really knowledgable, and provides lots of materials to set you up for success.

Good, knowledgeable professor who cares about students. I took JOUR150 online-only; Prof Yotova always responded in a timely manner to my messages and took my concerns seriously. Has high but clear standards. Every week there is two of these due: quiz (50 questions), discussion post, blog post. Group project is challenging but straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Yaros did an amazing job with his approach to journalism, as a student who isn't majoring in journalism but was interested in the subject he made the class approachable, fun and amazing. Overall, i'd take this class again and recommend him to anyone!

Yaros was an incredible professor for JOUR479. I thought he did a great job explaining the course and doing a good job of breaking down tough subjects such as the Digital Engagement Model. Everything in this class builds off of each other so make sure to not miss class as there are presentations each week that require peer review. Great class!
He is not one of those professors who doesn't care as long as his work is completed. He is quite hands-on and I like that about him.
The course is structured that as long as you follow along well throughout the semester, you barely feel any stress at the end of semester.
Prof. Yaros is innovative, flexible, caring and really listen to students. He is innovative in structuring and delivering the course materials.

Dr. Yaros is passionate about what he teaches and genuinely cares about his students. He is truly committed to good teaching and learning! As someone who created their own media major and sought a mentor, I knew I hit the jackpot after taking his class. He is a once-in-a-lifetime professor, and I highly recommend taking one of his courses

Prof. Yaros is a chill teacher overall. The lectures are live and informative. The weekly quizzes come straight from the lectures. My main issue was that lectures were not posted sometimes and the quizzes were hard to do because of this. A solid class for DSSP/SCIS to take, definitely.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's a really understanding professor and really nice! He actually really cares about the class and won't mess with you. The class was also relatively easy, and all of the quizzes came directly from the lectures.

Professor Yaros genuinely cares about his students, and I find that one of the more important elements of a teacher. Through COVID he made sure everyone knew what was going on and deadlines were stretched to benefit the students. He genuinely wants the best of his students and you learn a lot. One of the best Merrill has to offer.

In a semester that was completely online, Professor Yaros worked hard to make sure we still got a quality education. It's clear he's passionate not only about his work, but also students' understanding of course material. He was accommodating to students' needs and concerns and made sure due dates and assignments were clearly explained.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Yaros is easily the best teacher I've had in terms of responsiveness to students. He truly listens to students' concerns and makes the appropriate changes. He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about what he teaches, and truly makes an effort to make the lectures engaging and interesting. An amazing teacher all around!!

I took his class during the COVID-19 pandemic when we were forced to move online. After moving online my grade rapidly declined. HE noticed, reached out himself and worked with me to get me on track with the class & receive a decent grade. Easily accessible but prep for lots of quizzes and disc. posts that will add up if you miss too many of them.

Very insightful class and extremely important stuff for todays digital journalism. Professor clearly knows what hes talking about, and is also very open to student opinions and suggestions. Im greatly appreciative that I had the opportunity to learn how to use the various analytics tools in this class - a must for any young journalist today!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Good professor, but what's best about this class is the content and what you learn that makes it so engaging. A little boring at times from repetition of course material. Professor very clear about expectations--people who don't do well generally aren't paying attention. You don't have to show to class but sometimes he takes attendance for points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: He is very engaged in lectures and passionate about the topics taught; encourages discussion, but your grade does not rely on it; very willing and wanting to help you be successful in his class and set you up for success in the future. There are weekly take-home quizzes that count as hw grades and a large group project. Periodic attendance checks.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests? Not many--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof Yaros is awesome and really nice. He wants you to do well, so he gives great feedback and replies to emails quickly. This class is all based on technology, so if you don't like technology, don't take this class.  As long as you put in an effort, he'll notice that and you will do just fine. No final, just a final blog post.

Dr. Yarwood was the best professor I had at UMD. Her lectures are fantastic. I would recommend her to anyone interested in microbiology and/or soil science.

reviews.comment: She is a very kind and respectful person. I found her class to be hard cause I am not a fan of microbiology. But she tries to make class fun for everyone. If you put in a little time, you will get an A easily.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. She moves extremely quickly and jumps from different topic to topic aimlessly. She sometimes asks people if they have any questions and then immediately moves on and doesn't answer any questions when people raise their hands. DO NOT TAKE!

there were no exams during the entire semester but one final exam(not online) covering the entire course material of the semester. Most students didn't study until the end for the final, do not fall in this trap!

reviews.comment: In my opinion, this was the worst professor I have experienced in my college career. Professor Zhou does not prepare for her lectures. Basically every lecture she just reads straight from her slides that shes posts or STRAIGHT FROM THE BOOK under the doc camera. Only took attendance the last 3 classes. Class is way too much content. Group projects are easy (go to her office hrs). Overall learned little to nothing but the content is difficult to learn w/o practice

Great professor! Poor english, irrelevant tests to textbook, can't answer questions properly.

Dr. Zhou is a good teacher but sometimes she has trouble controlling the class. I wish she would just tell everyone to shut up when things get out of hand. reviews.comment: Zimmerman is the teacher that everyone wants. Her lectures are interesting and her delivery makes them easy to listen to. She is an easy grader and gives very clear assignments. I literally have no complaints about anything she did this whole semester. She is really just trying to prepare you for the workplace. I am taking her again next semester.
She's crazy, but awesome...

How to get an "A" in KNES 350 with Jo Zimmerman: 1)Show up to class EVERY DAY and take the clicker quiz.  2)Put at least some effort into the paper (everyone gets an "A" if you follow instructions).  3)Study the and memorize the highlighted slides before each test.  Yes the class is boring but it's an easy "A" if you put some effort into it.

I dont know what the other kids are talkin about. Yes it was an 8am but if your in college stop complaining. Her clicker quizes are pretty easy and you can use everyone around you to help out. The exams arent all the hard she gives you big hints if you go to the lectures whats going on the tests.

These previous ratings are ridiculous. She is a great teacher, and she tries extremely hard to help you out. Yes, there are clicker quizzes, but why be in college if you're going to complain about coming to class? Most of the questions, she practically gives the answers. And the tests are easy, just study the slides.

I took her 8am psych sport class. SOOO BORING. You have to go to class and do the clicker quizzes that she does just about all the time. Her exams are a bit tricky so you have to read the chapters and study her power points to do well. Not much work outside of the exams though.

Took 3 week summer course. Not much work involved.  Seemed like she kinda just made up an assignment on the spot and had us turn them in the next day Weren't really hard assigments though. 2 of the 12 days we were in the gym and 2 days for midterm and final. In total it was like 8 days of actual class. Pretty easy A for a summer course.

Professor Zimmerman is the worst teacher that I have had at UMD so far. She reads straight from the power point lectures, and makes what could be potentially interesting information, boring. She is also unorganized and completely useless when it comes to using any online tools for her class. Avoid if possible.
Got A's on every exam yet got a B for the final grade because I missed numerous clicker quizzes and in-class activities.. material not hard but you HAVE to go to class to get an A...
No Comments

This was an 8am class, but she was one of those teachers who reads the powerpoints to you. The material seems common sense, but when you get the exams, they are tricky and ask random statistical questions. The first exam average was a D that had to be curved 20 points. The worst part of the class is that you are required to take "clicker quizzes."

Absolutely horrible...seems easy when you are in lecture and are reading the book, but exams are harder than the anatomy exams. Actually teaches content in lectures, and also has prerecorded lectures for MATH461, which are actually incredibly good for learning content and make it super easy to self-study. reviews.comment: The content of this class isn't too bad. The homeworks can take some time but they really prepare you well and ensure you know the content. The exams were fairly straightforward. Yashinski is always willing to help and replies to emails very fast. One of the best undoubtedly

Best math professor I've had so far.  Great lectures--records them for people who can't make it to class, explains concepts clearly while going over lots of examples, is also very funny at times.  Highly recommend.

Professor Yashinski's lectures were very good. Additionally, he has an archive of his lectures on Calc III from when he taught it online, and they are almost exactly the same as his in-person lectures. Tests were a bit easier compared to other sections from what I've heard (averages in the 80's and 90's), so we did not get a curve.
The GOAT teacher. Great lecturer - clear, funny, interesting. Fair grader and very understanding. Made me love math again.

I had him for Linear Algebra, and let me just say - this is the man you want! His lectures were incredibly clear and easy to follow and he did a great job refreshing us on concepts we learned earlier in the course that we were a bit rusty on. reviews.comment: Teaches very clearly. Definitely not an easy course, but if you put in the work you will leave the class really understanding the material. reviews.comment: Extremely clear and straightforward presentation of the material. You'll know your stuff after taking his course. Not a walk in the park though. You'll definitely have to prepare for his exams, but they are all a reasonable difficulty.
I learned a lot. The exams and assignments were all very reasonable. After taking this class, I have a very solid understanding of all the material we covered.

Pre-recorded lectures and open note exams were a lifesaver during this semester with online classes. Matlab assignments had instructions for each of the commands necessary for any of the problems, so no guesswork (unlike other math courses at UMD). He is also a very nice and understanding person. Exams are on the more difficult side.

Taking him for FALL 2020 was the best decision. All exams and quizzes were open note. The exams were take home style and for the final exam he offered 2 days to complete. His online recordings were the best! I felt like i learned more in the recordings then i did with other professors via zoom.
He's awesome. Super clear and well-prepared lecturers. Class is as difficult as you'd expect from the material. His tests are also appropriate in difficulty, relative to the material.

reviews.comment: Professor Yashinski is one of the best math professors at UMD. I took it online and his lectures were very clear and he had enough assignments to balance out the class. Homework was optional but you needed to do some to be ready for his fair, but hard exams.
Homework is not graded so do as much as you need to. Good lectures and exams/quizzes are relatively easy.

Yashinski is a great professor who knows his stuff. Everything is graded fairly, with quizzes and exams mirroring questions from the textbook. He was very accommodating during COVID and made our exams open note and let us have days to complete them. The conceptual questions can be tricky, but just make sure you understand the textbook concepts.
Very nice guy! Exams can be tough, especially the true and false questions because they are conceptual and there's no partial credit.

Amazing professor. He is very clear in his lectures and makes even the most complex topics easy to understand. Really cares about his students! His exams and quizzes are similar to the homework problems, so as long as you do them you should be fine. Highly recommend!

reviews.comment: I have never been strong on math but I think he really made his classes clear and helpful. He tires his best to explain the materials and is one of the best math professors I have ever had.

Dr. Yashinski is an awkward and amazing professor. He explains everything clearly in his lectures and he's really approachable. I took his Math461 course and it was great!! Im a Psych major and was able to get an A. He makes everything so clear to understand. Def take him!!!

reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Absolute favorite professor at UMD. He's a great lecturer and can make sense out of everything. No matter the question you ask, he has a simple answer and is very knowledgeable. He's also pretty funny. Honestly I just go to lecture to see if he can keep up his good vibes and amazing lectures. I actually hate linear algebra, but I just go for him.

Given that this was a really hard class and that I am not a STEM major, I struggled a lot in this class, and it was by far the hardest math class I have taken here, but Allan made it a lot easier for me to understand the material he was teaching, and he was very generous during office hours to help students and he always answered email promptly too

Allan is a great lecturer; very humorous guy and definitely knows his subject inside and out! Will be definitely taking another course with him if given the opportunity. May seem a little awkward at the beginning of the semester, but he grows on you :)
The lecture is really organized and clear. Undoubtedly great professor

Very nice professor! I have time conflicts with my cs class and his math class. But professor Allan provided me a lot of extra office hours by appointment. His test is easy! Most stuff just very similar as the class material. Would take his class again.

He is a young awkward guy and he is very smart with Math. He knows his stuff and he expects 100% from you. He gives a ton of homework problems that take hours to do. His lectures are helpful and are from the book. Don't miss any lectures or you will be lost. Especially towards the end of the semester when the material gets hard. Learned a lot.

Allan Yashinski is a fun teacher. His lecturing blows the sense of linear algebra into your face. He assigns lots of 'recommended' hw which is actually a good thing to do when taking his exams and quizzes. His exams are very fair so he doesn't curve at all. I find him to be awkward in a good way and he writes fast.

reviews.comment: He is great; very organized and excellent lectures. A lot of homework, but not unreasonable.

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgeable about all things East Asian history, so I highly recommend asking all your questions. Just try your best with moderate effort and participate to succeed!

Dr. Zhang creates some of the most coherent and understandable lectures I have ever seen. You will learn a great deal about the subject material and leave feeling hungry for more. So long as you do all the assignments with moderate effort, you can get an A.

reviews.comment: Professor Zhang is a great professor and I would definitely recommend her class. The lectures were always interesting and the workload was very reasonable. I learned a lot in class. Definitely a good choice for anyone interested in China.
Bobby is extremely caring and wants to help students understand tools that have real world applications. He is very sincere and wants to push you.

I could not recommend Bobby more. He genuinely cares about his students and is willing to go out of his way to help you in anyway he can. This class isn't an easy A but 100% take it with Bobby if you can!

Bobby is easily one of the greatest professors I have ever had. Not only is he super thorough with the lecture information and responds almost instantly to emails, but he REALLY cares about each of his students. He is always giving real world advice and remembers even the smallest of interactions with his students. I could not recommend him more.

Bobby not only teaches well but will go the extra mile to help his students. I don't think its easy to come across a professor as good as him. Overall, the course wasn't very hard and he even lets you take a cheat sheet for the final exam. SPSS is used as well but you just need to press a few buttons to get some statistical results.

Excellent professor. This class isn't easy since there's so much information to take in. Bobby actually applies what he teaches you to real life examples so you can better grasp the material and does genuinely care that everyone does well in his class and will give you tips to save money along the way.

This is the hardest marketing class Ive taken so far but Bobby clearly explains the material. All the assignments except the tests can be done in groups which is a plus if math isnt your strong suit. Without the formula sheet we got to use for the final Im sure I wouldve gotten a lower grade in the class. No such sheet allowed for the midterm.

I recommend any Marketing major take Bobby for Marketing Research. He knows what he's talking about and tries to make things easy to understand. The second half of the semester was harder and more of a statistics class since it was all math but since he taught us SPSS it wasn't too bad. He taught us how to save money too. Overall amazing job Bobby!
I'd take this teacher's class any given day again; She was a great teacher to have for my freshman year.
Lazy professor. Lets TA's do majority of the work, If you have a good TA, you'll be fine. I did not. Quizzes every class period. -15% of discussion grade if do not show up
Be prepared for the amount of workload in this course. Professor Zeeger was very passive aggresive, especially when it came to grading certain assignments. 2 exams, and a group project. Study!

Three-weeks. Zero lectures of any kind by Dr. Z. reviews.comment: Interesting class. Straight-forward class. If you take notes on the chapters you should be fine. There are group activities but not too bad. Prof. Zeeger is nice and gives opportunities for extra points.

After the first day I dropped the class and the waitlist for the class disappeared. Thats how bad this class is. The TA makes the class really hard because she makes it an English class. A very sincere and passionate teacher with an accent but if you can get past that, it's a wonderful class to take

*Highly Recommend* Professor Zur truly loves accounting and has an accent. He truly cares for all of his students and is great at teaching. My grade was made up of smartbook hws, three take-home exams, and a group project/presentation.

Really nice guy who just wants students to learn and do well. Easy grader even though the material can get tricky. Very accessible outside of class and is genuinely interested in students' academics and careers. Lectures can get hard to follow after 75 minutes but that's not really his fault, the material is just dense sometimes. Solid choice!

This man convinced me to major in accounting. The most down to earth and genuine teacher I have taken at UMD. He was always available for extra help. Ana was super nice! She's always willing to help students improve, but her grading can be a bit on the harsher side. Not an awful class though. She is very energetic and easy to get along with. Really makes an effort to get to know her classes.

reviews.comment: I love Ana, she's one of the best lecturers in the Spanish department. She is super engaging and really cares about her students. I truly loved this professor and this class. The professor is very high energy, which makes the class interesting and fun. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ana is an incredible professor who makes classes very fun in a way that doesn't make us learn any less. She is very diligent at explaining ideas and phrases that may not make sense right off the bat (as is the nature of a foreign language class) and grades very quickly, with ample feedback. A great, open environment to practice communication!!!

This is my second time taking Ana (311 and 301 previously) & there's a reason I took her again! Super chill professor, makes you laugh, grades ridiculously easy (like free A's: takes off a few points even if you screw up badly) Would recommend, but 311 is a time-sucker because you'll probably want to write a script before recording your videos ://

She was a great teacher, and my first formal Spanish teacher. Her class really inspired me to take up a Spanish minor, and now I'm even trying to see if I can double major with Spanish. Her class was my favorite class my first semester in college and I hope I can take another class with her some time.

I love Ana! She is such a nice teacher! She's a little tough, and expects you to do the work. But, the workload is moderate and doable. she is a very understanding teacher and teaches you how to speak spanish easily
Overall, learning from her was a pleasurable experience. She's a nice teacher. Not that much discussion, however. You mostly listen to what she's saying.
Very helpful class. Teacher is extremely funny and has a great sense of humor. Can be a little strict but learned a lot. Definitely recommend her as a teacher.

Do not take this professor's class. For a lower level elective that was supposed to be "literature and media" it was an extremely heavy reading load with almost no media. Do not take aaron's courses. I saw another review described aaron as pretentious and that is spot on. reviews.comment: I took CHEM131 with Stocker the previous semester and bombed it, so I had to repeat. Geller is honestly the most amazing lecturer I've ever had. He's hilarious, interesting, and made a class I struggled with and hated, easy to understand. You'll be so lucky to take him.

Let me just say Chem131 was my favorite class last semester. Let that just sink in. This guy is hilarious and makes understanding chemistry attainable and enjoyable. He knows exactly what to say to make the concepts click in students' heads, and if it doesn't click, he doesn't make you feel dumb about it. By far the best professor I've ever had.

I took chem 131 last semester with a different professor and had to drop the course halfway through the semester. When I say Geller took one of the hardest courses at UMD and made it understandable, HE TOOK CHEMISTRY AND MADE IT UNDERSTANDABLE. Honestly if he's an option I recommend taking his class.

I took this class with a previous professor and had to drop it halfway. But Dr. Geller is the best CHEM131 professor at UMD. You won't regret. He's your best shot at actually understanding and passing chemistry. A bonus is that the dude is Hilarious. His lectures are often filled with laughter. I wish he taught ORGO too.

Geller made the lectures interesting for all. He even had funny intermissions in many classes. At some points he did go slow through material, but in the end we covered everything necessary. He put at least one super hard question on each test (supposed to be thought provoking), but in the end he curves 5-7 points so it makes up for it

Dr. Geller is the best professor I have had so far. He is the nicest, funniest, and most understanding professor who is always willing to help out, and even occasionally gives tips for lab. He made college chemistry 100% less dreadful than I had anticipated. The class is curved a lot at the end, and going to class is definitely worth it.

Chemistry, one of the most difficult general courses out there. But I certainly made the right choice with Dr. Geller. He was a wildcard, this was his first semester so I chose to flip a coin when choosing him because he had no track record. I made the right choice, he is the best person to teach Chem. I never understood Chem, but take HIM!!!!!!!!!

Dr. Geller's probably one of the best professors here at UMD. He's an extremely funny and cool guy. It's chemistry, so of course it's going to be difficult. But Dr. Geller is extremely good at explaining concepts and he genuinely wants his students to succeed. He makes every lecture interesting and easy to follow along.

Dr. Geller is the absolute best. Take chem with him! This was my first chem course ever ever and I learned so much. He is very clear in explaining concepts and truly cares about his students. He makes many office hours to explain concepts. He also emails back very quick which is very nice. Great teaching style, goes slowly and clear. TAKE HIM!!
A newer teacher, but he does his job very well. He's got a great sense of humor, and his lectures are clear and easy to understand. Sometimes he goes a bit too slow
He isn't perfect but he's your best shot at getting an A in Gec Chem 1

Enthusiastic, intelligent, but very old man. He loves maps. He also really loves flying through his powerpoints to explain them while you're left scrambling to write things down. He can speak perfect Chinese. :) Go to lecture because he doesn't post notes online, and there is a LOT of material. Very friendly. Great if you ever have a question -- his enthusiasm for the subject really shines through. Dr. Aftab's class was my favorite class of the semester. They're a new professor but they take feedback very seriously and try to improve their course. A lot of reading here, but Aqdas is a really nice professor that cares about their students and what they teach. Class discussions are thought-provoking and I would highly recommend taking any class they teach.

Aftab is the most wonderful professor. They truly care about the content they lecture and literally always respond and understand everyone's ideas.
