reviews.comment: Aqdas is Amazing. Love them to pieces. Accommodating when needed, even helped to plan against class anxiety. Their lectures are more discussion-based, but this is good for the content. Would take them again if I could.

Professor Aftab is an incredibly accommodating professor. It is evident they care for their students and want them to succeed. Every class I left excited and ready to learn more. I enjoyed their class so much that I made sure to look for classes they would teach fall semester. I would definitely recommend taking a course with them.
Afrouz managed our lab and was very helpful between classes. She provided very helpful feedback that helped me get a really good grade.

Afrooz is a really helpful infrastructure. Her level of knowledge in math is amazing compare to his experience as a non math major. In contrary to other math professors and number of students, she structured the time outside of class to be always available for any extra help. I recommend taking the course with her if struggle with math.

The first day of class she put on 2 videos to explain the topic. She vaguely answers questions. Get ready to teach yourself! She won't answer your question,figure it out. There's homework everyday but she assigns things she didn't teach. The class isn't hard if you have the right teacher. I literally had to teach myself. & decided to drop
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Aggour is a very knowledgeable and respectful professor who creates a positive and inclusive learning environment for students. He explains difficult topics in a way that makes them easy to understand. Exams and homework assignments were fair and similar to what we learned in class. 100% recommended!
One of the nicest and most understanding professors I have ever had. You will enjoy your time with him.
He is a nice and kind man. One of the bestest at the department ...
Best teacher i have ever had. Period.
good teacher overall, always last in class, first to leave, kind of hard to understand at times, exams ok
He is a knowledgable gentleman. Not mean at all!
He is a man

I did not once leave lecture understanding something that I didn't understand prior. Genuinely the most boring and difficult lectures to pay attention to. He starts class with everything already written on the board in a huge mess, and just reads it without actually showing anything to you. Exams were easy but you have to learn from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had a good time taking PHYS373 with Prof Agashe. Regardless, this is not an easy course and you have to put in the effort, i.e., do the homeworks. He held review sessions before each exam which was very helpful. If you can, take this course with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: You will be very far behind in the schedule very quickly. Frequently unclear in speech, unhelpful in answering questions. I slept through about 15% of this course and still knew almost all of the material on the tests because you will only learn and be tested on the bare minimum while he sludges through the other 80% of lecture.
only 20% of the grade is not a test or final, but he heavily curves everything so it works out. the grade you get may be good, but you won't learn

We are only 5 weeks in and he goes so slow we are two weeks behind. it would be okay if it meant he went over everything clearly but that's not the case. I've never thought it was possible to go so slow and be so bad at teaching

Her lectures were unbearable and pointless. I ended the class with an A only because I took AP calc in high school and studied everything I could from friends with resources from other professors teaching the class. Gave two stars instead of one because the mandatory online homework from a math site helped.
Would not recommend. Comes to class unprepared and rushes through important content. Does not prepare you for exams.

She didn't teach the material correctly if you take her you will be teaching yourself and the exams don't match the content she teaches. If you take her this class will be harder than it should be I have to attend summer school to recover the grade I got in this class.

Class is extremely difficult, awful administration makes it 10x worse. Don't take this class because you will have no free time and the teaching staff don't do much to help you succeed. Awful project descriptions, mostly unanswered Piazza, unclear grading, unaccommodating, no study material. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do not take CMSC 412 if you are allergic to C programming. Stop taking CMSC 412 and call your doctor right away if you experience kernel panics, as these may be signs of a rare but serious hardware problem. Common side effects include insomnia, headache, nausea and diarrhea. Ask your doctor if CMSC 412 with Dr. Agrawala is right for you.

I think he was an effective teacher. He asked questions to get us to think and to understand why things were the way they are. Lectures were dry, if you read the book, but the point was to give us the basics, not the details.  Exam questions were taken from the book. The projects were there to teach protocols and difficulty of net programming.

He's a solid educator. He clearly knows a lot about the subject he teaches. He says he's a tough grader, but he really isn't. As long as you pay attention and do the readings, you should be good to go.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Readings are long and participation is crucial so u have to talk at least once in class. No quizzes or exams but small essays and then a midterm and final paper. Cares about thoughtful analysis so its helpful to pay attention in class and use the arguments from class to help flesh out ur writing.
If you are looking for a teacher who treats their class as if it is life-saving material and you are a Ph.D. student, this is your guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Got way more out of this class than I thought I would, she's an awesome teacher.
Quizzes and tests are super difficult and confusing. I would have gotten an A if it wasn't for the final exam

I took Emotion with Heather a few years ago. I didn't major in philosophy, and it was an upper level course so it was challenging. But, seriously, she made this class FANTASTIC! It been like three years and I still think about it. Figured I should rate her because I honestly think shes one of the best teachers I had at Maryland.

I took Phil 100 and thought it was great. Shes super enthusiastic and always gave good examples in class to make hard material more understandable/relatable. The slides dont have a lot of info, so you need to go to lecture, but overall I learned a lot about things I had taken for granted, will look for more of her classes

I took philosophy through popular films with her and I am highly satisfied. She made the class look easy despite the fact that It was a very complex topic. She highly responds to student concerns. This makes her available outside the class. She also provides excellent feedbacks. I would take her again!
She is really understanding and makes learning fun

Lectures are very boring, but you should still go because she covers things that could be on a quiz in discussion. TA's grade papers harshly and don't tell you how to improve your grade on papers. Reading material is lengthy Discussion sections are not mandatory but there are pop quizzes and participation points
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: WORST CLASS! There are 3 papers and never goes over how to write them. The TA's grade them way so harsh. When you ask for help on the paper it is like pulling teeth, no one wants to help you. Her lectures are so boring and she just reads from the slides. There are quizzes in discussion and you never know when. SO much reading of difficult material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: The kindest professor I've had. She ended every class reminding us we are capable of anything and that she believes in us. Attend class and you should have no issues with the class or tests since she hints what she'll be testing. Highly recommend her class if you want to learn Excel by someone who knows everything about it and to gain a mentor.

Took class with her last fall. She really knows her stuff. Her lectures are clear/engaging.She always gives hints about what will be on exams. Accessible outside of class and genuinely wants her students to succeed.I highly recommend if you want to learn Excel from the best and gain mentorship from someone with extensive knowledge of the job market

Incredible professor and person. Wish I could take her class again. In addition to class content, she gave me really good advice for internships and future career paths. Made herself accessible to me outside of class. Couldn't have asked for a better professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best professor Ive ever had. Goes above and beyond to help her students and she is so kind. She gives great guidance, and takes the time to get to know all of her students and remembers everyone's names. She gives hints on what will be on exams in class so anyone who says that her exams questions are random I can guarantee you did not attend class.

I'm honestly surprised by all the good reviews. I'm almost done with the course and still have learned nothing in that class. She also never has your grade displayed on Canvas so you never know what your grade is. Most of your grade depends on the exams which are hard. I hate this class.

Love this lady! Dr. Karake is enthusiastic, knows her stuff, keeps students engaged, and clearly wants the best for each of her students. She regularly provides interview tips, offers opportunities to get certifications, and reviews material repeatedly. Dr. Karake's love for Excel and Tableau is contagious, and I had a lot of fun in this class.

Very nice professor. If you haven't really been exposed to Excel before, this class can get extremely difficult in the middle and end of the semester. We learn about Excel and Tableau.

She is patient, approachable, and accommodating.

Great teacher and person. Super nice and engaging HOWEVER the exams are wild. Huge curves on there, out of no where questions etc. My friends and I in the class would commonly joke that it wasnt worth studying because it basically isnt. Can bring in a 2 page sheet into exams but the questions are so random its basically worthless.
She was great!

Karake is such a sweet woman who takes the time to learn all her students' names and makes the class engaging. She has done so much in life which makes her extremely knowledgeable about the subject. Always go to TA office hours for the Excel projects and you'll do fine. The exams are kinda difficult but she allows cheat sheets.

The sweetest professor who really cares about her students. just go to class and pay attention to excel content. She pulls from the textbook and allows a cheat sheet on the test. Projects aren't that hard and there is one final group project.

Class is supposed to be how to work Excel. But she has readings about random business strategies that have nothing to do with Excel. Those readings gone over the first 10 minutes of class and then spends the rest of the time working excel. Shows functions once and is mad if you don't see how. Her exams are 57% and they are based on those readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great professor. Incredibly knowledgeable about Excel. No surprises on tests if you attend lectures.

Awesome professor, loves to teach. Remembers students' names. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you want a good grade, make sure you show up because she gives hints in class about what to focus on in the slides and textbook for tests. Anyone who says she has "gotcha questions" most likely didn't attend class regularly. Happy I took her class.

I learned so much more in her class than just Excel. She made the subject interesting, was accessible in person or via email even on weekends! Incredibly knowledgeable about Excel but also gave me a lot of advice regarding my degree and future career options. She's caring and funny. Would absolutely take another class with her if I could. Take her!

She's one of the best value wise: she prepares you well for the excel certification test and has lectures that are in touch with contemporary issues. As a class, it was at times disorganized and some Qs on exams were made so that you would have to know obscure details from the textbook. Overall, she's very charismatic and respectful: a good choice.

she is very energetic, but her lectures are not organized. exam questions are SO specific and you basically need to memorize everything from the slides and textbook. She also can be pretty rude sometimes for no reason and won't be sympathetic if you don't understand the material. The TAs are really helpful though (especially for the projects)

I have never struggled with a BMGT class as much as this one. Karake makes the excel projects very hard and she never responds to emails. The lectures are basically just her reading off the slides. exams are difficult and contain very specific questions from the book. Even accounting is easier than this

Dr. Karake is easily one of the best professors I've had at UMD and she makes sure to focus on what you will actually use in your career. She clearly loves teaching and makes it clear how much she respects and appreciates all of her students. Her class is my favorite every week!

Karake is a great professor! She has so much energy when she's lecturing which makes them more interesting. Walks you through excel and projects aren't hard as long as you pay attention and go to class. Would love to take another class with her. I definitely recommend!

A caring professor that shows respect for her students (reciprocated). Lectures and textbook heavy on exams, but not too difficult. Easy projects throughout the semester. Easy class as long as you show up and are prepared for exams.
Awesome professor. Dr. Karake is incredibly engaging during class and really makes sure you learn the material. Absolute no-brainer for BMGT301, this class was awesome.

Very knowledgeable in her field and will always have an answer to your questions. Even if I rarely showed up, she remembered my name and always made an effort to include people in the class, but not in a confrontational way. Exams cover a lot of the information from the book and I'd recommend going to class if you want to be prepared. Take her!!

Karake is my favorite teacher that I have had so far here. She focuses on making sure the students understand and has no problem going over something again if needed. Her tests are kind of random but as long as you pay attention and take good notes during lectures you will be fine. I highly recommend taking her, she made me love this class!

one of the rudest and unorganized profs I have had at UMD. the class was challenging but it didn't have to be. content was useless and outdated. wish she had gone over more excel tips instead of random slides.
tests are hard. so specific. I wouldn't take again
terrible. so rude. arbitrary grading. unclear expectations. a total mess.
She can do better

We had 4 projects, 2 midterms AND a final. She calls on people in class out the random. Most of all her class is just boring. She understands the topic but isnt the best person to explain the material so you have to read and do excel portions on your own.

Dr. Karake is incredible, inspirational, and cool! Her lectures are fun and engaging. The Excel skills are extremely useful and the concepts give a good general background to IS trends. Tests are very specific to the textbook/readings and TA office hours are helpful for the Excel projects. Definitely recommend taking a class with her!

Dr. Karake is the most phenomenal professor ever. She treats her students with respect and holds herself and her students to the highest ethical standards. She inspired and supported my journey to work for a top-level IT firm. Lectures are engaging, Excel skills are invaluable, and she is approachable inside and outside of class. :)

She is a "GOTCHA" professor, period. Can be nice but gets frustrated with students who dont know the answer quickly. Exams are TOO specific - you virtually have to memorize trivial things and the actual reading. She's incredible at Excel though. Group assignments not bad. She can be pretty mean sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took this class pre-covid. Had her at 8 am and she would take attendance and have pop quizzes sometimes (although relatively easy). You learn basic excel skills, and the class can be interesting. However, the final felt like a completely different class, as the content pulled random stuff from the textbook that wasn't covered in class, many failed

Dr. Karake is one of the best professors I've had at the University of Maryland. She is an extremely hard working teacher that cares whether her students understand the material she is teaching. She constantly asks if the concepts are clear to the class and has no problem going over things multiple times. I highly recommend taking her class.

she spent the whole semester trying to catch cheaters. ended the semester saying she is going to report a bunch of students. this woman does not teach AT ALL. her exams were impossible, she expects you to know the most trivial details ever from a textbook she doesn't even teach from. hands down the worst professor in smith.

Dr. Karake's class has hands down been my favorite so far. I wish I was able to take her class before covid because everyone says she is very engaging and a great lecturer. I learned the most useful things in her class and mastered Excel because of her. She is very well respected, caring and accessible outside of class. I highly recommend her class

Dr. Karake puts a lot of effort into her work and students and expects the same in return. Although her exams are tough, she is easy to reach and encourages her students to come to her with any questions and/or concerns. If you take her, you will gain so much more than the course material and you will also have to put in work for a good grade!

She is an amazing professor. I really enjoyed her class even though it was online this semester. I learned a lot and appreciated how accessible she made herself with online office hours. She would meet with me online one-on-one when I needed extra help before a test even if it was late at night. It's not an easy class, but it is SO worth it.

she asks random "gotcha" questions on exams so that she sets you up to fail. she doesn't teach at all and is extremely rude to students during lecture. her expectations and grading methods are unclear and I believe she curved grades down this semester. bottom line don't take 301 with her.

This class is a mess, especially online. She teaches Excel during class, but expects you to know random trivial bits from the textbook or slides on exams. She also tests Excel on exams, but you're not allowed to use Excel. It's really frustrating. She drowns you with redundant messages and honestly a lot of the time, no one knows what's going on.

I'm conflicted bc I love her as a person, she is VERY accommodating, however her exams are SO SO hard. The review sheets are completely misleading & have nothing to do w the exam. I studied SO hard and the questions were completely different to anything we learned in class/text. If you want to learn, take her but If you want an A, do not take her!!
She's nice but the exams are insane, and the level of difficulty is so much higher for exam 3.

Nice professor, Excel projects take forever. Her tests are absolutely insane though, in that you have to memorize every sentence of every chapter to do well. The questions (some are on topics we never learned about) are all "gotchas" and do a poor job of ensuring you actually understand the big ideas. Stay away if you aren't a good test taker.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Karake was great. You'll learn a TON about excel. It was disappointing that the pandemic moved everything online because her lectures were very engaging. The only downside I have is that the exams were extremely specific. You really do need to read the textbook before each exam

Karake is extremely knowledgable and the excel aspect of the class is extremely useful. However, her tests are ridiculous and don't focus on much that's actually gonna be relevant to 90% of the class. You can ace the quizzes, crush excel projects, study for days for the exams - but it doesn't really matter. Also makes 301 exams harder than 301F.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Karake is amazing. Exams are really specific and you should diligently read each textbook chapter before the exam. You will learn a lot in this class and very valuable excel skills. Lecture is very engaging and Karake does a great job of conveying course content. On top of that she is extremely caring and considerate with her students.

Great professor and one of the few who make lectures engaging. However, I worked pretty hard and had an A for the whole semester, but the final was ridiculously specific and my grade dropped to a B+. Very difficult to get an A in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Karake is the BEST professor I've had at UMD so far. Her BMGT301 is not easy, and the tests are pretty specific so going to class is very important. I did ok in her class but if I could take it again I absolutely would. She is such an enthusiastic lecturer and makes Excel fun and interesting. She's also super accessible outside of the classroom

I do not recommend taking Professor Karakes class. The tests (especially the final) were unreasonably specific and the multiple choice questions were often ambiguous. This was obviously very frustrating. I would avoid this professor if possible.

Dr. Karake is hands down the most incredible professor I have ever had. She is so energetic and passionate about the subject. Shes been a huge inspiration to me and I changed my major because of her. She is very accessible outside of class, and will make time outside of her office hours to meet with students if they have questions.

Karake is a really nice professor, she cares about her students a lot. She is extremely knowledgeable about the subject. Everything is great about her except for her tests. Her tests are so specific, they are not simply about definitions. You need to go to lectures, take notes. All of the questions in the test are not easily found in the textbook.

She expects a lot from her students, but she doesn't give clear expectations for what should be studied for tests. When you ask her for specifics, she gives vague answers and says you should know it all, which is unreasonable. She has lots of energy for the class, and you learn a lot on excel, but test expectations were unclear and that hurt people

She's very entertaining and the use of Excel is something everyone should learn the ins & outs of. She's very nice and if you see her in the building make sure to say hello because she will appreciate you for it.

Karaoke is a great professor. Her expectations are clear and she grades fairly. The exams aren't too hard if you study. She does care a lot about participation and takes attendance occasionally so I would show up to class. I had her at 8am but didn't mind because she makes the class engaging. Take it with her if you can.

She gave hard exams and hard assignments, yet I still enjoyed her class so much. She was super caring, passionate and was someone I could look up to. If you're struggling in the class, office hours are super helpful. But her exams were often unfair to me, as they were so detailed that there was barely any way to prepare.

She's an amazingly intelligent professor who cares for her students. If this is your first time actually using excel, definitely go to class. Her class is what made me want to major in IS/Ops! Tldr: excellent teacher and you should take her for 301
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Karake is awesome! She is so passionate about her subject and extremely knowlegeable. She is approachable and gives you great feedback. You need to work very hatd in this class. To be honest i was able to land a job with one og the big four based on what i learned in her class. I wish i could take more classes with her.

Karake is the best professor I've had at Maryland thus far. She is incredibly engaging, respected, and cares about her students. The material is easy; go to class and you'll have all the information you'll need to pass the exams. The Excel projects are simple. She cold calls in class, though, so do the readings.

Professor Karake was amazing. Go to class though, because she teaches Excel and Access in class almost everyday. If you read this review before classes start, then I would try and learn the basics of Excel, if you don't know them already. This class heavily applies Excel elements on exams and in homework. Overall she is a great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: I love her as a teacher

She is a great teacher who does her absolute best to engage her students, even at 8am. She's got a very impressive background but is extremely down to earth. So sweet and caring. The class is a mix of excel and access based stuff and lectures. The test aren't that hard. She puts a lot of stuff online but it still helps to go to class.

I took her for my information systems class and she is such a great teacher. She is fun, makes the lecture easy to understand and overall the class is not hard with her at all. There are Excel projects and 3 Exams but all of them are pretty easy. Also in the end there is a group presentation on a company of your choice which is also like an easy A!

A nice guy and can be helpful to students who show up to class. Outside of class he is rarely available/responsive to student needs. This is an easy class with a good intro to Android Dev, but prepare to teach yourself most things. Lectures are ineffective, but his code walk throughs help with labs and final group project.
Easy class. Eh professor.
Amazing Professor

Easy class but awful, irresponsible, ineffective (reads the slides at you) professor. Is very absent/selective about answering on Piazza, questions are left unanswered/answered past their relevancy. Class was a huge disappointment. The group project was the only thing worth the effort as that's how I learned the most (stack overflow/trial & error).
If you reach out to him he will help you no matter what. The most accomodating professor on this campus. I can not recommend him enough.

He teaches effectively and in a way that doesn't overcomplicate topics that don't need to be. His lectures were interesting for the most part. Super understanding about attendance and is willing to provide extensions on papers. He also drop multiple grades so the only way you could do poorly in this class is if you genuinely put 0 effort in

This dude sucks. Take his class, but be ware that it will be insufferable. No problem with the content, or the course load. He is just such a horrible classroom leader. I feel like this is a middle school classroom. Expect boredom and busy work. This guy has no idea how to engage college students and is a joke.

He's a great teacher!! His lectures are really interesting, he gives you the option to watch the recorded lectures rather than going in-person (although some lectures do have participation credit, so watch them!), and he's pretty funny. The 3 writing assignments are kind of hard to do, but the grading is very fair so it's not too bad. Great class!

Lots of writing assignments. Exams are pretty difficult, but great professor. Does his best to make lectures interesting and covers all the material, just a lot of material so exams are a little overwhelming. Readings every week that you must do because lecture doesn't always cover readings, but exams do. Really great guy, funny and there to help.

YOOOO ADAM IS THE BEST GUYS FR. HIS LECTURES ARE ACTUALLY INTERESTING AND IT WAS THE ONLY CLASS I LOOKED FORWARD TO GOING TO. TAKE PSYC221 WITH FACTOR. YES YES YES DO IT!!!!!! AND SO MUCH EXTRA CREDIT AND LOWEST EXAM IS DROPPED?? I AM IN LOVE WITH THIS CLASS AND PROFESSOR. GO ADAM!!! YOU'RE DOING GREAT!!!!!

Adam is one of the best professors! He's very clear with his lectures and understanding of each student. Flexible with anything you need, as well as giving you the option to watch pre-recorded lectures. Always makes everyone feel engaged and respected, 100% recommend having him.

He is a great professor and his lectures are engaging if you like general psychology. He is very understanding and will give extensions if you feel stressed. He engages the class and is funny and not monotone in his lectures. His tests are not too bad if you know the material and the assignments are graded fairly by the TA (I had Mackenzie).

The exams were graded pretty harshly, and often didn't give partial credit for things or the grade scaling was off. Homework was easy and very helpful, and there are rarely quizzes. I didn't go to lecture for most of the year, but reading the textbook and going over the lecture slides afterwards made it easy. If you can self-study, it will be fine.

absolutely horrific professor, never available to help, never considered student concerns, never replied to emails, created terrible lab videos and data sheets, laughed at students who asked for help, extremely disorganized and the TAs and her were never on the same page for anything. 1 exam is worth 33% of your grade and extremely hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is horrible. She doesnt teach, just makes her TA's do work which they don't do properly either. She wont even answer emails. Shes unorganized and takes off points for random things and doesnt give reasoning why. do not take her class!!!!

She had very fair tests, is willing to help if you reach out, and she was VERY accommodating during the pandemic. I think she's getting a bad wrap, but she really is trying her best and I think she's been very accommodating as is. Her accent can be a little difficult to understand, and her lectures can be a little funny, but she's a fair teacher.
what a nightmare. Guest's thinking: "hey why dont we make a final worth 33% of the final grade mandatory during a pandemic for a lab class." Worthless professor, inconsiderate and pompous

I can't really speak to Dr. Guest since the actual professor isn't really involved in CHEM132 and the TA has more control over your experience, but it wasn't that bad. Experiments aren't overly time consuming and despite the typos the manual is still pretty informative. Post-labs and exams are pretty tough, but the class is very generously curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Guest was the nicest and most caring professor I've taken at UMD. She genuinely wants everyone to succeed to learn biochem. BCHM463 is a ridiculously hard class no matter who you take it with but she makes it doable. If you work hard, go to her office hours and study you will do fine.

Guest is an amazing professor! Some people find her a bit hard to understand but I didn't have a problem with it. She's very clear otherwise and knows her material extremely well. She truly wants everyone to do very well so her office hours help incredibly much. Refreshing to have a teacher from the UMD chem department who actually cares. Love her!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Of course it is a difficult class but she wants everyone to do well and she is so friendly. If you find any reason to rate her poorly its because you wanted an easy way out in an upper level biochem class. Take this class with her! She has detailed lectures and her exams are straight reiterating lecture material. A true gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: exams are TERRRIBLE.

Lab was extremely TA-dependent but I had great TA. As for the professor, she was the one who made the lab manual and exams. Have heard some inaccessibility with her. Lab procedures had errors so it was confusing at times during lab. Exams were difficult, but reading the post-lab questions from lab reports help.

Only saw her once the entire semester I wasn't even sure she really existed until I saw someone in her office one day. A lot of work for a 1 credit class that does not remotely follow your gen chem lecture. Supposedly she is nice but her emails say otherwise.

All I can say is, if you have a good TA who leads your lab, and you know how to apply every single concept learned in lab for the exams, then yea you might be fine, but the entire thing is lead by the TAs and the professor lady only makes exams. The lab reports do take some time to do, usually 3 hours I'd say, but it is a 1 credit course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Too much work for one credit... ridiculous. You also have to pay an absurd amount of money to take the course (40 dollar lab fee, 50 dollar lab manual, a special 20 dollar chem lock, lab coat 15-20, goggles 10-15). Save yourself and take this course at you local community college.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Addei is a great teacher. I really enjoyed her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This instructor writes exams that are far too long to be completed during the exam period and which themselves are filled with typos and inaccuracies. She shows very little regard for the students and is by far the worst professor I have ever had. I would avoid taking another class from her at all costs.
Doesn't care about students

The midterm and final exams are nearly impossible and the material is not covered in the lab. The lab reports are difficult and some of them are quite lengthy. The workload is a lot for a one credit lab class and the grading is inconsistent. I do not recommend taking CHEM132 with this professor.

She is nearly impossible to contact, and the grading is greatly inconsistent because she does not grade your papers herself. The many TA's rotate class papers so you have a different grader for each paper, and the grading at times is very harsh. The lab manual has a ton of errors and is unclear, and the wording for post-lab questions are confusing.

reviews.comment: The lab manual has so many errors My TA was super cool but the other ones were super uptight. The labs are weird but if you go to office hours they basically answer it for you. Don't take lab on a monday bc they won't have the answers and then you're screwed. If the data doesn't make sense explain why or they'll take points off.

Don't take this class. I never met the professor and the class is run by TAs. Your grade in the class depends on the TA. The lab manual has an error every week. The labs require you to go to office hours every week and is a large amount of work for a one credit class. The midterm and final are impossible, studying won't even help. Good luck.

reviews.comment: The work for a 1 credit lab is a little much. My TA was extremely helpful, but it all depends on who you have. The lab manuals are poorly written. The exams are extremely challenging, but fair and the big curve makes up for this.

reviews.comment: Although this is a 1 credit class, it felt like a 3 credit class due to the excessive amount of work and time that was needed for each lab (1 lab per week). This class is run by the TAs. Definitely recommend starting your labs early and going to TA office hours every week. Midterm and final is hard and only 50 min long.

If you value your insanity, don't take this class. The TAs are dumb and don't know what's going on. The midterm and final are ridiculous and impossible to study for. I really wonder how this professor was able to get a PhD if she can't write grammatically correct sentences in her lab manual which costs way too much money and is mandatory to buy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: If I could give her a negative rating I most certainly would. SAVE YOURSELF THE TROUBLE AND DO NOT TAKE HER. TA'S dont know what's going on, she doesn't know what's going on, had it not been for a friend of mine who already took her class I would definitely have failed every single assignment. Exams are ridiculous and do not reflect labs
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: You never see Dr. Addei-Maanu, not once. The class is run by TAs and not well. My class was consistently without the proper instruments we needed to collect accurate data. The lab manual that she wrote is horrid, inconsistencies, incorrect and misleading wording and data throughout the entire thing. Mid-term and final are unnecessarily hard.

reviews.comment: If you study and work hard on the lab reports youll do fine. The professor is really hard to get in contact with. I kept having to re-email her as she wouldnt respond the first time. This class was also way too much work for a one credit class, and the grading is kind of picky. The class is curved, and the TA will give you points back if you ask.

DO NOT TAKE CHEM132 WITH THIS PROFESSOR. Her lab manual is poorly written to the point where you can't understand what she wants. Most of her TAs are useless and don't really care about the class, which has a big effect on your grade. The labs are unrelated to what you do chemistry lecture and the exams are unrelated to what you do in lab.

I have never once seen the professor, and she seems very inaccessible outside of class. She doesn't seem to communicate with the TAs at all. The TAs seem to care very little and are a little clueless. The manual is filled with typos, and what is expected on the tests is very unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This lab is SO much work for a 1 credit course.  The TA's were often out of the loop, many not speaking highly of the professor and said she rarely communicates.  Almost every lab had a correction that had to be written on the board, and the manual itself was poorly written with lots of typos.  Take this class somewhere else and transfer it in.

Extremely hard to understand her b/c of her accent which makes an already hard class even harder. Did not provide a study guide until third test which basically said memorize everything on the topics we've discussed. Homework questions do not help with test questions. Tests are long and hard and make up almost all of your grade. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I have taken many, many college courses and have two Bachelor's degrees and a Master's. She is by far the worst professor I have ever had. Unclear lectures, jumps around between topics, and hardly ever explains things fully. Homework has almost no relevance to test questions. UMD should be ashamed to have such a person on staff. Avoid if possible.

Shes a good Biochem Professor. Difficult to understand in class, but she is very helpful in office hours. The only thing that was particularly hard was her second exam which is the hardest exam I have ever taken. I would have studied for 3 weeks and still would not have passed it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She writes the lab manual, which is filled with typos. Grading is inconsistent. The exams are unnecessarily difficult and most kids receive D's. The class was curved like 9% at the end of the semester which was nice, but did not compensate for the lack of structure and poor quality of teaching. This class is completely based on your TA.

The Lab manual was poorly written. There was so many typo's and unclear questions. The questions also felt repetitive.  This was my first lab that I actually had to take 2 exams for. Failed both of them which brings your grade down a lot since it out of 100 points and labs are only worth 40 points. Too much for 1 credit lab.

This professor wrote the lab manual that is used, but it is full of typos, and lack of clarity throughout makes it seem like she is unqualified to run a class.  The TA that I have is the only reason that I am passing this class.

reviews.comment: feels like 3credit work for a 1 credit lab. I have never seen or heard back from professor addei when i've emailed, only my TA, who kind of has no idea what she's doing. they should train the TAs better because we've gotten bad direction several times that affected our grade because none of your work is graded by your own TA. curve? don't know yet.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: one of the most chill and kind professors i've ever had! so many extra credit opportunities that its easy to pass with over 100%.

Dr. Abi is an amazing professor and an amazing person. She is funny, very personable, knows exactly what she is talking about, and makes everyone who participates feel very valued. The tests are open note and open book, so if you read the book and pay attention during lecture you can get an easy A.

I have never heard anyone complain about Professor Nicolas. She was great when I took her FALL 2022 and encouraged me to stick with the psychology program. She tried her best to make the material interesting and related it to her real-life experiences.

She's amazing and cares about her students and their mental health. She's great at communicating and you can always expect an email back. She is very understanding for extenuating circumstances if you just ask. 1000% reccommend her, she is funny and personable and overall a great professor!
Dr. Abi is awesome, you can tell she cares about the students. Lectures are compelling and funny. Discussions are every other week. Highly recommend this class

This class in insanely easy and enjoyable, especially with Prof. Nicolas! She is so funny and she puts so much effort into laying the whole course out (what to expect, what to do/when to do it). I personally enjoyed how she structured discussion sections; sections would meet virtually every other week. Exams were also online and open note/book!
The professor is really sweet and tries to make the lectures engaging, but with it being online it was so hard to stay focused. Otherwise, the class is easy and I would suggest it.

This professor was awesome. Lectures were engaging, understandable, and gave you time to understand the concept, (visually, audibly, and kinesthetically). She was nice and gave the time to meet with you or address your problems, concerns, or even just comments about the class or other matters.
Very nice and interactive with the class, lectures are easy to follow and exams are all based on information she clearly goes over in class and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Don't know how anyone could not like her. She goes out of her way to give everyone an opportunity to do well in the class and makes lectures entertaining and relatable without being corny. She is also just incredibly nice.

I don't know what else to say but Dr. Abi is amazing, I wouldn't trade my experience in this class for anything. She's hilarious and makes the material so easy to understand with her personality and examples. Exams were open note and very straight forward and if they weren't, she would give points back for ambiguous questions. Loved this class!!

Exams online and open note! Very chill prof and easy class overall. Easy to reach via email. Engaging lectures, she tells jokes and relates the content to real life experiences! Textbook is online and completely free. Would take another class with her.

Dr. Nicolas is a kind and funny professor. She was always a few minutes late to lecture and had a bit of a focus on clinical psychology, but otherwise was excellent in all respects. PSYC100 was also very easy in that every assessment was open-note, so just searching the online (free!) textbook for key words tells you everything you need to know.

Prof. Abi is very understanding, often grants extensions, and you don't particularly need to attend lectures since her slides are posted online. Exams are open notes, online, and lowest exam gets dropped. There are bi-weekly papers (not too difficult) and discussions in class. Overall, she's a great professor and knows how to keep students engaged.

Prof. Abi made lectures interesting and engaging. Exams and worksheets are open note and usually don't have any short answer, but be sure to read the online textbook well and take notes. Application activities are interesting, and she posts her slides and lectures online for exam study. She's super down to earth--- would recommend!

I loved Professor Ades. His lectures showed that he was really passionate about what he was teaching, and it made it more exciting to learn. He was very responsive to student concerns and gave e me points back with no question when I had trouble seeing exam images during a midterm. Definitely recommend him!

The class wasnt bad at all! Lab was chill and Ades was pretty fair with the exams (they were all multiple choice for the online semester). I recommend that you write down everything he says during the lec videos, because his slides are just all pictures - youll be tested on what he says. The final is VERY SPECIFIC, so your notes will SAVE you.
Very caring man. Exams are on very specific details but definitely doable. Had a 99% all semester but the final was killer. Destroyed my grade
This professor is bad. For one exam 32 people received 100% out of a class of about 50. But I received a 66% studying hard and not being known for those low of scores when studied.

Terrible professor. Just blabs during lecture and doesn't teach. Jumps around from topic to topic randomly. Lecture slides are useless and he gives old exams for practice but no answer key. Tests are on specific details he mentions once and never again. Miserable class and do not recommend taking Dr. Ades at all.

Ades' class was one of the most challenging courses I've taken due to the sheer amount of info you have to know. He is very clear in what you need to understand for exams, and is passionate about what he teaches. I listened to his lectures after recording, *knew* them by heart to do well on exams. Final exam is an absolute killer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take BSCI433 if you are genuinely interested in cancer or the medical field, and are willing to put forth considerable effort - you will learn a LOT about oncology, from the field's history to mechanisms of drug action. Two free-response midterms (100 pts each) and a mixed-format final (150 pts) - you're allowed a single note-sheet for each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took BSCI 330 with Ades two semesters ago. By now, I have taken a lot of biology courses at UMD and hands down, this man is the best. His course is lecture heavy, but he truly knows what he is talking about. Very responsive to student feedback and you will walk away having learned something.

Dr. Ades is such an awesome lecturer. He let us use a "cheat sheet," so people could sorta blow off studying and get As on midterms (free response). They tried to do the same for the final (MC and super detailed, as he told us repeatedly it would be) and tanked. But 26% got A- and above--you can get an A if you attend every lecture and study hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Midterms were specific scored 100s on all of them. Final killed everyones grade. Went from an A+ to a B. Final was different format and different structure than all other exams which were free response. He opened up the final exam with "this exam should be thought of like any standardized exam/MCAT." Write down everything he says & good luck.

Final was awful, all multiple choice and ridiculously specific. The midterms are all short answer and I got As on all of them but I bombed the final so bad it dropped my grade 17% and I got a C for the class. Ridiculous, and not an accurate or fair way to asses how much we learned, only curves by 4% so lots of people failed DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS

Dr. Ades loves to teach and it comes through in his lectures. He is passionate about the subject, and he can make otherwise dull material crackle with interest. His stories are fun. He will tell you you don't need a textbook, but have one anyway. Study lectures verbatim to do well. His final is super tricky. Always pay attention to tiny details.

He is so awful! Avoid him!!! He is a nice man, but his exams are so hard and there are only pictures on the slides so if you miss something in class, there's not much you can do. There's also no textbook so you're pretty much screwed unless you have time to go to office hours (which I didn't).

Any class Ades teaches, you have to work for that A, that was to be expected. I learned a ton from this class and enjoyed it. However, in classic Ades fashion, he wrecked everyone on the final, but for final grades, he was really lenient. To do well, write down pretty much everything he says in lecture and memorize it.

Dr. Ades provides a lot of resources to get a good grade in the class.   He holds office hours twice a week and (for our class) would always give an extra ten points of credit for each of his 3 exams.  The exam questions were all written-response, but were to the point.  He posts powerpoint slides, but you have to go to class to understand them.

Took for BSCI330 in Fall 2010. The other reviewers must expect everything in life to be handed to them. Ades goes very in depth about topics, but this is an upper level class. Put in a decent effort to understand his lectures you will do well. Tests were typically out of 120 points but graded up to 100, so you can get 100s and still miss 20 pts.
HE is hard! if you do not study everyday for this exams you will fail. he is tough. i advise to do not take him.

very unconsiderate... He could not care less if you are failing the class. If you don't understand something don't even bother asking him for clarification. He will give you a even worse explanation. He assumes everybody has PhD knowledge. I have nightmares just thinking of his lectures. DO NOT TAKE HIM!

Wonderful Professor- one of the best I've ever had. He will certainly make you work for your grade- but he is always willing to help. If Cell Bio is important/applicable to you for future courses (including med and grad school) you should take Dr. Ades's class. You will learn more applicable material in his class than any other class!

If you have to take cell bio, DO NOT take it with Ades if you can avoid him. He is crazy, He gives out 40% Cs and isn't considerate at all. The stuff is interesting but he makes you lose interest because of his terrible grading system. His goal is to keep his grade distribution, not to help you out. Ask people about his final in fall 07.

Took this in 1998. One of the best 400-lev science classes.   Ades sometimes has NCI researchers guest lecture. Two midterms and a final exam. Only the top two scores count (ace the two midterms you don't have to sit for the final!)  Great class to learn (especially if pre-med), relaxed atmosphere and no worries on grades.

Ades is a great professor but expects a lot, a whole lot.  you need to go to every lecture and record them or take down everything he says otherwise you wont do well. he does make the material interesting and he himself is all about what he teaches.  the lab is hell and takes the same amount of work as a 3 credit class all by itself.

Lab is easy and boost your grade. But lecture exams are horrible. You must go to class to know anything on the exam. Most things he covers in lecture are not even in the book. I found it almost useless. He can be hard to understand bc of his accent. When he writes on the board it can b hard to read his handwritting. Very hard class!!
He is one of the best bio professors I've had at this university and the first bio class I've stayed awake in ever class.  His exams are fair and he really cares about the students.

A great teacher that knows what he is talking about. sometime focuses on the details. Exam are same as reviews posted online. Just study book and go over the review questions on webct. The material is very detail focused, he is only helpful if you ask for help.
Very interesting class.  If you are interested in cancer or the details of it...this is a very good class to take! Professor is helpful and exams are straightforward!

it takes some considerable effort for a professor to teach such interesting artworks without saying anything remotely interesting for a whole semester. if you want a textbook narrated to you by some outdated AI voice, take this class for an easy A! 

be nice to the TAs because they grade everything and you will end up working them most of the time

Good class and prof if you wanna cover a couple gened credits. The weekly homeworks and online discussions are super annoying but if you do them it's basically a guaranteed A. Don't skip discussion. Major group project is really not that bad. Fun drinking game though: take a shot every time she says 'um' or 'sort of' drove me crazy at 10am

She's a very lovely teacher and cares about her students. The assignments are minimal and easy but can get really repetitive. The lecture can get boring but it's honestly not that bad. Overall the class is easy and interesting.

Super good lecturer! Her lectures were always very entertaining and she really knows what she's talking about. Easy gen ed. The group project wasn't too hard at all either. There's just repetitive assignments that can get old each week, but they're not the worst thing in the world.

To be honest, I needed this credit from the course, but I'm glad I chose her lecture. Very knowledgeable in her field; even if you give responses/ask a question that you aren't confident in, she'll always loop it back to the lectures and respond to what you said. Her lectures are very interesting. I always felt encouraged to talk, never pressured.

Professor McEwen is kind and gives interesting lectures! I enjoyed the content of the class on Modern Art and Activism (also an easy A one). However, there are lots of papers to write and criteria for the group project is not always clear.

Prof McEwen was great as my art history teacher last semester. It was meant to be an easy GenEd, and was a generally easy class to get through. After a while, the repetitive papers that you have to write each week get pretty old, but McEwen is a great lecturer and very kind and understanding to all of her students.

This class is really easy to get an A in but a lot of busy work. There are discussion posts and weekly response papers (just 300 words) separate from the lecture content, no quizzes or tests. The sections decide prompts for the final which are two essays. There is also a group project but she's an easy grader. Don't need to read the Reed textbook.

Really nice class on mexican muralism. You only have to do the reading and write a paper with deadlines throughout the semester. The final exam is also a short essay. You have to read in order to particpate in discussion. Some weeks had more reading than others. Two presentations, one for one week's readings and another for the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. McEwen is incredibly knowledgable in her areas of expertise and encourages students to develop their critical thinking skills in a more effective way than any other professor i've had. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor McEwen is very sweet and open minded. This class was extremely easy, she gives you literally everything you need to pass. Our final was take home and open note, you could only fail if you didn't try. She showed us a lot of interesting art and really made us think about it. I really enjoyed her class.
Professor McEwen's lectures were pretty boring but the class was an easy A. Midterm and final are open notes and homework and group project are graded generously.

Made a boring class even more dull, not very enthusiastic about what is being taught. Pretty rough grader, non detailed prompts for assignments and class trips are a bit hard to get to and are also boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

Stated in the final paper instructions that we cant give or received any unauthorized assistance on this assignment Does that sound like "You cant use online research as citat" to you? Never stated we could not site or use sources, had a very non detailed prompt for final.
open note exams and very interesting content!

Professor McEwen was genuinely knowledgeable about the content and was super interested in helping her students succeed. I thought she was a great professor and I would love to take another course taught by her. She graded mostly based on student effort which I really appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor McEwen is genuinely interested in her students & the subject material. Good class to take if you want to speak your mind/you're interested in art history. Obviously it's not for everybody but I think it's a good class overall. Homework is minimal and the midterm/final  cake.

McEwen was both my professor and TA for the Carillon program, and it's clear she genuinely cares about her students and their interests. Her lectures can lean towards the monotone if you're not interested in what's being displayed. Otherwise, tests were open-note and graded lightly. It's hard to get below an A on each assignment and test.

I do not like Art History. I took this class to satisfy an institutional requirement. McEwen was very boring. Here lectures are canned and boring. This class is an easy A but the lectures are SO BORING!

Very knowledgeable but monotonous lecture voice. Presents interesting a new slides for such a low level class but sometimes the importancecontext of the art isn't clear. Tests will give your hand a cramp, and there is no way to pass without studying because there is a lot of memorization. If you miss a class get notes from someone or you wont pass

First year Professor and it is obvious!  This is a survey course but teaches like all students are Art History Majors! Makes an interesting course boring! TA's are disrespectful and rude, seem like they don't want to be there.

I cannot say enough how attentive, helpful and informative Professor Bennett is. I can't imagine taking 320 with another prof. This is one of the most difficult classes JOUR students have to take but she went above and beyond and held us to high expectations while being kind and understanding. I'm really going to miss her.

Professor Bennett is one of the best teachers I've had at this university. She is thoughtful and caring but knows when to push you and how to best challenge your abilities. She is attentive to student needs and is very approachable. Her flexibility with students and understanding was phenomenal and she always put well-being first.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Abbie has been my favorite professor at UMD so far. 320 is a hard class in general with a lot of involved assignments but she was really accessible and gave great feedback. you can tell by the way she handles assignments and class she cares about student mental health. I learned more in her class then any other so far and I highly recommend her.

I took JOUR201 and 320 with professor Bennett and they were some of the best classes I've taken at Merrill. She clearly cares deeply about her students and puts them first. The classes were both hard at times, especially 320, but I liked that she is currently a journalist so she could share experiences with the industry and provide real feedback.

Prof Bennett was such a great instructor. I had her for JOUR320 and even though the class is incredibly time consuming and difficult, you could tell she really cares about her students mental health and takes the time to make sure you're doing ok. I liked having a real journalist as a professor since she had a lot of real experiences to share.

I wouldnt say I liked her, but class was easy so it wasnt too bad. Her feedback needs improving. It was annoying not knowing why she took off points for things but I still got a good grade because she offers extra credit which can bring grade up. Another issue was her extra credit was watching a movie and she gave no resource to watch it.
Loved this class! I graduated last semester and Prof. Roni was the BEST professor I ever had. I took 3 classes with her. She supported me when I struggled. She really cares about her students.

I took advanced Hebrew with her nine years ago and loved every minute of her classes. She had huge expectations for the class which she did not flinch when stating which I found to be trusting and respecting us as students to fulfill the work. We read a YA book which was very tough but immensely worthwhile and wrote a paper. Great, positive teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Very easy relaxed lectures sometimes with small brief group discussions of literature. Participation grade comes from attendance. Weekly writing assignments were very easy and there are only a few short essays and one presentation. I wouldn't say I learned a lot from this class but it was enjoyable.

attendance matters, you can only miss 1 lecture before losing credit. The class isn't to challenging if you have a small background in Hebrew but if you don't the class moves at a fast pace. You get multiple attempts for online quizzes and not too much work out side the class. grades were based on 4 quizzes, 4 HWS, 1 midterm, 3 part final
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He should not be teaching this class. HWs are full of trick questions and are graded super harshly (it was common to see averages in the low 60s), even though most students are barely grasping the basic material. Doesn't seem to care about students struggling, demands you show work in HWs but barely shows any of his. If you can, DO NOT TAKE HIM.

Just a very, very dry class. Homeworks come up suddenly. We watched MANY YouTube science videos with annoying, royalty-free background music. Examples done in class aren't always the most well organized or easy to follow if you're trying to learn the material (if you know what's going on, it makes sense, but you won't make sense of it to learn it).

Professor Aydilek is a very nice and caring guy. He doesn't want anyone to fail but he's not afraid to fail you if he feels you deserve it. He makes all his own problems and doesn't give any review materials for the exams, so the exams are difficult. Homeworks are very important to understand.

He was not an engaging lecturer, relying heavily on the presentation of specific data from research papers he'd read. He often got lost half-way through his own explanations, which made it harder to follow along. While he was always willing to help, he had a hard time addressing the heart of what was confusing his students.
Great teacher! I enjoy his class.

The only reason to take this professor is if you have no other options. The man doesn't know anything. I feel sorry for his students. I really don't understand why he is still "teaching"! He has this horrid accent too, & it becomes hard to understand.
Striking blue eyes. Extremely helpful during exams and outside of the classroom. Class itself can be dull at times.
I would not take this guy ever again. He is the worst professor I've ever had. He is totally unprepared and unclear.
Add it to your Do Not Take List!
waste

Every slide is in someway or form tied to the class texts so if you just read the text you should know what is going on. Exams are difficult, usually short answer questions and problems but he does tend to be generous when grading. Homework is given but he justs checks to see that you have worked on it (no grading). Friendly guy ok class overall.
Might be a good person to hang out with but not made for teaching at a university with such a quality. I am not going to take any of his courses anymore unless it's mandatory for the program!
He was a great teacher, don know what those guys problem is...I recommend to everyone...
He so needs to QUIT teaching! a wierdo
impatient, dull, and taught exactly from the book. he did not seem to enjoy his job
Not recommended!!!
Doesn't even know what he is talkin about! He is so mean in givin grades, so watch out!

Great professor. He is one of the few caring professors I have experienced during my time at College Park. Come to class everyday and youll be fine. I wasnt a business major or anything close to it and he made sure I understood the material and could keep up. If you dont show up to class then theres not much he can do to help you.

reviews.comment: A really caring professor who wants all his students to succeed. Extra credit opportunities and very clear about tests. If you go to most classes and keep up with the material and examples in class you will do great.

reviews.comment: Hes pretty bad at explaining statistics and when you dont know something or sees that the class is struggling he will talk down on the students and make comments like haha if you have trouble with this test then I will see you next semester which really reflects poorly on his moral character. DO NOT take him.

It's a risky class to take if you're not already an expert in statistics. The class is only a month in and the majority of us are already completely lost. reviews.comment: She is Okay, but she could be better.
She's amazing!
great teacher,sweet, friendly, helpful, fun, with a bright smile. I'm going to miss her and her classes :)

Nahal is the best language professor I've EVER had (I believe I'm at 18 and counting....).  She knows exactly how to simplify complicated concepts and she's an expert at communicating in a clear and understandable fashion.  I have never fealt belittled in her class--which seems tough to say for most language profs.  Let's not forget...so gorgeous!
He is a great guy, and will really help you learn.
Not a good professor by any standard.
Lousy professor. Do not take his class.

A LOT OF HOMEWORK.
TEST ARE HARD

FMSC 332 is online for Fall 2021, so you can attend lectures on Zoom or watch the recordings on Panopto. Even though the semester isn't quite over yet, I'm almost certain I will end up with an A. There are quizzes every week, but we're given two attempts for each quiz. There are also no exams (just projects and essay assignments). An EASY class.

Prof Lewin is kind and flexible with deadlines. I found her/the TA to be relatively easy graders, though it typically took ages to get assignments back. I had a very difficult time paying attention during lectures (very information heavy), though perhaps that's because they were over Zoom. She made class very fair/doable during a pandemic.

Professor Lewin is such an amazing teacher. Especially in quarantine/lockdown, she was extremely accommodating to all of her students and genuinely cares about you. As long as you pay attention you will pass. The content is not hard and she makes it very personal and interesting. If you want an easy A with a great teacher, I recommend this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Lewin is sooo sweet. For her class you're expected to complete lotss of readings and discussions and online quizzes. However, as long as you try your best to show up to class and take excellent lecture notes you should be fine. Her lectures are also very very interesting!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took this class as a gen ed and it was my favorite class of the semester. Professor Lewin gives interesting lectures and I learned a lot from the class. If you attend lecture and pay attention, the exams will be easy. I didn't pick up the book a single time during the semester and got an A because of how much of the exam comes from lectures.

Dr. Lewin is the best! Her lectures are extremely engaging. Often she will relate a topic to her life so we can understand it better, and it also makes the class so much more interesting. She is also very reasonable with class assignments and tests, and gives you all the tools you need to succeed. I would take her again!

Dr. Lewin is an amazing professor and her lectures were always really interesting. The course was not too difficult or demanding. The textbook was only needed for the open book quizzes. For the exams, you dont really need to read the textbook. If you go to class, take notes, and study the PowerPoints, youll do well on the exams.

Dr. Lewin is such a kind person and is really receptive to student concerns. She attempts to make the lectures interesting and applies the content to real life examples. the tests are a bit challenging but theres only three and if you actually study you can easily pass.

Dr. Lewin was amazing! Her class, while lecture-heavy, is kept interesting by her lively spirit and her stories about her kids. There is one very important paper but it's a child observation paper that's actually a lot of fun. She has very clear grading expectations and is super nice if you have any concerns. Def study for tests though.

Don't expect to get your grades back on anything until the latest date possible. She does not respond to emails and picks poor TAs who can grade things harshly. The class was extremely boring and hard to sit through but there is random participation. Never been so disrespected by a teacher through email just by asking simple questions.

Some people have different reactions to this professor. He knows what he's talking about and makes class interesting when we discuss different cases. He provides good feedback on the papers, and we usually don't stay past 8:30 pm. However, he is not very reliable as he usually doesn't respond to emails for days or ever.
He is a relaxed grader who wants you to write clearly and concisely. He fosters exciting discussions about readings, and makes a long class go by fast.

He was frequently canceling class out of nowhere; once 10 minutes before, after everyone had gotten there. He was unreliable, assignment due dates were constantly changing because he couldn't keep up with a schedule. Took forever to get an assignment graded even though he said it would be in by the weekend.

Attendance is required, you cant resubmit anything, you get an automatic zero if you don't uploud something in a specific format, very anal about apa format

I have to take her for my classes so I'm stuck but this professor sucksssss she never answers emails or questions and makes us feel stupid for even asking

very strict about attendance, and apa formatting. lots and lots of work in this class you never get a chance to breathe. she tries to trick you on assignments which is super frustrating. this is for edsp423 idk why it says 420

She's great. Obviously cares about her students success, GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!!! I literally left class one day while everyone else was finishing up the project because I WAS DONE ALREADY BECAUSE SHE HELPED ME SO MUCH. 

I can't wait to take her next semester. She's funny too sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Branigan is a great professor, but the class is incredibly boring. If you're looking for an easy A to satisfy a couple of general education requirements, this is the course for you.

She is a good professor- no final or midterm she gives biweekly quizzes instead to cover all the material. We had weekly discussion boards that really didn't take much time. She grades attendance- so as long as you show up and do the work you can get an A. also one day was virtual and one in person which was nice.

Pretty much all assignments are pass-fail. If you do the assignment you will get 100 percent.  There were 5 quizzes in total and they were 15 percent of your grade. You need at least a 60 percent average on those quizzes in order to get an A(not A-).  I had a 75 percent average without studying for a single one. Class is easy.
Very nice, but oh so boring. Not hard to achieve an A, but it is so much unnecessary work. She does care tho and will be accommodating if you reach out to her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Branigan is very accommodating and explained sometimes complicated sociological terms very well. The class had participation questions throughout the lectures but she provides an alternative assignment if you need to miss class. Since it was online the lectures weren't recorded.

Dr. Branigan is very respectable and resourceful. Her lectures are very insightful and I found them to be interesting. Online, it can get pretty boring. You also *need* to attend class. I found that sometimes she could be very passive aggressive and she talked down to students, but other than that shes alright. Work wasnt too bad, just a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Branigan is a nice prof but the work load is heavy. Lots of readings, discussion posts, short papers, group discussions on zoom. It's NOT hard to get an A but it DOES take a lot of work. It's really not a hard class, just be prepared to do lots of mindless work.

Honestly more work than some of the 300 level courses. There are 4-6 articles per week and 1-2 podcasts per week that require 4 discussion posts per week. There are also 2 participation Q's per week, if you don't pay attention the whole class you'll miss the Q's. If you struggle at all she just says its your fault for not trying. Attitude problem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Prof Branigan is very kind. She genuinely cares about her material. Also very accommodating to pandemic issues. Lectures are pretty boring tho. Make sure you know the material before quizzes. If you pay attention you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a good professor and the content is easy. Lectures are not recorded. You have to do 4 group discussions that you have to record on Zoom. She would call people out at random and put them on the spot during lecture and share their discussion post as part of lecture. wasn't fond of that but otherwise an easy class!
I loved Dr. Branigan! Her lectures were never boring and I can tell she is a very smart woman who cares a lot about her students.
Prof Branigan made SOCY my favorite class this semester! She is so positive and clearly loves her material so much! I highly recommend taking a class with her!

SOCY100 with Dr. Branigan was one of the easiest classes I've ever taken. You could do the bare minimum for any assignment, and still get an A/credit. We have mini quizzes, and they're just 10 questions. Overall, we learn interesting material.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Great professor and extremely accommodating during the COVID pandemic. She got rid of the final and most of the work was just for completion. Extremely straightforward and easy class.

Not very organized. The grading in the grade book ain't clear so you don't know if you could possibly end up failing that class. She doesn't let us see our grades. The TA ain't clear in grading either.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really loved her class! She makes an effort to make the lectures more interesting, engaging and discussion based. I She definitely cares about doing what works best for students and gives a lot of small assignments so your grade depends on more than a couple big things. There was no textbook so the readings were just recent articles & podcasts.

Professor branigan is very fun and engaging. She is always trying to make life easier for you. Her exams are very fair and your grade is easily lifted by participation points. Her lectures are interesting. 10/10 would recommend

Easiest class to pass! Just show up for participation points. Only worry about reading responses due every two weeks and discussion questions, but you can work ahead of time. She teaches very well, and is kind, approachable and passionate. Very easy exams, she tries to make your lives easier. Highly recommend her! The best sociology professor ever!
Took this class in the summer. Easy 3 credits in 3 weeks

Professor Moore is a super sweet professor who genuinely has her students at heart. This class can be a little faced paced and annoying with the turn-around times on presentations but once you get into the flow it's less difficult. All in all, she was super nice and it was a pleasure being her student.

Took this as a winter course. She was a very caring professor, and very easy to communicate with. It was very clear what she expected and the workload wasn't difficult. Her feedback was amazing. Genuinely enjoyed taking this course so much.

Amber is so sweet and cares a lot about students. When not presenting, class is mainly reviewing the book which is boring and unhelpful. Gives great feedback about presenting and creates a supportive environment. Midterm is super long but no final test- just a presentation and paper. Solid comm class but not as interesting or helpful as it could be
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is very straightforward. If you actually try to improve your public speaking skills and participate in class you'll get an A. Prof. Moore is very easy to talk to.
