The only thing is NOT a Youtube class. You only make one Youtube video towards the end of the semester. The rest of the assignments are in class speeches and papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is amazing! Such a great speaker and person. We had a total of 6 presentations and one big final paper, but the topics were interesting. She will definitely help you improve you communication and presentation skills. You'll get an A if you do the work and participate. This class was a life-changing experience; I would take her again if I could!

I've never written a professor review before. This course meets at 8 a.m., and the instructor creates an engaging, discussion-based environment that encourages participation and critical thinking. He provides detailed, constructive feedback and is responsive to student questions.
Took ENGL 101 with him during my first semester here. He was accommodating and tried his best to make the class easy going.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Howard is sincerely one of the best professors I have had this Fall 2023 semester. He was charismatic and made sure never to bore you in his class. He creates an inviting and welcoming environment and gives great feedback with his grading. He is the type of professor who cares about your success & understands YOU ARE HUMAN!!

Very understanding and straightforward. Just show up to class and complete all the assignments and you will get a B or above. Even if you don't show up and you turn in all your assignments on time, he will still give you a B.

Professor Howards course is amazing! He makes his lectures interesting everytime which makes me want to go to class! There is never a dull moment. To understand material better, he incorporates real world examples. He cares about his students and makes sure to build a connection. He is responsive to emails. Do not take his kindness for granted.

I don't understand why there is a lot of hate towards her. If you actually care about your education, you'll do great! She is more than happy to answer any questions for you and creates a welcoming environment. Though attendance isn't mandatory, I highly suggest you go to each lecture since she gives out random extra credit just for going.

Obnoxiously tries to prove herself. Inserts her political opinions in teaching. She is an unreasonably tough grader with a heavy workload... and there is little forgiveness for mistakes since many assignments are graded incomplete/complete. One of the worst professors that I have ever had.
Very nice, chill lady. Shes smart and makes it easy to do well in her class. Cares a lot about her students wellbeing.

She is a very nice person and is interested in students lives and progress. She is a pretty good professor and knows what she's talking about. This class had pretty easy to understand material so it wasn't very difficult. It was graded off of the midterm, final, a handful of quizzes, and a group project. Overall she did a good job.

Great teacher! Every moment in her class was absolutely enjoyable. Shes extreme;y considerate and doesn't want you to fail. She lets you know whats going to be on quizzes and test so you know what to expect so nothing ever comes as a surprise.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Would take again

reviews.comment: Class could have been easy but AAS is so determined to prove herself that she complicates the material. The subject matter is not hard (and the book lays it out well enough), but AAS confounds concepts in lecture & altogether moves too fast through materials with unhelpful accompanying slides to boot. Not worth going to lecture unless your far gone
Dr Seate was unresponsive to messages and combative.

Enjoyed both of my classes with her. Made complex material very easy to understand. She does challenge students and can be a tough grader. She'll also put forth every effort to make sure you do well in her class. Just go to lecture, take decent notes, go to office hours and you will do fine. The "too strict" rep she's gotten is nonsense.

Dr. Seate is a great professor. Interesting, engaging, hilarious. Her exams are somewhat challenging, and she gives pop quizzes sometimes so make sure you go to class and do the readings! She likes when students volunteer.

You need a fair amount of effort to pass this class, especially if you're not familiar with philosophy. Professor Fyfe is really passionate about what he teaches and really tries his best to make sure you understand. He is also really good at answering questions. Prepare to immerse yourself in the material if you want a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: To preface, I took PHIL 152 online with Professor Fyfe, and he was a very passionate lecturer who was chill. The lectures were good, and we were graded on just three exams, all worth separate points. I got A's on all exams but got a B overall due to his lousy grading system. It is very inaccurate and it hurt my overall grade. Hope that changes.

For preface, I took PHIL152 (online) w/him at UMBC, but RMP doesn't have that option. He's a chill professor, and his lectures are interesting; you can tell that he's passionate about this subject. The class is also very easy and you're only graded on 3 exams, which are all open note, and mandatory attendance/participation. Would def take again;)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I found him to be a pretty good lecturer overall; I always looked forward to our class discussions. I can tell he's very passionate about what he teaches and he's always curious to listen to what students have to say. However, he was very slow on grading (one project that was heavily weighed took up to two months for him to grade).

Prof Fyfe was a great professor, especially for a beginner course in philosophy. There were 3 non-cumulative exams, a final paper, and one discussion assignment; that's it. The exams are open notes as long as they are printed or handwritten. The paper was a bit tough but just make sure you go to office hours and hand in a draft.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fyfe is an incredible professor and genuinely cares about his students. You can tell he's really passionate about philosophy but will also take the time to listen to the concerns of his students. Not only a great professor but also a super interesting class. 10/10 would recommend Fyfe and Phil140!!

Fyfe is literally the most understanding prof ever. I was once super sick and emailed him the night before an exam at 10pm asking if I could by any slim chance take it another day so I could be prepared and he was more than willing to find an alternative--SUPER chill with extensions and is generally a great person to learn from. 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Fyfe is one of the best professors I have had my first semester of freshman year. He has reading quizzes every week which made me actually learn in this class and be engaged. About two papers, two midterms, and one final. He is VERY lenient.

Fyfe is an amazing lecturer, and he seems really passionate about what he's doing. He has great communication and people skills. A really down-to-earth person. 100% would recommend to anyone interested in philosophy or a gen ed filler.

Class was very interesting with Fyfe. He is definitely an interesting professor to have. The class overall was very engaging and discussed bizarre topics. Reading quizzes every week, which are very basic (easy), 2 papers (quite a harsh grader), and 3 difficult exams. Doing bad on one exam can cost your chances of getting an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: this was the most engaging class that I have ever taken. I loved everything about it and recommend it to all of my friends
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Professor Fyfe is excellent in his lectures and always keeps class super engaging. Always accessible for help in and out of the classroom. He is a very funny and charismatic guy who makes class fun. Workload for this class consisted of a few weekly readings, two essays, and 3 tests including the final. Easy A and a great class for anyone to take.

Amazing professor and you can tell that he is very passionate about Philosophy. He has some wild life stories but it makes his lectures more interesting. There is not too much reading; about 3 articles per week. The exams are a little more difficult with a lot of material but you will def. do well if you try. Highly recommend this class.

Took PHIL140 online, asynchronous. Nonetheless, I enjoyed Fyfe a lot. His lectures are engaging, to the point, and well organized. He is a blast to talk to over office hours and very responsive to email. An "A" is very attainable, although the tests are not the easiest (but they are open-notes). I feel that I gained a lot from this class.
Amazing down to earth guy who teaches well! was an honest refresher to have such a good teacher! Usually all the philosophy teachers are cool but take him 100% if you can.

reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a great guy, and the lectures are really fun. You have a quiz (with questions based on lectures) and an assignment (source notes) due every week. I HATED the source notes, just seemed like busy work to me. Overall, a really cool class and a great professor.

Professor Andrews is seriously the funniest professor I've ever taken. I really enjoyed attending lecture, but attendance wasn't mandatory. Deadlines are reasonable. There were 2 big papers but they give tons of guidance and plenty of time to prepare. Really really good guy
Great professor who sets expectations clearly and gives you lots of time to complete assignments. Would highly recommend professor David. The only downside is the class really isn't interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Andrews has been my favorite professor so far at UMD. I took KNES287 online over the winter semester but the information for the class was really well communicated through the daily podcasts he posted. He also created his own website with everything we needed to make everything more accessible.

Taking this professor for the winter semester and was hopeful with the reviews. The content is interesting but overdone. It's clear this man believes that undergrad KNES students with no sociology experience will somehow write and think like a grad sociology student. Glad I'm only suffering 3 weeks of this course. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Andrews is an okay professor. He replies to emails if you need any help. Idk if it's b/c of the online classes, but his lectures were over 2 hours long, and makes this subject hard to understand. His exams are TOO extra giving 6 mc answers per question, and 3 answers for each 6 mc answers. Everybody was so mad after his exams, they failed them.

Professor Andrews makes the class engaging, but the online exams are extremely difficult and it is easy to get a C or D on them even using your notes. They are insanely specific and cover a lot of readings and materials. 300 word responses weekly and 3 term papers. An interesting class, but this is not just an easy elective. Only take for ur major.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Hard class for no reason. Great professor, but for the exams there is barely any time to look it up in your notes or in the readings. ALWAYS writing for this class. If I didn't have to take this class for my major I wouldn't. Liked this class at first a lot, until the first exam. Good luck.. it's so much not useful, non applicable info for PT.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Andrews is a fine professor. The hour and forty-five minute lecture, combined with the quiz and mini-essay was a lot to handle each day, every day, for three weeks. Dr. Andrews doesn't show quiz answers, making it frustrating when you don't get an 100 on the quiz and you want to learn from your mistakes. Take his class Fall or Spring semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 3 papers that are graded pretty hard, but exams are online and really easy if you use search and find in your notes. Lecture isn't too bad, kinda funny and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great guy with an awesome accent and sense of humor. Teaches the class in a discussion method by giving ideologies and then contesting them, or has us do that. Really witty, interesting and controversial topics, but he talks about them in such a great way. Would take again!

Dr. Andrews is a super great lecturer that loves to talk about his personal experiences & call on students to hear about theirs. The class itself is interesting but it covers almost too much. Your grade is all dependent on the TA. 3 tests & 3 essays in addition to weekly paragraphs. Tests are online but are not as easy as u might want/expect.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Dr. Andrews heavily lectures but they are interesting. The tests and homework are very manageable as long as you put in the time to study and learn the material. Pop quizzes (3) per semester. Offers OH and is warm to students. Also, he's British. Sunny is the TA I had so if possible take her - she is lovely. Long essays. Class requires time.
Great professor and very interesting class!

Sometimes speeds through lectures, but you can view them online.  Very entertaining professor, as long as you attend class and do assignments you will get an A. I had Shaun as  TA and he was awesome. Online tests, do your papers early (two 1500 words papers for the semester) so the TA can go over it and tell you what to fix. Loved learning material

Awesome guy, very nice and funny (and British). Loves talking about Fulham and English cricket. Tests are taken online anywhere you want with a huge time window to complete them, great professor. I would absolutely take him again.

Simply one of the best professors at the University of Maryland. He emphasizes the concepts of importance and makes very fair exams. Funny and great to talk to outside of class. You don't see very many professors nowadays who are helpful and kind.
Andrews is the man. Loved his class. Great professor, interesting, and not ridiculously hard and nit-picky like a lot of professors at this school.

Andrews is the ****ing man.  Period.  If you have not taken KNES 287 then you are missing out.  How to get an "A" in his class: Start your papers at least a week in advance (and possibly consult with your T.A.), and study the key terms he has posted on each section for the test.  I got an A+.
TAKE HIS CLASS!!! He is an amazing professor that makes class interesting and fun. He uses a lot of video clips and humor to keep you awake. Plus he's British!!

Very interesting class.  Very sociology based (great if you've taken SOCY100 before).  Professor Andrews is very witty and makes 75 minutes seem like 30 minutes.  Very easy to understand if you go to class. Going to class alone will get you at least a B in the class if you pay attention.  Got an A- in the class but I got a 100 on the Final!

Dr. Andrews was a great professor. He kept the class very interesting with his lectures which worked in numerous videos each class. Overall I looked forward to going to his class and would definitely recommend him to anyone.

Intresting class. Made you think about sports in a different way. Tests were kinda tricky. Put in study time and you'll do well. Average final grade for the class was 81%. Paper was 8 pages and kinda annoying, but managable. The TA makes or breaks the class. A few pop quizzes so its good to go to class and also to write down small details he says.

Intresting class. Attendence isn't mandatory, but explains the slides more in detail so it's good to go and takes notes on what he says because little details are fair game on his tests. Tests grades in class were in the C range. The paper is 8 pages and a little annoying, but then again I waited until the night before to do it.
Awesome Prof!

Great teacher and lecturer.  Makes class very interesting and plays alot of relevant videos to keep attention.  I genuinely enjoyed the topic.  It is not an easy A by any means though.  Paper was graded very harsh and the exams are sometimes hard to prepare for.  I enjoyed every class and never missed a lecture.
the class offers no preparation for the exams and my TA was worthless graded my paper way too hardly, basically cost me a good grade. ****!

Interesting class and professor. He's funny and makes the topice interesting. He uses PowerPoint notes (that you can pring out) and articles. Tests are pretty easy. There's a research paper that your TA grades. TAs are the ones that usually give you any help or clarification- not Andrews.

Hilarious professor!!!! I wasn't very interested in learning about sport but Dr. Andrews made this course my favorite!!  His british accent and lack of American "slang" makes for various unexpected fun times.  Awesome professor, great class and very interesting to learn about.  His book is boring, though. GREAT CORE CLASS TO TAKE!! 10 out of 10!
No Comments
Very interesting class, though I didn't expect it to be.  A few pop quizzes, but always really easy.  Andrews is cool.

The class content and structure are strong, but I sometimes felt singled out and hesitant to speak because the space didn't feel nonjudgmental. The professor could be dismissive, though she later apologized. If you're interested in engaging and thought-provoking content, this class is worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Don't take it! The class is interesting at some points... I found that the student-led discussion at the beginning of every class where we discussed current events was much more interesting than anything we learned in class. Professor Kaiser is a ridiculous grader. She is very hard on grammar, and will not be clear about guidelines for assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a very hard grader and often times does not communicate what she is looking for clearly. I have learned a lot from her and the lectures are compelling. Participation is needed in this class but I found it hard and intimidating. No pre req required but probably not for someone not fully interested in or doesnt know much ab public policy.

Professor Kaiser is extremely knowledgeable in the policy world. Her position with the Maryland General Assembly makes her a great connection to have for any GVPT or PLCY major. You are only graded primarily on the three main papers, which are fairly short, but she is a tough grader. Take some time to complete them and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Your grade depends on the papers you write. PLCY 201 has 3 for the semester and the prompts are given at the beginning of the semester. She is a very tough grader, but if you put in the effort and address the prompts, you can score decent
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Kaiser is a very nice person and clearly cares about students' thoughts and the topic. She is a tough grader, often unnecessarily so. She is a stickler for proper grammar and formatting, even on exams that were LONG. She is well respected as a MD policymaker and has great connections so we had some amazing guest speakers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Super sweet prof but her classes were very boring and she is a super heavy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Kaiser is an amazing professor. I took her class at Montgomery College, and it was the best class that I took during my time there. She gives her students good feedback, and her lectures are engaging. She encourages her students to participate, and she also gives out extra credit. I also met the love of my life while taking this class! :)

this class was very informative, every day she encouraged us to talk about news happening in the US. the essays were very straight forward, if you need more time then she would give it to you if you tell her in advance. she's very understanding and doesn't want you to fail. thanks to this class I met the love of my life, best class ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: She is a good instructor who cares about the material since she is a delegate, but the TA grades almost everything. Some weeks you only have to read some articles, some weeks half a book. The midterm isn't hard if you've read, there are short reflections due every week and a long term paper, and she has guest speakers every other week that are fun.

First semester in the UMD SIE program and took CHEM 131 on top of working a full time job. Dr. Schech explains every concept clearly and doesn't surprise you on tests. The discussion worksheets are great practice so do those and ask questions / engage with the material in class. She is very responsive via email and is extremely caring and helpful.

Dr. Schech is a great lecturer. She made gen chem fun and interesting even though the course itself is pretty difficult. You are required to purchase a $90 online textbook to access the homework assignments. No curves on exams but she adjusts the grading borders from the very beginning of class (see the syllabus).

Super great lecturer (explains concepts well, engaging, etc) and overall very fair. Class was a little homework heavy, but the homework was useful practice for exams and relevant to what we were learning in class and being tested on. Generally a fair tester and grader, everything on exams was covered/explained and generally was on practice exams.

I LOVE HER. The class was hard but she does a great job explaining everything. She was available outside of class and clearly cared about us learning. She let me stay past my time frame for OH multiple times until I understood. I never thought in a million years I would get an A in chemistry, but thanks to her I did. She is sweet and hilarious!

The SIE CHEM 131 is an evening class, therefore, students are coming to class from work or completed undergrad but are pivoting towards the sciences. Sadly there's no consideration, no extra credit pts or grace periods for homework.Lecture is 3 hrs long & meets once a week, but we only have an 1hr 15min for exams.

Dr. Schech is incredibly caring and gives you every resource you need to succeed.  Her tests are hard, and she goes fast in the lectures, but all of her lectures and notes are posted and she's always willing to help you in office hours or if you email her.  Highly recommend!

Usually lab reports for chem classes are very hard, but Dr Schech's lab reports were very reasonable. They actually correlated to whatever we were doing in lab and she lectures very clearly on the things we need to know before lab. The exams were very reasonable as well. Overall, this was the first chem labs that I enjoyed.
Actually had Schech for 271. Best chemistry lecturer I've ever had.

As far as chem profs go at this school, she is a gem. Go to lecture before your lab the next week and it is extremely helpful for the report. The reports are hard but if you set aside enough time, they are doable. Her review for midterm and final are also great, as the exams are hardish. She is overall great and really cares about her students!

This class is undeniably a lot of work. It can also be pretty tough. For labs, I recommend going to as many office hours as you can, including hers. START EARLY. They take a while and you may have questions along the way. For exams, complete all of the old exams and go on the ELMS page and complete the prelab walkthrough and watch all her lectures

I took CHEM 135 (but that wasn't an option to rate her). She is a very good professor and wants students to succeed. If you go to lecture and read the textbook when you get stuck, you should have no issues in her class. Tests are difficult and assess a broad range of knowledge so be ready. Makes chemistry fun for any student willing to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You really have to have time for this course. Unfortunately, I realized that too late. Plus she is not available most of the time in person office hours. I had a lot of mental stress this semester due to his lab.She is nice, but very strict grader especially on lab reports. Attend TA office hours if possible. The hardest lab I ever has in my life.

Dr. Schech is an AMAZING professor, and she's VERY good at teaching. She does absolutely everything possible to help you succeed (recorded lectures, shared ppt before the lecture). That being said, you should still do the readings and homework because the class itself is still challenging, but easier than orgo. I'm expecting an A in the class.

Schech is an amazing lecturer & makes sure her lectures are available on ELMS. Her prelab walkthroughs are also helpful. She often visits lab sections & is extremely accessible. She gives feedback on reports & provides plenty of study material for exams. That being said, exams are difficult & you will need to put in some effort to study for them

Dr. Schech is a good lecturer, and she really cares about the students. She will talk to you after class and she is responsive to emails. She does go a little fast, but that is true of a lot of STEM classes. I did struggle in this class, because chemistry is hard for me haha but there is definitely accessible help if you need it.

I recommend Dr. Schech for 131. She is very passionate about chemistry and teaching and it shows in her class. During lecture, she explains concepts clearly, although quickly, but makes sure everyones on the same page. Weekly homework and readings are manageable. Exams are a time crunch but similar to past exams she provides. Super caring!

Professor Schech's lectures are very engaging and clear. She explains concepts very clearly. However, the exams are VERY HARD. The exams are nothing like the concepts taught in the lectures and the study guides are nothing like the exam. The exams do not reflect the lecture material at all. Would not take again just because of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Such a great professor, hard material but she went at a good pace. The GSS was super helpful and I highly recommend. Study hard and you will do fine

I really liked her for chem. Explains everything thoroughly and is an engaging lecturer. Goes pretty fast but it's college so its expected. I thought the tests weren't super hard like all the other reviews said, just needed to study like for anything else. Gives old exams and had GSS for review. But we had to pay for HW and grade is test heavy.

Class was entirely online because of COVID, but the lectures were solid and the discussions were really helpful. Read the materials and listen to the lectures BEFORE you go to class. She gives partial credit given on exams for understanding/attempting the correct process. It's a lot of work but work hard, come to class prepared, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Took her online for lab spring 2021. The course itself is difficult, but she gave very clear outlines on what each lab needed to include, and descriptive video walk throughs. I highly recommend office hours to do well in the class, but overall she was a great professor. I learned way more from her class than my lecture professor.

Dr. Schech is an amazing professor. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succee. The exams are application based and require you to not only know the material, but understanding it fully. Dr. Schech is very accessible and is incredibly helpful in office hours. She gives a ton of partial credit, so don't fret getting the answer wrong

Let me just start off by saying that I am praying for anyone who has to take CHEM272... this is truly the most tedious & time-sucking class I've taken at UMD. Be ready to pull all-nighters because the lab reports take HOURS to complete. You have to keep track of significant figures for every single calculation. Schech is nice & approachable though
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are more difficult than anything we did during the semester because they require thorough, working, conceptual understanding of the material. Expect poor grades if you don't fully get things, there is no coasting by. Very organized, accessible, and friendly. But you have to study HARD. She also curves which is v nice.

Nice professor. However, ALL of exams are very hard. I dont think any of her exam average were over a 65. Everything was online this semester. However, I do not see why professor try to make it harder for students. I know another professor exams were multiple choice. All of her exams you had to write your answers. I
Extremely heavy on the lab reports and associated quizzes but will take away a lot from the class. Great premed and MCAT prep choice but a lot of work associated to get a good grade.
She makes great lectures that make it easy to understand the homework. However, her exams are so much more difficult.

Shes not a very good teacher. I don't understand her lectures and when I do the homework and practice questions do not match the level of difficultly in her exams. Terrible exams, super hard and I was lost every time. You only have ONE HOUR to complete the tedious set of questions she gives you. Which is like what? One hour is not enough at all.

Dr. Schech was a good lecturer, the classes were all asynchronous. The exams were ridiculously hard, be aware. Do well on the lab reports by going to office hours so that you can buffer your grade for the exams. She's a nice person and I learned a lot through her lectures, but the exams were way out of proportion with the labs.

This is the worst teacher Ive ever encountered. Her exams are monumentally HARD! and she doesnt give partial credit. Going to lecture, GSS and doing HW wont do you any justice. You really need a chemistry background in order to do well and pass in her class. I would choose a different professor unless your up for the unnecessary challenge.
I would avoid this professor at all cost. She writes the test her self and they are extremely difficult and hard to take. If you arent pre-med or bio avoid!

Lab reports were very time consuming and the exams was super hard. You cannot memorize anything for this class, you have to understand what you are doing in order to pass the exam. But she was super caring and very helpful if you asked her questions! You will learn a lot from this class

Dr. Schech cares for her students as a lab coordinator. She was very accommodating to the transition to an online environment as well. CHEM 272 is generally a difficult course but she tries to make it fun and relevant.

Dr. Schech is a very very nice person. She really knows her chemistry, and is always willing to ask tons of questions. Chemistry is hard though, no matter who you take it with. Exams are tough, study days before. Make sure you do well on homework's and it will really help your grade in the end. I struggled A LOT and still got a C.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Really nice, funny lecturer. Lab reports are time consuming but manageable. Make sure to keep track of error and you'll be fine. Graded on what you do with the data more than correctness. Final exam wasn't too bad, all things considered. She did a good job with a chem lab class that had to be moved to online learning. TAs were great for questions.

Really great person, but she did not match my learning style at all. Lectures would be pretty straight forward to me after a bit of practice and studying, but the tests were a million times harder than the practice we did in class. With the course transitioning to online instruction, I have felt completely lost and confused.

This is the worst teacher I have ever had for chemistry. When moved online, she gave even more work on top of the stuff we already had. Her tests are so hard and nothing like class problems or old exams, and she wouldn't explain them after. The TA was the only high point of the class and the only one who taught students anything. Take someone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Decent but class was so hard to pass. I was so confused in lecture and only understood anything in discussion, I wish the TA was the prof. Don't skip lectures, clickers during lecture and important concepts. She's very nice and funny but not great. Tests are nothing like the practice problems, old exams and GSS won't help. Take if no other choice!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Overall a good prof. Attendance isn't taken but you will not pass if you skip. Textbook is a good supplement, but focus on the notes you take from lecture. Discussion was helpful. Exams are tough but fair. Do a ton of practice problems and you'll be fine. She's friendly and explains things well. Definitely one of the better options for CHEM131.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Terrible at letting you know what you'll actually NEED to know--treats it like some kind of puzzle that you should unlock. Exams are stratospherically different from caliber of materials done in class. Doesn't reuse old exam questions or textbook questions, so even getting extra practice from GSS won't help. Take someone else.

I respect Dr. Shrek, she's an evil genius. CHEM272 is one of the hardest classes I've taken at Maryland, but also one of the best. I learned so much, and I feel much more competent as a scientist now. Experiments were cool, but lab reports were hard. Exams were dismal, but class curved by 4 percent. Not for everyone, but I liked her and lectures

Dr. Schech is a nice person, but her exams are NOTHING like her lectures. She would put problems on the exams that we had never seen before. The exam averages are super low, with the last one being a 56.6/100. I expected A's on the exams bc of my AP Chem background, which was MUCH harder than her class, but her exams screwed up everybody.

She was nice but her exams were bad. Tests were difficult even with AP Chemistry background. The tests did not follow the practice exams so it was pointless to look over them. Did not ever use the textbook. The lectures are very simple and easy to follow but don't expect the exams to be like that. Choose a different professor if you can.

She seems nice, but clearly she's not because she makes her exams ridiculously difficult. I get if she uses problems she went over in lecture, but she does not. Her lectures are simple but exams are extremely hard, which I am trying to make sense of. Maybe her point is to cater to those retaking the course or who already have chemistry knowledge?

Dr. Schech is a decent lecturer, but her exams are really unfair. There are too many questions to be answered in a 50 minute timeframe and they do not adequately reflect the material that is taught in lecture. Exam questions are way harder than questions she goes through in class & assigns for homework, making it very difficult to do well on exams.

CHEM131 has made me reconsider if I should go on my current major path. It has destroyed my weekend nights, and generally was not pleasant. Schech seems like a nice person, but quite simply I'm confused half of the time in her class. However, if you have some background in chemistry, I'm pretty sure you'll like her and do fine.

Tip: the lab reports are fine if you invest enough time to fill everything 100% and correctly show errors. Fix your mistakes from previous weeks and don't EVER save it for the night before (later ones take 5h). Exams: the topics are exactly what's in reports/the manual but she gives no practice. Make your own, practice 271 concepts too, get the A.

Schech lectures pretty well, but it's only helpful theoretically & not with lab reports. Tough grading on labs, which take hours upon hours to complete. Even doing well on those it can be tough to pull an A because of the midterm and final, which are difficult and bring down your grade. Practical is relatively easy. Class has a small curve.

This was the most ridiculous lab I've ever taken. I did fine on all the lab reports, if you spend hours on them each week you can too. Now the midterm and final, good luck. The midterm and final were out of control and had material that wasn't even taught. Annoying that you can do well in the actual lab but have those tests bring down your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class is just ridiculous, Midterm and Final essentially designed to ruin your grade and test you on materials you never knew one could do in a LAB. Also, this lab is barely curved only 3%. the only recommendation is going to Office hours and make sure your lab reports are perfect every week.

Dr. Schech is a good professor and you can get a good grade if you're willing to go to lecture and put the time in studying before the tests. The tests are challenging and they will be impossible if you don't study adequately.
she is a great lecturer but her test are very awful. They are actually so hard. every time I take them it is literally nothing on the study guide.

Overall she is such a nice professor! She really cares about the students and makes sure to give fair tests that we won't need to rely on 20 point curves. She made chemistry actually kind of enjoyable and is definitely one of the best chemistry professors to learn from. She gave homeworks which helped boost grades and tests were not too bad either.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: i skipped 20% of lectures and lost those clicker points, but still got an A. pay attention in class, and def go to it because it really makes a difference. the textbook (or some sort of text) comes with the mastering course code, so dont buy it, and you can just read that text to patch up any holes of knowledge. the curve really helps (84 --> 94).

the class material was relatively easy. Schech is one of the only chemistry professors who tries to make class as bright and interesting as possible - if you want dry and to the point, take someone else. she knows her stuff, tests are graded harshly but that's just chemistry for you. didnt buy the textbook, never needed it. homework was easy too

Schech's lectures were great and really prepared you for the labs every week. However, TAs graded the lab reports looking for any possible error and docked you 5 points for each one. Exams are difficult but manageable if you keep up in lab. Overall, you learn a lot and a good grade is possible but she will make you work for it. Go to office hours!!

Genuinely caring, amazing lecturer. She evidently has a huge passion for chemistry and really wants her students to do well. Her exams can tend to be theoretical but were really not too bad as long as you know the principles discussed in lecture very well. Chemistry used to intimidate me badly but after her class I found myself even enjoying it

She was the most frustrating professor I've ever had. Her lectures are hard to follow and dont't make much sense. She just gives examples of random things and expects you to understand. Her tests are the worst and she doesn't even review for them. She left 2/3 the way through the semester to have a baby and the sub was so much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Schech is nice and her course criteria are laid out well, but she is an extremely tough grader and doesn't seem to leave much room for mistakes. When the class first started, the atmosphere seemed like we weren't allowed to make mistakes. I don't think there's anybody else that teaches this class, but if you can avoid it, please do so.

Her lectures really prepare you for the labs. Even if, like me, you have taken gen chem 2 somewhere else and just need the lab, go to the lectures because she spells out everything for the upcoming lab. Lab reports are graded fairly and with good feedback from rotating TAs, labs can be a bit long for the alloted time, but overall an easy class.

At first, I really liked her. She tried to make chem fun. as the semester progressed, you could tell she was trying to rush since we were behind. We spent only 3/4 of lecture on Gases, which is a lengthy topic. She FLEW through it. Nonetheless, shes ok. Her tests are extremely hard and have nothing to do with the practice tests. Very conceptual.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's great! Relates to her students while teaching, and explains thoroughly. She's bright and happy, which makes it not boring to listen to her. Clicker questions make attendance mandatory, but its not a chore to sit through class. Truly, best chem teacher I've had so far.

Coming into this class, I thought I would leave with a C. However, from day 1 I read every chapter and went to every lecture. If you do this and do MANY practice problems (from the book AND discussion), you should do average/well on the exams. It is a very hard class, but if you study weeks ahead/don't procrastinate on studying, you should be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Exams were way to difficult and then got mad at us when we all failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: A lot of theoretical questions on her exams. The discussion TA was horrible. Very condescending and discouraging.

Attend lectures and take thorough notes, this class is definitely one that requires effort but comparing other chem 131 professors it is much more doable. Discussion isn't helpful and it is not mandatory, as long as you stay around/above average you should be fine with a curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Exam averages were around 60% all together, much better than other gen chem prof. As long as you do better then average you should be good. The discussion TA wasn't the best, kinda cocky and did not help much outside the class.

Her exam questions are very vague but expects very specific answers on the exams. Her study guides do not accurately reflect questions given on the test compared to her TA. If you do take her go to every lecture because her slides are practically blank and she doesn't post her lecture notes on elms.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher and breaks difficult concepts down so you can understand. Definitely have to study and practice A LOT. Sometimes her lectures seem so easy that it doesn't reflect the difficulty of the material/exams. Her averages are weirdly high so there might not be a large curve so make sure you don't fall behind. Study from the first day
You'd better run away
Course content is ok, but the instruction falls short.
Awful experience The instructor is often condescending to students and unhelpful.

Class itself isn't too difficult as long as you show up and do the work. As for the professor, she is often condescending to her students and unhelpful. Had to go to the other professor's office hours to get a pretty basic principal explained because Allison did not explain it at all. Hope she reads this so she can be a more thoughtful professor.
Awful professor . She cant teach. She misses the office hours and doesnt help the students at all
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Lehman is a nice guy who is passionate about what he teaches. The pop quizzes he gives are easy As as long as you put some thought and effort into them. Although his lectures can be ramble-y at times, the things he says are directly related to what is written on his slides. I personally would not mind taking another class with him.
Honestly, be prepared to teach yourself the material. TAS are really cool, though, and they all have a lot of office hours.

His first exam was a bit unexpected for me because he wanted you to know which things were discusses in class vs what was discussed in the textbook. This makes no sense for me because I feel like as long as you know the material you shouldn't need to know where you learned it from. Besides that he's fine. He's not the best and by far not the worst.

The content was pretty dry but the class is required for CCJS majors and he tried to make it as interesting as possible. He teaches a class on cannabis and discusses it a lot in this class too which I found interesting. Only a few computer assignments, one short paper, and three 100 question exams throughout the semester all of which were easy A's.

Hes kind and well-meaning but I never looked forward to class. His lectures are very boring and he doesnt try to make them engaging, he literally just writes on a piece of printer paper. His exams are oddly specific and some questions were just unfair. The worst thing is that he makes assignments not due at 11:59 and rather in the afternoon.

Dr Lehman is a spectacular professor. He has engaging lectures but he writes them on a paper rather than having them on slides, so be ready. As long as you do the readings and pay attention to lectures, you should be fine. Also, be sure to read the details of SPSS assignments, because I did lose some points on them. Overall, great guy and class!
Cannot say enough good things about Dr Lehman!! The nicest most caring professor , he will go out of his way to help you. Definitely take him!!

I didn't expect to like this class as much as I did. Doctor Lehman made class easy, fun, and engaging with his passion-filled lectures. I'm not sure how he did it pre-COVID, but we had three exams ("quizzes") and a final project, which could be about whatever we wanted. Highly recommend this class/professor! You won't regret it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The exams (he calls them quizzes) are open notes and book, so you should get 100% on all of them. He posts walk-throughs for the four big assignments so each takes only a few hours. Posted lectures are 15-20 minutes a week and reading is mostly optional. Recommendation: call into his office hours and get to know him. I got an A+ and you can too.

I love Dr. Lehman. I had him for CCJS200 and CCJS418P. Great professor, really passionate about his work and engaging. 100% recommend his marijuana, law and society class- super interesting. He makes learning easy and fun.

Such a kind soul!! He walks you through exactly what is expected for the programming assignments. His 3 tests (which he calls a quiz) are nothing more than what is in the lectures and what can easily be found in the textbook. The workload is reasonable, just pay attention to syllabus dates as he does not remind well in advanced when quizzes are.

Hes a super sweet guy and means well. My only real problem with this class were the 3 100 question quizzes that we werent even told about until a couple days before. Since this was online due to COVID Im more understanding that things are new & weird but he often left us hanging until the day before an assignment to tell us much. Hes cool tho

I took CCJS200 with Professor Lehman as well and during both, he was an amazing lecturer. He made assignments easy to understand/tests easy to prepare for. You do need to put a bit of effort in to get an A but he's very passionate/caring towards his students. He also studies marijuana and incorporates that into his lectures, which is pretty cool.

Dr. Lehman clearly loves teaching and he doesn't make this class hard! I also took him for 200 and I got an A in both classes. Read the textbook to review for the exam. SPSS assignments are also pretty simple and a big part of your grade so make sure you don't forget about them!

He is really funny and always finds ways to make the class relatable and interesting. He writes most of his notes on the board so you have to go to class to get the class lectures. There are small assignments that are really simple and easy to do so they are good grade boosters. He also tells you exactly how much of the textbook will be on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I never went to lecture. He puts his powerpoints up online. I use those to learn all the material the day before the worksheets were due, then went to my TA office hours to make sure I did it correctly. Don't take him if you can't learn independently.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of the best professor I had so far , this was my second time taking Statistics , hes very helpful and doesnt mind giving clarification. He would take his time to make sure you understand the material. I would suggest you take him for 200.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: GREAT Professor. He cares a lot about his students and will do whatever he can to help you pass. I've never received an A in math & I got an A in his class b/c of his teaching and willingness to help. He keeps you engaged and course packets are almost mere images of the exam. He doesn't put anything on the exams to stump you. Highly recommend!

Very good teacher and interesting class because he makes it fun. He almost always lets class out early and is very helpful when you ask questions. He wants you to get an A in the class. All lecture slides are online and are pretty simple to follow at home. Just study and do the practice exams and the discussion worksheets and you'll get an A!
So funny and a very straightforward professor. Doesn't try to confuse you on problem sets and exams too much. Enjoyed taking his class a lot.

Lehman was hilarious, he really kept the class interesting. He writes 80% of his notes on the chalk board, so you really do need to go to class to get them. Definitely go to class, because he basically spoon feeds you the answers to the exams and SPSS assignments. He'll also let you know about how much of the textbook you need to read for the exam

Great class. Kept the class interesting. Sometimes went a little off topic, but overall a great class. Easy tests, not many ( I think 4 or 5 total). Must study his lecture notes and read book to pass.
Class is extremely easy. 3 exams are easy as well. Professor makes the class somewhat interesting.
Great teacher, great class, go to class and read the textbook. Guatanteed A.

Nice guy, dumb class.  Really, you will not take anything away from this class.  But it's required.  Just takes notes in class and you should be fine.  Don't have to attend class if you want to read the book.  Computer assignments are real easy.  He isn't too helpful though.  I went to his office hours three times and he wasn't there.

Very into what he's teaching & loves when students ask questions.  Writes down lecture notes that follow the book, so going to class isn't really necessary.  Always available to help students and is really easy on grading.  Has the most random & hilarious comments to keep you from falling completely asleep.  Overall very friendly & helpful

He is so nice. You can tell he's really into what he teaches and his enthusiasm for the subject is entertaining within itself. I feel kind of bad for him cause a lot of students dont listen. Kind of goes off on tangents, but they're amusing. Usually lets class out early. Must read book to be successful on exams. Content is easy. I recommend him.
hard course, the exam is not followed by review sheet, don't take this course
I loved my time in class. This class expanded my mental potential. Hard grader but made info very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is very funny and nice when you get to know her.
Small tweaks to her class and she could be great

Professor Gandhi is not a bad professor; her lectures are very educated and the overall structure of this class was really laid back; but she is a very harsh grader, as the quizzes and open-note exams were graded with extreme attention-to-detail. Not bad, but could be a nicer grader.

Good lecturer and approachable outside of class during office hours to discuss class concepts and our project. The grading might be more rigid and tough than some other instructors but I thought it was generally fair. Don't hesitate to ask questions since econometrics tougher than a good bit of other ECON class material, but you can def survive.
reasonable/kind but strict. Lectures are important but if you miss them rely heavily on textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a nice lady and is accomodating. There are a lot of readings so if you don't do those you will be lost.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class was extremely difficult in the midst of a pandemic and she didnt curve the class. She median in the class is a C . She marks extremely hard and does not curve . I would definitely not recommend but if youre an Econ major you will end up with one of her class.

The course was structured pretty well. The concepts are pretty hard to get, but if you watch and attend the lectures and read the textbook, you'll do just fine on the exams. The weekly homework are pretty easy points. There is a big project due at the end of the semester, and you really do want to start on it as early as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I'm taking this class online due to Covid and I'll say Professor Ghandi does a good job trying to explain the concepts in Econometrics and she even goes over some example problems in lectures and on video. The issue is that her material does not relate well into the exam. Econometrics itself is very difficult so really you'd expect it from others.

The content of the class was very dense but she breaks it all down during lectures. I had a hard time with this class at first but going through sample problems in her lecture slides and the ones provided in the book helped a lot. This class can be a lot of work especially if stats isn't your thing.

I first thought gandhi's expectation is too high on us but As time went by, I realized how clear she is during the lecture and tries to explain clearly with many examples. Also, I felt she really wants us to do well and understand econometrics. I think I will end up with a C- in this course but am glad I took this class with her.

If you take your time in her class seriously you will succeed. If you study hard you will succeed. She is great at explaining the material and she brings a professional perspective into the class as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I find it so inconsiderate when professors make students purchase online HW that cost $130 when they could simply give out problem sets or distribute pdf versions of those hw. Also, her exams are way too long and tough for what she actually teaches. The average gpa for this course is 2.03, which means most students end up with a C.

I loved econometrics with Dr. Gandhi. Stat isn't my thing but she broke down concepts clearly and was happy to answer questions in class and office hours. Her exams are challenging but she does give you a good idea of what to expect by giving out practice exams. Overall, she was a great professor and I learned much more than I expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Grades to a C. Good luck doing well in this class.
the worst.

I failed the second midterm and the final. I aced the homework and quizzes, did well on the first test. that's the key. for the quizzes, do the study plan and the questions are the same with different numbers. do well on one of the tests and you can recover from bad test grades. way too hard of a class, however.

She's really nice and funny. I didn't like econ200 because of the subject, not because of the professor. I don't think any professor could make me like econ. Going to class is very helpful, but not mandatory. She doesn't necessarily curve, so it's important to do well on tests.

You will really work in this class for your grade. You need to pay attention, take notes and also read the text book and understand it. business stat knowledge will help too. she does try to help you if you are stuck with homeworks. good professor, but you really need to work hard for your grade.

She's a very intelligent, helpful professor. I took busi stat prior to taking econ stat w/her and I was dreading the class b/c I did extremely poorly in busi stat. After her class, now I thoroughly understand stat & like it. There were people who complained about her level of hardness but I think they were just lazy. Effort's required in her class.

such a cool ethical dude, very very smart and willing to help however necessary. often off topic during lectures but always talking about important stuff. wants his students to succeed and has a lot of really interesting takes!

Dr.Ali is a professor who tried to make the class interesting and cracks jokes that made him relatable. But he always is off topic when he gives out lectures and you can't use technology or he gives you a 0. Tough grader wouldn't recommend to take for funsies.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ali is an exemplary professor. He is responsive to student concerns, thoroughly knowledgeable, and seems genuinely impassioned by the information in the course. His enthusiasm for teaching and authentic amiability make him one of my favorite professors to date.

Asim pretty much always went off-topic in lecture, homework is graded pretty toughly (though this can depend on your TA, obviously) but as a whole this course was not worth the credits. The exams are hard to get A's on, since the answers often struck me as pretty subjective. If you don't regurgitate his notes, you won't get an A. If you do, maybe.

He is a very knowledgeable g and respected professor. The homework is reasonable, a short weekly reading review and four main papers. The materials we discussed in class are very interesting and can be applied to the society. I really learnt a lot from this class.  He also has extra office hour each time before you hand in papers.

Very very laidback. Often off topic during the lectures but it doesn't really matter because you're graded only on your response to the weekly reading and then 4 papers also related to the semester's reading. He's very chill and tries to make the class interesting, and he seems to really care about his students. Very accessible outside of class
Loved her. I encourage you to go to class even just for her awesome energy and care.

She actually cares about how her students are doing is so kind. She will have lectures that promote insightful thinking and as long as you try your best in the class you will get an A. She is very understanding and will grant extensions if you need one. 10/10 recc, can never go wrong with Dr. A
Very nice. Class is fun and easy. i recommend

Caring and interesting professor. Amazed that she memorized every student in the lecture's names. Learning demonstrations were not too difficult but be prepared to write a decent amount. Work outside of the class was very manageable as well.

Every time I listen to her lecture I feel like I am watching a TED talk. She really knows how to keep the class engaged and truly cares about everyones individual academic and mental wellbeing. She has changed my perspective on so many things. If you get the chance, and you don't mind reading two articles every week, take this class!

Professor Alexander is unlike any professor you'll ever have and you'll know exactly why when you take her class. You will love your first day of this class. Don't worry about how well you'll do because its impossible not to learn and do well in the course.
Mother Alexander is the best!

BEST teacher ever!she is funny hilarious.she even knew the names of all her students BEFORE the first class!Many ppl even added hum.dev. as a minor after taking this class.This class will greatly improve your memory skills, all you have to do is go to class and listen to Dr.A's funny stories! plus exams are based off the lecture slides and lectures
He is a pdf file. I had his class for a week before he was arrested.

This professor likes to expose himself

Otherwise he is amazing teacher.

Came here to write a bad review but it looks like my job has already been done for me. Wow, people really don't like this guy!  I don't have much to say that hasn't already been said, other than if you want to actually enjoy your semester, do not take his class. You don't realize how much ONE bad professor can influence your life until it does.

Listen, a lot of people don't like Dr. Apter and I will admit he isnt the best professor. But to me his classes are easy. So if you want to add a more laid back class to your schedule I would suggest taking one of his. The classes was easy, one of the forget about classes compared to how strenuous all other animal science courses seem to be.

I hope you don't have to experience the utter frustration that is dealing with Professor Apter. His lab quizzes are needlessly difficult. He always makes sure to throw in some “short answer” questions so he can deduct points. His assignment instructions are vague, but don't let that fool you, he has very specific expectations. Hard pass!

Do not recommend! Extremely stringent grading policies, no lenience for missed classes (doesn't matter if you have documentation or not). Strong superiority complex and just a condescending way of speaking to students. If you can avoid this guy, please do, no class or professor is worth your mental health.

Apter is the kind of professor who makes his class difficult not because of the content of the course but because of his arbitrary rules and harsh grading despite very vague instructions given. Oh, and don't forget the pop quizzes, which are put in as "attendance" grades! Fun times! You will regret taking this class, so just don't!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment:
Beware of this guy! Once he decides he doesn't like you, you are basically done for! He is not flexible, understanding or willing to work with you. To him, a car accident is not a “university sanctioned excuse” instead it is a “minor traffic issue.” 

You know, maybe he's right. I should've just left my car by the side of the road. My bad!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Apter is the WORST! Trust his abysmal rate my professor reviews on this one! He is not here to help you succeed, in fact he is hellbent on taking off points wherever he possibly can. Expects you to treat his class as the one and only priority in

Do yourself a favor and fulfill your gen ed requirement with something else. Apter is the kind of professor who thinks the best way to encourage attendance and participation in his class is by making students fear that they will drop a letter grade. Expect random changes in how the class is run, zero tolerance for absences, and utter rigidity.

One of the worst professors I've had at UMD. Notecards are given out each lecture for “attendance” but they are graded for accuracy. I don't believe that pop quizzes should count as attendance, as it is incredibly misleading. In October he started giving out the notecards at the beginning of class instead of the end to punish latecomers/ commuters.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do not take this class! Apter gives you notecards for attendance that are graded for ACCURACY. At that point call it what it is; a pop quiz. You WILL drop a letter grade if you don't attend class. Halfway through the semester he started giving out the notecards at the beginning of lecture instead of the end to teach latecomers “a lesson.”
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is insanely boring and attendance is mandatory. He is a very picky grader and even if you do everything right you'll probably still get points off. Huge semester paper with practically no guidelines. This is an upper level course however, and is still easier than many other ANSC required classes.

He's nice but lecture can be boring. The lab assignments can be confusing b/c his directions are often confusing. Read the directions. The midterms are straight forward and there is a big paper due at the end. I'd say that attendance is mandatory because if you don't turn in a notecard you'll get a zero and it definitely drops your grade. Excel!

ANSC227 was great! I wish my class had a little more energy to match his passion for the content we were learning; that would've made it even better. Labs were fun and there was no final exam. Take this class if you can!

I took ANSC282 and he made us do group projects throughout the semester that had very few guidelines. Don’t let this fool you! He is very specific about what he wants. I got Cs on every single one. Maybe it would have been easier if he actually taught us how to make a farming operation plan rather than just saying “okay go do it.”
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor in the ANSC department! So nice and interesting :)

Taken asynchronously online. Lab quizzes were incredibly easy, journals were graded generously, no exams. But you miss out on all the fun labs in an online session. Professor also seems checked out, with lots of copy-pasted emails with dates from the last semester. Probably better in person.

Dr. Apter is such a fun professor. Class was online due to COVID, but lab quizzes were fairly easy as long as you take notes on lectures. This gen ed was actually interesting too: teaches you how to do fun stuff like make cheese.

Dr. Apter is an interesting lecturer, but his assignments are graded way too harshly, especially without such clear cut guidelines. His labs usually end early, which is nice, but the weekly lab quizzes are a pain. We had an optional final at the end of the semester to replace the lowest quizzes. Solid class for a gen-ed if you put in some effort.

Apter is truly an awful professor and seems very sexist. His lab quizzes are super hard for no reason, his journal entry prompts are so vague yet graded harshly. There are no exams but he gives out notecards as attendance and grades on ACCURACY so you have to go to class because they're 2 pts each. DO NOT take him!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Apter has always mentioned how he wanted to make this course harder so it's not an easy gen ed. His quizzes are picky and specific. He complains how we get such low grades on the quizzes and claims that he basically gives us the answers. But that is completely false. He'll direct you to focus on wrong answers. His gradings are harsh for papers.

He did not round my B to an A from just .3 points away. Other than that he makes the material tolerable because he is pretty funny. As long as you go to class and lab and study your notes its an easy A-B
Likable professor, fairly easy if you follow directions

I had Professor Calderon-Cervantes in my first semester of college (Fall 2022). Overall, she was an "okay" professor. Nothing stood out about Professor Calderon, very average. However, PLCY100 was very lecture heavy, and boring. However, I forgot about presenting a group project and she still gave me a 90% on the project, which was very nice.

Dr. C is a sweet person, and her lectures were fine. Your grade is basically comprised of an easy asynchronous midterm, a final group project, and participation in discussion sessions. I would say that discussion attendance is crucial, but lecture attendance is not (neither is reading the textbook). Lovely class environment, easy A.

Attendance is absolutely necessary as there are barely any assignments to do, so she has participation grades. We didn't have anything due at all for the class until late October. No tests. Just a group project at the end of the semester. Super easy material. I think I had 4 things to turn in all semester. It was amazing.

Should be really interesting, but it's not delivered well. As someone who agreed with most opinions/leanings of Prof. Calderon, I felt it suffocating how much she made her opinion seem fact, teaching barely any general material. Grading was unclear,, and harsh. Seemed like an opportunity taken to just preach to students. Not good for a policy class

Professor Calderon is a strict professor but her lectures are very insightful and it's clear she really knows what she's talking about. Her grading criteria aren't always clear but if you reach out to her she will explain it in more detail. If you want an A, ask questions, participate in discussion, and communicate with her/the TA
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I mean, she's bad. Even as someone who agrees with the majority of her political points I understand that this class is unfairly bias. Quizes are worth a significant portion of your grade and you wont pass them if you don't read every. single. material. and there's a LOT. Assignments due in the middle of the day. Its not a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Honestly, this class felt pretty biased. Prof. Calderon takes FOREVER to grade things. For one week, she also assigns an insane amount of reading, podcasts, and videos. (I cannot stress that enough; it is A LOT) Her lectures are extremely boring as well. Overall this class did not feel like a 100-level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Way to much work for a Policy 100 class. She inserts her bias way too much and doesnt make the class easy for students.

I can't stress enough how badly I advise you to stay away from this professor. Horrible Horrible teacher who takes class time to mean a full hour to teach you her political opinions and why they're right to the point of ridiculousness. Worst prof. I've had at UMD!

Prof. Calderon was one of the worst professors I've had at Maryland. For an intro policy class, the level to which she inserted her personal bias into the class bordered on obscene. The required readings for class were largely opinion pieces that fostered an echo chamber and group think. Dean Joyce, who co-taught the class, was much better.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is rude, and a very ineffective professor. She thinks she knows everything in life, and thinks she is employed by a fortune 500 company.. I mean really? Treat others the way YOU want to be treated. Easy to earn a B, have to work hard for an A. She is really lacking social skills. I would avoid her if possible.

She is hot and knows the stuff well. All kudos to her for making the class seem like my world... as a reuslt I switched my major to literature. I hope she continues teaching, she is one of the best they have here.
She knew what she was doing and had the class captivated. I would recommend her to any student who cares about literature. She is also helpful and cares about her students.

It was a heavy book class. I think we went through 6 books thoughout the semester.  It was a challenge to do all the reading but the novels were great readings.  I would definately take this class again. Fun Exciting and very educational!
Lover her so much. she's so caring and she makes physics so easy to understand. extra credits really helps too

Dr.Heidrian is a nice and caring professor. She helps on the HW and uploads the solution on piazza. The only thing I dislike about her lecture is that she goes too fast. She never slows down and despite having an hour and 15mins class, she teaches as if the class is 50mins. Lectures are very boring overall. She does drop the lowest midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: After getting a C- in Calculus 1 last semester, I never would have thought that I would get an A+ in Physics. Dr. Heidarian is a great professor and makes complex physics concepts very simple to understand. She also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities in the exams as well as helpful practice problems outside of the homework assignments.

doesnt feel like she cares. Takes so long to get exams back, if its taking 3 weeks then prof should help the TAs grade. I've asked a couple questions on piazza and her responses were rude/sassy. I felt she didnt treat us with respect when we asked ?'s, &assumed we didnt try to answer it ourselves first or didnt read announcements (I read them all)

Cares about students & is a good teacher, but it's not translating well to online. Lecture videos hard to follow, jumping btwn powerpoint & written notes. Can't understand her notes even after watching lecture. If you pause the videos and do the problems, lectures take way longer than theyre supposed to. Feels like material is being overcomplicated

Took her for both 121 and 122, got A-/A+. She's super sweet and really wants to help you. Easy grader, tons of extra credit every exam that roll over to the next exam if you don't do as well. A lot of people had final grades that were over 100%. Seriously she wants you to do well. ExpertTA homework sucks but as long as you keep up you'll be fine.
there are extra credits problems on every midterm exam which helps a lot, and she also curves the exam grades.

Difficult as a professor because she can act in ways that are super passive aggressive and just un-empathetic to the students. The course is interesting and of course she seems passionate about it, but I would not recommend her.

Arianna is a difficult professor, although the course content is interesting. However, she can lack empathy for her students, is extremely passive aggressive, and often uses operant conditioning on her students (treating them like a dog) as soon as you do something wrong. I have heard horror stories about her from her lab- stay away.

Dr. Gard is one of the best professors I've had. Her lectures are very interesting & she's clearly an expert in the field. A few writing assignments that she gives great feedback to improve upon and these help with final paper. Does her best to decrease workload & makes sure students are doing well. Weekly articles, 1 book, discussion each week.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I initially signed up for this class without reading the review in her. Once I took the class I realized the review did not exaggerate. Please do not take this class! Her curve is high but not guaranteed. Her lectures make 0 sense. I learned everything on my own. She fumbles with technology for half the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I downloaded the wrong textbook for this class and did not notice for at least a month because her lectures are genuinely so bad.
do NOT bother going to lecture if you have her. You will be teaching yourself the course anyway
i have no words

I made the mistake of thinking, “all of these people giving reviews are over exaggerating”. It's worse than words can explain. By the third lecture I was completely lost. Don't make my mistake. Please

She's not a mean or bad person, just a horrible teacher. She covers roughly 30 to 40 pages of textbook content in a singe 50 minute class, and explains things in the most confusing way possible. Every single person I know who took this class spent upwards of 3 hours a day just studying the textbook to make up for her horrible teaching.

she is terrible. her writing is incoherent she expects you to already know chemistry and when you go to write down the important information she changes the slides on accident because she doesn't know how to use her iPad. don't take her unless you have no other option.
very bad lectures miserable homework if you take this class be prepared to learn all of the material on your own time

This woman is easily the worst professor on campus and don't know why she isn't yet fired. Her lectures make 0 sense because she does examples & more than half the time makes mistakes in them too. She spends atleast 20 mins of the class trying to figure out how to use the technology. Her exams are poorly worded and homeworks take 15+ hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She could barely read off the slides. The discussions were useless. The test prep was useless. The class got curved at 45% to pass because she is such a bad teacher. Genuinely such a terrible experience in her class. There are little to no resources available. Go for Griffith, I haven't heard one complaint about her.

Just a heads up for those taking CHEM135. Take Griffith or wait till another semester. Never take this woman at all COST. She is the worst UMD chem professor I ever had. Took Griffith after her and pass calmly since she relates it to engineering. Mignerey is just doing hardcore general chemistry with extra unnecessary work.

Professor Mignerey's lectures rarely *explain* new concepts when they are introduced, so if you want to really understand anything, your best bet is to teach it to yourself before lecture. Test averages were consistently low, and the tests were usually harder than the review material. Don't take this professor if you can help it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She doesn't even know what she is doing.
