reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I'm surprised Lindsay doesn't have better reviews. She seems a little cold/reserved at first but she's really great and helpful if you go to her office hours and she opens up as the semester progresses. She was my prof for poetry workshop and gave awesome comments, really helpful and as long as you actually try she is flexible and understanding.
Teacher is very unclear. She takes forever to grade assignments. She will expect you to write a paper without telling you what she wants you to write about.

this was my first class with Lindsay and though I did find her difficult, I realized that if you approach her for help, she is more than willing to clarify things. I did horribly on my first paper for her and subsequently met with her, and improved my next paper's grade by 3 whole letter grades! Shes amazing once you get to work with her repeatedly

At first, I was skeptical. However, her critiques of my work was some of the msot useful I've gotten. Even more so than some of the bigger name workshop professors. I've had Josh Weiner, Liz Arnold and Michael Collier, and Lindsay's comments were more thoughtful and sensitive. Take her workshops!

Horrible, monotone teacher.  NEVER TAKE HER! She grades her papers based on her own thoughts and if you don't have exactly what she thinks, you're screwed. She never gives assignment sheets, so you'll never know what you're supposed to write about.  Attendance is mandatory. She's very picky and has her favorites in class. SHE WAS THE WORST TEACHER!
She posts assignments last minute to, has no consideration for students, and is not a nice person
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Bely is one of the best professors I've had. BSCI400 was fascinating and changed how I understand animals!  She is incredibly nice, understanding, and willing to work with you. The textbook is easy to read. I had such a great experience in her class, I took another class; I didn't care what it was, I just wanted to spend more time in her class.

She had so many writing assignments and was really specific on the requirements of each literature review. I also thought the class was super boring even though I am a biology major I was literally falling asleep reading research paper after research paper- take any of the other cluster classes I've heard from friends they're better.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This was a very bio-heavy class (which I wasn't expecting). Also, I had to teach myself most of the material in order to do the assignments. I turned out fine, but I definitely had to put in more time and effort to really understand the material than I was initially expecting. Professor Bely is very nice & more than willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: This class took up more time than my engineering classes this semester. Assignments were graded very harshly and we had to read and analyze so many research papers. Very tedious class and bad professor - I do not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There was a written assignment due every class. Assignments were posted with very short notice, oftentimes in the afternoon before the due date at 9 AM, so it was hard to plan. She was not accommodating at all and graded harshly on participation. Everyone thought she cared too much about what was supposed to be an easy gen-ed.

Fantastic class and professor! Lots of memorization but it's all really interesting. You have to get the book for the (many) reading assignments, but it's super interesting. Exams were very reasonable and projects/assignments had clear instructions. Professor explains everything very clearly and loves to discuss the topics. Highly recommend!
Dr. Bely is really kind and makes class interactive and fun. She is very open to feedback and cares a lot about her students.

Cares so much for the topic and her students; she really does want everyone not only to pass, but to understand. Office hours super helpful. She tries to engage everyone in lectures. She takes sorta hard topics and simplifies them. She's very well spoken. You have to do the homeworks if you want to do well. Tests are difficult but possible.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: There is a small homework assignment due each class- some take longer than others. There were only a few big assignments. We discussed a lot of  technical details about regeneration and immortality. A lot of group efforts and discussions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Bely is really nice and sometimes even funny during lecture. The only problem is that her power points were hard to follow when going through them after lecture. So go to lecture so you don't miss what she says and doesn't include in her lecture.

Dr. Bely is absolutely fantastic! Her lectures are very informative and entertaining and for one lecture she even gives you candy (hershey kisses)! She is very clear on what she wants you to know for the exam and is always willing to answer questions both in class and during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really good and engaging professor, helped me learn content well. Things were presented in a way that made me feel really interested in psychology. Would highly recommend.

Dr. Jones was an amazing professor. The class was very straightforward; he made things easy. I would say even though he doesnt take attendance, he does do the end-of-class quizzes, which do require you to show up. Other than that, super nice guy, easy grader.
This class is very manageable. For me, the main struggle was tests and paying attention to lectures. He made them very hands on though and this lack of effort was only on my end.

Love this guy. Lectures are so engaging. There is a quiz at the start of every lecture so you have to get there on time, all the time, for credit. Regardless, he's wonderful. The textbook is online and free, sourced from websites and videos online. If you're into IO Psyc, he's the guy for you. Definitely take his class.

PSYC450 is pretty boring content-wise and it's a lot of coding in R. The current TA grades so unbelievably harshly for the R projects. there are also a few group projects in the lab which is dumb bc your grade depends on other ppl's work and it's already hard to code with ppl outside of lab. Dr. Jones himself is understanding and lenient though

Dr.Jones is great! 420 was super interesting, lots of good discussions. There's one major research paper that you work on the entire semester and a few other grades, but that's pretty much it. He's very understanding and accommodating if you are struggling and an need extension. I would def recommend taking a class with him!
he's pretty cool and funny

Dr. Jones was an awesome professor! Stats is a rough class no matter who the professor is but Dr. Jones was very open to feedback and accommodated to students very well. He is really funny and if you put in the work you will get a good grade. All of the exams had pretty good averages and I highly recommend taking Dr. Jones!

One of the BEST professors. I adored his lectures, worth attending. 
PROS: Funny class experiments. Extra credit frequently provided in class. 
Easy Assignments, Easy Exams, Easy Class.
He accepts giving credit for wrong answers if properly reasoned. 
CONS: long (but interesting) readings
I would definitely take another class with Dr. Jones.

I love Prof. Jones!! He really cares about his students and makes stat accessible and not as scary as it may seem. Class had a lot of homework due on Thursdays, but it wasn't unmanageable at all. He's a great lecturer and very accommodating to student concerns. Definitely recommend for PSYC200

Although Jones was an amazing professor, this class was just naturally very heavy in nature. If you have to take PSYC200, Jones is the way to go. There is a lot of HW, but it helps balance out your grade if you do bad on certain assignments or a test. Attendance is not mandatory but you do really need to go. Caring, funny, and understanding.
The professor is ok with teaching but you will have hours on hours of homework. He also doesn’t give any extensions as its “not fair” and will assign you a 4 page essay to hand in by 11:59 pm

i only went to two lectures and still got an a. jones is pretty convenient bc you can watch lectures on elms. you don't need to buy a textbook. his recorded lectures were always great. great for intro to psyc!

Dr. Jones is one of the best professors Ive ever had. His lectures were informative and fun, and the assignments and exams were very reasonable. There is no psychical textbook but instead a website shared by the psych professors. He definitely cares about his students and it shows! Its a shame I had to take his class online instead of in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at UMD. This class was challenging but Dr. Jones is very willing to help and really cares about his students. You can tell he is a passionate teacher who cares and enjoys what he does. Wish this class was in person because he is awesome.

Dr. Jones genuinely cares about his students and making sure we're actually learning the material. There's a lot of material for this class, so he asks for a lot of feedback, and he's willing to improve on anything. Very smart, down to earth guy that has a very receptive teaching style. Loved him!

Jones was great for PSYC100, but for PSYC200, not rly. he gives unnecessary formulas to calculate by hand when in reality your TI-84 is LITERALLY programmed to do those. thank god I took AP stat my senior year, so I mostly know the material. watching the async lectures is just supplementary material to me.

dr jones is such a nice prof, he really cares about what he's teaching and how you're learning. psyc450 was just sooo boring, but it was mainly the content and not him. he assigned an easy workload and was super flexible. awesome guy, very smart, cares a lot. the class itself was super boring tho.

great prof and class. work consists of modules every week: hour or two of reading, 30 mins of lecture videos, 20-30 question quiz on weekly topics, and one or two activities such as discussion boards or 2 pg papers. 3 exams, non-cumulative every 4 chapters/weeks or so. just go back and reread chapters/rewatch lectures. no work week after exam.

This class was an easy A, but there is a lot of reading to do every week. I suggest breaking it up into a little bit everyday and taking good notes for the exams since they're open note. I feel like I learned a lot and it was very organized, especially in the online format. Professor Jones tries his hardest to make it fun!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I enjoyed PSYC100 and learned a lot from this course. Dr. Jones and the TA's were incredibly helpful. They were all very accessible. I really liked the asynchronous format of the class.

This class was given asynchronously, but Professor Jones was very good about explicitly telling students what they needed to have accomplished for the week ahead. All work was due at the end of the week and could be finished in 3 hours. If you put the effort in, you will do well in this course. He was also available a lot to talk and help.
Professor Jones is really a great guy. Although our class was completely asynchronous this semester, he was easily accessible. His tests were fair and he is a quick grader. I totally recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr Jones is a great professor for PSYC 100. He connects with his students and is very available outside of class. His exams are fair. It is also not too difficult to receive an A in his class: all you need to do is attend class and study the lectures and readings. I would definitely recommend him for PSYC 100.

This class is SO MUCH WORK! The exams are open notes but somehow still really hard. But it isn't Jones's fault really, it's just an annoying time-consuming class. He was accommodating when we moved online, and tries really hard. I complained a lot about this class but he did what he could. It's not his fault he teaches a boring required class.

Great professor for psyc100. Be very careful about the due dates. Do the work and put the effort in, you'll pass with at least a B no problem. Fun class though really learned a lot a lot. Made me want to major in Psych.

Jones should not be teaching statistics. He is very nice, caring about students, and seems to understand the material of the course, but he cannot articulate. He spends loads of time speaking in circles instead of making a point. Homework rarely relates to lectures, and tests are extraordinarily difficult. I had to teach myself stats.
This professor is is great for 100. Lectures well, uses study guides, and will help you. Really a good new teacher.

Dr. Jones is my FAVORITE professor. I had him for PSYC100 and I changed my major to Psychology halfway through taking his class. He has a way of connecting to students and using technology to enhance the learning experience that makes his lectures fun, interactive and interesting. And the readings? Fascinating. I would read read them for fun.

While Dr. Jones exhibits passion for teaching, he is not a statistics professor. He's knowledgeable, but he simply cannot communicate information effectively to students. People are constantly asking questions. Homework is never on what was covered in class, and his lectures are monotonous and unhelpful. Maybe take Jones for PSYC100, not stats.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Jones is just a super nice professor, and he structures his class really well. From day 1 you know when every assignment is due and when every test is so there are no surprises and you can plan your schedule accurately. He also tries to make the lectures more interested and often involves the class with online clickers and videos.

Dr. Jones is a fantastic professor, a great human being, and an inspirational educator. The breadth of material in PSYC100 is quite expansive but he manages to keep it doable and interesting. He is also very fair in evaluating students. Yes, you gonna have to study and put effort into written assignments but you will also esquire useful knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: The exams are fairly easy and so is the grading on the biweekly writing assignments. Dr. Jones is an approachable, friendly guy and is one of my favorite professors at UMD.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Jones is a really nice, funny guy. He's very accessible and was very clear about what needed to be done. Nothing was overly difficult and he would hint toward things on the exams. The exams weren't too hard, but do require studying. This class was a pretty good experience.
Idk how this prof has had so many good reviews, one of my least favorites at UMD. Don't know if this semester was a bad one for her, but this class is terrible. So much work and so little direction.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: WORST PROFESSOR EVER! This course would be exponentially more effective and less stressful if it had a competent professor. Get ready for loads of group work but no in-class time to complete these lengthy projects. I would so much rather use time in class to work on the project rather than listening to her ramble on about whatever comes to mind.

This professor is so difficult because of how unorganized she is. Her lecturing just rambles into different tangents when we could spend that time doing the random assignments she throws at us. I have no idea how she is rated so highly and I wish this wasn't a mandatory course.
Dr. B is extremely caring and has a very unique background. She is truly a gem at UMD. My favorite INST prof.

Professor B. is an empathic and caring lady, giving students the benefit of the doubt, and is accommodating to any problem you face during the course. She may ramble on during lectures or say out of pocket things, which some people may find comforting, amusing, or offensive. She is primarily a researcher, making feedback slow. Highly recommend.

FOR INST380: This class proved extremely challenging due to disorganization, heavy workload, unclear grading criteria, and the professor's inflexibility and late grading. Delayed feedback and consistent controversial comments, seemingly for shock value, disrupted the learning experience. An immediate replacement for INST380 is crucial imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof B is an extremely nice, caring, and inspiring lady. I feel bad giving her such a bad rating, but her class was awful. The class was mostly common sense and I didn't learn much, but I still passed with an A. Complaints: Every assignment was unclear, she rambles for 30 mins before starting each lecture, an extremely drawn out group project, etc.
Love her. She's extremely nice and accommodating to her students. We didn't have exams but there is a huge group project. If you put in enough effort, you'll do well.

I had a wonderful experience being a student under Beth. She is an extremely caring individual who does whatever she can to help you succeed. She has plenty of real-world experience and is willing to share that with you. 490 was smooth because she was so organized, and guided you through your specific project with the client. Best professor in INST
The Exams were clear, nothing unexpected (Study guide and test were one in the same). Great teacher; if you put forth the effort then the class isn't hard.
Gives really good feedback on assignments. Also curved heavy in an already easy class. Just genuinely a good person and teacher.
She was best teacher i took year. Great response to assignments and helps the student pass the class and have a good grade.

Amazing teacher, would 100% take her again. She does clicker questions and sometimes in class assignments but not that often. She's a very easy grader and the tests are super easy as well. Very easy class overall.

shes by far my favorite teacher. Honestly the sweetest and tries her best to connect on a personal level. Tests are super easy and comes straight from the slides. You dont really have to show up but there are TopHat quizzes sometimes.

Bonsignore is the best 201 professor at UMD. She is an absolute sweetheart who gives you every opportunity to get an A. Make sure you make a groupme or google doc to help study for the class and the exams and final will be a breeze. The class is also tophat heavy, so make sure you're coming to class or you'll miss points. She really is a gem.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Really awesome professor. She is very nice and really cares about her students. Projects and courseworks are somewhat easy, maybe because she gives a lot of ideas on how to do them. Also, make sure to do the online discussions as those are easy points. Easy A if you don't slack.

Awesome teacher; very funny but class is lecture heavy. She tries to keep the class lively. The class itself is very easy bc she puts up all the slides from lecture. She wants you to pass and does everything she can for you to get a good grade. There's not really any busy work either.  Definitely would take this class and professor again.

Elizabeth is a great teacher. She always tries to relate to the outside world so that students could relate to what she is teaching. She is very nice and is always smiling/laughing. She creates study guides for you and gives you extra credit on midterms. She is also very willing to change up due dates if needed/requested. Totally recommend!
Not a good teacher, he rushes too much. And is very rude.

Bezejou's smart, but not a good professor. Doesn't use class time to lecture. You will walk into class with a board full of notes that you copy, but he doesn't expand on the topics themselves and explain each process and how he got to an answer. You have to ask specific questions. People in my class say they have to teach themselves.Character limit
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: It's been 47 years since my last math class, and it was a bit of a challenge to get back into it. My test taking skills are especially rusty. Anyway, I thought the course was well organized, each class built on the previous classes, the problems presented in each class built logically on each other. Will take again.

Prof. Bezejouh is a great teacher. The material is tough but he breaks it down through several steps for students to understand. Very important to know your prerequisite for the class. A lot of it is covered in first 5 weeks. Also a lot of the material on the test is a repeat of what has been reviewed in class. So stay on top with the review.

Lectures tend to only be problem examples with some explanation, grade hinges a lot more on how well you do on the difficult/harshly graded tests than the mountain of HW you get. He doesn't like questions, being annoyed  or making other classmates answer it. If you went from MATH015 to 115, there's more to do in less time. Felt stressful overall.

We had 4 exams, 12 quizzes and some homework assignments. The work was manageable. A respectful professor, however, does not explain content clearly at all. Rushes through the lecture and doesnt give any time for you to understand the material and ask questions. No extra credit. The 4 exams are mainly your whole grade so must do well on those.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Ive literally never had a worse teacher in my life. Hes so rude to everyone. Averages on the tests were Fs. He doesnt care about his students. Whenever a student asks a question he responds so rudely making us feel bad for even asking. If you get him for calc i recommend you switch out IMMEDIATELY.

Multiple students this year have had conflicts with Prof. Bezejouh, who has never failed to be accusatory, unprofessional, and rude. I have had to rely on the textbook for information due to the lack of clarity when the material is being taught in class. We are given review sheets before exams, but they are not an accurate reflection of the tests.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally the worst prof I would even imagine having. He teaches things in the most complicated way to learn them, and whenever I'd ask friends and tutors for help, they would say that he completely overcomplicated it. They taught me a way simpler and efficient way EVERY SINGLE TIME. He never explains anything and craps on you for asking questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof. Ben does not like questions. He will embarrass the questioner and act like you should already understand the material. He does not explain much in his lectures. Textbook was listed but not used and his lectures were not on subject matter but on math problems, so trying to follow along was like slogging through mud. Would not take again.

Professor B doesn't explain the concepts that much when he is teaching. He writes the answers down on the board and expects you to know it. I also asked a question in class one day and he responded with a snarky comment telling me why I asked that question which made me feel extremely embarrassed in front of the whole entire class.
The prof is ok at explaining concepts but emailing him about things is not worth it. He's rude and won't give a straight answer

only used lectures and does not fully explain the work he is doing during those lectures. A lot of work outside the class is required. You should have a solid understanding of trig and algebra before taking this class.

Ben expects students to already know most of what hes talking about. Granted most of my class has taken calc 1 before, but not everyone has. His tests are extremely difficult and the directions are vague. Youll see problems on there that are different from what youve ever done for the already absurd amounts of homework and test reviews.

Mr. Bezejou expects students to learn on their own instead of teaching them... he is quite hands-off - merely copying the equations from the textbook & sometimes going minutes without speaking; writing down the math without explaining. When he does explain, he's not very clear. Attend class & study as much as possible. You have to teach yourself...
He will expect you to know how process work, don't take class if you're not well-rounded in basic algebra and trigonometry.

Prof. Ben isn't a terrible teacher, but he talks very slow during lecture. Also, his thick accent doesn't help either. That being said, if you ask him for feedback or clarity on a question, he'll explain where you went wrong. Quizzes and tests are graded very harshly and if you don't do a problem the exact way taught, points are taken off.

I think most people will find this professor hit-or-miss. The course material is clear, he knows what he's talking about and he writes out all steps taken. The class moves very very quickly, though I don't think that's his fault. Tests are hard. Put in a solid amount of work and you should be fine.

Professor Ben is a great teacher; I had him for math 110 and he was very easy to talk to. He'd make sure you understood the material and would make time to tutor you if you needed it. He goes over everything in class, and at the very beginning of the semester he gives you a schedule with all your assignments and due dates. So helpful!
He isn't very helpful at all. He just expects you to know eveything

The class in and of itself is easy, but he is not a very good teacher. His accent is think and hard to understand. When you talk to him, sometimes he seems confused by what you are saying. Handwriting is terrible. Only take him if you either already understand the material or are willing to work on your own.
Difficult to understand sometimes. He isn't really much help either if you're poor at math. Try to get another teacher.

I took Ben's Math 115 class at University of Maryland and I believe that was his first semester there (Fall 14). Overall he was really nice, encouraging at times. I would definitely take him again. I learned a lot! He can be encouraging too. His quizzes and tests keep you on your toes. His tough grading comes from the top hes not to blame
Best professor I've ever had! I like Bill as a professor and as a good mentor.

This is by far the worst professor I have ever had the displeasure of taking. He does not respect students time nor boundaries. He expected me to respond to emails during scheduled student breaks. If I had more evidence that he is going out of his way to make my class harder I would have reported him

The vast majority of work I did in his 490 was pointless paperwork and navigating his convoluted coursework requirements. He is vague in instruction and far too harsh of a grader although the latter could be the awful TAs. Be ready to waste all your time frantically looking through slides and course documents trying to figure out what to do.

Bill Kules is the best Bill. There has never been a better Bill. Bill Clinton? Nope not as presidential. Bill Gates? Nope not as smart. Billiam Shakespeare? Not as good as speaking as Bill Kules. This is the Alpha Bill. All other Bills are cheap imitation Bills. Do yourself a favor and partake of the fine teachery that is this pinnacle of Bills.
I love Bill, and I would definitely take him again.

He takes points off for the littlest of things. There's no telling what he could take points off for. He doesn't do any actual teaching whatsoever, you have to teach yourself. I don't reccomend this guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Bill is a great professor who wants his students to succeed. To be successful, you need to read AND PRACTICE PROGRAMMING every day! Homework is heavily weighed so you need to do it! Ask for help when needed ASAP. You do not want to fall behind. I would definitely recommend taking this professor (or any other class he teaches).
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He's a great professor, but INST 630 is a programming INTENSE class. It is not something that you can easily get through if you do not pick up programming quickly. He is definitely willing to work with you if you need it, but for me the class was really hard. I am a Library Science major, not a Info studies specific major.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Michael Binder's teaching style presents challenges, characterized by disinterest, tangential lectures, and unclear instructional materials. His tendency to stray from relevant content and the difficulty of assignments frustrate students, raising questions about his suitability for his position. Reevaluate of his qualifications.

His attitude is what spoils the entire class for me. He uses accusatory tones on his students, telling them they should stop procrastinating and study more after everyone fails his exams. He accuses everyone of cheating. And grades you on attendance. If you miss ONE class he will badger you for an excuse note or dock your grade on the second.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Prof. Binder really knows his stuff, and is a great lecturer. He has a lot of material to cover, but he explains it well and is happy to stop and answer questions, and take more time in office hours.
You have to attend and taking notes, but if you do that, homework and exams are ok.
Prof. Binder does expect students to have physics and trig basics.

Most of the class kept failing exams, changed the structure of the exams that everyone was failing after the withdrawl period which significantly affected the class average but there was no warning beforehand. Difficult content but the TAs  expained nicely
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Binder is super smart and really cares a lot about sustainability. The lectures are often tedious and there are only a few grades for the semester, but if you attend lectures and take some basic notes on the slides you will pass just fine. Prof Binder is available for office hours or zoom calls for coursework or just to chat

Binder is a good person but not a good teacher. When the class preforms poorly on an exam he does not take personal responsibility, telling us to "study more". The class itself was him reading off slides. On a positive note, he genuinely cares about saving the environment.

This the worst professor I've had. He rants about politics during lectures. The class structure is atrocious, exams make up 75% of the final grade. The average score for the first exam was a D, and his response to the class failing was, "let this be a lesson to study better next time". He denied any responsibility and does not curve. Good Luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is an engineer who teaches architect majors like they are engineering majors. He is monotone and will drone on about information that's not needed. When it comes to taking notes if you do not get it on class you're out of luck, the slides he provides for studying outside of class are just pictures. He does not respect studio or other classes.

He was very knowledgable and passionate about the subject. The class was structured with quizzes that were varying levels of difficulty- at first, they were too difficult for students. However, the professor was accommodating and used student feedback to make them more fair. The midterm was a group essay, which was not convenient online.

Hes a tough grader and the semester project grading rubrics are not provided but worth almost a quarter of the grade. No respect for other classes time and course load especially studio. Places the responsibility of teaching outside of lectures almost completely on TAs. Will be rude, does not respect or address student concerns.

Professor Binder is very knowledgeable. His lectures can be kind of boring at times but he makes sure to be very thorough, as long as you pay attention youll do well on his quizzes. It was his first time teaching the course so it is a given that there were a few hiccups nonetheless, I think hell get perfect his teaching methods as he progresses.

I had Dr. Johanna Birnir in Spring 2023. Dr. Birnir is an average professor however, her research in the field has made her respected. GVPT201 was not easy and there were hard quizzes every week on the content of the class. The class is extremely challenging, especially if you do it on your own so make friends in the class! Dr. Birnir is okay.

Overall, Prof Birnir was super nice and knowledgeable. Taking this class online was tough, the lectures were very long and somewhat boring. Much of this class is statistics (plus some coding) and mirrors the concepts of Intro to Stats. She provides all the resources for you to do well, but asking for help is key.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The content in this class seems super overwhelming at first, but the professor and TAs really help out. This is a really good class to take to get a basic understanding of polling and coding using R studio. This class definitely gets easier with time.

Birnir is a great prof and knows her stuff but it's the class content and workload that got me stressed. There's weekly coding assignments and I went to my TA's office hours every week, I couldn't have gotten through this class without her. Manage your time effectively. As long as you do that, the class is not as daunting as it may seem at first.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Birnir is by far one of the most understanding and supportive professors I've ever had. I received a poor grade on one of the weekly homework assignments and the following day she sent me an email asking if I needed extra guidance on the material. The course schedule is also super organized and structured well.

Johanna is lovely and an expert in her field but the class was really sucky if you don't enjoy coding + statistics. The class was kind've a weird combination of subjects and hard to get through at times. She was wonderful though and always available by email
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is a great teacher. Make sure you ask questions in class and start your homework early before they are due each week. She has a wonderful personality. Keep in contact with classmates as well during this class.

Birnir is so nice and she knows what she's talking about. The subject being taught is just the worst. It's so boring. It's basically another statistics course. We had to code and interpret data. I would not recommend this class if you are not a gov major and do not have to take it, but I would recommend Prof Birnir. She is so nice and helpful.

GVPT100 is mandatory for Gov majors, but it's the worst. It's all statistical analysis. She is very into the subject, and does her best to make lectures interesting and help students. She's a good teacher, and I would really enjoy having her in another sort of class. She likes doing statistics puns, and most of them are pretty funny, actually.

She is brilliant, but not an effective teacher. At the close of the semester she has yet to give a numerical score for anything! Students receive constructive criticism but have no way of knowing what the actual letter grade is, even if they ask. This is not how you teach a class.

This class was incredibly boring, but it is mandatory for GVPT majors, so it's worth putting some effort into this course and completing all of the weekly assignments.  The exams were quite easy.  This is a government statistics course, so don't expect to learn anything intriguing.  Still, the skills you learn in this class are indispensable.
not helpful

This class isn't a great introduction to government and politics in my opinion. It basically focuses on getting accustomed with the SPSS software. I depended on the spss handbook which helped a lot. My TA was no help at all and neither was the professor. I struggled with the software and spent up to 8 hours at time so be prepared for that.

I was very disappointed in this class. I normally love government classes. I guess if you want to do political science in the sense that you do lots of polls and stats then this is the class for you, if not then I'd choose another teacher.

There was hardely any information about "government" taught in this class. It was entirely a statistics class, which isn't something I was expecting from an "introduction to Government" class. The class is taught totally out of an SPSS textbook, which just teaches you the logistics of analyzing quantitative political data. Pick a different teacher.

I found this professor frustrating: she teaches directly out of a 120$ textbook and does not delve into any conversation about government. Her course is entirely designed to get students used to the program SPSS. She was strict, challenging (one assignment took me 5 hours and I didn't finish!) and hard to get along with. I found her useless.
No Comments

Class was very engaging and interesting.  There was variety in the lectures, including video clips and group activities.  Professor Birnir appeared to enjoy teaching the class and made lectures a pleasure to attend. Fair amount of reading required to do well in the class. Still, highly recommended.

BEWARE!!! This course was ridiculous. I understand summer courses require a bit more time and work because they are condensed; this was vile. She had 7+  assignments due every week and then graded harshly. Final test AND final paper with readings + discussions due the same day. She doesn't give a thing but takes all out of her students.

Dr. Bianchini is extremely knowledgable of her subject - you truly won't find a better wealth of Medieval Spanish historical knowledge anywhere. Most of the work is graded by the TA and the grades are not given back in a timely manner. Discussion is extremely important, group work is a big component as well. The main grade is an article analysis.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I don't know why people are rating her so harshly, because she's a great teacher! She knows what she's talking about and her lectures are easy to understand. You will have to read and write, but that's normal for history classes, and I didn't find it to be excessive. Definitely recommend her classes if history interests you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I found this class RELS 289C/HIST289A to be extremely interesting. As a virtual class, the professor included video lectures, with note sheets to follow during the video, and short quizzes to test what you had learned. Discussion groups were also virtual, but most students were enthusiastic about participation.

if you're not interested in the subject don't take this class but I had no problems with Professor B. she spoke well and this is one of the few classes I've consistently wanted to ask questions in. the discussions were well run too. not too many papers, and the final assignment was actually quite fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A professor could not be any more useless. She is a very tough grader, she puts no useful notes on her slides, and you will not learn anything in this class because she will overload you with work. If you're smart you won't take her class, save yourself the stress.

DO NOT TAKE HERE. By far one of the worst professors I have had. I took her over the summer and she assigns an insane amount of work for a summer class, I learned nothing in this class because I was too busy trying to catch up on work, each day we had about 7 assignments due. She is an incredibly harsh grader and not an understanding professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally one of the worst professors out there. I was in a special situation the semester I took this class in and she was not ready to make any concessions for me even after knowing what I was going through. On the other hand, she penalized me for anything and everything possible. TA was the only saving grace.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Bianchini is really awesome. This class was really interesting in discussing facets of Iberia I had not known about. In discussion, you are graded on participation, which for me is never usually a problem, but because everyone has to participate grades are lower. Clicker questions in lecture, and a few written papers in class.

If a researcher wanted to study why students who graduate from big Universities are so poorly educated, in the humanities in particular, they need look no further than Professor Bianchini's class. Professor Bianchini wants students to memorize useless trivia, and makes her tests extra difficult so that she can tell herself that she's "educating".

Taking Dr. Bianchini's class was a delight. Her class does require rigor, but it is certainly not unreasonable. If you want to just GET BY as a history major, this class isn't for you. But if you really want to learn and challenge yourself, take this class. If you want to do well in life, you need to be willing to put in the hard work and EARN IT.
she is a really good lecturer. I had her for History of the Crusades and I ended up really enjoying it. Get prepared to write though. It is a really essay heavy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I signed up for this class and droped it ASAP because it was SO BORING. I kept falling asleep in her class. You just sit in a lecture hall and keep taking notes as she talks. Its just so dry that I couldn't continue.  You have to take notes all during lecture and she had some heavy reading you are suppose to do often.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: ATTEND. It's not mandatory,but literally everything on the test is from lecture. Do the email responses (paragraphs about reading),the points add up and make difference between letter grade. Participation points are sketchy,sometimes forgets you participated, so overparticipate to compensate. Lectures are matter of fact,no theatrics.

Tests are completely ridiculous. She expects you to remember 100+ terms, 5+ readings and info about them, and more. Like I understand this is a history course and upper-level but as a history MAJOR, her expectations are insane. I'm interested in the material but her rules and expectations make the class miserable.
Best professor
Hes not honest. Asked for a recommendation, he wrote falsely. Totally unexpected.

Bill Higgins has mastered the art of teaching really hard material in a way that is easy to understand. His sense of humor can definitely be a little rude and crude, but if you can roll with it for a semester, you'll learn to appreciate his class. This guy has taught really successful physicians and he's pretty much a historic landmark of UMD.

While he behaves pleasantly in front of a large class, he is a different character when serving as a counselor. Without offering constructive criticism, he degradingly judged my career goals and even hobbies; he made nasty comments about my running and tried to persuade me to quit, even though his room is decorated with sporting paraphernalia.

Hard class but if you take it take it with Higgins! He is awesome and loves students. You have to study though. Not a cake course. Heard he was hard for BSCI 440 also though I didn't take it with him. Ask questions! Participate!

Best professor I've ever had! Tests were challenging, but you'll do well if you understand the concepts and can apply them. This means doing lots of practice questions. I hope Higgins never retires from UMD so my kids will have him too (one can only dream!).

I liked the material we covered, but the tests were impossible. I typed up my notes from class, made study guides for the tests, read the book, and still failed every single test. The class has some interesting topics, but if you are looking for an easy class, just don't take it. And Dr. Higgins can be rude sometimes; we don't have the same humor.

Do not take higgins for mamm phys lab! he treats this class like it's the only one you have and assigns a lot of group papers! He also had very high expectations for the students and grades really strictly on assignments. You'd be lucky get even a B- in this class. He also doesn't curve. On the plus side, he is funny times during lecture.
He's awesome and fun to listen to, his lectures are great but, his doesn't really explain the material very well, and his tests are really hard.

Concepts are pretty abstract and not very relevant to professions in science, but easy to understand, but the tests are strange. You can walk into the exam having studied for hours, but get C's on all of the tests because they are entirely true/false and you can get them wrong even if you know the material. Fun and friendly guy though.
Master Yoda is the best!

This is honestly a completely useless class- it makes EASY concepts, EXTREMELY HARD- and the tests are ridiculous! I've never seen such low averages, and I'm a bio major- terrible class + terrible professor = DOOMED!

Below is an excerpt from my ERAS application for Anesthesiology residency, I matched and start residency in July09.  "It was at Maryland where I met my favorite teacher Dr. Higgins, my Mammalian Physiology professor.  It was at this point that I fell in love with Physiology.  He was an incredible teacher, not just of physiology, but also of life".
Cant teach awful personality. Thinks he is he Jesus Christ when it comes to biology!
Dr. Higgins is probably responsible for inspiring 90% of the undergraduates from UMD who go to med school to choose that career option.  Excellent teacher.

Higgins is a really bad teacher.  His personality is repulsive as well, so it is extremely burdensome to attend his lectures.  He was utterly useless when it came to gaining a better understanding of course material.  Notes were very poorly organized.  Plus he's a jerk on a power trip (still, after however many years).

Prof. Higgins's lectures move very quickly and he does his best to keep everybody interested.  BSCI207 is just one of those classes that nobody wants to take but since you have to you may as well take it with him.  The tests were hard and frustrating but he tells you EXACTLY what is on the test.  Don't study anything else and you should be fine.

This class was horrible. He is a nice guy but his tests aer extremely hard. He teaches is with another professor so it's hard to follow since they change the format of th test. Avoid taking this class. Lectures are not consistent and you learn absolutely nothing.

lectures are very disorganized and his powerpoint slides are useless cause he never follows them...his test are ridiculously hard especially since he just makes lame jokes in class and doesn't actually teach the material...sends all questions to the TAs who are useless.  gives off the impression that he cares but doesnt really

His lectures are quite strange as he sometimes does strange things before or after class. He never answers questions straightforward. AND his Exams are very very very very difficult. I honestly don't recommend him to bsci207 students.

He is the hardest professor of Biology that I ever had. His exams are very hard with a lot of mathematical graphs. I love Biology, but I have to admit that his class was extremely hard. He teaches too fast and most of the time hi doesn’t want to answer questions. He will send you to the TA (s). I never study so hard for a biology class before. Orga

at 1st, u may like him b/c he is entertaining and funny. However, he is extremely cocky, obnoxious, n very bad with confrontations. He does not have office hours n isn't very helpful. When you ask him questions b4/after class he will give u a short ans n will not explain. His exams are extremely hard (w/ many graphs). u'll need a recorder.

Higgins is the guy to take 440 with ! it'll be the hardest, most challenging thing you'll have take in your life - but he's an amazing teacher and that's an amazing class. TAKE it as long as mr. higgins is still there !

horrible teacher to take classes online with. dont waste your time or money with him. doesnt return phone calls or emails in a timely fashion. nor, does he try to help online students with course material.
horrible teacher. Thinks he is the best thing that ever lived and his class made me sick. Don't take a class with him

I did not like Higgins but I'll admit he's a very energetic, entertaining lecturer with obvious interest in his students' success and a love for teaching.  Reading of textbook was absolutely required.  Exams were difficult but he made plenty of practice exams available online, so preparing was straightforward.  Not an easy A.

I took his class cuz ppl told me he'd be easy, and he is, but you really gotta read, cuz he's not very thourough in lecture, but don't miss a single lecture, he'll tell u EXACTLY whats on the exam! If you do your work, this is an easy A, the exams are not too complicated.
Higgins is my favorite teacher of all time. Go to class, you'll get an A.
this man is the bomb.  great teacher, and really funny.  take 105 with him, absolutely.  he's the best teacher ive had yet in college.
No Comments
He is an excellent teacher, very engaging, entertaining and extremely thorough.  On the surface, he seems easy but don't be fulled, he expects you to know the material.
No Comments
Awesome prof best I ever had!
Higgins obviously cares about his students' success, though exams were hard

He knows nothing about customer experience based on my experience in this class. This is by far the most awful class I have taken in the entire world. Professor Motwani's Cloud Computing course gave me strong, industry-relevant skills that I now actively use in my job search. Dr. Motwani is a great professor! As an Accounting Major who started with minimal Excel skills, this class has given me a lot of practical knowledge. SOLID PROFESSOR! She taught me how to code, use tableau, excel, and make websites, all in one semester (without being too much). If you go to class and pay attention you will be fine. She's always happy to help, ACTUALLY HELPFUL, and good teacher. I am in graduate school now and I appreciate this professor even more because of what she taught me.

She's amazing... learning really is just learning with her. Not punitive in the least, and grading is an afterthought with her. She really wants you to learn and isn't about bogging you down with the risk of failing or anything like that.

She can be intimidating but if you go to her office hours she's very sweet and accommodating. Awful!!! I learned nothing in this course and ended up with an A.

avoid

Awesome professor!

One of the best professors I've ever had. He cares about his students and made sure nobody was left behind. It's the first time any of my college teachers have showed that kind of care and taken the time to get to know us. I would definitely recommend taking his class because you will learn a lot and have a lot of time to voice your own opinion.

LING240 is also a great class with a good foundation of linguistics, but it is definitely focused on the psycholinguistics side of things.

Prof is good, it's the course content which I have a problem with. I expected the content to be focused on the theoretical side of linguistics. Instead, this class was dominated by Phonology/IPA (which they needlessly made us memorize) and the scientific part of linguistics. Class should have been an easy A, but it was made unnecessarily hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

Professor Bleam is one of the worst professors I have ever had at UMD. She has made the course so much tougher than it needs to be. This is LING200, yes, a 200 LEVEL COURSE. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

Prof Bleam is an amazing teacher; her lectures are funny and interactive and she explains things in a way that makes sense to someone who's never taken ling. You definitely need to go to class, but reading the textbook isn't necessary as long as you understand the material.

Let me just start out by saying that I have attended EVERY lecture and discussion section. This woman is crazy and makes the content of LING200 WAY more complicated than it needs to be. For an intro course such as LING200, she should NOT be teaching; she needs to be teaching upper-level, 300-400 level courses. In short, do NOT take this professor.

I have had Dr. Bleam for 240 and 311 and she is probably the best prof i have ever had. linguistics is TOUGH to explain but she is amazing. She is absolutely amazing but linguistics is hard. she gives you everything to pass

she's cool
