While I appreciated his lectures sometimes, his prewritten PDF makes it hard to follow at times and did not help me learn at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: How I imagine if AI started teaching. The closest thing to a robot.

He'll literally never answer his email and always makes remarks about how fast he takes the exams. His lectures consist of prewritten notes and either goes very fast or very slow. Just not a great experience.

Knows his stuff very well and presents it logically, but not a very nice guy. Contrary to what his physical appearance may suggest, he is an intimidating guy that seems like he does not want people to pass. His class is easy though so you'll slide through just fine.

The more organized and neat professor ever. He lays everything out for you and makes it impossible for you to fail if you're willing to do the work. Good lectures with examples and straightforward exams, although he is meticulous about details. Lectures can be boring a tad boring but goes with the territory. Good demos in the lab. Great choice.

His lectures are quite thorough and you could probably skip reading the book. Be sure to do a ton of practice problems as that's the best way to get a good grasp. He's a tough grader, but he's very fair and provides a little extra credit. I don't think I could have had a much better lecturer than him for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors so far.  His lectures were very organized and he always spent time doing example problems so that we could master the concepts.  Tests were tricky, but he gives plenty of study materials.  He knows is stuff and is always willing to answer questions.

He does a really good job of teaching. Really makes it easy understand the material. Make sure you actually do the homework though.  Also, do all he old exam problems he gives you to help prepare for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bonenberger is possibly one of the greatest professors here at UMD. He is a genius in every definition of the word, wrote the textbook that you use, and makes everything just so easy. Definitely choose this man to teach you, his class was the most clairvoyant and organized of all those I have taken.

He's an amazingly organized and methodical professor and he's also a genius. He really understands what he teaches. He can also be pretty funny at times. The material isn't too hard to understand and the tests are fair; just go to the review sessions and do the practice problems before each exam.
very easy to learn from...looks like ron burgandy
Ron Burgundy is the best teacher ever!
His organized lectures make note taking easy and he does a great job at covering all of the important topics. Tests have been fair. Based off of homework and group problems done in class.

Extremely methodical and straightforward teacher.  He wrote the book, so he's pretty much the expert on the stuff. Picky about grading quizzes and homework, but the exams are done by all of the teachers.  To get an A, do ALL of the practice problems and you should be fine.  Gives some extra credit.  Also, don't skip class.
Got a haircut so hes not so 70's anymore. wrote the book so hes very helpful. tests are fair. hes a great teacher and puts up great notes.

This professor presents the lecture material really clear. He puts up "perfect" notes on the board. If you take notes, you'll guarantee to have "perfect" notes to study from. The only twist to this professor is that you can only use one side of the formula sheet except for the final exam which you can use both sides.

Best professor I've had. He wrote the textbook, so you can either read the textbook or pay attention in class. There is a sign-in, but he doesn't notice or care if you show up late. He allows formula sheets on tests. The class starts out with a low time commitment, but the homework does take much longer later in the semester. Get him if you can.
look at the two comments above this theyre perfect
No Comments

Bonenberger is very clear, knows his stuff, and writes everything on the board-so take notes. do and hand in HW on time, b/c its graded. he may look like he's still in the 70's but he can teach mechanics so that you'll understand.

Great teacher, extremely clear on the class material. very 70s style person. He writes everything you need to know in the class---literally everything. Perfect if you take notes because he's just a neat person when it comes to writings on the board. explains things with simple mind set so he's definately a great great choice if you are taking ENES.

Professor Boule's lectures aren't always the most interesting but she makes sure to cover all the content thoroughly. Lots of guest lecturers. The main work outside of class is weekly reading quizzes, but many were moved around because of guest lecturers so there were fewer quizzes than the syllabus said. Flexible due dates.

Attendance is mandatory as roughly 20% of your grade is in class assignments. The graders will knock 25% off your papers for small errors or not including small things on the rubric. For our final paper, we submitted proposals around midterms and did not get grades/feedback until TWO DAYS before the paper was due (INCUDING EXTENSIONS).
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Took this last winter and it was a breeze. Make sure to weekly readings before class & the slides will make more sense. No final exam & the mid-term was like 5 questions (in a bluebook). I wish she gave more feedback on essays but other than that great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: No textbook, weekly discussion boards, 3-4 article length readings per week. There is a midterm and two final papers but both of which are fairly reasonable. I did a short paragraph assignment that turned into extra credit and ended this class with a 100.1%. The topics are also super applicable.

I had Prof Boules for ENSP340 there just wasn't an option to choose that. I liked her, she's very sweet and caring for her students she is just a bit nitpicky with grading. I did well in her class, I just had some assignments drop points because of little things that annoyed me a bit but overall I recommend her. Super nice person
This class was so easy. I never attended, studied for the exams based on the lecture slides, and did the discussion boards and got an A. Def recommend.

Do not take her classes if you can avoid it, she is impossible to learn from. The speed of her lectures is very fast and she only reads off slides that she does not post. She provides very little examples and is extremely monotone, making it hard to pay attention and to take notes. She does not address questions in class and does not give feedback.

She was very attentive to students and class was very conversational. Lectures werent always the most informative but it wasnt as difficult as other classes Ive had. Overall very solid professor and fun to take if you participate. Show up to class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr.Heidarian is a boring lecturer in my opinion. She doesn't record lectures which could have been helpful since she can be monotone and boring. You'll feel like going to sleep in her class. Despite this, she is a wonderful and caring person. She does help you a lot on the hw and provide solution on piazza. But sadly her teaching doesn't help me
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Best lecturer and STEM professor at UMD. There is a lot to cover during the semester, but we got through almost everything except for the last chapter (which she provided good self study resources for). I was enrolled in phys131 the prior semester but I dropped it during the schedule adjustment period because of how poorly taught it was.

I thought she was a great professor. She provided a ton of extra credit during her exams. It was usually over 10 points. You need to put in some work and effort into the class but if you do all of the practice problems and understand them, you should be good for the exam. She also dropped the lowest of three midterms and her final was very fair.

The class was tough. She is an enthusiastic lecturer, and good at explaining things. Homework is tough, worse than MyMathlabs. Weekly quizzes are pretty much guaranteed for 100% which, along with labs helps your grade. Labs are tedious, but easy to get an A in. She posts a lot of good problem solving videos which were very helpful.

I had a tough time following the pace. The course loosely followed a textbook in which we learned 13 chapters and each of these chapters had up to 8 sections at times. In a span of two class periods, she would move on from one chapter to the next, it's way too fast for people who have never been exposed to physics before!!

It was so clear that she cares about her students doing - always supportive, allows you to drop your lowest midterm, and has tons of extra credit on the midterms. just study the problem sets really well!

I love her! She is patient and kind. Physics has always been hard for me but she explains things very simply. She also supplies a lot of supplemental videos we can always refer to for difficult problems. There's a lot of online homework, and it's often very difficult, but I found the exams to be much easier, so I was well prepared for them.

This professor is REALLY lenient and she wants all of her students to do well. We had two curves this semester on two of the exams, and one of them bought everybody's overall grade up by two letter grades! She also drops the lowest exam score and she has extra credit questions on all of them. Study the problem set questions hard!

Obviously, Physics is not an easy class, however, Dr. Heidarian really does care about her students and wants you to pass the course. She is very fair about grading and your lowest exam grade is dropped at the end of the semester. I would recommend taking 121 with her.

This class is really difficult but that's just physics. She's a fine teacher but there's not enough time to cover all of the material in class so she flies through it, defiantly set aside time to teach yourself the slides. The tests are the most difficult part of the class because you only get 50 min, so practice doing the practice problems quickly
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Im sorry but I had to drop this class. I thought this class would help me, when it came to biomechanics. the first two classes I attended was the worst experience of my life. she does not explain, she just teaches but then again I get it. This class is like pre-calc before calculus. If you get it you get it if you dont you dont.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: bringing back her rating. she dont deserve no dang 4 on this. RIP tho cause she's the only teacher. I had the best TA doe. Good luck tho
Decent teacher, and is fairly transparent about her exams. But her grade cutoffs are a bit ridiculous. For some reason, anything below a 95% is an A-, which I think to be absolutely unfair.

Best science professor I have ever had. Took 121 and 122 different semesters and liked both classes. Physics is not easy, but she does everything she can to help you understand the material, and is a quick responder to emails. SHE IS SERIOUSLY SO KIND AND CARES ABOUT HER STUDENTS.

This professor made my first experience with physics amazing. She does a great job of breaking down the important aspects in easily digestible videos. She gives you everything you need to prepare for her exams and clearly defines her learning expectations. Take her course if you have the opportunity.

hated/never understood physics before having her; lectures > book; very fair and passionate; MANY helpful examples throughout her lectures some for premed (connects to chem too); homeworks relevant to chapters; understand lecture? u good on exams; MAKE SUMMARY PAGES FOR EACH CHAPTER (helps a LOT); wish i studied more than 24 hours before exams
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Skip class? You won't pass.--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: suuuuper nice dude! but if you're not an english major or very very interested in the subject you'll probably be bored out of your mind. it's worth actually doing the readings and going to his office hours because he really has so much knowledge and is so excited to share it, but it can be easy to slack since he's a softie
Great Prof. Very funny. Super Chill class. Show up and engage in class and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Richardson is a really nice guy who is passionate about modern/postmod lit. Unfortunately, not much class discussion occurs -- it's mostly him talking throughout the whole class. If you want to learn something substantial about mod lit, I recommend starting out with someone else.

Interesting fellow, renowned po-mo literary theoretician.  He's kindof out there but the readings are interesting though though the discussions can get slow.  Come with an open mind and he will melt your literary reality.

Lots of reading. He's a really nice guy. Very compassionate.  However, the course material is a bit difficult...not an easy A. It's attainable, but not easy. A lot is expected of you. Lectures are B-O-R-I-N-G. There are only 2 exams and 1 paper so if you mess up on either of them...it's 1/3 of your entire grade. Take this course with caution.

Dr. Lacey is an awesome professor who truly wants his students to succeed. I've taken several classes with him, simply because of how awesome he is. He has a dry sense of humor, and values class participation, so he truly wants the class to be engaged. You will not regret taking a class with him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took CCJS325 online over the winter. The class wasn't hard it was just demanding & very paper-heavy. Every week we had one or two 2-page assignments, an open-note quiz, and one 5 page reflection paper. Midterm was open-note multiple choice and the final was a 4 page paper. Dr. Lacey's a great professor & super helpful, I definitely recommend him

He keeps his lectures quick and to the point. We were let out earlier almost every week. He lectures fast but connects almost every topic to a real-life situation making things easy to remember. He's a nice guy and will work with you. If you put effort into the course it will reflect in your grade.

He's very chill and has a good sense of humor. The entire class is lecture and you need to go in order to get the notes (they are important for tests and quizzes). Quizzes were open note and very straightforward and tests were all multiple choice or true/false and easy as long as you study the notes. Overall a good class and very interesting
Best professor. Lectures are mandatory in order to get all of the notes, but his lectures are so interesting. He makes it super easy to pay attention and is very funny. Cannot recommend him enough

Professor Lacey was my favorite by far this year. You have to go to his lectures because thats the only way to get notes but he always is conversational with the class. If you ask him to look over papers he will give you great feedback to review. He also gave great study guides that told you everything you had to know about the test.

Dr. Lacey is an amazing lecturer - very involved in the class and asked lots of questions and examples for students to participate. His stories were super interesting and clearly knew what he was talking about. Lecture slides were great, grading was great, only one paper + discussion attendance + exams. 100% would recommend any class he teaches.

This class is easy and the professor makes the content easy to learn. Half the time you will get out of class early as well. Participation matters once a week. There is a big group paper but it is not hard because you are given the whole semester to work on it. Definitely take this class!
Great professor always willing to help if you need it. Also gives extra credit opportunities throughout the course. If you pay attention you will do well.
bro is awesome
Great guy, classes are very easy if you just show up to class. I didn't read a thing and got an A in two of his classes.
Very nice prof and wants you to learn and get a good grade. Moderate amount of material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: AMAZING!!! 100% take his class if you can. He is very caring and extremely intelligent. Truly wants you to pass! If you show you care, he will make sure he does anything to help you do well in his class. Show up and take notes because he does not post slides but very little work except for larger projects that he makes interesting

Professor Lacey is such a good professor, if you dont attend lecture you will get lost because that is the only way to get your information for upcoming quizzes. Only 1 midterm and the final exam + several quizzes, he is very caring and responsive with students and emails. I would def take him as a professor again, he's great!

Prof Lacey was one of my favorite professors. He's extremely lecture heavy, as in you won't pass if you don't show up to class. I got by with an A without ever reading the textbook. His notes are sufficient enough. Quizzes about every 2 weeks, 1 midterm, and 1 final. Really not that bad, and he tells you what to expect on the final. Loved him!

Absolutely amazing professor, it's his first semester here and he's very kind and laid back. You will get assigned a group project that's pretty easy, just make sure everyone in the group in reliable. If anything, attend EVERY lecture, it's the only way to get notes. He's very caring and does his best to break down the content if you ask.

I write this review posthumously for Dr. Jarvis. In 1995, he was the professor for a new organic-specific path in the department. It was a smaller class compared to the larger organic class and was meant for those who would be focusing on organic and for chem majors. He was brilliant and funny. Taught and tested on a lot, but very fairly. RIP sir.

Bruce Jarvis was my chemistry professor a long time ago.  He had all of the characteristics  I noted above and that made him a wonderful instructor.  He had the capability to draw you in to the level of his interest in his subject and feel excited about learning it!  A true renaissance man of the 1970's and 1980's.  A true tour d' force!
Not a nice man.  ABSOLUTE stickler for procedural rules, including when contradictory rules have been put in place.  Even when he is in the wrong, he won't admit his mistake.
really good. very interesting lecture. upbeat, adds interesting stories when the class stops listening. hard tests though. and orgo in general sucks. try to get him if you can.
No communication from her at the end of the semester and decided to start grading terribly to fail students.
Bad teacher who grades based on her mood rather than you own work. Took off many points on an assignment that was completely correct based on examples provided. Stay away from her.
She makes the class very hard to succeed in. Her grading style is so bad that correct assignments get Fs.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She took off points on assignments that were completely correct and accurate based on examples provided. Inexcusable grading for this class. I would avoid her class at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough grader. Lost all points for an assignment for doing everything correct. Stay away from her classes.
Harsh grader and very petty. She doesn't give second chances to students. Very disappointed.
Avoid taking any class with her. Grades very harshly and takes off points arbitrarily. She makes it very difficult to succeed. Horrible experience.

This was the best class that I have ever taken. It is fully online and consists of short, life-changing activities each week. Brooke cares more about making sure you get what you need to out of the class as opposed to ensuring you follow the instructions exactly. She gives incredible feedback on your work and progress each week. Take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Mrs. Smith (doesn't want to be called professor) is a very caring teacher and she did a good job for a 1 credit class. The projects weren't too hard and sometimes you will do a group circle and do a class activity. So if you're introverted, like me, be ready to talk a bit.

Brooke is a really nice person and a great teacher. I never had to ask for an extension because this course is very light, but I'm sure she'd be happy to oblige if you needed one. IDEA101 in general helped me figure out what I want to do at Maryland so I would definitely say it is worth your time if you have to take the class anyways.

Terrible Instructor.

The assignments, and the content taught in her lectures hardly have any correlation.

Her assignments required us to work on the feedback received on the previous assignments. But she would grade those previous assignment AFTER the due date of the current one has passed.

She also hardly replied to our emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She does not teach and is so disorganized. Confuses herself constantly. Harsh grading by the TAs. Very poorly structured course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing professor!! Super enthusiastic and passionate about the material. I love his lectures. He is also informative and breaks down concepts in an easy-to-understand way. Cares about student learning as well. The only drawback is that his assignments could be a lot of repetitive busy work.

great prof!! i understand the flipped lecture styles arent everyones cup of tea, but it helps me so i didnt mind. super nice guy and very willing to help! im not the best at bio at all but dr buchner definitely puts the effort into helping you understand the material fully. the class lectures are a little tedious tho but overall i rlly good prof

This guy left a bad taste in my mouth. Don't take his class unless you want to be accused of cheating and reported to the honor council over drawing a clover as an enzyme on a 4 point homework assignment graded for completion (which we all got the same template for, were allowed to use the internet, and work with others on).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: THERE IS SO MUCH WORK! Do not take this class during a heavy semester. His assessments are ridiculous. The busy work is ridiculous and they act like you don't have 4-5 other classes to study for. The only good thing is that busy work helps balance bad grades I guess, but I did not enjoy this class. Take Erin.
Buchner was super cool and overall very knowledgeable! I enjoyed the lecture and lab!

Dr. Bucnher seems like a really nice guy who is also extremely knowledgeable about all things microbiology, if you're interested in that. My issues were not with him, but with the course itself. The lecture time itself is devoted to clickers, and sometimes seemed like a waste of time. Lots of busy work, especially in lab! Not too bad overall.

Don't recommend... Buchner uses a flipped lecture style, where you watch/take notes on the lecture BEFORE class, and then during class is clicker participation points. There are way more lab homeworks than lecture homeworks, some are very long. The assessments are "open note" but extremely are difficult and take a lot of time

This class was manageable. My main problem with this class was the flipped lecture style, making it so that we learned no content during the allotted lecture time. Lots of tedious busy work, be prepared to devote a lot of time to this class. There are lots of freebie points and the assignments aren't very hard, but it is annoying.

This class is 100% busywork. We had four assignments due every week and two lectures to watch in OUR OWN time, then we had to show up twice a week for clicker questions (and two labs a week). Very time-consuming with five-part exams. Nevertheless, I barely learned anything because completing the assignments took up more time than learning.

Dr. Buchner uses his lectures to inform and educate students about current events in micro and focuses on underrepresented microbiologists and UMD research. Lots of "gimme" points. Assessments were unexpectedly difficult and very time consuming. Lab was really fun. Surprisingly enjoyed this class and learned a lot - but you have to work for the A.

Be prepared to work for this class! Between lab and lecture work- there is s/t due almost every night. A lot of the hw is graded for participation though. There are 3 assessments that have 5 sections in them and they take days to complete. Those brought my grade down tremendously. If you forget to hand in s/t, he will give you an extension.

Buchner is a great professor, by far one of the coolest I've had so far. He gives lots of accommodation due to COVID. Most of the bad reviews I've seen talk about a lot of busy work which is true but MOST (almost all) of it is graded for participation. I had to take this class for my major but it ended up being an easy A. Would def recommend.

The workload of this class is more than expected for a 4-credit class. However, many assignments are only graded for participation, and in-person attendance in lecture is not mandatory. Dr. Buchner is a very passionate and knowledgeable professor who is good at explaining concepts. He makes the course incredibly interesting and is a kind person.

This class was taught as a "reverse lecture" this semester, meaning the lecture videos were posted beforehand and the class time was used as discussion. All this means is that a class that already has lots of pointless busy work associated with it just got more time consuming. And forget about office hours, not helpful at all. Avoid, avoid, avoid!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Buchner is a good lecturer with a sense of humor and care for students. His online class was very hard only because there was so much work, rather than because the material was difficult. He was kinda disorganized and kept postponing exams and staggering assignments on top of each other, which was the worst thing about his class

Buchner is surely the WORST PROFESSOR you could possibly have at UMD. We had 3 exams in this class, and each one being broken up into 4-6 PARTS took ENTIRE DAYS TO COMPLETE. He showed NO empathy for students, forgetting we had other classes. No one even had time to watch his mess of an attempt at lectures due to the workload. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS

The workload is completely unreasonable for one class. You'll find yourself so busy with assignments, that are completed primarily through google, that his lectures and assigned readings take a backseat. Be prepared to do a ton of work and come away having learned very little.

THE WORST PROF I'VE EVER HAD. He may be a funny guy but not at all good teacher. His lectures and assignments are not related at all. Too much work due each week, all of them require outside research cus his lectures don't help. Course unrelated assignments while learning nothing. Wish to learn? take another professor's course.

We started course material almost two weeks into the semester. He didn't have a schedule to upload lectures, just posted them in the middle of the night randomly. No lab simulations, just absurd research articles with almost no relevance to the class. Instead of a 50 min exam, it was broken into four large time consuming parts. Not considerate prof

Buchner is a good professor. His lectures are interesting and he explains concepts very well. The amount of work required in microbio is kind of insane. A lot of time will need to be dedicated toward assignments but, the material is simple and the grading criteria is clear. Definitely doable not the easiest.

Really nice professor, but inconsiderate of other classes. Gives a lot of homework, even during exam weeks. Have cried multiple times over this class. The content isn't necessarily too difficult, but having a lot of very long assignments gets very overwhelming. One section of my exam took me over 4 hours to complete. There were 4 sections...

Although he flies through content, he posts recordings online. He had online reviews before exams to help students. Dr. Buchner is very accessible in office hrs & genuinely cares for his students & our success. Microbio is a hard class, but if you go to office hrs on a regular basis, you will see improvement. He is very understanding & empathetic.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Buchner goes through an enormous amount of material in every class, but exams consist of a few specialized subjects which were not talked about much in class. The labs and class do not always sync up perfectly so doing the lab hw was always frustrating. TA's are also inconsistent. Mine graded hw on accuracy but others on completion. . . not fair :(

The worst professor I have ever had. Although he has a lot of energy, he tends to fly through lecture content. All the assignments were like research projects since he doesn't actually teach the material on any of these assignment. His exams were terrible with absolutely no curve and hardly gives points back. This man ruined my science GPA

If I can warn anyone to not take Dr. Buchner for BSCI223, please heed this warning with sincerity. His lectures are confusing, slides filled with images he creates that are not explained. Never gives answers to clicker questions. Tests are nearly impossible - studying for a week still can't help 100%. Lab is the only thing that boosted my grade.

Took Buchner for BSCI223 this fall semester, and was honestly one of my toughest classes. There were so many unnecessary online assignments due every week, and his lectures are so unorganized and confusing and the only reason why you should even go to lecture is for the clicker points. Exams are terrible but lab does bring your grade up a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Buchner is an excellent professor who is excited about what he teaches. He comes to class with so much energy and will help any student if they reach out. He has open office which makes him so accessible. His exams are very detailed, but things such as lab assignments make up for so much! Overall, I recommend taking him!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Buchner is just a character - he's the funniest, kindest man. If you can get Hyun Park as your TA, she's amazing too. There was a lot of busywork and exams are hard, but it's an interesting class

Excellent teacher who really cares about his students and how they are doing. Will talk to you in his office for hours. The class projects are pretty interesting and the labs are fun. The only thing to watch out for are the tests, You had to read a story to answer the questions and it was kinda odd. And the questions were packed with little space

Top top professor, to pass this class with a solid grade go to class, have at least 6 friends you can study with or do homework with, study a week before the exams and go to office hrs because you can talk to him about anything on your mind. You also have to understand the material in depth (it might seemeasy) unless you'll be an average student

He is my favorite lecturer at UMD. I just loved going to class but the tests are very hard and there is a lot of work to do for class. Lab is actually fun which is a surprise for a science class. Make sure if you're taking this class you're not taking any other homework/outside work heavy classes. If you work for it, you can get an A or B.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Hes a fast lecturer and although the material can be pretty dense at times, Buchner provides a lots of opportunities to succeed. Lots of extra credit opportunities, many small assignments that can add up to a good portion of your grade (some of which are only graded on completion). Definitely challenging but content was interesting.

I never been so frustrated in my life over a class. I don't even think Chemistry was this tedious and annoying. This class has an assignment due every 3 days. The exams are wordy and to long for the time given. I bunch of group projects and little tedious assignments just to keep you busy. This class will make you hate Microbio so get ready.
The class is tough but super fun. He is really interesting and makes sure to keep labs as well as lectures up to the mark.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sad to see the terrible reviews for Buchner. He really wants the best for you and while he may fly through material, he does record every lecture and posts them immediately. He made video conferences before every exam to help his students study. Not the easiest class but definitely not as hard as I am seeing others describe it.

Yes, there is a lot of work, but it's actually pretty easy. mostly it's just completion. The lab component I thought was fun. He's upbeat and posts his lectures online although he uses clickers. Lots of group projects in the lab part.

He treats everybody like they are microbiology majors or experts.  If you are a pre-med, public health, or environmental health like me. DO NOT TAKE HIM! He gives too much assignments and the tests were too long for the allowed time. I would rather take another professor after this.

Professor was difficult to deal with; exams were way too long for the allotted time; the lab work was sometimes excessive; exam grades were very low but there is a lot of extra credit offered to pull up your grades.  I learned tons in this course but this professor is not suited for teaching (flies through material, doesn't reply to emails, etc.).

It was an interesting class, but it could have been taught better. He goes through material very quickly, & insists you know every detail of it for tests. The tests were way too long for the amount of time given to take them. There is a lot of busy work involved with this class, but just ask questions, attend lecture, & do all of the HW.

James Butler was a great professor to me his lectures were very chill and interesting. The class had consist of weekly quizzes which was easy if you paid attention in class. He had 3 exams and 6 case studies which just required you to be in attendance. Overall, this class was an easy A just make sure to be aware of case studies because its random.
He is absolutely amazing. Very trustworthy and funny. Makes lecture material fun and engaging. My friend who  had him also agrees.

Dr. Butler is amazing! He is very understanding and provides exceptional feedback. There is a group project and midterm (must study that) and the class is straight forward and definitely accounts for community engagement. As long as you are participating here and there, attend class regularly you will do great. Amazing!!!

Dr. Butler is an amazing professor and his class is so interesting. There aren't a lot of assignments and they are easy. Tests are worth a lot but the information is this class is easy to learn and kind of common sense. He tells interesting stories and really connects with students. If you get the opportunity, take his class !!!

Dr. Butler is one of the best professors I've had! He is sweet, intelligent, and its obvious he really cares about his students. I never stressed too much about this class and the content was really interesting!

Dr. Butler is the best! Only had three exams throughout the semester, based off of his lecture slides- material is super easy to understand. Had a service learning paper originally In the syllabus, we weren't able to do the activity due to covid so he just gave everyone 100% on it instead. Really nice guy, very caring and understanding.

TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!! Literally the best class ever and Butler is the cutest professor ever. The material is actually very interesting and you're only graded on a few things. I could not recommend this class enough.
Very caring about his students. Easy to get in touch with him outside of class. Very flexible if you have an issue. Really just wants you to pass
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: LOVE DR. BUTLER!! Such a nice man who truly cares for his students. The material itself was interesting and we had many guest speakers come in to talk which was super cool. Would 100% take a class with Dr. Butler again. Not much homework at all, only like one paper on a TED talk every month and they are very interesting!

Dr. Butler is the best professor there ever was. He teaches everything during lecture but does not post the complete lecture slides (not ideal but you can usually find the notes either online or from someone else). He tells interesting stories and keeps the class engaged. Assignments are all easy A's as long as you put in effort.
Best professor I have had at UMD. If you take notes on the slides and read over them before the tests you will pass with flying colors. Definitely take him!

He's a great lecturer and actually wants his students to succeed. If you want a good grade, it's not hard, just make sure you go to every class and take good notes. His exams are straightforward but u do need to study. Overall, just go to class and pay attention and youll pass with a good grade.
He's an amazing professor!! Gives really funny lectures. Exams have questions based on lectures & the textbook readings. Easy class.

I love Dr. Butler! He's the best professor I have taken at UMD. His lectures are very engaging & he adds personal anecdotes to make the lectures more interesting. He is also very funny I find myself laughing non-stop. If you can stop by his office hours. He is a great person to talk to. I barely opened the textbook and the exams are piece of cake.

Dr. Butler is a very caring man. He is passionate about his class and thus makes lectures interesting. He has a sense of humor which would keep me awake throughout the lectures. The class itself is very interesting and he is very responsive. All in all, I had a great time. The tests weren't hard but make sure you study!
I love this man great professor

One of the best professors that I've had at UMD. He's an amazing lecturer and even uses personal anecdotes and humor to reinforce what is said on the slides. I went to lecture about like 6 times the whole semester- due to person issues not including the exam dates and I got a B+ in the class. Tests are hard but common knowledge and study slides.

I found this class pretty easy, but honestly I had already learned a lot of this information in previous classes (I am a Behavioral and Community Health major) so that's probably why. I went to the lectures just because I enjoyed listening to them. I never bought the textbook, power points and lectures were sufficient.

Took this as an elective because I thought it'd be an easy A, but it wasn't. Exams are super detailed on things that aren't on the slides, so you probably have to read the textbook as well. He's a nice person but won't give extra credit, grades slow, and goes through the slides fast. If you don't need to take this class then don't.
He is a good lecturer, but his tests are really heavy. Though this class is an easy A online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Butler is a great professor. I would like to emphasize that if you go to class, you'll be doing yourself a big favor! The tests are basically based on all the slides he presents.
Don't offer study guides but it is not need. Go to the lecture and pay attention to what he talks about and you will pass the class with flying colors.

Lectures and TopHat questions are very simple, but the exams and homeworks are very hard. The content from the lectures basically have nothing to do with the exams, but you do get a sheet of paper for an equation sheet and the curve is very good.

Nice guy, but one of the worst lecturers I've ever had. This is my second semester with him and it just keeps getting worse. Nobody ever knows what's going on because he's really smart but can't explain things at a level we can understand. I would recommend getting a tutor or using the physics tutoring services.

I agree with most of the other bad reviews. In recorded lectures, he sounds like he knows what he is talking about, but it makes no sense to me; its a bunch of physics jumbled up without having any clear meaning or use on the homeworks or labs. He didn't respond to my emails. This class isn't hard to get a good grade in, but I learned nothing

The recorded lectures did not help as much and the readings about simple things were too complicated. The exams were not too bad but I feel like I did not take anything away from this class. The labs that are associated with this class were not very representative of what we learned and consists of just knowing how to use softwares.

He used old recorded lectures so he doesn't have to interact with the class, none of the simulations work, the labs and TAs are a disorganized nightmare, the exams are much different from anything practiced in quizzes and lectures, everything is out of sync, the "textbook" is archaic and missing crucial parts, he's disrespectful in communication.

I don't care for the way he lectures at all, and I find them to be of little use personally, but that may be a personal issue. I find the textbook to be a bit better with explanations, but you may not have the same issue. He's a nice man, as far as I can tell. Physics in general is not a class that works well being asynchronous so be aware of that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I don't believe professor Buehrle is a bad professor, but the online adaptation of this class is god awful. It's a complete teach-yourself-free-for-all and there's no sructure. We're graded on things before they're covered in lecture, and the lectures themselves are vague and unhelpful. Don't even get me started on lab and the TAs....

He post 20 min videos 2x week, of him reading from the book. literally posting images directly from the book. maybe doing 1 problem for each topic. he then test on subject i've never seen. i spent 3-4 hrs studying a day 4 1.5 weeks. There were types of questions i've never seen on the test. hes doing the bare min work and test on untaught material

Big man Burls reminds me a lot like an alcoholic version of Winnie the Pooh. It is hilarious how the man can still lecture all the while 70% of the class is either asleep, talking amongst their friends or eating a three course meal. Although, I would recommend going to class later on in the year since he spends the entire class spinning in a chair.

He's grading policy has changed from previous years. I took him spring 2020 and he now has 3 exams (he curves and drops the lowest exam grade). He's lectures are useless and he tries to engage with the students, but fails to do so. Honestly, I would not recommend going to lectures as there are a lot of youtube videos out there for physics.

I didn't like his lecture style; rarely went to class. I read the book and did book problems and did really well on the tests. He definitely cares about his students and is open to questions. However, my grade in this class was definitely a result of my own efforts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class actually sucked. Burhle wasn't the greatest teacher and it seemed by the looks of the curve, that nobody in the class knew what they were doing. A 16% rounded to a 65% on the second exam due to how terrible the whole classes original scores were. His lectures were very boring and unhelpful and I found myself consulting the textbook a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lecture was long and boring, and the exams were difficult but had a good curve. The homework and most quizzes were very easy, but you have to put in effort to get a good grade
After the second exam I cried in the shower. Beware.
David is like a father to me. He cared for me like I was his own. Don't be mean to him just because you can't plug numbers into an equation.

Terrible lectures, incredibly challenging exams, and time consuming weekly homework. I stopped showing up to class after I realized all Buehrle does is go through unnecessarily derivations and simulations instead of teaching actual material. Nice guy, but don't waste your time.

The Best professor/teacher I have ever had. if you get him don't even worry about studying or passing bc its a guaranteed A+. Funny guy gives great examples in class. Also if you like StarWars he's the guy for you. he looks just like Luke! Have Fun!!!!!!

I already wrote a review about Buehrle for Phys131 and he doesn't change for Phys132, Still amazing, class is structured exactly the same, still a pretty easy chance of getting an A-. Last thing is I didn't experience this in 131, but if you get a bad TA for lab... best of luck, because you will be absolutely miserable, as my entire class was.

Well, his lectures are not related to the HW and the exams. He is a funny guy, but not a teaching material. This class is messy, but it's not really his problem. Reuses HW problems a lot and uses TopHat as clickers. You probably will get a decent grade in this class, but you won't learn anything.

Not a bad professor at all. He works with other professors so sometimes it seems like he's organized but it's just the physics department lol. Kind, funny, wry, and cool. Very understanding. Interesting lectures. Cares about the students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: One of the kindest professors I've ever had. Super concise and informative lectures and very easy to approach.

Class has no resources. Buehrle spends whole class deriving formulas and doing online simulations. No concrete examples or practice problems in physics!!! Pretty much you have to teach yourself physics so good luck. Take another professor if you have other difficult classes. There is a huge time commitment in the class due to the ineptitude of prof

Buehrle is a really funny guy but his lectures have 0% to do with his exams. Good thing is his exams dont hurt your grade that much, it was calculated that if you get 50% or every exam you can still get an A. Tons of HW and Quizzes, but majority of the answers are online. Tons of reading quizzes but he doesnt check so you can copy and paste.

Lectures are easy to follow as they are very basic concepts he discusses. Exams are extremely difficult but worth very little (avg are in 60s). Homeworks and free tophat points boosts your grade. I got 40% on the final and still got an A in the class. If you get 80% of total points you will get an A in the class. HUGE CURVE!

Buehrle is ok but the amount of assignments he gives per week is absolutely mad! The grading criteria for this class is pretty unfair. This class is the physics of biology but he knows nothing about biology and doesn't know how to apply the info. The only good thing about this class is that tests aren't worth much of the total grade. Tests are hard

To start, although the exams are heavily curved they're worth 80% of your grade. I stopped going to lecture halfway through the semester because you can learn so much more during that time by reading the textbook/doing the homework. If you did physics in HS you'll be fine. If not, you might have to put in a little more effort but it's very doable.

If you can learn from a book you might be ok, but his lectures are absolutely atrocious. He talks about obvious theory and just rambles about it the whole time while writing equations on the board & you're never quite sure if they're formulas or "examples". Big test curves and he's a funny guy, but I would never take him again.

he's funny, he'll answer your questions if you ask, but honestly if you havent taken AP physics then there's no way that this class will be easy for you. His exams are extremely hard and he's a terrible teacher.

Can be humorous. Sometimes is examples can be confusing and feel unfinished bc he rarely uses numbers. There is a decent curve. If you've taken AP physics, you should be fine with him. Online HW due every Friday. Quizzes in every discussion. If you don't understand, just ask a question and he will try his best to clarify.
Explains things well and uses examples thoroughly during lecture. Tests are easier than the homework and heavily curved. Funny guy and a great teacher.

Funny guy, but his lectures can be hard to follow. He tries to point out what's important, but he sometimes goes through the examples and material too quickly. Read the book and do mastering physics so you get the material. Exams can be kind of hard, but there are curves. His practice exams were not always helpful.

Really nice guy. All of the exams were heavily weighted. His lectures weren't very helpful and the exams were VERY hard (averages were in the 30's and 40's precurve). You have to go to lecture because he uses this online question thing for a participation grade.

If you truly want to learn physics, don't take this class. Sure, this class was curved and Buehrle is a nice man, but I learned nothing. I went to lectures just to earn the clicker points, and found them to be quite useless. Buehrle's lectures did not prepare the class for the homeworks or the exams. He restated ideas that were common sense.

He's really bad. His lectures are so beyond useless, and it shows in his abysmal exam averages. His exams are practically undoable, even to seasoned physics students. That being said, his class has a scarily large curve, and it feels impossible to fail. Avoid taking him, but if worse comes worst, just take him. You don't even need to show up.

Everything he does is theoretical during lectures. He does not do practice problems in class, and if he does (which he rarely does), does the most basic problem ever. Then the homework is ridiculously hard, the exams are ridiculously hard, and everything is ridiculously hard. However, he is a very good, confident speaker with good handwriting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lectures were boring and didn't have many examples so you'd just be listening to theories for 50 minutes. Sometimes participation questions take a lot of time out of the class. If you want to pass go to GSS, Slawski Clinic, and read the book. Very difficult if you didn't take AP Physics.

Super smart, clear, kind professor. He is very willing to help and respectful in class. There's a small quiz or exam every week which can be a lot, but it's nice that any one of them counts a lot towards your overall grade. The class can be difficult especially if you didn't take latn101/102 with him, but you can still get a good grade.

Awesome professor, came into this class not being super interested in Roman Law but he made it interesting. Lots of reading homework, but he doesn't assign too much all at once. As long as you put effort into your homework and show up you should be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Participation matters and he calls on everyone in the class so do the readings, tests and quizzes aren't hard. Pretty chill but the work get redundant. Not a hard class, just kind of boring, but he knows the material and is nice
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took his essays class and he was a good, respectful teacher. There was a reading each class and some could be difficult but others were really interesting. You write 3 essays (two drafts for all but one), 1 pitch essay, and 2 reading responses. He is a fairly tough grader but he gives good feedback. If you don't mind reading, take this class.

Professor Bucher is one of the best teachers I've ever had! He makes it "easy" to learn Ancient Greek by helping you to understand the mechanics of the language and to make sense of the madness. This is without a doubt a very difficult language, but a rewarding one. Attendance, preparation, and participation are mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Bucher actually adheres to his syllabus schedule wow. He values his students' time, and he NEVER makes you feel dumb or embarrassed for asking a question. Ancient Greek is really difficult, so while he's understanding and lets you miss classes, lectures are really helpful and if you dont go, you wont do well. He's very accessible and knowledgeable

This professor only works here for the power trip. She had changed a grade on an out-of-class assignment to a 0 because I was not present for the in-class assignment that week, even though i had previously scored 100%, and for other students as well. Strict on attendance being mandatory, but only goes through 8 slides for the whole hour.

My main concern with this prof is that our quiz grades are about 30% of our final grade and she words her questions absolutely terribly. I don't know if she intentionally is trying to give trick questions or if the poor and confusing wording is unintentional. I go to class and take very good notes and still end up with a 3/5 on some of the quizzes

Bustad is one of the wors! Had her for MIEH300 and she was boring and didn't put much effort into her classes but let me tell you, any class outside of that one, she's even worse!! She's very blunt about grades and is super tough. Won't give extensions easily either. Family emergency? Too bad turn your paper in! Any prof but her would be better.

Worst prof Ive ever had at UMD. Made online learning hell having to listen to her voice, tripping over words and rushing through slides she reads directly from (also no slides available to download without her voice, nor a textbook). Extremely strict on not accepting late work- when were in the middle of a f-ing pandemic. She did the minimum

Dr Bustad was boring. The class lacked structure and seemed more like busy work. The amount of work we did didn't match the effort of Dr. Bustad. Make sure you have a Good TA though, as they did a majority of the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Expectations were vague and almost non-existent for the whole summer. Hope your TA's are available and decent because Dr. Bustad is neither of those. Most of the lectures were taken from another university or easily found on the internet; plagiarized. She makes attempts to cover this up, but it is clear she has no idea what she is teaching.

Summer, 6 weeks. I say this nicely: Bustad does not know how what she is doing or how to teach - uses word-for-word info found on Wikipedia and other sites. Vague instructions, rubrics, whole class confused. Syllabus doesn't have due dates or schedule. Put in no effort. Skipped slides, skipped info on slides. Plagiarized so much, does not explain

This class was incredibly boring and formulaic. Bustad gave okay lectures, but the assignments and quizzes didn't encourage free thinking, and the whole thing seemed too surface level to be a college class. I took AP Env Sci and it covered better material...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The class wasn't even the problem. It's the fact that they made a "lab" portion to go with it. The TA's have absolutely no clue what they are doing and are not given a clear grading criteria. The actual lectures are quite boring, but she gives good information.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Bustad obviously knows what she's talking about, but doesn't know how to teach in an engaging manner. She read off the slides, adding very little, but you have to go because she often does graded in-class activities. She does not record her lectures, and she assigns a lot of writing (BORING and tedious). If you can help it, try someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class was the most boring class I've ever taken. Environmental health has so much potential to draw from current studies in the field however Bustad relies on broad generalizations about things like dump "liners" which makes going to class a snooze fest. A lab component was added this semester so pray that you get a good TA .
Dr. Bustad was so amazing. I had her for environmental health online and it was a lot of writing but she was very responsive and always goes above and beyond to answer your question.

- Highly recommend Buerhle if physics isn't your strongest suit
- You need to put the extra time in studying outside of lecture
- Drops the lowest 5 HWs, lowest 2 quizzes, and lowest exam (3 total exams, 1 dropped)
- Substantial curve on the final exam (may vary by semester)
- Had 3 double-sided cheat sheets for final (mary vary by semester)
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He deserves a 5/5 rating. The BEST physics professor at umd easily. He is really funny and an overall nice guy. If you go to his office hours he will be happy to help you. I would highly recommend taking his class if you can. The exams will be hard but he drops the lowest one and the class gets curved, so don't worry. If you study you'll be okay.
This is probably your best bet for Physics 161. He curves heavily, so you should be fine.
Terribly disorganized class. Labs and simulations dont work. Homework and exams are difficult. Its easy to get and A because of generous grading scale. Dont expect to learn physics though

My classmates and I literally do not know if this man actually exists. His online lectures were recorded like 2 years ago and his TA's do all of the grading. His lectures are useless he just asks questions in them which he answers with another question. Luckily he is also lazy so the exams are just HW questions. Easy enough with the curve.

Exams are difficult but doable, but pay attention to the time. Lots of points overall so your exam scores don't affect your grade too badly. Lots of lecture participation points. Homework is sometimes fine and sometimes hard - go to your TA for help. Textbook is online and free, and is sometimes useful - but not always.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy. Class itself isn't too bad - go to TA office hours for help with HW. Make sure to stay up to date on assignments - lots of points and different categories (HW, tests, lab etc.) are curved separately. Exams are hard and time allowed is just barely enough, but you'll be okay if you do well on other assignments. Textbook is online and free.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: This class is hard. His exams are doable but take a lot of time. He is a decent lecturer, and is really nice. Make sure to go to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Basically, to pass this class with an A you need to go to the course center for HW help, get good grades on the lab reports which varies depending on your TA and get at least above a 70% on the 2 midterms and final. His lectures summarize the info and make it seem real easy until you get to the tests which will take you for a RIDE. 83-85 is an A.

Lectures covers basic knowledge of material while hw, quizzes & exams are so difficult and in depth. Your best hope is doing old exams, he can repeat questions. Lab grades depend on your TA, but are all normalized to basically the same. LOTS of points, so can get an A with 6/70s on exams and some low quizzes if lab, tophat, & hw grades are high

Professor Buerhle is an decent lecturer, he works through problems in class, and he does an occasional demonstration. Great guy teaching a hard course, tests were difficult but if you read the book and follow through problems it's not too bad. Bad reviews are probably from the kids that won't put in the work. Overall tough course, work for ur grade

Professor Buerhle is a nice person, but this class was not enjoyable at all. His lectures go over the basic physics concepts with no real in depth or detailed examples. This causes most of the students to be confused on the weekly homework, quizzes, and exams. You will have to rely on outside sources if you genuinely want to learn and do well.

Buerhle has a great ability to convey the physics concepts in a way that really makes sense. The lectures were generally quite good. However, the test were on a whole other level. The lectures did not prepare us for the homework or the exams. Homework was very long. Exams were heavily curved. Nice guy, but didn't seem to care about student concerns

Buerhle's lectures were somewhat unorganized.  He was funny had lots of cool demonstrations but I didn't feel like I was really getting what I needed math-wise.  His tests were always difficult, but he was pretty generous with the curves.  Most of my friends hated going to lecture but still went hoping they would learn something.

It's questionable if I actually learned anything from this man. If you expect the exams to follow anything you did in lecture then you are in for quite the surprise. If there was no curve I am willing to bet half the class would've failed. Homework is excessive and you don't really learn how to do most of it so Google becomes your teacher instead.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: worst professor ever. Spends the whole lecture deriving equations & does not show how to do problems. I asked for a regrade for one of my exams he was very rude to me. You learn nothing sitting in lecture and there is way too much homework. However, he curves a lot, so you can pass. Don't take if other options. TAs cant even do exam questions.

Overall, PHYS161 with Buerlhe was one of the more mediocre experiences i've had here at UMD. He spends entire lectures deriving equations and talking about concepts, but rarely taught anything that was practical or could help prepare students for the frustratingly difficult exams that he gave. Khan Academy is the only reason i passed this class.
Buehrle is your best bet with physics II. We tend to repeat material in class from the class before and after, which helps enforce the topic. Do well on the homeworks to get an A.

He is a super nice guy, but that's about the only thing I can give him credit for. He spends every lecture deriving equations and doesn't provide much reasoning to his thoughts, so lectures are pointless. Discussion sections are only for taking quizzes, so you have to go. Tests are difficult, but the bright side is he curves them really heavily.

Dr. Buerhle is really "chill," but can be condescending. Lectures and assignments seem to be unrelated. Customizable formula sheets allowed for every quiz and test (including the final), as well as a "working" calculator (no restrictions). Most of the answers for the homework assignments seem to exist already online, just look for them.
All he does is derive equations. Homework and test completely different than what he teaches.

Literally just the nicest guy I've ever met. Very clear, concise teacher, more than willing to take any questions at any point, lenient grader. He asks conceptual questions a lot so it's not much of a busy work class as long as you get what's going on. Often lets class out early, but it's because his teaching methods are so effective. Love him.

I had taken 226 with Prof Burke and took 428U with him this semester. His course has taught me a lot about Latin America and his knowledge about the subject shines through. Lots of group projects but they are short and fairly easy. The lectures are worth attending - you will learn so much
Large class, topic is not easy, Prof Burke makes it enjoyable, lots of lectures but pay attention and do all assignments and you will be fine.

He was accommodating and asked for feedback from students. The class alternated between live lectures and sketching. The tests weren't hard if you studied and looked at notes. The only thing was that there were only 4 grades for the whole semester and a high grading scale. Even one B could drop you drastically. If you do the work, you'll be fine!

Professor Burke is knowledgeable and passionate on the subject. He is certainly engaging in his lectures. He sets a clear schedule and is flexible to accommodate students needs. I definitely recommend this course to anyone interested in an alternative to the generic European-centric architecture. As long as you do the homework you'll be alright.

Prof. Burke's class is one of the few architectural history courses that explores regions outside of the typical arch history education (i.e. European architecture and the course I took was Latin American Arch. and Urbanism). The content is super interesting and the workload is very manageable
Very laid back and understanding. Grades fairly

This was a 100 plus class, so prof. Burke did his best to keep us engaged and his lectures were pretty awesome if you were paying attention. The grade was based on two papers, which many dont like to work for, but that's college for ya... in samller classes ive heard he's great

So this class covers a large span of the history of architecture. In order to fit as much information as possible Juan fills his PowerPoints to the brim. He speeds through them very fast leaving little to no time for notes. Best thing to do is jot down main concepts and just pay attention visually to his slides.
One of the most genuine and nice people you'll ever meet.
I didn't like the class very much but Alison was great and it was clear she really tried to incorporate things that we would find interesting.

Burns is very nice but her class is beyond boring. Some of the stuff we talk about is just silly and doesn't feel like it deserves to be in a college level class. Lots of discussion but unless you think a certain way it's hard to chime in. That said the work itself is easy. All the assignments are online, plus one group presentation. It's an easy A

Alison is incredibly nice and understanding. I don't love the media class itself, but she really makes it something I can enjoy. She's incredibly caring for her students and just wants everyone to feel welcome. You can go to her with anything if you'd like.
I have loved CPMS100. It is such a fun class and I really enjoyed what we learned about. Looking forward to next semester!

Alison is one of the sweetest people you'll ever meet! She really is there for her students and open to talk about anything! The class is easy too but still pretty interesting. Lots of cool guest speakers this semester
She really cares about her students and their understanding of the material. It also helps that the media class is so interesting!
I loved Alison! She was such a lovely professor and was great at giving individual feedback. She really wants everyone to succeed in her classes. Definitely would recommend taking her classes!

Alison is one of the sweetest people and best professors I've had at Maryland. She has so much experience in journalism and really cares about her students. I know she'll always be accessible no matter what stage of college I'm in. I definitely recommend taking any of her classes!!

Alison was the best professor I had during my time at UMD. As someone who has real life experience in media and journalism, she provided great knowledge and insight to our class on the subject. She is also incredibly caring and made each student in the class feel appreciated. I highly recommend taking any class she teaches.
