If you have the option try to take someone else, if you don't then make sure you aren't slacking.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Loved Dixon, but I wont lie its a hard class. Orgo isnt supposed to be easy! Its important to go to lecture. shes always in her office and loves to help students understand the concepts. She can be intimidating but if you show commitment to learning she will love you. Also there is a very nice curve in the end! Hard class but loved it
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The absolute best. Very nice, funny, offers more than enough resources and prepares you very well for Orgo 2. Has a reputation for being difficult only because she teaches you a lot more than others and expects you to know it. Offers extra credit, and is very fair on grading.

Very difficult exams although she does put cutoffs after every exam. Make you do concept maps so better do them in a group. Homework before every exam and a very short window to do it. Exams are very long so you must practice. the textbook isn't very helpful but the Klein book was. A lot of emphasis on the final. Overall, one of the hardest classes
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Dixon was a very good professor who clearly knew her stuff and knew how to teach it effectively. Her tests are quite difficult, but it is possible to do well in the class as long as you study. You also don't need the textbook to do well in this class, she covers everything you need to know in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Started off 'nice.' But really isn't approachable outside of class and grades very unfairly. Is constantly emphasizing how you should come to her office hours, but doesn't actually help when you go. Not sure who she's talking about when she says people do well in her classes. 10/10 would not recommend and would avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Tough but fair professor, especially given the subject difficulty. Make sure to pay very close attention in lecture, and to start her homeworks early as they are pretty difficult. Utilize the office hours she is always telling students to go to, although half the time they do she can act a little bit dismissive and blunt there when under stress
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer! Everyone says orgo is their hardest class, but honestly it was my favorite subject and class this semester. If you go to all her lectures and do all the homework assignments it's not hard to get an A in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This is the toughest class you may ever take, but in the end it's worth it. Dr. Dixon has an open door policy, meaning she's always available for office hours. Don't take this class if you're not prepared to work harder than you ever have. She's very funny and keeps lectures interesting, and if you go to her office hours she'll know you by name.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I love Dr. Dixon and she is an incredible professor. However, I would not suggest taking her unless you are pre-health, are going to take Orgo 2, and are willing to work hard for your grade. Attend lectures and you're set for exams. She even does review days the class before a test. She's helpful in office hours and overall an amazing person.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Tests are crazy hard and grading base is so weird. Like average for test would be 30-40 percent and that would be like a C. If you miss one section your done just drop out:(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dixon is a good proffessor who definitely knows her material. Lecture can be very overwhelming so I recommend the green klein book to supplement your studies which really goes hand in hand with her lectures. Her exams are hard, but fair. Everything on the exams, you will be prepared for from lecture notes, discussion questions, and the homeworks
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dixon definitely makes you work for a good grade. However it is definitely possible to do well in her class. She has open office hours everyday until 3:00 so you can always get help. For chem232 she curved so that the average was an 80%. She is a good lecturer for the most part and prepares you well for future organic chem classes.

I wasn't terrified of Dixon's class on the first day, but I knew she wasn't playing around, and I could tell that underneath her smiles and laughter were very high expectations that would be really difficult to meet. All I can say is, if you take Dr. Dixon, prepare to put in a hell of a lot of work to earn the grade you want. Trust me.

I found Dr. Dixon to be extremely unprofessional. She would not help you at office hours unless she already knew you and liked you. Her exams are long and unfair. If you have questions and try to get help, you run the risk of getting yelled at. Honestly, she was a mess and overly stressed out most days. It's not worth the trouble if you ask me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Had 70 more points overall than a friend but he ended up receiving a higher grade than me. Awful curve, don't know how that slides at UMD. Good teacher nonetheless.

She's a fabulous professor! Had organic I with her last semester and I still come to her. Exams are hard and hw is time consuming, but you'll be so prepared in organic II. Her open office hours are really helpful too. The only downside is the competitiveness as her class attracts the pre-med freaks who screw up the curve.

Dixon is a good and funny person at heart when she isn't yelling or snapping at her students. She has open office hours which is nice but stresses out easily and won't help you if her office is crowded. Her long exams heavily test memorization and speed so if you like to think through questions on exams, taking 463 with dixon I would not recommend

Dr. Dixon is a great prof. She seems to really care about her students and wants them all to pass. But her tests were really hard and sometimes didn't reflect what was learned in lecture. Lectures are dense so try not to miss any
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Bonnie Dixon is a really good teacher. If you're taking organic chemistry in order to take the MCAT, DCAT,  etc, I would recommend taking her. Her hws are extremely hard and the exams have more material than you have time for but you do learn the material. If you choose one of the "easier" orgo1 professors, good luck in orgo 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you choose to take this awful person for biochemistry, you can say goodbye to your GPA now. There is absolutely nothing good that I can say about this course. Very difficult grader, and extremely difficult exams that are meant to confuse the students. Very unsure as to how she is still allowed to teach. Avoid her at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probably the worst experience of my life at UMD was with Dr. Dixon. Very difficult to follow in class, no direction or structure to the class. Not willing to help the students at all- unless your in a specific "group". Avoid her if you can. Her exams are impossible, and the homework he gives are just to make you go insane.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Prof. Dixon is the best orgo chem professor at UMD and told us we didn't even need to read the textbook to pass the class. Her office hours are always open and she is easily approachable. Her exams and Hw are freakishly hard, but you will learn alot. If you have a desire to do well, she will change the way your brain learns the material.

If I could describe my experience with Dr. Dixon in one word, I would choose AWFUL. She is the worst professor I have ever had in my college career. She claims to care about her students and wants them to understand the concepts. That's a lie. I went to office hours several times and she would not even pretend to help. UMD should be disgraced.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: As a junior, bonnie is the best professor I've had.

Professor Dixon is really upbeat, energetic, and caring. She really makes you work for your grade but its totally worth it.  I learned so much in her class.   Most importantly, she is very approachable outside of class and holds a lot of office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Dixon is an amazing teacher all around. She helps students out when she can with office hours, extra credit, etc. That being said, organic chemistry has its reputation for a reason. You have to really work hard in her class to get good grades. If you're taking this for an "easy A" just don't.

where to begin, I had her when I was a freshman and I am now  a Junior who still goes to her for help. Gen Chem was a not a favorite class by any means, and I did OK. But I love Dr. Dixon, she is the bomb and she loves her students. It is either a hit or miss it seems with students, GO TO OFFICE HOURS ALL THE TIME.

I haven't taken a chem class since 10th grade, but she was able to make chemistry so understandable (considering I struggle with chemistry).    She offers a lot of extra credit and the curve is around 5-10%   BIGGEST TIP!!! Look at the past 2 exams for every exam you take, she pretty much reuses 90% of them and changes the chemicals/numbers
One of the best professors I've had at UMD. Dr. Dixon's lectures are explained well and makes concepts easily understood. Her office hours are very helpful as well.

Prof. Dixon is the hardest chem teacher at UMD; however she is very nice and approachable and will help you IF you go to her office hours. She's really good at remembering you and figuring out what your kinks are. She is MOST DEFINITELY NOT an easy A! Still love her and all that she did to help me get through her class.

Dr. Dixon really cares about her students, evidenced by the fact that her research centers on improving ways to teach chem.  Take advantage of her daily office hours, ask her for test taking techniques BEFORE the first exam, and read Klein.  Her exams are fair and doable if you study hard and are prepared, but you NEED to work quickly to do well!

I was a LD student who had repeatedly asked her for help in finding someone whose notes I could copy.  After initially discussing with her and showing her my paperwork from DSS, she said she would find me a notetaker and make arrangement.  After I kept trying to follow up with her, I failed the class.  If you have a LD, this isn't the teacher for y

PROFESSOR DIXON IS THE BEST. Her lectures are phenomenal and very clear. In high school, my AP teacher told me to drop because she thought I'd never be able to do chem and I did. Professor Dixon proved her wrong and I put a lot of effort into getting the A I got. If it weren't for this professor, I probably would have gotten a B. LOVE HER.

The grades are as follows: 3 exams, 1 cumulative final, and 6 homework assignments.  Go to her office hours as much as you can, they WILL save you!  Her tests are difficult but definitely doable if you put the time into the class.  Use her to help you for the homework, and get the book "Organic Chemistry as A 2nd Language" by Steven Klein.

Dr. Dixon is a great gen chem teacher. As any incoming freshman (or new to college chem student) I was nervous for the course. I am a biochem major and love chemistry and Dixon enabled me to learn a lot and truly understand the material. Her exam averages are low, but there is a nice curve and as long as you pay attention you can easily get an A.

To start off: passing this class was ONLY by the grace of God. Dixon is a fair teacher and is helpful in office hours if you get her at the right time. Every single exam was hard: I failed every single one except the third (somehow I got a B on it because I got .1 points above the average!!!). Take her if you wanna truly learn EVERYTHING about orgo
Take her if you wanna pass the class and learn the stuff. Big Curve at the end.

If you want to get an A in chem, this is not the class for you. Her tests are extremely hard. Even if you took AP chem in high school, it is difficult to get an A. She really prepares you for organic chem though, so if you plan on a chem-related major, Dr. Dixon would be helpful. She has tons of office hours time and helps you a lot if you come

Best teacher I have had in college. Don't get me wrong, the class is difficult and the subject is hard but Dr. Dixon is so approachable and genuinely wants you to learn the material. She had like 20 hours of planned office hour every week, not including appointments, so there was literally no excuse not to go in for help. Amazing teacher.

Dr. Dixon is awesome. Her lectures are always lively and interesting (no danger of falling asleep). Her tests can be challenging, but if you study a little bit everyday and then a lot in the week or so prior to each test, you'll do fine. She has a huge curve (75% = A), so you just need to do above the average (not that hard, pretty low averages).

Dr. Dixon is really one of the best professors at Maryland.  Her exams are insane, but she gives you more than enough assistance in preparing for them.  The majority of people taking organic chem are pre-med, and Dixon knows this.  She wants you to be ready for the MCAT.  If you can do well in Dixon's class, you will do well on the MCAT.

She is an amazing professor or organic chemistry! You learn so much in her class and she knows how to peak your interest in lecture. She always keeps you on your toes and although she seems intimidating in lecture she is a pleasure in her office hours (which she offers a lot of). Her tests are really hard but she always curves to a B-.

First thing you should know, she is hard. Students they got B's in Dixon's class would easy get A+'s in any other professors. With that, be prepared to work hard, seriously. I strongly recommend Dixon if you have to take orgo II, it will be much easier.

Only take her if you already know chemistry like the back of your hand before you take the class. She is USELESS in office hours.  Any question you ask her will NOT be answered, even if you make it clear to her that you don't understand what is going on. She is rude and disrespectful whenever you try to get help from her.  Her tests are even worse.

the WORST professor I have ever had.  her tests were impossible, and she never offered me any help during her office hours.  she told me that maybe the stuff was not clicking and that she couldn't do anything to help me.  avoid this class at all costs

Expects you to have know some chem before taking her class. very difficult be prepared to study A LOT. she is a nice lady.. very FAIR but she doesnt give any free handouts. super hard class im glad thats over.
Very difficult and fast, but she does know her stuff and will explain everything in detail if you use her office hours.

No prerequisites but she expects you to have an extensive background in chemistry. Textbook is useless; she expects a much more in depth level of understanding. Gives super simple examples in class but super hard problems on tests. Rude & Arrogant.

Class isn't mandatory, but all of the stuff on the test will be taught in class and the textbook goes nowhere near as detailed orgo chem as what she teaches. You need to study for sure to get a good grade, and reading the text helps a lot. I took AP Chem, got a 4 on the test so it wash't too bad. Dixon is super helpful and really nice in office hrs

The class was pretty challenging for me and I had previously taken AP Chem and got a 4 on the AP Exam. I do not recommend Dixon if you have not taken AP Chem. Also she puts in too much orgo which is unnecessary. She's hot though.

Dr. Dixon is extremely helpful and knows the material really well. She's clear in what she teaches but skips some material that she thinks you should already know anyway. The course is difficult and based on orgo, definitely go to office hours! Don't miss clicker quizes and complete the Mastering Chemistry for extra credit!

She gives quizzes every two weeks, the occasional clicker questions, three "midterm" exams, and one final exam. If you do the optional mastering chemistry you can earn extra credit. She also gives an extra credit question every week that you work on out of class and e-mail her the answer before midnight. Big curve yay.

This was the only class at UMCP in which I got a C. She was very informative and know her stuff, but a lot of studying outside the classroom is needed for all the electron pushing. Took this class back in 2007, and her pace of teaching is comparative to my professors now (I'm in pharmacy school). She'll definitely keep you on your toes...

Best class I've taken so far in UMD! Lectures were always lively and never boring! Her review sessions and office hours are very helpful especially if you go with specific questions. Though not everybody does well on her exams, her curves are amazing!

Dr. Dixon is an amazinggggg professor. She does so much for her students. Yes, her exams are extremely difficult but you will not regret taking her class if you want to learn and not just pass with a letter grade. I would suggest recording her lectures, listening to them & re-writing your notes. Do all the wrkshts she gives & old practice exams.

Very challenging teacher, but knows her stuff. You MUST study every single day to be able to keep up. Moves quickly (with subject matter and the way she teaches in class). If you need help, GO DIRECTLY TO HER her in office hours (best and most efficient way). If you aren't really into science/not taking Orgo 2, take another teacher!
really hard but easy class if u you exactly what she tells you to do.
Very effective and intelligent chem prof. I recommend taking her for chem.

Had her for gen chem and got an A. However, there are things she says in lecture that just go over my head, and I'm finding myself struggling in orgo. Nevertheless, I find her to be very helpful if you attend office hours, and she is generally a nice lady.

Best teacher EVER!! I wouldn't have learned orgo without her. Her exams can be hard but they are extremely fair, if you know your stuff it is easy to do well.  I went to her office hours regularly, without that I would be falling behind.  I recommend her 100%.

Absolutely amazing professor. Her lectures are very comprehensible and her vivacity just keeps you awake. Her tests are not easy, but if you study, go to office hours, and do the practice problems, you should do well. She's extremely helpful at office hours, but you really have to go to her with very specific questions. Great professor, overall.

She's amazing. Extremely hard but she teaches well and she has office hours everyday to help you with whatever you need. Her tests are hard if you don't prepare for them but she curves and she makes sure you get the grade you deserve. TAKE HER.
She was an amazing teacher. Tough, but she forced you to know your stuff. She was always available to help you one-on-one.

Granted, she is the hardest organic chemistry professor. BUT, she is the most clear and helpful professor. She holds review sessions every week, which I highly recommend attending because they are very helpful. Do LOTS of practice problems, and you should do fine on her exams!
NEVERRR TAKE HER!!!!

If you want to learn and master organic chemistry for mcats/medical school, take Dixon! She teaches material that other professors don't cover (i.e. IR, fisher projections, etc) and makes her students memorize more material, but it is worth it. She has office hours everyday and holds a weekly review session. Take her if you can!
very helpful teacher but hard exams

Wow, she's an awesome professor!!!! Her energy lights up the whole room every morning!! She will never give up on her students! Very helpful and very patient!! came out ok from the class, but I truely enjoyed the learning!!! You will do too, and that's a promise!!

If she mentions it in class its fair game (and she will ask it)!  super entertaining and down to earth lectures and has a bizarre ability to turn a 255 person lecture into a small class-room type environment encouraging student interaction.  your grade will definitely reflect your level of effort. SLACKERS BEWARE!
She is a really good teacher, really likes being asked questions.  Really helpful if you come in for office hours or email her.
short and sweet: if you do take her, take an extra class for the semester so that when you drop it you won't be a part time student. :)WARNING: take another prof if u can!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Dixon is an amazing prof. If you are taking the class for the purpose of simply learning, I would suggest that you take Dixon because she will teach you the most. However her tests are nearly impossible so if you are looking to just get through orgo with a decent grade and don't really care about the knowledge you come away with, take another prof.

This class is not easy and she don't really make it easy for you, yes she gives extra credit but at the end of the class you notice it really is only like a point or two. Her test is extremely hard and the average score in my class for each test ranged between a 20 and a 30 out of 100. I would not recommend her or take her again.

Expect to work in this class. Devote at least 2 hrs for every hour spent in class. Go to review sessions n attend all lectures. Her tests are hell and cumulative. She is very helpful if you come to help. She does give xtra credit. Very easy to get behind n fail if u rnt on the ball

Dixon is a great teacher. def take chemistry with her. she really cares about teaching and about her students. she will go above and beyond to help you understand. the material is hard but if you go to class and do the work you will do fine. tests seem impossible but there is a huge curve at the end.
the tests are tough but her classes are intersting. she is very funny and will do anything to help you learn the material. you actually learn a lot.
She's a great professor who will really help you out if you put in the effort and go to her. However, she's one of harder professors in the Chem department so be ready to work!

Had her for Chem131, got an A ...HOWEVER, for Chem231, i realize why there are many people who hate her: difficult tests, requires too many things other orgo professors leave out, paces through material til last second of class, must devote HOURS outside of class, very busy woman, extreme organic nut, lower curve than others, mandatory attendance
k;k
Dixon moves a little quickly sometimes, and her exams are pretty difficult, but she is good at explaining things and is very approachable for questions. She is a pretty good prof.

very good teacher! she's funny and keeps you involved...its very hard, but that is just organic chemistry in general. she is always willing to help and holds review sessions before exams. she likes to see her students succeed so she has plenty of extra credit and generously curves. take her if you can!

She was a fun teacher and she seemed like an interesting one. But she went way too into detail without explaining why she was doing things... and the tests are VERY hard. pretty much if u go to every lecture you'll get some form of extra credit.  However, I don't think it's worth it.

I thought Dr. Dixon was a great teacher and she went out her way to help students with lots of out-of-class review sessions.  She is especially good if you are planning on taking orgo b/c she really concentrates on getting her students ready for that.  This is the first chem teacher that Ive actually liked!
She is funny and goofy but she gets very cocky and arrogant at times. Her tests are pretty hard. But she gives either a big curve or a lot of extra credit at the end of the semester

She is extremely helpful and goofy. Encourages questions and wants to help students learn. Her tests are pretty fair and she teaches everything thoroughly. Holds tons of optional review sessions. The only reason that easiness is not a 5 is because the subject is Chemistry. She is obsessed with organic chemistry though. If you take chem, get her.

great professor. she teaches chemistry in a refreshing way so you won't ever be bored. She is extremely helpful outside of class; loves to see students. attend every lecture and keep up in the textbook and do a lot of practice in order to get at least a B
she's a good teacher, very helpful, in and ouside of class.  very resourceful.  her exams are hell because she knows she's a good teacher.  but she's fair in the end.
Hilariously awesome, will teach you everything.
Amazing

I actually am surprised she has negative ratings. Very nice, willing to help any student who needs help, even outside of chemistry. Tests straight forward, very energetic and light hearted. Not serious like you'd expect from a CHEM teacher. Uses students for demostrations instead of chemicals. My best teacher so far at UMD!
She is definately very helpful, makes learning chemistry somewhat interesting and is very energetic. Tests are based on problems done in lecture.

Best teacher I've had so far. Dixon makes everything clear and easy to understand. Definitely take her. Test are easy as long as you go to lecture and pay attention. I don't know about her curve because I didn't need it. Very energetic too.

Out of all the science classes that I have taken at MD, she is definately the best professor I have ever had. Her lectures were clear, and although the tests were hard, they were more then fair. She never hesistates to help students who want to learn. I hated my science major so much i swtiched majors, so for me to enjoy orgo, she had to be good...
she is one of the worst professors i have ever had

Her tests were impossible, the class average was never higher than the mid-60s. She also taught the class with a heavy emphasis on people who were continuing in the sciences. She is obsessed with orgo and gets off on tangents about it. Her notes are not well organized either. On the plus side, she gets test grades posted within two days of the test

CAUTION: Do not be fooled by this professor's false facade! I often went to her office only to be met w/ a rude and arrogant attitude.  She teachs only easy problems from book and tests are often unfairly graded.

Irritating, teaches only easy material out of the book, puts extremely hard and unfair material on tests, contradictory, can't admit when she's wrong (which is very often), very annoying, doesn't know her stuff as much as she'd like you to think, very condescending about college-level classes. I hate her.

Gosh, She is one of my favorite teacher. I mean her class was funn. She is like the perfect package people search for in a prof. She is a great teacher with a sense of humor, her exams are not impossible, her curves can bring up a letter grade, she is always available for office hours. I very strongly recommend this prof.

one of my favorite teachers. she does a WONDERFUL JOB at teaching. shes around for help almost ALL the time. and she doesnt care if you didnt spent much time at home, she still welcomes students in her office. she makes funny demonstrations sometimes which seriously makes the class not only enjoyable but also helpful for learning the material.
Made class enjoyable
Very helpful and clear.  Sometimes goes off into organic, which is not necessary.  One of the most fun professors that I have had.
She was tough, but fair and VERY helpful.  The way she teaches helps you understand the material, and not just memorize it.

She's excellent.  Her class is not easy, but she is very fair.  First-rate lectures.  You will not be sleeping through her classes.  This is good because that would be the kiss of death in this class.  DO NOT fall behind.  But if you go to class, keep up with the lectures, and DO LOTS of PROBLEMS, you're golden.  Try to stay ahead of lectures.

awesome teacher, having failed orgo once before dr dixon is by far one of the best teachers i have had at md. she will go out of her way and do anything to help students learn. actually made a horrendous class bearable
No Comments
She's a hard professor.  You have to keep up with the work.  Her exams are challegning but fair.  She's really helpful and will do anything to get her students get better grades.
She doesn't know how to explain in easy way. she speaks too fast and hard to get the main concept. she makes organic chem much harder

I can't emphasize how much I love this woman (as a teacher). She's so kind, passionate, and tech savvy when it comes to the field of theatre. Dr Marshall's has done things such as make us do fun exercises, cool improve techniques, and the icing on the cake was feeding as New York style pizza on our last day of class. Take her as much as you can!

Fun and very energetic in class, accessible and helpful outside of it too. Lots of weekly homework with writing assignments TAs grade kinda harsh, definitely had to work hard but it was a fun class I actually made friends in. Not a fully easy A, hard to keep up if you skip. Take notes on analysis she gives you! It helped me so much for the midterm

TAs grade very harshly. Dr. Marshall is very fun to have and relatively understanding regarding mental health and other issues like that. She can be a bit unorganized but the workload for this class is very easy and I would def recommend this course as an easy gened.

Professor Marshall is a great professor who truly cares about her students. If you're struggling, don't be afraid to reach out to her; she is very understanding. Don't wait until the last minute to write your papers, they can be long and detailed. Not a difficult class as long as you follow the rubrics and put effort into the assignments.

Dr. Marshall is great and very personable as a professor. As someone who has taken this course as a Gen Ed and little experience with any theater, she understands that there are students in similar situations and tries to make the course a learning experience. A relevant course for our current times. She's pretty funny too.

She tries to get the class moving and wants everyone to participate, so if you're an introvert like me, you'll sometimes wish you could hide, but overall she was a great professor. If you're interested in a theatre class, I'd recommend taking it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Marshall. She brings so much energy into the classroom and what she teaches that it compels you to listen and understand. She also doesn't pretend like some of the class isn't interested or if the entire class is tired. She is aware. Fun projects, online lecture style. Works well with her TAs and trains them well.

This class is not an easy A, you need to do the work and late work is not accepted, you will get a zero. There are weekly quizzes, a final project (parts are due throughout the semester, midterm, final, and weekly reading comprehensions. There is a lot of work that is graded a little harshly by TA's but the work is doable. Stay on top of your work

Do NOT take this class if you want an easy A. This class has changed from the previous semesters. It has become a lot harder because the TA's are so picky when it comes to grading. The lectures were entertaining. Always stay on top of things because there's so many random busy assignments due at random times. Weekly writings, midterm, final.

This class is fun, but it's a lot of busy work. There is a group project that lasts almost all semester and you do have to go to DC to see a play. Make sure to stay on top of your work (quizzes, padlets, peer comments) and do kahoot participation in class. Overall Dr. Marshall is fun and this class is worth taking for a GenEd.

I don't mind that this class has a lot of work, I really enjoyed the class and the atmosphere. However, the grading is what really got students upset. The TAs are very picky and expect everyone to have this intense knowledge on theater! The expectations for these students is way to high, be careful with this class it is not how it use to be.

I thought this was an easy class but HA! kinda is, but the workload was outrageous. Make sure to look online for small quizzes, writing comprehensions, and etc. There is a midterm (that you had to go out and watch a play). There is a final project (make sure to have a really good group) and there is a final! Make sure to ask your TA questions!

I wish I knew how the class structure was changed this semester, I do not think I would have taken the class if I knew the structure was so different. They have included a huge project and a midterm and final. The workload is on the higher end, but the issue is that TA graded everything so harshly. If you want an easy gen ed, this is not class.!!!!

This class has been changed this semester and is no longer a fun, easy class. The workload for this class on the higher end, but the high expectations for these assignments make the class ridiculous. We had fun class lectures, however the TA grading the work was just not fair. Like I said, this class is not an easy A at all.

This class has been changed and it is not how it was. The class is not an easy A. There are reading comprehensions, weekly quizzes, padlets, projects, a midterm and a final exam. The TA's in this class grade the students work as if they are graduate students themselves, the expectations for this class is ridiculous.

I expected to love THET110 but was absolutely relieved when the semester ended. It was unnecessarily difficult for a 100 level class. Everything is graded by graduate student TA's who simultaneously expected students have have their mastery of content, yet graded difficultly (it takes a lot to get a 20/20 on the weekly writings).

Dr. Marshall is probably the coolest prof you've ever had, but the class is unnecessarily hard for a 100 level non majors gen-ed. Also the TAs are responsible for grading and it seems like they expect all students to have a grad school level understanding of theatre because A+ grades are almost impossible to get. NOT the class for an easy gen-ed A

Dr. Marshall is a big ball of energy! She keeps you on your toes. This class was filled with lots of busy work though. The busy work is easy but can be a pain to do. Lots reading analysis. Attendance is kind of mandatory because there are clicker points and Padlets points. You have to go see a play at Ford's theater which was cool.

Dr. Marshall is a great professor! She is very kind, funny, and engaging. I took this class as an Arts Scholars supporting course, and I thoroughly enjoyed it. There is essentially no acting, so if you are shy, don't worry! I would recommend attending lecture since she does clicker polls in order to give attendance credit.

DO THE EXTRA CREDIT AND YOU'LL BE FINE!! Dr. Marshall is really kind and is always willing to help. The readings are not bad but make sure you don't skip too much bc she gives about one clicker per week. Solid choice for the humanities gen ed bc she doesn't even make you memorize specific dates for the most part. Seeing the show in dc was fun. 8/10

Professor Marshall is a great lecturer. I genuinely look forward to going to the class because she does such a great job of keeping it engaging and funny. Yes, she does do pop quizzes on readings, but there aren't too many readings and if you pay attention and show up to class you will do fine.

Really good lecturer. She has a lot of energy and that transfers into her lectures. She does give pop quizzes on the reading, but if you have friends in the class it is super helpful to get them right. Pretty easy gen ed to complete

She does not round. I had an 89.8 in her class after the final that the class average was 70%. The final was so hard, and this is a student who went from a 98 in the class to a 89.8. I wouldn't recommend taking this as an elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You had to go see 2 plays (one in DC and one on campus) but the class is very easy overall. If you do the work and show up to class (theres participation every class) and do the extra credit you will definitely get an A. Professor Marshall is very kind and will always be there to answer questions

Pablo was an excellent professor. Pablo is very gifted at explaining things in a clear way and is great at fielding difficult or very specific questions. Pablo also connects things to previous math classes we've taken. Pablo is also just a very nice and understanding person, and plugged us with great exam review materials for the final.

Pablo was really good at teaching concepts through example problems that highlighted important concepts. He was also very thorough with his explanations, which helped me understand how to approach and complete problems. He also helped us reference various resources, such as previous exams in this course, which I thought was helpful as well!
Pablo's ability to explain and break down the concepts and topics made the class way less overwhelming. It was also really easy to talk with him and ask questions. Overall great guy!
I took Math 141 with him in the summer and he was a nice professor. His exams were really fair, and gave us bonus points as well in every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pablo is literally a king, I love him so much and he was FOR SURE a huge factor in my success in the class! He was so good at explaining concepts and applying them to problems that might be seen in the exams.
Pablo did an amazing job going through practice problems, preparing us for quizzes/exams, and answering questions. It felt like he genuinely cared about us and our learning. No criticism!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Cedillos was an amazing instructor for Calc 2. He was extremely patient and made the course extremely manageable and understandable.

If you are looking to take a summer class with him, be warned: the pacing is incredibly off. When a section is taught it will be followed by a quiz, this in itself is not out of the ordinary; the problem comes when the hw is due a week after the quiz takes place which is quite inconvenient. Also the examples on class are straight from the book.

Attending lectures was fundamental to my success in this class. The textbook can get pretty abstract and convoluted at times, but Cerrai covered all of the most important topics in a clear and concise manner during lectures. Her exams had extra credit problems and were relatively straightforward if you reviewed and remembered the exam content.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The most difficult math410 exams at UMD, we've compared them. It goes beyond knowing the material, there is an aspect of luck unless you are a truly gifted mathematician/problem solver. To make it worse, her lectures are ineffective. She def knows her stuff, but I don't think she enjoys teaching. She does curve generously tho and shes a character
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor was assigned to me after the professor I originally signed up for dropped. She is accommodating with due dates, but very hard grader and not very helpful in office hours. Would not take her again.

Cerrai is alright, if you don't mind not understanding the lectures, instead learning from the book on your own, or last minute homeworks announced for the day before the final, or being chewed out for getting a bad grade when asking about old exam problems instead of receiving help. Online classes are tough, but this was too much.

Had her for STAT410. She was ok. The material itself isnt hard and she explains nicely. Thought the first exam was hard because I didnt know what to expect. But her second and final exam were fine. Not too different from what we had seen in class. She can get annoyed if she asks a question in class and no one answers. Overall I would recommend.

She gets frustrated when students don't know something in class and isn't a friendly person in office hours. Hard to know what she expects from students in terms of testable material, especially because there are no resources besides a book which isn't similar to her exams. I got an A but still wouldn't recommend her. 2 stars because she is smart.

Its so sad that this teacher gets reviewed by STAT400 students. STAT400 is usually a class geared towards those in Eng/Econ/ minoring in stat/Business so there are hardly any math majors and thus, its not appreciated how good of a math prof she is. For STAT410 or any other upper level math class she is def the best option. Very straightforward.
God help you reading her lecture notes off the board. Avoid if possible
Lectures are pretty incoherent; learned much more from my TA. Class was generally easy

I found the teacher to be very boring.  I ended up skipping her classes half-way through the semester because I wouldn't learn anything (I read the book at  home and went to TA office hours for help).  Exams are fair and not tough if you know the material.  Quizes are straight from the hw.  hw prepares you for the exams.  Overall ok.

I really enjoyed this class! She is very clear, and lectures cover everything you need to know. She is also clear on what will be covered in the exams, and the exams are not super easy but you learn from them! Overall: great teacher for stats!
Nice person, but tests were more difficult than average.

Ms. Goldberg is by far one of the best professors I have ever had during my time at the University of Maryland, College Park. Ceil is very respected in the Professional Writing Program at UMD. She has over 20+ years of experience as an editor and knows her stuff very well. I would definitely recommend taking her if you want to learn/have fun!

If you want to learn Business Writing Skills take this class with her. You would consider her awesome if you truly care about your education and plan to attend class and do the work (She cares about students). Great professor to keep in mind when you are planning to ask anyone for letters of recommendations (for work or continuing your education).

PROS: Learn some useful writing skills in this class.   CONS: She is very critical of everyones writing.  Very tough grader no matter how good you are. Also, she gives a lot of writing prompts so be prepared to do a lot of work. Finally, if you are a person who is not on time do not take her class. She will deduct points if you're a min late.

Super nitpicky. I consider myself a good writer and ended up with an A in her class but come on lady. Would take off points because I wouldn't put a semi-colon. She says its important for the business world but in the business world people could honestly care less as long as your message is clear. Can also be super rude without even realizing it.

Honestly, she is the worst teacher at UMD. Seriously avoid her like the plaque. EVERYTHING is graded subjectively. She got her degree in Psychology, how the hell does that have anything to do with Business Writing? Anyways do yourself a favor and switch to an actual Professor and you will get something out of the class. Your welcome.

Never take a class with her. Uses vague rubrics so she can deduct extra points based on her own whims. Did not learn a thing about business writing; only her own personal opinion.  Worst, most arrogant and pathetic excuse for a teacher I have ever had. Someone like this should stay teaching community college. Can't believe she was hired by UMD.

She's a nice teacher, strict but fair. The assignments weren't hard, but she was very critical of your work. Her 'textbook' is only 40 dollars, which is good but it's a 100-page book of examples and it's only available in one place.

Class (Business Writing) is tough regardless of the professor, but very useful for professional career.  If you show up to all classes prepared and participate, you should do well.  I don't recommend taking the class during the summer as the reduced time frame makes it more difficult.
She is strict, but pretty fair. If you have any problems, talk to her. She is willing to discuss your mistakes and issues.

Gives no direction or guidance to the class. Leaves students to "figure everything out on their own". She will find something to deduct points for in your papers. She is unclear and takes points off of your paper if you do not see things the way she does.   I regret taking this class with this professor.

Despite the fact that this class is super hard and that you must attend everyday no matter what- it was worth it. Some people will not like her for sure because she is very strict and finds errors in the most perfect papers. Its not an eay A. But attendance in her class is worthwhile.
The worst teacher imaginable. She assigns homework for the next day at 11pm. She is lost in the clouds. Try to find a different teacher.
Horrible teacher. Really mean and nonsupporting. Gives no hope for a good grade. Not constant with directions. SWITCH-OUT!!!
She was so rude on my first day of class, I dropped the class immediately.

Professor Centorbi is a good lecturer. She cares about her job and knows a lot about geology. She is also funny. I took this class in Fall 2023. She drops one of the three midterm exams and one quiz. I did not give the class five stars because participation is required. But, she dropped the five lowest participation grades. All around easy class.

Homework graded on completion, which was nice! Other than that, very hard class. Quiz, long homework(s), and sometimes an exam packed in one week. Participation graded heavily. Not the kindest person. Exams always worded differently than what we learned in class, and I found studying for them to be extremely difficult. Would not take again.

She tests us on material we have never learned or done in lecture together. She words her exam questions differently than her homework questions, and tests you on things she mentioned as an afterthought in class. And due to her randomized testing, you can get the same question 5 times, so good luck to you if you get the wrong answer each time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class is a LOTTTT of work: a chapter, quiz, and video quiz every week. But, she makes it clear that the exams (4, plus an OPTIONAL final exam) are based on the video lectures, so you know exactly what to study, and the exams are all multiple choice. She gives 5% extra credit. She is also very kind and understanding about unexpected issues :)

WORST class and professor I have ever had. Each week, there is a whole chapter with questions due. On top of that, there are 5+ lecture videos to watch with a video quiz attached. Finally, there is a quiz every. single. week. When there is an exam, you get no break. You must complete all the same work on top of the exam. She is very inconsiderate.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Tracey be wildin' She gives you an exam that is due on the same day you have a quiz due. The final week has an exam and quiz due not to mention the cumulative final exam too. Set aside time to read the 30 page chapters (many pictures). She loves rocks so much its scary. Content Packed 100 class! She did offer up to 5% Extra Credit Online S '21
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I swear to god I won't go anywhere near this professor again. Insane courseload for a 100 level class, heavy homework assignments due weekly along with tests every 2-3 weeks. Material on tests is also very in-depth and impossible to memorize all of it. For an A in this class, you'd need to dedicate at least 15-20 hours a week. Ridiculous.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Organization and clear instructions were unmatched by any other class taken at UMD. Prompt grading, communication, and updates. Clear from Day 1 that work takes 6 hours a week (I took less). I struggled with Exams 1 and 2 but her helpful suggestions helped me alot (other professors can learn a lot from her!) Follow the schedule she gave!!
So much work. Literally spent hours a night in order to get through it. Even had a quiz and an exam do the same week. Not worth it. Dont do it to yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She's very nice. Not sure if this is every semester, but here's the workload rundown: There's a powerpoint/videos for this week's chapter, then by Wed., post some comments in discussion, comment on someone else's, then you have to take a quiz on that chapter by Fri. Test every 4 chapters. accepting with late work. Just a littlemuchwithotherclasses
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor is definitely knowledgable in her field but I felt like I was in an upper level geology class. There was a ton of work and exams have questions based on every minuscule thing she says in lecture videos. Even during a pandemic with online classes she had us download a software that watched us take our exams. Way too hard. Do not take this.

-way too much workload for a 100 level class (like 5 assignments a week, WHY) -Exams had questions not gone over in anything -doesn't understand how Extra credit works, thanks for that 0.4% bump for 4-5 hours worth of quizzes on top of extra studying -moved online, somehow ADDED MORE ASSIGNMENTS -takes it way too seriously, its about rocks
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: You will fail almost every test, no matter how much you study. Even if you attend every lecture, take thorough notes, and do all of the reading/work. There were even questions that weren't from the book or lecture. She does not care that the class average is a D. The class could have been decent if the professor wanted the students to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She really sucks and hates freshman connection students. Doesn't take feedback well and just is overall not a good professor. Her exams have chem related questions on there and she doesn't mention any of that in class. Overall bad class would not recommend with her.

She explains things well in lecture and office hours, but she can be sassy and rude when questions are asked, which is demeaning. If you study for her tests (a lot), and know exactly what she wants, you will do well. It's a lot, but if you put in the work and can deal with her sassy/rude attitude.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You put in the effort, you'll do fine. She'll see you are trying and will provide help. Exams are fair, for the most part. Not too difficult if you actually do the study guides (30+ pages for the final). Very approachable in her office hours. Wouldn't have passed without them. May not click with her teaching style, however I would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Take another professor. There are those that get along really well with her and I'm guessing those are the ones that gave her a good rating. My biggest problem with her is that she makes us do concept sketches but a lot of the information is not even in the textbook. I would not take her again and if I could go back in time, I would avoid her

This professor sucks. She talks to us like we are in an elementary level class. Her lectures have nothing to do with the online quizzes or exams, and are extremely boring. The exams are concept sketches, and some concept sketches were not provided in the book nor lecture???Btw this is coming from a STEM major.

Pretty easy class, but it requires so much more time than i was willing. im not a stem major, but this class was recommended. if you arent interested in this class, iwould not take it. theres so much memorization for her tests. the weekly quizzes are pretty difficult because you haven't learned much of it. her lectures are soooo boring.

THE class is SUPER EASYYYYYY. Take this class it is a cake walk. The exams are based only on the concept sketches which she posts well in advance before the exams. Other than this there are online quizzes which are 20% of your grade which is due at the end of the week. Lastly, there is an extra credit opportunity which is worth 5% of your total grade
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I guess ppl want to be handed grades. This was the easiest class I have ever taken. Homework was easy, openbook online quizzes, and you know exactly what will be on exams. Lowest grade in everything is dropped. Complaints were probably from non-STEM/science majors. Centorbi was a great lecturer, cares for her students and expects you do some work.

Love her! She is an interesting lecturer and really know what she is talking about. Tests are online and the lowest is dropped. Attendance is not mandatory but you have clicker ?s every class (your lowest 6 scores are dropped though). Overall, I was really happy with her as a professor. She is smart, funny, and passionate

Look. I'm a 3.6 student in the business school so I thought this would be an easy knockout for my DSNL requirement. Oh, could I have been more wrong. Her lectures have little to do with the actual exams (which are absolutely impossible unless you're a GEOL major). Deliberately goes out of her way to confuse students who presumed this was an intro

I thought that this course was going to be quite interesting and relatively easy; however, I found this class to be extremely hard. The professor had no respect towards her students and frequently compared us to her "smarter" classes. Although the information was interesting and well taught, the tests were hard, somewhat irrelevant and too specific
She's clearly interested in the subject. Sometimes the lectures seem to drag, but as long as you make sure you take good notes and put in SOME effort, you'll do great.

She doesn't understand that this is an introductory, genes class. She gives much more work than any other 100 level course I have taken and is stingey about giving points. Tests are often composed of at least 50% material we haven't even learned, making them impossible even though they are online. She also talks to you like you're in 2nd grade.

Tracey is EASILY one the best professors out there! She is kind, helpful, and cares so much about her students and it shows. Her lectures are clear, she's easy to get along with, and I learned a ton from her. Between the extra credit, fair exams, and in class activities, it's absolutely possible to achieve an A. Shame it had to end! Recommended.

I definitely recommend taking this course! The lectures are extremely organized and Professor Centorbi is very knowledageble about the content of the material. There are clicker questions every class that count toward your grade, so you need to go to class. Study hard for the online tests, read every chapter and study the lecture slides.

Wow- I totally disagree with the others. This was probably the best class I've taken at UMD. The professor is super helpful and nice(even though she sometimes seems mean in lecture). If you go to class and do the review sheets, this class is NOT hard but you do have to work for your grade. Easy A if you go to class.
She is not helpful at all. Her online tests are extremely hard and do not relate to her slides at all. You have to listen to every word she says in oder to get any points on the exam

This class was unnecessarily difficult. Throughout the semester, getting an A felt unattainable. She made you work like a dog for all your points. The extra credit field trip was okay (I guess) but in the end, I ended up with a B in the class. I would study for hours and hours for the test and still get a C. Many students had the same experience.

This class was way harder than it needed to be.. the material was not hard but she made it difficult. This class is NOT an easy A... you have to work for it. I would definitely recommend going to the extra credit field trip and doing the discussion board to boost your grade. Also, do the practice exams
Boring class, lots of memorization for tests, her voice makes you want to fall asleep, she makes the material more difficult to learn than it actually is.
boring class dont have to study that much just do the study guides before the test and you'll be fine, her practice exam multiple choice are exactly like whats on the test

Not necessarily an easy A, but it can be done with some extra work. She offers a field trip for an extra 15% on a test grade GO if you're between grades! Before a test do the study guides with the slides AND book. She may have 3-5 questions on a test that are not covered in her slides. For a non-science person her class is easy and to the point.

Recieving a grade other than an A is inexcusable. This class couldnt be any easier. I never read any of the chapters and hardly even went to lecture (though she is an excellent lecturer and I shoulda gone more often). Before the tests I just do her review sheets she posts on ELMS using her online slides posts. I aced the tests with flying colors.

Seemed like a really nice lady.  Lectures were straightforward power points taken right from text, although it did help to actually read chapters in book before tests.  Most info easy to understand, tests not too hard, final really easy.  Discussion was annoying with lots of busy work, but mandatory.

Lectures were very concise, often to the point of boredom. Discussions are pointless and if you don't do the worksheets then you're screwed. Often talks about morbid topics, how we are all going to die from things that are happening in the environment, etc. Easy to do well if you can pay attention and don't mind busywork.

Really nice teacher. I talked with her one on one after class one day and she has liked me ever since--always a plus when she deals out extra credit points. Go to lecture as often as you can, as she gives chances for extra credit only for those who are there. Willing to curve tests. Easy class, but lots of (unnecessary) memorization.

Centorbi is not a smart lady.  Lectures are almost entirely from the text word for word.  She seems to delight in making learning harder than it needs to be.  She treats students like children and is not trusting (eg. she refuses to hand out answer keys to tests after they are graded).  Tests are fair, but she's the worst! Don't take this class!

Ms. Centorbi was a decent teacher. While her lectures were not intriguing, her power point presentations were very clear. The tests were pretty easy because they were straight-forward and covered a fair portion of the material. The final exam was the easiest test since it was all multiple choice and mainly covered the last few weeks of the course.

Really nice professor. Her class is worth taking. The only problem that you may encounter is that you have to memorize a lot for the tests. I have been reading the chapters prior to taking the tests-- I am getting around 90%'s. Class average around 70%'s. She curves and does extra credit.

The class is interesting for those who like science without a need for math. Basic rock stuff, however tests/class are detailed so you need to study before tests. Professor contradicts herself sometimes, but the lectures are online so use those plus the review sheets she gives and the exams should be easy. Non-stressful A.

lectures are very boring and her voice resembles lullaby that puts you to sleep.... you might want to sit in the front row if you take her class.  the class is easy and attendance is mandatory cuz everythings from the powerpoint. warning: discussions are realllllly boring too.

She is just such a nice person when you talk to her after class. There is a LOT of material covered so you have to study. Tests were easy if you did the thought questions. Ten points of extra credit added to test scores made it an easy A.

She does her best to make sure everyone's clear on what she is discussing and help us along with extra credit when she can. The class is just tough. The material is not too hard, it's just a lot of material. The TA's grade stringently, so its a good idea to have her look over exams and she might give you some extra points when TAs were too harsh.
Centorbi's exams are straight from her slides and thought questions.

I don't like science but I had to take a course. If you have to, take this professor's class. She is really interested in what she does and puts a lot of effort into trying to get you to relate what she's teaching to your life. Tests are easy if you go to class and answer the questions on the study guide. Discussion exercises were easy.

Despite the fact that her lectures put me to sleep every class, she's not that bad. There's just a lot to remember but otherwise an A in this course is extremely possible. She cares that students do well in her class. She also is pretty passionate about geology and will send you tons of environmental articles by email.

This class was ridiculously easy. The powerpoints give you all the information you need, and her review sheets cover everything she will put on the test. As long as you go through and study everything on them you will do well. Lectures were a little boring, but the tests were very basic if you actually study.

one of the most boring class i ever took. discussion is annoying, quizzes every discussions, and random assigments--mostly busywork. study the notes online and attend review sessions. nice prof but easily annoyed by students.
She is a great teacher, and as long as you do the work, it's an easy A.
I got a higher grade than I expected. She is really nice and helpful. Tests are easy if you go to class. Extra credit and review sheets for exams-lowest grade is dropped.
This class is alot of work for a Core class and the discussion part of it, has alot of assignmnets. Teacher offers extra credit and the tests somehow don't really match up with the material.

She gives webnotes, extra credit and a curve. The pop quizzes aren't graded- just checked. The stuff is boring but she does the best with it she can. She tries to talk about stuff happening in the world that she is teaching. If you go over the review sheets, exams are easy!

She's really helpful and always takes lots of time to answer any question. I don't like the material but she tries. She offers extra credit and the exams are easy. Web notes outline every lecture so you always know what to expect.

This is a core non-lab science. The amount of work is heavy and there are pop quizzes in lecture. She drops the lowest exam but there are papers and readings due in discussion weekly. I would not recommend this course, too much work for a core.

Unless you're naturally good at math, you will struggle. A lot of people are willing to spend hours every day making this class their first priority, but for someone with other priorities, this class was just awful. They take off points for anything. Please avoid.

I am convinced that bots wrote good reviews for his calculus (MATH140) class. Chadwick stares at his board and reads off his textbook during lecture, and his real exams are SIGNIFICANTLY more difficult than his sample exams. In fact, I would even say that his sample exams were nothing like the real ones at all.

Occasionally confusing and sometimes showed up late, but Chadwick's lectures were very good, and he's a very caring professor. Exams aren't too difficult, but I recommend studying a lot in groups & attending TA office hours. If you have Chadwick & a really good TA, you're set as long as you put in the work outside of lecture.
Chadwick was a great teacher and was super nice and accommodating when I had a difficult time this semester

Maybe he is better than the other math professors but i regret switching into his math140 section. Dr. Chadwick DOES have very clear lectures but only some of the practice exams reflect the actual exams. fail one midterm or don't have any prior calc knowledge? good luck passing the class. he doesn't curve or round up. TAs were superior though.

Definitely the best option for 140, but expect Chad to be meek and awkward with a super avg teaching style. What's great about his class, though, are the sample exams--most of the time you'll be asked nearly identical questions on midterms, just with different equations. HW can be finessed via symbolab, and it only counts for 2-3% of your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Compared to the other math professors, Chadwick is pretty easy and his lectures are at a good pace to be able to take notes in class. Make sure to study a lot for the midterms and final as exams make up a big portion of your grade.

AVOID CHADWICK AT ALL COSTS!! we had hw 2-3 times a week & it only counts for 3% of final grade. he doesn't teach & just reads out of the textbook with no explanation at all. he teaches like you should know how to do everything already. exams make up 80% of your final grade. no curve when averages are in 60s. take literally ANY other professor!

For everybody saying this guy is an amazing teacher, is lying. They're only saying that because they have taken 2 years of Calculus prior to college. Of course if you already know the material, you are going to do decent, I would hope so if you don't have the IQ of a dead squirrel. Doesn't teach. Instead, he just freestyles the textbook.

Chadwick is not difficult. Just actually pay attention to class and not fall asleep, you should pass with an A. Obviously, you have to take notes in the class. The problems he makes you do in class will pop up on the midterms or exams he gives. Homework load is manageable too. Missing a few classes isn't the end of the world, the textbook is there.

There is only three webassign homeworks each week at most, and occasional (easy) quizzes during discussion sections that are usually problems that have been done during previous lectures. He's pretty good at explaining things and answers questions. He's also provides several practice exams from previous years that are extremely to the real ones.

Lectures are succinct explanations of the material from the textbook, and he is very willing to answer questions during lecture and office hours. He also reviews material prior to each exam, so you know what to expect. Homework takes effort typical for math, but is easy points. Hes a great and popular choice as his classes fill up quickly.
Do not take him, the homework load was a lot. Half of my class dropped him after the third midterm, worksheets given were a bunch of theory. TA was great!

An awesome person and professor. Really cares about his students. Exams are doable, unlike some other calc 2 classes.

reviews.comment: BEST OF THE BEST. CHADWICK IS A TRUE ANGEL. Please take him if you can. He makes the materials understandable, and tests are straightforward. BEST PROFESSOR EVER!

Dr. Chadwick is one of the best math teachers I have ever had. He is very organized; his explanations are clear. He is also attentive to his students, and he is happy to answer questions.

Chadwick is the highest of homies. He's super relaxed and gives few surprises. He was super approachable the entire semester and had easy to understand lectures.

Chadwick is the BEST choice for Math140, he gives the exact questions that will be on the exams and is super helpful after class and in office hours. He explains everything really well and writes very neatly. Great choice

Easily the best math teacher I've had. Chadwick is my favorite teacher here at UM. He's very clear when teaching and tries to make sure everyone is on the same page. Also he's hilarious, you'll have a good time in his class.

Very hard labs and tests, not easy to contact at all. Email your TA.

Go to TA office hours.

Worst professor I've ever had. She was never present and only appeared for the final review which was 3 hours maximum. She disappeared again afterwards.

DONT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS. IT WILL BE THE LAST THING YOU DO! She doesnt teach, doesnt respond to emails, is rude to students, doesnt give a damn about people struggling, the class is a mess, and the average on the the final was a 50%. You have been warned.

Absolutely terrible, 0/10 do not recommend.

You have to teach yourself almost entirely! Instructions almost always vague. Overall very unaccomodating and difficult. Don't stress yourself out, take someone else!

Literally awful. She doesn't help with anything and the assignments take hours just to figure out what she wants from you. The prelab quizzes have nothing to do with the labs or anything she goes over.

Sorry excuse for a prof, does absolutely nothing to help and has her TA's do everyone. Take anyone else but her. Extremely unaccommodating and just overall horrible

Would not recommend if you hate teaching yourself

AWFUL. A W F U L. take anyone over her. might as well learn from a rock.

reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

Taken 2 classes with Prof Cote and it's just been all around a great experience (and I am really bad at school). Very understanding.

Paul Cote is the best professor EVER! So understanding and caring of his students. Go to class, you will pass. If you do the assignment its an A+ easily.

Dr. Cote is awesome! He's super relatable and his assignments can be a tad bit difficult, but as long as you complete them with the criteria you get an A. Super cool dude and easy class that really helped my writing.

Only 2 essays!

Professor Cote was one of the best english professors I have ever had! prof GOAT is the best English teacher I've had. He's super accommodating and directs class so that it is relevant and geared toward your interests. Not super heavy on reading at all, and he's really understanding if personal life gets in the way of deadlines. Take him for sure.

Great guy! actually sees his students as people with lives and takes into account their wellbeing very understanding especially during the covid-pandemic. Actually listens to his students, made this class a lot more bearable since im wasnt really into english to begin with

One of the most phenomenal teacher I've ever had. Clearly explained lectures and criteria for homework. Very simple and well formatted homework geared towards getting feedback quickly. Lastly, I have discussed this with many of my classmates and almost everyone I know disliked the teacher and felt that they didn't learn anything.

He refuses to allow students to use their cell phones or computers to take notes in class, and will make rounds and regulate you like an elementary school teacher, and if he catches you looking at your cell phone or showing inattentiveness, he will call you out by name like an elementary school teacher (he mispronounces a lot of people's names).

he was a very computer-resistant person, and every time he submitted an assignment he required his students to print out a thick stack of documents and bind them in a specific way, and if you didn't do that, he got very angry. This is very environmentally unfriendly and he claims to be pro-environmental.

He doesn't accept most of the sources as citation sources, but asks you to find out what to cite in the organizations he specifies that don't meet his citation rules, so it's a dead end. It's almost impossible to do, and he'll dock you points in those areas.

His grading mechanism is on a 1000 point scale, which is 0.1% points, will drop you from an A- to a B+ because of 1 point. You could tell he didn't take a hard look at the papers submitted by his classmates because there were some very obvious details that people clearly wrote about, but he said they didn't and then deducted points unreasonably.
Then, at the beginning of the school year, he gives a barrage of guides and introductions, but many of them are contradictory, with lots of words but vague, unnecessary meaning, and confusing.

The classroom was not a place to discuss issues at all, but rather a place for him to put on a personal show and celebrate his work experience. He would either ignore and not talk about areas he was unfamiliar with, or he wouldn't pretend to know anything about them.

Also, his professionalism is suspect. We actually had a large number of researchers in our classroom who were working professionally in a variety of fields, but this professor was so obsessed with his own opinions that he would suddenly become angry and aggressive when students expressed different professional opinions.

Secondly he wasting a lot of time talking to students one-on-one about their "outlines", most of his lectures, if he was lecturing at all, consisted of political anecdotes and unprofessional opinions on the international situation. reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The stat lectures, and therefore the midterms, are pretty easy if you know anything about basic statistics. The coding homework can be pretty difficult, unless you have good TAs who will help you through it.

Coming into 201 I was nervous about the statistical coding we had but looking back the coding wasn't even that hard. The TA's were extremely helpful with the coding homeworks and the big projects she gives were easy. It does pick up but if you attention lectures and pay attention, you'll do fine in this course. She was lovely to have.
She is just not a good teacher, explainer, or lecturer. There is not much else to say.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was excellent but don't be fooled - Dr. Croco only plays a bit part. While she may be the best teacher in the GVPT department at UMD, she unfortunately only has one lecture in this series. Not a ton of work and a very informative class. A great option as an upper-level GVPT class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Take 309C! Very easy, very interesting. Major props to Dr. Croco for setting it up -- shows great creativity and care. Q+A is mandatory! Go to it!

Easy class, as long as you carefully read the syllabus- If you don't, you will find yourself in a huge academic hole come at the end of the semester. I would highly recommend it if you are looking for honors thesis topics

201 is known to be a more difficult class, and maybe it was because of the online environment, but I felt like I understood the majority of what Professor Croco and the TAs were covering. The HW can be a little hard but the TAs discuss it in discussion sections and the reviews/powerpoints she creates for exams are really helpful. Good experience!

This class isn't really a government class. It's more of a stat and CS class with government themed questions n examples. Croco is a nice professor, but she was honestly pretty bad at teaching all these stat concepts in lecture hall. The CS work is tedious and to do well without a background in this stuff, you'd need to put in a ton of extra time.

a really generous professor. she spells out how to do every single project/hw so its really easy to do well if you just listen to her. However, some people still find it challenging for some reason. gave so much extra credit. small curves on the tests. really funny. you don't really have to go to lecture at all

There's two side to class - easy stat lectures and hard code homework. The homework is hard and annoying. Exam was hard if you don't go to lecture but she doesn't take attendance. TA's graded harshly.

The class starts with a review of high school stats, but it get hard quickly after the first midterm. Her lectures are pretty good and she posts them online too, though it is definitely expected that you read before attending them. The TA's are super responsive to homework questions on Piazza. She grades fairly too

At first, she seemed like a really cool professor, but I soon realized that she is not a good lecturer. The first half of the semester was mostly a review from stats, so the first exam was fine. When we moved onto more complex concepts, she completely failed to explain them fully. She never said anything in lecture that helped me with the homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There's a fair amount of homework for this course but it's super doable. All the lectures are posted online so you don't have to ever attend in person. She's super funny and nice, her exams and grading are fair.
Tough class but great teacher

The Lectures, tests, and homework don't really cover the same material. Make sure to attend the discussion since that's where your 10% participation comes from. The homework wont be on the exams, but it is most of what is discussed in discussion. While the HW never covers the textbook, that IS what is covered on the exams. Pay attention to lecture.

Croco is an amazing lecturer who applied statistics to real life Government situations. However, this class is very time consuming. With practice, the database R Studio for the homework will get easier to manage, but the TA's are very approachable and help you resolve problems. The tests are very challenging but the final has a curve.

Croco is an awesome professor.  She is a class act and she is seriously down to earth and will make lecture go smooth with her personality.  R studio will be your worst nightmare but have faith and dont be afraid to ask her questions. Lecture isnt that important but I found myself going to every one because her tests are a bit difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you only take one GVPT class in your entire undergraduate career, then this is the one to take. You will learn how to read articles (what's important to look at, how can the findings be applied elsewhere, etc.) and HOW TO WRITE AND DESIGN YOUR OWN RESEARCH PROJECTS! This class is made even better by the fact that Dr. Croco is crazy smart.

Extremely difficult. Exams are pure memorization of intricate details in the readings. Too many complicated readings. Claims additional midterm reading (also pure memorization, regardless of what she says) was a response to a claim made on this site.
