Don't take unless you have a photographic memory or are only taking a couple classes. No books.

Professor Croco is incredibly knowledgeable and vested in the subject matter.  I had her in 2010 for her international relations course.  Her class is 'difficult' if you don't do work.  If you put in the effort, it's the most rewarding class you could ever take.  I would recommend this for anyone who is interested in Int'l Politics and Statistics.
Tons of readings every week. Good teacher. Difficult class. Tests are pure memorization of journal articles.
Imma kms for how he treats students. Lying about how his exams are based off homeworks, but presents a half alien exam. I wish he was fired.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Probably the most inconsiderate human I've ever encountered. Exams are worth 90% of the grade. With both averages on both midterms, with the first one being an uncurved 50% and the second being 64% with no intention of curving. Class is run poorly, too little time on exams, and review sessions do not match the content on the exam.
Do not take class with this professor, piece of trash!

If you haven't taken ENME202 you've basically already failed this course. MatLab HEAVY! Not enough time is given on the exams that are worth 90% of your overall grade. Questions posted to Piazza or by email usually were never answered or took 3-5 business days. Never gave a specific answer about a curve. Average on exams were around a D every time.

Flipped classroom. Matlab heavy. Final grade is 90% exams, 10% homeworks. Homeworks and exams are completed on PrairieLearn. Exams used Honorlock and had no partial credit. No practice exams or new practice questions were given until the final exam. No extra credit or projects. No grade breakdown was provided and he was secretive about the curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very accommodating, however when it comes to exams prepare to be asked questions you have never seen on homework or even discussed in lecture. Instead, he'll ask extremely obscure memory questions. This class will make your finals hell. End of november into december consists of 2 presentations, a midterm, and a 20 page SINGLE SPACED essay for final
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One midterm, one final essay, not graded on that much else. Aside from that, lectures are usually pretty interesting and he can be funny if you banter with him. Altogether fun class

Just a bit too much work for a graduate class; there are 2 exams, 5 HWs, 2 presentations, and 1 paper. Exams & HW are largely based off of his interpretation and thus are given arbitrary grades. Lectures aren't mandatory but can help. The book isn't required but can be useful. He Barely curves. Overall a fairly difficult professor & class.

Do not waste your time and money taking this guy (or his team). The most uninteresting professor who comes to class to just read through the lecture slides. You are better off taking the course with the other professors who actually teach. His exams are very hard.He might be a nice person, but that does not help you or your grade.

Terrible teacher. His homework assignments were pretty straight forward, but his exams were made to trick you. Also he is very unwilling to help you understand if you don't grasp the material at the level he expects of you. Take this class with someone else.
He was great. He really cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Wonderful class and great professor. I learned so much and since it was discussion based the material flew by.

I took Tony's class during winter term and it was awesome. He gives good lectures and quizzes. I love how the work was super spread out so it never got stressful even though it was a lot of stuff to learn in a short period. He was also my TA from before, always very funny and nice in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: for an online class it was honestly a lot of work but the materials are good and the class is just so organized and clear. the recorded lectures are pretty fun and well made, they also teach me a lot about art and society. kinda a harsh grader, but all the quizzes allow two attempts so you can improve your answers with his feedback.

Do yourself a favor and just drop the class if you have this professor. Never available outside of class, rarely if ever gives students a straight answer to their questions, and makes frequent cheating accusations for sloppy work. He will doc points from you, and he will accuse you of academic dishonesty.

Save your sanity, time, and energy and DON'T take this class with this professor. He never answered any students questions, or provided extra help, and expects you to know everything right away. Our class average was a 45-50, and we had study groups to prepare for the quizzes and exams. If you want to pass, I suggest another teacher.

DO NOT TAKE THIS TEACHER. He will not answer any of your questions, or he will just make you more confused. His lectures and lecture notes are so confusing. He just writes on the chalkboard and doesn't say a word at times . The mean average on the test in our class is 45-50. The class is not hard but this teacher MAKES IT SOOO HARD.

He is a really good professor, and the class is pretty easy.  Low effort for high payoff as long as you communicate early, low effort for high payoff. If you have an assignment issue, they will generally let you redo it if you mention something early.  The projects are graded easy, and the readings are low-key optional.

This class is easy if you approach it the right way. Any graded assignments are open note and have simple rubrics that can be easily completed. All course materials are posted in ELMS, so attending standard lectures is unnecessary. Be sure to check the assignments tab AND the modules tab regularly. It ended up as my least effort and highest grade.

He does not teach you a damn thing, he talks about his life for an hour, and then you have quizzes that have nothing to do with what he talked about. You have a better chance in this class not paying attention and just reading the slides. The TA's are basically useless. He also forces group projects, but sets up the groups in the worst way possible

I would not recommend this class. This class was SO POORLY ORGANIZED. There would be mistakes in deadlines, grading criteria, and even on the tests. The tests were on random things that popped in lecture. If they were not open note they would be impossible. Random assignments would pop up at random times making this class very stressful.

Loved him. Hes such a nice guy. He knows his stuff. The class is a piece of cake, as long as you show up to class and do the assignments youll be just fine. Theres 4 project assignments and they arent hard at all. The 4th project assignment was group based. Quizzes are easy. Hes not here to trick you, he wants everyone in his class to succeed

Professor Curtis is a very respected man. He may be a little disorganized at times but if you just do the projects and quizzes you should get an A. The projects probably took me about 2 hours every time and the quizzes can be done in 10 minutes with the right slides opened.

Professor Curtis is by far one of the greatest professors I have had during my time at UMD. His class is pretty straightforward, and dynamic. If you show up to his lecture and do your work you should definitely get a good grade. Group project was the hardest thing all semester, other than that smooth sailing

Ignore the bad review, don't know what class they were in, but mine was the most lighthearted and easy course I had. 4 main projects, the first 3 of which only took me about 2 hours to complete, I got 100's. Quizzes are all from uploaded powerpoints. He's just a fun, kind, knowledgable guy, whole class likes him. He loved talking to us.

Dr. Curtis is a respected man in his field and he is very educated but he is a very mean spirited person and will not help students in any way. By far the worst professor I've had at UMD. He has zero respect for his students and treats us like middle schoolers. He's a bad teacher, not engaging and I didn't learn anything. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Crawford is a harsh grader, gives unclear feedback, and doesn't have clear lessons. Please consider other english professors before taking her class.

I really thought that ENGL101 was going to be no problem but Professor Crawford made it a million times more difficult than it needed to be. The assignments and the rubric were always so unclear and she would change things up on us constantly. Her grading was all over the place and it was impossible to know what she wanted from you.
You will have a lot of writing assignments so be prepared to write.  She gives good feedback and encourages class feedback which helps a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: She's annoying and the class is a drag. It is not too hard but it feels like she doesn't have any teaching material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Crawford was an extremely nice lady. She was never rude and was very mellow. However, she was a very tough grader. I am used to getting A's in english classes, but she rarely gave out A's on big assignments, and her feedback was never the best. She was pretty chill about being absent though.

Professor Crawford is such a nice lady! I feel like I have actually learned something and improved my writing in this class. However, she is a very tough grader. The highest grades given for major assignments are usually a 95%, and you don't get much feedback about what you did wrong. Also, the class says you need a textbook, but you don't really.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Nice

Professor Crawford is a very solid choice for your professional writing credit. For every major assignment we review student examples and participate in at least one round of feedback. Every assignment builds toward the final paper, which makes it easier. She did a great job with online classes in fall 2020. Also a very nice person!

Super sweet professor! If you are stressed, just tell her, and she will give you an extension! Overall, grading is a little harsh for a 100 level English class, and there are just a lot of assignments over the semester, so make sure you are on top of your work. I would say my writing skills really improved from the beginning of the semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: A sweet lady and even learns your name! She grades fairly and expects you to put work in your papers -thesis and topic sentences are important. A lot of the class time is used to peer review or ask questions on the assignments. She gives good guides for each paper and resources. She makes you work through your questions and feedback can be vague.

She's a super sweet lady, but lacks in giving enough feedback to help her student's improve. If English is not your favorite subject I would not go with her. She does provide many helpful resources to write essays, but not the easiest grader.

Nice professor but makes you work exceptionally hard for good grades. It is a non-stop grind on writing. She also did not provide good feedback. On one of my papers, she said it was "very good" and I made some of her edits and got a C- on it. She also runs class as if we are clueless preschoolers. However, I think she tough us some things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 95% of class time is pointless. I can honestly say I have not learned a thing this year. Her grading is crazy harsh and she does not always give the easiest feedback to revise to. She is Impossible to please. Overall, I did not grow at all as an English student and do not recommend this professor. I feel like I am treated not as a college student.

She is a tough grader and gives more work than others. But as long as you put in the work for this class, you will get a reasonable grade. She is a great professor! This professor is accessible when you need her and will give descriptive feedback on your papers. I do not consider myself as an English advocate
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not a bad choice. Makes you work for your grade and academic papers seemed to be averaging around the 85% range. Makes you work for your grade but really tries to make an emphasis on the learning process of academic writing! Would not consider her to be an "easy A" but I learned some lessons. Discussions every week helped boost grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is AMAZING. It's true that she does give a lot of work, but it is manageable as long as you're organized. She also cares a lot, so if you go talk to her when you are having issues she is very willing to help. If you put in a little effort, you'll be able to get an A.

Professor Crawford is a very nice individual who has the potentially to really help you with your writing. However, she assigns more assignments than some of the other English professors, and rarely pushes back deadlines which are really difficult to meet if you have a lot of work from other class. Also, her grading is super unreasonable sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: No matter how hard you try in the class expect a B on every assignment because she doesnt care to give As. Even if you go to office hours and she see you are working hard, she will still grade so harshly.

Professor Crawford is a good teacher, but the amount of work she gives for a ENGL101 course is heavy. Others who also take ENGL101 have said they don't get as much work and at a slower pace. If you take this class you can expect to get a paper due every 1.5 weeks, and written homework 2-3x a week. She is also not a particularly easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Crawford is a great professor and really cares about the subject she's teaching. She's very approachable and nice, and gives reasonable grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: A real gem. Professor Crawford is really kind and caring. You have to work for a good grade somewhat more than in other classes, but it is totally worth it. She loves group discussion as well. The textbook is definitely referred to but is not totally necessary.
Great and Understanding Professor
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Nice guy, but he uses prerecorded lectures and doesn't really teach. Everything is online. He's also a super harsh grader. Make sure you follow the writing guidelines he posted exactly.
he's terrible... doesn't offer any help or guidance for exams. everything is just carried over from previous semesters, he doesn't do any teaching, AVOID AT ALL COSTS

Work professor I've ever had, you have been warned!!!!! The class should not have been this difficult. The professor has everything premade from previous semesters and doesn't do any teaching. He doesn't offer any help, office hours, or communication. For every elms quiz and exam you're not allowed to move between questions. Very harsh grader too!!

Hands down worst professor Ive ever had. Doesnt teach. No TA. No office hrs. Uses pre made lectures that are very short and only cover a fraction of the material. Quizzes every week are based on reading 60+ pages of extremely dense text per week. You are only allowed 1 minute per question and no going back to change answers after you pick one.

He assigns 5 question quizzes with a 5 min time limit, each based on book chapters that are around 60-80 PAGES LONG. Once you submit an answer to a single question, you can't go back. He puts stuff on exams he barely teaches AND doesn't curve. AVOID THIS COURSE, you're better off just buying the textbook and reading it yourself honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor refused to meet in person because it was online. I typically get As in biology classes, and I will probably end up with a C. He is a SUPER harsh grader, and will dock you 25% for something small. Emailed him asking for help and he told me to just continue what i was doing, despite getting 50s on every quiz. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!

If you're a conceptual Artist and want to take this class in order to progress in your art journey. Take the class but not with him. He is very so/so about his overall teaching style. He does not push you/constantly complains about being a part time teacher and disliking the class as well. Assignments are basics from a textbook and lack passion!

Please take any of his classes! He is extremely nice, understanding, and knows what he is doing. He walks around and gives great feedback as needed. Show up on time with an open mind and he will see your effort. We never had work outside of class as long as we showed up and had something to upload by the due date. I definitely improved by the end!

Professor Cullen was such a great guy. Very understanding and willing to give extensions, even last minute. Genuinely cares about his students and gives helpful feedback on projects. Really don't have to be an amazing artist at all, just put some effort and creativity into your work and you'll be fine. Highly recommend!

He is an amazing professor who genuinely cares so much about his students. He began class asking everyone one good thing about our week and one bad thing and he actually wanted to know and cared. He was very understanding and always willing to grant extensions. Just a quality guy. As long as you put effort into your drawings you will do just fine.

Peter is a super chill and patient guy. I took ARTT100 with him the semester that we transitioned into online and he handled it well. As long as you finish your assignments and participate a little you will get a good grade. I am not the best artist but he gives good feedback and was never condescending.

This was my first ever government class, and, even though I hated the material, I loved the class bc Cunningham is such a great dude. Doesn't act like a scary professor; he's just a dude who really really likes international conflict theory. Would recommend to anyone. Easy assignments, but lots of reading (not necessary to pass). 4 essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class was one of the nicest classes I have ever had. This is really heavy with the readings and papers but is very doable. He is so kind and actually cares about his students, when I had 5 projects to do in 3 days he let me get a week's extension. This man is so knowledgeable and such a good discussion leader. Phenomenal. 5/5 would take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Cunningham not only is passionate and knowledgeable about the course content, but also genuinely cares for his students. Class readings can be dense but talking about it in breakout rooms with classmates helps to understand them.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Cunningham was the sweetest Prof. I've had at UMD. He's so caring. I had him for Spring 2020, unfortunately during the COVID-19 pandemic. He was very accommodating and really tried to make us feel comfortable and less stressed during this crazy time. Before class went online, his in-person lectures were very clear. He is a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: It is very hard to fail her class. I had her freshman year fall 2023 semester, and I enjoyed the class discussions we had. She's also great at engaging her class. If I could go back, I'd 100% take RUSS287 again.

Although I'm pretty sure that this course is now called RUSS287, it was still an easy A. However, make sure that you carefully read a few of the articles Professor Martin assigns for the homework as the two graded reflections and final (which are all written and submitted online) will require you to have in-depth knowledge of certain topics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: The class was an I-series so there weren't many assignments. The class was many a giant group lecture and sometimes the conversation was all over the place, but it was interesting none the less. There wasn't much homework and no tests or quizzes, just a few in-class reflections. Super easy class, even though it may be boring at some times.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took RUSS282 in Spring 2016, but I really enjoyed this class! This class was mainly discussion about various aspects of Russian culture. We had weekly assignments that we had to submit online. Dr. Martin is such a great, caring, and understanding professor - I would definitely recommend this class to anyone.

Best prof I have ever had! She puts so much effort into really helping her students understand the language and culture. She is understanding and strives to promote learning and ensures you take as much away from her courses as possible. Definitely recommend any of her courses, she is beyond fair and understanding when it comes to grading.

One of the best professors in the school. Unlike professors in so many other departments, she really cares that you learn instead of just get As. She makes sure everyone understands and really tries to not make you feel pressured. The best part is that you do learn, a whole lot. Fantastic class.

LOVE this teacher! I have a bad history with Russian professors at my old schools, and I was really considering giving up on my goal of fluency. She is not a native Russian speaker, so she is really good at explaining things to native English speakers. She emphasizes the great importance of learning over performing well on tests. PLEASE TAKE THIS!
AMAZING!

Amazing teacher. She treats her students like adults and does not grade very hard. Great for core because it covers Diversity. You learn very little about the language but you wont be tested on it. She is very passionate and sincere. She's a very fair teacher who looks out for the best interest of her students. Definately take this class
Just an amazing professor overall! Highly recommended.

Great Teacher. Honest with students, not worried about grades but making sure that you actually take something from the class. She is very fair and understanding if something comes up and interferes with work. TAKE THIS CLASS for CORE

Very nice.  Very helpful.  Definitely knows what she is talking about.  Has realistic student expectations. She really just wants you to get interested in the culture.  Makes you think and kind of makes you not like the US.
She is incredibly helpful and wants everyone to do well. She doesn't really believe in bad grades if you try hard. Cares more about what you're learning than how well you take a test! Great Prof!

Just a really really nice person, she's like everyone's mom. She doesn't give out a lot of work and gives out I think almost all A's but is still a great teacher. She's obviously passionate about her subject and is good at explaining that pesky Russian grammar. Recommended.

Out of all the prof writing professors she's the best. Class was straight-forward, took it online. I actually found some of the assignments quite useful. Rubrics were clear. Discussions posts here and there. There's not too much reading at all. If you try at all you should get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Professor Cuffy was a great pick for ENGL101. She's clear on what she expects for the assignments and keeps the class interesting. She also picks a variety of readings and videos to watch to keep the class engaged. There are a lot of group discussions with your classmates. She can be a tough grader but she's really nice.

Professor Cuffy is probably one of the best English professors I have ever had. She does a great job keeping the class engaged. All the readings were very current and interesting. She gives great feedback on written assignments and will work with you when you are struggling. Be ready to talk with people around you and discuss the readings.

Great prof! As long as you communicate any issues, she will help you as much as she can. She can grade the essays a bit hard for it being a 101 class too. Attendance and participation is mandatory (worth 100pts) but she defines participation differently (not just talking in class). Readings are only articles that she provides.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Cuffy is honestly such a great professor. She cares a lot about her students and is a very thorough teacher. She gives an average amount of work and it is not very difficult to complete, as long as you manage your time well. She explains all of her assignments well in detail, and grades fairly. Also she has really pretty handwriting.

Best English teacher I've ever had. Her class was interesting and she kept all readings current and up to date. Come to class, participate, and do your assignments and you will do well. She incorporates a ton of cool Ted Talks to watch throughout class and for homework. Be ready to talk to people around you. This wasn't a boring English class!

Didn't like her at first bc she took forever to grade even though we only have 6 assignments that count towards our grade. Fair grader and if you pay attention to what she talks about in class you'll be fine. Flexible with stuff like word count/page length. One 8-10 page essay and final is a ted talk. Great teacher overall and I don't like English.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: simply amazing. she really cares for her students, is passionate about english and sharing interesting texts, and provides great feedback and grades extremely fair. would definitely recommend her!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I enjoyed ENGL101S with Professor Cuffy. My favorite assignment was the TED Talk. She is very nice and is accessible outside of class.

Hands down the best ENGL101 professor at UMD! Professor Cuffy's class was manageable with weekly readings and 3 essays. She's a fairly easy grader as long as you put effort, you'll be rewarded. One thing I love is that she exposes us to so many different types of texts. She gives great feedback and is willing to help students.
There are no real rubrics for the essays, but she makes her expectations pretty clear.

I agree with the past few comments. Definitely caring, and wants you to do well / be creative. She is very easy to talk to and very amicable. I hated English classes before I took her, but this class was great! I learned a lot! Make sure you participate and always give your best effort, and your grade will certainly reflect that. Take her class!!

Professor Cuffy is very approachable and easy to talk to. You can tell she really cares about her students. Sometimes assignments are a little unclear, but she's always open for questions or even office hours. Not too hard, but you do have weekly work due each Friday and 3 big papers.
She's very nice and a pretty good teacher. We go over many different readings, and she seems to care about her students.

prof. cuffy is an amazing human being. she exposed us to many different kinds of texts. she grades pretty easily and fairly, and your grade is based on the effort you put in. make sure you participate. she made engl101 enjoyable and manageable.

she's very well-spoken and professional. she exposed us to a diverse array of texts. typical english class of 4-5 "major" papers, and the rest some tiny participation/reflection points. she is a fairly easy grader and as long as you do not procrastinate too much, this class is a breeze. she is a wonderful professor.

I took her Writ101 class at AU! She's a very nice and understanding teacher and classes are painless to sit through. She grades pretty easily so if you have basic writing skills you should get an A on the assignments. As long you participate in class she'll like you and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Cuffy is super sweet and really cares about her students. She gives you one extension on a paper of your choice, no questions asked. Participation matters so definitely speak up. She grades pretty fairly so put the work in the class and you'll do well.

Super nice professor, she grades based off the amount of work you put in so most people in my class thought they got a fair grade, nobody really complained. Has an issue with explaining assignments and what is expected, but nothing a simple question wont fix. She's super understanding about personal situations and will help you out if you seek help
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Cuffy is a nice person and cares about her students. However, when I asked her for any extra opportunities to bump up my grade to the next letter grade, she proceeded to tell me that I was .1 away from being able to round it up. Ouch. I even did both the extra credits she provided already, so those felt like a waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: ENGL101 is supposed to be an introductory course to academic writing. Instead of taking the time to learn how to write academically, I was only worried about the grades I would receive. Professor Cuffy is a very tough grader. You have to work very diligently in order to do good. I go to the writing lab for every paper and only manage to getB orless
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: For a  prof. Who does not speak Spanish, she has done a good job in her writings on feminism. She needs to feed the subject because it is important for her personal affairs.
A lot of interesting material but prof. is disorganized; you can't follow lectures cz she goes from one topic to another. Terrible Spanish; not a model of what I want to sound like when I graduate.

I don't think she is a good professor. She lost my test and never mentioned about my test. Also, she uses her blackboard a lot but the notes she writes are very disorganized. So, there is no point of looking at the blackboard, you have to write down whatever she says. Last thing,be aware that Spanish teachers talk to each other about their students

Doctora Cypess is amazing!  I don't understand how anyone can't like her.  She really enjoys the students and what she teaches and that makes her classes fun.  She is very clear and helpful and she knows so much.  She is very encouraging.  If I ever get the chance to take her again, I won't turn it down.
No Comments

She's a very nice lady, but she does not know how to teach. We had one assignment the entire semester before the final paper and exam were due. She was not clear at all about the paper requirements. The Final itself did not have many questions concerning the architecture of DC, but included obscure history questions from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's sweet and all but not a good professor. The quizzes don't match the textbook. The grading criteria isn't clear AT ALL; there is a HUGE communication gap. The TAs weren't helpful. This was the most disorganized class of my life.

She seems like a nice lady but this class is completely disorganized. Posts the wrong information online, does not give clear instructions, and constantly tinkers with quizzes so you never know how to study. Lectures are lonnnnggg and boring on a subject that I (used to) find really interesting.

I love Cy. My favorite professor at UMD so far, it is really worth participating and getting to know him. He has really great insight and exhibits his art which is really cool. Hes a bit shy at first, but when you get to know him he is hilarious and very kind. Will always give extensions if you ask him (especially in person).

He pretends to be cool and organized but he is not. He says one thing and does another. Lectures unhelpful and disorganized. He had no interest in teaching the class but expected something amazing from students. Don't waste your time looking for his help. He was never at his office during his office hours mentioned on the syllabus.
Cy is an absolute legend. One of the nicest and coolest professors at UMD, and he is super knowledgeable. I highly recommend taking classes with Cy, and try to learn as much as you can from him.
He can be a tough grader, but is specific about grading criteria and will guide you in the right direction. Expect to put in a lot of work, but attendance is usually not mandatory.
Nice professor, but lectures are incredibly boring. Very hard to focus. Does not make the material interesting at all.

Do NOT take as an elective. Do the homework, memorize the terms from the book, and do the extra credit...she's liberal with the extra credit...and you'll be okay (as in a C or B). Unlimited tries on online homework and extra credit quizzes!!!

she is a good teacher but the subject matter can be tedious. she is very nice and willing to help during office hours. No curve but if you need one in her class you are an idiot because homework is 25% of your grade and you can answer questions unlimited times. just get around the average on tests (75%) and you'll get a b in the class.

did not enjoy the class. She speaks in a monotone... ALWAYS. TAs were not helpful. I had to drop the class and re take it with another professor. Does not curve, and a lot of homework is assigned. Subject matter is uninteresting as well!! overall horrible experience!!
Not an easy class, but if you put in the work you will be fine. Tests aren't easy but homework is 25% of the grade so its an easy way to get it up. Also extra credit is available and really helps

If you want a curve, do not take her. SHE DOES NOT CURVE. I REPEAT, SHE DOES NOT CURVE. I got a D in her class and have to re-take ECON, her exams were difficult and the TAs were useless. HW was tedious but not that hard.

I actually learned something from econ. Would not take it as an elective. I was surprised when I managed an A in the class because I did poorly on the first exam, but I did make up for that a bit with the other grades. I went to the 1st discussion, then the room got moved and I did not know where they met, so going is useless. Aplia sucks a lot

Lots of homework!  You will frequently have assignments due online based on the textbook readings.  They aren't hard; it just gets tedious.  She posts the slides from lectures online, which helps if you have trouble waking up in the morning.

You do not need to go to class-all the work is from the textbook + she posts her lecture slides online.Lots of hw from aplia,DO NOT MISS ANY!All of work is from textbook, so make sure to read it. Lastly,make so to use multiple resources to study for exam.Personally, I went over my textbook notes,then lecture slides, then review cards that she makes

Lectures are boring and pointless. Tests aren't bad, just study the book, but the homework is ridiculous and worth almost a quarter of your grade. She doesn't write the questions (Aplia does it) so lecture doesn't help with the homework at all. The questions are also much harder than anything in lecture, so you'll end up teaching yourself a lot.

she's nice, but this class was not easy.  the aplia hw was harder than her teaching level, she admitted that.  the final was SOOO hard and there wasn't a curve, it dropped me from a B to a C+. i read the chapters to study, it def wasn't enough.  lecture was very boring, she puts her ppts online.

Dr. Clement is an awsome teacher.  Her lesson plans are very straight forward and to the point. I could have studied harder for the exams, because she tells you everything that you need to know and what is going to be on the exams. Take this class, it's at 8 am, but I think it's worth it. Exams are based on class notes, so its better to go.

I'd recommend not even attending lecture, read the slides online, read the chapter, and do the hw and your set. tests are okay, she tries to throw in very wordy questions to confuse you. very dry, boring lecture, just annotates the slides  word for word.
Dont go to class, her lecture slides are available online and they just annotate directly from the book,so if you read the chapter you've just done the lecture. Tests are ok, not too bad.

if you have to take macro, take it with clement. i recommend not even attending lectures, just study the book on your own. discussion is not mandatory.. and not helpful either.study the chapters and know the basic knowledge, and you will do very well on the exams. if i had put one ounce of effort in the class,i would have gotten an A instead of a B
She computes the grade slowly. She's good but her TA's arent.

She is reasonably nice. She is pretty firm on NOT curving. If you look hard enough you can find her powerpoints on the textbook's website. You do have to read the textbook and understand the graphs, but I assume she is better than some other professors. The worse thing is that she takes FOREVER to grade things (the final took her almost one month)!

She is very nice. There is a lot of material to cover in the class so do your reading or you will be lost- unless you are a Macro genius. She writes a lot on slides and goes very fast in class so you will have a cramp in your hand if you try to write everything. It takes her forever to post grades.

I had a lot of issues with the way this class was structured. He is clearly passionate about the concepts in the class, however his lectures don't quite prepare you for the homeworks or exams. Little time was used in class for examples or applications, which is what was needed to succeed, given the homeworks and exams are what is graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I regret taking him so much.  Once you make a numerical error on an exam, TA's are instructed to stop grading and mark you off for the rest of your hardwork on exams.  This class really made me depressed.  I felt like the TAs and professor really wanted me to fail, which doesn't help with my natural anxiety and stress from school.  Avoid him 100%.

You will not regret taking Professor Czaja's class. It will need a lot of hard work on your end, but his lectures are very clear and he is very helpful. As long as you put effort during the semester, you are very likely to pass the course. Pair him with a decent TA then your chances of passing gets even higher. You will not regret taking his course

Prof Czaja is an okay prof. His exams and quizzes are fairly easy, but I hated his teaching style. He spent half the class wiping the board. Assignments: 3 exams (drops lowest), 27 hw's (drops 7), 7 quizzes (drops 2), and the final. His grading scale is on a curve (a 60 is a C).

He is a great teacher. He explains everything really clearly. I'm a bit OCD so I like the way he erases the board too. The final (written by Hamilton) was really difficult (MUCH harder than the 3 finals from previous semesters) and that dropped me from a mid to high A to B.

PROBABLY ONE OF THE BEST MATH PROFESSORS YOU WILL EVER HAVE... hes like really helpful during office hours if you dont get it in lecture and its rare that you dont. hes also a nice guy he isnt some professor lost in his work, he knows people. and he sounds like arnold schwartsineger.
HE IS A VERY GOOD TEACHER. HIS LECTURES ARE EXTREMELY HELPFUL. HE IS LENIENT IN GRADING. HE HAS A GOOD SENSE OF HUMOR

He is a good teacher and don't be alarmed if all you do in class are proofs b.c that's normal. He drops 2 quizzes, 3 hws (from online) and 1 test. He is helpful from the fact he gives a prac test b4 an exam which is almost alike. He gives lots of prac that will be on the final. from easiest to hardest: test -> quiz -> webassign. good class overall.

Czaja is a good guy. Explains everything pretty well, funny at times (delivered in a very dead pan manner, which makes it more hilarious), and tests are generally easier than other 141 professors. Rarely a few subjects won't be taught in class that you'll need to know for your homework--you'll find it in the book.

Good sense of humor. Easily better than other 141 teachers like Johnson and Rosenberg. If you can take this class with Czaja, I would highly advise you take this class with him. Quizzes fair, and very helpful. Has an accent, but not too strong, lectures crystal clear.

ARHU 230 with Professor Richter was very interesting. There was a lot of emphasis on film and watching movies, but I liked the course's format. The assignments were unique and the lectures were generally entertaining and short.

I took ARHU 230 with Dr. Richter this summer and the course was incredibly interesting. It was probably the most well-configured course I've taken at UMD and I would highly recommend him.  He told me he primary teaches in film studies and I plan to take a class with him there.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Disaster Cinema is a cool class with lots of fun movies. The professor tries to create a good environment on Zoom for everyone to participate. He did provide good feedback on a couple of drafts, but he's definitely also not the easiest grader. Do recommend but you need to be ready to do a lot of writing.

Migration Cinema was definitely an engaging class although it required a lot more work than I expected. Professor Richter worked with me to revise all of my papers and also helped me to understand the themes better by meeting with him. Do recommend, but plan to spend several hours a week watching films!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take him! You have 3 papers to write but the essay prompts were 1 short incomplete sentence, left up for interpretation but grades very harshly. He will tell you the deadlines are rolling deadlines but will penalize you for submitting it before the last day of class. Very rude when you ask for clarification on grades! No Rubric provided!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Daniel Richter is one of the best professors at UMD. I have taken several classes with him and they have all been extremely interesting. He is also very helpful with feedback but definitely prefers to talk to students than just respond to email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Latin American Cinema with Dr. Richter and thought it was an outstanding course. The online lectures were all excellent and he gave me very helpful feedback on the draft I sent. He's a very nice person and highly recommend him for film studies majors.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I would recommend Prof. Richter's Latin America film class especially if you want to learn more Latin American history.  We watched a lot of movies and I liked most of them. The discussons were usually pretty good and I thought the professor was pretty good with feedback albeit a little slow.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you want to take the most confusing class ever, take the class with Daniel Ritcher. His syllabus is the most unclear syllabus that I ever saw. he is not helpful and not available to answer questions at all. He doesn't give you any feedback and grade to let you keep track of your work until the end of the semester. He doesn't have any rubric.

Dr. Richter's Latin American cinema class was my most interesting class at UMD. I personally had a very positive experience since he gave constructive feedback on drafts and was very accessible in meeting with me after class. The Zoom classes were usually good, but I liked the ones most where he shared additional content. Highly recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Richter's Sports in Cinema class has been my favorite Film Studies class at UMD. I've liked almost all the films and the readings are mostly interesting. The online disccussins are generally useful, although attendance isn't mandatory so attendance is pretty up and down. I'd recommend the class as a cool elective.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Profesor Richter's Disaster Film course had a bunch of great movies and I definitely learned a lot about the disaster genre. The course felt more like a history course at times but he explained how that was his intention. The online format worked well enough and he was very helpful with the papers when I asked to meet him. I would recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Pretty underwhelming, treading water-ish. He didn't have us watch ANY scenes during class time (I don't expect full movies to be shown in class), so discussion fell flat. Not sure what he was looking for in the "scene analyses' since there was no rubric. We learned nothing of film techniques, camera work, mise-en-scene or anything related to film.

His class was lecture heavy but a cool professor. Be ready to read multiple books and watch multiple documentaries. He really wants you to pass so he'll work with you. Pay attention in lecture, that'll help if you don't read. Sometimes rambles and late with grading but I appreciated the late grading for emergency extensions. I recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hate romero so much. He grades based of how he feels. Dosent have a rubric. Had no patience. Dosent know how to teach or the topic he is teaching. They should have a a max age professors can teach at because of this man

Dr. Romero is a really nice, easygoing guy, but he's not a good lecturer at all. His exams/assignments are somewhat difficult, but fair. However, he takes forever to grade exams, so you won't know your grade until way after the semester.

I took him for 380 &381. For 380 ,He went over basic concepts and made sure the formulas made sense & we are not just plugging in numbers in them. He moved hw & exams when students complained. Exams are very similar to hw. But for 381 I do not know what happened. He was very careless and just reads the power points out loud and that is mostly it!

He is a good prof. Remember, read his PPT carefully. All of exam questions from ppt and homework. He gave us 3 exam and 1final exam. He just chose two of the first three exams. Also, he would put all Discussion questions on canvas
He is a good prof. Remember, read his PPT carefully. All of exam questions from ppt and homework. He gave us 3 exam and 1final exam. He just chose two of the first three exams.

Horrible Professor.  Clearly knowledgeable but cannot teach and does not care about students learning material.  Frequent errors in distributed exams and homework assignments, and is only accessible infrequently by e-mail.  Lectures are long, uninteresting, and full of poor explanations.  Would not recommend.

I'm not sure what changed in him but he was once a kind professor. Now, he comes off as avoidant and goes out of his way to ignore or avoid former students at networking events. It's disappointing to see in a field where annual networking is encouraged. It dampens my pride in being a UMD larc graduate when the people who taught you no longer care.

I actually had Professor Myers for INAG106 and was nervous for the class since I know nothing of pesticides but he makes the content very easy to learn. There are lectures every week that you would benefit going to because he is very intelligent and talks about interesting stories from his career. Overall super smart kind teacher.

I took Dr. Myers for an online LARC152 class. Dr. Myers was very kind and it was clear he cared a lot about the course. His questions were always straightforward and he was clear on what to know for the test. Great guy.

To be completely honest, this class was super boring to me because I don't exactly care too much about environmental studies. However, for what it's worth, Dr. Myers is an incredible teacher, and I certainly learned a lot whether I enjoyed the material or not. Super straightforward, and interesting (if it's your thing).
Jess is nice

This is a relatively simple class- if you watch lecture and skim the book, you'll be fine. Dr. Deitzer is straightforward and gives interesting lectures. There are weekly discussion posts, 3 exams (1 dropped), and a paper. The workload isn't so much, and you'll learn a lot. Dr. Deitzer cares about student feedback and incorporates it into class.

Her teaching ability is sub-par. She seems to lack knowledge/practical experience in the topic she teaches. She grades fairly harshly on tests and essentially tries to overload you with information from her lectures that dont even apply to the exams. Recommend finding a different professor for the corrections course.

This was a very interesting class with a very nice and enthusiastic teacher. It was obvious that Jessica knew what she was talking about and she did not just read off the slides like many other professors. As long as you do the readings and go to class you will not have a problem. The three pop quizzes were easy and acted as a grade boost.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's terrible. Don't take this class. The content is so subjective that questions fall in a grey area and are worsened by parenthetical attempts to elaborate (which are grammatically incorrect). Course has the potential to be useful and straightforward, but it's subverted by her inability to communicate in a way that's clear, concise, and normal.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Due to family issues which I expressed, I missed a few classes at the beginning of the semester. She then continued to put me down the rest of the semester because of my missed classes. She once spammed me over email and called me three times leaving long voicemails when I didn't come to class one day later in the semester. Severely inappropriate.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best professor ever!! Honestly, the most responsive professor I have had and the exams were straight-forward as long as you studied/did the work. She really wants you to succeed and is passionate about the course. The syllabus itself is long because it serves as a study guide for exams and she is very clear about how to be successful.

Professor Shapiro is a very nice woman, but teaches a very useful and straightforward concept-filled class in the most convoluted way possible. She types like she is speaking, which leads to slides, exams, and quizzes all full of grammatically incorrect sentences that are horribly confusing. Her exams are near impossible, no matter what  you study.

Professor Shapiro was one of the best and most caring professors I have had. She is really responsive to emails, teaches the materials well, and wants students to succeed.

The major class work consists of a few group projects and tests. The projects are not too bad, but the tests can be difficult.

Professor Shapiro is a very nice lady who truly cares about students learning. This class was difficult not because of the content but her overcomplication of things. I would read all the cases, never missed a class, and studied hard for the exams and got a grade I was not happy with. The exam questions are very difficult to understand.

Professor Debra is a sweet professor. However her class is unorganized and poorly structured. She had a syllabus that consisted of 40 plus pages which was frustrating. Her exams are insanely hard and the curve was very minimal. You actually have read each article carefully otherwise you will not be successful in this class. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Shapiro's class is very complicated. It is complicated in the form that the syllabus is all over the place, 43 pages long. She has handouts in almost every class. MAKE SURE TO READ. If not, you will be lost for almost everything and not be successful on the exams and pop quizzes that are in almost every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Enthusiastic professor who made herself available to help students at nearly all hours of the day. Course was well organized, predictable, & engaging. Professor made it a point to know all students by first name & personally acknowledge them. Very friendly & personable. Course concepts relevant to the real world & explained thoroughly.

Nice woman but class is not good. Content, group projects, and quizzes are easy but then exams are so hard for no reason and basically impossible to study for unless you can memorize specific details about multiple readings. Has a weird way of organizing and explaining assignments and you have to email assignments instead of uploading to canvas.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Debra is very passionate about her class and she is always available outside of class via phone for help. Her 2nd and final exam were very hard and did not correlate to the study guide provided. every class has a pop quiz based on the reading due that day. 2 group projects and 2 individual papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Based on the reviews, I thought this was class was going to be fine and not too bad. BUT, you really have to READ ALL the articles the professor provides THOROUGHLY because that will help you when taking the "pop quizzes" she gives. Study for the exams and make to read and understand. The exams aren't something you can just not study for and ace.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She truly cares about her students and their success. There are several case readings that you MUST read because there are pop quizzes. Exams are pretty straight forward and she even provides a study guide. There is exam review the class before each exam. The content she teaches is very interesting and useful. Overall, great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is absolutely amazing. So kind and funny, she really cares about her students. The pop quizzes are on the readings, so make sure you're keeping up with them. Participation matters a lot for this class but it's so interesting. 10/10 would take another class with her.

Very nice lady who really cares. Doesn't use a textbook, uses several case studies and articles. Class is discussion based so its important to do the readings. She's a bit all over the place but well meaning and passionate about the subject matter. As the subject matter isn't black and white there can be some ambiguity on tests and pop quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Very nice lady and very energetic. You learn and a lot and she loves what she does. Go to class, and you have to read everything in order to pass the midterm.
Dr Shapiro was very professional and I very much enjoyed her class.
very sweet, nice lady. must go to class and must participate. she really wants her students to do well

His lectures put people to sleep, and the group discussion was the only engaging thing. I have a B because of the midterm. He wanted us to do the readings but never told us. Plus the readings are 20 pages long and there are a lot of them. If you read the readings then you will do well on the midterm and ensure an A in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Iwamoto is quite passionate about what he teaches. Definitely schedule a meeting with him since its 1% extra credit and he has great advice. There's 1 midterm, 1 quiz, and no final, but there is a group presentation worth a good chunk, and a scientific analysis toward the end. Wasn't my personal favorite since it was lecture heavy. Still good.

Dr. Iwamoto uses this class to introduce many of the issues AA experience. However, he likes to use his own research, many of which were conducted in the 2000s, which lacks more recent analysis of the AA population. He also lacks explicit rubrics for written assignments but still implicitly wants students to share more personal experiences.

I found the class enjoyable and interesting as more light is needed on Asian American issues. Class is about half and half lectures and group discussions. These class discussions and weekly discussion assignments were good for hearing about other people's experiences and self reflection. The readings assigned can be a bit much.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: While he can be passive-aggressive at times, he was a solid professor. My only recommendations are to regularly check the syllabus because he will not give you reminders on upcoming assignments and show up to class because he'll do surprise in class assignments. Overall though his class is pretty manageable in terms of workload.

He is such an amazing professor. He really cares about his students and wants them to learn the material. He doesn't make it unnecessarily hard by any means, and doesn't stack up the work. I HIGHLY recommend.
One of my fav professors - one of the kindest people. Class inspirational and insightful. Could not recommend prof or the class more!

Iwamoto gives an extremely engaging lecture and is fair and balanced. Talk in class and pay attention to lectures and you should do fine. He gives an average about of work and is a fair grader. He completely lays out what to expect on the tests. Definitely take him.

Dr. Iwamoto was one of the most arrogant professors I have ever had. He would give us some assignments with little to no explanation and is terrible at responding to emails (and is condescending when you ask for clarity). Go to class or else he'll hold a grudge against you the entire semester. Do NOT recommend him.

Grades harshly. I Correct what he recommends makes no difference in his grading rubric. He Doesn't lecture. Posts learning resources from other authors that im capable of finding on my own without him. He posts nothing original. He never engages in discussion posts. He expects students to do this to each other. Taking his course was regrettable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!! THIS MAN WILL MESS YOUR GPA ALL THE WAY UP. HE IS A DIFFICULT GRADER.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: There is A LOT of reading. I read more in this class than my English class. He will pick on everyone to make sure you've done the readings. Learns names early on. Does not test on big picture things. He finds topics/people that may have been mentioned only once to test students on. You will do three oral presentations and two papers.
worst teacher ever DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!

The class I had him for was black culture. He required that we have a total of 4 textbooks in the class & we usually read 50 or more pages a night along with other readings. The class was pretty lame. I didn't feel like I actually learned anything. He usually spent each class asking us questions about what we read & occasinaly showed us a video.

Dr. Denise's passion for teaching and genuine care for her students is unmatched. She created a welcoming and supportive environment, making every session feel like a breath of fresh air. She helped me develop a love for communication. If you have the chance to take her class, don't hesitate, you won't regret it
Dr. Denise was by far my favorite professor here at UMGC.

Received a good grade in that class, but boy do not take this in conjunction with another. She will keep you busy. Assignments are grades to the T following the rubric. Like, seriously don't mess up or your grade will drop. Theres multiple quizzes and discussions a week PLUS millions of pages of reading. Just follow rubrics. That's all I can say.

There are at least 2+ discussions per week. Few assignments and projects. It's an easy class. She provides feedback and is responsive by email, but it's clear that she doesn't really care about her students. Follow the rubric and you'll be set.

Took SPCH324 online with her. Takes forever to post grades. 3 very detailed projects w/3,500average words single space. 3-5 short quizzes each week, discussions are extensive with 3 parts each main topic (two topics) and min responses of two per topics. The class subject was interesting yet you find yourself too busy keeping up than enjoying it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Took her class online. Too much reading and discussion requirements. She grades tough, 3 main papers with very specific rubics. Each was about 3400 words for a decent grade. Discussions where overboard, she required two main discussions with three parts each plus two peer responses per discussion. the usual APA and outside resources requirements.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you are taking a speech class COMM108 please take this prof. In very short words she is awesome and very very understanding. You really cant go wrong with her. Do you speeches and you'll be ok. Passed with an "A" I think the whole class did.

Professor Meusa is amazing! She genuinely wanted everyone to succeed and gave real feedback to help you improve. Professor Meusa was would always give priceless suggestions and advice during class. Definitely a class you should take!

Professor Meusa is amazing! Did an excellent job keeping the class entertaining and was always there for the students. She genuinely wanted everyone to succeed and gave real feedback to help you improve. Professor Meusa was would always give priceless suggestions and advice during class. Definitely a class you should take!

She's enthusiastic, patient, kind, and brilliant.  What more could you want in a professor?  Take this class because you WILL learn how to become a better presenter and a more confident speaker.  She's my favorite professor and makes the class really fun.  She encourages you to form bonds with others in the class and really cares about her students
I'm glad I didnt take INAG because this professor was hilarious and entertaining. She also gave out food sometimes which is also a plus.
Grading criteria was unclear, material was also not clear. Good personality but teaching was not great.

I skimmed the readings, no quizzes, term paper was not too bad, a couple group projects/presentations. Overall I didn't find the class to be difficult, it was manageable work and easy.... if you put effort you'll get the grade you worked for.

classes were not on course topic, and halfway through the semester it was just guest speakers instead of learning anything. grading criteria was not always clear and expectations were high for the lack of material given. seems like a nice guy, but would probably do better teaching in a high school setting

This professor ran out of course content with about 2 months of the semester remaining. He now runs class with a different guest speaker every single class. His course needs to be revised and topics need to be added to avoid this.

Overall, loved his teaching method and lectures. He really knows what he's talking about so don't be afraid to ask questions! I think he was probably one of my favorite professors within my time in the iSchool. Just be aware that he does mark down whos in class, so show up and be on time. Also there's a lot of reading weekly for the homework.

You can tell he wants his students to succeed but this is sometimes hard to appreciate when you have AT LEAST 4 hours of homework every week sometimes double that. Each assignment is 1-2 points so each assignment holds a lot of weight. Overall amazing guy but don't overload ur semester if your'e taking this class. Easier if you like the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Frezzo was overall a great caring professor, he always wants his students to succeed and get good grades, he even gives extra credit. The only thing is he does assign a lot of work weekly which consist of packet tracers, labs, and homework. As long as you stay on top of your game in this class and start assignments early you will do good.

Professor has extensive knowledge of course content and cares about his student's success as he always makes himself available to help students. However, his homework questions can be confusing and unclear at times. Professor also assigns a lot of homework that is worth a small number of points.

As a senior in UMD, I have never been more grateful for a professor than Dr. Frezzo.He knows the class content like the back of his hand and his teaching reflects that. This class is pretty technical, but push through the assignments, and I promise you it'll pay off. Besides that, he's kind and sympathizes with outside of school circumstances.
Amazing professor!

Definitely the most hands-on professor I've had, always available via office hours and email. There are a LOT of low point HIGH work assignments, but he grades lightly. Plenty of extra credit opportunities, and was more than willing to go beyond the scope of teaching for students. Take this professor 100%!

Dr. Frezzo definitely knows his stuff. The workload can seem a bit much especially if you're new to IT but he's very lenient with deadlines. Quizzes are untimed and allow unlimited attempts. Most exam questions are identical to quizzes. If you know networking or have prior IT experience, this class will be a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This class was my most difficult class this semester but Professor Frezzo was really engaging. There were a lot of assignments due each week BUT he gives you an extension of 1 week with no late penalty! There is a lot of reading and assignments but Freezo was always there to help students when needed! Do the assignments ASAP so you're not behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: INST 346 is not an easy course but being in a class of Dr. Frezzo presents the opportunity to learn the material from one of the best technology teachers around. Dr. Frezzo is very knowledgeable and well organized; his support is also unwavering (you just need to ask), especially considering that this is an online class. Truly gifted professor.
super quiet do not expect to be able to hear at his lectures. If you can hear he's saying nonsense anyway.

Though Prof. Dolgopyat is not the best lecturer (he tends to either speak very low or very fast) he still makes sure that people get the material by providing an ample amount of examples and by going over them thoroughly. He is very helpful and doesn't play favorites. CLASS: 2 midterms (worth 50%) HW's and final each 25%. Easy A if you go to class.

There's no doubt that Dr. Dolgopyat knows this material well (and is flat out brilliant), but he is perhaps the worst lecturer I've ever seen.  His lessons are downright incomprehensible, his boardwork is all over the place and impossible to follow, and he refuses to look you in the eye when speaking (making him unapproachable).  Avoid if possible!
No Comments

Professor Dharma designed a well structured course that enables students with a minimal understanding of C to be able to decipher and perform binary exploits by reading assembly. The professor has extensive knowledge of the topic, is able to explain incredibly complex matters neatly and was always eager to provide more information & assistance.

He doesn't speak English very well so you may have to watch the lectures 2 or 3 times. If you are Indian (which seems like everyone in the department) you will probably understand him. Overall the class takes effort to actually study and attempt to apply the material. You can do well in the class if you really apply yourself.

Professor Ganesan makes the difficult seem easy. Don't know C? Don't know assembly? No problem. He'll teach you. No kidding there is a lot of material, but I've learned so so much. He'll answer any question in class, but relies on TAs outside of class. Seriously, you will learn tons. I've taken 2 classes from him and am taking my 3rd this fall.
He makes sure you know what you're doing and you will probably be able to work on it very easily afterwards

The professor was new to this subject. As a result he mixed the concepts and material of the previous professor, Jonathan Katz, a renowned name in cryptography, into his own. The course went unstructured midway, theory and history of cryptography was explained but very tough practical problems were presented. Should make Java a prerequisite.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The professor has clear understanding of the subject. He is able to effectively convey what he is teaching. He is confident in what he teaches and expects students to rise. I was well versed with C/C++, I still had to watch his lectures again because his lessons were simply 2-3 steps beyond what programmers learn. I wish to learn more under him.

The professor is very knowledgeable, kind and very eager to explain again and again in order to make sure everybody understands. Show up in class and keep asking questions until you get everything. Study a lot! Homework can be challenging and time consuming! Manage time well. This is not going to be easy but you will learn a lot.

Dr. Dharma is incredibly smart, but that doesn't always translate into an easily understood lecture. The first half of the semester was great - I spoke very highly of Dharma, the second was lackluster. Brush up on C before you take this course. This course demands a lot from you, take it by itself. Do NOT take online, show up to class in person.

This course was mandatory and there were no other options for professors. Awful experience, couldn't learn much. Good luck to people who don't already know what he's gonna teach because you won't learn much from him.

This class like every other thing in life. Youll only get what you put into it. If youre lazy and refuse to do the work, itll definitely be hard and complex for you. But if you put in the time and put your nose to the ground, you will learn a lot and succeed.

I cannot stress this enough for you, DO NOT TAKE THIS GUY. He thinks he is smartest guy on the planet and tries to show off by making exams super hard. His exams are impossible. Even if you study his lecture slides, homework, project, memorize all his video lectures you will barely pass. His lectures are useless as they are not related to exams
not great

Not a very good professor - just read off lecture slides. Gave overly confusing exams that didn't necessarily correlate to the material practiced on homework. Homework itself wasn't really bad, & the project for the class was somewhat challenging but interesting. Would say try to avoid, but there aren't really other options. Really study for exams!

Incredibly confusing class for being introductory, she goes way too in depth with very little explanation about what things are. Some concepts can be interesting but she makes it very hard to comprehend things because of the way she organizes her lectures. Would not recommend.

She waits until the end of the semester to grade everything which is extremely inconsiderate and unfair to students. On top of that her lectures are hard to understand because she dosnt do a good job describing information, instead she just throws a topic at you and expects you to understand it.

Very in depth for a 100 level class. Lectures were interesting, but not well organized. Many test questions dealt with offhand comments she made in lecture, but I took this course in spring '22 so it may have been reworked. I made 50 pages of notes (25 pages of writing) so email me (glvandoren@gmail) if you want them.

Not very responsive with her emails. She is very informative and I never thought that would be a problem until taking this course. She makes excuses, so be aware of exam grades being sent late. She was also judgemental of her students in plainsight. Fortunately, lecture recordings are on canvas and some topics are intriguing.

She is not a bad professor but her exams are extremely hard. If you do not attend lectures or watch them after she posts them, you will 100% fail the exams. There is no textbook for this class so your information comes solely from her. I sometimes feel like I am teaching myself. She is a nice professor but I would never take her class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Horrible at explaining things in lecture and so disorganized. Also, for a 100 level class, this class goes into way too much depth. Take another lab (AOSC201 or ASTR101 if you're interested in astronomy). Also VERY unresponsive to emails.
She's provides you with all the information needed and labs are pretty easy. She goes a little fast during lectures but most of her power point are posted online.

First of all for a level 100 class, this class goes WAY too in depth. Second, she's a terrible lecturer who repeats a lot of info and is super confusing. You're better off taking another lab if you want to fulfill your gen ed credit. The exams are online and open note but still confusing because you don't learn much from lecture.

(jsyk I'm in ASTR 100, idk why only ASTR340 is listed.) Dr. Diemer is great. Super chill guy, really interesting lectures, and more than willing to clarify and answer questions. Demos often explode. As a woman, I particularly appreciate him pointing out where women in astronomy have been robbed of/unfairly discredited for their work. Awesome prof!
Simply the best ever.

Generally an effective professor. Taught concepts in astrophysics pretty well in the fields of general relativity, electrodynamics, and particle dynamics. Homework was definitely on the more difficult and busier side, but the professor does a great job in explaining concepts to you during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
The weekly quizzes are free points, and the best part is that there is no final exam!
Overall, if you're interested in data science, I highly recommend taking Professor John. The course is challenging, but with his support, I was able to learn so much and feel confident in my abilities. Thank you, Professor John, for being such an amazing teacher!

EXCELLENT PROFESSOR!! Weekly quizzes are pass/fail (free points) and THERES NO FINAL!! You are graded pretty much based on projects which are usually extremely fun to do! John is a very nice guy, even though i'm not the kind of guy who goes to office hours much, I could tell that he has a very nice and fun personality and he's very approachable.

Good lecturer, and really easy grading for projects and tests. However, was not at all accessible or responsive outside of class, and neither were TAs. This class simply needs more TAs for such a large class size. Some projects were vague and confusing in descriptions. However, it's an easy A once you put in all the work.

Incredible professor. He's lax about his grade but firm in how he teaches. His class inspired me to continue writing when any other teacher I have written for has made me feel miserable about writing. If you want a professor that values your work, take this professor.
He is one of my favorite professors because he is so good. He will do anything to help you succeed. If you want a class that will help you out in life take his class.
Very cool and chill professor. He would let you have extensions on papers if you needed them. He would take time out of his day to sit down and read through your paper with you and help you edit it.

Could easily be your best friend. Really cool guy, pretty hip to college age kids lives. He expects you to read from the book but doesn't make it mandatory, and strives to make sure everyone is comfortable and understands whats going on and whats expected. Cares a lot!

Doug was the most passionate teacher when it came to screenwriting. Learned so much about it and he inspired me to write more. Would take ten more times. Definitely worth meeting someone so genuine in your life.

Overall Doug was great.  He's extremely helpful and clear in his lectures.  All of the books for the class are extremely cheap, too.  The class has three big papers (two are 4-5 pages, the final one is 8-10) and each one is built off of the last one.  He also has a few quizzes and some online assignments, but overall not too much work.  1010

Shirelle is an outstanding professor. Her classes were very engaging, and she made sure to adapt the course to the class' interests. She is very committed to teaching and accessible outside of class as well. I learned a lot and enjoyed every class. Highly recommend taking a class with her. You'll learn a lot with a little effort and interest.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Pros: 
- Really interesting readings and films that offered rich and complex rage of perspectives
- Lots of historical and theoretical context to help us go deeper into the texts
- Warm, friendly atmosphere that made it easy to discuss, disagree, and dig deep

Cons:
- Demanding readings and very active class discussion. Must come prepared!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback
