He didn't actually teach us but that's not the point. Very temperamental, if you catch him on a bad day or are responsible for putting him in a foul mood, stay away for some time while he gets a chance to forget your name. Knows Brahms like a brother.
Extremely knowledgeble and kind. Helpful and encouraging.
Snooty and Extremely foul tempered if you catch him on a bad day!

Mr. MacClary is incosiderate to the time of college students.  For a one credit chorus class, students are required to attend several hours of rehearsal-- most of which take place close to finals.  Mr. MacClary caters to his "favorites" during voice juries and has nothing encouraging to say to anyone else.
very helpful and caring
Music always comes first with Maclary. As it should.
No Comments
No Comments
No Comments
Extremely knowledgeable, interesting, and a really nice guy.

If you are allergic to dogs don't come prof brings his dog every day that wanders around and disrupts lectures. At that the lectures are literally just him reciting the book so you don't even need to read atp. No electronic policy, will stop everything and stare at you until you take your AirPod out in a 30+ person class. Yeah no.

Professor Alwood is the best professor ever. He very obviously cares a lot about his students and what they take away from his class. The class itself was very interesting and I looked forward to going each day. The lectures never felt long, they were super engaging and the content was always interesting. Favorite professor and favorite class.

The lectures were interesting and engaging, and he made a strong effort to connect with every student. This class covers a lot of content, and you have to remember a bunch of tiny details. Your only grades are 3 exams so you have to do well on them. Take notes and study a lot.

He is a great & interesting lecturer. Class is engaging and we learn relevant things, but beware that the only grades are 3 tests, syllabus quiz, and participation. Show up to class, take good notes, read/skim the textbook, and you'll be prepared. He is clearly very knowledgeable and passionate about this subject, you will enjoy his lectures a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Alwood is great. He gives great lectures that are easy to follow along with, and he tells great personal stories about himself. The tests cover a lot of material and you need to study a lot for them, especially to remember certain details. Also there are only a couple grades for the semester and they are mostly tests so you need to do well.

It was truly a pleasure to have him as a professor, he is a very kind man. The class can get a little boring but he keeps it interesting with his own experiences as a former CNN reporter. He grades fairly. No assignments except for media diaries which are straight forward, and no midterm or final, just 4 tests. Highly recommend taking this class
I enjoyed JOUR150 with Professor Alwood. He was very knowledgeable about the concepts and I particularly enjoyed when he would tell us some of his personal experiences.
Professor Alwood is easily the best professor I have had at UMD. He is super caring. He has very interesting lectures and the content is easy to keep up with. Please take him! You will not regret it.

If you have the chance to take this professor, do it. He is the most caring, sweet, and understanding man you will ever meet. The workload in this class is extremely minimal, with only 4 essays (that are only a page each), and 3 mid-term exams. The only thing is you have to do somewhat well on those because thats your only grade besides attendance.

Laid-back & understanding professor. We had 3 quizzes/exams & a few papers. Pretty easy to do well because he makes it clear that the papers are graded based on connections to the book BUT they're graded based on how many connections other people had which kind of hurt my grade. Very interesting class and he really tried to connect to the students

Pretty easy course but at the same time thought it was hard to get an A. I didnt like how he graded the papers but just make sure you load them up with connections. Very willing to help you out and had some pretty good lectures.

Probably my favorite professor at UMD. Very experienced. He gives a couple of media diaries that were graded fairly and weren't too bad. 3 tests that are very fair if you study the study guide throughly. I ended up with a 77.12 and he bumped me up to an 80% (B-). Take him, he's the best! Just work hard in his class, and you will be rewarded.
There are 6 diary entries and 3 quizzes, the last quiz is counted as the final so there is basically no final. He is a super nice guy and this class is super easy. Highly recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Very sweet, understanding man, and teaches you what you need to know. Assignments are pretty easy (a couple media diaries and a paper).  Lectures can get kind of boring, but the exams are based off lectures which closely follow the book's material.  He posts study guides which are extremely helpful for exams.

Dull lectures. Graded mostly from 3 tests and five short papers and one final research paper. Kind of annoying doing the five papers but they weren't hard. He's a nice man but easy to fall asleep in class.

Really great and funny guy, very friendly and understanding. Lectures can get a little dull and the final paper is annoying. Tests are easy enough if you study (make sure to remember names of people he talks about in class) and the papers are very easy.

One of my favorite teachers of all time, he has a no non-sense policy with tough love towards his students. He is a very respectable and knowledgeable person once you get to know him. Pay attention and you will be on his good side and do not take advantage of him. Amazing teacher, would love to have him as a professor again.

Honestly one of the worst professors I have encountered in the chemistry department. He reads straight from his slides while randomly calling on students. If you have your phone in class he will personally call you out. Not accomodating at all with ADS. The worst part for me was that this professor actually thinks he's smart.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Based on previous reviews, I can tell that he's working hard to improve the way he teaches. I'm not a fan of his lectures, he just tends to rant about us being bad scientists. Sometimes, what he wants us to do clashes with what the TAs tell us to do. BUT, he is willing to help. Call it tough love if you will.

Absolutely just a terrible person. Lectures are mandatory and if you are more than 5 minutes late he berates you and doesn't let you take the quiz, even on the first day. If you ask questions he will yell at you and if you even suggest doing something different he will try to insult and call you wrong. Lecture is just 1 hr of him insulting us.

Way too much material to learn. It is only once a week so a lot of information is crammed. It's easy to pass but hard to get a good grade. Professor can be condescending and gets mad about students ditching class. One class he went after a kid who went to fill his water bottle. He knows his stuff and as long as you do well on the exam you are fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: There are multiple assignments due every week throughout the week, not just on lab days. 3 major papers 65% of your grade and they are tough! He gives zero direction or instruction. TA's were just as confused as the students. Did more work for 2 credits than my other 10 combined. Plan for extra time in the lab. Get your points, take the B.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: Never seen such a rude, obnoxious, and narcissist individual. Unfortunately, you can't avoid him for 483&484. At the beginning of the semester you might think he isn't that bad, but believe me when I say it will show later on. If you go ask him for help, he will degrade you as he gives you help.

You will learn nothing in this class because he teaches you nothing, he throws 70 big ass pieces of literature to read, yells that equipment sucks and that u do not try hard in discussion, gives no feedback on reports, u will be in office hours, quizess make no sense. Doing his major reports was the reason I relapsed on coke. Switch major&dont take

There are so many things about this class that is horrible and challenging. The 3 labs are tedious and harshly graded. 8 am quizzes... You don't really know what goes on until TAs explain. Dr. Stone is knowledgeable but rude/doesn't want to share. He seems to not care that much for students and teaches more out of annoyance. Tip: don't talk back.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: It is hard to get an A, but easy to get the C- you need. Too much material is crammed into too short lectures. The final is kind of hard, but is multiple choice with a huge curve. There is a homework each week that is somewhat lengthy but you get 9 tries on each set of questions so it is easy to get it right. Lecture quiz questions are super hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This was an easy class all semester until the final. The homeworks are all online and they can be done in the first week of school. There is a one question quiz before every lecture that is ridiculously hard but counts for very little of the final grade. The lectures are boring and the final was really hard but had a massive curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Stone is not painfully hard but he sure makes you work for a good grade. His lectures can be hard to grasp if youre someone with limited knowledge. Use the supplemental books Chang and Klein! Tests are the only grades mostly lectures, very vocab based, few math. No tests given back. Will throw in tricky questions! He is always welling to help!

For chem 134 he was the perfect professor seeing how you really just need the C or higher if you are trying to get into the engineering program. His class is designed to teach and not weed you out. It was awesome and he is a great teacher. Homework and attendance are needed to pass but not too hard and only once a week
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It's a lab class so of course you have to show up. Other than that, he is the worst professor I've ever had, the workload was higher than a 4 credit class for a 2 credit class, and he never actually teaches the subjects that you'll be doing in lab making you do hours of research to be able to do the lab, also the grading criteria is very unclear.

Mostly all you had was about an hour a week of online problems, but multiple attempts so easy A. Lectures were boring but there are participation quizzes so you have to go and the quizzes are ridiculously hard but worth little. The final was the only test, but he graded it on a curve with the mean being an 85. Solid choice if you know chem already.

He doesn't offer extra credit and the very few exams are almost 60% vocabulary definitions. He is helpful and explains things during lecture if you ask. His slides contain everything you need to know and are very helpful. My complaint is that he digresses a lot during lecture and is not always focused, making class confusing sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: tests are HUGELY based on vocab rather than math.--don't practice the math that much! I barely did any math in this class. make sure you look at the powerpoints, the vocab comes from there. don't ask for extra credit because it isn't offered. he's a good guy who is trying to prepare future medical professionals. get the kleins books!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Professor Stone is a great professor for Chem131. He not only prepares you for this course, but for more advanced courses in the future. If you attend the lectures and follow his studying tips with certain books, you will succeed in his class. While his tests may be difficult, he is very accessible at office hours to review tests. Take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: You have to basically memorize the powerpoint slides to do well. It's vocab heavy on the exams and although he spends entire lectures focusing on math problems, little math appears on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Personally, his lectures were not as helpful as I had hoped they would be. I had to rely a lot on my textbook, which meant that I had to do a lot of self-study. I did go to his office hours once, but he gave a pretty vague overview of what I needed to work on based on my exam. It would have helped if I got my exams back to see what I got wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: You have to show you understand chemistry by passing 5 exams. No math needed which is nice, but he will ask you extremely specific questions about vocab and concepts. Don't expect to be able to study from previous exams, he doesn't hand them back. You can only view your exam in office hours (prepare for a long line) and only with his supervision.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: you have 5 grades for the whole semester, 4 exams and 1 final. none of the math you spend most of the class is on the exam. if you only study vocab you will be fine considering vocab is a major part of this class. he knows what he is talking about and is helpful during office hours, but the stuff he talks about least is the stuff that is on exam
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: For intro to Chem class, this was tough. Didn't learn during lectures. You will have to teach yourself everything. His slides are extremely difficult to understand. You have to get all the review books he tells you to get and do all the practice problem if you want to do well. BTW the 2nd test and on is ORGO. His tests are all vocab, and no math.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Definitely knows what he's talking about, but when he relates it back to us students who know little to nothing about chemistry, it's just plain hard to follow. Had to teach myself everything later on based off of his slides since he really doesn't. He'll say the tests will have many math calculations, don't trust it, study the VOCABULARY!
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He knows what he's talking about but it can be hard to understand if you're not well versed in Chemistry. If you go to him after a test he will explain what you did wrong. Only does tests for your grade but there's a pretty big curve on the tests.

He is one of the more caring and patient professors at UMD. It is amazing to have such an eccentric, genuine, and sincere professor at a campus that feels a bit too detached at times. There is a lot of work, but he is preparing future doctors, chemists etc. Not an easy A but not insurmountable. He is very willing to help and is a fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Be prepared for a lot of work for a two credit lab class. The lectures were not as helpful as they could have been. Your own background knowledge is what really gets you through. He is very accessible, and will be happy to share his plethora of chemistry knowledge with you. You don't get too much assistance. If you work hard you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Teacher knows what he is talking about, but doesn' t know how to explain it in a simplest manner, for variation of student learning types. He is a good teacher, but really harsh grader.  I took summer class with him, so it was already hard, but he didn't make much easier. Computer for his class is required base; everything is to be done online.

Dr. Stone assigns more work in a two credit lab course than most do in a four credit course.  And on top of that, the class is for freshmen.  The work assigned is tedious and it is difficult to reach out to him to discuss anything.  He also tends to talk down to students during office hours and not be of much help.

Dr. Stone is awesome for general chemistry. Chemistry has always been the hardest subject for me, but he presents all of the powerpoint notes and information but then applies it to real-world situations which helps to be able to better understand it. He is the reason I got  good grade in chemistry.

Dr. Stone teaches a 100-level freshman chem lab as if it is his 400-level chem lab. He gives a bunch of assignments and makes us work more than a 2-credit course should make us work. He says he's preparing us for the future, but I found a lot of the work unnecessary. He also changes his assignments and doesn't announce it, which is frustrating.

Dr. Eaker was so awesome! Class was very discussion based and she was always very mindful of not giving us too much homework. She clearly cares about her students and wants them all to do well and learn. Highly recommend taking her class if you ever get the chance!

Class activities and readings each week that are not hard or heavy in content. Classes start out lecture heavy then fade as the semester goes, making the ending very smooth. Kind lady, who really cares about her students. Heavy on no electronics during class and provides AMAZING feedback. Just weekly assignments and one big project in the end.

The class is boring and only graded on two quizzed, a paper, and a project. Readings are light but sometimes hard to understand. We get biweekly assignments that she looks at but aren't graded, the process is stupid. Still better than TLPL 360 though, that one was way too reading heavy. This class is what I dread every week

Professor Eaker is definitely one of my favorite professors. She was very energetic, kind, respectful, and understanding. In the course, she provides articles for you to read, light discussion questions, only 2 quizzes, and a final presentation. The class is discussion-based. Overall one of my favorite courses!

Ethan Lick Eagle is a great guy. If you are a high performing individual, you will appreciate his wisdom. He is the teacher that will explain the shortcut to doing something better than the long way of doing it. If you have done well in previous physics classes, you will enjoy the pace he moves at. Otherwise, you'll probably be lost.

Very nice guy, but gives a lot of work. He gave more work than the other ENES100 professors did and also graded pretty harshly. You also need to participate to earn credit because he knows when you don't. A lot of extra credit opportunities were given.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't hate him cause he gives vague instructions. Don't hate him cause he is unprepared. Don't hate him cause he put emphasis on the unimportant things and glosses over the important ones. Hate him because his middle name is Lick. Overall good teacher, set aside time for the class, just do your work, have fun, and it's that simple.

Harsh grader and doesn't provide rubrics. You never know what he is looking for. Claims that you don't need prior coding experience but still assigns multiple coding assignments without teaching how to code. I also went to his office hours once because my computer wouldn't run program. He couldn't even recommend a specific computer to replace it.

I really liked Ethan. A lot of people dont, he just takes some getting used to. pretty young & incredibly extra but its nice to have a professor like that. gave like 100 extra credit assignments, theres no reason anyone shouldnt have an A. Hes pretty new so still working on finding a teaching style that works for him. cares about his student A LOT

He tries to be innovative in his teaching style, but it's a bad method. He thinks he's the smartest man on Earth and claims to care for his students, but I tried to reach out to him and he never emailed me back. Picks a few favorites and gives them the highest grades and attention most of the time. Unreasonable grading, idk if anyone will get an A.

Ethan is a great professor! ENES 100 is designed to be a very challenging course for students early in their engineering journey. Don't be too disappointed if you don't actually understand what is happening. Be sure to go to office hours. He's super accessible outside of class. He truly wants every one of his students to succeed. You'll learn a lot

Ethan is a good professor who cares about how his students learn and change throughout the class. He is a very tough grader and there is a lot of outside work, but part of that is the nature of the course. He doesn't lecture which can make it challenging, but if you work hard and ask him questions, you can be successful and learn a lot.

Nice guy, pretty good lecturer. It was maybe his first time teaching this course, and even if not, he wasn't the one who made the curriculum, but he knew the material nonetheless. Would sometimes be unable to answer a question, but this didn't happen that often. Fair projects. Adjusted well when we went online halfway through the semester.

tends to just read off the slides most of the time. course is co-taught but designed but another professor so Eastman just kinda does what the others say. Clickers in lecture count for a grade and projects are the same for all sections. There are 2 exams and 40% of course grade is based on projects.
Fantastic professor. Was not the best for first time coders. CMSC131 was tough. Loved Eastman, met with him constantly and he was always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Roger Eastman is a great Professor. He helps us understand the material, and if he sees, or realize the material was not taught or cover well enough, he tries going over it again, differently. He does live coding on certain days, so we can see how to use the materials we learn. He does really good exam reviews in lecture before the exams.

His lectures aren't necessarily mandatory, but he does a good job at explaining the materials in a relatable way, even if you have had no prior programming experience. He is easily accessible outside of class through office hours and emails. He wants all of his students to pass and is willing to take all sorts of questions.

Dr. Eastman knows his stuff. The course is difficult. I had one C programming course previously and I still found this difficult after the second midterm. Class starts of easy and picks up in difficulty rapidly and does not ease up. Be ready for long projects. No homework. Textbook isn't necessary but recommended. Lectures recorded but still go.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. Explains things clearly, however could improve his handwriting. Even though exams are given by filippou, he tries to help in the best way possible

Dr. Eastman has 40 years experience teaching discrete math, and his lectures show that. Hes very clear and concise when explaining concepts and will make sure everyone understands the material. I feared this class after my experience with Calc 2 but I can honestly say Ive enjoyed 250 a lot. Utilize the resources given to you and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Stone is like a football coach, he wants you to succeed, but he wants you to earn it. Not just give it to you. He's tough when he needs to be but he wants everyone to learn. He has a bunch of students but actually learns their names and about them. That's more than I can say about other profs. Don't take the failure of the system out on Stone

Dr. Stone can put a 200 person lecture hall to sleep in 10 minutes. He lectures on irrelevant details and has way too many words on his slides. His outright arrogance made this class the largest waste of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Okay teacher. Doesn't teach the same way or same things as other 131 teachers at UMD which is odd. He's a bit rude and doesn't seem to care about students that much. You'll never get your tests back so you won't know what to study but the test are curved so that helps.

This professor was super nice and the all the tests were curved, which was really helpful since the only grades in the class were tests. He did his best to make sure everyone understood the material, and he was often cracking jokes. There is a lot of material to learn, but the tests arent too hard. He made chemistry a much better experience.

This professor is horrible. My advice for incoming chem majors who have to take this class is to switch to a bio major for a year then switch back to chem once this class has been avoided. Stone is unhygienic, condescending, and not helpful at all, all the while thinking he's God's gift to teaching. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

He assigns an insanely heavy course load and makes assignments due over holidays. He never shows up to class, so it's really all up to your TA and I had a bad one so it was awful. If you ask for help he'll probably ignore you. Although he does give a lot of extra credit, even with doing all of it your grade will still be low. He's unreasonable.

i took him over the summer. He was  very understanding about the difficulty of the course. He worked problems in class very similar to the once on the exams. His exam are divided into vocabulary, concept understanding and work problems. Once you understand his testing style, his exams are very straight forward. I would take him again.

Puts all his lecture slides online which is a plus.  Tests are pretty hard even though the majority were multiple choice.  He curves all the tests using a T score rather than a curve which helped the lower grades out.

She was probably the best teacher I have had so far at UMD. She is so passionate about what she does, that It really inspires her students to be engaged as well. Weekly discussions on films that we had to watch were actually very entertaining and cool to do. If you show up, pay attention and strive to do well, you will

Excellent professor! Extremely knowledgeable and genuinely cares about her students. Definitely worth taking her class even if the subject doesnt interest you. Easy grader, well spoken, interesting lady. Very personable and helpful. Lively spirit that makes her class worthwhile
my favorite professor.  very knowledgable and interesting.

She is amazing. I truly enjoyed her teaching as well as her overal personality. Attending is necessary, but if you have a general knowledge of the subject you can afford to skip class. But the class is interesting so go anyway. Even though pretty easy she is one of the most knowledgeable and interesting professors I've ever had.

You must attend daily (all quiz and test materials from class powerpoints). Generous grader if you attend. Overall, I was very satisfied. No daily homework- only 2 reasonable projects (film review and 1 powerpoint.) Dont buy book- it is optional and you never use it as all test/quizzes from class.
Mme Eades is an excellent prof.  She expects students to attend class, but quiz and test materials come directly from lectures/ powerpoints.  she is rather generous on her grading as well.
She's a very good teacher, very understanding and helpful. She's very generous on her grading no doubt.

This class is very dependent on your TA. My classes TA graded very harshly. One small assignment due each week. Lecture isn't mandatory as the slides are all online. Exams are tough and I know of many friends doing poorly in the class due to the writing portions. Hard to get an A, easy to get a B.

Dr. Eaker is knowledgeable and more than willing to help! The textbook is an absolute must. Technically you can learn the material just by reading, but her lectures are really helpful as well. Discussion section is mandatory. If you do the homework and understand those problems, you will do well on the tests - Dr. Eaker wants you to succeed.
Also took PHIL256 with her. She is my favorite professor
Really pretty, smart, nice to students, sympathetic, great TA's. Take her class.

Let me just say how much of a pleasure it has been taking BSCI120 this semester. I really learned a lot about arthropods and have now developed a new found appreciation for them. Also, I would like to add that our teaching assistant Chris was super awesome--always helpful and made sure that the class material was engaging. I will miss this class!
dR. aRMSTRONG IS ONE OF THE BEST INSTRUCTORS I HAVE hAD AT MARYLAND. sHE REALLY KNOWS HER SUBJECT.I MADE A C OUT OF THE COURSE BUT I REALLY ENJOYED THIS CLASS.

I just finished taking my final and I REALLY DIDN'T want to leave the class because I really enjoyed my time in this class... Professor Armstrong is really a wonderful, kind teacher thats knows TONS of stuff about insects. Her TA, Jeff, is an awesome guy. He will answer all of your questions and is extremely nice. ATTEND ALL LECTURES AND DISCUSSION
The class is easy if you have any common sense and a little time to look over your notes the day before the test. Interesting and satisfies a CORE.
she is the best professor at this university, she is hilarious :))

The professor is alright, but it was the most poorly focused class I have ever taken. Lecture and discussion were completley unrelated, the power points were not useful, and the tests were oddly specific and jumped all over the place in terms of information covered. Nice enough, just poorly organized and uninteresting

I do not understand why Dr. Rodriguez gets so much hate. If you're taking this class you have probably taken chemistry in high school and its really hard to make a repeat of chemistry seem insanely interesting, but he cares and grades based on the class average so there is definitely forgiveness if you don't remember all of Gen Chem from highschool

Nicest guy ever. Really cares about what he is teaching and how is students are doing. Definitely go to office hours because they are super helpful and he is easy to talk to. Work load is very manageable and exams are not too difficult.

Prof. Rodriguez is nice and willing to answer questions, but he lectures straight out of the textbook and sometimes manages to make things more confusing. The textbook was so helpful to this course, and was the main way I did well on exams.

Rodriguez is an approachable and nice professor. However, his exams were way harder than his practice exams and homework problems; averages were in the low D range. TA discussions were not helpful in learning the material at all. Textbook reading and practice problems honestly saved my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His lectures are super confusing and discussion isn't very helpful either, even if you feel like you understand everything presented in the unit you will still probably fail the exam
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This CHEM271 class is preposterous. We have no GSS this semester, the discussion leader (stephanie) is incompetent and horrible at teaching chemistry, and the exam averages have been in the 50s. This is compared to Dr. Wang's class which has an exam average in the mid-70s and the students have told me that he is a good professor. Avoid Rodriguez!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took this class online / asynchronous with Jarzynski & Rodriguez co-teaching. Rodriguez has no idea how to explain things and is not responsive to concerns... would not recommend!! Feels like a three-credit class. Four exams (and a final) for 30 minutes each - literally hyperventilating the whole time. My 91  A. Do practice problems & go to GSS!

He's a very solid professor; lectures are effective and well-organized. Office hours and discussions are helpful and necessary to do well. The class is weighted heavily on exams (which are fair); neither problem sets (they're very difficult, but good preparation) nor quizzes (which are reasonable) are highly valued. You don't need to have taken AP.

A rather intelligent man, but lacking professor. His class is not an introduction class as much as a chemistry review for those who took A.P. in high school, meaning fundamentals were often skipped. Feedback on graded assignments is rarely returned and/or explained, at best.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst teachers I ever had. Attending lectures is a waste of time because he does not teach. He spends a lot of time talking about the history of Chemistry, he throws "tricks" on the quizzes to purposely confuse you, and half of the class is failing, while the other half that is not falling because they took AP in high school.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Final grades are based on almost solely on exam scores. Lectures are long and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Egan is very knowledgeable, but is way too demanding for an entry level class. Be prepared to focus and take clear notes, don't miss class or discussion. You will need to memorize literally everything. Not allowed to type notes either. Making and studying a quizlet is a necessity to pass the exams (I recommend Knowt instead).

She has been one of my favorite professors this year. If you are not good at memorization though don't take this class. If you like art history definitely take her class, but if it is not your thing you will hate it. She does a really good job of trying to keep lectures interesting. Loved her!

For the online class you have to watch two lecture ppts each week and are quizzes on them each week. The material is pretty interesting but the lectures can be super long. Make sure to participate in the discussions. Theres 2 Papers and one mid-term that is graded by your TA. Some effort is required to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Egan was great and very sympathetic to the stress of online classes. Few assignments, only one "real" exam and it was take-home with several days to do it. She is an interesting lecturer and as long as you keep up with the pre-recorded lectures and weekly quizzes it will be a breeze. Participate in the discussion section
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Relatively easy class, midterm was based off of lectures. No memorization needed (due to covid and online testing). Lectures were uploaded weekly as ppt files, had a weekly quiz. Two papers that count for a large part of your grade, no clear rubric and not much feedback given. Interesting material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Egan is super organized and puts a lot of work into her lectures and study material. This class is a moderate amount of work just because the recorded lectures are so long but if you put the time into good note-taking you'll be fine :)

Not enough good things to say about Dr. Egan. She's an engaging lecturer who makes everything clear and interesting. Tests are very easy if you can memorize a decent amount of works and listen in class (which isn't hard with her). The semester project was pretty arbitrary, but was graded lightly. Take her if you can.

I LOVE EMILY! She's so adorably quirky and passionate about the material which helped me become so passionate about the material and do well in the class. Her lectures go over what was in the reading so I ended up not using my textbook. Exams are essay based and really holistically test your knowledge of the material which I enjoyed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Egan is a solid choice. I've never taken an art history course in my life, and I put only some effort into this class. The two papers are very easy, but can be annoying. The tests only require you to memorize key bits of pieces in your notes, and details about them. Overall easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Egan is really passionate. Be ready to study and prepare for exams. one midterm, one final, two papers. go to lecture, a lot to learn

Professor Egan is a great teacher. She's very enthusiastic about her subject and her lectures are interesting. She gives you a list of works and terms for every chapter of the things that might come up on the midterm and the final (which is non cumulative). It's a fair class and if you study you'll get an A.

Dr. Egan is very nice and you can tell she's deeply passionate about her subject. This was the first art history class I've ever taken and it's hard, you must memorize many specific pieces of art along with their specific information. It's challenging and the lectures require you to take a lot of notes, but she's a nice person.
Amazing teacher, so charismatic and cares about each one of his students so much. Will go above and beyond to make sure that his students succeed.
Funny and chill.
Mike is caring, kind, and very entertaining. He's been one of the best professors I've had at the University!
He is a very funny, and is very easy to understand. If you go to class, you will pass
Awesome guy!
I wasn't sure how this class would fit after the first FIRE class, but Mike made it pretty decent. He tries hard and is fairly funny.

I never  got lower than an A- in an english class and it was my minor. In his class, I got 100% until the final, then he failed me. I emailed him and he said it was due to my "irreverent" and "uncaring" attitude. I came to see him to talk, but he did seemed to have confused me with another student. Need I say more? I got my first B...

Holy crap this guy was TOTALLY subjective! I got a decent grade in his class, but still - be wary! He grades based upon whether he likes you or not, not based upon merit of points presented. Lectures can be cool at times but, overall - I'd say, "Meh" and move on! Not worth it - and, no, I'm not bitter, I got a good grade, remember? Just be careful!

What little of his class I took was by far the worst experience I had at Maryland. Rather than teach his subject he decided to demonstrate his ignorance of biology and current affairs, and succeeded spectacularly at that. Moreover he was indignant about being factually corrected, and demanded an apology for "surprising" him.

Unlike any other professor I've had at Maryland so far. His grading can be very subjective at times, but ultimately it is what makes him a good teacher. By that I mean he actually has opinions on poets/authors and can offer some of his own observations, rather than what you can get anywhere else.
No Comments

This was the best professor I had at UMD. He encouraged me to change my major to English and was the reason I learned to appreciate and love lit. He is not easy, but if you are in college for easy, you are wasting your money..he really expects you to learn. Dont give a prof a bad rating becuase you got a bad grade because you didnt do****! He is an amazing professor and very kind and will take as much personal time as necessary to help you with school and non school problems!! Hes the best

If you write down everything he says and study that, you will do fine.  He didn't give a lot of feedback on the paper before turning in the final copy.  He is interesting and a charming old man but some might find him boring.  There really isn't a lot of c
Awful.

Want an easy A, without learning ANYTHING about the subject? Then take this class. He offers no insight, comes up with unlikely interpretations, then insists you reproduce them verbatim on the exam. Thinks of himself as poet, uses own work as examples in class ("every disorder is an order").

Accused me of plagerism when I submitted original work.  Lectures were of the T.A. vareity.  Was surprised he was allowed to teach.  He was very patronizing towards students.  Very unchallenging.  No new or original thoughts.  Lectures on tape are better
this guy is soooo boring. i hated every waking second. easy class though.
try and be a little interesting prof
worst teacher in the history of UMD. you should run if you see his name

Lectures are almost word for word from the text. Thick accent & his handwriting is appalling though. Very easy grading scale. Was out of 230 points, 131 was a B-. Attendance not mandatory but there are pop quizzes. He never gives back tests or quizzes and when you go to get it he makes you grade them or look. Obsessed with striped shirts.

He is a bit of an arbitrary grader, and keeping quiet and showing up will get you a long way.  Trying to understand how the test is going to be set up in advance or how he grades or what to expect on the test is all pointless.  You can study your behind off and still get a C.  Note: if there are any bad kids in the class he will take it out on all.
Prof. was 5-35 minutes late every day so far this semester. Lectures are practically word for word from the text.
He is very impatient when students ask questions, and does not readily make himself available outside of class. I was never shown my grade in the class, or even my grade on a test or quiz.

this guy is awful. boring class, confusing terms to memorize. teaches EXACTLY from the text, reads word for word from the text--which is good cause you can't understand a word he says. avoid this class if you can. very boring. teacher is unhelpful
He is very confusing.
Horrible teacher. Very thick accent, refuses to give help. Bad attitude. Always late. Didnt show up one time. Yeah.

Ejiogu knows his sociology but at times he can be very boring! the class is easy...he gives you hints to what will be on the midterm and final...he also grades fairly..however if ur looking for excitement...this is not the class to sign up for
One of the better professors at UMD.
Great guy.  If you show some interest in the class and ask some questions you will get an A.

supposed to be about contemporary social problems, he spent the whole semester talking aboud political violence and terrorism, not interesting at all. Very hard readings. Couldnt understand him all the time. Term paper 10+ pages on any social prob but cant use any internet sources. 2 Exams essay format have 2 cram all info 2 be tested on few topica

There's a lot of reading and i didn't find his lectures to be helpful at all. Some of the readings were complex and he wasn't very good at explaining it. Also, if you'd ask a question, sometimes he wouldn't answer it correcctly.

I really liked how he taught this class. The tests, compared to my other genchem friends, were extremely fair and there was room for error. Worksheets helped your grade, but there were no other grades. The book is definitely worth buying/renting; questions were similar to the book. Attendance to lecture/discussion wasn't mandatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: My semester, we had 3 tests and about 5 worksheets that went into the gradebook. Your grade relies not on how well you do on the tests but how you compare to average test scores are for the whole entire class. His tests are reliant on the things he says in class and are challenging but there's a huge curve. You will need to read to know concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Eichorn is pretty much a straight shooter, what he says in class is most likely going to show up on the tests and exams. Still l read the textbook though but its pretty much what he says in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is very mediocre. He wasn't a bad teacher, he was just sort of uninteresting. His test averages are low but there is a hefty curve at the end. He doesn't post his lecture slides online so it really helps to attend class. Also, he uses practice problems from class on the exams. A lot of his exam questions come from the back of the book too!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Has no idea what is happening in class and doesnt have any answers to any questions. The TA did all the work to cover for how bad Einstein is. Einstein will not even respond to emails with any questions and will just ignore them. He also will change his requirements after class so you get a lower grade for not being aware of the change.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lecture is extremely dry, and it only teaches how to use excel and low level statistics, not anything about Physics. He's not very approachable because he explains things poorly/patronizingly. I don't think it makes any sense to have to memorize statistical formulas for exams, so I did very poorly on the first one, but that's a personal issue.

Exams are pretty hard but if you know how to do all the Mastering Physics problems you should be okay. Einstein's lectures are basically him reading out the book and maybe does 1 sample problem on the board which I didn't like. I preferred a teacher who went through examples and stuff but he was still pretty funny.

Nice guy who you can tell cares about the students. Exams are difficult, but usually similar to the ones he posts on his ELMS page. Hard to follow in lecture but is accessible and always glad to answer questions or help. Grades fairly.

Ted wasn't the most approachable guy, and wasn't all the helpful when you needed assistance. This was an intro lab, yet he expected you to know complex things like partial derivatives and electrical systems. Overall the class was okay because there's only two exams that are EXACTLY like the review, and the labs are graded easily.
what a legend
Never take. Exams are nothing like the lectures, homework, or quizzes.
Lectures are awful and not helpful at all. Most of his time in lectures is spent doing convoluted proofs and never does practical examples. Learned most of the material through the textbook.

The class is inherently difficult,  physics 2 is not an easy class.   But does it need to be this difficult? No.  Einstein is a smart guy, and hes even kinda funny! But he requires extra weekly homework beyond the normal course load, has quizzes every lecture, even harder quizzes every discussion.  The exams are brutal, and the grading is harder.

You will have to live by the textbook. It's hard to understand the lectures because Einstein doesn't clearly define the variables he uses. You have to go to lecture because he has online quizzes that you need a password for (though you could just have someone get the password and send it to you).

Generally not a good physics teacher for an basic physics level class. He is very smart, but not very good at lecturing or answering questions. I would recommend he get moved to teach more advanced level classes or focus on his research, which is, what I assume, the reason this school still employs him.

The professor is a hit and miss. Make sure to keep record of all the equations and concept graphs(E.g phase-change diagram) as he might put them on the exam. His exams are a mix memorization and calculations; however, beware of what he might put on the exam. Sometimes he writes up a problem on board, and never finishes solving it. Be vigilant
Just an overall unreasonable person. Unhelpful and uncaring. Not sure how he ended up in education. Would not take again and would not advise you to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you go to lecture and review sessions you should be okay. exams are hard and long but if you genuinely understand the material you should be ok. he's open to questions and wants you to do well

He is a great teacher! He does actual examples on the board not just reads from slides, do the homework and the textbook practice problems, they will really help you learn the material. He answers all questions and encourages involvement in class.
Worst prof ever. AVOID!!!
learned alot

I loved Dr. Eichhorn because he seems to really enjoy chem and his students. But don't think you're going to coast through this class! It isn't easy and the tests will be long, sometimes too long in my opinion. However, you're given every opportunity to succeed. The homework and book are helpful, as are the TA's. Make extra time for this class!

He is pretty good compared to the other professors. I would recommend him over all the others teaching this course, but it is pretty hard regardless. You need to study and go to lectures. The exams are fair, but not exactly easy. Important to recognize when you are not understanding something and going to get help, or you won't make it through.
He didnt really teach but rather zoom through the materials. Not the best professor. His exams were pretty easy compared to Dixon!!!

Pretty nice guy. Goes through lots of problems in class and answers questions. I mostly taught myself from the textbook which was very helpful with lots of example problems. The online homework is pretty hard but the tests are easy if you do the practice ones given online. 3 tests plus final and homework every week. Be prepared to study.

Good teacher and makes some funny corny jokes, lol. uses a clicker ~3-4times/week. 3 tests: each of which are fairly easy;however, you must come prepared (unlike myself). gives prac tests which are good. online ARIS hw is really hard compared to book work or in-class work. go to lec to get worked out problems. writes own final. curve.."depends"
the practice tests on his website  are exactly like the actual test. if you do those and the online HW its easy to get an a

absolutely adorable! attending most to all lectures is essential for success, especially since your participation grade comes from your attendance (clicker questions almost everyday). completing his practice exams and going to your discussion session to review the practice exams will almost guarantee a C or better on the exams! i highly recommend!

he's so adorable! and very funny too. he always cracks silly jokes to keep you awake/interested. even though he looks old he's a VERY lively and enthusiastic teacher. the notes in class cover the crucial topics and he always gives lots of practice problems. going to class helps more than reading the text. i highly recommend eichhorn
he was a pretty good teacher but the final was very difficult and was supposedly "written by all the professors" but was so obviously not his test.
Excellent professor, easy to follow lectures, answers all questions.  Tests correspond to class work perfectly. I highly recommend.
Very friendly and funny, explains things very well

It's a good thing there is a big curve.I ended up with an A but there were some concepts where I had no idea what was going on.If you have a question you're basically told to "read the book."Sometimes we'd ask for a sample problem and he wouldn't do it cuz he couldn't think of one or something?I dont know.Johnson was a good TA for discussion though

Very funny!  Explains everything very well, and accepts questions during lecture.  Dr. Eicchorn will make SURE you understand!  Very fair and somewhat simple exams (if you study).  The exams are from lecture, so no definitions or boring names are included.
really good on the blackboard. Explains each probelm very well
He made this class really easy to comprehend.  Explains everything pretty well, and isnt too boring. Has a good sense of humor.
Her moods can overshadow her ability to teach.

do not take this class as a CORE requirement unless you like drawing. you have to go off campus for the projects and it takes a lot of time. if you want to get a good grade in this class you have to put in the effort. as a teacher she is really good! her classes are slide shows, but you can find more detailed notes online o the course webpage

If drawing is your thing then this is the class for you. Otherwise you will find it to be tedious busy work. The midterm tests are beyond easy, but she gets you on the final which is 30% of your grade. Even if you have a 96%you CAN NOT blow off the final. The TAs will give you a B if you have a 89.8 but got above 95 on everything else.

Lectures are dry, but she enjoys teaching. Tests are straight-forward. Although notes can be found online, I found it helpful to combine and review lecture notes and online notes simultaneously for test study guides. Text books were a very big waste of money, try to buy only the supplement.Only after the final I felt i learned a lot in arch.

Wow what a boring class. This professor turned something interesting into a bunch of lectures on filler material. The class would be so much more interesting if there was less bull, if it were half a semester or less the same material could easily be covered. It is so boring, you learn about nothing half the time, but the projects are interesting.

Mandatory discussion attendance, but notes from lectures are online.  Sometimes the lectures were long, but between them and the online notes it is not tough.  She would also put three possible essay questions online to outline and one of them would be on the test.

The lectures themselves aren’t terribly interesting (unless you’re an Arch major), but almost all the material is on the website.  The Professor is really nice and is more than happy to answer questions.  The assignments involved drawing and creativity, which I found to be a nice break from endless paper writing, and the TA I had was helpful.

Professor is nice, but lectures are dry, especially if it's in the morning.  If you're not an arch major or into drawing at all, do NOT take this class.  3 of the 4 assignments require drawing and are really difficult if you're not into that. My TA was really into Arch, so that was annoying and made it harder to get a good grade.

Unbelievably boring professor! You really have to fight to stay awake in this class. Exams are not very difficult. I hardly ever went to lecture after the first three weeks. Did I mention she is boring? Well, she is!

Level of ease depends upon your TA. There are lots of projects and lots of work to do. Most consider it easy, however if you get a very committed TA, you might see your grades slip. The material is very easy, and quite obvious at times. The class is quite boring. VERY VERY boring. You might find it impossible to sit through an entire lecture.

I feel like im taking crazy pills here. The class is SO BORING! like... SOOOOOOOOOOOOO BORING... like shoot yourself in the face because theres not point to all this. DONT buy the textbook. The assignments are SO STUPID and TIME CONSUMING. nothing in this class is hard... but you just wonder... why the hell am i doing this. exams are very ez.

Good teacher, but since it is part of the CORE program the material is fairly mandated, making the class slow and sometimes boring.  The projects involve alot of drafting/drawing but aren't hard to get As on as long as you follow the rubric.

The class isn't bad. Tests are easy, material is online. i never went to lecture... boring. The projects are challenging, and time consuming. Your TA determines your grade. Take this class just to get the core out of the way. It is probably the best option.

Excellent teacher, pretty easy class-lecture goes kinda slow because some of the people in the class make retarded comments and say a lot of stupid things but as far as the prof goes, you cant go wrong - she does a great job of making things very clear and presenting all the topics in class.  Exams arent so bad, just make sure you know the material

Relatively easy A as long as you do all of the work and extra credit in the class, although his grading on papers is ridiculously petty. My problem is more so his attitude, as he is very arrogant and talks down to students as if they are beneath him, and he seems to dislike teaching. However, if you can deal with that, it's a simple A class.

Main issue was never knowing how we were doing because they were usually six weeks behind on grading for no reason. Also, when they did start giving grades back the semester was halfway through and people were getting very harsh grades with unspecific feedback.
Easy A. There are papers due every other week and group assignments. Work is graded by the TA. No exams given.
such a silly man, I learned nothing from his lectures but I learned from the textbook. Very easy class

Class organization was poor, every student asked the same question a 100 different ways to try to get the answer out of him. Instead he would go around in circles never answering any of the questions. Teacher did the bare minimum and left most of the work to TAs who were equally as bad.

Literally a waste of time and money. We have finished the semester and he still has graded only 1/4 of our assignments. When we would ask for grades he would belittle and gaslight us. Not a good teacher and deliberately talked bad about his TA to another student. Only major assignment is a final paper, but have 2 1-page papers due every Friday.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Selterman was an amazing professor. His lectures were actually very interesting, and I learned a lot from them. He did not give us any tests but there were open note quizzes online in which we had the resources to find the answers. We also had essay's every other Friday, but they were not terribly difficult. Would recommend!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He gives weekly tests (majority are open note) on canvas related to the readings we do each week, which are fairly easy. Every other week, we have a discussion with the TAs, and the weeks where we don't have discussion, he would assign a paper, which were about 400 words. If you don't care to learn about psychology, but want an easy A, take this
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very easy A, just do the weekly worksheets and short SAs. Dylan is nice and sometimes funny but he goes off topic. He let you choose in-person and zoom, there are no exams or final projects, he gives a lot of extra credit, and the course load is fair. It's a great elective to boost your GPA and the content is very interesting.

I was excited to take this class and it was a big disappointment. TA's were harsh graders, and the whole class felt like busy work. Was definitely an easy A, but I don't recommend it. Its the last week of classes and I only have 11/27 assignments graded. This class was just a mess.

This class was easy. A lot of people complained about him in the class groupme for things that weren't issues. Like unclear instructions when we literally had all the instructions very clearly laid out for every assignment on elms. He is a bit slow on grading but you can just go to office hours one time to see if your doing the right stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Easy A but dont take this if you really want to learn psychology. This whole class felt like busy work and I felt no desire or motivation to actually learn anything. Selterman is not a good professor and sometimes seems like he has no clue what hes talking about. Also loves to go on long rants about his beliefs which is just annoying.

This professor is great at conveying course content to students and utilizing course materials (textbooks, articles, videos, and podcasts) to improve student learning. However, he will also deflect from student concerns and throw his TA under the bus if a student is concerned about the way an assignment is graded.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is a lot of reading that you have to do to complete the weekly worksheets that take a long time. There is also an essay that you have to do every other week on a prompt that he gives you. I did not learn a lot in his lectures, more from the readings. He takes a long time to respond to emails, but the TA's were very nice and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He isn't a bad professor himself but this class is based on research. I hated it so much! If you do not like writing then do not take this class because that is all you will do.

Dr. Selterman is amazing! After taking his PSYC221 course, and having a blast, this class was even better. It is a great option! Selterman cares about his students and our education system (he always goes on an entertaining rant about it). The class is paper-based but nothing too bad. Each class starts with a guided meditation. One of the best prof

prof selterman was my favorite professor ever. so caring and understanding with your grade and you yourself. he really takes the time to hear opinions and thoughts. this class had quite a few tests but if you study, you'll be fine. he was very personal when interacting over zoom. great class.

Not my favorite professor. Self-absorbed and doesnt care about your opinions. He will shut you down the second you show any form of thought that doesnt agree with him. He wants you to challenge him yet makes you feel bad about it. The only way to really win in this class is by doing the assignments, which are easy. The TAs are nice and helpful
I have taken this prof twice, & he was great both times! His classes are pretty easygoing & his lectures are very interesting. He didn't assign much homework and test were fair. Definitely recommend.

Really confusing rules. He does not communicate well with students. We had projects in place of tests. I learned little to no psychology in this class. The rules for projects were so vague and graded on a very strict scale. He also changed rules for extra credit last minute and didn't let us know? Very rude and I wouldn't recommend him.

Dr. Selterman is great professor that is understanding and helpful. We didn't have tests, but there was a quiz on the textbook every week and an essay due every other week. I personally felt as if the workload was manageable, but Dr. Selterman was always available to help any students that were struggling. Definitely recommend this class!

Really understanding, classwork is minimal, and there's no tests. One of the easier classes I've taken, but I still learned a lot. Professor Selterman is very friendly and very aware of students' stressors. Highly recommend this class.

Dr. Selterman is a nice guy and clearly knows a lot about psychology, but his projects are pretty confusing and unconventional, and I found myself thinking more about the work, and less about psychology. A great professor otherwise though!

Best professor ever! even during a pandemic he offered class time during lectures to let us talk about global issues and concerns. extra credit opportunities, lectures were always interesting and he had a great sense of humor. can't recommend him enough!!

I would not recommend taking any of Dr. Selterman's classes. I was told the same but did it anyway. That was a bad decision! I scheduled many office hour appointments and never had good experiences at any of them. One time, I had to wait 35 minutes outside his door for our SCHEDULED appointment. He was inside talking to a TA about partying.

I didn't enjoy this class at all. Each week you have to do 3 hours of reading and write a paper every 2 weeks. The lectures were a waste of time, you teach yourself everything. The lectures were extremely political and he allowed liberal students to make extremely degrading comments to conservative peers. I couldn't even listen, so disrespectful.

Prof. Selterman was great! His lectures were always interesting and class participation is easy. You could reach him through the course email but I had better luck with the TA. Definitely go to office hours. Every other week we had a paper due but it's not too bad once you get the hang of it. Final paper is big but not as intimidating as he says.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of opportunities for extra credit and the class is mainly graded on papers. there are no multiple-choice tests. he doesn't grade anything himself and there's no real way to reach him. his email is set up so it goes to his TAs.

Really loved him and lectures were great! I took this course online and participation matters because he uses polls. Overall as long as you attend lectures and turn in work on time, you should be fine.

The class is easy, and isn't too hard to do well in. However, the professor is very hard to deal with. Nice enough during lecture, but rude and dismissing if approached outside of lecture for one-on-one. If everything goes well in the class, class is a joke. If you need his help with something, get ready to be dismissed and ridiculed

THERE ARE INTERACTIVE ACTIVITIES, SO ATTENDANCE IS MANDATORY. GOOD THING IS, ATTENDANCE IS USUALLY ONCE INSTEAD OF TWICE A WEEK FOR EACH GROUP. HARD GRADING ON SCIENTIFIC ANALYSIS PAPERS IF RUBRIC IS NOT FOLLOWED. TERM FINAL PAPER IS A BIG DEAL. CHOOSE TOPIC AND DRAFT IT EARLY ENOUGH. GREAT COURSE! GREAT INSTRUCTOR AND TAs. VERY HELPFUL VIA ZOOM.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Selterman really'a that bad and I would def take one of his classes again. Lectures once a week and discussion once every two weeks, clickers in lecture so don't miss them. Papers once every two weeks but not that bad either. Nice guy and easy to contact him or the TAs when needed. Not an easy A but if you work for it it's manageable. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Selterman's class was not too hard. Discussion was every other friday and was easy. On the fridays we had off we have a short paper to write with clear guidelines. Gives lot of chances for extra credit. If you do the work it's super easy to pass. There are online worksheets and the textbook is an open source website.

Professor Selterman is endearing, knowledgable, and a great teacher. He has a great personality and all of his lectures are really interesting. Needless to say, he brings life to education. I have taken his classes before which is why I chose to take him again. If you put in effort he does the same outside of class- he's always available!

A good beginner class + lectures are recorded. If you do well on every other assignment and tests then everything balances out. 4 papers are hard especially if you have no background in reading academic journals. The final paper is unreasonable but does not take as long as said. He doesn't seem to care about his students and is teaching for tenure.

I absolutely loved this teacher. Even though the test were hard, I felt like I learned a lot in his class and he is an easygoing teacher to talk to. Going to class is mandatory because the power points he post are not finished. For me, I personally didn't think we had a lot of homework, we just had to read the textbook and do a quiz which is easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: selterman believes there is no other class besides his. The amount of work for a 100 level 3 credit class was ridiculous. He was a nice enough guy, but took the class way too seriously and made a lot of false promises when it came to extra credit and boycotting exams.

Selterman was alright. I was put off with his rants about the education system and other topics, but he is otherwise a great lecturer. Just make sure to do the weekly online quizzes and essay assignments, and you should be fine. Tests can be very wordy, but it is manageable if you understand how to apply concepts. The textbook is free.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Selterman definitely cares more about your learning than simply giving out grades. He encourages you to think outside the box. His lectures were very interesting and I never felt myself getting bored in his class. There were a few assignments I was unaware which bumped me down to a B so be careful. Good class overall though.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Selterman's amazing. There was a lot of drama about testing this semester in his class but he came up with a fair solution for everyone. The material is straightforward and he offers so so much extra credit. He posts Ponoptos and the slides on Elms, so you basically just go to class for clicker points. Good choice for an I-Series.

He gets a bad rap but honestly, he's an excellent psychology teacher. He's respectful to his students and treats us like colleagues, and he encourages inquiry. One thing to watch out for is his usual dare to the students to skip the exam. If you don't succeed the first time, don't try again. Do the work he assigns, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't see the fuss over Selterman. His course is very straightforward and as long as you do the assigned work, you'll be fine. I thought his worksheets were extremely informational but in lectures he does move very fast. Tends to go on rants about the education system which I never understood considering he's a teacher. Either way, I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If I had to go back I never would have taken this professor. He assigns a quiz a week each quiz is on a new unit of notes plus an essay every other week. He encourages students to protest exams but then sends out messages threatening to call campus police if students block doors in an attempt to protest. Hypocritical and assigns a lot of work
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: I enjoyed having Dylan as a professor. He was nice and approachable. The course material was not too hard but it was time-consuming. However, Dylan offered a lot of extra credit which was nice. Overall, he is a good professor who encourages his students to fight the system.

Prof Selterman really wants everyone to success, but his class is heavily lecture based and there are weekly papers/long worksheets. The worksheets are based off the readings in the online textbook. The worksheets aren't that hard there is just sometimes many readings , TA's grade the papers harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Preached in class the first day how the education system is flawed and how grading methods arent effective in teaching, then proceeded to dispatch his minion TAs to grade every paper with the upmost extremity. On top of this, theres a writing assignment and chapter assignment every week along with absolutely no study guide given before the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: TAs were awful, if they don't like you then you wont get a good grade. He talks about not liking grading system, but this class has one of the worst grading scales in UMD with an 94 being an A instead of the regular 93.
Tough class. Constant work. The exams are extremely difficult and have nothing to do with the lectures. Save yourself the pain and take another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: sa's easy. class good. selty daddy is sum hotstuff, especially when he has the scruffy beard, i wish he would keep the scruff all the time.

I don't really get the hate, he literally does everything possible to help students succeed. All lectures are recorded, you can make a cheat sheet for exams, the "textbook" is free and for the most part, homework answers came directly from the textbook. And follow the rubrics for the SA writing assignments and you should get an A on them.

I've heard a lot of bad things about Dylan, but he's definitely one of the best lecturers I've had. His lectures are PREPARED, CLEAR, straightforward, and interesting. Worksheets and SA's are simple and just require effort. Exams are very fair. He's an all around good lecturer to be honest.

As long as you put in basic effort, you should do well. I would sometimes spend a few hours and get 3-4 assignments done so I wouldn't have to do any outside work for that class for a few weeks, saved me so much stress! Highly recommend him, one of the easiest classes I have taken.

I took this class as my science credit. The online textbook is efficient very easy to use. We only met once a week so there was a LOT of work out side of class. The work wasn't difficult but it did take a significant amount of time. Assignments are very straightforward and fit the rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Gets such a bad rep. but tbh he was a great prof. He made it clear that he genuinely cared about students and improving our education system, and encouraged students to rebel against exams to seize control of our own education. Extremely tough grader, but just put in the work and ask for help. This class is manageable if you actively help yourself.

Had him for an intro to Psychology course and there wasn't a whole lot required of you, you just had to show up for clicker questions and do online 50 point quizzes every week and a short essay every other week. You'll get a good grade if you put in the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Actually one of the worst professors. His class is okay but he is rude and doesnt care about helping you. Good luck if you have to take his class lol. He went out of his way several times to make sure that i didnt get a good grade despite getting As on all of my work
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I loved his lectures. This was still the most interesting and engaging class I took this semester- I wish I could take it twice. The class wide discussions delved deep into different topics. He is apparently bias towards his beliefs sometimes, so he'd either preach his opinion or be objective. It was all thought-provoking regardless.
Talks about not liking grading system but grades really hard. Boring class. A lot of work. Kind of hard to get a hold of sometimes. I'd take another prof if you could

Selty was a very tough grader. He spent so much time talking about rebelling against "the system", but yet he changed the grading system so a 94% is an A instead of a 93% like every other class. He also doesn't round up grades which sucks because you could be fractions of a percent away from passing and he won't help you out. :(

Dylan explains things in his lectures well. He also offers lots of extra credit. But this class is a lot of work for an introductory psych class. There are papers every other week, three exams, in-class assignments, and a big final term paper. The TAs take FOREVER to grade and they grade harshly. You can do well, but you will really have to work.

Dylan is a great professor and makes the class really interesting. He encouraged us to boycott our 2nd exam, letting us do an assignment of our choosing instead. He also made the final optional, so I just took one exam, wrote a paper, and wrote easy weekly reflections (where you basically get full credit for writing about your feelings). Fun class.

Nice guy, bad teacher. Assigns essays every other week that are graded EXTREMELY harsh. Tests include paragraph long questions and "joke" answers. Discussions are useless and the TAs could care less. If you want/need to take PSYC100, take Curtis. Despite getting an A, I would not recommend him as a professor to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is bearable but just wish there was another teacher. Heavily lecture based but, he records the class so you can go back and see what was said. The exams were way different than study guides, grading took forever (with 2 TA's), long lines for office hours, very boring lectures that have notes that make no sense when you review them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The readings you do are very in depth and detailed. Do not take this class if you are not extremely interested in learning about psychology. The exams are difficult and require you to think about ideas rather than facts. He says that taking practice tests are the best way to study for an exam yet doesn't even give one because he's reuses questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Decent professor. Likes to try to cause class uprisings against exams when he gets bored. Lectures aren't bad, records them to allow them to be rewatched. Paper due every other week, online worksheet due every week. Main issue is with exams, he does not provide proper study materials for them.

I was skeptical of how my experience taking this class with Selterman would be after reading reviews. I quickly learned they were wrong. Selterman is a pretty good lecturer and only talked about himself on the first day and when asked about his research. He offers a ton of easy extra credit. Do the study guide and read the books. Interesting class.

I love Dylan. He's really great. He enjoys what he's teaching which makes the material easy to understand. Not that many assignments and if you show up to class and read the assigned chapters, you won't have to study that much for exams.

I took his PSYC100 class alongside ASTR300,330; PHYS260,261; and CHEM134. PSYC100 was far more difficult than any of my other classes. You have to fit a lot of information into a very short essay every other week, and the weekly worksheets are heavy. You cannot get by without the text. The savings graces: engaging, tests are multiple choice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Do not take a course taught by him, it's that simple. He presented blatantly false information, was extremely biased, was ineffective and had useless lectures.
