What he says in lecture is not even close to exam content, and there's nothing positive to say about my experience in his class. It was simply awful in every way to take a class he taught.

If you're even vaguely interested in psychology and have already taken PSYC100, then it's a pretty easy class. There are lots of opportunities for extra credit. He puts a lot of emphasis on the final paper but it is not as difficult of a paper as one might think, just go to office hours once or twice and you'll be fine.

Selterman is a very engaging prof. I was never bored in class. You HAVE to read the text they provide for you tho to pass. He just goes more in depth in lecture, which is also needed to pass. There are weekly writing assignments where you will fail if you use "their" instead of "there", but just proofread and you'll be okay. Overall, he's great!

Pro Selterman really loves Psychology and he is very good at it. His lectures are very interesting and the exams are more lecture-based, but as long as you do the worksheets that are given every week, you're good. He gives extra credit opportunities after exams. but he has those super hard TAs who give you as little grade as possible on essays.
Expect 0 sympathy from him or his TAs. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: If you made 7 small grammar mistakes on an assignment, prepare to lose 9.5 marks out of 20. Extremely unfair grading, even English classes don't grade as severely as him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you go to class and follow the rubrics for assignments carefully, this class should be fairly easy. He gives extra credit to get missed back points on tests, the class is extremely interesting and you learn things that actually apply to life, which makes the lectures more desirable to go to. He also gives deadline extensions on papers if needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Any positive review you see on here was almost certainly written by Selterman himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Nice enough guy, terrible teacher. Skip this one if you can.
He made the class very difficult for no good reason. Made the tests nothing like what was taught in class. Talks about and brags about himself way too often. Would NOT recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He's an amazing professor and he really cares about students actually learning the material rather than the grade. Beware of papers though! There are a lot of papers for this class and make sure you know how to cite because he's a real hard ass about those. Other than that, the class was super interesting and  I would definitely take it again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Doesn't care about students AT ALL. Encourages students to come see him outside of class to talk about personal and/or academic issues, yet he doesn't respond to emails until 2-3 days later. Very arrogant, cold, and full of himself. His lectures on content were great, and I even changed my major to psyc after his course, but would not rec.
He really doesn't care if you struggle with the course... and wouldn't meet outside class when asked. Highly suggest to take the course with a different professor

Easily one of the most egotistical human beings I have ever come across. His jokes are scripted and rehearsed. He repeatedly criticizes the concept of students aspiring to earn high grades instead of focusing on learning, yet he makes students jump through hoops to earn a respectable course grade.

I absolutely love Dylan! He's an amazing and brilliant professor. He really brings psych to life. He's also really clear about what he wants with everything, but make sure you follow his instructions exactly.

Class is unnecessarily difficult. I literally listened to this man go on a rant about how much he thinks universities should abandon their grading policy, and then his class turned out have the harshest grading system. He often says you can study the material and still not do well on the exams. Good lectures but too many obstacles that can hurt you

This man makes you think that you understand the material during lectures and discussion, but then gives you an extremely hard exams that discuss the topics gone over in lecture but in much more detail than discussed in lecture. Take Kurtis.

Dylan's intro psychology class is great, as long as you actually want to learn about psyc and are willing to work hard.  His writing assignments are graded really hard, but his tests are pretty easy (he lets you bring notes).  You can tell he really cares about what he does, and I think he's a pretty rad professor.

He's a great lecturer, very professional and kind. He's younger so he's pretty understanding and friendly. For this class if you didn't read you will not do well, and especially for this class he is a tough grader and he makes sure that the TA's are tough graders also. You WILL write a lot of papers and don't expect a good grade on the first one.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Selterman is awful. One of the worst professors I have encountered at the University of Maryland. TA for 221 was absolutely awful, but it doesn't surprise me. The apple doesn't fall far from the tree. Negative and mean in grading papers. No constructive criticism, just types whatever he's feeling. So rude and I hope I never encounter him again.

This class was very interesting and the material was very applicable. Selterman is also a great lecturer as well as extremely nice and caring. The exams are pretty specific in which you have to pay attention in lecture and read the books. He also gives a ton of extra credit.

Selterman is nice, but this class is not an easy A, you definitely need to put in the effort. There are clicker questions almost each class which count for participations points, not accuracy. He words the questions on his exams very oddly, and it makes it way more difficult than it should be. If you go to him for help, he is really helpful.

Fun class, and solid instructor. You will always be given everything you need to get an A. Helpful and willing to help, plus there are several opportunities for extra credit. Beware of the fact that the final exam and final paper are worth 45% of your grade. DO NOT slack off because you've received a good grade all semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is really a great guy and class is always entertaining. But his term paper is incredibly difficult and his tests are hard too. His tests are hard in the way that you can study all the info, but the questions are tricky like the SAT, you don't know which answer is right.

Your grade in the class is basically determined by the 3 exams given and a paper. He is very knowledgable in what he teaches. This course is pretty difficult in terms of being a general education course. Don't expect an easy A with the curriculum change.

Took his psyc 100 class which I did not do too bad in. Took his 221 class and did horribly. It was a combination of tough grading (got almost 25% off an assignment for putting "and" not "&" in a citation), tough tests, and me just not being interested. My advice is if unless you are a psyc major, avoid this prof at all costs for your own sake.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Though his lectures are intriguing, the course is way too difficult then it needs to be. Exams are very rigorous, with most mean scores around 50-60%, weekly online quizzes that are time consuming, essays that are graded harshly by TA's, and little opportunity for extra credit. Also, his exams aren't curved and he is often not approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Okay, so Dr. Selterman is a good professor make no mistake about it. However, his class is hard af. WAY TOO MUCH WORK FOR A GENED. You need to read alot from the textbook and then do a writing assignment every other week. The exams are extremely hard and he doesn't curve them nor does he change grades. This class will screw up your GPA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is just very average. Selterman is a fine lecturer, and does present the material in accessible ways, but he can be pretentious. Don't expect to win an argument against him about a grade or even criticize him, because like others have been saying, he's always right. Blended learnings aren't as big as a nightmare as they seem.

Great lectures and he's very helpful during office hours.  Lectures are discussion based and casual, exams are pretty difficult but he provides review guides. Power points are kind of hard to follow if you don't go to class. Keys to doing well in this class: showing up, asking for help, and starting the paper early.
He was not clear regarding how much certain  assignments affect grades and took the class way to serious for a gen ed course.

Be prepared to do A LOT of online reading from the open source textbook. If you are not interested in the material it will be a huge drag, but I did not mind because I liked the topics we were studying. Class was fun and interesting, Selterman was very friendly in office hours. It was a good GenEd class, made my semester fun.
Such a great professor for online class, clear cut and I expected a bad grade on my final paper and got a 100%.  IF YOU READ THE TEXT/BLOGS U WILL GET AN A.

I really loved this class. Some other people on here claim he's a tough grader but I  never received a grade I didn't think was fair/accurate. He's very personable and supportive of students- on the first day he said that you could come to his office just to talk about life & if you're 21 you could get a drink with him. Offers tons of extra credit.

Very knowledgeable, interesting lecturer. He is very helpful - posts lecture recordings and slides online, and is very helpful during office hours. This class is very doable, but take it seriously. Papers took effort, but tests were easy; never did the readings
He was not helpful at all and my grades in the class did not match my effort. I would not take that class again

He is a very good lecturer, and he knows what he is talking about. He, however, is a very tough grader, who makes no exceptions. I received a 0/20 on my first blended learning assignment, because I did not turn it in as a pdf. Having said that, he does provide some extra credit.

Selterman is a great lecturer, however he is a very  tough grader. Even if you have an A all semester and you get a B or C on the final paper, your grade will probably drop as well.  as it's worth 30% of the final grade.

This was a very mediocre class for me in terms of content, professor, and difficulty level. Selterman is a good professor. He's very clear and accommodating but not exciting to listen to. Everyone complains about the BL assignments but follow his guidelines and you will be fine. Tests are very fair. Do the extra credit stuff!!

I took both PSYC221 and PSYC334 with Selterman. 334 was easier by far because there were no blended learnings and the course material was not all over the place. Tests are easy and the only big assignment is the final paper. Good class for your major, take it.

Selterman is the Ted Mosby of social psychology. He's a great lecturer but your grade is entirely in the hands of the TA. His tests are easy but the Blended Learnings can seriously hurt your grade if you don't get them proofread by a TA before handing them in. I highly recommend the course b/c it's what got me to change my major to psych.

This is a neat class. But its a logistical nightmare. Dylan is a good lecturer however how he grades his class sucks. The blended learning papers are impossible to ever get a decent grade on. 1 mistake and you have an 85 on it. His final paper is extremely difficult and he makes things due at odd times like 5pm.

It's a great class for the content, but how the professor bases grades is absolutely ludicrous. Between the blended learning assignments and the final paper your grade is pretty much dead. The papers get graded super harsh and the exams aren't weighted much at all. It's a neat class, but a logistical nightmare. If you take it get another professor.

Dylan is a great teacher he is young and relevant and has a lot of knowledge. The class was very interesting and he kept the class's attention. He was willing to help any time and was accommodating. And a plus was he was rather attractive.

Very interesting class. Toughest grader I've ever had. The man knows his stuff and definitely explains it well, but no matter how much effort you put into the blended learning assignments, you get a D. The other day he posted the class averages for those and it was a D average. Tests are fair.

Dylan is a good teacher and he knows his stuff very well. but he should be writing for a psych magazine than being a teacher. his essays and blending learning assignments seem easy but i never got anything more than a D on them. and his ta's do not help at all. i put in so much effort in the final paper but i still got a D.

I took a class with him before this one and enjoyed it. He's a good teacher and always prepared, BUT he is always right. He thinks he's better than he really is. His grading system for blended learnings are impossible and his TAs are no help what so ever. He does not know how to control his TAs or his grading system.
Awesome professor! So nice. Just pay attention and go to lecture
One of the best professors I had. The course is very interesting though there is a lot of material and topics. I recommend this course. He's also so cute!

Awesome teacher.  Takes in interest in his students.  Lectures are interesting.  Exams are fair if you study for them.  He has multiple choice and a few free responses.  Attendance isn't graded but he tests both the book and lecture (lecture has materials book doesn't sometimes). Overall all amazing professor.  Highly recommended

In my opinion, Professor Kuz was a great instructor. Her teaching methods helped us not only understand certain concepts, but cleared up why they exist. There is lots of homework but to be honest that's what you need to practice math. Overall caring and wonderful professor, would take again.

Terrible if you are not the best with math, or not the best test taker. Over half of the final grade is exams, which feel like they are on a whole other level compared to the work we do inside and outside of class. She seems like she believes we should all be math experts although many of us are just taking this class as a requirement.

The professor is great. The lectures are clear and the explanations are great. The exams are easy if you prepare and learn the material. The homework is hard but it is a great way to prepare for the exams. If you are a math or a heavy math major she is awesome.

I went to receive help on homework for Calc 1, and THREE graduate students worked together and still had to look up how to do it. Lectures give no where near the information needed to complete homework. Practice exams do NOT line up with the actual exams whatsoever. If you can, wait to take Calc with a different Prof.

Professor Kuz was by far the worst instructor I've ever had. To start, she gives about 10+ hours of homework a week, but none of it is remotely close to what we learned in lecture. Exams are even worse though, they aren't similar to the homework or the lectures, so its honestly impossible to do well on them, but they are worth 20% of your grade.

This professor is terrible. I cannot understand a thing she says. She moves way too fast in lecture, talks quietly, and teaches in a confusing way. The quizzes (written by TAs) are easy, but the exam is harder than any practice or homework problem. She said the exams would be 5 questions--it was 5 questions with 10 lengthy parts. Avoid this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took elementary numerical analysis with this professor and it is honestly awful. She knows what she's talking about, however she teaches the material extremely fast and it is hard to follow the lecture material. For this high level math course I would steer clear.

Avoid at all costs. A low average exam score will be met with "the class didn't study hard enough". Do not schedule a class after one with her. Every lecture went beyond the time limit by almost 5 mins, due to the first half of class being the previous day's material. Even one absence will take a disproportionate amount off your attendance grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Class is structured in a way that allows you to retain the material. She obviously knows what she is talking about and is very kind. If you have to take calc, take it with her.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Only graded quizzes and test. I got 100% attendance and didn't miss an assignment and failed 1 of the 3 tests and got a d. If you are a good test taker take her class if you aren't she doesn't teach anything and you are just stuck with nothing to help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very nice professor. Does a good job at explaining the concepts and is always willing to take extra time after class to help students. Posts notes covering lecture material with good explanations on ICON. I usually found the textbook material confusing but would actually find it useful after she covered the material in lecture.
She's very nice and teaches well! Slight accent but you get used to it. Very helpful

Professor Kuz is overall an excellent teacher. She guides you through the lesson very well, and puts all the notes you need right on the board. She typically gives quizzes about once a week, and they are sometimes take-home. Professor Kuz is always willing to help, and has flexible office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you're in this class you're probably not so good at math, like me, but she really is a great teacher who will help you through it. At times slow, but that's just because she's so good at explaining the material. Homework after every class but easy and short (takes like 15-20 mins). Test are easy and basically the practice exams. Minimal effortA

Awesome teacher/ class for math. She does have an accent, but she writes EVERYTHING you need on the board. Gives a lot of optional homework that helps you understand, but not graded. Tests aren't hard, and she gives you lots of sample/ practice beforehand. Tells you when quizzes are, so you don't have to go to class but the notes help a lot.

Professor Kuz was a phenomenal teacher. All of the course content was explained very well and organized. She was extremely thorough and calm (easy to follow and listen to). All of my questions were answered and explained well. This was my first year of math that I did not have to go to tutoring. My favorite and most enjoyable math class ever.
She is really nice, sometimes her explanations can be confusing but she genuinely wants you to understand. If you go to reviews with her it is VERY helpful!

She is actually such a sweet person and genuinely wants you to succeed. She can be a tad sharp sometimes but i think thats just her culture. DO THE HW and DO WELL ON QUIZZES. Def go to math help and exam reviews. Should be a solid class but I shouldnt have slacked off so much
Very clear (sometimes too clear) and gives great notes! You should have no problem if you attend all of the lectures
She is mean.
Great professor. Really tech savvy and super helpful.

He is incredibly knowledgeable and helps you produce wonderful designs. He gives just enough structure to give you direction and gives great feedback/ helpful notes. He can help you solve any Sketchup issue!
The Photoshop, illustrator, and lumion assignments take a long time but he gives specific instructions and is very helpful/knowledgeable.

LARC160 is the worst class I have ever taken at UMD. The lectures are painfully dry. After the first 2 weeks I stopped going. For the Exams its multiple choice, but he lets you pick more than one answer, and justify why in the margins. This may sound nice but it is the worst test format I've ever encountered. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ellis' class was an easy A, like almost too easy. You really don't need to go to lecture, but go to discussion and do the discussion assignments, and you will legit get an A. It was really boring, but a good easy A for GenEds. Just do better than a 75% on exams, and you should be way more than fine.

Interesting lectures.  They are very different from the book. The exams aren't bad but multiple guess isn't my strong suit.  Go to all the discussions though and you are guaranteed to pass with at least a B. My TA took us out on the campus almost every class period. She was awesome.
This class was really interesting actually. Super easy. Just do the assignments each week. I'm so glad I took this class man. My british TA was the absolute best! So chill. Take this class!

Note: The course selection was unavailable, I took  BUSO 601: Finance I with her in the spring of 2024 for the OMBA program. 

It's very clear that at one point in time she was probably a terrific professor. However, she is not anymore. Terrible lectures, did not get money's worth $/credit. Astonishingly unprofessional.

Her voice is really annoying and lectures are painful to sit through. Her exams are easy though because she tells you exactly what will be on them in the exam review session. There are a ton of HW assignments that are pretty random so they are tough to do at times. Overall a good grade is attainable but class is not fun and you don't learn much.

This professor did not understand the concept of time management. She would spend 80-85 minutes of a 90 minute class going through slides that were exactly what the textbook said. Then she would try to cover 3-5 practice problems - the part everyone needed the most help with - in the last 5-10 minutes of class. This class requires office hours.

Although this class did have a lot of homework, however, it's manageable. Professor Kiss is an amazing professor and really wants you to understand the concepts! You won't regret taking this class with her!

Kiss is a tough but fair teacher. She really walks you through what will be on the exam, making it not as bad as it could be. The group project sucks a lot but canvas showed that she gave everyone an A when there were some bad presentations. There is some tough homework but its a fair and manageable class that shouldn't be too bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her voice takes a bit of getting used to. She moves fast through lectures. You need to practice your problems a lot. She makes herself available and responds to email promptly. I would recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She is a great professor. She responds to questions and ready to help. She's a decent grader. Her final is tough but do-able. The lecture is very very boring, but what do you expect for Finance? Overall, I definitely take her again.
Her voice is the most annoying voice I may have ever heard. She is annoying and I hate coming to class, also gives a lot of hw
She was extremely helpful in the class. As long as you show up, do the problems, and participate, you should succeed and learn a thing or two!
Has vast real world experience in banking. Makes great effort to help students learn the real world of finance. Definitely worth taking her class in Banking and Financial Institutions.
Ok class.  The reason it is easy is because she tells you exactly what will be on the exams.  The reading and the homeworks make it a good deal of work.

Took the graduate level version of Banking & Financial Institutions. Great class, but had ridiculous amounts of reading. She has decades of real world experience and I learned quite a bit (and Ive worked at a bank for several years)
No Comments

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR IF POSSIBLE. Prof. Eldredge is friendly and wants her students to do well, but there is way too much work. I have spent around 7 hours on her assignments every week. She expects way too much. 316 has around 5-6 assignments due a week, along with big semester projects such as a power point, translation pages, and a portfolio.

So I've had her twice & I'm traumatized. Her teaching style is no-nonsense & she doesn't play at all. She will assign loads of work, grade it in detail, rapid fire questions in class, & make you participate. Please don't take her unless you're willing to put 110% time & effort into every assignment. That being said, she really wants you to succeed
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Stay away. She is a very tough grader yet doesn't let you see your overall grade. She expects students to teach themselves the material by reading and answering essay questions due every class. There is so much hw; you can see she doesn't value students' time or sanity. Attend every lecture, take a mental screenshot of the PPTs, and talk nonstop.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE 316 if you value your sanity!!! It's been a year since I took it & I'm still not over the trauma. So much work (12 hours / week), please take 311 with a chill professor instead. Rapid-fires questions in class, I felt like I couldn't breathe. Hard to figure out what the homework is. She is insane & will tell you this class is difficult

Prof. Eldredge's ELMS page is VERY disorganized. It's so hard to figure out what the homework is and when it's due, and she gives SO much homework. Spanish is my minor, but I found myself doing more work for her class than the classes for my actual major. She randomly calls on you in class, so make sure u actually do the hw so u dont look stupid.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Loved HIST110 so much, lectures were easy to understand and Dr. Connor made sure that assignments and class info was communicated. Lots of lectures and slideshows, but you are able to look back and use them during quizzes and for midterms. Loved this class so much and appreciate Dr. Connor for a great semester. Would recommend!

She is a good teacher and really knows the information. You don't really need to go to class, you just need to use the lecture slides for the exams. There are 3 midterm exams and a term paper, all require a lot of writing and are graded very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Well, I do not know why they have her in here as Elizabeth Conners but this is for Dr. Elizabeth Connor. She is so kind, so sweet. She genuinely wants her students to pass. You can turn things in late, revise papers after they are graded for a better grade. Her lectures get a little "rambly" but she is always available outside class

When it comes to lectures and their content Eoin was quite solid and answered questions. However, the last 2 exams were unreasonably difficult (Exam #3 had a 52% average) and did not receive a curve. The first two exams had good averages and were quality exams though. He ended up curving the final grade as well after threatening not to.

Started off a bit rocky, but he communicates his expectations well. If you seek help and guidance you will pass the class, very interesting lectures. If you pay attention and practice outside of class and attend discussions you will pass. Highly recommend. Mackall The Saint!
As long as you do your due diligence he knows what he's talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Cool guy, but a bad math teacher. The whole class was failing and he still refused to give us a curve. Only grades are four tests and one cumulative homework grade. Lectures sucked, you have to teach yourself using the textbook. Super hard class when it shouldn't have been. Take someone else, take Washington he actually wrote the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honest to god, I've never done worse in a math class. His lectures are average, but he only has four grades for the entire semester. Not only does it seem like more than half of the class is failing, but he refuses to scale tests . He seems very chill and laid back, but his grading system is ass.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have 2 grades in this class: homework and exams. The homework is helpful in learning the concepts, but the exams are NOTHING like the homework and you aren't prepared for them at all. Lectures can be pointless, sometimes he makes everything more confusing. Take a different professor if math isn't your thing.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I would not recommend taking this course with this professor. He is a smart individual, but I found his lectures to be conceptual in a way that made the material very difficult to understand. Important to know- tests are taken over zoom (I took this class entirely online), exams aren't curved, and the textbook is super helpful.

He answers virtually any question and his primary goal is to ensure that you actually learn something. He will even tell you whats wrong with your work for graded assignments.

reviews.comment: All the assignments are reasonable and the text book is extremely helpful. The class isn't too time consuming.

Great professor. This class is kind of difficult. It was also my first college math class, so I definitely think I could get an A if I hadn't taken this as my first college math class. He was a great professor, it took a little while for me to really understand it, so take it seriously from the beginning
Teddy wible told me to do this.

Her son told me to do this

reviews.comment: She is a great and engaging professor. She talks super-fast because we have so much to cover. Concepts are difficult, as are some of the readings but if you work hard, you should learn a lot. Semi-tough grader but I hope to do better on the next paper! Lots of groupwork, interesting discussions. Enjoyable!

I took Prof. Enos during his brief stint of teaching at Georgia Southern. 
1. Attendance is taken for a grade. You need to show up anyways to really understand the readings outside of class.
2. READ WHAT HE ASSIGNS.
3. Show up, read outside of class, and take decent notes while in class. Guaranteed B for a class. You can get an A if you pursue it.

Overall, good prof. He assigns readings outside of class, but they're relatively easy to understand. DO THEM!! If he assigns them, there will be a pop quiz over them the day it's due. Take good notes! Exams are completely free response.

reviews.comment: Great teacher overall! Just make sure to apply yourself firmly in his class, be on time to class and with work, and be there everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This guy is awesome. I don't know if he's still at UMD, but he was able to explain rather difficult concepts in a very clear and concise manner. Super knowledgeable and seemingly experienced enough to address any possible question a student could have pertaining to the course.

Loved him! Very caring and understanding & truly wants to see you succeed. There were short easy quizzes for attendance, 2 papers, & 2 exams. His office hours are very helpful, he'll give you feedback on your essay before turning it in. The class did get a little boring though when people didn't participate but that's not super on him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Be prepared for weekly reading and in-class discussions. Dr Enos is great at responding to emails and answering in-depth questions. He is very knowledgeable about philosophy. I tried to take another class with him, but each class was full. Great guy, very fair, and also has an interesting personal backstory. Be sure to participate , it counts!!

reviews.comment: Professor Enos is a super cool guy, he knows the material super well and understands it might not be the most interesting thing to you. He likes class discussions so try to have an opinion on everything, even if you disagree with him. Essays are easy because he will give you help if you go to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Honestly, one of the best professors I've had here. The reading material is dense, however, he goes over the material in class which makes it so much easier. There is about one pop quiz every week which are easy and based on the powerpoint he just read. He's a really down to Earth guy and is always willing to work with you, not against you.
Very easy to talk to, very passionate about subject matter, and gladly will repeat himself if someone doesn't understand
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If doing the most was a person. Participation matters cause he gives weekly quizzes doesn't tell you when and has like no words on his PowerPoint, so go to class. Essays were hard to do because there are not enough sources for you to do it in an efficient manner. Homework was a lot of reading for no reason. Cool dude tho.

reviews.comment: Dr. Enos is a very knowledgable, has office hours 3x a week (although this is subjected to change), very open to helping his students. Lectures are a bit hard to understand, he has very few words on his slides, so it is important to go to class and listen to what he says not whats on the board. Has in-class quizzes so read the readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Casey is easily the best professor I've had at UMD. He is very passionate about the subjects he teaches. Super cool guy too. He also gives great feedback and is super accessible. If you have any questions about the stuff you're learning in class you can pass by his office hours and he will gladly explain it to you. Very fair grader too.

Professor Enos is a great teacher who cares deeply about his students. He is extremely reasonable and accessible, answering questions during class and after. He also always challenged me to improve my writing and presentations in a respectful and thoughtful way. One of the best teachers at UMD, and this was one of my favorite classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Iv'e had Casey for three classes now, and he is by far one of the best professors I've had at UMD. Cares about his students, wants everyone to get a decent grade, and is super accessible outside of classes. One of the few professors who responds within hours, and is willing to meet up pretty much anytime if you have any concern with the content.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Casey Enos is an excellent professor. He cares a lot about his students and shows that by having long office hours multiple days a week and he is always accommodating and kind. I also had him for PHIL 271 and he was the same in this regard. He is passionate about the content and inspires you to work very hard. Be sure to participate in class.

Professor Enos is awesome. He clearly wants every student to succeed and hes super reasonable if you put real effort into the class. Most of the workload involves reading papers that are pretty complex but he does a great job at clarifying things in lecture. The major assignments are easy as long as you pay attention in class and do the readings.

So its not an easy class, but what do you expect from 400 level? Casey is very reasonable, flexible, and ACCESSIBLE. Never have I had a prof more willing to work with students outside of class time and coursework. Genuinely cares about students and gives constructive feedback. Very knowledgeable. Just do the work to do well. Take adv of this GEM!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: TBH Casey is one of the best professors at the University. Not only does he care about his students doing well, but he goes above and beyond to help. The class isn't entry level and as such, you will have to read and participate. But it's not impossible. I have taken multiple classes from him and I can say that I recommend him 100% you won't regret
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have had at UMD. The only professor to treat philosophy papers like research papers. He is obsessed with sources and citations more than the content of the paper. He also leaves rude comments as feedback.

PHIL271 isnt easy, esp. if you havent taken PHIL170, but Casey is very accessible (office hours almost every day and all materials posted online) and is willing to work you through homework questions. Plus, there are extra credit opportunities. He also can advise you on other courses. Great instructor who rises to the students desire to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was ok. I felt like there was a bit of a learning curve if you've never taken an online class or a phil class. and those points, in the beginning, can definitely come back to bite you later. There weren't clear rubrics for papers and the class didn't make a lot of sense in the long run. If you've never taken a PHIL class, skip this one.

Casey is one of the best professor's I've ever had. PHIL261 was a partially online class that became fully online b/c of covid. Casey handled it all amazingly, always on top of things and very responsive. Passionate about philosophy and is a great person. Wish I had more of Casey and less of the TA. No pointless busy work which was very appreciated
really enjoyed this class. easy to engage to and not too stressful
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: As an engineering student, I took phil170 as a gen ed. Professor Enos runs circles around any professor I have had in my major. He actually wants his students to succeed. Quizzes in class are 1 question. Exams are extremely reasonable. Around exams he increases office hours. (around the final he holds office hours every day for a week)
Best professor I've had at UMD

Casey Enos is the absolute best professor I've had at UMD. Many people say that his classes are hard to be 100 level and it worried me but I was fine. He welcomes everyone to his office hours and I've stayed for an entire day before. The class sets you up for success as long as you put in the work. It was a fun class and he was an amazing teacher.

Professor Enos is fantastic, easily one of the best professors I've had. I am not particularly interested in logic, but he taught the class with such passion that I found myself enjoying the class more than I expected. While some of the concepts are a bit challenging, tests were very reasonable, and he is quite willing to help outside of class.

Enos is a great professor. He is the most passionate professor I have ever had, and he truly cares about how well the class does. The material is not very demanding, and the tests are not difficult at all. I really enjoy his teachings and he makes the lectures interesting and interactive.
A great option for intro students and up! A cool guy for sure.

He is very caring and accessible outside of class, bring any questions (doesn't even have to be related to class, can be about the department or philosophy over all), he'll happily discuss with you. The class has quite a lot of reading but I think they were all interesting.
Great philosophy professor. Readings are interesting and so are the lectures. A lot of discussion and loves to hear your opinion. Would definitely take his course again
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Taking PHIL170 over the break was definitely worth it. Mr. Enos gives his students more than enough material to excel in the class. Between his lengthy supplemental notes and even home videos, it is clear that he wants his students to succeed. Mr. Enos also provides timely feedback and holds four hours of online office hours daily. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Lectures are boring. Enos is kind, often talks about his cat. Loves teaching philosophy, if youre interested in it.

Casey is the best professor I've ever had. He really wants you to learn the material and do well. His lectures are interesting and he's a funny guy. He loves to get to know his students! You can talk to him about anything . The workload is also light, weekly quizzes that are easy if you read the material , and 3 quick papers. 10/10 would retake.

Professor Enos is a grad student, and PHIL100 is the first class he taught at UMD. I took it online over winter break (15 day semester). There were daily quizzes, 4 discussions, and 3 papers. He gave great feedback, and if you did better on the final paper than the first, he would curve your first grade. Great class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Jonathan is by far the chillest professor I've ever had. His class is really informative but light. He's kind of disorganized so be prepared to take assignments as they come. LOVES chic-fil-a and is easily the funniest professor at UMD. Couldn't recommend his classes enough.

An amazing professor in every aspect. He clearly shows care for the well being of students, and is always looking for ways to make life less stressful. He is able to teach in a way that doesn't make learning feel forced, but rather the knowledge comes naturally and in a fun way.

I had Professor England during Spring 2020 so I didn't see him the whole semester but during the time I did see him, he was a great professor overall. He cared about what he was talking about and wanted the student to learn the ideas rather than be tested on it. A bit unorganized but it was a pretty unconventional semester so I didn't mind at all.
Professor England is a cool guy and if you do your work you should do well in the class. He is very entertaining and would highly recommend people take his class. (just be ready to give quality work)
Professor England is so funny and he makes the material actually interesting and easy to understand! Definitely one of the best professors I've had at UMD. Final is not cumulative.
He is an awesome person! I didn't like him as a professor. Lectures are hard to understand and follow. The material is not presented clearly. This is not an easy A course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Funny, smart, knows his material like none other. my fav professor of all time. expect an B or A in this class.  -if u r from Baltimore, get ready to get hated on - get this man some Chick-Fil A

super cool teacher! relatively easy papers, quizzes, tests and material. Gives out free candy and makes material super interesting. The funniest professor I've ever had (wanted to name his son Jon-Quan) Definitely take this class, easy A if you put in the work. Don't be a bama though

Super cool professor! Easy class where you don't really have to do the readings. Funniest guy ever (wanted to name his son Jon-Quan) definitely take this class. Easy papers, quizzes, and assignments Gives out free candy and makes AASP fun. Don't be a bama though.

Best professor ever. Took him my freshman year and I'm a senior now. No one can top Jonathan. He is so funny. Class doesnt even feel like class. I was enrolled in his other class and was so mad that I had to drop it because of my work schedule. If you dont like chick fila when starting the class you'll def like it by the time you leave lol. Jonatha

Awesome teacher. I took this class because it was one of the only classes left when I registered but it ended up being my favorite. Discussions are thought provoking and class is fun. He's also a really funny, all-around nice guy.
He's a great professor. Nicest and funniest person you'll ever meet. He treats his students with much more respect than we/they deserve.

I really enjoy his class he's funny. I don't mind going to class at all. Even though he jokes around a lot he sitll expects you to know the material. His papers are due whenever you want to get around to them. It's fun!

He's a great professor. He knows his material and is very entertaining. The only thing I don't agree with is his class structure. There isn't really a due date for his papers and he doesn't talk about them much so you can easily forget about them. Just make sure you refresh you memory by looking at the syllabus and checking the class page.
I can't believe he has no ratings yet... He is the best!!!! very funny guy, you'll always want to come to his lectures.
Very insightful and kept me engaged in the lectures. Assignments during the Summer Session were pretty easy he provided us with the study material for the Final

More of the same. Requires attendence, Lectures seem to come out of the blue and are often random, but does sprinkle the material for the final in them. requires two papers 1 physical geograpy 1 on cultural geography. Final is easy. Essays only have to be a few sentences plus around 50 true or false questions. Overall pretty easy class.

i swear, i think everything he says during class he thinks up walking from his office to the classroom. really cutthroat about attendance, note taking, and pretty much every petty little thing that other profs don't bat an eye at. if you're a geog major then i guess it's an easy class, but i'm not and i think he's a bit of a loon.

Eney wouldn't let me make up a midterm I missed due to sickness unless I gave him a note from the health center... only the health center doesn't give out notes. This man should not be teaching at all, much less teaching gateway-required classes. Easy prof, but takes no prisoners and gives no sympathy.
Didnt put a pen to a notebook or any other piece of paper for that matter until the final exam. An extremely nice man and an extremely easy class.

His class was fairly interesting. He gets really worked up with all things Geography and has some really weird views on things. Like how gravity doesnt exist. BUT, there are 2 tests, and the lecture before each he goes through and tells you every question. Discussion work is pretty easy and there are only like 4 assignments. Pretty easy A
Easiest A ive taken. Read the newspaper every day in class and ate breakfast. Took one page of notes. Papers were annoying but he doesnt even read them only counts sources at the end.

Good class. takes random attendance once a week. 2 8-page papers due like a month into class right at midterms which is inconvient. easy final. does go on rediculous rants, but overall a very nice prof
They don't call him Easy Eney for nothing...that's all I'm going to say.
never went to lecture but discussion is mandatory. easiest A in my life (except writing 3 papers in discussion)

He's not one of my favorite professors. He's very full of himself, goes off on wild rants that have nothing to do with that day's lecture. Be very careful when writing his essays. He will say write the essay one way, then a week later will go off saying that's not how I want the essay. I guess the information on the syllabus doesn't count!

Some of the lectures so far: talking about how great physical geography is; clarifying that there is no such thing as gravity; comparing and contrasting the historical accuracy of two movies; comparing absolute versus relative position.  A lot of athletes take this one. *hint hint*

You only have to show up for class 4 times. The two days before the test when he reads the exam AND gives you ALL the answers and the test day itself.  Likes to stand on his soap box.  He really goes off the deep end with some of his rants.
two papers,  1 final      BORING CLASS  HARD TO SIT THROUGH

I took GEOG 330, 331, and 200 I think. Hes great, super easy, bring a laptop though cuz theres not much to do :) gives all answers for tests, papers turned in early can be revised again-again for better grade. I also had him grade my internship paper [A+]. Goes on rants about how the world is ending and its our job to fix it, hehe nice guy.
Excellent teacher
Easiest A i ever got...
No Comments

Easy Eney. Write one paper and take a multiple choice final where he gives you all the answers first. The easiest classes i've ever taken. Look around the room and its athletes and Greeks. Only have to go on "attendance days"....set up a phone chain with the suckers who have his earliest class - if he takes attendance that day show up to class. If not...stay home.
What a joke of a class.

This is prof is an easy A, but the class is booooorrrrriiinnng and he is not the sharpest knife in the drawer.  I highly recommend eney for a gpa boost, but not if you are really trying to learn something

Classes don't require a lot of work.  They are relatively interesting.  Everything he asks on tests  is covered in lectures and reviewed point by point before the exam.  If you go to class you can't not get an A.

This is probably the easiest professor in college park. He gives interesting lectures, which keeps people entertained. Here is the plus side. He gives you every question he will ask on the exams and the answers, so you ALL should get A's. I highly recommend him!
This guy is a ditz.  He only has a Masters degree.  His classes are easy, but don't take his technical writing class, he doesn't know what he's talking about.
This class is easy. The test are multiple choice and he gives you the questions ahead of time.  Only thing is you have to make sure you goto all of the discussion classes.
Class invovled two papers wich can be revised over and over until you get an A.  Final exam is True/False and short answer that are given ahead of time.

The easiest class I have ever taken in my entire life at any level of education. We had one midterm which was defining terms. We had two very easy essays. The final was 2 take-home 3 page essays. It couldn't have been easier. I went to lecture maybe twice and aced it. Take this class!!!

This class was the easiest i've ever taken. The midterm and final are the exact same format- all you have to do it define terms. She gives you the lectures online so you really dont even need to go to class. There are 2 papers which are super easy. I'd definitely recommend this class!

Dr.Engel is a VERY DIFFICULT professor.  Her grading system is EXTREMELY HARD.  And to make it worse, you  don't retain much of the information.  Try to take the class with another professor if you can.  If you can't, prepare to study for this class like a difficult science course to get a decent grade.

She has very fast-paced lectures, and if you miss lecture then you should be prepared to study extra to keep up. However, she is quite generous with extra credit and puts bonus questions on every exam. She will slow down or re-explain things during lecture if you ask her to, and she is very clear in her teaching. Overall a great professor.
Griffith gives a lot of extra credit for CHEM135, to the point where I had a 102% before the final. Just make sure to do the homework, and attend class to get the free points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lots of material crammed into a small amount of class time. She gave notecards on tests which was nice. Recommend writing on a whiteboard and printing that picture out to put on the notecard. Other than that class material is posted on canvas. Discussions were kind of useless too but GO TO THE LECTURES.

She gives a lot of extra credit; her class is hard, and you should be prepared to apply yourself to the fullest extent. It's the hardest class I've ever taken, but just know you will be challenged and learn a lot if you accept the challenge. She does not curve but does "grade cutoffs.".

Dr. Griffith is a great person but a not-so-great professor. She is accessible after class and does give a lot of feedback, however, she is not very forgiving. She strictly follows her syllabus. Any late work and you will fail the class. Expect to spend 30+ hours on one report. The hardest into level class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffith Herself is a nice person, but she's not exactly understanding at all. She goes 100% by her syllabus and does not allow extensions, extenuating circumstances, or any reason besides written letters to miss a lecture (which was Friday at 3 pm and worth 5 points each) Get ready for the hardest class you will take as a freshman

There's miscommunication between the TAs and Dr. Griffith, so it's better to go directly to her. I'll admit I came out of this class with a  better grasp of writing lab reports, but I was incredibly stressed the entire semester so was it even worth it? She's a harsh grader, but approachable during office hours (always go to office hours when u can)

Professor Griffith's CHEM135 is hard, that's nothing new. But she is a great professor to do it with. She explains things REALLY well. Her PowerPoints are well made (and evidently haven't changed much over the years), and discussions sections are a MUST. Also gives a lot of little extra credit clicker questions and super generous with the curve.

Griffith's exam complexity and digression from lecture material was upsetting. I studied more for this 2 credit class than any previous class. Exams were much harder than example problems we were given. I met with her for tips on how to improve my studying since I always got good grades with my study habits, she told me to "understand better" :(
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I spent more time on this 1 credit lab than all my other classes combined. Spend 20+ hours on a report and got a 53, class average was a 50. She didn't understand how much work she was assigning. Prelab, postlab, lit assignment, notebook grades every week. Barely got an A-. Very, very nice lady... awful class.

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffith made this class bearable. While the course is rather difficult, with Dr Griffith's teaching I felt prepared for the final. Her tests were hard but fair. Class was always pretty laid back and she'd banter with the students from time to time. Overall, Griffith is an excellent professor.

Prof Griffith is a good professor teaching a bad class. CHEM135 is a very difficult class and it is pretty much impossible to make it enjoyable in my opinion. Griffith did her best to teach us the material given the short time frame to do so. I don't take any more chem classes but if I did I would take her. Shes personable and treats us w respect

reviews.comment: Griffith is the lesser of evils. She's very sweet and easy to reach. Although this class is very difficult and you definitely have to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: CHEM135 with Dr. Griffith was fantastic! She was super understanding when I couldn't come to class and she sent me pre-recorded lectures from the previous year. Her lecture material is always well-organized and accessible. Also, make sure you come to class to answer clicker questions for credit. Highly recommend!

I am working on my second bachelors degree, and of all of the professors I have had, she is by far the best. You definitely need to study for exams, but she makes sure to give you plenty of opportunities and materials to study. She gives you a ton of access to previous exams, and most of the questions on the exams were similar to the previous exams
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffith is an amazing professor. She's not a drop dead funny type of professor, but she has her moments and manages to keep the lectures interesting. She really cares for her students and understands that chemistry isn't our favorite subject (because we're engineers). The course is difficult but she makes sure that we understand it.

I took Professor Griffith for a summer Chem 135. Due to the nature of an already difficult subject being taken in an accelerated manner as a summer class, the course was inherently very difficult. However, Professor Griffith was very helpful in office hours and really wants her students to succeed.

Griffith is really sweet and readily answers any questions you have. However, her course load is very heavy, expect long lab reports every week. She expects a lot from her students and is a harsh grader, but she will let students submit a regrade request. Overall she is very clear and direct, but definitely be ready to work a lot in her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This was a hard class but the amount of skills learned by the end make it worthwhile. Dr Griffith is very good at making her expectations for every paper very clear, and she gives structured guidance and helpful feedback. She is a great professor and although she grades hard in the beginning she does want students to learn and do well.

This class is a lot work, to the point where this two credit class takes up more time out of my day then my other classes combined (I'm taking Math 141 too). Despite that, Dr. Griffith as a teacher is very caring, passionate, and clear in her expectations. She does a lot to ensure the success of her students and is helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: There is a lab report due every week of this class, which usually took hours to complete and would then be graded harshly. Be prepared to work a lot outside of this lab. reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gen Chem is not easy at all but Dr. Griffith is great at explaining topics and also very helpful in office hours. Going online with her is no problem because she is extremely organized.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffith is really great and actually cares about if you pass or fail. She's really good at explaining topics, however I believe in order to pass the tests, going to gss and discussion is almost necessary. Her really upbeat attitude helps distract from the fact that this is a hard class

Dr. Griffith is an amazing professor who likes to make sure everybody understands the material before moving on to the next topic. Her exams are difficult but not unreasonable and there is a considerable amount of homework, but the homework really prepares you for the tests. She is by far the best professor I've had so far at UMD.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Clear grading criteria--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is very knowledgeable about the course material and other fields of study. CHEM177 is lab/guest lectures to prepare you for the upcoming labs and to expose you to new disciplines from academics in that field of study. The lab reports are the main grade determining materials and are harshly graded depending on the TA's. Be prepared for lectures!

reviews.comment: This is a very difficult class and takes a lot of effort. Griffith is a very great professor though and is caring. Her exam prep is very helpful and she tells you what type of questions will be on the exam. But it is challenging and homework can take a while.

I was scared to take this class but it was really fine! Griffith gives you access to all of her past exams and keys, and she is really straightforward about what will be covered. Her question formats are usually the same every year. If you take the time to do some practice exams and check answers, and you'll ace the class.

Dr. Griffith is a great teacher who seems to know the content very well and is very good at managing the course.
