(On the final exam, we were given whole questions ahead of time!)
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Literally the BEST professor ever! Take her for gen chem! She is always available for office hours or an appointment and makes time for you. Definitely cares about students and is super nice and considerate. She is also VERY smart and knows what she is talking about. The class isn't easy but put in the work and you'll do good.

Dr. Griffith has honestly made me enjoy chem. She is so nice and cares about her students. She gives a lot of extra credit clicker points and also gives hints about exams. Before every exam, she posts the layout of our exam and multiple practice exams, which is extremely helpful when studying.
She is amazing! The grade in this class depends on the whole class's grade, so it would change after every exam, but is is definitely a HUGE! curve!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She's super likeable and the lectures are clear and easy to understand. She doesn't mind adjusting the syllabus to take certain chapters off tests, etc. There's lots of extra credit clicker questions and a HUGE curve (at one point 80 and above was an A). Given this, the tests are very difficult. The averages are in the 50s, but it evens out.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffith is amazing! She's the nicest and most approachable professor I've ever had. She walks through a ton of examples during lectures and leaves you with "challenge problems" to do at home. There's usually an extra credit clicker question about that problem at the beginning of the next class. Chem is hard, but Dr. Griffith makes it fun :)

Dr. Griffith has been one of the most amazing teachers! Her stunning approach in the classroom lecture really engages! Shes companionate and extremely helpful! Her tests are hard! Study study! Her lectures are also captivating! Dont skip class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Griffith is the best chem teacher. She is nice and caring. She talks pretty fast at times but in general, is a good teacher. Her tests are straight forward and not super difficult.

Griffith is all around lovely. She'll teach you much more than you need for her exams and you'll really master the material for CHEM135. If you take 135 in your first semester, be prepared to step up in her class. She's great at answering her emails and tries her best to answer everyone's questions in lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffith is a very nice person. She tries to make class as fun and interactive as possible. With that being said, CHEM 135 is a very difficult class, that will require you to put in a LOT of time and effort. Homework problems are required. Tests range from moderately difficult to extremely difficult, but she is a huge curver.

Dr. Griffith is my favorite professor at UMD so far. I took AP Chemistry in high school and never completely understood the material until I took CHEM135. Dr. Griffith is very organized and she truly cares about her students. She gives a lot of hints during class and allows students to access her past exams for help.

The class had clicker questions almost every class, so although attendance wasn't mandatory you would miss out on points if you skipped. The tests are insanely hard with the class average usually being around a 50%, however the entire class is curved with the B/C cutoff being around the class average.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I took AP Chemistry before and did not really pay attention in High School, but those concepts helped me a little in this class. Her exams are challenging, but if you go through the notes and practice the problems she recommend you will definitely get a high grade. She is very caring and approachable do not hesitate to visit her during office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took AP Chem before this, so I thought the class was easy. The exams are very difficult so study for them! Go to lectures and you should do well on tests
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Chem 177 lab is hard. You will be required to do lots of lab reports and pre-lab assignments that are hard. Only 2 tests are the midterm and final. Midterm is the hardest test I have taken, but if you use it to study for the final you'll pass. There is a curve on the class but you need to pay attention in lab and really work hard. Go to office hour
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very lucky to have Dr. Griffith. While her exams may be challenging, she gives students the materials and support to be able to conquer those hard problems. She is very clear about her expectations, and wants students to succeed. It is clear she works very diligently on her lectures. One of the most inspiring teachers I have ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is one of my favorite professors at UMD. Hilarious, straightforward, clear, and concise. She states her expectations, gives hints during lectures, and provides useful problems during both lecture and discussion. Her exams might be harder, but that only means that the curve is higher. Get her if you can because her teaching helped me so much.

Griffith is an AMAZING professor. Her tests are difficult, but certainly manageable if you are willing to start preparing 3-5 days (depending on how comfortable you are initially with the material). Her lectures are entertaining, she gives a lot of extra credit, and prepares you very well for her exams. I highly recommend.
This is a really hard class but a she is a great professor for it, she cares a lot about students and the subject and makes the class interesting.

Griffith is a very intelligent person, and you can tell she knows what she is talking about. However, exams are the hardest tests I have ever taken in my life. I would read the textbook and attend class and still do poorly. Previous chemistry experience will definitely be an advantage. Otherwise, the class moves too fast, and is really challenging.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good teacher. Hard content but Griffith makes it understandable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Griffith is an amazing teacher! The class moves very fast so you need to get help ASAP if you are confused. Discussion worksheets are very helpful for test-like questions. She provides materials needed to succeed (posts all lectures and past exams). Class is curved so tests are very hard, but overall grade usually won't suffer.

She's thorough. Writes step-by-step how to solve probs (legibly). Her language is clear and direct. Will answer email (faster on weekdays). Offers 3-5 points bonus on exams and in some lectures (5 pts total) which were added to exam scores. Erased lowest quiz score and doubled highest quiz score. Posts old exams. Do all her probs to get an A!!!!

Griffith is a tough professor, but if you read and do the practice problems from the textbook you will be more than prepared for her exams. She also gives you past exams, so you will know what the format will be. In addition, she gives some extra credit through top hat which will help your grade. She does curve.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Griffith is a GREAT professor! If you have to take CHEM135, TAKE HER. This is a difficult class, but her lectures are very clear and well-organized. Attend class, do the homework, attend discussion, and you will be fine.

Tests are bombs to your grade. If you have to take this class, I advise that you don't take it with other heavy workload classes, because this class was a lot of work. Although she was a decent and passionate teacher, her tests were the hardest things that I have taken. I worked my butt off for this class and still didn't do too well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: I actually found the content (quantum chemistry) of the course to be quite interesting. However, I found Dr. Griffith to incredibly vague in her lectures, where she often blasted through the intricate details. The tests are on the intricate details, as quantum chemistry is microscopic, so lacking these details is setting you up for failure.

Dr. Griffith is absolutely atrocious. She is quite vague in explaining concepts and quotes the textbook the entire class. She is knowledgable of the material, but is terrible at teaching it. She speaks incredibly fast and her tests have the reputation of being the hardest out of all the other CHEM135 professors. Do not take.

Dr. Griffith is the best professor to have for CHEM135. She's young and already has her PhD so her youth brings vitality to a hard class. She recognizes that the course is condensed into a short period of time and offers A LOT of extra credit in class so don't skip! If you put in the work, you'll get results you want. Her office hours help a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffith's lecture slides come straight out of the textbook and when she clarifies concepts, she repeatedly quotes the textbook word for word. I would not recommend taking her for any course. She is very approachable outside of class, but her class is more disorganized and difficult than the other lecturers.

This class was a mess. The guidelines for the lab reports were unclear & there were no (college-equivalent) examples provided. The reports were graded too harshly & the class was graded on few things so it was hard to do well. Also no extra credit. Try to avoid taking this class - if you are a chem major, just switch out and switch back in later.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Griffith is one of the most horrendous professors at University of Maryland. She is incredibly nice, but that does not compensate for her inability to teach. She talks ridiculously fast and does not clarify anything.

Griffith was amazing. Yes, her class seems hard at the beginning but everything she goes over is useful for the lab. All the exams are fair, all stuff we had talked about in class or had done in lab. You'll get a good grade if you spend time on your lab reports, actually try to understand them because they will help your report and in the exams.
one of bubbliest and friendliest lecturers out there, but actually sucks at teaching.

The class was very hard, but Dr Griffith taught it pretty well. If you want to do well, you're going to have to put in a lot of extra time. There's a lot of material to learn and she goes through it pretty fast, but if you don't understand something she's very easy to talk to, and wants you to do well. Note: I didn't take AP chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She goes through the lecture slides really fast so it's hard to keep up with her sometimes. Her exams are really hard. She a good person and helpful on one-to-one if you go to her office hours for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: If you know what is best for you, you will not take this course with Dr. Griffith. Even the people who did take AP Chemistry did struggle in her class.

Elizabeth Griffith is one of the nicest and most approachable professors I have had the privilege of having at UMD. She teaches incredibly effectively, but her tests achieve a new level of insanity. With that being said, the content of the class is a mess and it is not her fault.

Don't confuse "hard class" with bad professor. It's true that you should just forget about taking this class if you havn't taken AP chem. You will get your ass handed to you. However, despite talking really quickly and not being the most forgiving grader, Griffith is approachable, and teaches effectively. The class is hard but it's not her fault.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: just don't
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a great professor, but DO NOT take this class if you have not taken AP chemistry. Taking this course without having done AP chemistry is like jumping into Calculus 3 without having done Calculus 1.
Dr. Griffith knows her material, is funny and inspiring!

I enjoyed having her as a professor, but many of my classmates didn't because she taught as much material as possible in lecture and moved quickly. Discussion attendance is mandatory and helpful. If you've taken AP Chemistry, this class is a breeze. The top 25% of the class received As this year. Her tests are difficult, but they're curved as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a great lecturer and easy to learn from. She explains things very clearly and concisely and only gives you the important info. If you don't have any AP chem experience you will need to study hard but she will give you everything you need. Also go to her office hours and discussions!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The class was difficult, but it was not impossible. Dr. Griffith put all of her slides, clicker questions, and in class work online. If you are interested in actually learning, the reason why most people go to school, than this is a great class.  Dr. Griffith makes the class interesting, especially with her sarcasm. Overall, I enjoyed it and learne
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Very tough class, but mostly not her fault. A lot of information stuffed into a semester. Slides can get boring sometimes, but she usually notices and tries to wake people up sometimes. Overall good lecturer.

She's new but she definitely knows what she's doing. She gives extra credit with clicker points which is nice, and she post all lecture slides online. The class itself is hard, but if you put the effort in you should be fine, especially with the curve that she keeps you up to date on. (I also want her whole wardrobe bc it's literally perfect)

Great teacher, lecture slides, homework, and discussion worksheets are very helpful, keep up with everything and the class should be pretty straightforward. She's a really nice person and really wants you to do well in her class.

As a person she's fine but she's not a great teacher. Her presentation slides are actually pretty good but the problem is the lack of correlation between homework, lecture practice problems,  even discussion worksheets with exam problem. Point distribution on exams also do not reflect understanding. Half the class comes in with AP Chem experience.

Dr. Griffith is new but she knows her stuff. She can be mean sometimes but she's also pretty funny. She's enthusiastic but it helps to not have a very full lecture. She gets annoyed with talking and it interferes with the teaching so if you have the option go to the lecture with less people in it. All around, good professor.

knows her stuff and is excited to teach students about it. CHEM135 is tough and a lot of material to cover. tries to fit as much in as possible, not a lot of example problems in class,recommends doing problems from the book. Definitely go to office hours and discussion for extra help.  A lot nicer than she initially seems. overall good professor

Dr. Griffith is easy to talk to, she's young, understanding, and knows all the in's and out's of cheating (so beware).  Extremely difficult class if you have no background in chemistry. I recommend reading before coming to class. She never gave insight on the exact materials that are tested, forcing you to study everything.
New teacher who gets frustrated easily, and  seems to only know some of the material.
Shes young professor who is fairly new to teaching, but the exams cover way too much stuff.  on the bright side she is gorgeous and has great fashion sense.
Good new professor. Helps you a lot. Go to class

Professor Lyons was an excellent professor. I had her during my first semester of college (Fall 2022), and she was an excellent professor to transition into. The class size is small for ENGL101, so she paid attention and cared about each student. The assignments were easy and graded fair. She is excellent if you are going into your first semester.
She was super nice and very passionate about her work. As long as you try you will get a good grade in her class. She offers late credit and extra credit.
she was cool, easy to talk to, not a hard grader if you put in effort

Honestly one of my favorite teachers. She is not trying to find errors in the papers and deduct a ton of points. It's more like she wants to help you figure out how to say something useful and support it as well as you can. I enjoyed the class and I would take this professor again.

This class is overall pretty easy. We met twice a week but would get work to do on Friday with no class, easy though. She is very understanding of extensions and super nice! She gives good feedback. Super sweet lady and just wants everyone to have a good time in her class. She can get a little boring but just do the work and you'll be fine.
I took the blended class, and the online assignments could take a while. Papers were difficult to understand exactly what she was looking for. She was also a hard grader.

She is a passionate writing teacher and was always willing to meet with me to discuss class work. If you actually attend and participate your writing will improve. I think the class is hard but useful and Dr. Lyons worked to make it interesting.

The prof is very nice & sweet but I would not recommend her. It was a blended class & the 2 lectures a week were so pointless we did nothing to help us prepare for our papers. She barley gave any feedback and graded unfairly. If you are good at writing then this will be an easy A if not try another prof. & we used the yellow textbook only ONE time

Gives you criticism but is not very constructive. Not very clear on her grading criteria. The class was partially online so that's where participation points came from but was still harsh on participation grading. Lectures are boring.

I took this class my first semester as a freshman and she was a great professor. Attendance isn't mandatory, no in class work. All assignments can be done without attending class. Sometimes I wished I didn't go since it was my only class somedays and you were abe to miss 6 classes... Emily is very nice and approachable!

Prof. Bruns is an excellent professor - she clearly loves what she teaches and genuinely wants all of her students to succeed. A LOT of content is covered in her class so you really need to stay on top of the lectures and go to class, but as long as you consistently go you should be fine. Easily one of the best professors I've had at UMD.

very nice and genuine person, not too hard of a class, just tedious. she BLASTS through the slides and speaks VERY fast. When she says "i'll give you a minute" it really means 15 seconds. (I've literally put my stop watch on to time her)... it's infuriating that she is unable to slow down even for a second.

She is a really caring professor that is very approachable. She always tries her best to make lectures interesting even though the topic may be boring. Worst exam score is dropped including the final. If you put time and effort into studying and understanding the subject, the exams are fair and straightforward. One of the best bio professors at UMD

If you attend her lectures and put in the effort to study for her exams then you can get an A easily. She tries to make every lecture engaging and is a very nice person. She is great at explaining concepts and encourages you to ask questions during her lectures.

I loved Dr. Bruns - she's so sweet and genuinely wants everyone to do well. She made class interesting and gave us some fun small projects throughout the semester to break up lectures. Overall, not too much homework and the tests were fair.
She is a very nice person and genuinely cares for her students. Her lectures are engaging, however, she tends to skip through her slides very quickly, so be aware.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Such a great professor, I can't recommend enough. Her enthusiasm and passion for the environment is very clear in her lectures and she really makes the content engaging. As long as you study from the material she says/has on the PPTs, you're good!

Bruns is an amazing teacher, she really understands and is passionate about the content. Even for things I wasn't excited about learning, she made it more bearable through her positive attitude. Weekly quizzes kept me accountable and on top of the lectures, as class was asynchronous.

Bruns is a great professor. The lecture were all recordings since it was online so you can watch them anytime. Test make up most of your grade and there are quizzes basically every week so be prepared. The wording can be confusing for both quizzes and exams but it's not too hard of a class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Totally the best teacher.  Best best class I took in college so far.  I learned who I am.
gives extra credit to boost your grade. no midterm or final exam, only papers. very interesting class, learned a lot
She was so awesome I took her her again for 210. Really cool, very open minded and intelligent. I learned a LOT!

took him for econometrics and he was great! the subject itself is quite difficult but he's a really good professor so if you attend classes, you should be able to understand and pass. He's reasonable and has extra credit questions on exams. if you're ready to put in the work and learn, take him.

One of the most knowledgeable professors in the Economics Department. I found him truly inspirational because of the way he thought and how he explained the most difficult concepts. He will explain concepts multiple time if you don't understand. ECON 175 is worth taking even if you are not a ECON major, it is very heavy in terms of work, worth it!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not be fooled by the level 100 class. This class was extremely difficult and I would encourage you to avoid all costs. The class relies on lectures entirely and the lectures have little to nothing in common so it makes it so hard to understand the material. The class is left to the TA's who grade papers and observe debates in the discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Reading the slides and not giving any examples. Even you ask a question, his answer is VERY AMBIGUOUS. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS EVEN FOR CREDIT!! It's a torture. Econ 200 or Econ 201 wil be good for substitutes if you want intro to econ.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great Professor honestly. Lots of people complained that they didn't understand how they were supposed to be able to do the final, but when I asked them what they thought was so difficult, they said they never took notes. Just take detailed notes and attend lectures and the class is honestly pretty easy.

Connected with students very poorly, never mentioned a homework or exam in class at all! Left everything to TAs, Syllabus was inaccurat Hes clearly VERY smart but I wouldnt recommend Econ 175 until Kap can understand that its a gen ed. In addition, the TAs were not helpful at all. Everyone in the group me of 60+ people had the same reaction.

Kaplan posts all of his lecture slides online to the ELMS course and they are exactly what is discussed in class. That is a huge plus. Other then that the guy is moderately interesting and certainly personable enough. I will say lectures sometimes can get really boring. If you're willing to put in hard work then he will be a great professor.

Don't take this class if you expect an easy A or even B. Lectures are impossibly boring and assignments are often vague and unrelated to course material. The debates are easy enough to receive a good grade but are ultimately a waste of time. You can learn just as much from the posted slides as you can from the lectures. Final exam is mainly essays.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Kaplan is a very nice man, but runs a very unorganized course with very vague directions/grading. His class is very lecture heavy, and he doesn't go into depth about upcoming assignments. Classes are fairly boring and the discussion portion of the course is pretty pointless with annoying debates. Fairly easy B, but difficult to earn an A

Ethan is very knowledgeable and a good professor. You will learn a lot from him but his grading is so gray for this class. He would not give any rubrics and when asked about his grading he would give vague answers. Good class to learn but don't expect any help on grading.
Gave a final paper and a final exam for a honors seminar, don't know any professor that does that especially for an honors seminar.
Really great native speaking teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Somewhat harsh grader, however I enjoyed and learned a lot from Yamakita-sensei's class.  This class is more speaking-based, so you will improve with speaking but probably not reading. The homework assignments and tests were fair; the tests are comprised of concepts that were went over in class. Make sure to check ELMS daily for hw assignments.

Love her, as she taught the interactive class. She enjoys teaching and watching everyone grow. Has a funny personality but won't hesitate to push students to do better. The class really isn't that hard if you just keep up with all the homework and read the book before class. It really pays off. Taking 102 with her next semester.
A great teacher! Class is interesting and engaging, and you don't have to be afraid of making mistakes in class. I wish I had her for lecture too...

I've had her for two years and you definitely can't slack w/ the work or you won't get a good grade. Her tests might be hard, but she basically pulls all the questions from homeworks, quizzes, and the required textbooks, so the test questions are something you already went over in class.

If you're one of those smart-but-lazy students, BEWARE. In all my other classes I have gotten A's and B's but I tend to procrastinate and it really hurt me in Yamakita-sensei's class. She's a nice and helpful teacher, though strict, and I really like her despite the grade I got. If you aren't prepared to work your butt off, take something else.

Yamakita-sensei is very thorough and explains grammar over and over.  She's understanding and gives out many assignments, which are relatively easy and based on the instruction.  The class is easy to follow, and students can learn a lot.  She's also generous and caring as a teacher.

She gives out a lot of homework and you have a quiz everyday, but it does make you learn the materials. Yamakita explains the grammar points really well and she will make you laugh too, which makes class really enjoyable. Her exams are tough though, significantly harder than Yaginuma, the other 200 level sensei (My friend showed me his class).
Quiz, homework, and conversation memorization every class so she expects you to work.  However, she does pretty well explaining the material and she is a kind person and dedicated to teaching.
Not the best language teacher in the world, but very friendly and has a lower difficulty level than some of the other teachers. Depending on how much you want to learn, this could be bad.
No Comments
Reid is a wonderful teacher and dedicates himself to the students.  All students learn a lot from these courses.  I hear he won educator of the year last year... I agree!
Professor Ewing really cares about his students. He is always there to help. I had no idea I would like transportation planning so much.

I've taken his class almost every semester and I love his courses. He is smart, clarity and easy to follow. What a great and nice teacher. I remember that he spent a whole Saturday to help me with my final project when I took his land use and transportation planning class. Whatever your question is and whenever you have your question, he is there.

I had three PhD level courses with him and I think he is very smart and knowledgeable. He is always responsive to questions and available to help. I basically have learned everything I know in statistics from him. I think his courses on statistics and technical writing is a must to take for graduate students who are interested in research.

he now teaches at the university of utah. he is smart however he always glorifies himself, and his work which gets really annoying. Has no idea what is going on in his class and does not know how to manage it. ridiculous ...
Talks down to students and plays favorites.
Really a great guy. Nice, supportive, extremely smart.
Worst human being ever!
I believe the professor is caring and covers the ideas well, however I do not believe there was enough practice.
She was someone who was very full of herself and did not care to help the students, and blame them for not attending all her lectures, when you only missed two or three.

Professor Seo was fantastic. She is sweet and prioritizes our understanding of the material. Gives extra credit for participation, and has the audience all vote on multiple choice conceptual problems constantly throughout class--very engaging and helpful. Unlike many physics professors, she uses slides so you'll never miss an important equation.
Easy tests that have problems exactly the same as HW. Students could submit which questions they would like as candidates for the tests as well. Overall a pretty easy physics class.

Very hard teacher. She loved powerpoints and went through them very fast. I had to mainly rely on the textbook for all my knowledge. The tests were extremely hard because most equations had to be derived. The only thing that made me pass was the webassigns and the labs (once you know how to do them "correctly")

One of the worst professors I've ever had.  Her accent is very thick and often not understandable.  Often wastes her students' time by going off on tangents rather than doing problems on the board, which is the best way to learn physics.  Often flips through her slides too quickly to absorb or discuss them and don't even bother rasing your hand.

This is not an easy class, you have to put a lot of time and effort into it. The tests were a lot easier then I expected but were still challenging. She is very nice and really really wants her students to do well. The lab reports were very long. If you are interested in learning you will learn a lot. If you study a lot you will do well.

Very thick accent, hard to understand, and does a horrible job clarifying topics when asked; better to just look in the book. Gives mandoatory in-class quizes and demands 5-10 page lab reports be written each week!(RUN!).NO other physics professor I know does this. Gives hard tests with VERY VERY tricky multiple choice questions (TA even agrees).
I liked her teaching style. She made powerpoint slides that were really helpful with diagrams that correlated to the book.

this prof is very nice as well as helpful (if you go to her personally), but I found the class difficult. HW is pretty easy and is done through webassign, class attendance is required because of in-class quizzes using those clicker things. my problem was the tests, since any equation used must be derived.
complete waste of time

He is a very nice and respectful teacher and I took him over a winter course for BMGT220. The lectures were long and after a while can get boring or repetitive. He would occasionally go on tangents talking about random companies rather than the topic at hand. Grades were based on HW and 3 exams which were all multiple choice. Best BMGT220 choice
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is one of the kindest people and knows how to teach very well online. Always prepared and held office hours weekly. Accounting is tricky and have to put in effort but he makes class much better!

great guy, and great lecturer. the class is assignment heavy and time consuming but not unreasonable. genuinely wants his students to pass as well as become more knowledgeable about the business world. expected a little too much participation but i guess he just wanted online classes to be a little more discussion based like his in person class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He is such a good accounting teacher. He wants to see you succeed and holds multiple office hours and "Sunday coffee" time to review. There are a lot of homework assignments but they aren't hard if you go to class. One midterm and final and discussion quizzes on Friday. If you go to class and follow along the lowest you'll get is a B. SOLID teacher
Would not recommend this professor, tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Accounting is dense, but Eugene makes it pretty fun. The exams are incredibly hard (Accounting is simply a hard subject) but he gives so much extra credit. He also curves every exam to about 84% so if you can pull off an average grade, you can get an A or B in the class.

Tax isnt necessarily the most exciting class, but Cantor makes it bearable and not too dry. He is extremely smart, his lectures are crystal clear if you pay attention, and tells stories here and there! The exams are open notes and uploads practice exams, but that doesnt mean theyre easy. If you have the option to take him, then TAKE HIM!
Took his class for my business minor and absolutely loved him. He's a funny guy and he gets the material across in an effective way. Highly recommend.

He is a great professor. I definitely take him again. He can explain and relates concepts to you. He is always well prepared in class. I took him at 8:45PM and he always manages to slip in a few jokes to make the class stay awake. 5/5, best professor ever.

I am really glad I switched into this class after enrolling w/ Finch. Cantor follows along w/ the textbook & simplifies tough concepts. He provides us w/ the solutions for each chapter and review materials that remind us exactly what to remember for each exam. The exams are open notes & Cantor provides students with everything they need to do well.

AH-MA-ZING professor. I don't even know why I signed up for corporate tax at all (I thought it was going to be like individual - it IS NOT), but he made this class so enjoyable. Be prepared to work HARD but it's better to do this than to take a class with a professor who doesn't care about you or your grade. This guy is AWESOME

I took Professor Cantor for BMGT 417 and he is AMAZING!!!! You will learn a lot taking him and come to see tax as more interesting than "geeky and full of number-crunching". The cookies he brings to class are the best!!! I absolutely loved his class.
Awesome teacher who provides students with every opportunity to do well. I would highly recommend him if you are interested in going into tax.

Prof. Cantor has an impresive resume but does not really mentor students.  It is too bad that a person with his experience does not make an effort to transmit knowledge to his students.  There was very little motivation during the course. Professor Cantor  did not provide the answers to the final exam.  Shame on you Prof. Cantor!
All over the place

Professor Cantor's tests are really hard however he does curve them. If you put forth enough effort you'll come out with a good grade. Overall he's good at teaching but not at reviewing for tests. I would recommend him to anyone.

The best teacher I have so far at UMCP but also the toughest class so far. Lectures are fun but exams are crazy hard and Cantor does not do enough practice problems in class for students to fully understand the material. However, huge curves for exams, VERY hard to get below B, if you have F in other course you would end up with B in BMGT417.

Great teacher, learned a lot. Tests are very difficult but there is a huge curve (~30% points). Attendance isnt mandatory but there are worksheets at the end of lectures that are graded, so you should go. Cantor is a fun teacher that really enjoys his job. Would love to take more classes with him.
Great professor, helpful. I took the tax class at night 7pm-9:30pm. I recommend him over pfiefer. His tests are hard but there is a curve. gives out great study material
No Comments
I have had professor Cantor for several accounting classes and he is great! He is always fair when grading assignments and tests.
Love him. Son's not too bad either.

I took this class as a sophomore with no prior CAD experience. It was awful. Professor Eslami was extremely unhelpful and rude during office hours and was an absolute stickler when it came down to grading. I hated using CAD for a long time after this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Good Prof.
Professor is fair, makes his expectations clear. Expects way too much from students, but it's not reflected in the grade you get.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Prof. Espy-Wilson explains the concepts in a very intuitive and insightful manner that makes it easier to understand what you're really doing and why you're doing it. However, her exams are very tough, with averages of 60% and 30% for the first and second exam respectively. These scores are mitigated by a heavy curve towards the end of the class.
I can not understand what she teaches. The exam also is hard. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS!

She is a great professor. Her lectures are extremely clear and well organized. The exams on the other hand are in Spanish. From lectures and the homeworks, you would think you know everything about the subject. But then you look at your exam sheet and it is as if you have never seen the material before. Oh yea, She is a very, very tough grader.
She is a fantastic teacher.  She presented all the material in a clear voice and answered all questions thoroughly.
Excellent teacher.  Very willing to help if you ask.  Tests are pretty straight forward.

She is a great professor.  Her lectures are word for word out of the book, but she explains some things better than the book.  Always willing to help and answer questions.  Talks about things that are out of the scope of the class at times (i.e. ENEE322) alot. Overall great person

This class is required if you plan to continue in Architecture and it's definitely a lot of work, but it's well worth it. It has been my favorite class so far and it really improved my drawing. Plus, Lester is pretty cool and always quick to answer emails (sometimes even at 2am) You can tell he really cares and wants to see his students succeed

Anyone who rated this class poorly is either lazy and/or daft. This class does require time, especially during the end, but if you're going into architecture this is exactly what your future is gonna be like. Lester is easy to talk to, extremely invested in every student, and a clever, talented guy. I have nothing bad to say about him an his class.

Lester is the man, by far the best professor I've had at college park. Very knowledgeable and really understands how to convey ideas to students and gives great feedback on work. class is time consuming and requires a lot of effort but pays off, greatly improved my drawing skill. definitely recommend

I absolutely LOVED this class. Lester is a master at what he does and loves the subject. His assignments are time consuming so I wouldnt take a full load with this one. You need to spend a lot of time on the drawings and follow the directions of you want get a good grade. If you cant draw and you do want a good grade, I wouldnt take this class
He's a passionate teacher who knows his stuff. If you get to know him, he is very personable and approachable. The class has a huge workload. Also, mandatory class 8am Friday, which sucks.

This was the most diffacult class I have every taken!! Lester has been teaching this class for over a decade and has a very specific idea of what the assignments are supposed to look like. If you don't fit into his boilerplate you are not going to do well. He doesn't explain he assignments well.

lester is not that great, I took 242 w him in summer, he was always in a rush and was not approachable! assignments were not that hard if you like drawing but some of them were unclear and needed his explanation but he never explained them cuz he didnt care!

don't take this class if you're not intending to spend at least 6 hours on your assignemnts because that's how long it will take to do at least a decent job.  escobal creeps a bit when he studies your face on his class roster to memorize names but w/e he tries to know everyone i guess. i'd say textbooks aren't required, but are good references.

Lester is truly the master of what he teaches and he does a good job explaining the notes.  The class is extremely challenging and takes a lot of work but is worth it in the end.  Some of the weekly assignments take a really long time.  He?s often late to class, which usually goes over its allotted time, but he?s a great teacher when he?s there.

Get to know your TA. I met with mine before every week. This class is very time consuming, dont wait til thurs night to do the assignments or it will def show. The assignments are pretty interesting, most of them are freehand, very annoying since i love the ruler. Participate lots on Friday (lester loves it). Amazingly, I earned an "A-"

This class really depends on your TA.  I had friends that had really easy ones and they got A's.  My TA gave me an 89.14.  I needed an A to keep a scholarship, so I wrote to Lester about my situation, he refused to help me and was not really approachable.  I did really well in the class considering, but I would avoid it if you arent in ARCH.

Be aware that the summer course is just as demanding.Compressed and less assignments,which can weaken your portfolio if you apply.Don't freat.Good course,good/fair instructor.Vague instructions,true,but u r a college student,ask ?'s.The answers are there.Be prepared to work hard.Procrastination is your worst enemy.You truly EARN A's.Good luck.

Assignments are not explained very well, but this could be to test everyone's creativity. Also, your experience with this class is very dependent on which TA you get, as their grading varies. This is a very time consuming class, so don't make plans for thursday nights, because you will be spending them finishing drawings that are due Friday morning

very enthusiastic about architecture but the assignments are never as easy as they sound like they will be. be prepared to always have someone better than you& to spend a fair amount if you don't already have drawing supplies.  this was the class that made me realize that architecture is not for me.

if u like architecture and drawing, u must take Arch 242 w/ Lester, dude is Awsome! try to take the course over the summer so u won't have to deal w/ any TA's. and then u will find out y i rate him 5 4x.

Great professor with an abundance of knowledge on his course. He is very clear and always willing to help. Tests are extremely fair. Definitely recommend taking 455 as an Option course and Dr. Spangenburg as a teacher.

Awesome professor. Makes the class very interesting and his grading system is nothing but fair. His exams are not confusing and test your knowledge. However, you need to come to class to take notes. But besides that, this professor is one of the best Ive had.
THE BEST..if you dont get ATLEAST a B, theres something wrong with you. He's extremely helpful and interesting.That combo is really hard to find..

Interesting topic. Tests were easy if you study the lecture notes. No book used. He was really helpful if you asked questions and if you don't get it ask him during or after the lecture- he's great about explaining. Assignments were 3 tests and a really easy (and fun) paper.

She doesn't explain well at all! Get ready to spend hours on homework that will also only make up 10% of your grade.
She is however ready to help but that doesnt really matter considering the course load.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Moody made it very easy to keep up with content in ECON200. This is likely because of the way she structured the content and created engaging lectures. I would highly suggest taking this class with her, whether or not it is required for you major, as she does such a good job teaching it.

I would NEVER recommend this professor. Yes, she's nice but nice doesn't mean you are good at teaching. She says "okay?" after every sentence. She doesn't properly answer questions. The exams are difficult and make it nearly impossible to study for them. The homework's useless and is worth nearly nothing. These reviews fooled me by taking her.

Dr Moody was by far my favorite professor this semester. The workload is fairly simple, one Smartbook and HW assignment for each lecture, and three midterm exams to properly spread out the content. She is very approachable and always has an answer to your question. Highly recommend Dr Moody for ECON200!

Professor Moody is one of the nicest people you will meet. She goes out of her way to give extra points and lets you miss portions of classes while still giving you an A for participation. With that said, she is not a very good teacher. The lectures are brutal. Questions in class are not properly answered. Easy grade for most but do not recommend.
Be aware of test and grades and group work. Rarely read emails.

I wouldn't necessarily recommend this class to others. She drones on a lot so lectures aren't extremely engaging and it's definitely doing way too much for a 100-level class. Unless you really care about both Econ and the environment, I wouldn't suggest taking it. The homework assignments are ok but there are definitely some harder questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Moody's lectures are pretty engaging and easy to follow. She doesn't assign too much homework and we only had a few exams/projects. She's very approachable and easy to access outside of class. Would recommend.

She is a nice person in general, but please do not ever consider taking econ here at UMD. You would be far better off taking it at a different college or at a community college. I had A's in all of my homework's, I attended every class (rain or shine). Unfortunately, the class grade is weighted heavily on the tests you take.

PROS: Super passionate professor, open book Exams, easy homework (but time-consuming), recorded and Zoom available lectures, many practice sessions with GSS, and the opportunity to choose the format of the Final Exam.  
CONS: limited time during Exams, making the "open book" concept practically useless
I will love to take Dr. Moody again.

I took this class as a gen ed/requirement for the business school. I had never taken an econ course before so it was quite challenging. There are usually weekly reading assignments and homework. She said the class was optional but I definitely recommend going because it'll obviously help you learn and she offers extra credit during class time.

I'm a STEM major and also stupid, and took this class as an elective thinking it'd be fun. And it WAS fun, but I over-estimated my graph-reading abilities, and how much reading I'd have to do. Dr. Moody made class interesting, answers questions, and is very clear with her lectures. There's huge opportunities for extra credit, too!

There is maybe 2-3 homework assignments a week but they are SO EASY if you just try and do it. I'm not an econ major but I've never had trouble with the homework. Dr. Moody gives so much extra credit, so make sure you take advantage of it!! It's econ, so you will have to put some work in, but 100% would recommend taking econ200 with Dr. Moody.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: When taking the class in person was very challenging. I had to attend several guided study sessions to understand the material. Professor Moody is not the best at explaining the material. My whole class is failing right now, If you are not a good test taker do not take this class you will probably fail if you are not organized and study correctly.

The content itself is hard for some but, she makes it easy to get help and practice. She is very lively in class and shows how much she loves the content she's talking about. Dr. Moody gives so many opportunities to get extra credit. Gives so many studying materials to be successful in the class. 

If you fail, it's probably your fault.

I really liked this class, even though I hate economics. Dr. Moody gives out A LOT of extra credit, and as long as you study and do your homework, you will do well on the exams. Dr. Moody also makes sure to take time to connect what you're learning in class to real world examples, which I find really interesting and helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was a nice prof and cared. The coursework was split pretty evenly across the semester. Weekly homework and reading assignments are in the bag, so be prepared. There is a lot of reading. She gave a lot of extra credit points for in-class activities, so that helped grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's super nice and understanding! Her lectures aren't helpful, but all the tests are based on the textbook anyways. Just study the textbook and pass. A lot of the homework is completion based and the final wasn't cumulative. She's the best! Super approachable if you have questions.

Class was easy but boring. I only went to two class meetings. Class requires McGraw Hill materials which you have to pay for. Major grades are two midterms and a final. Also small quiz-type assignments every week or so based on reading. Just read the textbook, take good notes, do the assignments, and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Moody is the best!! The people rating her poorly are probably just bitter they got a bad grade. The grades are test heavy, but they are so easy if you go to lecture and do the homework!! If you have the option, definitely take Dr. Moody- she actually cares about her students and their grades and EXTRA CREDIT EVERY CLASS.

Professor Moody is an amazing professor. She's so sweet and wants you to understand the concepts. She answers questions well and clearly, and if she doesn't, she'll re-explain. Moody is great at giving examples that help you understand the concepts. She's generous with extra credit and exempts some of your lowest grades.

So much extra credit it added 2 percent points to my grade. Nice and answer questions. Did make us use lockdown browser but not with webcam. Extra credit if you answer questions as you go along with the in-class lecture. Records lectures so you can watch later. Gives about 4 attempts for each assignment (guaranteed 100%) and drops 3 lowest homework

Moody herself is a very sweet and caring prof, I just absolutely hates how she ran her class. To deter cheating she proctored online exams and the platform she used for homework was unnecessarily extensive, taking multiple hours for just reading. This course also assumes you can attend Guided Study Sessions, so if you cant you're screwed.

She was really good at teaching 201. People who struggle with her 200 and 201 classes are the ones who try to rush through the online-homework without taking the time to learn the ins-and-outs of it. As long as you really teach yourself what's happening in the homework, you'll definitely get minimum-B. Besides that, she was great at lectures.

I took ECON200 with her. I am so bad at ECON. Go to lecture (all notes are posted online - but you can participate in EASY homework points through modlab here). Get a chegg account - pay for one month and nail the homework points. Go to the review sessions before exams. THEY HELP SO MUCH. Take the exam and do mediocore. Bam you got ur econ credit

I thought while she is a cool person in general she is overall not a very good teacher, and is a pretty harsh grader on exams though shes more leaner on other written work besides that. Overall unless you need the class, dont take it and dont have her

Her quizzes are really confusing a super hard because she asks very specific questions about it, the math in this course is also a little difficult, but she makes even harder by the way she teaches it
She doesn't help much in office hours. Her lectures are boring and make you want to fall asleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Boring lectures but an easy A. All midterms have practice exams that are really similar and she gives extra credit point opportunities during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Nice lady and the best choice for micro at umd. She makes the class easier by dropping homeworks but the tests are really hard. Content is interesting but pretty hard overall.

At the university of maryland, there are only two professors who teach microeconomics. For any non-econ majors, Moody is the better choice of the two but her class can still be a lot. The course moves very quickly. The final is cumulative and covers a lot of information. Moody tries her best to make the course a bit easier for students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Her class is very lecture heavy and can get really boring. For non-econ majors, the class is very difficult. Tests are all application based and the final is cumulative. If you constantly review the material, study hard for the exams, and go to GSS (go to Kayleigh's sections) you may do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: really good professor. everything that is on the test is covered in class. have past exams available and the exams are pretty similar to the past ones
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You won't find many professor better than Moody at UMD! It's actually so helpful to come to class. Unlike many classes at UMD. Moody makes the lectures so interesting and if you actually pay attention you learn enough to get an A. This class is also structured very well where you actually get tested on the main concepts you learn.

Amazing professor and easily understandable. Made Economics accessible for everyone and with some work, not hard to grasp. Tests were straightforward and didn't ask any "gotcha" questions. EC opportunities if you go to lecture.

Moody really does look out for her students. Despite teaching 800 students and having a lecture hall of about 300 students at a time, she's always open to questions and more than happy to answer them. After about every slide she pauses to see if anyone has questions. She's also very energetic.

If ECON isn't your thing, Moody is the easiest professor. She's very sweet and cares about her students. She also realizes that ECON200 can be hard for a lot of people and really tries to explain it well. She can be a little scatterbrained at times and the tests can be rough (especially the final) though.

She is fun and high energy during lecture. However, lectures can be slow-paced and repetitive, and she's pretty unclear when answering questions. While going to class is technically optional, it's necessary to get extra credit. I felt well prepared for exams from going to lecture.
Moody is a decent person, but terrible lecturer. Her lectures are boring and hard to follow. The TA's look for any reason to take points off on your exam so make sure you know your content.
I love Professor Moody! This was my first economics class and I found it very easy. She is super funny and knowledgable about what she teaches. Take her class!

The only other review for this class is pretty inaccurate. The only way this class is an easy A is if youre already a master in economics. Theres only 5 homework assignments worth 25% of your grade but the tough grading makes it more of an anchor than anything. The class participation is 25% as well so consider yourself ruined if you skip
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I dont know why Dr. Moody has a low rating. She is a good professor. Also, the class is an easy A, if you give some effort. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities. Fun class. Definitely recommend for ECON181.
Her lectures are a bit on the boring side but her class is pretty easy. She gives a lot of extra credit which can bring grades up a lot. Skipped easy lectures and was fine.

I went to most of the lectures, but I think they're only necessary if you don't understand the reading or homework. Though she drops the three lowest homework grades, I recommend doing all the assignments, because they help understand the material more than lecture does. There's also extra credit if you go to class. Do the work and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Moody is a great professor- she is very knowledgeable and teaches the content well. She gives many extra credit opportunities in class, so I would attend but it's not necessary. The tests weren't too difficult; however, I think the final was. The textbook is online, which is essential, but no need to buy a physical book. Overall good experience

She's a very nice professor and was helpful for me during office hours. Her lectures were very boring and it was easy to be on your phone or laptop the whole time. The grading on tests though, done by TA's, was atrocious. Never give half credit ever on problems and killed my grade. She also changes things up a lot on tests compared to sample ones

Lecture attendance is extra credit and homework/readings are easy. If you do all the readings, the tests are not too difficult. She goes out of order of the textbook for no reason. You don't NEED to go to class unless you don't understand the readings or you want extra practice. Exactly what an introductory course should be.
This class is an easy A and she makes it even easier by giving many points of extra credit. More than 3/4 of the grade is based on exams.

Get ready to feel like you're back in middle school with her lectures. The class is not that hard but do not get behind or you will fail. Make sure you study harder than ever, because just studying for those exams is not enough.

The content is not difficult and she is nice but she is not good at explaining . If you read the textbook and go to her lecture, you will be able to pass most likely. Grades are composed of assignments, hw, exams and extra credits in class. We have two exams and one final (cumulative) and the practice exams she posts online really help a lot.

Professor Moody is a nice person, but her lectures are almost completely unnecessary. You can get extra credit by going to lectures and answering questions, but you have to pay $10 for them to go towards your grade. She uploads all the powerpoints online after lecture so really you don't have to show up.

She is very bubbly and I enjoy it. Econ is a boring topic so of course lectures are dry but she makes it funny and provides the information necessary to best help you. She offers extra credit opportunities, is easily accessible, and provides great practice exams to help you prepare.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She's a total sweetheart. Very nice and loves what she does. However, she is very scattered. Lectures don't flow well at all and are disorganized/jumpy. Class is also WAY too reliant on technology. Textbook and ALL the homework is online and lectures are also online so when technology inevitably fails sometimes everything is derailed...

Shes kinda spacey, but overall shes a total sweetheart. Her lectures are a little jumbled and theres a hefty load of online work that is required to do; extra credit questions ONLY if you attend lecture. Overall shes really nice and wants everyone to do well. Shes just kinda jumps all over the place and the online work is annoying.
She is the kind of professor who give a high grade if you care about her class vise versa. She give tons of extra credit if you come to her class, and she give many chance for homework.

Moody recognizes that most people in 200 aren't econ majors, so she does her best to help you succeed. If I had to take another econ class I would take it with her! She is very friendly and gives extra credit for attending lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Not too hard. Some homework but it wasn't too time consuming. She gives extra credit if you go to class. But I still missed class and did fine.

This course destroyed my GPA. It is not as easy as people say. Moody's lecture is so boring that only a few students attend to. The group work is graded so hard. If your group did not be chosen to have a presentation, you have to take the final exam.
Don't take her class if you can't self study. Her class is a zzz and boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Really easy, all you have to do is read the textbook and it should be an easy A, you don't have to go to lectures, but she has extra credit opportunities every lecture so I would.
She posts her lecture slides and questions in class are strictly for extra credit so you dont have to go. You can teach yourself the material easily from the textbook too.

Erin Moody is a very amiable person and probably the most forgiving professor I've ever had. ECON181 is a new class, so it's not perfect by any standards. If the topic interests you, you can get a lot out of the class. If you just need to fulfill a credit, this class is pretty much an easy A as long as you're not extremely lazy.

Dr. Moody is so nice! The class was pretty laid back, spent most of it just discussing current economic policy. No exams. 4 homeworks that were graded pretty tough, but not very difficult. Group project at the end is torture. Find people ahead of time you know won't be too horrible to work with or you'll get stuck with the worst kids.
She gives long boring lectures and that take forever. Don't know how to study for midterms and the group projects are very disorganized.

Very easy class, she goes through everything way to slow. What she mentions in 3 lectures could be done in 20 min. Content is fairly easy but she has weird questions. Easy to get a good grade but not full score, hard to understand what she wants from assignments.

I got As in every exam just from understanding each problem set question, doing past exams, and attending every  lecture. The book was awful, but Moody's amazing teaching style made the material much easier to grasp and way more interesting.  Take her. I wish she could teach every Econ class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Terrible teacher, all she does is read powerpoint slides. Her voice is annoying and her exams are tough. She does not curve either

I absolutely hated ECON200.  I did not find the homework helpful and the textbook over-complicated everything. Dr. Moody is a nice person, however I wasn't a fan of her teaching style, as I found it disorganized and jumpy. She is very passionate about econ, but for someone like me who isn't, I didn't find her teaching effective. Exams were hard too
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Mrs Moody made econ my favorite class this semester, even though it's not my major. She's genuinely excited to teach the class and is continually engaging. I found the class really easy -- I skimmed the practice tests and always got an A+ on tests and the homework is super easy. She recommends printing out the power points, but I got by without it.

The only thing this class has going for it is that clicker questions are optional-meaning attendance is optional. other than that, this class sucks. Bad teacher, bad personality. Thinks she's funny--isn't. Thinks she's prepared for lectures--isn't. horrible powerpoints. only way to do well is read the book or have taken econ before. don't recommend

Dr. Moody uses blended learning (online and in-class) but if you follow all the assignments and complete them on time, it's easy to get a passing grade. For the exams, she can be confusing in her explanations, but she is open to feedback and very patient in repeating herself. Overall, she is very fun and made lecture very enjoyable.

class is long, but she's pretty funny. she can confuse you sometimes but if you go to her review sessions or office hours, she actually condenses the information into the main things you need to know. her practice exams are the exact type of problems on the exam

At first, she comes off like she's unprepared for lectures, but the class picks up after a while. Her PowerPoints don't do much good as a study tool by themselves. She really tries to give everyone an easy time understanding fundamental economics, she's also really funny! She also gives extra credit for clicker questions, which adds a nice cushion.

She's a really likable person & she's pretty funny!She relates econ to topics relatable topics. Her exams are straightforward and very simplified, JUST like the practice exams, so if you study those and really try to understand them, you'll do well. The only thing is that when she answers questions in class, her answers can be confusing.
Honestly her powerpoints were horrible!!!!!! And she needs to make them more clear and less conceptual for people who are non-econ majors

Great professor! Clear and detailed.  Game theory can be a tough class when taught poorly. Prof Moody taught the subject matter well. Tests were long but fair. Homework was long at times but not outrageous. No reason not to get an A in her class if you put forth the effort. Ignore the econ200 review below. Clearly the dumb dumb tried to cram.

She doesn't curve -- our class got a 70 avg on our test and she didn't curve it annoying voice doesn't prepare for lectures she's just the worst I had to study for over 24 hours just to get a B on the uncurved final
Knowledgeable and caring person but extremely boring. HW was pretty difficult considering his lecture didn't prepare you by any means. Exams weren't bad if u studied.

Professor Lichtenberg is very nice and clearly very knowledgable. The HW Problem Sets are really frustrating since the lectures don't prepare you for them and the equations that you need are not always clear or even discussed. The exams are worth an incredibly large percentage of the final grade, but they weren't too difficult if you studied.

Professor Lichtenberg explains concepts very well, despite the class being math heavy. There is quite a lot of material in this course and a ton of readings. The discussion assignments were very interesting, and the practice problems really help you learn how to graph equations. You get a lot of useful skill out of this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a great professor, and if you don't understand anything he will explain it for you until you understand completely. provides extra of office hours before homework due. Overall, he makes you work for your grade.
He isnt as bad as the other ratings say. He makes you work for your grade but you will learn valuable skills that will be useful after college.

This is by far one of the hardest classes I have ever taken. The homework is taken from graduate level classes and gives little to no instruction on how to do it. The lectures are extremely dull and boring and overloaded with information that he claims you don't need to know which then compromises the homework. Steer clear of this professor.
Gives extremely challenging homework and proceeds to grade it as hard as possible. If you are looking for an easy upper level class, avoid this one.

The lectures were very good, the homework and worksheets were very useful, and he made it very clear what we needed to know for the quizzes and exams.The exams weren't too bad, and the grading was reasonable. My only complaint was that my TA was pretty bad, but that is not Fawzi's fault. Fawzi is a good guy, and he really cares about his students.

He is an amazing lecturer! One of the best I've ever had tbh. He does make lectures mandatory, but he explains everything really well so it's worth it. Tests are kinda difficult tho, and most of the grade is based on tests and projects. I could listen to that man yap for 10 hrs deadass.
He's a gem in the rough that is the CS department.

fawzi is amazing. he's the reason I decided I want to be a cs major. Youll pass the class by basically living at office hours 24/7 and remember to pay the Iribe center rent for the semester camping there

I took 131 and 132 online so all lectures were prerecorded, but Fawzi was very engaging and his style of teaching really got me interested in the course material and made watching lecture videos seem like less of a chore. I would definitely recommend him for any CS class.

one of the best teachers you could ever have. took him online this semester and his lectures are so clear and tries to put in humor when he can. I knew very little about programming before taking this class, and even through the online format, Fawzi was very easy to understand. He explained things very well, and all of the TAs were very helpful in projects or anything you had trouble understanding.

Fawzi is a legend

Fawzi is the best! If you want to learn the material, take the course with Fawzi. He is as good as everyone says, and also is a very nice person. I will take any class he teaches.

Fawzi is one of the best professors I've had at UMD. He knows material very well, and how to teach it, and it shows in his lectures. I've taken him for both 131 and 132 and had not done any computer science before, yet came out knowing so much. Take Fawzi whenever you can!!!

FAWZI IS AWESOME! Best instructor I've ever had. He goes way out of his way to help students learn and is fun to talk with outside of class. He really cares about his students. Fawzi is awesome. He makes boring codes fun, he explains stuff in non-computer science language. I would love to take another class taught by him if there is a chance in the future.

Take this class seriously and show up for lectures, you're guaranteed to learn a ton and enjoy yourself while you're at it; Fawzi's a great instructor and a true pro
