reviews.comment: I would not take this class again. Shes unorganized and penalizes you for it. She changes her syllabus without telling you and expects you to read her mind. She can be nice at times, but is also sometimes a tough grader. At the end of the semester she throws you 4943849 assignments to finish.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She is a great professor. She gives a lot of homework and pop quizzes. She cares about the students learning the material.  As long as you do the homework, attend class, and understand the material, you should be good.
Great professor! She was so much fun! She might seem tough, but if you really try, she will to help you out. This class is also very helpful for public speaking!

Senora Canabal-Torres is a really sweet and hilarious professor. She is very helpful if you ask for help because in class she often goes on random tangents about stuff that is unrelated to what's being taught. But overall, if you pay attention when she is teaching and you take your own notes at home (on the grammar mostly) you'll be fine.

I love Professor Evans! I wish I couldve taken this class in person instead of online, but I can see why so many people like him! Really fun class, I play the violin and I really wanted to learn how to arrange music - this class is perfect for that! Very accommodating during a pandemic, I just love him! If you can, definitely take the class :)

The class takes place in the MIDI lab at Clarice (CSPAC) and is all about learning how to compose music with the softwares Noteflight and GarageBand. Professor Evans instructs the class in such a way that his students have freedom to explore their musical creativity within the assignment guidelines. It is the most fun class I have taken at UMD.

A very easygoing professor.  For HONR218M at least, he graded our finals not on an absolute scale of how good yours was compared to the class but on a relative one: if you showed improvement from where you started, you got an A.  The class was based on a series of music projects, and he gave ample time to work on them.  A great class and professor.

Evandro is egotistical and he definitely makes the class a lot harder than its supposed to be. Hell hold you to professional engineering standards and then spend class sitting at his desk eating chips or just not show up. During the Safety Lecture, he laughed while recounting stories where students were injured and hospitalized.

Evandro is not like any other professor. He really knows his stuff and if you ask him any question even from outside the class he would explain it so well and with so much passion that you would want to learn more and automatically get interested in the subject. His speeches are inspirational and he really talks about real life engineering.

Evandro has a huge ego but do things his way and you will do fine. He puts a lot of emphasis on the final project, but it's really not worth as much as the work before it. He's a decent guy if you talk to him one on one, but he has a very aggressive way of lecturing. That said, I'd choose another ENES100 professor over him.

As a person, he is not the best to get along with because he can be egotistical, intimidating and stuck in his own ways. He makes the class harder by focusing on winning so much instead of focusing on the content and goes off on tangents. He lectures for the first half of the semester, and then you work with your group for the second half.

Most egotistical person I've ever met; said "he's the teacher he wish he had". First day of class he wrote down all his previous winning sections. Will make the class way harder than what it should be. Not helpful during testing process and will just eat lunch. When grading he only cares about looks, not content. It made me a better perfectionist.

Evandro is very arrogant and stubborn. He will tell you that he is hated by all the other teachers, and there is a very good reason why he is not well liked in the engineering department. He is rude. He did not help at all during construction, and instead he would sit down and eat his lunch and play on his phone. Switch out of his class if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very cool guy. The work can be hard, especially if you don't have prior experience. He's a tough grader and has plenty of stories during lectures. First half of the semester is doing lectures, and second half is building robot, where he becomes very helpful and informative.

Very tough grader on Milestones and quizzes. Offers a great deal of extra credit to offset that. He's kinda intimidating due to an abrasive personality but can be very helpful. Expects you to win, very passionate about the course, provides lots of useful insights. Tbh, after the build phase starts the professor becomes mostly irrelevant.

One of the worst teachers I have ever had. The class is difficult to begin with and he only makes it harder by having extremely high, unrealistic expectations of first year engineering students and barely teaching anything useful.

Evandro really only cares about two things; winning the end of the year class wide competition and making sure you know that he's 'Not like other professors'. He spends more time stroking his ego than any professor I've ever had, and he's obsessed with peer evaluations and grading based on font size and bullet placement rather than content.

He plays favorites in a very unprofessional manor. He can be helpful, or your worst nightmare. He thinks very highly of himself; if only he were as wonderful as he is in his head. Many profs teach this class. I would recommend selecting a different one. Try to get Calabro, Sunderland, Gomez, Syramos; anyone else.

He started out really laid back but as the semester went on he got really irritating to be around.  Picks favorites from amongst the hovercraft teams and helps them more but the funny thing is those teams usually end up failing so don't go to him for help if your team needs it.
Inconsistent grading and very high percentage of grade is test dependent.

The assignments for 434 have no rubric, no examples, and no criteria. His assignment descriptions are one large text to make it easier for him to claim "we weren't following directions". You will 100% miss something small on the assignment and he will take off an arbitrarily large amount of points off.

Golub's 250 is HEAVILY test based (88% of the grade when I took the class, the other 12% was homework). His tests are difficult but fair based on the material he presents in class. The lectures are boring. He also covers different content than other 250 classes in a different order, so it's hard to study with other professors' students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: On exams he gives no points for any correct information, if one part is wrong, he will not give any points at all, that is an automatic 0.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Extremely vague in what he wants from the projects and will make up grading criteria that does not exist in the descriptions. Very poor lecturer with uninspired methods, simply going through a lazily created PowerPoints every day. Ask an absurd amount of question about exactly he wants for each assignment.

This dude was terrible. I barely understood anything he said. He would ramble through an hour class and everyone looked unimpressed and confused on all material presented. He acts like you already have prior knowledge of coding, but if you're someone like me this will be hell. You can show up but nothing will help you. Goodluck.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I found Golub really likeable and enjoyed his lectures, however I can understand why his lecturing style doesn't work for some people. He rambles sometimes and is a bit eccentric. If you want to do well, just make sure you actually listen in lecture! Resist the urge to use your computer the whole time.

This is the worst designed class I have taken at UMD, which is absurd in a class about design. The assignments are described and listed poorly, the hardest part of every assignment was figuring out what Golub wanted. With no examples given on what Golub wanted, it felt like we were stabbing in the dark and hoping for the best.
Good professor, very quirky. Just make sure you pay attention

Golub is arguably the worst CMSC professor in the school. He will show up with an idea of what he should lecture on, but will lose track and start ranting about some higher-level CMSC material like machine learning. Sounds cool, but once it happens every time, you realize you aren't learning anything.

Taking Golub with little programming experience really put me to a bad start. He was the only one that fit my schedule. Lectures don't help and he wasn't the nicest during office hours when I was confused about his projects. TAs really helped though! Projects and exams drove me crazy(horrible wording). I'm so glad its over. Don't take his class! :(

I took him because all the other professors were booked. He is the worse professor you can ever imagine. He will only give you points if you get everything 100% correct on the exam, a slight mistake gets you zero. He doesn't care for his students at all. The majority of students fail in his class. DONT TAKE GOLUB!!!
Please. Don't take his class if it is the first time programming.
Dont take this class, wait till next semster to get a diffrent professor. Dont come crying to me when your not doing so hot cause ur taking this guy.

He doesn't give any feedback on your assignments, making you rely on your peers for help. You could have no idea what he's asking for on the exams due to his poor wording. The class also has people who barely failed the exemption test; this means that there are people who have extensive experience in Java, who mess up any possible curves for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This dude is arrogant and only cares about his research. His lectures were pointless and I ended up self-teaching most of the course work. Some projects are fun but his descriptions make them very hard to understand.

Dear God. Do not take Evan Golub. The man meanders his way through 50 minute lectures containing 10 minutes of true class material. Avoid if you can; good luck if you can't. Personally, I had little difficulty with the actual concepts covered in this course. I have a bit of programming experience, but nothing that should give me a huge edge.

Golub's not a bad professor, especially if you have some programming experience coming in. Exams are fair. Definitely understand where the student complaints are coming from though. Work through a java course online before you take this class!
NEVER TRY TO TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: His lectures are sometimes boring and the exams can be challenging if you don't have much Comp Sci experience, but he is easily approachable and can answer questions you may have. The TAs are also helpful and friendly. The projects are pretty manageable but can be tricky at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Clicker questions are annoying and force you to show up for class. If you've taken any comp sci course before the class is pretty easy and less work than the other 131 profs. His lectures are boring and dry. Make sure to review the study questions he posts. Overall not too bad.

recently theres been a few instances where i devote my soul and entire life preparing for tests. I dont know what it is, or what organ i need to sacrifice next but it seems like no matter what i do i cant get a good grade on the tests. Im on my last kidney, lung, and leg here. reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: So, if you're pretty familiar with Java, you'll likely get an A in this class and projects will be a breeze, but Golub is a really bad lecturer. He doesn't make it easy to learn and you probably won't walk out of this class prepared to take other CS classes if you're new to programming. Avoid him at all costs.
Extremely off-topic terrible TA's lectures do not make sense

Overall he is a good professor, and truly cares about the subject and teaching the students, and seems to have refined the class a lot to meet the objective of the class. Some people seem to miss details he says, or zone out during his lectures. I found his stories to be pretty good to make 351 engaging, although he can go astray. Best 351 option.

reviews.comment: While Golub is great at taking student concerns into account and is very fair when curving the class, his lectures do not make much sense. He goes on tangents about his life during lecture and puts topics on the exams that he didn't cover/teach well.
Aight dawgs, if its your first time programming, and have never coded before, avoid this professor like u one of character from the walking dead running away from the walkers
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Like many people have said, this course is very easy for those who already know Java. Golub uses clicker questions so you have to come to class, but he gives back 2 points at the end of the semester and they are only graded for participation. Exams are fair as they are based on information covered in lecture and projects and they are curved.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Students taught themselves how to do projects, and the same information you "taught" yourself was then tested. This course with Prof Golub is a living nightmare and no amount of free time will allow you to succeed if you don't already know the material. While loving my first semester at college, I hated this class specifically.

Golub does not explain anything. Your best bet would be to take this class with another professor. His projects are meant for people who already know Java. There are no resources to help you study. The exams are hard and not easy to pass. They cover things that are not even taught in class. I wish I had dropped out when I had the chance.

I think many know this by now, but Golub is one of the worst CS teachers in the department. His lecture time is spent talking about himself or going off on tangents about irrelevant things. People usually just spend the whole time on their laptops doing work for other classes. His tests were fair. The projects had the worst wording I've ever seen.

If you are good at java his class will be brutally boring and you will learn nothing. However, if you don't have a good amount of experience in java it is easy to get lost and fail the class because he barely cover what is needed for the exams and projects he just goof off the entire lecture and once you are lost it almost impossible to catch up

I just started java and I didn't look at the reviews for this teacher, but then I found out that he gave so many projects (one every other week) and for someone who hasn't done java, this was brutal b/c I had to go to office hours everyday. Exams are hard af with trick questions and poor wording. Office hours are crowded . PLS don't take him. :(

Golub uses clickers, so you have to come to class. However, he doesn't actually teach anything. Instead of talking about useful things in the lecture, he told stories about his old jobs and that actually weren't relevant to the class at all and then expected us to know random things he spent 3 minutes talking about for the test.

Golub is not somebody that you want to take. His lectures are him rambling about what he has done outside of class. If you want any actual help from him you have to go to office hours. He is helpful one on one, but a useless lecturer. You will NOT learn from him. You must self teach at all times if you want to learn anything. Avoid at all cost.

He is a super swell guy. Golub is a little bit awful at just about everything. Actually, wait, he is more than a little bit awful. Evan Golub is not one of my favorite people, although I am sure that he is for about two people at least, who are probably now not existent anymore, like his ability to teach students computer science at the Maryland

He tries to to make the class engaging but this may come off as rambling to some people. He is very approachable outside of class and helps you works through any problem clearly without just giving you the answer. The course is a breeze if you have some java experience. Liking him as a prof. is hit or miss and based on what teaching style you like

reviews.comment: First semester, got him as my cmsc 131 prof. Just like all the other people said, boring lectures, didn't care about the students and really really love to brag about his achievements. Small talk at the first 20 min of the classes. Not recommended if you never had java before.

Good: -Is not too strict about laptops/phones in lectures, so long as you answer clicker Q's -Usually easier Bad: -Requires class attendance by grading your in-class response on "clickers" (TurningTechnologies ResponseCard) -Likes to brag about things he has done or things his students have done that don't relate at all to what you are learning
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you already know the basics of Java, this class will be easy but painfully boring. Bring other homework to do during lectures, so you can still get clicker points and not completely waste your time. If you don't know Java at all, you won't learn anything from him.

Alright broskis this is whats up y'all, k so if youve taken some hard core comp sci class before, then this is just another one of those if ya know what i mean dawg.  But  if ya havent even a clue bout comp sci then boy oh boy are u in for rough ride my friend.   Like ur probs gonna fail if u bring xBoxs to class or if u like being a social human..

His lectures are absolutely useless. He spends 5 minutes actually talking about relevant topics, and the rest babbling. His project descriptions can be annoyingly obtuse, making them more of a chore than the programming actually requires. His exams are straightforward if you pay attention to what he says during lecture, which you probably won't.

Golub honestly doesn't teach. He thinks he's hilarious and in lecture he'll often go off on useless tangents talking about something that doesn't matter or trying to set up a joke that's not even funny. He makes you use clickers to force you to come to class, but class is pretty useless whether you know the material already or not. Don't take him.

Take this course if you like: 1 Teach yourself everything 2 Attend every boring lecture  3 Professor boasting and bragging 4 Have horrible exams in which the topics are not covered in lecture nor will ever be used in your future career 5 Uncertainty about your letter grade because the professor change it to something he thinks "you deserve"

I could not understand any thing he talked in our class this whole semester. Maybe he himself can do some codes well. But he has no ability of answering any question raised by us student. I did self-study of all of the projects and labs out of class. I didn't ask any help from him because he just cannot help.

Golub is a terrible professor. 60% of your grade is determined by exams and the final, all of which ask extremely specific questions about things you don't need to know about when actually coding. I took AP programming in high school and got a 4 on the exam, but this class was still a struggle for me due to golubs awful teaching. Hope for a good TA
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I had done little coding before 131 and I did learn, but mainly b/c I read the optional textbook and put in extra time. He's not a difficult prof per se, but he's a pretty terrible teacher. His slides are devoid of useful information, his lectures are ramble-y and irrelevant, and students don't respect him and talk through the whole class. Avoid.

reviews.comment: The teaching style overall was very poor. I have taken Comp Sci before and the way I was taught here, it was horrible. I learned less, I mostly didn't understand what I was doing, the lectures nor the labs helped much. I think the projects suck. The instructions online are very poorly explained. The class was mandatory but otherwise a huge waste.

This is the worst professor. He talks about himself:-he spent a whole week talking about a selfie stick he coded for his android phone :X , then gives you a project to do that has nothing to do with the slides he provided.   Don't take the class!!! RUN!!
I know CS is hard, but this professor made it even harder for no reason. All he does in class is make stupid jokes and doesn't really teach you anything however expect you know most of the stuff.

This guy! The trick to doing well in his class is to trick yourself into being interested in his pointless, time-consuming tangents so you don't miss something important, because he sprinkles in important stuff into the 50 minutes of random crap that is the lecture. He's a terrible professor. PLEASE AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS!!!! My GPA dropped down only because of him. HORRIBLE PROFESSOR!!! He really is a pain in the ass. He keeps on narrating his own stories in class and never focuses on the main point. He is just complete TRASH.  Not only this, he never teaches anything properly and expects us to perform well on exams and quizzes. I shall never take this guy again
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Golub is pretty terrible, he often rambles for a good 15 minutes and never teaches the material in an easy to learn manner. You're much better off just reading the slides and looking at examples on the internet. However, he does clickers for a computer science class which is absurd so you have to be there to listen to him ramble.

Professor Golub is incredibly obsessed with himself. He makes jokes that only he laughs at.  He does a below-par job at explaining how the code actually works. It's very easy to find yourself sleepy and annoyed during lecture.  I strongly recommend choosing a different teacher for this class.

Had him for 250. Teaches 1 or 2 examples in lecture, but not the underlying principles used so you can apply them to different questions on the homework. Out of a 75 minute lecture, spent 30 minutes teaching, and the rest of the time he was talking about his undergraduate days. The TA's could have done an infinitely better job teaching the course
Oh god please never again.

He is not only the single worst professor I have ever had, he is one of the worst human beings I have ever met. His classes are boring, and explain nothing. He spends most of the time trying to make stupid jokes that no one laughs at. You will learn nothing from his class! I  got an A, but I taught myself everything. He is worthless as a professor.

He is the worst professor ever. You will not learn anything in his lectures as he wastes most of the lecture time going over his stupid stories. He will test you on the future material, that will be shown after you have already taken your test. Projects were really hard. You should start them early.

This is the worst professor i had in my life. I don't like the way he teaches. His lectures is long and is helpless. His Exam and final Exam is extremely hard and are made for someone who had experience for coding. If you never do coding before, please avoid this professor. Quiz are hard too and projects take a lot of time to finish it.
horrible person, horrible class

He sometimes makes me loose focus with his  tangents. I don't like how he won't let us start the projects until a certain date, giving us less time to work on it. The projects were interesting and helpful, but can take a while. There are quizzes and 3 annoyingly long exams. You don't need the book and he posts his lectures on the website.

He easily goes off topic so you won't even finish lecture sometimes, not to mention you will have to study a lot on your own if you want to comprehend the material.  Be sure to go to lecture, he posts the slides online but they'll barely make sense if you don't hear him explain them.  The TAs are awesome, teacher not so much
This guy will bore you to tears and waste all of your time.

This class is designed to essentially weed out those who are not meant for computer science. He didn't make an effort to make his lectures easier to understand. rather he made it really hard and often went off on tangents bragging about his and his students' works. if you have programming experience, this is fine but if you don't, find another.

Just a very confusing man. My best way to tackle his class was to go to lecture, listen to his main points and sit there researching and taking notes on the rest. He loves to give quizzes on stuff you barely think you covered, but thankfully doesn't make them worth much of your grade. You better pray for a good TA.
Overall good professor.  He conveyed the basics of CS well.  I felt he made the lectures interesting

Golub tried to be a funny guy, but ended up going off on tangents and squealing with laughter at his own dumb jokes. His lectures literally dumbed me down for CMSC132. If you're taking this class as a CS/CE major, don't take him.
Not sure why there are so many negative reviews... computer science by nature is tough to grasp at first, but Golub does a good job conveying the concepts.  Very helpful during office hours

This guy has rekindled my love for programming.  I don't know why people gave him such a low score. Not only is his jovial personality refreshing, but it makes you more interested in the material.  One of my all-time favorite teachers.

A waky and weird but cool instructor. I took him for an honors clss in photograph (which to my dismay involved programming things for some reason), but he is cool. Beware of falling alseep in his class- they can be very boring in the begining of the semester. But for the effort he puts in I say he is overall energetic and understanding.

Do NOT take Golub. He is very confusing, expects TOO MUCH from the students with very little explanation! It is a lot of work and the tests are set up for the student to fail. His lectures are boring, not to mention draining. Golub is not helpful and you have to figure out a lot of the material on your own...Avoid his class

Definitely the worst teacher I have ever had, he is also a bit prejudice and very basis. He teaches
Golub is a decent teacher, lectures are pretty boring but he is pretty fair. I have heard from others that Fawzi Emad is the better choice for this class.

His class is setup very structurally. Usually each class is about one topic and that one topic will turn into one question on his test. Make sure you can do each of these problems and you will do fine in his class

Pros: He curves heavily, which only highlights his failure to adequately explain the material to the class.  Cons: The book is TERRIBLE and the exams are AWFUL - they are either blindsides, mind-reading exercises or both, and account for more than 80% of your grade.  You WILL be tested on material you haven't seen in class.  Avoid Golub like death.

I guess I'm the only one but I felt like Golub was a very clear, concise and helpful teacher. Yes you have to go to class because he doesn't plus full lecture notes online. If you do go to class he gives lots of examples and his test questions are very close to the examples given in class. Go to see Golub in office hours he is very very helpful.

This is the worst professor I ever had. His lectures are easy to follow and understand, the homework is hard and you cant find too much help, and his tests are impossible. His "good ideas" don't help with anything. And in reality, i had an understanding where i can use this kind of stuff in the past, but because of him, I want to drop this major.
He is the worst professor I have ever had.  This is the only class I have dropped in college.  He is boring, nerdy and self-absorbed.  This man belongs behind a computer; not amongst society.

I can honestly say that I've worked hard in this class I'm still not doing very well in the class.  Why?  Trivial mistakes in your work can result in loss of all credit.  Tests, which are more than 80% of the final grade, are not based so much on lecture material as his "clever" ideas.  He has a lot of trouble communicating his ideas.

Pros: Nice guy; graphic tablet works for teaching; knows Algorithms very well. ----Cons: Test problems always feature concepts or techniques that are not covered; posts many "thought questions" but does not give GOOD answers to them even in office hours. Whatever you do, don't make even a small mistake on a test - it will cost you a full 25 points.

Bias alert: I'm currently failing 351.   Golub is a really boring professor teaching boring material.  He isn't all that helpful (posts only useless parts of lecture notes online) and is a very tough grader.  However, the class is fairly easy, I don't blame him for me failing.  He curves pretty well, but you really need to be attentive to get an A.

His lectures are okay, but his examples can be a bit hard to follow.  It's not difficult to do well in his class, but some of his exam questions are overly difficult and can be vague in terms of what he is really asking.  He is very helpful during office hours and will go out of your way to explain things to you before and after class.

I honestly have no idea who put this guy into a teaching environment. He tells the same mind-numbing stories multiple times in a semester, wastes class time babbling about unrelated crap, and tests you on concepts you have seen ONCE, tops, in a single step of a project. Boring as hell in lecture, don't buy the book- he wrote it.
Boring, not accurate to the class description. Miserable experience

Class is all about the Unix command line.  It's fine for me since I've used it before but a LOT of my classmates are having a hard time because they have no experience with Unix.  Notes are all online, so going to class is optional.  Most of lecture is spent listening to golub talk about how he traced this person or that person's internet traffic

Students of UMCP's Comp Science major.  Golub is an AWFUL choice!  He is an unreasonable, vague, and arrogant professor.  His tests are really hard.  His ability to teach is nil.  If you don't want to repeat any course he teaches, avoid him like plague.  I just want you to spare future frustration you will experice if you choose him.  STAY AWAY!

class is probably the most droning thing you'll ever experience. none of the material will ever help in any faction of life unless you're that big of a nerd. not a hard class at all, just painfully boring. bring your laptop for something to do. golub's definitely not on my fave profs list. he's not rude or anything but incredibly dull and nerdy.

Bad, unfair professor with an inflated sense of self-importance in himself and his subject.  Exams were impossible.  The paper required a ridiculous amount of garbage sci-fi reading.  Way too difficult for a 100 level non major course.  If you find yourself stuck, your only hope is the projects.  Just avoid this class.

If you want a decent grade, don't take this class. It's that simple. All the exams boast complete recall (i.e. fill in the blanks, absolutely NO multiple choice) and the classes are completely unhelpful. However, you can at least get all the material you need from the textbook.... wait nevermind there is no textbook.

If you didnt kiss ass he wouldnt talk to u.  I would raise my hand constantly in class and he'd never call on me (I was a cute girl).  When it came to the exams, we would have the exact same answers that he had in his lecture notes and he would mark them as wrong to show his power. We filed formal complaint which did no good because he has tenure.

Simply boring. Class becomes naptime very quickly. He does, however, allow laptops in class, giving at least something to do. He teaches from notes he posts online, and the class can be learned from reading them at home. The projects are incredibly easy if you just do them. Tests can be hard. He needs a new hair style…

So the material is very easy to learn if another professor teaches it.  But somehow, Golub manages to mess up whatever he teaches.  His tests are incredibly unrealistic and long, and he is very unorganized.  He goes off on tangents and his lectures put you to sleep.  I am decently computer literate, and i pulled Ds on his tests...wtf?

golub is horrible. he's not very lenient, and his exams are horrible.  i was interested in the class at first, but the way he goes about teaching the course is just poor.  he asks for thoughts from the class, but if ur wrong he basically makes you feel stupid with his response... he makes up his own complicated grade scales too. pick another prof

very friendly and kind.  however, not flexible at all, very forgetful and unorganized. assignments are computer submitted and 3 of mine were lost.  tests require a lot of memorization but are not too difficult and are graded easily.  lectures intolerably boring.

This course should be called "Networking in a command line environment." The tests require you to MEMORIZE all unix commands, the entire HTML, CSS, and Java languages. The class is a LECTURE, so if you learn how to do this stuff then you probably should be a compsci major. Otherwise, you're screwed if you dont get outside help from people who TEACH

Im sitting in class at the moment and I can't wait till its over. He is inconsiderate of test time. He doesn't give enought time to complete them. For an entry level class, it requires too much work from you. He isn't too helpful if you have questions. In other words, he tells you to go back to notes.

Very boring lectures, but would still recommend you goto them for the examples. Easy A if you do exactly what is required and FOLLOW the directions to the letter. So if he tells you to label a file someway label it that way and you should not loss points.
not very flexible with things at all. sees life in ones and zeros

Very easy course, and you get to learn how to use programs like telnet. This class was honestly EXTREMELY boring, but I learned a lot. DON'T BUY THE TEXTBOOK!!! You only need his lecture notes, so don't waste your money. You do need the "leonardo's labtop" book though. Good luck!!

His lectures were VERY LONG and VERY BORING. It's difficult to stay awake and get key points. His exam format is VERY LONG, over 45 questions and they aren't multiple choice or T/F. The subject matter is very interesting but the way he presents it and the way the course is set up needs to improve.
Kind of looks like the comic book store guy from the Simpsons.  Made us read a very good book called "Cuckoo's Egg".
I can't stand the way he teaches this course.  He makes it too slow and boring.
Made me work for what I thought would be a fluff course, but got a lot out of it.
She is a very hard grader and expects a lot of students. She makes her courses harder than most STEM courses.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She knows her stuff, a lot of reading and funny at times

Prof Merediz is very intimidating and strict  she controls the class based on fear of the students. She will make you work hard and does give pop quizzes. I would not take again  it was wayyy too much work for an Intro Lit class (we're talking three hour films). Clearly knows her stuff though

Profesora Merediz is knowledgeable, connected, funny, opinionated, clever, and will make you work your tail off. Pretty sure she personally knows all the contemporary authors studied, you won't BS her. She finds ways to help students wade through even the very densest material. She makes you want to know more. OUTSTANDING educator.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: She is extremely funny and genuinely cares about the students. She may come off as harsh or scary on the first day but the class gets better. Very discussion based but I don't talk and am currently an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof. Merediz is funny and outgoing. However, she comes across as abrasive with some of her answers to your comments or questions.  Her opinion rules the class.

Professor Merediz is a great teacher who makes sure students are engaged with the class material. Her classes are very didactic and you never get bored. I strongly recommend taking at least one class with her. She expects students to be prepared for class but you learn a lot.
Do your work and you will be fine. Read!-She is great. She knows her stuff
She is not easy but she is the best professor I have had, she knows her stuff, pretty entertaining. If you actually want to learn something take her class.
No Comments

She was the toughest professor I had at Maryland. Very critical and had extremely high expectations. But, she was the best damn professor I had there and I learned so much from her. I am so lucky that I got to take two courses with her. Sure, she scared the heck out of me; I guess that's the way I learn best. And, I did learn the most from her.
Uses blue books, makes us read a book she wrote with her dad.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is about race in the media. Ironically, it is taught by a white woman. She definitely has experience with race in the media, growing up traveling with her dad who was reporting. However, this woman didn't even know what the NAACP stood for. If you're teaching this class... you should probably know that.

Turned in at least 7 members of the class for plagiarism, all of whom were excused. Is not responsive to students, nor does she give good feedback. She either does not respond or is very rude in her response. Her actual lectures are pretty good, I do feel like I learned a lot from being in class. Enjoyed the class, did not enjoy her.

A very good professor that made journalism enjoyable for someone who doesn't like journalism at all! Her class was very discussion heavy which I loved and you still learned a lot. There is a group project at the end that is pretty open-ended. The only thing is that the final exam is based off the 'lectures' and they were pretty much nonexistent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Probably one of the best classes I took during the Spring semester. There's A LOT of group discussion, a few short papers, but no actual homework. The only problem was the class wasn't nearly long enough. As soon as the discussions got really intense, class was over :(

Fardina is great! The lecture slides are a bit heavy, but the concepts are explained really well. The exams are definitely harder than before, but the average is still pretty decent. I actually love the homework assignments! Oh, and there's this group data science project that's super helpful for your portfolio.

Dr. Alam is amazing! Her slides are clear and easy to follow, and she genuinely cares about making sure we understand the material. The homework is challenging but fun, like solving a puzzle. Sometimes the wording is a bit unclear, but she and the TAs are quick to clear things up on Piazza. Overall, she's a great professor!
The class is organized so well and Dr. Alam is very caring about her students. Few of the assignments were tricky but very enjoyable.
Faith is one of my favorite teachers. She's funny and does not take her job too serious. As long as you put a little bit of effort in theres no reason you shouldn't comfortably get an A.

Very passionate about COMM107 and first time teaching in the US but did a great job. Is a very fair grader and if you think this is a class you can just pass by not showing up or doing the bare minimum you might not get the grade you want. She takes attendance and gives out fair grades based on your work. Take her if you want to learn something
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really nice professor! It was her first year, but she was very understanding and push back deadlines. Show up and participate and it is an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Sumin was interesting, to say the least. She was difficult as a professor. When asking for help she will only help you once as it's "not fair to other students". I found this incredibly unfair. I didn't find her grading hard, but I found her class draining, especially ATTENDANCE.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (My review is for CMNS175 at UFV, not Maryland sorry) Very fun and engaging lectures. Class is graded on 5 assignments, 1 every 2 weeks. Clear feedback. To be honest her assignments can be done without attending a single lecture, however she marks attendance. Lectures kind of give basic info, wished she would go in-depth more
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Im taking Sumin for CMNS 175 and CMNS 465. She is the nicest and funniest professor. She really cares for her students and she make her classes so engaging. Her teaching style is very hands on and she will clarify anything you don't understand. She is a tough grader but she is happy to review your work in advance. I definitely recommend her.

Sumin is a passionate prof. I took her CMNS 125** online course and found that she set clear expectations for each assignment. All of her assignments were very interesting and fun to complete. She held "meetings" for 30 mins every Monday where she would discuss the upcoming assignment and told us what she expected. OVERALL she was great :D

Gives rubrics but doesn't follow them and grades everything differently. Gives harsh feedback in class for whole class to witness. Doesn't understand student topics chosen and will recommend to change topic. When students ask to not be called on calls on them anyways. Classroom doesn't feel like a good place for discussion. Knowledgable on subject.

For her paraphrasing is not paraphrasing its plagiarism. She doesnt make her assignment expectations clear enough for a student. She is one of the worst professors at the university of the fraser valley. It was a bad experience. She doesnt know her grammar and shes teaching communication. Extremely high ego and extremely rude and slow response.

Took CMNS125 at UFV with her and I would never take any course with her. She reuses material she made ages ago. No teaching, no explanation, no clear guidance on what she expects in her assignments. So many teaching errors. Never was she able to answer a meaningful question from a student. Grading? Definitely baseless. You'll regret taking her.
Comm107 is such a boring class but Sumin tries to make it fun. She is very sweet and even though some of her grading can be a little weird, anyone who takes her should get an A. It's not hard.

Besides the reading and the discussion posts, Sumin was a really great teacher and I would definitely recommend her. She is a bit brutally honest and speaks her mind, but 100% doesnt mean harm. As long as you try and prepare your speeches, youd get a good grade. She was always very nice and she rewarded those who tried in her class.

Sumin was a fun professor, but her grading was a little harsh sometimes. She is somewhat inflexible on rules and rubrics, but if you make an improvement, she will give you a good grade. Be careful about due dates and time requirements for speeches. Her in-class activities were fun, and the class had a pretty relaxed atmosphere by the end.

Professor Fang was really enjoyable and the person from 2016 obviously was not a good student because it is tough to not pass this class with flying colors. The speeches were fun and professor did a lot of fun games to make the lectures not boring. Helped my public speaking a lot and was my favorite c lass during that semester.

You absolutely have to go to class, she takes attendance right at the beginning. If you want an easy comm107 class don't go with her. A lot of comm107 professors are chill and lenient but she is pretty strict about rules. Turning in work late is impossible
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Charles tries to make evolution exciting. His lectures are full of stories and he seems to have a lot of experience. He writes his tests but you can take them in pairs. The only bad thing about his class is he likes to make uncomfortable remarks/jokes (think sexual selection) and while they are kinda funny, they probably should not be said....

I love the material covered in this class so I may by bias but I felt the class was easy. Everything he teaches comes from the text and is a good back ups to his lectures. He offers extra credit & provides you with his previous exams which are very similar to the current. I don't understand all the bad reviews, I found this professor very helpful.

This professor is the worst man you will ever meet. His lectures are horrible and he doesn't know how to teach. He is a terrible communicator. And if it's the last class you need to graduate, he could care less.
Evolution 370
fenster tries to be interesting and takes time out to engage the class, as long as you read the text his lectures make sense

verrrry boring.....seemed unprepared for some lectures at times. His tests are not horribly difficult but since he writes his owns questions, they are confusing and tend to have errors. Overall all he was an average profesor which equated to an average course
His class may be boring, but overall he tries to be funny, so it is a okay class!

He is a very boring lecturer, however he takes exam questions right out of lecture and past exams (that he posts on his webpage).  Also, his lecture notes aren't comprehensive at all.  Fill in the gaps with what he says and you're fine.  The only things I really hated about this class were the tedious papers.  I hardly did any work and I got an A.
He is not a teacher. bad lectures, often irrelavent notes. not very understanding or comprimising either. hope you get a good ta or you are probably better off dropping the class.

Horrible Lectures. Dont bother trying to pay attention if you get lost. Print lecture notes and use the text to fill them out. good T.A.+ read the text balance out bad teacher. Do the practice exams and quiz and the class aint bad
This professor was extremely boring and is horrible at lecturing, he just stands up there saying uhh the whole time making everyone more confused then when we started-including himself
No Comments

Professor Feehan is actually one of my favorite teachers I have ever had in my life, outside of college too. He genuinely cares about his students and will give you a run for your money in any argument you make (can be annoying but only because it makes you think). He is super chill with extensions if you need them and super knowledgable!

I loved this class. He was so engaging and the class discussions were so amusing every time. He also is very funny and personable. The workload in the class is slim to none. We had weekly discussions posts that were easy. Than a couple major assignments but nothing crazy. Overall I would love to take another class with him.
My favorite professor so far, taking a class with him again next semester. He gives very interesting lectures and everyone liked him. I looked forward to his discussions.

LTC feehan is a great professor, I took him for PLCY 401 and 101. he is a military official and takes his lectures seriously. However he makes it fun in a sense especially if you participate. He is one of the best professors at UMD and is very understandable if you do your work and come to class. Most of my other policy professors are boring.

LTC Feehan isn't really a professor, but an amazing lecturer for PLCY101. He's funny, introduces very interesting topics, and loves to see debates based on people's values, the situation of the present, and policy at the moment. I highly recommend! Attendance is not mandatory, but it is super fun and information to attend lectures/discussion.

Dr. Feng is okay. He cares very much and his main goal is to help each student succeed, and he is very flexible and reachable. The reason that he's only okay is that he has a thick accent, which makes him very hard to understand. The content he teaches, the content in the textbook, and the content on exams are not completely parallel.

Prof Feng is a great guy who clearly cares about what he is teaching. Unfortunately, there were 7ish total assignments for the entire semester so if you missed points on one then it was a big issue. His exams also got better throughout the semester but he has a more prominent accent that can be difficult to understand at times.

Dr. Feng is a great professor in that he's very accommodating for just about anything, he's very sweet and clearly cares about his students. Textbook is required, but free. However, the course is graded off of only a few things, exams contain random unrelated info, and he's got a thick accent that's hard to understand. But he's a great guy.

I had a really good experience with orgo 1. Homework is all for completion, and the exams are all fair. It's totally possible to get 100% on every exam if you just study enough. Extra credit trivia questions are on every exam too. Attendance is (kinda) mandatory because of clicker questions at the end of every class.

Absolutely the best!! He's so kind and his exams are very fair and the averages are usually much higher than any other orgo class. I would just say he tends to be a bit scattered in lecture but as long as you go over discussion slides and the practice exams you'll be absolutely fine. Such a wonderful professor!

Dr Falvey is the sweetest professor at umd. He is always so jolly and cheerful during lectures its really hard not to smile and laugh along with him. Exams are very fair and accurate representation of lecture material. Easy to do well on if you study. I highly recommend taking him if you ever get the chance. Overall Class average was pretty high.

Dr. Falvey is so so sweet. It felt like I was learning ochem from Santa. He explains things very clearly and included real life examples which made the class/subject much more interesting. Initially, I was scared of taking ochem but he made it much more enjoyable (still studied hard tho). Take him, You won't regret it!

Dr. Falvey made the material in orgo 2 applicable to every day life, making it less abstract and providing reasons for why you should actually care about the material. He essentially makes it impossible to fail the class through his extra credit, although his tests can be hard. I feel so fortunate to have taken him for orgo 2-- great professor!

Dr. Falvey is a very nice and enthusiastic professor, esp. for a 9 am lecture. However, I found that the way he presented information was unorganized. He also requires you to memorize equilibrium arrows for each step of every reaction. Not NMR nor synthesis heavy, usually only 1 question each per exam. Each exam is 60% from old exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is not as easy as everyone saying it is. The TA is not the best and she really doesn't help students, she posts old discussion worksheets and that is pretty much it. The exams are pretty difficult, however if you do all the homework problems that are assigned (it's a lot) and go to office hours you should be okay.

(Note: taken during covid-19 pandemic) Great professor. Orgo 2 is a hard class, but he broke it down very well. Lectures were extremely informative. His molecules of the day were fun, easy points on exams. Weird curve and extra credit policy, but it helps. My one problem is that your entire grade is based on exams. Would recommend to anyone!
He's a great lecturer, and makes an attempt to keep it interesting with his stories. Do the homework! Lots of exam questions are pulled from the HW.

Dr. Falvey is a phenomenal lecturer, and I can't stress how FAIR he is! You can't complain about him bc of your grade because he's so fair. Doing ALL homework problems (not required) & going to discussion helps. Exams were straightforward. He is enthusiastic which is necessary for a 9am lecture. Great prof, gives me hope for the chem department!

Falvey is a great professor and is straight forward! What he teaches in class and optional homework problems are the exams. DO THE TEXTBOOK PROBLEMS and practice the mechanisms and you will easily get Bs on the exam. Class grade is just clickers and exams. He's a great professor and is very interested in what he teaches!

If you have the option to take Orgo II with Dr. Falvey, definitely don't hesitate. He is a fantastic professor whose lectures are very manageable and easy to follow. The book problems and his old exams are very helpful when studying for lecture exams. I was never good at organic chemistry and managed to do very well in his class. Highly recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Falvey is a great professor for orgo. He's a great lecturer and his exams are manageable. Make sure to study the textbook problems and old exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors of all time. Dr. Falvey truly cares about his students and offers plenty of outside resources for help in class. All of his tests follow a consistent format, very similar to the practice test he has online for each exam. Many of the test questions are problems gone over in class, from book problems & tests.

Falvey is probably one of the best professors I've had. He is very fair and often reuses problems from old exams. Some material isn't taught in class, so go through textbook. No homework, but clickers are extra credit. He likes to call on people, but don't be too intimidated; he's super friendly. Definitely cares and makes class interesting.

Solid lecturer. Tests are challenging and you need to put in the work to do well, you get a free 10 points on every test if you learn the molecules he gives at lect, and he usually puts a few of his HW prob on tests. His extra credit is a "quiz" at the end of every class that boosts you one +/- at the end of the semester in addition to the curve.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you dread taking orgo, Prof. Falvey will change your mind. He has excellent pacing in his lecture, breaks down reactions/mechanisms on the board and explains what happens in each step clearly AND pulls exam questions from the recommended textbook problems and questions done in discussion/lecture. I barely passed orgo 1, I got an A in II.

Falvey's class is do-able if you have enough time to read through his old exams, and do all of his practice problems  because he puts random problems on the exams. He also expects you to memorize molecules that he calls "Molecules of the Day", which are a free 10-30 points. His clickers are NOT extra credit. READ THE SYLLABUS!!!

Take Falvey! He really wants his students to do well and do their best. He tries to explain things and will answer questions anyone has. Make sure you study all his old exams on blackboard because his exam questions are really similar to those

I haven't finished this course yet, but so far this is the best organic prof I've had. His exams don't try and trick you; most of the problems are directly from the text or posted problems. Lectures are interesting, funny, and clear. He's very involved in class, will email the class practice probs and knows students by name. I HIGHLY recommend him.

The key word here is: disorganized. The lectures are hard to follow and the explanations do little to explain the actual physics going on. It's possible to leave with a good grade and still not have a feel for what NMR is about. Nevertheless, it's probably the best course-based introduction you'll get to NMR at UMD. READ THE BOOK.

Lots of readings, lots of quizzes, but they help cushion your grade for the papers. Professor Feldstein has lots of knowledge to share from being in the business, but also makes lectures engaging and interesting! Participation is a big chunk of your grade, but the discussions are chill and open-ended. I loved this class, Feldstein, and TA Ivy!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This professor is easily the coolest person you will ever meet. He has so much experience in his field and literally tells stories about how he was beaten up and imprisoned while he investigated stories. His enthusiasm and candor are fantastic and lead to a wonderful teaching experience. He's much better in person than on Zoom!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Feldstein is really good at what he does and is very funny! Make sure to do the readings because it's usually quizzed but they're not insanely hard. Participation is also counted so beware to contribute to discussions but they're always interesting and a lot of time he just asks for your opinion on scandals. Would def recommend this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He was a great professor. This class was the most interesting class I've taken so far. Although there was a decent amount of work, it was very manageable. I think that if you're interested in scandals or the stuff on the syllabus, the class will be a cakewalk for you.

If you don't participate in this course then you will most likely fail or be close to failing. Your overall participation is graded at the end of the semester which means you have to attend class daily and participate in lectures. There are pop quizzes in almost every class which also means that you have to do a lot of readings in your spare time.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The class is manageable and the structure is the same all semester. Mandatory lectures (really interesting), short readings assigned every class and a pop quiz on on them at the beginning of the next class (very easy), 4 short essays (kinda harshly graded) but if you ask for feedback and participate a lot you'll be just fine. TA & prof. are nice!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: A number of essays throughout that are graded VERY harshly. I was lucky to be a good essay writer, but if you're not in the same boat, you won't fare well. Also, you MUST attend class and you MUST speak - often. The final paper was an insane amount of points. I took it P/F because of I was scared of what the final would do to my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: take this class! its very interesting and not that much work if u pay attention in class. just be sure to participate a lot b/c that will lowkey carry ur grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: i enjoyed the class. participation matters alot but overall it was an interesting class and the prof gave many opportunities for students to talk. there are a lot of readings but i just usually skimmed them before class. there are a couple essays but the ta gives back really good feedback.i would def recommend the class but u just need to put work!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you dont speak up in class, you will get a bad grade for participation. Some of the toughest essay grades I have received, which is especially strange for a GenED class. Unless you are a great essay writer and super attentive to detail, you will do poorly. He does not listen to student feedback and you will feel lost at some point.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: this class is super interesting and worth ur time. there's a lot of reading u have to do, but if u skim over it and contribute to discussion, you'll be just fine (all the topics r rly cool). u do have to write essays but honestly, they're not that bad at all. if you put in the effort you'll do much better than u think u might. would def take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Just pick a different I Series class. This class is interesting because you learn about scandals in history and current events but it was super unorganized with taking quizzes and general class structure. The syllabus often changed last minute. Unless you really like to write and are good at it, you'll be graded harshly on the essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class was very interesting. Although the lectures are long, they can be interesting depending on the topic but they are pretty interactive. The students get to voice their opinions on some subjects. This class does take some work. It isn't necessarily hard but it takes effort. Just turn things in and put in effort and you'll get a good grade.

There was a lot of reading and the lectures were basically discussing the readings, which could be repetitive. However, Prof Feldstein was pretty cool and had interesting stories about his time as an investigative journalists. There are not many assignments, but he still seems to be an easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Feldstein is a really nice guy and really engaging but the class is challenging. The TA is the worst, grades super harshly just to assert power. For an elective, it is unnecessarily difficult to achieve a good overall grade in the course. Learning about scandals and corruption is interesting but the stress of this class is not worth it.

I took SOCY410 and I really enjoyed the class. Professor Chen is an expert on demography and her lectures are never boring. Participation was graded through in-class assignments, studying for the one test was necessary (!), homework assignments were easy, & final paper was easy but a lot of work.

Dr. Chen is very smart, approachable, & is very passionate about demography. She focused a lot on China; we were a little behind on some readings but she knows & adjusts the exams accordingly- she really asks students if they want a quiz for extra credit that day or if a due date should get pushed back, etc. The textbook was a good read/relatable
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Chen talked very softly so it was hard to hear her over the slightest noise. Also she took up too much time talking about one topic so she was behind in the syllabus. She also went too quickly through the slides so it was very hard to keep up. Otherwise I thought the HWs helped with understanding statistics and constructing a hypothesis.

Learning from Pro. Flick was an awesome experience. He can be blunt but in a very nice and effective way. He truly believes that anyone can be taught to draw and if you do your work you will believe that at the end of the semester. He's passionate about art and believes in all of his students capabilities. He makes you take risks. Great TEACHER!!!!

He was very helpful. While it is an art class, he didn't tell you exactly what you needed to do to get an A, he allowed you to be creative, led you in the general direction and allowed you to explore it yourself. Very interesting, very fun. One of few classes I enjoyed attending thanks to the professor.
I thought he was awesome. Highly recommended
Head is stuck so far up his own a** not even the jaws of life can get it out.
No Comments
I liked him. Even though his comments can come off rude, hes just telling it how it is. If you actually care about the material and dont slack off, hes a totally great teacher.

At first she made the course sound really intimidating, but she's actually pretty easygoing with the assignments. She assigns a lot of homework all at once but it's usually not due for a few days. The only thing is if she says the test is in two days, read that as it'll really be in two weeks...also you'll never get your tests back.

Her class is enjoyable because she's funny but don't take this class if you care whether or not she actually grades your work. She doesn't. She gives everyone an A on exams because she doesn't have time to grade them or she forgets to grade them until 4 1/2 weeks later. She also likes to youtube italian music & shop on Dolce & Gabbana during class.

Professor Fleri is a really sweet, enthusiastic Italian teacher.  Very bubbly, warm personality.  She's very understanding about turning in assignments late and she really tries to make the class fun.  Only negative- takes forever to hand back tests/quizzes.  Otherwise great.

She seems like a nice lady, but the class is ridiculous. RIDICULOUS. Her TA is awful and even a harder grader than she is. It's all about how she interprets  the readings, and the midterm and final are awful. Papers are tedious, but easier than the exams. It is hard to take anything seriously in the class because of the nerdy texts. Stay away.
She knows her stuff, great discussions but she is a grammar and spelling nazi!

She grades way to hard, takes her class way too seriously. I did not take anything positive away from this class as I do in other classes. In other classes, you read a text and discuss it in ways that could benefit you in life, or at least another class. This class taught me about Orcs and elves and how do I apply that elsewhere in life? I don't.
Dr. Flieger's a great professor.  Her enthusiasm for Tolkien is contagious and her lectures are very clear.  Class grade is only based on four exams, but they're open book.
Great teacher! I like the Tolkien seminar that she teaches a lot. Mostly reading and the exams are based on her lectures which are really good. Highly recommend her class.

Full of nerds?  Heh, yeah, it is a class based on TOLKIEN.  She knows her stuff and has very strong opinions about it.  Encourages you to disagree, but time constraints usually preclude any real argument.  Lot of material in very little time.  Satisfying, overall.

You don't have to love myth to take her classes, you just have to be able to appreciate a breath of fresh air.  She is creative and educated and it comes accross with her choices of reading material.  One of the best classes I took at UMD
She's a tough grader, but you'll learn a lot.  Don't take her classes if you want an easy A.

I've taken 2 classes w/ her and am taking a 3rd one now (ENGL 639A). She is a wonderful, engaging professor who knows her material. She doesn't talk *that* much about Star Wars (maybe in other classes), but if she talks about Tolkien, it's because his world-building is a modern example of studying myth by making it (as is SW). It's all about myth.
If you don't want to discuss Lord of the Rings or Star Wars characters all day, don't bother taking this class.  It gets full of geeks.

I took her at UNC for COMM 471 Very knowledgable about monuments and commemorations. Very kind and creates an eviorment for great conversations. There is a lot of readings that tie to the class sometimes she gave pop quizzes but was lenient with grading and it didn't count as much against you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I love her so much! She is always ready to help you out when assignments and speeches. Very clear in what she wants but not a very tough grader. She will give you extra credit and gives great feedback. Overall I was extremely terrified of taking COMS but she is just the best!

Dr. Fitz is at UT Arlington now, + she's great. She's definitely passionate about what she teaches, and she actually cares about what our class discusses in our speeches. She can be very particular about the way things are done, especially outlines. Make sure you follow her directions to the T. Other than that, she's an amazing professor. 11/10!

Took her at UNT. Overall a good professor. You can tell she really, really, REALLY is invested in her comm. She's very good at explaining. Her personality can be kinda abrasive and cold at times. The test questions are very vague to where really any choice could be the answer, but she doesn't make the tests. But concepts are easy She is very smart.
She is very enthusiastic. The only thing is that Prof. Fitz can be particular about some things and it is hard to get everything right. Overall, it made for a fun class.

I only say this class was "hard" because she's weirdly particular. The material is straight forward but you can be deducted for some honestly stupid stuff, so you have to make sure you're on your game. There's no reason you shouldn't be able to do well, just read her guidelines carefully.

Taking COMM 230 with Ms. Fitz was totally awesome! She helps you tie all the concepts together and gives good examples on how to apply the material to when you are preparing for your own debates and presentations.

I loved Ms. Fitz! She was always super upbeat and actually made communication interesting and applicable to our lives. She is extremely knowledgeable despite her young age and gives a bunch of opportunities for extra credit. However, she is sort of a tough grader but it is absolutely possible to get a high A. Her tests are very easy.
Very passionate about her work and is a great teacher! Grading was quick and the long group project was made very manageable!

Dr. Fish is nice and listens to the students feedback. However, she can be petty when things do not go her way during lecture. For example, she got upset at the class because nobody was participating. She does unannounced in class assignments. She is an easier grader, but I think it's because the TA does the grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Love Dr. Fish! It's easy to tell that she is a caring professor. She takes student feedback into consideration, and is very accommodating. She does do unannounced in-class assignments, but you can miss a few. Grades leniently. Overall, a great professor and I would absolutely take her again.

Dr. Fink was wonderful! Her online class was straightforward, but a lot of work! You have to get a couple novels from the bookstore but you will use both throughout the whole semester. Pick a service project about something you genuinely are interested in and this class will be fun for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Fink is a passionate, accomodating professor who cares a lot about her students and disability studies. Even though she gives a lot of content to read and watch, they were all interesting and valuable to the class. Her grading criteria are clear, and she gives good feedback on every single assignment. I'd recommend her to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Fink is great. Learned a lot from working with her. Super supportive to students.
Very intense. Amazing gaining. High risk of A minus.
She is very nice, but too confusing and loves to go on rants.
Great teacher knows her stuff! boring class sometimes felt pointless and unnecessarily long.
Due dates must be followed. very easy to talk to. Knows her stuff!

One of the most amazing professors. He is very patient, laid-back, and shows that he genuinely cares about his students. He grades leniently (but fairly), and gives very detailed feedback. Although attendance is not mandatory, he takes it anyway for participation points. If you ever miss class on a given day, he is very understanding.

Easily one of the best, if not the best professor in the UMD English Department. He is extremely patient, friendly, and shows that he cares about his students. He is a very lenient (but fair) grader, and made Fridays asynchronous so that we could work on assignments. One thing to keep in mind is that he does take attendance.

An extremely nice individual who gives clear descriptions of assignments and course expectations. Gave students great freedom in writing assigningments in order to allow them to develop their own style and develop their abilities.

Professor Forrester was one of the best teachers I've taken in my entire time at UMD. The class was a Summer online course, so there were lots of assignments. Very relaxed and very helpful, though. You can tell that he wants to help you become a better writer. As long as you do your assignments and show effort, you'll get a good grade!

Prof. Forrester is genuinely a really great professor. He has a passion for teaching the course and as long as you're showing effort, you'll do really well. I'm taking him in the midst of the COVID pandemic, and he's accommodating to us as much as he can. Since everything's online, he's really been trying to interact w us like a regular classroom.

Professor Forrester is a great instructor and really cares about his students. The class is informative and teaches valuable skills useful outside the classroom. He greets students individually and offered opportunities to make up assignments for partial credit since he cares more about learning than grades. All around stand-up guy.

Best professional writing teacher! Seriously take this class. Course is super laid back and all the papers you do throughout the semester are connected and about the same topic. You can just pull stuff from previous papers for the final paper. He grades pretty easily and really wants you to do well. So nice and really funny guy!
Very good professor- very supportive inside and outside of class, and cares a lot about teaching well and preparing his students for experience outside of the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Best writing professor I've ever had! Take him if you get the chance!!! He really cares about all his students and you will no doubt become a better writer. He teaches a lot of practical writing skills that would be helpful for any career. The whole semester is a group project though, so pick a good partner. Go to office hours too, it's worth it.
Very good professor. Approachable, easy to understand. Definitely likes group work (in-class group work, nothing outside of class). Very good Prof, do recommend!

Poster from before, Meant to give him a better rating for easiness, accidentally gave him a 2. Anyways, if you really listen to his advice in class and apply it to your papers, then you should get a good grade on your paper.

Prof. Forrester is a really great professor. His classes are fun & you will learn a lot. This class wasn't a waste of time b/c most of the things taught in class are skills most employers require. Attendance & being on time most days is required. If you are on time and come to class, and do your best in the assignments, u won't have any problems.
He is a nice guy. He helps you with papers alot and there is alot of group work. take is class.

took intro into literature, very nice teacher, available to help outside of class, grades pretty hard on papers, for testes and quizzes, as long as you go to the class and do the readings, it's not hard, because he goes over most of the information in class. participation and attendance is mandatory...

He's a pretty good teacher. He tends to ramble on, so you need to pay good attention. He is always willing to help and very friendly. The class I took also was very easy, except for the essays. I found it difficult to get a B+ on the papers. Overall, I liked his class.
Took intro course in poetry and loved the class and the prof. Elicited technical and deep analysis from most students. Available outside class.

One of the best professors I've ever had. He's kind, gives great feedback, and genuinely cares about his students. When it comes to grading, he believes there's always room to improve, which I really respect. His critiques were super helpful, and I ended up taking two more of his classes because I enjoyed learning from him so much.

Foon lacks guidance and actual instruction. Conversations are infuriating, looping, and condescending. He grades based on personal opinion and caps at 97%. Hard work doesn't matter; feedback is nonexistent. Uncaring about life outside class. Just because he can make art doesn't mean he can teach it.

Great professor! He is funny, caring, and goes out of his way to get to know his students. He is a tough grader, but explains what you should do to improve. His class can be time consuming depending on the difficulty of your sculptures. Whatever you put into the class is what you get as a grade. Great professor in all but he can be a little tough.

The professor did not provide feedback on projects or grades. Had an unfair attendance policy, wouldn't accept excused absences.  Overall, way too much work and stress for an entry-level class, with random grading. It was his way or the highway, except the highway was on fire and random crap would be thrown at you like projectiles.

An absolute jem! Foon will meet you where you are at skill wise and artistically while help you grow. He wants you to have fun while making your art and learn how to do new things. Very funny, and caring man. I suggest anyone take this class, even non art majors. Projects do take some time, but it's worth it!
Professor Sham is super nice and funny. I registered all of his art classes. He is an inspirational teacher ever.
Nice professor and very cool. He is very helpful and give great feedback. Really enjoying his course

The most adorable professor! Very caring, funny, but at the same time definitely knows his stuff. The only downside to his class was how time consuming it was. So many other students and I would have to spend hours outside classtime to barely finish a project, which he has too many of

Foon is the best! He's incredibly fun to be around, and is really helpful with coming up with ideas and when you need help. He's very fair with grading, and very understanding. You will be crunched for time sometimes, but the projects are interesting and the class is rewarding and fun.

Take a class with this prof you won't regret it, he's a fair and understanding grader, organized and has a nice personality :)and you'll learn! as someone said here, the art dept has a few good professors, he's one of the few that's actually a good prof
