His class is pretty fun but time consuming, we never got enough time to finish projects! but he was encouraging and positive even when we didnt turn in great projects. Hes strict about attendance but overall a nice guy
Best teacher in the UMD art department, tough but fair very helpful and engaging

Foon Sham is awesome.  He is always encouraging, helpful, and positive.  The assignments in this class were fun and interesting and we were able to use a variety of materials.  He's tough on attendance, but he gives you opportunities to make up for too many missed classes, like museum/gallery trips.  Do your best and your grade will reflect it!

Bobbie is the best! Her lectures are very easy to follow, and are filled with extremely interesting, helpful and useful information. She is super flexible, and she made everything stress-free. I took her class at 9:30am and it was still so worth it! I cannot recommend Bobbie enough!

She is super nice, very understanding, and her feedback is really useful. She goes over any topics for her students if needed as some people in the class need refreshers, and she's really intelligent regarding journalism and writing in general. My only problem was some assignments weren't clear on ELMS, but she will answer any questions you have.

Bobbie is a PhD student but a better teacher than many adjunct faculty. Has a professional background in journalism and very knowledgeable. Made lectures interesting despite online format (due to COVID), gave lots of small assignments for participation points, gave good feedback on writing. Very caring, flexible, aware of students' mental health.
Overall great guy, really down to earth, helpful and very easygoing, great teacher!

Foecke is quite literally the best professor I have ever had in a college course. I have had him for 3 classes and I am taking a 4th with him next semester despite the class being at 6:30pm. He has been the reason I haven't quit my major and makes learning so much fun. I genuinely have learned more in his classes than all of my others combined.

Professor Foecke is my favorite professor (I've taken 3 classes with him now). His lectures are clear and very educational. He's great with questions, doesn't grade harshly at all, and has frequent office hours. If you show you're making an effort, show up to class, and do a decent job you'll get an A.
Excellent.  I finally understand thermo!

Easy class- I got B though because I didn't give it my ALL. Refreshing class, learned useful info I'll take w/me. To the other review saying "He's too interested in his students if you catch my drift," perhaps having a professor who genuinely cares and converses with his students is unusual to you...what do you expect from a *communication* prof.?

Ex military/construction guy with a heart of gold. He can come off bristly if no one participates in class convos (which is understandable). Truly cares about his students and isn't going to enable us in the way other classes do (take home exams, open note, etc) why come to college if you don't actually want to learn and nurture original thinking?
This professor is a bit too interested in his students if you catch my drift.
Entitled and annoying

This professor made COMM107 way too much work for the class. My friends in other COMM107 classes had half the work we had. For our presentations, he was a very tough grader and would take points off for very minor errors during presentations. I would not recommend taking this professor's course.

You have to be a VERY particular kind of person to get along with someone like him. Be prepared to be uncomfortable, and not in a beneficial way. He takes about four years to grade anything and is a reasonably harsh grader. He makes his own rules, and they change every day. I would stay away from him unless you absolutely have no choice.
takes forever to grade assignments and grades speeches way too harshly.

Easy enough class, but the professor is too focused on "winning" against his students. He claims slow grading as a virtue since he doesn't think students will look at his feedback until right before the next assignment (not true), and he justifies his faults through mental acrobatics. You can't argue with him because he invents his own rules.

Daniel Foster is a great professor whom is extremely knowledgeable on the subject. He can be slightly off-putting on the first day of class and can be a hard-ass at times but it's clear that he cares about his students and is extensively knowledgeable on the subject matter. Very funny at times and his lectures are pretty solid.

Dan really cares about you. He is understanding, if you need to turn in something late because a situation just talk to him. The class is all speeches which can be stressful but as long as you prepare you will be fine and receive a good grade.

Daniel Foster would be a solid teacher, but considering the other teachers that exist, don't take him. There is substantially more work for this class than others for no reason. A lot of people are saying he is a tough grader but that isn't true, he just scripts grades at an A- because everyone ends up getting the same grade on the speeches.
He's a very caring and understanding guy. Although the presentations are stressful he's very helpful if you reach out to him and will always make time to help you if you need it.

He was such a nice and funny guy, but way too harsh of a grader. HOWEVER, if you reach out to him outside class for clarification or extra help, he really does appreciate it and your grade will benefit because of it. Follow his rubrics and talk to him and you will love the class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Takes too long to grade assignments and give feedback, which is unhelpful as the speeches build upon each other. Grades too harshly for a gen-ed Comm class. Pick another professor, although he's personable, he's not worth it at all.

While he is a personable and likable guy, his class leaves little room for deviation from his specific formulas. His instructions have a special way of removing any variety in his students' speeches. He refused to craft his assignments in a way that made them manageable with online classes. Grading is far too harsh for an online Gen-ed class.

I agree with everyone saying Dan is nice and funny (sometimes). However, he is WAY too harsh of a grader on every speech and outline for a gened we are all forced to take. Also, he is such a slow grader you won't know what grade you are going to get until the very end . Go with a professor who is easy and make ur life easier

Dan is a professor that you can actually relate to. He makes oral communications bearable. Lectures are engaging and pretty inspirational and he made having to make speeches comfortable. You actually get to know him and build closer connections to other students since it's in a smaller class environment.

Even though Comm107 is just a GenEd, Dan really cares about your performance and wants you to improve. That being said, don't take him thinking you'll just pass without doing anything. Generally, there's not a lot of work, but he follows the rubric closely. Loved taking this class, didn't feel like another face in the crowd. Highly recommend.

Daniel is a very kind man that own well respected amongst his students. He helped me become comfortable with giving speeches. From the first day I knew that I would enjoy this course, which I did! Make sure to remember to do the quizzes and to practice your speeches. Dont be the person reading off or their note cards the entire time.

While I like Dan as a person, his class has made me very frustrated. He is extremely forgetful, and an insanely SLOW grader. It takes him over a month to post grades for speeches, while all of the other comm professors pump grades out the day after a speech is given. Without feedback, it was obviously very hard to improve.

Dan is a really nice guy, but too harsh of a grader for a gen-ed that everyone has to take. He does know what he's talking about in terms of public speaking, but he took it way too seriously. You really need to prepare your speeches and listen to what he tells you to do, otherwise you definitely won't get an A.
Amazing professor! Usually he is late for posting grades for speeches, assignments, etc. but he helps you out with anything related to oral communication even if it is not about the class.

Wow. Dr. Foster was one of the wisest and most intelligent people I've ever learned from, and even though he really makes you work for that A (You're going to want to practice your speeches for at least 1-2 hrs per speech), it was definitely worth it. He imparts knowledge almost no other teacher can give out and I loved it!

I was dreading this class, but Dan made it a million times easier to get through. His style of lecturing was entertaining and made class go by quick. He made you become so much more comfortable with public speaking, but was a little tough when grading. Also, he won't remind you of assignments you have to submit- so make sure you're checking online.

Really good guy. Take Dan's class if you don't want to be bored all semester and if you want to actually improve your public speaking. He cares about his students and makes time to meet with students when they have questions.

Dan is an entertaining & interesting professor, but can be difficult. He does not give out easy A's and calls people out in class often for not paying attention, answering questions incorrectly, etc. It can be a little over the top. Attendance is not mandatory and you do need the book. Not the best teacher, but not the worst.

Hes a great lecturer and a nice professor, but don't take his class expecting to get an easy A. There are plenty of other comm professors for that. Because this is a GenEd, that probably rules this professor out for most of you, but he is a fair professor and will give you the grade you deserve if you think of his class as a relatively serious one.

Dan is an amazing professor. He is very laid back and he clearly cares about his students. Dan wants you to be a better public speaker, and as long as you are willing to put in the work, Dan's class is a must. Attendance isn't mandatory but I highly recommend it because you learn so much. Dan is very interesting, very funny, and is very intelligent

To start, the professor told us to call him Dan which made the classroom environment feel relaxed and comfortable. He was a very funny, sarcastic, intelligent professor that made speech seem interesting and engaging. Attendance wasn't mandatory and the grades consisted of about 5 speeches including a group project and final reflective paper.
Does not care about his students.

Dr. Franklin is just a really uncaring and messy professor. He cancelled lectures without notifying any of the students, he posted one practice exam from 2012 (which isn't helpful at all for the exam), and he's not good at using technology at all. Your grade in the class is also completely dependent on the TA you have.
He's very chill when it comes to grading, but my god... he never leaves you feeling prepared for any exams.

I had him for ENPM609. First half of the course was good; hardware design seems to be his specialty. The second half, focusing mainly on software, went down hill. He used the slides which came with an error-prone textbook and pretty much read the bullet points. It didn't look like he was familiar with the material and his preparation was minimal.
Excellent teacher. Take this class you will enjoy and learn.

Dr. Franklin is an excellent teacher. He has a clear love and expertise in the subject matter and is able to teach with clarity and concision. He does not cram material into this course, but sets a good pace so if you pay attention and do the work, you will walk away having learned alot.

Attendance at the 206 lab is mandatory, but for lecture he reads straight off the slides he posts online. Has amazing handwriting, I've never seen such perfect straight lines drawn completely freehand.

I've had him for multiple classes.  He's a very good professor and his midterms are usually straightforward and easy.  But his final is usually hard with one or two complicated question(which will catch you by surprise).  He's a fair grader who looks for correct concept rather than correct answer.  I'd def take him again.

I had him for two classes 303 and 350.  He was very good in both although the 303 class was horrible (because of the course not the prof.).  Exams are easy and his grading is fair.  He expects you you understand stuff conceptually rather than memorize.  Attendance is "mandatory" due to pop quizes.  But EE majors be beware of taking him for 350.
Very nice person. he grades the exams, so he curves if needed. I would take him again.

Always late to class. was his first time teaching this subject and boy did it show.  Not many faired well.  A third of us are still waiting on our grades and classes start in a week.  AVOID THIS MAN!!!
He is a very nice person and cares a lot about his students.

He is a very nice person, very helpful. He cares a lot about his students. He made the first exam easier when he learnt that students were having problems. Also very good on changing dates to accomodate students.

He is a funny and nice guy, but he gives so much work for an 100 level course. Lectures cover the reading material, so if you read then you don't have to go, but it is a lot of reading. By the end of the semester, he was assigning like 100+ pages/week. If you hate reading, this class is not for you, and you have to read if you want to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Even with boring class content, Professor Barrenechea is the funniest teacher I have ever had. Participation does matter for this class, so showing up to every class is necessary. Overall, the class is a lot of writing and reading, but he is an extremely easier grader, making an A very attainable.

This guy is really friendly, and he really cares about his students. The workload is a little more than I bargained for, but it's worth it since you will get 100 on almost every assignment as long as you read the required readings
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of the BEST profs I have ever had. He was so funny and made Classics (which most of the class were not majoring in) super interesting and engaging. The fact he was able to be so wonderful thru an online format truly speaks to his abilities as a teacher and person- take this!!!!

It was such a fun class to take and as long as you keep up with the work you'll be fine. He's definitely my favorite professor I've had so far and made class very interesting. He was hilarious, understanding, and very open minded. I would take another one of his classes again!

Prof is a great guy and makes lectures fun. I only went to 5 of them and still understand everything going on. Discussions are important to attend & there's weekly homework - 250 words. He posts the lecture slides so it's a control F for the weekly quizzes. There's a ton of reading (80+ pages/week) but if you keep up you'll be fine. 3 big papers
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Barrenechea is one of my favorite professors I've had at UMD. He's hilarious, kind, and always knows how to cheer up the class. There is quite a lot of reading but you honestly could get around doing it. I definitely recommend taking his class if you want something fun to look forward to.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: clas170 is the easiest class. yeah it's a lot of reading, but you're literally reading the fun myths many of us grew up with - it requires NO brainpower. The tests are crazy easy too "name the 12 olympian gods" easy gen-ed with great teachers. Barrenechea is very intelligent, knowledgeable, interesting, and passionate.

Professor Barrenechea is a very kind and understanding professor. He tries his best to make his lectures interesting, which they are. There was not a single lecture where I found myself bored. Make sure to put detail in this homework they make a difference. Make sure to do the reading, its a lot. If you wont read then you wont pass, period.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class has to be the worst I have ever taken. Makes us read like 100 PAGES IN BETWEEN CLASSES for a 100 level class I repeat 100 level class. I got a major to focus on so I can't read. He gets bitter about attendance and discussions are a must. If you like reading this is the class for you if you don't save yourself and don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's nice and the class is very interesting, he makes you work for your grade there is no doubt about it! If you are looking for an easy A this is not it unless you love the classics.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: For a 100 level class, it's a very reading heavy class. Most of the readings are interesting, so it isn't that bad. The exams are really easy and he posts the lecture slides online, so you really don't have to go to class as long as you read. You have to go to discussion but it's really not bad and they're very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: For a 100 level class, he gives way too many readings. He has an accent and randomly calls on people in lecture so if you have social anxiety, you'll die. Don't need to go to lectures but need to go to discussions. Read the books or you will not pass because the tests are very hard. Do not take this class for an easy A. IT IS NOT AN EASY A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: What a funny professor. He really knows how to make his class fun and interesting whenever he teaches. Although it was a lot to do in the class, he helped out a lot during the papers. He would send it back with comments, and you would have to try and answer them. You'll love him. Be careful, his accent sometimes make it hard to understand him.
Professor Hildy is amazing, he knows a lot about everything in theatre major. He is accessible, clear, easy to understand, and just in one word "AMAZING". love him so much.

Dr. Hildy was my dissertation adviser at the University of Georgia.  He is one of the most thorogh and intelligent men I have ever met.  If you are in a graduate program, he is who you should want for your advisor.  He expects solid work and will push you.  Be intellectually curious and you will do well with him.

I took his classes while at the University of Georgia.  He is not a fantastic teacher, unless you are interested in learning. He will go out of his way to help you if you show you want knowledge.  He is very intelligent and focused on those things he is interested in.  He is a World Class Scholar.  I am glad I had him as a professor.

I had him at the University of Georgia and I found him to be incredibly intelligent and helpful.  You have to learn how to approach him and he is distracted sometimes, but for a good reason, he is truly one of the leading experts on his topic.  You would be lucky to learn from him.

He's a scholar not a teacher!  Rambling, disconnected, goes off on tangents.  Rude and sarcastic to students for random reasons.  I'm there to learn, not to have him go on and on.  He knows a lot and his books are good but I don't recommend him as a professor.

One of the world's leading authorities in his field, Theatre History and Architecture. He doesn't suffer fools and has very high standards for his students. Meet the standard and you'll learn a lot from him.

He rambles on and on about all kinds of topics which is occasionally interesting but often boring.  The worst thing is that you still have to read the book to learn anything and don't get much from the class, almost like doing independent study.  Yes his book is well written but his lectures are definitely NOT recommended.

Hildy knows his stuff- he wrote the book! I took theatre history with him and learned a lot about elizabethan playhouses and such. He's not super interesting, but if you already like  theatre history, you will like the class.
You can tell Professor Franklin really cares about her students.

She's an amazing teacher and can really help you one-on-one with math problems. Her style is old fashioned but extremely effective because she taps in to intuition. She explains everything so clearly so that it makes sense! She tries her best to make sure you understand, though there may be homework everyday, just think about it as good practice.
She's extremely helpful and very easy to talk to. Although, the class itself is very hard for the fact that it is a lot of material thrown at you everyday.
Jannah is genuinely one of the best professors I've ever had. She is such a caring person and teaching comes naturally to her. She is incredible. Please take a class with her if you can.
Jannah is the best professor in this department. For your own sake take a class with her.

Jannah is an amazing professor! Definitely take one of her classes if you're able. She cares a lot about all the students in the class, and works hard to create a comfortable class environment. She's really flexible with assignments and takes students feedback into account. She's overall just a really nice person and wants to see you succeed.

Jannah has done everything in her power this past semester to make sure her students succeeded in this course. She gives everyone a fair chance to get the grade they deserve and as long as you put in the work you will definitely pass. I have never enjoyed taking a course more and would love to take more classes with her in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Fusenig is super friendly and really made coming to class a fun experience. She encouraged our class to become friends with each other and made a fun and comfortable classroom dynamic. She is really understanding when it comes to grading or making exceptions as long as you have a reason and give her a heads up/discuss it over with her.

Jannah is the absolute BEST!!! She is so caring and truly wants you to be successful. She is by far the best professor that I have ever had. I learned so much from this class. If you have the chance, you need to take her class. You will not regret it:)

Textbook readings every like 2 weeks, DON'T have to buy the textbook she gives you the pages on canvas. Teacher is AMAZING, so young and kind. Super willing to work with you! Not an easy A if you don't want to do the work. This class is all about connecting the content to your life. Assessments are writing style. If you work hard its an easy A

took this class last semester for my major and i ended up really liking it. she was a great professor and was always checking in on us and made sure we were really learning and understanding the material which i appreciated. probably one of the nicest professors i've had. put the work in and you'll do great
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved this course, best one at UMD. Jannah was the sweetest and most genuine professor I've had. She allows one mental health day :') and helps so much during office hours. She really cares about her students and their well being and really wanted to see us succeed. I felt really encouraged and supported in her class & i loved her!!

Hands down the worse professor I have ever encountered. Yes the guy knows his stuff but can he teach? No, absolutely not. Very secretive about the curve. His teaching method and style just sucks completely. The fact that many students complain about him should be a red flag!
A great professor teaching a very difficult class. Most of the negativity is in regards to the subject matter, but does a great job explaining and provides good insight/examples.

If you haven't taken ENME202 you've basically already failed this course. MatLab HEAVY! Not enough time is given on the exams that are worth 90% of your overall grade. Questions posted to Piazza or by email usually were never answered or took 3-5 business days. Never gave a specific answer about a curve. Average on exams were around a D every time.

Flipped classroom. Matlab heavy. Final grade is 90% exams, 10% homeworks. Homeworks and exams are completed on PrairieLearn. Exams used Honorlock and had no partial credit. No practice exams or new practice questions were given until the final exam. No extra credit or projects. No grade breakdown was provided and he was secretive about the curve.

Trying to modernize the structure of this class while we are all on Zoom was a bad idea. This course failed to do what every other engineering course did during this time and the students paid for it. I do not recommend this professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tried to implement a "Flipped Classroom" method where we only did homework in class with no live lecture. In my opinion it went poorly, I do not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best class I've taken at UMD. One of the best professors, too. Very knowledgeable, very good at lecturing, and some of the most interesting subjects covered There are no exams, the term project is very fun, and the lectures are amazing. I cannot recommend him highly enough!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is tough with any professor but he responds to emails fast, he is nice during office hours, and his exams are fair as long as you do practice exams and hw problems. He may not deserve 5 stars but I thought the other reviews were harsh. His lectures were brutal sometimes but he also gives big curve, my raw score was an 82 but I got an A.
Teaches way too many irrelevant things in lectures that are unhelpful for exams

Fushman is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He gives you three exams and 5 quizzes. The first exam was fine. The second exam was absolutely awful. How do you know how youre doing in the class? You dont because he doesnt grade anything until 3 weeks to a month after youve completed it. His lectures are so dry, boring, and convoluted.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: VERY knowledgeable; she's got the inside scoop. Great teacher, very lucky to have her for JOUR100.

Really helpful, especially because she is in charge of internships. But the class is stressful - just accept that you will fail, and you will freak out. But then you move on, and you'll be fine. Be aware of the big time commitment, though!
This TEACHER (note: not class) is why I dropped journalism.  Professor is extremely discouraging and not very helpful. I would roll the dice with the adjuncts.

JOUR201 is hard, but it's meant to be that way. Make one mistake, you fail - but that's the way it works in all 201 classes. If you have a chance to take her because you're fast-tracked, do it. Being able to take 320, etc. a semester easy is worth it and having her means you won't have to roll the dice with one one of the adjuncts.

He's a very nice guy who will make adjustments to the course and schedule per his students needs. His lecture style is definitely a bit dense and very informative, so it can be hard to pay a lot of attention easily. I highly recommend.
Very bad experience with this professor. Did not teach well as lectures were confusing and convoluted.

Dr. Sriram cares about your success! Not only are his lectures engaging, he makes in-class activities to help you understand the topics. But beware, if you do not come to the lecture, you will miss out on a big chunk of material. Also note, some assignments utilize complex tools. Attending learning communities/office hours/emailing about Qs is key!
Mediocre lecturer: may have a strong understanding of first-principles, but has no business teaching them
My guy, what a legend

What I really appreciated about Dr. Sriram was his outside of class learning communities. These were held weekly(more often before exams), where he & a TA/TF would have a room open for students in the evening to answer questions/offer help. These were more approachable than normal office hours, & helped me on the homework & clarifying concepts.
Worst professor I've ever had.

This is my second time, Professor Gardner. He's very chill and kind. You will do well if you take notes from the slides and pay attention. He doesn't quiz on anything from the textbook that he didn't talk about in class, so don't worry about reading the notebook.  Every quiz and exam is multiple choice so very easy.

Truly an awful professor. Tries way to hard to make this course harder than it used to be. He cares so much about word counts to such an extreme. He sent like 20 emails about academic integrity requiring lockdown browsers because he is buthurt that the class is really a joke. Makes it unnecessarily hard. Wants students to fail. Dont take this class

Lee is an overall nice guy who has very structured lectures and will ask some questions to the class throughout the lecture that he basically answers himself. The assigned course load consists of discussion board posts, current events, reflections, and a case paper. Most people skipped the lectures because he posts them on canvas afterward.

Professor Gardner was very kind and you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches. His lectures were insanely dull to the point where it was hard to stay awake. In the class, you brush the surface of a lot of different subjects of business which is great if you are undecided. Grades are mostly determined by the two exams and group project.
Great professor. He cares a lot about the material and makes it interesting. His homework is pretty easy and the tests are a little challenging but fair. Overall great class.

nicest professor at UMD I've had so far-the lectures are interesting and he genuinely cares about students' well being. He radiates good energy and is understanding. Only two exams, each worth 20% and covers a LOT of material so prep in advance for them.

Amazing professor, taught me the fundamentals about business. Class is not that bad, its just really long. There are only two exams so study bc the wording on his exams are confusing from time to time. The group project was fun to do. Take BMGT110 with him!

Professor Gardner is absolutely amazing, easily the best professor I've had at UMD. He cares so much about his students and is really an expert on the subjects he teaches. He clearly loves what he teaches and this is evident through his excellent lectures. Definitely try to take Professor Gardner's classes!
Professor Gardner is wonderful! He's encouraging and I learned so much this semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Gardner is a good guy. He cares about his students and is very helpful and knowledgeable.

Prof. Gardner is awesome. evident he cares about his students (more than any other umd prof tbh), I'm glad I had him. As long as you aren't lazy, you'll be just fine. 6 discussion posts, 6 case discussions, 6 current events reports, 2 exams.

By far the best professor I've ever had in my entire college career, and made taking a 9:30am class so worth it. He is understanding, caring, and always willing to help his students. He makes any topic interesting and relates it to real-life, making it easier to understand the material. Now signing up for another class he's teaching next semester!

Professor Gardner really cares about his students. If you engage with him, he will like you as a student. His tests are based on what is covered in his lectures. It is a textbook heavy course, and there is a packet you are supposed to buy at the end, but I do not recommend buying it because he lectures about it anyways. Great mind for business.
Somehow turns mundane subjects into interesting lectueres and seems to really care about his students and their success. Applies in-class concepts to real-world experience.

Prof. Gardner truly wants each of his students to engage with the material and succeed. Participation is really important to him and goes a long way in developing a relationship with him. There are weekly discussion boards, which all get 100% (again, participation). Tests take up a large chunk of the grade but are pretty easy if you pay attention.

He seems to genuinely care about his students and he takes into account that we have other classes so he doesn't overdo the workload. He keeps his lectures interesting with anecdotes and tries to make the material relevant to current events. He is organized so you always know what you are supposed to be studying. My favorite teacher this semester

Genuine person who is extremely easy to talk to and understand if you make an effort. The class was purely lecture-based with little to no homework the whole semester. Tests are the biggest thing, worth 70%, but he offered significant help beforehand.

Leland is great. He honestly wants everyone to pass. The class is relatively easy but the exams are worth 80% of your grade. Though the exams are easy, if you did not read, you have to relearn everything since there is not really any reinforcement such as LearnSmarts. There also isn't HW except for the deliverables.
Talks sooooooo much, very boring lectures. On the good side it's a very easy class and will curve the grade if students do "poorly" on the exams.

Tries to be current and adaptive. Very understanding and in general, a nice guy. I really liked him---one of my better Smith school experiences. A lot of writing so if your communications skills need polishing this may not be the best class for you.
Leland was a great guy. Wrote my recommendation for the business school. Overall a good teacher and nice person.

I am only a few courses away from graduating with my BA. This professor required more than any professor I have had. The participation requirement was 3x the amount a normal online class typically requires. The professor was helpful in clarification and was an active participant in the discussion boards.

Overall it is an easy class, one midterm and one final. One research paper (8-10 pages), one article critique (3 pages give or take), one group project to be presented in class. It's a dry class but he tries to make it interesting and is funny at times. Not a lot of reading required for this class and participation isn't a big deal. No curve though

Knows what he is about. Had 2"D" on the mid-terms but still got a "B" because I had to write the final paper which helped my Grade. Wanted to drop the class but he encouraged me and showed me how to do well and I did.
No Comments

Made an 8:30 class interesting. Wasn't a huge lecture, so that was great. Encouraged group discussion, we were more like a group of friends than a class. Nice atmosphere. Tests were a tad too hard, and the book was ridiculously bad.
Genuinely passionate, but tough grader.
Choose any other physics professor.

The PHYS235 course was a nightmare. The lectures, despite being delivered by a great speaker, were hard to follow, often veering off-topic. Exam questions seemed random, requiring memorization of irrelevant details ("who did this scientist not know personally?"). Grading was slow, Canvas was rarely updated, and Prof. Gates was unresponsive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took the class on the Manhattan Project, because I assumed it would be an interesting class about a cool subject. The class ACTUALLY was a nightmare. The professor was incredibly unorganized, it was poorly structured, and the physics content was unreasonable, unrelated, and wrong half the time in his demonstrations. For context im a CS major.

Gates is incredibly clear during his lectures, but this course was tough. Homework schedule is a bit random, but not too many homeworks in total. Exams are rough and not too based on hw. Grades are based around the average (test avg: ~40% was a B). I can't recommend against him since he is quite helpful, but quantum and his course can be brutal.

I'm a physics major, and i think he knows his stuff better than any physics teacher i've ever had. I get the idea that he's very passionate about the subject. The only thing i did not like about his class was that it wasn't very clear what his requirements were for the students in the class. But aside from that, he's great.
No Comments
No Comments
teacher is racist

Essay exams; professor thinks outside box; prof has high expectations; many students take course too casually cause film centered (on representation), so students unprepared for discussions w/the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Most students thought that this class should have been a cake walk because the focus was on films.  I heard complaints about actually having to read articles ( the length) and having to write pagers.  They are/were attending a top university.  What do they expect?  This should be a life lesson, take note, life isn't easy

Class is about Native Americans in Film. She teaches almost solely film technique, which is incredibly boring to a Bio major taking this class as an upper level core. Mandatory quizzes at beginning of class, usually leave at the break halfway through. Quizzes are vague and extremely difficult, essays are a cakewalk. Prof knows nothing about subject

willing to help you out of class, anything to help you succeed. New to teaching so she goes by the book, but if you disagree with her, she will take your argument into consideration when reviewing your grade.

Took class thinking that it would be interesting, was very wrong. Assignments were very vague and unusual. Had to read random obscure and boring articles.  Class unorganized and boring take at your own risk.

It is a better use of your time to learn how to play the piano then go to lecture. Hailu yaps nonsense the entire class. Not only that but he is so boring that you will fall alseep. Worry not, you will have missed nothing as he doesnt properly teach any concepts. Also the TAs were grading extremely harshly. You basically have to do perfect

Babbles like a kindergarten teacher most of lecture and none of the stuff he teaches is on the exam. Very incoherent and somewhat rude, seems to have made Midterm 1 harder for us out of pure spite. I don't know why he has such good reviews.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very difficult to understand. His lectures are worthless. Be prepared to teach yourself the entirety of the course content, which is admittedly not terribly difficult relative to other classes you'll likely be taking.
Horrible professor that just bases lecture off of slideshows. Uses random equations / formulas with no context at all. And on top of all that he even gives out extremely difficult exams.

I think he was a great teacher. Some people say otherwise, I think establishing a connection is very important, going to office hours very much helps. As long as you want to pass the class you can. One thing is that his lectures are very monotone, which, to each their own, but if you're engaged in what is going on, it shouldn't be a problem.

Yes there's a curve and yeshe drops some quizzes but honestly, his lectures were so boring and the discussion was not helpful at all. I would not take him again, and I really feel like it was a waste of time
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Hailu is a straight forward teacher. If you attend lecture and do practice problems, you will succeed. You have multiple attempts on homework, but he doesn't give extensions. My TA helped with problems I didn't understand. His exams are exactly like the problems he demonstrates in class. I only relied on the textbook for extra practice.

Hailu isn't necessarily a bad professor, but I would recommend almost anyone in the physics department over him. His lectures are confusing and boring. He reads off of a powerpoint slide half the time and the other time is spent doing practice problems with little explanation.

3 EXAMS THAT ARE 30 PTS EACH AND HAVE 3 QUESTIONS! Each question has 2-4 parts, so mistakes really impact your grade. Attendance isn't mandatory, but he doesn't post his written examples (the majority of the lecture) online, so unless you can get them from a friend then attendance is necessary to learn/understand the material.

Took Hailu during the summer. Im not very good at physics and physics 2 was the last I needed. course was very fast paced bc it was summer. his teaching style is working through examples. homework's & ex. were very similar to exam given. If you carefully listen to everything, take notes and understand the topics you will do great in this class.

Took PHYS273 over the summer with Prof. Hailu. No complaints at all, really enjoyed this course with him. If you need to get your waves credit over the summer, strongly recommend taking it with him, you will not regret anything.

PHYS270 with Hailu was honestly a breeze. Lectures were boring, but he taught the material and did examples which he bases his exam problems on. If you just review the lecture examples you'll be good.

This man gave us an exam that was not similar to the final exam practice at all. I needed a B- to go into engineering and this man gave me a C- even though I studied ridiculously hard for the exam. Now I have to retake it and get another semester fix up my gpa. You never know how his exams will go.

Hailu is a great lecturer. With a mask on, he seems very unenthusiastic but that is just because you can not see his smile. When he takes his mask off you can see he is actually excited about what he is teaching. His exams can be difficult, but a B average will in the end get you an A with the curve. Also, do his in-class examples before the test!

Hailu's midterms were fair and his lectures covered the material. The final exam was not a reflection of the material covered in class, however. I would take him again if there were no alternatives, but would otherwise search out a better lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures were OK but solid in order to learn the material as he goes through multiple examples in class. I see people complaining about how boring his lectures, but I feel like that's unfair. It's physics, it's gonna be a boring grind, that's not his fault. His exams were relatively easy, but they are significant portion of the grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors Ive had. Super boring, half of the exams are easy the other half are hard. Only 2 exams and a final so you better not mess up even one exam. There is a curve. Hw and quizzes are very easy but not worth that much of your grade.

All of these bad reviews are garbage. Do the homework problems, lecture problems and maybe some textbook problems for good measure. First test was very reasonable. Hailu is present every lecture and likes to talk. If you can't stay interested because it is "boring", the problem is you not enjoying physics, not him being boring. Shut up and grind!

Hailu lectures in a very calm, relaxed manner that makes it a bit too easy to start zoning out in the middle of class. However, his methods of explaining material are very concise and easy to comprehend. They're quite valuable if you pay attention. Test are very fair; if you study a reasonable amount, you'll likely do well.

Hailu seems like he doesn't care. He doesn't give any practice for exams so you kinda just go in blindly. Typically understanding his lectures is enough for a B. He got lazy and the final exam had a problem he took straight from a midterm, so understand the problems he does and the TA recommended problems and you can get a good grade.

What you learn about in the lectures and what you do in the homework is basically what is in the weekly quizzes and the midterms. Although he is fairly strict in turning things in on time, he is definitely not mean. Handwriting and speech is intelligible, but not amazing.

He doesn't really give feedback on much, but I found his lecture notes for the class pretty fantastic. All I did was take notes and did the homework and I found myself very prepared for the exams. Great guy, I honestly don't know what the other reviewers are talking about for this class.

His lecture videos are quite monotonous but effective if you pay attention. He works through good examples so I never felt the need to read the book to supplement in-class instruction, but make sure to watch out for numerical mistakes in those examples! Quizzes and midterms are fair, final is pretty tough.

He is not the worst teacher ever, but he is really, really bad. He is heartless and does not care about his students at ALL. If you try to communicate with him in person or in email, he talks back with the rudest remarks. He has no basic human compassion. His lectures are never to-the-point. They are long and boring, and he talks very slowly.

The most cold-hearted and cruel professor that I have met so far. He even made the expectations of us learning online being higher than in-person settings. For some weeks, he made the HW problems extremely difficult and he didn't care if most people are immensely struggling. He always would say that they are easy and never would help us. AVOID HIM.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Good professor who knows how to teach and wants you to do well. He is hard to reach outside of class and occasionally doesn't respond to emails. His voice in lecture videos made me feel sleepy but he is a good professor for this difficult class.
Uninformative lectures, one of those classes where your better off reading the textbook than focusing on lecture content.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: That first "most helpful rating" is total bs. His lectures are absolutely terrible. He talks so slowly. Honestly I can't say anything good about him. Please don't take him for ANY class-you can thank me later.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Absolute garbage. Don't take this professor. He talks so slowly that when you play his lecture videos on 2x speed it sounds normal. He doesn't give examples/practice problems to prepare for exams. Also the only exams you take in the course are the midterm and final, so if you don't do well on one, good luck getting an A. Ruined physics for me.

Professor Gebremariam is one of those professors that you can just tell that he is being forced to teach students, which is clear when you email him, as he talks down to his students and acts like he is gods gift to physics. His lectures are mind numbingly boring and pointless. To make it even worse, the TA that i had was somehow has worse Hailu.
He does all kinds of little things to screw over students like not offering partial credit, changing questions after you've submitted them, etc. It seems like he does not want students to succeed

Hailu doesn't offer partial credit on tests, and each has 4 or less questions so if you get one part wrong you're screwed. "Lectures" are him reading off the slides the textbook company made, so his teaching ability is equivalent to a text to speech generator.
Worst Prof I ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He may seem easy, as his HW, quizzes, and even midterms werent bad, but he left us very unprepared for the final. It contained content he never covered in lecture or in any of the HWs/quizzes. If you decide to take him, be prepared for a surprise.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This man really can't teach. The only way to get through his class is by reading the textbook and understanding example problems. If you don't have a strong physics background I wouldn't take his class. Messed up the first midterm with like two problems, did pretty well on the second midterm, but I still need a 100 for an -A. 100 on hw and quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Talking basically on the Powerpoint, the only point going to the lecture is his explaintion of sample problems. His tests are reasonable and usually follow the powerpoint.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I definitely recommend taking Hailu's class. He is very careful in explaining complex topics accurately and makes few mistakes in lectures. His exams were incredibly easy (except for the final, which was not as much difficult as it was time-consuming). If you pay attention in lecture and try to understand the content, you'll have no problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I never went to lecture but always read the book. Tests are hard and not very fair. The homework was often not good practice for the tests. You can definitely pass the class if you read the book a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hailu is such a bland and unengaging professor, and his exams are only 40 points, so it's not easy to get an A on them. The only material graded is 3 exams, occasional quizzes in discussion, online homework, and a cumulative final.

He is a great professor and lecturer. I liked how he did a review before an exam, where he would almost explicitly tell you what would be on it so you know what to study. In this course, he also allowed us to bring in a study guide of however amount of pages we wanted. He would also bring his dog to lectures, which was nice welcome!

I enjoyed this class. This class is lecture-heavy, however, Hambrecht is passionate about what he teaches, so the lectures never seem forced or monotonous. He also brings his dog, Auggie, to class, which lightened up the mood some days. The course was mostly group work, so I definitely recommend him if you don't mind a giant project as a final.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Classes are just made up of lectures where the material doesn't really ever come into play. There are 3 or 4 quizzes based on readings in the textbook, and one 20 page paper on a subject of your choice. interesting class, paper is a lot of work. Not sure how tough he will grade the paper yet, there was no rubric.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Most quizzes were easy if you did the readings. No exams, but final paper was a bit rough and 9 pages long. There were two other assignments in going to a museum and writing about it, and a powerpoint. Professor was very enthusiastic about the material, and was clearly very intelligible about the subject. Lectures were very interesting.

Do not take this class if you're looking for an easy elective that doesn't require time and effort. Professor does not answer emails if you have any questions. Ten quizzes that are relatively easy. Took over a month to grade one paper. The final exam was a 9 page paper with broad questions that were extremely difficult to answer.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Really great professor, he really cares and is enthusiastic about the stuff he's teaching. He makes the material relatively easy to learn as well. Highly recommend

Very minimal readings from the book, mostly focus on lectures(he posts videos and slides. Grades super easy. Very nice dude overall, but kind of a mystery. Mentioned often his "past life as a grape/wine farmer in California", also references living and working in New York, but seems too young to have done so much.

This class only works if the students participate and do the readings before class. We didn't have many assignments, so attendance is a big part of the grade. Quizzes and exams were online and open note. The final was kind of like a Socratic seminar though where he would give certain material to study for and then ask you about it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is absolutely the worst professor I have ever had. Do not take his courses!!!! He is extremely prejudiced and Islamophobic, and makes this clear in his lectures, and he constantly makes students uncomfortable. How he still has a job as a professor God knows. There have been multiple reports against him and he still hasn't been fired. RUN!!!

This is the worst teacher at umd. He gives out so much work and doesn't even realize it. Trust me don't take him your better off not taking this class. The map quizzes were so hard because he won't tell you what to study. I felt very uncomfortable with his jokes when I went to his office hours.

WORST PROFESSOR EVER!! I'm surprised UMD can allow this type of teacher in their school. This guy managed to make a 100-level class a 300-level class. We would have a midterm, a paper, and a movie review all the same day. Grades you based on emotions; doesn't read your work. Makes bad jokes like "Im going to bite you". Doesn't respond to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor I have ever had. The amount of work in this class is insane. 6 papers, 4 exams (short essay questions and not including the midterm), and the final exam is a group oral presentation with no notes. Professor grades attendance and laughs when you get a question wrong. Grades assignments before due date. Assigns work day of.

The teacher is very disorganized and does not present good guidelines for assignments. Calls on students randomly and expects detailed expert answers. Expect students to fully understand and remember all specific details about the readings. Fails to let students know what is essential for readings and does not set up students for success.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This is probably the worst teacher/professor I've had in my entire life. It's easy to get a good grade but this guy is just awful. super unclear about everything, only addresses one viewpoint, assigns tons of random work that doesn't follow the syllabus and is very time consuming. He calls on random people and experts detailed answers. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Decently Easy grader but gives a lot of reading and writing assignments . Is not clear about instructions and does not answer emails. Calls on students at random for participation points and expects detailed answers. Slides are a bit unorganized but he reviews each topic multiple times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Kintiba comes off as nice friendly person. However, this personality has little impact on the class. The class itself is very disorganized. At times he will spend 80 percent of class time reviewing what we learned in the previous class. Also, make sure you have your camera on when he randomly calls you. If not, you will lose points.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Kintiba cares a lot about his students and he's very passionate about his subject but there are some things you have to be wary about. First, you will always get randomly picked on to answer questions. He can also be a little disorganized when it comes to due dates. If you have trouble speaking up in class, he might not be for you.

one of the most disorganized classes i've ever taken. didn't follow or update the syllabus. when we had assignments, they were short notice and didn't have clear criteria. was always unsure what to read/prepare for class sessions and he will randomly call on students. thinks he's being friendly but it comes off awkward. mandatory cameras on on zoom
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Extremely unorganized and lectures are full of misinformation. Does not respond to his emails and is not always present during his office hours.

Dr. Kintiba is like an uncle to his students. He really cares about your success in the class but I also want to make sure you learn. He likes his students to be engaged so hell call out students name and no cell phone use in class. One thing I didnt like was his change of assignment specifications last minute and not following his syllabus.

Pretty good professors class were different then the usual but it always feel like he cares about his student and truly want them to have a good grasp on the subject at hand unlike other professor that will be perfectly okay with not helping a student that having a hard time understanding everything.

Nice guy, but worst professor I've ever had: -moved a test to previous class without announcement -assignment specifications and dates are unclear -said he would be an hour late to class; never showed -isn't tactful when discussing religion, especially Islam (I'm not religious btw) -tested on arbitrary material -almost certainly forges grades

Definitely enjoyed Kurtzweil. He genuinely cares and you can tell he understands that oral comm is hard for some. He provides really good feedback and sets clear expectations for the class. Not saying I would take it again for fun but if I had to, Kurtzweil is the first prof i'm looking for!!!!

George was an excellent professor. Taught how to give good speeches while not stressing his students out too much. I didn't like the random group projects but they weren't bad at all. He was funny, interesting, and made an effort to get to know all his students. Take George!!!
George is amazing, great teaching style and enjoyed his class!!

George was a great professor that actually cares about his students' wellbeing. Not only was he an understanding grader but he truly made you feel heard and supported. I would take him again if I could. He makes every class enjoyable and understands that students have heavy workloads.

George is very understanding, relatable, smart, and an overall fun person. He made inag fun and I couldn't recommend him more. He also ends class early a lot and makes the lectures quick. The textbook is easy to find online so you don't have to pay for it and he gives a lot of credit for classwork and homework, which makes up for bad speech grades.

Super chill and always entertaining. Class is easy and speeches matter a lot for grades. Other assignments are basically all busy work. Has in class activities for points so you have to go to class. Random group assignments were kind of a pain but pretty easy. All speeches have an outline, if you follow it you'll a 100%. Would recommend for INAG.

George was an amazing lecturer. Was very understanding and cares about his students. Easy A, just do the work and show up. Tells fun stories and tries to make lectures interesting. Very easy to communicate with, answers emails quickly. He treats students with respect as long as you respect him.

George is a very nice guy and cares about his students, won't question if you need an extension. Assignments are very easy, and he grades easy on speeches. Definitely the class I never worried about, highly recommend!

He is an amazing human and professor. He comes across to you as a friend and as a person who cares about your success. The reason everyone gets good grades is because we feel inspired to do so well on our speeches due to the healthy learning environment he creates. Best professor ever.

Mr George is literally the man! Hes super chill and truly loves teaching and acts like one of your friends. The work is extremely simple too and the 4 essays he gives throughout the semester are extremely easy to the point where I would prepare 2 minutes before class and I would get a 95 percent. Take him if you have the chance!

George is great! His class was one of the best I have taken at UMD. There are a couple of quizzes a midterm and a final but the speeches hold the most weight towards your grade. He is a fair grader and is extremely considerate. He gives plenty of time for assignments and even cancels class so we have more time. Take him for a fun and easy class!
I have never had a professor that has cared more about his students. He is accommodating and genuinely wants to see his students succeed. I can not recommend this man enough. What a gem.
Best professor I ever had. I never comment on teachers through this website. But he truly changed my life for the better.
George is very funny and engaging. Make sure you come to class and participate, and if you do that, you'll do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Do not understand how he could have possibly gotten a degree in communication. He would email us to "never send him emails". He was very very poor at communicating to his students over email, and very rude. He had his favorites in the class and it was obvious. Take him if you want an A, but the experience was not fun. I do not recommend him.

Funny guy, always sharing things about his personal life I would warn you though that he actually grades your speeches & takes off points, unlike the other INAG / COMM professors, but still fairly easy to get an A if your speeches aren't total trash The semester was top-heavy & I thought the beginning was rough, but it gets better over time

Prof Gerhardt was super sweet and got me to enjoy writing again. Some of the assignments were busy work, but it really didn't matter because of her "un-grading", meaning most things were graded off of completion. It made my semester much less stressful, and I enjoyed attending her class

Pam is the best professor I had during my time at Maryland. This sounds like a cheeky superlative, but her Professional Writing Nonfiction Narrative class (398R) actually got me exciting about writing. Best of all: it changed my relationship to and perspective on the writing craft. I had my assignments done in advance, because I wanted to do them.
Very chill and tries hard to make sure people understand assignments. But she also knows most people take this class for the credit and is very understanding and lenient.
don't buy the book "On Writing Well by Zinsser" b/c she used the book 2 times.  Read the chapters on (google books) its there.
easy!!!!easy!!!!easy!!!!easy!!!!easy!!!!easy!!!!
Great professor makes writing tolerable and really helps you to understand writing techniques

great class, great prof. she's incredibly cool, this is the best class to pick for professional english req. the narrative that the class workshops really isn't as scary as everyone makes it seem. everyone is on the chopping block, and you get to read other student's writings. she's written for a lot of pubs and papers and class is always fun.
She was a great instructor.  I've never taken a writing class that had been so fun!  After her class, I became interested in writing again.
Nice teacher and fairly easy grader. Almost the entire course grades are made up of papers. Not as bad as it might seem

Has this real nasty habit of going overtime, but she's an easy grader. Often goes over the same material multiple times, and doesn't really give you any indication of how you're doing in a class until the class is over. Watch out for this class' big assignment---you've gotta write a huge paper and have the class critique it, which isn't fun at all.

This professor expects you to come in with previous knowledge, if you have a lot of time in your schedule it is possible to do. Although if you can help it PLEASE do not take chem with him, any one else is better. His tests also do not reflect his teaching at all.

Unless you know chemistry from previous classes, this class is not it. He explains chemistry in the most compicated way, his exams are nothing like the textbooks or his lectures. The average for every exam was always a 50-60.The only good thing was GSS and the textbook because they actually broke chemistry down to what it's suppose to be.

Took CHEM 231 and 241 with Dr. Friedman- and as he put it-  "everything you read online is true". Orgo is hard, and he doesn't make the class easy. He expects you to work hard, attend class, and struggle in everything. That said, if you do those things, Dr. Friedman is helpful, patient, accessible, and easily the best professor I've had.

Okay. Dr. Friedman has a lot of personality. I think he genuinely cares and he is so smart and he loves Orgo so much. That is probably his biggest downfall though. He assumes that everyone has the same level of Orgo knowledge that he has. His tests are impossible. You need PhD level knowledge to understand them. Good person, bad at teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His sarcasm and jokes are what made lecture interesting. He has very hard assignments and his exam averages are well below the averages for other orgo professors, but there is a curve to account for it. While it is frustrating at times to have a course so hard, it is not that bad in the end. He was way more caring and responsive than expected

An infuriating man who has no business being as rude and anal as he is. At the end of the semester, he will never tell you what the curve will be, so if you're in-between grades, be prepared to sweat. After the final he said he needed time to come up with final grades because it was "part science, part art," like BFFR this is a 1 credit chem lab.

Dr. Friedman has a bad rep for no reason. All orgo classes are hard, idk why people expect an easy A. He has difficult exams, but he provides a LOT of resources to prepare and tells you exactly how to succeed in the course. He genuinely cares about students learning the content and helps a lot in office hours.
lab prof and he will try to make everything difficult and toughly graded. hoping for a curve lol. even the TAs don't like him so best of luck

This is my 2nd time taking Orgo and Dr. Friedman was definitely better than my last professor. He and the TA genuinely want you to learn and understand and they provide lots of opportunities for help. As long as you go to lecture, do homeworks, and study you'll do well.

He's a good professor. Very approachable and will help if you need and explain the concepts during office hours. He responds to emails very fast and detailed. Orgo is a hard course. His exams were fair, the final was really hard though for the amount of time given. If you understand the concepts you will be good.

I've taken him twice (CHEM131 and CHEM241) and I thought he was great. Of course the class material is difficult, but he made funny remarks that made it fun to learn. We would sometimes have little slightly off-topic discussions about general orgo stuff which was fun. Very helpful during office hours. As long as u respect him, he respects you.

Professor Friedman was a great person overall. He was funny and it made his classes enjoyable. Organic Chemistry is a hard course, so no matter what, you are going to have to spend lots of time outside of class studying to succeed. His exam averages are usually very low, but he provides past exams to allow you to study which are super helpful.

Be realistic, it's a hard class, you're going to struggle. Also, if you're a professor in a course where half the students are Premeds, you're going to try to be abrasive to scare them off from constantly begging for an A. That being said, if you just go to him with a good attitude wanting to learn, he's super helpful and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Orgo 2 lab with Friedman is honestly not that bad. His lab reports are difficult but going to office hours and watching his lectures helped. The labs themselves are actually pretty fun. The worst part is definitely the midterm and final, they are extremely difficult and you will need to dedicate some serious time to studying beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unfortunately he's the only professor for lab classes so if you need to take the course for your major, good luck! Labs are ok and around the difficulty you would expect but it's the lab midterms and finals that are the grade killers.

Can't teach very well, and uses charisma/jokes to make up for it. The TA would try to make up for the lack of things he taught us in class, where he would just barely mention a VERY important topic. His tests are extremely hard, and too little time is given to be able to complete them. He curves. He's pretty friendly. Uses clickers for attendance.

Friedman truly does care for his students and wants you to do well. The tests have gotten significantly easier the last few years. If you do all the old exams on his elms you'll be prepared. Most people fail his exams but theres a huge curve so don't worry. Best advice is to read orgo as a 2nd language ahead of classes. I loved his lecturing style.

Friedman is truly a fantastic professor, and I simply cannot wrap my head around the fact that people dislike him. Orgo is tough, and although he likes to challenge us, he also prepares us extremely well for that. Don't get me wrong: his tests are hard, but he always asks things that we are capable of answering based on what he taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: friedman is the worst professor i have ever had. his tests are unreasonable, hes rude, and he thinks everyone is cheating and will attempt to accuse you with 0 evidence. TAs are generally trash. A lot of inconsistency in how they teach. No mercy on the exam grades (no partial credit). if you can take 242 with someone else then please save yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: this man wants you to fail. he judges how good his tests are by how many students cry during it. u tell me whether a 25% average is normal. he consistently goes out of his way to come up with graduate level questions that no one can solve. worst teacher ive ever had.

He judges how good hes test are by seeing how many people cry. No joke, this man thrives by seeing students suffer. His Organic Chemistry lab midterm has General Chemistry on it and 75% of it was stuff we didnt learn. Almost all of the averages are 25%.

Definitely one of the worst professors I've ever had to deal with. Usually, I don't like to give professors bad reviews but this class was too frustrating and was just unsympathetic towards me when I needed help.

He is known to be one of the "toughest" professors, but I say he is very good professor that wants nothing but the best for his students. He does dives DEEP DEEP into lecture that its easy to get lost sometimes. He wasn't as bad as people made him seem like. Organic chemistry is just generally difficult so be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: My best advice is to go to GSS and do practice problems bc his tests arent that hard if you know the material. I didnt go to him for help at all bc he overcomplicates a lot of things but GO TO GSS !!!!!!!
He doesn't seem to care about students. He is straight-up mean. On the first day of classes, he came in and bragged his test averages were 47%. That's a failure by the teacher at that point.

This class destroyed me. He is notorious for being one of the worst professors at UMD. His exams are impossible, usually all have an average of 30%. He refuses to acknowledge the difficulty and keeps saying this was very doable when literally the entire class fails. Ive never struggled so much in a class and walked out of every lecture confused.
Lectures are kept interesting, great at answering questions. Tests are a bit hard, grades are curved at the end of the semester. Homework is fairly easy if you keep up with the material.

I took Orgo I in Fall 2019. It was the worst experience ever. From the 1st exam I got an F and right before exam 2 was coming up, I simply withdrew from the class. I knew that I would not be able to succeed with this professor. The lectures at first seem straightforward, but the exams are like a whole different language. Just don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class destroyed me both physically and mentally.

The labs themselves are doable if you attend 1-2 office hours and collaborate with people (even my TA said to work with people). It's his exams that are the worst. Friedman has a rep for making the hardest exams and it's worst when all questions are MC. He also very very much despite cheaters and crack down on them hard.

Avoid this guy like the plague! It doesn't matter how good your labs are, his tests are unreasonably difficult. Usually 15 questions over 50 minutes. Test averages were horrible, about 35 to 50. He sets the class average at a B- (around 65 pre-curve), which is super low for the amount of work you'll put in. If possible, take another teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I only have 350 words to say this and its not enough so I will get straight to it. - Impossible exams (class average was 30%) -Blames everyone for cheating on Chegg -Extremely high expectations -Rude -Email replies are "thanks for your opinion" -Unconcerned for students Do yourself a favor and avoid this professor at all costs.

Post-lab questions could be challenging, but averages for labs ended up being around 86%.The midterm and final were unnecessarily hard, and when the class averaged 42% on the midterm, Friedman's response was rude, and put the blame on us. They didn't really pertain to material we learned in class, and there wasn't enough time given.

Was not responsive to students. Exams were unreasonably hard and had nothing to do with labs. Practice exams were far too easy compared to exams. If the lab is online again I do not recommend it. Even if you got good grades on the labs and worked on them for HOURS exams can destroy your grade.
PLQs are way too hard and the exams are nothing like the practice exam he gives you. Then he gets angry and tells students that his exams are fair after everyone failed.
You ask for help and he just responds saying he can't give answers. How does he expect us to learn if he won't teach anything. Awful professor especially with the covid situation. Do not take him.

Absolutely no consideration for students, on top of being rude. Just plain awful, PLQs are way harder than they need to be. Exam review was nothing like the actual exam. Midterm was on a Sunday and told a healthcare worker to take the exam on their lunch break. Didn't give enough time for students to take the midterm, many ended up skipping. AWFUL!

I was taking 242 w/Friedman and decided to drop the course. One of the most despicable professors at UMD. If possible, avoid. His lack of empathy for students situations is unreal. He offers no support, no guidance or no encouragement whatsoever. Truly a disgusting person. He makes PLQs ridiculously challenging on purpose for lessons. AVOID!!!!

Heartless. When school shut down I was homeless, and got COVID19. I still did all of my work and had a near perfect grade. but I didn't have a way to submit one of my labs on time. I sent proof that my lab was finished on time and he ignored all my emails so I explained my situation to a higher-up. He ended up grading but still refused to email me

Labs take the full three hours. Go to office hours. Exams are difficult and there's almost no use studying as Friedman is very clever and gives hard problems. Besides exams, I'd say this class is easier than 232 but in-class labs are rough - no partners so you have to know what you're doing and long lines to get reagents - takes forever. My 87  A

Friedman is a really good professor that will help you succeed if you put in the work. Organic chem is a hard class, and the material can get confusing, but he does a good job at making it understandable, and doesn't emphasize memorization like some others. His exams can be challenging towards the end of the semester, but he's always open to talk.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's rude. Not a good teacher and shouldn't be in charge of students. Doesn't care about you at all. Very sarcastic and not helpful. I can't wait to be done with his class.

Very hard, but doable, and definitely one of my favorite professors Ive had at UMD. His lectures are very dense (and he doesn't allow phones), but he's very accessible outside of class and will most likely remember your name. Definitely take him, its an experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: For Organic Chemistry II lab, it will be difficult but you will understand its value at the end. Decently curved.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Labs were pretty decent. Post lab questions were relevant to the associated labs but often involved outside knowledge - go to TA office hours for help to improve your grade. Midterm was easier than final, but neither were terrible. Lab practical was stressful but reasonable. Overall, this lab isn't as bad as some of the others.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I know ppl have a lot to say abt Dr. Friedman but he is my all time favorite professor. I had him for 131 and 231, and he genuinely cares about students understanding. He provides a solid foundation to continue learning chem. his class is hard af but he gives you so many resources and makes videos. you have to put in the work but he genuinely cares
really good at explaining the concepts and preparing you for orgo. the tests are hard with the averages being in the low 60s but he gives a generous curve
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Friedman is an alright lecturer, although he can get sidetracked by an 'awesome' mechanism that we don't need to know. He tends to speak over our heads as if we already know the material (supposed to read textbooks before lecture). Exams are unneccessarily hard and he brags about their difficulty. Don't take unless you have a lot of free time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy
