reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIM. He once said, "I forget that you're not all organic chemists, so Im not really sure how to teach it to you." On the last day of class he said, "we're going to debrief because taking a class with me is kind of like going through war."
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: His class has a massive curve which is nice but it is desperately needed by the end of the semester due to how hard his exams are. Your TAs took the exam last night and averaged a 70 is what hed say. Very easy to talk to outside of class but he speaks as if you already know the material and can understand everything he says. Take somebody else.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Absolutely horrendous. This man wants to see people fail. There needs to be a new lab coordinator. Koppel for Orgo 1 Lab was hard but FAIR. Friedman most definitely makes this lab virtually impossible to do well in, even when you study. When I tell you he literally had answer choices from a-n on the final.... A THROUGH N?!?!? No words.
Friedman is a super cool guy and is very willing to help. The only issue is the difficulty of the tests, but the curve will help you enough in the end.

You might ask yourself: self, should I take Dr Friedman? Nope. He is a funny guy with lots of jokes and catch phrases (like the one above) but his exams are the hardest. Often not easy to understand what the questions are asking. Exam averages in low 50s but gets huge curve, 75ishA-. Key to success is studying the past exams and answer keys
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I failed the course with a D+ but it was all my fault. Dr. Friedman was a great professor and very knowledgeable. Lectures were not boring and he's funny! The only reason I did not pass is because I did not put in the work. I studied 2-3 days before exams and scored poorly on them. Study hard and go to lectures and you will do great! He's amazing
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor with really great lectures and super helpful/accessible outside of class. He explains stuff really well. You'll definitely learn a lot if you go to lecture and keep up with the practice and homework. He also does late night live video reviews before tests. The only catch is that his tests are very hard, you gotta study past exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Friedman is what we like to call sadistic, he has no mercy for his students. His post lab questions are virtually harder than any homework you will ever do and its a one credit course. His exam averages are like a 30%. Just to top things off, he will literally send you to the honor's council in a heartbeat. Good Luck in orgo II lab, you ll need it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Lab was unnecessarily difficult and exams were too tough for the material taught.

Friedman is a great guy and a funny professor, but his class is ridiculously hard. His lectures are interesting but you learn most of the material doing the homework, and the tests are impossible even if you study a lot. He sort of roots for people to do poorly which makes it really hard. Save yourself the pain and just take a different professor.

I had to retake this class ( I took it first with a teacher who was actually considered easy). I didnt put in much effort and didnt pass by a hair. I was obviously scared to take it with Friedman, but he was amazing. Such interesting lectures, funny, yes you must WORK but youll be fine if you do just that. He really cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing teacher with great lectures. His exams are hard af tho, but he posts past exams that help out a lot. I do all of them before the exams and usually score around a B on them (without a curve). His class is harder than others, but you really understand the material. There's a curve at the end of the semester and its super generous.

His exams are pretty difficult but in general I think he's such a good teacher. He explains things very thoroughly and breaks everything down for you so you can genuinely understand. His lectures go by quickly and if you study for his exams and thoroughly know the material, you're going to do well.

Friedman was huge in helping me understand orgo. He is super approachable and can help you understand any problem, he even puts in effort to learn most students names. He definitely is tough and pushes students, but it pays off in the long run as you will have a much deeper understanding and be better prepared for orgo 2. Just dont procrastinate!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Friedman is the man! He teaches Organic chem in a way that makes it so easy to learn. He doesn't want you to memorize things just cause like other professors, he'd rather have you understand things fully so that you can be successful down the road on things like the MCAT. His tests are hard, but if you work hard and study you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Friedman is the best professor I've had throughout my time as an undergrad. This is the second semester I've taken him and he is by far the best orgo teacher at UMD. Is his class hard? Obviously, this is organic chem what do you expect, but he teaches it well enough where if you work hard you will do well. Would take him again if I could!

The only grades in this class are exams, so good luck if you are not a good test-taker. I showed up to every lecture, took lots of notes, did practice problems, and studied a lot. I still struggled on a daily basis. Dr. Friedman takes pride in his extremely difficult exams and often brags that even he found them challenging. Don't take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Organic chemistry is a hard class no matter which professor you take. However, Friedman is a very good professor who knows how to effectively teach the material. However, his exams are tricky and require a considerable amount of studying to master. Thankfully, he gives out old exams before midterms. With a some studying, you will pass his class!

Probably my best professor during the Undegrad years. Very good lecturer and honestly cares if students understand the concepts. Exams can be tough but if you pay attention in class and study consistently, you will do fine.

I honestly really enjoyed being in his class, but you have to work hard and come to lectures and discussions in order to do well. He is very fun and knowledgeable, however his exams are pretty hard. Even if you study everything he will still put something in there that you will most likely not have seen before, but the curve will save you!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Friedman's a really good teacher. He moves really fast during lectures, so if you doze off even for a minute you'll miss a lot. He's super helpful during office hours, but as everyone else said his exams are HARD. Study everything we did in class, but he'll throw a curveball at you just for fun. Only take him if you're willing to work really hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Prof Friedman, is a great teacher, his lectures were helpful. But his exams were so unnecessarily hard and throughout the course youll doubt your intelligence because of the grades youre getting. But if youre willling to put in hours of work, take the class. And he curves the class in the end my average on test were a 46% but I ended with a 75%

Grades are mostly based on exam scores. There's a lot of hw, 20 questions with multiple parts but each hw is 10 pts and there's 12 total. Lots of clickers. I got a low C on the 1st exam, low B on the 2nd, and flat 50 (yikes...) on the 3rd. The final is a different version of the same questions on the 3 exams. I got a D on the final (above avg)

Dr. Friedman has a reputation of being a difficult professor. I'm not going to lie it was a difficult and a very lecture heavy course but the way Dr. Friedman taught was great. If you pay attention in lecture and take advantage of his practice exams you can do really well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: Tough grader but really cares about his students and wants them to succeed. If you work hard you will pass. His curves are wonderful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Yeah, Dr. Friedman gives hard tests but he is a great professor and really makes sure you learn the material. He really just wants everyone to know chemistry and what the concepts are behind the topics so you will do well in much harder chem classes. If you actually want to learn and enjoy chem take Friedman hes the man!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Tests are tough--Would take again

reviews.comment: OK, YES, his exams are hard, BUT all you have to do is get above the average and you're golden! I usually get in the 70's, tbh could have worked harder, but I should end up with a B+ at WORST with the curve. He is an AMAZING teacher! He moves slowly and explains everything in depth. I've never even opened the textbook.
Learned a ton however, the tests are pretty tough. He is a good professor and great lecturer. Available outside of class and pretty helpful in office hours
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Friedman is very good about explaining chemistry in a way that's easy to understand. He is pretty funny and very approachable. However, his tests are very difficult with averages in the 50s, but a generous curve. For the exams, you will need to know the concepts behind each topic and be able to connect more than one concept in each problem.

I've had all the basic chem teachers, you know who they are. Dr. Friedman is hands down the best. He lectures in a way that you understand and is extremely accessible outside of class. Instead of a tutor, I went to his office hours everyday. Tests are very hard but he will tell you what to expect. So helpful, great teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you want to learn organic chemistry, take it with Friedman. Like any Organic Chem class, this class was tough too. Simply said, you must put in the work to earn the grade you want.  Friedman was very helpful at office hours and held reviews before each exam. He wants students to succeed! If you are looking for an easy A, not the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures were very good at conveying the material, however his tests are needlessly hard, requiring the synthesis of multiple concepts on 3/4 of the problems even if it had not been addressed before in class.  With orgo this is especial tough as you won't always knew what force takes precedence when combining concepts. Also mandatory attendance
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He was the lab director. The post-lab questions aren't too bad and the TAs are very willing to help. He also posts the lab set-ups (and sometimes videos about the more difficult topics) online in advance which is super helpful. The tests are difficult though.

Friedman is the best Orgo 1 professor I could've had. He lectures quickly, but effectively. He is organized, explains anything you have questions on, & is incredibly knowledgable about orgo. He's also pretty sarcastic in a great way. DO YOUR HW, SHOW UP TO CLASS FOR CLICKER ?s. Put in time and you'll learn tons and have a great basis for Orgo 2.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lectures reeeally fast, so I suggest you not take him if you can't keep up with the pace, though he does have videos based exactly on what he lectures on Elms. You won't know what your grade actually is throughout the semester until after finals. His exams are really hard, seeing as the averages are between 40-50%
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Friedman wants you to do well but, you have to work for it. He emphasizes doing a small amount practice problems daily. This is crucial when it comes to synthesis, NMR, IR, and mechanisms. He has videos on ELMS which are very helpful. He is very fast at grading and easily accessible out of class.

If you are a slacker, you won't like Dr. Friedman. If you are serious about your academics, and really want to learn the material, then take Dr. Friedman. If you want to take a class where you can earn an easy A, perhaps take another professor. If you want to nail the MCAT or become a successful chemist, then take Dr. Freidman.

This will be my fourth semester with Dr. Friedman.  He is an excellent teacher and is always willing to spend time with you in office hours. He is known for being "tough," but his class taught me to think critically of reactions- an aspect critical to chemistry majors and pre-health degree majors. I encourage you to take him and challenge yourself.

After two semesters with Friedman I have learned his value. He's not going to cater to you, but he doesn't want you to suffer. He is accessible and helpful during his office hours, and rlly tries to get you to think about why something happens instead of memorizing. Useful for chem majors, useful for life.  His sarcasm can be mistaken for rudeness.

Friedman works very fast. However, he provides so many resources that will help you better understand the concepts. It is very helpful to do old practice exams - try to understand the CONCEPT behind the practice exam problems, and you will most likely do fairly well on the exams b/c the concepts don't change. Understand rather than try to memorize.

Friedman is EXTREMELY attentive to his students and very organized. Replies to emails within the hour and goes out of his way to help students with any questions. Easy to talk to, great sense of humor, very prompt in uploading grades and notifications. He works VERY fast in lecture, so I HIGHLY suggest you read the chapters before going to class

I just took Dr. Friedman's CHEM231 class as a freshman (I tested out of CHEM131 with AP Chem). Going into this class I was quite scared, but Dr. Friedman was a fantastic and hilarious teacher who made the class easily manageable. Go to class, do the homework, do the practice exams, and study your reactions. That's what I did and I pulled an A.

Works extremely fast during lecture. Concepts are hard to understand, but he gives you as many resources as he can to help you. Working through previous semester exams will help you get a feel for what kinds of problems you should expect to see in his future exams - it helped me A LOT. Use as many resources as you can!
Very fast in class. If you don't go to GSS or office hours you'll have a hard time. Don't rely on the "old practice" exams. Your exam will most likely be nothing like it.

Dr. Friedman is a great lecturer and really wants you to do well. There are plenty of opportunities to do well in the class (GSS, online review sessions before exams, HW and participation clickers). The biggest knock against him is how hard he makes the class. Orgo is a beast as is but his tests are ridiculously hard at times. Curves well tho!

He's tough, but fair. There's always a big curve for the exams but that doesn't mean you shouldn't work for the grade. Everything he covers in lecture is on the exam one way or another and he follows the textbook to a T. If you actually want the help, he will be there. He's great if you're going into Orgo2.

Professor Friedman is passionate about teaching chemistry. His classes are entertaining and he explains concepts very well, although he moves very fast so it is helpful to come to class having looked over the textbook first. Everyone complains that his tests are too hard but in the end there is a huge curve so it ends up fine.  Don't be scared off!

Dr. Friedman is a great professor. He is able to explain orgo concepts very well and uses helpful analogies. He is also very funny and going to his lectures was almost fun. His tests really aren't that bad, I would definitely recommend for orgo 1.
such a nice guy and extremely intelligent professor and lecturer. he's probably the best orgo 1 teacher

Dr. Friedman always goes above and beyond for his students. I emailed him once on  a Saturday and received a lengthy response within the hour. He does exam review sessions online and you can ALWAYS find a way to get your questions answered if you are willing to reach out. GSS is a huge help!
I didn't learn anything in this lab.   It really depends on your TA but I never saw Professor Friedman, except for one time.  Be prepared to teach yourself everything.
The class is hard, but chemistry is for most people.  Be sure to go over practice problems and understand them.  I never went to GSS or office hours and did fine.  He is kind of hilarious.

He really gives you every resource to pass. The tests are hard but it is always stuff you have learned and gone over. His class is set up very well with a lot of practice problems. GSS is very helpful. He is very good at explaining things so office hours are very helpful as well. Awesome curve for tests so just worry about being at the average.

I had zero previous experience with chem before this class, but I still got an A-. No doubt he is the most difficult gen chem professor, and you will have to work very hard to get an A or even a B+. I studied the book outside of class and went to GSS. His lectures are sorta hard to follow so reading the book helps a lot. It's not impossible :)

Awful, avoid his class at all costs. Ruined my GPA, took my time away from other classes. I learned more in the GSSs than in his lecture. Expectations are ridiculous. Grade depends on whether you've taken Chem AP or not. If yes, then its an A or a B, or not, its guaranteed below a  C+.

Not a good teacher if you need reinforcement. Orgo is not a joke and you need a teacher that won't just teach and expect you to learn unless you really take the time. Other teachers are MUCH better at getting the material across to students, this isn't one of them.

He makes the exam extremely difficult and even jokes about it in class. He speaks so quickly about each subject you barely have time to comprehend what what he is talking about when taking notes. the textbook is necessary and worth reading inside and out to get a decent grade in the class.

He taught this class like everyone in it was a chemistry major. I was pregnant when I took his lecture and when I called him the morning of an exam to say that I was too sick to make it, he said I could come the next day at 7am only with documentation from a doctor to be able to make it up. He's not as flexible with making it up like he says he is.

My worst experience in a whole academic career! Instead of teaching like this, better don't teach at all! This class had almost dissipated my respect to the subject (chemistry); and this is scary! I really felt orphaned in the class, perhaps because I used to see the professor for about 40 min. a week for a jet-fast discussion of the upcoming lab.

Wasn't planning on commenting, but when I saw that professor Friedman was rated so low, i was so confused. He is literally the best professor I have had in college thus far. I have taken many science classes, and he is the best that I have had. Very very hard, but if you put in the effort you have a shot. Expects a lot, but also teaches you a lot.

I would definitely not suggest Dr. Friedman to anyone who isn't amazingly talented in chemistry. He gives very easy example in class then murders your grade on the exams. He does have online homework which can pull up your grade, but definitely not by much. I would warn any other students to stay away from this teacher if you want a good G.P.A.

His tests are extremely unfair, and are never similar to what he does in class. He is easy to understand and is extremely helpful. The book isn't  needed at all if you know what you're  doing. His past exams give you an idea on the difficulty level, but usually don't give you accurate topics.

Worst human being in life. I would not recommend him to my worst enemy. I got a good grade in the class but that's because I worked my a#% off all semester. He is extremely rude and really does not give a crap about his students. People have actually cried after going to his office hours.

Dr. Lee is a really nice guy and a great lecturer. He's clear and knows what he's talking about. the tests are not that bad really. He has good online help and teaches to the exams. The book is barely needed. Definitely go to lecture everyday. If you do, exams are fine.

Seriously avoid him if you can. If you are naturally gifted in chemistry you will be fine. Most students do not do well with him. The exams really are a wash. I have never had exams that bad in my college career. The problems he does in class are easy, but the ones on exams are insane. He teaches 3x more info than the book does.it is not worth it

Nice guy who is willing to help his students but exams are IMPOSSIBLE and lecture notes/examples don't help at all because he just shows easy examples in class and then throws the hardest most complicated problems at you on the exams. Take someone else if possible.

I thought he was the most interesting teacher ever.  He made chemistry really fun!  Unlike some other commentators I thought his tests were very straight forward.  You have to study a little and attend all of his lectures to understand the material, but he is an EXCELLENT teacher!

Dr. Lee is a great lecturer, but his tests are extremely difficult. You realize that his lecture notes don't help very much when it comes to the exams. We also had a terrible TA. Unless you're good at math/logic, you should try to pick a different professor.

Dr Lee is hilarious!  He was a good lecturer who always allowed time for questions.  However, his tests are very tricky, and it's important to study A LOT and know the material inside out.  Luckily there is a huge curve, so as long as you get above the average you'll be okay.  He made me actually like chemistry!
A wonderful teacher and should be teaching lectures, but unfortunately his exams were extremely difficult (looking at past exams didn't help at all).

Definitely try to avoid taking Gen Chem II lab with him. His lectures always seemed good when you were in class, but later realized that they were completely unhelpful. Lab reports were impossible and the TAs know absolutely nothing and are worse at Chemistry than most of the students. Friedman is a thoroughly unhelpful professor. Avoid!
Good class and really clear lectures. Homework is an easy way to make points but tests are really hard, though the curve helps a lot. Great teacher who explains the concepts very well.

He is a fun lecturer, however you won't be able to get an A in this class unless this is the only class you are taking in a semester. The TAs and the professor seem enjoying taking points away. The lectures do not help you prepare for the exams. If you have choice, stay away from this man. STAY AWAY.

This is for orgo I lab as this prof was the coordinator. Lab is lab, it's 3 hrs/week. If you are given good procedures it's not too hard. Post lab Qs are hard and only somewhat relate to what happens in lab. Midterm and final are, as always for lab, very difficult; luckily all are MC. Curve at least 6%. Much depends on the TAs

I am currently taking Dr Lee for Orgo I and have really enjoyed having him as a professor. As long as you attend all classes and take good notes, you'll be fine. Textbook is pretty useless, I've gotten B's on exams all year and didnt open the book once. The Klein book helps a lot tho. Overall, pretty straight forward porfessor. Very funny and loves

Tests are seriously impossible. I hope there is a huge curve at the end or I am in trouble. I am a straight A student so I have put a lot of time into this class and I am still very confused. I agree about the practice tests..they are completely different than the actual exam. I do NOT recommend taking him for org chem.

Decent lecturer, decent guy.  I learned a fair amount of organic chemistry.  However, I can't recommend him.  Here's why:  His exams are RIDICULOUSLY hard, and he brags about how hard they are and how he makes them impossible on purpose.  The practice exams resemble the actual ones only in that they're printed on paper.

I don't know what these people are on - worst professor! Never told you your grades after tests, impossible to understand basic concepts -  tests are impossible and focus solely on the "Princeton method" - Hi we're U of M students working full time taking the class at night  - don't have 3,000 hours to study! Stay away at all cost!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

He's really funny and sometimes inappropriate. He's clear and works through examples in class. As long as you keep up with the work, then you'll do fine. I am actually going to try to take Chem231 (Orgo) with him next semester.

Dr.Lee is an awsome professor. He made things clear in his lectures. I do recommend to read over the text before going into the class which will help you understand lectures better. Dr.Lee is willing to help you understand stuff if you go into his office. He made me to enjoy Orgo and so will you when you take his class :)

My class was chemistry-challenged so the curve was ~71% was an A.  He wasn't a bad teacher at all because the material itself was just infuriating.  He'll help you outside of class if you need it.  Voice cracks a lot too which adds some humor to otherwise boring lectures.

He knows how to teach Organic chemitstry II. He is very helpfull and he is always there for you. However, his exams are superrrrrrrrrr hard!!! You will learn in his class, but you might not get the grade that you want unless you burn your eyelashes studying(even then is not sure). I f you want to learn take it, if you only want a very good grade do

Biggest jerk I know. Only fun part is when his voice cracks! Arrogant and does very little to help students. Makes inappropriate comments to students at the bar. Creepy all around. Recommend transferring schools before taking him!
Great teacher, explains concepts very well.  He really understands organic chemistry at a fundamental level and can answer any question.  Tests are challenging, but in a good way.
I liked him as a teacher, definitely better and easier to understand then the Orgo teacher I have right now.  I wish he tought organic chemistry here.

funny guy!!! He's acually really funny and smart!! Only thing is that his teaching ways are not that clear and you have to review the book. He cares about his students and is very understanding. CURVES LIKE CRAZY although tests are hard. He's great just not the best chem teacher but he makes the class fun!!

Dude dropped the lowest exam and curved the other exams along with the finals. He is quick with his emails and very flexible outside his lectures. he uses the textbook for lectures. Quizzes are straight from the recc textbook problems and exam questions are similar to the suggested problems he post. Amin curves are crazy, man turned my D+ to a B-

Lectures are great, he records them and posts his notes too. Sometimes lectures were a little fast but it's fine, lots to get through. Textbook is good resource. If you want more on proofs go to office hours. Four midterms (3 curved for me) and a final (curved). Gives EC for finding lecture mistakes. Overall great professor, definitely take Amin!

Three hundred fifty characters aren't enough to explain how amazing he is. First, he drops the lowest test score which means you only gotta do good on three tests. Quizzes are based on book problems so if you do them all before the quiz should be an easy 100. OFFICE HOURS he basically becomes the best tutor you can ever ask for during office hours

Gholampour is the best professor you could ask for, genuinely great guy who knows his stuff. He gives bonus points if you answer questions during lecture. His exams were hard but that is bc the course can be difficult. He only tests on examples that were gone over in class and in textbook. 100% recommend. Curve was crazy my 69 went to a B.

he was great!! posted all of the lecture notes so you could go back, and began recording lectures in case a class was missed (it was awful quality, but enough where I got the point). As well as dropping lowest test/quiz and a curve, the homework was due at the end of the semester, super convenient.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Such a beast! Posts all his notes and is always open to help his students. He dropped the lowest quiz and exam and even curved the exams, but you definitely need to put the work in despite his generosity, he also assigned all homework to be due at the end of the semester and gives EC if you find a mistake in his work in lecture. TAKE AMIN!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Greatest ever
Great guy and curves heavily

Caring professor, difficult exams. Although the exams were difficult, he made it concise that it was to be similar to homework and lecture problems so it wasn't too surprising. Really responsive in email and WebAssign. Large curve as someone else has previously mentioned. Genuinely interested in the subject and seems to be passionate as well.

Many of us asked him about what he does to curve, but he mostly dodged our questions and just said that he'd raise the everyone's discussion quizzes up to the discussion section that had the highest score. Towards the end, he did that, dropped our lowest test, and raised our other 3 tests by 15%. He seems fair and I'd take him again.

Amin is a blessing that comes every so often in semesters at UMD. His exams are hard, but doable. He is very approachable and sweet. He analyzes the students way of doing a problem, and states the students mistakes. He does have a curve, but you will not pass if you get below a 50% on every exam. He is the best!!!! I learned so much from him.

He's a really nice guy! He gives clear step-by-step explanations of problems in lectures and is receptive to student concerns. The exams are difficult, but not impossible, and mirror what is said during lecture pretty well. He only introduced the curve at the end of class, but it was pretty fair.

Calculus is obviously not easy, but with this professor, it's actually alright. There's 2 homework every week, 4 midterms, a final, and quizzes every week during the weeks where we didn't have a midterm. The curve is amazing, my D+ somehow is getting to a B so that's great!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Big curve, hard class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: honestly i didnt go to any of his lectures bc it was confusing trying to hard understand him, i attended another lecturers. the quizzes during discussion are very fair. HUGE curve at the end end of the semester. I had a 69.21% on ELMS and got a B+ in the class so speaks for itself.

Best professor at UMD. He is the only teacher that I have met that seems to care about his students. His lectures are pretty good , but like all math classes read the textbook sections before class. His material is very clear and concise. Exams are difficult, but he does curve heavily depending on the average.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Math 141 is a major weed out, but I was so fortunate to take it with Amin. Great guy who is also very approachable and understanding. Has pretty hard exams, but at the end of the semester the curve is unreal. You will have to work hard in this class, but I will recommend to definitely take it with him.
Great professor who is super generous. Dropped one of the lowest tests and curved others.

This professor was really generous with his curves, adding 10pts on to tests with averages in the 60s. This made the class easy. His lectures were ok, but Id recommend using textbook to understand the material more. Doesnt prepare us well for final, but whatever.

I LOVE THIS MAN. Admittedly, his lectures are not great and are based a lot on theory. If you attend discussion, you can be successful. But, his tests are easy and don't include unnecessarily difficult algebra. He also curves a lot at the end of the semester which is unlike a lot of other calculus professors. Cutie. 10/10 would recommend.

One of UMD's best Professors. This man has a heart of Gold. If you get the chance to take him, do it! Amin is great at what he does and wants for you to do succeed. He's readily available in office hours and is great at explaining. Not to mention he gives extra credit for picking out mistakes in lecture and the curve for his class is real.

He is really nice and seems knowledgeable. If you go to his office hours for help, he'd help you. True, his midterms are pretty fair but that does not mean you shouldn't be prepared... Calculus is calculus, you still have to know your material VERY WELL. Final replaces everything if it's higher than the (rest + final combined). Fair enough?

This was the second time I've taken Calc 2 (I dropped it last semester-had it with Hamilton), and I was pleasantly surprised at how much easier it was to understand him. Even though he does have an accent, it's not super noticeable, and doesn't take away from his teaching. He was also just a really nice guy, which was refreshing to find.

Great professor. Clear and easy to understand in lecture, tests are fair and there are no surprises. His curve is amazing. Adds points to each test to make the average a B-, drops the lowest test and doubles the highest. Allows final exam to replace everything if it is better than the rest of your grades.

Professor Gholampour is by far one of the best professor's in the Math department. His quizzes and test are very fair since he literally gives you 5 sections to study and then gives you 5 QUESTIONS on the exam based on a section. If you practice and study, you will be alright. He also gives extra credit if you participate. Oh and the curve is real!
His grading policy is amazing. Droppa lowest test, ignores quiz+hw grade provided you have more than 50%, but puts very heavy emphasis on final exam.

Very good-natured. He will clarify anything you don't understand in his lectures. Tests are very fair and he gives you problems that take less than the 50 minutes given as long as you know the general concepts.

Amin was an awesome professor and he made the class very interesting. He was also very easy to talk to if further explanation was needed or for grade issues. He taught the material very well and made the class interesting

kind/reasonable prof but strict grading, deadlines and no extra credit. 321 is significantly difficult. Lectures are crucial and if you miss them you're likely to be confused. 13 hws lowest 2 dropped,1 paper, 2 exams, 1 final, weight of lowest exam is dropped and added to your final if you do better on the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I don't know what these other reviews are talking about. Professor Ghandi is great. She made the material interesting and understandable, while always providing clear feedback and assistance on projects. I'm taking her now for econ-stat and I chose to take her again for econometrics.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take her class. Lecture are boring and VERY tough grader.
She's unhelpful and difficult to follow in class. The average on the midterm was a 42%. Stay away.

AVOID TAKING HER CLASS. LECTURES A VERY BORING...COPY NOTES THE WHOLE CLASS WITHOUT TIME TO LET INFORMATION MARINATE...FORGET ABOUT GETTING MISSED NOTES...LOST GRANDMA N HAD TO ATTEND FUNERAL, SHE DIDNT CARE
Avoid this professor at all costs
Dont do it
Good professor, answered questions well, made everything make sense intuitively. Great class

This class was not too bad, it really helps if you go to lectures and discussions, do the homework, and go to office hours if you have additional questions. One-sided formula sheet was allowed for exams and she let us know ahead of time the types of questions that would be on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She has no idea how to teach an undergraduate physics course. I took E and M with her PHYS272, and it was a complete wreck. never uses the chalkboard, only lecture slides filled with screenshots of the textbook so there is little to no additional information she brings to the course. Would not consider taking her again for any course.

Michelle Girvan is great! A genuine angel. I'm currently taking PHYS270 and Girvan most certainly gave me the best experience out of the three general physics classes. Breaks down the information and doesn't dump too much work on your head at once. Doesn't grade too harshly and absolutely gives you everything you need to succeed.

Girvan is a great choice for physics II, her grading method is very helpful. Lectures come straight from the book, but she explains the topics well. Doing well on the mastering physics homework will help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Girvan has great lectures. She does lots of examples in class. She also does the quizzes in class, drops the lowest quiz, hw, and test. On top of it she curves each test to have the same avg and std dev as the first, and leniently curves the class in the end on top of everything! As long as you do the mastering physics it's (hard) helpful.

Genuinely the worst professor I've had. She teaches only for university funding and doesn't enjoy it. Her dry humor is insufferable. She's a tough grader but gives little/no feedback, and grades aren't posted until after the final. Mandatory attendance, too.

The amount of reading needed for this class is simply not attainable at all. It honestly made me angry how much she made us read, as if we don't have 5 other classes?? But then wants to talk about mental health and taking care of oneself? I'm not done with the class and can confidently say it was pointless. I mean she is nice and considerate, but..

The amount of long excruciating readings apart of the class was slightly unbearable. Not many assignments, so performance in each of them really matters. Easy class if you like Anthropology, but if you are just looking for a class that doesn't require much work, probably find a different class. Lectures consisted of millennial humor and tangents.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Took ANTH265 with Dr. Gilchrest this semester as an easy elective. The course-load is pretty light and topics are somewhat interesting. Lectures are pretty boring and not mandatory, most people just skip them. Not a fan of some of her opinions or cringe millennial humor. She's also a very slow grader, which is less than ideal.

The class itself is easy, no tests just various assignments. The TA does most of the grading, but none were too harsh. Lectures are mandatory and boring if you're just taking the class for the credit, the attendance system barely works, and I can guarantee that Dr. Gilchrest will make you cringe with millennial humor. Not a bad class overall.

Giuliano is the nicest guy. He truly cares about his students and wants them to do well and he makes classes really fun. Ignore the bad reviews, I'm 99% sure there's one troll who made review bombing her full-time job (check planetterp). 
As for this class, take it in winter so you don't miss the hands-on demonstrations!

The class is not a conventional statistics class, which is fine considering its applied to bioengineering. But where the class fell short is the professor. Scarcelli lacks the ability to explain the material well & his questions are bizarrely worded. He refuses to answer any questions that would clarify his confusing wording on exams. Avoid him.

Professor Scarcelli is an ineffective professor due to his inability to communicate the course material clearly and concisely. Students are more confused about the way he phrases his questions than the concepts themselves. If you ask him a question, he answers with a question. His lectures and the textbook are awful, so good luck taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The class is not a conventional statistics class, which is fine considering its applied to bioengineering. But where the class fell short is the professor. Scarcelli lacks the ability to explain the material well & his questions are bizarrely worded. He refuses to answer any questions that would clarify his confusing wording on exams. Avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment:
Get ready to do a lot of reading if you take this class. You def can't read the summary online because test questions are directly from the books and the lectures - most of the time the mc is on small details that you only get by reading.
Other than that, the material is interesting. Gimpel is also a great lecturer.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: If you are looking for a straightforward government class, this is not the one for you. Although he is a brilliant and kind human being, he structures the class in a way that unless you are extremely fluent in Excel, you will wash out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A truly great professor
Dr. Gimpel was great! He genuinely cared about the students and helped out whenever we were needed. I would definitely take him again, as his lectures were engaging and he made the class really fun.
Extremely subjective grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: I don't know what the other person is talking about, Prof. Gimpel is one of the most down to earth Professors I have had. He lectures primarily using the chalkboard. The assignments are mostly based on the reading, which I think makes many students upset because it can't be done quickly the night before it is due. I now view elections differently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had. He writes random things on board and has no organization & seems to make up facts when teaching. He's offensive & says things like rape culture is not real. He uses a 3 hours class to show us what politico is and then makes us scroll through fb pages/ask us about tinder. I learned nothing about elections. DON'T TAKE

Dr. Mark was absolutely wonderful! 1000/10 recommend him. Course follows a textbook, but he made it clear if you come to lecture, take good notes, and study them, you'll be fine on all the exams. Text helps as a secondary source. Exams are very fair, he'll tell you what's on it. Take lecture notes and you'll be fine. And he's such a chill guy.

Prof. Mark is amazing! Business law is generally a hard class but he makes it a lot more easier to understand and is great at using real world examples. I definitely recommend this class if you are planning on taking B-law.

I love this man. He's so funny and makes boring lectures kinda fun with his insane pop culture knowledge. Attendance isn't mandatory but I recommend because there's a lot of info on the exams. Doesn't use slides but explains things slowly and with details and will gladly repeat if asked. First of three exams is the hardest so don't be discouraged.

Professor Mark is a really nice teacher. His lectures are very well put together and easy to follow. He stays within the textbook so it's easy to follow and understand. His exams also truly reflect the contents of the exam. Would definitely take his class again and recommend him to others!

I really liked having Professor Gilmore! Class was a light workload, and he cracked a few jokes in lecture which made it more entertaining. He's also very willing to meet with students outside of class to discuss assignments, which I found helpful. Definitely recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Take Gilmore! His class is an easy A. He doesn't care if you skip, he is an easy grader, no exams just a few assignments that are super easy. Take the class if you need an easy A, not if you actually want to learn as he usually skips class and even when he doesn't, his lectures don't have anything to do with the class.

I loved having Professor Gilmore! His lectures were very interesting, and going to class was never boring (when he was teaching - some days were taught by the TA which were no fun). Lots of reading but not always necessary, and a good amount of writing assignments, but I still enjoyed the class. I recommend Prof. Gilmore for law classes!

NO. If you can avoid it, do not take the class. Gives a pop quiz that almost everyone fails. Changes due dates of papers. Posted prompt at 10:00 the night before it was due. Did not grade until the END of semester. Did not grade for content on papers. Confusing lectures: often stopping to say "uh" or "um". Did give extra credit though.

How this woman ever got a degree or a job is beyond me.  Horrific public speaker, blatantly manipulates data to make wrong assertions and prove her points (some of which have some merit, to be fair), makes incredibly ignorant, borderline **** comments in class.  If you never take another piece of advice, take this:  Run, do not walk, away.

TA"S run the class basically. All the professor does is read straight from the lecture (which she posts online by the way, so you don't even have to go to lecture). Her teaching skills are kind of bad (constantly says ummm, uhh, umm, uhh every other word). Easy class though. Just about 5 papers , a midterm and final. don't buy books either.
Great TA's. Bad professor for lecture.
Very hard to follow during lecture. TA's are usually great but professor is terrible.
terrible communication skills during the lecture!

Professor Peter is great, genuinely a kind person and wants you to do well. Usually an easy grader as long as you put in effort, which you'll want to do anyway just because he's so nice. Easygoing and understanding guy

This man is the bomb diggity. He is so chill the polar ice caps seem like Hawaii in comparison. Professor Peter is a generous grader and barely gave us homework. My favorite thing about him was that he would correct and explain the mistakes in our writing. He also drew smiley faces. Just study from the in-class picture assignments for the tests.
Prof Peter is super relaxed and helpful. His classes are always very chill and he makes sure to always answer questions. He is a great professor!

Professor glass is very very old and frankly seems like he has a hard time keeping up with class. He fell asleep in a class early on in the semester and is a pretty harsh grader despite the fact that there are only three grades in the whole class (two essays and participation

The class is not difficult but this professor don't care bout his students, I got a D- in an amazing essay just because I included a title with a word and the professor don't liked it. I dropped the class. Professor really dont' care about the students.

Dr. Glass is a cool guy who has both eloquence and intelligence. At first, lectures were concise, helpful, and analysing the assigned readings (Plato, Machiavelli, etc.). However, mid-way he began to go off-topic and talk about US politics and Trump for 50 minutes straight. 3 papers and 3 pop quizzes (lowest quiz grade dropped) make your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Glass is quite radical but interesting. That said, the lectures are long, boring, and don't help. Grade is based on three papers and nothing else. Not hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Glass was fine. His lectures could get a little side tracked and werent always helpful for the assignments. Grades are based on only 3 essays Tas really make or break your grade. They claimed they would round you up if you were borderline and went to discussion but then tell you after it has to be an 89.5 or above.

This class was so hard to sit through. He made 50 minute lectures feel like 2 hours long. He's a nice and knowledgable dude but he's super boring and hard to pay attention to. He sits in front of the class and just talks. No slides, no writing, nothing. The class is graded by 3 papers that the TA's grade.

Really boring guy. Don't have to go to lecture but the discussion is mandatory. TAs do everything and mine was a tough grader. Quite a few readings but you can get along by googling what the philosophers believed and argued.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a one of a kind guy. So experienced and smart. He tells stories about himself if you go to lecture and I really enjoy it. Lectures are not very structured and hard to follow but if you listen he gives a lot of insight. 10/10 personality. Dont need to read tbh

Lectures are not mandatory and I wouldn't recommend going unless your TA sucks. Gives a bunch of readings and I did 20% of them and I still got an A. He is ancient but is really interesting and you can tell he's seen a lot. It's easy to fall asleep in lecture but it doesn't matter because there are only 3 papers and readings are easy to sparknotes
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is SO old but he is SO cute! Very knowledgable! Lectures are not mandatory and you do not need to go to do well as long as you go to discussions.

This class is the easiest A you can imagine. Attendance is non-mandatory so you don't have to show up to class unless you don't understand the readings, but honestly half the readings you can google and/or sparknotes. The class was 3 papers each worth about 30%, and the prompts were given a month before they were due. Didn't show up once, got an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great and thought-provoking lectures. They were like poetry; I felt like I was missing my favorite TV show whenever I had to miss class and I was upset at the end of the year because the season ended. Very intelligent and the concepts taught are extremely important as well.

This class was fantastic. There were no tests just 3 papers. You have to do a lot of reading because the class is based off of 9 books to discuss political theory. If you show up to class and discussion, it is fine. I genuinely thought I would hate this class but Glass and the TA's made it very engaging. I wish I could take it again!!!
I love this man. He is awesome. Thought provoking and throws in his dry humor too.
great professor; smart and funny; loved his lectures

i took his classes all three years of college, winter and summer courses. Abstract thinker yet a realist. He makes you think about the how and why of social behavior. His classes made me think long and hard. He cared about his students and their ideas.
He is an awesome teacher if you can handle and listen to his lectures.

I didn't like his appraoch to teaching.  I'm really interested in gov't/politics and we just talked about movies we watched.  How are we suppose to study?  His instructions were never clear and our study guide was possible essay questions.  He didn't give a lot of feedback on the midterm which made it harder to prepare for the final.

Hes really nice, very passionate about his subject.  Has a lot of personal stories to tell in class which makes the material more interesting.  Use books a lot but they arent textbooks so its easier to get through them.  Awesome TAs! discussion attendance recommended because its not just a review of lecture material, starts there and branches off

I have mixed feelings about Prof Doug. He's super laid-back and funny during class which makes it easier to participate and get to know everyone -- which I really enjoyed. But, his feedback tends to be illegible and vague (e.g., he'll write "vocab" or just put slashes through stuff) which is frustrating if you want to improve your grammar.

The class requires 10-15 hours a week outside of the class for homework and projects. He takes attendance every day & if you miss more than 2 classes he docks participation. His expectations are too high and he gets pissy when we don't live up to them. He gives unreadable feedback and doesn't like to give extra help to anyone. Way too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He threw us into the language with no guidance, gave hours and hours of work, and harshly graded everything. When I asked him why my participation grade was so low despite being one of the most vocal in the class he said he just expected more from me with no reason as to why. All his criticism nearly brought me to tears. Take any other professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Definitely some work, but a nice guy and helpful if you go to office hours. Likes to joke around with his students. Punctuality is really important to him as well. Attendance is mandatory.  Lots of participation, but it helps!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: By far the best Spanish professor I have ever had. I took his class as a Spanish grammar refresher course, so it wasn't hard for me b/c I had already learned the material, but he very invested in helping students when they're confused. He calls on students all the time to read their writing aloud, but it's totally fine if you mess up.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Make sure you participate. Even if its early in the morning, and everyone is tired, he will become angry and frustrated when you don't raise your hand to answer en espanol. Be prepared to be called out if you are late. The tests are moderately difficult, and you will have to do some studying. However, he's funny and amazing at teaching spanish.

Prof. Doug is awesome, he really is there for the student. He make sure you understand and gives great feedback. If you really want to learn Spanish, take it with him. He's very down to earth and really wants every student to succeed. I wish he would have taught my 103 course instead of Daybert Linerez. Definitely recommend him to anyone he's good.

This professor is literally the worst professor I have ever taken in my two years at UMUC. Forgets to grade assignments, very condescending when answering questions and asking questions on the post. Asks questions that are not related to the topic. Ridiculously specific grader. Save yourself the stress and pick any other professor.

Professor Gluick was a very condescending instructor. If you asked a question in the Ask The Professor section he would take forever to answer. And then his answer was very belittling and made you feel really stupid. The test were pretty difficult. You were given 2 hours and it took 2 hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Absolutely the WORST "teacher" I have ever had the displeasure of being forced to work with. AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS! He is vague, unhelpful, and unprofessional. If you ask him a question, he will answer it BUT his answer won't actually address what you truly asked him.

Professor Rahmoeller leads all his classes like Socratic seminars with all of our tables arranged in a circle. He doesn't lecture very much, but goes over the basics of the ethical principles, using his own experiences in making decisions at the FDA. It was a chill class - discuss principles, write 5 short papers. Would definitely recommend.

One of the easiest, most enjoyable classes you'll find at Maryland! You'll learn the basics of ethical theory, and then apply it to biomedical research and case studies. Only four papers (3-4 pages each), a final paper (4-5 pages), a presentation, and some quizzes. No exams. Class is always discussion-based and we had fascinating conversations.

Interesting class. Good professor. He is knowledgeable. Interesting material. There are papers (usually 1-2 pages) due almost weekly whereas there are a few papers (4-5) pages also. There is a presentation and a final paper. So, there is work but the class is interesting and some of the debates/discussions were also interesting. Highly recommend.

I would highly recommend taking this class.  He is very nice, knowledgeable and fair.  The material is interesting, and he is really interested in student input.  Workload is not too bad either-- 1 paper (2-4pgs) each week, 1 research paper and 1 final paper.

He really knows his stuff.  The workload is not bad at all, there is one big research paper for the year and no tests.  I find biomedical stuff to be interesting, so I really like the class.  I think he is a very good professor, fair grader, and very well informed.
Very interesting class, the workload is fair and Rahmoeller is nice and breaks down the class well.

He is the nicest man you will meet. This class requires a pretty heavy workload, but if you put the effort into it, he will give you an A. Course material was really interesting and he makes you interested in it. This man knows his stuff.

If I could give him negative rating, I would. He comes to class unprepared, makes many mistakes without future clarifications, no examples. Therefore, you'll need to read from 3 different sources. Announcements and study guides (if you are lucky) typically come a day before assignment/exam. Good Luck taking his class!!
Textbook was ~$170 but using it is the only way you will pass this course. Lectures were a waste of time; totally confusing teaching style. Nice guy though..?

The book was awful and provided almost no examples on how to do problems. Glaz was worse. He gives assignments that don't look difficult (and likely aren't) but the materials and teacher combined do not give you the tools needed to do well. He posts solutions after hw is handed in, but always incomplete solutions with errors. Do not take his class.

This guy is an aweful professor. He has trouble with the problems that he does in class and leaves the students wondering what happened. If you are going to take Math 220, do not take him. Wyss-Galiffent is the guy to take.

Lectures are incomprehensible. Very hard to follow and he mumbles/chuckles to himself a lot. HW's from the book and tests are fair.  However, don't expect to only learn from the book as the it doesn't cover nearly enough as what is actually taught.

Don't take any class with this professor.  He has no lesson plan, gets the problems wrong as he teaches them, and does not speak clearly, so you cannot hear a single word he says.  If you must take him, then prepare to teach yourself the whole semester.  Avoid him like the plague.

Simply put, a terrible professor. His lectures are extremely confusing, you leave class wondering what just happened. You end up trying to understand everything in discussion or by teaching yourself, which is pretty hard for this class. My only advice would be to take another professor (if possible) or take during summer/winter.
Expect to teach yourself the material. extremely boring. unfair grading
Even with a speaker, he is incomprehensible. His lectures are not coherent. If you want to pass the class, expect to teach yourself everything. He bases most of his exams off of test bank.

Prof. Glaz's lectures are hopeless. He rambles, mumbles, and never finishes a problem.  I went to lecture 3 times, once for each of the 3 exams.  The TA's are always helpful.  The grading is very fair.  I think Glaz may have been thrown into teaching this class.  He seemed completely unprepared.  If he teaches Calc again...DON'T TAKE HIM!

Professor Glaz is THE WORST TEACHER on the Maryland campus. His lecutures are completley incomprehensible, which I attribute to his comple and utter inability to teach! AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS!!!! Honestley, I can't believe this man makes a living as a teacher.
cannot teach. will make you even more confused after leaving the class, learn by the text instead. grading is fair.
No Comments
No Comments

will ramble in the middle of a problem, tell you unrelated advanced facts that have no bearing, and then not finish example when it gets to the informative part. gave a test on material we had not yet convered, yet refused to acknowledge this error.  chuckles endlessly to himself about god knows what. grading is fair though. pray for good textbook.
AMAZING teacher! Could not ask for a more easy going teacher! I strive to take as many classes as I can from Dr. Glenn, he rocks!

He is one of the sweetest professors ever. I was not interested in plant science, but he made it seem better. We went on a fieldtrip which bought the class alive. I would absolutely reccommend him. He really cares about his students. Great professor!
Outstanding Teacher!

I never thought I would be so interested in corn and soybeans. One of the most easygoing men alive. Really knows his stuff, students ask him a lot of questions tangential to the topic, and he is able to give very detailed answers. Tests are simple, just study what went on in lecture. He will do what he can to make sure you succeed, honestly.
KIND
No Comments
THE GREATEST AND EASIEST LAB PROFESSOR EVER!!!!! He is a very chill professor and cracks jokes all the time. You WIll want tot go to his class and he makes learning about grass really interesting.

This is one of the easiest classes I have taken at UMD. Not only does it count for CORE lab science, Prof. Glenn is one of the nicest men I have ever met. He truly wants every student to succeed and does everything he can to keep lectures interesting.

Negotiations was one of my favorite classes I've ever taken. I came in scared because it was a "experimental" course, but I'm so happy I took it. Mrs. Langa Basit know's what she is talking about, and the assignments we do in class are super fun and engaging. Prepare for your negotiation, set a realistic ZOPA and don't go above/below it, easy A.
Avoid her if you can, too much work for such a silly class.

Pros:
- Kind and pleasant
- Uses GroupMe instead of email for class communications

Cons:
- Crazy hard tests
- Asks people for their opinions for all of class, and then when you take the test you can only use the book, so you feel unprepared

I honestly don't know why her ratings are so low, but she was one of the kindest, most engaging professors I've ever had. I went in with low expectations, but she was very funny, accessible outside of class via GroupMe, & she genuinely cares for her students. Try your best to show up to lectures and participate, & start the final paper early!!

Amazing professor, but the quizzes and the final exam were overly difficult, and hardly reflective of course content or the study guide. The in-class negotiations were interesting, and she did a great job teaching the course, but this class seems like it's meant to give you an A-.

Save yourselves, idk what else to say.  No question the biggest waste of time. You'll spend 95% of your time in the week doing work that ends up having to do nothing with the class.  You have a half note sheet for weekly quizzes and they won't even help you.  The quizzes are impossible and the grading criteria is awful, good luck if you take her...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not sure what else to say about this professor besides her being the worst professor in the world.  Her weekly quizzes are so hard and I have a note sheet.  I take good notes and still end up not doing good.  Be prepared to read before AND after the class.  If you want to save yourself from the stress, please do not take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easily the worst professor I have ever had in the business school.  She assigns work before and after class and acts like you aren't taking other classes.  The weekly quizzes are weird, sometimes you do well on it and other times you fail even if you did study.  She assigns readings on readings and it is so hard to balance.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The worst professors I've had in the business school, and impossible to avoid having. Patronizing to students, doesn't let you see what you got wrong on quizzes and punishes you for it, and writes extremely confusing test questions. Have her for 364 and she's equally bad there. In class negotiations could be fun though. Still, avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Really sweet! Class isn't too difficult but it basically all just busywork. I think this class is like that regardless of the professor though
Super nice! Weekly negotiations are easy but the final one is graded harshly. Final essay and a group project due at the end of the semester.

Terrible class, 90% of class time was spent in breakout rooms. Doesnt really teach anything at all, just put people into groups every class. Makes you watch Ted talks and then write about them. Wastes class time to talk about her family and even has her own GroupMe so people dont speak out about how ridiculous and unorganized the class is. 0/10

She's the only reason I didn't drop out, such a genuine professor. She's very accommodating to students, she let me miss class due to my broken router #zoomuniversity and still provided me with all the information I needed. I highly recommend taking her class !

Her class is a lot of fun, and there is a lot of valuable knowledge being reached. She teaches you to have to negotiate and although that does not sound serious. You come to realize how important that is. She is a good professor at UMD.
You have to participate in class and work for a good grade, but the class itself is stimulating. The professor clearly knows her stuff

Considering this class was called "Leadership and Teamwork", she was not effective at connecting the material to real-life leadership successes in business. Her teaching style was too theory-heavy for a practical skills-oriented class. She's clearly knowledgeable, but does not make the material relevant or meaningful.

I took her negotiation class. This course requires huge efforts, lots of in class exercises. But the teacher won't grade you on these. She is unreasonable and just grade you based on her bias and ridiculous reasons. In the end, you will have a ten pages paper and she will give you a very long list of requirements, which is helpless for ur grade.
She is so well organized and engaging. This was a great class. She is one of the better professors I've had at Smith.

He is highly unprofessional. He ignored my emails three times about grading until the department chair intervened. In our meeting, he dismissed my concerns  because he can not explain my score and insult me twice. The experience was disrespectful and made me feel discriminated against.

Professor Golden is unprofessional and refuses to give real feedback on assignments. Do not take this class if you expect to use creativity when improving your oral communication. His retaliatory demeanor does not reflect the values of UMGC.

Jim Golden is not a professor I would recommend to anyone. He is very out of touch and does not respect the struggles of students. He is passive aggressive and rude at times. The class work is easy, but his grading is inconsistent and he is bias towards personal feelings towards students. Good luck ever reaching him outside of class.

Professor Golden is rude and his sense of humor is not for everyone. He teases and sort of picks on students and often rambles on about life instead of focusing on the lecture. His grading is hard to gauge and if you're thinking about contacting him to review a grade you can expect a rude, passive-aggressive response, non-helpful response.

Overall, what Professor Golden looks for most is effort. I am not someone who is enthused about presentational speaking, but he saw that I tried to give somewhat effective speeches and I ended the class with an A. He can be kind of intimidating in that he likes to tease and have "gotcha" moments, but if you play along he isn't a huge bother.

This class was easy. But I did not enjoy the professor. He is so hard to contact. Multiple emails just to ask a question, sometimes doesn't answer at all. You literally have to hunt him down. Messes up your grade often and takes forever to fix it. Sometimes rude. Overall, knowledgeable but horrible to interact with. Warning, take someone else.
Took a long time to give grades and feedback, but would give extensions if the class asked. The syllabus was just a guideline.

Super easy class, but this guy... Not sure if it's because stuff is online this semester but he's very hard to get in contact with, took forever to grade, and posted assignments last minute. Class wasn't hard, just frustrating. Nice guy, but if you can, take a different teacher or wait until you're in-person.
By far my favorite teacher at Maryland. He is truly there to help his students and inspire them to make a difference. Amazing teacher overall

Prof. Golden is one of the nicest teachers I have ever had. He is so genuine and truly cares about each of his students. Throughout the whole semester, he was encouraging and took time to get to know his students. He is a great man and an even better teacher. You will leave the class with such great experience and knowledge.

Golden is hilarious. His grading is fair - just stay within the time limits. However, he isn't always specific on where points were lost. Classes were much more entertaining and engaging than I thought they would be. As long as you're prepared and come to class ready to participate, this class is a breeze. Would definitely recommend him.

Jim Golden is a great professor for COMM107. He kept everyone engaged, and the class was very entertaining. He can be a tough grader, but as long as you come to every class and BE PREPARED for presentations. If you put effort into the class you can snag an A , and you might actually leave with more confidence in yourself.

Professor Golden is a great choice. I learned a lot in his class, and if you follow his grading criteria and show up to class it should be an easy A. Professor Golden is funny and a really caring person. 100% would take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Jim Golden is a great communications professor. He is always willing to help out any student who asks for it because he wants his students to succeed. I would recommend anyone who wants to take communications at UMD to take him.

I loved COMM with Professor Golden. He goes on tangents often and gives motivational speeches instead of teaching which I enjoyed. However, he is also very experienced in the communication field and gives good pointers. He genuinely cares for his students just don't get on his bad side. Show up to class, prepare for speeches, and you'll do fine.

Professor Golden is one of the most personable teachers you will find at this school. Makes you work hard for your grade but is always so positive and passionate about his job that it helps his students to thrive.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Professor Gowin was a great professor. Gives very clear instructions and provides tailored, constructive feedback to improve. Do your work and follow the rubrics; and you will get an A. I personally saw myself improve my speech by the end of the class.

Professor Gowin is an active and engaged professor! She's a tough grader on the speeches, but she gives constructive feedback on how to improve. She was very responsive via email. She values discussion participation.

I was skeptical about an online speech class, but it was actually very helpful. Prof. Gowin gives great feedback, constructive criticism and has clear expectations. She points out where you need improvement AND what you're doing well on. Weekly discussions and readings were easy. Quizzes were easy if you read the course content. Highly recommend!

The class itself kinda feels like a joke. Gowin didn't really teach much and more graded our speeches and told stories. She grades really easy as I got an A on every speech even if it wasn't my best. She is a really nice person and have no complains about her or the class.

Prof. Gowin is a nice person and means well. But her class is not interesting and very little is taught to help you become a better public speaker, she mainly explains each book chapter, you are supposed to read before class and you take weekly quizzes about them. Also shes a VERY harsh speech grader & attendance counts towards your grade

Professor Gowin is a decent teacher. For all of the assignments, she puts up very detailed rubrics so you know exactly what to include. In terms of speeches, she is a relatively tough grader, and takes off 3 points for every 10 seconds over or under the time it was supposed to be. She tells you to read the textbook, but you don't really have to.
Great Teacher. Really enjoyed the online speech class. syllabus was very clear and grading was very reasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: SHE IS TERRIBLE!!!! She is super rude and is a terrible professor. Her guidelines are terrible and when you ask her a question, she totally attacks you. She attacked my character at one point. I wish the Comm department would realize how terrible she is to students and stop letting her teach this class because it's not fair for anyone!!
Easy class, helpful teacher. Good instructions. I enjoyed her positive feedback and projects. I recommend her.

She is the worst instructor ever... There are only 3 class meetings and one assignment to turn in at the end of the semester.. She does everything by email and classes are pointless and you graded by whether you came or not, not by the contents of your work.

SHE IS HORRIBLE!!! I mean she really needs to learn to be more clear in her instruction and when she asks students to do work. She e-mails you a syllubus and cant be reached for help, then she fails you because of her errors.

Extremely nice and great professor, best math instructor I've ever had.
Would recommend taking, I'm really looking forward to take Gruber again for 140 next semester.

Professor Gruber is a really caring professor, and you can tell from the first day alone. He accommodates so much so to balance and make it so that all students can learn and be prepared as much as possible. The TAs are also great resources when he personally isn't around to help. Records his lectures so that people who miss class can catch up.

He is a very good professor, his lectures are very good at explaining concepts, much better than any other class I've had. There isn't that much homework it's really just one or two things to do each week. My only issue is that he has a rule on quiz days where even if you finish early then you can't leave and you have to wait till class is over

Dr.G is the best professor at UMD He is so caring and understanding with his students.The class has biweekly quizzes and gradescopes, all of which are fairly easy. There are only 2 midterms and 1 exam, compared to other teachers who have 3 midterms. I suck at math and managed to get a B in elem calc?? only by the magic of Dr.G was this possible!
GOAT math professor
I loved this class! TAKE HIM!
He teaches very clearly and well, and if you don't understand something he will explain again as many times. He makes everything very clear and is always available to help.

Prof G is the best. Very self critical and will admit when he could've explained better. Goes out of his way to make supplementary videos to help clarify content. Quick email responses, and extremely forgiving course structure/partial credit. Quizzes help pad your grade so exams are less stressful. Don't be afraid to ask for help!
bests professor I have ever taken. 100% would take his class again. Very respectable and always made time to help his students.

Honestly one of the best professors I've had this semester! His class is very straightforward and the exams were pretty easy if you studied. He's so patient and offers so much help to students who struggle with the material. He just wants you to do well! Thank you Mr. G!
The most caring, kind and helpful professor! So incredibly helpful and sets very clear criteria for the course. So happy I took his class.
Omg Mr G is the best. Im so bad at math but he offers so many opportunities for extra help and office hours. He really just wants to see everyone succeed.

Sean Gruber, otherwise known as Mr. Grubs, is quite the jokester. As a University of Maryland Alum, he knows the cirriculum like the back of his hand. Through his love of patty paper, classical music, and geogebra, he covers all important aspects of geometry. I highly recommend taking this class with Mr. Grubs.

Mr. G is great! He is very personable and really cares that you understand. There are only two short homework assignments per week so it is really manageable and you can get extra credit for asking questions about the homework in class (board points). The class is really easy and he posts what you need from the book so no need to purchase.

Mr.G is very friendly and makes it a point to get to know all of his students. He gives good feedback as well as partial credit on exams which is very helpful. He is open to give extra help to students who feel they need it. He gives a lot of resources that can help you study. Class is fair but can be difficult if you dont understand whats going on
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: His course focused on history. The readings we had mostly focused on John le Carre and Graham Greene. This is my first class but he seemed chill. I guess this will be a nice course.
