reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Greene is an amazing professor. He really cares about his students' success, not grades. He will give extra time on exams for everyone, and he clearly tells you what will be on each exam. By the end, you will have a deep and conceptual understanding of all the concepts. He also has many cool in person demos.

Professor Greene is my favorite teacher at UMD so far! He makes classes fun & engaging & does a lot of cool demos. He's caring and wants to see his students learn and improve at physics. He's kind, intelligent, & funny. He's always willing to help you as long as you are willing to ask questions, and he explains topics in an easy-to-understand way.

PHYS272(H) had a flipped classroom approach (watching assigned lectures) which allows you plenty of time to go back and take notes and digest things at your own pace. The synchronous lectures were an opportunity to go in depth which I found really cemented the understanding of the concepts. Questions are answered clearly and quickly.

Professor Greene is an amazing professor. His class, while difficult, was one of my favorites I have ever taken--in large part due to his personality and teaching style. He is funny, nice, and extremely knowledgeable. I highly recommend him if you get the chance to have him as a prof!

Professor Greene is an excellent professor, dedicated to ensuring we understood key concepts. For a course during the pandemic, he still gives lots of information, and more group collaboration than what Ive seen in other classes, which was quite helpful. He is happy to clarify tests and problems in office hours, or chat about science!
Richard Greene is an excellent professor. He made sure that all his students were doing well, while also maintaining a manageable course load and an approachable demeanor.

Professor Greene is one of my favorite professor I've had in University. He is direct with the content he is teaching and simplifies everything. He is funny, easy to talk too, and a nice person in general. He is also a well known name in his field and has a lot wisdom. Fast e-mail response and will talk you up about anything. Highly recommended.

I am so glad that I enrolled in Professor Greenes class. He was able to impart his knowledge of the subject matter in an understandable and enjoyable way. His lectures are great and filled with important and engaging materials as well as fun experiments and jokes.
Great professor, explains things well and keeps class interesting.

Prof. Greene's classes are not very lecture heavy and are formulated around doing the homework. His course consists of two lectures and one discussion per week, and two to three pages worth of homework due per week. His lectures give a more general outline and sometimes are filled with fun experiments and history lessons. overall a great course!

Dr. Greene is a great professor and very knowledgeable about his subjects. He makes going to class fun. Due to the nature of physics, his classes can be hard for many but he's fair with his grading and if you put in the effort, do the homework, go to office hours you can earn an A.

Prof. Greene is an amazing professor. He is a really funny person and makes class really enjoyable due to his great personality. I feel like I learned a lot during his class. As he tells everyone at the beginning, he gives a lot of homework, but honestly it makes it way easier to understand the material and succeed in the class.

Dr. Greene was a fantastic professor! I learned a lot and it was a very fun class I looked forward to basically every week. I highly recommend taking his class (be aware that PHYS272 isn't easy with anyone, but he certainly helps.)

I like Dr. Greene. He's approachable and funny, and very very smart. His lectures aren't that great though. The material he goes through in the lectures is way easier than the homework and the tests, so honestly you could skip class and just study hard and be fine. He gave a huge curve at the end, and his TA Nick is the best. I recommend his class.

Professor Greene is a funny experimental professor. He brought us surprised experiments. He had a small brake in the middle of his 1.5 hour lecture, which was really useful. It is true to say that the course material is hard. However, he considered the materials for students. If you study hard with the textbook, B is not very hard to achieve.

Tough course for those with no prior experience. When he says the best way to learn physics is by doing problems... DO THE PROBLEMS. I always heard this before and almost learned the hard way; I can't stress it enough. Using solutions manuals to check is fine but if you don't do the problems yourself with full effort, you will fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class is not difficult by any means, however Dr. Greene is not an effective or considerate instructor. He is incredibly harsh and can never be approached with a question without giving overly harsh criticism. He sat on his phone every class period. Easy A but choose a different professor.

PHYS174 lab isn't set up for lectures, so without some previous knowledge it would have been hard. Even so, some concepts still was challenging, but Dr. Greene will gladly help in or out of class. He is entertaining and generally concerned for the success of his students. He responds to emails promptly. He is one of the better professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The lectures are outdated, recycled videos of hers that can be found on YouTube. The textbook for the class is written by her, expensive for the content as it is a transcript of the lectures. 1 point assignments except for the heavily weighted final. She seems more interested in research, which she's good at, but uninterested in teaching.

The grading for this class takes FOREVERRRRRR, there are tons of students in this class (60+) and only one TA so expect multiple weeks for something to be graded. Every single assignment is based off two templates that you have to use to submit an assignment, the worst part is the assignment itself is extremely annoying to fit on the template.
No zooms or actual lecture videos. One of the assignments is to get 10,000 likes on either your first or second post, and you can only get an A on it if you do.
Class is nothing but propaganda
Outdated content and unprofessional professor

Overall, the course was a bit outdated in terms of tutorials and videos. Her lectures are from 2019, and yes they're good but outdated. You'll have to seek tutorials on softwares on youtube instead of the ones she has posted. If you're taking it during the summer, it's fast paced and some of the assignments are a bit vague.

Professor Golbeck is a good professor, she posts weekly lecture videos each week pertaining to the module topic that comes with a weekly quiz. Most of the homework will either be a Analysis or Visualization. The class overall wasn't that hard but I feel like the TAs graded assignments very harshly for someone that is just learning visualization.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She is extremely intelligent and well respected in her field. This class was a moderate amount of work but really nothing crazy. She doesnt assign any busy work for the most part. You dont need a super solid grasp of the material to get an A. Overall a good person who listens to her students needs.

Shes very arrogant and gives pointlessly difficult assignments for a 100 level class. For example, she expected all her students to get 10k likes on a social media platform and made that due the same day as a 100 point midterm paper that was pages long. Save yourself and do not take this class.
TOO MUCH WORK FOR 100 LEVEL CLASS, SHE IS VERY RUDE
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very good instructor. Enrolled in her info studies class on becoming a social media influencer and a lot of the information she had to provide was very insightful and useful. Will have an assignment every week -- a few projects throughout the course. She provides good feedback and is accessible if needed. Nothing too difficult. This course is fun.

One of the worst professors I've ever had. Not only is she not helpful when you are confused about an assignment but also she complains about her students on her public twitter account. If anything don't take from her, she's miserable and she'll take her misery out on you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Golbeck is very clearly highly-regarded in her field, and she does a great job! She keeps lectures concise and clear. I put in less than an hour each week. For the midterm/final it took a long day of writing, but that was it for the semester! Professor G is fair and clear, not sure how anyone is complaining! Easy A.

This class was unreasonably difficult for a 100 level Gen Ed class. Golbeck was almost never accessible through email, and when she was, she was needlessly rude. Gephi projects were very vague and confusing, with one 1500 word paper and also getting 10K interactions on social media for a full grade!! Don't expect regrades from TAs either. Avoid.

I should have made this review when I took this class a while back. A shame cause she seemed like she would be a good and also nice teacher at first, before the semester and at the start, for at least a while, but that ended up being really false, not true at all. Always goes way too overboard on her monthly to daily commitments so does none right!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: INST155 is certainly different than its description, but it's not a difficult class. The basis of the class is around social network analysis and using a software named Gephi. If you are unsure about this class, look up Gephi and what it's about. I didn't love Gephi, but this class is still an easy A for someone who at least puts in some effort.

INST155 is not like the class listing at all, nothing like the listing. Golbeck doesn't answer promptly to emails/questions and wants you to buy her own Textbook (on libgen). This class is graded harshly for no reason, and has so much work for a 100 level course. I would have never taken this course as I thought it was an easy A which it isn't.

She is one of the worst professors I have had. This class was online, and she replied to emails but was very rude and never clear about assignments. All grading is done by the TAs, and if you have an issue they don't help to change it. There aren't too many assignments but they make no sense and for an elective it is a terrible class.
Sooooo overrated.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I think the main problem is that there are so many assignments and only 1 TA. My class had around 93 people and only one TA. This means our assignments took forever to get graded. Another issue is that some of the assignments had very unclear grading criteria. The class was hard per se but the overworked TA and unclear grading criteria were rough.

Good for programming especially if you struggle in that field. Super genuine person and amazing at explaining material. It is nice to have a professor who actually understands students and tries their best to work with them. Definitely a great professor at UMD.
By far the best lecturer at UMD Engineering/CS program. Very engaging and easy to learn from.

Amount of hw is very fair for online class. Email her if you have any questions. I would say if you follow her instructions you will easily get A. Try to submit work on time. She is one of the best professors in UMD you should take class.

Professor. Jen is the best!! I have learned a lot of introduction of Information system. Grade is very fair for me. She's fair. If you have any questions email her, she would response and help you out. Late work accepted and this is the one I like her. She's very kind and nice. You should take her class !!! You will proud to be her students.

Never interact with her but she seems like a person who understands students' struggles. She extends deadline if you ask her early. This class is not too bad except for the propagation project where you have to get 10K interactions (otherwise you will lose points). Not too stressful as gen-ed and the midterm and final are papers if you like writing
Decent teacher but a bit of a narcissist. If you can look past that then all is well.
I wish I could take all my classes with her.  What a great teacher!

reviews.comment: Wonderful, helpful and always cheery. Makes being in class entertaining, useful, and educational.
She always puts the students needs first.

What a fantastic professor. The readings may have been long and overwhelming, but as long as you did the few assignments that she asks and made some impression on her as a student, you will not only learn something, but come out with an easy A in the class. She truly cares about her students.
Professor Golbeck's professionalism and dedication to her student's success make her an asset to any academic institution.
Professor Goldbeck was really supportive and helpful when we had questions.

WONDERFUL professor! She really knows the material well and wants you to learn it. Always available for email with questions if you dont understand something and makes the class really educational without boring you for a second. I really recommend her class, even if its late at night, very worth it!
VERY GOOD COURSE.  She is very helpful and taking any course like this is a way to improve the resume easily.
Jen is a very good teacher in an interesing class. She is very helpful and always responds quickly to email. If you are someone who wants to take an introductory course, I highly recommend her.
He explains nothing, uses weird notation, I literally couldn't tell which topics he was even trying to teach. Tests are okay, but only 2 midterms, 4 long questions each.

reviews.comment: Lecture gets boring because he just reads off of his screen so its kind of hard to pay attention. I wish he works on a problem and writes it down so the class would be engaging. Hes a nice guy. He accepted my quiz late because of a technical issue. Some professors wouldnt but he did. He replies to emails fast and answers questions clearly.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a decent lecturer but includes a lot of engineering and physics concepts that don't appear on the exam. He does answer questions clearly so don't be shy to ask during lectures. There are very few assignments so exams are a pretty big part of your grade, highly suggest dedicating a lot of time doing his recommended practice problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Honestly I stopped going to lectures after going for the first 2/3 of the semester was absolutely useless. His lecturing is so god awful and overly conceptual and he had no logical ordering in how he taught at all. The curve was huge but it's needed when the teacher teaches nothing. Just take MATH240 if you can

Has a very nice grading scale and gave a lot of extra credit, but he's just such a horrible lecturer that I can't recommend this class to anyone else. Exams were unpredictable and overly conceptual (though he did take it a bit easy on us on the final). Not sure how he gets such good reviews for other classes but do NOT take him for linalg
He does care about his students and hopes for everybody to pass, he has a fair grading scale although a little bit boring when it comes to lecturing. But a good teacher still.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Would take again

reviews.comment: his lecture is clear and i found it helpful for understand the textbook,especially when it comes to harder chapters (he gives the detail that the textbook skips and the textbook skips a lot ). He gives massive curve and easy exams when the average is low. fyi 410 is the kind of class u have to read and practice a lot by yourself .

He is a good professor and grades very leniently  (you shouldn't get below a C). At the end of the semester, I honestly felt like I didn't learn much. Maybe cause his style is confusing and he would write a lot of stuff on the board not related to material. I'd still take him again. I thought he was nice and fair. Really nice handwriting too.

Dr. Grillakis makes the course material very clear and easy to understand. His exams were easy and very straightforward, as were the MatLab assignments. You can tell he is passionate about this subject as he likes to explain other things (physics related) just for fun. Show up early and sit toward the front, he is quiet and begins 5-10 min early.
He is very clear about his grading criteria. exams are similar to practice exams and not very hard. there are 5 matlab projects which are easy and short.

His lectures are almost pointless to go to because he only talks about how equations are derived. If you are interested in learning that type kind of stuff, then take him. Either way, his tests are the easiest of all the teachers, and he is a nice guy.

Professor Grillakis is a good professor. Most of the exam problems follow homework problems but its good to go to lecture because he adds problems in which one will have to respond yes or no and why. Most of those problems are based on lecture content. Other than that he has a good grading scale, 86 is an A-. He is very calm, patient and exotic.
Dr. Grillakis is fairly quiet and mild-mannered, so don't expect to be entertained by his lectures. But his tests are easy and his instruction is pretty clear, with lots of examples and explanation.

We had to download files for the matlab project, but the links didn't work. When I emailed him asking about it he simply replied 'There is matlab tutoring available' completely ignoring my question and being useless.

He's a nice guy but has the world's thickest accent so no one can understand him. His microphone hardly ever works and he talks to the chalkboard the whole 50 minutes so even if you can understand him, chances are you won't be able to hear him. I loved calc 1 and 2 and now I dread going to class. The only grades are 4 exams and 4 mat labs.

Not particularly interesting, but he is a fair grader. Make sure you do the practice problems he hands out. Superior to many math professors I had at UMD. His syllabus was pretty balanced and I didn't feel like the class went to fast.
This guy is **** 24/7 - basically the coolest prof in the world- easy grader too.

Math410 is seriously overrated in terms of difficulty, especially if you take it with Grillakis.  If you're taking it, you're a math major, and if you understand calculus and how to write a proof (which you learn from reading the book), then no issue.  Do the homeworks, read the book, ace the tests, and you'll be fine.

Pretty good teacher. His lectures are clear, and presents proofs differently than textbook which is helpful. Homework was weighted heavily in the class, and he was willing to help in office hours. Exams were difficult but possible if you understand the homework. He had a large curve in my class.

Helpful professor and really a kind person. His lectures are straightforward though rather boring. Most of the time, you're better off practicing problems from the book. Tests are fine with a few days of prepation. No homework or quizzes so you have to be self-motivated to keep up with the material.
really hard...i thought i was gonna fail or get at most a C.  i somehow ended up getting an A.  he must 've curved it like CRAZY

He's extremely approachable outside of class and will answer questions to the level of his students.  That being said, if no questions are asked he will continue as if you understand the material perfectly (even when the proofs are difficult).  Make sure to visit his office hours and you'll be fine.
Extremely theoretical, unclear and skips many steps.

Knows his stuff. Best Calc Prof in the world. Still finds it difficult to teach. skips steps and often loose track. very Hard to understand. He canbe helpfull. Exams only 3/4 questions, very hard. Go to lectures/ do suggested problems in the book. Go to Math tutoring room/ or TA hours.it helps alot.
No Comments

Professor Gray is incredibly kind and clear about her expectations! She clearly cares a lot about this course. That being said, the quantity of reading and the intensity with which she grades are way too much when compared to the content's lack of depth. This class has taken up a lot of my time and I've learned very little.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This class is a waste of my time. She is unwilling to entertain opinions that differ from hers.

Extremely picky/harsh grader. Randomly made her class a 94% for an A despite it being an upper-level course. About half of your course grade is based on a group project that the highest scores in the class will be B+'s or A-'s on. I'd definitely avoid this teacher. Also a ton of reading/busywork homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Steer clear of this one. She will warn you that there is a lot of reading. What she doesn't tell you is that 40% of your grade is based on a semester-long project. In that project, she will look for minor things to make sure you don't get an A. Doesn't give back major graded assignments until the end of the semester.

HW isn't hard, just watching videos & discussion posts of your thoughts. Jenkins really listens to everyone's ideas, you get a long grace period for overdue work, and she is enthusiastic & knowledgeable! Very picky and kind of intense about behavior in class (talking, texting, etc) but is very sweet otherwise. 100% recommend if you like the topic.

Textbook is used. Jenkins is very big on participation and attendance. She wants everyone to participate and share. Lectures can be boring. As part of a required text, she makes you buy a tv series on amazon. Shows are 45m long. This class was blended learning. It was okay, discussion questions were often annoying to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors. The blended learning lecture felt more of a facilitated discussion at times, making it interesting and immersive. The material was genuinely interesting and the movie assignments were fun to watch. Make sure to participate in class and study for the two exams to do well in the course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Jenkins is a great lecturer who cares deeply about what she's teaching. She wants her students to do well and is easily accessible for questions. Participation in class counts and watching videos, and writing discussion posts are a large part of the class. Her no phone rule may be annoying, but it forces you to actually pay attention.

Prof. Jenkins is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She is so in love with what she teaches us, and it makes all the students attentive, even the ones taking the class just for Gen Ed credit. She is spectacular! Oh and, do NOT under any circumstances take out your phone! She will see and call you out!

Easy to contact outside class and responds fast. This class consists of watching videos, answering discussion questions, skimming the book and talking about answers from the book in class. Lecture is a little boring since it just covers the readings, but I wouldn't say you have to go other than participation. Midterm and final worth 70% of grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had. Fair grader and is so encouraging and kind. I wish I could've had him for my other writing classes.

Very wholesome and kind professor. He is so lenient on due dates and assignments that the students take advantage of his kindness. He's very well learned and gives great feedback, also. Please, do not take advantage of his man. He is a national treasure.

Professor Gulli is great. Very understanding and he has a way of explaining things well and making them much more clear and understandable. If you should ever need him to explain more, he is happy to do so and very helpful. I feel like with every discussion post response, I learned something. He was great and I highly recommend.

Take him! Professor Gulli is an awesome professor who genuinely cares about his students and is always willing to help them. He responds quickly when you email him and grades essays fairly. Assignments are very straightforward, just make sure to read the materials he provided. I really enjoyed the course. Definitely recommend.

Professor Gulli was hands down one of the best professors I have taken to date. He is extremely caring and helpful to his students and gives an incredible amount of feedback on everything. If you show up to class and participate in all discussions and assignments you will pass this class very easily. I highly recommend taking this professor!

I wish more professors were like Dr. Gulli. He's educated and is an expert, but he is not condescending, which is awesome! Do your work, show interest, and you should be ok. Dr. Gulli corrects you while explaining what you did wrong. If you get a chance, take his class, you will not regret it and you'll learn from him, too!

Professor Gulli is a so great professor. He gives the students so much respect and recognition, his goal is not just to focus on the completion of homework, he cares about the knowledge that whether we actually learn something, and also give us more flexible time to submit the homework to help us understand the knowledge that he taught.

Professor Gulli is a great professor. This is literally the easiest class you can take through all of college. 100% recommend taking him as he makes the class interesting and fun. Always gives great feedback on assignments and allows big extensions.

5/5 IGNORE PREVIOUS RATING I RATED 4 by accident.I took Professor Gulli for ENG2150 at Baruch College. He is literally one of the best professors I have met. I took the class asynchronously but met online for office hours a few times. The work for the class is so straightforward. A total of 3 papers, literally so easy and he grades really nicely.

I took Professor Gulli for ENG2150 at Baruch College. He is literally one of the best professors I have met. I took the class asynchronously but met online for office hours a few times. The work for the class is so straightforward. A total of 3 papers, literally so easy and he grades really nicely. 100% recommend taking Prof. Gulli.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Fantastic professor. Caring and is flexible with due dates. Doesn't try to dock points for minor reasons on the papers.

One of the best professor I have had so far. I would recommend him to anyone. He is more than willing to help you with the material and to explain further into detail. He is easy to get into contact with. He is very understanding and cares of about his students. You can't go wrong with this professor at all. I promise you won't regret it.

Absolutely amazing! He was one of the best professors I have had in a very long time and I would highly recommend anyone to take his classes. You can tell that he truly cares about student success. He offers extremely extensive, constructive feedback, & provides amazing explanations on the concepts presented in the course. He is a wonderful person!
Amazing Professor. Very caring and wants all of his students to succeed. He will go out of his way to help you improve wherever he can help you, and he responds to e-mails and questions very swiftly.

One of the best professors at UMUC! His willingness to help every student blows my mind. His passion for teaching sets a sturdy foundation for a great learning experience and successful term. Grading; exceptionally fair as he understands/respects our own personal limitations and that we all have busy lives.

Professor Marr is an excellent professor. His lectures are very captivating, and often don't even feel like class because of the real-world examples used, along with the collaborative nature of his classes. There is a wide variety of assignments/responsibilities that make up your grade, so make sure to keep up with them all to ensure you do well.

I have never written a review before so please do not take this lightly. Do not take any class with Gregory Marr. He is disrespectful and degrading when speaking with his students. The bulk of his work is busy work and does not provide any real benefit. His exams are significantly more difficult than other professors'. DO NOT take 364 with him!
Enjoyed every lecture of this class and I would definitely take it again. Professor Marr make the class interesting and you can see that he is passionate about his course in the way he teaches its.

Personally, I wouldn't bother enrolling in a course with this professor. Not only has he been incredibly unprofessional and disrespectful when conversing with students, but he is not accommodating to student's needs. He goes on tangents during the lectures, so nobody actually listens, but you have to go to class otherwise he will tank your grade.

Professor Marr has a very interesting personality which obviously makes class very interesting as well. Even when I would try not to pay attention to the lecture so I could do other classwork, I would still end up getting sucked back into the lecture. It's hard not to pay attention. However, at times he lacks in professionalism.

Professor Marr is an average professor but he makes you buy so many stuff that you only use once and never use them again. The resources he made us buy were not helpful at all it was just a waste of money honestly. He grades staff slowly like he hasn't graded our midterm yet and it has been more than a month since we took that exam.

Gave amazing and interesting lectures, but felt a bit frustrating to work with individually. Lots of assignments and grades, but most are really easy and the exams are open note/book, so as long as you stay on top of everything it's a pretty easy class. He also required us to buy a lot of extra resources for no reason, which I did not appreciate.

Makes you buy a bunch of external tools you will use once instead of just putting everything on elms and saving us money. When you rarely meet synchronously, it is a waste of time that doesn't teach you anything. Grading for small assignments is unclear because he doesn't communicate, and you're on your own so it is easy to lose small points.

So much homework for an online class. He makes it 100 times more difficult by having so many different online platforms being used for one single class. Rarely have synchronous lectures and do not learn when we do.

He is just annoying. Like one of those people you cannot stand. He tries to be cool by playing music nobody cares about. Hod forbid if you try to challenge his logic. He makes you spend money on unnecessary things like journals, games and a discussion platform. Like seriously stay away from his class. Unnecessary assignments and group projects.
