reviews.comment: Professor Hinc was one of the best professor I have had at UMD. She is not a harsh grader and leaves great feedback. The class consist of weekly discussions, four different projects, and 4 different voicethreads. The class wasn't hard overall just got to make sure you do the work early and read the modules other than that this class is a easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Does not bump your grade no matter how close you are, takes off points for absolutely no reason, grade is decided off the first page of your paper. Also does not change grade even if it was incorrectly marked off.

If you need the get your professional writing credit, TAKE THIS TECHNICAL WRITING CLASS WITH DANUTA HINC!!! You learn in her class but she is genuinely the best, dopest professor I have ever had (there a few runner ups) but seriously she is amazing! It's a class I never want to skip because she is so nice & smart & her energy is amazin. UGh do it.

Prof Hinc's class was pretty engaging. She encourages students to participate in discussions and express their opinions. Most of the assignments had flexible deadlines and had a peer graded version before submitting the main assignments. It's a good way to get feedback from other students. There's no final exm but there's a group project at the end
Professor Hinc is very caring and always willing to help. She was always there to answer any questions. I highly recommend her. The course wasn't too challenging or overwhelming for a summer course.
I have learned a lot of useful stuff in her class. She is caring and gives good feedback. I wish she taught other classes. I would take her again.

Class had lots of assignments but many of the smaller ones (such as discussions and other hw) were super easy. One final group project plus 3 assignments. Overall fun class, loved the professor, and loved the class discussions. I was never bored in class! Would take again.
She is the best teacher I have ever had! Take her class.

Mrs. Hinc is one of the nicest professors I ever had. Very understanding of her students, and wants them to pass. She cares about the way you write, and will offer you to rewrite a paper you feel you didn't do well on. Take her class, she's one of the best. Also, you will be able to get use to her sarcasm very easily.

Professor Hinc is not only an amazing english teacher, she is an amazing person as well. She cares for every single one of her students and she provides a ton of extended deadlines if she sees you need it. Her class is by far the most interesting and informative class I have ever taken in my entire life! take her!!!! shes the freaking best .
She is the best; totally interested in her work. She is helpful and she will do whatever it takes to make it work for you. You can revise your papers in her class. Her class is informative and fun.

Professor Hinc runs a class that is a lot of fun to attend and also very informative. This is by far the best elective course I have taken at UMD and I recommend her for any student who needs to take Engl 391.  She is very helpful and assignments are always clearly explained and graded. I would take her again if I could! :)

Hinc is really cool and intelligent. Classes consist of discussing politics/current events en route to teaching rhetoric. Very passionate about writing. She is very close  with her students.Available to help at all times.
Excellent professor. Very helpful, cares about her student. Good writer herself. Highly recommended!
The best teacher I had in four years at UMD (mechanical engineering). Nice, helpful, knowledgeable.
Excellent teacher. Nice person. Cares about her students. Always available to help.
really unclear about what she wants for assignments. nice person, but harsh grader

Be prepared for more readings than a grad class and readings are necessary to do well on exams and assignments. You can never miss class - she gave me 0% on in class assignments I missed because I had covid. Her exams questions are very specific and average grades are in the 70%s, She gives unclear instructions for the paper and will change it.

While Dr. Hitchens is actually a pretty nice person, this class was god awful. The initial content of the class wasn't that bad, is was the exams and grading that screwed me over in the end. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The fast lectures, abundance of information, many readings, harsh grading, specificity of test questions, and more, made me absolutely dread this class. It consisted of getting 3 books with required readings from those and outside sources, 3 exams, unannounced group assignments & a paper. I have never gotten below an A & I expect a B in the class.

Her lectures are super interesting. Her expectations for a 300-level class are ridiculous. Exams are graded harshly, involve application and memorization of small details. The final paper has an insane amount of requirements and is confusing. There are unannounced in-class assignments that are complex and graded harshly. Lectures are too fast

The class subject is interesting but the Professor talks super fast and very quickly goes over material. Tests are theory and application-based and one of the most difficult styles of tests Ive taken. Seriously felt like a grad school class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Does not matter what semester you take this teacher she will always be busy, and something will always come up.  Out of the 15 weeks, II took the class, she was there for 3, and did not start grading assignments until after the semester.  Hyper political as well and makes the entire class about race.  Literally CRT

I took her at Georgia state University Overall she was so nice however she canceled most of our classes we hardly had any classes which really impacted our learning and she was a tuff grader she looked at the smallest details in the essays, and she didn't give extra credits at all .Don't take her if you want to have classes and good grades.

i took this professor at GSU and she was honestly great at giving feedback and holding discussions in class,but it was obvious she has too much on her plate,and often cancels class which negatively impacted my performance in this class along with technical issues that were never resolved. kind of disappointed but she was nice
Great Teacher and very approachable
Kiyanna was honestly my favorite professor that I've ever had. She gives really good, detailed feedback on all papers, and genuinely seems to care about her students.
No tests, just a lot of papers. She is super cool but a somewhat tough grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: Lyra is the BEST. Literally one of the sweetest, most understanding women you may encounter at UMD. Don't get me wrong- ENGL398R is one of the more laid back English classes but still requires a great deal of effort and participation. Lots of area for improvement though and she really wants to see students succeed.

Took her 398R class (don't know why the website put 293 instead). Great teacher who gives reasonable assignments. Prepare to complete a group project- there's no way you can slack off on it, because there are individual evaluations and lots of editing workshops where other students will look at your group's work. The TA was awesome.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Group projects

reviews.comment: Be prepared for an amazing professor who caters toward the class's learning style and is dedicated to seeing you improve. It's a difficult class but it's also very rewarding. Her blended learning classes were an interesting change of pace and introduced you to the digital media writing world using modern day twitter and websites. English was fun?!

Lyra is an extremely caring professor and does all she can to make the classroom an enjoyable environment for students. The class is group-project heavy, but she takes into account our team reflections and grades fairly. There's a lot of regularly assigned homework, but she's understanding and will often move assignments around to cater to students

Lyra is great! This class meets twice a week, once in person and once online. At first, there is a lot of homework but towards the end there isn't much. Take the small writing assignments seriously because they help with the major ones. I recommend Lyra and I am not a fan of English.

Great class. None of the work is too difficult. If you put effort into the assignments, you will get an A in the class. All of the small assignments she creates will help with writing the major assignments. She is a tough grader but rewards students who are respectful and put forth effort towards making themselves better writers. Take this class!

She is overall ok but not the best. She is and has to be one of your last options. She is a very tough grader and gives confusing homework and assignments that she expect you to understand.  Do not read the previous comments, those were people who actually love English. For those who don't, look the other way, please.

Great professor. Really likable, and very casual. Decent amount of work, a lot of reading, discussion boards, and writing papers, but as long as you do the work you will get an A or B. Easy grader, you can revise papers to easily raise your grade.

Take the class! Ms. Hilliard is an excellent teacher whom I had in 2011. Since then, we have kept in contact as she is always a friendly person to talk to about classes, life, and daily happenings. She proves as a mentor as well as a teacher. As for the class, she tends to play music for the in-class drills, and the work is hard, but so rewarding!

She does a great job explaining what has to be done. She makes an otherwise boring class pretty fun in any way she can. Personally, I've never been partial to taking English classes, but she did a pretty good job making it entertaining. The only downside is the heavy workload, but what do you expect from ENGL101? Otherwise, it was great!

Lyra is a great English teacher. She's really knows all the material. She was very understanding and helpful. She was always willing to help students in anyway possible. The workload for ENGL101 is heavy, but she still made the load lighter.  I would recommend her to everyone. She's a great teacher, but the work she gives is hard.
Had a poor experience with her as a grader. She assigns bad grades to students for completing assignments exactly as described.
Bad communication and the toughest grader on correct assignments.
Grades arbitrarily and takes off points for doing everything correct. No remorse for students or second chances to succeed. Terrible teacher.
Bad teacher who grades based on her mood rather than you own work. Took off many points on an assignment that was completely correct based on examples provided. Stay away from her.

This class was awesome! I encourage everyone to take it as it is actually life-changing in helping you discover more about yourself and the various paths you can take in the future. The assignments are enjoyable to complete, and Christina gives great feedback and likes to see you succeed in the course!

I had Christina for IDEA 101 which is a student seminar class for Carillon. She was really cool and easy to talk to but it was more so the classwork and homework that annoyed me. Not her. The projects and such just got redundant and took up my precious time for other classes. But other than that, the class was very cozy and engaging. Recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class and thought she did an excellent job teaching it. Her rubrics are very clear, and she makes sure you know how to get the points you need ahead of time. Overall, very enjoyable lectures and a fun time if you're into politics or anything of the sort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Engaging lectures but huge lack of instruction for major assignments. She posted past poor student examples to go off of which were never accurate. She avoids answering questions and is a very harsh grader. I spent hours on papers and still received Cs. Very little partial credit and zero clear instructions. I would never take this course again.
Kind but super strict, don't take as a freshman tbh!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Roberts was by far one of my favorite professors at UMD. Her class was pretty interesting and consisted of giving many speeches but she always made them fun and enjoyable. If you just do the work and occasionally speak with her whenever you need help, getting an A is guaranteed.

Professor Roberts is awesome! I took her class for an OC credit, and as a nervous public speaker, I can say that her class was not that bad. Reading materials were posted online for weekly quizzes, and the speaking assignments were appropriate for a 300 level course. If you enjoy topics of national security or want an interesting class, take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: She really helped me improve my public speaking skills and made the class fun. Assignments were fair and speech topics were always interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I don't like her class
A lot of homework but I think her grading criteria was pretty straight forward to obtain an A.

This class was online due to covid and the professor would record and post her lectures. She had discussion posts to make sure you watched but they are only 30 mins. She is always there to help or even look over your writing before you submit it. Each piece of writing has clear directions and a certai outline so make sure you are doing it correctly
she is the perfect English teacher. You will learn a lot in her class. She truly cares about students success. Recommend!
Guidelines for assignments are confusing and the teacher fails to clarify. No feedback from rough drafts from teacher. No clear system for deducting points. Can't even explain it if you ask.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Incredibly passionate about geology and paleontology. Very knowledgeable about topics he teaches. Can seemingly answer any relative question. Doesn't grade on attendance, but there will be a 5 point single question assignment each lecture. Accounts for 8% of total grade. Uploads all lectures online.

The topic of this class is interesting, but lectures are very fast-paced. This class is harder than you would think a class about dinosaur would be. As long as you get your participation points, pay attention in class, and study you will get at least a B.

Dr. Holtz was a fantastic professor! He's really passionate in his lectures, he's super funny, caring, and supportive, and makes the class really fun! Attendance is mandatory, but he records all his lectures and provides lecture notes. Exams are open note. First exam was easy, but the second one was brutal, so make sure to study and you'll do well.

I took Professor Holtz's class purely for fun, and I don't regret it at all. His lectures were always energetic and easy to understand, and he always welcomed questions and comments. Professor Holtz is clearly incredibly knowledgeable about his subject, and I wouldn't recommend anyone else.
I had holtz for geology last year too and he was amazing. Great lecturer and really cares about the topic and teaching it

I took Dinosaurs A Natural History with Dr. Holtz. He is an internationally respected dinosauria paleontologist who is also a great lecturer. He gives extra credit on every assignment to supplement your grade. He has clicker quizzes every lecture to grade attendance and drops five at the end of the semester, so you get five absences for any reason.

He has recently decided to show his true colors as a tenured professor who thinks he can get away with anything. He admitted recently to making an exam incredibly difficult as punishment for his students who he believes aren't taking the course seriously enough. honestly this semester I have just been appalled at his behavior and immaturity. thanks

Do not take this class. Lectures are very unorganized and he goes through material very fast. The course is based on memorization. Lots of quizzes and multiple midterms.The discussions are so pointless and have nothing to due with the actual class. TAs have no idea what they are talking about. Lectures are so boring but necessary to get material

This class was so much work for being a GenEd. You have quizzes every other week, with 3 midterms. There are homework packets weekly and are graded on accuracy and sometimes harder than the quizzes, and are time consuming. Midterms are memorization heavy and cumulative. Lectures are long and boring, discussions are a waste. TAs are incompetent.

Super nice and quirky guy. You can tell he really loves talking about the topics he teaches. A lot of the concepts are really complex, but you aren't expected to understand it fully. Only critique is that his power points can jump around a lot, makes it a little difficult to keep up with.

Great professor and a really fun class! Lectures can be pretty terminology heavy and you are expected to know a lot of features and dinosaur groups, but homeworks/exams are open note, lectures are recorded, and his online lecture notes have a lot of the information if you miss something. Super interesting if you like dinosaurs.

Professor Holtz is a cool and quirky guy who really, really loves dinosaurs. The class is basically all lectures, they're recorded so you don't have to show up to class, and then there are open-note quizzes every Friday. It gets to be a tonnn of information but the open note makes up for it. If you're into dinosaurs, it's a cool easy class to take.

AWESOME PROFESSOR! very passionate about the subject, and genuinely care about students. His lectures are like telling stories, and as long as you attend lectures you will get an A. Awesome class and interesting materials.

holtz is a great lecturer & makes you interested in fossils at 9:30am. The class is a BREEZE. 100% on quizzes from pure deduction alone. The exams require more effort but are just rote memorization. Holtz is rly smart and super engaged with his field, which is refreshing - he goes to all sorts of conferences and is SO passionate about the subject!!

Great prof, take his class!! And for the people saying that you have to memorize sooooo much - like yes, you do you have to memorize everything, but that is the only thing you have to do. It requires no critical thinking and the tests are formatted really easily like matching and fill in the blanks etc. Definitely an easy A if you study

Dr. Holtz is very over rated. His lectures are incredibly boring and he talks through things very quickly. The quizzes every week are NOT easy and attending discussion is a must. Exams are also not easy and require lots and lots of memorization. It is not worth taking just to knock out two gen eds in one class.

Hands down the best lecturer I've had at UMD. For everyone complaining about the amount of memorization required, he warned us to drop the class in the first week if you weren't able to memorize the content.

He's a nice guy, but the class is very hard. A TON of memorization and you need to know your stuff very well to do well. Mandatory discussion sections once a week where you take an annoying quiz. Strongly suggest not taking it if you aren't interested in the subject. Don't take it if you think it's an easy non lab science for gen ed requirements

Dr. Holtz is interesting to listen to and is very passionate about the subject. There are a lot of quizzes and homework but they are very straightforward. Do everything that is assigned and manage your time completing the work and you will do great. Dr. Holtz also essentially created an online textbook so we can save $ and that's definitely a bonus
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Holtz was awesome. The class itself (probably because it's an I-Series) was pretty demanding. There was a ton of busywork that didn't make much sense and a quiz in discussion  every week, but there is no textbook, and he posts detailed lecture notes online. I went to like 5 lectures all semester and still got an A. There's tons of extra credit

Even though this class didn't have a meeting time, Dr. Holtz still kept an open channel of communication with the students and made sure we all always knew what we were doing and what was expected of us.

LOVE Dr. Holtz and this class! There are many opportunities for extra credit on the exams and weekly quizzes. You get to see a lot of cool specimens and samples in the lab. Dr. Holtz is so interesting and passionate, I would definitely take this class again. It is fairly technical though. If you aren't interested in geology, I wouldn't take it.

Dr. Holtz has extremely long essays filled with too much content.  We have quizes every week and 2 homework assignments due each discussion. Not to mention the semester long projects.  He is not understanding about illnesses and told me to write an exam with my non dominate hand because I'd been in a car accident and broken my dominant hand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Holtz is very upbeat and his lectures are very entertaining and enjoyable! We have a decent amount of work and you should spend some time studying  notes/vocab if you want to do well on the quizzes. I also like how he makes an effort to get to know his students.
Holtz is the best prof I have had at UMD! He is hilarious and his lectures are great. Tests and quizzes are easy.

Holtz is the man!--as a man. what i mean about that is his teaching is iffy but he's hilarious and helpful. either way, gives tons of extra credit, easy tests/test grader but a lot of busy work for discussion and a group project. If you need an I-series or something i would recommend since I went to like six classes and still got an A. No textbook

geology 204 is not a hard class but its also not easy. Lectures are long and boring but if you go they definitely help. If you go to lectures and pay attention then you can easily get an A in the class since he offers extra credit on all assignments. If you skip class, you probably wont fail, but it also isn't a guaranteed A. nice guy--bad teacher.

I can't overstate how amazing Dr. Holtz is! His lectures are so entertaining & he makes everything easy to understand. He definitely cares about his students and it is obvious that he is passionate about paleontology. Attendance isn't mandatory but he gives participation grades almost every class. Really funny and nice guy. Would HIGHLY recommend!

Dr. Holtz is an amazing, engaging lecturer with loads of enthusiasm. It amazes me how many people skip lectures, because they really are entertaining... and because all of the class material comes from lectures. If you don't attend class, don't expect to do very well. Highly recommended. You will learn a lot.

This prof is highly overrated! Very disorganized. Arrogant as hell. Disrespects students time. Waits til last minute to provide grading rubrics, etc. Runs over in lecture & posts extra hour lecture online (required watching over spring brk). Dull discussions w 1st grade style busy work. Avoid!!! WILL MAKE YOU HATE PALEONTOLOGY!

I loved this class! Holtz is obviously well-versed in the subject (Dinosaurs and evolution - you really can't go wrong) and seemed to have fun teaching and interacting with the class. There was lots of extra credit, online exams with 5 day time limits (except the in-class final exam), and an abundance of corny jokes. Con: the group project. Ugh.
I've taken two classes with him and they have both been very interesting. You learn a ton and he makes it very easy for you to get a good grade. He knows his stuff and his lectures are great.

This class is hell.Mr. Holtz, although passionate about the class, makes the class torture for the students.Although is isn't difficult to receive a good grade in this class because the tests are online, it is the most tedious class to sit through.He also made us go to DC for the smithsonian museum, which was annoying. Would NOT recommend to ANYONE

Remind me to never take a class with him again... He graded homework way too harshly and was not an interesting teacher.  The guidelines for this class are ridiculous and Holtz is just not a good teacher.  Never again
Best teacher I had this semester, he was really into the material and the projects were a lot of fun and he was really good at teaching.

You'd be a fool to miss out on taking a class with Dr. Holtz.  I had him for GEOL102,GEOL104, GEOL228, GEOL331, GEOL338,CPSP118G, and CPSP218G and would do it all over again.  Dr. Holtz is an extremely dedicated, extremely knowledgeable professor.  Classes may not all be "mandatory", but you'd be at a disadvantage if you didn't attend. Recommended.
VERY engaging, available after class, great teacher. Interesting in his lectures.
GREAT TEACHER.  Very energetic and loves what he does. Beware of his corny jokes though.
It's awesome.
Dr. Holtz is one the most enthusiastic and intelligent professor I have ever had.
Gives fun lectures and is very enthusiastic about them.

Amazing. Simply Amazing. I took GEOL104 (Dinos) and couldn't get enough so came back for another round.  It was a bit boring because of how much I knew but still enjoyable.  Either class is fun but taking both isn't as advisible.
Possibly the most enjoyable class I've taken at College Park was with him.  Always a joy to be around him, although you could easily get by not going to class.

I went into the Earth, Life, and Time program with the sole intent of obtaining an easy A I was not interested whatsoever in the subject matter. While I am still very uninterested I can say that Holtz is a fantastic lecturer and apart from the content I found his lectures both exciting and entertaining. This program is an easy A.

He's really funny in a nerdy way.  Some of his jokes are so lame you can't help but laugh.  His material is straight out of the class notes, but the notes online are more 'barebone' and not quite as thorough.  I enjoy Dinos though so going to class wasn't an issue.  Overall very easy and very enjoyable - I'm taking another Holtz Dino class next sem

This class was very lecture heavy, and attendance was taken every class.  The tests were surprisingly easy as long as you did some light studying.  Half of tests were open note, so taking notes on lectures was important.  All homework assignments were from chapter questions in the textbook, so it is important you have it before the class starts.

Dr. Hunt is a really nice guy and is super passionate about astronomy, but I lost focus during most of the lectures because he tends to ramble. He also assigns a lot of homework, and the exams are not very easy. Be sure to pay attention and stay on top of the homework, and you should do fine.

I would highly recommend Prof. Hunt for ASTR100. He is very passionate about the subject and his lectures are very interesting - I learned so much in this class! Not too much hw, if you pay attention in class you'll do well on the tests. I really enjoyed this class, and Prof. Hunt is very caring.

Professor Hunt is so kind and accommodating. He genuinely wants all of his students to succeed in his class. You can tell how passionate he is about astronomy which made lectures more engaging. He does tend to ramble a bit but it is only because he is so passionate about the topic. If you have to take a lab take ASTR101 because it is so easy!!

He was a fantastic lecturer, and very entertaining. As long as you pay attention the course is very easy. The homework was alright, and the exams weren't difficult as long as you understood the basics.

No way to really track your grade. Grades are not received for weeks if at all making it difficult to fix mistakes for future work. Also slacks on responding to students and makes excuses. First C I've ever gotten. Would not recommend EVER!

Content is interesting, but very difficult. Full understanding of a concept is needed in order to understand the next bc it builds on top of each other. Professor is nice, however her wording of certain concepts is very confusing. Exams are extremely heavy and again, wording is confusing and very tricky. Major assignments also difficult.

This class is full of fairly difficult content, but Dr. Huang's lectures are super engaging, and that makes it worth it. The first unit is the hardest one In my opinion, the class gets significantly better in Unit 2 and 3. She's also very energetic and super friendly. Expect to get cold-called during lecture.

Dr. Huang is truly an amazing teacher. She gives really interesting, upbeat lectures and makes sure that no student is left behind. She is so helpful, and if you ever have a question she is more than happy to help. This class is difficult; however, Dr. Huang makes it so that if you take the initiative, you'll succeed!

Dr. Huang really knows her stuff and is an engaging lecturer. We had three important writing assignments and her exams are really difficult (lots of trick questions). She teaches the material in a way that is meant to be learned comprehensively, so memorizing is not too helpful. She posts study guides and is very open to questions!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she's a super nice lady but not a good professor. i've gotten A's in every HESP class so far, but i'm just not understanding the material she teaches in this class. somehow she makes it more confusing and she words her questions weirdly on exams

she is the worst profess i have ever had. she is not capable of explaining things. she talks in circles and is really smart, but should stick to research because that seems like her passion. her tests are confusing even if you know the material. i dread going to her class she should chose a new profession she is so awful

Prof Huang finds a way to make interesting material really boring. She lets you bring a notecard to every exam, but her exams are pretty hard. Its all application and not really testing if you know the material or not. Not a lot of homework. The textbook is pretty much useless. She also takes forever to give grades back.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Very nice as a person, but DONT take this class. The class is pretty bs and is just a requirement for bmgt majors, but she cares too much. SO MUCH BUSY WORK. If you miss one class, your grade will go down by almost a whole point. The final was ridiculously hard. I had an A+ all semester and participated in every class and got a 74 (average was 69).

Professor Liao is really nice and her lectures are very straightforward. She makes this class absurdly easy and is super fair. The assignments take zero effort and are basically graded on completion. The only things that suck about this class is attendance is mandatory for a participation grade and you have to pay for packback for discussions.

She is very kind and a good professor, but she cares too much about this class. It is really easy material, but she assigns so much busy-work that makes you feel like your time is being wasted. You can't skip any classes or else your grade will drop due to missing the in-class assignments. Her classes also often run late, which is pretty annoying.

Professor Liao takes the class very seriously and isn't flexible with absences: I missed once and my grade dropped over a full percentage point because of it. She is really passionate and nice, but this class is just not the one to care this much about. Lots of group work and concepts you have heard about in other classes. Boring mandatory lectures

Dr. Kwon is kind and passionate, but his lectures make me want to end it all. He cannot explain concepts well or interestingly, is way too self-conscious about keeping students engaged which turns into a negative feedback loop, and has a painful sense of humor. Every lecture was absolutely agonizing. At least the notes were thorough.

He is the most kind and understanding professor I've had so far at UMD. His excel assignments and exams can be somewhat challenging, but he makes sure that everyone does well on them. He is also very funny and so sweet. Attendance is optional, but I think its worth it to attend.

Very caring and nice but it's hard to understand what he's teaching because of his accent/grammar and he talks very fast. He curved the class A LOT because most people didn't understand the concepts. He doesn't explain things very clearly for people with little prior tech knowledge but its only his first semester so take that with a grain of salt

Very caring professor and genuinely wants his students to do well. In my opinion, his accent and occasional grammar slips don't impede understanding at all. Exams and quizzes are open book and open note and he provides additional resources to help with the Excel assignments. Workload is light. Definitely take him!

It was his first semester teaching this course and was very understanding of students. Although he did have a strong accent and not the clearest english, he really really wanted every student to do very well and ensured everyone got at least a B. Tests are online, open book, and he adjusts if the questions were unfair. DEF take him!!!

She is so nice!!! She allows a cheat sheet for the exams, and the exam questions are easy. The calculation questions are similar to those examples that she has taught step by step in class, so sometimes multiple choice questions may be even harder. In a word, TAKE HER!
The goat.

Professor Hyman was by far a great accounting professor. Her lectures are enjoyable and she focuses on creating enjoyment in her classes. She uses Kahoot in every class as a review and has prizes for her students. Usually for class once you completed the end-of-class assignment you could leave early.

Lenient about homework due dates and can get a couple days extension for them. She's a pretty good teacher and is decently thorough in lectures. Office hours are quite helpful too. If you stay on top of your work and put in a good amount of effort, you can definitely get an A.
she will lecture, bring in her dog, isnt a bad professor, the course is just weird and annoying especially the tech assignments and midterm

Incredible teacher and person. She will help you out if you are in a bind and is very understanding. Also just a great lecturer. She has a very good grasp on the material and will make extremely complex ideas as clear as 2+2. Definitely recommend taking her class and getting to know her she's the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really helpful and informative teacher who encourages you to do your best on the work. He's also very understanding when it comes to late work and will usually be accomodating if you miss something.
Great professor, made me more interested in sustainability. The group projects were interesting and even though I didnt know excel much- google and the files he had helped
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Not hard if you get a good group, start projects early, and pay attention to the stuff about excel. Dr. Page gives good feedback, but can seem condescending at times. Definitely take this class if you want to do research, and was actually pretty interesting. You'll get an A , but Page can be a little trying. No tests, only a huge project.

Ian Page thinks he is above everyone in his class and has a lack of respect for his students. While the class is simple for FIRE120 it is essential that you get a good group otherwise you are screwed because you are stuck with them the entire semester and they determine your grade. He moves to quick through the lesson to learn anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: If you decided to do FIRE and you are not a STEM major and do not have a clue on how to use Microsoft Excel, do not take Ian Page's FIRE120 class. He expects a lot from his students and is extremely meticulous.
Ian's a good teacher, but he failed one of my assignments for improperly labeled axes. What a stiffly stifferson!
Ian Rowe is a cool guy. Eh kills rats and doesn't afraid of anything...
Ian is awesome - and good at science too! Be sure to choose his lab if you have the choice. He is very approachable if you have any problems, concerns or just want to chat.

Professor Meftahi is truly passionate about what she teaches and cares a lot about Iranian history. The class is somewhat unorganized because the lectures go in many random directions but she is always in a good mood and eager to teach students. It's an easy class so the un-organization doesn't really matter. Highly recommend taking this course.
Truly caring and passionate.
She is passionate and cares for her students!
Loved this course!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Icaza is very lenient on turning in late work. She is an easy grader, understanding and accessible out of class. Get ready to do loads of homework but as long as you do all of the work you'll pass without a doubt.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took ANTH201 at MC with her and she is a good Professor. She will understand if you have any personal issues and give you time as long as you talk to her. She gives detailed feedback so make sure to explain on your test in detail. She is one of the best Professors I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof Icaza is so compassionate and her class is very straight forward. Lecture/discussions every class that are not boring and do not require much attention. Some easy papers that she breaks down nice and simple. Super sweet, SUPER liberal. She really cares about her students and is super knowledgeable.

Prof Icaza is just not a helpful Prof. she did not make this subject interesting and did not come prepared for class at all. Might as well take her classes distance learning as she makes you do all the readings and learn all the material while she just sits and waits for people to ask questions during class. Final was also not on the class subject.

She is a great professor who tries to make lectures engaging. The workload isn't too much. The papers written are done in groups of around 4. The average lecture consists of answering questions that students have, lectures are heavily based on the previous nights reading. The class is easy as long as you do the work.

She's a wonderful professor who cares a lot about her students. The discussions in class were very engaging and she tries her best to include everyone. Her grading is okay, she can be harsh but there is enough work to save your grades. Overall, she's amazing.

Honestly, bless this woman. I still had to take an Invol. Withdrawal (my fault & covid) but when I started falling behind she was communicative, kind, and understanding. We met on zoom to discuss a plan and she understood the stress of deadlines and anxiety- I literally cried for a moment in relief. I've never had a professor do that.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Her class is the reason I added the anthropology major. Such a sweet professor. Lots of discussion in class. There is a decent amount of reading but it makes the class so much more enjoyable if you read. I would go to office hours just to chat with her. Made my first semester amazing! Would recommend to anyone interested in health.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Tanya is so funny and entertaining, both during lectures and in normal conversation. She makes you work for your grades, her tests are no joke - make sure you read the textbook and lecture notes thoroughly. Her passion for anthropology is apparent and infectious, I learned a lot and would highly recommend despite the challenging tests.

Tanya was the best. Every quiz was online and open note, and were the questions that would be on exams. She is hilarious, and wants to get to know her students on a personal level. Her wit is just like no other. She is sassy and straight forward, so she'll tell you what you need to know but also call out your bs. For exams, KNOW her study guide.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Not only does she genuinely care and want her students to do well but she is always available and willing to answer questions and explain something. She gives enough extra credit that if you don't do too well on the midterm and final you can still get a good grade. Definitely recommend taking her class.

She is funny, nice, and overall extremely helpful if you ask for it. She is honest with her students about needing to actually study. Not an easy A class, but I definitely learned a lot from her. Very in depth and excited about her information.

Icaza is a card. She can be a little too wacky at times, but she's a really nice, interesting person if you talk to her. Only problem I have is with her tests: they're impossible! She'll give an open-ended question but looks for certain information without specifically asking for it. She does give a review of all the topics on the test though.

Do not take her. Grades extremely difficulty. Also normally an A student, but she is just unfair with her grading. You will follow her rubric exactly and she will still take a substantial amount of points off. Plenty of times where I had to have her go back and reread my work so I could get my notes. Lousy instructor. Don't take her.

I really dont like her! I took the class online and she graded quite unfairly on most of my papers! Im normally an A student but i found myself almost getting a D! She grades at a level that i would only expect from a grad student. BEWARE!!!!

Icaza, is amazingly a great professor. At first I felt there was a level of hierarchy but that changed by the 2 or 3 night of class. Her class is an easy A. I highly recommend anyone to take this course with her.

Icaza was an excellent lecturer. She kept content interesting, knew her information and is an cool person to get to know. Attendance for class counts for a participation grade, but the labs are mandatory. I would recommend this class to anyone with minimal background in bio (ie. HS bio)who needs a lab science that touches a lot on social sciences.

Not my favorite professor. Not terrible, but has a tendency to be condescending and self-righteous. She says "ya'll" at an annoyingly frequent rate. These qualities kind of took away from her good ones.
A very rude person who does not care about her class and students. Thinks she is funny and aggressive when people are disinterested in her rude "jokes".

For a one credit course, this class was a lot harder than expected. We have a couple major assignments that you submit THROUGH EMAIL not elms (this was super annoying). She is rude at times and never responds to emails. Shes a tough grader and doesnt really care about this class. Although shes an excellent advisor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Way too much work for a one credit class. Grades absurdly hard for resume's. Doesn't add things to the calendar section of canvas. She's also got an attitude. Do not take her. Very knowledgeable about advising, but that's my only positive comment.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: UNIV100 usually sucks because it's boring and most professors that teach it are strict but Iceney made it fun somehow. She has a booming personality and is very relateable. Being an adviser as well as an instructor, she can answer any questions relating to you as a student and resources around campus. She is here to help always.

I can't believe I'm paying for this class. Ibrahim is basically a no-show for the class and most groups have no clue what's going on. He barely lectures and just uses old videos taught by someone else where you can't even see what's happening in them. Such a frustrating and disappointing experience.

Professor Ibrahim is extremely knowledgeable about systems development and is a very good professor! You do have to put a lot of work into this course to do well, but Professor Ibrahim provides a lot of extremely helpful feedback so good grades are not out of reach. His exams are very fair as well, no curveballs. I highly recommend him!

VERY hilarious and down to earth professor! 403 and 407 are practically group projects, but him and his TA provide as much support as you need to be successful in the class. The group projects are A LOT of work, but as long as you follow what Ibrahim and the TA says, there's no way you should fail the class. Definitely recommend him for any class!

407 is a continuation of 403. You group will make or break your grade. Professor Ibrahim is great because he will work with you to address participation problems. If they arise make sure to address them early because he will help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great guy! Knows his subject matter and presents it in a straight forward way. Most of the info is in his presentations(not just the slides) and he wants students to participate/pay attention ie he calls out students in the back for being on laptops. You work with a group for 2 simulations and presentations of case studies during semester.

Great guy! Knows his subject matter and presents it in a straight forward way. Most of the info is in his presentations(not just the slides) and he wants students to participate/pay attention ie he calls out students in the back for being on laptops. Class has one big group project and 2-3 tests, he's helpful and wants your to succeed.
One of the worst professors I have ever had. Never helps.

One of the best college professors I have had. Very easy going and very helpful. He is very approachable if you have any questions or concerns and he is very knowledgeable about the subjects he teaches. His exams are challenging and you do need to study, but he goes over everything that will be covered beforehand. I highly recommend Dr. Ibrahim
Ibrahim is awesome!  He jokes with students and is very nice.  He is very approachable and reasonable.  He doesn't waste students' time with unecessary assignments/lectures.
he's so nice and funny, his exams were very easy
Very easy-going, appreciates humor and likes to kid around with the students. Exams were succinct, to the point and he goes over questions exactly as they will appear on the exam.
He is a very nice guy, class is not hard, but do study for exams
Dont remember what class it was ... but this professor is really easy going and helpful. I would recommend him.
Had 2 classes with him. One was extremely easy, the other i almost failed. A nice guy, but not a great teacher - not that good explaining things.
No Comments

This was a very interesting class. The class had a textbook that was free online, but I never needed it.  All tests were to write timed essays on your choice of a few given topics from lecture (so notes were pretty important for the class). There was a weekly discussion post, but it usually took less than 30 min to write and was graded very fairly.

Disclaimer: NOT a history major. With that being said, this guy's lectures were mid, he has a habit of saying "and so on" or "stuff like that" etc, right as he starts to talk about an important historic event and moves on to the next topic. As someone who isnt a history major, that was incredibly annoying. Essay prompts always very left leaning.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Decent lectures. Thought provoking assignments. Completely arbitrary grading criteria. There is no clear difference between an 80 and a 95 in this class. Also said "Nobody gets a 100 in my class" 

If you like a professor who is late to every class and reassigns normal work to be due during finals week, take this guy. Otherwise, stay far away.

Smead is a great lecturer. He expounds beyond what you see on his slides; you can tell he is passionate about his job. 2 midterms and 1 final. Exams are taken on Canvas (midterms: in person, final: online). 1 discussion post due every week on Sunday @11:59pm. 1 essay (1750-2000 words) due by end of semester. TAs are extremely slow graders.

Took this course spring 24. Smead îs passionate about history, but I found his lectures to be boring, Tests were online, at home. Discussions led every week by TAs who also did most of the grading. Makes you buy his book for a writing assignment.

Professor Smead is a cool dude. The class is 3 exams, which are 2 essay-based questions. They are all online through Canvas but you have to show up in person so you can sign a paper saying you were there. He posts slides online so you could not show up for any of the lectures and do fine. Overall, a pretty easy class to take care of a Gen Ed.

Dr Smead is a good professor. Attendance isn't mandatory, and he posts all of his lectures online, and he also explains them in more detail in class. The only work you have to do is the discussion due every Sunday, and it isn't required, but taking notes can help you, especially on the tests. The tests were all online and isn't hard if you do notes

Professor Smead is an expert on American history, and provides a perspective that is both critical and honest about this country. He uses a textbook, but honestly as long as you take notes and do the work, you will pass. Very easy class, he can be somewhat disorganized, but is a fair grader and flexible.

Smead is your average history prof. Unfortunately, political bias leaks out into his lectures and it is clear where he stands on various issues. His teaching style is not very engaging but I appreciated the conversational feel. He is not a bad guy by any means but I would not call him a great prof. Make sure you spend time writing your essays.

I had Dr. Smead in Spring 2023. He is hilarious and knows a lot about history. He is an excellent lecturer and the class was amazing and I learned a lot. The midterm and final exams in the class are take-home, which is great. I did however give Dr. Smead a 4 and not a 5 because he makes you buy his book and laptops/phones are not allowed in class.

Smead is a GREAT lecturer with a very pleasant, dry, old man kind of humor. Your weekly hw will depend on what TA you have, but it will always be easy/manageable. There are two midterms and a final, all essays. You're really pressed for time though, I would recommend coming up with a few claims for all the topics you're being tested on beforehand.

Professor Smead is a great lecturer and you will leave his class knowing significantly more information than you knew prior. He's very straight forward with his assignments and even gives you small notes on what you should read up on for the exams. I couldn't recommend him enough
Professor Smead is very knowledgeable, but the lectures are very dry. You have a weekly discussion board, a couple essays, and a few exams. It's not hard but you wanna stay on top of everything.

Dr. Smead is my favorite professor at UMD. If you reach out to him he will go out of his way to help you in any way he can. His lectures are sound like well-narrated stories and were interesting if you pay attention. He really cares about his students and is an overall amazing professor. Exams are online and open note, easy gen-ed too.

I didn't like professor Smead's lecture style at first. He went on a few too many tangents and I felt skipped a lot of interesting aspects of the periods we were learning about. As the semester progressed, his class grew on me a lot. His lectures became like listening to a well narrated history documentary and it was easily my most favorite class.

Prof. Smead is very knowledgeable but his lectures drone on and are very monotone. His lectures are pretty long (40 minutes at least) and they're interesting to listen to if you have all day - if not,watch them at 1.5x-2x speed. Most of my interaction with HIST 201 was with the TA, so I would be more concerned about them, not the professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Smead is a great teacher! Because of the pandemic, everything was online, so it was all self-paced. There were powerpoints along with audio clips of old lectures which helped me better learn the material. The only thing is, I wish he would provide better feedback for essays & discussion posts. He just graded things and left minimal if any comments.

THIS PROFESSOR IS KNOWLEGEABLE BUT HIS ENTIRE COURSE IS BASED ON THREE EXAMS WHICH MEANS IF YOU FAIL ONE EXAM OR GET A LOW GRADE ON ONE EXAM YOUR OVERALL COURSE GRADE WILL BE AFFECTED. HE TEACHES THIS COURSE LIKE IT IS A 200-LEVEL COURSE WHEN THIS IS A 100 LEVEL COURSE ! HIS TRACHHING AND GRADING STYLE WILL RUIN YOUR OVERALL GRADE OR GPA. FTP!!!

Professor Smead is one heck of a history professor. HIST266 pretty much involves explaining US history in it's entirety, and the class itself is very interesting. You're graded on weekly online discussion posts, a few midterms, and a final. Attendance isn't mandatory, but keep in mind it's lecture heavy. Our class ended up taking the tests online.

The class was easy as long as you know your basic history. On the tests, I'd barely study and I'd go into small amounts of depth, noting things Smead talked about in class, and I'd get A's on them all. Discussions are definitely worth going to.
Professor Smead was great. He was entertaining and knowledgeable. Your grade in the class will depend on the TA, and the discussion sections can get a little boring but overall great class.
One of the most knowledgable people I have ever had the pleasure of being taught by. The grade received is dependent upon how your TA grades your stuff, but take this if you like history.

Howard Smead is a very good professor. He makes history interesting and he knows what he's talking about. The class is NOT an easy A. It's one of those classes where it's really easy to get a B but, super tough to get an A. Which TA you get is super important they grade essays which are worth 80% of exam and they decide if you get an A or B.

Dr. Smead is the best! I had a lot of health problems first semester, and he was super caring and accommodating. He is extremely knowledgable and passionate. He assigns a ton of reading, but it isn't required to get a good grade. Some of the texts are long and dry, but if you're invested you can learn a lot.

Terrorism is an amazing class. You only have to do one presentation, one paper, a journal, two papers, and you have to participate. Do another presentation for extra credit, it's worth it. Participate and talk after class to help your grade. If you care at all about the subject, you'll love this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I was so excited to have this professor. He sometimes can go on tangents and has some unorganized powerpoints, but he is very knowledgable and passionate about what he is teaching. He is very approachable and flexible with the class schedule.

Dr. Smead is the GOAT. I would highly recommend taking his class. For someone who's not a fan of history, I had a blast taking his class. You learn A LOT. Nonetheless, It isn't a hard class nor is it easy, but as long as you attend lectures/discussions, you should pass his class with a grade to your likely.

Personally, I found the lectures fairly boring but he posts his slides and attendance isnt mandatory. The main issue Ive noticed is that the tests are composed of essays and grading is not standardized across TAs, meaning that one TA had a high in the low 90s with and average in the low-mid 70s while another classs average was an 83.

He's kinda all over the place in lectures. Often behind the syllabus. Doesn't matter- he makes jokes throughout. Not a huge history fan, but I enjoyed his class and learned a lot. I procrastinated so the textbook annoyed me, but it's actually helpful. Try to keep up with the reading on syllabus- if you cant, it's good to read to prep for the tests

Smead knows his stuff. He is very good at making boring things a lot less boring. He does make sarcastic comments that don't bother me because I agree with his politics, but definitely could understand how it would piss someone else off. He is very chill and seems willing to explain things and help students the best he can.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Mr Smead was one of the best professors I had during my time at Maryland. While I didn't necessarily agree with his politics, I thought he did a good job of being fair and objective. His lectures were clear and concise. If you enjoy the subject matter, you will do well in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He is a good professor and knows the subject but he has a hard time keeping liberal politics and his opinions out of the classroom. This can be a huge deterrent to coming to class. Your grade is based on three tests so be prepared to read if you want an A or at least show up to all of the classes.

Very laid back professor. We were supposed to have multiple tests and papers for our class, but he said "screw it" and just gave us a few take home tests instead. He is an entertaining and engaging lecturer and answers questions thoroughly, which is good because lecturing is all he does in class. Would definitely have him as professor again.

Smead is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had, and his gruff, sarcastic humor frequently make the entire class laugh. However,  he really gives name to the "absent minded professor." Lectures are hard to follow. The few grades are harsh, not explained and arbitrary. Unnecessarily difficult, although admittedly I'm not a HIST major.

The lectures could get boring at times but overall weren't bad. However I strongly recommend no one takes this class because of the TA Peter, I did well on tests did the reading and papers the best I could and got a C+ in the class because I did not raise my hand multiple times a discussion section. I never missed a class either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Smead is a good professor, but his TA's aren't great. I had Peter Libero and I would definitely stay away from him. Lectures are OK, tests are always essays, but the length and number of essays varies from time to time. TA's grade exams and are generally very tough graders.
He's funny and makes history clear and come alive. I wasn't a big fan of US history before taking his class.

He was an okay lecturer. A bit unorganized and is usually late. He'll try to tailor the class to fit the students interest but we missed a portion of the material in doing so. The best part is that he puts his lecture slides AND lecture recordings online, but discussion is a must. Its a convenient and interesting class; I recommend it.

Really funny guy who makes lectures pretty interestingentertaining.  All exams are just essays and identification and he puts up study guides before each one.  So just study what he tells you to and you should get a decent grade.  Recommended.

Overall, Professor Smead was not that great of a professor. Contrary to popular belief, his lectures were not that great. He was very disorganized and terrible at time management. By the last day of class we still had a whole month of the syllabus we had yet to cover.  He often got distracted. His final is cumulative and every test is just essays.
Great lecture, didn't mind going to it at all. He makes it all interesting. I'd definitely recommend taking it, and I'd take it again if I could.
HUGE FAN. Best professor I've had in college.

I took this course at UMBC and absolutely loved it.  Professor Smead is very clear in what he wants to communicate to you and his tests aren't too bad.  You just have to take really good notes when he lectures, and you should be prepared for his exams.  Awesome professor.

Interesting class. Good discussions. He lets us out of class sometimes 10-20 minutes earlier in spring 2013. The grades were 1 presentation, 2 papers, one final paper-two essays), and participation (500 points total). A few people had a second presentation and it could substitute the final or could be included in the grade with the final as well.

The bulk of this classes grading falls onto the TAs, but Dr. Smead is a great lecturer. He's fast paced, and funny which are rare qualities in history professors it seems. He's very knowledgable, however, we didn't finish the course material because there is so much to cover in US History from 1865 to present.

The honors seminar is interesting.  He is not a easy grader.  The average for participation was a 87.5 and the high was a 95. There are 5 grades, each worth 100 points (2 papers, one final paper-two essays, participation, and presentation). A few students had a second presentation (a couple substituted it for final paper). Interesting class.
So much fun to listen to these lectures-he is very knowledgeable and passionate!

Since they changed the class from 180 to like 202 or something, its an easy class IF you get a good TA. He doesn't do grades but he does give you good material and overseas the TA's tests so they won't put random stuff. TONS of reading but you can BS your way to a B or better. A bad TA though could make this an awful class.

Think the course changed. Anyway again not sure how Smead can get a good grade he basically tells you day one "don't see me about grades I don't know about that see the TA" so again you're at the mercy of your TA mine is average but it could be really bad depending on the TA you get. Tread carefully.

There's a lot of material to learn but he tries hard to not make it more difficult than what it could be. Take good notes, pay attention, and you'll do fine. Book reading comes very handy. If i could, i'd be very inclined to take his 300-level class.

Great professor. Pretty good overview of the second half of American history considering how much there is to cover. Super easy class if you pay attention, take good notes, and study. I just used the textbook as a supplement to the lectures
Great lecturer and super engaging. You don't have to come to class if you subscribe to the itunesU and listen to the lectures online.  Tests weren't too bad if you study hard!
Most entertaining lecturer in the whole school. He loved talking about sex, and constantly made me laugh!! Try 2 get 2 kno your TA 2 get a good grade

He made the class interesting. Clearly had biases, but kept them in check as well as he could. Go to class, because the slides are way too vague to study off of. if you have to miss class, subscribe to the itunesu account he has, they can be helpful. The paper was tough because it can be hard to find primary sources. take good notes in class.
Such an awesome class! Smead made it so interesting, I actually enjoyed going to class. I only got a B because my TA was a tough grader :(

super funny guy. great lectures. only three grades and no papers. I had a great t.a. which helped a lot. Pretty easy, just read the textbook and to class and listen to the lectures and you can get an A
I absolutely loved him. I actually liked going to class because he made it interesting which is saying something because I am the worst about going to class. Highly recommended.
This guy is real funny some times.

He's a nice guy and a decent teacher but nothing to write home about. There are only 4 grades total and he is a pretty tough grader.  I think the kids that think he's so great must not be doing the homework bc his entire lecture is always comprised of a dumbed down version of the reading in the textbook. Also, he sounds clueless a lot of the time..

This guy is great. The way he presents lecture makes you never want to be absent. He is very humorous too, one of the funniest professors. His exams are all essay. There was one 5 page paper. You must include as much detail in exams or he will take off points (like dates, names, etc). He is deff. one of the most well rounded professors. Not hard.
Its an easy class 3 exams 1 final no papers. There are some quizzes in discussion but if you go to lecture they're pretty easy. You do have to read a bit for the class but otherwise its an easy A

I think he is overrated. Not as "Great n interesting" as everyone says but a fair class. He is an ok teacher. He does hesitate and stutter several times in every lecture.  If you do all the readings they u'll do fine. The only assignment are readings and exams are essay format. It is not bad if u hav a good TA b.c they do the grading n explainin.

Believe it or not I hated history before I took his class, after i took his class..i have grown to love history! he is very funny and makes history somewhat interesting! Attendance to his lectures are not mandortory but definatley to discussion. His exams are essay format and not very difficult if YOU DO THE READINGS! Over all GREAT CLASS

GREAT teacher.  Very smart & knows what he is talking about.  He is very funny and has good guest speakers come to class.  The class is very interesting and as long as you follow along w/the lectures and take notes it's an easy A.

Lectures can be dry (and if early in the morning, skippable)  but he is very clear and concise  with what he expects and what you'll have to do to get an A.  Probably the easiest class I took all semester.
Its important to take notes with him, because the tests are pretty much based on the notes, and some of the reading.
Alright class overall.  Pretty good TA's and straight forward readings and tests.  Put effort into it and you'll get a good grade.

wow. excellent teacher. this guy knows everything that is, was, and probably will be history. class (terrorism) is graded on 1 presentation, 1 paper, 1 additional presentation/paper, and class participation. good feedback, very knowledgable... highly recommended. if you dont like history, get this teacher, hands down.

Great Professor. Tests are a lot of writing (essays) but you are given the option of which question to answer which makes them quite easy (as long as you did the review).  I know a fair amount about history, but still attended every class cause he is a great lecturer. He makes funny remarks and made boring history quite interesting.

Only TAs grade so really all I can say is that he is an interesting lecturer.  Lecture was funny, engaging, intelligent and well presented.  Technically you don't have to show up but they were always interesting and help you learn the material much more easily.
I liked the class overall but thought he was kind of overrated. Granted, the class is interesting enough, but it's definitly a review.
Hated history until I took this class.  If you do all the readings and go to lecture and take good notes, its easy to do well in this class.

I LOVED Smead's class!  I didn't miss a single lecture.  He's really interesting and turns boring American history into something you actually want to learn about.  If you're looking for an easy A, take HIST157!

Very interesting class - not even a history or government major, just picked it to complete CORE requirements, but i think its my best class here so far! makes lecture very interesting and funny, although sometimes he doesnt think through assignments, especially when assigning students toread a whole book in a matter of a week without thinking that they have alot of other work to do...
No Comments

Smead is a very unique professor-he can turn boring subject matter into interesting material. Class consisted of 3 exams and 1 paper. Exams were essay questions only. You need to be able to expand a lot to get a good exam grade.
No Comments
No Comments

He definetely enjoys what he does and it makes it easier on the class.  There was a lot of reading and i did take lots of notes, but i enjoyed the materiual and how it was taught.  Dids I mention he might be a liberal....?!?!?!?!?
one of the best lectures ive ever had.

Incredible professor - very approachable with amazing knowledge of subject. Class composed of student presentations with very little actual lecturing. Two projects plus a final exam with extensive reading requirements. Made class very informal and entertaining, despite its being 2.5 hours long. Always felt like I could have stayed another hour!

One of his assgnments was to plot a terrorist attack against U.S. interests both home and abroad.  Would not cooperate if you perfer not to write such an essay for fear it will someday come back to haunt you.  Does not think through assignments very well, but nevertheless he is easy and gives a lot of A's.

very funny guy, though maybe not so much if you're a conservative. gets pretty angered if you leave class while he's still lecturing. tests are pretty easy, especially when students are sending completed study guides out over the listserv.
Best lectures. Even made reconstruction interesting. Definitely a former hippie, and still holds those beliefs...

Lectures were interesting however once you come expect to stay for the whole class. (He REALLY hates people leaving during his lecture) Exams are normally straight foward, & yes you have to read all books for the class. Overall an interesting course. Should not be to difficult to recieve a B atleast
agreed...best teacher ever. classes are interesting, plus he is really cool guy. grading is somewhat easy, but fair.
Very interesting and good lecturer.  Made the class great and interesting.  Discussion was boring though.
best teacher ever
