Great lectures, very knowledgeable, good organization. I learned a ton. Only complaint: he did not grade my final exam, which left me with an "Incomplete" for the class. I had to turn it in again 3 months later before it defaulted to an "F."  He accused me of not turning it in and eventually gave me a "C." I'm not sure if that was out of spite :(

He is extremely smart. It was an extremely hard class though. The entire 3 hours is lecture with no visual aid. If you have know knowledge of the subject, like me, you will have to study constantly. Many in the class I was in were frustrated. I would recommend this class to someone with a lot of interest in the subject.

(islamic civ.) he's blind, so the teaching style is straight lecture. this makes it difficult to pay attention. your grade is based on 3 tests (including the final) and "participation" in discussion. my TA pretty much gave our class a heads up on the tests (which are in essay format only). i got an A in the class, with little interest going in.

Professor Ali was a fantastic teacher that I cannot recommend enough.  If you have the least little interest in any of his fields of teaching then he's your man.  He's objective on a region and subject that is nigh impossible to remain objective on.

STUDENT NOTE, THIS TEACHER IS 100% BLIND.  Because of this he lectures the ENTIRE time without  visual aides.  Sometimes he teaches with the lights of so feel free to turn them on.  He knows a lot about the Arab/Israeli conflict.  He is an Arab from Palestine so I thought the class was somewhat , just somewhat biased.
He is really passionate and very interested in his class.

I TOOK THIS CLASS DURING FALL 2004. HIS CLASS WAS QUITE INTERESTING. LOTS OF MATERIAL BUT I HAVE A FETISH FOR LEARNING, SO I IMMENSELY ENJOYED THE CLASS. MY ADVICE: WRITE FAST AND ASK QUESTIONS AFTER LECTURE OR DURING OFFICE HOURS. SOME OF THE MATERIALS ARE CONTROVERSIAL FROM AN ISLAMIC PERSPECTIVE SO DONT TRY TO START ARGUMENTS BASED ON THE QUR'AN

I took Dr Ali for the History of Islam. With no prior knowledge, this class was VERY hard. Hoowever, he was extremely knowledgeable on the subject. His blindness resulted in a very brisk lecture style, since he can't see audience interest or reaction. The TA was worthless mostly, unhelpful in the extreme. Go visit Dr Ali in the office! Worth it!

i learned a lot after i finally started understanding what he is saying. he talks very fast and doesnt really stop for questions (just one of the perks with having a blind professor). however, he is very intelligent and definitely has a lot to offer. so just GO TO LECTURE. and you will be ok.
...you other people need to stop ****in and just do your god damn work. lazy asses.
as mentioned, there are only 3 grades. his heavy accent was a problem for me. the TA was bloody useless and didn't seem to know jack beyond what the book already told us.

4 words ...Midterm,Final,Group Project. He lectures 50min streight the rest of the time. The TA sucked, and a lot of our grade depended on her since our professor is blind. She seemed like she didn't even know what we were talking about.

I took GVPT368A with Professor Satlzman. This was such a great class because not only did I learn so much, but the professor taught it very well - it's clear that he's knowledgable and passionate.
He very much encourages participation and will cold call if you don't raise your hand once per class. It ends up helping with the assignments tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Saltzman is great. He is very engaging and entertaining in class and cares about his students. There are papers (no tests) throughout the semester which aren't too hard and aren't graded so harshly. Overall an amazing class.

Dr Salztman is an incredible professor. My class with him is about Israeli politics. Since he's originally from there, he's very qualified to teach these types of courses. Lectures are very engaging and the assignments aren't too bad. The prompts of the assignments are straightforward and chances are you'll be fine as long as you do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ilina is hilarious and sweet. She brought cookies for our final class together. The material can be hard to understand @ 1st but class practice and discussion give ample oppurtunity to ask for clarification. TA Michael was very helpful! If you go to lectures, take notes, and study, you'll be fine. You have to practice to really learn the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: she can be confusing at times but she's super sweet and funny. if you study and go to class the test is on everything you learn during lectures. only annoying thing was she answered 2 out of 6 emails this semester.
Poor thing clearly knows the class material but is trying to teach IPA (pronunciation) with a thick Romanian accent... She tries her best but it gets very, very confusing.
Inoue-sensei was awesome and made class fun to participate in and actively learn. The language itself is super difficult but she makes learning the language a lot of fun and keeps you motivated

Tough grader and pretty nitpicky about errors-which is excellent for us Japanese majors. Hilariously funny and is able to convey difficult topics with general ease and clarity. Highly, highly recommended for the serious student of Japanese.

I had Inoue for six semesters of Japanese and adore her as a person.  She is super fun, a hip gal who knows all the cool music, etc., but at the same time, she is a REALLY tough grader. You ABSOLUTELY should use her office hours to get to know her so you can understand her personality and understand the grading system because her grading is strict!

I had been learning Japanese for about 7 years before i took this class. I barely made it out with a D. THAT is how strict this woman is! DO NOT take this class under her unless you either already know Japanese or are a seriously good at learning a new language.
No Comments
HARDEST GRADER EVER but extremely entertaining and fun.  Overall a fun class.

A really nice and funny professor. She is strict on grading but is willing to help you outside of class if you need it. Ocassionally has trouble explaining concepts in a way that relates to, or is understandable to a native English speaker. Makes class super funny though, which almost makes up for the harsh grading...almost.
Inoue-sensei is really fun to have. She's a bit tough on grading, but she's very nice and helpful, and genuinely wants her students to improve.

Japanese is not at all an easy class to make it through, with a lot of practice involved, but Inoue-sensei definitely willing to help (and be merciful), and makes the class as interesting as possible.
This class is extremely difficult and not for the weak. However, Inoue is very energetic and happy, which will rub off on you and keep you moving along. She is one of the better teachers to have.

Professor Inas, she seemed very nice and lenient. She made learning Arabic very enjoyable, and I definitely would take another Arabic class with her. The only issue I had was that we did not get to talk to her very much. The Final Oral was 5 minutes long, and was asked to name a few adjectives...that was it for me. I wish she challenged me more.

She is simply awesome.  She is super lenient with grades and attendance.  She understands that there are commitments on our lives.  She does enjoy assigning interactive projects kinda often.  But it is WORTH it.  I HATED doing projects for other classes, but because there are no real big tests, or other things, the sporadic projects are it.
rocks

Really good professor who cares about his students. Almost every class was discussion-based so as long as you read the assigned novels, complete the online discussion boards and talk in class, you'll do well in his class
Really good professor, super funny and likes the material that he teaches. open discussion style classes so try to participate. he cares for his students and is a great choice

Professor Infante is easily the best professor I've had at UMD! He is incredibly passionate and it is obvious that he cares for his students. This class is discussion based and reading heavy. There are a few papers assigned throughout the semester, but none too painful. Lots of analysis is expected in papers, in class, and in weekly blog posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He has no clue about aerodynamics. The class is muddled and confusing. He needs you to be in class or he tells you to come back next year.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Chopra is an amazing professor. He only cares that you learn the material, not that you're able to memorize things. He grades incredibly fair. He gives you the text book, which he wrote for free. It is also the most useful textbook for learning that I have ever had. I honestly wish more professors were like him.

This class is hard.  Going to class was boring because it was early in the morning.  The class is taught in ITV so if you miss a class then you can watch the lecture videos posted on blackboard.  A warning though, Chopra hates it if you miss class.  The hw's are hard because he only goes over basic examples in class and the hw's are totally diff.

I highly recommend this professor. There is a lot of reading, but it was one of the most interesting and enjoyable classes I have ever taken. The class is discussion based, so if you like that then you will really enjoy the class. The professor is very engaging and makes the class fun, but still thought provoking. She gives very helpful feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't take her unless u actually WANT to do A LOT of work. Reading is 30+ pages/night, and u do talk about it. Quizzes have extremely specific questions. Essays take forever. I'm a math major and I have to spend more time on this class than I do on my 400 level math classes. Personally don't enjoy doing this much work for non-major classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Don't let the 5 fool you. This is a class that requires a lot of work! But if you're up for it, Satelmajer is truly amazing. Of course it helps if you have some appreciation for Austen already, but it certainly isn't necessary to do well. Read the books, go to class, and participate in every discussion with reference to the text.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very good class
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Satelmajer is fine, but don't you dare be late by 1 or 2 minutes because if you are, she will mark you tardy. If this happens twice your "participation" grade will drop down to an A- and so will your whole grade. She also thinks that her class is more important than any of your major classes and will argue with you if you disagree.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Very nice professor but sometimes hard to understand what she is saying. The class is completely online and she gives very few homework assignments and tests throughout the semester. She is easily reached via email and doesn't take that long to respond to you. Very understanding if you submit an assignment late or miss a test for personal reasons.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although she was a new professor, her lectures were very clear and her quizzes/exams consisted of nothing else but what she taught during the lectures. If you just pay attention and look through the examples she gives during class, then there's no reason why you shouldn't be able to get a good grade.
Terrible Professor who employed a "Flipped classroom", had to pass this class by relying on online professors.

Great class if you have taken an algebra class before. He moves super fast because there is a lot of ground to cover. Sometimes his Greek accent made it hard to understand him and resulted in a lot of people talking throughout the lecture. Like any MATH113 course, there were weekly quizzes (which sometimes were take home), 3 tests and 1 final.

Really nice guy, but doesn't get much respect for class because of his quiet personality and thick accent. Super difficult professor if you've never taken calculus before, but people who already have- got  A's without much effort at all. Very easy grader on exams. Gives quizzes every week. Lecture hard to follow because of the speed and his accent.

A quiz every week, 3 exams plus the final exam, tons of homework, and a thick accent with a super high, squeaky voice. Knows his stuff but expects you to know it also. Not that tough of a grader on exams/quizzes.

Markou does not answer questions well at all and has a hard time looking at the class when teaching. You can have your hand up for 10 minutes before he notices. He faces the blackboard more than the class and gives quizzes every week.

His exams are actually quite fair. He curved the tough exam. He is a good teacher with only downside his accent. His curving is very generous. Expect more than 50% to get an A or B. Also very helpful and approachable!
Very helpful professor
He is good teacher. He is there for the students. Gave us extra reviews for all major exams. Has accent but very helpful. Overall a good experience.
He is a decent instructor. Definitely knows his craft. Relies heavily on textbook. Exams a bit hard but easy grader.
Markou is a good professor who sometimes is hard to understand. He is always helpful if you ask for help, and is a pretty nice grader despite the challenge of the exams.

I got a 5 on the ap test and love math. This teacher tought so horribly that I got a 60 on an exam because I studied off of the notes I took in class. There were proofs on the exam and he explicitly said that we didn't have to know proofs. Over all, it was a bad experience and I'm lucky that I passed

Has a slight accent doesnt speek to loudly but hearable, only seems to go over examples in the book with proofs which arent helpful,your as well off studying the textbook and showing up once a week to take the quiz. Nice guy but isnt too helpful/direct with your questions about grades and hw. Drops 1 exam 1 quiz Exams were tough with curves on some

Dr Hamza does a very thorough job at explaining everything that is important to know in the class, and he is always willing to answer questions during lecture. The exams are not designed to trick you, they are made to see if you truly understand the information. Dr Hamza is a fair professor who loves genetics and wants to see his students do well.

I passed because of the grace of God. The only grades come from exams and they are DIFFICULT. The UTA who is also a jerk is the grader. I don't even know how to tell you to study, but study smart. He was very lenient with the curve, but the curve is not huge. If you find yourself way below the average on the first exam, just drop the course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a very nice professor overall, but his tests are incredibly hard to study for. The lectures are heavy and sometimes fast paced. Best piece of advice is to study smart not hard for this course. Do not be afraid to ask questions. Also read the text book for context, attend GSS, and do practice problems. Good luck to future students!
Only 3 exams are graded for the whole course. Be wary and attend gss meetings. Also get the text book!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Hamza is a great professor. He is extremely knowledgeable and can answer any question you throw at him. He wants his students to really understand the material and loves to interact with his students. This class is a challenging course but if you take the effort to study and ask questions you should be able to pass his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Hamza is an amazing educator. Because he is so proficient in the subject, he sometimes assumes that you know enough of the material to skip ahead a few steps, but if you just point it out to him, he is incredibly receptive. He really wants you to learn and be successful, so see him in office hours too. Other than that, form study groups!!

Dr. Hamza started out the semester seeming really intimidating, but as you get to know him and his teaching style you realize he is really just trying to help you learn.  I learned a LOT in this class, and you really get a lot more out of it if you ask a lot of questions, even if they seem "stupid" at the time!  He is a really good professor!

He teaches by PowerPoint presentations that are posted online. Review the lectures but concentrate on reading the textbook as it gives more details. He recently dropped the quizzes so your grade is riding on two midterms and the final exam. The class is curved but make sure you are at the average or above or you are screwed.

Pop quizzes are 25% of your grade and each test is 25%. The tests are extremely hard, but in the end he will curve. He may come off like a jerk at first, but if you're confused and go talk to him, he is incredibly helpful. But go talk to him early before your grade suffers.

Professor Morris is a nice guy, very funny and passionate about political science. Everything in this class is graded by the TAs.  Fair amount of work. Midterms were fair, no surprises - as long as you show up to the lectures and discussion section, and read the textbook, you should be fine.
Morris is a great lecturer. Really passionate about political science and knows how to explain material in clear ways. Wish he didn't use TAs so much, but he has a huge class, can't complain too much
He's really cool and the class is fun. Sadly, he uses TA's, so, your grade is at their mercy.
He was great. His TA, Jill, was a tough grader and wanted the most minor details in the exams.
I had him for Public Policy. Wasn't interested in taking the class, but it fit my schedule. He made it one of my all-time favorite classes. Tremendous lecturer. Down to earth and unpretentious...
This guy is intelligent, hot and has a southern Texan accent, you can't beat
He genuinely wanted his students to succeed.

Take this class!! Professor Chinoy is amazing at his job, extremely supportive and cares about his students. The work is manageable, as long as you're participating and incorporating the detailed feedback he provides, you will be able to succeed. Although tech isn't allowed during lecture, everyone stays engaged and learns a lot.

Prof Chinoy is the most caring teacher I've ever had. He takes lots of time to give you detailed feedback on your writing. He is extremely accommodating if you need an extension for any reason. If you're looking for a JOUR200 class, Prof Chinoy is a great person to kick off your Merrill experience. He also has lots of experience and great stories!

Prof. Chinoy was great! I'm looking to major in journalism so his lectures were particularly interesting. He gives extensions on almost every assignment and is super responsive. His comments are also really insightful, with no vague critiques but specific lines in your writing. He genuinely wants you to become a better writer and journalist.

Professor Chinoy is the best! The class includes a bit of work, but it is all fairly interesting. Chinoy is highly experienced and has a lot of great stories from his time in the field. He gives extremely helpful feedback on writing assignments and truly wants you to improve. You can tell that he cares about all of his students. Take this class!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Chinoy is great, really nice and understanding of students! Good amount of writing in the class, but he's an easy grader. Had him in COVID times, and he was really flexible -- gave extensions for almost every assignment. He's an experienced journalist, who knows his stuff and he makes class interesting for the most part. Definitely recommend

Professor Chinoy was easily one of the most caring professors I have had at UMD so far. He really makes sure all of his students are succeeding and truthfully does his best to create a good learning environment. 10/10 would recommend taking one of his classes.

I had Professor Chinoy during my first semester and college and he was super understanding and helpful. He gave extensions when requested and was there to talk through issues. He's also a very knowledgeable writer and improves his students with personalized, detailed feedback.
Most caring professor you could possibly have. Would recommend 11 out of 10 times. He genuinely cares about his students and their well-being.

What an absolute saint. Ira is experienced and knowledgeable and he pours his passion into his classes. He is more prepared than you could ever imagine. Every lecture lines up perfectly with the allotted time. He works with students and prioritizes his class. His wife was ill during my semester, and he still came everyday and bent over to help.

Ira is simply the best teacher Ive ever had. He was always available to help students and his biggest concern is making sure that students improve their journalism skills. He grades fairly and grades on how you respond to the feedback he gives you. Hes a former professional journalist and is highly knowledgeable. He teaches a great class.
Amazing professor. He gives amazing feedback for everything and encourages students to meet with him for anything. Makes class very interesting
Doc. Ira is the BEST Professor I have ever met in school. Everything is good except the news quizzes. Great lecture, fair exams. U wont regret for taking his class

Professor Chinoy genuinely cares about his students, and he does everything in his power to ensure that they succeed. He grades all the papers and tests himself, providing individual feedback every time. He also has years of experience in the field, so he really knows what he's talking about. Overall, Professor Chinoy is amazing!

Best professor by far. His lectures are incredibly interesting, and he is very accessible outside class. He will read your paper before you turn it in gladly and gives great feedback. You won't regret taking this class.

Ira is one of the best teachers I've ever had. He is very accomplished in the journalism field and cares greatly about his students success. If you have things going on outside of class, he is always there to help you in any way that he can. His lectures are interesting and he never gave us busy work. All assignments had purpose and were meaningful

Ira's lectures were always extremely interesting, and all of the power points can be found online afterwards if you happen to miss class or need to review. He is always willing to accommodate students, and will not hesitate to meet after class if needed. There are a few extra credit opportunities throughout the semester.

Prof. Chinoy is very well-respected and wise, so journalism students have a lot to learn from him. He makes the classroom environment very welcoming and resources are accessible for you to do well. He is always willing to help. His stories from working in the field make the lectures engaging and interesting. He made me a better student journalist.

Professor Chinoy is always available to chat during office hours. He is a great lecturer and always has interesting stories to share about his life experiences working in Journalism. He's a great professor and I would definitely take him again.

Professor Chinoy is one of the best in the Journalism school. He really cares about his students and does not make this class hard at all. The only thing that sucks is the news quizzes but we have to get used to them anyway. I was very happy with my grade in the class and speaking with him in office hours really helped me as a writer.

He's an amazing mentor, and encourages his students to come to office hours to chat about life even after you leave his class. Very accomplished but humble and knowledgeable. Genuinely cares about his students, and sparks students' passion for journalism in classes. He's the  best professor I've had and why I'm a journalism major. Gives great recs.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof. Chinoy is the textbook professional. He's a pulitzer-winning journalist who has great historical perspective on the development of journalism, which works perfectly for JOUR200. He's a fair grader who emphasizes deadlines for good reason and keeps the class engaged with entertaining lectures.

Ira Chinoy is the purest gem at the University of Maryland. He goes the extra mile to ensure class was enjoyable and engaging. He is an award winning journalist with great experiences to share. He's a quick grader who gives stellar feedback. He cares very much for his students and makes his office hours feel like a chat with your grandpa.

Professor Chinoy is the best! He really makes the material relevant and interesting by being able to show similar trends in the past and how they compare nowadays. In addition, he's helped a lot with our writing. His feedback has really helped me improve upon my own writing.

Professor Chinoy is the type of professor college students wish for. He's extremely experienced and successful, he creates an atmosphere that makes you feel like an equal, and he genuinely cares about your general success. I'd strongly recommend taking his class.

Prof. Chinoy is the best. He's always encouraging students to come and chat with him during office hours. He's not only helped me understand some concepts during our talks, but also has helped me in other classes that I've been struggling in. He's a wonderful teacher, and he puts a significant amount of effort into preparing his lectures.
Professional, loves teaching.

I took Mining the National Archives with Ira and it was fascinating! I took the course in the summer so I think because of the time crunch the course load was very demanding but I thought all of the work was really interesting as was the required reading.  Ira is extremely personable and also very eager to help out students.

Ira is as nice as he is brilliant. His assignments can be tedious, but the only way to learn computer-assisted reporting is to do the work. Once you master the basics, you realize the possibilities, and Ira will gladly help you achieve them and inspire you to go beyond them. I also recommend his class that meets in the National Archives.

Ira is a nice guy, but good lord. Most people don't want to be computer-assisted reporters and most newspapers don't require it, at all. This class needs to be an elective, and Ira needs to stop inviting students to his office for hour-long chats. The class is boring enough on its own.

Ira is extremely helpful and knowledgeable. He's one of those professors who encourages you to participate and never makes you regret it.  His class will definitely help anyone entering the journalism field. I definitely recommend it and taking him!

The class is very boring, so be aware of that. There is a ton of studying that goes into it. Exams can be rather tricky, so study his lecture slides and read all chapters at least twice to secure your success. It's just one of those courses you have to suck up and deal with. Just don't brush it off though, like its no big deal and you will be fine

I was not a huge fan of Professor Forseth during my semester with him (Fall 04). His lectures were highly boring; he had a somewhat monotonous voice; it was at 9 in the morning. In terms of easiness, the tests for me were pretty simple. Understand the material and the tests aren't all that difficult. The TA I had was excellent, and he really helped to clarify the things the professor didn't explain well.

Forseth is a good man. He makes his tests pretty long so you have to think fast. Some of his TAs are horrible, so make sure you get a good one. I love bio, but this class is pretty boring. Just get through it so you can move on to the fun bio classes. Good Luck!

Berlin is the best lecturer. It is obvious that he is so passionate and knowledgeable about history. There's a good amount of reading for discussion but it's all very interesting. Exams are on ideas and topics, not dates and details which is nice. This is probably the best class and best professor I've ever had.

Seriously one of the best lecturers I've ever had, and I've had a LOT of them.  He is one of those rare professors who doesn't seem to think teaching a low-level undergraduate course is a chore that is beneath him.  Not only is he a fascinating lecturer, but he also seems like a genuinely nice guy.

Professor Berlin is one on the most zealous professors I have ever met. Going to his classes and listening to him talk about history made me want to change my major. The TAS are so helpful. Berlin is great, he loves history and thats contagious.He is very accomodating and his office is always open.Lastly,He does not forget names.

Prof. Berlin is an awesome dude, he goes through his slides fast but thats because he spends most of his time on the main points that you need to know. Don't get up and leave his class he'll make fun of you as soon as you leave and gets really mad. This dude is awesome.

Professor Berlin is a wonderful guy. He's very nice and his lectures are interesting. This class had a ton of reading and too many required textbooks (10 for one class!), but I thoroughly enjoyed it. Professor Berlin respects his students and values their opinions. He always encourages asking questions, and he's very approachable.

Berlin knows his stuff, he's written books and everything...he moves very fast and gives a lot more info than necessary, but the bright side is he gives the test essay question via email before the actual test day, so you know exactly what to study for.

I LOVE Professor Berlin. He's really nice, and he looks like a teddy bear. I want to hug him, no joke. He's always around to help, and he makes sure you understand the material. He pretty much gives you the test questions, and brings cookies to his "brown bag" sessions. There was lots of reading, but you could get away with not reading most of it.
It's a fine class to take if your looking to fulfill a requirement.  He's very knowledgeable and always happy to answer questions after class.

a really nice guy and is very enthusiastic about what he teaches.  I honestly rarely go to lecture because it is too early in the morning for me but if I actually study for final and put effort into the papers I will get a B and lecture is not necessary.  Lots of reading though, I had to buy about 6 books, most of which were not interesting
Great teacher. Really easy course. Might not be an A, but do half the work and get a B+, if you like history.
I went into this class thinking I was going to hate it, but it was actually one of my favorite history classes so far. He's not an amazing lecturer but extremely knowledgable.  Take it if you can.

I went to a total of four lectures all year. I never read anything, just skimmed what was needed for the papers. He gave a list of vocabulary words for the exams and "hinted" what the essays would be. The TA's were great. I got a B+ and would have had an A- if I studied a little more for the final, instead of just half an hour.

he really knows his stuff especially when it comes to slavery. He sends every student a list of vocab that outlines the unit, hes nice/through about answering questions, and the TA's go over exactly whats going to be on the tests. He even made cookies for us.the class makes you think w/o being incredibly hard.i got a B+ w/o doing 95% of the reading
It's not an easy class, but if you read the material and go to lecture you'll be fine. And he brought us oranges for the final.
It's a difficult class with a lot of information to fit in a short period of time, but Professor Berlin is really nice and can be funny, don't take the class if you aren't interested in the material
No Comments
No Comments

There is sooo much reading.  Although he tries to make it interesting by making you "THINK HISTORICALLY", it just makes it really hard.  If you end up in his class, don't sit in the front row.....he has a spitting problem.

Terrible class!
Seems like a nice guy but not a good teacher. I didn't learn anything.

As long as you go to class and skim through the book you will get no lower than an B.

Take this class! He really knows his stuff and his lectures were not boring whatsoever.  Keep up with the readings, they really help on the midterm and final. One major paper and no pop quizzes. You come out with a lot of knowledge. Very insightful and you cannot get anything below a B.

he's very knowledgeable on the material and is passionate on the subject. go to class. he is attentive and notices when a student doesn't show up. he's also easy on the eyes which is a plus

So many papers

Great professor who really cares about the material being given and wants his students to succeed. Yes it is a class thats test heavy and studying is super important. But the lectures are interesting and if you study a good amount you will do well

Hard class but people blamed covid for not studying

the best MATH prof. EVER ! and AMAZING guy ! great personality ! moreover, he has a motorcycle !!!

Amazing guy!! take him !

Justin is all that is man, visit his office hours, make sure you understand his material, if not, go to him to understand it, he will gladly help.  His notes are brilliant and the work load is decent.  Nothing too heavy, nothing to light.  Make sure you get him, not a T.A.

Justin is the HOTTEST prof ever!!!!!!! Completely drop dead gorgeous!!! I have never had perfect attendance in a class, but I definately did his. Amazing teacher too. Passionate about teaching, not burnt out like other teachers, extremely good at making the material easy to understand. Even sends email on a regular basis. However since he's such a good teacher there arent very many curves cause everyone seems to do well in his class.

Great professor. I came with 0 understanding of anything pre calc and left feeling I understood almost everything. Most kind, caring professor. So sweet and helpful. Made math easy for me to understand.

She cares about her students and their successes. The feedback is always constructive and she is incredibly helpful. If you have the option to have her, definitely take the class!!!

Amazing teacher. Very engaging discussions and not too tough of a grader. Definitely reccomend

hard to get an a on papers but she's really nice and accommodating.
Also on every paper she will give you feedback before the final due date so u can figure out what she wants

Prof. Joshi is one of my fave profs ever! Even though attendance is kinda mandatory you can miss two weeks of class before she cares. She says she grades participation but it's only a small part. reviews.comment: Professor Joshi is one of the kindest professors at UMD but if you are looking for an easy grade there are better options. If you do take her class make sure and take her feedback seriously on the first couple assignments because she will grade harder as the class goes on.

Prf Joshi made writing interesting to someone who didn't really care about writing or English. The workload was pretty heavy to be honest but not overwhelming if you space out your work. She's a great professor for students who are actually interested in English classes. If you want to learn to write, she's great - gives good feedback and is super nice. Professor Joshi is a great professor, she really wants you to become a better writer and is always there to help. Great Prof! Just show up and do the work. Very understanding and lenient with deadlines. I'd definitely take him again.

great teacher

Like the reviews say he is very unorganized. You can figure that out by looking at his desk and clothing alone. This translates to his teaching which is all over the place. Writes very sloppy on board. Skips way too many steps in a math problem and is bad at explaining things.

not be the best professor, but i love the guy. very very unorganized. very clear and helpful. i would recommend him to anyone.

very caring teacher. i am learning a lot.
pleasant guy, good sense of humor.  dedicated, timely, and fair.  good class I learned a lot.

great teacher!

Make sure to study and ace online quizes and HW (repeats some questions on test). He gives you the essay questions,so know them. On difficult MC questions, always go for partial credit. Attend class for tophat.

This class was NOT easy as advertised by the others on here. His quizzes/exams/HW's were NOT straight forward AT ALL.  They were all worded weirdly and some of the answers differed from those in the book. Also be ready to show work for math on tests even if he tells you that you wont have to.
Great class, great professor. Learned a lot and it was pretty easy to get an A. Highly recommend it!
Awesome professor. Go to lecture, its fun anyways. Reading the book goes fast. Tests resemble the HW questions. He also provides past tests to look from. Requires effort, but not painful.
Loved this class!A lot of fun ! Do ya hw on time be in class and yall be fine

Great class! Lectures are comprehensible, well structured, and never boring. Professor is awesome (definitely one of the best at UMD!), knows a lot and explains material very clearly. I've learned a lot in this class and highly recommend it to all majors!

great professor, keeps class interesting and his exams are fairly straight forward and easy to  pass. do the all the homeworks well and all the quizzes and you will have room to mess up on the exams and still get an A. He made the material interesting too.
great teacher, one of the best at umd. tests are easy if you study a little bit the night before. gives past exams to study from.

Prof is fair. He wants students to learn the material and issues but he makes it entirely possible to earn an A if student is willing to do a minimal amount of work. Prof. Leonard is a great lecturer and he knows what he's talking about.  There's a lot of room to mess up. I personally loved this class and feel that I learned a lot.
he is a fair teacher and is respected in his field. he kept lectures as interesting as they could be depending on the topic and he gives study guides and essay questions before exams.

gives upto a possible extra 10% in the class, so there is room to mess-up.  Very knowledgable. Keeps the material interesting.  Gives sample midterm and finals to help you study. He uses some of the same questions as well. Uses webct and is nice to look at.

Absolutely recommend taking her class.

extremely boring way of presenting material, extremely boring lectures

Study and do the homework and you will do fine!

Khachik is very helpful if you ask. He asked during lecture a lot if people have questions and will tell you to come by anytime you have questions throughout the day. Not sure what his issue is but you're better off asking your TA for help. Honestly one of the most unhelpful teachers I've ever had. Acts like you're a bother for emailing a question.

This was my second semester taking orgo 1 with khachik. The first time i recieved a D. GO TO EVERY CLASS AND WRITE EVERYTHING DOWN. To study for the tests, look over the notes and the email he sends out. He is incredibly helpful. Use GSS. Study your butt off for the 3rd test. Curve is anywhere from 9-20pts/semester. I learned a lot.

Although he knew his stuff, he was very disorganized in relaying the information to the students. I find this very confusing because I tend to learn better when things are organized. If you are one of these people, I suggest you take another professor for this course.
Awesome! His tests are easier compared to other professors, and he is really fair. Definitely take him instead of the others for 241

He teaches straight from the book, and his tests are straight forward. He does have office hours, so I don't know why previous reviewers think he doesn't have any. He really is a nice guy, and is fair if you try hard.

Yes, his tests are easy but he doesn't teach AT ALL. I felt like I sold my soul to the devil because I tried so hard to learn but he was useless! No office hours, doesn't care, terrible teacher. You will not learn organic at all and then have fun taking mcats! I got a C and I put in everything into the class. But I couldn't learn it by myself!

Dr. Khachik is great! At first I thought he was a stubborn guy who hates curving and wouldn't care if ur 0.0001 shy from ur dream grade. I was proven wrong. He makes rational considerations. I also took Khachik because I thought he was going to be easy. He wasn't. At all. It was hard to understand what he was saying and you need to study ridiculous amounts because there is no curve unlike the other teachers.

He is a great teacher! Very willing to help and very fair.
Really easy teacher. Exam questions are directly from the book. No  curve though. If you just do the hw and remember the reactions, its and easy A.

Khachik was a great teacher considering how much orgo blows. the subject requires lots of reading and practice, so don't go in thinking ANY ago proof will be easy by any normal definition. HE IS THE BEST TEACHER EVER!!!!

Best organic chem teacher ever! His test are really easy, and you can tell he wants his students to do well. Emails everyone a study guide about a week before each test. Really great guy!
The easiest Chem teacher I ever had. He really want you to succeed. His tests are extremely easy... He even give out hint out on tests!!!!!

She's a really nice and friendly professor, but her English and grammaer are horrible. It's sometimes really hard to understand her because she has such a heavy accent. really cute professor

Dr. Paczolt knows what she's talking about and comes off as passionate about her work BUT she can be extremely inconsiderate of student concerns especially during a still ongoing pandemic. INCREDIBLY organized, accessible. Youre gunna learn a lot. Transcribe every word of her lectures to pass. But youll have no idea how to study for the exams. Its a race through your notes. Still, shes very fair. There is no curve but she gives a little extra credit and has fluff assignments. You can get an A but you need to put in the time.
