reviews.comment: Professor Paczolt is amazing, she really accommodates to the students needs. She is thorough when explaining lecture topics. Its a tough class because, well, its genetics but she does a great job teaching. I took her for summer and cant say enough good thing. The exams are hard, you definitely need to study but they were open note and she's fair.

ONLINE BEWARE. If you have a job or any other summer classes, DO NOT TAKE HER. Expect at least 8-13 assignments due Mon-Fri. Exams are intense and are not based on lecture material. Lectures alone are 5-6 hours of videos a week. Expect to spend 3 hours+ daily on assignments. Exam averages at 58%. She does not curve and will fail half the class.
She's fine but she rounds an 89.9 down to a B+ which is just cold :(

Based off of lectures and topic quizzes, Dr. Paczolt is amazing. I constantly felt like I had a good grip on the content but her exams were much more difficult. A lot of exam questions will make you jump through loops to get the right answer. Take a different professor if you can. The cons outweigh the pros in this case.

Very difficult professor. If you have to take her, my recommendation is to transcribe her lectures word for word or else you will miss important things that she will test you on. I wish someone told me that earlier on. She is not responsive to student concerns and can be quite condescending. She doesn't curve - I had 89.91% overall & received a B+
She was a good professor, not gonna lie. But her exam was incredibly difficult. If you can avoid taking BSCI222. Please do. Otherwise, you will have to study your butt off to get the grade you want.

I'm impressed with the way Dr. Paczolt handled online lectures and teaching. Her videos are very clear and straightforward (although lengthy, there's A LOT of content). She's passionate about what she teaches and she's good at her job. She provides review material and has a very organized canvas page. What more can you ask for.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. P is incredible. During our online semester, she was great at providing tons of resources and extra materials to help understand the content. Navigating through her elms page to get to lectures and quizzes was extremely user friendly, I don't think I could say that about any other professor I've had. She knows how to run an online class.

Dr. Paczolt was a great professor during the normal semester, but she really went above and beyond when we switched to online partway through. She was incredibly accommodating and supportive when students reached out to her. She wants to make sure you understand the content and teaches it well. She's enthusiastic about the class and it shows.

I learned so much from this class! Dr p is a great professor & person that really cares if you do well. She provides you with everything you need to succeed, and if you put in the work it's not difficult to get the grade you want. But you WILL need to put in the work, the exams are super hard.

Before signing up for genetics I looked up dr p. and the reviews were terrifying. I thought I was gonna fail. Im in her class now and I dont understand the hate. Her exams are always fair and she only ever asks what she said in class. She also has videos on elms, you can literally watch those and you set for the exam. Just study & youll be good.

Shes very rude when answering questions even in office hours. Her exams are extremely specific and even if you know the material you will lose points bc she expects you to write stuff that isnt in the question. She makes this class unnecessarily hard and makes an interesting course hard and annoying.

Can't answer questions and is very vague. She often contradicts herself. Even though she is unable to speak intelligently about the course she teaches she expects you never to make a mistake. The tests are incredibly specific and graded harshly. If you understand the general overview of the topics thats great but that's not what you'll be tested on

One of the worst professors Ive ever had, disrespectful towards the class, frequently could not answer student questions. More helpful to teach yourself since she doesnt explain topics. Your discussion TA will teach you more than she will. Avoid taking her !

Dr. P was great. I personally didn't go to her office hours, but I went to TA office hours and it helped me a ton. Her practice exams are helpful --- if you put effort towards this class, you'll do well! She wants students to know the material well - not just to memorize everything.

Don't take her. Her lectures and slides are REALLY confusing; she just reads off from the slides. She makes the tests so hard, she tests on the most irrelavent minor details. I had to study soo hard to get a B in each test. If you can please avoid taking her.!

DO NOT TAKE HER PLEASE. I came into this class with a pretty strong background in genetics but her lectures are just awful. She does a great job at muddling easy concepts and is unable to explain anything when asked - she simply repeats herself. Material is not that hard but her wording of questions on exams is atrocious and frequently misleading.

The professor wants her students to know the material but she is not lenient. She is one of the I learned this you theres no way you cant professors. Unless you are a 3.2 or higher average, I dont work and have the time to dedicate my life and time to this class over the others, then keep it moving.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: The tests are pretty hard but the clickers and panapto recordings are really helpful! I recommend rewriting notes and viewing the recordings to study for the exams. She posts old exams too which are helpful for studying.

Good lecturer. Packs alot into her lectures, so be sure to watch the Panopto recording to get it all. Her slides are a bit of a mess, so utilize the summary skeets she uploads. Canvas quizzes, worksheets, and discussion grades really help pull up your grade. She does attendance clicker questions. Dont get behind- its hard to catch up again.

I really loved Dr. Paczolt, the way she teaches is exactly how she expects you to learn. If you go to lecture and take the quizzes and do the homework, the material is not hard to learn. I LOVE that she does panopto and clickers. Those posted lectures help so much when studying for exams and the clicker points added a significant boost to my grade
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Paczolt is one of the most difficult professor for BSCI222. Her exams are incredibly rigorous with no margin for error and she expects you to be able to follow through her lectures without falling behind (which is not doable at her pace). Her lecture slides, outlines, and assignments all contradict one another from time to one. Do not take pls
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. P is the best professor is my favorite! She's super approachable and wants the best for her students. Her exams are reasonable and easy to get through. I would definitely take her class again if I had the choice.

This is probably the worst professor I've ever taken at UMD. She expects you to know every single detail from every single slide. She also ENJOYS tripping up students with trick questions. She has a very strict guideline for points and will never give you the points you deserve.

She was a very nice teacher. Going to lecture helps since the class is more on the lecture-heavy side. She gives cool real-life examples of every topic you will go over. You need to fully participate in order to get through the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Paczolt offers an abundance of tools that other professors don't even bother to include. She provides pre-made lecture outlines for you to takes notes on that will also help you organize your notes, as well as indicate which topics are important to study. Lectures would be re-recorded on her own time if there was a problem with the original.
Terrible lecturer. Doesn't do much more than reading off from her slides and gets stuck when asked a question. Organized though.

Avoid this professor! I think if she took this class she'd get a B; she knows her slides and that is it. She spends 15 min on the irrelevant and review material but spends 2 min on new complicated material and only tests on those 2 min. Then blames the class for the low average. She talks slowly and her voice is very annoying, also very sassy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Great and clear lectures; easy to understand and good at explaining difficult concepts. Dr. P is an engaging professor and is easy to listen to. You have to work for your grade (actually read the textbook). Discussion is a lot of work (kind of pointless though). Lots of extra credit. Very fair tests and fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Please, take anyone but Paczolt. She is very inexperienced and bad at lecturing. She will spend 15 mins on irrelevant topics,  but 2 mins on the stuff that she actually will test you on. Exams weren't that bad if you memorize everything on her slides. She forces you to do those annoying discussion stuff that she won't even test you on. Tedious work
pretty terrible. She simply reads from the slides, and never explains things in detail. She is nice but very inexperienced avoid taking her if possible.

Her exams that covered the slides, and did not dive too deep into the specifics of the notes. Rather, she basically wrote exam questions that were similar to the practice problems she gave us. The class is tough, but not impossible to get an A in. Lectures are kinda boring, but go because there is extra credit. She is an okay prof, and very vague.
Gives extra credit, if you pay attention in her lectures then it'll be way easier to study for the exams.

Lectures were boring and not really engaging, but he's nice. Exams are heavily weighted in the class; two midterms are 40% (20% each), and the final is worth 35% of your grade. Attendance is not mandatory, but there are in-class questions (not based on accuracy) that you can get extra credit with.
He cares so much about what he's teaching

Prof Kiemel is a nice guy, cares about the course. Lecture was super boring but gave opportunities for extra credit which was cool. The discussion attendance is mandatory but the assignments are fairly easy and interesting.
He was a super chill prof who cared about what he was teaching. I would definitely take him again.
Very reasonable professor, no gimmicks in terms of coursework and exams. Super insightful course

He is a very good and easy going professor, the exams are very easy if you study the ppts thoroughly, he gives extra credit as well. The attendance was not mandatory but extra credit, nine assignments and weekly quizzes that are very easy. If the effort is put in, it is an easy going class with an achievable A.

course is structured so you pass if you put little effort. It's challenging 4 an A or better.  weekly discussions require you to present to the class biweekly, the lectures canB dry. For an A must pass 10/12 quizzes, 5/6 present, and 90%+ avg on all 3 exams (2 exams being 25q and final being 50), finals cumulative and tries to trick you tbh 2.7/5.

The way that Dr. Kiemel grades the class makes it impossible to get lower than a B in the class if you just do the work. If you put a little effort into studying for the exams, an A is super attainable in this class. Overall, the lectures are boring, but I would highly recommend this class if you want an easy A.

I had him for KNES226 and I thought the class itself was very interesting. Its not too challenging, its pretty easy to get a good grade if you try and go to discussion. I thought the lectures were interesting but I could see how someone thats not already interested in this class would have a hard time focusing

Such a nice person. Gives great lectures and you can tell he's really into what he teaches. I found the material interesting which helped. Tests are not bad at all, but still study. Make sure you do well on every quiz (online) and discussion assignment and you will get a good grade.

Prof Kiemel really knows the field in which he teaches, and delivers wonderfully well-structured lectures on the content. This can be a little dry, but if you keep engaged by taking notes and trying to understand the big picture, you won't have an issue. Exams are based directly on the online quizzes put out, and are easy. Grading is very lenient.

Dr. Kiemel is a great guy and really cares about his students. He makes the distribution for grades different in that what normally would be a B+ is an A-. Course content is overall interesting and should be an easy A if you put in some work.

I took this class online during j term, and it was alright. Definitely not as hard of a winter class but just be prepared to take a lot of notes and watch a lot of lecture videos. In order to stay on track you will probably have to do a little bit of work every day, but it's not too bad at all. Very interesting (physical therapy related).

The guy lectures very boringly. You can get all the lectures online and he just talks about them in class with everyone basically on their phones or laptops. His grading system is weird to where you can easily get an A when normally you'd get a C. Beware of his tests though. They are full of "All of the above" questions that are hard than expected.

So his lectures tend to get a little boring and people constantly skip them, but the material is very interesting and you can tell that he really cares about it. His grading system is different, but it's really good and reasonable. The discussion exercises were pretty interesting and the exams are really easy. I recommend this class for the easy A

Let's be real the class itself is very interesting but Kiemel himself is very boring and puts students to sleep. However, this class is extremely easy cuz your grade is based on levels of achievement, not percentage. Basically, don't turn in stuff late and "pass" assignments will get you a B. Put in some effort for the exams  A+

Prof. Kim is amazing. He has valuable experience from being a lawyer himself and his assignments were very helpful for pre-law. His assignment guidelines were super clear and he always outlined exactly what he expected from us. His contract grading makes the class less stressful and almost gurantees an A if you do the work.

Professor Kim was great! Enjoys making class entertaining with activities and his humor. He grades fairly: no one getting below a B on assignments unless you really messed up. My advice: go to his office hours and the writing center to get great feedback. It really shows you are willing to put in your best effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Take his blended learning class. The in-class time was useful and also fun yet serious. I don't like english classes but his was great. He gives great feedback and is willing to help out whenever you need it. Rubric and instructions are very clear so writing papers is easy. Plenty of resources are provided to help with papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Kim's lectures were more like social outings. I never felt that class time was spent well, and his assignments were quite vague. His is point deductions were unjustified, but he never gives below B. I wouldn't suggest him if you are inexperienced in writing; he just kind of expects you to know what you're doing. **CANNOT GET GRADE ABOVE A**

CHOOSE HIM!! His assignments are clear-cut and he gives a lot of feedback, so your writing should improve by the end of the course. As long as you put in the effort for final papers, you'll be fine. I actually love coming to class, & I hate morning classes (attending class in general I guess). Also, DON'T BUY Fearless Writing, use library's copy.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Doesn't go over prompts and asks basic questions as if he was teaching theoretical physics.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's really sarcastic and I enjoyed going to his class. Not a super tough grader and is very helpful with each writing assignment. Assignments are fairly straight-forward and he really puts an emphasis on preparing you for law school.

Prof Kim was a really great teacher.  He splits up large papers so you have multiple drafts due before the final.  They're easy points and helpful because you have a basis long before it's due.  He's a fairly easy grader and really wants his students to become better writers.  As long as you stay on top of your work its an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He means well. Be cautious if taken in the summer. Theres a lot of writing papers, especially within 6 weeks. I'm sure it's easier during the fall and spring semesters when theres more time to do your work. He's really helpful if you just ask. I advise you visit him during office hours when you need help with something. Just do it ahead of time.

I get why people don't like him but honestly I found his dry humor amusing. He's really smartand gives you relatable topics for every paper. One of my articles was about the effects of war another was about why it's important to recycle. Doesn't really grade hard once you realize all he wants is replicas of his sample papers that he gives you.

In most English classes you can get a feel for how the professor grades or what they want to see and then write according to that. In this class, it's all guessing. He is never clear about grading or what he wants, making it almost impossible to get an A on any of the papers. Kind of monotone. He's friendly, but don't expect to learn anything.

Professor Kim is by far one of the most contradictory professors out there. His explanations of assignments are always different, and you never really understand what he wants. Dry sense of humor, makes fun of students, has no interest in the class, and doesn't teach you anything worthwhile. My advice: switch out.

Great professor! Though lectures aren't fun he makes it easy to understand. Good amount of assignments so exams aren't the only thing that dictate your grade. There is a group project at the end of the semester which can be a lot if you don't have a great team or time-management skills. Overall he's a very caring and kind professor.
Prof Kislaya Prasad is the besT!!!
No Comments
No Comments

MBA course - Managerial Economics and Public Policy. Not your typical microeconomics course. Exams are much more difficult than the Prof prepares you for (lectures, course materials, etc.), and the readings from the book won't help either. That said, he significantly eases up on the grading.

This class is really hard and you have to put in the work, but it was so clear that Prof Kim wanted you to pass. He will extend deadlines, add extra office hours, make OH appointments, and walk you through problems for an hour after class if you ask. He really cares about teaching and cares that you learn the information.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had Prof Kim during fall 2020 aka covid season. i thought i knew physics, turns out i don't. his lectures are basically straight from the slides and he avoids all questions. anytime you ask a question he ignores it or dances around it. and don't even think about asking your TA for help. if ur taking this class as just a requirement, ta's wont hel

He often grazes over questions asked by students and doesn't really clarify on topics he acknowledges are confusing. Even during online class polls most of the class gets the wrong answer, but he does not do a very good job on explaining why their choice was wrong and continues to move on when more than half the class is still clearly confused.

He's one of those professors that are too smart to be teaching a low-level class. He doesn't really understand why others don't understand problems; and he shows that by saying during lecture "you should just know it." He also says during lecture pretty often, "you should be able to get this in 1 second."
Professor Lape was a great professor who cared about her students. She was willing to meet with students in office hours and was a fair grader. The class was not unreasonable and pretty manageable.

SHE NEVER CHECKS HER EMAILS. She always says "feel free to shoot me an email to ask me about (etc)" or "send me an email and we can talk about (etc)" and she will literally never respond or respond at the very last minute with a two word response. Absolutely enraging.

Kisa is such an amazing professor. She is always open for questions and the writing in this class is not too demanding. It is a very relevant class if you are planning to pursue a career in the health field. She is very understanding and her office hours are very helpful.

Get ready to write a lot for this class. Prof Lape is really understanding and is really helpful when it comes to teaching this class. I had to learn a whole new style of writing for this class and she did a good job of teaching me what to do and what not to do. She was also very understanding of student's issues and would always try and help out

Kisa is a great instructor for English. I took her ENGL395 class during the pandemic when we were all online. She was accomodating throughout the semester and would truly listen to her student's concerns. While this course involves a lot of writing, ample time is provided for each assingment.

Shes a very nice lady. If you put in an effort, youll do well. She cares about her students and is willing to work with them. There is however a lot of work. This class required way more work than classes for my major and I spent the most time on my work for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kisa is great. Her class can be boring at times, but it's doable. She is definitely not an easy grader, but she is willing to help you out if you ask for feedback. Reading quizzes can be annoying but she goes over the content before, essentially giving you most of the answers to the quiz. To earn an A, you have to put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Ms. Lape was very helpful. She always answered my questions and met with me during office hours.
Ms Lape gives regular reading quizzes and weird topics for papers(which she grades pretty tough).

Bro, take Keller in the summertime. I haven't taken bio since 10th grade, and let me tell you, I had a glorious time, bruh. Take him in the summer. The practice exams were helpful, he was mad helpful, and the worksheets were like max 3 pages.

Overall, Dr. Keller is pretty nice. Attendance is not mandatory, but he has extra credit questions for in class only, so I would go. He records his lectures and posts them. He gives a list of topics for each exam, which is very helpful when studying. His tests are pretty fair and he tells you exactly what he will test you on (aka the topic list).

I had him in Fall 2020; he was a nice, chill guy but his tests were tough and I lost a lot of points because to get credit, the exact term was required! He also gave out a lot of homework and assignments. If you don't have a biology background or haven't taken AP Bio, good luck!

Amazing professor, he includes documents where he covers everything he talks about in lectures. Good study guides and great professor. Few quizzes and homeworks but really help prepare you for the tests. Lecture isn't mandatory and he records them all but he offers clicker questions where you can get extra credit points.

AWESOME GUY. Lecture is engaging and interesting, tests are honestly not hard at all if you study. I havent scored below a 90 on any of the 4 exams, and am expecting the final to be similar. Course is designed to help you succeed. If you come to lecture and take notes, you will do well. If he is an option, take him!!!!

Professor Keller's lectures are engaging, but you'll need to stay focused to do well. Using unstuckstudy with the provided study materials can make exam prep a breeze. Attendance is key, so don't skip class. Overall, a challenging but rewarding course.

Do not skip class or you won't pass. I loved Dr. Keller's lecture style but I wish I paid more attention and was keen on his speeches, thats where the information is. The tests are hard but you need to make sure you go to all GSS sessions and do the study guide through and through. Hard to do well in this class but the information is worth it.

Professor Keller has a great personality. Going to lectures is the only way you'll do well on the exams because he explains in detail what you'll need to know. He gives extra credit for participation (via point solutions), and only keeps the grades of a few worksheets. Your grade really comes down to weekly quizzes on ELMS and the 5 exams.

I had him for the summer. Exams will make or break you. If you do not have a background in biology, then this class will be difficult for you. He also changed the grading scale of the class last minute and made me think I was going to pass. Please beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really liked Keller. If you're taking him I would recommend taking notes on what he says rather than what is on the slides. His study guides are also extremely helpful. I was sadly focusing on many other classes and wasn't really able to focus on his class which is why I got a C. I will say sometimes I felt like he oversimplified some concepts.

Lots of material but Dr. Keller explained it all very well, quizzes every Friday and some worksheets that we worked through in class, it's good to know the material inside and out before exams and he makes it clear what is covered before. Clicker questions are sometimes quiz questions! Make sure to study a lot! Some grades were dropped at the end

His class is relatively easy. Although he doesn't upload panapoto videos, all of his slides are online and easy to read. He's also VERY lenient when it comes to grading. His worksheets and quizzes are easy A's and as long as you attend the exam review sessions with GSS you'll do well on his exams.

I loved Dr. Keller for BSCI170! He makes sure to explain complex topics and processes in super simple terms making things easy to understand. He makes it very clear what will be on exams and puts together summary modules for each unit (they're great for study guides). He also does clicker questions during class for extra credit.

The only bad thing about him is that he is very specific on his exams and will not accept answers that are not worded how he wants them. Other than this he's a pretty funny guy and his work is relatively easy. His weekly quizzes are harder than his exams most of the time. If you study enough and read over the material he provides you'll be set.

Very engaging lectures and is great at explaining material. Exams are fair and not super hard as long as you study. He lays everything out in his modules and records the lectures so attendance isn't mandatory.

Keller made everything really easy to understand and made complex topics fairly simple. Exams aren't too difficult if you put in the time to study. All the information is laid out in detail on modules and is explained really well. He made class really interactive and enjoyable.

If I would have taken any other professor for this class I probably would have failed. Keller's lectures are straightforward and he makes sure to post the slides and recordings of each class. The exams are so simple. I did not read the textbook nor did I pay attention in lecture but I got 100 on all exams by just memorizing the study guide modules.

hes a very nice guy
tests are hard but not impossible

Professor Keller was very nice and funny. His lectures were clear and simple. He offers Clickers that is a form of extra credit. He sometimes gives you classwork, which aren't too difficult. The exams are fair and clear to understand. As long as you study effectively and use AMP resources, you'll pass this class.

Keller is so sweet, but in order to do well in his class you really have to pay attention to his lectures and even possibly rewatch them. His exams are fair, his final wasnt. He recycles old material so try to look at past exams to study.

Lectures are engaging and well done. He's great at explaining and it really shows that he does care about what he is teaching. Funny and very understanding. However, notes taken in lecture may not help in the long run so I would recommend spending more time looking over material posted on canvas. Exams were tricky and difficult.
Exams are very difficult. However the work was manageable. Hard to reach with email but is a nice professor.
Overall good teacher, but he gets a big passive aggressive at times and does not listen to the concern of his students. He lectures well and the material id pretty straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He will give you an extension on any quiz or worksheet (he's very understanding). Amazing lecturer so pay attention+take notes. Super sweet and funny guy. Knows his stuff. Clicker questions for extra credit. *Sometimes* hard to reach via email He is a tough grader and wants specifics. Exams are hard but if you study hard, you'll get an A.

While he seems to be a decent person his decision to not listen to students while we were concerned for our health and those who are close to us during COVID made it apparent what mattered more. He is funny during lectures but make sure you study and go to GSS for a good grade. Also the grading criteria is on the syllabus so make sure u read that

Like any class, you will have to put the work in to do well. Dr. Kellers style of teaching makes tough biology concepts easy to understand. There are also other ways of getting help if youre still having trouble. Follow directions and take advantage of your resources and youll be all set!

I think that Dr. Keller was an amazing professor for BSCI170. He offers his students plenty of resources to perform well in his class (I.e. study guides, extra credit, practice problems/worksheets). I would also highly suggest attending his office hours and GSS sessions. It is imperative that you read his syllabus thoroughly!

Pros - Dr. Keller is a decent lecturer, information is conveyed clearly through his own speaking and his slides - Lectures are relatively engaging, with light humor Cons - Bad at communication (i.e. emails) - Highly passive-aggressive - Amidst the COVID-19 pandemic, Dr. Keller refuses to look out for the health of his students. He does not care.

If I could give negative points, I would. Keller was so rude when requesting flexibility for accommodations (for disability purposes). He also makes his own "points system" so your true grade is not what Canvas reflects, told us this 3 days before finals. Made us take finals in person, even with COVID shutting the rest of campus down. Expect H*ll:)

Here's the thing, I loved Dr. Keller as a lecturer. But, now we're at the end of the semester. His grading policy is confusing, and I already was aware of it from the syllabus. You really won't know your grade until he springs it on you 2 days before your final. I even calculated the points myself like he said to and apparently I was wrong. Crying.

Dr. Keller is a great professor. He wants all his students to do well and teaches information that you need in order to do good on the exams. The exams are straight from the lectures and by studying the content a little, you are guaranteed to get a good grade. He gives about 20 points extra credit through clickers as well.
Dr. Keller's lectures are incredible. I don't understand his low rating on this site. He makes even conceptually difficult concepts incredibly easy to understand. 10/10 would take any class with him.

Dr. Keller is the ONLY choice for BSCI. He is an incredible teacher as lectures are engaging and clear. His addition of worksheets helps break up the lecture that allows it to go by faster as well as lets you learn. Material is concise and clear. Exams are EXTREMELY FAIR - USE THE STUDY GUIDES ARE VIDEOS HE GIVES!!!!

Professor Keller has a great personality. The lectures were engaging and clear. As long as you make use of his study guides and resources, you will do well on exams and quizzes. He answers any lingering questions you may have and makes it clear what he expects on exams. Better choice out of some other Biology professors.

Keller is the best out of all of the BSCI 170 professors, who had abysmal midterm averages. Keller clearly cares about the success of his students and is an amazing person as well as a professor. His lectures make it easy to understand content and he's clear about what will be on exams and makes sure not to include nitty-gritty details on exams.

I have no idea why Dr. Keller has such low ratings on here because he was an amazing professor. Lectures are easy to follow, attendance isn't mandatory but if you DO attend you get extra credit points, and lectures are all posted on ELMS anyway. Exams are easy if you follow the study guide he LITERALLY makes for you. 100% would recommend, great guy
Cool dude and good teacher

Very good at explanations during lecture and one on one help. Is enthusiastic and cares about what he is teaching so the class is not boring. Specifically lines out what will be on each test. Overall very helpful, caring, and great at helping you understand the topic.
As long as you read to modules youll do fine

Professor Keller is an amazing professor who really cares about the wellbeing of his students. I don't know why he does not have better ratings, maybe it is because he is a bit of a tough grader and you have to listen to lectures (whether in person or in the videos he posts), but either way he is really awesome. I really do recommend taking him.

Dr. Keller is such a GREAT teacher!! I cant not stress this enough. I dont know why he has such a low rating when hes one of the best teachers I had so far at UMD. He cracks jokes during class and is great at explaining different concepts. He also give extra credit (clicker questions) during class. He gets a 10/10 for me!!!
HIS EXAMS WERE UNREALISTIC. He gave way too many questions for a short period of time. The weekly quizzes were too hard for not teaching the material. He does not care about his students at all.

I was surprised to see such a low scoring for Dr. Keller, he's amazing! His sense of humor really makes the class fun especially on days we have long topics. His lectures are straight to the point and he strongly encourages you participate (Go to GSS and office hours)! Go to class because most of his test are based on his words. Fav teacher at UMD!

Dr. Keller is such a great teacher. He not only makes his lectures very easy to understand, but he also gives extra things like putting a lecture summary with the important key ideas w/ it & curves the grade. He is also so funny, and makes it actually interesting to learn about Biology. He is also very very caring!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I can't speak to how he is in-person, but he was extremely accommodating and understanding for the online course!! Although ur final grade is heavily dependent of the exams, he is an amazing professor and explains the content very well!! His syllabus gives lots of room for a few missing assignments to not interefere with your grade. 100% recommend

Dr. Kellers lectures are very straightforward and he tells you everything you need to know for tests. Hes very organized and hes very understandable. This is a stress free class if you stay on top of things.

I've taken many bio courses and Keller is the best. He explains complex things in a way that is very digestible. That being said, bio is never a cakewalk. You have to work and take in-depth notes. Studying is a must but if you watch every second of lectures you'll be okay. Very organized. Only thing that bothered me was the final grade system.

Dr. Keller was a great teacher. He explained concepts really well in his lectures and his grading was very fair. Each unit has a mini quiz (easy) and every few units has a test. This reinforcement really helped me understand the material. I really appreciated the way he organized canvas; it was very clear and made learning the material much easier.

For an asynchronous online class his notes and lecture videos were very good and I understood all the concepts he taught. He's a little picky about word choice but overall a very good professor and very fair. Also, you don't need the textbook but you should go to the GSS before tests because it helps a lot.

I really enjoyed taking BSCI170. I enjoyed the asynchronous nature of the class combined with Dr. Keller's weekly office hour. He was super kind and very responsive to emails. He responded in one minute when I emailed him one time. I would definitely recommend him.

Dr. Keller is a fantastic professor! He had lectures that were easy to learn from and the class was well-formatted, especially considering he was online because of COVID! Take DILIGENT notes and ask questions and you'll get an A. He is super understanding and truly cares about his students. You'll definitely leave prepared for future bio classes!

The lecture videos for online class were very thorough and well organized. Exam weren't too difficult as long as you studied A LOT beforehand; there were a handful of very specific questions. Class was pretty straightforward, but lots and lots of information. Free responses depends on if you say it the way he wants you to say it.
I love this guy! His course is hard as a first science course but its not suppose to be easy. He is a very organized person as well.

Professor Keller is a nice guy, but his class is quite hard. Lectures can be very long but very informative and helpful. The weekly quizzes sometimes ask questions that are too specific to what was in the lecture, making it much harder. Exams have been pretty hard. He expects your answer to be exact to words he expects; if not, you get it wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller is a great guy. His lectures are straightforward, quizzes + worksheets are open note (some can be a little tough but nothing crazy). However it is not an easy class. This semester was difficult bc of COVID and I wish it was in person, but that's not his fault. The final was harder than the other exams because it was more conceptual.

Dr. Keller did really well for online learning. He was super caring of his students and he made the material very doable. It was simple enough: notes, quiz, worksheet, exam. I really appreciate his personality and kindness during online learning; he responds quickly to emails!
Great teacher. I dont understand how anyone could give him a bad rating. Trust me, take his classes! Not too hard you just need to put some effort into it for an A.

Material and lectures are dense, but Keller's class is simple: do the lecture, do the assignment, take the quiz, take the exam. Only 1 homework per unit and he reveals the answer key to homeworks after they are turned in, so you can always check your mistakes. One quiz per unit, and grades are pretty quick.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller adapted well to online learning. His lectures were asynch and depending on the unit were only about 10-25 minutes long (usually closer to 10). Workload was not bad, but tests had questions about finer details: you had to prepare well. Overall, his lectures were interesting and he taught well.

Dr. Keller has a wonderful personality; he's very relaxed and you can tell he loves his job. However, you really have to work for your grade in this class. Tests are hard, and you fill fail if you don't study. There's a lot of note-taking for his lectures, but there's one quiz a week so that's good.

Dr. Keller is a great professor, he is very lighthearted. You can tell he enjoys what he does and is very good at it. With class being online this semester, there was a lot of reading/watching of video lectures, and the online quizzes and worksheets get confusing at times. Even so, I definitely recommend him. He makes things easier to understand!

Keller is a really sweet guy. I Had him for online so it was a bit different. All his class is, is graded classwork, unit quizzes, and the exams. The classwork can be a little hard but you have your resources. And quizzes are open note and all the answers are in his lectures. Exams honestly are difficult, but his class is not stressful.

This class was literally such a breeze, and I am NOT GOOD at bio in general. If you watch through his lectures attentively and take great and in-depth notes, you're set! I literally got As on every exam. He also seems so nice and he really wants us to learn. He doesn't try to trick you at all on the exams and quizzes, very straightforward. Love him

I love Keller bruh he was the GOAT. But seriously tho he's amazing but beware the tests cuz he's specific on terms. If you study a few days (3-4 days) before the exams u should be fine. Hella extra credit given & group activities once a week in class. If u need extensions just ask. I wouldn't say it's an easy A but super doable fr fr
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Keller is a great professor. If you put in the work, time, and effort, there's no reason to panic. I strongly recommend going to GSS and any review session you can!!!! This seriously is the reason I did well. His clicker questions are worth 20 points in extra credit so make sure you go to every lecture!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: lectures were boring & his teaching style didnt match w my learning style (may not be that way for everyone). very tough/nit-picky grader. Wednesday activities were helpful in learning the material & when we switched to online he was very flexible with deadlines. exams were tough & hard to score well on. clicker points help boost your grade

Keller really wasn't that bad. Lectures were amazing and very helpful, he does clickers in class that give you 20 extra credit points. Wed activities were hard unless you had a good group or had friends in the class. Don't bother getting the textbook I never used it. Nice guy and responds to emails quick. Def recommend over any other BSCI170 prof.

reviews.comment: His lectures and slides do not prepare you enough for the exams. Most of lecture is a waste of time but you should go to ask questions.

reviews.comment: This has been the worst and hardest class I have ever taken in my life. If you haven't taken AP bio or any prior "advanced" biology, good luck. If you don't have to take this class, DO NOT take it. He doesn't care about you or your grades. All these reviews are so accurate so please, trust us.

reviews.comment: TOUGH GRADER TOUGH GRADER TOUGH GRADER. I tried so hard on every one of his tests and they all averaged at about a 70 because he's so nit picky about word choice. Slides have little to no information so you really have to pay attention to what he says. Also don't waste your money on a textbook, he told us to buy one and I never needed it once.
The man cannot teach at all.

Keller grades all of his tests horrible. He is unfair for example, when you put down what is correct in your own words (not his phrasing) and get points deducted. Overall when it comes to tests. Grading need to be based on a students ability to answer a question independently; not memorize his answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller was a decent professor. His lectures aren't that interesting, but he emphasizes what you need to know on the exam (you just have to pay attention!). If you ask him what you need to know for the exam, he'll tell you.

The class was alright and the material wasn't too hard to understand. Dr. Keller is boring in lecture tbh. Midterm exams were similar from past semester so they weren't that difficult. Go to GSS, review old exams, ask Dr. Shields questions in review. Watch for the prep quizzes. They're a pain to the grade.

It is really important to show up and do clickers! They count for 20 extra points at the end of the semester! Dr. Keller is a pretty good professor, just as someone who took AP bio and didn't score high enough on the AP test to waive the class, it's an overall boring lecture. Pretty easy A coming from a bio major. Tests are a little hard though.

Yes exams are difficult, but their is plenty of opportunity to boost your grade. I learned a lot. You need to come to this class prepared to learn, he gives you notes packs.. print and bring them in ahead of lecture. The point is to be able to make small notes onto them not go in an write down everything he says. Screw up on a test and it will refl
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a terrible prof, his exams are difficult and class average on them are 70, 65, 68, 75. Even if you study 10 hours for an exam, the way he words the questions are really tricky. He also does no curve and he does not give + or -, so if you got a 79% in the class, it's still a C. His slides have 2 bullet points and he explains them. Very boring

Dr. Keller is a terrible professor. His lectures don't even match the tests half the time and he is just a complete jerk. Whenever you try to talk to him about anything serious relating to your grade or an assignment, he will reply back with a snarky, passive aggressive comment and make you feel worse then you did before.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Keller's style of teaching isn't good at all. He expects you to learn everything needed through his slides, although not everything there is needed for the exam. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He kept everything simple, and his notepacks/lecture slides matched up very well with the tests (he also emphasizes stuff you're tested on), and I believed his grading was very fair. There are also GSS sessions, and you can earn a bunch of points with clicker questions, so as long as you put in some effort and make us of resources you'll be good.
Just awful. Dont take his class. Youve been warned.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: keller was alright. not the BEST professor but definitley not the worst. there are alot of online quizzes and it can be hard to keep up sometimes if you dont try. the clicker questions are also very important for your grade. keller isnt always eager to give back points on exams. the homework and test questions were also worded very oddly someitmes

Dr. Keller is rude, confusing, and uncaring. I went to every single lecture and ended up having to spend at least 3 hours after each lesson trying to teach myself. His lectures are unhelpful as he seldom explains concepts and instead just reads the 2 bullet points placed on each slide. Take Dr. Shields - her exam reviews saved me countless times.

Dr. Keller wasn't a bad professor, but he wasn't great either. His slides had about 5 words on them that made no sense so you really have to listen to what he says and be an auditory listener to get the information. I never read the textbook. Weekly learning activities are helpful. GO TO DR. SHIELD'S REVIEW SESSIONS!!!!! They're incredibly helpful.
