Dr. Keller acts like we should all be experts in Biology after listening to his lectures. When I ask him a question I immediately feel like the imbecile. The stupid activities are unhelpful and childish. Keller is funny and a nice guy. But I have not enjoyed his class at all
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Okay so here's the tea, and it is piping. His lectures make absolutely no sense, his monotone voice is impossible to pay attention too and his slides help absolutely no one. He is a good person and a nice guy but I want to cry every time I walk into this class.

Prof. Keller doesn't do plus or minus grades, and he doesn't round; I finished the semester with an 89.4 and received a B. If you don't have any background in Biology this class can definitely be confusing, and the group projects/activities don't do much to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Bought the textbook and never used it. Tests can be hard, just study more. His lectures can be boring but he's a nice guy. Not a bad class.

Dr. Keller is a pretty average lecturer with difficult exams. There are mandatory group activities every Wednesday that are pretty easy grades. Also, if you go to the majority of lectures you get extra credit points at the end of the semester.

Keller is a really tough grader. On tests you can get 0 points if you don't word something the way he wanted even if you have the right answer. Doesn't post lecture slides and isn't very helpful with questions. You're better off with Shields. The study guides are helpful, but the tests are more on application that knowledge of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller was a really nice professor who was clear in his grades and what he was going to put on tests. There weren't too many tricks, the tests were fair and mostly off of lecture stuff. He's def a professor dad though so he's going to try and throw in some dad jokes and things but otherwise he's a good choice for biology.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Keller was not necessarily the best teacher, but the way he structured his class, it was not difficult to receive an A. Everything on the exams can be found either in the online note packs and/or the red book study guide. Studying both of those materials allowed me to receive an A on all of the exams, including the final.

I took Dr. Keller's MW class. His lecture was very vague. He does not write the tests, and his lectures do not sufficiently fit them, nor do his study guides. On them, you must have his exact wording, or you won't pass. It is hard to get ahold of him outside of class. If you have to take him, take his 3 day/week class. I don't recommend him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Extremely boring lectures, but ultimately got the job done. Said the word 'critters' more times than I could handle. Tests are fair but kinda got screwed as he doesn't give +/-.

Not a bad professor. The class is just generally difficult, but the exams are more straightforward than what most people say. As long as you pay attention to the lecture slides and see what he emphasizes, you will do well. STUDYING is key. Extra credit was given with clicker questions and this semester he added an 8 point "curve" which is rare.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: You have prep and elms quizzes which are short and simple weekly, as well as Wednesday activities to help you learn. Your ULA or the TA's are a great source to ask questions to considering Keller doesn't respond to emails much. He is specific in what he wants on the exams but you will know if you attend lectures. I highly recommend Keller/shields.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's not the best out there but he's not the worst. The only real way to do well in his class is to have past exams from a friend or something. Beware his hand-drawn diagrams on exams are absolutely terrible and confusing. Make sure you stay on top of things if you plan on doing well. Pay attention to the grading in the syllabus.

Doesn't communicate clearly about whether he wants specifics or big ideas. Tries to be funny and relatable but ends up being annoying. Doesn't spend enough time on each lecture slide even though that's what his tests are based on.

We have clicker points, which barely helps your grade and when it is a test day, you THINK that you perform well, but end up straight failing. When my friend went to ask him how to perform better in the class and he just told her to do better -_-. Take his class if its the absolute LAST RESORT.

The worst teacher I've had in a long time. He doesn't respond to any emails and doesn't care what you have to say anyways. His lectures are boring and confusing and if you don't show up you won't know what he wants you to say on the tests, because that's how he grades- based on what he wants you to say. TAs grade super harshly too

Clickers are the only thing that will keep you awake during his lectures. Not very responsive to emails or questions after class. Never saw a TA the whole semester but they managed to grade everything with ridiculous harshness. If he's the only person left you'll manage but you'll also have to put in work teaching yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Keller is a good lecturer. Class participation was only necessary during Wednesday activities, but if you go the other day it is definitely helpful and he gives extra credit clicker questions basically every day. Based off what I've heard from friends with other professors, he's a good one. The test can be confusing though.

He is a pretty vague teacher and uses a lot of words like "stuff" and "things" so when you take notes on his lectures you can often end up not understanding what you wrote. Speaking of lectures, his slides contain little information and what you need to write down is what he says. Lots of room to get a decent grade though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His teaching style is very ineffective, he basically stands in front of the room and reads off a PowerPoint. He is also very hard to get a hold of outside of class and doesn't take questions seriously. You basically have to rely on the textbook for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller is great. Although some say he is a tough grader, it is because you need to explain concepts on exams in his words. This is easy though if you go to lectures, listen and take good notes. Gives great examples and is one of the more understanding professors at UMD. Plenty of opportunity for extra credit just by showing up to class.
Hes a nice guy and in my opinion the best bio teacher.

His lectures can sometimes be boring, but its important that you go and pay attention because he explains things more in detail than on the slides. You have to put in a lot of study time to understand the material. Grading is mostly based on exams but there are clicker questions you have to answer in class.

Exams are graded based on whether you used his phrasing or not, which can be annoying. Good lectures if you go, and you can get EC by answering the clicker questions in class. He does group work every Wednesday, which isn't horrible if you get a good group. It's actually quite helpful!

He can explain what's written on the slides. I don't think his lectures are too horrible but clearly not the best nor interesting. The tests were reasonably difficult. If you skip the group work day, you will lose points. There is group project, so hope you get a good group because you don't get to chose them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The one word I would use to describe him is awful. Not only are his lecture boring and uninteresting he is not a helpful teacher. He will not answer ANY emails (I've sent 9) and he doesn't seem to care for his students whatsoever. He can also be condescending and rude.

Please take my advice and don't under any circumstances take a course with Dr. Keller. I have honestly had the worst time in his class, as he makes you fight for every single point. I think he understands biology, but I don't think Keller is intelligent enough to understand anything else. His grading and justification for it is just plain dumb.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Hard to get the grades you want when you think you are able to... He requires us to view many materials yourself and take a quiz for that before he actually teach them in a much simpler way, and prepare a lot for the pointless activities. The quiz and homework questions, exam grading and especially regrade can be pretty unreasonable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: You will have to teach yourself mostly in his class. His lectures don't have a lot of material in them. They don't fully explain the concepts you need to know. You might need to rely on outside sources and sometimes the textbook to get through this course. Study all of Professor Shield's activity materials and all the other worksheets to do well.

The exams are very difficult and it's almost as if he forces you to think in the way that he thinks about biology. Aside from that, he is very thoughtful and humorous at times. The weekly online quizzes and clicker participation help boost grades.

Dr. Keller is great lecturer. His tests seem easy but the questions are very vague and he expects very clear answers and you will lose points easily even though you are confident your answers are correct. Overall a fair professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Easy class. Kellers a corny dude but it's funny. Study his slides and pay attention in lectures and you're good to go! What I will say is make sure to GO THROUGH THE EXAMS HE HANDS BACK to make sure it's graded correctly. I got knocked off a letter grade because the grader made mistakes and a lot of others had the same problem. He fixed it though!

Not a terrible guy but he gives so man corny jokes that you begin to despise him. Test are 100% subjective, you could give a completely correct answer but get the question wrong because it wasn't the answer HE was looking for. Every Wednesday there are group activities that are completely useless. Textbook is optional. Keller gets on your nerves.

He's a fun guy, but expects you to know everything he says during his lectures, his slides are only outlines and don't include details, and his study guides are only sometimes helpful. Everything assessed is said during lecture, and the textbook barely helps. He also does not curve (even if the average is a 50%), and he doesn't use the +/- system.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: look at pictures in your book, since lecture alone will not cut it. test questions are specific. try to get your hands on old exams to see what he looks for. he tests on stuff he says in lecture, so make sure you write down the stuff that he emphasizes. you're gonna need to study. the class is quite annoying. go to GSS sessions if you can.

Lecture attendance isn't mandatory besides Wed activities but there are usually clicker questions Mon & Fri. Tests are heavily based upon what Keller says in lecture but if you don't attend PPT slides are really vague. Extra credit is useful and Dr. Shields review sessions are helpful. Keller isn't the worst lecturer but can be unclear at times.

You can tell that he does not write his own test because some of test questions are not covered in class. He does understand it's a hard topic that requirements lots of memorization and tries to pass out some study guides to prepare people. There is a textbook but its not really needed.

Decent person but horrible professor. Tests are ridiculously hard, mostly because of his ambiguous questions and if you don't answer exactly the same way as he does, you get no points. He makes the class more complicated than it needs to be. No curve and no plus/minus grading so your 79% is the same as someone else's 70%.
No plus minus. Fairly hard tests. Lots of in class activities. Okay class- I missed making an A by .2 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The class is just very unclear. His questions on exams are weirdly worded and vague, and he takes off points if you put more information than he wanted. The class is really hard to follow. He doesn't post textbook readings, he doesn't follow the powerpoints, and the study questions accompanying lectures aren't helpful
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This is coming from someone who took this class twice with  him. I took it in the spring and then again in the summer. The class moves at a faster pace in the summer, but tests are more straightforward. I wish he taught the way he does over the summer during the semesters. Most important thing is listen to what he says and study very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Here is one of the most honest reviews you will get for this professor. I have never gotten below a B in any of my college classes until I had this class. Keller is a nice professor, but the tests are ridiculous and are very unclear. There are no multiple choice and its all fill in the blank, drawing diagrams, and short answers. EC is available.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller isn't a bad guy, it's just that Cellular-Molecular Biology is a tough subject. His system of grading is annoying because you won't know your real grade until the end of the semester. He also does A/B/C/D/F grading.I taught myself out of the textbook because the lectures by themselves aren't enough for you to understand the material well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller is awesome. The majority of people who don't like him are people who don't know how to work in college. Put in time studying and use the 10000 awesome resources and answer keys he lists on his page and you'll get an A/B in the class. Pay attention in lecture because he emphasizes certain things that he hints will be big on the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is the worst professor I have ever had. He does not teach the material in a successful way. He also does not give +/- grading , so as soon as you lose 100 points you might as well not work because you are getting a B. He says to "keep it simple" constantly, but on exams he grades super harsh and says to add more detail.

Terrible professor that dissuades a lot of people from biology. Slow, uncommunicative, and does not do +/- grading. Makes the material much harder than it is. If the university really wanted to improve their biology/STEM departments, they would let this man go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller is a smart man who is willing to help you understand important concepts during office hours. It is much more important to write down what he says, rather than what is on the powerpoint. Good professor, but exams can be tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He would be an exponentially good professor, if only you were actually able to contact him outside of his class. He has actually said to students that he never checks his email because he's to busy, which is inconvenient if you can't attend his office hours. Other than this, he is pretty funny, and a good lecturer. Be prepared to read the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He doesnt do +/- grading but thats because if you put in effort, use his study guides, go to lectures, and review handouts you'll do fine. He's very well organized to the extent that I may not need to use my textbook to study. He has handouts, warm ups, ppt slides, and lecture questions online to review and study. There are a few group projects.

I enjoyed Dr. Keller's class. I took both BSCI105 and BSCI106 in the same semester and had no problems in either class. He's a kind man who tires to make lecture interesting. You can tell that he likes what he does and takes a few shots at Chemistry majors here and there (but I agree with him, sorry Chem majors!). No +/- grading scale.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Keller was a solid teacher who made BSCI 105 a smooth experience for me. His lectures are very clear and concise and he always lets you know what you are expected to know. He gives adequate resources as well and is always available, approachable, and accommodating as well. This class wasn't overly difficult.

awful. forgets to enter students grades in elms. exams are nothing like his lectures/textbooks. odds are the only reason he teachers is because he is required to to continue research. he offers study guides for exams but they arent much help. avoid if possible

In past semesters where averages have been in the 60s for an introductory bio class, the man has refused to acknowledge his inefficacy in conveying the material. He does not do +/-. So despite the past history of low averages, he will not curve and your 79.9 will be a C and your 89.9 a B. Do not take him unless you like dealing with nonsensical BS
This guy is rude and unclear. You will gain nothing from going to class, he is simply a terrible person. He laughs when 20 percent of the class gets a clicker question right.

He's kind of picky with words, but if you pay attention and understand well what he said, you should be fine. He's helpful in and out of class. Ask questions if you don't understand and he'll explain again until you get it. If you skip his class, you'll miss a lot of things.

He's a pretty straightforward teacher, doesn't move on from a topic if people don't seem to be getting it. He does give a lot more information than needed in his lectures, but it doesn't hurt to know. He gives a study guide before each exam but the questions can be somewhat vague, however they do reflect what the exams cover.

He's not nearly as bad as people on here are saying. He's actually great in the sense that he doesn't teach straight from the textbook. He's more concerned about us actually understanding the concepts rather than just throwing information out. And he always has a positive and enthusiastic attitude during lecture even though its a introduction class

My biggest problem was that he never responded to emails!! Horrid teacher with unclear tests and unfunny lectures. The GSS people and TAs had no idea what his deal was. They could only do so much before the tests killed you with his unclear questions. Only thing good about him was that he didn't do plusminus grading.
Keller made the class very hard and barely made the material understandable.  The lab was extremely easy, though.

He teaches way more than you actually need to know for tests, but he gives out study guides! Make sure you go to class to get the clicker points because those help out your grade a lot! Dr. Keller likes to make little jokes so if you laugh at them, he'll probably love you
Keller is a great professor. He's very approachable if you show interest in learning the material and hes willing to work with you if you need help in doing better on tests.

He makes it very easy for you to pass with an A if you work hard and pay attention. You can really tell that he cares about if his students are learning or not and he works really hard to keep the students entertained on such a bland subject. From what I've heard he's very approachable for office hours. Also, go to GSS sessions!

He was a nice guy and clearly  put effort into his lectures in an attempt to make them interesting, but overall the material is very difficult and the tests are hard. I recommend creating a study group and going to class. It's amazing what clicker points can do for your grade.
He's overall a really nice teacher and actually does want you to do well. Its a lot of information but if you read the powerpoints and study from the book you'll be fine

Dr. Keller is a great professor! keeps things simple and to the point, if you pay attention and study you will do very well.  Exams are very fair and will not take longer than 30 minutes if you know the stuff!

Keller was a good professor. Lectures were boring, but there was crucial information needed for the exams. If you attend lectures, he tells you what is on the exam. GSS for this class is extremely helpful. Exams are simple, and he makes corny jokes, but overall is a nice guy and wants you to do well

VERY boring lectures, posts all powerpoints online so i never worried about missing classes(only downfall was missing clicker pts). Didnt present material in a way that was easy for me to understand. Tons of material presented but simpler exams. You can tell he wants you to know a lot of bio but wont test on all of the material he teaches.
Unapproachable and doesn't show interest in students. It's an easy A but otherwise I wouldn't expect anything else from him.

Keller was a great teacher and really wants the students to do well. You can tell he loves his subject and is excited to teach it. The tests are pretty hard and you definitely have to study a lot, but you'll learn a lot. He shows cartoons and animations of concepts in Bio to keep the class fun, and always jokes around. Overall great professor!
Nice guy, tests are really hard.  Kind of boring to listen to sometimes.

He provides you with an overwhelming amount of information for tests that concentrate on two/three specific areas. His tests are difficult and the lectures idiotic. More times than not they result in a cartoon being shown.

i agree with the comment before mine, i think he is a good teacher that really wants his students to understand the material. i would recommend to take him, yes it is a hard class but if you take him your grade will reflect the amount effort you put in. i wonder why the first comment says he is "unapproachable and rude" when that's not true at all

He is a funny guy whose voice cracks a lot during lecture and has one of those hiccupy-nerdy laughs that makes the whole class laugh.  He explains the information in very basic ways in order for you to truly understand--like if something contains a bunch of nonsense you don't need to know for the exams, he'll just call it "stuff."  I enjoyed him.

Lecture is not mandatory, lab is super mandatory! The course is very very hard and I saw some pretty smart people get D's on exams.Example: One exam the highest grade before bonus qs was like 84. That being said he provides you with lots of resources for his impossibly hard tests, I would recommend for bio majors, but it is not! a casual class.
I had this guy as a lab head in BSCI 105. Keller is unapproachable, and is pretty stark and borderline rude.
He doesn't explain what he wants very well. He will give you an A for effort, but if the mistakes (that he doesn't explain) continue he will start to take lots of points away.

KP is a great teacher. Class is super chill and enjoyable. He's very flexible and caring, also pretty funny which is always a plus. You can tell he truly wants his students to succeed but is also super mindful that his class is not your only responsibility. He gives great feedback as well. Really smart guy and super encouraging to his students.

100% recommend taking Konstantinos (Kos) Pozoukidis for ENGL393 Professional writing. I took him during the winter which was a 3 week course and had 3 major assignments in total. The work is what you would expect, but he gives good feedback and grades real easily.
Totally amazing dude. Took him for a gen ed intro poetry class and have zero regrets. Highly recommend, just take his class.

Really cool dude. You can get a good grade by not doing readings until in class. Opportunity for extra credit. Willing to have class outside on nice days. Easy grader. Likes to have class online, it's easy and you don't have to go to TAWES.

Great professor and great class. There are a handful of writing assignments, but none are too long. Highly recommend taking English 101 or the equivalent before this class. I found it fun and pretty easy, but the foundation I had definitely made it that way. He is kind, approachable, and gives great feedback and cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: He is a PHD candidate but is a really friendly and helpful instructor. I am a freshmen and took ENGL255 by mistake without knowing its a 200 level course. At first, I was struggling but the prof helped a lot and is very funny and friendly in the class. Around 8 classes are online on a Google Doc which weren't easy. Def take him. Extends deadlines.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The class was online & tailored around textbook (must purchase). The content is clear, straightforward, and incredibly useful. Prof. is knowledgeable and always willing to provide insight and advice (Great class). Best advice I have is take detailed notes for the exams and read through the modules he provides in order to understand calculations.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: There are 6 tests altogether (5 regular tests and one final) which were okay since there was a lot of content. Everything you do in this class is online. Projects are simple/straightforward if you take the time to sift through the notes in his modules. This class taught me so much about real world finance. Professor Knight is kind & accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: There wasn't many reviews about this teacher so I thought it would be okay but BEWARE. Alot of math involved. I recommend that you take pre requisites in accounting, economics, and basic math before taking this class. His tests are really tough! Mostly math problems. Worst class to take for elective.
Rude and too confusing. Avoid this professor
Took him over the winter, a great teacher but more importantly a great person. Very interesting in his lectures can make anything interesting.
He's the best, very nice and very accommodating. If you have the book you can skip the whole semester and get at least a B, usually an A.
The best professor at the business school. His lectures follows the book, so its easy to understand.

Lecture was incredibly boring as he would talk in circles and not get anywhere.  Only about 10% of the class attended regularly.  However, the class is pretty easy as long as you read the book.  Knight is also a really nice guy

Professor Knight is VERY nice.  Lectures are helpful, but not necessary.  Reading the book is IMPERATIVE and you must read is carefully.  I recommend going to all quizzes even though you only need to 5;  it will help a LOT on tests.

Do not waste your time going to class.  Final grade based on 10 quizzes (only best 5 count) and two exams (which are significantly easier then the quizzes).  Going to class DOES NOT HELP.  You must read book to do well on quizzes.  Some questions are very detailed and would only be known if you really read the book.  Only about 15 out of 200 went.

He was dull. Very dull. Don't bother going to lecture, just read from book and you'll do fine. You have to read the book very carefully because that is what the exams and quizes are based upon. It was annoying because sometimes the questions would be so stupid and broad. Overall good, easy class.
Lectures directly from the powerpoint slides, you can get them from blackboard. Good to go to class to find out about extra credit opportunities.
No Comments

This teacher is very nice and understanding. He knows how to properly deal with his fellow students and teach the material.  His class is based on 10 quizes and 2 exams and you get to keep the best 5 of your quiz grades.  If you do good on the quizes you will do excellent in the class. Definitely take his class if you can!

this is a VERY boring class but it's required for business majors. he reads straight from the powerpoint slides that you can download off blackboard. don't bother going to lecture-read the book and attend discussion.

FMSC341 is the course that every student should take before graduating. The knowledge that you gain will set you on the path of financial success regardless of the income bracket you end up to be in. Professor Knight skillfully presents the material so it is digestible. Make sure you brush up on your Excel skills prior to starting this class.

Unprofessional. Took this class online. When I said I was struggling with the class he responded that I didn't study hard enough. Teacher can't take constructive criticism. Ask for discussion after tests but doesn't care about feedback. Needs to better communicate with students

He is very entertaining and does pretty well keeping your attention.  I stuggled because I don't do well in math/econ, but still managed to get a C with out putting a large amount of time into studying.  In his summer class we just had lecture and 3 tests.  You will be in class the majority of the scheduled class period. He is very helpful.
HE was a GREAT Prof. so Funny!I found the class hard b/c math is not my thing or Finance or econ major.He said if u major in one of those you'll get an A easily in the class.HE WAS GREAT!TAKE HIM!

Bill is hilarious with his jokes. He was a good teacher. He has a unique style of teaching., but it made you learned. I would recommend going to class though. I'll never forget about widgets and zercs after this class

I enjoyed this class so much with Professor Knoks! The work he gave was very reasonable and it was rather interesting. He picked a lot of good papers to read and base the homework off of. He is also really helpful and understanding and is easy to each out too. Definitely take this class with him if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I took PHIL 170 over the winter semester having to get my analytical reasoning credit out of the way.  I never expected a 100 level course to be so difficult.  Do the readings, email Knoks when you have questions and take it seriously and your work will pay off.

When starting PHIL170, I was really excited to learn more. I did really well on the first quiz and assignments (a lot of reading) and I was pleasantly surprised. However, technical difficulties caused me to drop the course and I have never had a more rude professor in my educational career. Super unhelpful and just disrespectful. Avoid at all costs

Not a difficult professor at all. I didn't particularly like the subject, but he made it a little less miserable. Not a ton of opportunity for points, but I thought his exams were pretty easy. Do not take if you hate group discussion! He loves what he teaches, so sometimes he can get a bit frustrated when you don't share that passion.
Lectures were helpful in breaking down the material. I didn't really learn much from the class. Discussions were fun. Exams didn't make any sense.

reviews.comment: This class was so stupid. The tests he gave were the most confusing things I have ever taken, despite the material begin easy. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE!

reviews.comment: Andrew is a GOD.

reviews.comment: Cool professor, easy class! Pretty light workload; got an A without an overload of work. Topics discussed are interesting too.
Great intro philosophy class

reviews.comment: If you work for it, you will pass her class. Pay attention, read, watch the movies and do the extra credit!!! P.s there are 3 take home quizzes, 1 group project and one 5 page essay.
Quizzes are impossible. Essays are also impossible. She is the toughest grader I have ever experienced. Don't ever take this class. Ever.

Knollmueler's quizzes are impossible to work through unless you have memorized every minute date and detail about any and all films mentioned in lecture, even if only in passing.  Very stuck up and pretentious about her vast knowledge of European film, and has little interest in anything else. Not eager to help students who ask for assistance.
She's cool and really knows her stuff. Just pay attention in class, watch the films, and participate in class for a good grade.

Dr. Knollmueller's quizes were impossible, even though online and with the help of google.  The papers weren't too bad, really likes your own interpretation.  She expects you to be knowledgeable about film, otherwise you won't be able to participate.  Must attend lecture- lots of info for quizzes from her speeches you wont find in the textbook!
Her quizes are incredibly specific, and incredibly difficult.  I have no idea how to do well in her class.

She was very passionate about film espically old classic hollywood films. She requires you to buy Netflixs for the class. You have to do a 5 paper film anaylsis at the end of the semester. She likes it when you speak up she requires that you do talk in class discussion just make sure you kow what your talking about. Overall Good teacher!!
Hot. Criticism on papers is very constructive. Your writing will improve. Frequent short readings from textbooks.

Not a lot of reading, maybe about an hour max before each class. Pop quizzes every week which are pretty easy. Midterm and final are quote identification and essays and are easy as well. She's very clear and responsive to emails. Overall, an easy class if you put in the time.
She is a very very hard grader...stritct with attendance to class and her voice is very very annyoing..also requires A LOT if text book reading.
Awesome professor.  Not only is she really good looking, but her class is fun, engaging, and easy to learn.  She is extremely fair and shows a lot of films to help with clarity.
Nice, fair, clear, well-organized. for a young professor she really knows what she's talking about. good balance of providing her own interpretation and leading discussion.

He's old, and he is not keeping up with technology/ new views. Don't reply email so just ask TA. Critics he thinks he's open minded and nope. I did my painting without his sug and he rated it bad. TA got mad at him a few times too. But meaning if you are good at painting it's a very easy A grade; otherwise you may want to find a better prof.

Professor Klank was an alright teacher. His lectures were confusing and hard to follow. He was very nice and always asked for feedback on the texts we would read. I would not have made it through this class without the amazing TA. Her communication was not the best, but she was very understanding and tried her best to connect with students.
He's very close minded; will shoot down your opinion if his is different. His lectures are mundane and rarely have a true topic or purpose. Couldn't recommend him less.

This guy should not be a professor. Seems to be stuck in 1970's academia in the worst way. The content could be interesting in some other universe. It's not a hard class at all, just say whatever you think he wants you to say. Poor TA.

Klank is absolutely the worst professor I've ever had. Each class is filled with tangential ramblings (and personal stories) that are supposed to say something about art but utterly fail to. If you want confusion, self-contradictions, and a professor that cuts you off whenever you challenge one of his "insightful" notions, this is the prof for you!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This man is the worst. He literally does not know what is going on in his class and the TAs do everything. If your discussion is not what he specifically wants to hear he will give your class a bad grade even though he literally doesnt ever talk about art theory in an art theory class. Clueless and would never recommend him to anyone.

This was my favorite class at UMD. Klank is open to ideas; anything you say can be true in some way. He is not a traditional professor, like he doesn't lecture with powerpoints, but gives real-life examples of concepts. The subjects of the class are not meant to be learned through traditional lectures. Easy A if you speak in discussion!

Easy way to get an A as a gen ed. Only 1 small assignment due per week, one in class exam where the TA literally goes thru the test the class before (MUST go to review session or you'll fail) and no final. Highly recommend taking. As a professor he's clueless and has no clue what's going on. The TA runs the entire class and he's a super nice guy

Professor Klank is a nice man, but a truly inept and ineffective professor. During his lectures he does not cover the material and instead opts to talk about himself and his past life for an hour and a half. Thankfully, I had a wonderful TA who taught me more in one class than Klank ever did in an entire semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is your typical white liberal man who thinks he is more woke than he is. The second you challenge one of his ideas he pretends he didn't hear you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests? Not many

reviews.comment: The class sucked my soul out. I hated it. It was difficult to understand and even more difficult to reproduce the already vague content material on the midterm exam. *Sigh* wouldn't do it again if you paid me. I only took it because I needed it for my major.

Self absorbed, arrogant, ridiculous. This class will cause nothing but stress and confusion because Klank has no idea what he's talking about, and cares more about bragging about his life, the famous people he's seen, and how great he is than actually teaching anything. The BIGGEST waste of time. UMD should be ashamed for requiring this course.
I was interested in the class, but he talks way too much about his personal life and gets upset when you don't understand the theories

The course work consists of take home examinations, midterms, papers, and frequent field trips. Overall, the class is informative if you are willing to be open minded. If you attempt to enjoy the class, the chances are you will. The teacher is understanding with deadlines and the TA's are helpful. If you make the effort you should get an A.

I took this professor for ART 150 and it was the worst waste of time ever. If I told you everything he does  wrong I would be here all day but basically if you want an easy A, go for this class. If you want to actually learn, don't sign up. He doesn't do anything but brag about himself and assigns you really tough readings. Enough said.

when you choose a seat:don't sit near the front, you'll smell something funny- believe me. This guy seems make up what he lectures about, the class is very much based on his opinion of art, meaning this is a very very subjective class. He'll treat this class like a philosophy one. Boring class, textbook use is real low- borrow instead of buy

Full of himself and such a BSer. You get the feeling that he makes up his lessons as he goes along, especially since he CONSTANTLY rants how great is. When students call him out on his misinformation, he talks over them to shut them up. His art is just terrible- he's very pretentious and this class the reason for the BS "starving artist" mentality.
I didn't get a grade for the class until about 4 months later.

Bring required reading for that week to every discussion, attend every lecture or points off-you have trillions of papers and readings, but if you have mastered the art of BS language...you can get an easy B+ to an A. I do not recommend this course though...you have to take field trips on your own time and money and do a LOT of readings.

You don't learn anything about art in the class.  He talks about his life than art but his life is interesting so sometimes lecture is fun.  The good thing is he knows he doens't stay on topic so the lecture right before the exam he literally wil read off the exam and tell you the all the answers.

I have a lot of experience with several art professors. Klank is by far the worst. I can appreciate an offbeat prof (which occurs often in this field) but Klank is just narcissistic. Not only does he not include student discussion in critiques, but he goes off on tangents on reg.He has a closed mind about art, yet believes that he's so open minded.

I've had a lot of crappy teachers, but Richard Klank is by far the worst. He is a self-absorbed moron who freely worships at the altar of his own half-baked--if that--'insights' with little regard for matters of actual interest or importance. He needs to be fired.

Klank is the worst professor I've ever encountered. When I took this class, it was more challenging because his TA had no communication with Klank. I got a A in the class, but it was like pulling teeth to get a real idea of assignment expectations. Students literally cried. He spends more time talking about his dead friends than the work.

this professor was truly out there- went on tangents ALL lecture then when he realized class was ending would try and cram in actual information he didnt discuss.  assignments were unclear and often without warning.  overall the class wasnt difficult, but a lot more stressful than need be.

1. exams dont require studying at all, the hardest question is probably "define beauty" 2. despite what people say, you dont actually have to go to musuems, just get the names of works from the internet 3. the whole class is based on participation and effort, papers arnt graded on content,they dont grade discussions,just to scare you to participate

Klank is a space case.  He lives in LaLa Land. the course material is confusing and stupid.  i regret taking this class.  Klank + the TA = utter confusion and frustration for a complete semester. consider yourself warned

I really enjoyed this class, although the material was difficult to understand sometimes. Klank is very disorganized when it comes to due dates, but none of the exams or assignments were overly difficult. Take this class only if you're very patient and interested in the why's of art and life in general. Also be prepared to do a lot of museum trips.

this guy is an idiot! he condradicts himself constantly....it not clear about due dates or assignment expectations. the syllabus is not very clear and he only worsens the situation by switching due dates and assignment guidelines from what the TA and the syllabus has said.
No Comments

Ken Klotz is a great martial arts teacher. He genuinely cares about his students, and he's great at making sure you understand the fundamentals behind each movement. His class was so fun to take every week, but you have to make sure you are practicing moves outside of class to make sure you do well on the exams.
Good learning experience.
Awesome professor! Makes class so much and he really cares about his students and what he teaches. Definitely take his class.
I really loved taking a class taught by Professor Kleykamp. She is incredibly insightful and funny. Her lectures were always interesting.

reviews.comment: An amazing teacher who really cares about her students. She made the class fun and interesting! would definitely take her again.

A good class and helpful professor. The tests are a little hard but her study guides clearly tell you what the main prompt will be. She does NOT post the slides on elms or allow people to take photos so be prepared to take notes!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: This class was a good experience. A solid choice if you need an elective. She grades fairly easily and there aren't many assignments. The exams were a bit tricky but if you start studying a couple days in advance you'll be fine. She was pretty funny and made class interesting at times.

Shes definitely difficult. Lots of homework. The curve is pretty nice, class average rounds to a b-. Take someone else if you can. Her lectures are fine, but the notes after are meaningless, and she doesn't record them.

Take her only when you absolutely have to
She doesn't do makeups, its homework heavy (adaptive quizzes and regular homework), attendance not mandatory
You might think you have studied enough for her exam but truth is you haven't
You have to re-teach yourself and practice questions constantly
TAKE THIS CLASS ONLY IF YOU HAVE NO OTHER RESPONSIBILITY

reviews.comment: Be prepared to teach all of the content to yourself outside of class. Dr. Koppel is by far the worst when it comes to explaining material. Not to mention her outside resources are useless and do not match up half of the time. Her methods are so unhelpful, she makes it hard to retain or ask anything in class because of her demeanor. I warned you :(

Her lectures are clear and the points from lecture are similar to what you are tested on. She usually does not give very detailed explanations and to ensure you fully grasp the material you need to do a lot of practice. She had a really good TA who essentially would re-teach the material to the class in a way that students could better grasp.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Success depends on your TA. The post-lab questions are extremely difficult with little direction and you have to get help from outside sources because the textbook is not helpful in that regard. The labs can be confusing and challenging. You must go to office hours if you want a good grade in this class.

I was nervous going into this class after reading reviews and registering for the six week summer session alongside the lab. However, I found Dr. Koppel to be a decent professor. The material seemed overwhelming at first, but just stay on top of things and you should be fine. The class was well organized, though beware that it is exam heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Offers a lot of outside resources and help. The class is structured in a way that the homework is due the night before the exams, there are 3. The exams are pretty much structured like her old ones so review all of those. The curve is godly. Got below a 50% on the final and the curve was about 15% for me at the end.

I think the way the whole class is set up is difficult. When doing the experiments you'll think "okay I got this" but wrong. Our TA nor professor teach us how to answer the post-lab neither does our professor so it's upsetting that we have to basically become scientists to figure out the post-labs. I'm not sure how they expect us to figure it out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This class is DIFFICULT, and its not Dr. Koppel that teaches it. Your success really depends on the TA you have and how much time you put into the lab reports outside of class. To succeed you will NEED to go to TA office hours and not be afraid to ask for help. Getting a good grade in 232 is possible but you will need to work HARD!

Dr. Koppel is not a bad option when it comes to orgo. She is a good lecturer (a little fast at times) and her exams are EXTREMELY fair. She gives you all the information you need to succeed and if you work hard outside of class it is very very possible to get a good grade. She seems to really care about her students, and I would take her again!

Not as bad as everyone says she is. It's organic chemistry so regardless of your teacher it will be difficult. Her lectures are for the most part easy to follow and she holds review sessions before exams. Tests were difficult but also fair and she gives lots of partial credit. Be prepared to study a lot. While it's difficult, it's not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The assignments and exams during this class was very hard. Even when I'd go to TA office hours for help, I would get no higher than B's on my lab assignments. The midterm and final were also very difficult.

Dr Koppel's assignments and exams are very fair, they reflect things that were taught in class and the class is curved. My biggest tip for her class is to do the past exams that she has posted and make sure you fully understand the correct answer. Her notes are unorganized and doesn't make sense so I would suggest going to class.

My advice is to do all of her old exams (to the point you think it's easy), all of the GSS review packets, practice problems, discussion packets, etc. The exams are given with the assumption you've done all these things. Listening to the lecture is only 1/5th of the understanding you will need. Good luck. Shes really tough but fair.
This was legit the worst class Ive ever taken. Grading criteria is not specific and most of the post lab questions dont pertain to what you did in lab at all. Horrible.
referred to me as the girl with the rag on her head so Im gonna go with racist.

Really not that difficult. Just gotta get all of the answers from TA's because its impossible to know what she's looking for otherwise. Like just go to multiple TA office hours to complete your postlabs. The exams suck, but again, class is curved so a decent grade is doable. Lab book is useless so you def need the TAs to carry you.

You only ever interact with your TA so just pray to get a good one. Midterm and final are difficult so make sure your lab grades are stellar. 10 labs, fair prelab quiz each class, post labs (difficult, go to office hours for help). Labs range in length and difficulty. Nice curve (averaged 85% on labs and 50% on the exams, got a B+).

Lab reports were awful, only about 2 of then actually related to what was taught in lecture. Some reports were based on irrelevant articles from 1930s. There was no reason to be taking a midterm, its only purpose was to drop students grades. Only saw the prof once when she did a review and was inconsiderate of some peoples questions and concerns.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Orgo I lab went something like this. Clutched up on all the experiment post labs (11 total), failed the final, failed the midterm, heavy curvegot an A-. The exams are very difficult and she knows it. As long as you stay just above the horrendously low averages, youll be perfectly fine.

WAY too much work for 1 credit - spent hours on this class. She realized that some TAs were showing students the answer keys, so she took the answer keys away from the TAs. How are you supposed to learn when your TA doesn't know what she's looking for? Lab manual was riddled with errors. Everything is required to be pen and paper. Not worth the $.

For a 1 credit lab, this course so excessively challenging and stressful. On top of that grading is harsh and you have to spend time going to office hours, which may be inconvenient sometimes. The lab experience wasn't that much, not as fun as I expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The work and stress is unnecessary for a one-credit class. The instructions were usually unclear and we would get contradicting answers from her vs the TAs. Clearly does not like to see students thrive and complains about low grades when we are not really being taught anything, but will also accuse you of cheating if you score "too high"

She teaches both the lab portion of orgo and sometimes will teach the lecture portion.. The labs are time-consuming, but go to your TA's office hours and you will be fine. There is a long paper at the end of the semester that she is very unclear about. The tests are multiple choice/matching and if you are relatively intelligent, you can pass
Very upbeat, helps keep you awake.  soooo much discussion, and a lot of work.

I don't recommend taking her class, unfortunately 202 is required for socy majors and she was the only one teaching it last semester..She doesn't take criticism or suggestions well, has a slight attitude problem, and expects wayyy too much for a 200 level course.

Marsh is a young and enthusiatic professor, who cracks jokes and laughs along with the class during lectures. When it comes to the course, it was very hard. There are 2 midterms, a final, a research paper, weekly labs & lecture hw,  and in-class asignments. Her grading scheme & syllabus needs serious revisal though.

She cares about students and tries to help them succeed. I feel a lot of the bad reviews come from earlier in the semester. She honestly just didn't have prior teaching knowledge to gauge where students were at, but she listened to feedback and improved. She wants you to pass and now that she's taught a class I think it'd be safe to take her again.

She's a new professor so she still trying to learn but overall she takes students' feedback and applies them. Made sure everyone passed and curved grades a lot. There are clicker questions in every class so attendance is mandatory. There are 3 exams and the final plus 3 in-class worksheets. It's not as bad if you study and go to office hours.

If I could give this class zero stars, I would. I HIGHLY RECOMMENDED NOT TAKING THIS PROFESSOR. Take Keller, or anyone else. FIRST EXAM IS STRAIGHT ORGANIC CHEMISRTY, SO IF YOU DONT KNOW THAT, THEN YOUR COOKED. She gave the worksheets out and expected you to finish them in 30 minutes while another professional let you take them home.

I had Dr. Kris Miler in Spring 2022 for GVPT170. She is an excellent professor and very nice. I would recommend her. She knows a lot about the American political system, and her lectures are good. The class was easy and informative. If you attend lectures you will get an A on the midterm and final. Dr. Kristina MIler is an excellent professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The lectures are mostly going over the reading, though they cover less than the readings do. You could probably get away with just going to lecture, though if you read the textbook and go to lecture you'll barely need to study for the exams. The exams didn't focus on too many details/memorization and were mostly important concepts.
as long as you show up to the discussion section and participate, you will be fine

Extremely knowledgeable and encourages questions in lecture (she plans buffer days in the syllabus in case questions push the lecture off schedule). Lectures are just an in-depth look at the weekly reading so you can get by with missing lecture. Its clear she cares about the subject and her students, overall a great professor and class environment
Love Miler. Her tests are kinda hard but shes a really good teacher. She loves the subject and it makes it interesting.
Miler is a good professor and her lectures are intriguing. Only two exams and two papers throughout the semester. Quizzes in discussion classes, though.

One of the most knowledgable professors I've ever had. She is incredibly enthusiastic and is usually open to questions. Great intro to politics class. You kind of need to read a lot for the tests though.
She was the best! SO understanding and tried her best to make the class interesting.
Was very understanding. Comfortable to communicate with. Provides great examples.
The class is not that hard its just very reading heavy and boring. She's super nice and understanding just a really boring class :(
She is a great professor. I truly admire how she analyzes feminist texts! It is really interesting and the workload is pretty easy.

This is a person who couldve been the Einstein of research but chose to have a family and try her best to teach the humans around her to the best they can understand. The knowledge you get is priceless and you begin to look up to her. She knows how to teach and select TAs, too. If you want your humor sharpened, pay attention to her every word.

Dr. Kramer is accomidating to her students but her lectures were very disorganized and random. Make sure to take adavnatage of the extra credit because she does not give any leiniency when final grade determination. Dr. Kramer is a very nice professor and her canvas page is very organized and she posts the lecture slides which is nice.

I feel like the other comments on this page are a bit overly harsh. There is definitely room for improvement, as with most courses, but Dr. Kramer truly works hard to try to help students. You can tell she has good intentions and wants her students to succeed.

Dr. Kramer is a pretty bad lecturer and you'll mostly learn from the online videos and find yourself doing a lot of self-teaching. Exams are completely application based with very few questions that are direct recall. Homework assignments and the online quizzes are pretty manageable, though.
Her exams are toooo long! u must come to class she takes attendance with clickers. Lab is very easy. Reading the book and teaching yourself is probably your best bet if you choose her.
Kind of confusing, but the material is not hard. I never went to lecture, but got a B just from reading the book. And lab was good.
Lectures are very disorganizing and the tests were wayyy to long!  The labs were easy, fun and it did pull my grade up after fiascos with lecture.  Should really rethink teaching

she really tries hard to explain things during lecture but it just ends up being more confusing than it actually is. the material isn't that complicated but she just has so much trouble explaining simple things in lecture. it gets really irritating but the tests aren't too bad.

She tries hard and is very approachable, but her lectures are insanely disorganized and garbled. Cannot tell if it is poor course organization or her personal poor lecture organization, but it results in easy topics becoming confusing.

Jeremy is a VERY kind professor. Whether or not you met the project criteria, he is always constructive and positive about your work. Fair warning, he can be disorganized. He dropped 2 of our 4 projects because he gave our class many extensions, and only put in grades at the end of the semester. Be prepared for that, and you'll do great. Loved him!
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really great guy and will help you outside of class. He doesn't care if you make the next best thing; he just wants you to learn. He'll even come in for extra hours if needed. Great professor and highly recommend

Jeremy Kunkel is a supper good and nice professor. He really care his students. Also, he gave us good guidance on our designs and art works. Easy class, and great professor. I would love to take another course from him, and if he taught another art course, I would definitely take it.

Jason Kuo is such a sweet professor! His classes consists of watching movies and then writing papers about them. As long as you follow the prompts you'll get a good grade. He responds to emails quickly and is understanding when it comes to late work. He is really passionate about his classes. The films were interesting as well.

Professor Kuos FILM329D online class is awesome! The movies are pretty cool and are eye openers! Grading is straightforward: watch the movies, follow directions, write the 3-5 page paper, turn it in, and boom!�� youre done. If you have any questions, Professor Kuo is quick to respond! Take the class!! Trust me!
We just watched films and then left class. He never taught or discussed the movies. There is one paper that is 60% of the grade, but he doesn't read the assignments so it doesn't matter.

Since it is only a 200-level course, the structure of the class should be simplified rather than complicated. Some of the quizzes were easy, while others were difficult to understand. He just gave us a YouTube video to watch. Final exam is ridiculously hard compared to quizzes. Avoid taking any classes with this professor.

He is an okay professor, but won't respond to your emails. If things don't make sense expect a bad grade and no help/respond from him. Put together and well organized, but material for assignments is not completely provided and points are deducted if not done well. If you dk excel don't take this course, you will struggle a lot with no help,1 exam!

Only gave us pre-recorded lectures and powerpoints for the first 9 weeks of class or so, then just gave us youtube videos to watch. Final Exam was ridiculous compared to the quizzes and everything else in the class. He seemed horribly uninterested and distant the whole class, hard to learn much of anything from this professor in this format. Avoid.
The whole Chocolate Milk Concussion thing kind of ruins everything, doesn't it?
Useless, boring class with a difficult to understand, uninterested professor. Avoid if you can.
I went into this class thinking it was going to be the hardest KNES class from shear hear say.  The truth of the matter is, it isn't hard.  KNES360 in my opinion was harder.

Professor Shim is a really good guy with a great sense of humor. The class can be very tough and confusing at times but he does his best to make it as easy as possible. You will definitely have to do a lot of work for this class, though it's more the class then the professor.
Hardest Class. Is going to keep me from graduating on time and walking this spring.
Very difficult class, No curve

Dr. Shim is a cool guy. The class is difficult if you've never had physics before. Otherwise it's pretty basic. I would recommend taking a physics class before this because it can be difficult and he even says that you should. He takes points off for wrong answers on exams and quizzes. Do well in lab because it helps your grade. Easy to get a B.

He only grades negative on the quizes, not the tests, so it's not that big of a deal. The class is pretty boring, and it's hard to pay attention b/c dr. shim talks so slow and quiet, but he's a really nice guy. the class is pretty easy as long as you put in some effort.
great teacher, easy class if you know how to do math, his problems are very basic and easy, his examples are the same as the questions he puts on his test.

This prof scores tests on a negative grading system and exceeds expected student requirements listed in course prerequisites. Average test scores are 60% due primarily due to negative grading, where every wrong answer costs you more points than if you skipped it altogether. Unapproachable, confrontational teaching attitude! Avoid him at all costs.

Very smug. I did not feel comfortable attending office hours. The discussions made you feel like you didn't really know what was going on. Will let people talk and talk and ignore students who are not extroverted. Do not worry about the big papers as long as you follow the directions.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kyle gives students opportunities to enhance their critical thinking skills by challenging their opinions on various topics and compelling them to use primary sources to further develop their arguments. He also provides helpful feedback on assignments. I would certainly recommend being in his section (for any course) again!
Just rants about whatever he wants, regardless of what the topic of the class is. Very smug.
Dr. Smead is great, but Kyle is awful.  Goes on tangents about labor and personal beliefs.  Overly difficult with grading.
Best professor I had at Maryland. tough but explains hard concepts easily. I learned problem solving skills from him.
I was really looking forward to taking this class.   Test are really freaking hard.  Never gives the answers to midterms and post solution to hw behind glass at his office.
One of the best professors I have experienced. Teaches fundamentals with easy to understand lectures.

This class was hard but this dude KY Choi is the bomb, he will make you reach for more by inspiring you to use your head well. Trust me by the end of any semester with him...You will know you did learn something.

This class wasn't too hard as a non-major. The grading is based on the rubric and the suggested content, so be sure to stick to those closely. The reading isn't really necessary, which lightens up the workload a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lengthy discussion posts that get old quickly & ridiculous quizzes that are hard to do well on. This class made me lose my marbles as the content was philosophical (as stated in the title) so be mindful of that, however, the essays weren't hard but were graded by a grad TA. The content was over my head but Kumar knows his stuff

Not tech savvy, but good lecturer. Grad TA was a hot mess. Beware of the massive group final essay. No clear instructions whatsoever. Very subjective grading. We got bad grades on our OPINION-based midterm essay if the TA didn't agree with our point of view. Not the hardest class, but just be prepared for some frustration.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: he reminds me of my dad and i miss my dad

Dr. Kumar's lectures were very interesting and easy to understand, but covered a lot of content in a short period of time. The quizzes could somtimes have questions that were worded strangely, but nothing was too difficult. The worst part of this class was by far the group project, everyone in your group gets the same grade, and groups are assigned

Decent class, Very open about his views and does not seem very open to other opinions like the other GVPT professors I've had. weekly discussions and decently hard quizzes. Overall not the worst but not good.
He was a really good professor in general, he is just super liberal though

Please don't listen to these reviews. Don't get me wrong, Dr. Kumar's class was really hard, but I would be lying if I said I did not learn a lot from it. Additionally, Dr. Kumar is funny, a good lecturer, and genuinely cares about his students. I would just step it up on your essays, he is a tough grader. Good professor tho!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Kumar is a very good lecturer. Class comprised of weekly lectures, a 400+ word discussion post on the topic for each week, a smaller individual paper, and a group final project. No midterm or final exams, only 4, 10 question quizzes. Class was very chill, but he grades sort of harshly, so make sure you step up your game on your papers.

Professor Kumar makes class lectures very interesting. He is very passionate and cracks jokes here and there. Quizzes were a bit challenging since the wording was confusing. However, if you go to class, quizzes shouldn't be so bad. You definitely have to put in work to get an A. The group project shouldn't be so bad if you get a good group.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Kumar was by far my favorite professor of the semester. His class was genuinely interesting and made students think. The grading is not unfair by any means- mostly completion of discussion then an essay, final group project, and a few 10 question quizzes. He goes over the quiz questions in class usually, lecture is necessary but not required

Honestly reading these reviews I was worried but the class really wasnt that bad. Lectures could be a bit boring but quiz questions and answers are taken directly from lecture notes. Also beware of the group project - I got screwed with my group. Despite only 2 out of 5 people doing the majority of the work, we all got the same grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: The class was super interesting, and you could tell that Kumar is really passionate about this course. As long as you attend lectures and take notes, you will do fine in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He words quizzes in a confusing way on purpose and they tank your grade if you do not do well. A lot of material comes from lecture, so definitely helps to come to class. Discussion posts and essays weren't terrible.
Lectures were engaging and low workload. Honestly dont see how people struggled in this class. Group project at the end sucks though.
Interesting lecturer who has a passion for his study

A disorganized and dense instructor who is condescending in his manner and with his approach. The topics discussed in my class were overly-complex and the tedious discussions and worksheets only made them more confusing. Save yourself the time and headache, and do not enroll in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Kumar lecturing style made the philosophical concepts more digestible which is appreciated. The course grade is heavily weighted on quizzes and a group essay. The quizzes often were written strangely which plummeted grades. The TA in charge of the group project was awful at communicating what he wanted which left people confused.

The lectures were not interesting, to say the least, but he was alright. The readings are very dense, it's a pain to get through them. The papers were awful because he didn't elaborate enough. It's just an okay class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: GVPT241 during an online semester, Kumar has a great personality and makes his lectures interesting, you can tell he really enjoys the subject matter. Did not buy a text book for this class, and did perfectly fine without it.

One of the worst professors I could have had. His lectures were dry and completely useless since the entire grade was based off of two papers and a final project. Refuses to help you improve your writing. He made a mistake grading my group's draft because he forgot what concept he assigned us and did not give points back.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: *Took this class online because of Covid. Dr. Kumar's lectures were terrible. He would ramble, not make sense half the time, and rarely took questions and when he did he usually didn't answer them well. My TA was the saving grace in this class (Youngjoon Lee) but otherwise, this prof was awful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Kumar made dry topics relatively interesting, but he was very disorganized in class, and at times it was hard not to zone out during lectures. His grading criteria was a mish-mush when it came to papers, and he was unable to provide support for disputes between the TA's.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Kumar taught an interesting class. I relied more on my TA, and other TAs, to help understand the essays/lectures. He was very hands-off, especially once class transitioned online. The essays were somewhat difficult but graded leniently. The pop quizzes were annoying, but it's a staple of some courses. Overall, you should put effort in.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Read the text to incorporate quotes into your essays and try to start the essays early. The lectures help a bit but your grade is determined by your TA. Please make sure you are following your TAs guidelines. Readings and papers are a lot just have a schedule on when to do them and youll be fine
Grade is based on the TA, but he sent out the criteria and all the TA's interpret it differently which is a problem. He always seems behind on everything and like he's not prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Kumar is the kinda of professor that lectures about whatever he wants to talk about for the first portion of class before actually covering material. His slides are typically vague but what he says is much more helpful with the essays. Most likely you will have to take him for GVPT241, really focus on what your TA wants with your essays
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He usually spent the first ten minutes or so talking about modern political issues. His viewpoints were very skewed towards one side of the political aisle. Otherwise, he made the sometimes very dense readings much easier to understand. This semester was graded off pop quizzes in discussion and papers, no exams (even before the outbreak).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He is an awful professor with a poor understanding of historical and modern day political affairs. I would definitely not recommend taking him for any government related class. At the beginning of the semester he said it was his first time teaching the course, and it showed.

I really like taking his class, Prof. Kumar taught my freshman connection block of GVPT241 and he made it really interesting. His lectures were really in depth and allowed students to discuss and give feedback as he went which was really helpful for my understanding. Although the papers are hard he gives you a lot of time to do them. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's an alright lecturer and made the dense readings much easier to understand. The biweekly quizzes were super ambiguous and posted inconsistently. The midterm and final weren't too hard and open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are so dry and boring and are basically pointless if you have done the assigned readings. Grading on exams are super weird and he takes forever to give tests back. Don't take him if you dont have to

Kumar's good for GVPT241. If you actually do the reading, you'll be just fine. I would recommend going to lecture, because there are participation activities that affect your grade. If not lecture, 100% go to discussion. Grade consists of two exams, term paper, and reading quizzes. Kumar is nice, good guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Although Professor Kumar is a passionate and nice guy, his lectures are pointless to attend. They mostly go over the quizzes (you have two a week), which he constantly either forgets to post or are all do at random times. He's very unorganized, comes to class late and rambles on all lecture. Most of your learning comes through the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: The professor is an intensely good lecturer. Not aligned with the current expectations of online organizing that most students are going to be expecting, but if you do the readings and pay attention to lecture, you'll be fine. Frankly, I can't imagine having a bad time with this professor if you actually care to learn about the subject.

I had a terrible negative experience with this professor. He was not very clear with his lectures and would not stay on topic. He barely used PowerPoints to teach so that made it hard to take notes in his class and catch what he was saying. Not to mention he was pretty condescending and rude. Save your time and energy and don't take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor is very passionate and knowledgeable about his field. While he is knowledgeable he was disorganized, went too quickly in lecture by jumping around a lot, and never kept up with putting in grades which made it hard to know where you needed to improve. He did not put grades in online and just gave you a final grade on overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. is a nice guy, and seems to care about his students. He is extremely passionate about what he teaches and studies. However, he was extremely disorganized and never gave any clear grading expectations. His feedback was not very clear, and he hardly updated canvas. If you are not passionate about this area of history, I do not recommend.

He is very disorganized and moves from one topic to the next. There are a lot of readings to do with discussions. He gives out A's for them usually. He is extremely strict with no phones in class. Exams are not that bad and the research paper takes some effort but is doable. There is a lot of information to learn so it is important to go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
He is very knowledgeable about his content; to put it simply, he is a teacher who forgets he is teaching ADULTS who don't know much about the subject matter.

He moves from subject to subject in his lectures without checking for understanding. He tries hard to be helpful and understanding, but that is only 1/2 of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof is passionate about the course content but the is very disorganized, as are his lectures. Graded discussions were posted at 10pm and implied to be due the next class, he only started giving concrete due dates after half the semester. Most of the difficulty comes from following the prof's lectures and assignment schedule rather than content
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Do the reading. He isn't the most organized professor, but this is college, you have to be prepared to pick up the slack. He is incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about South African history. He incorporates the music of South Africa into the class and the final paper gives room for creativity.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: I dropped his course after 2 classes. He seems to be a nice guy, but his lecture style and powerpoint slides were the most incoherent ramblings I've ever experienced. I honestly could not believe I was in a college level class, and I wasn't able to take a single thing away from either of the lectures I attended. So glad I escaped.
There is a lot of reading assigned, and you will need to come prepared to discuss it. His class is interesting, and he definitely wants students to learn. Gives good feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read
