reviews.comment: He was so passionate about South Africa, I took his class knowing nothing of South Africa's History and at the end I learned so much and enjoyed learning it. Although his quizzes are simple, if you didn't take notes in class or even at least skim the readings you might struggle but he is always willing to work with you. Participation matters!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Extremely knowledgeable on South Africa. Some heavy reading was required for this class, but professor always willing to work with you if a concept needs clarification.
The class is very interesting and it keeps you intrigued because the topics switch ever week or two.  Landau is also a pretty fair grader which makes the class better

He has good expectations for his class, explains things well and is understanding. He doesn't allow electronics and I highly reccommend being on time. The material is somewhat challenging and there is alot of reading but, he welcomes questions and encouraged us to visit him at his office.Do the readings and engage in class and you will do fine.

I'm smart so I have no problem with his course. If you're intellectual capacity is limited, however, Landau is not the professor for you. Landau does not use power points and expects his students to derive their own interpretations from lectures. In my opinion, he has fair expectations and is a strong lecturer.

Professor Landau has a roundabout way of lecturing - he wants you to "make connections" between the lectures. Many people found him confusing. Personally, I understod his lectures better than most but I don't think I would have gotten an A if not for the great TA that semester, Chas Reed. Exams were moderately hard; short answer and several essays.

this guy comes on strong. He hates cell phones or electronics of anykind. One guy was texting during a lecture (in a big room) and dude comes right up behind the kid and askes what he is doing, tells him to put it away and to see him after class...in front of everyone! This was like week 2 of class. hes tough-actin', but takes himself too serious.

Best accounting teacher I've ever had. He teaches in humor way, so we never get bored. He is willing to help students when they need help. If you try to work hard, you will get A for sure. I highly recommend Prof. CK.
Happy happy everyday
Best professor ever!

I love Dr. Schnitker!!! Not only were her lectures extremely interesting, I also think that the assignments for the class were pretty straightforward and easy enough to understand and do well on. Loved being in her class :)

she was really awesome. I'd totally take her class again. Her lectures were easy to follow on, often was able to connect material to her students. The exams were relatively easy. Make sure to go to the discussion classes bc of the weekly quizzes based on very short readings. I often only spent like 10 minutes on readings. Super flexible class.

Loved this course! Exams were very easy if you took notes on lecture. Slides are posted online after class so attendance really is not mandatory. The weekly quizzes in discussion are equally easy if you did the readings. Only word of advice, start early on the papers so you can get as much direction as you need before you are too deep!

Although Professor Schnitker's exams are fair, you must know every topic that she tells you to review in order to do well on them. The weekly quizzes are basically free points if you do the assigned readings. START EARLY ON THE PAPERS!!!! If you put in the effort for this course, you should come out with a solid grade.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor was actually very rude to me and my fellow students. A few times I reached out to her and asked to meet for extra help and she was not willing to help me. She was also really passive-aggressive about showing up to class and looking at the screen. She would come at kids for being on their phones. Professors get Fs too...

Disregard these other reviews, I feel like this professor gave pretty good lectures but if you fail/get a bad grade on one assignment you're screwed. You are only really graded on a few assignments and this past semester the TA I had Jessica was awful and extremely unfair. The TAs grade everything so make sure you have a good TA or switch sections.

Kind and sweet lady. Easy A. No extra credit and you're only graded on a few things. Exams were fairly easy, weekly quizzes were even more easy. First paper was about 3 pages, final paper was about 5-6 pages. She gives amazing lectures and helpful exam reviews. There is a clear political bias in the class but her lectures are enjoyable

Musc 215 is such a cool class, I cannot recommend it enough!! Dr. Schnitker's lectures are really interesting. The only homework is to read one thing per week for a 5 question multiple choice quiz every Friday. There are also some papers but they're not too bad; one literally requires you to go to a concert!

This class was really awesome. I recommend anyone to take it as it opens your eyes to how music connects to identity. The professor kept lectures interesting and you get to discover artists that you've never heard of before. There isn't that much work to do. There are two semester papers that can be graded a bit tough, so you gotta start them early
Knowledgeable professor, great lectures, and accessible TAs made this class one of my favorite classes at UMD. You can tell she is very passionate and well-prepared in each class.

As a business major, this was a very interesting class which provided deep analysis of music history and terminology without being overwhelming to those without prior experience. Dr. Schnitker gives off the impression that she cares about her students and does everything to make quizzes/ essays as straightforward as possible. Interesting and fun!

A good professor overall. However, the two papers were kind of annoying and also get graded a bit harshly. They were two lengthy (3-4pg. &5-6pg) papers which were a bit too much on top of a midterm and a final. Weekly quizzes are on the assigned readings. TAs grade everything. Professor only lectures. Highly not recommended to take ENGL101 & this.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good professor and would recommend to anyone in need of an elective. The only issue was papers were annoying and there's weekly quizzes which were the only way to get good grades outside of papers and two exams. Other than that, good professor overall
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Her lectures are always interesting as she modifies them regularly to fit the current music trends, but she balances this with the important historical facts too. Slides are available online, but go to lectures; they're so engaging and inspirational. Also brings in guest lecturers to some units for a cool perspective from someone of that culture.

She's a great lecturer, and this class itself was taught very well by her. Reading quizzes every week in discussion but they're pretty self-explanatory. Lectures are posted on ELMS, so missing class is not the end of the world.
She's nice enough but she has some pretty clear political bias . The class is petty easy if you show up to discussion and lecture.

This is one of the best gen ed classes to take by far! I really looked forward to go to her lectures every week because she kept the information and teaching style interesting. As long as you take notes and have somewhat of an interest in any music, you'll love this class! :)

this was my favorite class by far. Lectures are very interesting and she breaks them up by having music and videos. As long as you take notes in lecture you will do fine. quizzes every friday are super easy, and the papers are not difficult. if you need a gen ed definitely take it

Recommended MUSC215 to all of my friends. The class is fascinating if you have even a small interest in music history. Laura really knows her stuff and gives great lectures, the TAs were also really cool. Show up to lecture and discussion, give yourself a week to polish each of the two papers, easy A.
Laura just does lectures. The TAs grade all of your assignments. Attendance mandatory for discussion.

One of the best professors I've had! Really good at presenting material in an interesting way. Would for sure recommend this gen ed with her. Quizzes are easy if you do the readings, but they can get tedious. Grading on papers can be a little harsh, so you do need to start before the night before. Go to discussion and lecture if you want an A.
So good

The lectures are unclear, and it seems he does not always know what he is talking about. He is also not the kindest to students in class; he will kick you out of class for talking or using your phone. Also, will change due dates for the day of, and not give students grace when doing so.

I have never written a review for a professor in my entire life, but this is worth it. Do not be fooled by Planet Terp reviews. Presenting in front of this professor is awful, you will do your work, present and STILL feel like an !diot. Be prepared to be questioned while presenting. If you are shy/bad at presenting, this class is not for you.
Confusing lectures combined with complex assignments made this class more difficult than it needed to be when compared to other professors.

Throughout the semester he struggled to articulate many concepts to the class and on many occasions it was apparent that no one in the classroom knew what they were doing. The mid-term was extremely difficult and had no relation to the practice exam. Also had to go to every class because of the pop-quizzes. Overall, would advise to avoid him.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This teacher and class are amazing I recommend it to all my friends. The content of the course is really well organized and the topics are very interesting. It can be a bit of work at times but the topics are so interesting its worth it. The teacher is so nice, funny, passionate about what she is teaching, and interacts well with the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: She is very sweet and a nice caring person, but her class was a lot of work for a Gen Ed. She is funny and the topic is entertaining, but there was so much reading...
A great professor who cares about the student a lot. Late grader, but very kind and easy to talk to. Great reading materials but stay on top of them. Very participation based.

Sina cares a lot about her students and isn't afraid to share her own life stories during class or make dirty jokes. I wouldn't take the class if you're shy and don't like participating because the whole class is discussion-based and participation is 200pts. She also waits until the end of the semester to grade everything which is really annoying.

She was a really great professor who cared about her students and was incredibly passionate about the material which made the whole class experience great. Some weird grading practices but keep up with the assignments and you'll be fine.

Sina was an amazing professor. She created a very intimate and discussion-based atmosphere and positive learning environment. Really took the time to get to know her students. I loved her class so much and the readings she assigns are so interesting. Not the fastest grader, but an amazing professor and person!
Seems to not understand when students ask questions and never reply to emails.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: She speaks with an accent, but she's really not that difficult to understand. Lots of extra credit opportunities, and out-of-the-box assignments. Generally likable and approachable. Downsides are a disorganized and sometimes confusing elms/canvas page, and never knowing if she'd be a lenient or harsh grader. Overall really liked her.

She seemed nice at first but then things became really weird and she was irritated by everything. There is a lot of readings but the topics were interesting. She grades everything at the last minute so she doesn't have to talk to people about their grades.

The class is pretty much self-taught. Hence the reading. She barely speaks English. She is fake nice. She waits until the end to grade so she can hide behind her computer. She gives busy work throughout the semester. She does have her favorites though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Don ever take that course. It was one of the most tedious classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment:
Professor London is so tuff and she is the best professor ever in the whole wide anthropology world!  

You would be so lucky to take her class! Just don't be mean.

I took her for 3 different classes and she's consistently one of the best teachers I've ever had. She has amazing stories. She encourages you to participate and expects you to.  She grades fairly. She's brutally honest. She's always available for help or advice. Definitely take her if you can!

She's a real sweetheart. She does only talk about herself during her lectures but they're really cool cases that she's been on. There are 8-9 "labs" that are actually activities per semester and you have to write about 2 pages on 5 of them. Her TA grades super easy. There are 2 unit exams. Final exam is the third unit exam, all very easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher! Make sure you read her powerpoints for test and participate during class. She is willing to help and has a clear grading criteria. Pretty easy course!
Superb class, superb teacher.

Professor Sefton, if you're reading this shoutout to you. I took your class this semester and you really showed us all the love and passion you have for what you teach. If anything it might've rubbed off on me, and as someone who really doesn't enjoy going up to speak infront of people that says a lot. Personal, likable, and funny, keep it up!

In my opinion, she is an exceptional professor who consistently offers assistance whenever required. There have been various instances where her guidance during office hours proved invaluable in clearing up all of my uncertainties. Despite coming across reviews criticizing her grading style as overly strict, I disagree.

Very passionate, engaging, and material we learn is useful outside the class. She is approachable and makes the class a comfortable environment. Her rubrics are clear and she gives reminders of assignments several times. We had a lecture on psychology which I really appreciated and enjoyed. Very available for office hours, I highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Sefton is a great prof. to choose for INAG110, the toughest part was writing speeches and then presenting them which is something you'd get in any INAG110 class. Only 4 speeches overall, so very little required public speaking if thats something you hate. She is caring and gives great feedback.

Dr. Sefton is a great teacher not only in terms of being caring and funny, but she is very clear with what is expected from students so there is no room for confusion. She also answers emails in a timely manner keeping lines of communication with students open. I also tend to enjoy making the required creative visual aids in this class.

Dr. Sefton was a great teacher and knows what she is doing when it comes to public speaking. Although she was a tough grader she gave great feedback and acknowledges when you improve. She genuinely cares about her students and was very reachable. The workload was manageable but you definitely have to work for your grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Sefton makes an a big effort to see all of her students succeed. She gives good feedback on assignments and has clearly laid out expectations for all of them. She delivered all information in a great way. I would definitely recommend her as a professor!

Very good professor! Truly cares about her students. If a shy or more quiet type, class may be challenging (it's COMM), but not impossible. Makes clear that she can help with presentation preparation and is widely available, creates a friendly class environment. Professional, good expectations for class, prepares you well for the working world.

Great professor! There are 4 types of speeches, but Dr. Sefton does a really good job of making the expectations clear and giving you everything you need to succeed.  Dr. Sefton is always willing to help students with their speech outlines during office hours, so take advantage of that! Overall this class really helped me become a better presenter!
Throughout the semester there are 4 presentations. There is one paper and 2 exams. This class helped me build confidence in public speaking. Overall, this class wasn't bad.

She is AMAZING! She goes above and beyond when giving feedback. She really cares about her students and covers everything that will be on tests. She is not a harsh grader, just turn things in on time and you'll be fine. I learned so much and I am a much more confident speaker. I genuinely enjoyed her class and wish she taught other courses!

She is an incredibly nit-picky grader which causes what you'd think is an easy-A, comm credit, to become a complete nightmare. Although she is informative when you ask her questions, but the lectures only really help you on the small assignments and not the big-pointers that really pull your grade. Overall, would not take with her again.
This is a terrible professor. She is way too strict about grading for a gen ed. No late work accepted under any circumstance. Take any other professor.

Dr. Sefton is a great professor. After the first week, I thought that she was going to be very strict and not terribly student-friendly, but I was wrong. She truly cares about her students and will do whatever she can to help them succeed. I would certainly recommend taking any course that she teaches.
Great professor! Would HIGHLY recommend!!!!

I can't stress this enough: if Dr. Sefton is available, take it! You will receive an automatic A if you complete your assignment and show up to class.  I got an A on both the midterm and final exams after only 30 minutes of studying. She tells you all you need to know about the exam, and it's quite easy. 10/10 class would definitely take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lori is very harsh on her students and is a very hard grader. I would not recommend signing up a class taught by her. She is not a good communicator either. Many other options go with one of them.

she was not a good professor. She was not sensitive or empathetic to my serious injury despite me showing her several doctors notes and notes from ADS. I required surgery and she did not give me any lecture notes or time/ help to catch up. I am physically unable to walk and have been given many university excused absences. Still had no help.

She's a great professor! However, she is not very empathetic. I came to her to tell her how I have 3 final exams on the same day and it was all back-to-back and to allow me to please let me take it in one of the makeup days. My mental health was declining just because of the many exams I had to study for. All she said was no. Don't expect niceness.

She is very passionate about her field and it shows in her teaching. She truly cares about making lectures enjoyable and ensuring we understand all the information. Make sure you show up for lectures. It's a lot of info but anatomy isn't supposed to be easy so just do the studying. Awesome professor

Dr. Lombardi is great! She cares about her students and makes lectures enjoyable. She explains really well and even records her lectures for students who can't make her class. She is one of my favorite professors here at UMD and recommend taking her!

Dr. Lombardi is great, and it's easy to fall into a flow for her class. She is also extremely smart and passionate, though sometimes that translates as her lectures being extremely fast. Be prepared to have to re-watch the recordings to verify what she said. Overall amazing teacher though, for both anatomy 1 and 2. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Lombardi is probably the best professor to take a class like anatomy with. She has interactive lectures so they aren't boring. She gives great analogies as well. She does go really fast so I recommend taking notes on the lecture before class and then taking notes on what she says during the lecture. Her exams are pretty in depth.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: literally best professor I love this women. Her exams are so straightforward and if you know the information from the slides you'll literally get a 100%. if you have to take anatomy take lombardi

I really enjoyed this class and Dr. Lombardi! She was very informational, and I feel like I've learned a lot. You definitely don't need to know anything about science or economics to do well. Dr. Lombardi does talk very fast when she lectures, but the lectures are recorded so you can go back if you missed something.

Dr. Lombardi's course is everything you need to know about basic anatomy and physiology without going into crazy hard detail. She is an entertaining lecturer, a kind person, and an incredibly knowledgeable professor. I highly recommend jumping into one of her sections if you find a seat.

This is my second A+ in Lombardi's anatomy class & I did it by taking VERY detailed notes on each lecture and attending GSS. She explains hard concepts very well and truly wants you to learn. This class isn't hard if you put the work in, but can be time-consuming. Lab is more physiology-based than 201 was so you really have to know your stuff

Dr. Lombardi clearly knows what she's talking about and gives detailed analogies so that everything makes sense. Lab is synchronous, lecture is not. Make sure you take notes on what she says. I took DETAILED notes (she talks so much too) and found the open-note exams to be very easy since the answers were literally right there. GSS is very helpful!
While this class was difficult at times, Dr. Lombardi tried to make her lectures as concise and easy to understand as possible. She is clearly a very smart woman who really knows her stuff.

Lombardi's a great choice, taken during covid online. Lecture's are uploaded asynchronously every week and need to take notes to do well. Tests are really hard and timed. She's great and the TA was great too. You have to attend lab synchronously so choose a good time. Overall a really great choice, super educational and a great teacher.

Goes fast but her analogies are helpful. Tests are somewhat difficult but if you put the work in and pay attention you'll do fine. The textbook is helpful in studying concepts. Some assignments during lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great, great professor. The content is definitely a lot harder than in her BSCI 201 class but if you study for them, they are quite straightforward. My biggest struggle with the class is that she gets so passionate that she talks too fast and you miss really important information.

Prof. Lombardi is very nice and passionate about anatomy. She knows so much about it and is clearly an expert. Lectures are clear. She does not post panoptos and she tests on things she says outloud that sometimes aren't in the slides, so just go to class. Print the slides to write on in class bc she talks too fast to write everything.

Lombardi is a good professor but I wouldn't say her lectures are AMAZING as others are. I have friends who have taken O'Brien who performed much better. Lombardi doesn't record lectures and gives little to no study material. Tests are very very specific. She is a brilliant woman who knows her stuff. But having her didn't make or break anything.

The ecology part of this class is much more interesting than the economics. She's a very clear lecturer and the midterm was very reasonable. TAs graded more harshly than they needed to though. Slides don't always have all of the information, so it's good to go to lecture but not necessarily mandatory. I would take her again for other classes.

Lombardi is a great lecturer! That's super important in anatomy because there are 5 million different things you have to learn. The hard part about this class is the lab which is worth 40% of the grade. Got to memorize so muchhhh. But, it's the same for other anatomy classes so, if you have to take anatomy then Lombardi is the best option by far.

I loved Dr. Lombardi for 201! I'm retaking her for 202. She is very passionate in her lectures. It makes the hour and fifteen minutes go by pretty quickly. Her tests are straight forward--mostly application questions you reviewed in lecture, so make sure to go! Attendance isn't mandatory, but she does give random participation assignments in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Okay so BSCI201 is not an easy class and you will have to study as most people can expect but Dr. Lombardi is an amazing lecturer, she does speak fast but the content is solid and if you record the lecture and listen to it later it helps, but honestly she is a good lecturer and she pieces things together well.

Anatomy and physiology is a ton of information, however she makes it very interesting. She talks a bit fast so I recorded her lecture but overall this course can be very easy if you study, watch videos, and etc. Always did good on exams, always aced quizzes in lab. Lab is solely memorization.

Dr. Lombardi teaches a hard topic, but her enthusiasm makes lecture interesting. Her tests require a good amount of studying, but she is fair. The lab makes up almost half of your grade and memorization of pretty much everything is required to get at A but is manageable if you use the study guide. Effort is required but an A is possible.

The lectures had a lot of information, but were very interesting. We do group activities and this helps with understanding. Her tests are a little tricky with the multiple choice questions she asks because they are not so straightforward.

This class was super easy. Study and memorize the material and you will be fine. Some exam question are a bit tricky, like she is trying to confuse you. She gives lots of extra credit, but it always felt like I had exams because there were 3 exams and 3 practicals, so a total of 6 exams before the final. Make quizlets it really helps!

Professor Lombardi is great! Super kind and approachable. Good lectures. She taught the first half of AREC200 which was the ecology part. The midterm was pretty easy and we had a helpful study guide. Not a difficult class if you have any background in science or economics. I recommend Lombardi!
Tests were very fair. Memorize everything.

Her lectures are interesting and she posts powerpoints that I would follow along with during class. Take detailed notes and make sure you understand the concepts. She replies to emails quickly and was an absolute amazing teacher. Her classes fill up quickly!

There are few extra credit opportunities like surveys, drawing assignment and some in within the exams. Her lectures are clear, interesting and memorable. She actually helps you understand physiology and retain information.

I love her so much. Honestly, she is only a handful of professors that actually care about her students and want the only the best for them. Lectures are very interesting and she uses a bunch of pictures and diagrams that really help when trying to understand how the body works. I wouldn't mind taking her class again, shes that good.

Dr. Lombardi is passionate and encourages student involvement in the class. The midterm was very easy and even had some extra credit questions. The final was written by the other professor though (Holzer). There was no textbook, but just a few readings which were posted on ELMS. Minimal effort for an A.

Lombardi is a great professor. The best anatomy professor on UMD campus. Everything on her exams, she says in class. So if you miss class then that's on you. She gives extra credit and is very clear in class of what she expects.

I really liked her and the material is straightforward, but her exams are really hard. If you study hard and really grasp the concepts, then it is easy to get an A. She gets really specific on exams, so know all of the information. She offers extra credit on her exams and outside extra credit to help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I'm just here to confirm that she is a great teacher, she was straight forward. Also she gives tons of extra credit that are included on all her exams (4 including final). I think the straight forward part and the test coming straight from the slides and lecture notes taken in class is what makes her an amazing. Take her!

She was really passionate about Physiology.  All her lectures were pretty clear, so the tests were basically straight from the lectures.  But, you really have to study since there are only 2 midterms & 1 final.  She also gives you tips that help in lab.  I totally recommend her!

Loved A&P with Dr. Lombardi! It doesn't get more straightforward than with her; her organization and clarity are impeccable. Go to every lecture, take notes on everything she says that isn't on the slides, and study, and you'll get an A or A+ (at least in the lecture portion of the class) with little difficulty. She frequently gives lab tips, too!

Dr. Lombardi teaches a hard class with hard material but makes it very engaging and often does interactive activities to keep you interested. She's funny, enthusiastic, and really wants to help you learn. You still have to study a lot to do well, but she does everything she can to help you memorize.

Professor is clear in grading expectations and encourages lecture participation. Tests/quizzes are very reasonable, and he offers helpful study guides. Lectures are interesting and he makes his content personable and relatable. Attendance-wise, if you miss the checkins in class, it will affect your grade.

Great prof!! During lectures, there were check-in assignments that were not difficult at all and he went over them as well. 2 exams and 1 non-mandatory final were not too bad and he allowed a cheat sheet. He clearly knows and cares about what he's teaching and is very caring and accommodating towards his students!!

Literally can not say one negative thing about Prof Doan. Sweetest, most accommodating guy ever and genuinely understands that students have lives outside of class, other classes to worry about, etc. Class is not very demanding - you'll get an A if you answer the 3 questions he asks each class and the exams, which he allows a cheat sheet for

Great professor. Readings were a bit boring for a while. Mid-semester class got very interesting and interactive. He grades pretty leniently and offers chances to improve your grade. He is well-respected and very informed on sociology. Definitely one of the better professors in the department

Professor Raschid goes out of her way to make sure you finish your work with an understanding of the topics. I am finishing up BMGT402F with her right now and she has been beyond helpful OUTSIDE of class to assist me when I am struggling. I will say that some instructions are unclear on assignments, but if you ask questions, she will guide you.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: by far one of the worst professors. she may be intelligent but she doesnt know how to teach and shes incredibly rude and condescending
useless course; horrible professor; no respect for students; minimal knowledg of the subject
She's very chill and lenient with grades.

I just finished my last class for Dr. Lucas. She is a really easy going professor. She definitely became one of my favorite teachers I've had so far. Although we did not really use the textbook, she still incorporates the main ideas in her presentations. Overall, she is great at giving feedback and providing comfort to those presenting.

One of my favorite professors this semester. She really cared about her students' success and was wiling to be flexible. She is a very easy grader, but still helps students learn and improve with each presentation. As a business major, I liked how she combined communications with the business world. Would definitely recommend taking her class.
Great professor. Really cares about her students. If you put effort in you will get an easy A.
She is pretty average. She's not the greatest teacher I've ever had, but she leads some good discussions and is interesting enough. Not a super hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Melissa Lucas is incredibly annoying and unqualified as a teacher. She doesn't know how to plan a class and relies too heavily on students to basically lead the class for her.  She is incapable of giving useable feedback on assignments and she is unwilling to work with students to improve. I would strongly recommend not taking her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Because of her class, I am now pursuing a communication major. She was very friendly. I recommend that you take the time to get to know her. When I had concerns about grades and what was expected of me, she was able to give me useful advice. She's a fair grader and I highly recommend her!

Her exams are not related to what she talked about in lecture, and she thinks everyone is communication major Wouldn't take her again ever Also she moves her hands in a wierd way when she lectures which drove most of us crazy wouldn't recommend her

A very engaging and personable professor, also very fair, allowed me to submit a final paper past the due date because of personal tribulations, he is very understanding and easy to approach. He creates a very welcoming environment in his classes, and is probably one of the most human professors I have ever met. I took Eng395.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class was very interesting and the material was relevant to current events. Lucci was a great and funny professor. He always advocated for mental health and encouraged you to take time on your assignments. He is also very understanding if you regularly participate in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lucci is the best professor I've ever had! As a person struggling mentally during the semester, he was very caring and accommodating if you talked to him. He had student-teacher conferences, and he goes over your paper with you so you learn from your writing. Discussion was a big part of class but they were fun to participate in! I recommend!!

I really liked Mr. Lucci's teaching style and his emphasis on writing about contemporary social justice issues. He makes his expectations about assignments really clear in class, but is friendly and open to addressing individual student concerns. He also gave donuts at the end of class :)

It was awesome learning Science Writing under Mr. Lucci. I think what really sets him apart from other instructors is not only his flexibility, but his ability to adapt to student demands and concerns. He goes above and beyond in his teaching by hosting several individual student conferences a semester to discuss his feedback on major assignments.

Lucci has been the best English prof ever! He offered many one-on-ones and helped guide me to write my paper. I really liked how he helped prep your writing for real-world situations, which it really is different from school writing. He doesn't give busy work like I've experienced in English courses in the past, so definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably the worst professor I have had. I was excited to finally take professional writing but you won't learn a thing with this dude. He doesn't even know what he is teaching himself and he does not give rubrics HHAHA. Not only that, you do not get any feedback (in an English class....?). Extremely hard to meet with him outside of class too.

Professor Lucci literally does not know how to teach. He gives lectures that have almost nothing to do with upcoming assignments and never gives rubrics and then gives out random grades. He is hard to meet with outside of class as well. I highly recommend you don't bother taking any of his classes.
Laid back class. Professor assigns useful and practical assignments and provides constructive feedback.

Prof. Lucci was great! Despite the many summaries, peer reviews, and papers we had to do, I enjoyed the class. He really emphasizes revision so, going to office hours is really pivotal to getting a good grade. The final was a paper in which you chose the topic you wanted to argue. So, pretty easy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: OMG. Professor Lucci is hands down one of my favorite professors ever. I'm not an English major, but after his feedback and teaching I feel like I could be. He is so caring, he always reaches out to the students to make sure they know he is there to help with anything. He always puts into consideration students are human too taking a lot of classes

Hands down Lucci is one of the most enjoyable and memorable professors I have had. Very sweet and understanding, is very easy to communicate with, and makes really good conversation! My class was particularly small, and Lucci was able to facilitate a lot of really cool discussions. I really appreciate his passion for education and his patience.

Prof. Lucci was an absolutely awesome English teacher for my freshman year. He gives clear and in depth feedback and is super laid back when it comes to giving more time for assignments IF you let him know that you need it. Overall a great teacher to have, make sure you ask for clarity if you need it and be prepared to do weekly readings (textbook)
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Delayed almost every paper by at least a week

Participation and effort really matter in this class. Its less about the specifics of your work but more that you come to class and actively try to learn- as long as you show up and follow rubrics and take feedback, youll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy, but he only lectures and assigns A LOT of papers.
Was the actual best. Thought writing wasn't my strong suit but he thought I was great and pushed me to be better and was so chill. Very understanding and we watched so many John Oliver videos.
Extremely nice guy. Gives good feedback and loves his students.

Loved having him as a professor. Very considerate about students doing well in class. Does assign some readings every once in a while, and he makes sure of going over them in great detail. Still regret missing the last lecture of the semester when he gots donuts for us :p

Takes attendance every class. Papers are graded easily and he gives you a lot of extra time to complete them. Great instructor, would take again. Likes you to participate, but if you don't you won't get penalized. Does give a some reading and sometimes goes over them, sometimes doesn't. If he does, he expects you to participate or he'll give a pop.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment:
+ engaged with students
+ tests are well written and reflective of material
+ writes on chalkboard which is beneficial to intuition

Dr. Lumi references her slides while speaking but does not show them on the projector. Instead, she uses the slides as a skeleton to her lectures and writes everything on the chalkboard. Good for intuition!

Professor Stevens' class was one of the best classes I have taken. There is a lot of work for this course, however, she makes sure that you understand each concepts clearly. She explains things VERY well. The exams were based on more mathematical concepts, so you'd have to make sure that you are very confident in your math abilities.
An amazing professor! Her class is not easy, but you learn a lot. Go to lecture and study and its very possible to succeed! She's very accomplished and a cool person overall.

Terrible lecturer, doesn't know how to be there for her students, makes the exams unbelievably long and doesn't give enough preparation for exams. she was gone the week before our exam and the poor ta had to do all the work. unfit professor.

Prof. Stevens is an outstanding lecturer and human being. Extremely approachable, VERY knowledgeable, and overall I felt smarter just by listening to her talk. Take your Macroeconomics class with her-you won't regret it. Tests are hard, but that's true for all ECON325 classes.  5 stars for singlehandedly inspiring me to continue studying economics.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Delegate Luedtke had the most enjoyable lectures to attend. He really cares about making people excited about public policy. His grading is pretty easy but the rubric is not always clear.

Super nice dude who is down to Earth and interacts with his students. He does great lectures and is super engaging. Grades consist of 3 essays totaling 50% which you have more than 1 month per essay and are easy.  20% Midterm and 20% final which is known to be easy. 10% participation which is never checked because he does not grade attendance.
Super good lecturer, class is very engaging, highly recommend this class even if you're not a policy major.
This man is literally GREAT. I had an 88 in the class and he rounded it to an A-.. bless him
Keeps the class engaged, up to date on current events and cares for his students. Definitely take this course.

Amazing professor, his lectures always feel like a Ted Talk in a way that they are extremely engaging. Would absolutely recommend. There is a heavy emphasis on readings and papers, but the class is so good that it's not an issue.

Luedtke is a state Delegate and I can't think of anyone better to teach this course. He's funny and engaging and makes public policy interesting. This course gives a broad overview of the many aspects of policy and Luedtke clearly has a depth of knowledge and experience that he's happy to bring to and share with the class.

Easily my favorite Professor so far. His lectures are amazing and you can tell that he has experience purely from the way he talks about politics and explains what he knows. The only difficulty in class comes from the few graded assignments, but as long as you do your work, you're fine. Last point, he is hilarious and genuinely cares for students.

Great Professor. Had him for PLCY201 and 100. Lectures were interesting and he was very personable, and class was an easy A as long as you studied somewhat for quizzes and fulfilled all the requirements for essays.
Great professor and does a great job at explaining policy problems in an interesting and engaging way.

I really loved Professor Luedtke's class. He took what could have easily been a dry, boring class and made it into one the best classes I've ever taken. I think that the readings he chose were genuinely interesting and useful.

One of the best professors I've had. Prof. Luedtke truly cares about his students and the material he is teaching. He makes class fun and engaging. Make sure you start your papers ahead of time because they are kind of long. Participation is super important and part of your grade. Take this class it is great for everyone.

Professor Luedtke is an amazing professor and person. His class is entertaining and he keeps it interesting. His class consists of writing two papers, five quizzes, participating at least once a week, and a midterm/final. It is easy to get an A as long as you do the readings and pay attention in class. Best professor Ive had so far :)
He was the best professor that I have ever had at Maryland. His experience as a politician genuinely aids the class. I would take all of his classes if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Honestly, Eric is the best professor you could ever ask for. He made a class that could have easily been boring and dry, filled with readings and papers, but instead, he made it discussion-based and entertaining. The class is an easy A as long as you pay attention in class and do the work.
Eric is truly an inspirational leader, definitely wanted to come to class and was excited to learn

ERIC IS AN AMAZING PROFESSOR. HE IS EXTREMELY APPROACHABLE AND IS VERY RESPONSIVE TO EMAILS. PARTICIPATION AND ATTENDANCE ARE IMPORTANT AS THERE ARE 5 POP QUIZZES (HE TELLS YOU THIS AT THE BEGINNING OF THE SEMESTER), BUT HE TEACHES IN A WAY THAT MAKES YOU WANT TO BE INVOLVED IN DISCUSSIONS. HIGHLY RECOMMEND AND EASY A WITH MINIMAL EFFORT.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Eric is an awesome guy with a big heart for education. In terms of course material he is very straightforward and teaches to the quizzes and tests. I thought that some of his lectures were bias toward his political party (he is a politician) but I think he knows this and does his best to refrain. Great class, easy A.

In the beginning, Eric was friendly and inclusive, making all new students very comfortable in the college setting. However, as the class went on it seemed that he became less and less prepared and made stuff up on the spot, making it hard to study and prepare for quizzes and exams. If you dont do the readings you will struggle but wont fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: This class could have easily been dry but Eric made it lively and interesting! He is down to earth, cares about his students, and easily one of my favorite professors that I've had at UMD.

Eric is such a great professor who brings his experience as a MD Delegate. The readings are manageable and he assigns two papers which focus directly on the course content. My class was seminar styled, so it's important to do the nightly readings in order to know what's up. Very nice, funny & respectful, and easily accessible outside of class.

I loved this course. Eric Luedtke, a state delegate, has a wealth of knowledge on the subject from his own experiences. He genuinely cares about his students and wants everyone to do well. I encourage anyone who has the opportunity to take a course with Eric Luedtke to do so !!

Eric is an amazing professor. Being a Maryland State Delegate, he incorporates his own political experiences into his lectures. He also connects his lectures to the modern political scene which is cool. His class is participation driven, though. Overall it's an easy A and he's a super chill and helpful dude, I highly recommend taking this class.

Horrible. Dont take. So boring. Taught myself this whole class. He makes absolutely no sense with grading. Expects you to read his mind. Never ever taking again and if you can pick someone else for this class DO IT.

This class was okay but nothing special. Prof. Lynch has an extremely tiring voice and says um uh um every other sentence. Honestly couldve taught myself this material. One midterm and final, a 1,000 word paper (with cool topics to pick from) and discussion posts. If you need the credit then take it but its nothing exciting.

Not a bad guy, just a horrible lecturer. You will never be able to get any notes down. The final is cumulative, and the tests include essays despite what the syllabus says. There are extra credit opportunities though. The content was interesting, but not worth the stress of trying to write as fast as he can speak every single class.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures were difficult to bear, especially early in the morning. He uses a lot of filler words like "um" so it's hard to pick out the important content. Class is all copying slides which you don't have much time to do, and slides aren't posted after class which makes things so much harder than they need to be. Basic "take notes, take exam" format.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: His lecture style includes giving you 30 seconds to take down a paragraph of notes from a slide and saying things like "Well the slides are for me, not for you" when asked to go back. Not giving enough time for students to get adequate notes has been a recurring issue every lecture, all semester.

had to take this as an elective but dear god was there so much work. Bi-weekly papers 4-5 pgs. based off of the readings and and a huge 10min page paper in the end. Lectures were worthless the only reason why i attended was b/c my TA took attendance. The only way to pass is read the text, she tries to highlight it but it does not work in her favor.

Dr. Bolles is a smart women who I'm sure has seen her fair share of criticism for what she believes. I think if you have an open mind, you can learn a lot from this class. I think many students go in with preconceived notions and a chip on their shoulders. If you're not a know it all and open minded, it can be a rewarding experience.

Intro to Women's studies was my hardest course this semester. Bolles focuses more on race issues than women's issues. There are 6 three page papers and a 10 page paper where you have to do a "field work project." Bolles shows some interesting films and often has guest speakers come in, but the class wasn't that great.

McCauley's passion for his topic is contagious. He is the best presenter and lecturer I have ever had the privilege of listening to.

McCauley is the Lebron James of UMD teachers

AMAZING course and professor. He's very passionate about what he teaches and it shows. Exams are a bit strange sometimes but not terrible, and they're the major grades. There's one big research paper but it's honestly not bad. GVPT210 is one of the best classes I've taken at UMD!

Professor McCauley is my favorite professor at UMD. His classes are very reasonable in terms of workload (lots of reading in this class but I skimmed over a lot and still did well), very accommodating to all circumstances and a great lecturer. Take any of his classes

Professor McCauley was a wonderful professor and everyone would talk about how much they loved him in our class GroupMe. He made clear power point presentations that displayed multiple sides to an argument and was always tolerant of opposing beliefs. He also always gave reasonable accommodations to people facing hardships during this pandemic.

Professor McCauley was an amazing teacher. The class was split into 4 exams and a final group paper (which online was a bit difficult) but he was understanding and supportive of individual situations. He even held an in-person, socially distanced study session so students (most of whom where 1st year) could met their professor in person.

Prof McCauley was one of the best professors I have ever had in college. He showed so much care for all of his students and really displayed passion for the subject with a lot of experience and knowledge to share.

An awesome professor at BSOS. I took a 400 level African politics class with him in 2013. Challenging course work and great class discussions. Expect a lot of reading, no text book required but lots of articles and scholarly publications. Expect a few papers, plus a 10-15 pager at the end of the semester. Midterm and final were easy.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--SO MANY PAPERS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: he is hands down the BEST professor i've ever had. the grading really depends on the TA though, so you can ask prof to help with your paper, but he by no means grades it. he took the time to memorize everyone's names with a class of over 100+ students. he genuinely cares about his students and i'll def be taking more classes taught by him.

Easily one of the best professors available at UMD. You won't get any day to day homework and there are no textbooks. Although attendance is mandatory, you will genuinely enjoy the lectures. The only con is that there's a 10 page research paper but it is graded very generously.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: TAKE ANY MCCAULEY CLASS. He is amazing at lectures and you will genuinely want to go. He knows how to present all sides of the issue at hand to make you as knowledgeable as possible. Super caring about his students, and tests are really fair.
Really good guy, interesting lectures, and genuinely cares about his students

One of my favorite professors. He has interesting experiences that really made me think, and good examples and engaging lectures. Probably the best professor I've had at UMD. I made the mistake of not reading some of the readings when I deemed they were too long, but if you complete all the readings and write a good paper, then easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor!! He kept the class super interesting and you really learn a lot! He posts slides but there's not a lot of information in them so you still need to attend class to get good notes. You're graded on 2 tests, a paper, and attendance/participation in discussion, and nothing's too hard. He offers curves sometimes but he doesn't use A+s

A good professor who teaches a really interesting class. Very clear and easy to listen to in lecture. Engaging. Tests and paper aren't difficult, just make sure you write every possible answer. Approachable and cares about his student's learning. Wants to make a positive impact. Loves his job and research. Don't understand geeking over his hotness.

Take any class with McCauley. He's an amazing teacher. In a fairly big lecture, he actually took the time to learn almost everyone's names. He doesn't make the class too difficult, but it is really interesting. He makes a point to stay objective, and also takes the time to make visuals for chart/graphs/data, so that he can present facts.
THE GOAT
great class. seriously recommend
One of the best gov professors. He makes controversial subjects approachable from an un-biased perspective. Honestly take any class of his

If you're interested in international development, then this is the perfect class for you. It makes you think about stuff in different ways/introduces you to new topics. Plus, the professor is chill and the exams are fair. Take it.

It is a pleasure listening to his lectures.  You can tell by the way he speaks how enthusiastic he is about what he teaches.  I hope I can have him again as a professor.  He influenced my decision to major in Government & Politics.

Prof. McCauley is amazing and he's so hot. Very knowledgable about the course and gives great lectures. He is a really nice guy, very helpful, and charismatic. You'll fall in love with the class and him. Highly recommend taking this class if you're interested in Politics, Policy, International issues, etc.

Extremely knowledgeable on the subject and very willing to talk to his students. He touches on a multitude of topics (corruption and development, micro-finance, etc.) and makes all of them interesting. I never found myself zoning out during class, although that could be a testament to his handsomeness.
Never take one of his classes. Please

Midterm and final make up 90% of grade. Do not take.

reviews.comment: What can I even say about Professor Mcdaniel. He is the only professor that I have dropped his class after the first day. Do not take any courses with him
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was a summer course, so there was a good amount of work in short period of time. However, Dr. McDaniel was very accommodating to my needs due to my work schedule and was also responsive to any questions or concerns I had. The course is enjoyable and Dr. McDaniel was very fair. You just have to be on top of the lectures and the readings.

Easily one of the worst professors I have ever had. The class only has like 5 grades in total, so if you do bad on one you're toast. He doesn't post any lectures so can't ever miss class. The notes don't really help and the exams are basically all short answer and long essay questions. Shouldn't be hard than knes300/360 but, it is , makes no sense.

Dr. McDaniel is, with respect, the worst professor I've ever had. He takes his job way too seriously and shows no care towards any student. When you have a question, he won't answer it and will shoo you away. He doesn't post lectures online, so if you're sick, too bad. He adds on extra work and expects it to be done by the next day. Don't take him.

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had, period. He is super rude in every way, even when responding to kids that raise their hands to participate. He will talk down on you. reviews.comment: lecture: 2 a week. 2-3 question quiz immediately after. lectures lock before quiz opens, but if you keep the panopto tab open, you'll still be able to watch after it locks. discussion: 2 easy group presentations, short wkshts graded on completion. -posted many lectures late and pulled out an 8 page paper as final with no preparation. DO NOT TAKE!

I never actually met Dr. McDaniel because I took KNES222 online but every monday and wednesday he uploaded a lecture and then It would delete itself from canvas, and we would have a lecture quiz after that. Discussion consisted of two group presentations and discussion attendance is mandatory unless it's an asynchronous week.

Most unreasonable and bizarre professor Ive had. Super picky about the littlest things like turning in ppt copies 24 hours before presenting, 4:30PM deadlines, etc. Takes the class way too serious and thinks its a bigger deal than it is. Class is real easy until the final paper: If the TA grades it, youre fine. If he grades it, tough luck

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had. Doesn't give anything but 2 Midterms and a small presentation that he doesn't give A's for. Takes this class way too seriously. If you are looking for an easy option class for KNES, do not take 483 unless you are already a marketing major. If you do take him, god bless you.

I barely got a B in the class, however it was hard. There are two pop quizzes that he gives out. He drops the lowest. He was very vague with a lot of his assignment, that he ended up giving everyone an extension. His deadlines were at 4:30 PM and will drop your grade if late. Class is mandatory as he doesn't upload lectures. Avoid if you can.

reviews.comment: Dr. McDaniel is extremely unreasonable. He is very stubborn and is very picky with small details, dishing out large penalties for minor infractions. While the class was very light for most of the semester, he gives you a 10 page paper right at the end with less than two weeks left that is 40% of the grade and is very harshly graded.
Easy class but probably the most annoying professor i've ever taken. Super serious and any misstep is a 10 point penalty.

Still havent recieved my grade from fall 2016 but Dr. McDaniel was a good teacher.  He made it clear what we had to learn and the format for projects. The material was not difficult whatsoever and most of the grade is left to a final paper rather than exam.  Good elective to take if interested in gambling.  I'll update if he ever gives me my grade.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a great guy, but maybe not a great teacher. He doesn't grade things quickly and doesn't give clear instructions for assignments. If I had a choice, I wouldn't take him again, but I have to. He may have had some personal issues this semester, but that's not excusable when it affects my grade. Again, he's a great guy, but he needs to shape up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Was a great teacher.  MY class about gambling, he showed interest and involvement.  Gives a good amount of readings and lots of group projects but they are not ver hard.  Lectures are interesting but attendance is graded.

Dr. McDaniel cared about us doing well and was always there to explain what you didn't understand. He is one of those professors who really wants his students to succeed but is going to make them work and learn.

This was an amazing professor, all assignments are clearly outlined. The Professor always made sure to make all students feels comfortable for any questions or explanation's and explained it until there was absolutely no confusion. The standard for the class was a bit high but as long as you show up and try to participate you'll do great!

I absolutely loved prof Mccourt. Incredible person with a vast amount of knowledge and easily approachable. Take advantage of office hours, ask questions, participate in conversations and you'll do fine. Grades fairly with good feedback and keeps class engaging. Definitely the best honors professor to take at GW.

Professor McCourt is really educated on and passionate about the subject of philosophy. Course consisted of three papers but for the final paper you have the option to do a more creative project. McCourt is super friendly, keeps the class engaging, and gives strong feedback. I would recommend him to anyone!

good at explaining concepts and elaborating on textbook material during lecture. Gives lots of practice so it's pretty easy to do well on graded assignments. The guy is hilarious if you like dry humor. Just the right amount of assignments. Easy to pass if you try.
Just the best, absolutely take him if you can!

Very straightforward class. The final exam is significantly harder than the other two exams in the course. I didn't find doing any practice problems outside of discussion/review sheets necessary. Do the readings and attend lecture and you should get an A.
So easy going and its easy to get an A if you put the effort and work on

Professor Mccourt was my favorite professor so far. Class lectures were so engaging and fun that you won't fall asleep in your chair. He does assign us weekly quizzes but he gives you full credit as long as you try your best. He doesn't assign any homework besides short readings and a few writing assignments. Never at any point did I dislike him :)

Great professor! I like how he initiates discussions with the class that flow naturally and it really helps us learn the material well. He explains everything very clearly and can make even the most confusing philosophical reading easy to understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor McCourt knows his stuff, can answer questions well in class, and makes a boring subject more accessible. The final exam was significantly harder than any other exam and I don't think we were prepared well for it. The rest of the class is fine though.
Definitely the easiest class I've taken. Hard towards the end, but the exams are basically the review sheets (exam 2 was only questions from the review sheet). Really good class and environment.
Probably the most straightforward class I have ever audited. He makes the somewhat difficult material seem like a breeze, couldn't recommend more.

McCourt is a great professor, he explains the materials really clearly and always go over examples to make sure the students understand. All discussion worksheets are basically participation grades, and they are very helpful. His exams are super fair, nothing pass the review sheets.

Given the difficulty of the class, Professor McCourt was very great in teaching and making sure we got the problems understood. He was nice and even gave free points for doing the work or even attempting it!

I love Thomas! He is such a nice guy and gives great advice for speeches/presentations for this class. He made the class very laid-back and stress-free. He lets you go early and has lots of assignments leading up to presentations to make it hard for you to fail his class. I say taking COMM107 with Thomas was the best decision I ever made!

Pros: he allows multiple submissions (before the deadline) and provides feedback quickly, giving opportunities to improve grades and quality of submissions. He also responds quickly over email.

Cons: He uses A LOT of bad words during class. Poor language is offensive to many and quite unprofessional for a university teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very understanding professor. He presents the lectures in a way that is not boring, and is very nice and lenient when it comes to the speeches. He breaks down the speeches nicely, and fosters a very comfortable environment when its time for the speech.

Thomas is super nice and understanding! All around chill guy. Quizzes are super easy, a 10/10 is almost impossible. Also very lenient with grades on speeches. I wish I could take this class again and I love the way he runs the class. Keeps lectures interesting.

Very passionate about rhetoric, makes lectures interesting. He's incredibly clear and the material is quite structured so pay attention and you get an A. He has quizzes on the news so those can be unpredictable, but they're generally not too difficult. He can be a bit anal when grading papers, but overall good professor, easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Big lecture, vary boring. Most dont show up after the first few weeks. quizzes on friday. Exams matter a ton they basically make or break your entire grade. The typical student strategy for this class is to show up to nothing study a ton before each exam and get a decent grade then rinse and repeat. Final replaces all quiz scores.

This is an asynchronous, 5-week course. It is all busy work and writing discussion posts. By the time he grades the first assignments, you're already done with the course and can't fix mistakes because most poorly worded assignments are already turned in. Expect to write 3000+ words in less than 5 weeks he curves a 93% to an A+ which helps
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer! I have never had an accounting class that was this fun. He makes the content easy to understand and is willing to slow down when students need him to. Best professor at UMD :)

McMillan is a solid lecturer, but gives less to work with practice wise. He also has weekly reading assignments that felt excessive at times. While his class isn't too difficult, it's definitely something you shouldn't blow off till the last minute. Overall, he seems caring and does his best to make the subject less dull.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For as dull a subject as managerial accounting is, McMillan is able to throw some jokes in here and there and keep you engaged as much as one can during lectures covering boring material. There are fewer study materials to go off of compared to BMGT220, but overall if you have questions McMillan will happily answer them.

He's a very engaging lecturer and clearly loves what he teaches. The Connect reading assignments are outrageously long and his lecture slides on ELMS don't always match up obviously with class. Overall though, he clearly cares about his students and tries hard to make accounting as engaging as possible.

He is very kind, however, not a great professor. The class is not very challenging, but the final is. No extra credit or curve. He is very unorganized, does not follow the syllabus, never puts in grades correctly, and seems to have no idea whats going on sometimes. His lectures are unorganized and his slides are filled with mistakes and typos.
solid professor

It is very clear that she is passionate and wants you to succeed in this course. However, her class has some pointless and confusing aspects like how she refuses to put her lecture slides on ELMS, her homework being very hard for no reason and being impossible to solve using notes, and the fact that she wont let you pee during exams.

Once you look past the slight quirkiness, you can see what an amazing professor she is.  Excellent, clear lectures, homework assignments designed to help students better understand the material, and reasonable expectations on exams.  100% would take again.

Professor Mercado's ENEE222 was pretty good. Lectures were clear, tests and labs were well organized. My only complaint was that the homeworks were unnecessarily hard, especially compared to test problems.
She's amazing!!!!!
Good professor. Knows her stuff. Teaches well. I feel like I've learned a lot.

This is probably one of the worst classes I have ever taken. Besides the fact, that I learned NOTHING, I lost all interest I had in this topic. I will never take a comm class again. The group project was horrible. It was a horribly planned class. Also, I could never understand her...Worst class ever.
Great class with interesting stuff! The professor is very nice and seems well-prepared for every class. I enjoyed the videos too!
The instructor was good. Her lectures were clear and easy to follow. The course material was interesting. The movies shown during class illustrated the lecture topics well.

Good teacher, knows her stuff. But it is difficult to understand her sometimes because of her accent. She also goes really fast in her in class notes. altho class is not mandatory, its very helpful. do extra credit!

OMG ... The group paper thing sucks ! Overall read the book,study lec notes (be in class) and be nice to TAs since they are grading. Oh..and btw be careful with choosing ur group members !!Miena has an accent and lecs are boring.

Dr. Messman was an interesting and engaging lecturer, and her course was very easy to complete and follow. She was helpful with my accommodations and made sure I knew that my health came first. She was a little hard to get in touch with at the beginning of the semester, but life happens. I learned a lot in the class without it being a burden/chore

Dr. Messman was a great and caring professor. The course was very informative and manageable with weekly lectures and short multiple choice quizzes. It also consist of 2 exams, a reflection paper and little discussion which was all very simple and easy to do. I would recommend HLTH377 to students that need a elective to take that as a class.

I loved Dr. Messman's course! Very informative and straightforward. As long as you study the material you will pass. She offers 3 bonus extra points for students, and if I were to take this class again, I would! Great for any SPH student needing an elective.

Taking HLTH377 with Prof. Messman has been great! You can tell she truly cares about her students and is very knowledgeable about the material she's teaching. The lectures are interesting and easy to follow along. She is clear about what material will be tested as well. Overall, a great class!! Take it if you can!

Prof. Jenna is awesome. One of the most stress-free, yet educational courses I have taken. Very clear with expectations and offers some extra credit. The content of the course is actually interesting and you can tell this prof. wants you to succeed. Very accessible & reasonable! The class is self paced so your grade is up 2 you. Take her if u can!

Jenna is absolutely AMAZING! Really strives to make info accessible and relatable and you can tell she really cares about what she does/teaches as a sex educator. In-class TopHat participation big part of grade (easy tho). Emphasizes what info is important for exams. Was extremely lenient and understanding in the transition to online due to COVID19
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Jenna is a great lecturer and very passionate about what she teaches. Overall, if you show up to class and do the TopHat assignments you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Made this class very engaging and fun. Assignments were very easy because she made grading rubrics very clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Jenna is AMAZING! Her lectures are so interesting, entertaining, informative, and relatable to college life. She gives many bonus opportunities and emphasizes what's going to be on the exam while lecturing. There is only one midterm, one final, one reflection paper, one final paper, and Tophat participation during lecture.

Jenna is super nice, hilarious, and caring. She wants everyone to succeed in the class, gives a lot of bonus opportunities and really cares about students. She is one of the best, most interesting, and cool professors at UMD.

Jenna Messman was an amazing instructor throughout my adventure with HLTH377, Human Sexuality. She's a caring, passionate, and inspiring teacher who opened up all her students' eyes to the varying aspects of human sexuality. She provides opportunities for extra credit and cares that her students pass. Highly recommend taking her as an instructor!
I did not like the single lecture I attended.

reviews.comment: Don't choose her if you need organization. Lecture disorganized and explanations only verbal. Expect to annotate, comprehend, and organize notes during lecture. Slides change quick and erased after class. Pick another teacher you will have a better chance as guided notes, quizzes and homework provided. A good teacher will determine pass or fail.

10/10 for sure. Dr. Stocker is a phenomenal teacher and lecturer. Orgo is hard no matter what, and no professor is going to make it super easy. BUT if you go to every lecture, study hard, pay attention, and give your best effort, you will do extremely well. Dr. Stocker makes this subject extremely manageable and fun! The octet rule RULES!

The lectures she gives she doesn't provide the annotated one she did in the lecture that day.  The lectures though weren't really helpful cause everyday after we have class I would have to teach it to myself all over again by a whole different person.Midterms and finals are you grade decider which for people who struggle with test taking is bad.
