reviews.comment: As a person, I think Dr. Stocker is nice and an interesting lecturer by using applicable scenarios to understand concepts. As a professor, she goes extremely fast in lectures and blazes through topics without breaking them down long enough and building up to more complex problems. VERY tough grader but the curve is nice.

Orgo with Lenea Stocker is challenging, but her teaching style works well if you put in the effort. The lectures move fast, so GSS and unstuck AI are must-have resources. Overall, a rewarding class if you're willing to grind.

Dr. Stocker is good at breaking down hard concepts and making them easy to understand. Her exams aren't easy, but they're fair. As long as you pay attention in class and do her practice exams, you'll know exactly what to expect. The only problem is that she doesn't post lecture recordings, so you can't ever afford to miss her class.

I am not a fan. She grades extremely harshly. If you are sick, good luck. She doesn't post any lectures and often refuses to help when asked. Expects people to know concepts that we have never seen before. The HW length is ridiculous. Unless you want to spend all your time teaching yourself, find another professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
I only came here for grade/curve reference because I know how hard orgo is. I got a C- with grades of:

- 71/100 for exam one which translated into a B and above the average
- 30 and 42 out of 100 for exams two and three which is below a c and average
- 52/150 for the final exam which is below average c

Stocker teaches very quickly. Other classes like kopple were way behind us in terms of material. You can do the problem sets to help and hope for the best. She gives you old exams to practice on but she only provides one or two keys which only have the answers, not an explanation. Not helpful.

Orgo is hard, and Stocker tries to make the lectures interesting but she moves extremely quickly and it is hard to keep up. She also made the exam questions much harder than necessary in my opinion, and trying to finish the exams in time was difficult. Go to GSS and STUDY HARD outside of class. Practice problems will help a lot. Do the old exams

Stocker is a good professor but she teaches very fast and after teaching you a topic she will give you a hard question and tell you to practice it. We are ahead of the other chem classes and there are several topics you have to learn in order to pass the exams. Discussions did not help either, GSS is so much more helpful. Did not enjoy this class.

Professor Stocker is one of the most intelligent Professor. I want to express my gratitude to you for everything you have done. I sincerely appreciate all the effort you spent assisting me on numerous occasions. I appreciate the course very much. I thoroughly appreciated your talk and your wonderful sense of humor.

Orgo will not be a walk in the park but Stocker does her best to make things relevant for us and really does want us to succeed. She holds office hours all the time for questions and it's also a great time to work with other students that show up. She's super nice and a great teacher considering how difficult the subject matter is.

You must try to get Dr. Stocker as your professor if you are taking CHEM231!  Orgo is a notoriously difficult subject, but Dr. Stocker is an excellent lecturer.  There are no tricks on her exam.  If you have adequately practiced past exams, you will succeed on her exams.  Take lots of notes in lecture.  She is supportive and there to help you!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I highly reccomend Dr. Stocker! She was an amazing lecturer when I took orgo I over the summer. Although she tends to go through material quickly she was a phenomenal lecturer who explained things very clearly and covered everthing in detail so that you could easily grasp everything that she expected you to know for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Koppel last spring and retook orgo 1 with Stocker this summer. Koppel is good but tougher, and she's not as approachable. Stocker conveys information better imo by using everyday analogies. For example, she explains Fischer and Newman projections using pictures of her cats and is generally less intimidating than Koppel of Friedman.

I can say without a doubt, stocker is one of the best in the chemistry department. She does move at a very fast pace and requires you to memorize a lot of content, but the way she structures her lectures makes it easy to stay engaged. Just do all the problem sets, practice exams, and ask plenty of questions, and 
 you should be fine.

She moves extremely fast and her tests are way too hard. Teaches a topic for twenty minutes one class before an exam and expects you to know it. As far as I've seen, you either have a social life or you do well on her exams. Don't recommend, take Koppel.

Almost listened to the bad reviews and dropped her class, would have been the worst mistake ever. She is an amazing professor. It is organic chemistry so yes, it is going to be difficult, but just put in the work and do her practice, go to office hours, try on the homework. You'll be fine! I am so grateful I took this class, she is the best BY FAR

The one thing I regret about this class is not going to office hours to develop a personal connection with Dr. Stocker. You earn the grade you get. It's possible to get an A if you put in the work that she outlines for you. Study for exams by the practice that SHE GIVES YOU. She expects a lot from you, as she should. you will not regret taking her.

Stocker is really nice and tries to make the content enjoyable but moves entirely too fast and doesnt like when you ask questions. The examples done in class are way simpler than the ones on the exam. Her office hours are helpful if you can manage to go when there arent a hundred people there which is almost impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You need to be at the lectures because she does not record nor post annotated slides. Her tests are hard and are slightly similar to the homework. But her tests definitely are multistep and more complicated. Your success depends on GSS, office hours, and a good TA. However, in the end, all the exams were heavily curved.

Stockers curve makes her the best orgo professor at UMD. Her curve is very generous, a C is the average and about ten points higher is a B. As long as you are on average with everyone else you will pass the class or even do better. Her exams were fair and her lectures were fast paced. This is an extremely hard class but she is the best prof for it
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I had Stocker for CHEM135 and CHEM132 as well and I can without a doubt say Stocker shines when she is teaching Orgo. She doesn't post notes online. Complicates some topics but emphasizes important patterns. Get ready to memorize & practice mechanisms, but Stocker is a safe choice. Huge curve btw, ended up with a 68% curved to a B+.

reviews.comment: Dr. Stocker is by Far the BEST organic chemistry professor UMD has! I ended getting a C in the class only because I was recently diagnose with ADHD. TAKE HER, solid choice!!!

Orgo in general is just a tough class but stocker is certainly the best out of all your options. Shes so kind and sometimes brought her son to class lol. Generally, very caring. reviews.comment: avoid

Dr. Stocker is truly an amazing professor I met so far at UMD. She's a great lecturer, very organized in terms of topics. She's very funny and she actually cares for her students! Her homeworks are harder in someway than the exam, her exams are straight forward!

This class was a disaster. The labs were often unclear and the videos were sloppy. Dr. Stocker needs to work on her lecturing skills to speak more clearly and not stumble on her words so much. she overloaded the curriculum with unnecessary material and accused 150 students of cheating. she has no regard for the success of her students and takes pride in the fact that her exams are almost impossible to pass.

Hard exams at least during covid. Ive never been actually prepared for an exam bc the questions are purposely very confusing. She seems very sweet but is ruthless about grades and will make you give 100% every single week.

The exams are way harder than the rest of the course work, probably because she wants to make it impossible for cheaters to pass but it means that honest students' grades also took a hit. The exams are all much too long for anyone who needs to actually think about how to answer the problems instead of intrinsically knowing the answer.

Absolutely miserable at teaching. The assignments are completely random, the tests are riddled with mistakes, and she spends half her lectures saying "Uhm" or "K" or "Alright" it'll drive you crazy. Not good at online teaching at all. The exams are very hard and she makes the tests 1000 times harder than the exams.

This class has been by far the worst college class I have ever taken. I believe she once used to be a good professor, but since COVID happened and classes were moved online. Her exams have been ridiculous, but ill give credit where it due. Her lectures aren't bad it's just that 50mins isn't enough time to do an exam.

Dr. Stocker seems like a great person, but this class just wasn't it. Maybe it was the fact that it was online, or maybe just this course in general, but this class sucked. obviously no matter who you take for orgo, the class will be demanding but Stocker legit made it so much easier than i expected. ppl loved to complain in the GroupMe abt her not curving but she did (my 87 became an A). TAKE HER U WONT REGRET IT

inconsiderate to students, especially during the pandemic. the only orgo professor who did not cancel an exam due to covid and did not curve the class. dr. stocker will refuse to show you your grade. save yourself and take another professor.

if you think you want Dr. Stocker take her as early as possible to learn her teaching style because its WHACK. She basically only teaches using practice problems which is fine. Dr. Stocker is amazing. Orgo is not hard as long as you study consistently and keep up with the material. Use the orgo as a 2nd lang books to practice what Stocker teaches! Her exams are SO FAIR. She never puts anything on them that was not covered in class. She also has all her past exams in her office as a resource. She is funny and loves cats!

Dr. Stocker's lectures blow my mind every time, but I love it. She is an amazing lecturer and makes me love chemistry even though I'm terrible at it. Most exam averages are about 50% which hurts self esteem, but the curve helps at the end of the semester. I love Stocker, but get ready to work really hard if you want to get a good grade.

Dr. Stocker does a really great job explaining tough concepts. She provides practice exams in her office, and those are key to succeeding in her class. Also, she is usually in her office, even outside of office hours, so go to her for help. 500 out of the 650 points in the class are exams, so very exam heavy. You don't need a textbook for her class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Wonderful! Was always very respectful and easy to talk to outside of class. This was the first time I had taken chemistry in over 4 years and she truly made it very digestible and not nearly as scary as other people make it out to be. Super nice, 11/10 would recommend every time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Only grades are exams and clickers so no room for error. Tests are extremely hard, definitely an everyday class. You have to work extremely hard and may still not get the grade you want.
Stockers a good choice
Hard grader, hard tests. Test and clicker questions are the only graded things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: best gen chem 1 teacher. very clear and concise; great pacing. I was able to understand all of the material completely. the clicker points are graded for accuracy but were fine. the tests were fair. homework assignments were super helpful to study for tests. she had a kinda nasally voice but seemed nice, only bothered me a little bit.

Dr. Stocker is an amazing teacher. She has office hours just about every day of the week. Since her practice problems can be really easy, she lets you take pictures of past exams and will help you with any problem you are stuck on. She is also a great lecturer; she makes orgo fun and exciting because she makes sure you understand the mechanisms.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The labs are easy. However, the midterm & final exam are EXTREMELY HARD. I received an avg of A's/B+ on lab reports, read the whole lab manual, studied really hard for exams but still failed. (Avg on the lab exams were around 50%). On the lab exam, there are 10 MC questions & have answer choices A-H. One of them had A-J. Designs the test so we fail
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall, Stocker is a clear lecturer. Her teaching style simply wasnt for me. She doesnt recommend working out of the book, only her prob. sets (which are nothing compared to exams). You will learn a lot by attending class, but it is courses like these that make me wonder why there arent many point opportunities for such a tough subject. Shabby.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I had her for orgo I and II, she is very conceptual (acid-base chem) heavy on her exams. Exams make up most of your grade. She was bit disorganized with her problem sets, because it's the first time she's teaching it in the sem. Her lectures were still very clear. She won the 2018 dean's outstanding lecturer award, and definitely deserves it.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The labs are easy to do, but the midterm and final are hard. The averages for both were 50's. Overall, a ok class.

Stocker was solid, but at the mercy of the subject. She takes complex concepts and makes them make sense (like 70% of the time). She's good help at office hours, but everyone else goes too so try to get there early. Lots of clicker questions. I didn't do well on her tests, but I know some people did. Despite that, she curved my grade from C- to B.

Stocker is a good teacher but her tests are extremely hard for both I and II (test questions are harder than her homework or the Orgo 2 book). I would probably recommend another professor, but she does curve heavily.

She explains material so well, it is amazing. I am usually the type to zone out in class but I found myself looking forward to her lectures. Her exams are very difficult so it is important that you never get behind in this course. She is very often accessible outside class if you don't understand something.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Ive taken stocker twice, both classes extremely difficult. The averages are so low, everyone I knew in the class always felt like they could never be prepared. Also felt like there werent many point opportunities other than the 3 exams where averages were 50% and the final. I do not recommend, but she is one of the nicer and clearer lecturers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. Stocker is a great Professor. After almost failing GenChem, I was terrified for Orgo but ended up with a B .... which could've been an A if I'd taken it seriously from the beginning - with that being said start studying FROM the beginning, be on top of it, go to her office hours (useful!!!!), and do practice problems + all the problem sets!!

I had a 43% throughout the entire semester so I've been feeling on edge the entire semester. My grade mostly focused on the exams. There are only 3 homework- wish there was more so I could get more points. Granted, she did say that mastering orgo doesn't help students much. Overall, may the curve be with you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Stocker is super caring and highly respected prof. Lectures are actually fun and easy to understand with clicker questions and practice problems. Tests are really hard and no matter how I prepared for them, I never did well, but she provides plenty of test prep materials. Study the lecture material after each class and use your resources to do well
Amazing professor. Orgo is difficult no matter who teaches, but Stocker makes it easier. Explains everything well and thoroughly prepares for exams. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Her tests mirror problems on her problem sets and lecture, with the final mirroring the prior 3 tests. You don't need a textbook. Do the previous tests, go to GSS and her office hours (but not right before the test or there'll be 50 people in there...) There's clicker questions to help. Overall highly recommend. She also loves referencing cats fyi.

Overall, great teacher. Super nice, she knows her stuff, and she is clear about her expectations. Her lectures are detailed and IMPORTANT, so go to every one or else you'll miss important material. Problem sets, GSS, and office hours are KEY to passing this class. The curve is INSANE at the end of the class, don't freak out, but study hella.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: My classmates love her, while her teaching style is not for me. While orgo is basically a memorization class, Stocker teaches heavily on the theories behind the reactions when the tests are on "questions-answers-without explanations". However, she is an amazing person and she does know and love orgo.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: An amazing professor and really nice person who genuinely cares about her students.

She's so nice but I had a really hard time with this class.  If you haven't taken Chemistry in awhile or don't have background in Chemistry, she may not be the best professor for you.  Lots of material is assumed that you know, so her lectures seemed disjointed to me.  She does clicker questions in class which are decently difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Stocker was awesome. She is really passionate about what she teaches and it shows in her lectures. I hate chemistry, but she made it enjoyable.
Super hard grader but theres a huge curve at the end of the class. Always open for office hours and is really helpful

Dr. Stocker is an amazing professor.  She is always willing to help if you go to her office hours. She also has old exams in her office that you can take pictures of.  She gives homework and clicker grades (half participation, half accuracy), and curves final grades.  GSS and problem sets help a lot.

She is an AMAZING chem teacher. She teaches all of the topics great and if you go to all of her lectures, write down EVERYTHING she writes (she's very lecture heavy), do the online optional practice problems and the mandatory HW and study it before the test, you'll do fine. Sounds like a lot, but chem with her was actually great. -DS2k17

I LOVED her as a teacher! She is so sweet and knowledgable. You HAVE to go to lectures because almost all the test material is dependent on lecture notes. There are also clickers. Go to her doing office hours early if you do not get material. As long as you understand lecture material and do the practice tests, you should do well!

Dr. Stocker has extremely good analogies to teach a lot of concepts (Warning: She uses cats a lot), and they really make things stick. Chemistry has historically been hard for me, but she made it enjoyable and digestible.
Dr. Stocker is the best! Her tests can sometimes have tricky parts but she curves so it's okay if you don't get everything right. She is super nice and accessible during office hours!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: She's great! She does curves. She emails problems sets for practice and eventually sends out the key for them. Practice and memorization is key for this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr stocker was overall a great professor in my opinion. go to lecture if you want to fully understand the material and get clicker points. Definitely do your homework, it's the same points as an exam and its never that hard. Do problem sets if you're struggling, always look at old exams to be prepared!

With very little chemistry background, I overall think Stocker was good. She's funny and her practice exams are helpful. It is definitely a hard class, but if you put a lot of effort in you should succeed. I enjoyed learning with her and compared to my friend's experiences with other chem professors, she seems to be one of the best choices!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I liked Dr. Stocker as a professor and person; I just am not about chemistry. She teaches very quickly and sometimes leaves us in the dust trying to put things together, but the GSS and office hours make up for the confusion. You HAVE to study to do well on tests or else you're screwed. Tests can be a little long which makes it more stressful.

Dr. Stocker is welcoming and motivating. Although tests were difficult, the problem sets that she provides are extremely beneficial; I was more prepared for the exams because of them. Dr. Stocker also gives students time to process clicker questions before answering them. Lectures were very engaging and easy to follow.

It's organic chemistry, tests are hard. However, she is open to questions and helping and is easy to talk to. The lecture are lengthy but I didn't even break open the book. Her lectures cover 99% of the test, even small things. Tests are curved, homeworkoptional, but do it, understand it, and you'll be above the curve. Funny and caring orgo prof.

Dr. Stocker is one of the best professors I've had at UMD. While the material was very challenging, I enjoyed the class largely due to Stocker. Her explanations and lectures are clear. The weekly practice problems (optional) are great reviews and definitely help for exams. Grades will mostly come from exams but she does do clicker questions too.

Dr. Stocker's class is the way to go for Orgo I. Don't let the bad rating and low averages fool you. Yes, her averages are very low, but this means its relatively easy to get an A if you are a step ahead of your peers. I remember one of her midterms in particular, a 28/100 (!!) got you a C. Mess around and get a 70 on an exam? Your looking at an A+

Dr. Stocker is def one of the best, nicest chem teachers out there! Her lectures are very clear and she is great at explaining concepts! Tests are difficult but if you do the practice sets and look at her old exams, you can get used to the format and get a really accurate feel for what will be on the test. She is super helpful during office hours

She is a nice person. However, it is impossible to complete her tests. In a 50 minute time period you must complete almost 90 minutes worth of work, making the best you can possibly do around a 60. Would not take again, and recommend to all other that they become a liberal arts major.

Dr. Stocker is a great prof. Orgo is not an easy class by any means, her tests are not easy but they are not impossible. I always went to her for help, I was rather embarrassed with my minuscule knowledge but she wanted me to learn. She wants to help and she can help, a great person. Lectures are not great hard to follow but, that's the material

If you are looking to take CHEM135 with Stocker, it's likely that you, like myself, will never be taking a Chemistry past 135. The administrators at Maryland know this, so they require A LOT to be covered in a one-semester class. This class is extremely tough, but Stocker is a great teacher. Beware, though, she goes all-out with Organic Chem.

Her lectures are amazing. Chemistry has always been my worst subject and she makes it easy to grasp. She's also super accessible and her office hours are pretty much all day every day. Go to office hours instead of discussion. Her tests are hard and the grading is tough. The best way to do well is to do a ton of practice problems!

You don't see her, but that's how labs work. My TA was awesome and very helpful. The reports are challenging and the exams are difficult, but don't drop the class... It's curved a good bit. Also, you need the manual, obviously. Overall it was fine.
very long lab reports. never actually saw her, only my TA. class average was a 50%, but the course is heavily curved

If you went to every lecture and took notes (copy what she rights on the board) you will be fine. Very clear understandable lectures, always felt like you learned something after lectures. Exams were difficult but she curves so that a 70 is an A. I didn't get an A because I commute 40 minutes and the class was at 8 am so I slept in a few times.
The professor gave wonderful lectures and made sure everyone was able to understand the material. He was very accommodating when I had some outside-school circumstances.

w teacher
his son is hot

He goes through material very quickly with little explanation or examples. Most of your learning will be on your own. I attended every lecture and did every homework and still didn't understand anything, but then I found a YouTube series going over the same material and that series did a much better job of explaining the subject matter.

Professor Mellet cannot teach differential equations to save his life. I had to go to Professor Levermore's lectures in addition to his to understand what was actually going on. Especially if you have to take upper level math or engineering courses, it is crucial to have a great foundation of differential equations. Do not take him.

Good teacher, goes through lecture quickly so one will have to understand the material after class on their own. Two midterms and a final, final and 2nd midterm were fair. Seemed a little passive to me though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Would take again

reviews.comment: Professor Mellet is an absolutely atrocious professor. He blasts through the material weeks ahead of other professors and extremely vague about the concepts and theorems. I highly recommend taking Justin Wyss-Gallifent instead for this course, even if it means that you have to postpone it a semester or two

Mellet is a pretty solid pick in terms of teaching ability. The accent might be annoying at first, but after a while you get used to it. The guy definitely knows what he's talking about and you can ask questions in the middle of lecture any time. You're expecting to teach yourself the MATLAB component, but they're graded pretty leniently anyway.

He's a nice guy, but I went to every lecture and NEVER understood what was going on until the TA taught it in discussion the next day. The Matlab projects are impossible (even the TA said he didn't know how to do them) and you have to learn it all on your own. Take Justin for this class, even if it means pushing diffeq to another semester.

This class was pretty straightforward. Mellet followed the textbook the entire time, so you didn't even need to go to lecture. His lectures can be hard to understand because of his accent, but it becomes easier to understand him after awhile. He's willing to help you if you ask, pretty nice guy. Great class

Great teacher, Had trouble the beginning of the semester- moves at a very fast pace, but really picked it up near the end and realized just how fair his tests are. Final was hard- but doable. Really eager to help one on one.

Linear algebra back in '08 or '09. Accent aside, hard to hear and understand. Homework and lectures are straight from the book. Exams are very fair. I skipped half the lectures but attended discussion (good TA) mostly regularly, and did all the homework and occasional extra problems. Got an A-. Never personally met prof. Lay textbook is excellent.
Had him for linear algebra. Great professor. His notes are clear and tests are made directly based off of the book. Pretty easy class if you put the effort in to go to class and take the notes.
He was a good teacher. I found his french accent amusing. Calc 3 is much easier than calc 2 and he did a good job teaching.

please, if u love urself, please dont take this class. the amount of work she gives u is ludicrous for a level 100 journalism class. i spent more time on this woman's assignments than i did studying for ochem2. yes the work is easy but i think i have carpal tunnel now from how much i had to type and scroll from her assignments
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: I don't even know where to start. I am a junior and I have never had difficulties taking online classes or writing-intense courses. However, Professor Moeller makes journalism 175 the most tedious and uninformative class ever. This entry-level course takes hours EVERY DAY to complete assignments that do not even teach me about media literacy. Crazy

Dont take it its not worth the gen ed. The TAs are in charge of grading and when my TA took points off for bs things I sent an email to the professor outlining why I shouldnt have lost those points and she just ignored my emaill. I was right at the cutoff for a A- and the professor just wouldnt respond. Its busy work but in my opinion not worth it

The lectures weren't very engaging, so I stopped going to them early in the semester in order to spend more time on the weekly assignments which took like 6 hours at least to complete. They aren't very hard, but they require a lot of article reading which was tedious. Also the professor was difficult to reach, but the TA was easy to get a hold of.

Professor Moeller is super accommodating if you are honest with her about what you're struggling with, and is overall incredibly nice and caring. The course itself is an insane amount of writing, but her grading for the bulk of it is fairly lenient, especially in the summer session.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Yes, the class is a lot of work; however, the professor states this in her syllabus, so don't take the class if you don't want to do a lot of work. That being said, it's a lot of "reading," but many students (like myself) can skim and grasp the information to answer the questions. The projects weren't too bad; the student examples were helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: This was such an unnecessary and repetitive amount of work for a Gen Ed, it took more time out of my schedule than any of my core requirements this semester. The discussion posts took me between 6-8 hours per week to complete. My word counts each week ranged from 3000-5000 each week, this was typical feedback from other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: JOUR175 is all online, but don't think that means it's easy. Every week you gotta read like 30 articles that she assigns, and then summarize them, then add your own insight for each one. I end up writing almost 5000 words a week, and this is just for regular homework. There are also projects that ironically are less work than the homework imo.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This is pretty much all the worst aspects of school rolled into one. Lots of work that feels like busywork, the amount of time for each question does not equal the points given, most questions are simply "read this and summarize", questions are repeated week to week/ within the same assignment, unclear expectation of how much to write.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I don't think Prof Moeller is a bad teacher herself. I just don't like the way the online class was structured. She gives weekly quiz's that are full of readings and complex questions which can be very time consuming. I feel that the quiz's just become busy work at some point. I feel that groups should be allowed for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Only 3 synchronous classes during the semester. At the start of the course I was not sure if it was something I wanted to take so I stayed after one class and discussed with her what the class really was and the amount of work needed. She helped me understand and I ended up enjoying the class and the readings (not so much the writing).

Dr. Moeller is the sweetest person I've met at UMD. She gives really good feedback and answers your questions about the covered topics. This class itself is a bit writing+reading heavy but the contents are not hard to learn. Wouldn't say it's an easy A because I put much effort into the class, but I definitely recommend for gened (DSSP, DVUP)

This online class was the worst part of my semester. Each week, there are huge homeworks that take around 6hours if you want to get an A-. Though the content is interesting and Prof Moeller is very likable & smart, I could barely keep up. There are also substantial media projects due in rapid succession on top of everything else. Beware!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Easily the most boring class on campus, but still an easy A. You only have to show up to half of the lectures, but those will be the longest hours of your semester. Most of it never feels like it pretains to the topic we're learning about. Put in 2-4 hours of work a week and you'll get an A.

I don't even know where to begin. First of all, do not sign up for this class. It is jam-packed full of readings, quizzes, blog posts, special projects, expensive field trips, and group projects. The teacher, the TAs, and ELMS all had different instructions for all of this homework, making it unclear how to do well on your assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: The lectures were interesting but the news quizzes every class could be a bit challenging. The prof was kind of scatter-brained and discussions were packed full of projects. Overall, it was okay for filling two Gen-Ed classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is incredibly interesting. Lectures change based on what's going on in the world, which is exciting. There are a lot of projects but it's a good class.
TA's teach more than she does. Lectures take forever. She calls on random people so pay attention. News quiz every class.

Very energetic teacher but class is boring. 5 question world events quizzes in every lecture. TA's grade in an inconsistent way. You don't learn much from this class except for current world events. 2 field trips required, often scheduled during weekdays. I don't recommend the class.

The class was pretty interesting if you're into journalism and media. It meets once a week for lecture and then another time for discussion. Class isn't mandatory, but you lose points if you don't show up because there's a news quiz after every lecture. All the assignments are done online and you also have to take two field trips for the class.
Awful class. most boring teacher, always late, rambles, not helpful, lazy, annoying

Really easy going professor, extended deadlines for nearly every single project we had and even cancelled a research paper that had been on the syllabus because no one wanted to do it. The class isn't that interesting (lots of research & must be very familiar with lexisnexis) but she's really funny so she made it bareable!

I took this as a winter course. It is not the first time she has taught it. She is a nice person and an ok prof. But she has massive problems explaining what needs to be done for projects (projects that weigh HEAVILY for your grade).So students are bewildered and have many questions that she tries to address, but doesnt ever seem to give the answer
She was a great prof and the class was awesome.  I definitely recommend taking it even if you're not a Journalism major.

I had mixed feelings. She was strict to the point of being mean at times, but she was a good teacher. The class was interesting and I learned alot, especially thanks to a great TA (paul in fall05). She goes way too fast with her slides. One plus is that there is only one lecture and discussions are very helpful and fun. Mine even did a secret santa

this class media literacy was great!!! very interesting...the teacher was great!!! i got an A++ its very easy ..um having a bad TA can make it a bad course tho..I had Andrew and he was great! my friend had another TA and received Bs on like every paper even tho she was a great writer...anyhoo..the professor is great!
I don't know which HONR class you were in! but she rocked.  Yes you need need to work your ass off, it's an honor class dummmy!! maybe you're in the wrong place, and baby she's hoooot!!!

Maybe she's cool for journalism, but for the Honors Seminar "War and the American Experience" she's awful. The class is impossible to get an A in, if you work your ass off you'll wind up with a B+. She totally blew up at the class at the end of the semester because she thought our 10 pg research papers were crap. Ridiculous. And she's not hot.
She's awesome! highly recommended class and professor!

She's strict. Got really pissed at students for missing an assignment after it was pulled from the web, which we couldn't help of course. I had Jad, he was tough and discussions kinda sucked. Paul seemed cool though and was funny. Lectures are really interesting but no attendance is taken. I got an A and liked it. If i got a B, maybe not so much.
Course is beyond awesome and the professor is great, a life time learning experrience... highly recomend.

Best course ever! Make sure u follow instructions and come to class. Discussions were a riot, lots o fun and learned a lot. pretty hot professer and male  TAs very helpful,especally Jad, avoid the other female nuttzi TA... kinda freaks me out
I went to lecture once, she's kinda hot.

She was a great professor the material she presented was interesting the TA actually were engaing with the sutdents to make sue that we are learning especially Paul M! He was great. But the material is interesting and it isn't that difficult to learn it applies to every day things! I recommend people to take her class!!

Terrible use of time management...tries to cram 2 hours of powerpoint slides into an hour and a half class, without posting the slides on the web.  The TA's are the saving grace of this class: Indira and Jad actually care if their students are learning the material

Professor Moeller uses extensive powerpoint presentations that are often clear and interesting. She talks VERY quickly and moves onto the next slide without notice. Her videoclips are fun and engaging, however, and the class is definitely worth while!

If you are not familiar with algebra, you will not do well with this teacher and you should definitely not take it in the summer.  Tutoring was a waste of time.  The class was held in a basement, with poor lighting and was very boring.  I had to drop this class.  There was no help for me or preparation for the finals.

Had Mr. Flynn for PreCal when I first got to UMD. He is excellent, because he usually teaches small classes such as these. Very reasonable, kind, understanding - it's just a matter of you, as a student, opening your mouth and having the initiative to ask questions when you don't really get something. A+ for this great guy!
Kind of boring but thorough and very sweet.
Good teacher. He explains things very well.

The man just doesn't teach well. He doesn't cover things clearly and isn't clear when he does attempt to teach. All he does is write some formulas and then do some problems, no description. It's bad, don't take a math you don't already know/have a tutor for with this man.
Good teacher. Class is not easy, but the difficulty is fair and there is no BS. Definitely recommend.

Professor Subasi is one of the best UMD professors in accounting. He is helpful, sums up the chapters for you in class and was kind enough to hold exam review sessions. Accounting in general is a tough subject but if you put in the work, it won't be that bad- especially with him as a professor. I miss this class!

Professor Subasi is an amazing professor! He is willing to help even outside the classroom. It's good he provides his own notes in addition to the textbook. He listens to students. If you work hard, he is more than willing to write you recommendation letters. He simplifies the course content and does his best to make sure the students understand.
Good teacher, caring.
Prof. Subasi teaches at a good pace and makes sure everyone understands.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: The class is mainly graded based on tests and take home quizzes. His tests are hard but fair, entirely based of off material he provides in class. Attendance isn't required but he randomly started doing attendance quizzes so go to class! If you pay attention, take notes, and ask good questions you should do well.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Out of all 310 professors, I would take him over everyone else. Overall, the class is tough, but the workload is manageable. There are 2 exams and 1 final, and they are very hard. Although you don't need the book, you do not know what to expect on the exams. He gives you notes and he goes through them during lectures, but overall a decent professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The exams were difficult because they cover a lot of information, but you are given all the material you need. Make sure you do all the practice problems because some of them are similar to exam questions. Subasi is a nice guy, though he may come off as frazzled at times. He doesn't like people who don't show up so we got "attendance quizzes"
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall okay teacher. You can tell he is a little nervous, which effects his train of thought sometimes. Later in the semester his teaching becomes much better. He speaks clearer, and gets the right pace. He does care about people understanding the material, so don't be afraid to ask questions. He answers almost all of them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Muncy is one of the best profs at this university. Engaging lectures, good discussions. You'll actually want to go to class. Reasonable assignments, understanding and empathetic person who is incredibly knowledgeable. Can't recommend enough.
Professor Muncy is AMAZING! Incredibly kind and sweet, her lectures were fascinating and the class was fairly challenging but not impossible. Amazing, amazing class 10/10 would take again!

Dr. Muncy is truly an amazing professor! I am not a history major, but took this class because I was interested in learning more about women's history. Lectures are mandatory (attendance is taken through "lecture engagement") but she makes it so worth it to go to class with her incredible knowledge and enthusiasm towards history. Take this class!

Professor Muncy was absolutely amazing. Such a kind woman with such a passion and spirit for the subject matter. The class was challenging in the right ways and did not require a ton of time and energy to do well. I feel like I learned so much in this class and would absolutely take again, couldn't recommend more!

Muncy is fantastic. Asynchronous lectures. She thoroughly and thoughtfully responded to discussion posts, however. Tests were open book but timed, and no choices of questions. Muncy was able to consistently weave an intention of "liberating" us through the material. As a person, Muncy couldnt have been kinder, gentler, and more inspiring.

Professor Muncy was one of my favourite professors EVER. She always worked with my work schedule and let me submit my assignments late (no penalty). She had great lectures that you could tell she was passionate about what she was teaching and provided feedback on everything. Just be prepared to do a fair bit of reading for discussion sections!

Great professor! She explains everything clearly and is extremely enthusiastic about womens history! The lectures are easy to understand, the isnt much homework, but there are a weekly readings for discussions that can sometimes be a bit lengthy. Participation in discussions is mandatory. Overall, the class is easy to pass if you pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: By far the best Professor I've had at UMD. She inspired me to change my major to History.

Professor Muncy is, by far, my favorite professor to date. Prior to the beginning of the course, she sent an e-mail to the class stating that she "could hardly wait to meet us and get started." I have never had a professor seem so genuinely interested and excited to get to know her students and teach us everything she can in such a short time.

I recommend Dr Muncy because she is super caring and truly wants you to succeed, she is flexible and accommodating of disabilities. She is also hilarious and knowledgable so lectures are great. However, it is a lot of reading and participation during discussions is mandatory so you can't get away with not reading. Tests are kind of hard.

I choose to take hist211 for one of my geneds. Professor Muncy and the TA are both amazing and really kind people. The lectures are great however class and discussion ARE mandatory. Discussion is graded kinda harsh and is worth 25% of your grade so make sure to do the reading before hand. Really great class but most of the class gets a B so beware!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Loved her class. I would take it again. She's fantastic and there was never a dull moment. Just be ready to read.
Great teacher who really made her lectures interesting, I would make sure to attend them! Also, don't miss discussions or the readings for them (they're actually pretty interesting too, don't worry!)
This is by far my favorite professor! She's so interesting to listen to and never gets boring. Her lectures are engaging and fun to attend. Would definitely take a class by her again!!
Awesome!!!!!!!!! I took ALL of her classes!
So passionate. Is willing to help you with anything and he work load was light. Maybe the best history professor at UMD!

Professor Muncy is definitely a very passionate person.  she's extremely enthusiastic about the course content which makes the class interesting to sit through.  the workload is moderately light..only 2 written exams, 1 bibliography and 1 major paper. i would recommend this course
One of my top 3 favorite professors at Maryland.
Muncy is great. She's passionate and engaging. Makes history interesting. Class isn't too much work just some reading and 2 exams (1 essay question each). Very enjoyable overall.

The lectures can be dull, but the course material is engaging and helps you think like an economist. Homework is minimal, with just a few videos and two time-consuming but easy projects. Exams closely align with lecture content, are graded fairly, and are usually generously curved, including the non-cumulative final exam.

This professor is terrible. The worst teacher and class that I have ever taken in my life. The most boring lectures I have ever attended. He expects you to read countless articles and watch hours of recordings outside of class. Not even close to worth it for an I-series. DO NOT TAKE.

It is super evident he wants to connect with students by remembering names and asking about their majors (which is nice considering every other time you feel like just a number at UMD.) Assignments and exams aren't bad at all as long as you do the weekly HW and have an understanding of what's going on, plus he is always happy to help students!

Be aware, when he says he grades for A's, it's all lies. Absoultley horrible at teaching and expects students to do everything on their own. That wouldnt be a problem, but in the recorded lectures he leaves a lot of stuff missing and expects us to fill it in, never giving the correct answers. DO NOT TAKE this class.

at the beginning he makes this class seem very simple saying "I grade for As" which was a bigger lie than OJ being not guilty. The prerecorded videos are hard to follow and he never addresses teaching material in class other than just doing example problems. His exams are very vague and he is a very strict grader. Good luck getting a A

This class may be a 100 level course, but it is far from that. Even though there is no homework (except for the presentation and paper), the exams are so complicated and annoying that trying to get a decent grade on it is almost impossible. If you're looking for an easy I-Series class, then do NOT take this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This class may be listed as a 100 level one but that's in name only. The tests are pretty hard and the only reason I didn't completely bomb them was because he curves them. Lectures aren't that helpful either and you could skip it and look at the ELMS slides. If you need an i-series credit, you should steer clear of this class and look elsewhere.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Despite the changes to classes because of COVID, Murrell did a good job of listening to students and making sure that our input was taken into account when he designed the course. He does his best to teach content in a way that students will actually learn something. He cares that his students do well and that makes a big impact.

He's a nice guy but lectures are boring. He takes simple concepts and goes over time. The paper, midterm and final are each worth 25% so that's 75% of your grade. There are discussion quizzes every friday based on the readings which are assigned articles and videos. The tests are nothing like lecture. You have to make a presentation in discussion.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a nice guy, but the lectures are incredibly boring. Heck I'm writing this review in his class right now because I'm bored out of my mind. Going to lectures isn't needed to pass this class, and the class isn't that much work. If you go over the slides and readings on your own time, the tests aren't bad and you can easily get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE FOR REAL.I am a computer science student, and i have already taken the microeconomics(ECON200). But his lecture is still hard to understand, and I personally think it should not even called a 100 course, because the reading work is heavy and the exam contains a lot of those reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dont take this class. He does not even grade the course until the end and everything about his course is really bad. For example, if you have questions about the paper you have to write in the course that is worth 25% of your grade, make sure you ask it a week in advance, otherwise, you will not be able to ask any questions about it.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Chill professor. Tests are straight-forward and curved up. Interesting lectures and concepts. Scottish accent

He's obviously intelligent and knows what he's talking about, but he doesn't teach. He uploads the Powerpoints for lectures weekly, and during lecture, he just reads off the presentation without presenting new information. I ended up skipping lecture and teaching myself. At least you don't have to buy a textbook.

She basically just reads from the powerpoints every single class but you still have to go because she gives pop quizzes. The lab was unnecessarily long and extremely boring - you only do one hands on experiment. Assigned work even during spring break and did not accept anything late. Does not seem to care much about her students.

The class was enjoyable at first but then at the very end of the semester the professor started making quizzes on lockdown and made the final in person instead of online like it originally said on the syllabus. Feeling overwhelmed? Too bad you HAVE to go to class because she doesn't tell you when pop quizzes are and you have to sign in.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever! She just reads from her power points which are not posted until after class. She has pop quizzes almost every week so attendance is mandatory. During the last class, the review was not even posted for students who were not able to attend the class. She just makes everything so troublesome as if she seeks students failure.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I took her for MIEH 300 and she was great. Lectures aren't mandatory but discussions are. In the lab, you participate in group work that is straightforward but make sure to follow the rubric. Our exams were online. There are weekly quizzes and assignments. Ended up with an A which is more than capable to achieve. Just do the work & follow instructi
i just can not stand labs, this makes no sense to me and you are at the mercy of the quality of your ta

The class depends on whether you have a good TA and who your lab partners are...you will not like it here. It is not fun. If you can get credit for this elsewhere, like a community college, do yourself a favor and do that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Everything depends on your TA honestly, I've never had an experience with the actual professor.

Take her. She organizes the class so well, teaches clear, and gives you everything you need to succeed. Weekly quizzes and problem sets give you a great idea of what you need to know. And for exams she gives you an entire prep module that is SO helpful. Even then, she gave you opportunities to improve. I wish more teachers were like her.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Doesn't upload full slides so either have to go to class to get them in which she goes to fast or rewatch lectures on your own at home. Have participation questions or a problem set every class. Doesn't care if you show up late. Posts review resources that are very helpful and exactly like tests.
Show up, take notes, and study. You'll be fine.

i dont usually write reviews but for her i had to, shes a terrible person not even proffesor, inconsiderate and unkind she was so mean and rude even the TAs are scared of her and hate her, i have never met anyone that is so rude for absolutley no reason. DO NOT TAKE HER even if she is the last option just waitlist if you have to -100/10
Do not take this professor. There is no curve on exams and no extra credit. Does not care about her students. Difficult course as it is with much easier professors to take.

My recent completion of a course under the instruction of Dr. Mohan has left me with an indelible mark of dissatisfaction, marking it as one of the most challenging and unpleasant academic experiences I've encountered. While I value the importance of a rigorous education, Dr. Mohan's approach seemed to veer into an extreme.....
Please be sure to attend every class and take notes ,this is a ridiculously difficult class for no reason make use of office hours and set a significant amount of time aside to study
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Mohan is very harsh when it comes to grading. If the papers are not submitted her way specifically, she will automatically give you a 0% and no chance to resubmit. The TA does all the grading in the class, so it also depends heavily on your TA.
Refers students to office of student conduct regularly, many students end up with zeroes on assignments and letter grade reducations which cause them to almost fail. 0/10 recommend.

This professor is generally unkind and sets rigid rules, seemingly with the assumption that being harsh means she is a better teacher. She proves this wrong, as she is simultaneously harsh and bad at teaching. Do not expect compassion.

She was not exceptional as a professor she simply just read off of the lecture slides and that's really it. The class itself was difficult if you don't have any prior biology knowledge. Her exams are difficult and are not multiple choice. She does give resources like practice problems to prepare for the midterms and finals. Overall she was ok.

Attendance for lab was mandatory. Usually the labs didn't go on for the whole 3 hours. Honestly, she was really strict and sometimes harsh abt her grading criteria but as long as u read over the criteria a good 4 times, u were fine. She's easy to reach through email, and was even generous. Your grade honestly depends on how harsh ur TA grades.3.5/5

I did not ever see Dr. Mohan because this is a lab course, but the way that she designed the course was not too overwhelming or difficult. I think that anyone could do well in this lab, as long as they actually pay attention when they study for the pre-lab quiz. It helped me to know exactly what to do. Almost never took the full 3 hours.

The professor is not the nicest when it comes to emailing her about missing assignments or missing class, but overall you deal with your TA more in this class. As long as you have a good lab group the class is not all that bad. There are pre-labs and post-labs that can be timely so it is a lot of work for a 1 credit class.

I never met Swarna because TAs run the actual labs. She just writes the book and creates the lab work for the day, so it all depends on what kind of TA you get. Thankfully my TA was responsive and a fair grader, so this course didn't hurt very much but there was definitely more than a 1 credit classes amount of work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Mohan is an excellent communicator, and teaches the class very well. She talks very quickly, but posts her lectures right after class. Her canvas is super organized, and her exams reflect the material of the weekly, open-note problem sets. Overall, amazing teacher, but studying is still definitely required to do well in the course.

She is one of the great professors I have had, she honestly cares about her students, responds quickly to the emails, and gives a week to finish the makeup labs. If you do your work and come to the class every week there is no way you won't get an "A" in her class. She is very well organized and straightforward.
TA's run the course.

She was one of the worst people, not even just a professor, that I have met. All together awful person. I had to work with her one-on-one and she wouldn't answer my questions at all. When asking her if her goal was for her students to do well she just shrugged her shoulders. Do not recommend her.

The TAs run this course, so I have never seen Professor Mohan before. The coursework is hard, but my TA was so kind and forgiving. The TA really makes or breaks your experience. The grading was a bit much though.

Mohan has 3 grades in the gradebook, weekly quizzes, discussion posts (which are due at odd times, submittable from the end of a lecture - 2 pm/5 pm) which she doesn't let you submit after, even with a medical excuse. Exams were hard and based all on lectures, which was just her spitting out information, not teaching, with surface-level answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I lost my A with the 3rd exam. Lectures super heavy and exams are hard. Shes not the nicest person and is very rude when you try to ask questions. Her lectures go by way too fast and she will ask questions and if no one answers she will say that she will wait until someone participates. If only another professor was listed I wouldve not taken her

Dont take her class ever, I wish I would have read her rating on here. Literally the worst professor ever. She doesnt want you to do well in her classes. If you have an option always choose another professor!!!!!!!!

Dr. Mohan was a pretty good lecturer! Her lectures really prepare you for the exams and weekly quizzes as she asks questions during lectures similar to the exams. She is accessible outside of class and is really helpful during office hours! If you work hard and pay attention it will be easy to get a good grade in this class.
The TA ran the class, never had a chance to actually meet the professor. Workload was a lot for a 1 credit class, however it was manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She really does nothing for the class. TAs run and grade everything. The only time I met her, she was kinda rude to my class.

Mohan grades very harshly, being extremely nit-picky when grading this semester's lab reports, resulting in a very low average. There's a grading difference between TopHat and the canvas grade, resulting in you only getting partial credit if you get the question correct on the second attempt. Hard lab, even worse for lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Normally I don't say anything bad about professors because I know we all have stuff going on outside school, but for Professor Mohan, I need to warn people. Do not take her if you can help it. She could not care less about her students and she is not even in class, never saw her once. She is nasty in her emails and acts like she hopes you fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I never write reviews but for her I had to. She is a HORRIBLE person. I emailed her several days before a lab report was due asking for a ONE DAY extension because I had to go home to put my dog down, and she sent me what was either an automated response or she genuinely just did not care. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Havent even met the woman. From what I heard she isnt very nice though. The class is taught by a TA
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor is so strict and is not willing to help at all. Shes also a VERY picky grader and will take off points for even the tiniest mistake. She is unapproachable and does not try to connect to her students in the slightest. She created her own system instead of using canvas and would not fix errors in her own learning system.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A lot of work for a one credit class, something is due every other day. The professor is not reachable or approachable. Very condescending when approached. The TAs will be primarily teaching the course, but I'm sure they're overworked too with the amount of grading needed.

Dr. Mohan is an okay professor. Her lectures are easy to understand if you're 100% paying attention. The problem is she doesn't help whenever you need help, she will just say "read the lab manual" even if you did 20 times. There is a bit too much work for a 1 credit lab class, & some of her assignments are just a ton of work.... & she won't help.

It was a very organized course, assignments set Monday-Friday. Be prepared to do about 5 assignments each week. She is not lenient when it comes to grading, so make sure you thoroughly read the manual and watch her videos. The TA provides great feedback on lab reports.

Dr. Mohan laid out this class very well. There is quite a bit of work though. If you set aside time to read and take notes on the 10 pages per week in the textbook, all of the assignments should come pretty easily. I will mention that Dr. Mohan takes plagiarism more seriously than any other professor I've had so it's best not to plan on cheating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: For a one credit class, the work load is astronomical. Something is due 4/5 days a week. The work and requirements are laid out in the beginning of the week which is cool, but professor Mohan is a tough grader and not always willing to help when needed.

This class is incredibly difficult for a one credit course. Mohan is not accommodating at all and is a very harsh grader. The work load is outrageous and she is not willing to help you pass this class. I recommend you do not take her class.

I wrote a lab report and the turnitin score was high. I didn't plagiarize it, but she was convinced I did and refused to hear my case.I was given a zero on the assignment which caused my grade to drop. She also denied an extension on a lab report despite me having mandatory military training.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst, least understanding professor I've ever encountered. The rumors about her are true. I had no option but to take her lab section as it's required for my major and I spend more time on this 1 credit class than any of my 3 or 4 credit classes. It's ridiculous how the bsci lab is SIGNIFICANTLY harder than bsci170.

This class is overwhelming. I spend more time on this 1 credit class than I spend time on my 3 and 4 credit classes. The class is very difficult and it sucks out all my energy. We have assignments almost every day. This is my worst experience ever with a difficult class. Some TAs are good but some are very harsh grader. Cant wait to finish this.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's inaccessible to students, either doesn't respond or responds with condescension. We have assignments due nearly everyday, and they're graded ridiculously harshly (especially for a one credit class) & without feedback. She's also not understanding for most circumstances. Overall, manageable but dreadful class with an unhelpful professor.

DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. It is a 1 credit class and we have something due 4/5 days of the week every week. We have a lab report and she has given NO guidance at all and is so condescending. She asks that you don't ask her for help. AND she says you may have only 3 extensions with good reason; if a fourth time you have a good reason, you will get a 0.

This woman is obtuse, arrogant and down insolent. This stupid class is 1 credit and the volume of work is ridiculous. The class is not hard but if you have question she refuses to answer or clarify. She should not be a professor. She should be in a career that does not require interpersonal skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Biology is difficult so that was a given but the online format was hard. Her instructions were confusing and assignments were due almost every weekday at noon. However, you get 2 attempts for quizzes and I ended with an A so it is not impossible. She is very knowledgeable and professional so I believe it may be this format that throws things off.

This class was very easy. In the beginning it was easier but it got more difficult as time went on. Even though it got more difficult it was definitely doable, her grade cuttoffs for an A were below 90% but her weekly quizzes were super irritating and inconvenient. Overall, she's okay and if you put in some effort you will get an A.

I appreciated that the class & assignments were asynchronous. I think the concepts could have been easy, but I didn't understand what she meant a lot of the time. I don't think I would have done well without a tutor. I recognize that it is very hard to teach during this time, so she deserves a lot of credit. It was just not my learning style.
I found BSCI171 to be a very good course. I enjoyed that students could attend any TA's office hours. There were office hours multiple times per day and the TA's were very helpful and kind.

It is not really Mohan as much as it is her TA's. They are extremely tough graders. Mohan is nice for the most part and responds to emails quickly. You have 3 assignments due every week. If you read the Lab Manual and listen to her lectures you'll be just fine. Good luck to anyone thinking that because it's a lab it'll be easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Mohan for lab online and be warned when it says that you only have her once a week. That's a lie. She literally gives work with deadlines three times a week and she makes them due at noon. You have quizzes twice a week but they aren't too bad. The online labs are fun but her lab reports get tedious. She makes us buy her lab manual.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Mohans class was not very hard at all! There are definitely an absurd amount of assignments for the class being worth only one credit, but they arent very hard. Your TA will be your main contact and will grade just about everything. Watch the lecture and read the lab manual and you should do great!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Mohan is strict and straightforward. She is not very helpful herself, especially since this class is asynchronous, so if you need help you have to ask a TA. The lectures are not that long but do not provide adequate information for the weekly quizzes. Overall this class is a LOT of work (labs, quizzes, lab reports) all for just 1 credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The professor herself isnt very helpful. She has a policy that makes late things automatically a 0 with no compassion. She is very cold and when she answers emails she doesn't seem to care at all if you explain a difficult situation. The class starts of easy and all of a sudden gets really hard and over the top. The TAs are really tough graders.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this class online bc of COVID. She was the WORST. Her lectures didn't help with the assignments to do, and these couldn't be turned in late. The TA's did more in teaching me stuff about this class than she did- she did like a 15 minute lecture for the week and was like 'done!'. I had no clue what I was doing for the entire semester.

TA's are the one's who will be teaching you in this class. But Dr. Mohan is very helpful with answering questions via ELMS. BSCI171 isn't tough at all. The practical is simple! Just study before hand and your grade will be set for the semester. There is a big project due towards the end. Make sure you give yourself like 3 days to do it!!!

Professor Mueller is an amazing professor. Class is an easy A, with no exams, just 4-3-2-1 essay quizzes which are not too crazy as long as you put in an effort to it. He is a very laid back and chill person and is also quite funny.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: Easy A. No exams. Only 4-3-2-1 quizzes due every other week which are basically on your thoughts on the readings. One group project at the end of the semester.
Dr. Mueller is such an amazing proff. He really caress about his students a lot.
Empathetic and just really cool. He makes class fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Mueller is the best teacher. For SOCY 241, his assignments were 4-3-2-1 Essay x5 (1 was dropped) and Final Group Project. It was easy. Not any regurgitation or exams needed to be studied or memorized. Although you need to read and comprehend the material. Overall the best teacher. Wish more UMD professors are like him.
Absolutely loved him! Super sweet, caring, Very little homework, very understanding, easy grader. Definitely take him!

the class is really straightforward. To pass exams, go to class and read his slides afterwards. Depending on your group, it is out of your control on who your members are so good luck with hopefully having people that will do the work since you all get the same grade for it.

Jeff was amazing, he taught his classes in a way that helped me to remember concepts very well. The content from lectures is really all you need to pass the exams, and he even hosts a Zoom meeting literally giving topics you need to know that are very similar to exam questions. The group project should be a breeze if you have a reliable group.

Rating this guy anything other than a 5 is criminal. Jeff was by far the best and most interesting professor I've had so far. The class only meets once a week and the homework is very minimal with it mostly being Pearson online texts and a group project at the end of the semester. It's very important to pay attention during the lectures. Tests MC

To succeed on the exams you must pay attention during lectures. They aren't boring but are a bit long. I personally didn't use the textbook because the slides and videos are enough in my opinion. Assignments never have a clear rubric, just try your best and ask questions. Overall a good professor and fairly easy class!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Mund is a great professor who cares about the class and the content. The lectures are not super boring, as he will try to include as many real-world applications of the content as possible. The tests are very easy as long as you show up to class and pay attention to the lectures. If you do all your work, no extra effort is needed for an A.

Professor Mund made BMGT110F enjoyable. The jokes, powerpoints, and real-life applications were extremely useful. Creating a business plan throughout the semester was not a skill I thought I would have this early on, and I appreciate it. However, the business plan is a group project. If you aren't a group person, consider a different instructor.

Mund is one of the most engaging professors I've ever had. He makes it easy to listen in class. He does want everyone to participate, so he calls on people randomly. The workload is not bad at all. Much less workload than some of my other classes.
Best professor. He really cares about his students. I definitely recommend him again

Great teacher. Big group project thats pretty easy if you have partners that do their work, but there is no clear rubric. Easy midterm and final based heavily on lecture material and not every detail in the textbook, he gives his slides. He calls on random people in class but he doesnt go hard on you if you dont know anything.
Amazing teacher. So nice and really cares about his students. Definitely take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Mwepu for the most part is great, but there were times when his tone would come off as if he was annoyed. One time I asked him, "How many questions are on the exam?" He said (no kidding), "I cannot tell you that," as if this question really irritated him. It's shocking considering other professors tell you how many questions are on their exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr Mwepu was a great teacher. The exams are challenging but he gives you all the information, in class paper practice/examples, videos, in depth study guides. He is a lenient grader and gives a lot of partial credit and extra credit. Grade breakdown is nice exams aren't weighted too heavy. Textbook is not needed lectures have everything.

My favorite class this semester. It was challenging however he made it easy and very truly cared about all of his students being successful in this class. Need to go to class, he explains most things that would otherwise be difficult. Two pop quizzes but never got grades for them  He is so funny unintentionally and I wish he taught more classes

I would not recommend taking this professor. He is not the best at explaining things and gets an attitude when students try to ask questions during lectures. He does not always respond fast and is not always the most welcoming when it comes to needing help in the course. There is a lot of homework as well for a 100-level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This professor gave me such a love for linguistics and I am truly excited to go to class. He always has something kind to say and he genuinely is so proud of his students when they get something right. The coursework is balanced and if I ever had questions, he was quick to respond with an answer that really made me think.
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is very personable and caring. He's a funny guy, I like his class. I will say that you NEED to know the IPA chart for the English alphabet during the course of this class. If you study the power points and in class assignments, you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Mwepu is a very funny and kind man, but he sometimes is confusing and doesnt answer questions right. You dont need to do the readings as long as you go to class. His lectures are interesting and worth going to. I wouldnt take this class again, but I would take him as a professor again. Tests are easy as long as you take good notes.

Very lecture heavy, mostly reads off of slides. Keeps the class interesting with stories. Not very tech savvy. Cares a LOT about his students, will be very understanding of any absences or late work as long as you talk to him about it.

I tried so hard in this class and Im not gonna say he wasnt lenient with everyone, because he was. But it was because his class was extremely difficult and work heavy for no reason and the students could NOT keep up with his unrealistic expectations. Im a Pre-Med major and Im taking some challenging classes but this one takes the cake.
