reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One day due to technical issues I could not join the lecture, he was very understanding and offered to organize a zoom meeting to go over the lecture again with me since I missed it. He genuinely cares about the topic and wants to help students prosper and enjoy the content he is teaching. Best professor ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Too harsh of a grader, the content is very interesting but it is ridiculous to be taking off points for such small items. I got a higher grade in a much harder class than this one. The professor needs to rethink the grading rubric
This Professor is too harsh of a grader. There is no reason to be getting a B in this class. Ridiculous rubrics for this class.

Such a difficult grader, many points taken off without reasoning. The final is super difficult, especially considering that there are no other exams of that type in the class. He's really sweet but the class is not very engaging and the grading is really tough considering the course content.

Seo is one of those professors that you know genuinely cares about the course content and the students. Sometimes, you'll lose points here and there on an assignment that you feel you shouldn't have but he does leave long feedback on the big projects. Provided lecture notes are very detailed and all of the assignments relate directly back to them.

This professor's workload is super redundant. He has a group project towards the end of the semester that entails a 10 -12 page report, along with a individual assignment that is also another 10 pages. Both of these project overlap each other and basically is a repetition of assignments. VERY tedious grader, & grades are screwed towards the end.
Great professor. Very respectful, listened to the students, and engaging. Class was fairly interesting. Easy grader if you try.

Hands out all power point slides and is a very nice professor. His lectures can be boring, but he Shows passion for the subject of leadership. A lot of team activities and presentations. Only one final at the end that is based on lecture slides. Overall, very nice and understanding professor.
Great professor
By far the absolute most amazing professor you will ever take at your time here at university of Maryland.
Amazing professor that is really engaging and loves working with students
He is a great lecturer and knows his stuff. Truly a great teacher

You don't see Dr. White unless you go to office hours. It's just labs, it's pretty easy if you do the work. The TA I had was very nice and helpful. Dr. White has office hours but only once a week. This isn't a difficult class at all, the professor just really doesn't matter because you don't see her at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I don't recommend anyone taking her class. She is very hard to understand and she doesn't listen to understand. Don't bother asking her any questions, she thinks she's always right. Not sure how she got a job at a University when she doesn't have a Ph.D.

She was a difficult professor. The amount of homework was way too much, the exams were difficult (sometimes they were from the textbook, but with over 200 possible problems per chapter, you probably can't memorize them all), and she was not accommodating at all about conflicts, even though she taught a 1 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor White is a nice woman who is clearly very knowledgeable about chemistry. Professor White + CHEM134? She made me I wish I had studied harder to get a 5 on AP Chem. This is a 3 credit course disguised as a 1 credit course. The content is hard and there is a lot of it to cover, and Professor White's organization of the course is its downfall

Prof. White takes a hands-off approach to running the lab. She implemented Friday review sessions that were phenomenal; I finally began to understand the experiments. She is a great teacher, so attend her office hours and review sessions. Exams are extremely difficult. Reports are graded harshly. However, the course is curved 8-10%.

You see Dr. White for 30 mins at the beginning of the semester and thats it. Everything is done by TAs. This class is supposed to be taken with CHEM135, but the material in the lab will always be far ahead of of the material covered in CHEM135. The lab reports are graded harshly and points are taken off for everything. Good luck if you take this.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I had bad luck in choosing a partner. We split after working on 2 reports together- Professor white didnt make it any easier. Any questions I sent her were forwarded to the TA responsible for grading that specific paper. Some TAs answer your question with a question, so imagine getting forwarded to them because she didnt bother responding to you.

It is pivotal that you get a good partner for this lab. You write a report together every week, if they don't pull their weight it will sink your grade. Dr. White gave informative lectures and fair exams. I enjoyed the class and the lab. The variety of equipment used gives a wide array of experience and was the most useful lab I have taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Worst experience ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Wonderful, supportive professor. Really knowledgeable about the arts and their relation to the mainstream culture.

REALLY into his subject matter. Vast knowledge of 20th Cent. US culture - he saw Snow White in theaters in NYC as a child. He loves documentaries and foreign films; always shows great ones. Likes friendly class discussions; GET involved in discussions. Lenient with deadlines; gives real feedback. Loved him. Strange assignments, graded fairly. Fun!

Lounsbury is one of the few professors at MD who CARE and really helps his students. His knowledge vasts so many interesting concepts,his wisdom alone has allowed me to reach great heights in life since graduating.He is a first class human being.In 2012 there will be a large contribution to the AMST department dedicated to his name from my family.

I think Dr. Lounsbury is getting a bad rap here. The guy is extremely knowledgeable about the material and willing to discuss any sort of ideas you may have. The questions are open ended on the papers and while it takes some effort you can make your own meaning. I tend to write papers at the last minute and NEVER got less than an A. Open your mind.

He was completely unclear in his questions and papers. He also tended to mumble for about an hour of each class, regardless of who could hear or understand him. The class itself would have been great if it was instructed by a different professor. I would not at all recommend signing up for one of his classes. Nice guy, horrible professor.

Dr. Lounsbury is old-school (think 80s cultural criticism), quirky, but amusing. Has a habit of holding up 5 fingers no matter what number he is saying. Says "play-zure" a lot. Shows rock and roll documentaries. Good classes if you keep your sense of humor.
he knew a lot about the course, but was way too behind the times. he often mumbled to himself so you couldn't hear him.  just not worth having on a monday night from 6:30 to 9:45
nice guy...but a terrible teacher. maybe he was a good teacher years ago but now he has probably just been teaching for too long.
Dr. lounsbury shows movies that are not your typical stuff, but they are quite mind opening. this class really made me think a lot and he encourages interesting discussion, not stupid stuff

Lounsbury is a nice enough guy but he rants for 45 mins and then wants to open up a disscussion when there is only 5 mins left. In the middle of posing questions he mumbles to himself and no one can hear him.

we watched a lot of different movies and analyzed them extensively. Dr. L knows his material well and is open to any interpretation you may have of the material. with the exception of the class being late at night (hard to stay awake after a long day), the class was interesting - i recommend it
He was a nice guy, but a little behind the times. I wish he structured the class differently. Easy to get a B in the class. Watch some good movies that I wouldn't have watched before.

The man is a ranting lunatic.  The class is easy enough, but he is...behind the times, and tends to reply to logical comments with a string of false logic that has nothing to do with what was said.  oyy.

Franck was a nice teacher who taught everything in a clear manner and I think he's one of the better MATH120 professors. He liked my class so he was really funny. He gives the concepts for each section and then goes through examples with you. There are quizzes almost every class on the previous class's material but he only keeps your best 10.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You usually can get to his class from Math015 to avoid the most hated math professor in the entire department (Rosca). The class wasn't bad nor was it good, the midterms were way too easy compared to the final exam. You will be putting in minimum 30hrs a week to fully understand concepts taught in class because he's pretty vague about the material.

Franck was okay. This lectures were simple and clear, but he gives a test at the end of class for the majority of the semester. Not to mention, he left on a trip for about 2 weeks right at the end of the course and my class was left with a sub who was VERY unhelpful. Franck never went back over the topics the substitute was supposed to teach
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a great teacher who can explain the concepts in very simplified terms, but he is a jerk. He does not care about your life outside of the classroom, and in his room, it's his way his rules and he is not afraid to tell you that in front of the whole class. Just isn't a nice guy. Great teacher tho.

He was a really good math prof especially having to teach math online. There was a test at the end of most classes, but they were super straightforward. The exams were also very fair and nothing unexpected for the most part.

I loved him! His lectures were okay but his sense of humor about math made me actually appreciate it! We had a quiz every day at the end of class but they're straightforward and easier than the many homeworks he assigns. His tests weren't too bad either. He dropped many quizzes and many homework scores and was super accessible outside of class.

She's a really tough grader and there's no clear grading criteria for her essay questions on exams. She always says that she looks for "critical thinking" but it's not really possible to demonstrate that with super broad questions when you've only got a very short time to write your answers during the test.

Andrade is a challenging professor. While the material isn't too difficult, her teaching style is confusing and often unrelated to tests. Final grading is inconsistent with curves applied to some but not others. This course would benefit from a new teacher with a better approach to the material. This is a required CE course so try and push through

Professor Andrade is an amazing professor and truly cares about her students. She is quick to reply to any email and communicates very effectively. She is an amazing professor to have in any study abroad experience and enhances the class with her knowledge and lectures.
she makes the class much harder than it has to be

She seems nice but boring in her ENCE100 class. don't be fooled she's a very grouchy professor who strains us with tedious conversions and a subject matter that has nothing to do with civil engineering. this class is required so just bare through.

Lectures and homework had nothing to do with each other. We were expected to teach ourselves the math problems. Weird mix of a sociology and math class, like why couldn't we have a sociological-engineered perspective only class? We already have enough math classes.. Class was way harder than it needed to be. Don't get me wrong, she is very cool tho

Very great class. Being an engineering major, it was nice to have a different type of class. Lectures we would talk a lot more about real world problems as opposed to the normal lecture. The end of the year project was a very fun debate amongst our classmates. If you put in the work you will reap the benefits.

She is never going to explain any problems in class. Her lectures contain data and simple conceptual stuff and make you think critically about topics, but nothing similar to quizzes or exams. She doesn't give clear feedback on group projects so cant really revise them for final submission. Final is tough and graded heavily, dropped my grade 4%

Natasha is one of the best people you could travel the world with. She is so knowledgeable & has such an appreciation for different places. This class as an incredible experience & Natasha contributed to that so much by being as passionate as she is about combatting climate change & helping engineers think critically & from perspectives new to them

Natasha is the best professor I've ever had. She is a genius & she is realistic & passionate. 215 was challenging but enjoyable & she cares deeply about everyone's success. This class forces you to think about climate change & other serious problems which is a great growing experience

She is the worst professor I have had yet. Her lectures are not helpful whatsoever. She will lecture about real life examples of engineering for sustainability, but when it comes time for the quiz/test she asks you to do calculations that she never showed you how to do in class. Unfortunate that she is the only ENCE215 professor.

Natasha was an amazing person to get to know during my study abroad course. She cares about every individual and does her best to get to know everyone on a personal level. In the short period of time that I had with her, she became one of the professors that I will definitely reach out to from time to time as a friend rather than student.

I took Natasha for a study abroad class and she really made sure everyone was able to make the most of the trip! We learned so much in the short period of time we were there both in the classroom and on field trips. Natasha is a very caring professor who makes sure you are learning but is there to help you along the way. I highly recommend !
Turns engineering class into a english class. Come on! it's an engineering class, we don't want debate!

Studying abroad with Professor Andrade was a great experience. She did a great job planning the trip so that it was both fun and educational. She is very knowledgeable and passionate about the course material which made the lectures and field trips extremely interesting and informative. Would definitely this class.

Dr. Andrade clearly cares about what she's teaching about, and it comes through. She can be a relatively tough grader, but she does everything she can to keep it very fair and it is happy to explain anything. The only down side is her lectures are pretty conceptual, but quizzes, hw, and majority of tests are on methods and calculations.

Andrade is very relatable, nice person. Cares about students' learning and always looking to improve the course. Makes class interesting and all of the learning is done in class. Is very fair when it comes to grading/course load. There is a large group project and tests can be hard, but if you do the HW and put forth effort you will be fine.

Overall, her lectures are decent. She explains most of the slides in her lecture recordings, so its important to watch them. She uses Kahoot for attendance (worth 5% of your grade for participation). For exams, study her water break questions, the HW questions, and the TNR Redigest questions, they are typically on the exams.

Dr. Ngeve is great, you can tell she cares and wants everyone to pass. She will constantly ask for student feedback. The exams let you have a flashcard and the final was opened note but it is a ton of material. If you do not need this class DO NOT take it as a gen-ed

Professor Ngeve tries her best to help everyone and wants everyone to succeed. She goes out of her way to ask for feedback and is very caring and willing to help. Homework is sometimes ambiguous but she helps to make it clearer. Lectures are structured well, exams are often fast paced and contain questions regarding small details covered in lecture

Doesn't go through lectures thoroughly. Does this thing where she goes slowly through the review, then will speed through the rest of the lecture, making it impossible to even process what she said. However, she did ask for feedback and has improved her pace some over the semester. The TAs are also very strict with grading (hence the tag)

Dr. Tran Nguyen is cool. She has a lot of patience and her office hours are flexible. I didn't know anything about filmmaking and she was really great about my entry level. Take her class, it was one of the more fun, easy ones TDPS has.

Just show up, she really cares about attendance and if you miss a class you really miss a lot. Be prepared to do some work outside of class, the projects aren't the easiest but they are fun and most of them are group projects. But other than that, the class is really easy and she gives good feedback. I highly recommend her class in the spring.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Tran Nguyen's class was one of the best classes I have taken. It was super hands on and she is really great about meeting outside of class. I was falling behind because of family stuff and I had covid and she was really understanding. Plus, the projects are really fun. Take Process and Play if you can!

Dr. Tran makes you work for it but is really understanding and easy to reach. I have been able to get meetings with her outside of her office hours and she was really helpful. The class is hard and there is a lot of reading, do not take it if you want an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Tran's class was a lot of work and reading but overall, worth it. There are not many reading lists that are as diverse as hers and she is great on a one on one basis.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is really helpful if you go see her during her office hours. Dr. Tran Nguyen gives feedback and drops your lowest grade. Great class if you need an elective.

Dr. Tran Nguyen is the best! She is tough but really cares about her students. If you do the readings and participate you will get an A. Her feedback on presentations help and drops your first grade if you do better the second time.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She gives extra credit and cares about her students. Make sure you read! She truly will call you out if your not reading or prepped for class.
It's a lot of reading but most of the readings are easy and she talks about them in class to make sure we get it. She also does mid semester check in to make sure we're not falling behind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: I just read the review from above, it makes no sense. Van does not give out homework at all, there is only one paper in the entire course and she practically helps you outline it via the presentations. And the one pop quiz that was for zero credit just to see if everyone is getting it and on the same page. Def taking her spring class

Van's great! She doesn't give out much homework, she really cares about her students and I've had great office hours visits with her. You just need to show up and have done the reading for class, and her feedback on my presentation was helpful.
She doesnt help at all. She is not clear and doesnt answer any questions. Dont take her classes
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: he grades super harshly and is not clear when asked specific questions. does not post answer keys with his review material, so it is difficult to know if you are studying properly. I'm a senior with a very high gpa and he is the first professor I've ever rated, and the worst I've ever had

If you get a bad team then you're tanked and will spend 8+ hours on every lab report, but otherwise Vince is a very passionate and forgiving teacher. Grades are pretty generous depending on your lab section instructor. Learned a lot

So I took this class over the summer and it was nothing like I expected. He really makes you dive into the material and understand every last detail until you can spit it out like a machine. That being said, I learned so much about vibrations but he is a VERY harsh grader. Just a warning..
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Vince is a great professor, but he moves VERY FAST through material and lectures. He both talks and writes fast. That being said, he usually works out problems from the book although he does not explicitly say so. Not an easy A. Lots of material covered in a very short amount of time. Exams are lengthy. 1 problem set/week. 2 exams + final. 1 proj
A good teacher but a very hard grader

Karen Nelson is by far the best professor I have had during my time in school. She is not only incredibly kind and respectful, but she is also very dedicated to her course and extremely intelligent! While the material in class may be a bit difficult, she does everything she can to make it as easy as possible to understand and learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: You can tell that Professor Nelson cares about her students' progress, she offered several opportunities to meet with her to discuss upcoming projects which I found super helpful. The lessons were also super engaging and fun. Also Professor Nelson was super easy to reach out to, and is very understanding of late work and absences.
Fantastic teaching, and fun besides. Demanding course, but she keeps it lively all the way through.

Prof Nelson is great! Her assignments and lectures are engaging and fun, even with Zoom University. The work she asked of us in this class wasn't overwhelming either, as many classes can be. She asked us what we were interested in and molded the course's direction to fit, which was super nice. She's also very enthusiastic and approachable to boot!

Attendance isn't exactly mandatory but you do have in-class assignments that are graded so if you want an A, you can't really skip. Clear assignments, not a tough grader but not easy either. Mostly short papers; as long as you argue your point effectively, you'll get an A. Personally, she is one of my favorite Professors at UMD. 12/10
His English class was very enjoyable, especially the in-class activities we did.
Great professor, easy on grading, I would highly recommend for English gen Ed credit

He seems unprepared for the class a lot, leaving modules on ELMS 'locked' even when the deadline is approaching. It is obvious that teaching is his passion, but I wish he put more preparation into explaining the course concepts, he really breezes thru all the slides. Overall good prof, needs time mgmt. skills and better communication with students.

Professor Nelson was one of my favorite professors at UMD. He tries really hard to get students involved and interested in English. He's a bit of a tough grader and makes you work for an A. There is one mandatorygroup project about gardening which is a huge pain, buthHe also ends up dropping some of the writing assignments later on.

Really great professor. He cares about students, will work with you if problems come up, and makes this class fun. If you show up, do the work, and put forth some effort, you'll get an A. He'll tell you that himself. When I took it, there was a garden-based service-learning component, so there were opportunities to get out of the classroom.

Awesome professor who really cares about the students and will help you succeed. Assignments aren't too bad and he offers solid feedback on all of them. Also offers numerous extra credit opportunities throughout the semester.
His class is very easy, just follow the examples in the textbook. I only got an 89 because I missed many classes due to personal issues.

I wish he taught all of my classes, he's reasonable, cares about his students, and is willing to work with you. Assignments are not bad; he has writing assignments and reflective writings (you choose 5 of 6) and is clear with what he wants. Go to class, he's funny and relatable. I never did any of the readings. You'll get an A if you just try a bit

Professor Bennet is a great professor when it comes to lectures. He has some of the best lectures in the stem department. The only problem I have with him is the difficulty of his tests. His tests are extremely difficult. You never know what material is going to be on the exam. He also isn't very accessible outside of class. He is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Bennett was okay but his way of organizing the lecture was really confusing for me. I have ADHD and trying to keep up with him jumping forward and backward a bunch of slides while making jokes made it very difficult to keep up. I failed the first few exams but once I adapted, I got an A on the final and the third exam.

Professor Bennett is one of the better STEM professors at UMD. His exams are not difficult contrary to some reviews. He makes real-life connections to the content and is clear about expectations for grading. There was no reason for the class the petition for a curve in a 200-level bio class when the exam averages were good. He is also a funny guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall Bennett was probably one of my favorite professors. Students who do not like him typically do not but enough work into the course (its anatomy, anyone should expect to be studying regularly to get a good grade). He is funny and he truly wants his students to succeed not only in class but in their future jobs, which is why he does not curve.

Professor Bennette was a decent professor. In general, Anatomy is a content heavy course that you really need to prepare for, and Professor Bennette's lecture slides gave you all the information you needed. Although somewhat monotone he would say outrageously funny things, and his stories really help you understand the material.

I've never written a bad review before, but this guys exams are unnecessarily difficult. Unclear grading criteria, mislead the students in regard to what we'd be tested on, very unenthusiastic and monotone. Rambles on off-topic things, & says some very uncomfortable stuff. Would not recommend unless you want a difficult semester
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: quizzes and tests are pretty easy. All lectures are online. You only interact with the TA in person since he lectures asynchronously online. Attendance isn't taken but some group work happens and parts are assigned in class so attendance is good.

I sent him multiple emails throughout the semester and never received a reply. He does not seem present or involved in this class at all. His quizzes are unnecessarily difficult and though the tests are open notes, don't let that fool you.

The professor is almost non-existent as far as being involved with the class. The lecture is online (asynchronous) and the discussion is in person. I've reached out to the professor numerous times through email for questions about grading and exams that I would rather the professor answer than the TA. I never received any responses.
Dr. Sehgal was pretty nice, and easy to talk to. Most of our work was graded by the TA's, so make sure you have a good one. Exams were open note, but not to the point where you don't have to study.

This class was very disorganized and lacked communication. The professor was lazy and relied on TAs to do the heavy lifting, but most of them did not, leaving us not knowing what was going on. Due dates were changed, assignments were added and cancelled - all without telling us. Neil is a fine lecturer but beware that the quizzes and exams are HARD
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: One of the most interesting and relevant classes I've taken. He made it so easy to stay entertained during class and his lectures were easy to understand. Easy A class, and open-note exams!

Professor Sehgal is so great and really shows he cares about what he is teaching and makes health policies interesting. He also really shows that he cares about his students, which is really nice. The only bad thing about this class is although the exams are open note, they are still kind of hard and the notes won't always help you.

Professor Sehgal was a funny instructor who cares about health policies. His class was welcoming and encouraged participation. Though attendance wasn't mandatory, he offered easy points for showing up. He occasionally discussed his political views in class, which was quite distracting. This class was not overly challenging but offers great info!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Solid Professor

I loved Dr. Mogul. I thought the material in this class was interesting and my TA was great. There are a TON of papers though, and a pre-lecture before almost every class they aren't hard but they are time-consuming. The class is graded off a grading contract so you'll get an A if you do the work. 
.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: Weird and very uncomfortable classes.  Her lectures are hypocritical and make no sense.  Easy class, but no logic and very biased.  Also very offensive material to minority groups.

The content of ENEE200 in my opinion is quite uninteresting, but I can't speak positively enough about how great of a professor Dr. Mogul is. She shows an undeniable care for students, and even sat on the phone with me for 45 minutes to help me deal with personal stuff. Lots of reading/writing, but fairly easy to get an A.

Professor mogul genuinely cares about class and her students, so she tries to make lectures enjoyable. Class content is not super interesting but if you put in effort, participate, and do the work you will get at least a B+ if not higher. Lots of reading and writing but no exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: USELESS, BORING but engaging class. She will ask you to stand in a circle and answer stupid questions and move a lot in the room just like in a primary school. Lectures and discussions are tedious and phones and laptops are forbidden so you cannot do anything else but suffer. And there are assignments every day, heavy reading and writing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS especially do not take the winter or summer session. Stupid activities in class and read a lot, Almost tons of boring reading materials and also the reports that 1-1.5 single spaced long(everyday). If u r not engineering students, don't take her class; if yes, take the regular sessions or another prof. GRADES are fine tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Mogul is a great person and makes class more enjoyable and easier. Some interesting content but pretty boring at times. No exams in the class but lots of reading and writing. Group activities make class more bearable.

Dr. Mogul is very nice and tries to make the class more enjoyable. There are a ridiculous amount of papers and essays required for the class, however, as long as you try a little bit you will get an A. Lectures are mandatory and during discussion participation counts, but again as long as you put it a little effort, you'll be fine.

Dr. Mogul tries to make her lectures engaging and interesting. I found her sense of humor hilarious. She mixes things up a lot if she thinks it can be done a better way. There's no midterm or final, but instead a draft and then final portfolio. They aren't hard just much writing. Weekly 1 pg papers that are on a considerable amount of reading.
