The only problem with the class is there is like a total of 100pts for your total grade, so not doing well on one assignment could be hard to recover from.

This class has 3 assignments and they're graded harsh. In a nutshell, it's about the factors that led to success in Apollo missions, but every lecture he just gets heavy into engineering and nobody pays attention. None of the assignments have to do w/ the lecture. Doug grades harshly and sticks to a pretty strict rubric. Don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very boring lectures. It seems interesting at first but he loses everyone once he gets into the engineering of the missions more in depth. This class is structured horribly. There's only 4 assignments, one of them being a selfie you need to take for 5% of your grade. One group project, and 2 papers. The lecture material had nothing to do w assignme
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Oard is a good professor. He is more than willing to help students when needed. There are three exams, one of which is dropped so you can possibly skip the final. Although exams are open computer, they are CHALLENGING so you WILL NEED TO READ! Lectures are posted online, so you SHOULD re-watch them to prepare for exams (or if you missed class)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This man is by far the hardest professor at UMD. His review session are a joke because if you ask a question all he says is "You know the answer."  Exams are ridiculous and hard to actually pass.  I would recommend any other BSCI professor over him.  If he is your only option for a professor, I recommend taking it next semester.

Dennis O'Conner's class is hard. He is not very helpful and expects you to know his lectures word for word. He does not like to Repeat himself at all. His study sessions are not helpful and he does not care if you pass the class.

"Can you explain what the okazaki fragments do?" "i COULD... but i don't want to."  teaches straight from the powerpoints, which are like 65 slides each. DOES NOT CURVE!!  in class he will say "question 27 - ....." which makes you think it will be on the test BUT ITS NOT. do not take his class!!! other bsci professors curve! NOT FAIR.
No Comments
Great teacher. Gives lecture notes to follow. Foreign. Will easily get A or B. Tip: Sign up to make case presentation on first day to be considered for grade B can turn to A!!
very good professor, really knows the subject well.
na

The late Professor Odell came to the University of Maryland, College Park where he taught for over 40 years. He loved showing his students see how facts and logic could help them develop sounder views than they may have previously held. He was a visiting professor at Oxford, England and Trinity College, Ireland, and wrote seven books on philosophy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took Dr. Odell's class about 10 years ago and he is, by far, my favorite professor. I find the complaints on this site hilarious. It's incorrect to say he didn't care about other people's ideas. He did, but he most definitely challenged you to defend them. He forces you to think more clearly and logically. I am forever grateful to him for that!

I loved 100 so much, I took his ethics course the next semester. Touchy topic, hence the bad reviews from people w/ deadset ideas on this subject who wouldn't listen. The exam Q's were given in class, so easy tests; the paper was harder, but we were given chances to talk to TAs. Interesting topic, memorable lectures.

I loved his courses, not just because I agree with him 100% either: I don't. You who cry bias need open minds. I loved how he gave lectures (memorable, albeit fast). It helped to have a recorder to fill in notes after, or use a laptop, and study w/ other students. He was one of my favorite profs ever. EASY tests- he gave you the Q's in class!
great prof.

okay so long story short...Professor Odell- go to the discussion sections, participate there, and know the study guide (gives you the questions on the exam, basically)and you'll get at least a B if u have half a brain.

I had Odell for contemporary moral issues and he was fairly bad. As for all you odell lovers, I'd say you like him because you have the same ideals. I on the other hand saw him as extremely condescending towards others views and didn't like anything but his own theory, FBPC, which i thought was only half practical. I loved the class not the teacher

He was completely arrogant and never wanted to here what anyone else had to say. He would shoot down anyone else's point of view. His lectures were boring. The only good thing was he told you exactly what you needed to memorize for the tests, but if you actually go to lectures, don't take this with him, hes terrible.

The funny thing about Odell's course is that it's entirely based around this one theory that he invented that no one in the philosophical community accepts as worthwhile. "Folk based practice consequentialism" is, at best, referred to as a pet theory by the few people who have given the time to pay attention to him.

This was an extremely EASY class... you NEVER need to go to lectures... the material is extremely interesting..as far as you odell haters.. maybe you didnt like him because he is wise and knows how stupid and unrealistic God is

Jack ODell was the most interesting professor I had while a student at Maryland. The occasional negative ratings on this site, are pretty much the work of cowards and blowhards--people who didnt like Odell shutting up their inane ramblings--and didnt have the courage to fire back at him in class; so they do it here. AMAZING man and teacher.
No Comments
Odell is pretty arrogant, but he knows his stuff. PHIL 100 is a pretty tough 100 class I thought. Vocab is really important.

Odell is interesting and concise. He is also extremely fair as far as exam content and curves the exams generously. In my experience, the students who did not like Odell's class were the students taking philosophy to fill a CORE requirement and had no real interest in philosophy. If you have a real interest in philosophy, Odell is good to take.

I did not go to lectures and got an easy A because of my T.A. Mr. O'dell does not do much for the class since he does not grade or answer questions.  If you can get in mr. Klaffel's sections I would def. Take this course.  If you don't like going to lectures  you can take this class and still get a good grade.

Odell is a good prof but his lectures are EXTREMELY boring.  The exams consist of LOTS of vocab(about 80 words on the final) and essays. Plus theres an 8-10 pg essay due in the last discussion section.  You really have to work hard in this class.  Somehow I ended up w/ a B.  The readings are difficult to understand and consume a lot of time.

The class concepts were challenging but to actually pass it was extreemly simple. He lays the tests out clearly. Odell offers interesting points and his own personal opinions, encouraging the students to think. The TAs are very helpful, but discussion is only necessary to get participation. I enjoyed Odells opinions even if not like my own. TRY IT!

The lectures made no sense all he did was read off of his handouts! My TA did nothing to help me understand the class material.  I would definately not recommend taking this class unless you loved philosophy!
I learned absolutely nothing from this class. It was a complete waste of my time. The lectures are boring and hard to understand and my TA was no help whatsoever.

very boring lectures... he talks way to fast for you to write anything down. And at first the class didn't seem so bad but then he started to talk about God and you don't want to get him started on that topic! He wants to be a famous philosopher but all he was able to do was teach at UMD... I wouldn't recommend taking this class to ANYONE!

My TA was the reason that I passed the class. Odell is very pompous and gives obscure lectures. I asked what our essay format should be and he laughed saying: "Well it should have an introduction and a concluding paragraph and supporting body paragraphs. An idiot could figure that out".
No Comments
bad lectures, it was crosword puzzle time for me

overall, odell seems like a neato fun angry athest.  He seems like a teacher i'd be entertained talking to. though when it comes down to things his highly unclear lectures and the difficult to understand readings offer little help for the tests and his TA's tend to be oddballs.
His lectures are hard to understand, wouldn't recommend him if you want to take phil100.  It's hard enough to understand the readings, don't even understand what he says most of the time in lecture.

Dr. Odell is one of the finest professors at this university.  His lectures are energetic, and he inspires students to think through the material he presents.  I changed majors to philosophy after taking his contemporary moral issues class.    Odell works especially well with students who demonstrate that they are thinking.
He sqwaks like a parrot and can't teach at all.
Nelson's 131 class is tough but rewarding. His lectures are engaging, and he cares about students. Utilize office hours and tools like Unstuckstudy to stay on top of the workload.

Nelson is knowledgeable but unprofessional. He often distracts from the material and embarrasses students, like calling out a student for her insulin pump beeping. This behavior impacts students' comfort and participation. He does record lectures though and grades fairly.

Out of all of the computer science professors, Nelson is definitely the best one. He is funny and cares for his students. He really takes the time to get to know each student by name. However, I did not learn anything from lectures or discussions. I taught myself everything and passed the class with a B. Office hours are the key to success!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Took this class as my mandatory computer science credit.  Lots of work but Nelson explained things well and even recorded lectures so you could still get the material if you missed class.

I found this class somewhat difficult, but Nelson made it much better. He really cares about his students and made the class fun with his great sense of humor. Lectures are recorded and the class was based on 8 projects and 4 exams including the final. Don't procrastinate and find friends in the class or go to office hours to make the much easier.

He has a great sense of humor. Lectures are often him discussing a topic and then giving examples, potentially drawing an example to help visualize what is happening. He gives a lot of heads up on what will need to be known for a quiz, exam, or project.

CMSC132 was, is and will be my favorite CS course at UMD, taking it with nelson just made it more fun! If you end up taking it with him, please remember to do all the work on time and listen to all the advise that he gives. I went from struggling to keep up in CMSC131 to enjoying CMSC132.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Nelson is the GOAT for 131. A tip to everyone taking 131, DO NOT PROCRASTINATE.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I took CMSC 131, 132, and 216 with Nelson. He is hands down the best professor I've ever had and truly cares about his students. He posts all his examples, has very organized websites for each class, and posts practice exams. Projects are very time-consuming but the directions are clearly outlined. Would take him again if he taught more classes.

If you don't have that much computer science background he's good since he makes a lot of analogies to help you understand the concept better. Even if you don't get it right away, he gives you little breaks to discuss it with your neighbor and ask questions. His tests are very similar to the practice exams, so study those and you'll be fine!
Nelson is awesome. If you're in FC, you're lucky he's your only choice. He's so funny during lectures and he's always able to keep your attention. An excellent professor for an excellent class.

Nelson is great!!! If you're the type of person to get kind of bored during boring old slide lectures then he's good for you! He relies on examples in the lecture and a few small concepts from the slides. He gives us one-minute breaks in between heavy topics/examples so that we can discuss them with our neighbors which is helpful.

Nelson is a great choice for an intro to programming. His lectures are entertaining and he genuinely cares about students academic and personal well-being. He wants you to speak up about issues and will frequently extend deadlines when he sees the effort being made. Start projects early and practice writing code by hand for exams.

Nelson is clearly a super caring guy. He acknowledges the difficulty of CS and wants everyone to do well. His lectures are also great and keeps you engaged with jokes and stories. However, make sure you don't blank out during lectures as you can miss important info. Projects and exams can be tricky, so make sure you are on top of everything.

Class isn't mandatory, but if its your first CS class go to class or just quit the major while you can. The dude is funny and makes the class entertaining. Computer Science is one of the hardest subjects at umd, so if you don't know Javascript beforehand good luck. The Projects are hard, so are the exams, but if you study you got it.

Professor doesn't curve and when everyone did bad on Exam 3 he said to us everyone did bad but I don't curve and won't for this exam. The TA's talk in circles when you ask them for help so basically you aren't getting help. I would not recommend this class and I wouldn't take it again

I would not recommend this class if you have never taken a computer science class before. There are a lot of time-consuming projects, but he is very lenient with giving you more time if you ask. The tests are extremely hard, like studying for 4-5 days and still failing kinda hard. Nelson does make the lectures not so boring but this class is hard.
Amazing professor. Funny, helpful, does everything right. So lucky to have him
Very helpful professor. Shows understanding for students who are stressed out. Highly recommend.

Nelson is an amazing professor! I took him when the class was fully online so I never got to meet him, but the way his class was run was so easy to follow. The workload is really doable if you watch lectures and attend lab, and he's quick to respond to emails

Nelson does a great job of making a potentially boring class, extremely fun. He explains the concepts well and adds in humor to make it bearable. This class is a lot of work, of course, but here are a lot of ways to get help if you need it. I am going to take his classes as many times as I possibly can.

I'm a newbie when it comes to computer science, but Nelson has been an amazing professor. His pre-recorded lectures were very helpful. This class was definitely difficult, but if you watch the lectures, you'll be fine. I definitely recommend studying for the exams and completing the writing assignments too.

ALWAYS DO THE WRITTEN ASSIGNMENTS. LITERALLY FREE POINTS. I'd recommend putting your phone down during the pre-recorded lectures otherwise you'll fail. If you put in the effort you'll succeed. The wording for some of the projects/exams were kind of confusing. I like the way he says "prototype".

It was a computer science course, so it wasn't easy, but Nelson was amazing. Truly a great teacher and very accommodating to students needs. If you're taking a computer science class, definitely try to have him as your professor!!

No formal live/in person lectures. This class aims more to those who have previous coding experience than first timers. Has a heavy accent that is sometimes hard to understand. All TA lead. It is all project and test based. Very fast paced and a lot of learning on your own is required.
absolutely amazing

I am a math major and have no experience in programming. Since we are in quarantine, his recorded lectures were difficult to follow; If I cannot comprehend enough, I would message him that I do not understand, he tells me to go to TA first, and some TA's make me feel uncomfortable by being rude. In other words, the professor would not help.
This man made 216 a blessing to take

Nelson is one of the best professors I've ever had. He gives out a lot of homework and his projects and tests are rather difficult, but his lectures are really helpful and he knows how to keep the class engaged. If you want a good Computer Science professor, take his class.
Nelson is really funny and seems like a nice guy, but I didn't find his lectures to be very helpful. I wouldn't take a class with him again.

I loved Nelson, for his exams you definitely have to study. I would recommend practicing a little bit everyday, and for every small question ask a TA because it likely will be on the exam. Turn in projects on time and you should pass the class.

A solid choice for a computer science professor. He keeps the class engaged, and his lectures are really good. He gives out a lot of work, but I guess that's expected from a comp-sci class. 100% recommend him.
There are lots of projects, quizzes and tests in his class. If you don't like to do the work, then don't choose him.

If you are non-native speaker or don't have background, DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. He has horrible Spanish accent and ALWAYS tells jokes. If you have background, you will be good. Otherwise, you'd better take other professor's class.
One of the best CS professors out there. Lectures are hilarious, but you don't have to go because he records everything. Provides lots of old exams that are similar to the actual one.

I loved Nelson, but his exams you definitely have to study for effectively. I would recommend studying a little bit everyday, and for every small confusion ask a TA because it more than likely will be on the exam. Turn in projects on time and you should pass the class.

I had 0 programming experience before i took his class. I never missed a class. The same night, i would go and watch his lecture videos. I showed up to TA office hours 4-5 days a week for about 3-5 hours a day for months. I didn't learn a thing. Lecture worthless, Homework difficult and no correlation to actual lecture. Goes too fast. BAD
Do not take if you have no prior computer science experience. Goes faster than other professors and makes assignment impossible. No curve. He is really funny though.

Nelson is a highly praised professor and now that I have had a class with him, I can see why. His lectures are engaging and hes pretty good at explaining the material. Additionally, Nelsons exams are fair, he provides us with exams from previous semesters, they are extremely helpful to study from. 10/10 would recommend. ily Nelson

Amazing, and very funny professor. Lectures keep you well engaged, and he records them for you to re-watch later. Projects can sometimes be vague and tough, but if you go to office hours you will get lots of help and do well. Great guy very nice and approachable, and he genuinely cares about his students. Would take this prof again!
tests are hard, projects are easy, lectures are great, nelson is everyone's dad

Nelson is the GOAT. if you ever get the chance to pick Nelson do it. he is a hilarious guy that can also get lots of work done. the course load is just about equal with other professors and he is a fair grader. gives out the past exams to help you study. you will not be disappointed if you pick him.
Nelson is extremely sweet and understanding and also respectful to women.
BEST PROF OF THE DEPARTMENT! 5/5 MADE CS EASIER. I WOULD NEVER LIKE CODING WITHOUT NELSON. MY SECOND DADDY
luv nelson <3

Nelson is a very good lecturer and gives reasonable exams. He is also very funny. The jokes are a hit or miss depending on the person. Some people love his jokes because they make class interesting, while others find it distracting and annoying. It's really up to you. Also, he posts lecture videos online!

I had Nelson for 132/216. He is a very engaging teacher and makes sure to get to know people as best as possible in a large class. His lectures are boring at times but he does his best by throwing in jokes that can be annoying at times. The projects are interesting and challenging. Prepares you well for exams/quizzes with study material. Highly rec

One of the best professors in the department. His lectures are great and keep you engaged, unless you're not fond of jokes. Once in a while he goes off on a tangent, but it keeps the class entertained and makes lecture worth it. Lectures are also recorded! You need to start projects early and study a lot for exams. All grading is fair.

Nelson is a snag when it comes to CS professors. He can get off topic a bit during the lecture, but that's just him trying to make it a little less boring. He is a very fair grader, and overall the exams were very fair. Project descriptions can be a tad bit vague, but he will always answer questions for those that have them.

He's one of the best intro CS professors here and makes sure that the students are engaged throughout the curriculum. Still projects and tests are tough for 216, but if you pay attention in class it all should be manageable.

I took Nelson for 132 and 216, and I learned so much from him. He truly is a great teacher and has a really good knack for explaining things. However, while he keeps class entertaining, sometimes his jokes cross a line and can easily get annoying, and that gets deterring quickly.
Amazing professor!

Nelson is hilarious and his lectures are entertaining; however, he records all lectures, so attendance isn't mandatory. He responds to student concerns (e.g. changing the release tokens from 24 to 12 hours after a student suggested it) and is fair. You will need to work for your grade but he provides plenty of practice exams.

I was new to CS when taking his class. He is funny & caring that he extends projects if needed. He is a great professor. Although he posts his lectures online, I recommend going to class every time and then rewatch/take notes bc that was very helpful for me on the final exam. Projects are hard but other students are willing to help you understand.

He's alright but exams are unreasonably weighted. For example 1 problem on an exam may be 35-45 points and if you miss it you're done. Was not really clear on which topics would be emphasized on exams; barely curved. He does try to accommodate students, but he is also unwilling to change his syllabus. Overall he's still better than other professors

Nelson is fantastic. Hes really knowledgeable about his topics, and hes always willing to help anyone who needs it. Hes also probably the funniest instructor in the school. Also, dont text in class. He will absolutely call you out on it, and you will be a meme both on Piazza and on Reddit within the hour.

Nelson really cares about his students and is very responsive to all student concerns. Not a great lecturer but he keeps it entertaining; exams and quizzes are very fair and he gives out lots of practice exams. Definitely recommend
Daddy is a great professor. You won't ever regret taking him.

Genuinely cares about helping students - gave several extensions when the class was struggling, and takes feedback well. Sense of humor is hit-or-miss, but he's not boring. Personally I skipped lectures and watched the recordings on 2x speed later, but if you learn better in person he's responsive to questions.

The man is a saint. He's super funny in class but he's also very kind and considerate as long as you follow directions and don't do anything stupid. His lectures are intuitive and he provides tons of resources for you to study from.

The lectures were very engaging. Attendance is not mandatory as he records everything. Quizzes and exams are not that easy but quite fair - he posts old quizzes and exams for review. One of the better CS profs at UMD.

Nelson is good at explaining the general concepts of the class material, using interesting analogies. He also interacts with students on a very friendly level which no other professor does. However the big problem is that he jokes around frequently in class, which didn't allow me and my friends to pay full attention to his teaching.

Cons: Spends too much time goofing around in lectures. Project descriptions can be unclear. Some of the exam questions were terrible. If you email him, don't expect more than 1 sentence as a response. Pros: Lectures weren't boring. Even though the project descriptions were confusing, I learned a tremendous amount from them. He records everything.

He is such an amazing lecturer. He makes the material fun and engaging. He interacts with students and although he records all lectures, his humor and charm are the reasons most people go. He likes to know students names and it's very funny however I get a bad vibe from him as if he doesn't like me. I've tried talking to him but it doesn't change

This class is super hard, especially because its hard to switch from java to C, but Nelson made it way better. This dude is hilarious and extremely smart, and that combination makes it super worthwhile to go to lectures. You will be entertained and enlightened at the same time

This man was worth taking an 8am section. He is so engaging and makes coming to lecture so much fun. He once stopped class just to ask a student what he was texting to his girl friend. The entire class will be engaged by his programming jokes and gimmics. He really inspires me as a student and a programmer. Just don't talk over him when he teaches.

I would definitely take another class with Nelson. Although, he might be scary a few times, he is generally hilarious and tries to motivate the class as much as possible. He puts lecture recordings online which is nice so you don't have to really attend class but I highly recommend attending lectures. Also he can be a little bit of a tough grader.

I have nothing against Nelson, but I had trouble taking him seriously because of his frequent jokes/sarcasm. He certainly knows the material. His lecture recordings are great (I rarely went to class). He simply isn't the type of person I can learn from, and I know others who agree. He doesn't curve and he gives a lot of minus grades (92.7, got A-).
Funniest professor I've ever had. He's also a good lecturer, would recommend

Nelson is funny and often makes jokes during class. Some students may find this distracting/annoying, but I personally found it made me more engaged. He also records his lectures and posts them on Panopto which means if you ever don't feel like going in/didn't understand something during class, you can go back later and watch the lecture online.

Nelson was the most enjoyable professor I've taken in CS. He just has a way of getting across the material in an engaging way. I found his exams fairly easy. His projects were daunting at times but are definitely do-able. Everyone needs someone like Nelson during their CS career. He truly cares and works with students. He won't do you wrong. Take!

For CMSC132/216 Nelson is a very solid teacher. Not sure where people are getting "rude" from- he does jokingly 'pick on' students but checks to make sure they are comfortable with it. He is very caring and genuinely listens to feedback from students. As someone with depression and social anxiety, I found Nelson's accessibility amazing.

I really enjoyed Nelsons class. He got to know me on a first name basis which I thought was very encouraging. I met with him in his office hours from time to time and was really enlightened by our conversations. He uses humor and a dynamic personality to keep his students attention. His projects are tough but bearable. I would highly recommend him

He is incapable of answering nuanced questions that can't be answered from the slides. Usually, he told me my question is too long, and would move on, without letting me clarify. On exams, even if your code is right, if it's not his way, he'll take off points. He can get away with it because his childish humor keeps him popular amongst students.

He's a funny person, but his teaching style is not up to par for a graduate course.  He assumes that all of the concepts he covers are 100% understood by everyone in the class, which is not the case.  However, he's willing to help and extends deadlines if most people in the class are having a lot of trouble on an assignment.

He's okay. Very funny, but can be kind of rude. Near the end of the semester he started to get meaner and we started to not like him as much. Tests are extremely hard, as are projects, you really need to work hard in this class. Attendance is not mandatory but he will not like you if you miss a few classes.

Not suitable for Graduate classes I believe . H e just wants to get over with lectures and go home. Won't teach you much, won't go to details in anything, I thought that's what grad classes are for. He doesn't know many of the things himself, take his slides from him and he has no clue, reads off of slides and sample codes.

I don't think I learnt a single bit from him, he is pretty much useless, knows almost none of the slightly advanced materials, keeps asking you to don't care about stuff. If you want to actually learn, RUN FOR YOUR LIFE.

Nelson is hilarious. He's a genius when it comes to C and Linux, and he's an excellent lecturer. I wish I could take more classes with him, but he mostly only teaches 216. It was a great experience, and I learned a lot.
He's funny and keeps the class engaged. He is super friendly and helpful. His tests are HARD. If you are good at programming this class might be easy for you.

Got a c- but still loved the class because the material is really interesting and Nelson makes class pretty entertaining.  Also he's a really understanding guy, so if something crazy happens in your life he'll do what he can to help. Tests are REALLY tough though and some projects take a huge amount of time to complete.  Prepare to work a lot.

Good teacher, but in lecture he will pick on a few students. It started out as funny, but quickly becomes repetitive. Be prepared for a lot of work, especially if you're taking a lot of other classes with this one.

Be Careful with this guy. He is nice tries to be fun, but in class he can be rude to students. He also tries so hard to be the funny teacher, because he doesn't know how to teach Computer Science. I learned nothing from him, but got lucky that I could self teach the curriculum. Not recommended for inexperienced students.
Excellent intro programming teacher! Very funny!
He does a good job and he cares about his students.
Extremely fun teacher. Just go with the flow in class, and he will make sure you're prepared.
Would prefer Salsa dancing to teaching "YAVA"

Great sense of humor. Make sure your cell phone is turned off in class. He loves teaching and does a great job, explains things well and is very good in office hours. Exams were good, not easy but all the material was covered in class. Projects were also good, well designed for learning material.

One of the funniest professors I've had in a long time; Nelson has a great sense of humor and he's smart as hell to boot. Take one of his classes if you want a once-in-a-lifetime teaching experience from a man who knows what he's talking about (and is very good at transferring his CS knowledge to you). Highly recommended.

Wonderful professor!His class is for those who doesn't like extremely creative or additional thinking on exams. But(!) you have to study a lot and know all the content of the slides he provides.The projects are pretty reasonable,they simulate real small development processes out there.Although he looks too energetic,treat his job seriously.Recomen.

Projects are hard, but he isn't the one who designs this class, so don't get pissed at him for that...  I think after all he is a little not right in a head, but then again none of us is perfect, if you're sort of catch his joke style/ behavior in general then you'll have the best time in class ... U'll love him!
Nice guy, good teacher. He is helpful and friendly. Projects were easy and interesting.

He tries to keep the class entertained. He teaches well .I did not like presentations initially but they were very helpful and to-the-point for reviewing before exams. The exams can be a little tricky. The project's difficulty level goes from average to hard to easy.Hang on for 3/4th of the class and he gives away some easy points during the end.

Hilarious professor who wants everyone to do well.  Is pretty clear about what you need to know for exams.  Class can be difficult if you're not focused.  Study hard, join a study group, start projects really early, study past exams, and you'll be fine.  He can waste class time by going off on tangents, but he's just trying to keep you awake.
Not the easiest class. Projects and tests are hard! As far as teaching- he's not bad but he doesn't cover nearly as much information as is on the exams or projects. TA's are useless.

Nelson is a banshee. In class you will have tons of fun. Topics of discussion may include; vehicular manslaughter, system adminstrator abuse, road-side sales technique, social commentary of students lifestyles and health choices. Picks one student to make discussion with. What you will learn about actually computer science may vary...mostly nothing

Great class-- if you really take the time to learn the material you can get some high-paying jobs with the knowledge from this class. I just wish Nelson would stop saying how everyone looks so sad and unenthusiastic-- some of us are just shy! That's my only problem with the class. What we are learning really is interesting (at least to me).
A hilarious dude.  While you can get by not going to class, you'll want to go just to listen to the standup he performs at the front of the class.  Also a very nice guy, and likes to help students.
Super hard projects and tricky exam. If you're not a CS major, avoid him

hilarious teacher. Alittle bit hard to follow because he interrupts an explanation alot with a joke or something but overall pretty good at illustrating tough concepts and quite enjoyable to be in class with.

He was a great teacher, who I still miss!  He was not only funny, but he knew how to teach. I stayed w/the program because of him.  He only asked that you stop screwing around and actually do the work.  He was by far one of the greatest teachers the University has

For a computer science teacher, he's pretty hilarious. You don't have to go to class except on a few days where he has in-class discussions. The projects are easy. The tests are kinda hard. He puts all the notes online, so even if you skip, you can still teach yourself the material.

Nelson is a great, fun and interesting teacher. Tests are not too dificult as far as comp sci is concerned, just study. If you can get Nelson take him he is the man...he even teaches dancing with his wife.

Nelson is a great professor to take. Projects and exams are challenging but he does much to be fair with grading. Lectures provide a source of amusement throughout the course of the semester- despite jokes to the contrary, he cares greatly about his students and takes away from his own free time to find ways to make the course better.

Nelson tells some very funny jokes in class.  His outlook on life is such that relationships can be expressed using UML diagrams and inner classes represent the baby inside of the mommy class.  Unfortunately, he seems to be uninterested in helping students do well in his class.  He even said to us that we are just "temporary variables" in his life,

Nelson is the MAN! whoever says his class was hard in any way is a total moron. if you have trouble in that class, YOU DONT BELONG IN COMP SCI or COMP ENG!! he posts lectures, and goes straight off those. I would ONLY go to class for laughs. otherwise, i barely went, never took notes, studied night before exams, killed the easy projects, aced class

For those of you who think Nelson is a bad teacher, you obviously have not taken a lot of comp sci classes. He keeps people awake and paying attention with his hilerous antics while explaining everything in a clear manner. Projects suck thought.

Nelson makes the class enjoyable enough to get through but the projects are not the clearest AND the exams are the worst. There is so much information on the lecture slides, you aren't sure what to study
Gets all the information across in a clear, understandable, 'and' hilarious fashion.  Wonderful just to be around, and truly cares that you do well.

Nelson is a funny mother.  Before I took his class I thought, how funny can a comp sci professor be?  But he answered that question time and time again.  "Guys, is that ok?"  And don't talk to him about computer-anything outside of class.  He isn't kidding.  I've seen**** go down.

Projects difficult due to unclear expectations and specifications.  Grading is unfair based on course material regarding sofware engineering.  It's not that you won't konw how to program something, it's that you won't know what the expected results are; on which you are graded.
Best teacher I've had.
Best comp sci teacher ever, nothing more to it
What an excellent professor. Fascinates a bit much about being attacked by his students but otherwise one of the best professors a person could hope for.  Not any easier though...
He's a great teacher, the lecture note supplements are very helpful. He's funny too, once he even died his hair pink.
Nelson is pure awesomeness.  He's hilarious.  It's actually almost 'fun' to come to class.  He often ends classes 10-15 minutes early.  And he still manages to teach the material very well.
he's a standup comedian

Nelson is great.  He creates a very comfortable classroom environment and he manages to stay on topic enough to teach the material.  Like most CSMC classes grades are solely on projects, quizes and tests.  All of which are easy to average difficulty.
easiest i series course to take

Kelley taught my first Landscape Architecture class and I could not have had a better first experience. Very kind and caring professor with lots of interesting guest lecturers. Super fun gal. She really made the class fun to go to and it was probably my favorite class of the semester. I would not hesitate to take another class with her again!

She was very knowledgable and passionate about urban agriculture. She had guest lectures which helped change the pace of class and made it more applicable. Plenty of chances for extra credit to boost your already high grade. One group project which is manageable and interesting.
Shes a good professor, however her online lecture videos are incredibly long. Her classes aren't difficult, just very time consuming.
Absolutely amazing. No other words needed
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Omi is fantastic! She is such a nice professor and her classes are quite fun. You must read the textbooks and take notes during lecture. I would love to take a class with her again.

I had Dr. O for my first Honors Humanities class. He honestly cares about his students and their opinions and works hard to ensure class time is not run like a dictatorship. The content is focused on reading academic papers, so be prepared. Once you learn how to read and use resources effectively, assignments will be easy and beneficial.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Ontiveros is wonderful and this class is so unique. All of the content is engaging and it's clear that the professor loves teaching it. There are readings, quizzes, and in-class assignments but they are all relatively straightforward. Much of your grade is determined by your TA, however, I think it's easy to do well with just a little effort!

Easy class, Nice Teacher, if you miss an assignment, or do bad let him Know. You can find a way to make it up.

If you get a B- or lower in this course you didn't do the work

Dr. O is the best, he is so nice and super engaging in class. Super easy class and covered lots of interesting topics. The grading wasn't tough at all and all the quizzes was info word-for-word from class so it's pretty much impossible to do bad unless you don't do any of the work.

Prof Ontiveros's class is interesting. The thing is it lacks the transition in linking the history of Maryland (for instance jumping fast from the end 1600s to the beginning of the 1800s already). Assignments include quizzes, county groups, projects, and classwork. Your Grade in Engl 142 comes from your TA. Choose the right section for the right TA
A real G, the best professor ever. He cares a lot about what he teaches and loves what he does. Class is easy-peasy if you do the readings and have a brain cell.

Dr. Ontiveros is one of those rare professors where it's very obvious he loves what he teaches and loves his job. I took this class at 10am but I never had any issues with going because it was always entertaining and pretty easy. There are 2 readings every week, and there are reading quizzes. As long as you do the work you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Kasso is very approachable and helpful. Even though Linear Algebra was a tough class, he made the classroom an encouraging and open space where all questions (even really dumb ones) were welcomed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: First off, Professor Okoudjou is an extremely intelligent human being. He can do calculus problems with ease that any given math major would struggle with. That being said, however, he isn't the greatest professor. Lectures are extremely fast and lack details/info of stuff that may be on the test. It's a hard class, but there's better options.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He has a strong accent but you get used to it. You can tell he knows calculus well. Not the best choice if you have never taken calculus before. Class is fast paced and he has terrible handwriting. He is a good teacher and is very friendly and helpful. Tests are a bit difficult. There isn't really a big curve either, he just drops a lot of stuff

Most difficult professor for calc for sure. If you don't already know calculus well you don't do well in this class. His exams are significantly harder than exams for other classes. I would definitely not take his class again.

Okoudjou is a good teacher, but if math isn't your thing he isn't the right teacher for you. His Calc 1 tests are probably the hardest out of all the teachers, not because he doesn't teach well but because the examples in class and on practice tests are way easier than the actual test. Also, lots of quizzes in lecture and discussion. Gulick is easy
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: you'll think you have the material the night before a test and go in all confident just to realize you've been bamboozled. hardest math140 teacher out of all of them. don't recommend at all

He goes over everything in lecture, but his examples are too easy and don't reflect what you will see on worksheets or exams. He gives random pop quizzes in discussion His tests are known for being hard to pass, but once you get used to his testing style it's not so bad. I feel as though I learned al lot despite my low grade, maybe gonna retake it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Had Okoudjou for MATH140 i ended up with an A but it was a challenging class. IF i could describe his class it would be hard but fair which according to me is OK
Not a bad professor, but not the best. Pretty hard for 410, but is very helpful in office hours and was a very nice guy.

Okoudjou is the worst professor.  He spends a lot of time explaining theorems instead of relevant practice problems. When he explains certain concepts, he is not clear on how he arrived to a specific answer. He just expects you to know it all.  Therefore, your textbook is necessary. The tests administered are harder than other MATH140 classes.
Cannot read his handwriting sometimes

Okoudjou does not curve and gives harder tests than the other calculus teachers. His explanations are good, but he is a firm teacher. His grading scheme is weird, dropping an unspecified number of homework assignments and quizzes, and you won't know how you are doing in the class until the very very end.

This class was absolutely ridiculous. His exams are much harder than any other teachers and he does not curve the class. I received a 79.4 in the class and was given a C grade. He drops a test, but refuses to drop the precalc test (which is generally everybodys worst).

WORST CLASS EVER, WORST TEACHER EVER, I got an a in AP Calc in high school and got a 4 on the exam, and wound up with a C+ in this class because he is literally the worst teacher I have ever had, AVOID AT ALL COST!

The actual exams are way harder than the practice exams, and all he does is read theorems in class instead of doing practice problems. If we do go over practice problems they are incredibly easy and nothing like questions on the exams. Also there are pop quizes. DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS

He is a terrible teacher, all he does in lecture is go over theorems that you never use, and then you get to the tests, they are harder than any other professor's and have nothing you have learned on them.

He's as beautiful as his beautiful theorems. He has an accent but you get used to it after a week or so. He calls on random people a lot so be careful. No cell phones allowed and no talking.. he gets very mad and will call you out. But GREAT PROFESSOR. LOVE HIM
tests are ridiculously hard. he teaches well in lectures and you may feel like you know the material going into the test, then you see the test and want to cry
Great and hot

Okoudjou is a good prof, knows what he's talking about. Teaches you how to do the problems as well as the theory behind the work. His tests are relatively easy, attend all of his lectures so you don't miss the quizes! He doesn't like to be interrupted in class by talking (aggravates him a lot!) Definitely advise going to reviews!

For me, Dr. Okoudjou's class was very challenging but he was always very helpful. His lectures are clear and useful and the discussions are very helpful. The workload is quite heavy but Dr. Okoudjou is willing to help and if you work hard, attend class, and seek out help if you need it, you will be alright.

Good prof. Commands the classroom, exams were fair, discussion was really helpful. The prof is approachable, teaches the material well, and is enthusiastic. Especially compared to other math faculty, he's easy to understand.
seems to know the material, but does not know how to impart it to students. His technical vocabulary is very bad (you don't GUESS in math) and his worksheets are terrible.

He is a pretty good teacher; he always tries to get the class to understand, accepts any question in lec and is in general a nice guy. He posts prac test with answer keys (unlike other prof) and these are pretty close to the actual tests, which are fairly easy. 1 quiz/2 weeks, which actually help towards exams. Lectures aren't thrilling however.

The other comments here are bit harsh on this professor. This is the first time he taught Calc III, and he does a better job in comparison to other calculus teachers. He shows great enthusiasm and highly encourages students to ask questions and see him in office hours, UNLIKE OTHER MATH PROFESSORS. And I love his francophone accent!

His lectures are right out of the book, but because I almost never pop open books I find the lecture to be useful. Unfortunately this man decides to teach the easiest examples and then his tests are a million times harder than anything we learned. Same with worksheets in discussion. Find a good TA, youll need him/her

The other comments listed are pretty accurate. He also likes to give pop quizzes when attendance is low in lecture. Completely unhelpful when it comes to your questions. You basically have to teach yourself the material. Worksheets in discussion are ridiculous and almost unrelated. Tests are outrageously hard. Especially compared to other teachers

He was a fairly god teacher, his accent washard to understand at first but its easy to get used to. The way he teaches material i thought was pretty easy to understand, but his tests are quite hard. He gives examples you've never seen He does give easy questions in addition tho so it is really easy to get at least a 60. Lecture isnt terribly boring

I didn't really go to class because I kept falling asleep anyways and just reading the book later. He pretty much copies the book onto the board, so there isn't really any reason to go to class. On the other hand it was an easy class: I got an A+ by reading the book and not even going to class.

You might as well sit in your dorm for one hour every day and read the Linear Algebra book and do practice problems and easily pass the class. Kasso doesn't teach anything new; what he does during his lectures is copy theorems and definitions and solve examples already solved by the book.

He is super, super nice and answered every email he was sent (within about a day). He assigned A LOT of work and the instructions were pretty vague for some of them. It was a little confusing at first. However, he's the kind of teacher who will give you credit just for putting something down, the only thing he graded harshly was our first essay.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: If you like to read/write he's awesome! I loved this class because I learned a lot from him as well as other students. The atmosphere is receptive and it was pretty chill throughout. I was encouraged to write and it was just great. As long as you do the few assignments, you should get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Onyenezi is a wonderful teacher, he is very receptive with a great sense of humor and really cares for his students. The discussions in class were always interesting and he really places importance on giving good feedback and being respectful. Overall a pretty chill class that I looked forward to.
Very respectful and nice professor who understands students very well and is not hesitant to make the work load a little lighter for periods of high stress. Great Professor.
A great and understanding professor who accommodates students needs especially during the pandemic
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--So many papers

reviews.comment: Prof Onyenezi is one of the nicest and most wholesome people I've ever met. As a woman I'd feel safe letting him hold my drink, and I cant say that about many people. He genuinely cares so much about his students and class discussions were always interesting and engaging. Gives good feedback on workshop pieces and overall great teacher. Love him.

Chika was such an amazing professor for my Beginner's Fiction Workshop class, he is respectful but gives helpful feedback on your writing. Due to the circumstances surrounding the pandemic, he was very understanding and chose readings and assignments that were enjoyable! I highly recommend taking a class with him!

If you are nervous about learning a new language then take Profe Oñate! She is very caring and wants everyone to succeed. However you have to participate, come to class and do your spanish labs online. Otherwise you will enjoy the class. Her classes get filled very fast, so try to get in asap!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Profe Oñate is the best for span103 & 203! There is a reason why her classes get filled first! She is very firm but in a tough love kind of way because she truly wants you to learn. If you want an A , you definitely have to have to work for it. It is impossible to not pass... unless you just dont show up to class or do your spanish labs online!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: If you are looking for a class where you sit back, look at slides or are lectured, this is not the class for you. This is an interactive dynamic class! Be prepared to learn and speak Spanish. This is my second class with Professor Carla Oñate, and both were fantastic! The professor is upbeat, and brings enthusiasm and experience to every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: COMM456 is the best class I've taken at UMD, I could not recommend Dr. Olson enough. She makes classes extremely engaging, she is extremely knowledgeable about the content, cares deeply about her students, and sets you up for success. I find myself thinking about this course because I genuinely want to the most out of any course I have taken at UMD
Dr. Jade is very caring and give respect to students. I am so glad that I have her in my academic journey.

I expect COMM to be another english class that I would sleep through and not get anything out of. However, I was inspired by the obvious real world applications of the courses material. Jade Olson is an intelligent person. She doesn't obfuscate simple things or overcomplicate basic ideas.

If you have the option to take her, TAKE HER. She is SO detailed in her instructions and feedback. She is extremely thoughtful of student well-being. Best professor I've ever had in my degree program. A true gem for sure.
She is amazing. If you are taking comm107 I would highly recommend Dr. Olson. She is very knowledgeable and engaging. She really cares about her students well-being.

Dr. Olson was one of the best professors I've had at UMD. Super understanding, super accessible. She really cares about her students and wants us to do well. She's honest with the class and super funny. She lets you use notecards for every presentation and is super lax about visual aids. Definitely take her for COMM if you have the chance!
Jade is one of the best instructors I have had at University. She cares deeply about her students, their success, and their wellbeing.

This class is useless, and the professor is downright horrible. It's painfully boring, and there's no clear way to prepare for the exams. He treats this gen ed class way too seriously. He piles all the big projects into the last week of class, and only gives A grades to about 15% of the class, while the rest of us who also did the work, get B avgs
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was unclear about grading, his exams were in no way connected to the class, and he was also unclear about assignment instructions. He is not good at explaining things and he is not accessible outside of class. Definitely avoid him if you can.
Picks which assignments he felt like grading and never answered questions or emails.

Professor Schlake is a very nice person. But, overall I don't think he's a very good professor. He doesn't explain any projects throughout the semester and you will not be able to reach him outside of class, even though he provides you with his phone number. If you show up to class and participate in group work you will get at least a B .

Oliver Schlake was a good professor who was passionate about his work. The exams can be a little bit difficult because they're based on small pieces of information on his powerpoints that are sometimes easy to miss. The projects contributed to most of the grades. They were interesting and weren't graded too harshly.

He is upbeat and passionate about business. Unfortunately, the structure of the class does not make sense. He takes attendance via paper tickets so do not lose yours. Big portions of your grade are based on what the class think of how creative your ideas are. The exams he gives are wrong & even when proven so, he is doesnt give back credit.

Fantastic lecturer, doesn't read off slides and can easily give an engaging speak for 2 hours. Exam difficulty fluctuates. Very little homework and quizzes, but heavily oriented around group projects and presentations. Out of class events were mandatory and was a large part of our grade. Project criteria were vague, but grading was lenient.

Long assignments that are majority of your grade are graded very harshly with no support. You had to learn R on your own and it was unnecessary. Class had no organization and professor was especially monotone and time spent in-class before the final was quite useless.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Long papers are graded very harshly with no feedback. Coding assignments are unnecessarily time consuming. Class had no organization and professor would spend most of the time correcting his own mistakes.

Honors students, pls avoid this class at all costs. Don't be fooled by thinking that it sounds interesting or it would be worth it to take this class. It is supposed to teach you R except you are required to learn it by yourself and then do data projects that are FAR beyond the scope of what you were taught. Tons of unnecessary work. DO NOT TAKE.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you genuinely want to learn how to code without losing your sanity, avoid this class. Coding tutorials are assigned in a horrible order and do not make any sense, terrible for a class that doesn't require coding experience. His lectures are stale. He assigns unnecessary papers that are graded very harshly in the midst of finals week.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Avoid this professor at all cost. The grade in this class is based on too few assignments that each account for over 10%. His lectures were extremely dry and boring - I think I actually fell asleep on one or two occasions. The man loves his group projects more than his painfully unfunny Swedish jokes (yes, you heard that right). Effort is not worth
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed working with him and his TA. I am inspired by this professor in the way he works and thinks. What he lacks in entertainment in the lectures he makes up for by watching the videos on your own time and taking notes. This class was great for people who want to think and learn. He is mentor material

Prof. Olson is a nice guy and effective teacher. He teaches off of PowerPoints which are posted online. His lectures were bland at times but he explains the material very well. There are 2 exams, best 5 out of 6 homework assignments, and a final research paper and debate, which is formatted like a group project. There was no final exam or book.
Only a couple tests, but they weigh big on your grade. Go to class and pay atention and you'll be fine.

Ugh this class was such an annoyance. The homeworks are actually pretty easy and mostly graded for completion. The exams were awful and had terrible averages. He basically scribbles random things during lecture and doesnt answer questions easily. Go to TA office hours, they were pretty helpful. Theres a fat curve at the end too. Went from C- to B-.

Probably one of the worst professors I've had. Genuinely nice guy, just sucks at teaching. He uses weird notations and conventions, jumps through steps without explaining, gives nonsensical answers to student questions, and goes off on useless tangents. He also wrote the book, which while it helps, is pretty bad, even for textbook standards.

He will not post your grade, at all, for literally the entire semester, and he didnt hand back homework assignments except maybe one or two randomly - so no one in the class ever knew how well they were doing until a grade appeared on the transcript. Doesnt teach the material needed on homeworks, lectures are almost random trivia. Nice guy though

Professor Morozova is a very nice person, and her class is very informative. However, her class almost always runs over time, sometimes pushing 10 extra minutes. Participation is important, and she tends to cold-call people, so if you're reluctant to answer, be prepared to be called-out. Some instances of this are downright embarrassing.

There is a lot of homework that needs to be done and the test are a bit confusing. With online learning now, I think she did her best to adjust to Zoom than some other classes. She expects a lot of participation from you and the class is entirely in Spanish, so be ready for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The content of this class isn't hard but classes were unorganized and there was not enough communication. I felt like I didn't learn anything and relied on prior knowledge. There are two exams with 3 parts, and a lot of homework. She also took forever to grade things and was not that helpful.

Loved Orel. Such a kind professor. She truly does her best to help out her students, even in an asynchronous environment. Gives extensions on virtually everything and her grading isn't necessarily too harsh, so long as your paper is well thought out. There's lots of assignments, but that's expected from 394. Absolutely take it with her if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Outstanding professor. She cares deeply about her students and understands that we have other things in our lives beyond classes. She is lenient with deadlines as long as you communicate and she always replies to emails incredibly quickly. Some assignments are confusingly worded, but she is not a strict grader as long as you clearly tried.

Took her online class, everything was cut clear from the beginning. All the assignments are uploaded + she sends weekly reminders of everything due. Super quick response time to emails. She gives excellent feedback on your essays/comments. Genuinely cares for students and is somewhat lenient with deadlines. She offers a good amount of extra credit.

She's awesome. So nice. And really is aware that you have work in other classes. I wish every teacher was like her. She gives major extra credit just by going to the writing center. Awesome teacher and I recommend everyone to her.

Completely asynchronous this semester and often confusing. Feedback on assignments was very minimal. Final grade consists of midterm, final, and three film analysis papers. If you take the class online, you only need to go through the slide deck and take notes. The lectures are a waste of time. Don't need to do readings to do well on exams.

Really enjoyable introduction to political ecology. Prof Orr presents challenging material in an accessible and engaging way. Weekly readings and reading summaries provide a solid foundation to the study of human-environment interaction.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Makes you write thesis summaries for each reading every week and grades them unfairly. Assigns a final project worth 15% of the total grade with no guidance whatsoever. Lectures are extremely long and pointless. There are also mini quizzes before every class and you are required to use clickers.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If I had one hour left to live, I would spend it in his class, because it feels like an eternity.

Ondov is a wonderful human but a horrible professor. He rambles in lectures and leaves much to be desired after class. The best way to study is to know the topic beforehand from the book, and then come to class to figure out his "special way" to do the problems (this is because he will take off points on tests if you do some things the book way)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Ondov is an extremely caring professor and person. He genuinely wants you to learn chemistry and appreciate its many applications - whether you are a chemist or not. You can tell that he loves his work. He is most helpful in office hours and will make himself available if you ask. You will get great explanations one on one if you meet with him.

Dr. Ondov clearly knows the material very well but is not an effective teacher. His slides are hard to understand and he just reads them during lecture with little explanation. His tests are rarely straightforward and often have random questions that were not even covered by the textbook or lecture slides. Do not take him.

Not a good professor for a class that is mandatory for students to pass in order to get into engineering school. Very nice guy, but his lectures are horribly put together and hard to follow. Discussions aren't helpful, Skipping class to teach myself the material was better than actually going to lecture or discussion. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: A very sweet old man but wow not a great lecturer. A 'talk to the board' type :( he's not mean at all, he's actually very kind if you approach him in office hours or after class. I just don't think he's a great lecturer at all. Definitely, don't take if you have a weak chemistry foundation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS. Unless you are very good at chemistry coming in or have the option to make this class your main focus you will end up with below a c in his class. hell the man hasn't had a test yet this year he didn't mess up at least one question on. He never gives feedback either so you have no idea what you did wrong
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: AVOID HIM.... LIKE SERIOUSLY DO MOT TAKE HIM... EVER!!!!!!!!! His tests are unnecessarily hard and homework is way too long. He also talks forever and goes on to things for a good portion of class only to tell us after we dont need it for 135. He should never teach a low level chemistry class
Best professor I had during my undergrad at University of Maryland

Horrible professor. Lectures are useless. He rambles and nobody can understand him. His slides are full of errors and are extremely messy. There is homework and tophat which is worth only 6% of your entire grade (no help to your grade). Averages on all exams are 70s. If you get averages on all exams, you will end up with a C in the class.

Dr. Ondov was the first professor I had at UMD( for CHEM131), and I hoped that that would be the last time I ever saw him. Unfortunately, he was the only one teaching 271. The content isn't hard, but this man is very confused/ing. He goes off topic a lot and his lecture slides are convoluted. Going to discussion and reading the textbook saved me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Ondov isn't a very good lecturer. He always seems confused even when he's describing things he's lectured about millions of times. On top of that, his exams are extremely difficult and he isn't accessible outside of class. He gives lengthy online homeworks every week. Try and take CHEM131 with a different professor if possible!!
Has student's best interests at heart. Class is challenging.
Do not expect to learn anything from him. Only take him if you have an amazing background in chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: You don't have to show up for lectures in this class except for the exams. The book is a better teacher, plus he posts his slides. Tests were unnecessarily long and computation heavy, but it was doable in the end. Ondov clearly knows chemistry but is probably better at teaching more advanced material than the basics. Not the worst but nothing great
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Ondov is one of the better professors in the chemistry department. I admit that Ondov is a boring lecturer, which leads a lot people not showing up. He gives you everything you need during the lectures. Chemistry classes are all weed out classes and Ondov is your best bet at a high grade with high understanding.

Get ready and buckle down for a bumpy ride. Ondov is a very poor lecturer. Along with his monotone capable of putting anyone to sleep, his slides are often messy and he goes on tangents. Prof. Ondov is by far the worst lecturer I unfortunately had to take. His exams do not reflect the material given. Not to mention, his slides are always wrong. He makes too many mistakes, period! He really goes off on tangents and his thoughts aren't connected. You just have to learn by textbook in his class.

GO TO DISCUSSION. The TAs are really the ones teaching the material. If you're still confused, go to his office hours!! Bring sample problems. Overall, Ondov is a horrible professor. He teaches as if you already know every word of the text book. He seems like a nice guy and the TA is quite helpful. MAKE SURE YOU TAKE AP CHEM BEFORE THIS CLASSSSSSSSS!!!!

Ondov is well-suited for instrumental. Yes, he can ramble and be all over the place, but he won't kill you with unimportant details and lets you know the most important things for an experiment. Do the homework, and learn how every instrument and analytical technique works.

for all you people saying he is nice.. he's not. i know him personally and he is a horrible, horrible human being. the way he teaches in your class is exactly how he is outside of class: except he feels as if he is better than anybody who exists and he is generally crazy, prone to anger and will not hesitate to verbally knock you down.

Lectures are disorganized and hard to follow. Has difficulties speaking (ummm... inserted between every 2/3 words). Very nice guy though! Go to discussions since TA's are the ones to sort out his teaching mess.
HORRIBLE!!! Lectures were terrible. Never wanted to go. I always got lost in what her was trying to say. He does a problem on the board but doesn't thoroughly explain the answer. Hated it.

Mr. Ondov let say... his class had is very dry, I went to his office hours and it was no help for me,  the exam where pretty okay, the disscussion class helped  b/c the TA can help in clearing what Mr. Ondov had lectured

Very nice guy, but extremely boring and difficult to follow. Put it like this unless you sleep for 20 hours th night before, you can count on being asleep during every lecture...when you force yourself to come.

To be honest i think i learned more in high school chemistry.  If anything, his class confused me more.  Ondov tends to ramble on and on during lecture, and also during his office hours.  I went once and somehow he ended up telling me about the civil war.  Lectures are not helpful, discussion was.

He is a little bit unclear, but if you go to lectures (not mandatory, but clicker quizzes are given so you might as well go) and read the textbook along with the material being taught you should be fine. Very confusing.... likes to ramble on and ends up putting you to sleep.

His lectures were definitely fun and engaging, and he made the material easy enough to understand. Three tests, a few homeworks, and a group project that's actually really easy. He's an amazing professor. Really knows his linguistics and simplifies the concepts for you. There's a few exams and a final project but they really aren't that hard. He's really accessible outside of class too so you really shouldn't have a problem.

No homework! No papers! Just memorize the info, show up to lectures because he throws in a lot of hints as to what will be on the test during lectures. Review the quizzes as well, a lot of those questions are on the test. Easy class with lots of great info!

reviews.comment: Let me start by saying, I HATE MATH. I loved Orsetti's class though. He went over homework daily and always stops to answer questions. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had in any subject. Highly recommended. I took Math 113 with him in the Fall of 2015. Very clear and concise. I was out of school for about three years and my last math class was in 2008. I had a lot of trouble getting back into it. Professor Orsetti rejuvenated my confidence in math. You must attend class. Homework is not always collected, but is always reviewed. Quizzes are pretty much the same difficulty as the homework. His tests are fair. You are not going to see anything he hasn't taught you. His lectures are energetic and keeps you awake. I had the class at 8am by the way. It is unfortunate he does not teach the higher level math classes. You'll know what I mean once you get there. If you have the chance to take Professor Orsetti, do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures--Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really great at explaining things during lecture. Tests and quizzes were very fair and based off of previous homework.

I love math but Mr. Orsetti made math very interesting. He helped us connect the math we were doing with real world applications. His class is funny and I enjoyed waking up to go to the class. He is funny and interesting
Prof. Orsetti is a very good professor.  He takes a lot of time introducing new material and is always available to help outside of class.  He really cares about the success of his students.
Great personality. Good balance of professional and friendly. Clearly knows material and enjoyed teaching
Good teacher

Orsetti seems like a nice guy but can be quite pompous and arrogant at times. If you do badly on something it is always somehow your fault. Attendance is mandatory and homework collection is sporadic...be careful what you get into
Best Math Instructor EVER!

Orsetti is awesome.  The way he teaches makes it impossible not to learn at least some of the material.  Always willing to help out a student in the middle of a lecture or outside of class.  Also prepares you well for each of the three tests.

Great teacher who clarifies the subject matter in a very understandable way. He is always there to answer questions and help you out. Works at a good pace to keep the class moving but not rushing. Definitely recommend for any math course.

I not only learned how to solve equations, but why we are solving equations.  He makes math interesting, by dissecting each component of math giving it purpose.  Otherwise 2 + 2 just equals 4.  He tells you WHY
Best Math professor I have ever had. I hated math but came out enjoying it after I took Math 113 with Santuria Orsetti.
One of the best math professors I've ever had! The class was pretty boring, but he made it bearable, always made sense, and the workload was fair.

i didn't have him as a professor, but he tutored me weekly and i understand more about precalc from him than from my own professor. really great at explaining concepts and makes you understand. very helpful!!

orsetti is great. very straight-forward but he makes it more interesting that you'd expect a math class to be. the homework can be a lot sometimes (and he collects them randomly so you have to do the assignments nightly). he just has a way of making something that looks like sanscrit absolutely understandable- if that's what math is to you.
He is the best math teacher you will ever know. He makes you understand math, be a perfect porblem solver, and love the course. He is awsome, #1 recommended.
good professor, but gives no curves.  He knows how to teach the information so that you'll understand it well. Do all of the homework, and ask questions when necessary, and you'll do fine!
real cool dude.  helped me learn**** i have never been able to understand before.
i love the guy hes so cool and if you listen to what he says ull understand it very clearly

This guy is awesome, i reccomend him to anyone who doesnt like math.

an awesome teacher who took his time and left no one behind.  Always knew what was expected of you. Homework every night collects 10 random.  Take him if you need a good math teacher who knows what good teaching methods are all about
Had him over the summer at AACC, awesome teacher, explained everything and answered questions and made sure everbody understood. Made class fun and interesting.

Dr. Orlando is super nice and down to earth, but also will be honest if you're doing something wrong. The material itself isn't difficult, but you're surprised by how much you've learned by the end.

She is great, a very powerful woman. Extremely intelligent and demands excellence from her students, so be prepared to do a lot of reading and quality writing. But she is very fair on grading, and will help you if you care enough to put the effort in. The books we read are really interesting.

Amazing prof! cares about her students, Makes the class interesting! Enthusiastic! Loves what she's teaching! Take this class would like to learn more about French speaking Black countries and people.It has a lot of readings but her tests are easy. Most of the class has As and Bs so far! Take this class for HL core
Dr. O is a great teacher! She's really passionate and very interested in what she teaches and you can't help to feel the same way.  I'd definitely recommend her!

The best class I've ever taken. Do Not take this class unless you can devote some serious time to it. She takes attendence every class but doesn't include it in your final grade unless you speak up enough for her. Did not enjoy her at all learned absolutely nothing that I didn't already know.
The homework is not easy. The exam is terrible. The important is reviewing previous exams.

One of the best professors I have had at UMD.  Taught the material very well and gave reasonable exams.  I would strongly recommend going to his lectures, since a lot of the test questions and homework assignments are specific to his class.  His lectures are fairly good anyways.

Very fun engaging professor.  In my 4 years as an engineering student, this was the only class I literally looked forward to going to and could stay attentive the enite time.
No Comments

This class is wayyyy too had for a 200 level course. Most of the class is reading, and he has 30 mins of lecture. Also you are graded on your participation in class. Avoid this professor if you can.

Great professor. If you want to be a better writer, his classes will make you a better writer. I learned more in this class than 90% of my other classes.
