If you are thinking about to take this class. Just don't take it. If you need core class for history,look for other history classes.

Very understanding and helpful professor. There is a lot of readings for the class but do read the articles because they will be on the exam. Don't hesitate to talk to him because he is easy to talk to and will try his best to help the students.

I honestly hated every minute of this class. Maybe it was my own fault for taking a class I wasn't particularly interested in, but this class was absolutely terrible. I would not suggest it to anyone. It was Asian Americans during World War II, by the way.

Excellent lectures, well prepared, and responsive to the students who made an effort to participate. I would recommend her to anyone .

Miss Owens is very nice, but she can be boring.  The class was easy enough, but she wasn't very clear and confident when teaching.

Really great professor, who actually cares about how his students do. If you go to his office hours he will go above and beyond to make sure you understand what is going on. His accent takes a little getting used to, but his notes are organized. Does give a lot of hw though.

he is really great guy and will go above and beyond to help students. he is the single most approachable and smart professor I have ever had. you can see he really want to teach and make sure students understand the material. Really hard to understand. Gives in classes quizzes so you have to go. Only up side is he basically give the practice exam as the real exam just changes the numbers. If taking his class use the practice exams.

Had to drop. Not a very experienced lecturer and doesnt have a lot to offer when it comes to professional experience
Professor Oudin is really nice and gives good lectures. The simulations are cool but a lot of group work. Go to class and you'll do fine.

I am fortunate to have Dr. Oxford as professor.

Dr. Oxford is the best professor I have ever had in my lifetime. She has taught me how to be a caring person.

Dr. Oxford is one of the most distinguished professors in the field of second language education and I was lucky to be one of her doctoral students. Whenever I needed her help, she was always ther

I have no idea what the two other students are talking about. I had taken several courses with Dr. Oxford. She is the BEST!

Professor Prochno was a very good professor. Hes a knowledgeable and respected leader in the industry and his experience shows in his lectures. The class felt very unorganized as if she came up with lessons the day before. Grades vary based on your TA and are not consistent with their grading. Just find another class

This class is not hard but it was harder than it needed to be. lectures are very random, so you could be talking about one thing starting the class and end up on a whole new topic by the end. So many wording mistakes on quizzes that go unnoticed. Professor doesn't make herself accessible. 50% of your grade will be determined by the last 3 grades.

very unorganized and grades too harshly for an intro level course.Too much is left up to the TAs and grading differs heavily between them. It is very hard to pinpoint what you are learning at any given moment in the class, which makes exams very difficult to prepare for. Alternatively, I've heard great things about Luedtke, take his class instead.

I truly just do not know how a professor could mess up teaching an introductory course this badly. Class time was filled with random group assignments (busy work) and lectures on random topics that taking notes was useless for. TAs were the most random graders and so disorganized between each other and the prof. Do not take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pearson is a sweet lady but a horrible professor. She turned an introductory level course that was known for being easy into a class that everyone hated. Class time was pointless and full of busy work, and she made assignments during the last 2 weeks worth 50% of our grade. Since taking this class I have lost interest in public policy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Carruthers was honestly an amazing professor. He's incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about the material he teaches, and it shows. I can see how one might find the lectures boring but I found the material interesting and applicable outside the classroom.  The class itself was a bit challenging, not horrible but def requires effort.

"Wisdom Thru Cog Sci" This class rekindled my love of psych. He can explain studies in a very down-to-earth and useful fashion. He uses a lot of empirical studies to inform you on life-making decisions. The pace is enjoyable and engaging. I learned so much about soc-psy, cog-psy and neuro, and things I can apply to my life AND my future classes.

Really interesting class. I took it online so I never met him (discussion is run by the TA, and lectures are asynchronous) but he seems like a really nice and intelligent guy. The workload is less than I would have expected, but the weekly quizzes and papers are graded fairly. One big group project. Solid choice, and a really cool class!!

Very much enjoyed having him. It was very structured and organized. The professor and Ta was very understanding. Grades were very appropriate. I also made amazing friendships working in the group project. Would definitely take again. Just make sure you do the readings and go to discussion. Put in the work once a week and youll be fine

This was one of the most interesting classes I have ever taken. I'm so glad I decided to take this for an elective credit. The material is somewhat difficult to understand but is worth learning. I definitely got a lot out of this class even though it was online, it's probably even better in person!

If you don't go to lectures, you won't understand the slides he posts. However I found his class and lecture extremely interesting and never regretted going to class. You HAVE to read the studies to do well on the quizzes, but again I found them interesting and worth the read. The group project was pretty fair. Wish he taught more classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: the class content itself was very interesting. if you take it in person, he will still post the slides but they will make literally no sense, so going to class is kinda a must. there are weekly readings and quizzes that honestly depend on how much you payed attention that week. what killed me was the midterm/final papers.

The class itself was interesting. However, the lectures were taught with the lights dimmed and Carruthers has a soft British accent so a lot of people fell asleep. The weekly quizzes kill but the group project is fair and organized. The final and midterm are not difficult as you are so prepared. Only advice, get ready to ready a lot of studies.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Carruthers is a cool guy. He's really knowledgeable on what hes talking about. I never went to class (which in hindsight I regret because the final would've been easier), but still it wasn't very challenging. There's a big group project which is annoying, but if you're confused just go to office hours and he'll led you in the right direction.

He explains the content very well during lecture, but the readings he assigns are insane. There is a weekly quiz in the discussion section and they aren't many questions so knowing all the answers is pretty important.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Very skilled lecturer, one of the best I've had. However, the tests were abysmal. You're expected to write multiple lengthy essays in a short time frame, such that I found the limiting factor wasn't knowledge of the material so much as the literal speed at which I could write my ideas down. The group project also felt fairly gratuitous.
I fell asleep during his lectures, and his dicussions with his TA were eh, ok.  But it's an easy class, put forth some effort.  The topic of his lectures are good though.
No1 goes to lecture when the notes are online. Discussion is mandatory. I got a B+ in the class and i never attended lecture. Good professor for the class.

I took this class to fulfill an HO and because it looked interesting. It was in the beginning but then got boring later to the point where I would daydream in class. Nobody showed up to lectures because the notes were online. Discussion attendence was much more rewarding! The papers, though easy, took thought. The final is worth 1/3 of the grade!

Personally, the lectures were a tad bit boring, his lectures were exactly like the notes he has on-line.  This is why hardly any students came to the lectures.  I think it's worth your time to go to discussion.  Overall, it's not a bad class, take it if you're interested in philosophy.

This isnt an easy A class, you actually have to think about the concepts. But he makes everything very clear, there is only 2 papers, a midterm and a final, and a discussion grade. ur TA gives out the grades but carruthers does read over every paper and may change ur grade! grading is relative to everyone the in class.get sungwon tho, he is amazing

This was a really interesting CORE HO class. Carruthers is an intelligent man and he really knows what he is talking about. Attendance is optional and most lectures have less than 50 people in them because the notes are online. The structure of the course is really simple, but your grade is completely dependent on the TA. Sungwon is amazing.

Great teacher. Teaches philosophy without letting personal opinion interfere too much with his class. Really does try to thoroughly answer all questions asked in class. Uses overheads in class, posts them online as well. Class had an exam, two papers, and a final, plus a discussion grade. This was my first PHIL course and I loved it.
He knows what the hell he's talking about.  He's an excellent teacher.  And he's British.  What more could you ask for?

Fantastic teacher. Sparks renewed interest in philosophy generally. Has original ideas you won't forget, new takes on subjects that clarify, explain and sometimes explain away difficult problems. Understands your ideas, too. Take him if you can.

Reminded me of Sikowitz from Victorious, but with less comedic affect. I thought he was funny tho, and a good teacher. Vague with directions but if you ask then he explains it clearly and will help you out. There are group assignments throughout the semester which I didn't like because then your grade is based off everyone elses but cool overrall.
Goated professor

Prof G was a funny teacher. The class was all about food and there were only a few assignments. He was a slightly harsh grader and did admit that, but it wasn't too bad. You could always ask him questions about your grades and assignments. Overall the class isn't bad and he's a cool guy.

Unless you are a huge fan of cooking and have some amazing back story about how a recipe changed your life do not take this class. I took a PROFESSIONAL WRITING class and all we did is talk about food and write recipes. I would of liked to learn how to write a resume or even improve short stories. Sure it is an easy A. But not worth it.

Alright let me dispel some of the rumors here... Prof. G really is a cool guy. He's quirky, but it works! Yeah, he can be kinda vague on assignment descriptions, but if you just ask him for help he'll guide you through it. He wasn't an easy A, but he wasn't a hard A either. Do the work and ask questions. You'll be fine (and probably get an A too)

Class somehow became Tolkien101. If you find Tolkien and fairytales interesting he's great I'm sure. Every paper and project related back to Tolkien. Also, he made regular papers group projects somehow which sucked because the your grade relies on the capability of other people which I don't think is fair for a random English101 class.

Professor Grybauskas really taught me a lot about Tolkien and the absolute wonders in his writing. I enjoyed class, even as someone who doesn't like to read. Just know what happens and be able to participate during daily discussions. Him and his TAs were very knowledgable. He's great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of the most engaging lecturers I have had. My biggest complaint is that our workload was higher than the other honors classes on two big assignments. However, he was very willing to look at essays before they were due and give feedback. I usually hate English classes, but his great sense of humor and interesting assignments made it bearable.

He's a funny dude and none of the assignments were too demanding. No long essays either. However, he's one of those English professors that is very vague when describing assignments, then will grade you harshly afterword. Participation is also huge. I don't recommend taking this class once a week for three hours, it's super pointless. Solid choice.

I had Prof. G. first semester for ENGL101S.  Overall, I loved it. We only had a few assignments - none of them were a huge chore and I feel like all of them mattered and were insightful.  Class was amazing, he's a really funny and nice guy. Not everyone can appreciate his deadpan-style humor but if you like it, it's amazing
top guy- brilliant professor who teaches aspects of rhetoric and composition in a clear yet entertaining way. 100% would take another course with this professor again.

He's funny, so he makes class enjoyable. But he's infuriatingly vague when it comes to expectations, grading criteria, etc. He's one of those English teachers who says "Great work! You did everything right! A-." In the real world, completing everything correctly is a 100%. Avoid Grybauskas for the sake of your GPA, or be prepared to fight for an A.
I'm sure this class is very boring and mostly pointless no matter who your professor is. That being said, Grybauskas is very funny and his class is fun even if it is pointless.

He is a funny, quirky guy. Each assignment was beneficial and purposeful, generally longer.  One assignment is writing a 2 page summary on an essay. My class had to read a 20+ page essay where other classes wrote a summary on a 4+ page essay. I learned so much for someone who does not typically like English. Thankful to have stayed in the class.

he is singlehandedly the worst english teacher I've ever had. He grades unbelievably harshly, and lacks substantial evidence as to why.  The class was filled with awkward silence which he attempted to fill with horrible, horrible jokes.  Escape while you still can.

This class was the bane of my exsistence. This teacher (he is not a professor) grades very very critically, less than 10% of the class got an A. I frequently took my work to the writing center, which they said it was fine, and then I'd get back a C as a grade. This teacher made this class exceptionally harder than it needed to be, do not recommend.
This professor is a MUST TO TAKE!! Just take him if you're doing 180, you'll get an A for sure!

Such an amazing professor. He has a great attitude, very genuine and compassionate. Speak up it helps especially because a lot of what I learned involved speaking up during our discussions and lectures. He really made me think cricitally about the topics. It was a great class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: queer citizenship was a tough course but worth it. he really opened up issues I hadn't thought about before regarding lgbtq people.  there was a lot of flexibility in the discussions, but there was so much content, he had to remind us of readings from the beginning of the course to make connections.  overall, I loved this course and christopher.

Just ran into Christopher after over a year from when I took his class.  As enthusiastic and encouraging as ever.  I've never had a professor that doesn't act like a professor.  He's just a great guy that cares about his students! He always asks how things are and asks how he can help.  Such a nice guy.  I miss that class.

Christopher was truly an amazing professor. I came into the class knowing NOTHING about the subject and came out knowledegable. Christopher really cares about the students as long as you put effort into the class. I grew a lot from this class and would reccomend it!!!

christopher is a great instructor that gives lots of feedback and is truly engaged with every student in class. he wants everyone to be included and will make sure you participate. he's a good guy, and I recommend taking his class.

Christopher is a very helpful and interactive professor.  His class was always fun to go to, but make sure that you do the readings so that you have something to contribute to the in class discussions!!!

The only class I actually looked forward to. Even when Christopher was upset, because we didn't read, he was still forgiving. Only class where I've been encouraged to get to know my fellow classmates. He's a great instructor and kept the class going at all times. We did visual exercises that were the best. Fair amount of reading/writing.

I love this class and Christopher.  There was a lot of reading, but the discussions are helpful.  Christopher really breaks stuff down to help us understand, but he does expect you to come to class prepared to offer something critical.  He was also very helpful outside of class always offering feedback for improvement.  I Recommend Christopher !!!!

Best Latino/a Studies class I've taken and learned so much about sexuality and immigration. A lot of work but worth it in the long run.  I feel like I learned more in this class than most of my classes combined. Christopher is very good at explaining things and open to all questions. He's very knowledgeable.

He seems tough but is really actually very nice and easy going.  He does expect everyone to read and participate in discussion. Even if you don't get it right away, he helps a lot!  Come to class prepared to discuss the readings and their utility, and you'll leave with an A, plain and simple. Great class!

Hands down one of the best classes ever. A lot of theory, but I actually learned a lot because Christopher really explains everything and can tell when students are having trouble. Open discussion. Cool guy, way easy going, very go with the flow, funny too.  I recommend Christopher.

Christopher has by far been my favorite professor in my three years at UMD. He is incredibly passionate and very helpful. He is clear about his expectations and will guide you through them step by step throughout the semester. Maintaining an A is as simple as coming to class prepared and engaging in discussion.

Christopher is awesome, very down to earth.  Expects a lot from students but will give back greatly if you are equally invested in the class.  I think this was the best class I've ever taken mostly because Christopher creates a real friendly environment and the discussions are insightful.  Highly recommend taking a class from Christopher if you can

The instructor is great! I wish this class had a TA, so I could be one. You will learn so much the material is great. Just make sure  you read and participate in class and you will be set to understand the concepts once the instructor explain them. You will love it!

Christopher's class was simply amazing. He worked nonstop to create an open environment where we could discuss topics candidly as well as academically. The assigned readings were complex, but do not let this scare you away!  Christopher is so helpful and supportive with helping the class make connections. Hands down one of my favorite instructors!!

Christopher was my favorite teacher this semester. His class was really fun, interesting and engaging (discussions rather than lectures) and not over-demanding (yes, he expects you to read, but it's college). No text book, just PDFs so you save some $$ too. Take his class if you have the chance, you will love both it and him (my whole class did!).

Christopher is an amazing professor. He pushes you to do your best in the class and there is nothing wrong with that. He is very helpful when things are unclear. He also helped me become a better writer. You are an adult in college, it's not supposed to be easy, so grow up, study, and do your work. You should do fine if you do.

Christopher is a fantastic teacher if you take your education seriously. If you're the type to text or mess around on your laptop during class, don't expect him to give you any respect because you aren't respecting him. He assigns a fair amount of reading but if you do it then you shouldn't have any problem getting an A in his class.

I think it was a rough class for everyone b/c Prof. Lounsbury was so unclear.  Christopher is the one person that helped me understand what was going on.  Even though he acted like he hated everyone, he was still extremely helpful to me.  I think students are unfair to him because I saw how they treated him and Prof. Loundsbury.

Christopher is way cool! He helped me a lot.  He doesn't spend much time with people that don't take school seriously.  Don't bother taking a class with him if you're not serious about your ed.  Otherwise, he's one of the best profs I've ever had.  And don't bother reading the negative reviews of him, they were from students that were jerks.

He was very rude when having to deal with him one on one.  He kept saying things like I needed to work on my analysis but when further questioned, he did not provide any other answers.  I agree with a previous comment that he can be nice when he wants to be but watch out if he doesn't.  I think his rating is way to high.

He is fair.  Demands a lot from students.  Interesting and creative.  Overall, if you're an American Studies student, you need to take this class with Christopher; he has taught me more about American Studies and what American Studies can do and what it does, than any other AMST course I've taken.  He's really big on poststructuralist thinking too.

Christopher is the most challenging instructor I've ever had.  He incorporates everyday "texts" as learning tools, and even has a few tricks up his sleeves that challenge students to think outside the box.  He is very dedicated to students' learning.  Don't be fooled by his performance, as he taught, not everything is what it appears to be.

He is nice when he wants to be be. When he is having a bad day, he will let you know it. I really enjoyed the class in the beginning of the semester, but he let it fall down in the middle. I feel he was unfair, because his grading system changed in the middle of the course, yet didn't bother to tell us. But the class is very useful in everyday life
No Comments

I LOVE LOVE LOVE this class and christopher too.. he's veryy easygoing and open to students' ideas.. This class, Popular Culture, isnt just about tv & movies, but more about how American culture and our personal lives are affected by popular culture.. It really changes your view on so many things.. Plus the papers are real easy n fun to write.

Best professor I got at UMD so far. You will need a lot of time after class to work on projects and small essays.  Bloomberg Certification have to be done in the first two weeks (5% of your grade) and you will use it during the entire semester. Final exam was multiple choice and avg grade was 4/10 but you can skip it if you follow his sillabus.

Prof Perfetti is an incredible professor as you will learn more about Finance in this class than any other class you take in college. He is straight-forward and down to business as he wants you to learn as much as possible each class. You will have to work in this class, but the work is graded very easily so if you put the time in, you will do well

Professor Perfetti is a good professor. He will teach you straight from Bloomberg and walk through excel models with the class. In terms of work, there is a homework assignment due every week(usually a 500 word paper or an excel file), one midterm, and 4 group projects. The final exam is excused if you attend 90% of lectures.

Joseph Perfetti has a lot of connections with C-suite execs on Wall Street. He went to Chicago's Business School, which is where modern finance was born. This guy knows what he's talking about and conveys it effectively. The trading challenge is tough, but if you remain on top of it, you do well. You get out of this class what you put in. Take it.
Honestly save urself

I had Peer for AGST130 and PLSC275. Both were miserable experiences. Her lectures are rambling, with little structure and no indication of what we would be tested on and what we could safely ignore. Exams are memorization only, so are manageable but tedious. Avoid like the plague.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Peer is a tough professor. The work load Its completely unnecessary. The book that was assigned, dont waste your money on it. Three group projects were to many for an online class. All that being said if you reached out to to get for help she would help. If you take her class maybe that be the only class you take for the semester though..

Peer's class is a hectic mishmash of fermentation facts with little justification of why each topic is covered. I'm not sure why it's important to memorize the names of different fermented foods and bacteria. At the same time, we didn't cover the Krebs cycle. The quizzes are 50% of your grade but the information tested is minutia from lecture.

From day 1 I let the prof. know I would need extra help with the lessons. I did the class via Zoom due to COVID. 8 wks was made into 7 & all quizzes were timed. I would stay after, take notes, share my screen to try to understand & keep up but she seemed like it was an inconvenience or you were stupid if you didn't understand right away. It sucked.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Be ready to teach yourself the entire class. She would lecture us but we would be so confused so i had to go home everyday and read the entire book page by page to understand every concept. She is really nice but i know many people in that class that failed or dropped out because of her teaching style. I think she should stick to MATH115
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: For math professors, she's a great one. I don't enjoy math all that much but she made it easy to learn and provided good feedback. She was always willing to help and allocated times that students could come in outside of class to get extra help if needed.
Lillian was a great teacher that was ALWAYS willing to help. She grades super fast and tries to give you as much credit as she can.
This guy loves the semantic bureaucratic power.

Quizzes and Exams are much harder than any other 132 classes, and it's not even close. He literally said  “Every semester, students tell me that the exam felt harder and different from past exams. The fact that the exams are different is intentional.“ Exams and quiz scores are in the low 60s.

Pedram is an ok professor. I don't blame those who give him low score since the course itself is just poorly designed. Pedram is a good lecturer but his project instructions can be so unnecessarily wordy and confusing. Is the same on the exams as well. They do it to throw you off rather than help you. His grade scaling is bad compare to Nelson.
I give a lot of credit to the TA's, but Pedram was great. Had no issues, although strict, he was fair.

Expect 2-3 grading mistakes on every assignment. TAs are lost, and leave rude comments while grading rather than explaining why you lost points. If you get a problem right but it isn't done "their way", you get half credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: CMSC131 in general is extremely hard for people who have no prior coding experience. Pedram did record every single lecture so that was very helpful if you needed to review any material at a different pace or if you just need to rewatch to get more content on your own.

Put some respect on his name. Pedram & Nelson coteached this semester and had the same material. Yeah, Nelson's the goat, but honestly, Pedram grew on me throughout the semester. His teaching style is really monotone, but he doesn't waste time and explains the course material very well. He also records his lectures. Don't stress if you take him.

Pedram is so much better than everyone says guys... He is not the best professor I have ever had, but he is no where near as bad as everyone says. If your a CS major and can pay attention to somewhat boring lectures you'll be set. He posts everything and is a very nice person. It not easy, but no CS classes are!
never take this douche

The class is very hard especially if you have no prior coding experience, but Pedram was super caring. any professor teaching 131 is going to be difficult- because its a difficult course. If you met with him in office hours he is really understanding and gives good advice and resources outside of class. if he is your only option you will be fine.
This is no an introductory course. IT SHOULD NOT BE. The class average is a 60. I doubt the students are the problem.

I was decent at object-oriented programming coming in to 131, and expected this class to be an easy A (rest assured it was not). Pedram's lectures will make you want to die from boredom, but pay attention(!!!)--this course moves fast, probably even faster for those with no coding experience.
Would not take it again unless it was my last option which it was. Lectures were awful. Unaccommodating, no resources made aware to student. Rude in emails.

Pedram was very nice, and I was doing very well at the beginning of the semester with HTML and CSS. However, once we got into JavaScript and the more complicated things, he was not explaining things very well. His lectures were a bit disorganized. I wish he had us create more web pages since that's one of the main things in the course description.

I had a love hate relationship with Pedram. He is very kind and cares for his students but the tests and projects do not reflect that. I had a solid programming experience prior to 131 but it definitely was a challenge.And projects picked up out of nowhere. If you're a good student you can succeed but beware, the exams are very challenging.

Pedram's a good professor, I understand why he's the lowest rated one though. If you can, try to get another professor, but if he's the only option, ur fine, you just gotta learn some stuff on ur own, not too bad in my opinion.

Pedram's exams and quizzes are extremely fair. In particular, his TA's this semester were exceptional. Some advice: start the projects the DAY THEY ARE ASSIGNED and JOIN A STUDY GROUP!!! Don't be swayed by the bad reviews here to take another professor; Pedram is a solid choice to take CMSC131 with.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Was pleasantly surprised considering the reviews I saw here in January. Pedram's lectures were easy to follow + he answered questions in good time. Class was project-heavy, but if you get a bad grade on one you can do better on the next. (Given this WAS CO-TAUGHT WITH NELSON, so maybe the shared course material is what made the difference.)

It was so bad I wanted to give you a zero but thats not possible so I give you a 1. This man does not care about students at all. He would give practice exams that were nothing like his exams. Exam 3 was entirely coding and no multiple choice/ fill in the blank. The final destroyed me, 3 methods on circular arrays(20 points each). WTF IS THAT???

Pedram was a good person to take CMSC132 with. He and the TAs worked hard to make the class a good experience, and it showed. There were a lot of projects, sure, but Pedram's lectures and positive attitude made the class more enjoyable. A little boring during some of the lectures, but still good.

Pedram's exams and quizzes are difficult. the exams and quizzes were brutal, project difficulty is exponentially harder than examples in lectures. the projects and quizzes require you to use things he has quite literally never covered. it is quite confused. does not help students who are struggling.

Honestly, quite possibly one of the worst teachers. Not available outside of class, project difficulty is exponentially harder than examples in lecture. Had him online and also quite boring and sounded lethargic in the video recordings. Exams are nothing like the projects and there's no theory. Just grades. If you want to do well, teach yourself

There are a lot of negative reviews about him, but after taking him I personally think he is a good teacher. There were quizzes every two weeks and they basically were just writing code. I think the exams and quizzes were quite easy if you go through the lectures and he did provide previous exams for reference. TAs in this class are very helpful!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I have coded before so the content was not difficult but other people did seem to struggle with it somewhat. TA's are super helpful for this class so make sure to go to discussion. The vast majority of your grade will be through projects so make sure not to procrastinate.

I took this class during Covid so it was online. I honestly did not find the material difficult at all and I've never coded before. His lectures were concise and to the point. The code examples that were provided to us made the projects and exams easier to comprehend. I'm not saying the class was easy but I'm saying it was doable.

This man is an absolute menace to society. If you have never coded and want to take this class (if its still offered online in the future) ABSOLUTELY DO NOT! Lectures are async. so he blows through material with no explanation and the projects and quizzes require you to use things he has quite literally never covered. It is downright impossible.
He is not a supportive professor, does not help students who are struggling. They say the class is beginner friendly but that is a complete lie.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was a bit worried about the semester as I have heard previous negative reviews about Pedram but he wasn't as bad as they put it. Everything up until the third exam seemed to be quite alright and most people were achieving A's but near the end the work started to be more difficult. The projects are very doable and reflect what we were taught.

Lectures are very, very, very slow and putting it at 2x speed is a must. Projects and quizzes were fair. Due to the nature of online learning, exams became more difficult and a LOT of people grades tanked as a result.

Pedram's lectures will put you to sleep or confuse you. He clearly took advantage of the online semester and just recycled old pre-recorded lecture videos and edited them in where he felt necessary. His exams were difficult and not "meant to be taken in 2 hours." He will disregard any pandemic concerns, and won't be kind about it either. Stay away.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lectures were nice and thorough during this online semester. Projects were certainly doable and TAs were very accommodating. But my god were the exams downright devastating. They were extremely difficult. 8 hours for each midterm, 12 for the final. And although they were designed to be done in "2 hours", be ready to spend the entire time doing it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pedram does an Ok job at best with lectures, the lectures did help me learn a lot but the exams weren't reflective of the lectures at all in any way. Pedram is a horrible exam writer and this is his biggest downfall.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: 2x speed for lectures is necessary, and lectures are fine but boring. For the most part exams and quizzes are not too bad.

Taking CMSC132 online, Pedram's an informative lecturer, generally wasting no time, very straight to the point. Not very engaging but explains concepts very thoroughly. The benefit of taking this class online is that one can revisit these concepts as he has recorded lectures. Generally fair when granting extensions. Exams are relatively difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: A good lecturer who really knows their stuff. A lot of projects in this class, but if you enjoy the topics it should be a fun challenge to learn and complete them. Don't let projects take over, exams are a big portion of your grade. Lectures can sometimes feel dull, but I came out of the class knowing a lot more, and their lectures really helped.

Do not take this class (or professor)! I took this class thinking it'd be an easy intro to coding, but I was wrong, as the 2nd midterm average was a 55% and final exam average was a 69%. I got a B despite showing up to all of the lectures and studying pretty hard. Pedram's lectures will simultaneously put you to sleep and teach you very little.

He just reads off slides. Moreover, he is a terrible exam writer. His exams are tough. He usually co-teaches with another teacher, which is why he had decent reviews before. But, if he isn't a co-teacher don't take him. He has no experience writing exam questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing at teaching but gives the worst exams ever. No partial credit for projects. He had good reviews before 2018 because he used the old teacher's exams instead of his own. I studied a ton and still got crushed by the exam.

Lectures were pretty good as well as the explanations. Though, the quizzes were brutal, you basically have to review 2-3 weeks of material before taking them or else you'll do (very) poorly. Projects were simple; start early and you'll be fine. The exams were not easy but not impossible - though some questions were very nitpicky.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a decent lecturer but those quizzes and exams are damn hard. The projects might take some time but are almost always doable. He doesn't give any practice exams and so you have no way of knowing what you will be tested on.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pedram's exams and quizzes are difficult. He doesn't provide practice exams and instead has an unhelpful review day which consists of him reading off of old lectures. Although his lectures can be dry, he does provide example codes. Overall, I found that many beginners struggle in his course.

Unless he is co-teaching with Nelson DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE. he gives no practice exams or indications of what will be on the exams, projects are ok, and quizzes are hard. His average grades are a 75 and gives NO CURVE WITH THE CLASS

Pedram was an ok lecturer but his exams and quizzes were terrible. I felt like I understood the material when it came to projects but once I started the exams or quizzes apparently not. They're riddled with trick questions even the TAs said they got wrong or material we barely covered. TAs are also harsh in their grading on projects and quizzes.

exams are difficult, might be a bit different from what you have expected ( score distributions and question types) , and projects may take a while, they were complicated, but of course you can practice what you have learned through those assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Exam sucks

Pedram was a decent lecturer, if you're familiar with Java/OOP you'll basically know everything in this class and you won't need to go to lecture. Projects are all really stupid and take a while to finish, but nothing too impossible. Exams/final are exactly like the example exams they give, so study those and you should be fine.
Had pedram for CMSC131 and his lectures/exams were very straightforward. The exams covered the material covered in class with little to no tricks and he's a super nice guy.
Good heavens these lectures will put anyone to sleep but ok professor regardless. Do your projects and you'll be fine as the quizzes and exam are sort of a repetition of the concepts you did.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Pedram knows what he's talking about when it comes to CS. He is pretty good at explaining the concepts and his assignments are straight-forward and clear. His exams are fairly difficult though and can get confusing (I wouldn't say he puts "trick questions" in but they do take quite a bit of excessive work in my opinion). Overall a good professor.

He did a very good job of explaining material. He had a good structure for the course and made sure to go over any relevant material before projects and labs were due. Showed example code often along with slides that clearly defined the material. He also posted both the code and the slides on Canvas which gave easy access to class material.

Pedram can be painfully dry sometimes but if you stay awake, his lectures are incredibly helpful and he will reiterate many concepts to insure everyone gets it. If you have a background in CS it can be repetitive but he's such a good professor for people starting out. Workload can be heavy but that's expected for CS. Pay attention and youll do well
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures can be kinda boring and his voice is really monotonous, but he is very thorough and well explained if you have the attention span for it. However I did have a lot of experience coming into his class, but definitely a solid professor to take regardless.
Pedram is a great professor.  Very easy to talk to.

Pedrams lectures can be painfully dry at timesbut hes helpful and clear, and his standards are reasonable. There are better CS lecturers at UMD, but you could definitely do much worse than Pedram as well. Dont love him, but definitely dont hate him.

SUPER BORING.  Half the class is spent lecturing on "how to be a better student" and not on material at all.  He goes off on serious tangents, reems students for not doing well enough.  He calls out students who use computers for notes and he refuses to answer in-class questions.  Just awful all around.  Expected more from UMD.

His lectures are boring and he spends more than half that time going off tangent telling stories or saying other irrelevant things. Unfortunately lectures are mandatory because of clickers, but you'll probably learn more in the discussions sections and by reading the textbook. Review old exams and clicker questions for an easy A.

Pfeiffer is a boring professor. It's hard to stay awake in his lecture, and you have to attend because he uses a clicker to track attendance. Always tells stupid stories that will bore you to death.  Basically, the guy's a horrible teacher - you will get real familiar with the textbook because that's the only way you'll learn anything in this cours

i love pfeiffer.  he's very nice and helpful.  lecture gets boring, it's hard to make accounting easy.  attendance is mandatory because of clickers.  read the book / go over old exams to study.  hard not to get an A/B with the curve.
Cool guy! easy to understand but the lectures sometimes made me sleepy--but how interesting is accounting anyways? he is a great teacher! highly recommend!!!
Good sense of humour, lectures are fairly interesting, read the textbook!! Practice exams are the key to an A.
GREAT GUY!!! easy class!! we love him!!
Thank you Pfeiffer!!!!!!!
Funny Guy

He's nice, and slightly funny, but lecture is still a sleeper. He doesn't exactly teach what is on the exam. I don't know what to say, I hated accounting so much, who knows if he was a good teacher or not. But he was really nice to me. I had a family crisis and he let me make up the exam even though it falls outside the valid **** excuses

He's nice, and slightly funny, but lecture is still a sleeper. He doesn't exactly teach what is on the exam. I don't know what to say, I hated accounting so much, who knows if he was a good teacher or not. But he was really nice to me. I had a family crisis and he let me make up the exam even though it falls outside the valid bullcrap university excuses
very boring class-didn't learn much...make sure to attend discussion sections.
No Comments
he gives you most of the exam answers in class or they are from previous year's exam... which he also gives you

Stay away from this guy. I only barely passed 221 because of the TA's help. His lectures only partly pertain to material in the book and he always goes off topic. Your best bet is to rely on the TAs and the textbook for help.

Class time comprises more of stories that are only somewhat related to materials for lecture. Be sure to make love to your textbook diligently all throughout the semester, it'll probably be your only means of actually learning anything in this class. Great guy in general, just not so much in terms of teaching course material. Takes attendance.
Keep far far away from him, take Cantor in the evening and you won't regret it. He taught me nothing in the whole semester, basically read the book line by line and did the homework to get A.
avoid taking this class if you want to actually learn about tax. single most annoying professor i've had, most obnoxious laugh on the planet, and liberal beyond belief.
He is a nice professor, but his tests are really hard,  its easy to run out of time during the test. he uses the whole class time, and he tends to go over the time alloted.

One of my favorite professors at UMD.  He extremely fair, and is always willing to help the students.  Lectures are generally boring through the fault of the lecture material and not the professor.  Attendance is pretty much required because he uses clickers.  Exams aren't hard if you study the practice exams!  A+ professor.

Clicker questions provide the opportunity to earn some valueable points. He posts all of his material online. The exams are almost a joke, and you get to drop two homeworks, but I didn't feel as though the class was a joke where I didn't learn anything.
He's okay. But you can only get extra points on the exam IF you get 100% of the test correct. Each question is worth 10 points, so your in deep if you miss 3 or 4 questions.
very dry class, but the lectures were very informational. unfortunately for anyone about to take the class, he is switching to clickers and attendance will now be mandatory for you guys :(
He tells an otherwise 2 minute story in no less than 45 minutes, and even extends class to finish a pointless and completely irrelevant story.

Must read book and must attend class.  Participation points for showing up and extra credit for each day you show up.  Extra credit on EVERY test.  All together 92 points of extra credit based on doing things my must do anyway like showing up for class and taking tests.  All tests are open book and you are allowed to bring one note sheet per ch.

Pfeiffer's the man. I think he's hilarious although most find his sense of humor to be awkward. Most will admit he has the best laugh ever though! He really wants to get the material across and values all the students who attend his classes as those are the one's he is most willing to help. He's a very good lecturer and offers real world examples.
Funny guy, easy, pretty much does the homework in lecture. tests based on previous, almost same questions...except final.

Pfeiffer taught Accounting I and II for all the people trying to get into Business school.  He was a decent teacher, all you had to do was pay attention, and put the effort forth.  But if he saw you slackin in class or thought you were just some frat guy/gal that was just there to party he didn't give a damn for you, he really exected you to learn.

Exams mostly based on old exams and gradesummit. if you go over that you'll do well! goes over all hw problems before collecting them. quizes pretty easy-same as hw. tries to be funny-sometimes is. he is very helpful.
Great guy.  Funny.  Easy exams.  Everyone does well.

I enjoyed the array of concepts we went over in his class. Many reading prompts, a few written papers, and written midterm and final exam. I appreciate how flexible he was with excused absences, as there were times when I got sick or had extracurricular conflicts. Overall, relatively easy and enjoyable class.

Prof Joyce was great! Loved that class was mainly discussions. Some things to keep in mind if taking PLCY101:

1. Participation is graded, so you must attend class!
2. You must be good at writing to receive a good grade in the class. There are 3 papers and the exams are essays.
Absolutely incredible professor. I would recommend to everyone. He genuinely wants students to learn and helps to support them in everything they do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This is the first course that I've taken that I feel has prepared me for the real world. Professor Piety is very passionate about teaching his students how to code. He is always willing to help but ultimately wants students to learn how to utilize their resources to find answers they're not sure of. The course was challenging in the best way. 10/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Piety is a caring professor, who really wants to engage his students. Although sometimes tough when grading, he always is pushing his students to think for themselves, instead of simply giving them the answer. He encourages participation,  self expression, and open discussions which make his classes more interesting and thoughtful.

Assignments are vague and even if you meet with him, you wont get much clarification. Unless youre a mind reader, theres no way to figure out what he wants on assignments. He will then grade quite harshly. His ELMS site is very difficult to navigate. Do not take his class.

One of the worst professors the iSchool has to offer, I was a bit optimistic considering a friend was taking him so I switched into his class but then downhill from there. Lesson of the story, hes not a great teacher for other classes in the iSchool and avoid him at all costs. He will go out of his way just not to teach you.

Philip Piety tries to act like he's your friend. But don't trust him. He drops peoples grades by 1 letter grade every semester. He has the most complains of any professor in iSchool at UMD. if you can choose another professor to take a class choose them.

He is very repetitive in lecturing with each class starting with about a 15 minute lecture that usually repeats things he's already said. His grading is tough, vague, and indirect. Much of the time it seems as if he expects students to have read his mind and he puts up a veil of flexibility that is later obscured with nitpickiness.

Professor Piety is willing to let the class guide the content and shape of projects. Some initially were frustrated by the broadness of project or test guidelines, but Professor Piety walks the walk: when he provides opportunities to give ideas for test content or project parameters, he means it and listens. Students can help shape this course!
DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class will make you work for you grade. His class is almost a replica of the real world where you have no clear guidance and you feel lost all the time but are still held to high standards. Piety will prepare you for the real world better than any other iSchool class. I recommend taking if you want to be pushed and prepared for life postschool
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Phil is a great prof. He expects you to be as invested in the class as he is. He genuinely wants to see everyone do well. Pretty funny guy. Very down to earth.

Dr. Piety is a great instructor. He knows the material well and tests you on what he taught (and what you read). You MUST attend class, participate, AND READ! otherwise you won't pass. Get ready for group work. There's LOTS of it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Philip is nice as a person and is an ok teacher. His lectures are boring if you're not into computer science. The textbook has so much information in it and it is hard to retain it all for the exams. He randomly picks people to write on the board and he usually picks people sitting in the front row or back row.  The excel assignments were tedious.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Awesome professor, kinda quirky and dorky but keeps the class interesting.  Tests are simple, if you study the tests shouldn't be too difficult. He is easy to speak to and will listen to your comments/ questions/concerns.

Professor Piety is a really good professor. I was hesitant to take him because it was his first-semester teaching here and I didn't see any reviews but he is a very good professor. His tests aren't super easy or super hard, they are fair. He is a lenient grader as well. Biggest tip I can give is pay attention to the case studies and important topic
Absolutely loved Dr. Phaire! The class felt like a safe space for me, she was an easy grader, allowed extensions when needed and gave great feedback.

Honestly, don't take this class if you're looking for a chill gen ed. The teacher grades things last minute (2 days before semester is over) and she grades harder than most profs. She can also be passive aggressive at times. You don't learn because she doesn't teach. Overall I would've never taken this class had I known this prior.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's honestly the best. Her goal isn't to get you to pass a class, but to help you grow as a writer and as an individual. She cares about every one of her students. In all honesty her class is a gpa booster.

best class I've taken at UMD. I'm not even an asian American studies minor. He doesn't just teach from a syllabus, but goes off of each students thoughts regarding the subject. This makes the class engaging for each individual. He also treats everyone with respect irrespective of background, race, etc. Fun class for an elective.

Professor Nash was by far my most favorite professor here. He was so passionate about asian american issues and his class is not difficult at all. If you attend class, do the readings for the quizzes (only like 4 quizzes) and complete all assignments, a guaranteed A+. There's also extra credit! Would take him again
Great guy. I took it because it fit in my schedule without any interest, but he made the class AMAZING. Passionate, intelligent, charasmatic and overall the best prof I've had.

Nash is one of the most passionate professor I have ever had (I'm a senior now). Class was once a week so attendance was taken. Class usually are easy to follow, he encourages lots of participation. No exams, just short papers and a final group project & presentation (and there are 2 class field trips Annapolis & DC)! Overall, class was fun!

Find another professor if you need any of her courses as a requirement. I've never has such a bad teacher until her. She's ending future careers by the day. How she got a job is here is insane because she can't teach to save her life.
save yourself

Her writing style is basically her writing the answers on the board and then going to the next question. She doesnt really take the time to explain the concept, she just speaks about it while she's writing (which is kind of difficult to understand with her accent also). If you're someone like me who sucks at math, i wouldn't reccomend her. Nice tho
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly she's a great person but not that well of a professor. On the syllabus there were word problems due for each day and she never told anybody that we didn't have to do them, severely time consuming. A lot of quizzes that barely do anything for your grade. Writes problems out on the chalkboard but never explains anything…

If I could give 0 stars or anything in the negatives, I would. Nothing (or VERY few) things are clearly explained. Professor mumbles a lot and rushes ahead of students. Please find another professor if you value your grades and don't have money to waste. I'm sure Pinksy is a kind person but she should not be teaching. FIND ANOTHER PROFESSOR. Awful.
If you can switch professors because she suckssss
horrible teacher, just copies notes on the board and doesn't explain them, no communication with students
Doesn't communicate well with students
Professor does not know how to teach. You basically have to learn yourself from the textbook. She does the work without explaining and copies from her notes. Find a different professor!
You really have to teach yourself to pass this class. The prof seems like someone who is not at ease in the classroom.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor was a grad student and did not teach anything. She simply copied and pasted her notes on the material on the board. I ended up teaching and learning most of the material on my own with the book. I learned more that way than I did from the professor.
Not a native English speaker, hard to understand, teaching style is very weird

DO NOT TAKE HIM! DO NOT TAKE HIM! DO NOT TAKE HIM! Even if he is the last option, waitlist for a different teacher or take it next semester WITH A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR. If you are incoming students don't think “oh I'll be alright, I'll just ask questions” - NO, please don't do this to yourself. Only take this class if you can teach yourself calculus
this guy needs to retire.

If I could rate him a 0, I would. He doesn't teach the material and often goes on unrelated rants. He's rude and yells frequently, even during tests, making it hard to focus. He gets mad when students ask questions, which makes it harder to learn. This is a required course, and he's the one making it far more difficult than it needs to be.
mean. kept screaming and talking during our first midterm so we couldnt focus.

He doesn't actually "DO" the examples in lecture, but he provides them and has prerecorded lecture videos in place. I say this to say, if you're like I was and can't make every lecture, you'll be just as well off as the people who went to lecture.

Teaching style is rushed and unclear with little regard for whether the students are keeping up or understanding the material. The teacher tends to provide vague answers, leaving students even more confused than before. There is minimal engagement, and the professor is concerned with getting through the material than comprehension.

Great lecture outlines and class location in ESJ. Lectures are a bit boring but easy to follow along if you pay attention. Discussion groups help the most!!! Never miss these. Also beware of pop quizzes in random lectures, Fall 2023 were not graded but if they were it would not have ended well. USE MATH TEST BANK

He records all lectures so you never have to attend class if you don't want to. However, your test are going to cover way more content and be way more difficult than any other math 120 section. He generally showed up 10 mins late to a 50 min class, and never covered all the content. You will only learn from math lab assignments, not lectures

Terrible teacher but the class is not hard just use khan academy instead of going to his garbage lectures. He sucks at teaching and just talks about himself the whole time but the tests are not hard if you just go to discussions and do practice.
Very closed-minded when it comes to external situations. Will not budge his rules at all no matter what you are going through

Do NOT take Pilachowski if given the option. His lectures are wasted with him talking half the time and never covering everything he needs to cover. He doesn't care about MATH120 as he teaches higher math so any question he makes you feel like you are dumb and when he does teach he goes way too fast. Over all not good teacher at all.
Very rude, he gets mad at you for asking questions. Lectures are incredibly vague and in the form of a powerpoint. My saving grace in this class was the TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Pilachowski gets too much hate, but he's actually very considerate with how he structured the class. He gives 2 homeworks and 2 worksheets every week and drops the lowest scoring 6 of each assignment at the end of the semester and the lectures are very helpful for learning the material. The exams were always comparatively easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a great teacher, and the class format (asynchronous videos, synchronous Q&A sessions plus discussions Tu/Th) is actually pretty well thought out. He's a caring man and someone who's a pleasure to talk to. His class is definitely difficult and you absolutely need to read the book and watch the lectures to succeed, but that's math for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: You'll be okay if you already have an understanding of calculus. He's a very nice person, but his lectures aren't the best. A majority of your final grade will come from the three tests so you have to do well on those if you want a decent grade.

Tim isn't a good prof. The only way I was able to pass this class is because it was online and I took calc in high school. I never went to any of the zoom lectures because all he did was read off the slides. He doesn't give answer keys to the review guides so that was extremely frustrating bc we couldn't check our work. Choose someone else!!

expect him to read off of slides. I took calc ab in high school and I still struggled in this class. He was rude to some students for asking too many questions, and I basically had to teach myself the materials. The only reason I passed is that he dropped 12 assignments.

Tim reads quickly off of his PowerPoint slides and stuffs tons of content into 50 minutes, and ends up rushing through it all. Basically he expects you to teach yourself. The only pro like everyone else said is that he drops the lowest few quizzes. He gives pop quizzes in lecture once a week. Do not recommend if it's your first time in calc like me
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I see how he would be bad for Calculus, but he's good choice for STAT400. He's funny and explains well, reads off his slides. Posts lecture outlines with examples. Exams are nearly identical to those on TestBank and he lets you have cheat sheets. Doesn't do minus grading and always rounds up. Weekly quizzes made by the TA. Drops 2 HW and 2 quizzes.

The only thing he does is read off of the power point and says it is because of his bad hand writing, but he wrote on the board once and he has great hand writing. Also if you never took calculus before then DO NOT take this class. The only reason I passed was because of my previous knowledge, and I still had to reteach myself everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: don't recommend taking if you haven't taken calc before. doesn't show you how to do problems on the board, just lectures off slides. If you are taking this class, go to discussion, you can ask how to do problems if you're confused and was the only helpful part of this class. Hw was annoying. practice exams are extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I wouldn't take Tim if this is your first time taking Calc 2. There is a small curve that can bring you up by 2 percentage points at best. He does drop some WebAssigns, Discussion Worksheets, and Lecture Quizzes. Show up to class on time and stay throughout the entire lecture - he gives a 5 minute pop quiz at the start or end of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Tim is the absolute worst professor I have ever had. He does not teach at ALL, just expects you to know what is going on. He only uses powerpoints and there are daily pop quizzes that have no partial credit. Do not bother going to a review session, he gives you a test and tells you to find the answers with friends. There is a 2% curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Listening to him is very irritating and he will make you feel dumb for asking questions. He would assign 3-6 homework assignments due all on the same day. The way he teaches is by reading off of his very WORDY powerpoints very quickly. He's overall a not so great prof in my opinion
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: His test are exactly like the testbank exams. He is not as hard as everyone says he is. You don't have to go to class but there are random graded clicker questions but he drops the lowest 4 so it's not bad. And discussion has graded worksheet but drops the lowest 4. There is a lot of homework though but if you do it early it's not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Tim was an ok teacher. Cons * He does not teach well , mostly self study. *Gives pop up quizzes . * Uses slides to explain math(Math should be taught hands on, he never solves a problem on paper all he does is show steps on his computer). Pro's Drops like 5/12 quizzes and few discussions. EXAMS ARE VERY SIMILAR TO HIS PAST EXAMS(Big plus for him)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: If this is your first time taking Calc I would strongly advise against taking Pilachowski. He teaches off of a powerpoint and can go too fast sometimes. He rarely answers questions, the most questions hes answered in one lecture is two and my lecture had about 200 people in it. If you have taken calc before, hes fine.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He's not a bad professor, however, explanations aren't his forte. Other than that, he's a passionate and funny professor. Just be prepared to go to office hours and the GSS', especially if you've never taken Calculus.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The most boring professor every in the history of the world

Professor Pinker's class was interesting. I took AOSC400 last fall, and you definitely need the prerequisites. Homework's consist of intense calc and physics, but exams were more conceptual. The class is lecture heavy. Dr. Pinker knows her stuff, but I think she could work on her engagement a little bit as a teacher. She is nice and understanding.

I mean, nothing really bad about the professor other than she talks very monotone and does not make much effort to keep class engaged, especially since she requires everyone to show up by doing clicker questions that count towards attendance. If there were no clicker questions, i'm sure the attendance would be much smaller.

honestly not much good or bad to say about her. lectures were kinda just boring and a lot of people just stopped coming. she talks about the same things over and over again so its not that interesting. but she tries to make jokes here and there. shes basically a cute little old lady. would probably be a better grandma than professor.

It's pretty clear that her main problem is that she's not very tech-savvy. Unfortunately, since many times require technology these days sometimes it does seem like she's a little scattered. I personally found her slides very helpful when studying for exams so I didn't attend lectures as much since the slides were posted online.

She's sweet, but an hour and fifteen minute lecture about wind directions can be pretty taxing... caught myself zoning out multiple times during the semester. Uses clicker points to make sure we all show up to class; if she didn't, pretty sure no one would be there.

Pittman was a very easy going professor. The class was very fun to take and the films we watched in the class were very interesting. Easy grader and not much writing assignments or homework. Just watch the movies and get ready to discuss in class! If you can take this class or teacher I highly recommend!

Hes a very personable teacher who actually cares about his students well being. In the beginning of the year he said he was not concerned with the grade we get but that we learn something valuable. He is a really interesting guy and very social. He does have a specific way of teaching and a specific way he wants us to write but ive learned a lot.

Professor Pittman is an amazing teacher, I would take his class again if given the chance. HOWEVER, If you are a more introverted student this class will take a little more energy out of you. A typical class day would require speaking and conversing with other students and participation matters. You can go from a C to an A just from participation!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Just participate! Turn on your camera and he is sure to like you and help you succeed. Awesome lecturer who taught me about many different cultures through film. Use the class to help you structure your essays. Easy!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pittman was a great professor who genuinely cared about his students; he was engaging and talked to us about anything we wanted to talk about. He is very specific with the structure of how he wants your papers to be written, but if you stick to the structure and participate in class, you will earn an A. You learn a lot about Buddhism which is cool.

Pittman was the best english teacher I've ever had. He made the assignments easy to understand. His curriculum strays from the usual but its not necessarily a bad thing. If you like Buddhism take his class. If you like science and math you'll like Pittman. The way he explains essay structure is like a formula and you can use it for any essay.
Just ignore that guy who got a D he's just mad about his grades.

I would not take English 101 with him again, and id recommend the same to other people. Made the class unnecessarily hard, and gave tons of work. Did not care about his students. I wish I had taken another professor

At first, I thought he was an idiot, but he grew on me over time. He makes the assignments easier than you initially think. There are some things that might seem odd like how he talks about the Buddha and wants exactly 5 sentences in a paragraph, but he also taught me alot on how to improve my writing. Also, his rants are hilarious

Will was a great professor who has a very specific way of teaching. This isnt bad as the way he teaches simplifies the writing process and teaches you to write better from the ground up. Lectures were always entertaining and I came away from this class learning a lot more than just how to write papers. I would recommend Will to any student!

Mr. Pittman is an amazing professor. He's really funny and nice and really wants to help you improve your writing. Although he does have a specific way he wants you to write, I find it actually very helpful in keeping all your research and ideas organized. The textbook was technically required, but you can easily go the whole semester without it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The BEST ENGL101 professor in the University! Just go to class and participate and the rest will be taken care of. Easy and clear instructions makes completing assignments very easy and quick.

Pittman is a great teacher who makes class time interesting. There are very few graded assignments,as he hates grade. He gives few papers and no quizzes or tests. He asks that you stay involved in the readings and make sure to apply them to the final paper. I'd definitely go with him as he makes class interesting and doesn't make writing stressful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Great teacher, really focuses on the development of writing rather than the end product. Speak up and you'll do fine.

Great guy and hilarious. Wants to see you improve your writing skills and do well  in the class. Downside is he doesn't use elms. EASY GRADER. Funny social and political commentary in his lectures. Raise you hand a few times in class and he'll love you.
Literally an amazing teacher. Taught me so much that i impacted my life with. He's very understanding and actually tries his hardest until you get your head straight.
Writing style may be different, but it is basic. Essays are easy in his format and will not take long if you take your time.

Professor Pittman's way of teaching class is very interesting. He would have the students in class stand up and discuss with each other on various topics. Even though I'm not the best writer , he is always there for me when I wanted my paper looked at before submission. He's very approachable and do talk to him!
This professor is really nice and helpful!
One of the best professors at the university. Class is fun and interesting and as long as you show up, pay attention, and do the homework, you will do very well on the tests.

False advertising - More of an economics class. He took the most basic of concepts and made them nearly impossible to comprehend. He is an absolute genius, but there's a difference between personally understanding the material and being able to convey it to others. He could only do the former.

If you plan on taking GVPT221 dont take his class its a once a week class for 3 hours and his office hours were at the most inconvenient time he made simple concepts complicated by over explaining and his tests were nothing like his class examples
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You are required to attend the 2 hour 45 minute lectures despite the fact that you won't learn anything because he makes the simplest concepts difficult to understand. Avoid this class if you don't want a C or worse.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Game Theory is a difficult subject as it is, but sitting through 3 hours worth of lecture once a week, without being able to ask questions/having no clarity, you would be absolutely lost taking this course w/Swistak. If you want to teach yourself this the entire year, god bless you, but if not, be ready to catch a fat C like the rest of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Takes an incredibly simple topic (introductory game theory) and obfuscates it to the point of making it needlessly difficult. He makes attendance mandatory so you have to sit through 3 hours of his awful lectures each week. Additionally he loves to waste students' time by not actually teaching during his lectures and instead just rambling on.
Awesome game theory professor. Passionate but clear explanations. Sometimes goes quite off-topic, because he knows anecdotes about all the great names in the field.

Was a summer section and I found it odd that he turned an introduction of Government and Politics into several class sections on game theory, but he made the subject interesting and very much worth the time invested.  Anyone who didn't like this guy's teaching methods obviously just missed the boat on the entire subject and should be euthanized.

The people mad about this guy have totally missed his point. He's a genius ? the class is HARD, but it's not impossible. Study the example questions and you MUST MUST MUST go to class ? don't bother buying the book though. He never even mentioned it. Prepare to listen to stupid people whine about not understanding algebra, but he's patient and fun.

You really have to be good at math and interested in it to take this class. It is like no other GVPT class at Maryland. The class wasn't difficult because of Swistak, it was difficult because the material is so hard. He's a pretty cool guy, but the topic can be very challenging.

Professor Swistak is a Genius, from his pacing up and down the chalkboard in between thoughts to his dry humor. Game theory is his PASSION. Awesome challenging Professor, take the class to be interested. Swistak is notorious Game Theorist One of the required books includes several theories which Swistak was the First to Disprove. Take the class

he's great! he loves what he's doing and it shows in his lectors. yes he has game theory in the course but build a bridge and get over it! It's really not that bad plus he there's a lot of philosophers he talks about. He's sarcastic, funny and classy and quite honestly very stylish. Take him!

GVPT100 with Swistak was an amazing experience. Don't expect to be spoon fed. The guy is brilliant, funny and accessible - if you're smart enough to take advantage of it. If you don't come to class and simply read his notes on line you are an idiot. Have patience with the groundwork he lays. He will challenge you to think on a professional level.

Okay so there have been a lot of bad reviews for Swistak. A lot of complaints say he focuses too much on game theory. Yes he uses a game-theory framework to teach the class but the class is not a game theory class. Game theory goes way more in-depth than what he presents. Great teacher overall, interesting lectures, and very funny too. Take him.

Terrible teacher, it's useless to go to his classes because every lecture is posted online. He doesn't have a very good grasp on the English language or any semblance of grammar skills which made the tests difficult. A class focused on his interests, game theory, rather than anything that a competent GVPT 100 professor would teach

I took him for GVPT100. Argue ALL your wrong answers on the exams so he will give you more points. Never go to lecture it's useless and he posts the notes online and never read the readings. Study his lecture notes and you'll get an A. Its run as a game theory class and not an introductory so if you hate game theory don't take it.

Attend lectures and pay attention for an easy A.  Professor Swistak's unique methods and passion for game theory make his classes fun!
