He offers ample opportunities to improve your grade with extra credit and test retakes.  If you have problems with the material, he's very helpful in office hours.  One note - don't bother buying the book!
Excellent.

Swistak is the reason I am dropping the GVPT major. I had him for 100 and thought I knew his style well enough to do well in Game Theory. Not so. He's as unclear as ever, if not moreso! The final straw for me was how disrespectful he was to his students; my last class I almost walked out. Having a low F, I decided a W was better. Not looking back!

I found the class (GVPT100) to be a really interesting and fun mix of game theory and traditional government courses. There IS a strong game theory component to the course - if you can grasp it (it's not too hard) you'll do fine. If you don't get it, then you really ought to drop, because it's in the entire course. That aside - highly recommended.
very good

Everyone thinks this class is hard but dont be fooled. It's only hard if you dont go to discussion. I got a B+ and I never paid any attention in lecture or read the books(only went for pop quizzes). He'll take a month to teach something where you can learn in discussion in 1 day. Tests are EXTREMELY easy. They are identical to the practice exams.

this was probably the hardest class i have ever taken.  I am a history/poly sci major and as i recall there was no mention of game theory on the course description.  This is a game theory class not a gvpt100 class.  If you enjoy game theory and are interested in its subject matter then take htis class.  If you want a basic gvpt class dont take this

This class seems really tough about the time the second test comes, and it may be a little tricky if you dont like paying attention. But you learn everything In Discussion. After test 2 it is easy, he post notes online, and practice tests. Those are a MUST.

swistak really made things interesting and made me pursue more classes in game theory.  he does only teach about game theory but it is really easy to understand. just read the selected material and its an easy A.
material was extremely difficult to comprehend and poorly taught. some tests i didn't recognize the questions at all

Learning about game theory would be fine IF THATS WHAT WE SIGNED UP FOR. If you want to get a gov100 lower level credit for a gov400 class, then take this course. If not, then don't. Swistak is also just a bad teacher. He will have one simple concept that he will dance around in circles to tell you about, just so you sit though his 90minute class.

All this negative stuff about Swistak must be from kids who failed basic algebra.  Game theory isn't something to be afraid of when you've got an incredibly clear and engaging teacher like Swistak teaching it.  Both me and my roommate who has Swistak for GVPT100 recommend him highly.
Although he knows what he's talking about he does not explain the material well at all.  Also, the material he teaches seems to have nothing to do with government and more to do with economics.
He knows that he's talking about he just doesn't know how to communicate it very well to his students

This class is strictly math-based, and I didn't hear the professor mention the word "government" once in this class. Even having open notes 10 min. tests, a bad TA will screw you over. No papers. Just math, and game theory. Don't give up on government as a possible major, just don't take this class with this professor.

Ditto pretty much everything everyone else said. However, he does let you have a cheat sheet for the tests (front and back) and he posts his lecture notes on the internet. 3 of the 5 tests were verbatim the notes... the other two were were out in left field. The final is optional and If you put an ounce of effort into this class, you wont need it.

I thought I wanted to become a gvpt major, but i changed my mind... Swistak makes things SOOOOOOOOOO unclear and if you don't have a good TA, you won't do well. Expects people to do a lot of reading and gives a pop quiz like every week. If I had to take a gvpt 200 level course, i definitely feel that he didn't prepare me for it at all!!!!!!!!!

If you want to learn about gvpt, don't take this class. He takes a bizarre math approach to teaching, which never really becomes clear in its relation to government. Though the information he taught on Game Theory was fascinating, I would have preferred to learn it in a Game Theory class, not a politics class. He's funny, but unclear. G-W instead.

if you want to learn about government, plain and simple dont take this class. i was looking forward to this class and ive been greatly disappointed. he teaches game theory and cooperation, havent mentioned politics yet. hes somewhat funny, but lectures are for the most part a bore, assigns lots of reading and TONS OF POP QUIZZES

his lectures are pretty good.. but he takes a scientific/mathematical approach to political science... if your not comfortable with math he will tell you to drop the course. and if you don't have a good TA you have a slim chance of doing well.

Clearly very knowledgeable about his particular focus in the field, but seems to think that every other aspect of polisci outside of his field is irrelevant. If you want to learn about game theory, this is your man, but if you want to learn about any other basic principles of government or politics, another GVPT100 professor is highly recommended.

I had an opportunity to interact with Professor Pike a few times over email. Her grading and feedback reflect a professor that truly cares. She provided helpful clarifications for class assignments and careful discretion for things not were not as clear. I would absolutely take her again.

She WILL grade according to the rubric and submission requirements. She's responsive and has enthusiasm for the career that bleeds over into her (long) extra submissions to learning materials, which I appreciated! Bad students blame others instead of themselves. That's what these 1/5s are about, trust me. You will emerge from her class stronger.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Just awful
Literally sits there and thinks of different ways to make things complicated than it has to be. Enough with the last minute additions already....

This teacher sets unattainable standards, grading harshly and lacking fairness. Their disregard for individual circumstances adds to the demoralizing experience. Avoid if you value well-being and genuine education.

Heartless & lacks compassion. Had medical emergency, with ER bill for proof. Gave 50% grade deduction for late work. Said I should have planned early... Sorry for not foreseeing an appendicitis and hospitalization for 2 weeks for surgery recovery...
Unrealistic expectations. Will destroy your GPA.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Professor Pike was fantastic! She grades strictly but very fair! She prepares you for each assignment and those assignments prepare you for the next. Great feedback from the labs helped tremendously along the way.

Professor Pike is one of the best at UMGC. I love her detailed feedback on how to improve my code and she is very responsive when I tried to reach out for help. She grades all lab assignments very quickly.
Give it you all and try your best. Work with her and she will with you. Try to understand the material and ask question whenever possible, she considers them all and provide feedback accordantly.

Absolutely one of the best professors that I've had. She grades exactly as she says in her announcements and according to the requirements. She truly appreciates your time when you spend it. Even for an 'A' she will give you tips on how to improve. Great teacher, knowledgeable, very kind and gives amazing feedback. Would take 1000 more times.

Been a student at UMGC for 11 years now (I'm in the military, don't judge). Professor Pike is BY FAR the best professor that they have. She gives the best feedback, reads every line of your code, and helps you learn from a project, even if you got 100% on it. You won't find any "good job" here. Even nominated her for the Drazek award she deserves!

Professor plank lectured organic too quickly using power point slides and I found her class to be very hard to follow. She did not explain things in a different way if people did not understand. She would answer emails quickly but with very brief, unhelpful responses.
homework is weighed heavily compared to other courses and is almost identical to test content. I didnt have to study at all outside of just completing the homework.
Make it more understanding.
Very tough class. She didn't teach mechanisms very well. Other than that, she was personable and wasn't bad for her first year. The curve bumped up my grade 20%.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Taylor did a great job teaching this class. She had more availability around exam time, responded to emails until the night before the exam and was overall very responsive to student concerns. Her expectations were clear and she provided practice problems and homeworks similar to the exam. Her final was very fair - nothing too unexpected.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: For her first time teaching, I didn't think she did that bad. Pace wise, the lectures went by a little too fast for my liking BUT she does take the time to ask if students have any questions. She also puts out hw and prac. exams which helps to study. The material is Orgo 1 is a huge leap in terms of difficulty from Gen Chem so just, be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: testudo couldnt save me
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I thought a younger professor would relate to the struggles of grades. It went downhill from exam 1: the next 2 avg were 41 & 51 and the final exam avg was 55. Her curve favored those who did really bad. My friend got A's on all exams & her curve was only 3%. Plank is responsive to emails, I just wish our grades didn't suffer bc it was her 1st yr

First week of class you should remember everything from Gen Chem. If you're confused first week from this review it will take forever to catch on when she actually starts teaching new material because she does not go into detail. Too fast pace at times going through one chapter each class. Minuscule explanation.

This was Taylor's first-semester & she's a graduate PhD student. I get why some students didn't like her teaching style-- she tends to rush through information and her slides aren't the best. But Orgo is an inherently hard class so if you go to class and put the work in so you can do well. Plus her exams seem much easier than Friedman's.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Taylor Plank did a great job for Organic Chemistry I. Her lectures were informative and easy to follow. She also provided numerous opportunities to contact her if you felt behind or needed extra help-- even on weekends! That's how dedicated she was to her students. Don't feel disswayed to take her, because it's possible to get an A with hard work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Be prepared to study a lot on your own and study weeks in advance for exams. Her power points for mechanisms are not great, her exams are incredibly hard and she knows it. i have never been more stressed by a class so if you get her... good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Taylor just talked through her slides and did not give any examples of what she was teaching. She just completely blew through everything, and left a lot of people not understanding what is going on. Would not recommend, especially at 8 am
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Like the comment below, Plank really does not explain the lectures well. She reads through the slides and expects her students to follow along. In reality, most of her students are lost and stressed about raising their grade the whole semester. Her curve is not as generous as other classes. I'd advise you to take a different professor if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Honestly, I gave her the benefit of the doubt since this is her first year of teaching but she really doesn't convey the material well and rushes through lectures. Typically we are way ahead of all the other classes and end up learning some unnecessary orgo 2 material. Tests are unpredictable so be sure to understand EVERYTHING.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Orgo1 with Plank was very difficult. She teaches the material by talking through the slides and giving a few examples, but does not explain each concept well. I usually walked out of lecture not understanding anything, and self-studied all of the material. Don't depend on the curve b/c there's always a portion of the class that messes it up. Study!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Plank is possibly one of the best UMD professors I've had... Her lectures are incredibly organized, clear, and easy to follow. She doesn't move too fast, she stays on topic, and uses physical models to explain concepts. She also provides lots of examples for each concept. Haven't taken any of her tests yet, but I really understand the content.

She is the most disorganized teacher I have ever had. All of her assignments are so unclear and she gets angry at students for asking for clarification. Not to mention, her feedback is not to helpful and she wastes class time talking about nonsense.

She is a nice professor, and she really cares for her students. She is also very flexible and willing to work with her students in styles that suit them. If you put in effort in her class, you will be fine.

Took this class with Prof. Plydell last semester--she is absolutely FANTASTIC!!! She can initially come across as somewhat eccentric, but if you take the time to talk to her and let her get a sense of your way of learning, she is very considerate and accommodating. Papers are easy, and she basically lets you pick your own topics. GREAT professor!!

Fantastic professor. Not the most interesting class, but if you show up and provide a little effort, Sarah makes note and it reflects in grade. Teaches course matter very well and actually CARES about her students doing well - something that is a rarity today. I highly recommend Professor Pleydell

This class is entirely based on the readings, so if you're a spark notes person, you'll fail. Otherwise, she was great, there weren't any book quizzes, and there is never homework. Most of it is just weekly short journal responses and group projects. Final and midterm is a paper, but she is SO HELPFUL. If she likes you, you'll get an A ;)
Completely amazing!!! If you treat her poorly, I will find you.

She is an amazing teacher. I was hesitant at first to take her because I heard she can be tough but let me tell you, she is just simply amazing. VERY HELPFUL. She goes over your paper in great detail and lets you do a redo if you want a better grade. Gives comments on paper if finished before do date. She really wants to see her students succeed.

Pleydell created a very interesting syllabus for us to study for the semester-there was a central focus to our work and papers throughout the semester which made the class much more interesting and engaging. Pleydell created a great environment to work in, and provided feedback and help whenever I needed it. Great teacher and mentor.

Pleydell was the teacher that inspired me to add the English double major. She made the class accessible, but she provided unbelievable insight. Her one-on-one work and willingness to help made her one of the best teachers I've ever had at Maryland. She really goes the extra mile for her students, and I felt privileged to take her class.

This is one of the best class I took. She provides insightful analysis for all the readings and plenty of guidance for papers. You have to keep up with the readings, journal entries, and participate in the class discussion to get an A. Overall, I learned a lot in this class and my writing style has improved tremendously.Highly recommended!

This is one of the best class I had as an undergraduate. She provides insightful analysis for each reading and plenty of guidance for papers. You have to keep up with reading, journal entry, and participate to get an A in this class. Overall, I definitely learned a lot in class and my writing style has improved tremendously. Highly recommended.

Ms. Pleydell is an excellent hands-on teacher. She would always have suggestions about how to make each individual's paper better. She WILL hep you one-on-one if you need that help. She is dedicated. definitely on of the best teachers I've had.

This was her first year teaching English 101 to non-honors students, so she treated us like Honors. It was a LOT of work but she grades relatively easy (in my opinion). I passed with a B and I put forth moderate effort. Just do the WORK and you'll get through it. Somehow.

Sometimes boring, sometimes interesting, but that's how most honors seminars tend to work; you get as much out of it as you want to.  If you can write (i.e., bs) well, then you shouldn't have a problem.  Don't feel obligated to do the readings, but participate in discussion.

I dont know about her other classes, but in the honors seminar Knowledge Across Disciplines, she was great. I think part of it is that its a great class, but she really does help you think about things in a different way, and even a science major like me got an A in this very writing and  reading related course.
She is spaced out, doesnt know the subject matter, avoid her. If you wanna take a class by her....dont. Simple.
Pleydell is crazy.  There is no structure in the class and she seems like she's on a cloud all the time.  If you like spacy teachers and an easy A take this class.
Ted is the GOAT!!

I found Ted's class to be quite interesting, but that is probably because I am interested in polling and that sort of thing. If you have had stats before then this class will be a breeze. I liked Ted as a teacher, some of the kids were pretty rude to him and that sucked. He is smart and you can learn a lot from him.

Ted is so monotone. He is well versed in what he is teaching but cannot express it properly. That is where he lacks the most. His tests were really difficult, the class was shocked because it almost made no sense compared to all that he taught us. He is a solid, only take him if you need to type.
stan owns

Awesome professor. GO TO LECTURE because everything on the tests was from the lecture, and sometimes he would put random stuff that we only discussed briefly so it's important to pay attention.  but paying attention isnt hard to do because class is interesting.  Would definitely recommend it.

A true professor in every sense of the word. Good man, take his class. I came in just taking it for a mandatory core requirement, and I left with a love of poetry and a new way of looking at the world.
i love him, he is the greatest! def. go to class cause he tests you one what he says during lecture!

Had him for ENGL243. Go to class, write down what he says, and go to discussion. If you like poetry you will love this class and professor. He is very smart and everything on the tests has been stated in class, no surprises. Great Teacher.

Wonderful man & professor. Has a deep knowledge of poetry that he doesn't flaunt but only uses as needed. He'll say lots of things worth writing down & coming back to. Can be gruff & brutally honest in workshop (i.e., not for those who can't take or don't want real criticism. I found his honesty refreshing).
One of the very best writers and teachers you'll ever have. Extremely helpful as a mentor and model for writing.
Fabulous teacher, very smart, really good poet, and charming too.

Bad teacher and rude 
Don't take if you have other options 
That's it
One of the most stubborn and stuck up professors around. Only take its your last option.

BMGT367 is pretty much a guaranteed A with any teacher. However, Susan Powell is a really nasty person. She is super condescending and talks down to her students. I would advise taking it with someone else if you don't want to have to deal with the annoyance of listening to her.
She does a good job teaching and the class is really easy. However, she is kind of intimidating and talks down to her students.
Her lectures are good. A lot of assigned readings for homework to do the quizzes. The exams were kind of hard.

Love Dr. Porter! Class was very interesting and exams were very easy if you took notes during lecture. Quizzes can be a lot because of the heavy readings you have to do with them but, exams can make up your grade. Beware of in-class assignments, those can really drop your grade! Other than that, 10/10!

Pretty easy class. For the second exam, the average was a 93%. Content was interesting and she would engage the class heavily during lectures. Two papers were straightforward and mostly opinion based. No textbook, so lecture notes and articles she posts are key. The only drawback of the class was the pop quizzes but they were still easy.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lectures are straightforward and easy to understand. She does a good job incorporating research and stories to better explain the content. Exams and quizzes are fair. In class assignments are simple. She gives chances for extra credit during exam reviews which is helpful.

Super straightforward class and you have to try pretty hard to not do well. Great professor who is interesting to listen to, has done super interesting research, and is really approachable and helpful in office hours. Lots of content but it's easy to understand, and exams are exactly what you would expect.

Great Professor with a true passion for Corrections. Classes left a lot to be desired, can be summarized as an endless onslaught of PowerPoint slides. Extremely random usage of quizzes and other in class activities. Bring a laptop to class for notes, less you risk carpal tunnel from writing so much.

Not my favorite. Very vague and doesnt explain things very well. If you asked to clarify something, she would just say its in the notes, which was annoying. There were 3 exams and they werent too bad, but we did convince her to have a review sessions after the 1st because the information was so random at times.

Really nice professor! She does in-class assignments that boost your grade and maybe 2 papers that aren't too hard. Generally very easygoing and straight to the point. Her exams aren't hard and you don't even need to buy the textbook as long as you study the notes and attend class regularly.

One of the nicest and easy going professors I have had at UMD. She does not do a midterm but three quizzes (multiple choice and short answer) and a final (all multiple choice). There is also a paper. Everything else is in-class assignments. I would highly recommend and would easily take her again.

Super nice professor, probably one of my favorite ones I've had! Her and the TA's were very responsive to student concerns and accessible for feedback. You can get away with skipping lecture but she did make them fun, discussion was mandatory for participation. Definitely need to skim the textbook for the weekly online quizzes but overall easy A!
easiest A of my life

Nothing wrong with the class. Biggest things are a midterm, final, and an UnEssay (final project) which account for a majority of your grade. Do well on those you are fine. Sad that this class was online. Wish the entire music history sequence was split into 3 semesters of music history rather than 2. Very kind and understanding of mental health!

One of my favorite teachers I've had! I really enjoyed her class. I skipped a lot of lectures, but I honestly wish I hadn't because they were so interesting. Super charismatic and fun. Powlison is super easy-going and caring. Tests were easy and you can skim the text book in a minute to answer the reading quizzes.

This was the most fun class I have taken at UMD. It really is not that difficult, Dr. Powlison will claim that the textbook is necessary, but I didn't use it. As long as you attend the lectures, or view the posted lecture slides you will get the information you need. Attendance is taken at discussions though, but the discussions are usually fun.

She's kind of bland as a professor and doesn't seem all that caring. She does lecture well and puts them online after class so you could easily do well on exams and not show up to the class. She's fine overall though

Dr. Powlison is AMAZING. She makes the class really interesting and she's so sweet. Just take notes in class, read the textbook, and you'll ace the exams. There are only two papers, three exams, and one group project. Highly recommend
She's very nice and understanding, and lectures were helpful although you have to pay attention and follow along.

Jan was an enthusiastic and informative professor.  The class covers HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.  The first two languages are relatively easy, while the third definitely takes a little more work.  Attending class and keeping up with material is the best way to succeed in this class.
I took web design in high school and then took this class to learn javascript. She was very confusing about the basic stuff and I had to explain it again to people in the class that I knew.

122 is supposed to be a class for those with no programming experience. I think that sometimes Plane tends to forget this. Projects are tedious, difficult, and at times, frustrating for anyone who has never coded before this class. It's simply too fast. A patient TA that is articulate in English is a must.
Assumes that the theoretical ideas behind code is the best way to teach how to code. Seemed more like a review class than a lesson. Definitely avoid if you have not programmed before.

This teacher teaches the intro to comp sci course and really takes her intuition for programming for granted. I think the people who rated her positively had a backround in java before her class. Not enough examples, pretty much just administers tests and tells you to talk to TA's for help. Dont take her if you have the chance.

Jan was a pretty good professor. She provided a lot of examples on lecture material.  Be sure to take notes because lecture slides don't give any detailed information, just the general idea. Projects were kinda difficult to start, but once you get the jist of it, it wasn't too bad (assuming your following lecture). Overall not too bad of a choice.

Dr. Plane is a very good professor, but the only downfall is that she expects too much from her students. Projects were too long and exams were impossible to finish within the alloted time. She gives a small curve at the end but be prepare to work in her class to earn at least a passing grade.

Great professor! She is very nice, funny, knowledgeable and can answer any question. I don't understand the people leaving comments and saying she is hard. You must realize that the class itself is not easy at all. This course is very challenging and you will not get an A except if you study every day. Exams are hard but fair.
Good teacher, funny but hard tests

Assumes you know java like the back of your hand already, bad examples, too many "cats", not very helpful when approached, doesn't respond to emails too frequently. I wouldn't take her if you have a chance.

She has almost destroyed my once infinite excitement for computer sciences. She teaches this intro course as if the students already have a background in Java. There is little to no practice with most of the topics covered in tests or quizzes until you are asked to apply what you "learned" during the test/quiz. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. EVER. PERIOD.
very bad at lectures. projects are not very well explained. don't take her class!!!
A bad teacher. Bad at lecturing, projects were unclear, tests were hard and unfair, and quizzes were  impossible. I would never take her again.
Helpful but difficult prof.
She's a great teacher for cmsc250. Shes very clear, easy, and extremely helpful at office hours. Have quizzes every week to keep you on track, a cs course you dont need to worry about.
She is a really good teacher. She just demands alot of stuff from you

plane is horrible - she was OK for 250, but thats just because i could understand the material from practicing... she is by far the worst 212 prof at UMD. but she is just dirt worthless at lecturing - annoying voice, even more annoying laugh, stupid jokes, the list goes on.  DONT TAKE THIS PROF!!!

Her lectures are painfully uninteresting, so it's hard to pay attention to her and consequently hard to understand the material.  Homework assignments are freakishly difficult and leave you thinking you have no idea what you're doing.  Programming projects are Hell.  Expect to stop by office hours four or more times each project if you want a B.
No Comments
She explains things very clearly; but it would help to have more sample problems as her weekly homeworks and quizzes do not always leave you feeling as though you have a firm grasp of the topic.

Professor Mihai is a very reasonable professor and he listens to the students. I took CMSC 423 Bio Info with him and three tests were worth 60% in total (very test heavy). It does not matter how you did on other assignments, if you mess up on the exams, you are done. But according to my experience, his classes are easy to pass but hard to get an A.
His lectures are great!
Great professor, gave me a recommendation for an internship.

This man sincerely cares about his students and their success. He is a terrific lecturer and gives solid code examples to explain the topics. Tests can be pretty difficult though, the averages for the last two tests were in the 50s. That being said, the man bent over backwards to give students opportunities to raise their grades.

Professor Pop was such a great instructor for CMSC131. He clearly cares about the students and is willing to go the extra miles so the students have a better understanding of the material.  He teaches students how to think critical and not how to write code.  I would definitely recommend professor Pop for anyone looking to take this class
Professor Pop's codes are precise, concise, and art... I really learn a lot from him. A great Professor!

One of the best Computer Science professors I have ever had. He is very nice and listens to his students. He asks for feedback all the time to help the class do better. Lectures are amazing and are interactive (he puts some tricks in his code). His projects were fun and useful in the real world. He sparked my interest in CS and programming

Solid and underrated professor. Super knowledgeable and respected in the industry, if you need a recommendation letter, this is the name you want it to come from. If you go to class and pay attention you will be fine. I actually learned so much with her. Great explanations and discussions.

I didn't like how highly participation (ex: talking in class, sharing answers) was graded on the scale, she keeps a tally every time you speak. Other than that, I think the class was fine. No textbooks, exams were timed essay format/ case based. Make sure you know what you're doing bc they account for alot. No textbook or any conceptual exam.

It's midnight and I am STRESSED so I'm writing this to give you a chance to save yourself. This is a class for extraverts where participation is everything. You do assignments before class and it's all discussions. The group project is heavy and most of your grade too. The exams are essays. The final is 3 essays for 30% of your grade. AVOID!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She has a very straightforward teaching style that is very helpful for the tests. Her criteria is clear and she gives very in-depth feedback—more than the average professor does. I would take her again!

Professor Pramschufer is an extremely nice professor and I wish I could've given her class a higher rating - I enjoyed coming into her class every single day, but her grading is unreasonably difficult. If you're coming into this class expecting it to be an easy way to get credit for a gened requirement, trust me to not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Pramschufer is a really nice person but not so much as a grader. She's very nitpicky with essays and will only give feedback if you go out of your way to attend office hours. The rough drafts you submit to her will barely have anything. If you want to do well, go to office hours.

Must attend class for participation grade, weekly informal writing assignments, a handful of papers probably around 4 or 5 and 1 or 2 movies to watch a week. 300 word summary questions and 150 word comments alternate each week for HW.Tougher grader but meet for office hours and she will guide you and is super helpful and nice.

This professor is one of the nicest professors I have ever had. But, I have gotten a C on almost every assignment I have turned in. Multiple people in my class also got C's on assignments they worked very hard on. I feel like I deserved better than a C on the majority of the assignments in turned in. She is a very sweet lady but a very hard grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Professor Pramschufer is one of the nicest professors I have taken. She cares about you and regularly gives students the option to resubmit their work after it's been graded so they can bump up their grade. She doesn't make you buy the English 101 textbook either. One thing is she has a lot of peer review work so keep that in mind.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's overall very nice. Gives decent enough feedback and gives enough extra credit opportunities. If you don't show up for peer reviews she'll take off point of your paper. You do a lot of peer review so if you have bad peers you'll get bad feedback. You do some textbook reading, but it isn't worth it to buy the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I agree with the others about the disorganization. It's sometimes interesting, but I recommend another class.
Nice professor and teaching assistant. Class was sometimes disorganized, but we had good class discussions and Dana brought in some very interesting guest speakers.

Dana is a very nice person and a very good journalist, but this class is so disorganized. The syllabus is wrong, and she changes assignments all the time. Tbh the TA Michael is holding the whole thing together and at least makes sure elms is organized for us. It's an interesting class, but be warned about the organization.

Very dismissive/ "I don't Care" guy, but for the easy A, you can overlook that part. The grading is so good, i.e: (A+ 96.5, A   93.5, A-  89.5 , B+ 86.5 , C+ 76.5 ). Had an in-class activity once a week, online 5 question quiz due Sunday's. And that is all, probably spent no more than 30 mins a week on this class. Worth the easy A!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Besides the final group project, workload is almost non-existent. However, Mr. Pratt can be condescending and takes the class way too seriously when he knows everyone takes it as a free gen-ed.
Take this class. Just take it. The final is the majority of your grade, but it is pretty simple to get a good grade if you follow the criteria (and don't procrastinate).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Mr. Pratt knows his stuff. Although he's a bit of a boomer, he's been in the entrepreneur business for years and knows what he's talking about. The class is super easy, two major assignments and a final presentation. Other than that, it's an easy A. The most difficult thing about the class is forming a group haha.
He is very experienced in his field and seems to care about his student's success.
rude and unrespectful. CAN'T BELIEVE WE ARE WRITING A WORD DOCUMENT WHILE WE ARE ON ZOOM AT A MARKETING CLASS. STUPID COURSE SETTING AND EXTREMELY BORING.

His class is a super easy A . The work is kinda tedious but not challenging at all. You can also use common sense on a lot of the quizzes. He tries to get people to participate more so he does call on people at random sometimes. Overall he's a nice guy and his lectures can be pretty interesting. Take this class!!

Easy class but make sure you stay on top of your work. Lectures are posted on ELMS so you do not need to go to class until the days when the Final Projects are being presented. If you do all your work you will do very well in this class. Every class is a lecture and you usually get out early. Pratt is funny and knowledgable with funny stories.

Attendence isn't required except for the last 3-4 weeks where you do individual analysis, I skipped that day and my grade dropped from 92 to 59 but I attended every class and did well on final project back up to A-. Easiest class you can take in UMD. The work isn't bad. The 12 question: 200 word/question sucked. It's graded on completion tho.
Love Pratt. He is the man.

The class itself is easy. The assignments are busy work HOWEVER, there is a final group project that you must present to the class. It's challenging if you have terrible group mates (you don't pick). Try to get perfects on the online quizzes & analyses so you don't stress out about the final project as I did (clutched an A & did most of the work).

Attendance is not mandatory. Lectures are quite boring but Michael is cool and if you attend it is a good time to get other work done. TAs grade everything and were very accessible. Your entire grade is based on online quizzes that are extremely easy and one group project that is also very easy if assigned a smart group. Online textbook is required

Attendance isn't mandatory for his class, as you can learn everything in the lecture by just looking it up in either the textbook or the slides. If you do attend his class, though, DO NOT let him know your name, as he will call on you more. I learned that the hard way. If you get good teammates for the final project, this should be an easy A.
Very easy class. All lectures are posted online so class is not mandatory, never takes attendance. Do all of the online work because they are very easy grades.
Quizzes are the only thing that I strongly disliked. They were weirdly worded and tricky. I ended up getting a A- because the TA wouldn't round my grade (I had a 92.6%).

This is honestly the easiest class ever. Pratt is nice and funny. The quizzes are funky, but the TAs can help you out. The whole thing is like one big group project. I had an awesome experience with this class, I would highly recommend.
idk always used paper and stuff
She's the goat 😍
The professor comes to class angry maybe about something in her day. She then takes out all her anger on us.
Very Caring
This teacher is online savvy
She gives amazing lectures
the best teacher ever.
She not that bad
I love this teacher, would reccomend
THE BEST TEACHER EVER
She was my least favorite teacher out of all my 13 years experience.

This was the worst class I have ever taken in my life. Not only was she extremely condescending and made everyone around her feel less than, but she also gave no rubrics, study guides, or extra credit, making it impossible to get a good grade on anything. She was extremely nitpicky and her grading was randomly subjective.

I liked Prof Rozenblit. If you show interest in the class, she'll show an interest in you. The tests and papers are fair. If you read the reading assignments and take notes, it's not hard to do well. Lectures can be dry at times, but if you like the material its easy to stay engaged. Shes no-nonsense, but a great professor who knows her stuff.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her grading is extremely inconsistent and extremely confusing. Her lectures are often more similar to rants rather than anything else. There is no way to pass this class unless you write exactly what she wants how she wants it. There is no room for any educational growth.

Wow. I have never had a more condescending professor in all my years of school. Very rude individual, while on top of that, just a terrible instructor. Her lectures are beyond confusing, on a topic that is pretty straight forward. Not to mention she is the worst grader to ever exist. Her grading method is BS, and her slides/ notes offer no help.

Absolutely terrible professor. Her lectures are all over the place and have no consistency. She is frequently contradicting herself, and acts like a spaz. Her grading method is putrid and makes absolutely zero sense. She has no tech abilities, so even her slideshows are terrible, while she doesn't know how to use canvas whatsoever. DO NOT ENROLL!

Other than the fact that she is extremely condescending to students, the only time you can see your grade is when it's on your unofficial transcript. She doesn't have a specific grading criteria, it's "you get a good grade if I like it". You have 2 tests, 2 essays, and a participation grade and that's about it. Doesn't post anything helpful online.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She's really enthusiastic and it's clear she loves to teach. Participation is a requirement in the discussion sections and if you don't go to lecture, you won't pass the class. Overall she's a solid professor and is interesting to listen to, however, there's a 10 page paper that really could be a 5 page paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is so condescending to the students and rude with her answers to student questions. I went to her for help one time and she just explained further why what I did was wrong with no explanation as to how to help improve my grade or what to do next time. I will never take another one of her classes again.
awful teacher. not nice.  her ego is so big that she does not listen to what students say.

Dr. Rozenblit is very smart and is an obvious expert on the Holocaust She is moody however and one minute can be nice and helpful and the next mean and testy! She does not take kindly to questions! Overall an interesting course as you learn so much Her TA Scott is great.  Be warned she assigns a ton of work!

She is a very clear speaker. Tends to be a little tangenty, but overall very clear. Knows the material very well although you can stump her. I found her a little self-righteous at times, and she seemed to be testy when she was asked to repeat herself. The class is very interesting, but she can be vicious.

She is a wonderful teacher! Her lectures are very clear and understandable. If you don't understand something she is more than willing to explain it better. She is very friendly, energetic and she really knows what she is talking about! She is also very helpful and understanding to student needs! You will love her!!! :-)
good lecturer, charismatic & approachable
Rozenblit is an exteremely hard grader.  Her lectures are okay in interest level but she tears your handed in work apart.  She is an easy B but doesnt really give A's. She is SUCH a merciless grader.
Professor Rozenblit is very nice and cares a lot about the subject. The 10 page paper was a bit too much, but other than that it was a good class. Watch out for the TA though!

You take lots of notes. She is really into this topic. Lots of information to know. 2 exams- in essay form. If you are interested in Jewish History you'll like this class. Three books to read in class-but don't have to read them bc she gives good lectures in class. have to write one paper!

I took 4 classes with Professor Rozenblit.  Her lectures are clear, concise, and easy to follow.  She expects attendance in class, but is very flexible when problems arise.  She is extremely sympathetic to student life and will help whenever she can.  She's fabulous!

Dr. Prior is effing awesome. His lecture style might not be for everyone, but I enjoyed his method since he's great at explaining difficult concepts and very knowledgeable, meaning any questions asked in class were answered well. Really good, really funny, and very helpful, even outside of class. He made me love this class despite its difficulty!

Dr. Prior may be your type of lecturer, or he may not be. He sticks to the information on the slides, rarely goes on tangents, but does expect some participation from the students in lecture. He's very approachable and available if you have additional questions. The exams are kind of difficult even when you study!

Dr. Prior is extremely knowledgeable and his lectures are so clear. If you watch them and take adequate notes you will pass the class with flying colors. So many opportunities to earn points and in combination with the lab, there is no reason you can't do well in this class. Extremely interesting and fun too!

Dr. Prior is easily my favorite teacher at UMD. KNES 360 is labeled as top 2 hardest classes in the major. I filled 2 notebooks with material, I've never taken a class w/ so much material. But, Dr. Prior is an AMAZING teacher, his voice is calm, gives great practice, and he shows he cares & knows the class is hard. You HAVE to study a lot to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Above everything else, Dr. Purtilo truly wants to set you up for success, inside and outside of 435. 435 is a course where you learn by doing, and not one where you will be lectured and tested about software engineering. You'll have to learn how to think like an engineer and work in a team, like you might in the real world.

Professor Purtilo is an excellent teacher and has a genuine interest in the progress of his students.   The principles I learned in his class have been applicable throughout my 35+ year career.  I have kept in constant contact with Jim for 20+ years and I am proud to call him a great friend I consider him to be one of my mentors.

I graduated after this class and immediately went full time at Amazon. He told us to review his class in a year. Purtilo was my worst CS prof. His emulation of a software engineering environment has no parallel to the actual job. He had high expectations but no action to help us reach them. Avoid this class. Youd be better with a real internship.

Optimistic beginning. First quiz, falsely accused cheating. Horrific teaching style. Zero technical content taught. Abstract grading standards. Gave project description, completely changed it towards end, blamed us. "JIRA acceptable", disregards it. Endless work, zero gain. Useless, hypocritical, confusing, condescending. Worst "teacher" EVER had.

Purtilo is by far one of the best CS professors at umd. Purtilo gives students hands on experience working with teams and truly ingrains what is expected out of students in a professional setting. He doesn't go easy on his students but he easily makes up it for with his devotion to the course material, education,and professionalism. Take this class

I was looking forward to the most popular and challenging CS course, but because of Purtilo the class was demoralizing and not intellectually stimulating. Directions for the non-final projects were extremely unclear and he gave different answers to the groups so your always left failing a criteria for success. The final project was a joke/ failure.

Super easy A! As long as you follow and stay on top of assignments, youll do well. This class was asynchronous which definitely did not help because the class is discussion based. Also, she never responds to emails or questions. Overall, super easy and barely had to put much effort into this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Group projects--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She's aight but her communication is ass, she responds once/month . Don't listen to the 5 ratings because those were student's who high key tryhard at everything. The class was an easy A but instead of a final she gives you a online research paper and make sure you get it done early because when finals week happens you're gonna be in a tight spot.

Being online was the biggest challenge for this class. It was asynchronous and a discussion based class; those two do not go hand in hand. She does not respond to emails. Her assignments were clear and easy to manage.

Sweetest lady ever! She was so kind, and made the class extremely interesting. A very easy A if you follow her study guides, as she directs you to what is exactly on the exams. There is also only 3 midterm type exams and no final. Would def take again!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kimberly is such a sweet person! She's very passionate about the subject which makes it more interesting. There are two books you need, to write the two papers and to study for her exams, but other than that you don't really need to read them. Her exams are exactly like the study guides she provides. You can miss up to 3 in class activities.

For me, this class was a very easy A. There are many notes to take during class but you can have a laptop out so it's not that bad. She also gives you a lot of time to write. The tests are almost exactly like the study guides and the final exam is not cumulative. There are 2 papers to write but the topic is very flexible and I enjoyed writing them.

theres lots of notes to take! theres 2 papers and 3 exams and the final exam is not cumulative so you should be fine. Its not a hard class you just have to study. theres also in class assignments and will only lose credit if you miss more than 2 assignments.
The discussions were the most interesting part of the class. The material is heavy but easy to get through

She's so cute and sweet, I literally just want to give her a hug and talk to her about my problems. Classes are all lectures and discussions and overall it's pretty fun. The only thing is that you have to do readings to do well on the exams because a lot of the questions are based off of them. Overall fun fmsc class

She is so sweet and a really nice lady. The books for the class weren't necessary except for one of the papers. She doesn't post her slides online so going to class for notes is important although she doesn't take attendance. Only negative is that she talks very low sometimes.

She's really chill, not judge-y or biased, especially on a lot of the controversial topics. I was one of only 3 men out of the maybe 30-ish students, which was a little awkward, but I would still take her class again because of how fun and interesting it was (plus easy way to knock out an I-series and a HS credit).
take her parenting class if you need low maintenance 300 plus level elective. easy discussions, open book midterm, and easy three-part final project.

I was dreading taking this class but I REALLY enjoyed it! If I could take more classes  with her I wouldn't think twice! Weekly discussions, Weekly quizzes the first 5 weeks of class and no discussion the last week only the final. Participate and submit the discussions on time and you are guaranteed an A+. Discussions are very interesting! RECOMEND

Dr. V is really nice. The coursework is easy and even though some of the topics are controversial, she does a really good job of not forcing any particular viewpoint down your throat. Very approachable and sweet. Sometimes she mumbles when she talks though, so it's good to sit in the front. You only need the textbook for one paper.

Really nice. The coursework is easy and even though some of the topics are controversial, she does a really good job of not forcing any particular viewpoint down your throat. Very approachable and sweet. Sometimes she mumbles when she talks though, so it's good to sit in the front. You only need the textbook for one paper.

She is really nice.  Class consists of two papers (easy, just follow the rubric), three tests, and weekly quizzes.  Quizzes are easy you can take them three times and it shows you what you got wrong.  Tests can suck if you don't study but I got 100% on the first.  Plus for extra credit she lets you write anything you studied that wasn't on the exam

Bill Pugh is a smart man; however, his lessons were not very kind to brand new beginners. If you have previous knowledge of programming take him so you won't be bored out of your mind and you will actually learn something. If you are brand new to programming I would advise against taking him. He made it pretty challenging.

very educated man, but doesn't have a single clue of how to teach an intro class. Projects are not only lengthy, but not explained at all. Tests are curved but only after they are made extremely difficult. lectures towards those with experience while leaving those without behind. Takes surveys asking about student comprehension and then ignores it

Clearly well educated, but completely misses the point of the class which is to teach coding to people who dont know it. All of his lessons are rushed reviews seemingly aimed at those who know what they're doing. While his extra credit is very generous, its only giving after administering difficult exams or projects with little to no detail given.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He really knows his stuff but the material taught is definitely not beginner friendly. However, even if you have no experience, he gives lots of extra points and the tests are very leniently graded. The class is also more focused on actual coding - not so much about the intricacies. If you have prior programming experience, it's an easy A.

I'll get to the point, he's not cut out for an intro class. He knows his stuff but he needs to learn how to teach to students without previous coding experience. Every lecture felt like a review for students who knew the concepts and not for students who are still learning them.

Bill seems like a great guy and is incredibly smart but he really should not be teaching an intro class. Lectures were filled with jargon without clear explanations and some projects were thrust unto the class with hardly any information as to what he wanted. Some of his presentations seemed as though they were prepared an hour before the lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Not ideal for people who are new to programming. I have some experience and the class and the tests and homework were still rather difficult. The biggest issue was by far that, when assigning projects it wasn't made clear what was expected. You receive a shell of code and are expected to finish it without much instruction to what the code does.

He's extremely smart & very knowledgable, but may be TOO smart for an intro level course. Taught us as though we were VERY familiar with java; tried to break things down but often times got carried away. TA's were a big help for his class, so get to know yours. Gives about a project a week and only 3 exams which are mainly based on the project info
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Bill gives a lot of extra credit to people who are failing the course, but not to those who are doing well, so it inflates the grade a bit. His teaching is so-so, his lectures are very confusing but his projects are well designed.

Lectures are unclear and full of programming jargon as if the many beginners in the class understands what he is saying. He gave a bunch of materials that obviously wasn't for beginners, and mostly accommodated the ones that knew java beforehand rather than the beginners (even though this is an intro class). He's nice but don't waste your time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Must take.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Hard as hell. Very sketchy lessons: if you don't already know how to program, you will have a really hard time with this guy. Otherwise take it for a nice challenge.
he's a good teacher

He writes his own texts, read through them and don't just do the homework but really think about it. This will help you in the long run. His projects are pretty hard but do-able. If you like programming they will be pretty fun. Expect some to take 20+ hours if you  have no experience. I learned a good amount taking this class.
Its a good thing that I have spent 7 years programming before. If this was my first time, I would be lost, confused, and spinning in circles.
His accent makes lecture a little boring at times but he is very helpful, especially at responding to emails quickly late at night the day before the project is due.

Dr. Qu is an extremely smart man and very willing to help his students if you go to him. There's is nothing against foreign teachers but his staggered English makes it a little hard to stay awake during his OPTIONAL but HIGHLY RECOMMENDED lectures. It's a plus that he posts all of his lectures online. HIS PROJECTS ARE IMPOSSIBLE!!! IMPOSSIBLE!!!
Homework assigned after every lecture. Tests are difficult, but graded fairly. Very nice guy, always willing to help.

Clear lessons, but projects can take up too much time for a 100 level class. Worth putting in the effort though considering he makes this 4 credit class pretty straight-forward if you just pay a bit of attention. Fair guy, understands students.
He is a good teacher but the projects he give are really hard,need a lot of work and knowing poeple who know programming very well.
he's a good professor, but you'll have to work hard on the projects.
Professor Ray is academically inspirational. Also, while many reviews do not quite capture this, she is hilarious and fun!
An absolute genius.

Extraordinary. Rare. She is possibly the best-read person you will ever meet. Her feedback can run into tens of comments for the shortest of papers. Extremely clear-sighted, super articulate and caring. She pushes you to your limits and expands them.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I was just accepted to a PhD program and Sangeeta's class was one that inspired me to go to grad school! She introduced me to postcolonial theory, which changed my life. The class was brilliant. We read a ton, and in the end I learned more in that class than I can describe.

I took 448C. Can tell Prof. Ray enjoys what she teaches. Gets upset that people don't talk in class but talks 80% of the time. Don't have any grammatical errors or that's your grade!! Participation and attendance is important. Decent feedback on papers but late with emails. Locks discussions and isn't really reasonable when you're late so...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: An immense amount of assignments, an unrealistic amount of reading, and will hold a grudge and grade you down. Disorganized and it shows in the class lecture and grading methods. She will call you out by name and make you feel dumb. Very open and transparent with their views. I was very excited for this Professor and ended up very disappointed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: She is so funny and interesting to listen to. However, she often dominated discussion in what's meant to be a discussion based class. If you are shy, you are NOT going to get a word in. She's not very responsive on email and she's pretty disorganized. Doesn't really stick to the syllabus/schedule at all. Still though, she knows what she's doing.

If you're taking it as a graduate course, don't expect an easy grade. That said, she was an amazing professor. She wants you to interrupt her to talk, which is fine so don't be scared, jut make sure you solidly back up anything you say. She's challenging but she truly pushes you to be your best. That's rare and commendable.
great professor, interesting class
Is interesting, but asks for a lot.
Took her class during height of PC movement on campus. Very opinionated, but she knew her material well and was open to different interpretations, as long as you could back it up.
brilliant professor tho a bit scattered--dresses smart and is very knowledgaebale--loved her

I've had two classes with her and written all of my papers in the present tense--perhaps the previous poster doesn't understand verb tenses? If you read her published work you will find that she, too, discusses lit in the present tense. She can seem arrogant, but I honestly believe that's just confidence. She really does want to help her students.

Its true. Her lectures are sometimes scattered, her handwriting is defintiely bad. But she doesn't put too much pressure on you. She chooses interesting books and get you involved. She is easy to talk to you and is always interested in your view.

Very intense and interested in her topic; engaging though sometimes a bit scattered.  The woman's a genius, and if the previous reviewer COULDN'T learn from her, s/he has only him/herself to blame for his/her ignorance and immaturity.

Incompetent. She can not spell or punctuate correctly. She recomends students start papers with "I thought that…" Does not understand why her students write in the present tense and claims to have never heard that the present tense should be used when discussing literature. Both arrogant and stupid.

Overall I will say this is one of those classes where you must put in the effort to pass. Grades aren't free to you and the class is organized via online lecture videos that you must watch before class. People complain about these but I found them very helpful for studying. He's a nice guy but be ready to study each week for weekly quizzes.

Tougher class but Basu does a good job.  Definitely take notes on his online lectures and go to class too, exams are pretty difficult.  Weekly quiz during discussion on Fridays, make sure you understand the material and go to office hours.  Lot of material and TAs are overwhelmed but if you're a business major you have to take 220 sooner or later

Avoid this Prof if you can. Readings and Homework huge time sink, but have nothing to do with quizzes and exams. Most of your grade is with the quizzes and exams, they are purely multiple choice, and designed to confuse and trick students. Course is designed to fail students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I haven't even gotten my final grade yet but even if you held a gun over me I would never take this class again. I would not wish this upon my worst enemies. I have never taken such a horrible class in my entire life. On average, 6-12 hours each week (at least 4 hours on hw) are needed to pass this class and this doesn't include in-class lectures.
Although he is a decent human, it waste of class and money, I studied 99% of the material on my own and purchased a separate toturing to survive. He doesn't qualify to teach.

This class took up so much of my time every week since the hw doesn't prepare you for quizzes and tests. Spent my time doing hw and doing lots of studying on top for the weekly quizzes. He expects you to watch his 1hr+ long lecture vids outside of class. The TAs taught me more than he ever could, USE THEM.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Basu is a very sweet and funny person but as a professor, he isn't the best. I took accounting in high school so I thought I'd be fine but he makes the class unnecessarily difficult. I didn't like the format of the class because I spent most of my weekends watching his prerecorded lectures which take so much more time than he says + no curve.

Basu can be very frustrating. His lecture videos that you have to watch on your own are very boring and take an hour. In class, he goes through examples despite nobody really understanding the concept. For reasons unbeknownst to mankind, he will tell everyone to stop writing when we are trying to take notes. I recommend reaching out to TAs.

Basu makes accounting way more difficult than it could've been. He expects us to complete his lecture videos before every chapter which takes 3x as long as he claims them to be. Exams and the weekly quizzes are nowhere close to the homework. The TAs help a LOT, so go to office hours. Lastly, be prepared to spend 70% of your time on this class.

While Professor Basu did great teaching an online class the semester before me, he seemed to have started back up in person without reverting the course back to its original format. He never gave a lecture in class and would only go over practice problems you were supposed to have done before class. I would not take him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst and easily the hardest class I've ever taken. Class needs to be improved, as it is nearly impossible to get an A or a B+ for most students. Quizzes and Tests are way harder than anything you will do during the lectures.

hw does not prepare you for the weekly quizzes in discussion, it also takes the avg of your 2 attempts rather than your highest. He expects students to go to lecture and watch an hour long video outside of class. The midterms and quizzes are mostly questions on concepts rather than actual accounting most of the time.

Accounting was the worst class. Ever. I don't wish it upon my worst enemies. Unfortunately mandatory for business majors, but if you don't need to take it, DO NOT. A lot of work, exams are ridiculously hard, in person, and not open note. They are also worth half your grade. Basu is honestly a nice guy buy awful class.

The class is self-taught with his annoying prerecorded videos and in-person lectures are review questions where he gets mad you cant teach yourself accounting. Moves fast, tests are HARD, weekly quizzes and hw don't translate to exam. TAs are godsends tho. Infuriating at best and painful at best. Seems like a nice person but a trash teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Unfortunately Prof Basu is not accommodating at all. The overall setup of the class is poor as he only reviews practice problems in class and you basically have to teach yourself all the material. He also gets moody.

Being the only professor for Accounting I hes unavoidable, if I had an option I wouldnt take him. He doesnt care about his students while he says he does. He is not able to accommodate any missed quizzes which are weekly, if your sick too bad. The final replaces any lower grades throughout the semester, but its impossible. Good luck.

Professor Basu assigns quizzes every single week and the homework assignments take forever to complete and is the only opportunity to earn more points outside of quizzes and tests. Furthermore, the material he covers is very challenging for first time accounting students and he does not hold back. I will be fortunately never taking him again ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dont take this class unless you absolutely have to. Basu is the laziest and the worst professor I have ever had (and that says a lot). He uses online lectures to teach so you have to teach yourself. The exams are worth 200 points but only 25 questions (each MC question is worth 8 points). If you get a few wrong you will end up with a D at best.

Expects way more out of his students than he should. If you get a little lost it' hard to come back because of how quickly he moves (all while at the same time seemingly going extremely slow). If you're good at teaching yourself things, I'd assume this class is slight work. Basu loves to crack jokes, which keeps lectures a little more interesting.

One of the worst professors at UMD. He would post lecture videos on canvas and only go over problem sets in class. The discussion sessions serve no purpose except for quizzes and his lectures are a waste of time. Avoid him at all costs if this class is not required. The university should seriously consider having other professors teach this class.

Hes not a terrible professor but the structure of the class is terrible. The lecture videos are not helpful for the weekly homeworks nor the quizzes. And we have to watch before class. He provides practice material but theres not enough time to go over it as we finish everything else. In person lectures are not worth going to. Not accommodating.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: So bad. Period. Just the absolute worst professor that won't even change the final exam to online even when we have an absurd COVID-19 case spike in the last few days on campus.

The fact that he's the only bmgt220 prof is just terrible since he's the absolute worst at teaching. You have to teach yourself all the content bc he doesn't teach anything. Ull spend at least 4 hrs on this class per week. Exams and weekly quizzes are not at all like what u learn in class. If ur a business major good luck ull need it
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Basu does not do a good job at explaining concepts in depth, which will be the end of you in this class. Must learn material before coming to class since lectures are more problem set oriented rather than explanatory.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Basu is a nice guy, but his teaching style is specific to a certain type of student. If you need concepts explained to you in person, do not take this class!!! The lecture is completely comprised of going over practice problems, so if you don't understand the material before class in the videos he gives, the lectures are a HUGE waste of time.

DONT TAKE THIS CLASS unless it's a prerequisite which was for me. The worst thing I've ever taken. TAs are so helpful, but Basu's lectures are so time consuming and waste of time. He provides a lot of materials, but you don't even have the time to get to it because of all the Hw, online lectures, and practice quizzes EVERY WEEK.

Basu is a great professor for a very hard subject. He is really good at lecturing, but can get confusing at times and moves quickly. You'll need to put in several hours a week to have success in his class but overall he's a great professor.

This class is tough, and Basu's teaching style is not for everyone. You watch lecture videos over the weekend, and during class we go over review problems to prep for the weekly quizzes. Watch the extra practice vids if you want to do well on the quizzes and exams. Overall a pretty good prof, approachable and happy to help students with questions
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Basu is nice and wants his students to succeed but the class is excessively hard and the structure is frustrating. It's a fully flipped classroom which makes the content harder to learn and he doesn't provide step by step solutions for practice exams. Some of the quiz and exam questions are overly vague/confusing.

Prof. Basu should reformat the way this class is taught. I'm a student who needs to learn how to do the concepts during the lecture, not with videos. The average grade on the first midterm was a 65% from a class of almost 500. Only doing practice questions during class will not help most students learn. Overall awful experience with Prof. Basu.
Avoid him at all costs!!! His exam questions just didn't make sense at all
Basu is a nice person and has a good reputation among students. However, his ability to teach is not it. This class will teach you how to teach yourself when the professor doesn't.

220 is very difficult but Basu gives you all the resources you need to succeed (several attempts on HW, practice problems with solutions, works through problems during class, recorded lectures). If you consistently put in several hours of work each week and take advantage of every resource, an A is possible. Basu is a friendly and helpful prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was tricky, but Basu was very friendly. If you participate during lectures (and keep your camera on if you're still online), he will like you better. While he may not always explain things clearly the first time, he responds well to questions, so don't hesitate to ask. Take advantage of the TA office hours for the homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Lots of homework that you have to do, however he gives you a lot of resources to make sure you'll do well on the midterms and finals. All grades lower than the final (excluding midterms) are replaced by the grade you got on your final, so you technically don't have to do any work during the semester. Easy if you're good at math.
Basu is the reason BMGT220 is so difficult. He is terrible at explaining things, especially in his online videos and lectures. No wonder so many people complain and have PTSD from this class!

During the Pandemic, Prof. Basu's class was a breath of fresh air. He had the class so well organized and I loved the resources he provided. During class, he focuses on practice problems, which means you really need to prepared for class. If you follow the structure he lays out for you, you'll do great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Basu gives you everything you need to succeed in BMGT220, but ultimately it's up to you. He provides prelecture videos for every chapter, tons of practice quizzes, problems from that chapter that appeared on exams, and copies of every PPT with and without answers. You need to work hard, but Basu makes this course very manageable if you're devoted.

Basu is a great guy but man is this class ALOT of work! Get ready to be studying non stop accounting all semester. TA's were great as well. If you already have a heavy course load you wont have enough time to do well in this class.

bmgt220 is significantly harder than bmgt230, especially if you are more of a numbers person and less of a conceptual type person. basu is not the best at explaining things and his lectures are a mess/snooze-fest. be prepared to study hard or visit office hours. class is curved so that 90%A.

Basu is a wonderful professor. the class is tough for lots of students bc the information is so new to them, but if you read the textbook before class, take the prelecture quizzes seriously, and study for the weekly quizzes youll be good. good TAs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Loved this prof. Lectures are engaging and easy to follow. Likes to know students' names. The exams are all MC and really test you but are always fair. You have to put some work in to do well but it's nothing unmanageable. GO TO EVERY CLASS attendance not taken but doesnt post the completed notes. Weekly HW doesn't take too long. Read the textbook
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Basu is a nice guy and a good professor. The class is just tough though and he does probably the best he can do for a class this tough. I'd recommend him for anyone that needs to take accounting. Just make sure you go to lecture and print out the slides associated with them or you will be in big trouble.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Basu is a very nice man but his class takes A LOT of effort. His exams were very difficult and weren't curved. However, if you can do well on the final, you can redeem any low quiz/homework grades which is nice. Overall, I would recommend him, but study very hard for the exams, print the slides, do the work and GO TO CLASS.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I was able to take this class as a freshman and do fairly well. But achieving a good grade in this class requires an ungodly amount of studying and dedications. The lectures are mind numbing and the exams are designed to trick you rather than test your knowledge. Basus teaching style is painful and i wish the best of luck to anyone taking BMGT220.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Yeah, this class is pretty difficult, but I think if you take advantage of the resources that he provides for you (himself, the TAs - big shoutout to Brita and Vania), it's not impossible. Do go to all his lectures, they'll help (the textbook helps w/homework, but not his tests). Practice for the Friday quiz with past quizzes online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I love Basu! He's so nice, helpful, and funny. Go to his office hours! The more he knows your face, the more likely he is to help you out. The concepts for this class were easy for me to understand, but I know there were a lot of people who struggles. Almost half of the people in my discussion dropped after the "w" date. The weekly quizzes helped.

He is a great professor overall. Accounting 1 is a hard class in general, so he definitely made it a lot of work. But his weekly homework and quizzes are really what helped me learn. I would definitely take him again.

Basu is a good teacher that teaches a really hard class. Accounting 1 and 2 are tough and boring classes but he gives good lectures and is very willing to help if you approach him after class or during office hours.

Dr. Basu has clear guidelines on how to study and do well in this course. Follow it and you'll get an A. Take notes when watching the videos and go to lectures for clarifications and you're set. Great professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Basu is really great. He tries to keep you engaged in class even though Accounting can be pretty boring. There is a lot of material and things to learn, but he does a great job of teaching everything clearly. Even though you don't have to go to class, I would advise you to go because he breaks everything down really well.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY
