reviews.comment: Class isn't mandatory, but to fill out the power point notes you need to go to class. You get multiple attempts on the homework so it's not bad. All quiz grades (lower than final exam grade) get bumped up to whatever you get on the final.

Basu may come off as mean, but he knows his stuff. He provides power point slides he will go over through each lecture, and has pre lecture quizzes that prepare you for the upcoming chapter. Pre lecture quizzes and quizzes are curved up if you get a higher grade on the final exam than what you did on the quiz (Ex. A in final brings C in quiz to A)

Progyan Basu is extremely professional and clearly knows his stuff, however, I can see how he can be unappealing to some. He is very calculated and technical, so if it's your first time taking accounting, be sure to actually read the chapters. He'll give you a list of how to get an A in his class, so commit early to following it and you'll be happy
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Class is tough. Theres no doubt about it. There are a lot of things you have to do in order to do well but if you do them all, the chances of doing well are pretty high. Go to every lecture, read the textbook, watch the videos, study for the quizzes and do all of the practice problems and you should be good. It's time consuming but it pays off.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: It is a really hard and challenging class. But Basu is a Great professor. In order to get an A in the class you will need to attend every lecture, do all pre-lecture quizzes, read every chapter, do homework, and do lot and lots of practice questions/problems after each chapter. Very time consuming, but it is the only option to do well in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor ever, I went to his office hour and he was not patient and helpful at all. And his accent was terrible, I couldn't understand what he's saying in the video or in class. Terrible professor.

Basu has good and clear lectures, but since it is Accounting it gets boring real fast. We had to buy Cengage for homework, but homework was fairly easy. Weekly quizzes reflected HW well. Tests were multiple choice but long.

This is one of those classes where you learn the information ahead of time through pre-lecture quizzes, do examples in class, and have homework and a quiz every Friday. You don't have to do any of it because the final exam grade replaces all 0s but you will most likely fail if you do that. You can get a good grade but you'll need to put in the time

Accounting is extremely hard but Professor Basu makes sure that his student understand the materials. He goes over many example in class to help his student fully understand the concepts. But get ready to work "Extra Hard" if you want to pass the class with an A or B.  The exams are really tough and he definitely doesn't curve the test at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Okay, so I've never taken a business class before and I actually enjoyed learning about accounting thanks to Prof. Basu! His grading policy is straightforward so take it seriously from the 1st day of class! Exams are really hard, so practice not only the numerical/formula based problems but also the conceptual problems - those are the tricky ones!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Basu goes over a lot in one lecture. Make sure you understand the material because every Friday there will be a quiz, and it's a hit or miss (either you know it or you don't).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Material is very hard but he does his best to help you understand. 87% is an A-. Exams are all multiple choice, 25 questions or so.

Dr. Basu makes the lectures worthwhile if you put the efforts into reading, completing your pre-lecture quizzes, and seek help when needed. Don't let a chapter go by if you dont understand it, seek TA's help immediately. His explanations are very clear and easy to understand.

This class is a lot of work, but if you weren't ready to work, you wouldn't be taking this class. The lectures are really helpful, so if you want to do well, you have to go! Basu is a nice guy, and genuinely wants to see you do well in the class. The exams are pretty straightforward. If you study the past exams in advance, you'll pass.

If you want to do well in this course you have to go out of your way especially if accounting isnt your thing. I highly recommend going to office hours and getting to know your TA's. The exams are the hard and the wording can be tricky. Plus they are only 25 questions mc so if you get 5 wrong, your grade is going down the tubes.
A great professor who cares about his students doing well. Very clear, sometimes engaging, and goes through a lot of examples in class. Just wished the exams weren't so hard and short.
One of the best professors I have had.  Very good at explaining the material.  I rarely opened the book since His lectures were far more interesting and helpful.

He is a very nice man however, his class is extremely difficult. I though that the exams were near impossible especially the final exam. I found that his powerpoints he uses in class are the exact same examples and definitions as the book so going to class was basically the same as reading the book. Before this class,  had never gotten a C.
Relatively easy teacher, I never had to study and got a B+. Zero JE's for BMGT220, kinda came back to haunt me in bmgt310. Easy class but didnt really learn much.

AH man this class is hard, watch out guys because there is a lot of little details and memorization. NOTHING LIKE HIGH SCHOOL ACCOUNTING. Other people posted that he gave a curve but he didn't for our spring 2009 classes. He's helpful and attendance mandatory, but if your the type to cram at the end, I will advise not taking this course.

The tests are hard but there is a huge curve (he doesn't put the curve in until 2 days before the drop date). Just work hard and you can get a good grade. He is very very helpful, visit his office hours with questions.
No Comments

Nice guy, Has an accent which can be unclear sometimes.Uses powerpoints but many test questions cant be found in the slides.  Must read the book and do homework to do well in the class.  Everyone does badly on the exams but he gives a nice curve. Definitely take this class.

what a great, caring teacher! he's very clear but it's accounting that's tough...not him. he bases grades on online hmwk, and uses in class clicker quizzes which brought down my grade a bit; it made me learn though cause i had to learn concepts ASAP. if you feel like you're struggling, ASK for help! he will help you! hard for me cause im bad at biz
The GOAT. Do yourself a favor and take his class. Seriously.
Raph is a great professor. He's funny and cares about his students a lot. I enjoyed his energy throughout the semester

Raph is laid back. He loves cracking jokes. He expects us to put in the work to grasp the material. We cover 27 theories, 2 per week. We read the chapter, listen to a lecture, complete a 3 paragraph reflection, and then attend discussion sections. Its not hard, but very time consuming depending on if you read the chapter or you attend the lecture.

He is a great professor, it is clear that he cares about his students. There are weekly quizzes, a couple of projects, and readings, but it's nothing you can't handle. If you keep up with the assignments, you should be fine. He's also funny which is an added bonus.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: if you watch the lectures, you are guaranteed an A. all projects are discussed weeks in advanced and there are only 3. he let us decide the format of quizzes/exams and we did a weekly quiz. so easy. 90 minutes for 20 questions that were probably all multiple choice. command + f the book and you will get an A. my TA Yumin was so nice too!

He is my favorite professor so far. He was really understanding with covid and structured class around everyones needs. We had to show up to class once a week and work in groups, everything was super interactive and easy as long as you read the material. He knows the material really well and is a really cool guy.

I never write rate my professor reviews but always look at them when signing up for classes. I felt compelled to write about Ralph because he is the best teacher I've ever had. Ralph is a super nice guy and is extremely smart- so it does sometimes get hard to follow along. HOWEVER- he sends you a summary every class of what is important! 10/10

This professor was one of my favorites. He is a lot to take in at first but eventually becomes your favorite professor due to his timeliness and amazing feedback. I enjoyed going to his class everyday!

Probably one of the best professors at UMD. Kind, caring, and actually wants his students to understand the material and improve at speaking. If you want more feedback, go to office hours and just chat with him. Grading was fairly easy, just practice your speech beforehand and you will do well.

Dr. Mazzone is my favorite professor! Definitely take this man for a class. He actually applies the concepts from lectures to everyday life. He will give you feedback in the form of questions which makes you think critically. Please take him for any class. You will learn so much.
Was an awesome teacher. Make sure to put time into the presentations and you will do just fine.

Raph setup this class in a way that makes other professors seem out of touch. Lectures are lectures - but in our class he supplemented the book content with real world examples and related personal stories(often comical) to the material. He genuinely cares about his students.

He is a really interesting person and tells good stories and relates them to the class. His lectures are engaging and informational, but the seminar classes can be boring unless a good point of conversation arises out of the assignment. There are 1page discussion papers due every other class but they are graded basically for participation.

A great professor overall. Genuinely cares about his students. If you have time-conflicts or something comes up, just communicate and things will be figured out to accomodate you. He pushed back the final multiple times to help those who weren't caught up with their drafts.

Radford is really nice, however he is extremely unaccommodating for students. He follows the syllabus to a tee and will not allow students who are struggling to switch topics on a paper. He does not understand that students are burnt out and stressed and will not accommodate for students.

Professor Skudrna allows everyone to talk, but if the class goes silent, he calls on someone at random. In comparison to my Diff eq, Phys, and Enee classes, the workload is tremendous. I highly recommend taking his class if you want a lot of writing assignments, being called someone else, and having a lot of work to finish with short deadlines.

I took ENGL243 (What is Poetry?) w/ Radford. Such a great prof. Lots of discussion throughout class but he makes it a safe environment for everyone to convey their own ideas about poems. I used to hate poetry, and took this class as an elective, but Radford made this class very enjoyable & gave me a better appreciation for poetry. Highly recommend!

It's Professional Writing so you're obviously going to be writing a lot. That said, if you need feedback, you need to ask directly or go to the Writing Center- in an asynchronous online class, I only got peer review feedback from my writing. I did not buy the textbook and did not use it once. That said, he was great over email communication!!

Radford is amazing! He truly cares about his students and is constantly there for them! He is beyond helpful and his feedback will really help you grow as a writer. Take advantage of his office hours before a major assignment as they were very helpful and helped me perform well on major assignments. Radford made English my favorite class!

Such a good professor, if you do the work on time and show up you will pass with an A or B. Gives really nice feedback about your writing and really motivates you. Such a nice teacher 10/10 would recommend.
Super easy if you keep up with assignments

He is a great choice for ENGL101. He is very nice and helpful and is a very fair grader. Make sure to participate in class and bring your textbook for book checks. There are a lot of papers, so start writing sooner rather than later. Draft workshops are mandatory but helpful. All grading criteria are clear and listed and you can ask questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Radford is such a gem!! He's a great professor and really helps you understand the rubric and criteria for assignments. In addition, he provides really useful resources to help you understand how to outline the essay and how to approach it. Also he is pretty easy on the eyes ;)
Professor Radford is understanding and flexible!!! He makes business writing fun and relevant!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Radford was great! He outlines all of the grading policies at the beginning, and grade calculation is easy because the class is out of 100 points (most of the essays were 15 points). As long as you show up every day, turn in drafts on time, and try your best you should be able to get an A. I turned in a draft late once unfortunately and got an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Radford is probably the nicest prof I've had at UMD so far. He's  super helpful and easy to talk to, and as long as you don't suck at writing, you'll be fine in this class. As far as the reading, I just skimmed it right before class and was fine. He's a fair grader and is always willing to talk to you during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Love the lad, great teacher, great friend.
Great Teacher.  Highly recommended for English 101.  He really cares about his students and is very approachable outside of class.  He is really chill and really is a nice fair grader.

Radford is a very nice, relaxed and chill guy. Most of the assignments that you do, are not too hard. As long as you follow the rubric when you write your essays, and do the homework readings, you will get a good grade in his class. He is also eager to help you improve as a writer and is easy to meet up with. Overall, Radford is a good professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: One of the nicest men to walk on campus. Class is decently relaxed and students are kept engaged. He grades fairly (and sometimes generously) and gives good feedback on papers. He is a great professor for this course.

This class taught me so much about non-profits and Holden really knows her stuff. She is always available by email and after class to chat. She truly cares about her students and wants you to do well. All of her assignments have a rubric which she sends back to you. As long as you email before midnight, you will get an extension on projects/papers.

Professor Holden is kind and allows extensions, but her disorganized ELMS page and overwhelming workload make the class incredibly stressful. Large assignments are due almost every class, and even with my interest in nonprofits, it felt almost impossible to manage. Finals week was a nightmare, and sadly I wouldn't recommend her class to anyone.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely adored Professor Holden. She was extremely kind and understanding, very flexible with due dates and deadlines you just have to email her before the assignment is due. She will always approve extensions even if you need an extension for your extension. The workload is a lot for this course, but I learned so much and took my time.

This is a very fast-paced, disorganized class. She often forgets to put all the important details needed for the assignment and scatters them throughout several documents, emails, and telling the class in her quick rambles. You will constantly be working on assignments or peer reviews. Save yourself and take another prof writing class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dont take this professional writing class, the amount of assignments is ridiculous. She is a very hard grader almost impossible to get an A, unlike most other professional writing classes. This class was supposed to be easy but was my most stressful class, do yourself a favor and take someone else.

I'm a confident writer and found her class difficult. You are turning in assignments most days of the week, not always at the same times, so it's easy to miss them by accident. Her ELMS page is a nightmare; a thousand links/pages, you can't find anything. Not always clear what she wants. Not a bad prof, but class is disorganized/overwhelming.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Prof Holden is perhaps the best professor I've had at UMD. She is incredibly responsive to student concerns and really wants to help students. However, this class isn't easy. There is usually 2 written assignments/week and there is A LOT of peer editing. Be ready to work, but an A is very attainable.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--So many papers

reviews.comment: "The grading lacks transparency, as scores are given without clear criteria or detailed feedback. This makes it hard to understand areas needing improvement. A clear rubric would be helpful."
Dr. Renzi is the best!!! Highly recommend! She has a great energy and always puts on great lectures

Professor Renzi is AMAZING! I have really enjoyed having her this semester! She is so sweet and cares about her students. She is a wonderful teacher and her lectures are always insightful. She is also very organized and a pleasure to work with. She does not use a textbook for our class, nor does she give tests/quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Renzi is a gem! She cares so much for all of her students and will do whatever it takes to ensure you get a great grade, as long as you put in the effort. She never assigns textbooks because she doesn't believe in them. You will have heavy weighted assignments that take time and effort to do, but it's all really beneficial in the long run.

One of the best professors I've had at UMD. I would recommend everyone to take this class. She is caring, and wants all of us to succeed but does not give you an easy A without putting in work. Exams are very straightforward, with extra credit opportunities available. Great class.

Never used slides and rarely wrote on the chalkboard. Yells at you if you do not understand items on the study guide and attempt to ask. The only saving grace of his class was that he only used questions directly from the study guide and there is only one paper that you turn in twice for edits.

reviews.comment: Took professor Rey for philosophy of mind and while the material was fascinating I was thoroughly disappointed with his abrasive teaching style. Not only that but he cussed me out over a paper assignment. do not recommend
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Don't take his class if you aren't an A+ student. Very tough grader. Difficult to follow during lectures. Never uses chalkboard so most of his teaching is him sitting down and talking to students. I witnessed him tell a student to read a book after the student asked a question that was on the review sheet..during the review session. pop-up quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Without a doubt the worst professor I've had at Maryland. While being online is normally a bonus for most students this professor tries to make it his own mission to waste time whether it's the incredibly boring lectures, hundreds of pages of readings, or the impossible tests where he expects you to know every concept and detail. Avoid at all costs
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is a bit disorganized sometimes. He is a great philosopher and does the work to sway you to his way of thinking.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment:
This review is for his MSML604 course-  my biggest tip to pass easily is look up the IIT KANPUR course on YouTube.

Pros: He's very knowledgeable in his field
Cons:
- Not very approachable if you need help, limited communication styles
- Not a good lecturer, just kind of runs through the slides and re-iterates the bullets

Took principles of machine learning class (MSML 603). His explanations are horrible, and acts in a way that shows he doesn't care whether students actually understand the lectures or not. He IS experienced and educated, but he only works for payment and is not a real teacher. Besides, I saw him a few times underestimating and discouraging students.

Worst professor Ive ever had. Perfectly nice guy and definitely intelligent, but does nothing help students succeed. Theres HW due every couple of weeks, 2 exams and a final. There were no resources to study aside from HW solutions that only gave half explanations, and if we were lucky a review PowerPoint. Useless lectures, and exams are horrible
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor is the worst in the ECE department. So many people in the class, took the entire semester and are now having to retake the course because of the final grades. He also doesn't let you have any idea what your grade is, or what you scored on the final until it's too late and in Testudo. He should not be teaching, and I got a good grade.

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE, save yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor is the worst professor I have ever had in my entire college career. He does not care about his students in the slightest. The majority of his class will get Cs or fail, but he thrives off of this and does not take any accountability. Only take him if you want to experience the worst professor in existence. He should be fired.

By far the worst learning experience I've had at the University of Maryland. The professor shows no regard for the success of his student, can be seen by his course grade distributions as well. Exam averages are extremely low, yet he chugs along with no intention of improving scores or catering to the students' learning needs.
I love La <3 He is amazing

Prof. La is the best! Although looks so cool at the first few classes to approach, he turned out to be very friendly & serious about student's understandings of his lecture. Always trying to make his words clear and everyone satisfied. Delivering key ideas besides tough & boring texts. He even remembered who's who in the entire class!
Prof. La was the best!

Professor La was the best. He seemed complicated and unfriendly at first but if you read the book and show up to his problem session (totally done by him), you will learn alot. The material is hard, just read the book and ask the TA if you don't understand anything. I would love to take another signals class with him.

I thought she was a tough grader but you could tell she is passionate and knowledgeable in what she does so I commend her for that. I get it if your not interested in this subject this class could be challenging but if you are curious and interested then she is the professor to have!

This class is overwhelming and punitiveWeekly assignments,no deadline flexibility, and empty promises of extra credit make it frustrating.The professor grades papers just two days beforeth final one is due, offering no feedback to improve.Instead of fostering learning, the focus seems to be on making things unnecessarily difficult.Avoid this class!

Dr. Richardson was an amazing lecturer and professor. So much so I had to ask if he was teaching any other classes. He doesn't. This class was eye-opening, and while the readings were heavy, it makes sense given the content. Dr. Richardson always brought in guest lecturers who hammered home just how relevant the course material was. Amazing guy.

He is such a good lecturer and with his class being 2 and a half hours he made them feel so much shorter. He keeps you engaged and always makes sure to teach you so much. You learn a lot in this class but be ready to read. The quizzes are difficult but if you pay attention in class you should be perfectly fine. Amazing professor with high standards
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great prof and interesting material. Extremely reading heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: DrRichardson is a good guy and a great teacher. However, you need to be on top of your game if you want to succeed in this class. The quizzes and tests are extremely difficult and specific. Attend all lectures for the guest speakers and videos, as he asks a lot of questions about them on his exams/quizzes. You will most likely get a B in this class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Don't take his class if you like your GPA. The lectures are interesting but quizzes and papers are graded so harshly and unfairly. The midterm and final ask random questions about specific info. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Lectures are interesting enough but assignments are unfair. Quizzes ask for such specific information (names, statistics, random terms) that you can't possibly recall them from the extensive readings. Papers are graded too harshly. If you try to argue that its unfair, you're shot down. I was incredibly frustrated by this class from start to finish.

Heard rave reviews after taking 100 with Dr. Nichols, which I loved! 187 was an absolute nightmare. Many group projects, inconsistencies with assignments, &the tests and quizzes are gruesome; so many readings, then tests on the most specific of questions. I thought this would be an enriching elective, but it was more like a stressful major course.

Everyone should take this class. It is eye opening. It is inspirational. No matter how much you already knew about the issue before, you will still learn new things. Professor equips you with the knowledge necessary to educate others as well. Be warned though, there is a ton of reading and the  quizzes are based on minute details.

The class was amazing and I learned SO MUCH. It was almost a system overload. My only issue is the amount of reading and structure of the exams. We read about 3 books (cover to cover) and I would say 30-40 news articles. Reading is absolutely necessary  because the exams and quizzes reference the smallest details from the readings.

Very passionate about issues against minorities and how the criminal justice system works/not works. Grading takes really long but there aren't too many assignments. Your going to want to read though because there are many texts. He also has funny stories and perspectives. You don't have to go to every class but you'll most likely enjoy going.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He wants to appear smart by giving impossible problems, but when asked questions, he is bad at explaining. (This review won't allow me to use the true words I want to use for this review.) Stay away from him!

It wasn't the most "fun" lecture but Dr. Sanner clearly knows the subject he teaches and he'd say some funny stuff in class. As the course progresses, the homework and labs get more difficult but it's never more than what you should be capable of if you're putting in the work. He's also available out of class and makes his expectations clear.

Robert Sanner has multiple homeworks and labs that hardly effect overall grade. His tests are far more convoluted than other professors. He does curve his exams but that is because the are so poorly crafted that the before avgs are around 40-50. Do not take Robert Sanner, he does not care about you and it will be very apparent if you take him.

Sanner is very knowledgable, but he is very intimidating. He has very high expectations of his students and is more often than not condescending towards them. The lectures are boring and long, and his exams are extremely difficult. If possible, take ENAE202 with a different professor, otherwise prepare yourself to be frustrated and confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His courses are tough, but he throws in a lot of useful insights and cohesively connects topics right until the very end. Homework and exams require a LOT of time and effort, but they help you learn the concept well. I would definitely recommend it if you are interested in learning the topic!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: YIKES controls, what else should I say? Sanner struggled a lot with ELMS in the online format and made IMPOSSIBLE exams. Instead of just simply submitting our work we had to write out in words the steps we took to solve the problem. Homework was literally impossible and took DAYS to complete. Exercises were helpful, but covered the easiest material

Dr. Sanner has excellent lectures that communicate a lot of information, but the labs and homework don't help practice the material as much as practice reading comprehension and exactly what he tells you to do, which makes understanding the material more difficult. The class is curved, and he announces it at the beginning of the course.

Maybe one of the shortest professors I've ever had. Like, very minimal, one-sentence answers. Whenever I go to his office hours, I would always leave feeling dumber than I went in. He's very knowledgeable of the topic, he's just a very strict prof. If you're able to learn in a very closed-off environment, take his class. It just not for me I guess.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't come into this class as an engineer, come into it as a mathematician. Despite what others have said: if you understand the material, homework is at most 10 hours without help. His lecture slides are the only resource I ever had to refer to for assignments/exams. They could honestly be published as an introductory linear controls textbook.

Overall his lectures are very detailed and specific, and he explains all coding concepts very well during class. However, even though his labs are not too difficult, some of the homework sets he provided (especially in C++) are extremely difficult and time-consuming - get ready to spend a lot of time on them and also for late nights.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Sanner is very verbose. HW take 24 hours with help from friends. Exams this year were brutal. Had questions not posed in class - very annoying. Leaves u feelin used and abused. He makes basic concepts feel grander. Know part frac decomp & Laplace transform. Get ready to solve for numbers. He will try to scare u. Final proj is trash - very verbose.

He's rude when you ask questions, so I couldn't even ask for help. He has potential; he cares about the subject, is very knowledgeable and tries to give us practice. If only he were kinder and stopped making lectures super boring. He should make an effort to make the material interesting and try connect w/ students. Everyone will benefit that way!

Controls. Need I say more? This is the class that is the true weed-out for this major, and will absolutely consume so much of your time. You need to start working as soon as possible, and go to office hours when stuck. Working with others is key in college, but Sanner has seen every trick in the book, you will get caught if you cheat.

You've read the reviews, this is a hard class. Start homework early to get a better understanding of the subject. Notes are posted online, but always try to make lecture for the same reason. Exams aren't that bad if you go over past exams and homework. I hear office hours are helpful for both. The final project will cover EVERYTHING. Good luck.

Probably one of the hardest professors in UMD. Does not care at all about his students, would fail everyone in his class if he could. His lecture have the most basic examples, however, it is impossible to take notes as he scrolls up and down code that is already written. Homework and lab + he does not realize some of his students have no coding exp

Sanner is just not a good professor. He does not care at all that most of his students have absolutely zero programming experience. His homework is crazy long and time consuming and it is impossible to take notes during lecture because he scrolls so fast through the pre-written code. Extremely difficult class, all he does is show how smart HE is.

Prof Sanner is a nice guy; with that being said he's not the best for those who dont have experience with programming. He expects that everyone understands his lectures and gives very difficult lab exercises and home works. Hard to take notes in class bc he just scrolls through pre-written code the entire lecture. Home work takes average of 6 hrs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Realistically I should have tested out of this class. I attended a little over half the lectures and right now I have a solid A. Exams make up 60% of your grade. You also write all your code for those exams. (Kinda annoying and dumb). Sanner is very eccentric and loves his job. He reminds me of Bill Nye.

Dr. Sanner is a teacher who truly cares and knows about what he teaches. He is by no means a bad professor. The only complaint I have about the class setup is that his examples in class are very simple, yet the homeworks on the same topic involve higher level math than I was able to understand, regardless of my ability to create and edit code.

He's a good professor but he has a lot of quirks. He doesn't specify when he switches from topic to topic, that some variables (say Q) from previous section has no relation to Q in the current section. And due to lecture/notes overlap, he will end one topic one day and start a new one on same day (understandable). He doesn't make it clear it is new

I liked his course so much I wound up working with him on a technical paper, so this review is probably a bit biased, but the paper did very, very well and that was also thanks to his guidance.   Most AE courses have a curve that is variable.  Sanner's does not. Bust your ass and you won't need it; he teaches everything you need to earn an A. Earn.

I took control theory for Dr Sanner's first semester at UMCP. He was extremely difficult and seemed to revel in blowing us undergrads away with his MIT acumen. He really played up his own intelligence and put on "the genius show" for the aggrandizement of his own ego. Unfortunately, not much help to those of us trying to learn a difficult subject.
Doesn't use the text, all whiteboard.  Text is useless.  Leaves major pieces out of the notes. Gives cryptic, non-answers to specific questions. Nice guy, really into it.
Great prof!
Please keep comments clean
Pretty easy if you pay attention, tests are fair, just know what youre doing in labs and youll know what youre doing on tests.

Extremely difficult course. Prepare to spend at least 30 hours on each homework assignment.  Exams are over weekends, you'll use every hour he gives you.  You'll learn a whole lot.  6 hws, 1 midterm, 1 final.  The class is worth every tear...
Good introductory control course.  Dr. Sanner covers the basics of control theory well.  4 exams, 1 medium scale project.
Prepare  for a brutally difficult course.  GO TO CLASS.  The notes you will take with him will be your textbook--he's that good a teacher.
worst professor ever

I've never had a worse professor in my life. You can see that the guy knows the material, nonetheless, he does not know how to communicate. He has very, very bad English which makes it unbelievably difficult to understand the material. He believes that your lack of knowledge is due to skipping class when the overall grades speak for themselves
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ruhi is a very knowledgeable professor in the OMBA field. His lectures are engaging, interesting, and extremely applicable to OMBA majors. The course is difficult, and there are some difficult concepts. The content gets easier as the course goes on, but you HAVE to go to class, take notes, and do the practice. Great class and good prof.

Taught material well, cold calls students during lectures which I hated at first, but found myself to like bc it forces you to pay attention/follow along. All notes and simulations taken directly from book - if you want to ace the class then read before coming to class, and do practice problems. Exams are fair, he can grade tough at times tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is the second course that I have taken with Professor Ruhi. He is honestly a super nice person and wants to help his students learn. With that being said, it is extremely difficult to get a high grade in his class. He cold calls, grades homework by accuracy, has no rubric for projects and puts concepts on tests that he never goes over.
Definitely need to go to class and put in the effort if you want a good grade in the class. Challenging but not impossible.

you need to read the book, hes a good professor but the content is just hard. the exams weigh a lot and its hard if youre not an avid test taker. he explains things well but its the application and doing it yourself that youll start to make mistakes and where things get hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Ruhi is such a nice person, but it is almost impossible to get an A in his class. The simulation in his class sucks because your grade is dependent on how well the other groups did. He also goes fast through lectures, so you definitely need to go back and rewatch them.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class online cuz of covid, but I loved prof ruhi. He's good at explaining the content. I did have the luxury of pausing and rewatching lectures, but honestly the content is very easy. Its all plug and chug in excel. He is kinda a hard grader cuz he doesn't give partial credit for homework but it kinda makes sense since its all on Solver

Professor Ruhi has taught this class for years and clearly conveys the content of the course through his lectures. There is not too much homework, likely 1-2 hours every 2 weeks. The content was interesting and the exams were fair, although the exams were each worth 39% of your final grade. It will be a considerable amount of work but doable.

Worst Professor I think I've ever had, rather than explaining concepts in a way that helps you understand him, he just shows you his way to do it and doesn't allow for any alternatives. If your way of thinking is more open, and you truly want to learn the content rather than just replicate random spreadsheets he makes, don't take this class w/ him

He is not helpful during office hours or when trying to talk with him in class. He'll blow you off and make you feel like an idiot for not knowing the right answers. The lectures are dry and confusing, and he will assign random assignments at the tip of the hat. Only class I'll have an assignment specifically for thanksgiving!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would not take this class if you can avoid it. The material should be very easy to understand but he burns though lectures and does not care if students are lost, which is frequent given his broken English. He will call on you randomly and will make you feel stupid if you ask questions, even when he does not know how to answer them himself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He's pretty funny in a sardonic kind of way. Get the online textbook, know how to use vmware if you're on mac, and definitely go to class. If you are able to follow along in class with the problems he does, the exams will seem like a breeze. Also, if you can ace the hw sets, you can ace the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Ruhi can be intimidating when it comes to asking questions in class. It seems like he gets frustrated for you needing clarification. This class would have been a lot harder if I had not taken AP Stats in high school. Although, the examples he gives in class give a good insight to the tests. He always gives a formula sheet, too.
Teacher is passionate about what he teaches, very thorough and explains what is expected for the exams, assignments and homework.

He's smart but he's rude to his students. Very bad at explaining the concepts to students. Ask him for help? He'll act like you're wasting his time. If there's another option, take another teacher. You'll spend hours reading the textbook and watching youtube trying to teach yourself.

Seems to understand what he is doing, but is easily the worst teacher I've had at communicating what he is talking about to students. His lack of proficiency in English can be a challenge at times, although accent is clear. Can be incredibly rude at times, calling out students for not knowing answers.

Intelligent but bad at explaining material. Expect to teach yourself. Office hours always packed. He accuses you of skipping class and looks at you like your an idiot when you ask questions to clarify his confusing lectures. Only professor I've seen yell at a student or call them a liar. A is possible, B is likely, C is common. Drop rate is high.
Confuses me, gives good examples, I learn better from examples on hw then teacher himself

This is a difficult subject, but Ruhi does a good job of explaining the material. Exams are tough, but they are manageable.  Discussions are graded.  He does have an accent, but is definitely understandable.  I would recommend this professor.

Ruhi is very nice and helpful but has quite an accent. He makes the exams easy enough.  This class was Business Statistics. I took AP Statistics in high school, so it kinda helped with acing the class and the exams. He posts all his notes online. I only looked through the book (online) if I doubted anything on his slides.  I recommend him
Bad.

Although this class is extremely tough, Prof. Ruhi works hard to teach his students well. His grading is very fair and he always responds to emails promptly, even on the weekends. As long as you attend lectures, you can do well in the course.

Awesome teacher. He gave plenty of examples and the class material built on itself very well. Provided review times before tests. I never did the homework but had no problems. (I am a bit of a math-oriented guy - 780M/650E/600W SAT, FWIW.)  Only downside is you got to walk to Van Munching, on the outskirts of campus.

One of those classes that either clicks or doesn't. He's a nice guy whose willing to repeat things to you over and over, and his tests/quizzes are straighforward. Class isn't mandatory but he gives MAJOR hints on what to expect on tests and exams as well as help w/ the homework. Very possible A
One of the best professor i ever had to learn from.
Professor Ruhi was one of the best teachers I've ever had. He was always so helpful and nice. Dr. Ruhi really wants his students to learn the material.

A great teacher. He really DOES want students to do well.  He has an accent, but honestly I can understand him better than any math teacher I've ever had.  He's very logical.  LISTEN to his advice and DO the HW.

One of the best math teachers I've ever had.  He runs through the problems in a logical order, and the homework is really similar to the exams.  As long as you do the homework problems, the exams and quizzes will be really easy.
No Comments

He's the best!!!  He gives 4 quizzes, midterm, final and two individual projects.  Exams are not that hard as long as you study and do exactly what he tells you to do. He is an awesome teacher!!! 4 Quizzes will give you an idea what real exams look like. Take his class. You will have a great semester wit him!!!
Super nice guy who will do everything in his power to help you do well in class. DEFINITELY recommend him if you have the chance to take his class!
No Comments
hes an awsome teacher!!

The saving grace of this class is a little something called "consistent with previous error", which means you can basically completely screw up your algebra, get the wrong answer and still get credit anyway. Do the practice exams and work earnestly in discussion and it'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Rosca, isn't bad. Her accent is understandble, her handwriting is fine. I don't know what everyone else on this rate my professor is talking about, and I kind of supsect its just a cope from people who got filtered by her class. Basically, DO EVERY PRACTICE EXAM and have an IQ above 90 and you'll be golden.
Lectures can be confusing with the professor's rushed explanations and hard-to-read handwriting. You'll need to do a lot of self-study, but tools like Unstuck study can be helpful for exam prep.
Constantly gives snarky remarks when asked for help with something. Terrible lecturer.

Absolutely terrible professor, there's no use going to lectures because she explains things terribly and makes it more confusing. Be prepared to teach yourself everything. The tests are very similar to the practice exams which is helpful.

Honestly she's really not that bad. If you put in the work and study hard, it will show. Obviously not the best professor that I've ever had but it was manageable. Go to class, do your homework, read the textbook, ask questions, and you will be fine. Not an easy A, but also not nearly as bad as everyone is describing her.
There is absolutely no other way to say this but, DO EVERYTHING YOU CAN TO GET A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR. If you don't have a choice, nothing to say but prepare for the storm.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Rosca's lectures can be very hard to understand because of her handwriting, and boring lectures so be prepared to teach yourself most of the material. This is the HARDEST teacher I have ever had and refuses to help during office hours referring you to the help center.  Do not take any class with this teacher.

Just can't finish all the problem sets in the exam and you won't have enough time to think about the every questions in the exams. Try to avoid her at all cost.

Dr. Rosca is a good teacher. She's clear and helpful. BUT if you have accommodations through DSS she will fight you tooth and nail which is really sad. She is not understanding of students who learn differently. Also, the tests are impossible to finish in the allotted time, even for students who get the material 100%. Its a weeder course. Be prepar

Don't expect to learn anything if at all from lecture. Instead, crack open the book. To other math majors: this class's concepts are not as easy as everyone always says. It's what we call "fake" math.

when she gives you pop quizzes,prepare to read her confusing way of writing and  ugly hand writing.  pretty sure I would have passed the quizzes she gave us if it was printed on paper. She also complicates the most simplest things by the way she writes and talks. you'll be teaching yourself everything from the online homework and textbook problems

Overall, a very difficult professor for this class.  Unfortunately, her tests are set up to test your knowledge of advanced integration instead of the chapter material, which is ridiculous.  There is an abundance of better professors you can get for this class at UMD, so try to avoid her.

Wording on exams is so confusing. Has a lot of  confusing "fluff" in her lectures. Attend class for any hints on exam questions, but STICK TO THE TEXTBOOK ONLY. NOT THE SLIDES (which she posts online). HAVE A FRIEND WHO'S TAKEN THE CLASS BEFORE GIVE YOU THEIR MATLABS!!! They're a giant pain and take so much time!
She is not a very good teacher and her tests include material we haven't gone over at home or in class. She often gets confused by her own work. Avoid having her if possible!
Very difficult to understand. Bad teacher.
The class goes fast. Miss a single day, and it takes a serious amount of work to recover and get back up to speed. Still, good class, hard subject matter, but not poorly done.

Dr. Rosca is a very good teacher. She explains very difficult concepts systematically and is always available if you have any questions or concerns. Some of the other reviews said her exams were atrocious; I don't think that's fair. Her class is all about mastery and gaining mathematical maturity. If you do the homework and THINK, you'll be fine.

She is very concerned with her students ability to succeed in her classes. She uses powerpoint slides from the publisher, however, she did go over examples and complete them on the board. If you had questions or were confused about a topic, she was willing and very able to explain concepts. She was willing to move exams for students within reason.
AVOID HER AT ALL COSTS!!! She doesn't explain anything at all. I ended up teaching myself EVERYTHING out of the textbook. Also, her exams are extremely confusing.
Hard to understand and doesn't explain things well. All of the homework is online, and you'll end up teaching yourself most of the things out of the book
Very dry teacher and hard to understand because of her accent. Not helpful or interested in her students at all even if you ask for it. AVOID!

Ruiwen Shu's homepage for relevant class info (UGA)
Came to class 2 times in first week only but first test felt pretty easy. He posts all notes and non-mandatory attendace. Can use the wayback machine on his website for earlier diffeq class test/notes. Understand all the notes and the test will be fine. Gives ample example problems for practice.

I had him from MATH246 (DiffEq) but this wasn't an option. Shu was a great professor that never gave - grades, so even though I had an 80 I had a B. Lecture examples are exactly like exam questions. By far the best Math prof. I've had at UMD (which isn't saying much). The matlab projects were very hard though.
Average amount of homework and fair grading. Pretty good lecture notes. Exams can get difficult, but if you study you will do fine.

He was a decent professor. In lecture he wrote notes on pieces of paper under a document camera. It was difficult to understand what he was saying, but manageable. Some tests were impossible while others were okay. He really varied when I took him. He posted his notes online and responded to emails very quickly. Not a bad pick for a weedout class.

Horrible lecturer. Decent guy, but his lectures are horrible. Doesn't use slides. All of his lectures are him writing on a piece of paper and projecting it on the screen. No resources available and TAs clueless. If you have never taken calc before DO NOT take this class. Literally people wrote a petition to math department fix the unfair class.

Ruiwen Shu is a great professor that gives very clear and decisive notes. He does well at explaining everything and sets up his notes so that they are easy to follow when you review them later. There were a lot of exams and homeworks, but that was just the nature of the class (MATH141). Exams were rather straight forward.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is very clear and has high standard. Difficult, but worth it.

His lectures can be confusing because he likes to skip over steps he finds "easy" to him. Also if you ask him a question in lecture, he doesn't answer it in depth. The lecture doesn't really help with the homework/quizzes/midterms since the examples in class almost never are on the same difficulty as the ones you are expected to solve.

Lectures are very difficult to understand. He is not clear in his explanations and even if you ask a specific question it will not make it any more clear. He has certain aspects of the grading policy that will help (curve, a few dropped homeworks, etc.) but if you can avoid having him as a professor, do it.
Very open and fun teacher made you feel at ease

Sam clearly cares about his students and the class has a personal feel. He also makes A LOT of jokes. I quickly felt comfortable speaking even though I don't normally like doing so.  Attendance is mandatory and class requires paper and pencil. Grade consists of some easy take-home quizzes, communication activities, and mostly three big speeches.
Take. His. Class. You're in for a surprise. Be ready to learn how to present speeches, but other than that... you will love Sam.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Sam Rubin is the king and the man! If you need to take a communications course, INAG 110 with him will be an amazing experience! He makes it fun, engaging and everyone feels like family. Sam genuinely cares about all his students and is accessible 24/7. Do yourself a favor . . . sign up NOW for this class with Sam! You will not regret it!

Sam's alright. He can be aggressive, and repeats the same jokes, which can get annoying. Final grade comprised of informative, persuasive, and professional speeches, three exams, and a bunch of reading quizzes that can be completed by skimming the text. Prepare for speeches and use feedback Sam and your classmates give, and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I highly recommend Sam's section of INAG 110. He is one of the best teachers at UMD. There is no one who cares as much about their students or who will put in as much effort to try and make the class engaging. Speeches are fun b/c you can talk about anything that interests you and tests are all multiple choice (directly from his lectures/textbook).

Sam is amazing. I didnt do any research before signing up for his INAG110 class and I was really nervous to take my OC credit but he made it a very pleasant experience. He cracks jokes and makes us all feel welcomed. He is extremely caring and got to know the whole class very well. This is one class I will definitely miss. Also a fair grader. :)
the best professor i've had at UMD so far. he made online classes extremely fun and it made me so excited to attend :') TAKE HIM you won't regret it!!!!!

Sam is a good choice for INAG110. He gives good feedback on your speaking, but keeps the class from being too hard. He really wants you to do well in the class and also wants the class to be fun. Sam uses his humor all the time to try and make the class less boring, so if you like that in a professor he is definitely your guy.

Sam was by far one of the best professors I have had at UMD. He genuinely cares about his students and as long as you are willing to put in the work, will ensure you get what you need to out of the course. He is accessible and always willing to answer questions, whether about the class or about life. Don't be afraid to have fun in his class!
Attendance is not mandatory but is important. But going to class is worth it as Sam always makes it fun and interesting.
Simply the best! Get over your fear of public speaking and have a great time doing it! This will become your favorite class.

It's a class on public speaking so attendance is definitely mandatory. However, Sam is a one of a kind teacher. He takes an intimidating class that anyone would fear and will turn it into your fav class yet. He is HILARIOUS, light-hearted, fair, respectful, easy grader, and more. You have to try very hard to not get an A :)
Take him or you are stupid. He is great and this is the best class you will ever be in your college career.
Such a great teacher, loved his class so much. Take it if you can.
Professor you must have!!!! He is so great !!! Classes are funny with several strict acceptable rules. Love it!

Sam was the best professor I've ever had. He made the strangers in my class feel like a family. He was so supportive and never failed to make our entire class burst out laughing. Definitely take him if you can, but it's really hard to get into his classes because they fill up so quickly.
He changed my whole college experience and I am lucky to have had him,

Sam is absolutely the BEST teacher I have ever had! He is the most fair grader and his lectures will make you want to come back for more! Forget all the other speech instructors and take Sams class! It will be a life altering experience you will NEVER regret or forget!

Sam's class is great. He gives everyone fun nicknames and jokes around a lot. The class is incredibly easy as long as you show up on time and do your assignments. No need for the textbook. His grading is very fair and almost everyone gets As. You'll be glad you took this class!
If you ever have the chance to take a class with Sam, do it. You'll never regret it

Take his class, you definitely won't regret it. Extremely funny and always makes a point to be very accessible to students outside of class. He answers phone calls from students at 2 in the morning to help them with assignments. If that doesn't make you want to take his class idk what will

Sam presented a lively, vibrant personality (along with a funny, outrageous sense of humor) that enabled students to get out of their comfort zones and emerge from their "shells," which in turn encouraged them to interact with each other and motivated them to feel comfortable and confident delivering speeches.  Amazing class, amazing teacher.

Sam Rubin is the absolute BEST instructor at UMD!  He truly cares about all his students and is focused on their success!  His wit and humor eliminated the fear of speaking with everyone in our class!  This guy is an unbelievable motivator, which is why you will WANT to do well in the course!  Take Sam Rubin's class---you'll be glad you did!

Sam was my best professor ever, and I think the rest of the class liked him, but his jokes can be misinterpreted as offensive. After you peer-review someone's speech, he may prompt you to say something like "And I can't live without you.".  If this would be uncomfortable, do not take Sam. Hilarious prof, easy grader. Class ran over at times.
He's a great person - funny and energetic! Really cares about his students. His exams are easy, we pretty much never used the textbook and never really had homework.

Sam is both an amazing professor and individual. He takes personal interest in making the class as enjoyable and student-friendly as he can. Written exams are just a formality, the real grade is based on the Informative and Persuasive speeches and a group project (which you will love). Take this class with him and no one else. Easy and enjoyable A.

Class is required for GenEd requirements. Great teacher. Very energetic. Very helpful, maybe too helpful. He gives out his home phone number. He provides the class with notes every time. He repeats lines from the notes to clarify and emphasize, but it gets very annoying, especially if you understood it the first time. Speeches are easy enough.
BEST TEACHER EVER

Take this class if you can. Sam is fun, energetic, and informative. He gives you a hard time if you miss too many classes though. I would have gotten an A otherwise. Don't bother buying the book either, you can pass the tests without it.

Sam is AMAZING! I truly dreaded taking this course, but would have missed out on so much if I had not.  He has got to be the BEST instructor at UM! He knows his stuff extremely well and how to relate it the students!  Very funny!  If I could take this class again, I would!  HIGHLY RECOMMEND EVERYONE SIGN UP TO TAKE THIS COURSE FROM SAM!
Smooth class, and caring soul.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: First semester FIRE is really easy, it's a 3 credit class that feels like a 1 credit class. Thanicha (she insists we call her by her first name) is overall pretty good. She struggles to communicate a bit sometimes, but it's always brief. There are also randomly assigned long term groups which you might get unlucky with. Overall I strongly recommend
Really helpful and cares about her students a lot.

Real easy to talk to and is super helpful with every single assignment. The class is coding heavy but she prepares you for it and does give a file with code as a guideline for assignments. Learning RStudio is esp helpful for data analysis work. The work is monotonous and you need lab hours to get a good A, but other than that it was fun.

I loved Dr. Rush! Everyone else saying she is a tough grader is wrong. I got A's on both of the papers and the midterm and final were graded pretty leniently. She is very knowledgable and lectures were always fascinating. Sometimes there were pretty long readings, but otherwise I would definitely recommend!
This professor needs to work on her lecture style and classroom techniques. Almost always divides the class into tiresome discussion groups.

Dr. Rush's grading is extremely harsh and honestly has no reason to be. If you're taking this as a gen-ed or "easy elective", think again. This class is not about "illicit activity" and should be just called pirates. I would not recommend this class to anyone not interested in pirates. 2,000-word essays and midterms/final exams written by hand. No.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Rush is awesome, as is History of Lawlessness. She's incredibly knowledgable, unintentionally hilarious, and a very entertaining, engaging lecturer. I also loved James, her TA. Both were very helpful and accessible, and I learned a lot in this course. I highly recommend this course; comparatively not much work but very interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very fun class :) Familiarize yourself with MLA formatted papers before taking

There is no textbook but there is a short book that was used throughout the semester. While attendance is not mandatory, Dr. Rush learns everyone's names so she knows who is not there. But you are also allowed two "stuff happens" days. I 100% recommend her. She is awesome! Also not a tough grader, just follow her instructions!
The professor grades as if were all grad students and every little detail matters. One mistake is a whole letter grade, and practically impossible if youre not a history major
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Great lectures, Im usually never bored in her class and Im always taking notes. Professor Rush makes each topic super entertaining and interesting. She is a harsh grader, but I respect it.

Dr. Rush is one of the best instructors I've encountered during my time at UMD. She can be nit-picky with grading but grades fairly (leaning towards generously). Her lectures I found fascinating, and she is incredibly knowledgeable. Participation is key in her class, and she is very clear with grading criteria in assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I really like professor Rush, I had her for Hist233. The class is not too hard and it was around 40 students so it was easy to let other kids talk. You can take notes on the computer. She is very nice and understanding.
Classes are interesting, with pictures and videos that help you understand historical phenomena
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Good lecturer. You can get away with not reading occasionally, but you should probably do it just in case. She is very nice and definitely knows what she is talking about. She grades a little harsh on essays, but it isn't really that bad. Overall, she at least doesn't hate to teach and it could be worse.
