reviews.comment: Shes an insanely hard grader. I worked so hard in that class because I realize turning in a decent paper is C material. Do not take this class for a gpa boost, did not help me at all. Terrible lecturer boring af.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Rush is a good lecturer. Her class is very lecture dependent, and your grade is determined by relatively easy, straightforward major projects. This class has no quizzes but you are given points for attending class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Rush is clearly very well versed in what she teaches, but I really didn't enjoy being in her class. She has a very short temper and constantly yells at kids and actually takes away their phones. I didn't know we were still in high school. Attendance is mandatory. I dropped the class after the first essay. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE

Do not take this class. It may seem like an easy A and you get Gen eds but the class is horrible. The professor is nice but she is an extremely hard grader, you accidentally leave something out in your essay? Too bad cause you end up getting a C- on the assignment. The participation grade helps a lot but everything else combined can hurt your grade
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Really interesting class made better by a passionate teacher. She does her best to make the material interesting and incorporates a lot of group discussions and role-playing activities. She's kind, funny, and a fair grader for assignments. Read the articles due for every class and take detailed class notes since the information isn't found online.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is very nice and her class in interesting and she makes it easy to use notes. she tries to switch around her style of teaching by having videos and class. very tough grader, so i would beware if you were looking to pat up GPA. I would take it pass-fail because it is super interesting

I really enjoyed this class mainly because it was a class on pirates, vigilantes, robbers, etc. The tests are all based on memorization, which include a midterm and a final. There are 2 papers which she grades somewhat hard on but they were fun to write. The reading isn't bad at all and is enjoyable at times. All in all she's a great professor.

Anne Rush is so sweet, hardworking and dedicated to her students. Definitely recommend this class. Lots of readings but no text and just a paper for the final, so do the readings if you want to participate in discussion. There is a participation grade. Get on her good side, she's an amazing person. Lots of cool discussions.
Nice lady, class kinda dragged on

While my class was quite small, and she was able to give us all the attention we needed, it doesn't mean that she wasn't a great professor, because she was!  There is a lot of information to memorize for exams, but many options for ID's on exams. Not too hard of a grader, but very big on participation, and attendance(Show up!!), and cell phones.

The class was mostly lecture, but she included a lot of discussion and was always willing to go over questions you do not understand. She grades the paper's hard, but is fair with it and had a million notes on what you could have changed. You can tell that she really wants you do to well. Great class overall, but hard to get an A in.

Even though she seems tough, I thought she was a really good teacher.  She's really smart and knows what she's talking about, and the assignments aren't too bad.  There's quite a bit of reading, but it's not all completely necessary if you go to class and take notes.  I was intimidated at first but she's actually very nice when you talk to her.
She's very thorough and isn't reluctant to yell at students for talking in class (must be British influence from teaching their history) but she's very energetic and is also extremely helpful.

She simply doesn't know what she is talking about she is really disorganized and skips around alot, its hard to understand what she is saying. I was really disappointed because I thought her class would be really good.
Easy class. You even get credit for attendance! It is mostly concept based.

Great professor, very interested and involved in her teaching. If you ask her questions in class she will research them at home and give you detailed e-mail responces that are awesome! Really excited about the British Empire.

I learned so much from Prof. Rudy's class. There is a lot of reading, and the papers take a lot of work, but the course challenges you in the best ways. I left every lecture taking something valuable with me, and Prof. Rudy is an incredible orator. The work definitely isn't impossible to do, and you read brilliant works by a diverse set of writers.

I learned so much from Prof Rudy's class! His lectures are fascinating and the work is manageable if you schedule ahead. There are 3 essays and he gives you a lot of freedom/creativity to pinpoint a part of a reading that interested you and make a compelling argument about it. He values different interpretations as long as they're feasible!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He assigns a lot of reading and assignments. We had an artwork presentation, two groupwork assignments, reading quizzes, three essays, and a final exam. He is very sarcastic with his comments on essays. He that thinks he's open and understanding when he's the complete opposite. He's not understanding to student's struggles and unyielding.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He arrives 5 minutes late everyday, talks about his personal life instead of the assigned reading, and takes FOREVER to return papers. He'll gut your paper if you don't parrot back his own views about feminism , queer theory, and colonialism. Avoid if u can.

Professor Rudy is an absolute professional. I took his ENGL312 course online, which was extremely well organized. He managed to create a dynamic learning environment online through video lectures, engaging discussions boards, fair quizzes, and thought-provoking writing assignments. He is passionate about his work and his students. Take his class!

Professor Rudy approaches literature as a practical reader, without excluding open-debate and student interpretations. I took his Engl 312 class online and 379k on campus and found him very helpful in both courses. If you respond honestly and think about the assigned text, then you will have success in his courses.

Created this account just to rate professor Rudy.  His class can tend to be a little closed-minded in that the readings lean too far to the left.  His personal effort and enthusiasm is unmatched.  Take him if you can

He's a great teacher and makes class very interesting. He's also very interested in what the class has to say, so it's a great discussion based class, not just a teacher droning on and on. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches which is a good thing. If you don't mind a bit of hard work (term paper and final) then he's the professor for you.
very professional, hard course, lots of reading, easy quizes each week but hard final overall.... all quotes from all the books from the entire semester.  I got a C

Great teacher! If you want to be challenged, he does it. Really cares about students intelligently. Amazing pedagogical style and fascinating insight- excited about what students say. Wonderful for the intelligent literature aficionado.

completely useless and boring. can become borderline rude when giving feedback on your writing. has blatant favorites, and if you're not one of them, don't bother. does not foster an open discussion environment. AVOID!!
great teacher. i loved this class. he's a really good speaker and he says a lot of intersting things.

Best professor I've had at UMD. If you really want to learn and open your mind in a new way, he is the professor for you. Awesome discussion, he's very open to new interpretations of texts as long as you can textually back yourself. If you're willing to put in work, you will definitely reap the rewards - loved him!

Prof. Rudy is one of the best professors at UMD, at least for someone who is willing to work towards their own education. He is very sharp, insightful, and helpful, but he will recognize your ability in the beginning of the semester and won't let you slack off. Typically tedious readings, but mind-blowing discussion - he really loves his job.

Single handedily the most interesting class I have taken thus far in college park. His passion is contagious, teaching style absolutely pleasant, and the class a sheer delight. If you can only take one english class and enjoy poetry then there is no better class to take. Rudy is open to all ideas and premotes students' expression in positive way.
Jason is a very knowledgeable professor.  The material is extremely dull however and he is a very hard grader.  Only take this class if you have a lot of time to devote to it.
He is probably the nicest college professor that I've ever had.  He really cares about his students and is very passionate about the course material.

Intro to the English major. Relatively new teacher, quite concerned with student interest, participation. Discussion helpful, albeit at times slow. Four papers a semester and a midterm, nothing too hard.

Had Ryan O'Grady for INST600 and he was awesome. Super friendly and personable, reasonable about granting extensions if requested in advance. Clear rubrics and grading criteria. Responds quickly to questions. Broke final research project down into manageable steps. As long as you do the work and put in the effort you will do well.

Prof. O'Grady is a first-class professor. I just had him for INST 311 in spring 311 and it went very well because Prof. O'Grady was clear with his assignments, emails, instructions, etc. NO VAGUE ANSWERS FROM THIS GUY!

Professor Grady's class was well organized and he made it super easy to learn. I learned a lot in this class and fill like it prepared me for the real world. The group project was also a great learning experience. I would highly recommend taking him.
If you get a good group this class should be a breeze.
Literally the nicest guy I have ever met. Great lectures, very chill guy. Take his class.

This class was among my easiest and most manageable, as Ryan's lectures were clear and all the course materials were well organized in the ELMS page. The lectures were interesting, though sometimes difficult to takes notes on because of the pace. He also offered lecture recordings and Zoom access to every class, so attendance wasn't mandatory.

This class across the board is not technically challenging, but the semester-long group project is what's truly important, as well as the two exams. While the project is not difficult, it is long, and your other group project members are going to be key in whether or not you end up doing well, or carrying the entire team on your shoulders for an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Group projects

reviews.comment: O'Grady's class was extremely well organized, making it super easy to learn. I learned a lot in this class with very little stress. I would highly recommend taking him.

Some of the assignments he gives are ambiguous in what the end goal is, but he's an easy grader and was always prepared at the beginning of each week with the weekly content. No complaints, and I would certainly take him again for any other course.

Professor O'Grady is a good professor who makes his expectations clear. The course is designed so that you really interact with the material and understand it. The work was not too bad, although it was too much at times but still manageable. The lectures were in depth and the readings could be lengthy at times but the class wasn't bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took INST201 online with Prof O'Grady and I highly recommend anyone who is able to take this class to take it. It's a very interesting class because the material learned relates to the world we live in that's full of technology. We had weekly discussion posts, 2 midterms, 1 final, and some other small assignments. This class was really easy!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great guy and amazing prof. People say he grades hard or his tests are hard, but if you read the textbook and stay on top of the material (actively listen during class) you'll be fine.
Prepares you well for the tests and quizzes, grades harder than other sections.

Ryan is a great guy but the topic itself is very difficult. Problem sets are not similar to exams, so make sure to study all concepts. Lenient grader, make sure to not leave any blanks on problem sets or exams.

Don't trust him about how to prep for the exams - he pulls from everything and you need to do practice problems well beyond what he provides. You should take his class while take a MIT or course era course simultaneously in order to learn enough to do well.

Professor Cooper is a really cares about his students. If you read the textbook and do the online quizzes before class you are sure to do well in the class. He keeps lectures interesting by using videos and encouraging student participation. He also posts all the notes online so it's easy to stay on top of it.

Professor Cooper is a great guy and really cares about his students. His class is a little harder than other sections, but he knows what he is talking about and tries his best to set his class up for success. He drops hints in class about what to study and most of the stuff on tests/quizzes come from the powerpoints (which are posted online).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Although he has good intentions, Prof Cooper voluntarily made BMGT110F much harder than it needed to be, and much harder than every other section. He is the only professor who gives quizzes, and on top of that THEY GET REALLY DIFFICULT. The exams are all True/False Explain format, which seems simple enough, but the questions are very poorly worded
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He expects you to read two chapters week and complete short online quizzes per chapter. There are 4 quizzes total, in a True/False-- Explain format, at first they are pretty easy, but once you start doing well he turns up the heat, A LOT. I would not recommend. He made the class a lot harder than it had to be. One group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Ryan is one of the few professors on this campus who truly cares about you as a person. He is extremely sweet and doesn't want to give you a hard time. He will readily give extensions on assignments. As long as you actually do the readings, you'll be fine on the exams. That being said, be prepared to read 50-100+ pages a night. We had seven novels.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Ryan is so great! 
-cares about students
-listens to concerns
-interesting lectures (lots of reading but easy to catch up in class)
-forgiving of missing class
-some texts/movies in english
-good grader! (also gives extensions when needed)
-our mean was a 91 for class midterm!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: Do not hesitate on taking Professors Long class he is the nicest professor I´ve ever had, plus his classes are incredibly interesting .

Highly recommend taking his class on crime and impunity. He is one of my favorite Spanish professors that I've ever had and the class is very interesting. I feel like I learned more about new topics than what you usually go over in a Spanish class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took Professor Long's class fo the fall semester and I am taking another class with his this semester. He really cares about students and he's such a sweet man.
Professor Long is one the nicest professor of the department, and he loves the Spanish language as much as teaching it. Do not hesitate in taking his class.
nice dude pretty chill class

Boring lectures. Post online. Test are hard. Takes forever to put grades up. Nice guy, but seems new. Has a linguistics degree but teaches programming. Goes fast in lectures and isnt very helpful when asking questions. I would take somebody else if I could.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Anton taught this class alongside Aric Bills. Bills was by far the better professor. Anton was not good at explaining the material at all but he made himself available at office hours and did care for his students. Wouldn't recommend him if you are not strong at Python. The class is very tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hamill is great! That 2 hour lecture could be a bore but with his stories, it makes it better. He says exams are super easy but the wording can be kind of tricky so, make sure to brush up on lecture and the textbook beforehand. There are no slides for this class so, it is important to go to lecture and take good notes. Other than that, great class!

He's a really enjoyable professor. He teaches based on his own experiences as a police officer who also has a law degree and It was super interesting. There are a lot of things you have to memorize but as long as you memorize the material that he brings up repeatedly in class then you will be fine

The professor is caring and he is great but it can be hard to follow lectures because you are taught through his stories and life experiences. There are 3 exams and a couple of small papers but your grade is based on your exams and because lectures are hard to follow that is why I got a B.
Amazing professor especially for a once a week, 2 1/2 hour class. highly recommend.

I love Hamill but he doesn't check his email and it about drove my class insane. Also... he is not very organized or very good at making exams... his wording can be very confusing and that's why I did not come out on top with an A grade.
Very engaging lectures with interesting stories from his career as a cop that ties into lecture material, making concepts easy to understand.

EVERYONE TAKE HIM. Hamill literally made me love my major so much more. 2.5 hours seems like a really long time and it is but I look forward to it every time because they are so interesting. He is a cop and a lawyer and teaches you through stories that you will remember. This is a class I genuinely learn in and enjoy. Barely any work.

His lectures were so entertaining and he usually will give you a lot of answers to test questions. Even though its a two and a half hour class we ended up having a few of them online and a few cancelled and the ones that were in person usually ended early. Great professor can't recommend this class enough.

Do not let the long class times scare you away, Professor Hamil is by far the best professor to take. He's a licensed attorney and police chief so he has great stories and is super knowledgeable. He really cares about his students and their success. He'll usually end class early too so it isn't as long as you think. Favorite professor by far.

Don't let the 2 and a half hour class scare you off, there are way more pros than cons. Hamill is a police chief so he's totally qualified to teach this class. The lectures are interesting and as long as you pay attention, the tests should not be too bad. And while 4 papers may seem bad, it isn't, they're worth a small part of the grade.

Any two-hour lecture is a slog, but Hammil is the guy to do it with. The tests are some of the easiest I've had in college and the "papers" are no more than 3 pages double-spaced. He almost always lets you out early and peppers his lectures with interesting stories. He'll tell you what's on the test in lecture, so show up. Not a hard class at all.

Professor Hamill made me love my major even more. He is not very organized, but he always brings real life examples that helps people understand concepts better, especially some of the boring topics. He is funny, he loves teaching, and he has so much experience worth listening to.

Everyone should take this class. Hamill is passionate and one of the smartest people I've ever met. There are short weekly papers and two independent studies (police ride-along or visit to court) you'll want to do anyway. Lecture is a must since tests are just based on what he says. You'll never open the textbook, don't bother getting it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took the 2 1/2 hour class once a week and it was fine. He is so funny and tells awesome stories. I never felt bored or lost. He uses experience to teach and it's great. Lots of papers but only a few pages so not bad. Tests were easy and fair. He is a cop and a lawyer so he is really smart and knows what he is talking about.

He is the best teacher you will ever have. I took his 2.5 hour lecture (once a week) and it was by far my favorite class. He tells you a bunch of stories and makes the material interesting. The exams are very straightforward & based on what he goes over in class. There aren't that many assignments, plus independent studies were very fun! Take him!!

Hamil was one of the most unique professors I've taken. He doesn't have lecture slides. Instead, he talks unscripted about the class concepts and supplements them with stories from his police work. The lectures are long but interesting and you can tell from his speaking that he loves what he does. Pretty chill and easy class.

I loved Professor Hamill's class! Lectures are long but he makes them very entertaining through his stories. You gotta write a couple of papers but they are fun to do. There are three exams but make sure to listen to his lectures, take good notes, and read the end summary of the chapters. Overall, the class was worth taking!

Prof. Hamill really just talks for most of lecture, but his stories are really interesting and are good applications of the material we discuss. He makes it pretty clear what will be on exams and there's no trick questions. There's a textbook, and he references it sometimes, but I don't think its NECESSARY to read it. Overall, I've loved his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I've had at UMD. He really cares about his students and is absolutely willing to work with you should any issue arise. While attendance is not mandatory, he doesn't post notes online, so going to class is pretty crucial to passing the class. He makes it interesting and is a very caring and approachable professor.

He is a cop and has a lot of great stories which make lectures fun. The 2.5 hours of class were never unbearable. All of the info on the exams come from the lectures, so it is important to show up. I was sick the week before the second exam and thought that I'd be fine studying the textbook - learn from my mistake.

Prof. Hamill is absolutely great. The below comments represent him accurately, his lectures are always interesting since their current events. Just 3 major papers & 3 major tests. All fairly easy just take notes since he doesn't use powerpoints. Also actually read his packets that he hands out, they're always on the exams and help with the papers.
The class is interesting because he provides real life examples. He doesn't post lectures online, so you can't pass if you don't show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor.  His experiences and stories make class very fun and interesting (even a 2.5 hour class)! He makes it noticeably clear what is very important and what you should know and review for the exams.  A few papers but they are fun because you can write about police ride alongs you went on.  The best professor Ive had in college so far!

Hamill is an engaging lecturer and he uses his police background to give real life examples. I only had him once a week so class was long, but he started a lot of class discussions which helped to break up the monotony. He doesn't put the class on Elms so keep the syllabus handy. Definitely don't skip class, and don't forget the due dates!

Professor Hamill's one of my favorite professors here at UMD. Although i only had him once a week for a few hours, he made the class engaging with his real life cop stories and how they pertain the criminal law. And honestly if you show up, listen, and take good notes then you really don't even need the book. Barely used mine tbh
Long class but this professor makes it easier by keeping you entertained. Requires a normal amount of work and effort. Attendance not mandatory by the professor but required if you want to pass.
amazing professor ! by far my favorite. even though its a long class, he makes it really interesting so time goes by fast.

No way is Hamill overrated, he's been one of the best professors I've had at UMD. You have to do weekly case briefs and read the textbook to keep up, attending lecture isn't mandatory but is a must if you want to do well. Skipping the once-a-week class is like skipping a whole weeks worth of classes, don't do it and expect to get an easy A.
Overrated? No way!! If you actually ATTEND the class and do the work, you can't get less then an A.

I wish I had actually listened to the review on ourumd that said he's over-rated, because he is. He is VERY funny and has great stories, but he doesn't teach. The class lacks organization and you WILL have to thoroughly read the textbook to do well on his exams, which are worded poorly. This is coming from someone with a 4.0 minus this class!
LOVE HIM

He is the best Professor at UMD.  If you are going to take CCJS 230 take with Hamill.  Easy A.  Case study are easy.  test are so easy, he will let you use notes on test. his test take no more than 45 min.  Even though the class is 3hrs but it doesnt seem like 3hrs. time goes so fast.  take him and you will get an A in his class.

AWESOME!!! first test was OPEN NOTE! 2 test was on election day so it was TAKE HOME! his class is really interesting and he teaches it well. the Case Studys are easy as well :) the cases are interesting as well. He's funny and it doesnt even seem that long with him teaching PLUS he lets you out early and have a break for snacks. HIGHLY RECOMMEND
Encouraging, interesting, fair, flexible, engaging, approachable.  Case reports and exams are the grades. Go to class even though it's not mandatory.

hamill is the man.  he's the coolest guy, has a lot of experience and he's really funny.  the class is pretty long but he usually gives a 15 minute break to go get some food and let's out a little early.  he's an awesome professor and i recommend this class to anyone :)

He is AMAZING.  He's hilarious, and he's smart.  The perfect Professor.  The coolest Professor and Captain you'll ever meet.  Don't BS his class.  His lectures are fun.  Do the assignments, go to lectures, and you'll do just fine.
Great Professor.  Is a Captain for Montgomery County Police.  If you have an interest in the topic, you will love the class!
He's a great teacher! The exams are ok, and the he's very clear on what he expects on his assignments. He's definitely NOT one to pass up, esp. if you're interested in Criminal Justice or policing.

Hamill uses real life examples rather than book examples. He keeps class entertaining by using students for examples. Very funny and creates a discussion. One class we spent 2 hours debating the death penalty. Fun, easy,and fun again. Briefs are easy, exams are easy, all you need to do is study your notes and you'll be fine. Easy A

AMAZING!! V. qualified (cop for almost 30 yrs and practicing attorney), and if you learn well through examples, def. take his class b/c it's full of entertaining and RELEVANT examples. If you go to class and don't slack off, he's the first to admit you'll get an A. Case briefs due every week, you can miss 2, easy way to get 50/350 points!

CPT Hamill is an awesome teacher!  He is well qualified to teach this class as a Mont. County Police Officer and a Lawyer.  He makes class fun and makes the material understandable for everyone.  I highly reccomend his class!
Great prof. If you have questions, he responds quickly. Don't really need to read the readings, but they're fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely take his class because he is one of my favorite professors at UMD! He is super hilarious and loves to talk about mythology, which made me love mythology and made going to class a lot easier because I almost looked forward to it. The class is an easy A as long as you read the passages which he doesn't overload you with and go to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Amazing. Entertaining, keeps you engaged. Goes on tangents, but in a good way. You will not regret taking this class. Each week, you have a 5 question quiz and an essay; for the essay, you'll get a 100% if you write something. For the quizzes, you can get 5/5 by reading sparknotes. I still recommend reading the book, at least for the essays.

Professor Moore was absolutely hilarious and gave incredible lectures. While sometimes we would go off on a random tangent, he always had fun with the class and got through all of the material he wanted to. He made my first semester freshman year fun. Even if you're not interested in mythology at all, take this class! You wont regret it!
It's a good class, a lot of reading but if you do it you'll be fine. He goes off topic a lot and it's really fun I wish he taught more classes.

Fantastic professor. Hilarious and makes the class interesting. As long as you do your reading and attend class, you'll do fine. Lets you turn work in late and doesn't care as long as it's in before the end of the semester.

Charming, funny. Straightforward grader. Tends to go on tangents and makes unbearable sports references, but he was lovely and he was my favorite professor this semester. Reading and attending lecture is mandatory to getting an A in his class. Generally responds to email in a timely fashion. Exams are based on the assignments given in class.

Prof. Moore is an awesome professor! Makes the class very interesting with his sense of humor and overall teaching style. Easy class to take, just as long as you do the reading! Very approachable and is willing to accommodate for students. Definitely take this class!

One of the greatest professors I've had! Makes mythology fun and entertaining. Tests are straight forward - he tells you exactly what to study beforehand! Quizzes are sometimes a little difficult, but if you read, you'll be set. Really enjoyed his class!
Ryan is an awesome teacher! He makes class really entertaining and is works really hard to accommodate students and their needs. His tests are straightforward and easy. His class was awesome

He is a very entertaining teacher who makes the class fun and interesting. He makes the material as clear and as concise as he possibly can and is very helpful with any questions you might have. He does give somewhat of hard quizzes, because even if you read, he focuses on small details. His class is easy if you keep up with the readings and study.
No Comments

the class was fun Moore makes myths come alive, he has a wonderful sense of humor, and is very engaging to the class, although his quizzes were nitpicky and very detail oriented he was a very fun teacher all around and did not have unreasonable expectations, he might assign a new textbook however because he was constanttly complaining about the H&

Professor Moore is one of the best teachers I have ever had. His sense of humor is unbelievable and he always finds a way to make his class interesting. I loved attending his class, and his tests weren't hard at all. He gave quite a bit of quizzes and essays but they were all graded easily and fairly, and they were very brief. Moore is amazing.

This is how you run a class. Ryan Decker is superb. A young professor who is clearly teaching as a side gig yet you wouldn't know it by the passion he shows. He knows what he is talking about, has a great dry sense of humor, and is always willing to answer questions. Project heavy class with NO EXAMS and easy pop quizzes as others have said.

take economics of entrepreneurship!! this class was hard, but extremely interesting and very relatable to real world economics. is class was the best class i've taken at maryland. just dont skip class cause he does quizzes every class but you can literally write anything and you will pass the quiz. hes a hard grader but he curves. TAKE RYAN DECKER!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Ryan Decker is an awesome professor, I would take him for economics of entrepreneurship if you can. He brings an enthusiastic and energetic vibe to class. The class is mainly research based , and is one of the more interesting classes I've taken at UMD. One thing, Decker is a tough grader , he expects good work. He does curve when necessary.

Curtis is extremely unorganized. During the semester that I had him, he messed up our grades on several different occasions. He is known for being the hardest psych professor because he does not teach the class anything, his study guides are not helpful at all. If you can register for any other psych professor.

Ryan curtis is the most condescending person I have ever met. He always has a poor attitude in lectures, makes concepts harder than needed, and horrible about meeting with people and his TA sucks as well. Do not take this class. It will ruin psych for you.
THE WOAT. loves to make simple concepts into super confusing test questions

Dr. Curtis is a great professor. He really makes stats easy for people who don't understand math at all. Also going to his office hours frequently REALLY helped boost my grade. He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities and is fair/rational when homework/tests are harder than expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is god awful. He literally put everyones extra credit scores in out of 15 instead of zero so people got scores of 3/15, 4/15, 5/15 on EXTRA CREDIT which is supposed to boost your grade. This error brought me down a letter grade and negatively affected my GPA. Not to mention class was awful too and tests were disproportionately hard.
do not take psych stats with dr. curtis. he's nice but the class is wayyy harder than dr. stratford's. my lab TA really saved my grade in this class.

exams were on concepts we didn't learn in class. exam 1 was easy but exam 2 was awful (aka he's inconsistent with writing exams, made it hard to study). homework schedule didn't match the syllabus. wasn't available outside of class and didn't reply to emails. do not take him for stats, i'm good at math and this was rough

Can't stand Dr. Curtis. Complicates examples in lecture, making homework extremely difficult to complete. Gets irritated when students don't answer his questions correctly. No feedback on homework, so you can't even tell what the right answer is or why you messed up. Messy organization of assignments. Lab and TA are an absolute mess. DO NOT TAKE!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Curtis really cares about his students Lectures are boring and sometimes confusing Lots of examples in lecture BUT the online homework is harder than most of what we do in class The lab is awful the TA was bad at explaining R Studio and anything related to stats He would give us equations that we didn't even learn and basically teach us his way

Ryan Curtis seems like an intelligent man, however, he is very condescending to his students and gets mad when they do not understand things that he has yet to teach. The entire class is just watching him do example after example, and it is taxing and upsetting to sit through a lecture.

Dr Curtis was an amazing professor, his lectures were engaging and were peppered with activities and videos, and his general vibe was very easygoing and casual. although the exams are multiple choice, don't underestimate them because they can get really tricky and are a chunk of your grade. attendance isnt mandatory but you won't want to miss class

100 was blended learning. The Lecture wasa good measure for the class content. It sticks with me. 334 were regular Lectures. Don't miss information in lectures which I found there to be more of on tests, or attendance grade. He genuinely cared about the classes/us. Applied myself in both classes, but also enjoy psychology. Lots upset he goes.

Dr. Curtis was the best professor I had this semester. He teaches Social Psych in such a fun and interesting way. I would definitely take him again if he wasn't going to Colorado! He offers a ton of extra credit at the end of the semester, which boosted my grade a TON. Take Curtis 100%.

Professor Curtis is very good at his job. His syllabus is very clear and concise, however, he does not respond back to any emails. His TA's are harsh graders when it comes to grading. They make unreasonable errors that cause you to go directly to Dr. Curtis' office hours in order for a regrade. A lot of unnecessary busy work
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: There is literally no professor like Dr. Curtis. On the first day of class when he told us this would be his last semester at UMD, I wanted to legitimately break down crying. No professor has lectures like his. He finds ways to make them interactive and fun and I genuinely look forward to class every day. He also cares so much which helps a lot.

I took PSYC334 over the summer when I was going through a huge thing relationship wise and I can honestly say Dr. Curtis's lectures were so helpful. I actually learned about how to deal with what I was going through and in a way he acted like a therapist. Definitely the most interesting class I've taken at college and for sure the best professor.
My favorite professor at Maryland. Highly recommend any of his classes, they have all been enjoyable, interesting, and manageable. Overall, a great teacher and person.

Dr. Curtis is probably the best professor I've had at UMD so far (entering my sophomore year). He's very helpful, knowledgeable, intellectual, and knows how to make his lecture fun and entertaining. PSYC100 is a pain in the butt, not hard, but just a lot of busy work (six 1-page papers, 3 exams, and weekly homework worksheets). He's great though.

Dr. Curtis is by far one of the best profs I've had. He's very particular about things and the points may seem scary but the work is really manageable and if you have an amazing TA then you're good to go. He keeps lectures interesting and gave so much extra credit. I never met him but he seems really cool and funny
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He makes class so interesting and so much fun! He gives us a LOT of online textbook reading, but he's super clear about what we need to do well and honestly, if you actually listen to him and put in the effort, you should do fine.
I had Curtis my freshman year. He lost half of two of my exams..... and then gave me zeros. Not very willing to help students. PSYCH is a pretty cool subject though, you wont be bored

The TA's grade papers. The worksheets are graded by ELMS. Exams are graded by the scranton machine. The course is a lot of work. Professor Curtis's lectures are not very clear because he talks fast and moves on quickly. Grade drops quickly, but doesn't go up quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE IF IT IS NOT REQUIRED FOR YOUR MAJOR. This class was not required for my major and i am taking it and will prob end up with C/C-. Literally one of the hardest tests I've ever taken. Please do your self a favor and do not take this course if not necessary!!!!

Thus far, this has been my favorite class at UMD. The structure of this class helps you to learn. His lectures are long but he makes the entire time interesting. You can meet with him and he's very understanding. The exams are fair, the quizzes are fair (as long as you read), but the essays require the most time and effort-TA's can grade harsh.

Absolutely loved his class, it was actually the highlight of my week. He made the subject super interesting (even for a non-Psych major like me) and even though the class was over 1 hour long it didn't feel like it. Writing assignments are graded somewhat strictly however (but he doesn't grade them, the TAs do)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: okay this class is extremely difficult and if you are not putting in hours and hours of work you won't pass. ALL of the TAs are tough graders for the scientific analysis papers but if you have David Ampofo I would drop. The tests are extremely hard and there is a research requirement. prof promised 100pts extra credit opportunity, we only got 70pt.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Too much expectation for 100 level class. Do not take if youre not a psych major or its not a requirement. Also, if you want to wait 10 full days for a grade this is a great course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This is the most interesting class I've ever took. Its work but fairly easy and enjoyable. 10/10 recommend

He is what makes the +1hr class worth it. The class itself is a lot of reading and work, but such an enjoyable class. He knows what he's talking about and gives a pretty clear grading criteria. He does clicker questions each class. You will definitely need to study, everything comes from a free online textbook and he doesn't post powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Even though this is a class I somewhat struggled with, I still believe Curtis is a fantastic person and a great teacher. He really loves and is invested in interpersonal relationships and he makes the topic very interesting to learn more about. If you study a good amount and take notes during lectures, you will absolutely succeed in this class.

I read the entire textbook cover to cover but I LOVED IT. The content is so interesting and useful for everyday life, you'll never be bored in this class. Amazing lecturer. A lot of work and papers including a group essay though. You will have to work for an A. Clicker questions every class. Brings in his family on the last day of class. LOVE HIM
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Curtis is a great professor and I really enjoyed taking my class. He is a solid choice/class to take. Just beware he is a very slow grader and you won't have your exam/paper grades back for a long time. Also, he never responded to any of my emails the entire semester. So either make sure you don't need to email him or you find another way.

I feel like Dr. Curtis has the potential to be a good teacher, but the way the class is structured and his expectations of his students make it unnecessarily difficult. The amount of work needed to get a good grade is too much for what is supposed to be an intro class. If you really like Psyc, I'd say go for it. Otherwise, I wouldn't recommend it.

Dr. Curtis is an awesome professor, but the class itself is very rigorous. 3 Exams, weekly worksheet quizzes and Blended Learning assignments. If your TA grades your BL harshly, email the assignment ahead of time for feedback(makes a big difference in grades). Dr. Curtis is very approachable during office hours and gives a crapload of extra credit.

Great professor! TAKE HIS CLASS, you won't regret it. The final is only partly cumulative but he gives you a good idea on what it will be on. Reading is essential but the book is so interesting! He is a natural teach and really gets concepts across. One of my favorite professors.

AWESOME PROF! I wish I could just take his classes every semester.  If you have the chance, take a class with Curtis, you won't regret it.  His grading is pretty clear and there is a good amount of writing involved.  The exams are pretty straight forward.  PAY ATTENTION WHEN HE TELLS YOU WHAT IS GOING TO BE ON THE EXAM or says "this is important!!"

Overall really liked this class. Curtis is an amazing teacher. He explains everything really well, the only problems you'll run into are with your TA. Just work really hard on the blended learning assignments and if you study for his tests they're pretty easy. I look forward to going to his class. Recommend it if you like psyc.

Excellent professor and cares about his students. Class was tough and the group paper is long but he will help you with anything you need as long as you make the time to go speak with him. Weekly busywork assignments help your grade as well as a very modest participation activity.

He's absolutely incredible. I love going to lectures because he gives great examples and makes it easier to understand. Extra credit: sing Tina Turner's "What's Love Got To Do With It?" He's funny and makes the early class so worth waking up for. You could technically pass without going to lectures, but you miss clicker points. Plus he's super fun!

Nice enough teacher, class expectations are clear.  There was tons of material covered, and the format of the exams only covered around 10% of what we were required to learn.  Also, Dr Curtis never replied to any of my emails during the ffirst five weeks of a six week class. I had to contact the department to have them hunt him down for me.

Ryan is enthusiastic and knows his stuff.  His class is really interesting and it teaches you a lot of cool stuff.  I find myself thinking about the stuff I learned in Psych often in daily life.  The class isn't an "easy-A" but if you do the homework and show up to lectures it isn't too hard to pull a good grade.

He is nice and class is very interesting. I like psychology very much. Class is interesting but you really need to do a lot of work to get good grades. Clickers for participation. Prepare to make great effort and memorize .

By far, one of the WORST teachers to ever walk the face of this earth. He expects us to teach ourselves the material and successfully pass these online worksheets. 2 days later we meet in lecture to discuss the topic of those worksheets. His teacher's assistants are just as awful, and grade incredibly hard. Though, he gives extra credit.
Dr Curtis really made lectures interesting and relatable. I genuinely wanted to go to class

Professor Curtis is very engaging and kind. He's patient with explanations and really likes to get students' thoughts on the topics being covered. Tests are easy if you come to class and pay attention. Definitely would recommend.
He was really chill and easy to talk to when we had questions. Undoubtedly made class interesting.

This class has a lot of work: weekly worksheets, 3 exams, writing assignments every other week, pre and post test quizzes. There is no textbook to buy, but there is an online one that the department made itself, most of the important information is linked to external sites. Generally though, I look forward to this class Curtis makes it entertaining
He's a great professor! Very interesting material and he explains it well. Some of the test questions are tricky, and you have to write two papers, but all-in-all very fair and interesting.

A LOT OF WORK for a intro class!  He is a good lecture BUT he grades really hard and doesn't curve grades.  Their are every other week BL assignments that are graded harshly. Worksheets due every week. Test are really hard.So if you are looking for a intro class to PSCY this class is miss leading. Ok professor but the class is HARD!

A LOT OF WORK!  He is a good lecture BUT he grades really hard and doesn't curve grades.  Their are every other week BL assignments that are graded harshly. His class is like a weed out class(trying to get the people out who should not be a PSCY major) So if you are looking for a intro class to PSCY this class is miss leading and test a HARD.

I love this professor. You have to study hard in this class, but he is one of the best professors I have ever had! He is very clear, helpful, and approachable. If you ever have the chance, take a class with Dr. Curtis!!

As long as you read the book you should be totally fine. His lectures are pretty interesting. There is a TON of work for this class. There are online quizzes for each chapter that have to be done before class, wiki project, pre & post test papers, and goals reports. There is extra credit to cushion your grade.
His exam reviews are very comprehensive, he is always warm and open to questions. All-in-all a wonderful teacher! I would recommend this class to anyone interested in the subject.

You need to PAY ATTENTION and ASK QUESTIONS. Dr. Tahamont is really not bad, I don't know why she has received so much hate. I know that some of us are not math people, but it is required for CCJS majors. I think that the bad reviews come from people who didn't want to put in the work just because this is a 200 level course.

Dr. Tahamont is really not bad, and I think she is one of the most misunderstood professors at UMD. She wants her students to succeed in class, but she doesn't know how to make it clear. She is trying to make the class bearable; she values student feedback. She is easily accessible outside of class for help, and she is great at answering questions.

She isn't even a bad teacher. I have no idea why so many people gave her bad reviews the subject is hard but that isn't her fault. She post all her slides and records all her lectures and uploads them after class. You can use notes on all exams as long as its on paper and she will give you credit for a wrong answer as long as you show understanding

Dr. Tahamont is not as bad as her ratings suggest. The material is difficult and she moves quickly, but neither of those things are her fault. She does want her students to succeed, she just does not know how to make that clear. Attendance is mandatory for your participation points, but they're fairly easy since it's mainly group work.
The worst professor I have ever had! Do not take this class
Hard class for not the best Proffesor

As a current TA myself, the TA's and the professor were not on the same page. I would put three times the amount of study time into this course, still be able to use notes on the exam, and BARELY get the B. She definitely knows the material, she simply does not know how to present it at a 200-level. I would suggest taking this course Dr. Lehman.

She has been one of my toughest professors to date. She doesn't clarify the content well. I recommend taking this course online over the summer with Lehman if you can. She nor the TAs are ever on the same page and the TAs were trying to do the best they could with helping us in discussions. By the 2nd exam, 1/4 of the class dropped out.

I am sure Professor Tahamont is an amazing person outside of the classroom but, she is not a good professor at all. She moves through content way too fast without allowing anyone to digest the material and she tends to not give solid feedback or answers for incorrect answers or questions. She can also get pretty snippy with students so, beware!

@ the beginning Tahamont said she didn't know math, that she wasn't good at it and laughed when she said it. I thought it was an inspirational thing--it WAS NOT. She's probably a great statistician, but a horrendous professor who had PPT's with mathematical errors EVERY WEEK and limited our correct learning of material. Never gave back prob sets.
She is incompetent and doesn't deserve to teach at a university like UMD.
sucks

The problem sets and the tests have a lot of concept questions, but she never defines any of them in the slides (even the guy who subbed her complained about it). what's left is full of equation and calculation errors. Final paper has 4 pages of requirements with > 20 bullet points, and if you follow all of them, expect only a 90 (her own words) !

Whenever given the choice to take this class with another professor, do it! She didn't take the time to explain or make sure the class understood the material, instead acted like everything was common sense. She blamed the students for our grades even though everyone struggled. She even told us that there was no way for us to pass the final paper!!

Professor Tahamont is knowledgable about the subject but does not always know how to teach it. The concepts are confusing and she moves fast in lecture. One of the most frustrating things was we were expected to use excel for multiple big assignments but were never taught how to use excel. On tests the wording often seemed made to be confusing.

Professor Tahamont is a very knowledgeable professor, however, her teaching style is not the best. Expect to teach yourself everything from YouTube videos and by asking other people because she is incredibly hard to follow. Her exams are worded in a way to make it difficult to understand compared to the practice problems she gives.

The homework is vaguely related to what she teaches in class. The homework requires the use of excel which she has refused to teach. Her exams are graded very subjectively, which for a math class makes no sense.
Terrible. Does not teach how to do the homework and the tests are worded for you to fail. Hardest class I have ever taken and I have never had trouble with math courses before.

She does use recordings which is helpful.  However, the homework is vaguely related to what she teaches in class.  The homework requires use of excel which she has refused to teach.  Her exams are designed in a way where she expects "a large distribution of scores".  She does not expect us to do very well on any exam which is  so frustrating.

Professor Tahamont is very passionate about what she teaches but I question her teaching style. First, she moves too fast so it can be hard to keep up. Next, the power points and prep assessments have many technical errors which is confusing for someone trying to learn statistics.

The one review that said her classes are mandatory and then gave a 1 star is very misleading. Her classes were a joy to come to each week. She gave students various ways to her extra credit on the exam, one being throwing paper balls into a trashcan. Her tests were specific to the content she gave during lecture, but were also fair.

Dr. Tahamont's exams are some of the hardest in the department BUT she gives a ton of participation and extra credit. Go to her office hours, she's really easy to talk to and will help you study correctly! The class is super interesting, she keeps you engaged and there's no textbook. One of the coolest profs around, 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: I took Tahamont fall 2017 and let me just tell you--worst mistake I ever. Basically to break it down for you, if you are someone who only shows up for exams, good luck! Her classes are basically mandatory because we have a "group activity" every class for points. Her exams are a NIGHTMARE. Pray that she changes her methods if you need to take this
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Easiest 5 stars I've ever given. She really cares about her students and makes COMM101 fun. Clear expectations, fair grading, and engaging lectures. Highly recommend!

She was a nice lady, pretty good. Graded very strictly for a freshman gen ed communications class, which I found to be unnecessary. For example, she submitted the wrong template for us to fill out an outline with, then gave everyone a very low grade. She was very unwilling to give any leeway and only gave back a couple of points.

Prof. Sheikh starts off somewhat boring but once she gets to know the class becomes a great teacher. She is funny and really engages with all of the students. Her grading criteria is sometimes unclear but is usually very reasonable. I would recommend her class for COMM107, just participate and do all of the assignments.

Professor Sheikh is great, her lectures are very clear and concise and she grades well. Gives great feedback and really tries to help you succeed. She's a very chill professor and I never dread going to class, we did have some textbook quizzes but were easy, participation was graded as well. Overall not hard and a great person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Respected

reviews.comment: She was good. Class is easy, have to participate
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She is very unclear with her grading. I also dont think she genuinely liked teaching and seeing her students succeed as she made it very difficult to get good grades at times. Confusing and can be rude but it is not a hard class to do well in if you participate and show effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't recommend taking this class with this professor. She makes this class very boring and seems very unenthusiastic in lectures. Also, she does not clearly explain the grading criteria well, and this cost me a lot of points. I recommend taking this class with a different teacher.

Professor Sheikh is a very nice person, but she was really unenthusiastic and boring in class. It's an easy A as long as you follow the criteria for the speeches, and she grades pretty easy even if she writes a lot of comments on your presentations. Overall it was nothing special at all, but I guess communications isnt meant to be fun anyways

Show up to class, participate in the breakout rooms (covid, zoom university) and you will get an easy A. She gave super good feedback, yet graded very high even if it looked like your grade should've been worse based off her comments. She was super flexible considering online classes, DEFINITELY take her class.

Sabeen is a pretty good comm professor; very easy in grading. Participation is graded, but that is the case for all comm classes. She also gives good feedback and lessons to us, but sounded kind of bored in class. However, it's an easy A, so take her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: The professor didn't answer questions at all. The grading criteria was not clear. There was not opportunity to make up test or essays. The professor would not consider the effort put in the work if it didn't meet one of the requirements he would grade 0, and also graded late. Students need to know what was wrong to not repeat the same mistakes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Had two quizzes, a discussion post based on the readings every week with the readings being 12-25 pages long and was so tiring and exhausting to do. Two papers. Two Exams. This class took up the most of my time from my other STEM courses. If you aren't too knowledgeable or passionate about the environment this might not be the class for you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Good professor. Lectures were interesting but a lot of important content is not visually displayed on powerpoints so be prepared to carefully listen. Made content understandable for people who have no prior knowledge of philosophy. Super knowledgeable on the material.
Very interesting class, and lots of opportunities to ask questions to help understand the material. Consistently do the weekly readings and discussions and you should have no problem earning an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Scull is an engaging lecturer whose passion shines through.  I now see virology in a completely new lens.  I strongly recommend taking this professor.  Beware that there aren't a lot of assignments, so all points count!  Don't miss out on the extra credit assignment!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Scull is a nice & kind professor, really responsive to emails & questions. Records lectures so attendance isn't necessary. Gives many quizzes throughout the semester instead of exams or a final, but pay attention to wording and small nuances which are tricky. 4 projects (2 papers & 2 posters), grading rubric is unclear and last one graded HARSHLY
So kinda and always accessible either after class or during office hours.

Dr. Scull is not a great lecturer and just uses powerpoint slides to lecture. The class was out of 250 points and she gave us 10 points of extra credit to write 2 paper: one on a virology seminar and another on a recent virology paper. Tests (all short answer) were 95% of the final grade and were not too hard but she words questions weirdly.
Nice guy but harsh grader, feedback doesn't always make sense, SO much reading
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: While Dr. Trudell is very caring and considerate about personal issues, he is a TOUGH grader. I dont think I received a single 100% on any assignment all semester, not even on a self introduction. Because of this, it is impossible to receive an A (4.0) in his class. The material was interesting, but his morals as a professor arent the best.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If I was told I had a terminal illness and only had a limited amount of life left on this earth, I would choose to sit in on classes with Trudell because he somehow made it feel as if time was frozen. His lectures were the dullest things I've ever experienced and his pedagogical approach was a nightmare & 0/10, least favorite class I've ever taken

Professor Trudell is an enlightening professor that never ceases to amaze me. His extensive knowledge on Renaissance literature and song is quite refreshing. Don't be surprised if you hear him play Renaissance ecclesiastical music at the beginning of class. A great professor who values discussion and input, and is very organized and fair.

Professor Trudell is a great professor. His knowledge of poetry is amazing. He conducts discussions instead of lectures-- allowing students to form their own opinions. Overall, he is neither a harsh grader nor an easy grader. If you work hard in his class and close-read the material, you will get an A.
Grades way too harshly

Professor Scham is my favorite professor I have ever had. He truly cares about teaching students and wants to share the knowledge he has with his students. I found his lectures to be highly interesting which generated a lot of questions that he was effectively able to answer.

He's a tough professor, but he's knowledgable and he is equitable if you talk to him about anything you're struggling with. I think it's important to talk to the professor whether it's asking questions or sharing thoughts if you want to have a solid experience in this class. Overall, he's solid and I would take a class with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a great man and a Great professor. He has accomplished so much in his life. listening to his lectures and seeing his works are truly inspiring. The class itself requires you to dig deep into the literature to truly understand it you have to work hard to get a good grade but it is achievable.

One of the hardest professors to understand. I honestly had anxiety every time and not knowing there would be unannounced quiz almost every two weeks. But the good think is that the quizzes are weighted equivalently to homework grades as you've received them in high school. Cannot speak clearly enough and people would have to learn on their own.

reviews.comment: I took this class for a gen ed credit and it was totally not worth it. I was exhausted and ready to fall apart every night doing the 100+ pages of readings for the week. Interesting topic, but he's hard to understand and there are better classes to learn about this stuff.

reviews.comment: Going to lecture is required, the professor clearly knows a lot about the issue and many opportunities are available outside of class for learning about the subjects. reviews.comment: He is a very nice man and I respect him, lectures can be pretty boring though. The pop quizzes are annoying and there is a ton of reading, but if you work you should succeed!

reviews.comment: Professor Scham is an incredibly learned and experienced man. He is clearly very knowledgable and passionate about  his subject and I admire that. However, his lecture slides never match up with what he is saying which makes note taking difficult. Also, he had a stroke which made lecture difficult to understand.  Overall the class was worthwhile.

This class taught by Paul Scham is one of the best classes I have ever taken. I learned so much about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Professor Scham managed to teach this incredibly controversial issue truthfully and impartially. He expects a LOT of his students, but believe me it's worth it. He is incredibly knowledgable about the topic.

Prof. Trotman talks to her students like we are fifth graders, the entire class lasts 2 hours with content that could be fit within 30 minutes. Quiz questions are created to trap you, and she makes them due on Saturday nights. These quizzes also make up a big part of your grade and she has no tolerance for late submissions. I did enjoy this class.

Her class was very interactive and each session will taught me different ways to enhance communication. She gave very nice personal feedback for a

reviews.comment: Professor Trotman challenged me and held me to a high standard. I have been interviewing with several companies and some of them included presentations and networking events. reviews.comment: No. He ignore students' question and always unkind.

Professor Das is a poor lecturer. He gets angry at students when they ask questions and will aggressively shout at them and say that the answer is trivial. Additionally, it is challenging to follow what he writes on the boards as his handwriting can be misleading (i.e. his M and mu look identical) and he switches boards often leaving me confused.

Some people may not like Prof Das because his lectures can be intense and largely theory heavy. However, there is no doubt that he wants his students to be successful in his course. If you go to lectures and do the hws and labs, you will be fine. His tests are incredibly fair given the material he covers and examples he goes over in class.
This class was a waste of time

The professor spends the majority of the class telling her personal stories. We have to remind her when the exams are, or she has to ask the TAs about basic course logistics. 70% of the class had to go talk to her about exam grades because random points were taken off for the sake of proving that organizational behavior is complex.

She's incredibly unorganized and relies heavily on TAs. She seems to make the class as she goes. The class is 25% things you need to know, 25% gibberish and 50% her personal life stories which are most often so random and completely unrelated. This class is honestly a pain.

reviews.comment: Dr. Silio was a great teacher.

Don't do it. Basically to pass his class you have to study his past exams on the IEEE testbank. Recently it has been down, so I don't see how it is possible to pass his class. The book is basically useless, and his lectures will make your eyes heavy. Always talks about old, outdated technology.

ENEE244 is an extremely important course, so if you want to LEARN, please do not take him. I do not recommend Prof Silio for any freshman or sophomore for this course. But if he's your last choice, then get handouts from previous students just to do well in the class and READ THE MATERIALS TEXTBOOK FOR UNDERSTANDING!

You arrive to this class prepared with your laptop ready to go. No - not to take notes, but as an escape from the drone you notice emanating from the front of the classroom. The drone's source is Professor C. Silio. He is explaining the obsolete intricacies of the UNIVAC1100: A machine that is nearly a half century old. This class is useless.

Unfortunately the comments in regards to speaking out in class are fairly accurate. He will mock incorrect answers, and he does spend a lot of time talking about irrelevant examples (you'll hear lots about Motorola) and his grad students. Exams are difficult, but not impossible. He is very good in office hours if you can keep him on track.

In order to do well in his class you must keep up with the homeworks, and thoroughly practice his practice exams. If you go to his office hours a few  days before an exam he pretty much tells you what types of problems to focus on, and it's legit. Get hold of previous practice exams and study them because his in class exams are very similar.

Silio completely ruined the course. He enjoys mocking his students when they ask questions, as if he were some sort of deity that could never be "unclear" when he's teaching. DO NOT take this class w/him, or you will completely regret it. If you want to try your luck with him.... you'll graduate a semester late. Smart, but not fit to be a teacher.

He is a horrible teacher.  The guys knows a lot, but he isn't a good communicator.  Of our 1.5 hour class, he devotes half an hour for stories about his Phd students. But, I learned a lot in his class DESPITE him.  His exams are hard (average around low 50%), but if you do well on the final, he replaces your lowest exam with the final grade.
He is hard,  but if you practice his old exams (!) you could do good. There is not easy way, you have to practice a lot to do good on his exams. Go to his office hours, he will debug your programs.
Makes exams too tricky and promotes "cheating"
DON'T TAKE HIM
Awful.

Very bad teaching. Unforgiving grading. Criticizes textbook, but forces us to use it plus a lot of his criticisms could be applied to his own teaching. Lastly, a few students have asked somewhat dumb questions and Silio retorts with evident frustration (rather unprofessional of him). Avoid Silio.

this **** doesn't explain****. his lectures are ripped right off the damn book. he rips his students when they ask him questions. he shows absolutely no respect to his students. this isnt a joke. he seriously treats his students lyk crap in lecture if they ask a basic question. mother ****er is a nazi.
Very nice person. Emphasises a lot on hardwork. Exams are kind of tricky but avergae is low and he curves fairly. Old exams always help in his class.
He is a very good professor, and is very understanding.
