reviews.comment: Do not take Daniel Sidman. He is a very harsh grader and gives very little feedback. Any attempt to get help or reach out will be ignored for minimum of a week. Office hours are useless as he will not give you feedback, or give you very little feedback on what you did wrong. Attendance is not mandatory, but he will grade you worse if you don't go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall a great professor. For a gen-ed, I thought he took the grading a little too seriously but I did end up learning a lot in his class. My only big complaint was that we had to purchase a mandatory digital textbook ($75). He cites it in lectures and does ask you to read it pretty consistently, but I think it was a waste. Just get it on libgen.
I think I got ptsd from taking him. He gives no mercy on assignments and tough grader. He has no personality.

homework for every class & for every major assignment, there was a reflective paper which was pointless. Most of the assignments were just filler work and just to kill time. Take this class with a friend if you have this professor because without a friend it's a pain. It gets really tiring really quickly and I'm glad I'm done with the class.
Professor Sidman's your average professor I would say. He's really good, and you'll easily pass English with him as long as you show up.

PROS: Enthusiastic, making the mandatory attendance pleasant (some of us used this class as a study hall, and he seems to accept it). Took time to respond to most assignments with short but realistic comments. Fun questions during attendance sessions. No Exams! Some of the assignments could be repeated. Recorded lectures. 
CONS: No extra credit.

I am going to be honest, at first I had only taken Singer due to the time slot. I saw the reviews and I admit I was scared. However, he has been by far my favorite professor I have had at Maryland. We only had 25 people in our class, but we did well because Dr. Singer teaches well. Participation matters, but Singer works with you to do well. 10/10.

Dr. Singer seems like a chill dude, and you can tell that he's really passionate about physiology. However, he likes to go on tangents on stuff that won't end up being tested on.
Like another person said, Dr. Singer claims he curves the median to a B-, but in reality expect a miniscule curve, even if the averages are in the 60-70 range.

I told someone one time that I liked him as a person and their response was "this is the first time we ever heard anything positive about him." If that doesn't sum him up, idk what does. I liked him as a person (he's an acquired taste). But unfortunately, I'm not looking for a friend, I'm looking for a professor. He is anything but a good professor
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do you really want to understand physiology? Take Dr. Singer. He is organized and breaks down the material in terms a student can understand. A piece of advice: come to class prepared (mainly focus on understanding the figures in the textbook. You do not have to read the entire chapter before class). Participate in class. Definitely ask question

Dr. Singer seems like a nice guy but he's one of the worse professors I've ever had. I was really excited about this class because I love A&P, but with this prof it was a nightmare. He made everything way more difficult and confusing than it needed to be. Take another professor unless you're ready to have a trash semester.

clearly very intelligent but personality does not mix well with teaching. class is not hard -- there is nothing cutting edge about physiology concepts discovered 100 years ago, but Dr. Singer makes it hard for no reason. you could write the same thing as your neighbor and get halfcredit. take with another prof, even if you have to wait another sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Singer. What a professor LOL. He was something else. Has 5 exams in the class. Kept on saying I will curve the class so that a B- is the median of the course. If you do well on every exam but one (Well as in like getting the top score of the class when averages are in the 50) you won't get the grade you deserve. Sucks how profs dont understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hard grader, not an organized teacher as far as providing content, is not readily available for students. I did not find him to be very professional either.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: HE IS A HARSH GRADER. He barely gives out any partial credits. He has a very superficial personality. He will legit sass you when you try to go to his office hours to get partial credits. DO NOT TAKE HIM. TAKE WITH ANOTHER PROFESSOR
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Singer is an awesome guy. He knows his stuff and is very down to earth. His tests can be challenging but they aren't too tricky if you study hard. BSCI440 is a notoriously hard class so you should expect it going in. He is respectful and personal. I would recommend him.

Pretty good prof. One homework a week. Attendance not mandatory but I would recommend going to lecture helped a lot and he does video record them but the quality sucks. Quizzes are easy. Exams are harder and on more specific problems. Formula sheet for each exam.
super chill and the best physics instructor I have ever had

I didn't enjoy him as a lecturer, he was very boring and I could barely tell if he cared about teaching. The only thing good about this course is the curve. I bombed every single exam. The key to this class is getting good grades on homework and lab reports. Tophat is used heavy. I also pray you don't have Ninad as a TA!

Funny lecturer, definitely watches Rick & Morty in his free time. The class is very easy to pass. Every once in a while he'll make an exam too long or grade something in a really annoying way but if you bring it up to him, he will almost always be lenient in changing the grade for the class. He wants his students to pass and offers a decent curve.

I never actually met him, since this was just the lab section of Physics 260, but the labs were alright. Not too hard, but nitpicky with the grading. I liked that the final exam was online. Don't worry.
i knew more about physics before this class. with no hyperbole i would rather be kicked in the head by a campus horse than take this man as a prof again

Never saw him once. He communicated through a couple petty emails the entire semester which he seemed very irritated in. This guy should not be getting paid and its a shame on his integrity as a professor and person to be so negligent and rude to students.

You don't need to know physics at all in order to pass this lab, as every formula you will need is provided in the lab handout. Just make sure to show up and complete it. Be sure you're at least a little familiar in Excel. Taking him again next semester for phys271.
Straight forward and to the point. Had him twice, but dont really know who he is as the TAs run the labs. Show up, complete the lab, and youll most likely get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: It was Professor Seversons first time teaching PHYS131 (and it was all online) so I wont judge him too harshly. He bases the curve off how the class is doing, and imo he teaches better than Buehrle. Hes disorganized but hes lenient with hw and exams. The lab is chill and I didnt have too much of a problem with reports. Overall, not bad :)

Do not take PHYS102 with Severson, the course is so disorganized and the lectures are not only boring but will most likely make you more confused. His notes are so hard to follow and basically make no sense.
I love this man more than life itself
amazing phys270 professor. tests were fair and somewhat on the easy side, just doing his practice problems did wonders.

reviews.comment: Great professor! Gives you all the materials to do well (good lectures, solutions to recommended problems from textbook). Tests are fair and not rediculous

The lectures are helpful and you don't need to buy the textbook. As long as you pay attention in class and study a little bit for the midterms you'll get an A. He gave an extra credit problem worth 3 exam point

Professor Severson was a great teacher for this course. It's required for HESP students, but he made it easy, fun, and doable. He was encouraging, available for office hours, and really made the material simple for us. He ended up curving 1 exam and dropping 1 homework. All around a nice guy who just wants you to do well.

Dr. Severson is a great professor. He makes the material relatively easy to grasp and the homework he gives is very indicative of what will be on the quizzes and tests. He's really laid back and is very thorough with his examples.

Awesome professor! Super good at explaining complicated things like relativity and quantum mechanics in a way that makes sense to your average student. Tests and quizzes are more than fair. Really down to earth and approachable.
He is just such a great professor, take him and you won't be disappointed.

His weekly quiz during the discussion is very easy if you have an idea of what is taught during lecture as they are meant to be easy points. His tests are medium difficulty but he provides opportunities to earn extra credit for each exam. The hardest part might be the expert ta homework assignments but he drops the lowest hw and quiz grade.

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer and it was quite intensive- everyday lecture 1hr 20 min. Most of the stuff that Matt taught in lecture was not useful towards the examinations, and a lot of the time I found myself zone-ing out due to his monotonous voice. However Im giving him a four because his exams are fair and he grades easily.

I had him for 161 first and liked him so I decided to take him for 261. I never actually saw him in 261 because the TA taught class and graded everything. It was an easy A; the cutoffs were such that as long as you showed up to every lab, did the homework, and have a general idea of what you are doing you would earn an A! I never had to study.

reviews.comment: The lectures can be a bit boring, but overall he's a pretty easy teacher. The mastering physics component is the hardest part of the class. A bit of extra credit is available throughout the course.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is the best professor I have taken so far. I started the class with a failing grade, but he encouraged me to try and not to give up. I ended the class with an A. If you have taken AP Physics or go to lectures/discussions, do extra practices and go to office hours, then you should be fine. Overall, he's hilarious and I learned so much from him.
Matthew Severson was a great professor. He is like those good rookie athletes, unexperienced but good. His tests were very fair and nothing there seemed tricky. He cares about his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He's an easy professor if that's what you're looking for. Plenty of extra credit and he doesn't even put calculus on the exams. Lectures were pretty boring in my opinion. A very good class.  It was harder for me b/c I have never taken physics and a lot of other students took AP physics (curve was against me).  It is a great class.  You'll learn a lot. Do practice problems from the book and GSS problems. Get the solution manual.  Homeworks take a few hours, but worth the time.  Quizzes are given in TA sessions.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Severson is an amazing teacher. He is clearly passionate about what he teaches.  He actually cares if you understand the information, and if you are wiling to learn he is willing to teach you. Would definitely take him again

I learned so much from this professor and the guest speakers were always interesting. There are no tests, only 3 essays but they are very manageable. When he got a few emails that people were struggling he let class go 2 hours early and extended our deadline. Very nice man.

He is a really nice guy! The class is very long and there are no breaks and some classes have dense lectures. However, really cool guest speakers come in almost every week. Such a nice guy! He is super funny and makes lectures interesting! However, the weekly quizzes you have and exams seem to be testing you on completely different material. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Slevc is a good lecturer overall. The class lectures were helpful although the PowerPoints were a bit confusing at times. There were weekly quizzes when I took this class. I loved Mem&Cog with Professor Slevc! His lectures are short, brief, straight to the point and interesting to watch. He gives weekly quizzes that are fairly easy most times and assignments that are sooo much fun to do. Highly recommend!

This class was taught asynchronously and was fairly easy. He gave less than an hour of lectures each week and a quiz and/or a simple assignment each week for credit. Dr. Slevc doesn't tell you what the work for the week will be on the syllabus but it was never very difficult. He also seems like he'd be a nice guy if the class was taught in person.

Robert's an awesome guy. Memory and cognition wasn't a hard class to begin with, but Robert made everything accessible, giving many real life examples of phenomena. It's important to go to lecture considering his exams include diagrams that he makes on his powerpoints. The quizzes prepare you for exams well. Not to mention, tons of extra credit!!

So, Smith is very passionate about what he does, however I hated this class. The only grades that count are the "weekly quizzes" and the 4 exams. Go to class for any extra credit opportunities. The exams were way harder than I expected and they are hard to study for with taking other harder classes.

PLEASE READ
He's a great guy, he really is. However his lecture style is me talking to myself in the mirror- completely all over the place and sorta sounds like he's just doing it for fun. learned a lot tho

Dr. Smith is a great professor. He shows he really cares about his students, and he really knows how to make students engage in the learning. Good guy!

He is a very fair grader, left me with a B+ instead of an A but that was the breakdown detailed in the syllabus. Missed it by 1 question on the exam.  Study hard!!

She is super nice and very passionate about what she teaches. Lots of writing assignments, but the rubrics are very thorough. She wants to give extensions, so don't be afraid to ask. Shea leaves comments on everything and is easily found outside of classes to ask questions. Amazing person!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Yvonne is a glowing beacon of light in a sea of darkness. Her teaching style is clear and precise and she always helps her students understand what she is trying to say. She facilitates intellectually stimulating discussions and she is always respectful to her students. Easily one of the best teachers I have ever had.

One of the best teachers on campus! She has very easy to understand lectures and always posts the powerpoints from them. She has a very clear grading criteria for writing assignments. I took her class in a 3 week session and excelled! UMD should make her a permanent teacher instead of a graduate assistant!

Such a sweet and cool professor, I definitely enjoyed her class. And it's a class that, so long as you read, is an A. She does a great job of taking a topic that some people find discussing uncomfortable, and making it pretty comfortable. However, be prepared for group projects and discussions, as that is prominent in the class. Would recommend.

Not a hard class, and very little work. However, I think the things I learned the most in this course were how to eloquently create something out of nothing, and the art of connecting the dots between loosely-related ideas in the most unconventional way possible.

Professor SB is really kind and intelligent, and wants her students to learn and succeed. She definitely struggles with technology which hindered class sometimes, but nothing too bad. Half of the class is structured with your assigned small group, which people have mixed opinions on, but it's honestly fine. Interesting and easy class, little work.

Smith-Bynum is a sweet professor who was also adjusting to having classes online. This led her to be a little disorganized with assignments but it wasn't too bad. There were weekly journals and group discussions but they are easy and if you like your group members, it can be fun! There was only one paper so the class so it was an easy A.

Her class was a little unorganized but a huge part was due to it being fully online. The deadlines for most assignments weren't extremely clear but she was so helpful when I emailed and would respond impressively fast. She was also really adaptable to our situations and moved an assignment back when the wifi in our dorms wasn't working.

Class is based on participation in group meetings (4 people), weekly journals, group project, and a paper. She provides some leeway with some assignments and is understanding. Very interesting class as well, although it is very very liberal.

I am only halfway through this course, but I needed to write a review. Dr. Smith-Bynum is just so extremely sweet. Her grading is very fair and pretty easy. However, there is a lot of reading and lecture material. It's a pain to get through, but it is worth it because you can get an easy A if you push through. Don't be scared to email her!

reviews.comment: prof. smith-bynum is really nice and so funny, she makes lectures easy to enjoy. I liked this class a lot!
good

Professor Smith is one of the best professors I've ever had. She really believes in her students and helps them out whenever possible. She always allows for late discussion posts and really cares if you're sick or not doing well. I have had her for multiple classes and each one has been great. She grades easily too and has so many cool stories :)

Martha is an absolute unit. She's sweet and caring and very interested in seeing her students succeed. I did minimal work in this class and got an A or B. The lectures can be very sleep-inducing because she has a very calming and slow lecture style so make sure you bring icy cold water to stay awake. Come with an open mind.

Professor Smith was definitely an influential teacher for me.  She really cared if students were grasping the information. She is available through email, but may not respond immediately.

Professor Smith is really kind and helpful. The grading was fair and the coursework manageable.
Tons of reading and boring material. I definitely DO NOT recommend this course.

Prof smith is great. i love prof. smith. she's a great speaker and public reader. i love when she reads out loud. when you take english, make sure you have her.

It seems like only one (possibly 2) are getting over B+. All my friends "failed" or got a D. When you take her class, the very first mail you will get from her is that she won't answer to her students with e-mail, nor she will help her student since she has approx 180 students in her class

No Comments

As a straight male, it was horrible. Allowed female students to stroll in at any time, but if a male was late he was called out in front of everyone. very liberal and forces her opinions on you. if you disagree she will put you down. doesn't like boys who take the class. lesbianism gets brought into every lecture one way or another. she is very biased in her opinions. A LOT of reading and half barely even gets mentioned.

Dr. Smith is very close minded and while she encourages you to participate she really only has one right answer in mind - hers. She does not like men in the slightest and was seriously discriminatory to the male in the classroom as a woman I was embaressed.

biased and capricious grading!
Get to know her. She is great and willing to help you with anything!

Class is pretty simple. Very lecture heavy but she posts them online so you can watch them later if needed. There are 5 homework assignments and 5 quizzes but no final. Homework assignments are extremely easy and she posts detailed instructions.

Great prof!
Kate is a really sweet lady. She is a good teacher and makes long lectures interesting.

Great class..Great teacher. highly recommend the class.

Kate is great! HESP202 is a great class. Its really interesting and she makes it very simple. Study the notes (off the power point), diagrams (she gives them) and there are a few things from the text but not much. Overall, great class. HIGHLY recommended!!!

Skinker is a good professor, but she can be unfair when grading papers. Do NOT exceed 2 pages when you write your papers because she will take 5-6 points off, regardless of the content. Overall, the class is interesting and pretty easy. 3 exams, 5 quizzes, and 2 papers.
I love Kate Skinker, she is so interesting. She made the class really engaging and fun. Such a good teacher.

3 tests and 3 homeworks make up the entire grade. Fairly easy class, no discussions. Notes aren't online but she lectures right off powerpoints that are really detailed. Very helpful and usually makes class interesting.
Great teacher, very straight forward. Take this class with her. Very nice.
Great professor. The class is easy, tests come directly from the notes, and the final is a half hour long and not cumulative. Just show up to lecture or get the notes from someone and you'll do fine.

Interesting class, lectures are clear. Material is useful to know, even if you're not a HESP major. really easy but quite interesting class. prof is very clear. attendance not mandatory as long as you get someone with good notes. i didn't use the textbook at all...a waste.

Best class and best teacher! If you're at UMD and need a humanities credit, definitely take this class with professor Skye. Put in the effort and get an A. Not a strict grader.

reviews.comment: Truly an amazing teacher, one of the best I've had. She understands the needs of her students and works to make the classroom a comfortable environment. If you have the option to take her, do it, you won't regret it.

Just take any class with her. Please! Devoted to communications and her students. If you are shy about public speaking, she works to make the class and environment where you are comfortable speaking in front of. Definitely the best COMM107 teacher on campus! She is very fair and will always be there to support her students. 10/10 recommend taking her course!

reviews.comment: Great professor! She made me want to go to Comm class at 9am. She is very energetic and passionate about her students. Shes great in easing the anxiety of public speaking. I would totoally recommend her because not only is the class fun but its also very interesting.
I really love her. She is such an amazing teacher. As long as you go to every class and follow instructions, A is not hard at all. She is also very negotiable. I highly recommend her.

Professor Skye is hands down the sweetest professor on earth. Not only is she so kind, but she makes the material in this required COMM class fun, and easy as possible. Great professor teaching much needed material for all CEE majors.  Why is this class an elective and not required?

Loved this professor! One of few classes at the grad level! Could use some more real-world cases though..

He assumes that people who take his class already have a Ph.D in Math. Don't take this professor if you can help it!  He stands at the front of the class and reads slides.  Tests are really difficult and graded like the SATs (1/4 points are taken off for wrong answers).  Homework takes a really long time to do and is graded harshly.  Stay away!

The guy can not teach!! He assumes we know the material and he goes through it extremely fast. The required homework takes days to do, but what can I say all finance professors are just like him. He reads off the slides and makes the subject really boring. Exams are really hard

Disorganized, egotistical, and dismissive of students. Lectures are rambling with no structure, and grading is vague and unfair. Get ready for inappropriate comments. Workload is excessive and stressful, with no real support. Creates a toxic environment.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Saul is an extraordinary educator, blending intelligence with wit and humor! As his student, you'll face challenges that push you to excel. His courses demand commitment and deep engagement, offering a transformative learning experience far beyond just earning an easy A.

This professor was probably the worst I had for any college class. Such a subjective grader and the way he talks to his students feels borderline inappropriate. There were many times I felt uncomfortable in his class.

There were many moments in the class when comments were made that dismissed or devalued the contributions of female students. This created a discomforting and unequal learning environment. He acts like he knows everything and is very defensive.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Saul Sosnowski expresses proudly to their full potential all seven of the cardinal sins. Misogyny, discrimination, and pride is so prominent in every single lecture that it must be a result of years of intentional development. They say you need 10 thousand hours to be considered a master, in the area of making you miserable, Saul has done 20.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Sosnowski caused me so much stress I ended up in the ER the Saturday morning he called my CELLPHONE, while I was still SLEEPING, to interrogate the authenticity of my work and threaten to report me to the board, which landed me in the ER testing for heart palpitations and being medicated for a panic attack, then he refused to grade my work.

Saul Sosnowski is by FAR the best professor I've had at UMD. He is incredibly over-qualified to teach this class. The professor has met and studied with many of the writers we cover in class. His lectures are amazing and I never got bored because he keeps the class involved by asking questions that help understand the reading. He is also HILARIOUS!

I'm jealous of anyone who gets to take a class with the GOAT! He's hilarious so make sure you laugh at his jokes to get on his good side. Super chill and teaches for funsies so don't take him seriously. It takes a bit to get used to the fact that he doesn't use PowerPoints, but you only need to know the main ideas for exams. Would recommend 100%!!

This man is the GOAT of the Spanish Department. Super easygoing and knows how to make you laugh. You def have to take a class with him at least once. Having said that, the workload is a LOT (65 stories) so I would not recommend if you're taking other heavy courses. Actually do the readings and you WILL get an A! Easy grader, just wants you to learn

Gives an unrealistic amount of work and will jump around the syllabus/barely cover certain texts with no indication of what is the most important thing to focus on. Will call out people/embarrass them if it's clear they haven't read. I don't feel that I learned very much as the workload/teaching style was very anxiety-inducing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Saúl's a great professor and I would 100% recommend him... just not for a 400-level class. The workload was quite literally insane  about 65 readings in one semester. Just reading the syllabus was intimidating. So many people dropped & I wish I did too. Like hello, we have other classes!! Praying for anyone who has to write a 8-10 page paper ahhhh
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: To start, this class literally gave me depression. He calls us gringos in the middle of class. I could not hate this class more. There's only 4 assignments for the entire semester and he doesn't even post the grades. There's no powerpoints or anything, just him talking the entireeeee time, its so boring, no wonder we tune out.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I agree with the other review! 362 has lots of history and he loves it. Lots of long readings but he makes is bearable. You can tell that he teaches for fun & doesn't care much about grading - as long as you put in effort, you'll be good! Exams are reasonable. Not hard to get an A. Wants you to learn and could not care less about grading. Take S!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Took Prof Sosnowski this semester for a heavy literature course & hated myself throughout the semester... the readings are long (take forever) and sometimes I don't understand his lectures (him talking to us for 75 minutes, no powerpoint or anything) So many tangents that it's hard to figure out what is important Grades pretty easy or favoritism
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Sohns for HESP411 and the class was informative and so much fun. She came into class every day with a smile and sometimes with treats. She is one of the kindest professors I've had and is always willing to help students stuck or chat. Would definitely take her class again.

A doable class with the dedication! Lectures can be overwhelming with info but she was super helpful outside class. ALWAYS ASK QUESTIONS cause there's a lot to learn. Textbook considered "highly recommended" but i recommend because supplemental readings help with HW, Quizzes, etc. Did a great job for ZOOM classes. I wasn't even a HESP major/minor!!

Dr. Sohns is a great professor, her lectures are very clear and almost all of the information you need to know is in the powerpoint. The worksheets and quizzes are very similar to exams. She really cares about her students in and out of class and is willing to make changes to class based on student feedback or just have a good chat.

Very tough grader, class participation is graded and she takes attendance. The semester is based on a final project where we analyze/make an argument about an artifact. She is very specific about the guidelines and the work you submit.

Professor Soeder is very nice and caring. The coursework is very easy so long as you practice your presentations thoroughly before presentation day. She is clear in her rubric of what she expects and is a relatively easy grader. In-class activity points are given each class so attend because they add up.
Dr. Soeder is a nice and easygoing professor. As long as you do the work you will do great in her class. I recommend taking her classes as much as possible if you need COMM credit.
Absolute rave of a class. The guys with the shirt.

This class is very interesting, and she is a great professor. She really knows how to lead discussions and encourage people to participate. Be mindful: participation is graded (it is a seminar). Assignments aren't too bad, if you pay attention you should be good. All in all, I liked this class!

You have 9 textbook quiz through the year each only 10 questions and have 20 minutes to do them. The textbooks is online and you can have it our during the quiz. I never read the text and manage to do good on them. You get participation points from coming to class, and there is basically no classwork. Nice Teacher Easy Class, Easy Grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: An easy A. She was a pretty easy grader and gave good feedback to help improve. The discussions are nice and you don't really have to read the textbook. There is one group project and it was fun. Overall a good teacher and fun class.

Very informative discussion-based class, should be called Women & Gender Studies (not COMM). Workload super manageable. Writing assignments and group project graded harshly, but keep up & you'll do well. Mix of readings, documentaries and news sources for weekly readings. Not too accessible outside class. Review notes for exams and you'll do well.
n/a
An awesome professor! Very great at explaining the concept and willing to help and answers questions thoroughly!

I really enjoyed this class. He's a great lecturer and explains difficult to understand concepts in easy to understand ways and also includes examples all throughout his lectures, which helped me remember some parts of the material. His tests are straightforward and based on his lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He's passionate about the what he teaches and clearly does it because he enjoys it. He's incredibly helpful, will meet with you outside of hours, and if you email him your notes he'll review them. I'd highly recommend, but expect to have to work to do well. If you go to every lecture, read the textbook, and review the notes you should get an A.

Overall, a really great professor. His lectures, though, go for all three hours with only a 5 minute break in the middle so be prepared for that. Very knowledgeable professor, very passionate about biology. His exams are pretty straightforward. All of them will includes essays - be sure you go into DETAIL. I wish he taught more SIE biology courses.

I took BSCI105 with him in the summer. He is a very clear and engaging teacher who knows his stuff well. His lectures are fun and you leave the class feeling like you learned a LOT of useful information. His lectures are organized and entertaining. He says many quoteable phrases that help you remember the material. Exams are reasonable and clear.
Great professor who knows his stuff!  Tests are challenging but you can master the material if you study.  Lectures are entertaining and informative.
Definetly the better of the other professors for 105
He makes it very interesting.  His tests are mostly from his notes, so you should try to go to class, but he posts them online.
He has a wonderful and fun way of teaching biology that I have not seen at any other school. Should you have to take BSCI105 I definitely would recommend taking this class with him.
No Comments
No Comments

PSA to all Duke Students: this is an old profile of hers. For opinions from actual Duke students, make sure to include the school in your search of her name. She is an amazing teacher, and some of these reviews do not reflect that at all. Take her class!!!

An amazing professor and really cares about growth as a writer and an individual. She is extremely accomodating and very cognizant of the social climate and validates various forms of english, like AAVE, and not just "standard" english. Tad disorganized, but is very receptive to student concerns and clarifies without hesitation if asked. LOVE HER!

Chill Prof. Plays music in class, curses a lot, but she is a good teacher. Explains things well, always encourages us to ask questions or ask for help. Makes us feel comfortable and ensures us that if we need more time on something, she is willing to give us more time. Bulk of class is group work.

She is disorganized and our first grades were entered very late into the semester. I guess it is ok, because we do less work than other classes. She is over the top and is not really EXTREMELY knowledgable on non-profits.

The first day Dr. Spinner tries to scare students by implying there will be a lot of work, but the readings are interesting and the assignments are reasonable. Super understanding & genuinely cares about if students are learning and happy. Gave 3 unexcused absences. Very modern & won't bore you like other classes. 10/10 would take Dr. Spinner again
If you want to go to law school. Take Spivey. You will save yourself a lot of anxiety during your first year. If you pay attention, you will feel prepared for law school.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Spivey is the best. His classes are very test-heavy, so it's very important you study. He's a busy guy, so it's hard to get 1v1 time with him, but thankfully he's a lenient grader and will more often than not boost your grade at the end of the semester:)

There is a reason why everyone in the department raves about Professor Spivey's classes. His class is challenging, but you gain so much from it. He cares about his students and will work with you to make sure that you are successful. I'm in GVPT439B with him now and both of these are the best courses I have ever taken at UMD.

Great Professor. Keep up with reading and briefing cases throughout the semester. Go to lecture, they're engaging and will help a lot with the tests. Where you're called on in class, be sure to be able to argue your point with logic and evidence -- he will push back (but that's the fun of it). An "A" is very attainable, plus he gives extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Spivey is my favorite professor at UMD and I couldn't thank him enough for providing classes that have made me realize how much I love law. Definitely make sure you read the cases and readings because participation matters, but he is a very fair grader and gives students input on their grade. He has made me so happy I chose my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Prof Spivey has very engaging and interesting lectures, but the class grade is based on exams, so if u dont do well on the exams your grade will suffer. READ, show up to class, and take notes if u wanna pass. Also, he sucks at responding to emails. Other than that, great Prof! lol.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Spiveys lectures was always entertaining and full of information. His method of teaching helped me keep digging deeper into the hypos and learn the concepts better. Just make sure you actually read the material before coming to class as he loves calling on random people.

There's a reason why Spivey is iconic at UMD. He teaches like a real law school class so there's more discussion than teaching. You learn the content before class by reading and then talk about it in lecture. He has discussants assigned for each class that have to talk about that day's material, that's how you learn. Exams aren't bad if you read.

He's a great lecturer and really knowledgable about the law. He administers difficult, but fair exams with hypothetical questions similar to those in law school. It's a challenging course that requires you to be knowledgable about the cases and you must understand how to apply the law to hypothetical scenarios.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Spivey is my favorite professor at UMD. This class is not just rote memorization; you have to actually think through the hypotheticals that are given to you and they're often very interesting. Dr. Spivey is also hilarious and you will enjoy every single lecture. I would highly recommend taking him.

Spivey makes lectures lively and enjoyable. He is an expert on law and never lets you forget it, but not in a pretentious way. He is very easy to talk to and clearly wants his students to succeed. If you talk to him outside of class, he does everything in his power to make sure you're successful. The material is hard though, so stay on top of it
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I have never had a better professor than Prof. Spivey. His lectures are extremely interesting and insightful. You do not really need to read for the class; however, if you want to succeed then you should read as much as you can. He makes some very boring law concepts into very interesting discussions. All in all I would highly recommend Spivey.

According to other reviews, this was supposed to be an easy A, not when I took it though. I felt like I was putting in so much effort into the class and yet I was still getting marks off for stupid mistakes. Maybe it was just my experience, but I would not take this class with her or her TA's again.

I took this class just for the Gen Ed but thanks to Professor Spivy changed my major to ENSP. She really cares about her students and sometimes extended the assignments. Her lectures are interesting and informative - textbook not required. The final was even open for the whole week so we could do at our convenience. Definitely recommend.

She is so passionate about what she teaches! Attendance isn't mandatory and she posts all lecture slides. All assignments are very doable but the exams can be very stressful as they felt so long to me. I had sadly had a TA who was extremely harsh on all the grading. But this professor was awesome, I recommend!

In class she just lectures but in discussion you're able to ask the TA's questions. There are a couple homework assignments, two tests, and some extra credit assignments. Study and look over the material and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pretty easy class, sorta lecture-heavy but you can work off the slides if need be. Final paper was long, but she makes you do it in steps so it's actually pretty easy. You can tell she cares about both the environment and her students, definitely recommend!!

Dr. Spivy is probably one of my favorite professors! She so obviously cares about both her work and her students. The exams are very fair, just show up to lecture and use the posted slides to study the night before the exam. Would definitely recommend :)

I really loved taking Intro to Environmental Science with Professor Spivy! She really cares about environmental science & it's obvious through her teaching. She's super sweet & really fostered a fun class relationship even though everything was online. Definitely recommend taking this course!

I LOVED Prof. Spivy. I took her class as an undecided student considering an ENSP major, and the quality of her class was so amazing that I am now convinced. She very clearly cares for each&every one of her students, &her lectures are informative, bring in current events, &open to discussion. Tests were fair, as long as you take notes and read txtb

Spivy is cool, I like her. She is passionate and keeps things interesting. I took her Fall 2020 so everything was online and there were no problems. The only hws were checkpoints to the final paper. Not too bad. There were 3 EC opportunities...25 pts each, choose up to 2. No textbook necessary unless you're good at keeping up with readings.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Annette is such a queen. shes also my advisor so that might be bias. her lectures are so interesting and she has so much experience and it shows. the tests aren't difficult as long as you listen to what she has to say. her exams are basically straight from the lecture slides. also accessible out of class and extremely helpful. she's full of info

Professor Spivey is a great professor. You can tell that she genuinely cares and the subject she is teaching and it makes you want to take action in evironmentalism. Her lectures can go a bit fast, but she explains the material extremely well. Exams are easy if you go to the review sessions. They tell you what you need to focus on.

She got sick and we had a free 100 exam. So that was cool, but the other exams were pretty hard. You also have a 10 page paper due which sucks, but the grading is pretty lenient on that part. It is a fine class, but not the best.

A few easy homework assignments that will help you with your final paper. Gives really good feedback. Extremely caring and offers extra credit. The exams are a little hard (10 short answer prompts) but she knows what she is teaching. Pay attention & PARTICIPATE to get the full 75 points. It does require some memorization esp. for her exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Offers extra credit that was helpful. She knows a lot about the subject and lectures are important to go to because she discusses a lot of material that isn't on the slides. The exams can be tough if you don't explain enough just make sure you really know it. Overall she's a great professor and is very relaxed.

Very, very nice professor. I would recommend everyone in ENSP to take her. Show up to lecture, and do your homework. Take discussion seriously. Her lectures are very straightforward, and she is able to answer questions about the given topics very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her extra credit assignments were a blessing. As for the exams, she gives us a verbal list of what we would expect to see. There is also review session that is based on the exams. Also, you do not need to read the book for this class as long as you read her slides which are available online. There is a major paper due at the end of the semester.
I love Annette! She is very understanding and is very passionate about what she teaches. You do not need to read the book to get an A in this class. As long as you study her slides you will get an A.
My favorite Professor! Loved the fire program. She truly cares about all of her students
Dr. Spirito is so kind and amazing! However, Fire is just overall boring. I wouldn't recommend this program to incoming freshman.

Dr. Spirito is a kind and hardworking professor. She genuinely cares about her students and will make sure you understand the research you are doing. Her dedication and commitment to her students shows in the success of her students. Many students get other research positions because of her. Take her class!

Dr. Spirito is very friendly and wants all of her students to succeed. The class isn't hard just time consuming, but the experience that comes out of it is amazing! If you are looking for a research experience this is something that you should definitely check out! The assignments are pretty easy and lab is relaxing.

Dr. Spirito is such an understanding professor. If you don't understand an aspect of your research project or mess up in a procedure, she always takes time to explain and acknowledges that research can be hard and everyone learns at different paces. She gives you opportunity to be independent with your research, but will also guide you too.

I literally love this class. It's my favorite class. Dr. Spirito is so crazy smartshe expects a lot out of you but is also very patient. You learn so much and have so many incredible opportunities to really take charge. I can go to her for anything whether it's school or life; she is filled with both passion and compassion and I LOVE HER.

One of my favorite classes and teachers as of far! Dr. Spirito is always there to help with questions and explains content very clearly. I have gained a lot experience and learned many things from her. The research you get to do is really interesting and fun while the assignments are not difficult but very helpful. Definitely recommend this class!!

Dr. Spirito is the best professor, and FIRE172+FIRE272 were my top two favorite classes I've had at UMD. You will not regret taking this class. The research we did in class taught me how much I love research and how fun it can be with a team of friends! Very good choice for a science stream. Perks: We are in a newer building than the other streams.

Dr. Spirito is an amazing teacher. After having her for a year now I have learned so much with her. She takes time for her students and explains everything with clarity and patience. Research is not easy but Dr. Spirito is so helpful and makes research fun and clear. She also exposes you to so many great opportunities.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: The class is boring. Very hard to understand the point of the class. Better off taking a different class for a gened credit. This class isn't worth it.

This is a research class where you work on a project with your team. You go to lab 6 hrs/wk + 1 hr/wk meet up. We had assignments due every week, but nothing too hard. The best part was working in the lab. Dr. Spirito is very helpful, kind, caring, approachable, and an amazing research educator. I would highly recommend taking this class!!! :)

It's a challenging class no matter who you take, but TAKE HIM! Speer is probably the best professor I've ever had at UMD. He KNOWS & is passionate about the material he teaches & therefore, is a great professor. He is so good at explaining concepts & teaching. Helps you understand things that may be hard to get just by reading the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: this class will take over your entire life. the schedule is as follows: week 1: quiz (with groups), week 2: midterm, week 3: break and repeat for 14 weeks. You will always be studying mamphys. Upside is 50% of exams are from the textbook so you can memorize those. Need solid understanding of information, exams are all application.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Speer was definitely challenging but you can get an A if you work for it. Group quizzes in discussion so choose your team wisely. Exams are application based, require lots of detail, & he looks for key words. Read the textbook & do all practice problems (50% of exam comes from here). He explains clearly/slowly and does case studies for application!

There is a lot of material to learn and you have to be able to apply them, not memorize them. Speer's lectures are clear and through. His exams are challenging but do-able. The curve was reasonable as well. You can get the A if you put in the work for it.

You NEED to read the book, review the slides, get outside help if needed. Exams are mainly case studies - know how to APPLY known physiology to real-life scenarios. Lectures covered main concept but but you need to put effort into knowing examples, diagrams, etc (THE BOOK IS THE BEST).The class is very interesting, highly recommend!

440 is a hard class so dont even think about framing if. Speers exams are challenging but fair. He genuinely cares about kids. Super smart and enthusiastic. The topics are super interesting, spec for a premed kid, and he is the kinda teacher that makes you wanna take more classes with him.

Dr. Kate is fantastic and you can tell she truly cares about the wellbeing of her students. She is crystal clear with criteria/expectations and is also a generous grader. You can tell she wants her students to succeed and grow. Trying hard in her class was unexpectedly personally rewarding and I learned a lot. It's a no brainer to take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Kate is the best and I would recommend everyone to take her class. She cares so much about her students and the class is interesting
For an Engineer major she made theater class very interesting! For a good Gen-Ed I recommend everyone to take her classes.

Justin's class always made my day. A lot of classes we, as a class, would get carried away through discussions which would really open everyone's eyes. He's hilarious and really woke so you learn so much in this class. His projects are also really cool and I enjoyed all of them. If you put in effort, which is not hard, you'll truly enjoy it.
Very funny

Justin was rad. His class was really easy, but it was an intro class so that's expected. He was super respectful of intersectionality, and made sure to correct himself if he messed up in that sense. Plus he was really funny and just an overall likable guy.
Amazing teacher, great conversation. Really doesn't even post notes you just discuss the readings and pop culture
Best teacher. 100% recommend

Justin was an amazing professor. He made you actually enjoy the topics in such an enlightening way. He was also very 'hip' to contemporary issues so that made it a plus! The class is sooo interesting and definitely a safe space. Take this class to learn and enjoy! there's no textbooks just novels that you def need but they're actually interesting!

Justin is an amazing professor, I looked forward to going to this class everyday. He teaches his class as though it's a discussion, he wants to hear everyone's thoughts and opinions and it's obvious that he loves what he does. His teaching is so enlightening and gives you a new perspective on so many different views. Definitely pick him for a prof!
Justin's awesome!! So funny and so nice! He made it a class I wanted to go to!

Justin is a great professor! He is young and understanding, as well as creative a fun and engaging environment in his classroom. He cares a lot about his students, and is very clear and helpful when it comes to what he's looking for in his assignments. Easy-ish grader, if you put the time and effort in and participate, it's an easy A!
Absolutely unorganized but have unrealistic expectations from students
He had no clue on what he was teaching. Was not prepared for classes. Was not giving any feedback.
Avoid him.
Was not prepared for classes. Was not clear when explaining subject . Avoid him.
Poor explanation of materials. Expects participation when students don't know what he is talking about and gets clearly frustrated with the students.

no guidance nor motivation, unclear explanations and focuses only on a very few front sitting students and completely ignores the rest of the class. As far as homework solutions and explanations - it's very poor!
Horrible Professor. Avoid at all costs.

I took both her INST352 class which was online, and INST451 which was in-person. 

Professor St. Jean is very experienced in what she teaches, is very nice and caring, and has easy assessments. The grading rubric for any of the papers is clear and she doesn't try to confuse anyone. Great professor, would take her class again.

Professor Jean was a great professor. She had interesting slides to present with her lectures. The class consist of weekly discussions, four different quizzes, 2 papers and a few search modules. The class wasn't hard overall just got to make sure you do the work and watch the lectures other than that this class is a easy A.

BETH IS AN ABSOLUTE ANGEL. Of all of my professors she was by far the most caring. Be ready to read lots of studies in her classes but put in effort and you will be fine. She is very passionate about information science and you can easily tell. She wants her students to succeed. Highly recommend her for any course!

Everyone LOVES Beth - she's super kind, caring, smart, an INCREDIBLY easy grader, very willing to help students out if you email her reasonably ahead of time. Course was a bit basic for anyone with relevant work experience but the discussions were interesting and I had a lot of fun with the group project. Def get to know her, she's AMAZING.

Interesting class, lots of group work, lots of discussion. Be prepared to turn in something every other week, not a lot of time in class to work on group projects, keep organized with those. She doesn't seem to like to give 100s but you can get pretty darn close. Super nice and understanding. Would take her again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: She has no compassion for the external hardships her students experience. I told her I had an emergency with my family and asked for a one-day extension, she said no. Although it is a public health class and appears to be easier make sure you place it as a priority class she is here to collect her money and leave.

Personally, I did not like SPHL100, the total of over 10,000 points for this class was ridiculous. The semester long group project I also did not enjoy, but in the end when it all came together it was okay. Dr. L-H barely came to class this semester so her lead TA was teaching most of the lectures.

Loved the class, professor has a way of speaking because she is so passionate about the topic. That said, it is a flipped classroom which I did not like but it is manageable. You do the readings and watch lecture videos before your "Enrichment Activity" which is basically a lecture. Loved my TA she was really helpful and lenient with grading.

Dr. Latouche-Howard is AMAZING. She is very kind and caring and will meet with you to help you understand the material. The problem with this class is the TAs are very specific on their grading and the tests can get very specific on things we barely covered.

This professor is HORRIBLE. She read straight from the power points, which were taken straight from the book, and simplified to the point of being useless. Her power points, quizzes and TESTS were filled with with so many basic typos and so poorly written that it was very difficult to understand. No substance. To top it off she was bitter and rude.

Dr Lewis really knows her stuff and always did a great job at answering students' questions and facilitating class discussions. And the class workload is doable especially since student presentations summarize readings each week. Only complaint is that grading takes awhile but otherwise I really recommend taking the class.

Quite possibly the most unorganized professor I've ever had. Claims to be "understanding" but is just okay about extenuating circumstances. Heavy amounts of reading, and she expects you to remember what's in them. Bad at scheduling so workload is horribly uneven and there will be weeks with back-to-back papers due. Wish I didn't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Slowest grader I have ever dealt with. It is June 2 and I don't have my final grade yet. Took a month and a half to grade the midterm. Any positive attributes she may or may not have as a professor are rendered completely moot by the fact that it takes her forever to get a freaking grade in. Would give a 0 if I could.

Dr. Lewis is a great professor. The class was interesting, she tried her best to make the online format engaging. Her class was not lecture-heavy but required a lot of reading (2-6 per week). Most of them were okay other than the ones that dealt with philosophy. As long as you follow directions, know your vocab, and do your work you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Lewis is very caring and fun to talk to. She cares a lot about her field and her students but she is a VERY slow grader. It's the last week of school but I still don't know what my grades are going to be since the last grade I have is from over two months ago.

Dr. Lewis is one of the best WMST professors at UMD. She tells you exactly what is expected of you from day one. Her syllabus is super organized and clear. You do reading notes often, but make sure you do them. They're the "extra credit" built in the syllabus to fluff your grade. Must do a discussion lead (presentation) w/ a partner & a final paper
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Her grading was subjective, so the tough grading is only if she doesn't like you. She also gave unclear instructions and failed to explain intentions with her assignments. She, at best, pretended to care about students. I had to move dorms the day the final was, and she didn't give me an extension because the field had to be even amongst students.

Took this in Spring 2019. Dr. Lewis does a great job with this class! It is heavily discussion based (+ some writing) - there are always readings and then either students or Dr. Lewis will give a presentation and lead a discussion on the material. Strongly recommend this class for anyone looking to learn more about feminism and women's issues.

The work was fair, and as long as you showed up to class and did the assigned readings (besides more theory stuff with Stryker and Butler... they were interesting) However, the major issue with this professor is how SLOW it takes her to grade. Still waiting for 3 major grades, one of them was from early March but I likely will get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: I never really had any issues in this class. Readings are pretty straightforward MOST of the time (unless you're talking Judith Butler or Foucault, but we only did those rarely). Reading Notes are an easy 15/15, exam wasn't hard and comes entirely from the study guide. I'd just make sure you do the readings and participate in class, and you're good
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Veilleux is great if you have a question in lecture and always tries to get your attention with demonstrations which are easy to understand. The homework's can be difficult but if you pay attention and take notes, it's not bad. Overall great professor and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Puts too much information on sides so it's hard to know what matters. Has somewhat illogical and subjective grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I wouldn't say his class was anything special, but he did a good job and I think I was able to learn a lot, even though my major is unrelated. Overall, his class was fun with very little stress.

Veilleux is really interesting & loves space a lot so it's fun to listen to his lecture. The discussion quizzes are easy, but the homework, lecture quizzes, and some of the labs are difficult. I listen to lectures & am still confused. The midterm was just a bunch of the discussion quiz questions. A lot of work but makes sense for a 4 credit lab.

He's a good professor, with great lectures and very easy-to-get-along with. He definitely loves it when students asks questions of the unknown and loves to be engaged during lecture to show us amazing experiments. The only flaw with him is that his study guides for exams are terrible and VERY general, therefore people score lower on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: He is fine. Only 5 homework total. Lots of stuff to learn. Disc are fine with a worksheet. Tries to be funny. Cool experiments in class. Lectures are boring at times.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Good professor who makes the content easy to understand. You do have to study for this class and read the textbook but for the most part I did the bare minimum and still managed to get an A. it also helped that I found the content interesting but he makes lectures fun with experiments and actually made me look forward to my early morning class

Wonderful professor! Loves astronomy and is great at teaching it. Some of the lectures can get a little boring, but some of them have cool experiments/demonstrations towards the end. If you show up to lab, discussion, do the (easy) homeworks, study for the exams, and show up to lecture to answer enough of the attendance questions, you'll get an A.

She was an awesome professor! She's very caring and understanding towards her students. I really enjoyed her way of teaching and she is also really good in giving feedback on assignments. Overall, she's helpful and kind.

By far the best professor. She is fun, outgoing, takes the time to get to know her students and goes the extra mile to ensure her students succeed. I am beyond thankful to have taken her class. You will have the absolute best time having her as your professor. She will work with you if you have any issues. Take her! Trust me you won't regret it!

She is a great professor!I have her right now for ENGL101 and she's new to UMD.She is very accommodating and very understanding. She grades very easily and makes assignments very understandable. She also has a great personality and one of the few professors who care about her students and makes ENGL101 bearable. I recommend taking her class!

She is not clear on what she wants for her assignments, and the class is too politically charged. She also deducts points on assignments for very small mistakes. If you do have to take the class, be sure to follow her rubrics instead of the videos she posts.
It is not a hard class, but there is a lot of reading to be done. It is difficult to figure out the expectations of the professor. She does give a lot of opportunities to earn extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I'm not even political but her liberal bias is crazy. She thinks everything is because of racism or sexism (HINT: mention this in your papers to get an A guarenteed). Idc about her opinion, but one of my classmates was conservative and always got bad grades on well written work. I told him to complain to the dean but he was too scared. Class was ok
Generally pushes a far-left bias in the class and gives lots of assignments and readings. Would not recommend to any student.
Dr. Syrmos is AWESOME.  Very fun professor.  Easy grader.  You definately want to be in his section for ENES100.
Incredibly easy class and Proffessor. Just remember to do all the HW and stay ontop of your teammates (Mine tended to procrastinate) Syrmos is a very good proof and is always willing to help.
Very good teacher and very interesting. Great class. If you are going to be taking ENES100 take it with him!
Dr. Syrmos was so nice, and ENES100 was seriously easy.

This class was a joke. Insane amount of work for a 100 level class. She thinks her class is way more important than it is. It's useless. also makes you buy a $70 textbook that SHE WROTE HERSELF. She never comes to class I saw her the first day and never again, all her lectures are guest speakers and TA's. I wish negative stars were an option
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Not great... preferred Organic Chemistry over this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Most annoying teacher I have ever had. She just forces you to pay for a 70 dollar textbook that she wrote so that she makes money. On top of that, any technological errors give you a 0 on the assignment.Overall, very greedy teacher with no respect for others.

ngl the class structure is not okay at all. i'm currently taking this class and you can't even get access to the weekly quizzes that are done, even if you review them with your TA. i don't know what my grade will be but we'll see. the class is just complex for no reason
very unorganized class and structure is awful, its online aside from discussion and an enrichment activity weekly. However material is not hard and as long as you do everything you'll be fine.
Very nice and sweet professor. No exams, just weekly quizzes that are based on textbook reading, in-class discussion, videos, etc. You have to attend class to know the material.

Dr. LH is a good professor. Class structure is garbage. You do all the lectures asynchronously & they expect you to come to discussion having watched ALL the lecture videos, plus the 2-3 additional videos within the textbook, & THE 1-3 READINGS which are journal articles ranging from 15-30 pages. So much work for a 100 level class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: took during summer and it was easy. Very straightforward.

This 100 level course was so complex for no reason. They wouldn't give you access to a PowerPoints to study even though the all information for the quizzes were on there. The semester-long project was pretty complex for a 100 level course as well. This class was just really annoying and the way it was structured.

SPHL100 is a class that is led by a whole team so you don't have a lot of interaction with the professor. Her lectures were interesting and she seems like a nice person. This class is just hard for an introductory level course and the TAs grade all your work and they grade strictly. It's a lot of work but very possible to get a good grade.

I am super surprised at the previous ratings as I took this professor this semester and she was amazing! She has definitely made some changes in her class as we did weekly quizzes instead of exams. Her grading was straight-forward and so were all her assignments. This was not a difficult class. This professor is also so nice and so were her TA's.

Dr. LTH is THE BEST professor I've had at UMD. I took this class during COVID, and she was the most accommodating and caring professor. The class material is easy if you put in the work. There's a group project that takes place the entire semester, but it's nothing you can't handle. I couldn't recommend Dr. LTH enough.

Graded very harshly for a 100 class, harsher than some of the upper level classes. There were mistakes in the syllabus, the discussions took a lot of time and were graded harshly while the final paper prompt was vague and hard to complete. Tests were confusing and weirdly specific. Interesting class but scares prospective public health students off
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Howard is a nice lady, but this class sucks. Her grading is such that if you make several small mistakes on homework or discussions or exams, you cannot possibly get an A. The class is not bad overall, but the grading is just absurd. CHANGE THE GRADING DR HOWARD. Give out a few As

Not a good professor, and her TA's are awful. I had a really bad experience in this class. For a 100 level class, she is insanely hard at grading. This is NOT AN EASY COURSE. This is the hardest 100 level class I have taken. This class scares people away from Public Health, and from Pre-Med fields. Do not takee Dr Howard, AVOID HER.
Good luck. This class is so much harder than it needs to be and the TA's were not any help and they graded very harsh.

First off, she takes this class WAYYYY too seriously. For an 100 level course, she made us sign and turn in the syllabus and on top of that told us not to contact her but to contact the TA. She also requires you to buy a textbook that you can find online for FREE. And then she tells you to read an obscene amount of chapters that you don't need to!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You don't really see this professor for half of the lectures since there are also guest lecturers and TAs presenting material. She seemed like she was reading straight off the slides without actually explaining the major concepts. Recommend typing notes since she rushes through the material. TAs were definitely helpful and approachable throughout.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Disorganized and made me rethink my major...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: SPHL100: you will never see this professor. she always does online lectures and guest lecturers. For a 100 level class, this class is very difficult. Not many points in the gradebook. So every point counts. Good luck! I hope other SPHL classes arent like this since I'm a SPHL PH major... #Lazy The TAs are amazing tho! TAs are so approachable!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, if you plan on going to medical school and you are a public health major, change your major. This is my opinion, but finding research or getting into labs is much harder as a public health major. Save your self the trouble of this class and each one after it and go into genetics and micro or bio or maybe something completely different. gg

The class itself seemed to be too hard for a 100 level class. The TA's expected a lot from us. But make sure you go to every discussion class because each time you do a graded assignment that is a large chunk of your grade. Final group presentation in discussion. Interesting material at times, but can get boring. STUDY for exams they are TOUGH.
She gives many online lectures (which means u can just stay home). Her powerpoints are posted on ELMS. Exams are 30 MC online. Pretty chill course. She's very sweet and her lectures are interesting!

In this course you don't get to know Dr. Sylvette A. La Touche-Howard because she only does lectures (that's if there isn't a guest speaker). Any questions or concerns are expressed to the TAs. Basically, the TAs run this course. I wouldn't take this course again. TAs grade harshly.
HLTH140 online (winter) is really easy and Dr. LTH makes it a pleasant experience. Would highly recommend the class, as it is an easy A.

Dr. La Touche-Howard shows that she cares! She puts a lot of energy into her lectures and really wants us to "get it", we did a lot of "theory to practice" activities in class and prepared our own health campaign initiatives. I learned so much! Perhaps the most valuable course in the department!

This class is one of the hardest classes in the department. It takes a lot of time and a lot of dedication. We have to prepare for internships, prepare a grant proposal and a lot of other professional development activities. Dr. La Touche-Howard kept on encouraging us throughout the whole process, could not have made it through without her!

I Love Dr. La Touche-Howard. Although she has a lot going on, she always makes time for her students, she gives you so many ways to get in contact with her and she always has a listening ear. She really loves what she does and it shows!
I took winter session class. It was intense but everything was clear. There were no surprises. You have to keep up on the material she provides and the assignments.

Does not know what she is doing. Constantly changes her mind on things. Worst teacher. Do not take. I repeat do not take. Really not cut out to teach this class. Final project was a disaster because of her disorganization. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

Worst experience i have had in my entire college career. Dr. LA Howard is the most unorganized professor and is not a suitable teacher for this course. Although she is a very sweet person and presents well, but is very slow at putting up study guides and other important information and changes rules constantly. DO NOT TAKE HLTH 371 with her.

She will not email you back if she thinks your email is not important or if she said it in class.  She is never clear and expects students to know what to do without instruction.  At least she smiled sometimes.

Supposed to be an easy class.  I took this as an elective and it was the WORST class ever.  I also took 371 at the same time with her and she had be cursing and dying the whole semester.  Pointless assignments.  Tests are written poorly.  No one left the final feeling literate. Does not email back if she thinks your email is stupid.

Not the easiest course that I have ever taken but Dr. La Touche-Howard really tried to work with students to help them do their best. There is an ongoing group project throughout the whole semester which all seems to come together in the end but you have to stick with it. Both the professor and the TA were helpful if you had any questions.

one of the most disorganized classes i've ever taken. literally shes a mess and made the class do group work every class period because she's lazy. her TA Chelsea rae is AWFUL. maybe thats why the class sucked
She is so great. Really helpful and genuinely wants her students to do well. She is always smiley and really practices what she preaches. You can never leave her class upset or sad
Great instructor. We played knowledge jeopardy which was both fun and educational.... Took course during the summer. No exams. Had to write a ten source annotated bibliography instead of a paper.

She was great. I took her STAT 110 through USCL this spring. The class was really easy, follow along and you'll be fine, she was hands off because it was a self-paced class. There were like four assignments per week and around three total tests, including the final. I would 100% recommend the class to anyone.

Dr. Mazzullo is really nice and friendly. Although her class isn't hard, she talks and moves on pretty fast. This makes it easy to fall behind and become confused. She is also very lecture heavy and tends to talk a lot, there were even times she kept us a few more minutes after class was over. She is nice but talks and moves fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Mazzullo is so nice. She helps us work through some assignments in class. Tries to make everything as clear as possible. She can be a little disorganized though. But honestly as long as you do your work you'll be fine. And she and her TAs are always ready to help answer your questions whether in class or through email.

Very nice woman, but not a great teacher. She often messes up and doesn't realize until someone points it out and doesn't explain things well. If you put in the work on your own time you'll do well. If you're good at math you're fine.

My best professor at UMD so far. She REALLY cares whether or not her students understand the concepts she's teaching. You could ask her any questions at any time and she would get an answer for you. Only negative was the software we had to use. It seemed unnecessary for people not going into a stats field. Overall though, great professor!
I loved Susan's STAT430 class. Super nice, accommodating, and really easy, with extra credit. I learned a lot too! Absolutely take her if you can.
Love this professor. Super sweet, kind, caring, and easy class. I learned a lot from her as well. I highly recommend that you take her if you can.

One of the most kind, passionate, and caring professors I have met in the math department here. She truly wants to see you do well and learn SAS. If you show up to class she provides answers to the class assignments as incentive for joining her lectures. I could only wish more professors shared a similar passion for teaching as she does.

I was nervous to take stat because I hadn't taken math in several years, but she put me at ease. There is definitely a decent amount of work for this class (it feels like you are watching lectures, taking quizzes, and completing assignments almost every day of the week), but that means you should be prepared for the exams. She is a sweetheart!

Sue is the greatest to ever do it. She is the nicest person in the world and is very good at explaining all the content and giving you plenty of practice.
