reviews.comment: The course was severely disorganized (probably due to the pandemic), so the final grade was decided almost exclusively by one homework and the final project. I managed to get a good grade pretty much entirely due to my prior knowledge of the subject. He gave grades generously in the end, but the class was not very informative.
He is hard to understand as he doesn't explain concepts or ideas well at all. Online resources are probably your best bet to pass. He generally teaches higher level courses.

Had this guy for math 135, absolutely terrible teacher. He does not explain ANYTHING in lecture and that is why only around 15/200 kids showed up each time. He writes things in extremely complicated formats and doesn't stop to explain anything he is doing. Very very confusing and had to rely on the book which is equally as terrible as him.
He is a professor that you dont need books. Pretty clear notes and matlab code
Very great professor. The lecture is very clear and organized well. He is helpful in office hour. He is only professor who teach how to code I have met until now.

Messy lecturer. Super hard to follow if you're new to Calculus. Office hours were unorganized, and did not always respond to emails. Discussions are mandatory. Lots of online homework that takes up a lot of time. Tests are very long, and it was a struggle to finish them in 50 min. Don't take him if you are actually interested in math.
This guy is the worst didn't learn anything from him all semester. I was lucky to have the GOAT TA to help with the class but this guy was a clown. Definitely don't take him if you have the chance

Don't get the poor reviews. His breakdowns were infrequent and he was extremely prepared. His lectures (though not his website) were super organized. He explained things very well. Tests were fair and the homework prepared you for them. Couldn't ask for more. Just don't buy the book. He posts lectures notes.
I can't speak for other classes he teaches, but when it came to Math 120 this man didn't know how to teach at all. Tests were hard too, and were graded roughly.

He does not clearly explain the topic in lecture and when he gets stressed he has panic attacks. If you have to take him it may be better to go to another math 120 teachers lecture or study from the textbook.
Don't take him, he's horrible. Worst math teacher ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Does not answer emails so if you have a problem, go to his office hours. Tends to have panic attacks during class. Almost like he cares about what he is doing but cannot get the information out in a clear timely manner. If you have him all I can say is...."good luck and god speed".

Has a medical condition which negates his ability to hold meaningful lectures. Does not use a textbook. Throws himself on the floor in fits. Loud bursts of panting and crying. Completely disinterested in providing feedback-we took an exam 2 months ago and have yet to get them back. Does not respond to emails. Do not take his class.

Had a panic attack about once per week which was distracting. Often I would approach him after class with a question but he would just panic, and couldn't answer. Never replied to ANY emails I sent him. Because of these last two things, I do not recommend taking his course. Also, homework is very difficult if you don't have much coding experience.
Great professor, straightforward notes. Has the occasional breakdown in class, but other than that I found him to be very helpful
Fairly good teacher. Has some hiccups doing examples, otherwise good at explaining the material. Come to lecture+discussion and do the webassign and you'll be fine.
Von Petersdorf is a fairly good teacher. If you attend lectures you will have no problem grasping the material. Tests so far have very been fair and most homework is optional.

A bunch of people I know warned me against this professor due to his lack of clarity and organization.  He's in fact the exact opposite.  The tests are very fair, he does great reviews, and if you attend lectures and do the (optional) homework, you'll get a good grade in the class.
No Comments
Avoid any class with him.  He's nice, but difficult to learn from.

He makes the class harder than it really is...the tests are on stuff we learn but like 10 times harder. Lectures are most of the time unclear but attend both lectures and discusion. The TAs should be able to clear up what he taught in class

The class is relatively easy although attending is a must since it's all based on lecture notes. von Petersdorff can be very unclear at times but he is very willing to help if you go to him with questions.
No Comments

Great prof! All projects are scaffolded so that they build on each other. Group projects and discussion boards are optional. There is no busywork or bothersome mini assignments. If you lose points on an assignment, you can resubmit the assignment again after receiving her feedback! She replies to emails promptly.

The content of this course is straight-forward. Nevertheless, Weaver manages to obfuscate the coursework expectations--it seems like she enjoys catching students off guard in regards to due dates. My suggestion to her: a student's effort should be dedicated to learning content not to memorize the ever-changing syllabus.
If you can put up with her for the full 37.5 hours, you'll get an A. She's irritating and unreasonable, but her assignments are preschool-level easy.
Prof is unperceptive to student concerns and criticism and is usually unprepared for class.

Not accessible outside class, so don't expect any response to your email. She is often 5 min late, but if you are 2 min late (once in a semester) when she is punctual, she will deduct your marks. There is homework every week but you only get your grades at the end of the semester. Most grades don't come with comments. No phone or laptop is allowed.
Little full of himself

Josh was a great workshop prof. He's a respected poet and had a close relationship with Thom Gunn, etc. His workshop was mostly based off grades from 6 poems which you submit & he hands back with a 1-6 grade, you can revise over & over to improve. He's an interesting guy, blunt in a necessary way, friendly. Had us do fun in class writing exercises

This professor is not for everyone.  He expects maturity.  He expects students to consume the course material through the texts.  Often, he will ask a question, you will answer, then he will continue to stare at you until you continue to develop your answer.  If you are not comfortable with that sort of tension, you will not enjoy this class.

Weiner encourages group think and is generally snide with students who express opinions contrary to his own. He favors certain styles of poetry and will strangle voices of students that stray from his view of "good" poetry. Match his standard? May be nice. Worth the risk? You decide.
have to memorize alot of stuff. way to hard for a intro course

absolutely horrible... he is a terrible lecturer and thinks that everything he says is genius (it's not!) He is very unapproachable and spends very little time on anything interesting involving poetry. If you enjoy reading poetry, he will ruin it for you.

horrible. the worst class ever. boring. he reads an essay every class.  doesnt speak but reads. tests are extremely hard. he uses metaphors to describe everything, and you can never figure out what they mean

Very attentive to students. Known to finish a line in a poem for you or give you a kick-ass title. Generous with his time. Honest with students about the strenghts and weaknesses of their work. Helps students expand their vision of what a poem does. Very well read in poetry and theory. Quote: "Go meta!"
No Comments

Dr. Weiss has a perfect balance of professionalism and personality, he's genuinely hilarious, and it feels like you spend most of the class just chatting with him, BUT, you get more work done than you would in most other classes, he makes everything easy to grasp. His grading is a little tough but it's completely fair and his feedback is great.

Dr. Weiss is truly amazing! I entered this class having to relearn everything from high school, and though he can be classified as a tough grader, he does it to truly challenge your writing. His feedback is extremely helpful and he's hilarious! If you take this course, prepare to put in the work. But it's all worth it in the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Weiss is a funny guy. He's generally pretty chill during his lectures and was very forgiving when it came to attendance and participation. While he can be a tough grader, he does so in an effort to introduce freshman students to their first English course in college. Highly recommended.

Dr. Weiss handled the online learning situation well. He gives great lectures during synchronized meetings. The papers assigned are tough but certainly reasonable. He is a tough grader, but at the same time, he gives feedbacks because he wants you to succeed. He's also really funny, and lectures are pretty humorous with his voice included.

Dr. Weiss was literally my favorite professor this semester. Take his class if you actually want to learn something and get good feedback. I've definitely gotten better as a writer during this class. This class isn't an easy A... you have to work for your grade, however the work is manageable and he'll help you both in and outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Take him for ENGL101 if you actually want to learn something. He's gives really good feedback, but is a "tough" grader so if you don't like that there are a lot of easier professors to take. I went in expecting an easy A with subpar effort but found I actually had to put in work to get high A's. Totally worth it in the end. He's a cool dude.

I had a great time taking Dr. Weiss's class. He relied a lot on the textbook, but it made sense for the course. ENGL101 is an easy A if you use the textbook (I didn't use it). He is a very funny guy even though he tries a bit too hard, but his grading is very good. He is a tough grader but gives great feedback.
You have to work for your grade, but he is always there to help and gives good feedback.
Enjoyable classtime led by a very nice guy, hardish grader though. Expect to work hard for an A, but he is very accessible outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Best professor I've had at UMD. He really cares about his students and will help you with anything you need academic and beyond.

Dr. Weiss is an amazing teacher. Although his grading can be tough at times, he does provide clear feedback on how to improve and even provides the opportunity to revise a paper at the end of the semester. He makes you work but he does provide you with the groundwork and understanding to get a good grade in the class.

I took my first English class with Dr. Weiss. Simply one of the best professors. If you are a good writer, you will definitely get an A. In my case, since I was a immigrant and wasnt that good in English, I still received a B+. Class is fun and he allows you to take extension. Great professor.

Dr. Weiss is absolutely hilarious and makes it enjoyable to attend class. He gives great feedback and you know he is thoroughly reading your assignments, and isn't skimming it. He makes the material we're learning relatable and gives great examples when explaining it. Would definitely recommend taking ENGL391 with him.

May be THE BEST English professor you could ever get. I always looked forward to attending his classes, and English is my worst subject! I did do things a bit last minute so I didn't get an A but I still managed to get a good grade in his class! Highly recommend
Great guy! Would 100% take any class he taught. Very relatable, fair grader, and entertaining professor who goes out of his way to teach material in an engaging way. Take his class!
He is SUPER friendly and funny. Weiss gave me great feedback on my writing while also making me feel comfortable enough to approach him with any questions.
Dr. Weiss is the best ENGL101 teacher, I highly recommend taking his class. Very helpful preparing you for assignments and gives great feedback. Overall, just a nice guy, too!

Apart from giving helpful feedback on papers, Dr. Weiss is just an overall nice guy. Additionally, he seems to be one of the easier teachers for ENGL101. If you put in any noticeable amount of effort, I seriously doubt he'd ever give you less than a B. Write something half decent and it will definitely get an A. Take him if you can.

Dr. Weiss is an excellent professor who is probably reading this right now (Hi Dr. Weiss).  Definitely one of the best to take ENGL101 with at UMD. Dr. Weiss will help you become a better writer and a better thinker in general.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Loved his class! Having him for my first class of the day got me to wake up in the morning. Great and interesting discussions and thourogh feedback on assignments. Shows he cares about student's well-being as well as developing their writing skills. Assigns a lot of readings but I stopped reading them after a while and got by completely fine.

Super cool guy. Loved going to class just to hear what he had to say. Lots of papers but every ENGL101 class has those. Feedback is good and helpful. Definitely would recommend him for anyone to take. You really do have to write well to get a great grade in class. But he doesn't give less than a 80 to anyone who tried.

Dr. Weiss is a solid choice for ENGL101. The class was not very difficult, but there is a decent amount of writing. Dr. Weiss cares a lot about his students. His lectures are very laid back and interesting. He assigns a lot of reading but I never found it necessary to read the assigned readings. Overall, Dr. Weiss is a great prof for ENGL101.

I'm not sure if I learned a whole lot in this class but I really enjoyed having this teacher. The work was manageable and he gave me an extension longer than I asked for when I needed one. He wants everyone to do well and you can tell he's passionate about the subject matter. Nerdy and funny, overall a great teacher to have.
I would say this teacher is kind and u just have to participate in class and focus on what she says cause it might be important for the quiz .I like her she is a awesome teacher.
Harsh grader. Only a 1 credit course. Very boring topic, bad timing
Mrs. White is a wonderful teacher! If you're debating on who you should take for "Step 1" (TLPL101), take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Weil's lectures are some of the most engaging and interesting lectures I've taken in my college career. He really does know his stuff. While there is some reading to do, honestly its pretty optional. The only difficult part of the class are the exams which have about a 60-70% average, but are curved heavily.

Dr. Weil's courses are basically just an opportunity for him to have an audience. He may have been the head of his field at one point but now he's a out-of-touch blowhard. I feel bad for his grad students. I assume he's still around just for the name recognition.

Dr. Weil is a really nice professor, very helpful and understanding when it comes to questions and things of that nature. Honestly, there is a fair bit of homework that takes a lot of time and doesn't count for much so that sucks. Your worst exam grade gets dropped at the end of the semester so that's worth it for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Funny, eccentric teacher. Pretty sure he's one of the top soil researchers in the country and it shows. His tangents while not important to the tests, are really interesting. Make sure to pay attention to his lectures and you don't need the $30 notes book that is offered in the book store. The lab and homeworks help your grade, make sure to do them

This class was an absolute pain. Endless homework, impractical at-home labs that consumed hours, and timed close-note exams. Ray is a nice guy but this class was incredibly stressful, and an unreasonable amount of work. Interesting material, but exhausting and time consuming.

God, I love Dr. Weil. I took him Fall 2020 and I was scared bc of the online semester but he good job transitioning online. The purest man in existence and LIVES for soil. Tests are a little tough, but there are discussions posts u do each class+weekly labs and 2txtbk Q's due each week. The course is curved HEAVILY (currently @ a 77%B+).

Fantastic and hilarious! I never thought I would enjoy a class about soils. He makes hard exams, but they are all multiple choice. Make sure you pay attention during the lecture because the textbook is a beast to read. Lab grade will help you a lot! He reminds me of an older Indiana Jones, but with soil. Would hands down take a class by him again.

Great class. Dr. Weil is one of the top soil scientists in the U.S. and it shows in how passionately he teaches. You learn a TON of very important information about the chemistry/physics/biology of soil and how it relates to ecology and agriculture. Tests and Lab requires a decent amount of effort and memorization, but overall not too difficult.
Soil lab will save your grade. Attend lecture. Do the homework. Friendly professor, but stay interested in the topic in order to grasp the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Look the class is informative, he wrote the textbook and the lecture guide and lab book you have to buy. Lectures are pointless rambles and there was more tedious work in lab than 2 semesters of ORGO and another of Micro Bio combined. If you are interested take it but if not yeesh is this going to be a bad-busy semester for you. TAKE. WITH. CAUTION
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class itself is really hard. I don't understand much still and the tests are really hard. Though his grading scale is largely curved... 50-64 is a C, so if you get 500 of the 1000 points you get a C. Lab was fine and my TA was great. Just depends how you study. Also, go to class and do the pair shares, it counts as extra credit at the end.

Dr. Weil is a very cool guy, knows just about everything there is to know about soils. I am not interested in soils whatsoever, so the class was quite boring and I didn't go. You don't have to go to lecture, just go to labs and learn material before the test. Tests are very hard, 50-64 is a C, 65-79 is a B, and 80+ is an A, so it's not too bad.
Very poor teacher.

Prof Weil is a greta teacher. The class is boring and semi helpful if environmental science is your thing. Not a hard class however the TA's are not good. I had this one TA who you could barely understand cause her chinese accent was too damn thick. And she is a very tough grader. Anywho, the class is impossible to fail.

There are millions of extremely boring activities such as spending half an hour looking how fast water penetrates soil. The professor is a nice hippie but the content of the class is extremely boring which makes it hard to focus!

I don't know how on earth there are negative comments here! Dr. Weil is a great professor, really knows his material (he wrote the textbook- do the reading before class and you're golden), and he keeps the class very multidisciplinary. It's not just a 'dirt class', it's an ecology/biology class, and that is a good thing! Labs took FOREVER though.

Boring class, boring teacher, he always teaches this class at eight in the morning. Has two field trips to farms on saturdays that are just as boring as the class. With all that said, the class is very easy. I slept everyday except exam days and the day I gave a presentation and I still got a B.  If you pay attention at all an A is very possible.

Easy class for a science class.  3 tests and you can drop one so I didn't even have to take the third test.  He gives a study guide before each exam which is exactly what is on the tests.  There is a big curve.  Don't buy the textbook the course packet has everything you need

I hated this class. You will too unless you for some reason have an interest in DIRT! I had no interest whatsoever in soil before taking this class and I still have no interest in soil. Tests are 25 mc and 2 essays. Not too hard just boring! Professor gives lightbulbs to those with the highest test grades. Stupid dirt class

This class blows.  It is so boring and very difficult for an INTRO class!  Hated going to lecture, ridiculously difficult exams, big curve but the grading system makes no sense so I still have no idea how I'm doing.  Lab takes forever, expect to be there the whole time.  Don't take this class if you can get out of it. I'm a B student but may get aD

this is really an ecology class; really nice, always willing to help, uses his own travel pictures in lecture which is interesting, and is really into what he teaches and how you can apply it to everyday life(the TAs weren't that accomidating)

Great Professor... makes soil fun... this class is pretty straight forward and there is not alot of reading or homework... if you go to class, listen, and go to discussion you'll have to review for the 4 test (you can drop one) you'll easily get an A.  There is one project too but there is a great curve

A bit dry in lecture, but occasionally pretty funny. He's getting old so he loses track of his thought process at times. Very chill grader, you can tell he values critical thinking above 100% accuracy. The books he assigns are great. And attendance is whatever if you know your stuff. Wrote me a recommendation even though I slacked and got a B
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Way too much reading of books and documents.  Very vague when it comes to explaining what will be on exams.  Seems like a nice guy, just not a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Hottie

I really enjoyed this class and would highly recommend it.There is a lot of original document reading involved, which can be tedious at times. Having said that Prof. Ridgway is the nicest guy ever and he is the main reason I enjoyed this class. Quite a bit of work but if you put the effort in it's an awesome class with a great professor.

This class is VERY Hard. You will never stop reading! We read 6 whole books, and that doesn't include the numerous solo documents. That being said, he is wonderfully nice. Takes discussions during lecture very seriously, so come prepared. I'm terrible at History, but I learned so much in this class and he is very helpful.
No Comments

he is a fair grader and although attendance is not mandatory i really recommend you go to class as much as you can as not everything is on the slides, if you have any questions go speak to him during office hours, that helped a lot. overall great professor i took many of his other courses and they were all worth it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
He knows his stuff. Very academic, expects students to know architecture terms.
Lecture is the main important thing in the class. If you take notes, and keep track of the vocab in the textbook, exams are easy.
1 research paper project.
Prof. can be hard to reach by email; seems really busy. But usually available in office hours and happy to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Prof. Williams clearly knows his stuff and is passionate about architectural history. I really respect that he can admit when he does not know the answer to a student's question and will look it up and send what he found out to the class. However, his lectures are often long and can include long tangents. Some content is covered better than other
Excellent professor, very responsive, and genuinely wants to help you pass the course. Weekly reading assignments but he gives a good summary and easy to understand what is expected
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: A caring, excited educator. Easy grader and lenient with students.

He's one of the best professors in this school. He cares about being a good educator, and his interest in the topics comes through. If you actually do readings and participate/ask questions, the class isn't boring at all. He's nicer, more understanding, and more helpful than almost every other professor I've had in my 6 years at this school so far.

Other reviews are accurate. My biggest issue is that he uses big words for no reason. It makes it difficult to understand him. This class has mostly freshmen and sophomores, not historians. He could have such better communication if he just spoke at the level he is teaching. Questions on the exam made no sense just because of how he phrased them.

Lectures seemed to go on for much longer than an hour and fifteen minutes. Lots of long tangents and rants. I also took art history and history classes and I did not get the sense he knew everything he was speaking about enough to be lecturing on it. Some information presented as fact during lecture was questionable, or just not true.
This class was extremely boring! He teaches way to much information and the exams barely relate to what he teaches. I would not recommend taking this class unless you have to.

Overall, this professor was clear about what was expected. You have three tests all open note, weekly reading assignments, and one final paper. Be prepared for a lot of information, and TAKE NOTES. The tests will have things that he displays in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures can be a little long sometimes, if you like history courses then you will like this class. If not, you might struggle. He's very passionate about what he teaches. There's a reading and drawing you have to do for each class and one final paper. The tests are super easy if you have been paying attention to overall themes

He seems like a nice guy, but he's a little too passionate about the topics. The class is dull and he's distracting; it's really hard to know what to focus on when he's gone into such detail. He can be approachable and wants to help students out, but he doesn't answer emails often and I had trouble getting the feedback I needed for the final paper.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't know how he gets low ratings. He lectures a lot, but if you actually pay attention, they're sO interesting and he throws in some actually cool facts. He loves answering any questions and discussing with students. He's the nicest professor I've ever met in the ARCH school. The readings aren't bad, and he's really helpful with the paper.

Professor Williams is very passionate about world history but it is very badly translated through his lectures. Hes very monotone and tends to go out on long rants that are very unnecessary for the class. I zoned out through most of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Williams knows everything there is to know about the material. So much so that he doesn't know when to STOP TELLING YOU THINGS. Dullest, longest lectures of my life. The class and tests were easy. Plenty of textbook reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great story teller uses a lot of coco-cola analogies

Professor Roberton is understanding and knows his topic very well. He doesn't have any lecture notes so the exams are hard to study for. Luckily, he curves heavily so you're able to do just well in this class even if you feel like you're struggling.

the lectures are pretty much just rambles but when you're able to focus, it's interesting and you learn a lot. do the problem sets; the tests are exactly like them. he was an ineffective teacher, but made up for it with a huge curve (passing was around 45%). don't buy the textbook we only used it once the whole semester two ungraded problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: While Professor Williams was certainly very knowledgeable in his field, he doesn't do a good job of explaining concepts. His lectures weren't structured really well as there was no PowerPoints. You would just have to follow along with what he says and wrote down on the board. The class itself was pretty easy, and he records his lectures.

He is amazing, easily the best economics professor I've ever had, and ECON/AREC481 has been one of my favorite classes. His lectures are extremely interesting and engaging and the problem sets prepare you well for the quizzes and exams. He clearly cares deeply about all of his students and is all around an excellent professor!

Rob is a brilliant economist and an okay teacher if you ask the right questions. He rambles a lot in lectures and doesn't give good examples of the math he expects you to know for exams. The problem sets are best way to study for the exams, and if you understand them, you will do fine on the exams which are basicallythe only thing you are graded on
YAIIII CALCULUS. very god teacher...very hyper and enthusiastic about maths..decent exam ..take him
Very enthusiastic about math and his students.  Easy to follow, tests are very straightforward.  Really wants to help his students.  Definitely a good professor.

Dr. Wright is a great professor.  His lectures are very clear and easy to follow and he loves it when people ask questions.  Also, it's very funny how enthusiastic he is about math.  He will do cheers and tell math "jokes."  He's awesome.

Great teacher, you can tell he really loves math. Tends to over explain sometimes, but is very useful when you need help. I always felt comfortable asking questions in class. Will often tell cute stories in the beginning of lecture. Attendance not mandatory, but I missed one lecture and was lost. Make sure you show up to discussion for the quizzes.
Has no concept of how Elms works. Will post assignments online, (not under assignments tab), with no listed due date but will penalize when are not completed on time.

Having only taken her class I'm not sure if she does a horrible job teaching the material or if it was me.  Personally I felt like the tests, which were a huge portion of our grade, were nothing like what was taught in class.  She was really nice and willing to explain in class but it did not help at all with the tests for me.
SHE IS THE WORSE POSSIBLE TEACHER EVER! SHE TEACHES EASIES MATERIAL BUT GIVES HARDEST TESTS! SHE GRADED EXAMS WRONG! AND THEN APOLOGIZED AFTER FAILING HALF THE CLASS! SHE IS TERRIBLE TEACHER@

Professor White is a great teacher. She wants every student to succeed and makes every effort to help them do it. She provides a lot of practice material(extra problems, old exams) to help you prepare for exams. Be prepared exam problems are not the same as the ones practiced in class, but same concepts. Make an effort to study and you'll get an A.

She is very helpful. You have to study when it comes to her exams because they are hard. She provides you many tools for studying. She is a great teached overall. Take her class if you are a hard studying student. She trys her best to make finance as simple as possible. Finance is HARD. Many people change their major becuase of this class.
If you can take someone else take your chances with them. Do NOT take this course if you are a junior/senior who will be having interviews on fridays (in the fall)...they're not excused.

DrWhite is a genuinely nice teacher. She wants you to do well. GO TO CLASS! it is the best way to understand material and examples. Go to her review sessions, they're extremely helpful. Before the class started, i was praying for a B, and got an A+. Get a good group for the project and don't procrastinate for it. If you put in effort you'll do well

She does a very good job with a boring subject.  She is very knowledgeable about the material and eager to help students in any way she can to understand the info.  She's really approachable and actually cares about her students, even in a big lecture.  To do well in the class read the book, attend lecture, and really understand the old exams.

Good teacher. I went from thinking I would barely pull off a B to getting an A- in the class. If you dont study or go to class it is obviously going to be hard and youre going to think shes a bad teach. Do old exams and understand review problems.
I LOVE DR. WHITE!

OMG...what a hard class.  Studied like crazy and still failed the tests.  Had a horrible group that did nothing and got screwed on the group project as well!  MOST IMPORTANT LESSON LEARNED: go over old tests and memorize!  Wish I had figured this out sooner in the course.  You must get used to her impossible questions!

what were you talking about?she is the best. she is the most helpful prof I ever had. she gave review sheet, answered all questions, and even had review time before the exam. what else she needed to do? many students received an A in this class. you should drop out school if you get bad grade in this class.
extremely boring, her test reviews manage to cover everything she doesnt test on, do what someone else said, take it in the summer and with anyone else

THIS CLASS IS EXTREMELY HARD!! She's a nice person, but No ONE understood her during lecture because she would lecture so fast. She expects you to know the material already and she has the softest voice that will put you to sleep. I recommend taking it in the summer with someone else!!!

This class is FREAKing HARD. She is BORING as hell but if you like teachers with a low mono-toned voice be my guest. One word "STUDY" or your screwed. Class??? f**k that Study the material your self its better and GO TO REVIEW !!!!
Her class is hard and she is sooo boring that it's almost imposible to stay awake during her class!!
sHE'S NICE BUT REALLY BORING!!!!!! iT'S IMPOSIBLE TO LEARN BECAUSE SHE IS SOOO BORING!!!

Her voice is like a lullaby, she speaks softly and puts you to sleep, if you're not interested in finance.  For the most part you can study the book and do fine but if you are clueless to the subject, go to class.  FACE TIME HELPS with her. GO TO THE FRIDAY SECTIONS and keep your cheat sheet for each quiz so you can make a master sheet for the fina

She's extremely helpful. I have emailed her several times with questions and she's responded very quickly. Helpful for office hours too. Wants you to do well. Class can be boring. She knows the material very well though and conveys it pretty well. Go to lectures! DO EXTRA CREDIT!

Ignore the last comment posted.. She is probably THE most helpful and encouraging teacher I have had in my academic career. I went from a C to an A in a matter of 3 weeks.  She WANTS her students to ask questions and do well. She REALLY cares about you learning in the class. Take her course if you have the chance!!!

She is so nice, but she can't teach anything worth crap. I eventually formed a study group and we stopped going to class. We studied the chapters, and then did the practice tests she puts online and memorized the answers to them and how to do them. Using your TA's for help is also really beneficial. I went from a 45 on the first exam to 95-100

Professor Worsnop is incredible. He is patient and very generous with his time. I went to his office hours countless times, and he explained numerous concepts with clarity. While there are no textbooks, there are pre-recorded videos (by him) for you to watch before class, which are very helpful. You will be well-versed in R at the end of semester.

Professor Worsnop is an amazing Professor! Entering grad school with a different major than undergrad, I do not have a background in Stats. But, after attending his office hours a few times, I have been able to learn and understand the concepts! He really breaks it down well. In addition, his lectures are great . If you suck at Stats, TAKE HIM!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Worsnop is an incredible professor. He really cares about his students and is the kind of professor that wants students to learn what they *need* to learn from stat without having it have to be their number one priority during a pandemic. He put so much time in creating resources for learning the material and is a great teacher.
I was not able to understand what he was saying in class.
Very knowledgable and caring. Pays attention to what students learn.

His lectures are hard to follow as he rushes and mumbles through slides, barely teaching anything. Trying to learn DBMS in his class feels like watching a sped-up Marvel trailer and being asked to summarize the entire universe. He's not a mean professor, but his teaching style needs a major overhaul to be effective.

The professor's teaching style is, unfortunately, very hard to follow. The pace of lectures is extremely fast, leaving little time for students to fully grasp the material. Additionally, a strong accent makes it challenging to understand key concepts, often resulting in confusion and frustration.

I got into a car accident that resulted in surgery and had to miss class for 1.5-2 weeks. When I reached out to him explaining what had happened he asked me if I was able to do my online assignments in bed in order to expedite my studies because the program is hard. 0/10 professor everyone complains about him and rightfully so!!!

The wrost prof in MSBA program. Boring lectures and unclear grading criteria, sometimes you get points deducted for not doing the things implied, and other times for not EXACTLY following the instructions. I stop caring about this class in late semester because it gives me nothing but headache. It is a shame that a useful class was taught by him.
its difficult and hard to communicate with him

I like his class. He's not super energetic, but he's good at getting everyone to practice. At first, it can be boring, but when we start using software, it gets fun. Python can be tough if you only rely on his teaching. My suggestion would be to learn the theory beforehand join in on the activities in class, and do some studying outside of class.
HE SHOULD QUIT TEACHING
Super unprofessional and terrible at teaching, one of the worst professor in my life

I would rather throw my money down the drain than take his class. Learned absolutely nothing through the course as he just gave high-level information on various topics but never really explained 1 thing well. It would have been better to focus on quality instead of quantity.
THE MOST TERRIBLE EXPERIENCE IN MY LIFE!!!
Do not waste your money and time unless it is mandatory course.
Do not take it if it is not a required class for you. You def have much better options.

You are wasting your tuition fee if you choose his course. Lecture was heard to understand from every aspect. I think I can be a professor if all I need to do is reading the powerpoint with nobody understood. Thank you, University of Maryland.
Professor Lee is knowledgable. He well explained DBMS and SQL. Great course and Great professor.

Prof Lee is pretty nice and extremely knowledgeable. He always knows the answers to your questions right when you ask. The class is set up very fairly with in-class acts and labs to practice problems, but the final still sneaks up on you. But overall, you have to do a lot of work on your own time to do well.

He is not a good professor. Yes he's knowledgable and nice, but not so great at explaining. Basically, think of it as having to put more effort than needed in the class because he makes simple concepts hard. The class itself isn't hard IF you're willing to teach yourself. His lectures are one of the WORST ever. Esp if u have trouble concentrating!!

I really liked taking this class with Professor Lee! The classwork/homework is not too difficult at all, and you receive a ton of feedback before you have to turn in the project. The final was also super fair. Overall, I would definitely recommend Professor Lee for BMGT402! He is a great professor and wants to see his students do well.

Clearly very knowledgeable but you have to put in double the effort by trying to decipher what he is saying and learn the material at the same time. He's also very nice and responds to email promptly. But you're gonna have to do ALOT of your own research in order to do well on HWS. There is only one final exam at the end, and it's tmrw for me RIP

He is actually not as bad as other students said. His PPT slides are clear and help students understand the course material. He does have an accent, but you can still understand him as long as you pay attention in class. I think he is a good instructor, and you can learn a lot from the course if you put in effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Awful teacher through and through. Accent is so thick I can't understand half of the stuff he says, doesn't really answer questions in class, and won't answer emails. Lecture slides are incomplete and he hasn't even tried to adapt to the online environment.

I registered late & his class was the only one available & now I know why. It's simply terrible! I'm sure he's intelligent and competent but NOT as a professor. I can't understand a word he's saying due to his extremely thick accent. But even disregarding that, he makes things extremely difficult. Doesn't explain properly. HWs are so hard. AVOID!!!
AWFUL, worst teacher @ UMD. Why me! Dont let this be you too!
Waste of my money

Worst instructor I've had. Not clear at all, gives horrible lectures, and gives no structure to the course. Lacks professionalism you would expect from an instructor as well. I do not recommend anyone taking his course and think he should not be able to teach undergrad or grad students.

Had to put this in because someone left him a five star. Easily worst professor I've had at UMD. Accent is extremely thick and it is hard to understand him. Gets frustrated with the class if everyone is confused, which accounts for 90% of the time. Makes simple VBA concepts extremely difficult. Don't take him if you can avoid it.

reviews.comment: Adam is a great professor. His lectures are pretty standard, but his slides are very useful for doing hw and projects. Projects can be challenging but you really learn a lot. Overall a great dude.
So nice and all the assignments were easy. She was always so understanding. Definitely take a class with her if you have the chance.
Great Teacher, the class was a lot of fun and I learned a lot. If you get the chance to take her before she leaves, do it.

Carly was a great teacher! She was super helpful especially when in-person class abruptly ended and we went remote. While the work is challenging it was very rewarding and I would definitely take another course with her again!!

Hours of homework for an entry level art class. Graded on very few things so you can easily fail. Each portfolio can make or break your grade, and late submissions are a zero. I attended nearly all of the classes, but the class before the first portfolio/spring break was cancelled by the professor, so I couldn't submit it in time, Ended up failing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weird to force us to her show at class time. Honestly just to have people go and not for us to learn. Her excuse was for us to learn how gallery works but it's not in this class syllabus. In class is more abt critiques + know other artists than to have time to draw/ work. It's good if you are new to it, but pointless if you alrdy took art classes.

Professor Wyszomirska was great in person. Her feedback in class helped me grow my knowledge in the different drawing styles. The portfolios you create throughout the semester really matter and can impact your grade, remember to save all your work. Her at home assignment feedback was not the best, they were vague and did not help me improve.

Professor Wyszomirska understood that everyone was at different levels of experiences with art but still graded very fairly. As long as you actually put effort into your projects, you will do well. She often pushed back the due dates on assignments to make sure we had time. I felt like I learned a lot about the process of drawing through the class.

An excellent professor. She gives really great projects that challenge you and help you develop your own approach. You're encouraged to experiment, and although there's a decent amount of work, it all comes together and you'll want to keep creating when the semester is over. There's no textbook, but there are some good readings and videos.
good professoreasy A as you do all things she asked you to do
This is a straight A course as you do try and go to the course. She is a nice professor

absolutely loved this course! it was only 3 weeks long but I really feel like this was one of the most currently applicable psych classes I have taken so far. The work felt purposeful- I actually enjoyed the reflection papers a lot. If you need a summer/winter class, take this! also the TA & teacher were super helpful & responsive :)

I took the class during the winter semester 22, it was easy as long as you took the time to complete the assignments. Every day there was a lecture video, an article, and a discussion or reflection. In addition to a quiz on Fridays which was very straight forward as long as you take notes. I really learned a lot and especially useful information.

Dr. Wydra is so sweet and the class was really easy. You just watch lectures/videos, read an article, and complete a paper/discussion. It's all pretty simple and the quizzes are only like 20 questions and if you took notes during lecture you'll know everything.

his lectures were so boring, and the ta's were such tough graders. the exams were challenging. he just goes over so freaking much, it's so hard to keep up. also, you'll do fine without the textbook, i never once read it. but, very challenging course, ended with a c and trust me, i tried.
He is very passionate about the subject and clears up all misconceptions. I found the lectures to be somewhat boring, but his explanations are useful!

pretty okay professor, he posts all his slides, so if you miss class it's not a big deal, but very lecture heavy and you have so much content thrown at you. exams were a bit challenging and textbooks were pretty useless in my opinion.

He is a great lecturer who knows his material really well. There was 5 pop quizzes with the lowest grade dropped. Pretty straightforward if you did the readings (2 court syllabuses and a chapter). There was also 3 papers that I put a lot of work into and thought were pretty hard. However, I thought everything was graded fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Great class overall. You have to be on your toes from the beginning. Only two midterms so very little room to slip up. Pop Quizzes in discussion that are heavily based on the textbook readings. Term paper is the most time consuming but he gives a month to work on it and an extra credit opportunity with it. Grades fairly, cool intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This is my second time taking Wohlfarth and I appreciate his teaching style. Very straightforward and outlines clear criteria to do well in his class. My only recommendation is to not procrastinate the short papers like I did. I wasn't really paying attention to deadlines and then I had to grind all three out in two days-not fun. Overall great prof
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: While I appreciate that the professor uploads the lecture slides online, going to class is a waste of time to have the professor spend half of the lecture reading quotes from opinions to you. Grades the short papers harshly,  though you WILL NOT get feedback, minimal if asked, on how to improve. They will be graded at the last possible minute.
His class is genuinely interesting and he gets really into the material. There is a pretty straightforward midterm and final, three papers, and one group project.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: GO TO DISCUSSION. it sucks but there will be pop quizzes that are your only grade in canvas until the last quarter of the semester. he is fine but the lectures go by very fast. you should go to class but it is not 100% mandatory if you study really well for the midterm and final. tests are only a lil hard if you study a lot - still a lil tho
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is extremely interesting if you like learning about the U.S. Supreme Court and government. Professor Wohlfarth is an amazing professor who cares about his students. This class does have pop quizzes during discussion, however I found these to be easy if you re-read your notes. I highly recommend this class and this professor.

Wohlfarth's lectures are bread. They're standard. They're kinda boring. They're what you'd expect. Grades mostly rely on TAs, so results may vary. My TA... wasn't the best. So beware about that. Regarding tests, they can be confusing and worded in a weird way. This wasn't the worst class in the world but it wasn't the best either.

I liked Prof. Wohlfarth. Lectures and tests are strongly correlated which is a plus, but wording on MC exam q's was confusing sometimes. A few quizzes throughout the semester, three exams, and a paper. Overall not much work except studying, and lectures were clear and helpful for exams. Attendance not mandatory, but definitely helpful.

Lectures are very useful but not recorded. Class is pretty easy if you go. It's just 3 exams on the lectures (60%), the paper (20%), and quizzes announced in lecture the week of (15%) + 2 surveys (5%). Reading wasn't super necessary. One was more of a suggestion as he just follows it in lecture, and the other was only necessary on quiz weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Wohlfarth was an awesome lecturer, very informative, and has a clear structure to his course. There are several short papers (2-3 pages) throughout the course and has a group project. So if that's not your thing, beware. The TAs are the main interaction you have and he's not the best at responding to student emails/requests.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Wohlfarth is a great professor who really knows what he's talking about. He's very patient and answers questions thoroughly. We didn't have a ton of assignments throughout the semester though so I suggest taking every assignment and quiz pretty seriously if you want to do well. Overall, great class to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I highly recommend Professor Wohlfarth. Very passionate about his content, quizzes are fair and he outlines everything you need to know form them, and the exams are also very fair and he is a generous grader.
Amazing lectures and great guy. Respects his students and answers every question with patience

Amazing lecturer. Really knows what he is talking about. Enthusiastic and is clear about each topic. Midterm exam was about what I expected. Pop quizzes in discussion which sucked but weren't terrible. The lowest is dropped thank god. I really enjoyed going to his class and he used the powerpoint as a guide instead of fully relying on it.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He knows exactly what he's talking about and is very good at explaining material. Two exams, four short papers, and a group "oral argument". Not hard, very informative. Don't take it unless you're into constitutional law.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Wohlfarth is a very passionate guy who loves what he teaches. Even though he posts his slides online 10 minutes before the lecture, so you don't have to go, I still went to every class because he was enjoyable to listen to. The TA's that I had in this course were also awesome and extremely helpful. It's a great course and he's great too.

Go to lecture, read the book, and always be prepared for a quiz on your discussion readings. Your TA will be very important in the class as they grade everything you do. Professor Wohlfarth was dry at times, but I blame that on the material as he would occasionally used anectdotes to keep our attention. He's a good teacher and lectures help you.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: If you don't go to lectures, you won't fully understand what is going on. Professor Wohlfarth makes it interesting!

Patrick is a great professor because he's really into government which makes you really want to learn about it too. It's obvious he wants you to do well. He offers a few extra credit opportunities and flexible office hours. If you go to lecture, discussion, and do the readings you shouldn't have trouble doing well.
Dr. Wohlfarth is the best. Very cool guy

Completely unhelpful. All his grading is done via his T.A.'s. When I tried to appeal to him he ripped my paper apart even more. He's a severe nitpicker. I wrote "six billion dollars" and he crossed out six and wrote 6 crossed out dollars and put a $ in front of the 6. Don't take him if you can help it. You will regret it sooner than later. Promise!

Professor Wyatt is absolutely amazing. I loved his lectures and every time we read a new piece, he shed light on the amazing writing and relevance it contained. He was inspirational and engaging. I also found him incredibly helpful in office hours, he really wants all of his students to succeed. Will definitely try to take more of his classes!
Thinks he is much smarter than he actually is. Once he has a grade hes decided to give you he sticks with it no matter what improvements occur to your work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I would definitely recommend taking Professor Wyatt. He is engaging, insightful, and sincere. If you read the works, write good essays, and participate in class, you will get an A.
I dreaded going to this class after a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Wyatt is extremely knowledgeable. As the course went on, I came to like and respect him more and more. You will learn if you invest in this class. He's one of the best English professors, I'm sure of it.

He's a good teacher, really interesting IF you're an English major. Rewards longer papers. Also, the whole class is discussion, so if you don't talk, don't take it. We literally just sat in a circle and talked all semester. All in all, pretty good.

I did not like him. I don't want dull lectures about life. Do NOT forget your textbook in his class, write essays the way he wants you to, speak a lot in class, and you'll do fine. I wouldn't recommend him for an easy A or interesting class, but not too bad if you HAVE to take 301.

I went into this class an Elementary Ed major and came out an English major. Professor Wyatt is the most engaging, interesting professor I've yet to come across at UMD. Regardless of your major, if you enjoy reading in the slightest, I recommend this course and even more so, this professor.

One of the best professors I've ever had, there's so much to learn from him. He's kind of a tough grader on papers, but aren't all English teachers? He really helped me learn how to become a better writer. My best advice is to do the readings and participate as much as possible-- but most importantly, definitely show up for class!

Look, Wyatt is a nice guy but his lectures are insanely boring.  The people who say his lectures are great are probably English majors who are really into what he talks about.  I would not recommend taking this class if you are trying to fulfill CORE credits.  The reading is not bad but the papers are graded a little too tough.

Amazing, amazing professor.  His comments on what we read transcended the books and made everything so relevant to real life.  His lectures were full of insightful life lessons.  You can tell he's such an intelligent person and really cares about what he's teaching.  TAKE THIS CLASS!  Besides all of this- it's easy!!
I love this man. If you're passionate about learning, please take him!

I liked this class a lot. 2 papers, midterm and final. Discussions are mandatory but they get cancelled a lot. There are a few pop quizes but they're really easy. Books mostly are interesting and if you don't finish them its fine as long as you have some notes from lecture or use sparknotes. I would definitely recomend it!

i never read the books, but i went to every lecture and took good notes. one midterm, one final, both open book open notes. quizzes in discussion. def suggest taking this class IF you're going to attend lecture.  he knows what he's going to say so its not hard to follow, he doesn't take ?s in lect.

Spectacular. Grad school course: didn't speak for first hour, wrote down things students said, then used our comments to say what he wanted to about what we'd read. I couldn't believe it kept working all semester.
I absolutely loved this professor.  His lectures were wonderful.  He was very passionate throughout all the lectures.
I agree with the other review. He's a great prof and I really love his class.

I love this class and Wyatt is such a great prof. He's so passionate about his teaching, and amazingly clear. He is very helpful too, and takes all his students seriously. It's as if he sees us as just as important as the writers we're reading. Take as many classes as you can with him! You'll really love them.
Homework wasn't easy - gave a lot of hints. Exams prepare us for the qualifier exam. Used the book a lot. Sometimes explanations were difficult. But overall good teaching. Learnt a lot.
He's a nice guy.  Will help you however possible in office hours.  Immaculate english, sense of humor.  I'd recomment him.  I got an A and didn't put in a whole lot of effort.

Ji is one of the best physics professor at UMD. Ji is not only a funny guy, but actually teach physics. His exams (including finals) aren't cumulative, and is based off homework. My best advice is do the sample problems in the book and the homework he gives you, and you should get an easy A.
he is good in explaining ideas... interesting

He has very good english, something some professors lack.  Homework was the hardest part of the class, but thats because the textbook was hard to understand at times.  His teaching of the material was very understandable.

Nice professor and tries to make material clear for students. She could try and be more assertive in class, people would often talk or openly text while she was trying to lecture and it was distracting.

Xiaoli Nan is one of the nicest teachers I've ever had. She is very understanding and accommodating to students. She explains everything really well and creates an environment where it is easy to excel and you learn a lot. I would definitely recommend this class or any with this teacher!!
Nice enough, needs to be more strict w/ class, students seem to always try to walk all over her. But she has high knowledge and great interest in Communication.

Professor Nan is great! She just transferred here from Wisconsin. She is so nice and so helpful. She takes attendance in the class so that's the only drawback. You have 2 "quizzes" where she tells you what will be on them, and one 15 page term paper. Good class. One of the best at UMD.
Such a harsh grader. I have had to redo almost all of my assignments and some I had to redo several times. Feedback is not very clear either.

If you can, avoid her. Her grading is really petty and outrageous. I have two TA's and they are literally the only reason why I am even passing. They grade most of the day to day stuff but it all comes down to the major assignments. The timeline is unrealistic as well, they expected us to write a proposal in a week and a half research and all.

She does not know what she wants to say. Horrible grader and think that people have no other class except her English class. Don't take her. I never had a problem with writing before taking her class. Impossible  during the entire semester.
She is amazing and sweet, definitely recommend her!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I feel this class is unnecessarily difficult due to the sheer workload you are expected to complete. on my 1st week of joining the class, I was expected to read and analyze 42 pages followed by writing 3 essay papers, a cover letter resume, and a personal statement as well as multiple discussion sessions. as a gen ed course, this is excessive.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I've never really had a problem with writing research papers/essays until I took Professor Yaqub's class. She grades very harshly and the feedback she provides is pretty vague. She's an incredibly nice person but makes her professional writing class a lot more strenuous than it should be. I would avoid taking it with her if you can
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class is supposed to be a lot of work, but not particularly hard work. I have talked to my classmates, and we all are putting in levels of work that do not at all reflect the grades we are getting. The advice we receive in response to our papers is basic at best and ultimately unhelpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Andy is a godsend, especially during online school and the pandemic. He assigns readings that are engaging and reasonable in length. Always understanding and helpful. Took his class for a GenEd and it was the highlight of my semester.

Andy is a fantastic professor who really cares for his students and purposefully makes lectures engaging and relevant to pop culture. There is a fair amount of reading and papers but the books are ones you want to keep reading. He is a gem of a professor you should absolutely take any of his classes.
Great guy. Super responsive and makes sure everyone knows what they need to do. You would have to try to get a bad grade to receive one.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dear Michigan Students, He is funny, take him if you want a laugh. Best, A student from UMD

*Took this class online because of Coivd. Dr. Yeo is hilarious and is really chill. He's very easy going and is not a stickler. You still learn stuff but it's all really easy, and if you need to email him he responds quickly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took this class for gen ed even though I wasnt interested in a stem major. Even though I wasnt interested in the content itself, I highly recommend him for fire students. The class is extremely easy and hes so lenient with deadlines and grades. He always gives feedback on assignments and allows us to resubmit. Hes truly amazing!

Very friendly and caring professor. Determined to set us up for success. Even when classes became online, he worked hard to make sure we have an optimal learning experience. I highly recommend the AUSS stream!
Hilarious and admired professor. Easily the best professor you can take for first semester of FIRE, as the class and material itself is rather unbearable. Gives great feedback for group work.
Group projects are really fun. He is really funny and holds amazing lectures. He's willing to help with whatever you ask him to and will always make your day better!
Great professor :) loved his class and he gave great advice and cared so much about his students! Do recommend!

First semester freshman here and I had Derrick as my Fire120 instructor. He quickly became my most favorite professor at UMD. He is friendly, caring and understanding. If you are late to submit your assignment, hell give you an extended deadline, if you have a proper excuse, without hesitation. Strongly suggest students take him

Derrick is a great professor who cares about his students and basically lets you pick and manage your own project. He gives you advice throughout but a lot of it is hands on learning with your group. He is also a great person to go to for help with other classes or advice in general.

Dr. Yeo is an amazing professor. He respects his students and is very approachable. He is very friendly and is easy to talk to. He is also a very dedicated RC Hobbyists and is the faculty sponsor for RC Flying Terps the drone club on campus. Would highly recommend taking his FIRE Stream.

There are weekly quizzes and 3 huge tests. If I tried a little harder then I would've gotten an A. This class is pretty easy especially if you have taken a calc class before. The professor and TA are very helpful if you don't understand something!

Was a great instructor. As long as I paid attention in lecture, I didn't have to do much outside work. She's not a professor yet and was very humble about it. Wanted students t succeed, and respected us.

Sarah is a good teacher and wants you to understand the material. For this class, the quizzes and exams slightly vary from Levermore's, so that makes it harder to know exactly what will be on them. However, I still thought everything was fair, and I would definitely take her again.

Yeakel was a great choice. Her tests are crazy hard, but she prepares you for them. She's a really good explainer, and wants you to ask questions to make sure everyone understands the content. I ended up getting an A+ in the class. I worked for it (I'm not naturally good at math), but it's definitely doable.

Great professor! She goes through material at a good pace and stops to explain things. There is a lot of homework, but the problems do help you for the exams. Exams are difficult as well but if you go over notes and the practice exam you'll do well. Discussion section helps a lot too.

She's an amazing professor and does a great job at explaining. At the end of each class you have a good understanding of the concept. Discussion helps because it's a review of what was learned in class. There is a lot of homework, but enough time to do it. Her exams are hard, but if you study old exams and go into office hours you should do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: worst math teacher i have ever had. not even close. makes exams extremely difficult and creates problems much more complicated than any examples shes been over in class. she also decided to change the weights of our grades a week before finals, which dropped everyones average by 9 points. thought i had a 91 only for it to be changed to a 82. awful
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I mean it's a math class at UMD so what do you expect. Her lectures are very boring and not helpful but youtube and math success will be your best friend. I have seen improvement from my exam scores ever since. The average for exam scores is around 70-78 %. I will say her exams are very hard but doable if you do a lot of practice problems

Yeakel is not awful but wouldnt recommend her at all. She explains things well but doesnt give examples that are at all similar to the exam, and shes terribly boring. The lecture hall is always empty. If youve taken calc before, showing up to class is useless. Exams are hard though, and lots of homework and weekly quizzes. Julian is a great TA

Professor Yeakel is a great teacher. She paces through the subject at a normal pace and stops lecture to answer any questions the class has. She also offers many examples of each topic in class so you get a good grasp of every topic in Calculus. The test themselves are moderate and sorta difficult, but there is decent curve. Id def recommend her
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Sarah is a fantastic teacher and will stop for every single question a student has, will take ample amount of time to answer these questions, and will speed up or slow down lectures based upon how we absorb the material. She is a great teacher who thoroughly teaches each concept. Her tests are very hard so you must really work for your grade.

Prof. Yeakel is a good math professor. Although I did bad in the class it was 100% my fault 0% hers. She is very clear in her expectations. She stops lectures to answer student questions and never hesitates to slow the pace of lecture. Just shoot her an email and she has many available time slots to go over work. Work hard and you'll receive an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Prof Yeakel is amazing at explaining the material. If you do the assigned homework you are likely to do well in the class. Use the testbank for exam preps because they are fairly tricky. Sarah made math fun for me and I really appreciate the detail she went into explaining the concepts. She is much better than the alternatives at UMD.

Dr. Yeakel is great. Her tests are hard and her homework can be difficult at times but it is all to prepare you for the final which would be difficult if you did not have her as a teacher. In addition, she is very friendly and always willing to help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Tests were very lengthy and difficult but similar to the homework, which was also lengthy. She's nice and tries hard for everyone, but she is hard to keep up with in lectures as she talks pretty fast. Her tests are the hardest I've seen for this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was a difficult class with a lot of new concepts to learn, but she is a really amazing teacher. Her lectures and notes were very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Yeakel makes you work for your grade, but if you're good at math and a fast learner, you'll be fine. Her lectures are fast but if you don't go, you'll get behind. I didn't use my textbook ONCE... but you needed the code for homework online. The textbook is really just for practice problems or if you don't understand lecture material.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Yeakel is a good person in general, but she is very straight face and teaches in a very fast pace. If you haven't taken math in awhile, I wouldn't recommend you taking her class. You learn like a thousand things in one class and you're expected to know everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. He gives solid lectures that make you understand the material and he knows when he's not doing so hot, so he will re explain. The exams are handwritten code, which is no bueno but he makes sure that the TA's grade on logic and not syntax. Overall one of the best engineering professors I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great professor who is passionate about the subject matter in this class. Very well structured lectures and supplemental material makes learning the subject matter natural. The class was extremely relevant to me as a computer engineer and the projects were difficult but very relevant and engaging. Do yourself a favor and start on them early.

Dr. Yeung was very willing to work with me. I skipped the introduction class to programming in C because of computer science in high school.  I never used C before, but Dr. Yeung's willingness to help and clear lectures allowed me to pass the class easily.

Programming is hard, especially if you don't really "get it." Professor Yeung is extremely challenging, but his lectures are clear and he is extremely patient and helpful when students don't understand. He is also a very easygoing, approachable person, and his lectures are generally light-hearted and moderately-paced.

Good teacher, hard to come across good programming teachers. He sometimes goes a little slow, but he is clear. His tests are open note and open book. His projects are challenging, definately go to him for help if you need it.

Yla is very smart but her test, homework questions are written in a very confusing way. She is considerate when grading, but her teaching methods are not great. The assignments are not written well and cost a huge chunk of your grade for small mistakes. Her assistance on assignments is hit or miss.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Tausczik really knows how to teach and care for the students. The exams are open note, which is very helpful, there shouldn't be a reason you would do poorly. For her first time teaching this course, she was awesome.

Professor Tausczik is a great stat professor. She is more than willing to help students succeed in class. Although her exams are open note, you need to do your part to adequately prepare for them, as they are worth a majority of your grade. There are only 2 tests and a final so STUDY!!!!

Absolutely one of the most enjoyable electives I've ever taken. I got an A by attending lectures and involving myself with the content. It was easy to develop a passion for what Professor Yonkos was lecturing about. He made things enjoyable with funny stories and related them to much of our daily lives. The tests were online and somewhat difficult.

This man is great at giving lectures. Attendance isn't mandatory however, lectures are extensive, and exams may have questions about something he said during a specific lecture, so I don't recommend skipping a lot. No homework, but grades mostly come from discussion assignments, so attend, participate and keep up with the course content.

Professor Yonkos gives a lot of notes. Each lecture is about 30-40 slides of notes. And sometimes exams can be very hectic, but there are extra credit questions. Also there is a reading and quiz every week for discussion. But aside from that, he's a really cool and a flexible grader. He's also very easy to reach.

I took ENST233 online with Dr. Yonkos and the lectures were uploaded and the beginning of every week. We had timed quizzes on Thursday mornings that were no more than 10 questions and then there was an optional zoom class at 9:30. Discussion was mandatory and we did group work for participation grades. There was one essay and a presentation.

You really don't need to go to class. All lecture slides are posted meaning you can studying everything a few days before and get an A on the tests. There is a paper in discussion and one group presentation. Very easy and interesting class.
Took ENST233 and scored an A. If you show up to class and just pay attention to what he explains in class you'll get an easy A.

ENST 233 is like the feeling of waking up in the morning and getting a text on your phone that school has been canceled due to snow. AMAZING! Professor Yonkos is the man and if you need a DSNS I cannot recommend this class more. He gives out a study guide before tests so just use it to guide you through reviewing the slides he sends out. Easy A!

Dr. Yonkos is a caring professor and know what he is talking about. There are two midterm exams and a final. One research paper and one group project. It is a nice course to take for non-STEM majors looking to fulfill the non-lab science gen ed requirement. Overall is a lot of material to understand but keeping up with the lectures is the key.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The tests were okay if you review the powerpoints. Theres no homework besides a paper and a group presentation. The teacher himself is great and approachable. Overall, this is an easy class.

I've learned more in Lance Yonkos's ENST class than I've learned in any other class in my life. Yonkos is a great teacher. He is smart, logical, funny, and passionate about what he does.   Show up to class, learn the information, and you'll pass. The tests aren't gimmes, but they are very reasonable and no trick questions or anything.

Great guy but he talks a lot and often flies through Powerpoints. He prepares too much material that's meant to fit into one class period, so doesn't always get through everything he wanted to discuss. Lectures are posted on ELMS and textbook isn't needed. One midterm and final. Discussion has a paper, group presentation, and participation points.

Dr. Yonkos is an amazing professor. He explains everything thoroughly and doesn't bog you down with too much homework. There's one paper and one group project which is always annoying, but it's not a bunch of work. You learn a LOT of good info and the tests are very fair and straightforward. Would definitely take other classes with him.

Yonko's is great! His exams are pretty straight forward, use the study guides, go to class & take notes. He also posts lectures in case you miss. Study the red starred items even if they aren't on the study guide!! Most of them are on the exam. I plan on taking Yonko's again in the future!

Dr. Yonkos is a great professor. He provides study guides and is willing to set aside office hours for students for extra help with exams. He provides plenty of examples to get the main idea across to students. His presentations and lectures are very clear, informative and are full of information.

He was very friendly and a good guy to listen to. It is also nice how he posts his lecture slides online in case you need to refer back.  Also prepared you for his exams so you knew exactly what was on them.
He makes it interesting, definitely knows his stuff.  His tests were very easy as long as you look over the lecture slides he posts online, very approachable and funny guy.
Love him! Super funny, clear power points, great study guides with all you need to know about the test. Recommend for non-science majors.

Yonkos is great. He is very clear in lecture and he is very nice and helpful.
