He is willing to answer any questions you have, and he tells you almost everything that you will need for the exam on the lecture slides.This class involves a lot of memorizing and reading, but put a little effort in and pay attention in lecture and you're gonna be fine.

So I haven't taken Dr. Yotsukura for a regular class, but she ran the Language Partner Program and I would 100% recommend it for any SLLC majors or minors!! The workload is very light (1-2 hours a week), and it is a non-intimidating way to practice your speaking and listening abilities

She is very patient with students and definitely reaches out to students who need help. She has helped me many times throughout the semester, not only with class but also with my (numerous) questions about the Japanese program / major at UMD.

She obviously knows her stuff. If you have a question about anything she'll answer it correctly. One thing I didn't like was that she randomly calls on students during lecture, which I believe should be reserved for the interactive classes. If she see's you're struggling she will reach out to you.
Missed a few classes, but otherwise an easy A.

Not too bad. As long as you do a little bit of the readings and participate in class she'll like you, which goes a long way. Her tests aren't really that hard if you study the terms in the book. She also misses a lot of classes, which I guess good or bad depending on your viewpoint.
bias demanding teacher DO NOT TAKE HER!

Toughest grader I've ever seen, but generous curve. Mediocre at explaining material. Lectures don't always match textbook. The class had a low average on one midterm, and she claimed it was due to nobody studying hard enough in a condescending e-mail--despite test review materials just listing types of problems--nothing on how to solve them
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Tough exams. The class averages were consistently in the high 60s. Its one of those frustrating classes where amount of work put in doesnt translate to a high grade. Her lectures are uninspiring and treats the class like review. Avoid if you can. Otherwise you better hope you get a good TA.

Most people that rated her bad did not get a good grade in her class. She's not the best professor and there are obvious needs for improvement, such as her accent making it hard to understand some parts of the lectures, but honestly just pay attention and stay up-to-date on your work and you'll be fine.
Not a good lecturer, but class is not too hard if you have a good TA.
The lectures were difficult to understand. The stuff that was taught during the lectures was rarely on the worksheets. The TA mostly taught us during the discussion section.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you haven't taken calc in high school don't expect to do well. Makes tests unnecessarily long and difficult to finish despite comments from both students and TAs. Doesn't seem to take any clarification questions or complaints seriously and brushes most of them off. The lectures seem to be crammed with textbook review instead of teaching.

This professor was difficult. Learned more from my TA than I did in class most days. Could score in the B/A range on HW and WSs, but did much worse on tests. Delayed giving out midterm grades for about a month until the day after the withdrawal period ended. I did well in high school Calc, and that was NOT the case in this class.
Awful at explaining concepts and don't expect any clarification if you ask questions.

Prof. Kovacheva is not a good math teacher. Very messy handwriting that's hard to read during lecture, and very thick accent that's hard to understand. There's basically an assignment due every day. Homeworks/worksheets aren't terrible, but her exams consist of very difficult questions. Even if you go to class and study, don't expect an A.

Do not, repeat, DO NOT get this teacher. Only teaches directly from the textbook, which means very complicated and confusing lessons, learned more from TA. Delayed grading a major test by 3+ weeks. Assigned two homeworks without telling anyone after consistently only assigning one per night. Wants a C average in her class, refuses to curve tests.

She doesn't actually teach, more just a review of calculus. Her handwriting is tough to read and her accent is hard to understand. Definitely do not take this class if you have never taken calculus before.

Find a different professor if you have not taken Calculus yet. She does not teach and it is hard to understand her because of her accent and terrible handwriting. Treats it as a calculus review rather than actually teaching it.
You cannot slack off in this class, be ready to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She may be good at calculus, but she is awful at teaching it to students. If you have never taken calculus before you will have to teach yourself most things and even if you have you'll still have to teach yourself things. Your expected to remember everything from precalc. Would take any other professor
She treats it like a review rather than teaching the material

She was the worst professor I have had at UMD. Her accent makes her a bit hard to understand, but even if she didnt have it, she would still be a bad teacher. Passive aggressive and kind of rude. Take anyone else literally

Yordanka made things a lot more difficult than they needed to be and her exams were harder than the other sections. She wasn't very considerate of student concerns and was pretty condescending. Lectures were hard, so much hw, discussion worksheets were made difficult on purpose, and even the TAs didn't like her. Definitely skip if you can.
This professor made this class a lot harder than it needed to be. She is possibly the worst teacher Ive had in my entire life. I highly do not recommend her... choose the other professors over her...
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Awful! You cant understand her at all during lectures. She speeds through material and she adds extra hard questions on discussion worksheets and tests. Also if you want to copy her notes, you wont be able to understand her writing that much. Just terrible. Take someone else!

Terrible teacher especially in such a large lecture. She is so hard to understand while she is teaching and is not good at explaining things. She often laughs at the questions asked. She was a first semester teacher in Spring 2020 and was so nervous to talk to students and interact. She works through the material so fast. Take anyone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: 4.5/5. Really good lectures. The only downside was sometimes I didn't understand the feedback. Extremely accessible outside of class and will work with you to understand the material
Excellent teacher

Young is THE GOAT. He teaches everything you need to know, and as long as you read the book and do problems you can get a good grade. He also gives a lot of extra credit, which other professors don't do, and his extra credit helped push my grade up to an A. He also does not give out minus grades so that's a bonus. Overall outstanding professor.
ok professor
Such a fun and joy to be with him for Virtus seminar. The lectures are inspiring and you will learn a lot from them that would help you with your coursework in other core classes. HIGHLY RECOMMEND

Dr. Young's lectures are engaging - as long as you take notes, you have a good chance of understanding everything you need to for the exam. Make sure to complete practice problems - as copying down an example doesn't give you the knowledge you actually need. (Also, he's a big geek, and is very approachable.)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Young is a funny and engaging professor. He occasionally doesn't know what he's talking about and doesn't put much thought into his responses to student's questions, but he's enthusiastic and clear in his lectures.
Tons of extra credit on exams, easy to follow lecturers. You will need the textbook extensively for the steam tables. Overall great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I thought Professor Joshi was the better of the two 726 teachers. I appreciate how he allowed students the opportunity to be in-person or online. He went over all the R material at an understandable pace. With that, the final exam was extremely difficult given the time frame and the fact that this was the first time many students were using R.

The class was very disorganized and inefficient. Examples were not clear and they were confusing. Avoid this professor if you have the chance. Not a good lecturer, doesn't have experience teaching classes, and his final exam will give you anxiety due to the lack of organization and misinformation.
Doesnt give structured lectures. Confusing Lingo.

Ur grade is mostly made by group projects and writing assignments based on readings. No traditional textbook, but u will have to buy a virtual coursepack for the class. However it's like 70 bucks and you might be able to cut down that cost if u can find some of the articles for free online. No exam final. Just do the work& u should get a B at least
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took her class at UMD last year. She is a tough grader and expects you to prioritize this class over other courses.

Professor Roe truly is an amazing professor who cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Her grading is very fair. She gives very good feedback on papers, and is very flexible. She makes arrangements for students whenever they are having issues; she cares a lot about our mental health. Going to class was genuinely fun. Would take again.

Great professor. There is no midterm or final in the class, the class is structured around about 3 main papers you have to write. Professor Roe does give off 'high school vibes' but I 100% prefer that over a boring professor. Class is pretty straightforward and 'easy' to get by.
Like the previous post says, she is nice. However her high school teacher vibes are somewhat annoying. I feel like I'm listening to a child.

Prof. Roe is so warm and welcoming and she genuinely does want all her students to succeed. She give off high school teacher vibes in a college class which honestly is refreshing. She's also very flexible and will take in student feedback and push back deadlines if needed. Would absolutely take her and she is one of my favorite professors.

Dr. Choi is definitely qualified in his field, but he doesn't seem to love teaching. The majority of assignments are graded on correctness on topics never taught in class. It's finals week right now, and about 20% of our assignments have been graded thus far. Dr. Choi means well, but he has the tendency to make you feel dumb for not getting it.

Dr. Choi prepares you for professional science. We learned how to critically plan, execute, and interpret experiments, and importantly, how to recover from mistakes. Do not be intimidated by him! Work hard, participate, and go to office hours. He loved seeing us grow confident enough to teach other students and present at poster fairs.

Even though I did receive a good grade in this class, I wasn't a big fan of professor Choi. He was extremely harsh with this grading comments and kind of made you feel stupid. His instructions weren't very clear, therefore there were a lot of miscommunications throughout the semester. Not great, not awful.

Before you leave umd make sure you take her class. Shes really sweet. Shes really big on participation and its a good way to make yourself known to her. She also encourages A LOT of group discussions. She assigns weekly readings but they are not as bad or long as other classes would be, they just give a nice introduction to that weeks module.

Rachel is amazing. With a school as diverse as UMD she is able to teach the most difficult, touchy topics with the greatest care, taking into account the kind of students she has. Her assigned readings are not that bad, They are essential in what shes teaching and would be discussing. Its really an easy A but you learn a lot too. Glad I took her!

She is the sweetest and most understanding teacher. The only reason I would not take her again is due to the boring and low energy atmosphere of the class. She tends to just assign a bunch of readings and documentaries for homework then have you discuss in small groups during class time while she speaks in the middle sometimes. Very boring.

She is a sweet, very understanding professor. The class was incredibly easy, with no midterm or final. However, I did not learn anything in this class, and feel that sociology classes should probably be more informative. Participation constitutes like 50% of the grade but I skipped frequently and still got an A. Overall very accessible professor.

Yu (Rachel) is one of the kindest and most caring teachers I have ever had. She is accessible almost 24/7. This class was extremely easy; grade was based almost entirely on weekly homework "mini-writing" assignments which are graded easily. Attendance is not mandatory as lectures are unnecessary to pass but Rachel will call you out if she notices.

Group or partner assignments every week in discussion that are hard to complete and everyone's work is compared against each other in grading so it's hard to get an A even if you do everything the assignment asks. Essay's on tests are hard and specific so make sure you do the readings and remember author's names. Posted slides aren't helpful

Group projects & discussions alternate every week(TA grades them ranked against the other groups in the class) Midterms are quite difficult, few multiple choice and at max two essays. Pay attention to EVERYTHING said in class rather the slides bc those are what the exams are based on. Tends to drone on when some things can be quickly explained.

Attendance is optional. She gave out an attendance sheet maybe once during the semester for extra points. Tests are difficult. Based on readings from textbook and lecture notes. TA was more helpful than professor. Be prepared for a group project at the end of the semester. Not difficult at all. Just beware of tests, they are difficult.

The class itself was interesting but she is kind of rude and objectively grades subjective questions so you on papers, if you don't write exactly what she wants to hear, you'll get a C. If you don't know the answer to a question, she makes you feel bad about it, assumes you didn't do the homework and will tell you to figure out the answer yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Good class and interesting so you won't lose focus. The class is designed so if you go to lecture you will do well.make sure you get a good TA, s they will be doing the grading and whatnot
This class was fantastic. It helped me learn a lot. She's really a hip instructor.

This class was amazing. Professor Suzuki was so energetic and enthusiastic it was hard not to be interested in this class. She is not easy, though. She gives a lot but expects a lot from the students. For anyone that wants to learn about the Japanese historical context surrounding its art and artifacts, this is a great class.

I hated this class.  She talks on and on and it's really hard to pay attention and pick out what information you need.  She talks weird too, pauses in weird places and emphasizes strange words.  Tests are completely open-ended and really hard.  You have to go to the lectures because there's no other way to get the info.

He is such an amazing professor! Very understanding and flexible with due dates. Provides really good feedback on assignments which I feel helped me improve tremendously! I would definitely recommend!!!

I had him in my first semester freshman year and he may be one of my favorite professors. He's super friendly and approachable. I went to his office hours a couple times to ask for feedback and he is very helpful and respectful of your ideas. He grades mostly based on completion and effort, so getting a good grade was pretty easy. Would recommend!
He is the best English professor that I have ever had!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Frank is a very nice person. He is very understanding and accommodating with due dates if you communicate with him. The class was very laid back, and a lot of the time was spent receiving and giving feedback on writing assignments with other students. The workload is very manageable and he provides a lot of opportunities for guidance.

Super friendly and caring person. Course is laid out in a way where you get an A unless you miss multiple classes, or very clearly are slacking off. Show up to class and do the assignments and it's basically a guaranteed A. Zach is a very effective teacher and encourages you to ask him for feedback. Coursework is very manageable. Highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I've never had a professor want me to succeed as much as professor Frank. He meets with all his students to provide feedback on each assignment, and you can tell that he spends a lot of time outside of class grading and coming up with meaningful comments that can actually help us improve.

Zach tells you at the beginning that everyone will get an A if you show up, participate a bit, try your best on the assignments, and improve your drafts. Very chill professor and flexible with extensions. Low workload / stress. Gives great feedback for how to improve your writing and always available outside of class before major assignments due
Hands down best professor I've had.

Professor Zach has to be one of the best professors I've taken at UMD! He was really understanding and always receptive to our concerns regarding grading/deadlines. He truly cares about his students and wants you to succeed. I learned a lot without feeling crushed by the stress of assignments, he made ENGL395 genuinely enjoyable :)

Zach was hands down the best professor Ive had at UMD. He is caring, empathetic, and super understanding. He is very easygoing and available to offer extra help if you need it. Not a single mean bone in this mans body. If you get the chance, enroll in his course. He is phenomenal beyond words.

Lectures were unclear most of the time. Handwriting is very bad. If you are able to teach yourself most of the material, you'll do fine. If math is a hard subject for you, then this professor probably won't help.

The class was kinda a mess he had no practice exams and when he did they were always nothing compared to what he tested. Handwriting is absolutely horrible and to me the lecture was just messy. its my first time taking calc and overall the subject is hard on its own.

His handwriting is so bad that you won't know what he is teaching. His exam reviews essentially do not help you at all on any exam- basically teaching yourself. The TA's basically help you so much. On the first week, he'll probably gaslight you into thinking you're the dumbest person alive- but will start the next with with easy pre calc

He is a really good professor and does a good job presenting all of the material. However the class is very fast-paced, and it seems like he talks and writes in 1.5 speed. He is receptive to all questions (and if you don't like speaking out in big lecture halls, he has a google doc for questions which is helpful). Overall would highly recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: great lectures, makes what is expected clear.

Dr. Yearwood is a cool guy and did not give any homework for this class. The only assignments in this class were 3 exams, each worth about 33%. That being said, you want to do good on every exam (at least a B). He also tells you what will be on the exams in the exam review. Overall interesting class to take.

If you do not have any interest in geography please do not take this class. The final grade is made up of 3 exams (33% each) and if you do not understand the slides you will not do well. He posts the study guide and makes us go through the lecture slides all over again to answer the questions because he encouraged us not to take notes in class.
Unimaginably easy class, he literally tells you what's on the tests. No homework.

DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!! He makes it seem like he wants to see us succeed but I got the lowest grade I've ever gotten at UMD on one of his exams because he tried to trick us multiple times throughout the test. His lectures are useless/unorganized and all he does is talk about random stuff. AWFUL!

The course was pretty straightforward and easy to do in regards to lectures and assignments. For assignments, there was only 5 easy assignments during the duration of the Winter semester. Make sure to participate during the zoom sessions. The only downside for the course is that Dr. Yearwood posted grades at the end of the semester.

I liked Dr. Yearwood. His lectures were a little boring, but he made them more entertaining by his random tangents he would sometimes go on. There was like 0 homework which was nice, and he tells you exactly what's gonna be on the test (all MC). Pretty easy class. I took it for my major, but it'd be a good gen ed credit too.
Yearwood was so bad, I want to give him a zero, but I can't do that, so I give him a one.

Yearwood is a joke of a professor. There is only about 150 available points for the semester. He refused to move the final exam online despite many students voicing their concerns with rising covid cases. He made people with covid take a zero for the final if they couldn't show up in person. He does not care about his students or his class.

Grade is almost entirely based on 3 poorly structured and poorly written exams. Lectures are useless- his teaching style is disorganized and he rarely says anything of value in class. You will get as much value from studying his slides (not a lot). Trust me, your time is far better spent doing literally anything else.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easiest credit ever! You dont have to show up for class and he posts everything onto a PowerPoint. Although it's a low maintenance class you do have to study for the exams, but most of the answers are on a Quizlet. The prof himself is really chill and he enjoys talking about the wonders of life, very entertaining.

The grading for the exams doesnt make any sense. Worked hard on the response and he took so many points off without any explanation. I am not sure how he made those decisions but my answer definitely worth more than 1.5 point. Just avoid if you can.

Takes points off for the most ridiculous things. Exams are weighed way too heavily and its hard to bring your grade up no matter what you do. Does not like you emailing him and is rude. Don't take if possible
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Awful professor. Extremely lazy. He wants grading to be as easy as possible and therefore expects you to read his mind and guess word for word what he wants you to write for exam answers. Even worse, he takes points off if you go above and beyond and explain the answer in depth. Strange, odd style and disorganized teaching method.
Horrible class avoid at all cost exams seem straight forward but he takes off points for the little things. Would not recommend this class even to the person I hate the most

Material is pretty easy to understand but the grading is tough and the fact you're not graded on many things does not help. He claims the exam answers are in the videos and slides but sometimes they're not which makes it even more work when completing exams and the answers are almost impossible to look up. prof also was kinda rude when emailing.

The material in this course is very easy to understand. However, the grading method that the professor uses is more than confusing and a bit unfair. I was able to pull a good grade, but I had to email the professor for points back and when emailing the professor, he seems very condescending. Additionally, there was a severe lack of communication.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I took this course because I heard it was great and not difficult. The format online was definitely very independent but people are being dramatic you can easily get a 100 on the exams you just have to over explain and he didn't really make that clear at first. He seems like a nice dude people need to give him a break. I recommend.

I've heard great things about this professor and this course. The online structure of the class is poor and he changed the exams during the pandemic to open response only. The class is not difficult, the downside is the exams because he is very picky and it's hard to do well. If you have to take it online don't do it, if its in person youre fine.

I was excited to take this course when I registered for it prior to the pandemic and the subsequent shift to "remote learning." However, this class has been dreadful thus far. The professor puts such minimal effort into teaching (posts picture slides every few days) and then attributes low exam scores to low effort on behalf of students.

I was so excited to take this class. I took him Fall 2020 at the height of the pandemic. He posted ppts consisting of mostly pictures with an occasional 3 min video of him giving an update. The tests were ridiculous! Most of us got low C's. Couldn't get my grade up after that. I (+others) reported him bc he was not grading us reasonably.

I took this class as a GenEd, and it was ok until we went online. He put minimal effort into this class during the pandemic. He only posted lecture slides and didn't lecture or even upload a recording of the lecture. The exams were "open-answer" questions and he demanded ridiculously specific answers for them.

I've heard that this is one of the easiest classes at UMD but I took this online due to the pandemic. The one exam we had in person was easy but the remaining online exams were extremely difficult and harshly graded. He was not nice or understanding when it came to the switch online. If you're taking this class normally, I think you'll be ok tho

This is the sketchiest professor in the GEOG department. Class was easy at first, but once the pandemic came everything went haywire. All of the exam questions were trick questions. He comes in at the end gives everyone extra credit trying to be a savior. If you can take this class with another professor then go for it.
Exams are written responses due to online classes. Demands extremely specific answers for each question. Doesnt lecture at all, only puts the slides up.
Gives the dumbest exams. If you dont answer the questions verbatim, then its wrong. Goes on about his personal life in lectures. Very disorganized, but Ill cut him some slack due to COVID-19.

Dr. Yearwood is super chill and cares about his students. His lectures aren't really mandatory because he tells you what you need to know for the exam. They aren't as easy as he says but as long as you study you'll do well. Don't bomb the first exam because it'll be hard to recover.
Not difficult, but your grade is almost wholly dependent on tests. Lecture is optional and usually pretty entertaining.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Group projects

reviews.comment: Keith Yearwood was my favorite professor this semester. He is such a cool guy and really just wants you to do well and learn about the course and about life in general. Super laid back and always available for office hours. He is extremely clear about exactly what you need to know for each exam so as long as you pay attention you will get an easy A

One of the best teachers ever! really cares about his students and wants them to do well, an amazing lecturer too. Would definitely take another one of his classes in the future. grades by few things though and tests are a bit tricky so be prepared. The notes are all online so you don't have to go to lecture but he'll make it worth your while

Dr. Yearwood is a very funny and entertaining professor. His lectures are definitely not mandatory, because all of the notes are posted and his test study guides are the EXACT QUESTIONS ASKED ON THE TEST. It really cannot get any easier than that. Now that being said, you really have to know the answers. The test questions are tricky so be careful

he always let us out of our lectures significantly early and canceled class a decent amount of times. he hypes up the tests to be a lot easier than they are which is frustrating but they're not that hard. he always gives a study guide which is helpful. just make a quizlet and study and you'll be fine. also, the powerpoints are all online and no hw.

Pls avoid Yearwood AT ALL COST!!! He thinks they are easy and straight forward but that's simply not true. There are only 3 exams and if you messed up one exam, you're basically doomed for the entire semester. If you don't have to take his class, DON'T!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The easiest class I've ever taken. Tells you the answers to the exams and watched movies half of the classes. Professor Yearwood genuinely cares about his students and tells super funny stories.

Yearwood explains how he is such a good eacher and if you listen and go to lecture you will pass. That is simply not the truth. His tests are much harder than HE thinks they are. While his lectures are quite interesting and easy to follow, the information does not match the materials on the test. And he can be real rude when the class struggles.

Only 3 grades that are each exams. He is very funny so lectures aren't boring, but he barely goes over notes and skips a lot of information. Test heavy, and his tests aren't as easy as he says they are.

Definitely take Yearwood to fulfill the natural science and iseries geneds. His tests are completely multiple choice but can be a little confusing if you don't read the questions properly. The slides are posted online so it's okay if you don't go to every lecture. I wouldn't say it's an easy A but I don't see why anyone would get lower than a B+.

A nice break from my stressful classes. Lectures felt like I was in middle school. Concepts were very easy and he tells you what's on the exams. Study and you can get an easy A or B. Entertaining lectures and I looked forward to them but skipped when I had other stuff to do. He realizes people don't show up and makes jokes about it. Cool dude

Get your science GenEd done here. Professor Yearwood tried to make it interesting and relatable. He understands that his class is taken for a GenEd, so there's no HW, just 3 exams and a discussion grade. Exams are multiple choice so you should study a bit and be fine. 10/10 would take his class again.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Highly recommend

Barely went to this class because it was super early, but when I went I loved his lectures. He is an intense guy, but he is actually a super nice guy who is smart and very cool to talk to and listen to. Exams were pretty hard so you definitely need to study multiple days in advance.
This is NOT an easy A! The tests are very confusing because the wording sucks! Unless you are a great MC test taker and study word for word then this will be an easy B.

This was one of my most stressful classes. This class is not an easy A no matter what other people say. He's rude to students. This class is definitely an easy B if you're okay with that. He gives the amount of answers on the test to get a B beforehand, but you have to do a lot of extra work to get to an A. He's also rude to students.
Easy B. You need to study to get an A. He won't give extra credit.

Dr. Yearwood is an awesome professor. I could have easily skipped any of his lectures, but they were just so entertaining I could not resist. He always gave out a study guide before the tests so you would know what to look for on his multiple choice tests. His tests had some trick questions. His accent is also awesome

Started each lecture complaining how poorly students are doing, the lack of attendance, we're asking too many questions, & mocking students. Never answered my emails, didn't answer questions during exams. Exams were subjective & confusing; questions asked which was the least accurate, synonymous definitions ("shake" vs "tremble"), etc. Frustrating.

HE DOES NOT GIVE GOOD FEEDBACK! I have went to office hours to see what I got on my exam and he told me to leave because he thought I was making a big deal. I took another exam and had questions about the wording of the question and he told me to just answer them and walked away! He think it is so easy that you shouldn't care which I did not like.

This class is very easy information and only based off of 3 exams and they are all multiple choice. You do not have to do anything in this class besides study the guides he gives! But beware, the MC can be tricky if you did not study really really well.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you're taking him for GEOG140 don't worry about the GEOG200 reviews, they sound like actual geog majors. Keith knows 140 is an easy science credit and makes that abundantly clear, but his lectures are still pretty interesting if you feel like going. Show up to a couple discussions for points, study the review guides, easy A.

Worst professor I have had in my time at the university. Would spend half the class complaining about attendance. He was arrogant, disrespectful, and condescending. Sent out several emails mocking students answers on finals. Incorrectly calculated my final grade.

I would encourage you all to not look at the negative reviews! While there are only three tests, worth 75% of your grade, he gives you all of the questions in advance with almost a week to prepare. The other 25% of your grade is discussion, and if you just show up, there's no reason why you can't get 100% in that category-an easy Natural Science!

DrKeith  is an cool prof, the best I had so far. He teaches a level above he tests, but his tests are easy A's.  Attendance not mandatory, but everyone shows up to the lecture before the exam date. He gives you some answers and exactly what will be on. PowerPoints are posted online, when he wants to, but he might have some interesting lec. stories.

Worst teacher I have ever had. He is so rude. He sucks. Save yourself and don't ever take his class. Also, he is mean to students when they try to make appointments with him. Literally should not be able to teach!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Showed up to one or two discussion and about 30% of lectures and got an A. Ridiculously easy, you barely have to attend class. But he will incorporate life lessons and he is passionate about going beyond just geography. He wants the best for his students and he is funny about it--made me want to show up. The easiest A you will get. Take it.

Awesome teacher and a really great guy overall. Gives 3 exams and gives you all questions on it in the class before it. Really passionate about what he teaches, very simple class overall. He even told my class he designs the class to help you get an A. Super easy class with material that is quick to pick up. Take his classes if you get the chance.

You don't need to come to class. You don't need to pay attention in class if you do go. The tests are straight from the study guide that he gives a week prior to the exam. Study the study guide and get a A on the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Had him for GEOG140. Super easy class; your grade is only made up of 3 exams, which he gives out a study guide for. He uploads the notes online so you don't even have to go to lecture. As a lecturer, he's fairly good, I guess. You might find him a bit annoying, but overall I feel he is passionate about what he teaches.

Prof. Yearwood is an awesome guy. For my class, there were three exams. Before each exam he would give you a study guide that was nearly identical to the actual exam. No textbook, no homework. You do one presentation in the discussion that takes minimal to no effort and the powerpoint itself can be done in one class. Highly recommend this prof.
The greatest professor you will ever have at UMD.
Best ever

He gives only 3 exams in the whole semester. That's the only bad thing that I can think of about his class! I took his Freshman Connection class on Natural Disasters so my experience may be different than others but I loved his class overall! Yeah its kinda hard bringing up your grade once you get a bad one but the material isn't that hard!
He gives you everything you need to be able to do amazing in the class. just show up and pay attention! He is also so sweet and understanding and tries to teach you life lessons as well as geography.
He gives 3 test so it's easy for him to mess you over
As a first-semester freshman, he showed me that not all professors are like the ones in the movies. Super funny and taught me a lot. Taking another class from him next semester!

She is a tough grader for a 1 credit UNIV100 class, and also only provides vague feedback on assignments. Class activities always felt forced and she often had mandatory assignments to go attend university events and functions. UNIV100 is annoying class to take in general and she made it more difficult than it had to be.

The class is redundant, but Anzyl herself is a caring person. Except for the journals, you should be able to get an A or B on most assignments. There is more to this class than it seems, though, so remember to do the work, as not doing so can set you back. She will understand if you get sick and miss out as well, just let her know ahead of time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hope to god that you don't have to take UNIV100 in the first place. The course is set up as an extended orientation, which I feel is kind of pointless and redundant. As for Anzyl herself, she is a nice person. She is very accessible outside of class and gives some moderately good feedback. However, she is a tough grader, so be prepared for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Environmental History is boring as it is, and a monotone lecturer does not help. Prof may have the most flat voice of all time and it does not help when trying to understand this already uninteresting material. This class is entirely dependent on completing the extensive and dense weekly readings. There are only 2 essays essays and the final. 4/10.

History 205 was a fantastic class. The perspective was interesting and a new way of viewing and analyzing history. One final thing, although this was TA Justin Shapiro's last time teaching the course, I will acknowledge him on a job well done. He knows the subject and only wants to see you succeed, and is not condensing whatsoever.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Avoid hist205 and probably any of his other courses. The T.A. Justin Shapiro is very condescending and not helpful. The class is unnecessarily difficult to get an A in and I really regret taking it. I am passionate about the environment and was genuinely interested in the class at the start but Zeller's lectures were unbearably monotonous.

I would recommend this class with this teacher. As far as assignments, there's a wkly discussion (1 para. - super easy), 1 3-5 pg paper, and midterm and final, for which he gives you all the terms you need to know ahead of time. You don't really need to read the books; he covers everything in lecture. He's great - plus he has a German accent :)

Professor Zeller was great.  I took an online class with him in which the duration of the course was shortened from 16 to 8 weeks.  The material was condenses, but I felt he did a great job presenting the material.  He didn't go overboard with the assignments and was fair when it came to grading. Enjoyed the class.
Go to class, take notes; he's pretty clear about what's important/what to write down and remember. Generally friendly and helpful when you ask questions. Recommended.

Professor Zeller is useless as an educator. The material he covers is ill-defined, and it is difficult to determine what he wants students to get out of it. Grading in the course is arbitrary, at best, and based on standards that he refuses to share with the class. Avoid his courses if you can.

Good professor! Thought I was going to have a hard time in the class since I was the only junior in the class, but I ended doing well.  He likes to see you in class most of the time.  I recommend this class, history 407, if you like history and or like technology.  He is random with some of his work, but likes to also work it into the flow of the c
Terrible professor! Do not take this class with him. Almost everyone in the class got a low B or C, even though this is just a scholars class. His grading is harsh and doesn't make any sense.
prof zeller isnt so bad, its not true you cant get an A in his class, exams are fine if you can write well

Note- I took El-Amine's class at American University not UMD. I was very nervous about taking his class but I absolutely loved it. As long as you show up and show interest in the material, you will do great. He has a lot of interesting information to share and is easily accessible and approachable.

Zein was on his phone most of class and showed very little respect to his students. This included smirking and rudeness in his emails and conversations. He lost my homework and entered my grade wrong several times and then told me not to contact him again unless it was significant when I emailed him politely asking to correct my grade.
DO YOURSELF A HUGE FAVOR. DO NOT TAKE ZEIN'S CLASS!!!

Beware of Zein! When Zein is not having a good day, he is MEAN and that is everyday. Zein is not very professional and his teaching style is all over the place. I would not take Zein's class. He's a joke

Tells stories- fun to listen to. Helps out when he can. Is cool like 98% of the time but every once in a while if he's having a bad day he can be seriously mean. Worth it though, he's a great teacher.

I really liked Zein-- he spends enough time on course materials that you learn a lot, but he breaks up the monotony of Arabic grammar and vocab with little stories about Arab culture or his own life experiences.

Make sure you figure out the assignment schedule early. I already knew much of the material going into the course and because I didn't do much homework, struggled for my C+ in the end. Go see Zein during his office hours for advice, he's helpful and often sympathetic if you explain what you were going for in a presentation, ect. I learned a lot.

Don't listen to the other reviews. Zein is a wonderful professor you just have to put in great effort! He does not hand grades out you have to work for your grade. He offers help if you ask for it as long as you show effort. He is a very nice professor and very personable. If you show interest in learning, he will absolutely do all he can to help!
I would not recommend Zein to anyone.

Zein is cool as a person, but an awful professor, at least for my class. He seemed bitter that he didn't get a TA. He seemed very lazy and did not explain ANY material in class besides words on a case by case basis. He told us it is teach yourself style and class is for practice. I can get practice for free elsewhere. Pick another professor.
Zein is the greatest professor! This class is challenging and very intensive, but he makes it so much fun!

Grades are not posted online and there are 4 assignments each worth 25% of your grade. She doesn't use powerpoints which can be difficult since you have to write everything down as she's talking. Topics are interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: My class was basically just conversations about different facets of homophobia in society. It took me a little while to feel comfortable sharing (because I'm not a member of LGBTQI comm. but everyone else was), but once I did, it felt just like a really woke conversation. She cares about the cause and wants everyone to get something out of class.

Class was pretty good. Shes Sorta old fashioned (doesnt post grades or lectures, uses an attendance book) but nothing wrong with that. We had one personal assignment and a group project. We had two 100 question exams so STUDY, READ AND TAKE NOTES. She always looked for our opinion on stuff. HowverShe could have been clearer on the group prject tho.

I took Dr. Zeiger's class for an elective in my major. She is simply just an awesome professor. I would take her again and I will recommend this class to anyone in my major needing an elective. She shares personal stories that relate to lectures when necessary, allowing students to get a better understanding. Come to class, and take notes.

Robyn's been at UMD for 100 years, and doesn't BS her students. You learn a lot in her class, really easy grader (REALLY cares about her students), and is overall really chill.  It's nice to focus on actually learning rather than stressing over grades - and she knows it. You'll HAVE to read for exams, & she doesn't use ELMS... but super low stress.

Dr. Zimmerman is a great lecturer/teacher. He does not give unnecessary homework. His lectures are simple yet inspirational, very practical as he makes sure everyone in the class grasp the information before moving on. I will take his classes again!

The kind of guy that confuses himself even more than he confuses the class, which is impressive. His teaching style was nonexistent, and he often relied on other students to explain the material in class. Avoid taking him if you can.

He has no idea what he is teaching. His grading scale is messed up. If you ask him for help he responds by saying to go "read your notes" even though he can't teach. I do not recommend this teacher if you are not knowledgeable of the material beforehand.

I am currently in his class and we are 4 weeks behind in material.  I sit in the back of class doing crossword puzzles because I am so extremely frustrated.  None of the information is conveyed and we never stay on topic.  It's unfortunate, cause I was really looking forward to learning theory this year.

Professor clearly knows his material although he sometimes is unable to relate the information to the students. He is a dedicated teacher and friendly outside of class. Serious students who are willing to undertake a serious and committed approach to music theory and form will benefit the most from his courses.
No Comments
Very bad.  Worst professor in the school of music and the worst that I have had in my 4 years at Maryland.  Avoid at all costs.  If you have to take his class, go - and bring a crossword.
WORST TEACHER FOR ANYTHING! DOESN'T RESPOND WELL TO CHALK!
Worst theory teacher!

After this semester, Dr. Zafft is taking a break from teaching. The class was online during Fall semester. The exams were sometimes difficult and it was a lot of reading/videos but you did it at your own pace during the week. There was discussions, exams, and a paper. If you complete discussions that can help your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I wouldn't recommend taking this class online. There is a lot of readings, lectures, and videos to get through each week. There is also discussion, papers, and exams in addition to everything so it is overwhelming. I would recommend taking this course in person so you don't feel so overwhelmed especially in the summer.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Zafft is hilarious and really knows what she is talking about. There is a lot of reading and she has frequent quizzes throughout but you can drop the lowest one. There is a big paper but it is simple as long as you don't leave it for the last minute, it is a lot of work. I would definitely recommend taking this class in person, not online.

Dr. Zafft made this class enjoyable, which made up the fact that you couldn't skip class (doesn't post lecture slides). She makes the otherwise dull nature of theories and such engaging by including jokes or showing documentaries in class. Only downside I saw to this class was that the exam averages weren't the best, but study and you'll b great.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Zafft gives really interesting lectures and I found the material to be very interesting. There were no exams in this class, which was awesome. She gives daily clicker quizzes and drops the lowest ones so you have to do the readings, but they aren't bad. She tries to make her class really manageable for students and doesn't overload with work.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Took her winter course and lets just say Im glad Im done. She alleged a textbook was not required however provided scanned copies of other textbooks online but did not specify what the titles of the textbooks were or their authors. Rather odd since in academia crediting authors and books are required. It is also a copyright infringement.
Grade is made up of participation, daily 3-4 question quizzes & weekly reflections. No exams & Dr Zafft is hilarious. If you dont want to guess on daily quizzes the book is mandatory.

Just finished 451 online with her, and it was awful. Why Zafft decided to go with all essay questions for the exams (they're worth half your final grade) is beyond me. Her "lectures" were prerecorded, boring, and about as engaging as listening to paint dry. Thankfully you can speed them up which helped, slightly. Avoid at all costs, she's terrible

BORING Professor and boring course! the lectures were prerecorded yet distracting as you could hear everything going on in her background. Such as her dog, a person running water, and moving dishes. She made the course much harder than it needed to be and it will not be applied to my real life work experience. The information is outdated.

Professor Zafft should stick to teaching the lower level courses. It was disappointing how she offers little to no assistance in a upper sequence required course. It was even more discouraging when a student would inquire about feedback or clarity in an assignment her responses were short as if you are supposed to already know the material.

Prof. Zafft was easily one of my favorite profs ever. She makes lecture kind of fun, even though some of the content can be quite dull. Grades were largely based on exams, but they were easy to ace if you studied a bit. None of the lecture slides are online though, so attendance is key. She was easily accessible outside of class too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Zafft's lectures are informative and entertaining!! She cares for her students and always puts in effort to communicate with them. The class itself isn't hard if you attend lecture and read the textbook. MAKE SURE YOU GO to DISCUSSion for participation. I missed one discussion accidentally and it dropped my final grade to an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A very good professor. Grades very fairly. Very funny and interesting lectures. No homework except reading a book and 1 theory paper. Tests are fairly easy, all multiple choice, and the final is not even cumulative. Would definitely recommend her!

Zafft makes CCJS105 easy to pass if you put in enough work. Exams are hard (especially the second one) if you don't go to lecture and review the material. The book isn't necessary but it's super helpful for studying. She makes lecture interesting for an intro class and has a great sense of humor. There is one theory paper, not too hard.

Material itself isnt difficult to understand, but the quizzes and exams are more difficult than they should be. The quizzes are short answer instead of MC which makes it harder, and some of the wording for exams could be misinterpreted/tricky. Her criteria for the paper is also very unclear and doesnt give constructive feedback.
Zafft grades things way too harshly for someone who doesn't provide good instructions on papers or constructive feedback.
Great teacher, funny and keeps you interested. One of my favorite professors at UMD. Tests aren't exactly an easy A, but if you study you will be fine.
Used the book JUST enough for it to be necessary. Exams are definition heavy but fairly easy.
This class was very interesting and not too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tests? Not many--Amazing lectures--Would take again

reviews.comment: Prof. Zafft is great. Had her for CCJS225 and CCJS345. Her lectures are always interesting and she knows how to relate to her students. Tests may be a little challenging, but she gives multiple opportunities for extra credit. Attendance is mandatory if you want a good grade and she's very helpful in office hours.

This class was honestly such a breeze as long as you took good notes and put in the effort towards studying for tests, which are all multiple choice. She offers multiple opportunities for extra credit and is such a funny professor. Love her!
Great teacher! Must study for tests.

Dr. Zafft is a great professor. She's hilarious and keeps her lectures interesting. Her tests are kind of hard, and worth 75% of your grade, but she gives extra credit. If you go to class and take good notes, getting an A shouldn't require much effort.
Zafft is a funny teacher. Class is definitely light on material compared to other ccjs classes. Not a bad class at all though.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Pretty good class and pretty good lectures. Her exams and quizzes weren't difficult as long as you read the assigned texts and take notes during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great class and great professor! Make sure you actually read the textbook and attend lecture because she takes attendance and they take attendance in discussion too. If you stay on top of your work you'll do fine in the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Zafft is amazing. Her lectures are very interesting. Her exams aren't difficult if you read the textbook and take notes. This was definitely my favorite class. As long as you go to lecture, read the textbook, and take notes, you should get an A.

Dr. Zafft was so funny and made criminology really relatable. Although she sometimes watered down course material too much in lecture, a majority of what was on the exams were taught in class, meaning you do have to get the textbook to do well. Her discussion sections weren't the best, maybe a B-, but lecture is amazing. She made me really love it
exams are difficult...
He is a fine teacher and has a passion to teach. he is unclear about syllabus sometimes but always accessible if you send an email. not the best i had but not the worst either.

This is probably the worst class that I have taken at this school. The teacher is so unorganized that he lost my exam and made me retake it. He also was never clear when any assignments were due and he would randomly assign quizzes the day of. WOULD NOT RECCOMEND!!

This instructor did an absolute terrible job. He spoke with a very strong accent was hard to understand. His instruction was so poor that not even 50% of the class showed up. Then he also was very unclear about when the homework was due. Do not take this class. 1.5 stars

She's amazing! Professor Zomback is a respected expert. Throughout the course, it was clear that she cared deeply about her students and was very flexible with her curriculum. Her lectures involved well-paced lessons with frequent participation grades. Attendance isn't mandatory, but her teaching style and professionalism make the class.

Jenna is great! She is so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. She takes care to avoid all types of suprises and unexpected questions and really wants you to do well. Her office hours are super helpful and she will answer any question you have. Homework is also complete-at-your-own-pace.

Please if you're taking Math 120 take Jenna. She is great, I've never taken calc before and I got overall a pretty easy A. She makes the material easy to understand if it's new and is super lenient on homework due dates as long as it gets done. Discussion quizzes are easy and helpful. You can get clicker participation in class.

Dr. Zou was one of if not my most favorite professors to have learned from in my college career. She has a level of insight and care when addressing systemic racist issues that's motivated me to want to learn more even outside of the classroom. She focuses her assignments to be more written so you can reflect and personally apply them.

This is overall a pretty great class. Professor Zou is super friendly and presents information in an engaging way. There are clicker questions and discussion sections, but there are also a lot of opportunities for extra credit, due date extensions, and dropped grades. One downside is that her TAs grade papers and they can be a bit harsh at times.

She is a great teacher and her lectures were very easy to follow. There are a few essays you have to write but the rubric is clear and the TAs are very useful for answering questions. You do receive a grade regarding how much work you put in, but as long as you go to lecture and study you will do good in the class.

I love her! she is so personable, understanding and very clear. She gives you grades based on the work you put in so I really appreciated that. She grades very thoroughly too so make sure you are putting effort into your work. She was very easily accessible outside of class. If I could take her again, I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A solid professor who makes you work for the material, but you leave the class feeling like you learned something.

Professor Zou is my favorite professor I've had so far at UMD! I took her PSYC 232 (Psychology of Racism) class first semester, and then PSYC 221 second semester. She is relatable, caring, and gives extremely interesting lectures. She is very accommodating to your needs and overall is an amazing professor. Take her classes if you can!
Amazing professor. Alweays super understadning and really cares about her students.
One of the best, most understanding professors. She understands that everyone is human and treats her students well. Her class is easy as long as you pay attention in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I think she truly cares about her students, however she is not the clearest professor. Grade was based off of two exams and one paper only, although you have the chance to retake everything. Lectures were based entirely on the book. No rubric for the paper, kinda confusing to know exactly what she wanted. She's super nice but wouldnt take again
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is so thoughtful, caring, and understanding. She is more focused on you learning than giving out pop-quizzes or tough grades. She is always open for feedback and will ALWAYS answer questions. She is the best teacher I ever had and ever will have at UMD ever.
WONDERFUL

I took him for literature at UNT and he is one of my favorite professors. He brings out interesting works to read on and we discussed them in class. I respect the fact that he genuinely cares about his work and wants us to learn and give him our opinion on how we feel about it. I highly recommend taking his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: He was not a bad professor part of the time. He  had his reasoning's for his assignments and he included good meaningful lectures in his classrooms. Though I could be very frustrated by the fact the he never replies to his emails, he did help me get the grade I needed in this course. Thanks Professor Zuehlke!

I LOVE THIS GUY, he is passionate about his work and encourages his students to excel and break past the typical boundaries on thought. He encourages his students to form their own views and even debate with him in class. I've taken another class with him before and came back because he is an amazing professor. There are a lot of readings and work.

He recently moved to University of North Texas where I took his class. He's very informative and open to questions if you don't understand something. Pretty funny guy. Kinda hippie looking but very smart. He keeps your attention but some of the readings can be somewhat hard.(There's a lot to)But definitely goes by his syllabus.

i will just say, I am in love with this man. He's hilarious, cute, and well-dressed. But he is also just a fantastic prof. to have in your first year of college. Yes, he can be a tough grader, but if you work hard and are engaged in discussions you will not only get at least a B, you will learn a WHOLE lot.

I took this class because I love to write, and Karl made every effort to destroy that passion. He encompasses every English-snob stereotype, and allows no room for points of view, opinions, and styles besides his own. He fails to understand the difference between constructive criticism and cruelty, and despite my A+, I regret taking this course.

At first Karl comes off very rude and mean, but over the course of the semester, he proved to actually know what he was talking about. There are four papers, and as a student who usually does well in english, I was a little disappointed in my grades, I got a C on three of them and an A on one of them so he definitely grades hard.
He's great! He's an easy grader and he really gets you to think!

4 papers to write in 4 months of class and you have to put FULL EFFORT into them to get an A. he is considerate. too many journals and readings for every class...generally really hard... if there exists an easier prof. please take then instead...but pretty much every engl101 student HAS to write 4 papers of similar topics so yeah
meh
Karl changed my life.

Karl is not a very good teacher at all.  His explanations of assignments are very vague but his expectations are very specific.  It is nearly impossible to do well in his class unless you have already mastered the material before taking his class.  I didn't feel like I learned a thing from him.
Zuehlke's teaching methods are very interesting and he does a very good job keeping the attention of student. His class is a fun class to be in. However, he can be a tough grader sometimes.
He is an exceptional teacher... I took him as an online professor at BCCC... He is an extraordinary professor... I will highly recommend anyone to take him if they want an easy A....
not very fond of his teaching style ( he does read out of the book) but he was a nice guy and he lets everyone know what they need to do to pass.

the person who doesn't like this professor is an idiot he is seriously the nicest man and just wants to help everyone.. he wants every one to get an A so he isn't sneaky he tells you what to to.. if you do your work you'll get an A if you don't you won't and thats how it should be

Tells you exactly what you need to know. 4 exams and 2 outside assignments in court/corrections. Read what he goes over in class in preparation for exam studying and you'll be fine. Very helpful and extremely nice man.

Read the capsules, get an A, plain and simple, 2 exams and 6 outside assignments in court which are very simple. Only meet 4-5 times a semester, we met at the beginning, for the midterm, to turn in the assignments, and for the final. Very simple.

I seriously don't know what's wrong with the people who said this man is excellent. I honestly cant believe he gets paid by the university.  If administrators saw him teach, they would give him the boot.  He doesnt teach, he literally reads the book to you for an hour and then gives you a middle-school level exam.  Easy A, but a waste of education

He is a great professor- very helpful and straightforward.  For lectures he reads out of the book.  Make sure you know the rule of law for each case and you till do just fine on the exams.  The text is great because it tells you exactly what the rule of law for each case is. This is a good class to take if you are looking for an easy one.
cool class went to lecture one time besides the exams and got a B he wants everyone to get A's so the questions match up with the book. f.ucking easy man
Excellent teacher

Very nice person, and the class is really easy if you memorize all the cases (use flash cards). But the lectures are BORING-he reads out of the book. The only learning you will do will be in your reading.
excellent great man

Easy teacher...easy exams, excatly from the book. Class lectures very boring. Go to class though he takes role. No trick questions on exams, only 2 exams and one final, 4 easy court case due late in semester. Nice teacher.
exams are exactly your notes...
Dr. Z is amazing.  He makes sense and is very clear in explaining subject matter.  I would reccomend him to anyone preparing for law school.  Very intelligent and has lots of stories!
Wonderful, caring man.  Great teacher.  Easy classes.  He was one of my favorite teachers on campus!

This man's classes are a waste of time.  He will read out of the book. Very popular with athletes, because he is a  big  fan, and will  help  them pass.  If you want an easy A, take the class. If you want to learn something, take another class!
No Comments
One of the best professors at UM. A great mentor. A great scholar. Goes above and beyond to help his students.

Taking her class as an integrated upper level Geography requirement. I thought the topic- social urban problems- sounded interesting but her teaching method (or lack there of), condescending attitude, and lack of respect and regard for students make this class close to unbearable. She is a poor professor and a poorer communicator! Terrible class.

Mila is good for the student that comes to class to learn.  She is not a professor that spoon feeds you; she expects you to do your part as well.  Her tests are harder than anything and her papers require research than you could ever imagine.  But, you walk away a better student.

This is not a hard class. Demography is very interesting and Zlatic is experienced and intelligent. Engage her in class, ask her questions, she has great stories to tell that supplement her lectures. She likes to go on tangents but they are eye opening. Papers are tough to research but just do exactly what she say and your gold. Never compare to US

I took her for political geography and this has by far been the EASIEST upper level class I've ever taken. There is one huge term paper but she makes you do a proposal, outline, and a rough draft which makes it easy to get a good grade. People who say she's rude are clearly all American- she is Croatian and obviously there are cultural differences.
has a tendency to go on tangents, but generally very interesting.  Really easy graded

This is a good advanced studies core class, but if you have a very big work load already I don't recommend it. Yes, she is strict about attendance, but generous with guidance and assistance. You should be prepared for the tests-they're hard and sometimes oddly worded. But overall, no big complaints, she definitely knows her stuff.

Yes, she is strict. Class can be boring and tests are hard. Papers are graded fairly especially if a decent writer. I always got 100%, you just have to follow directions. She wants students to do well and repeatedly tells everyone to email or stop by office if they need help. You will need to do a lot of learning on your own/book.
She's totally nightmare!! I hate her! she can't teach, she's so boring and not interesting, and if you do not have, don't take her classes!

Just do your work, you will get thru it. Don't act like she is there to cater to you. Its really hit or miss. I had her for MANY of my classes- so I got used to it. Just do what she tells you to do, read the slides, and attempt to listen/participate and you walk away with a B. Turn papers in Early- do exactly what she says to them. Not that hard

she is very socialist and hates capitalism, and America.  she is very condescending as well.  She critiques your papers by leaving comments that are not grammatically correct and will even write "LEARN how to write!!!" how unproffesional

I feel the reviews are a bit harsh, heres the deal: Yes you have to go to lectures, Yes you have to read the book (which was painful mind you). Yes she likes to talk about cities (Because that is what the classes are about). I barely read the book and went to class, the term paper is dry. BUT she has an optional turn in draft date so easy grade

Class was mediocre, not horribly boring or interesting, just ok.  the real problem is with her papers.  She's really unclear about what she wants and you have to keep meeting with her to get her to be perfectly happy...and then she changes her mind.  B+

I'm incredulous at the reviews here. She's not a great communicator, but she is very intelligent and if you care about the class you will definitely learn many things. Her "tangents" are probably her best teaching aids. Never felt her to be condescending, although maybe confusing at times... Also, don't bother with the textbook, we never used it.
I HATE HER!!!She is an absolute nightmare and should absolutely not be allowed to teach or communicate with anyone of the human race. NEVER EVER take her classes. She is unfair and confusing

She is unfair and condescending. Very rude to her students unless you suck up to her. Her class is boring and she cant make it through more than 7 slides in an hour. She is sometimes hard to understand. Her papers are ridiculous and unnecessary. Then she makes you talk about them the class after theyre due. DONT take this class unless you HAVE to.

she is hard to understand, talks down to everyone, if you didn't live in a city for your whole life she will hate you, or if you say anything negative about cities. She doesn't back up what she says at all, so expect utrue gross generalizations. She also preaches her own beliefs ALOT! she is very socialist and hates capitalism, and America.

The rest of her reviews on here, and anywhere are absolutely right. It is a hit or miss with her as far as clicking with her overall- grades,lecture,papers. She is a good person outside of her class, and I even did her study abroad in Croatia- BUT- still is not a GREAT teacher, informative, but teaching college classes-should not be her thing

Not an interesting professor at all. She cant speak clearly and is very hard to follow. Most classes she just rambles on for the class time, going off on tangents and not encouraging class participation. She seems very rude and cold towards students at times so be careful when speaking out in class. Overall very boring and only take her if have to.

You will write lots of papers. She has her own unique style and format that she requires for the papers, most of which is very confusing and/or illogical. Her lectures are boring. She will repeat the same thing over and over and often stutter and stumble her way through in a very monotone voice.    Group work also required. Avoid this class.

her slides are pretty much the bulk of the lecture, and she posts them to blackboard. if you don't know blackboard before the class, then you'll know it well after it b/c it's the only way she'll let you turn things in. she was a little vague about the projects we did and didn't really describe them well until after we did them the wrong way.
goes off topic a lot, but she's interesting
Mila's a nice lady but this particular class was pretty BS. Be nice to her and get on her good side.

She was a good teacher only if youre interested in the subject. I made a big mistake in taking Political Geography and not knowing anything about either.  She expects everyone to know a good amount of political or geographical info. she has a thick accent and her english isnt the best and she takes long pauses when she talks. lots of patience neede

she doesn't teach in a classic way, but i think that she did a really good job. the only thing is that she does pick favorites. she is very knowledgable and i learned a lot! i enjoyed this class very much, but it is a matter of taste.

I know many people don't like her teaching style, but I learned a lot in this class. Her notes are very clear and the content of the class is great, but she's like your worst middle school teacher when it comes to class participation: she tries to find the person who didn't do the reading so she can humiliate them. Ok class, I got an A.

She is a very cold teacher.  Difficult to follow and understand.  No people skills whatsoever.  Her assigned work and exams are awfully confusing. She is a very rude lady and very un-inspiring.  She drags the geography department at the University of Maryland way, way down.  Its a tragedy that she is a professor.
